frederick-tranter-bath-breeze.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Frederick Tranter's Bath Breeze blend; records place it in the aromatic class.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-liquorice.z: Referred to as a licorice-root-flavored version within the Kendal Gold shag series; no reliable sourcing giving details specific to this version's composition and character could be found.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-liquorice.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of licorice root and anise.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-county-se.z: County Seat is The Country Squire tobacconist's apple-flavored house blend. The top note is kept measured, with the cavendish and natural leaf underneath balanced so as not to overshadow the flavoring. On the smoke, apple sweetness is steady but not overpowering; the leaf's own nutty and grassy notes stay in the background. Nicotine is low and the burn is cool. It suits smokers who like fruity aromatics but want to avoid a syrupy intensity. It is among the blends sold by weight at the tobacconist's Jackson shop.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-county-se.o: Leaves a scent of baked apple and cinnamon-free pastry.

sutliff-tobacco-company-600-mixture-79.z: Mixture No. 79 is one of the old market blends of American pipe tobacco tradition; Sutliff's bulk version, numbered 600, carries anise, vanilla extract, and a touch of whiskey flavoring over roasted burley leaf. Its markedly anise-forward character sets it apart from most aromatic mixtures on the market. Its body carries burley's fullness, while its flavor is sweet and cola-like; tendency to bite the tongue is low. A distinctive example for smokers seeking to sample classic American bulk blends and anise character.
sutliff-tobacco-company-600-mixture-79.o: Leaves a sweet, heavy, cola-like scent dominated by anise and vanilla.

dunhill-standard-mixture-medium.z: Standard Mixture Medium is the middle grade of the Standard Mixture line Dunhill established in 1921. It's an unadulterated, ribbon-cut English mixture built from Virginia, oriental and latakia leaves. Latakia isn't as dominant here as in Full; however, compared to other members of the same family such as Mixture 965, its soot proportion is noted as clearly standing out. It's a medium-strength, medium-flavor blend, built for balance suitable for all-day smoking. It suits smokers seeking a measured but clear latakia character and those wanting to become familiar with the classic English repertoire. For many years it was a familiar product found in duty-free shops' five-tin sets; after Dunhill exited tobacco production, the recipe has been continued under the Peterson name.
dunhill-standard-mixture-medium.o: Leaves a heavy soot and burnt-wood scent in the room; the impression is strong enough to cling to clothing.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-winter-edition-2.z: The 2014 installment of Kohlhase & Kopp's winter-season limited series; no verifiable source could be found regarding this edition's contents and casing.

havana-magasinet-husets-spesial.z: A topped house blend prepared for a tobacco shop; there is not enough sourcing on its composition, cut, and production period.
havana-magasinet-husets-spesial.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

edwards-honey-cavendish.z: This is one of Edward's Pipe & Tobacco's in-house, cavendish-based blends prepared in the shop; not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition and character.
edwards-honey-cavendish.o: Could not be described due to insufficient records.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-military-force.z: Military Force is an English mixture built from Latakia, toasted Virginia, aged cube-cut burley and Oriental leaf. Latakia gives the smoky frame while burley carries the body and the Oriental adds spicy top notes; despite being layered, the smoke does not turn harsh. The manufacturer states the blend was prepared with smokers in the US military in mind. Suitable for smokers wanting to warm up to smoky mixtures or seeking a medium-bodied English blend.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-military-force.o: Leaves a wood smoke and soot aroma, with a dry spice trace behind it.

niall-of-nine-gut-stone.z: One of the blends prepared in very small batches under the Niall of Nine signature; not enough independent source material documenting its composition and character could be found.

city-cigar-company-lost-lagoon.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of Lost Lagoon, a house blend from the tobacconist City Cigar Company.
city-cigar-company-lost-lagoon.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-lord-nelson.z: Lord Nelson is one of Wilke's light aromatics constructed for all-day smoking. According to the maker's description, Virginia carries the body, joined by a small amount of black cavendish, topped with a vanilla note. The casing is measured; rather than masking the leaf's flavor, it brings forward Virginia's bready, sweet side. Staying in the lower-medium band for both nicotine and flavor, this record appeals to smokers wanting to move from aromatics toward leaf-forward blends, or seeking a low-intensity option for long bowls. It's part of Wilke's non-aromatic bulk listing and comes in various sizes.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-lord-nelson.o: Leaves a scent of light vanilla and sweet hay.

savinelli-the-balkans.z: The Balkans is a Latakia-forward mixture from the Italian pipe house Savinelli's series. Its structure holds virginias, earthy burley, spicy Oriental leaf, and a high proportion of latakia; the aroma that greets you on opening the tin gathers around wood smoke and dark earth tones. The medium-width ribbon cut makes packing easy and gives an even burn. The smoke is creamy and intense. The virginias leave a measured sweetness in the background, the Oriental leaf adds a floral, lightly astringent edge, and the latakia builds the profile's dominant smoky body. A blend for those accustomed to the fullness of Balkan-type mixtures who seek a full-bodied, layered smoke; it may be heavy for those used to aromatic tobacco.
savinelli-the-balkans.o: Leaves a scent evoking campfire smoke, wet earth, and dried fruit in the background.

robert-mcconnell-pure-virginia.z: Pure Virginia is a single-component, ribbon-cut product made entirely of Virginia leaf. It is the plainest member of Robert McConnell's pure component line, prepared without flavoring to preserve the leaf's natural taste. Its purpose is to support existing blends or to serve home blenders building their own mixtures. Smoked alone, its strength and flavor intensity stay low, which makes it well suited for use as a base or mellowing component in a blend. It is a starter component for smokers new to blending who want to understand Virginia's role within a mixture.
robert-mcconnell-pure-virginia.o: Leaves a dry-hay, faintly sugary tobacco aroma.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-skandinav.z: The Skandinavik series' base version; no sufficient primary source describing the blend's composition could be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-colts-sig.z: Colts Signature Blend is the aromatic premium entry in Scandinavian Tobacco Group's Colts line for the Canadian market. Its body is built by black cavendish; the sweet acidity of light Virginia and burley's dry, nutty base are added. Cocoa, hazelnut, and whiskey are used as top notes; so the casing sweetness and the leaf's own taste stand side by side. Being ribbon cut, it lights easily and burns evenly. Aimed at those seeking an aromatic blend with a noticeable body and not excessive sugar load.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-colts-sig.o: Leaves a scent of cocoa and toasted hazelnut sweetness mixed with whiskey's grainy edge.

ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-instant-crus.z: Referred to as a Virginia-Burley-axis small-batch blend tied to Ken Byron Ventures' Yoshimi's line; not enough sources could be found to document its composition.
ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-instant-crus.o: Could not be described due to lack of accessible records.

cornell-diehl-big-ben.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Cornell & Diehl blend Big Ben.

pcca-calumet.z: Calumet is one of the English-style blends McClelland tinned in limited numbers for the PCCA club; no independent source describing its composition could be found.
pcca-calumet.o: No source could be found to describe the room note.

w-o-larsen-w-o-larsen-edition-2022.z: This is one of W.Ø. Larsen's annual limited editions; no reliable source could be found regarding its composition and character.
w-o-larsen-w-o-larsen-edition-2022.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

racine-laramie-dr-charley.z: Dr. Charley is Racine & Laramie's best-selling house blend. It is a lightly flavored mixture built on plug-cut Burley; according to the shop's description it burns cool and mellow, leaving no bite on the tongue. It is described as burning slow and even, leaving dry white ash, and not requiring frequent relighting. Thanks to this burning behavior it suits smokers looking for a low-maintenance, all-day blend, as well as those wanting to get to know Burley character in its plain form.
racine-laramie-dr-charley.o: Leaves a light trace reminiscent of dry nuts and toast.

connoisseur-light-cavalry.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Connoisseur blend Light Cavalry.

lane-limited-golden-cavendish-slices.z: As its name suggests, a Lane Limited blend of cavendish-processed, sliced form; no notable independent source could be found.

edwards-mark-iii.z: No sufficient independent sourcing could be reached to document the composition and character of Mark III, a pipe tobacco from Edward's.

cornell-diehl-anthology-1992-2022.z: This blend, released in limited quantity as part of Cornell & Diehl's anniversary series, does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog; details cannot be given as not enough sourcing could be found to describe its content.

e-a-carey-mixed-coconut.z: A blend registered under the E. A. Carey name, said to be Virginia-forward; it does not appear on the maker's current blend list, and no reliable source could be found describing its composition.

pipesandcigars-com-scottys-great-hiatus.z: Scotty's Great Hiatus is cited as a blend connected to the Scotty's Bulk Blends line pipesandcigars.com had prepared under its own name; no independent source could be found documenting its content and character, so no detailed specification is given here.

sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-pipes-martin.z: Recorded as one of the special blends Sentimiento Nacional prepared for a tobacconist; no independent source to confirm its content could be found.
sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-pipes-martin.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

torben-dansk-999.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Torben Dansk blend called 999 has been found.

teds-pipe-shoppe-blackberry-winter.z: A house blend from Ted's Pipe Shoppe listed as an aromatic; no accessible source describing its composition could be found.

owl-shop-st-johns.z: St. Johns is the full-bodied English mixture among the Owl Shop's house blends. Turkish-Oriental leaf and Perique are added alongside latakia; the shop's description highlights a smoky, spicy character. With its unflavored structure, high flavor intensity, and pronounced nicotine fullness, it's intended for smokers accustomed to Latakia-heavy mixtures. It would be a heavy first blend for those coming from aromatic tobaccos.
owl-shop-st-johns.o: Leaves a scent of wood-fire smoke and spice.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-gidleigh-honey.z: Gidleigh Honey is McGahey The Tobacconist's honey-flavored house blend; the maker's description notes it gives a light, soft smoke and doesn't bite the tongue. Sufficient sources regarding the blend's leaf composition and cut could not be found.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-gidleigh-honey.o: Leaves a soft aroma carrying honeyed sweetness.

w-o-larsen-selected-blend-no-04-loose-le.z: No reliable source could be found regarding the composition and character of this entry in W.Ø. Larsen's numbered Selected Blend series; the series as a whole generally consists of light, moderately cased Danish blends.
w-o-larsen-selected-blend-no-04-loose-le.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

peterson-de-luxe-navy-rolls.z: De Luxe Navy Rolls is prepared from hand-selected Brazilian and African Virginias pressed together with Louisiana Perique into a rope, then sliced into coin-shaped rounds. The blend comes from the Dunhill catalog; after Dunhill stopped producing pipe tobacco, it was continued under the Peterson name with the recipe and tin artwork preserved. The smoke is medium-bodied. Virginia's ripe sugar opens with honey and citrus-peel associations; Perique adds depth in the direction of plum, pepper, and fermented fruit. The burn is slow and cool. It suits smokers familiar with Virginia-Perique blends who are used to rubbing out the coin slices and who age their tobacco.
peterson-de-luxe-navy-rolls.o: Leaves a measured trace recalling dry hay, plum, and a light pepper.

wessex-campaign-dark-flake.z: Campaign Dark Flake, the dark Virginia flake of the Wessex Brigade series, is produced by pressing and slicing Virginia leaf that has undergone a stoving process. The product description states it arrives dark brown, partly broken apart, and ready to pack into the pipe; the cut is flake, and the content is unflavored Virginia. Its character is deep and full, yet soft; it sits in the medium band on the strength scale and is described as intense enough to hold its flavor even in windy outdoor conditions. Since it arrives in the tin quite moist, airing it out for a while before packing is a common practice. This is a blend suited to smokers seeking unflavored, dark Virginia taste who are accustomed to preparing flakes.
wessex-campaign-dark-flake.o: Leaves a dark, bready, lightly caramel tobacco scent.

cafe-artin-original-choice.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named Original Choice under the CAFE ARTIN brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-special-d.z: Special Dublin Vanilla is the vanilla-flavored variety of the series. The base is built by lightly pressing and cutting Virginia leaf of US, African, and Brazilian origin and combining it with dark black cavendish; here vanilla replaces the whiskey echo that defines the series. The smoke is mild and sweet, leaving no sharpness on the tongue; nicotine load stays between low and medium. Suited to those seeking a classic Danish-style vanilla cavendish character and to pipe newcomers. According to records, the series is distributed in Europe by Scandinavian Tobacco Group, and the tobacco is prepared following the Danish production tradition.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-special-d.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and caramelized-sugar scent.

wesleys-no-1-rhodesian-blend.z: No verifiable information could be found from maker or retailer sources regarding this blend known under the Wesley's name and described in records as a plain Virginia character.
wesleys-no-1-rhodesian-blend.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-burley-flake-1.z: Burley Flake #1 is the first member of Cornell & Diehl's five-blend Burley Flake series. It is an unflavored flake in which dark burley and red Virginia are pressed and sliced; only a small amount of perique is added on top. The series as a whole is built around burley leaf, aiming to show how it changes with different components. Dark burley forms the blend's body and nutty, earthy core; red Virginia adds a bready sweetness, while perique brings a thin plum-and-spice edge. Because of its pressed structure it burns slowly and gives a cool smoke. Nicotine strength runs high. According to available records, the components draw closer together with aging. It suits smokers accustomed to flake preparation who want unflavored burley.
cornell-diehl-burley-flake-1.o: A light plum sweetness mixes into an aroma of toasted walnut and dry earth.

erik-stokkebye-afternoon-melange.z: Afternoon Melange is a classic English mixture built on aged Virginia and oriental leaves with a noticeable proportion of latakia. It is presented ribbon cut and sold in bulk; among the maker's day-part named blends from the same period, it carries the highest latakia share. The smoky, sooty character dominates, with the orientals adding a spicy, faintly sour layer on top. It suits smokers who love unadulterated, medium-bodied English mixtures and don't mind latakia's scent lingering in the room.
erik-stokkebye-afternoon-melange.o: Leaves a scent of pine smoke and soot, with a spicy dryness underneath.

watch-city-cigar-justice-mixture-15th-an.z: This is a limited-edition English blend Watch City Cigar released for its anniversary; no sufficient source could be found regarding its composition.
watch-city-cigar-justice-mixture-15th-an.o: Records note it leaves a smoky scent typical of Latakia-containing English blends.

pipesandcigars-com-starlit-night.z: This is a blend offered under the American retailer pipesandcigars.com's name; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

peter-stokkebye-kentucky-nougat.z: This is one of Peter Stokkebye's flavored blends; no sufficient first-hand sources documenting its content and character could be found.
peter-stokkebye-kentucky-nougat.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

park-lane-tobacconist-park-lane-no-7.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Park-Lane No. 7, one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

straus-tobacco-private-stock.z: Private Stock is one of the counter blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; records indicate the shop was founded in 1880 and that most of its house blends were named after Cincinnati neighborhoods and landmark buildings. Since no independent source on the blend's composition and character could be found, this record is kept at listing level only.

jack-lee-blend-honey-malt.z: This is an aromatic product flavored with honey and malt from the now-closed American blender Jack Lee Blend; no reliable source describing the leaf composition could be found.
jack-lee-blend-honey-malt.o: Leaves an aroma of honey and malt.

lane-limited-medal-of-honor.z: One of Lane Limited's English-style blends; not enough sources could be found to document its composition.

theodorus-niemeyer-flying-dutchman-black.z: Flying Dutchman was one of the best-known pipe tobaccos from the Theodorus Niemeyer house, founded in Groningen by Meindert Niemeyer in 1819. This version, called Black Cavendish, is a Cavendish-forward, milder take on the main blend: Burley and Cavendish-processed Virginia leaves form a dark-colored mixture ready to be rubbed out by hand. Licorice root and vanilla can be sensed in the pouch aroma; the casing is measured and does not mask the leaf. Its smoke is light and nicotine is low; despite being aromatic, the taste stays away from pronounced sweetness, running plain and mellow. A typical example for those wanting to get to know Dutch-style house tobaccos and after a low-intensity blend for all-day smoking. The brand later changed hands, production moved to Denmark for a period, and records indicate the blend was withdrawn from the market in the early 2010s.
theodorus-niemeyer-flying-dutchman-black.o: Leaves a sweetish aroma in the room reminiscent of a licorice root and vanilla mixture.

der-pfeifenladen-300.z: One of the numbered house blends of a German pipe shop, recorded as a straight Virginia type; no independent source giving a detailed profile could be found.
der-pfeifenladen-300.o: No reliable record could be found for the room note.

bennington-tobacconist-no-10-bahia-apook.z: No. 10, Bahia Apooke is one of the oldest among the shop blends Bennington has kept since 1965. Golden Virginia ribbon from the Old Belt region is hand-mixed with a considerable amount of Cyprus Latakia; long-cut St. James Perique is added along with a small amount of Kentucky white Burley for mellowness. The structure follows a classic English mixture line, but the addition of Perique moves the blend beyond the ordinary Latakia-Virginia equation: alongside the soot and leather note comes a layer of fermented fruit and pepper. The Burley share softens the smoke and thickens the body. It's aimed at smokers familiar with Latakia mixtures who want to add a spicy depth to that base.
bennington-tobacconist-no-10-bahia-apook.o: Woodsmoke and leather notes are joined by a plum-like tangy edge.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-apple.z: Referred to as an apple-flavored version within the Kendal Gold shag series; no reliable sourcing giving details specific to this version's composition and character could be found.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-apple.o: Leaves an apple and sweet tobacco aroma.

paul-olsen-no-46.z: One of the Virginia-forward blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

bufflehead-ring-necked-duck.z: Bufflehead was a brand producing small batches in the United States in the early 2000s, naming its blends after waterfowl; since no independent source describing this blend's content and character could be found, the entry has been left incomplete.

vegassmokes-browns-special-blend.z: A blend classed as aromatic bearing the VegasSmokes name; no independent source confirming its composition has been found.

nice-ash-cigars-awesome-amaretto.z: An aromatic blend flavored with amaretto, as its name indicates, prepared at Nice Ash Cigars' shop in Depew; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.
nice-ash-cigars-awesome-amaretto.o: No description could be found in the records.

bosphorus-2016s-value-flake.z: Value Flake is one of the products Bosphorus introduced in 2016. It is built from red Virginia, Oriental, burley and perique leaf, and due to the special fermentation method applied, nearly all the slices come out nearly black. It is pressed into flake form; since it is moist as it comes out of the tin, airing it for a day or two before filling reduces wetness and clogging. Perique's spicy intensity and the fullness burley gives determine the blend's strength; yet the Oriental and Virginia taste, along with the light bitterness and spice characteristic of Turkish tobaccos, stays distinguishable. The smoke is cool and sweet, and this sweetness does not mask the tobacco taste. Suitable for smokers seeking Perique and a strong blend, wanting a full fill later in the day.
bosphorus-2016s-value-flake.o: Leaves the fermented leaf's sweetish, lightly spicy, woody aroma.

charles-fairmorn-dark-fired-shag.z: Dark Fired Shag is a nearly black, very finely shag-cut Virginia tobacco. The leaf is darkened through a steaming process; this process files down the leaf's sharpness, leaving a deep, full flavor that is not harsh on the tongue. Because of the fine cut it catches quickly, so it should not be packed tightly when filling. Charles Fairmorn is a German firm whose origins are traced to an old Lübeck tobacco import house; it was founded in Hamburg in 1978, moved to Dingelstädt in 1996, and to Lübeck in 2006. This record is aimed at smokers seeking an unflavored, dark Virginia smoke with the quick pace of a shag cut.
charles-fairmorn-dark-fired-shag.o: A woody, smoky aroma from the fire-cured leaf is felt with a dark, sugary base underneath.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-dutch-aromatic.z: Kendal Gold is the umbrella name for the shag-cut tobacco family Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. produces in the town of Kendal in England's Lake District. The family's body is built from Brazilian- and Indian-origin, heat-cured light Virginia leaf; largely stripped of stem, it's cut into fine golden strands. The producer steams and softens the tobacco, cuts it, toasts it on a hot cylinder, and then applies the top flavoring — so the family's members are versions of the same body offered with different scents. The version known as "Dutch" carries a sweet, lightly spicy top flavoring familiar from Dutch-style aromatics; it's listed under this name within the producer's numbered Kendal Gold series. Beneath the aroma, the Virginia body carries a herbal, light-lemon sweetness. The fine shag cut lights quickly and resists going out; since it burns fast, it calls for a slow tempo. Nicotine is measured. Suited to smokers wanting a mild, flavored tobacco that can be smoked all day.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-dutch-aromatic.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly spicy, and sugary tobacco aroma.

g-l-pease-regents-flake.z: Regents Flake is a blend built by placing a generous measure of Oriental tobacco, especially Izmir leaf, over a base of red and bright Virginia leaves. A very small amount of perique is added to bring out the fruity side of the Virginias and enlarge the exotic, near-floral qualities of the Oriental leaf. The mix is pressed into cakes, fermented, then sliced for boxing. The tin and room aroma carries an incense-like line. In the smoke, Virginia's measured sweetness joins with the Oriental leaf's spicy, sweet-tart character. The coating contains no added sugar or flavouring. It suits smokers seeking a more measured intensity than the brand's other Oriental-heavy records.
g-l-pease-regents-flake.o: Leaves a spicy, lightly floral aroma reminiscent of incense.

el-rincon-de-la-pipa-no-1.z: Not enough sourcing could be found for No. 1, a blend from the maker El Rincon de la Pipa.
el-rincon-de-la-pipa-no-1.o: Could not be described due to lack of sourcing.

spezial-pipe-tobacco-company-roulette.z: Referred to as a Virginia-and-perique-forward blend from the maker Spezial Pipe Tobacco Company; sufficient independent sources introducing the blend and the maker could not be found.
spezial-pipe-tobacco-company-roulette.o: No description is available in records.

john-middleton-inc-cherry-cavendish.z: John Middleton's cherry-flavored Cavendish blend; no verifiable information on its profile could be found.
john-middleton-inc-cherry-cavendish.o: No verifiable information on its room note could be found.

edwards-honey-bucc.z: This is one of Edward's Pipe & Tobacco's in-house blends prepared in the shop; not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition and character.
edwards-honey-bucc.o: Could not be described due to insufficient records.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-dark-vanilla.z: Kendal Dark Vanilla is the fine-shag-cut, vanilla-sauced version of the brand's unflavored Dark Flake leaf. At its base is dark, fire- and air-cured leaf; vanilla adds a fine sweetness on top rather than masking that base. Because of this, it falls closer to the classic English aromatic approach where the topping is kept restrained, rather than the heavily sauced American-style aromatics. The fine cut lights quickly and needs frequent tamping. Suited to smokers wanting a lightly sweet top note without losing the dark tobacco taste.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-dark-vanilla.o: Leaves a lightly toasted, sweet vanilla aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-dark.z: Kendal Dark is an unflavored blend combining Malawi-origin fire-cured leaf with India-origin air-cured Virginia in a fine shag cut. The very fine cut makes the tobacco easy to light; on the other hand, loose packing is common to prevent it from burning too fast. The taste is earthy, smoky, and dry, carrying no sugar or essence topping. Nicotine, contrary to the mild impression given by the fine cut, is high. Suited to smokers seeking dark, essence-free English-style leaf, and to those with a tolerance for nicotine.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-dark.o: Leaves a dark tobacco aroma reminiscent of smoke and dry wood.

rattray-jocks-mixture.z: Jocks Mixture is a very dark-colored, full-bodied, slow-burning Rattray mixture. A large share of black Cavendish builds the blend's sweet ground; a measured amount of Latakia is added on top to create a smoky layer. It is a ribbon cut and packs easily. Its slow burn suits long smoking sessions; the taste stays mellow relative to its body and doesn't turn sharp. It suits people looking for a smoke that sits between an English blend and Cavendish, where Latakia is balanced by dark sweetness.
rattray-jocks-mixture.o: Leaves a sweet dark tobacco aroma with a light hint of soot.

paul-olsen-balkan.z: No reliable source could be found for the Paul Olsen pipe tobacco called Balkan, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

mclintock-amaretto.z: McLintock Amaretto is an aromatic variety that appeared in Berlin-based Planta's McLintock line; no source documenting the blend's leaf composition and cut could be found.
mclintock-amaretto.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of almond liqueur.

ashton-type-3.z: Ashton Type 3 is referred to as a Virginia-based blend in the brand's numbered series; no adequate independent source verifying its content and character could be found.
ashton-type-3.o: According to records, not enough information could be found to describe it.

the-tobacco-barn-vanilla-fudge.z: Vanilla Fudge is a house blend in The Tobacco Barn's light aromatics group. A Cavendish-forward body is joined by some fire-cured leaf; as the name suggests, the casing is built on an intense, creamy vanilla, and this consistency gives the blend its "fudge," or soft-candy, association. Nicotine is light, and the casing is distinctly prominent on the palate. Suited to smokers after aromatics centered on a sweet top note rather than the leaf's own taste; it may read as too sweet for those used to unflavored Virginia or Latakia blends. As with high-moisture aromatics, smoking it slowly and in moderation reduces the sensation of tongue bite.
the-tobacco-barn-vanilla-fudge.o: Leaves a sweet aroma in the room reminiscent of a creamy vanilla and sugary cocoa mixture.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-colts-ame.z: The Colts line was introduced in select markets in 2009, inspired by the cigar series of the same name. American Mixture is an aromatic blend carrying vanilla and walnut notes over fermented black cavendish; its base holds mild African-origin burley and sweet South American Virginia leaf. It is ribbon cut, with moisture typical for aromatics. On the flavor side, cavendish sweetness and a nutty direction from the casing come forward; nicotine stays light. Suited to newcomers to aromatic blends and to those seeking a light tobacco during the day.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-colts-ame.o: Leaves a scent of vanilla and toasted walnut.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-brindleys-.z: Brindley's Mixture Match belongs to the Match line Sutliff set up to reproduce classic blends, and it is based on the old mixture of the same name. The base is Virginia- and burley-forward, with a measured marshmallow-character casing applied over it. Records suggest the original blend's casing also included orange. On the smoke, light dried-fruit notes leaning toward fig and plum sit alongside an occasional tart sharpness and burley's earthy side; these layers give the blend a texture beyond simple sweetness. It is aimed at smokers looking for a medium-bodied profile focused more on the leaf than on flavoring.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-brindleys-.o: Leaves a light scent recalling sweet candy alongside dried-fruit and earthy notes.

g-l-pease-barbary-coast.z: Barbary Coast is a G. L. Pease blend built on cube-cut burley. It is rounded out with matured red Virginia and Louisiana perique; a small amount of brandy is applied and the blend is finished using the producer's own processing method. In the flavour profile, black walnut, bitter chocolate, and dried-fruit facets appear; burley's dry, earthy body is balanced by perique's plum-spice edge. The cube cut makes for an easy, slow, cool burn. Considered full in nicotine, this blend is for those leaning toward burley-based mixtures and a lightly topped American style.
g-l-pease-barbary-coast.o: Leaves an aroma of toasted walnut, cocoa, and lightly alcoholic dried fruit.

brigham-heritage-blend.z: Heritage Blend is the full-bodied blend in Brigham's classic English-mixture lane. Its composition includes small-leaf select Latakia, bright Macedonian Oriental, and naturally prepared brown cavendish. Latakia sets the blend's dominant taste; the Oriental leaf adds a dry, spicy edge to it, while cavendish adds a softening sweetness. Body and flavor are full, and the room note is distinctly lasting. A blend designed for experienced smokers accustomed to heavily Latakia-laden mixtures, seeking one intense smoke during the day.
brigham-heritage-blend.o: Leaves a long-lasting aroma reminiscent of heavy wood smoke and incense.

dunhill-standard-mixture-mellow.z: Standard Mixture Mellow is the lightest member of Dunhill's Standard Mixture family. It's a light-to-medium-bodied English mixture of latakia, oriental and Virginia tobaccos, ribbon cut. The word "mellow" in the name describes softness, not a lack of flavor: because the latakia share is kept low, the blend's core is built on a grassy, bright, lightly white-peppery Virginia character, with the orientals leaving a fine spice in the background. With its toasted-bread-like tone and smooth finish, it forms a middle step for those accustomed to Virginia blends wanting to move toward English mixtures. Production under the Dunhill name has ended; the Standard Mixture name has since been continued by other makers.
dunhill-standard-mixture-mellow.o: Leaves a scent combining toasted bread and light wood smoke.

pfeifen-huber-virginia-golden-flake.z: Virginia Golden Flake is one of the blends bearing the name of the Munich-based tobacconist Pfeifen Huber; the profile is left incomplete because no sufficient sources confirming its composition and character could be found.

pipesandcigars-com-yule-log.z: This is a blend offered under the American retailer pipesandcigars.com's name; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

brigadier-black-alamo.z: Alamo is a blend in the aromatic line of Brigadier Black, an American retailer brand. The line was originally designed for limited production and later turned into a permanent product; manufacturing is contracted to an American maker with long experience in aromatics. The blend consists of a combination of soft burley and black cavendish, topped with a sweet casing evoking nougat and mocha. Burley forms a nutty, dry base while cavendish carries the sugary intensity. Nicotine is low, flavor medium. A profile suited to fans of coffee- and sweet-evoking aromatics and to those new to the pipe.
brigadier-black-alamo.o: Leaves a dark, sweet aroma reminiscent of roasted coffee and sugared almond confection.

dan-tobacco-ascanian-no-1-riverside-blen.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of Dan Tobacco's Ascanian No. 1 Riverside Blend were found.

g-l-pease-cumberland-20th-anniversary.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Cumberland [20th Anniversary].

uptowns-smoke-shop-black-lung.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Uptown's Smoke Shop blend called Black Lung has been found.
uptowns-smoke-shop-black-lung.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-old-english.z: An Orlik record noted as burley-based; no independent source describing the blend's composition and character could be found.

philip-morris-revelation.z: Revelation was reportedly launched in 1923 by the Continental Tobacco Co., and after that company passed to Philip Morris in 1934 it was sold under the Philip Morris name for many years. It was later produced for a time by House of Windsor before going out of production entirely. It is one of the more frequently mentioned records in American pipe history for its association with photographs of Albert Einstein smoking a pipe. Period descriptions state the blend was built from Burley, Virginia, Carolina leaf, Latakia, and Perique, combined moreover in different cuts; this structure allowed the tobacco to pack more evenly into a pipe. In doing so, at a time when the American market was dominated by plain Burley-forward blends, it offered a more complex construction that included Latakia and Perique. Today it is known only from old tins or from blends made in tribute to it.
philip-morris-revelation.o: Leaves a lightly smoky, warm tobacco aroma recalling nuts.

g-smith-sons-old-london-sweet-cut.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of G. Smith & Sons' pipe tobacco Old London Sweet Cut could be found.

casey-jones-beyond-brave.z: Casey Jones is a pipe tobacco line named after the American locomotive engineer who died at his post in 1900 saving his train's passengers; Beyond Brave is the line's base blend and is sold in sizes ranging from a 1.5-ounce pouch to a 12-ounce box. Burley forms the body of the blend; black Cavendish adds sweetness and darkness, while a small amount of Virginia lends a light citrus tartness. The top flavoring is built around vanilla and caramel, applied at a level that does not cover the tobacco's nutty base. It burns cool, does not bite the tongue, and has a light nicotine level. Aimed at smokers seeking a soft aromatic they can smoke all day.
casey-jones-beyond-brave.o: Leaves a creamy vanilla and caramel aroma with a light nutty trace.

hearth-home-viprati.z: Viprati is a Virginia-Perique blend in which three separate Virginia leaves are combined with a notable proportion of Perique and a small amount of fire-cured leaf. Its base is made up of sweet bright and ripe red Virginia; Perique adds seasoning in the direction of spice and plum, while the fire-cured leaf adds a light smoky layer in the background. The blend bears the name of Italian pipe maker Luigi Viprati and was prepared at his request for something close to the classic VaPer style he loved. It's an unflavored mixture; it's aimed at smokers looking for a Virginia-Perique that's spicy but keeps its sweetness. It's part of the brand's Marquee line.
hearth-home-viprati.o: Leaves an aroma where light smoke and pepper traces accompany sweet dried-fruit.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-scotch-type.z: No reliable source could be found for the Orlik Tobacco Company A/S pipe tobacco called Scotch Type, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

lambert-butlers-the-garrick-smoking-mixt.z: The Garrick Smoking Mixture is an English mixture that appeared in the Lambert & Butler firm's old catalog and is no longer produced; since no independent source describing its contents could be found, the record is left incomplete.

elephant-castle-the-roanoke.z: No sufficient independent sourcing could be reached to document the composition and character of The Roanoke, a pipe tobacco from Elephant & Castle.

pcca-noel.z: For PCCA's blend called Noel, no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

ken-byron-ventures-the-patience-of-docto.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to fill in the profile of Ken Byron Ventures' The Patience of Doctor Silence.

savinelli-leonardo.z: A blend said to be in Savinelli's aromatic line; no sufficient first-hand source on its content and character could be found.
savinelli-leonardo.o: Recorded as leaving a sweetish, casing-derived scent.

gawith-hoggarth-co-moorland-mixture.z: No verifiable sourcing on the producer or retailer could be found for this mixture, credited to Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. and said to contain Virginia and Latakia.
gawith-hoggarth-co-moorland-mixture.o: Records indicate it carries the smoky aroma typical of Latakia-containing mixtures.

lane-limited-john-rolfe.z: One of Lane Limited's aromatic blends; not enough sources could be found for its contents and character.

mccranies-coventry.z: Coventry is one of the aromatic-class bulk blends from McCranie's shop; no reliable source could be found on its contents or flavoring.

uhles-big-dipper-blend.z: Big Dipper is one of the house blends from Uhle Tobacco Company, which has prepared its own blends in Milwaukee since 1939. Per the maker's description, Burley and black Cavendish are added to a golden Cavendish core, with the taste cased toward vanilla and a light hint of chocolate. It can be counted among the aromatic wing's medium-intensity examples: nicotine load is not heavy, and the sweetness is measured enough not to fully mask the tobacco's character. Suited to smokers after a sweet everyday blend, newcomers to aromatics, or those taking a break between heavy Latakia blends. Since Uhle's sells only through its own shop and website, the blend isn't seen in wide distribution networks.
uhles-big-dipper-blend.o: Leaves an aroma led by vanilla sweetness with a faint cocoa hint behind it.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-argosy-bla.z: Match Argosy Black is a black-cavendish-based blend Sutliff produces as a model of its old Argosy aromatic. The topping is built around vanilla and chocolate; tobacco flavor stays measured behind that sweetness. It's light-bodied and low in nicotine; the burn is soft and doesn't turn harsh toward the end. Aimed at smokers seeking a pronounced sweet-flavored, light everyday blend. Records indicate this Sutliff version leans somewhat sweeter than the original.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-argosy-bla.o: Leaves a scent of vanilla-cocoa and baked sweets.

peterson-holiday-season-2017.z: Since the 2000s, Peterson has released a Christmas mixture each year prepared solely for that season; the body is largely based on the trio of Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish, with only the topping changing from year to year. The 2017 edition uses amaretto with fruit notes and a touch of vanilla. Being a limited production, it was only on the market in its release year.
peterson-holiday-season-2017.o: Leaves an almond liqueur, ripe fruit, and vanilla aroma.

john-aylesbury-sir-johns-burley-flake.z: Sir John's Burley Flake is a Burley-forward pressed flake produced for John Aylesbury by Kopp Tobaccos. The leaves are carefully pressed and sliced; select Virginias that lend natural sweetness join the composition. The maker describes the blend as a natural composition free of artificial additives and rates its intensity at four out of five. It's offered in a 100-gram tin. On the taste axis, Burley's nutty and cocoa-leaning side sits alongside light spice and Virginia sugar. Nicotine is pronounced; suited to smokers used to rubbing out flake who want an unflavored Burley character.
john-aylesbury-sir-johns-burley-flake.o: Leaves a dry, earthy aroma reminiscent of nuts and cocoa.

gawith-hoggarth-co-syrian-latakia.z: This product is not a finished blend but a single blending leaf sold on its own: pure Latakia. Latakia is produced by curing Oriental leaf over smoky fires for an extended period; this process gives the leaf a nearly black color and an easily recognizable tar-like, smoky aroma. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. offers this leaf as a ribbon cut; it can be smoked on its own, but is more often mixed in measured amounts into other blends to add smokiness. The "Syrian" in the name refers to the leaf's historical origin — the original variety processed around Latakia, Syria. Records indicate Syrian Latakia production ceased decades ago, and nearly all the leaf on the market has since shifted to Cyprian origin; indeed, the pure Latakia the producer currently sells is described as Cyprian leaf. The Syrian-type leaf is considered less sharp, sweeter, and more reminiscent of smoked wood. Smoked on its own, it gives a heavy smoky taste sitting atop a woody, floral, lightly spicy core; it is unflavored and a component that needs to be dosed according to the blend.
gawith-hoggarth-co-syrian-latakia.o: Fills the room with an aroma of pine smoke, tar, and burnt resin.

mcclelland-calumet.z: Calumet is an unflavored Virginia blend McClelland prepared for the United Pipe Clubs of America (UPCA). It's ribbon cut, carrying a calm, mild, lightly sweet Virginia character. Aimed at those wanting a plain, low-nicotine Virginia smokable all day.
mcclelland-calumet.o: Leaves a lightly sweet trace leaning toward dry hay and toasted bread.

cascadia-pipe-co-open-water.z: Open Water is the aromatic member of Cascadia Pipe Co.'s five-blend, nature-themed series. A base built from select Virginia and Burley leaf is covered with a top flavoring made from a blend of fruit essences. Like the other Cascadia blends, it is offered in pressed-cake form. The flavoring is measured compared to classic aromatics; Virginia's natural sweetness and Burley's soft, nutty base are not smothered. Nicotine is low to medium, and the cake structure lets it burn cool and slow. It needs to be sliced and rubbed out before filling. Aimed at smokers who avoid heavily cased tobaccos and want a measured fruit aromatic.
cascadia-pipe-co-open-water.o: Leaves a sweet fruit essence and warm tobacco aroma.

robert-mcconnell-rich-dark-virginia.z: Rich Dark Virginia is an unflavored, ribbon-cut blend made solely from dark Virginia leaf. The maker states no casing is applied, the aim being to let the leaf's own taste stand out. Dark Virginia is less sharp than pale Virginia but gives a deeper, more bread-like flavor in return. Because of the ribbon cut and low moisture it can burn fast and heat up the pipe, leading to tongue bite; it calls for slow smoking and a loose pack. It suits smokers who want an unflavored Virginia and wish to follow the flavor line of a single leaf type.
robert-mcconnell-rich-dark-virginia.o: Leaves a bread-like, faintly caramelized tobacco aroma.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-back-bay.z: Back Bay is a Virginia-Perique record in Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blender's special series. Perique is worked into a bright Virginia ribbon-cut base at forty percent — a proportion notably above the usual five-to-fifteen-percent Perique share for the type, pulling the blend's character toward the spice side. The Virginia side offers tart citrus, grass, bread, a floral edge, and measured sugar; Perique adds a piercing spice with fruit notes reminiscent of dried plum, fig, and raisin. Body is medium and rises somewhat in the first third. It burns cool and steady, requiring few relights. It suits smokers seeking unflavored Virginia-Perique who aren't shy of the spice coming forward.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-back-bay.o: Leaves a spicy scent reminiscent of dried plum and tart grass.

fincks-cigar-company-money-bag.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for Finck's Cigar Company's Money Bag pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

cornell-diehl-yale-mixture.z: Yale Mixture is a ribbon-cut English blend built purely from Virginia and Latakia. Records indicate it was released in August 1996, designed as a reinterpretation of the now-discontinued Carreras Craven's Mixture. With Latakia kept low, the smoky leaf spreads through the base without coming forward or masking Virginia's sweetness. Its two-component structure keeps the blend plain and legible: Virginia's sugary, lightly tart taste and Latakia's peppery, smoky tone are sensed in turn. It's described as a recipe written for smokers approaching English blends for the first time, or those who don't want Latakia to dominate.
cornell-diehl-yale-mixture.o: Leaves a smoky scent reminiscent of wood-fire smoke, with a lightly sweet tobacco trace behind it.

peter-stokkebye-blue-grass.z: No sufficient sources confirming the composition and character of the Peter Stokkebye blend Blue Grass could be found.

cornell-diehl-or-olam-light-of-the-unive.z: Or Olam (Light of the Universe) is Cornell & Diehl's take on the classic Virginia-Perique mold. Red and golden Virginia leaf are combined with Perique, topped with Oriental varieties; a small amount of red Virginia Cavendish is used at the finish, aiming for a soft, sweet close. It's ribbon cut. On the maker's scale, strength is light, flavor and room note medium. Virginia's breadlike sweetness, Perique's plum-and-pepper spice, and the Oriental's dry, lightly tart contribution move together. Suited to those who like an unflavored Virginia-Perique construction but want a blend that isn't too strong. It belongs to the brand's Hebrew-named Or Olam series.
cornell-diehl-or-olam-light-of-the-unive.o: Leaves a subtly spicy scent from Oriental leaf over dry hay and honey tones.

mcclelland-royal-cajun-special.z: Royal Cajun Special is the lightest member of McClelland's series built on the Cajun Black component. The mixture combines two separate stoved Virginias with a tangy-sweet, lemon-yellow Virginia leaf and the smoky, sharp-character Cajun Black. Cajun Black is a component made by smoking Virginia-seed leaf and then fermenting it in a barrel in the Perique manner. In the smoke, Virginia's bright, citrusy tang dominates; Cajun Black adds a woody, smoky layer on top. Body is at the lightest end of the series and suits daytime smoking. Suited to smokers wanting to start the series from the beginning, or to try the fermented leaf in a measured dose. McClelland stopped production in 2018.
mcclelland-royal-cajun-special.o: Leaves a trace where lemony tang meets a smoky wood aroma.

w-o-larsen-selected-blend-no-32.z: No reliable source could be found regarding this blend from W.O. Larsen's numbered selection series, so its details could not be recorded.

stanwell-extra-fine.z: Sufficient sources describing the composition and character of this blend, sold under the Stanwell name, could not be found.

mac-baren-amphora-mellow-blend.z: Amphora Mellow Blend is one of the lightly flavored members of the Amphora family. Per the manufacturer's recipe, the blend's body is built from burley and Virginia leaves; selected oriental tobaccos provide balance. Turkish sources note that Kentucky leaf is also part of the mix. It's a ready rubbed/ribbon cut, meaning it's prepared fine enough to pack directly. The brand originates in the Netherlands and is produced today by Danish Mac Baren. The mint casing applied on top is not enough to create a pronounced menthol effect; it stays as a background coolness that doesn't mask the tobacco's own taste. In the smoke, the oriental leaf's dry, spicy line and the earthy, nutty tones of Kentucky and burley come forward. It sits in the medium band for nicotine. Suited to those seeking a lightly flavored blend that preserves tobacco character and can be smoked at any hour of the day.
mac-baren-amphora-mellow-blend.o: Leaves a lightly cool, minty, tobacco-toned and dry room note.

chacom-4.z: Chacom #4 is the unflavored flake blend in the line. Various Virginia leaves are pressed with pressure alone, without heat, and then rested further in cake form; this method keeps the leaf's color light, in chestnut tones. A small proportion of Perique is added to the blend. Sweet bread and oven notes lead the flavor, alongside a grassy tone and a measured citrus tartness; Perique adds dark fruit and white pepper. The smoke is dense and creamy. Though the flavor intensity is medium-to-high, nicotine is moderate, making it suitable for those seeking a flake they can smoke throughout the day.
chacom-4.o: Leaves a baked dough and dried fruit room note.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-gotham-court.z: No sufficient source could be found documenting the composition and character of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Gotham Court.

sutliff-tobacco-company-irish-creme-xk-7.z: Coded XK-7, Irish Creme is one of the long-running members of Sutliff's bulk aromatic line. A creamy, lightly sweet sauce reminiscent of Irish cream liqueur is applied over a burley-and-Virginia base; the ribbon cut is the customary form for bulk-sold American aromatics. The blend is light-bodied and low in nicotine; it's prepared with a measured moisture-and-sauce balance to reduce tongue bite. On the flavor side, leaf character recedes, with creamy sweetness taking the lead. Suited to those new to the pipe and to anyone wanting a light aromatic to smoke throughout the day. With Sutliff's production halted in 2025, the blend now depends on remaining stock in the market.
sutliff-tobacco-company-irish-creme-xk-7.o: Leaves a sweet, milky scent reminiscent of cream liqueur and vanilla.

smoker-friendly-classic-black.z: A mixture in the Smoker Friendly chain's private-label pipe tobaccos that, from its name, appears to be black-cavendish-forward; no independent source confirming its composition could be found.

pcca-full-balkan-reserve.z: A blend produced in limited numbers by McClelland for the Pipe Collector Club of America (PCCA); records place it within the club series' Balkan line, but no reliable source documenting its composition and character could be found.

esoterica-tobacciana-cardiff.z: Cardiff is a ribbon-cut blend in the virginia family of the Esoterica line, produced by J. F. Germain & Son in Jersey. According to available listings, its virginia-forward structure is accompanied by light flavoring; it is positioned as a plainer take from the same family as the line's other virginia blends. On the smoke, flue-cured leaf's hay and bread-crust tones come through with measured sweetness; there is no smoky or spicy element. It suits those seeking a straightforward virginia that can be smoked at length through the day.
esoterica-tobacciana-cardiff.o: Leaves a lightly sweet scent evoking dry hay and honey.

sutliff-tobacco-company-fox-hound.z: Fox & Hound is a traditional English mixture in Sutliff's Tobacco Galleria line. Red Virginia, Turkish/oriental leaf, burley, latakia, and perique are used together; the cut is coarse ribbon and comes out of the pouch fairly moist. Body is medium; latakia's smokiness is balanced by perique's plummy, spicy touch and burley's nutty texture. It's a record for those wanting an unfussy, non-heavy latakia blend suited to all-day smoking. Available in 1.5-ounce pouches and in bulk.
sutliff-tobacco-company-fox-hound.o: Fills the room with wood smoke and dry earth.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-vice-cat.z: This is a blend carried under the Wilke Pipe Tobacco name; as it does not appear in the maker's current catalog, no reliable information could be found regarding its composition and character.

diamond-crown-black-honey.z: The Diamond Crown name is best known for J.C. Newman's cigar line; no independent source could be found describing the composition and character of this pipe blend sold under the same name.

up-down-dealers-choice.z: One of the counter blends from the Up Down Tobacco shop in Chicago; since no source documenting its composition and flavor structure has been found, the record is left incomplete.

georgetown-tobacco-persuasion.z: Persuasion is counted among Georgetown Tobacco's English-style house blends. Its composition includes a generous proportion of Latakia; this weight is balanced by Oriental leaf and Virginia. The blend has been revised over time and is now offered with a finer cut; the fine ribbon cut makes packing the bowl easier and keeps the burn even. On the taste side, Latakia's smoky, resinous core is the deciding factor; Oriental leaf adds a spicy, lightly tart edge, and Virginia adds a bready sweetness underneath. It's an unflavored blend. Despite the high Latakia ratio, the smoke stays mild and cool. Aimed at smokers seeking classic Latakia-forward English mixtures who work with unflavored leaf taste.
georgetown-tobacco-persuasion.o: A smoky wood-and-incense aroma comes together with a lightly sweet tobacco scent underneath.

pfeifen-huber-labyrinth.z: Labyrinth Mixture is one of Pfeifen Huber's medium-strength flavored house blends. The mixture contains broadly cut Virginia, black Cavendish, a small amount of Burley, and hand-rubbed flake pieces together; this structure gives a layered smoke where different cuts meet in the same bowl. The flavoring is built on a trio of vanilla, orange, and apple. Its body is light and its nicotine low; the flavoring is noticeable but kept to a level that doesn't cover the tobacco's own taste. Fruity freshness comes forward first, vanilla sweetness at the end. It suits smokers wanting a soft, sweet aromatic who find heavily flavored blends too much.
pfeifen-huber-labyrinth.o: Leaves apple and orange-peel freshness followed by vanilla sweetness.

milan-tobacconists-colonial-pastime.z: Colonial Pastime is one of Milan Tobacconists' blends positioned between an English mixture and an aromatic. According to the shop's description, Burley, Virginia, black Cavendish, and a small amount of latakia are all present; the flavoring carries associations of wild berry, vanilla, whiskey, and hickory wood, with a sweet spice at the finish. In terms of smoking character it leans toward English mixtures, while the room note resembles that of aromatic blends. Its body is light to medium. An in-between construction designed for smokers who like latakia's smokiness but don't want to give up aromatic flavorings either.
milan-tobacconists-colonial-pastime.o: Leaves a lightly smoky wood aroma alongside sweet fruit and vanilla.

dan-tobacco-hamborger-veermaster.z: Hamborger Veermaster is an unflavored flake pressed purely from golden Virginia leaf. Its name comes from a mid-nineteenth-century German sea shanty about a four-masted sailing ship setting out from the port of Hamburg. The maker positions it as a traditional English-style Virginia flake. The flavor is naturally sweet but not syrupy; dry hay, bread, and light citrus tones come forward. It burns slowly and evenly, giving a cool smoke. Strength and flavor sit at a medium level. A fitting starting point for smokers accustomed to unflavored flakes, or those wanting to move into the flake format.
dan-tobacco-hamborger-veermaster.o: Leaves a plain, sweetish tobacco trace reminiscent of dry hay and honey.

upshall-upshall-english-classic.z: Recorded as an English-style Virginia-Latakia mixture bearing the name of the James Upshall pipe brand; no independent source documenting its proportions and cut has been found.

davids-blend-gourmet-blend.z: This is one of the cavendish-based shop blends from David's Fine Tobaccos; no verifiable source describing its composition could be found.

pufferspipes-com-mid-atlantic-waterman-b.z: No reliable source could be found documenting the content and character of Mid Atlantic Waterman Blend from the seller PuffersPipes.com.
pufferspipes-com-mid-atlantic-waterman-b.o: No information describing the room note could be found in available records.

davidoff-limited-edition-2017.z: This is a limited-edition pipe tobacco Davidoff released in 2017; no verifiable source describing the blend's composition could be found.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.z: Cândido Giovanella is a brand produced in the Curitiba region of Paraná and considered one of the oldest pipe tobacco names in the Brazilian domestic market; the maker is Imigrantes Ind. e Com. de Fumos Ltda. Alemão Cacau is the cocoa-flavored version of the brand's "Alemão" line. Its base is sun-dried, lightly toasted golden Brazilian Virginia leaf and black Cavendish; a measured cocoa flavoring is applied on top. The cocoa leaves a dry, chocolatey background rather than a heavy syrupy sweetness. Being light in nicotine and mild on the palate, it suits smokers in their early pipe years and those looking for an everyday smoke. It's usually sold in bulk or in airtight aluminum packaging.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.o: Leaves an aroma of warm cocoa and baked dough.

mcclelland-captain-cool.z: Captain Cool is a light flavored blend in McClelland's Premium Aromatics line. The maker's description calls it a cool-smoking tobacco that doesn't bite the tongue; it carries a pinch of vanilla with a mint touch as flavoring. The cut is ribbon and moisture is kept measured relative to typical aromatics. In the smoke, the flavoring's cooling line stands out more than the tobacco's own taste; nicotine dose is low and body is light. The mint-vanilla combination sets the blend apart from McClelland's other aromatics. Suited to smokers seeking an aromatic profile who want a mild, non-harsh, everyday tobacco. Discontinued when McClelland stopped production in 2018.
mcclelland-captain-cool.o: Leaves a lightly vanilla, cooling mint aroma.

alfie-turmeaus-second-wave.z: One of Turmeaus tobacconist's house mixtures noted as Virginia-based; no accessible source documenting its content could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-zen-pants.z: A small-batch edition referred to among Ken Byron Ventures' English-type blends; not enough sources could be found to document its composition and character.
ken-byron-ventures-zen-pants.o: Could not be described due to lack of accessible records.

ken-byron-ventures-fore-glory-2022.z: Ken Byron Ventures' 2022 limited release; no independent source could be found to document its contents.
ken-byron-ventures-fore-glory-2022.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

punakawan-culture-edition.z: Punakawan is one of Indonesia's small-scale pipe tobacco blenders; there is not enough source material describing the content and character of this product called Culture Edition.
punakawan-culture-edition.o: No information describing the room note could be found in available records.

campbells-smoke-shop-14-kentucky-rough-c.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named #14 Kentucky Rough Cut under the Campbell's Smoke Shop brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

planta-mild-english.z: Planta Mild English is a pipe tobacco blend for which there is not enough independent source material.
planta-mild-english.o: Not enough records could be found on the room note.

tabac-manil-reserve-du-patron.z: One of Tabac Manil's burley-based blends; no accessible source could be found to fill out the profile.

cornell-diehl-strawberries-cream.z: No listing for this strawberry-and-cream-themed aromatic blend, Strawberries & Cream, from Cornell & Diehl could be found in the maker's current catalogue or major retailer listings; its composition could not be confirmed.

cornell-diehl-snug-harbor.z: Snug Harbor is a mixture built on a Burley-based body with Turkish leaf, Latakia, and Perique added, topped with only a light casing meant to sharpen the natural sweetness and room note. It's ribbon cut and is generally referred to under the heading of a light aromatic English mixture. On the smoke, Burley and Oriental leaf come forward together, building a nutty, lightly tangy line. Latakia's smoke is measured, and Perique adds spice. The casing is noticeable at the start of the bowl, then recedes, leaving the leaves' own taste in front. It sits at a middle point for those not wanting to go fully into smoky flavor but who find unflavored blends too flat.
cornell-diehl-snug-harbor.o: Leaves a smoky scent alongside leather and cedar, with a light sweet trace behind it.

rattray-buckingham.z: Buckingham belongs among Rattray's flavored blends. It is a ribbon-cut mixture bringing together black Cavendish, light and dark Virginia leaf, and Burley; walnut and Bourbon-vanilla flavoring is applied to the blend. The flavoring is pronounced, but the tobacco body beneath it isn't erased: Virginia's sweetness and Burley's earthy fullness are felt throughout the smoke. Strength is medium. It suits fans of flavored tobacco as well as smokers who want real tobacco taste under the sugary flavoring. The Rattray name draws on the Scottish pipe-tobacco tradition; the brand's tobaccos are produced today in Germany.
rattray-buckingham.o: Leaves a light whisky-like trace along with sweet vanilla and roasted walnut aroma.

richs-balkan-superior.z: Balkan Superior is a Balkan-style mixture among Rich's Cigar Store's Portland house blends where Latakia and Oriental leaf take the lead. Reports indicate it aims for a profile close to the old Balkan Sobranie tradition; the Oriental proportion is kept high, with Virginia remaining a secondary component supplying sweetness and balance. It is full-bodied and unflavored, with soot and spice dominant. It suits smokers used to classic Latakia-heavy mixtures. Its current status is unclear since it does not appear on the shop's current house blend list; a portion of Rich's blends were prepared for many years by shop blender Steve Books, with some recipes passed to the store after his retirement.
richs-balkan-superior.o: Leaves an intense wood-soot and spicy Oriental-tobacco aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-black-swan.z: Black Swan, part of the Sutliff Private Stock line, is a light, black-cavendish-forward aromatic. Its topping is a plain vanilla, accompanied in the background by a very light dried-plum note. Rather than an artificial sharpness, it aims for a sweetness reminiscent of freshly baked pastry. Strength is low and flavor intensity is measured; black cavendish's high moisture slows the burn and keeps the smoke cool. Suited to smokers new to aromatics or seeking a soft blend for all-day smoking. It went out of production when the Private Stock line was scaled back.
sutliff-tobacco-company-black-swan.o: A light dried-plum scent mixes into sweet vanilla pastry.

wilsons-of-sharrow-contemplation.z: Contemplation is one of the aromatic blends from Wilsons of Sharrow, produced at Sharrow Mills in Sheffield. It's a coarse-cut mixture ready for hand-rubbing, based on Virginia leaf and black cavendish. A casing carrying honey and tropical-fruit notes is applied on top. Virginia's own dark citrus sweetness combines with this casing, while the black cavendish adds a mocha-like, creamy softness that balances the blend. Nicotine stays mild while flavor intensity runs high — meaning it leaves a full aroma in the mouth without building strength. Its slow burn and heady scent suit long, unhurried sessions. It's well suited to newcomers to aromatic tobaccos and to smokers seeking English-made fruity mixtures. Wilsons of Sharrow is one of England's oldest tobacco businesses, producing snuff and pipe tobacco since 1737.
wilsons-of-sharrow-contemplation.o: Leaves a scent of honey, ripe tropical fruit, and a hint of coffee.

cup-o-joes-5-bigfoot-flake.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the Cup O' Joes brand as #5 Bigfoot Flake; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

pipesandcigars-com-ro62.z: RO62 is one of the blends the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com sells under its own name; there is not enough independent source material documenting its content and character.

ken-byron-ventures-right-meow.z: One of the limited-run blends Ken Byron Ventures released; not enough sources could be found regarding its contents.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2014.z: Christmas Cheer is the straight Virginia series that Kansas City-based McClelland released once a year, in limited numbers, from the 1980s until the company's closure in early 2018. The series' idea is to present a single Virginia batch selected from that year's harvest on its own; each year is thus considered a separate record, and the year on the tin defines the blend's identity. The 2014 release was prepared the same way, with selected matured Virginia leaf pressed into cake and tinned as broken flake. Records indicate it was prepared from a batch selected from the 2014 harvest. Unflavored Virginia character dominates the smoke: natural leaf sweetness over a bready, herbal base, with a faint tang and a lemony sharpness in the background. Nicotine dose is measured, while flavor intensity is pronounced; it burns cool when smoked slowly, but tends to bite the tongue when rushed. Since the flake's moisture can run high straight from the tin, airing it before packing is common practice. A record aimed at smokers seeking unflavored Virginia who are considering cellaring the tin; not suitable for those expecting an aromatic.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2014.o: A tangy, sharp trace characteristic of McClelland tins mixes into an aroma of dry hay and toasted bread.

rattray-high-society.z: This is a flavored blend sold under the Rattray name; it is not part of the brand's current product list, and no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.
rattray-high-society.o: There is not enough source material to describe its aroma.

the-tobacco-haus-especial-de-carlos.z: No independent source documenting the composition of this aromatic blend from The Tobacco Haus shop in New Braunfels, Texas has been found.
the-tobacco-haus-especial-de-carlos.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

cornell-diehl-berry-good.z: Cornell & Diehl's Berry Good is an aromatic built on the brand's traditional burley-heavy cavendish base. Some Virginia and Green River Vanilla leaf are added to the base, followed by a raspberry-based flavoring. The cut is ribbon, and the tobacco arrives on the moist side. On the smoke, the fruity flavoring is pronounced; the burley base balances the sweetness with a dry mouthfeel and a light nutty trace. It sits between light and medium in nicotine. It suits smokers who love fruity aromatics and want some leaf character alongside the sweet flavoring.
cornell-diehl-berry-good.o: Leaves an aroma of raspberry jam and vanilla in the room.

wessex-subtle-aroma.z: No sufficient source could be found confirming the composition and character of the Wessex Subtle Aroma blend.
wessex-subtle-aroma.o: According to the records, no scent description has been documented.

dunhill-a-11000.z: A discontinued mixture referred to by its code number under the Dunhill name, for which no verifiable source on its composition could be found.

cornell-diehl-scots-pub.z: A blend, no longer in Cornell & Diehl's current catalogue, referred to as Cavendish-based; no adequate source documenting its composition was found.
cornell-diehl-scots-pub.o: No adequate information for a description could be found in records.

villiger-latakia.z: This is a Villiger pipe tobacco named for its Latakia emphasis; no independent source could be found documenting the blend's proportions and cut.

pipes-pleasures-pipe-dream.z: No sufficient sources were found documenting the content and character of Pipes & Pleasures' blend Pipe Dream.

blatter-blatter-concerto.z: One of the counter blends from the Blatter & Blatter shop in Montreal; no reliable source documenting its composition could be found.

peter-stokkebye-virginia-no-701.z: This is a Virginia blend numbered 701 in Peter Stokkebye's numbered bulk series; no sufficient first-hand sources detailing its character could be found.
peter-stokkebye-virginia-no-701.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

honore-honore.z: No verifiable source at the maker or retailer level could be found for this blend, described as Virginia-and-Perique-forward.

mcclelland-no-2025-english-cavendish.z: No. 2025 English Cavendish, part of the 2000 series in McClelland's bulk catalog, is unflavored despite the word "cavendish" in its name — here, cavendish describes leaf processed with heat and pressure rather than a flavoring. Per the maker's description, lemon-colored Brazilian leaf and orange-toned Middle Belt Virginia are prepared as small flake pieces, topped with Xanthi Oriental. The small flake structure lets the tobacco be rubbed out easily by hand and burn evenly. Its character sits between light and medium, with Virginia's sweetness upfront, supported by the Oriental's tangy-spicy edge. Since it contains no Latakia, it lacks the smoky weight of heavy English blends. Suited to smokers seeking an unflavored Virginia-and-Oriental taste, wanting a non-fatiguing blend smokable all day. McClelland Tobacco Company stopped production in 2018, so the blend is no longer on the market.
mcclelland-no-2025-english-cavendish.o: Leaves a tangy-sweet, dry-hay and lightly spiced tobacco aroma.

karl-erik-private-blend-no-15.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Karl Erik's Private Blend No.15.

motzek-hallo-twist.z: Hallo Twist is one of the Motzek workshop's entries continuing the twist/rope tradition. Virginia and perique leaves build the flavor backbone, while black cavendish supplies a supporting sweetness in the background. The tobacco is sold wound into rope form; before smoking, it is cut into thin coins with a sharp knife and rubbed by hand before being loaded into the pipe. On the taste side, dried-fruit associations (plum, raisin) and a peppery point from the perique are reported; the light vinegary scent natural to twist tobaccos comes from the way the tobacco is preserved and largely dissipates during drying. The maker rates its strength as three out of five, placing it at medium body, making it an accessible starting point for those new to twist tobaccos. Since twist tobaccos burn slowly, a small-chambered pipe is noted to ease the packing and lighting process.
motzek-hallo-twist.o: Leaves a dark tobacco aroma with a tangy fruit scent reminiscent of dried plum and raisin.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-aniseed-brown-.z: Kendal Aniseed Brown Pigtail is a fine hand-twisted rope tobacco. Indian-origin air-cured dark Virginia leaf and other strong Virginias are rolled together and flavored with anise. The name "Pigtail" comes from the rope's fineness; before use, coin-thin slices are cut and rubbed out. On the smoke, anise's sweet spice is pronounced, with the fire-cured leaf's smoky, earthy body underneath. Nicotine is high and the smoke thick; suited to those accustomed to rope tobaccos who don't shy away from a hearty smoke. Kendal ropes have traditionally been used both in the pipe and as chewing tobacco.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-aniseed-brown-.o: A sweet spice aroma reminiscent of anise and raki is accompanied by smoky leaf.

d-r-tobacco-vengeur-platinum-blend.z: Vengeur Platinum Blend is the version of Daughters & Ryan's Vengeur line with a higher proportion of light-colored (gold leaf) Virginia. Per the maker's own marketing, the blend uses no chemical flavoring; its character comes entirely from leaf selection. Its composition is flue-cured golden Virginia, Burley, and Oriental leaf, ribbon cut. On the smoke, a grassy, sharp, lemony Virginia base sits underneath nutty, earthy Burley with a light cocoa lean, and Oriental adds spice and a light smokiness in the background. Body is medium, flavor intensity high. Suited to those who like unflavored American mixtures and want blends where Virginia sweetness is balanced by Burley's earthiness. It reads sweeter than the Regular version in the same line.
d-r-tobacco-vengeur-platinum-blend.o: Leaves a woody scent of roasted leaf and tart grass.

abenaki-tobacco-co-black-cherry.z: Black Cherry is a cherry blend Abenaki Tobacco sells under its "signature aromatics" heading. Per the maker's catalog, light Cavendish and Virginia are added to a toasted black Cavendish base; a measured cherry essence is applied for sweetness. Unlike the sharp, syrupy structure common in cherry-flavored blends, the promotional text notes the flavoring is kept light. The black-Cavendish-heavy base gives the blend a dark, sugary body; the Virginia leaves a light tang in the background. It's not a heavy tobacco on nicotine, making it suitable for those looking for an aromatic they can smoke all day. Abenaki Tobacco was a small outfit founded in Conway, New Hampshire; since its own sales site is no longer live, the blend's current status is uncertain.
abenaki-tobacco-co-black-cherry.o: Leaves a combined room note of sweet cherry and toasted Cavendish.

wessex-dark-cavendish.z: Wessex Dark Cavendish is a blend built on dark-roasted cavendish leaf. According to retailer descriptions, Perique is added to the mixture and it's flavored with vanilla; Perique builds a spicy contrast alongside the cavendish sweetness. It's offered in broken flake cut, and nicotine load is kept low.
wessex-dark-cavendish.o: A dark, lightly spicy undertone accompanies a sweet vanilla scent.

planta-danish-black-vanilla-flake.z: Danish Black Vanilla Flake is the pressed-flake form of Planta's vanilla-cased black Cavendish blend; beyond the cut, no verifiable source could be found for further composition details.

castello-collection.z: Collection is the unflavored Virginia blend in the tobacco line released under its own name by Italian pipe maker Castello; according to records it was introduced in 2013, with the blending done by the American manufacturer Cornell & Diehl. It contains only rested red and light yellow Virginia leaf. The lemony tartness of light Virginias and the bready depth of red Virginias are given together; since no casing is used, the flavor comes entirely from the leaf itself. High natural sugar content calls for a slow smoke. Suitable for smokers accustomed to unflavored Virginia who enjoy following the development of single-leaf blends.
castello-collection.o: Leaves a dry hay and baked bread room note.

sutliff-tobacco-company-panna-cotta.z: Named after the Italian dessert, Panna Cotta is a creamy aromatic in Sutliff's Private Stock line. A small amount of burley is added to a Virginia and black cavendish base; Madagascar vanilla bean extract is used for flavoring. The cut is ribbon, and the leaf's moisture is moderate for an aromatic. The scent that fills the room recalls vanilla, caramel, and buttery sugar candy, while the taste on the palate leaves a softer, plainer vanilla sweetness. Nicotine stays light. It falls within the interest of those looking for a sweet, creamy aromatic for everyday smoking.
sutliff-tobacco-company-panna-cotta.o: Leaves a scent of vanilla cream, caramel, and buttery sugar.

cigar-connoisseur-elizabethan-mixture.z: Elizabethan Mixture is a classic English-style house blend the Cigar Connoisseur tobacco shop in England sells in bulk. Its base is Virginia, topped with Latakia and Turkish (Oriental) leaf. The cut is coarse. Though its moisture level out of the pack is suitable for smoking, available records recommend resting it in a jar for a while to let the flavors settle. On the smoke, aged Virginia's sweetness and Latakia's smoky depth keep their balance from start to finish; neither component overwhelms the other. The ash is light gray and clean, burning without going out. Strength rises slightly toward the end of the bowl, while the overall character stays on a sweet-and-hearty line. It is a structure suited to smokers looking for a classic Latakia English mixture, wanting an unflavored, medium-bodied everyday blend.
cigar-connoisseur-elizabethan-mixture.o: Leaves a heavy aroma of smoky Latakia together with dry tobacco leaf in the room.

john-aylesbury-sir-johns-broken-virginia.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to document the contents and character of John Aylesbury's Sir John's Broken Virginia.

lane-limited-strawberry.z: Lane Limited's strawberry-flavored aromatic blend; not enough sources could be found to document its leaf composition.

synjeco-elephant-dung.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Synjeco's Elephant Dung pipe tobacco could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-kasimir.z: Kasimir is one of Sutliff Tobacco Company's latakia-based mixtures; independent sources do not provide sufficient information on its composition and production status.

hu-tobacco-tigray.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the Tigray blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.
