mcclelland-no-2010-classic-virginia.z: No. 2010 Classic Virginia is an unflavored blend bringing together lemon, orange, and orange-red toned Virginia leaves from the Eastern and Middle Belt regions. Its ribbon-cut structure packs easily; the smoke shows sweetness, citrus tang, and an herbal base. A bulk product that can serve as a starting point for those wanting to get to know McClelland's Virginia handling and for those who love straight blends built from a single leaf type. Aging in a tin or jar concentrates its sugars. Discontinued when the brand closed in 2018.
mcclelland-no-2010-classic-virginia.o: Leaves a tangy dried-fruit and hay aroma.

pipesandcigars-com-green-river-black-cav.z: No independent sources sufficient to complete a full profile of pipesandcigars.com's blend Green River Black Cavendish could be found.

thepiperoom-com-pat-o-malleys-donnybrook.z: An aromatic blend in ThePipeRoom.com's Pat O' Malley's series, taking its name from Ireland's Donnybrook Fair; no independent source confirming its composition has been found.
thepiperoom-com-pat-o-malleys-donnybrook.o: Records describe it as leaving a sweet, lightly boozy aroma.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-bootleggers-deli.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Bootleggers Delight blend.

milan-tobacconists-triple-crown.z: Triple Crown is an English-style mixture built from soft latakia, Turkish tobaccos, and black cavendish. The cavendish's presence softens the blend's edges and keeps the smoky character measured. With its cool burn and non-biting structure, it's an entry blend designed for those wanting to move into English mixtures; it also suits those looking for an everyday option with a low latakia load.
milan-tobacconists-triple-crown.o: A lightly sweet tone sits beneath a soft, smoky wood aroma.

sillems-blue.z: Blue is one of the color-named aromatic blends in the Sillem's series. Tobaccos under the Sillem's brand are produced and distributed at the German Kohlhase & Kopp facilities. The blend's body is built from cross-cut golden-yellow, red, and dark Virginia leaves; brown cavendish and nutty burley add depth and measured sweetness. The flavoring is built on fresh lime along with maple syrup and caramel; the citrus sharpness cuts the syrupy sweetness. Nicotine is light, the smoke stays cool and mild, and the room note is noticeable. Suited to those who enjoy citrus-syrupy aromatics and want a light tin tobacco they can smoke all day.
sillems-blue.o: Leaves a fresh-lime scent mixed with caramel and maple syrup.

mcclelland-mellow-apple.z: One of McClelland's apple-flavored blends; no sufficient source describing its contents and character could be found.

john-aylesbury-commander-flake.z: No reliable source could be found to document the contents and character of John Aylesbury's Commander Flake blend.

samuel-gawith-st-james-plug.z: St. James Plug is a tobacco Samuel Gawith prepares in Kendal by pressing Virginia leaves together with Perique and leaving them in plug form without slicing. The name comes from the St. James Parish region of Louisiana where Perique is grown; this leaf is fermented under its own pressure in a barrel, adding a plum-like, peppery sharpness to the blend. Virginia's bready, fruity sweetness and Perique's spice meet in the middle in this record; nicotine is a bit above medium. A blend for smokers who seek slow burning and concentrated flavor in pressed tobaccos and want to get to know the Virginia-Perique family. The plug format keeps moisture inside, so the tobacco needs to be sliced with a knife or crumbled; this structure also suits aging over time.
samuel-gawith-st-james-plug.o: Leaves a light spicy trace beside a dried-plum and grain scent.

connoisseur-scottish-classic-mixture.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Connoisseur blend Scottish Classic Mixture.

peter-stokkebye-amsterdam-shag-no-93.z: Amsterdam Shag No. 93 is a very finely cut shag blend from the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye. In the composition, Virginia leaf lays down a base recalling grass, wood, and light bitter orange; fire-cured Kentucky and Burley leaf add a nutty, earthy, spicy depth. Though the brand originates in Denmark, this series has long been produced in the United States. Because the very fine cut catches fire quickly and burns fast, moistening the tobacco before packing and packing it loosely helps balance the burn rate. Body and nicotine are medium. It suits smokers experienced with fine cuts who are seeking a near-unflavored everyday blend; the same tobacco is also used for rolling cigarettes.
peter-stokkebye-amsterdam-shag-no-93.o: Leaves a dry hay, nutty, and light wood-smoke aroma.

timm-no-name-weiss.z: The white blend, the best-selling variety in the Timm No Name series, is a mellow aromatic. Virginia, Burley and black Cavendish leaves are cased with Mexican honey and bourbon vanilla flavoring; scent and taste stay close to each other. The smoke is mellow and nicotine is moderate. Aimed at those who smoke classic honey-vanilla aromatics daily and want a large package.
timm-no-name-weiss.o: Leaves a sweet, creamy aroma reminiscent of honey and bourbon vanilla.

watch-city-cigar-ernie-morning-pipe.z: This is described as a light aromatic house mixture from Watch City Cigar, associated with the shop's blender Ernie and intended for morning smoking; no published maker record could be found.
watch-city-cigar-ernie-morning-pipe.o: Could not be determined from the records.

wesleys-mocca.z: This blend, registered under South African tobacconist Wesley's, does not appear in the current house-blend listing or the online shop; no source could be found documenting its composition.
wesleys-mocca.o: No description could be found as no source was available.

erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-2012-anniv.z: 4th Generation 2012 Anniversary Blend is, according to available listings, a flake-cut, Virginia-forward blend; not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition in detail.
erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-2012-anniv.o: Could not be described due to insufficient sourcing.

sutliff-tobacco-company-trafalgar-527.z: 527 Trafalgar is a mildly aromatic English blend in Sutliff's bulk line. Its content includes burley, cavendish, and Virginia leaf along with a small amount of latakia; an aged-Jamaican-rum casing is applied over it. The cut is ribbon. Because the latakia proportion is kept low, the smoky character stays in the background, and the blend runs softer than classic heavy English mixtures. The rum casing gives a measured sweetness that doesn't mask the tobacco's natural taste. Strength and taste intensity are medium. It suits smokers wanting to transition into smoky blends or looking for a lightly flavored English mixture.
sutliff-tobacco-company-trafalgar-527.o: Leaves a scent carrying rum sweetness over a lightly smoky base.

schurch-amoun-english-v.z: A blend in the Schürch house's classic English mixture line; no sufficient source documenting its leaf proportions and cut could be found.
schurch-amoun-english-v.o: Recorded as leaving a smoky, woody scent.

city-cigar-company-kitsilano-cherry-blos.z: Kitsilano Cherry Blossom, a house blend from the tobacconist City Cigar Company, is referred to in available records as an aromatic; not enough sourcing could be found to document its content.
city-cigar-company-kitsilano-cherry-blos.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

samuel-gawith-commonwealth-mixture.z: Commonwealth Mixture is an unflavored, ribbon-cut English blend made entirely of Virginia and latakia leaves. The latakia ratio is high and gives the blend its dominant character. On the smoke, Virginia's natural sweetness is balanced by latakia's smoky, salty, and spicy side; the body is full, the smoke intense. Suited to smokers accustomed to Latakia-forward blends; being ribbon cut makes packing and lighting easier than flake presentations.
samuel-gawith-commonwealth-mixture.o: Heavy campfire and tar-echoing soot scent fills the room.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-hazelnut.z: The hazelnut-flavored aromatic blend from the Boswell workshop; no sufficient source describing its content and flavor profile could be found.

sterling-tobacco-co-sweet-briar.z: Sweet Briar is a light-colored blend marketed as Sterling Tobacco's best-selling aromatic. Its weight is carried by coarse, cube-cut burley; a touch of bright Virginia and a light aromatic topping are added alongside it. The result is a lightly flavored scent reminiscent of briar wood, which is where the blend's name comes from. On the palate, the flavor line stays predominantly tobacco-focused; despite a creamy body, it has a lively edge. Nicotine level is low. Designed for those seeking a light aromatic whose topping doesn't overpower and that leaves a floral, sweet room note.
sterling-tobacco-co-sweet-briar.o: Leaves a sweet scent reminiscent of honeysuckle blossom; a trace of honey, vanilla, and caramel lingers behind it.

backwoods-green.z: Backwoods Green is the aromatic entry in the brand's pouch series with a mint-forward direction. A mint-based flavoring is worked into a sweet, Cavendish-heavy base; the cut is ribbon and can be packed straight from the pouch. The smoke comes cool, leaving a refreshing trace on the palate. It's on the light side for nicotine, with flavor intensity kept low. It suits those looking for mentholated profiles or wanting a light, sweet, cool smoke during the day; for a palate accustomed to dark Latakia mixtures, it will read as too plain.
backwoods-green.o: Leaves a cooling mint and lightly sweet tobacco room note.

cornell-diehl-burley-ribbon-cut.z: Burley Ribbon Cut is the ribbon-cut form of the specially processed burley leaf Cornell & Diehl uses in most of its own blends. The leaf is sourced from Kentucky and Tennessee, and it is unflavored. It can be smoked on its own, paired with a Virginia, or used as a cooling, body-giving component in home blends; burley's slow-burning and low-sugar qualities reduce a blend's tendency toward tongue bite. It suits smokers looking for a nutty, dry, unflavored taste and burley's characteristic high nicotine, as well as those building their own blends.
cornell-diehl-burley-ribbon-cut.o: Leaves an aroma of dry hay, walnut shell, and light earth.

cornell-diehl-founding-fathers.z: Founding Fathers is a lightly aromatic blend built mainly on burley and black cavendish, supported by Virginia. The ribbon-cut mixture is given a pomegranate flavoring; Cornell & Diehl ties the fruit to its cultivation in the garden farms of Founding Fathers like Mount Vernon and Monticello in the eighteenth century. The blend's color is a mix of brown and reddish tones; the tin note carries notes of coffee, syrup, and confectionery. On the smoke, burley dominates and delivers nicotine unusually pronounced for an aromatic, while the pomegranate sweetness stays in the background. It suits those who want the sweetness of flavored blends while avoiding a body-less smoke.
cornell-diehl-founding-fathers.o: Leaves a sweet fruit aroma of coffee, maple syrup, and caramel.

richs-meerschaum.z: Meerschaum is a mixture Rich's Cigar Store builds from Latakia, Burley, and Virginia leaf, described by the maker as an "American-style English blend." Latakia's smoke is balanced by Burley's dry, walnut-like body, while Virginia leaves a light sweetness in the background. The blend is designed with meerschaum pipes in mind, considering both the smoking experience and how the pipe colors over time. It suits smokers looking for an unflavored, medium-bodied English blend who don't want a heavy dose of Latakia. It is sold in bulk at Rich's stores in Portland.
richs-meerschaum.o: Leaves a trace of wood smoke and dry nut aroma mixed with a tart Virginia sweetness.

esoterica-tobacciana-dorchester.z: Dorchester sits in the virginia-perique wing of the Esoterica line, distinguished by its fine shag cut. It is produced by J. F. Germain & Son in Jersey and is listed under the virginia family in retailer catalogs. The fine cut lets the tobacco catch quickly and the flavors open fast; virginia's bready sweetness is joined by perique's plum, fig and peppery spice tones. Because of the fine cut it needs care in packing and smoking pace; it suits smokers familiar with the VaPer palate.
esoterica-tobacciana-dorchester.o: Leaves a slightly tart, fruity scent evoking dried fig and black pepper.

ascorti-veneto.z: No adequate independent source documenting the content of the Veneto blend, carrying the Ascorti name, could be found.
ascorti-veneto.o: No reliable information on the room note could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-cherry-bon-bon.z: Cherry Bon Bon is built on a black cavendish base produced by roasting select Green River burley leaf and then slowly steaming it. A dark cherry note and a touch of warm bitter chocolate are added on top, building the confectionery association its name suggests. It has a drier texture than most black cavendish blends, though because cavendish packs easily it needs a light hand when filling; otherwise the draw tightens. It burns at a medium pace, cool and without biting the tongue; the cherry topping is measured and fades in the final third of the smoke.
sutliff-tobacco-company-cherry-bon-bon.o: Leaves a scent of dark cherry and bitter chocolate.

mcclelland-2013-holiday-spirit.z: This is the 2013 edition of the Holiday Spirit series. In the series, a mild base of Virginia, Burley, and Cavendish leaves is sweetened with dark rum, pecan, and cocoa; nicotine load is kept low. A blend aimed at those new to aromatic tobaccos and those seeking sweet, seasonal smokes. Since McClelland stopped production in 2018, the series is no longer made.
mcclelland-2013-holiday-spirit.o: Leaves an aroma of dark rum, cocoa, and toasted walnut.

timm-planters-punch.z: An aromatic blend produced for Hamburg's Timm pipe shops, taking its name from the rum cocktail of the same name; no source documenting its composition and production status has been found.
timm-planters-punch.o: Records describe it as leaving a sweet, fruity, boozy aroma.

j-f-germain-son-club-mixture.z: Club Mixture is Germain's Virginia-forward everyday mixture. Red and light-yellow Virginia leaves form the base; two separately processed Cavendish tobaccos are added to soften the smoke and round out the sweetness. The result is a straightforward, cool-smoking tobacco without sharp edges. It's built to be light enough for all-day smoking; both nicotine and flavor intensity stay below moderate. It contains no Latakia and carries no heavy flavoring. It suits smokers wanting to experience Virginia's natural sugar in a softened form, or looking for a restful option among more intense mixtures. Production continues on the island of Jersey, where the family has been based since 1820.
j-f-germain-son-club-mixture.o: Leaves a sweetish aroma of hay and light caramel tobacco.

super-value-amaretto.z: Super Value is a budget aromatic pipe tobacco line produced in the US and sold in large-volume bags. Amaretto is prepared by applying an almond-liqueur-style top flavoring to a coarse-cut mix of light cavendish and burley leaves; domestic and imported leaf are used together across the line, and the profile is kept light. It offers a low-nicotine, soft, non-biting smoke. Suited to those new to aromatic tobacco and those seeking a light, sweet mixture for all-day smoking.
super-value-amaretto.o: Leaves a sweet scent of almond and marzipan.

mcclelland-tgl-toasted-cavendish-latakia.z: TGL is one of the blends McClelland sold in bulk. Toasted Cavendish is joined by Burley, golden Virginia, and a small amount of Cyprian Latakia, building a sweet but full-bodied smoke. Since the Latakia share is kept low, the blend doesn't take on an English mixture's sootiness; the smoky note remains only a background balancing the sweetness. The blend sits close in structure to the discontinued Lane HGL: the same toasted Cavendish, Burley, and Virginia joined by measured Latakia. It lights easily, burning cool and slow; nicotine level runs below or in the middle of medium. Suited to those who like a sweet Cavendish base but want a bit of smoke alongside it. McClelland closed in 2018, so the blend isn't produced anymore.
mcclelland-tgl-toasted-cavendish-latakia.o: A fine wood-smoke trace runs beneath the sweet Cavendish aroma.

solani-660-silver-flake.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Solani blend 660: Silver Flake could not be found.

tabacum-h1.z: No reliable source describing the composition of this Tabacum blend, recorded as based on cigar leaf, could be found.

rattray-marlin-flake-british-collection.z: Marlin Flake is a Virginia, black Cavendish, and Perique blend in Rattray's British Collection line. It is cut into long slices, coiled, and tinned; the dark, mottled colors in the cross-section show the high Cavendish proportion. In the tin note, Cavendish's tangy sweetness comes forward in place of Virginia. The slices are brittle, but the first light and burn throughout the smoke are trouble-free; it leaves a clean gray ash. In the first half of the smoke, Cavendish sweetness dominates; past the midpoint Virginia becomes pronounced and Perique's black-pepper-like bitter edge kicks in. Being prone to moisture, it calls for slow smoking. Strength ranges between light and medium. It suits smokers transitioning from flavored blends to unflavored Virginia blends. The Rattray name draws on the Scottish pipe-tobacco tradition; the brand's tobaccos are produced today in Germany.
rattray-marlin-flake-british-collection.o: Leaves a fairly heavy tobacco aroma along with a tangy sweet Cavendish scent.

charutaria-cruzeiro-ltda-tabaco-blend-ch.z: The entry has been left incomplete as no reliable source could be found for Charutaria Cruzeiro Ltda.'s Tabaco Blend Chocolate blend.

grants-tobacconist-custom-blend-no-2131.z: One of Grant's Tobacconist's numbered custom blends; there is no independent sourcing for its detailed composition.

cornell-diehl-golden-ash.z: Golden Ash is a Cornell & Diehl blend combining coarse-cut and cube-cut burley leaves with light Virginia slices, topped with a small amount of Latakia. Because different cuts sit together in the mix, the tin contents look varied. Burley's dry, nutty body forms the blend's backbone; Virginia adds a light sweetness, while the small Latakia portion contributes an understated smoky tone. Being unflavored and moderate in strength, it makes a good starting point for smokers new to English blends who don't want a heavy dose of Latakia.
cornell-diehl-golden-ash.o: Leaves a dry tobacco aroma reminiscent of nuts and wood incense.

mcclelland-panache.z: One of McClelland's limited-distribution aromatic blends; no sufficient source describing its contents and character could be found.

faders-nova.z: Not enough independent sourcing documenting the composition and character of Nova, one of the house blends of the Baltimore-based Fader's tobacconist, could be found.

havezaethe-minstreel.z: A Virginia-forward house blend from a Dutch tobacconist; there is not enough sourcing on its composition and production period.
havezaethe-minstreel.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

cornell-diehl-black-gold-maple.z: Black Gold Maple is a ribbon-cut aromatic combining black cavendish with golden Virginia's natural maple flavoring. Cornell & Diehl markets the blend as a smoke intended for autumn. Cavendish provides sweetness and softness while Virginia keeps the blend's dry, grassy side alive, preventing the smoke from turning into a flat, uniformly sugary composition. Nicotine strength is low, and room-note intensity is moderate for its category; the aroma stays more in the background than filling the room. Flavor level, however, is pronounced, with the maple note carrying through the bowl. It suits those wanting an aromatic smoke while avoiding heavy fruit flavorings, and anyone seeking sweetness without a spice or smoke layer.
cornell-diehl-black-gold-maple.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly caramel-like aroma reminiscent of maple syrup.

peretti-st-james-mixture.z: This is a blend attributed to the L. J. Peretti shop in Boston; no published source confirming its content and character could be found.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-winter-time-2018.z: The 2018 edition of Kohlhase & Kopp's seasonal limited releases under the name Winter Time; no verifiable source could be found giving content and casing information for this year.

robert-lewis-wingfield-mixture.z: Wingfield Mixture is an unflavored ribbon-cut blend prepared from aged Virginia leaf with a very small amount of black Cavendish and Latakia added. Being a ribbon cut, it burns evenly and cool. The blend is named, according to records, for Walter Wingfield, the inventor of the earliest form of lawn tennis and a longtime customer of the Robert Lewis shop. With no flavoring present, the leaves' own tastes come forward: citrus tartness, dry hay, oak, and earthy notes appear in varying measure. The Latakia amount is too small to make the smoky layer pronounced; black Cavendish softens it with sweetness. Strength sits in the middle of the medium range. It suits smokers looking for a plain, balanced, unflavored Virginia-based blend.
robert-lewis-wingfield-mixture.o: Leaves a dry-hay, oak, and light citrus aroma.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-old-english-cu.z: A burley-based blend records indicate was originally produced for the American market and later listed under the Orlik name; not enough independent source material confirming its details could be found.

timm-no-name-grun.z: The No Name series is an economical tobacco line, presented in plain packaging, that Dan Tobacco produces for Hamburg's Timm pipe shops under their name. The Green variety sits on this line's unflavored side: Latakia is added to Virginia leaf, giving a spicy, smoky, classic English-style mixture. Since it carries no sweetening casing, the taste comes entirely from the leaf; the Latakia proportion keeps the blend on a medium-bodied line. Aimed at those wanting to smoke Latakia mixtures daily in a large package.
timm-no-name-grun.o: Leaves a smoky, tar-like wood aroma reminiscent of a campfire.

robert-mcconnell-maduro.z: Maduro is a blend built on combining heat-pressed dark Virginia leaves with Perique; Burley and black Cavendish also enter the content. A light top note evoking naval rum is applied. Being ribbon cut eases packing and gives an even burn. The dark pressed Virginia gives the blend a toasted, sweet, bready foundation; Perique adds a measured spice and dark-fruit layer on top of this. The rum casing stays at an intensity that does not cover the tobacco taste. Nicotine is low. Suited to smokers seeking a dark, sweet Virginia-Perique standing somewhere between cased and unflavored.
robert-mcconnell-maduro.o: Leaves a warm scent carrying dark sugar and rum sweetness.

e-a-carey-full-bodied-black.z: Full Bodied Black is the fuller-bodied counterpart to Classic Black Aromatic, E. A. Carey's best-known blend. The maker states it preserves the same taste and scent direction while increasing body and flavor intensity; its black-cavendish-forward structure carries the blend's dark color and sweetness. It's described as smoking cool and not harshening the tongue; however, its flavor and topping intensity are above the brand's light aromatics. It is built for those who enjoy black aromatics but find the lighter ones too plain.
e-a-carey-full-bodied-black.o: Leaves a dense trace evoking a dark, sweet, sugared tobacco scent.

dunhill-my-mixture-bb1938-babys-bottom.z: My Mixture BB1938 Baby's Bottom is Dunhill's full blend built on Virginia and latakia. Its base combines red, lemon-yellow and orange Virginia leaves, topped with Cyprus latakia; it is ribbon cut. Wood, smoke, tannin and spice stand out in the flavor profile, with latakia building a smoky base while Virginia gives it sweetness and roundness. Contrary to what its name suggests, the blend is strong and heavy in nicotine, so it appeals to experienced smokers. Per records, the Baby's Bottom mixture was first introduced by the London tobacconist H. L. Savory & Co., dating back to 1885; after Dunhill acquired that firm in 1932, the blend was reintroduced in 1938 under its own "My Mixture" line. It is not produced under the Dunhill name today.
dunhill-my-mixture-bb1938-babys-bottom.o: Leaves a scent of dark wood smoke and tannin, with a light spiciness.

mac-baren-vanilla-cream-flake.z: Vanilla Cream Flake is a pressed aromatic in Mac Baren's classic series. Its base holds matured Virginia leaves and mild black Cavendish; this pair is pressed and cut into thin slices. A silky vanilla topping is applied over it, and the cream association in the name comes from this flavoring's mild structure. Despite being an aromatic, the flake form lets the tobacco burn slow and cool; the flavoring doesn't fully mask the leaf's natural sugar. Nicotine load is low, the taste proceeds along a vanilla axis and keeps its balance through the smoke. The slices need to be rubbed out and aired for a while before packing. Suited to those who like aromatics but also want the smoking rhythm of pressed tobaccos.
mac-baren-vanilla-cream-flake.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough aroma.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-72.z: No. 72, one of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's numbered bulk blends, is recorded as an unflavored English-style mixture; no verifiable source describing its composition could be found.

hu-tobacco-coming-home.z: Coming Home is a flavored blend HU Tobacco introduced in 2021, prepared with summer in mind. Its base is built from ready-rubbed, high-sugar Mysore-origin Virginia leaves; a small amount of strong Burley is added to this. The flavoring is honey-based and rounded out with rose oil; because of this, a pronounced floral layer sits atop the sweet base. It offers a medium-strength, uncomplicated structure, aimed at those wanting to experience Virginia sweetness with a floral flavoring.
hu-tobacco-coming-home.o: Leaves a floral aroma reminiscent of rose water alongside honey sweetness.

peterson-irish-cask.z: Irish Cask is a ribbon-cut blend prepared by resting Virginia, Perique, and black Cavendish leaf in sherry casks. It was reportedly sold previously under the name Irish Oak. The cask resting gives the blend a wine-like sweetness and depth. The smoke is medium-bodied; Cavendish lays down a soft, sweet base, Perique leaves a light sharpness in the background, and Virginia carries the tart side. It suits smokers seeking wine- and whiskey-associated flavors who don't want a heavy fruit topping.
peterson-irish-cask.o: Leaves a trace recalling wine cask and sweet raisin.

chris-morgan-bayou-buck.z: Bayou Buck is a blend where a generous share of perique is balanced against ripened red Virginia. Perique carries the spicy, plummy side, while red Virginia gives a tangy sweetness and dark fruit; the blend also has Green River Burley added, toasted into black cavendish, and this component gives the smoke a creamy body. No flavoring sauce is used. The blend is one of three tobaccos pipe maker Chris Morgan prepared together with the Sutliff Tobacco Company; the others are Jackalope and White Rabbit. It suits smokers looking for the Virginia-Perique structure paired with a round, burley-derived body.
chris-morgan-bayou-buck.o: A creamy, lightly toasted base lies beneath the dark fruit and peppery spice aroma.

mcclelland-m-60-brandywine.z: No sufficient independent source describing the contents of this blend from the numbered bulk aromatic series could be found.
mcclelland-m-60-brandywine.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of brandy.

milan-tobacconists-my-finest-kind.z: My Finest Kind is Milan Tobacconists' house blend resting solely on cavendish leaves. According to the maker's description, different black cavendish tobaccos are combined in balanced proportions; sweetness comes first on the draw, with a light vanilla taste remaining at the finish. Its body is thin and its nicotine load low. A fitting entry for smokers looking for cavendish sweetness in a plain, single-axis form who don't want a complex leaf construction.
milan-tobacconists-my-finest-kind.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and cooked-sugar aroma.

peterson-hyde-park.z: Hyde Park is prepared by pressing and rubbing Virginia and Burley leaf into broken flake. Its flavoring uses a small amount of rum and maple sugar; the aim is not to mask Virginia's natural sweetness and Burley's body but to bring them out. The body sits between medium and full, and flavor intensity is high. Burley lays down an earthy, nutty base while Virginia adds sugar and a light tartness. It suits smokers who enjoy working with pressed tobacco, who want to avoid heavy aromatics but still like a light flavoring; reportedly its layers become more pronounced with aging.
peterson-hyde-park.o: Leaves a measured trace recalling sweet rum and burnt sugar.

danish-import-red.z: The red-packaged edition of the Danish-origin Skandinavik series, also listed as "Full Aroma" in retailer records. It is built on select Burley and Virginia leaf, ribbon cut, and follows the Danish aromatic tradition — a blend with more pronounced casing than the other members of the series. Nicotine sits between mild and medium, giving it a build suited to all-day smoking. It suits smokers wanting to get to know the Danish style of aromatic, or those looking for the easy-lighting nature of a fine cut. The product is distributed in the United States market as imported Danish tobacco.
danish-import-red.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly spiced tobacco scent.

dan-tobacco-london-blend-no-250.z: A pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source on the blend's composition or character was found, so no further detail is given.

holger-danske-sunny-delight.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for Holger Danske's Sunny Delight blend, so its content and character could not be recorded.

bufflehead-merganser-decoy.z: Bufflehead was a brand producing small batches in the United States in the early 2000s, naming its blends after waterfowl; since no independent source describing this blend's content and character could be found, the entry has been left incomplete.

peter-stokkebye-turkish-blend.z: Turkish Blend is a ribbon-cut blend in which Peter Stokkebye gives Oriental leaf top billing. Although it also contains Virginia, Turkish tobacco largely determines the blend's character, giving an earthy, dry-grassy, spicy profile. With its unflavored structure, medium nicotine, and intense flavor, it speaks to smokers seeking the taste of Oriental leaf on its own. Its kinship with Oriental-forward blends produced in Turkey is clear; it is a tobacco that makes itself known even when the palate is tired, such as after a meal.
peter-stokkebye-turkish-blend.o: Leaves a dry, earthy, spicy Oriental tobacco aroma.

smokers-paradise-clearwater-dublin-fog.z: One of the shop blends from the Smoker's Paradise tobacconist in Clearwater; no independent source describing its composition could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-red-line.z: Red Line is a blend in Ken Byron Ventures' unflavored Virginia line. Per the manufacturer's description, it's built primarily on red Virginia crops sourced from Carolina and Brazil; spicy dark Virginia leaves are added to raise the blend's body and nicotine load. Since the dark leaves are kept in the background proportionally, the flavor balance stays on the bready, fruity sweetness of red Virginia. Since no casing is used, the taste comes entirely from the leaves themselves: dried fruit, a light lemony tanginess and a sugary aftertaste come forward. Smoked slowly, its tendency to bite the tongue lessens, though a fast draw can give the sharpness typical of Virginias. Suited to smokers seeking unflavored Virginia and wanting a medium-bodied, all-day option.
ken-byron-ventures-red-line.o: Leaves a tangy-sweet tobacco note reminiscent of dry hay and stale bread crust.

park-lane-tobacconist-black-crush.z: One of the black-cavendish-based house blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park; no usable source could be found to confirm its composition and character.

peter-stokkebye-perique.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Perique in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

peter-heinrichs-chateau-henri-no-13.z: Chateau Henri No. 13 is a Virginia-Perique mixture in the Chateau Henri series of the Cologne-based house Peter Heinrichs. Per the maker's description, selected Virginia leaves are hand-rolled and processed into curly cut; a pinch of Louisiana Perique and double-fermented black Cavendish are added to the blend. The curly cut allows the slices to be rubbed out for packing and gives a slow, cool burn. Virginia's bready sweetness forms the blend's backbone; Perique layers a sharpness recalling plum and spice on top of that sweetness, while black Cavendish rounds out the texture. Nicotine strength doesn't rise above the medium band, while flavor intensity is pronounced. It is a suitable record for smokers wanting to get to know the Virginia-Perique family who are used to working with rolled cuts. The Chateau Henri name comes from the firm's tobacco and pipe shop in Bergheim.
peter-heinrichs-chateau-henri-no-13.o: Leaves a dried-fruit sweetness with a light peppery spice aroma.

davidoff-private-stock-no-1.z: This is a blend once offered under the Davidoff name, not appearing in current catalogs; no verifiable source about its composition could be found.

my-smoking-shop-blueberry-black-cavendis.z: Blueberry Black Cavendish is an aromatic built on black cavendish, flavored with a blueberry sauce. The same blend, sold in bulk under the Century name in the UK, has also appeared on shelves as Blue B. Cavendish following the 2017 naming change. It is ribbon cut and, being packed moist, burns slowly. Nicotine is low; the taste left in the mouth is the sweetness of the fruit sauce more than the tobacco itself. Suitable for smokers looking for a fruity aromatic who don't mind it leaving a noticeable scent in the room.

lane-limited-captain-black-gold.z: Captain Black Gold is the series' light-colored member; per the manufacturer's description it's built on golden cavendish leaf, and the blend's color is distinctly bright. The cut is ribbon; it's available in pouch and tin. In the smoke, body is balanced, taste is soft and single-plane; the matured light leaf's lightly grassy, citrus-leaning side comes with measured sweetness. Nicotine is low. For smokers who find the syrupy sweetness of dark cavendish blends too heavy and seek a lighter, milder aromatic.
lane-limited-captain-black-gold.o: Leaves a lightly sweet room note carrying a hay and citrus dimension.

ken-byron-ventures-alchemy-parish.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Ken Byron Ventures' Alchemy Parish blend.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-candy-a.z: Mr. Christian's Candy Apples Deluxe is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

rattray-summer-edition-2015.z: Summer Edition 2015 is an aromatic blend prepared for summer 2015 in Rattray's seasonal limited-edition line. Virginia leaf in light and medium brown tones is combined with black Cavendish in ribbon cut, flavored with raspberry and peach-cream aroma. Opening the tin gives a sweet, jammy scent. In the smoke the peach note is pronounced at first, turning into a creamy sweetness in the middle, and shifting toward a nutty tone near the end. Nicotine is low and the smoke light and cool. It suits those looking for a light fruity summer aromatic and collectors of limited editions. Being a limited edition, its production has ended.
rattray-summer-edition-2015.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity aroma recalling raspberry jam and peach cream.

peretti-no-name.z: No Name is an aromatic blend among Peretti's American-type offerings. It comes from Robert Peretti and is known by this name because, in the house's own records, it was seen as having a distinctive, unnamed flavor profile among pipe tobaccos. A burley base gives a cool, slow burn, while cavendish and its applied topping build the blend's pronounced sweet side. The smoke is mild and low in nicotine, leaving a sweet, creamy layer on the tongue rather than a heavy tobacco body. It suits smokers who enjoy the aromatic line and want a low-strength blend they can smoke all day. Being aromatic, its moisture can run high; airing it out briefly before packing improves the burn.
peretti-no-name.o: Leaves a sweet, creamy scent recalling confectionery.

straus-tobacco-wenceslas.z: An aromatic blend that the Cincinnati-area Straus Tobacconist releases once a year, in a limited run, for the holiday season; since detailed maker information on its composition could not be found, this record is kept limited.
straus-tobacco-wenceslas.o: Leaves a sweet, spiced aromatic scent.

sutliff-tobacco-company-dark-chocolate-b.z: B25 Dark Chocolate is an aromatic made from a combination of black cavendish and dark-toned burley leaves. The sauce is built on a full cocoa, carrying less sugar and less moisture than many chocolate aromatics. Because the ribbon cut runs dry, it lights easily and has a low tendency to bite the tongue. Suited to smokers seeking a dry-smoking chocolate aromatic that emphasizes bitter cocoa over sweetness.
sutliff-tobacco-company-dark-chocolate-b.o: Leaves a bitter-cocoa scent with limited sweetness.

c-b-mller-co-a-s-osborne-63.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named Osborne 63 under the C.B. Møller & Co. A/S brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

alfie-turmeaus-wavecrest.z: Wavecrest was one of the aromatic house mixtures prepared at Turmeaus stores. It was based on combining bright, golden Virginia-heavy aromatic tobaccos; per records its recipe consisted of combining one measure of Gawith Hoggarth New Prince with one measure of Gold Block, with a vanilla-and-maple-leaning flavoring defining the blend's top layer. It's a cool-burning smoke, light on nicotine; while the sweet sauce is noticeable, it doesn't fully mask Virginia's own sugar. It was removed from the list along with Sweet Leaf following a regulatory change affecting the store's own mixtures. It suited those new to aromatic tobaccos and those looking for a lightly sweet blend they could smoke all day.
alfie-turmeaus-wavecrest.o: Leaves a sweet trace in the room leaning toward maple syrup and vanilla cake.

drucquer-sons-red-lion.z: Red Lion is a light-to-medium-bodied English mixture built around light yellow and red Virginia leaves, containing Cyprus latakia, toasted black cavendish and very little burley and perique. The cavendish addition gives the blend a natural caramel sweetness and softness; the latakia proportion is kept enough to show a smoky character without taking the lead. On the palate it runs smooth and balanced, with no sharp edges. Because its nicotine level is low to medium, it suits morning or midday smokes. It suits those wanting the smoky framework of English mixtures while also seeking a sweet base, and smokers looking for a soft entry point into latakia blends.
drucquer-sons-red-lion.o: Leaves a trace mixing soft soot with a caramel-like sweet tobacco scent.

leonard-dingler-ltd-nineteen-ofour-1904-.z: Nineteen O'Four is a pipe tobacco line from South Africa's long-established tobacco manufacturer Leonard Dingler, its name taken from the year 1904. The company dates to the early twentieth century, remained a family business for a long time, and later passed to Swedish Match. The series' base rests on Burley and Kentucky leaf; this structure gives the smoke a nutty, bready and earthy body. The product is sold in 50-gram folding pouches and is largely aimed at the South African market. Nineteen O'Four (1904) Cherry Blend is recorded as the line's arm distinguished by its cherry flavoring. The casing is applied at a level that doesn't mask the Burley base; the smoke stays cool and body stays at medium. Of interest to those seeking an aromatic profile but avoiding syrupy weight, and to those curious about counter tobaccos specific to the South African market. Hard to find outside the country.
leonard-dingler-ltd-nineteen-ofour-1904-.o: Leaves a room note of ripe cherry and a light hint of almond kernel.

cornell-diehl-briar-fox.z: Briar Fox is an unflavored mixture where Virginia and burley are pressed into a cake. It is one of Cornell & Diehl's best-known tinned products and is considered a measured example of the brand's Virginia-burley approach. Pressing lets the two leaves' flavors meld together; the smoke reads as a single tobacco taste rather than separate components. The smoke is clean and direct: burley's nutty, earthy, lightly woody body combines with Virginia's natural sweetness; complexity increases toward the middle of the bowl, and the result shifts toward a spicier direction. Nicotine and flavor intensity are medium, making it an all-day blend. According to available records, it was a personal favorite of Danish pipe maker Peter Heeschen. It suits those looking for an unflavored, straightforward everyday mixture.
cornell-diehl-briar-fox.o: Leaves a warm aroma reminiscent of baked bread and toasted nuts.

wesleys-no-43-old-gold.z: Old Gold, among Wesley's house blends, brings together the softness of Oriental (Turkish) leaf and Burley with the light sweetness of matured Virginia. A subtle top-flavoring applied over it adds scent to the blend; the maker describes it not as a heavy aromatic but as a calm mixture for everyday smoking.
wesleys-no-43-old-gold.o: A light flavoring accompanies the nutty Burley and sweetish leaf scent.

a-c-petersen-premier-cru.z: Premier Cru is a blend following A & C Petersen's classic English mixture design: Virginia at the base, with measured amounts of Latakia and Oriental leaf added over it. Deliberately reining in the Latakia ratio lets the Virginia sweetness read through without the smoky side taking over. It's an unflavored blend; strength and taste are medium. It suits those new to Latakia-containing blends or looking for a balanced English mixture without a heavy smoky load. Like the brand's other products, this blend is not on the market today.
a-c-petersen-premier-cru.o: Leaves a lightly woody, smoky room note with dry spice.

holger-danske-vanilla-and-orange.z: Vanilla and Orange is a blend in the aromatic line of the Danish brand Holger Danske. It's a ribbon-cut mixture in which Virginia and Burley leaves are combined with black Cavendish; as the name suggests, it's flavored with vanilla and orange. It stays very light in nicotine, while the taste it leaves on the palate is moderately pronounced. The flavoring is kept measured enough not to entirely mask the tobacco's own taste; in this respect it's a mixture worth considering for those new to aromatic blends or looking for a light smoke during the day. When smoked, it leaves a trace in the room carrying vanilla's sweetness together with orange's citrus aroma.
holger-danske-vanilla-and-orange.o: Leaves a citrus aroma in the room reminiscent of sweet vanilla and orange peel.

planta-golden-irish-coffee-mixture.z: Planta Golden Irish Coffee Mixture is a pipe tobacco blend for which there is not enough independent source material.
planta-golden-irish-coffee-mixture.o: Not enough records could be found on the room note.

peter-heinrichs-no-60.z: No. 60 is a Peter Heinrichs blend built predominantly from light-colored Virginia leaf, with a small amount of Burley added in. The maker describes it as a tobacco pressed and sliced Navy Cut style; the slices are rubbed out before packing and give a slow, cool burn. Virginia's lightly sugary base, recalling grass and hay, is the determining factor; Burley adds a measured body to that base. Flavoring is kept very low, and bite is minimal. It suits those wanting to get to know natural Virginia sweetness without exaggeration, and smokers seeking a light flake.
peter-heinrichs-no-60.o: Leaves a thin sweet trace alongside dry hay and lightly sweet straw.

cornell-diehl-repose.z: Repose is a light aromatic blend combining cube-cut Burley with Turkish-Oriental leaf and bright Virginia, with dark rum sprinkled on top. The cube cut keeps the tobacco loose in the bowl and lets the ember catch easily. The rum casing is applied at a level that doesn't mask the blend's natural nutty, dry tones, so it moves more like a flavored Burley mixture than a sugary aromatic. It stays cool when smoked slowly; smoked fast, the tongue bite typical of Burley can appear. It serves as an intermediate step for those wanting to move from aromatics to natural tobacco taste.
cornell-diehl-repose.o: A light rum sweetness is sensed over a nutty tobacco scent.

mccranies-black-angus.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found on Black Angus, one of McCranie's Pipe Shop's house blends.
mccranies-black-angus.o: No reliable description of the aroma could be found.

charatan-eventide.z: Eventide is a dark English blend built in the Charatan line to stand in for Dunhill's Nightcap. Virginia and a small measure of Perique are layered over Latakia and Oriental leaf; the cut is ribbon. It is the richest member of the series: alongside the smoke-and-wood layer comes spice and dark fruit from the Perique. No casing is used. Nicotine is high, so it is built as an end-of-day blend not recommended on an empty stomach. Suitable for experienced smokers accustomed to dark, full-bodied English blends.
charatan-eventide.o: Leaves a heavy smoke, charred wood and spice room note.

mcclelland-frog-morton.z: Frog Morton is a Latakia-forward, ribbon-cut English blend McClelland released within its Craftsbury series. Its composition holds a large share of Cyprian Latakia balanced by Virginia leaf; records indicate the Latakia share runs to roughly two-thirds of the blend. In the smoke, soot, incense, and faint cocoa-coffee associations are joined by a citrusy sweetness from the Virginia. Being below medium in nicotine and burning cool and dry, it's often cited as an entry blend into the world of Latakia. Later members of the series were derived by adding Perique, Basma, or barrel shavings on top of this main body. Production ended when the brand closed in 2018.
mcclelland-frog-morton.o: Leaves a sooty wood and incense aroma reminiscent of a campfire.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-bulls-eye.z: Bull's Eye is a pressed blend Danish Orlik built on Virginia and perique, also carrying a share of black cavendish. The same production has counterparts sold in different markets under the names Peter Stokkebye Luxury Bullseye Flake and Davidoff Flake Medallions; the difference is the name and distribution channel. The perique share is kept lower than in other Virginia-perique flakes, so the spice doesn't overpower Virginia's sweetness and overall strength stays measured. Rubbed out and packed, it catches easily, needs few relights, and keeps its taste down to the bottom of the bowl. It can be recommended for smokers seeking a mild Virginia-perique or newly getting acquainted with the type. Its production under the Orlik name has ended.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-bulls-eye.o: Leaves a thin trace of spice within a scent of dry grass and dried fruit.

fincks-cigar-company-peach.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for Finck's Cigar Company's Peach pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

pcca-city-lights.z: City Lights is one of the aromatic blends McClelland tinned in limited numbers for the PCCA club; no independent source describing its composition could be found.
pcca-city-lights.o: No source could be found to describe the room note.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-lizzie-blood-red-virg.z: No verifiable composition and character information could be compiled for Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Lizzie Blood Red Virginia.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-lizzie-blood-red-virg.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-your-welcome-2021.z: A year-stamped limited edition in Ken Byron Ventures' pure Virginia line; not enough sources could be found to document its composition and character.
ken-byron-ventures-your-welcome-2021.o: Could not be described due to lack of accessible records.

solani-633-virginia-flake-with-perique.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Solani blend 633: Virginia Flake with Perique could not be found.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-poniatowski-va.z: A vanilla-flavored, cavendish-based Orlik aromatic; not enough independent source material confirming its composition and character could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-live-wire.z: Live Wire is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

gq-tobaccos-soft-scotch.z: Soft Scotch is a blend where GQ Tobaccos pairs a Latakia body with a flavored top note. The blend's main component is smoky, sweet-woody Cyprian Latakia; black Cavendish adds a creamy vanilla taste and softness. Vanilla is applied on top along with a whiskey touch. The result is a mixture where smoke and sweet topping sit side by side: the smoke is creamy and mild, the taste medium in intensity, and nicotine stays low. Suited to smokers who love Latakia blends but want a bit of sweetness, or to those considering a move from aromatics toward English mixtures.
gq-tobaccos-soft-scotch.o: A creamy vanilla and whiskey trace layers over the aroma of smoked wood.

the-tobacco-barn-cambridge.z: No sufficient source describing the leaf composition and flavor profile of Cambridge, listed in the medium-to-dark toasted Cavendish group of Tobacco Barn's house blend list, has been found.

milan-tobacconists-honey-smoke.z: Honey Smoke is one of Milan Tobacconists' bulk aromatics. According to the shop's description, Virginia leaves, golden Cavendish, and fire-cured leaf are brought together; vanilla, honey, and coconut stand out in the flavoring. It is ribbon cut. Using a small amount of fire-cured leaf gives the blend's sweet core a lightly smoky frame; this sets it apart from purely sweet, unflavored aromatics. Its body stays light. A construction geared toward smokers who like honeyed flavorings but don't want an entirely sugary smoke.
milan-tobacconists-honey-smoke.o: Leaves an aroma of toasted marshmallow and honey.

dan-tobacco-sam-malloys-no-4-extra-stout.z: This is a pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source about the blend's composition and character could be found, so no detail is given.

smokers-haven-exotique-mixture.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Smokers' Haven blend Exotique Mixture could not be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-greve-ham.z: A Virginia-based blend said to be aimed at the Scandinavian market; no reliable detail on its composition and production history could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-greve-ham.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay and light sweetness.

cornell-diehl-black-frigate.z: Black Frigate is prepared by adding Latakia and Turkish leaf to the navy cavendish base Cornell & Diehl uses in its Blockade Runner blend. This brings together, in one body, the sweetness of Virginia leaf rested in rum and Latakia's smoke. Though the name references the naval flake tradition, the product is not a sliced flake; it is pressed and cut as an old-style crumble cake. The tin note carries rum-and-fruit sweetness together with smoke and spice. On the smoke, Latakia stands clearly in front, with unsweetened black cavendish and Oriental adding depth to it. Nicotine strength is above medium. According to available records, resting it for about a year changes its character. It suits those looking for a bridge between rum-soaked Virginia and English mixtures.
cornell-diehl-black-frigate.o: A rummy, fruity sweetness seeps out from beneath the smoky wood aroma.

peter-stokkebye-xxx-premium-latakia.z: This is a product sold in bulk under the Peter Stokkebye name that, as its name suggests, is Latakia-forward; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources describing the blend's composition and character in detail could be found.
peter-stokkebye-xxx-premium-latakia.o: Leaves a smoky, woody aroma from the Latakia.

black-cat-cigar-company-black-cherry.z: Black Cherry is one of the bulk-sold house aromatics from Black Cat Cigar Company in East Norriton, Pennsylvania. The blend's base is toasted black Cavendish, with light Cavendish and Virginia added. Most of the sweetness comes from the Cavendish process, while the cherry topping applied over it is kept measured. Nicotine stays light, and it burns cool. It suits smokers who want a cherry aromatic but avoid an artificial-tasting intensity, and who enjoy working with bulk tobacco.
black-cat-cigar-company-black-cherry.o: Leaves a sweet room note of cherry and cooked sugar.

tabacos-catarinenses-ltda-havana-cereja-.z: Havana Cereja is recorded as a cherry-flavored tobacco in the Havana line from the Brazilian maker Tabacos Catarinenses; no sufficient independent source describing the blend's composition could be found.
tabacos-catarinenses-ltda-havana-cereja-.o: No reliable record of a room note could be found.

bbb-danish-mixture.z: A Cavendish-forward mixture from BBB prepared in the Danish style; sold in 50-gram tins. No detailed manufacturer statement on its leaf composition could be found.
bbb-danish-mixture.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly toasted room note.

stanwell-danish-truffles.z: Stated to be part of Stanwell's aromatic wing; no verifiable maker or retailer source describing this blend's composition and topping could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-bas-matica.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Ken Byron Ventures' Bas Matica blend.

sutliff-tobacco-company-tobacco-galleria.z: One of the aromatic blends in Sutliff's Tobacco Galleria line; no accessible source documenting its content could be found.

mac-baren-hh-highland-blend.z: HH Highland Blend departs from the HH line's unflavored approach, pairing a latakia-containing blend with Scotch whisky. It contains fully matured Virginias, ready-rubbed burleys, latakia and a small amount of fire-cured cavendish; a thirty-year-old Glenfarclas single malt whisky is reportedly added to the blend. The tin note leads with a smoky, sweet meeting: latakia's smoky scent is topped by whisky's sugary, lightly sour tone. In the smoke, latakia's woody smoke and Virginia sweetness move along a medium-bodied base, with the whisky note appearing at the finish. Suited to those who love latakia blends but want a smoke softened by a sweet top note rather than a fully dry English mixture. Moisture is at a level ready to smoke directly.
mac-baren-hh-highland-blend.o: Leaves a trace where campfire smoke and sweet whisky intertwine.

peretti-tropical-fruit.z: Tropical Fruit is a Peretti blend prepared by combining aged black Cavendish with fire-cured leaf and flavoring it with exotic fruit essences. The maker describes it as one of the house's smoothest and coolest-burning blends. Nicotine is low and the taste is built directly around the flavoring; the Cavendish's sugar carries the fruit notes. It suits smokers who enjoy pronounced fruit aromatics and are seeking a mild, non-biting daytime blend.
peretti-tropical-fruit.o: Leaves a ripe tropical fruit and sugared pineapple aroma.

310-pipe-tobacco-holts-101.z: This is one of 310 Pipe & Tobacco's aromatic house blends; there is not enough available documentation of its composition.

danske-club-burgundy.z: A blend from the Danish brand Danske Club said to be aromatic; there isn't enough reliable source material to confirm its composition and character.

samuel-gawith-2014.z: A limited-run Samuel Gawith record from 2014; no independent source documenting its content and character could be found.

dan-tobacco-sweet-mango.z: As the name suggests, this is an aromatic blend topped in the direction of mango; not enough sourcing could be found about its composition and character.
dan-tobacco-sweet-mango.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

nording-no-4.z: One of the numbered blends tied to the Nording name; no reliable source describing its composition and character could be found.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-winter-time-2020.z: Winter Time is Kohlhase & Kopp's limited aromatic series prepared for the winter months; the 2020 edition is one installment of this series. The blend is built by putting black cavendish and some burley alongside Virginia leaves and cube-cut Virginia. On the casing side, coconut, fruit and vanilla notes come forward. Burley gives an earthy, nutty, bready base; golden Virginia brings a citrus-leaning tanginess, grassy freshness and light spice; black cavendish carries the creamy sweetness. It's a cool, clean-burning mixture, light in nicotine. Being a limited run, it wasn't renewed afterward. Suited to smokers interested in sweet, fruity aromatics.
kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-winter-time-2020.o: Leaves a sweet room note reminiscent of vanilla, caramel and a freshly baked waffle.

pipesandcigars-com-blending-dark-fired-k.z: Dark Fired Kentucky Burley is a single-varietal leaf sold in bulk for blending. This dark leaf from the Burley family is cured over an open fire; according to the maker's description, this process gives it a more measured smokiness than Latakia, a pronounced earthy taste, and considerable fullness. As a blending material it is used in two directions: adding sharpness to Latakia-heavy mixtures and thickening the body of Virginia-heavy mixtures. It can also be smoked alone; it suits those looking for an unflavored, dry, high-nicotine leaf, as well as home blenders.
pipesandcigars-com-blending-dark-fired-k.o: Leaves a dry, smoky aroma reminiscent of open-fire-cured wood and soot.

arango-royal-comfort.z: Royal Comfort is a mild aromatic blend built on aged red Virginia leaf, lightly toasted Cavendish, and a small amount of Perique. On the flavoring side, notes of fresh fruit, barrel-aged whiskey, and earthy vanilla stand out; the cut is ribbon, which makes packing the pipe easy and helps achieve an even burn. Its light nicotine and mild smoke make the blend the kind of aromatic that can be smoked all day. Records indicate the blend was first released in 1981 by R.J. Reynolds, but wasn't long-lived. The Arango Cigar Co. name brought it back in 2025, with production undertaken by Cornell & Diehl; the brand is of US origin. It's a suitable option for those looking for a light, sweet profile on the aromatic side, as well as pipe beginners; since the Perique share is low, the spice stays well in the background.
arango-royal-comfort.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and lightly fruity room note.

planta-image-latakia.z: Planta Image Latakia is a pipe tobacco blend for which there is not enough independent source material.
planta-image-latakia.o: Not enough records could be found on the room note.

planta-anno-mmviii-exotic-mixture.z: This is a blend in the German maker Planta's limited-production Anno series, named after a year; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

sillems-red.z: Red is one of the color-named aromatic blends in the Sillem's series, produced by Kohlhase & Kopp. Its body holds a high proportion of spicy-sweet Virginia flake, joined by twice-toasted black cavendish. The tin holds a mix of broken flake with large and fine golden-yellow Virginia leaf. The flavoring is built on ripe apple, cherry, and mirabelle plum; a fine lemon tone balances the sweetness. Nicotine is light, the smoke is cool and fruity. Suited to smokers who enjoy fruit-centered, sweet but non-syrupy aromatics.
sillems-red.o: Leaves a light lemon scent mixed with ripe apple, cherry, and yellow plum.

gatlin-burlier-smokies-smoke-eaze.z: Not enough sourcing explaining its content could be found for Smokies Smoke-Eaze, one of the house blends of the Gatlinburlier tobacconist in Gatlinburg.
gatlin-burlier-smokies-smoke-eaze.o: Records do not document a room note.

tinder-box-north-sea.z: Tinder Box is the name of an American tobacconist chain founded in 1928 that sells blends prepared for its own shops under its own name; North Sea is one of these house blends, though no sufficient independent source describing its composition and character has been found.

cornell-diehl-old-joe-krantz.z: Old Joe Krantz is a burley mixture blender Bob Runowski created in memory of the grandfather who introduced him to the pipe. Per Cornell & Diehl's description, dark burley and cube-cut burley are combined with red Virginia ribbon and perique; it contains no Latakia or Oriental leaf. Turkish-language sources describe it as coming in a coarse, chunky cut, with an intense raw-tobacco aroma released upon opening the pouch. Throughout the smoke, perique's spice takes the lead; the body is full and heavy. Because nicotine content runs high, smoking it quickly has been reported to cause lightheadedness, so a slow pace is required. When it arrives on the moist side, a brief drying-out period helps keep it lit. It suits smokers accustomed to strong, nicotine-rich burley mixtures, but is a demanding tobacco for beginners.
cornell-diehl-old-joe-krantz.o: Leaves an intense, raw-tobacco aroma with a musty-tangy note from the perique.

wolfway-white-izmir-tutun.z: As the name suggests, this is a single-varietal product based on Oriental leaf from the Izmir region; no verifiable source could be found.

savinelli-giubileo-doro.z: Savinelli's blend classified as Virginia-and-Latakia-based; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

vegassmokes-five-star.z: A VegasSmokes blend described as plain Virginia; no independent source documenting its composition has been found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-butter-pecan-b33.z: B33 Butter Pecan is an American aromatic built entirely on black cavendish. The cavendish is prepared from roasted, steamed Green River burley leaf; a buttery vanilla and roasted-pecan-direction topping is applied on top, presented in ribbon cut. Nicotine is light, bite is low, and flavor intensity is measured; the defining element is the topping itself. Suited to smokers who enjoy sweet, dessert-like aromatics and seek the topping over plain leaf taste.
sutliff-tobacco-company-butter-pecan-b33.o: Leaves a scent of buttery vanilla and roasted pecan.

lane-limited-orienta.z: Not enough independent sources could be found documenting the contents and character of American blender Lane Limited's blend called Orienta.

gawith-hoggarth-co-bobs-square-cut.z: Bob's Square Cut comes from the same family as Bob's Chocolate Flake; it is a blend that combines Virginia, Latakia, and Burley leaves with chocolate, cocoa, and vanilla toppings. The main difference lies in presentation: instead of being cut into flakes, the pressed mass is cut into small square pieces. This cut lets the smoker load the pipe directly without rubbing out flakes, notably shortening preparation. The topping dose is measured; on the sweet Virginia base, cocoa and vanilla are present but not smothering, and the Latakia stays in the background. The square cut burns a bit faster than a flake, so it stays cooler when smoked with slow draws. It is a good record for those who want the taste of pressed tobaccos without dealing with preparation, as well as those seeking a moderately flavoured blend.
gawith-hoggarth-co-bobs-square-cut.o: Leaves a sweet cocoa- and vanilla-dominant aroma, with a light trace of smoke and flowers behind it.

mac-baren-scotch-skaret-ready-rubbed-lim.z: Remembered as a ready-rubbed release said to have been produced in limited numbers; since no independent source documenting its contents could be found, the record is left incomplete.
mac-baren-scotch-skaret-ready-rubbed-lim.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

milan-tobacconists-sangria.z: Sangria, named after the Spanish fruit wine, is one of Milan Tobacconists' aromatic house blends. According to the maker's description, burley and Virginia leaves meet in balanced proportions, topped with a generous share of black cavendish; the aim is a light-bodied smoke leaving traces of spice and sweetness on the palate. Suitable for those avoiding heavily sugared aromatics and looking for a fruity, spicy direction instead. Its low nicotine load places it among the blends that can be smoked throughout the day.
milan-tobacconists-sangria.o: Leaves a sweetish aroma reminiscent of spiced fruit wine.

alfie-turmeaus-own-blend-whisky.z: One of Turmeaus tobacconist's house mixtures noted as whiskey-flavored; no accessible source documenting its content and character could be found.

peterson-summertime-2015.z: Summertime 2015 is a limited edition blend released as part of Peterson's Summertime series specific to that year; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient first-hand sources confirming its content and character could be found.

samuel-gawith-sweet-black-cavendish.z: Sweet Black Cavendish is a dark cavendish product obtained by pressing the leaf into a cake, heating it, and letting it ferment. The sweetness in the name comes both from the process concentrating the sugars and from a light added sweetening; still, it carries no pronounced fruit or vanilla aroma. Nicotine level is very low, the smoke cool and mild. Smoked alone its profile stays plain; its main function is to add volume and sweetness to another blend. In this respect it sits on the same shelf as Pure Black Cavendish, differing only in that the sweetness is a touch more forward. Suited to smokers wanting to soften a blend they find harsh, or building their own aromatic blend.
samuel-gawith-sweet-black-cavendish.o: Leaves a mild scent evoking sugar, light caramel, and baking.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-coronado-oriental.z: Coronado Oriental is a club blend Wilke Pipe Tobacco prepared specifically for the San Diego Pipe Club. The brand has kept up its tradition of producing private mixtures for shops and pipe clubs since its founding; this record is the Oriental-forward member of that line. Oriental leaves and Cyprian Latakia lead in the blend, joined by a small amount of unsugared, creamy black cavendish. The Oriental gives earth, wood, grass, and spice, while Latakia adds soot and a floral layer; the cavendish serves to soften the sharper edges. The flavor stays on a sweet-sour, floral, grassy, and smoky-fire line throughout. It burns cool and steady, needing an average number of relights. Body is a little above medium, making it accessible to both experienced smokers and those new to Latakia mixtures.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-coronado-oriental.o: Leaves a scent of campfire smoke reminiscent of dry spice herbs.

chieftain-lazy-day-mixture.z: No reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Chieftain blend Lazy Day Mixture, so the profile has been left incomplete.

nording-pointer.z: One of the aromatic members of the tobacco line released under the Nording name; not enough independent source material documenting its composition and top flavoring could be found.

pipesandcigars-com-thumbprint-cookie.z: Thumbprint Cookie appears among pipesandcigars.com's sweetly named monthly aromatic blends; no source could be found verifying its content and character, so no detailed specification is given.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-sweet-bur.z: Sweet Burley is The Country Squire's own take on the classic sweetened Burley type. The Burley leaf's nutty, earthy character is preserved while a light sweetness that doesn't weigh on the palate is added on top; vanilla and nutty notes come forward, with a cocoa-leaning taste reported in the background. The ribbon cut lights easily, burns fully, and leaves no dampness at the bottom of the bowl. Nicotine is low. It can be smoked on its own or used as a base or mellowing component in house blends; suited to those after lightly sweetened Burley and a mellow tobacco to smoke at any time of day.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-sweet-bur.o: Leaves a scent of roasted nuts and light vanilla.

vegassmokes-five-star-premium.z: A VegasSmokes blend described as a Virginia and Perique combination; no independent source documenting its composition has been found.

motzek-toms-white-twist.z: A light-colored twist tobacco from the Motzek workshop's Tom's Twists line; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

rattray-black-virginia.z: Black Virginia is a ribbon-cut blend based on Virginia leaf darkened by steam-treatment, in a color that is almost entirely black. The tin shows black and dark brown strands together; its scent isn't sharp but leans tart-sweet. Both nicotine and body stay on the light side, making it suitable for long, cool smokes. It suits smokers looking for a plain Cavendish sweetness without Latakia or spice, or newcomers to the pipe wanting to steer clear of heavy blends.
rattray-black-virginia.o: Leaves a lightly tart, sweet, dark tobacco aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-kentucky.z: This is one of the darkest ends of the shag-cut tradition Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. continues in Kendal. The blend rests on fire-cured Kentucky leaf; records indicate the brand also uses this leaf on its own in products such as Kendal Kentucky. It is unflavored, with the taste coming entirely from the smoky, woody, earthy character left by fire-curing. The fine shag cut eases packing, but since the burn can be fast, it needs to be smoked slowly. Nicotine sits at the upper limit. Aimed at smokers accustomed to working with dark, strong, unflavored tobaccos.
gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-kentucky.o: Leaves an aroma of heavy wood smoke and roasted hazelnut.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-royal-club.z: No independent source confirming the composition of the Royal Club blend registered under the Orlik name could be found; it should not be confused with the brand's similarly named Club Mixture blend.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-royal-club.o: No description could be found in the records.

d-r-tobacco-penhooker.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the D & R Tobacco brand as Penhooker; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-rum-pigtail.z: Sweet Rum Pigtail is the rum-topped version of pigtail Burma tobacco, produced by twisting fire-cured leaves into a fine rope. The producer sells these fine ropes suited to both chewing and pipe smoking; they're cut into small discs for use. Rum is pronounced in the pouch aroma. On the smoke, the initial sharpness gradually gives way to a sweet, spicy, creamy taste; underneath, the earthy core of the fire-curing remains. Being intense in nicotine, it calls for slow smoking. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. is one of the English producers that continues traditional twist (rope) production at its Kendal factory, hand-twisting fire-cured leaves into rope form. Because twist tobaccos don't go through a pressure-cooking stage, they stay intense in nicotine; records indicate these ropes are sold for both chewing and pipe smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-rum-pigtail.o: Leaves an aroma combining sweet rum and spicy tobacco scents.

g-l-pease-renaissance-reserve.z: Renaissance Reserve is among G. L. Pease's limited-production blends; records indicate only 500 tins were prepared. Cyprus and Syrian Latakia are used together, joined by Virginia leaves of varying maturity and Balkan Oriental leaf, and the mix is rested for months before boxing. The proportion of the two latakia types is set so the Cyprus leaf doesn't overpower the Syrian leaf; the Oriental component is pronounced, while the Virginia trio establishes balance through the depth of the matured leaf, the tartness of the red, and the background support of the golden leaf. It is not in production today. It is meaningful for smokers wanting to get to know the classic Balkan line containing Syrian Latakia and for those with a collector's interest.
g-l-pease-renaissance-reserve.o: A spicy, lightly sweet undertone accompanies a heavy incense and leather aroma.

chacom-5.z: Chacom #5 is the darkest blend in the line. Cyprus Latakia builds a smoky, woody, peat-like layer; Perique adds a spicy depth toward plum and raisin; Virginia carries a grassy sweetness and citrus tartness. Being an unflavored blend, the taste comes entirely from the combination of leaves and deepens as the bowl progresses. Nicotine and flavor intensity are high compared to the line's other blends. Suitable for experienced smokers accustomed to dark blends combining Latakia and Perique, seeking an evening smoke.
chacom-5.o: Leaves a smoke, burnt wood and peat room note.

tsuge-premium-pipe-tobacco-first-days-of.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Tsuge Premium Pipe Tobacco blend First Days of Spring has been found.

w-o-larsen-limited-edition-2020.z: This is one of W.Ø. Larsen's annual limited editions; no reliable source could be found regarding its composition and character.
w-o-larsen-limited-edition-2020.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-autumn-blend.z: Noted as one of the seasonal aromatics Boswell prepares in its Pennsylvania shop. Since no separate entry could be found in the manufacturer's current blend list, its composition and character could not be detailed.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-autumn-blend.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet, spicy aroma.

sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-original-aro.z: According to records, an aromatic product blending Argentine leaf from the Jujuy-Perico region with European-origin essences; no independent source stating the additives used and the character could be found.
sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-original-aro.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

peter-stokkebye-black-majesty-no-28.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Black Majesty (No.28) could be found.

smoke-king-britannia-mixture.z: One of the house blends the Leeds-based English tobacconist Smoke-King sells under its own name; since no independent source documenting its composition and character could be found, a detailed record could not be compiled.

larus-brother-company-inc-edgeworth-jr.z: Edgeworth Jr. was reportedly launched around 1936 by Larus & Brother Company. Its target audience was explicitly stated in its marketing: pipe smokers who were also accustomed to cigarettes. Accordingly, the blend was built as a Burley-forward, low-intensity structure calibrated to sit close to light cigarette taste. Body is light, smoke is dry and soft; rather than heavy flavoring, the leaf's own nutty taste comes forward. When the company's Richmond production ended in 1974, the line's smaller arms were also withdrawn from the market. Today it's a historical record found only in old tins, showing how the period's pipe market competed with cigarette habits.
larus-brother-company-inc-edgeworth-jr.o: Leaves a dry room note toward nuts and roasted grain, close to cigarette smoke.

park-lane-tobacconist-orient-express-sce.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Orient Express (Scene 2), one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

kaptn-brammers-blauer-peter.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for Kapt'n Brammers' Blauer Peter, so the profile is left incomplete.

motzek-motzek-8.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called Motzek #8 could be found.

w-o-larsen-selected-blend-no-32-curly-fl.z: This is one of W.O. Larsen's numbered selected blends; no reliable source could be found documenting its composition and character.

mcclelland-no-110-just-plain-nut.z: Remembered as a nut-noted, Virginia-and-Burley-based blend from McClelland's bulk line; no sufficient source describing its contents and character in detail could be found.

sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-original-esp.z: Referred to as a blend in Sentimiento Nacional's aromatic line; no sufficient independent source on its composition and character could be found.
sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-original-esp.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

house-of-windsor-country-doctor.z: Country Doctor is an example of an American-style English mixture. The bulk of the blend is made up of cube-cut Burley; yellow Virginias, smoky Latakia, and spicy-sweet Perique are added to it. Cube-cut Burley burns slowly and cool, Latakia gives a smoke layer, and Perique adds an accent in the direction of plum and spice. The result is a profile in between — neither a full-bodied English mixture nor a plain Burley blend. The product belonged to House of Windsor's classic over-the-counter line and ceased production when the company closed; match blends prepared by other makers exist today. It suits smokers looking for a classic American character, Burley-based with measured Latakia and Perique.
house-of-windsor-country-doctor.o: A spicy edge accompanies the light smoke and dry-walnut aroma.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-northwoods.z: Northwoods is Boswell's Latakia-based English blend. J. M. Boswell built the blend originally for his own smoking in the early 1980s and put it up for sale at customers' request. Per the manufacturer's description, toasted virginias join a soft, measured Latakia base; the cut is ribbon and it comes out of the tin at a moisture ready for smoking. The body is full, the flavor intense; yet the Latakia proportion does not turn the blend into a one-note smoke bomb. Smoking notes report traces recalling Virginia sweetness, cocoa and woody tastes underneath the smoky layer. Suitable for smokers wanting to get to know Latakia blends or seeking a balanced English blend.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-northwoods.o: Leaves a lightly sweet trace underneath a wood smoke and incense aroma.

park-lane-tobacconist-orient-express-sce.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Orient Express (Scene 1), one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-robo-burlesq.z: An aromatic small-batch blend in Ken Byron Ventures' Yoshimi's line; not enough sources could be found to document its composition and character.
ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-robo-burlesq.o: Could not be described due to lack of accessible records.

new-york-pipe-club-bedloes-island.z: A club blend prepared for the New York Pipe Club, named after the island where the Statue of Liberty stands; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

sillems-councilor-1695-flake.z: Councilor 1695 Flake sits on the Sillem's series' unflavored Virginia-perique wing and is produced at the Kohlhase & Kopp facilities in Germany. A flake obtained by pressing red and light-yellow Virginia leaves is joined by a proportion of perique that is high relative to the brand's other blends. The 1695 in the name references the Hamburg roots behind the Sillem's name. On the smoke, fig, raisin, and stone-fruit tones such as plum come forward; perique adds a peppery sharpness and a full, creamy texture to these.
