When dried sufficiently, a light coconut-like sweetness can also be detected. Nicotine is in the medium range. Suited to smokers accustomed to unflavored Virginia-perique flakes who take the time to rub and air the tobacco.
sillems-councilor-1695-flake.o: Leaves a lightly peppery scent mixed with dried fig and plum sweetness.

cornell-diehl-xx-flake.z: XX Flake is one of two commemorative blends Cornell & Diehl prepared in 2020 for Smokingpipes.com's twentieth anniversary; the two X's in the name refer to the number twenty. Its composition includes light-colored Virginia leaf alongside two separate Oriental tobacco varieties and eighteen-year-aged Perique. After pressing and cutting, the mixture is tinned as broken flake. Its profile is described with spice and citrus notes coming forward, with the Oriental tobaccos layered over a Virginia-Perique skeleton. Its pressed structure and high Virginia proportion make the blend well suited to aging. Being released in limited quantity, it isn't in continuous production.
cornell-diehl-xx-flake.o: Leaves a scent of breadlike sweetness, dry spice, and a light citrus peel.

petersen-sorensen-tradition.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Petersen & Sorensen-branded Tradition blend could be found.

elephant-castle-deerstalker.z: No sufficient independent sourcing could be reached to document the composition and character of Deerstalker, a pipe tobacco from Elephant & Castle.

lane-limited-royal.z: Not enough independent sources could be found documenting the contents and character of American blender Lane Limited's blend called Royal.

cornell-diehl-captain-bobs-blend.z: Captain Bob's Blend carries the name of Cornell & Diehl's customer and friend, Captain Bob Coffey. A small amount of Latakia and perique are added to a Virginia-and-burley base, topped with a grape-like flavoring. This structure places the blend somewhere between the classic American-English mold and the aromatic mold. The flavoring adds a fruity layer without entirely masking the natural leaf tastes; Latakia and perique provide smoke and spice in the background. It suits smokers curious about the intersection of flavored and Latakia blends, open to unusual fruit notes.
cornell-diehl-captain-bobs-blend.o: Leaves a lightly smoky aroma in the room mixed with grape-like fruity sweetness.

pipe-republic-folkestone.z: No reliable sources on Pipe Republic's blend Folkestone could be found, so its content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

davis-and-son-tobacconists-port-of-call.z: Port of Call is one of the bulk-sold house blends of Davis & Son Tobacconists in Wilmington, North Carolina. The shop presents its house blends under a separate heading in its own list. The blend consists of golden virginia soaked in plenty of rum and honey, along with mountain burley, and is ribbon cut. Virginia gives the blend a sugary base, burley a dry body and medium nicotine; because the topping is applied heavily, both taste and room scent are pronounced. It suits smokers seeking sweet, boozy notes while also wanting to taste the tobacco's body.
davis-and-son-tobacconists-port-of-call.o: Leaves a warm scent evoking honey sweetness and cane rum.

ken-byron-ventures-turkey-dressing.z: Turkey & Dressing is a limited-release blend from Ken Byron Ventures classified as an aromatic; no reliable source could be found to document its contents or casing.
ken-byron-ventures-turkey-dressing.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

dobies-four-square-original-mixture.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of Four Square Original Mixture, a blend from Dobie's.

upshall-upshall-aromatic.z: The Upshall name comes from the James Upshall pipe workshop founded by Barry Jones and Ken Barnes in Suffolk; no source describing the composition of this aromatic tobacco sold under the same name has been found.

dunhill-my-mixture-october-89.z: A record left over from Dunhill's custom blending program, not currently in production; no independent source describing its composition could be found, so a detailed record couldn't be compiled.
dunhill-my-mixture-october-89.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

peter-heinrichs-chateau-henri-no-8.z: Chateau Henri No. 8 is a classic English mixture in which dark red Virginia leaves from North Carolina's Salem region are combined with red Kentucky and Turkish tobaccos, rounded out with some Latakia. The maker describes the blend by its smoky taste; because the proportion of dark leaf is high, it is a heavy structure in both color and body. The Virginia and Kentucky base gives sweetness and fullness together, while the Oriental leaves add dry spice and Latakia adds a smoke layer. Nicotine and flavor intensity sit above medium. It suits smokers accustomed to full-bodied mixtures containing Latakia who are seeking a substantial blend for the end of the day.
peter-heinrichs-chateau-henri-no-8.o: Leaves an intense aroma of smoke and cured wood.

pfeifen-huber-jubilaumstabak-huber.z: This is one of the anniversary blends Pfeifen Huber has released to mark its founding anniversaries; no sufficient sources establishing which year it belongs to or its composition could be found.

bennington-tobacconist-no-28-royal-dutch.z: No. 28 Royal Dutch is the Cavendish-centered blend among Bennington Tobacconist's shop blends. Three separate imported, mellow Cavendishes are brought together; the mixture is aged for several years in wooden casks and prepared in a Cavendish cut. Time in the cask mellows the leaves and takes off any sharpness; the result is a low-nicotine tobacco with a pronounced sweet side that lights easily. The maker highlights that the blend stays lit, meaning it doesn't often need relighting. It suits smokers looking for mellow, Dutch-style Cavendish mixtures who avoid heavy Latakia or high nicotine; it's not demanding for pipe beginners either.
bennington-tobacconist-no-28-royal-dutch.o: Leaves a sweet room note of lightly toasted sugar and dried fruit.

bbb-scottish-mixture.z: A Scottish-style mixture sold under the BBB name; no reliable source describing its content could be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-clan-full.z: Referred to as an aromatic version in the Clan series; no sufficient source documenting the blend's content and character could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-clan-full.o: No detailed description of the room note could be found in the records.

ken-byron-ventures-verg21.z: Ken Byron Ventures' Verg21 is reported to be Virginia- and Perique-forward; no independent source could be found to document its contents.
ken-byron-ventures-verg21.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

straus-tobacco-kentucky-gentleman.z: One of the house blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; no verifiable source describing its composition could be found.

comoys-of-london-english-mixture.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Comoy's of London blend English Mixture.

thepiperoom-com-full-mast.z: No independent source confirming the composition of ThePipeRoom.com's Virginia-forward blend Full Mast has been found; the brand's own site is no longer online.
thepiperoom-com-full-mast.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

cornell-diehl-warped-saint-espresso-2023.z: Saint Espresso is a Cavendish project Warped and Cornell & Diehl release as a seasonal limited run. The blend brings together three separate Cavendish types: C&D's own Carolina Red Virginia Cavendish, black Cavendish made from Kentucky leaf, and Cavendish prepared from Dominican cigar leaf. The leaf is steamed and toasted; the aim is a dark flavor evoking espresso without adding a heavy external flavoring. Ribbon cut. On the flavor side, bitter chocolate, cream, and roasted-walnut tones come forward; sweetness comes mainly from the leaf's own sugars, giving a more tobacco-forward profile than classic heavily sauced aromatics. Nicotine load is medium. Appeals to those looking for something between an aromatic and a straight tobacco, suited to smoking alongside coffee. The 2023 release is that year's batch of this recipe.
cornell-diehl-warped-saint-espresso-2023.o: Leaves a dark, warm scent reminiscent of roasted coffee beans and bitter chocolate.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-lipc-long-island-soun.z: LIPC Long Island Sound is one of the club blends Wilke Pipe Tobacco produced for the Long Island Pipe Club. An example of the brand's tradition of preparing private mixtures for clubs and shops, this record is built on cube-cut white Burley. The cube-cut Burley defines the blend's character, giving nut, earth, wood, a dry tartness, and occasional traces of spice. Since the cube cut lets the leaf burn slowly and cool, the flavor stays steady throughout the bowl. There's no casing; sweetness comes only from the leaf itself. It suits smokers seeking a plain, dry, nutty American Burley character who don't want aromatic or smoky layers.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-lipc-long-island-soun.o: Leaves a plain scent reminiscent of roasted nuts and dry earth.

peretti-scottish-flake.z: A blend attributed to L. J. Peretti's shop in Boston; no published source could be found to confirm its composition and character.

peter-stokkebye-amsterdam-no-83.z: PS83 Amsterdam is a blend in Peter Stokkebye's bulk line that combines sweet, citrus-leaning Virginias with fire-cured Kentucky leaf. The ribbon cut makes packing easy, and the tobacco comes relatively dry from the maker, keeping the burn even. A floral, forest-fruit-leaning flavoring applied on top gives the blend an aromatic shell. The resulting profile layers dark-fired Kentucky's smoky, earthy side over Virginia's sugar, so sweetness and smokiness are perceived at the same time. The body is medium. It suits smokers transitioning from aromatic blends toward natural leaf character or seeking a smoky sweetness.
peter-stokkebye-amsterdam-no-83.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity aroma mixed into a smoky wood scent.

cornell-diehl-jolly-old-saint-nicholas-2.z: No adequate firsthand source on the composition of this blend, the 2018 release of Cornell & Diehl's annual year-end series, could be found.

cornell-diehl-cavicchi.z: One of Cornell & Diehl's aromatic blends; it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog, and not enough sourcing could be found to describe its composition.

tabaqueria-xian-elemental.z: A house blend from Tabaquería Xian listed as an aromatic; no accessible source describing its composition could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-13.z: Wilke No. 13, in the maker's own description, is one of the shop's most recognized numbered recipes, known by the nickname "Wilke's Magic 13." The mixture contains Tennessee Burley, Latakia, Perique, and Virginia along with Wilke's own Royal Scot blend. The Royal Scot addition gives the blend a light sweetness and roundness, while Latakia smoke and Perique spice build the framework. It's aimed at smokers seeking multi-component classic American-English blends at medium strength.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-13.o: A light sweet, spicy trace accompanies the smoky wood scent.

olaf-poulsson-no-88-black-flake.z: No. 88 Black Flake is the flake member of the Olaf Poulsson line, prepared in Danish style by German manufacturer Dan Tobacco (DTM). It's one of the rarer black-cavendish-based broken flakes on the market. The leaf undergoes extended hot fermentation, a process that softens the body and darkens its color. It's offered in a fifty-gram pouch and a large two-hundred-fifty-gram package. The measured topping applied runs toward vanilla and forest fruit, though per the maker's recipe the leaf's own natural impression stays dominant. Thanks to the flake structure and moisture from fermentation, it burns very slowly and coolly; it's light in nicotine. It suits those seeking a mellow, sweet, long smoke, and those wanting to get used to packing flake.
olaf-poulsson-no-88-black-flake.o: Leaves a lightly caramelized scent at the sweetness of vanilla and dark forest fruit.

cornell-diehl-sugarplum.z: No listing documenting the composition of Sugarplum, a Cornell & Diehl blend, could be found in the maker's current catalogue or reliable retailer pages.

comptons-of-galashiels-reserve-21.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Compton's of Galashiels blend Reserve #21.

wessex-gold-slice.z: Gold Slice is a blend built solely from light-colored Virginia leaves, pressed and then cut into flake. It belongs to the plain-Virginia wing of the Wessex series and carries no flavoring casing. Since light Virginia's natural sugars concentrate during pressing, the smoke rests on hay, dry grass, and a lemony sweetness. It stays smooth when smoked slowly, though it can produce sharpness on the tongue if rushed. It suits smokers accustomed to rubbing out flakes before packing who want to trace unflavored Virginia taste.
wessex-gold-slice.o: Leaves a sweetish scent leaning toward dry grass and baked bread.

sutliff-tobacco-company-pipe-force-episo.z: The fifth episode of Pipe Force is among the series' most unusual blends: stoved Rustica, Katerini Oriental cavendish, and stoved Virginia are pressed into a thick crumble cake. Nicotiana rustica carries far higher nicotine than the customary Nicotiana tabacum. The rustica gives a barbecue-style smoky tang and floral spice, the stoved Virginia gives caramelized sweetness, and the Katerini provides a grassy, woody background. Because the nicotine load is high, it is aimed at experienced smokers used to full-bodied smoking; the cake is rubbed out by hand for use. It is a limited production.
sutliff-tobacco-company-pipe-force-episo.o: Leaves a scent of barbecue smoke, floral spice, and burnt sugar.

tobacco-land-joes-mix.z: Joe's Mix is recorded as an aromatic house blend from the tobacconist Tobacco Land; no verifiable source has been found for its maker, composition, or character.
tobacco-land-joes-mix.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

milan-tobacconists-kings-ransom.z: King's Ransom is Milan Tobacconists' traditional English-style house blend. Two separate virginia types and select burleys are combined with oriental tobaccos, topped with a generous proportion of latakia and a very small amount of perique. Its unflavored construction gives a medium-to-full body. Latakia's smoky character sits at the blend's center; nutty tones appear in the background, with a spicy sweetness from the perique showing at the finish. Geared toward smokers accustomed to unflavored latakia blends who are looking for an everyday English mixture with a pronounced body.
milan-tobacconists-kings-ransom.o: Leaves a smoky-wood and campfire aroma in the room.

d-r-tobacco-rowland-regular-blend.z: Rowland Regular Blend is an American-style mixture from North Carolina-based Daughters & Ryan (D & R Tobacco). It's built from nutty, earthy Burley, sweet Virginia, and spice-giving Oriental leaf, topped with a light, not-heavy cocoa-leaning flavoring. Being ribbon cut, it packs and lights easily and burns evenly. Body sits between mild and medium; its low nicotine load keeps it suited to all-day smoking. A fitting choice for those wanting blends where tobacco flavor leads and casing plays only a rounding role, as well as smokers looking to move from aromatics toward natural American mixtures. The Rowland family also includes lighter-bodied Gold and Silver versions alongside Regular.
d-r-tobacco-rowland-regular-blend.o: Leaves a scent where dry-leaf warmth mingles with a light cocoa sweetness.

gawith-hoggarth-co-aniseed-twist.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Aniseed Twist blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

planta-bank-of-england-happy-hour.z: The Happy Hour mixture in the Bank of England line is one of Planta's unflavored English-style products. Latakia and a small amount of Oriental and Java tobacco are added to Virginia leaf ranging from light to medium brown; no flavoring is used. The cut is a loose ribbon. Its character rests on a measured smoke and spice sitting atop a sweetish Virginia base; strength falls in the medium-to-above-medium range. It suits smokers familiar with classic Latakia-based English mixtures. Planta's Berlin production ended in 2019, with the brands passing to Danish Mac Baren; this mixture reportedly does not appear in the current catalogue.
planta-bank-of-england-happy-hour.o: Leaves a smoky, pine-tar-like aroma reminiscent of wood fire.

leavitt-peirce-cake-box.z: Cake Box is the house blend of the Leavitt & Peirce shop, operating in Harvard Square since 1883. It takes its name from how it was prepared in its founding years: the mixture was reportedly made at home in a large cake tin by one of the shop owners' wives. In the shop's own promotion, the blend is described as the mixture generations of Harvard students turned to for years. It's a classic American-type mixture sold in bulk over the shop counter; the base leaves carry a measured casing, and body is medium. Of interest to those curious about the palate of university-town shop blends, and to those seeking a balanced bulk tobacco for everyday smoking. Available only at the shop and through its own sales channel.
leavitt-peirce-cake-box.o: Leaves a sweet, warm room note reminiscent of freshly baked cake batter.

georges-smoke-shop-georges-blend.z: The house blend carrying the name of George's Smoke Shop, founded in 1986, is reportedly an aromatic mixture created by the shop's original owner; no published detail on its leaf composition and toppings could be found.
georges-smoke-shop-georges-blend.o: No record of the room aroma could be found.

peter-stokkebye-mango-no-44.z: This is one of Peter Stokkebye's numbered flavored series blends; no sufficient first-hand sources documenting its content and character could be found.
peter-stokkebye-mango-no-44.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

jack-schwartz-importer-blend-120.z: This is one of the numbered house blends from the Chicago tobacconist Jack Schwartz Importer; no reliable source describing its content could be found.

tinder-box-black-russian.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Tinder Box pipe tobacco called Black Russian to record the blend's composition and character.

e-a-carey-europa.z: Europa is E. A. Carey's pressed cavendish-based aromatic. Per the maker's description, the blend's own natural taste is light, and a fine wild-berry-like topping is added on top; after pressing, the tobacco carries an unassuming sweet profile. It offers a very light smoke that doesn't harshen the tongue, and its nicotine load is low. It suits newcomers to the pipe and those seeking a mildly fruity aromatic. In the Carey catalog it's mentioned alongside Black Raspberry for its similar fruit direction.
e-a-carey-europa.o: Leaves a light wild-berry and sweet tobacco scent.

cornell-diehl-granulated-perique.z: Granulated Perique is not a blend but a single-component tobacco: crumbled pure perique leaf, native to Louisiana's St. James Parish, fermented under pressure in barrels. Cornell & Diehl ties this product to the tradition begun by Pierre Chenet in 1824, and offers it in granulated form for easy mixing when building blends. It is not designed to be smoked on its own; its nicotine and flavor intensity are very high. It is used in small proportions by smokers building their own blends or wanting to add spice and fruit depth to a Virginia blend they already have.
cornell-diehl-granulated-perique.o: Leaves a sharp pepper and ripe plum aroma together.

friedman-pease-kismet.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Friedman & Pease's Kismet blend.

elephant-castle-the-stout.z: No sufficient independent sourcing could be reached to document the composition and character of The Stout, a pipe tobacco from Elephant & Castle.

chonowitsch-t-12.z: T 12 is a blend combining top-grade Virginia leaf with steam-cured black cavendish, with a small amount of Oriental leaf worked in between. It is built on the contrast between light and dark leaf; the smoke stays light and carries a sweetish air characteristic of Danish tradition. The blend series consists of small-batch productions that leading Danish pipe maker Jess Chonowitsch had prepared to accompany his own pipes. According to available records, each batch is blended and rested in small quantities. It suits those looking for a light-bodied Danish mixture whose sweetness comes from leaf processing rather than a sauce.
chonowitsch-t-12.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly caramel-like aroma coming from the steam-processed cavendish.

peterson-special-reserve-2005.z: This is the 2005 edition of Peterson's annual limited Special Reserve series; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient sources giving that year's composition and topping information could be found.
peterson-special-reserve-2005.o: Leaves the sweet aroma typical of aromatic blends.

mac-baren-rum-maple.z: Rum & Maple is one of the old names in American aromatic tradition, now produced by Sutliff within Mac Baren. The body of the ribbon-cut blend is built by nutty, earthy Burley; bright Virginia leaves are added to give it clarity. The two flavorings the name comes from, maple syrup and rum, are applied as a topping over the leaves. The smoke is mild and cool, with nicotine load kept low. In taste, the flavoring's sweetness stands out more than the leaf character; maple is the main axis, with rum as a sharp accent behind it. The gap between the tin note and the smoked taste is what's expected of aromatics. Suited to those seeking a light aromatic smokable at any hour and to beginners wanting a blend that lights easily.
mac-baren-rum-maple.o: Leaves a sweet trace with burnt sugar and maple syrup aroma.

john-middleton-inc-gold-and-mild-nutty-v.z: John Middleton's vanilla-and-nut-themed aromatic blend; no verifiable information on its profile could be found.
john-middleton-inc-gold-and-mild-nutty-v.o: No verifiable information on its room note could be found.

ole-shenandoah-single-cask.z: Single Cask is one of the aromatic blends in the Ole Shenandoah line working the barrel theme; no published source describing its composition could be found.

d-r-tobacco-raccoons-delight.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the D & R Tobacco brand as Raccoon's Delight; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

mcclelland-no-705-walnut-liqueur.z: No. 705 Walnut Liqueur was a Virginia blend in McClelland's light aromatic bulk line. Per the maker's description, the blend's backbone is built from lemon- and orange-toned Carolina Virginia leaves along with differently processed Virginia types, joined by a small amount of high-quality Brazilian leaf. The flavoring applied over it, evoking walnut and brandy, is a non-masking layer that sits atop the tobacco's Virginia sweetness rather than covering it. The blend was aimed at smokers seeking a light aromatic that preserves Virginia character rather than heavily syrupy aromatics. It's described as a low-nicotine, low-bite record smokable all day. Since McClelland Tobacco Company halted production entirely in 2018, the blend is no longer produced; only old stock circulates on the market.
mcclelland-no-705-walnut-liqueur.o: Leaves a lightly alcoholic sweetness reminiscent of toasted walnut and brandy.

d-r-tobacco-blenders-bench-katerini.z: Katerini is an Oriental tobacco grown in the region of the same name in Greece, coming from Samsun seed stock; Daughters & Ryan sells this leaf on its own in the Blenders Bench line. It's counted among the most sought-after Oriental varieties. Its flavor structure carries a light honey sweetness, floral tones, and a subtle sharpness that shifts between sweet and bitter. Nicotine is low, aromatic intensity high. A component leaf for blenders wanting to add Oriental character to Latakia-heavy or Virginia-heavy mixtures.
d-r-tobacco-blenders-bench-katerini.o: Leaves a scent of honey, dried flowers, and grass.

torben-dansk-no-2-oriental-mixture.z: Torben Dansk No.2 Oriental Mixture is noted as an Oriental-forward mixture in the brand's numbered series; no sufficient independent source describing its composition has been found.
torben-dansk-no-2-oriental-mixture.o: Records describe it as leaving a dry-spice and grassy aroma.

blenders-gold-rich-vanilla.z: Rich Vanilla is a vanilla-coated aromatic blend combining imported and domestic leaf cut in a long Cavendish style. It's produced by Sutliff and sits among the Blender's Gold line's large-tin, everyday aromatics. The vanilla coating is the blend's most prominent feature; the tobacco's own flavor takes a back seat to that sweetness. The blend has a high humectant content, so it comes out of the tin quite wet and needs airing before packing; if it isn't dried enough it tends to gurgle and bite the tongue. Nicotine is low. It suits those looking for a heavily vanilla-flavored, mild, inexpensive everyday aromatic. According to records the brand has changed hands, and the product may have been distributed under different names.
blenders-gold-rich-vanilla.o: Leaves a sweet room note of heavy vanilla reminiscent of sugared pastry.

mac-baren-dark-twist-roll-cake.z: Dark Twist is a roll cake made using the old-fashioned twisting technique. Selected Virginia tobaccos and Mac Baren's signature cavendish are placed inside whole Virginia leaves and twisted together; the resulting rope is sliced into rounds and packed by hand. The dark-colored rounds are crumbled before filling and give a rich, sweetish taste; the cavendish sweetness in the blend balances the tanginess of the Virginia. It sits above medium in nicotine and flavor, so it should be smoked at a slow pace.
mac-baren-dark-twist-roll-cake.o: Leaves a dark, rum-like room note with a hint of sweet dried fruit.

ashton-type-2.z: Ashton Type 2 is referred to as an English blend in the brand's numbered series; no adequate independent source verifying its content and character could be found.
ashton-type-2.o: According to records, not enough information could be found to describe it.

missouri-meerschaum-luminaire.z: Luminaire is an unflavored blend built from red virginia, cavendish, Katerini oriental, and St. James perique, pressed into flake form. It is produced by Cornell & Diehl for Missouri Meerschaum, and takes its name from the illumination that came when Anton Tibbe installed the first electric power plant in the town of Washington on New Year's Day 1892. The flakes rub out easily and can be smoked at the moisture level they come in from the tin. The taste profile is described in terms of woody and leathery tones, light spice, and dark fruit; the tangy sharpness from the perique balances the virginia sweetness. Aimed at those interested in unflavored virginia-perique blends.
missouri-meerschaum-luminaire.o: Leaves a subtle aroma evoking dry hay, tangy fruit, and leather.

super-value-cherry-cavendish.z: Super Value Cherry Cavendish is a ribbon-cut aromatic combining burley with cavendish leaf, topped with a heavy cherry note. Per the maker's description, the palate side is kept soft, with the emphasis placed on scent; as a result, the taste in the mouth stays behind the tin and room note. The blend sits in the inexpensive bulk wing of classic fruity shop aromatics. Suited to those seeking a tobacco that foregrounds cherry scent, has low nicotine fullness, and is technically undemanding; not suitable for those expecting leaf character to stand out.

cornell-diehl-byzantium.z: Byzantium is a distinct take Cornell & Diehl brings to the classic Balkan mixture. What sets it apart from the usual Balkan structure is that the blend contains no Virginia at all; as a result, Oriental leaf comes to the fore, and Latakia, lacking a sweet foundation, comes through more starkly. The components are limited to Cyprus Latakia, Oriental leaves, and perique. The Oriental's dry, incense-and-spice-leaning character forms the blend's backbone; Latakia brings smoke and resin, while perique adds depth and a plummy sharpness. With no source of sugar present, the smoke settles into a mineral, dry direction rather than a sweet one. Nicotine sits between medium and hearty, while flavor intensity is high. It suits those wanting to trace the Latakia-Oriental relationship without a Virginia veil.
cornell-diehl-byzantium.o: Leaves a heavy wood-smoke aroma together with incense and dry spice.

cornell-diehl-mocha.z: Mocha is Cornell & Diehl's ribbon-cut aromatic blend built entirely on a black cavendish base. The flavoring is described as an even split between espresso and bittersweet chocolate; these two notes form the blend's flavor axis, with the tobacco's own character staying in the background. Thanks to the black cavendish base, the smoke is mild and nicotine strength is low. It suits smokers on the aromatic side looking for a coffee-and-chocolate pairing, wanting a light-bodied tobacco with high flavor intensity. As is common with cavendish-heavy blends, moisture content can run high, and slow smoking is key to avoiding tongue bite. Cornell & Diehl produces it in small batches at its facility in North Carolina, USA.
cornell-diehl-mocha.o: Leaves the aroma of freshly brewed espresso and bittersweet chocolate.

mab-stiavnicky-flake.z: Stiavnicky Flake is a pressed tobacco from Slovak manufacturer MAB, named after the mining town of Banská Štiavnica. It's prepared by combining air-cured burley with dark fire-cured Kentucky leaf in a balanced ratio, then presented in flake form. It's reportedly modeled on Peterson Irish Flake and is referred to by Slovak retailers as the local counterpart to that blend. It's an unflavored, full-bodied tobacco. It gives an earthy, nutty, woody and smoky taste, with measured sweetness and floral, lightly spicy notes in the background. Like any pressed tobacco, it takes a bit of time to light, but once it catches it burns slowly and coolly. It's heavy in nicotine, making it a blend for experienced smokers.
mab-stiavnicky-flake.o: Leaves a room note of dry wood smoke and charred walnut.

g-smith-sons-special-latakia-flake.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of G. Smith & Sons' pipe tobacco Special Latakia Flake could be found.

motzek-plug-no-5.z: A Virginia-forward plug from the Motzek workshop's numbered pressed-tobacco line; sufficient independent sources for detailed composition information could not be found.

rivertown-tobacco-works-dark-70.z: Dark 70% is an aromatic bulk blend from Rivertown Tobacco Works, made entirely of black Cavendish leaf. The ribbon-cut leaf is flavored with a casing built around dark cocoa and milk chocolate, carrying a light vanilla behind it; the maker's stated aim is balance, keeping the sweetness from going overboard while holding onto cocoa's faintly bitter edge. The Cavendish base itself gives a bready, woody, sugary ground, so the leaf taste doesn't disappear entirely under the casing. Nicotine is low and flavor intensity medium; it is a cool, slow-burning smoke suited to long sessions. It is designed for smokers who like chocolatey-sweet aromatics and want a mellow blend they can smoke any time of day, as well as tobacconists building their own mixtures. The brand was founded in the US to offer bulk blends at an affordable, consistent price.
rivertown-tobacco-works-dark-70.o: Leaves a fine vanilla aroma over roasted cocoa and milk chocolate.

e-a-carey-vintage-black-aromatic.z: Vintage Black Aromatic is the dark blend in E. A. Carey's black cavendish line. Per the maker's description, two distinct toasted black cavendish aromatics are processed for longer than usual to achieve a deep, dark taste; the blend follows in the footsteps of Classic Black Aromatic, which introduced the brand in the 1970s. The tobacco is produced in Denmark. The nicotine load is light to medium and the flavor body runs dark and sweet. It's a record for those who enjoy heavily sugared aromatics and seek a dark cavendish character, and it appears on the brand's current list.
e-a-carey-vintage-black-aromatic.o: Leaves a dark scent dominated by sweet, burnt-sugar notes.

low-country-pipe-cigar-black.z: One of the house blends of South Carolina-based Low Country Pipe & Cigar; described as Virginia-and-latakia-forward, but not enough sources could be found to describe its character.

w-o-larsen-avalon-mixture.z: Avalon Mixture is a W.Ø. Larsen blend named after the legendary island King Arthur is said to have withdrawn to after being wounded. Its structure is simple: a small amount of black cavendish is added to Virginia leaves, and the mixture is flavored with a red-wine casing. The blend's defining feature is its low strength; it carries no spicy or sharp side and stays light in nicotine. The wine flavoring brings a fruity sweetness but isn't intense enough to mask Virginia's own taste, so the natural leaf notes can be traced throughout the smoke. The ribbon cut makes lighting and burning easy. This is a profile aimed at newcomers to aromatics and smokers seeking a light, all-day-smokable blend that doesn't bite the tongue.
w-o-larsen-avalon-mixture.o: Leaves a fruity, lightly tart scent reminiscent of a wine cask.

bentley-virginia-honey-dew.z: Virginia Honey Dew is an aromatic blend in the Bentley line. Gold and red Virginia leaf is combined with black Cavendish's lightly spiced sweetness; the blend is flavored with bourbon vanilla and honey. Its relatively fine cut is pack-friendly, and the tin's moisture level is smoke-ready. Honey and vanilla tones dominate throughout the smoke; further into the bowl, Virginia's tangy fruit taste becomes more apparent. It burns evenly, leaves little condensation, and, per the maker, is less heat-sensitive than most aromatics. It suits smokers starting out with sweet aromatics as well as those who prefer light blends.
bentley-virginia-honey-dew.o: Fills the room with a sweet honey-and-vanilla note.

newminster-no-17-english-luxus.z: No. 17 English Luxus is Newminster's take on the classic English mixture. Its composition includes African hot-air-cured virginia leaf, black cavendish, Mexican burley, and Cyprus latakia. It is a medium-thick ribbon-cut blend with no top flavoring; latakia's smoky tone runs alongside the sweetness rounded out by the cavendish, and it burns relatively slowly. Produced at Mac Baren's facilities in Denmark, the Newminster line is known for its affordably priced bulk tobaccos, distributed in the US market through Sutliff and Villiger. No. 17 is a good option for smokers just moving into latakia blends or looking for a straightforward English blend for daily smoking.
newminster-no-17-english-luxus.o: Leaves an aroma of smoky wood and toasted leaf in the room.

peter-stokkebye-bulwark-flake.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Bulwark Flake in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

tabaqueria-xian-campos-de-flandes.z: One of Tabaquería Xian's Cavendish-based house blends; no accessible source documenting its content could be found.

j-f-germain-son-germains-brown-flake.z: Brown Flake belongs to the traditional flake line of J. F. Germain & Son, which has produced tobacco on the island of Jersey since 1820. It's a pressed tobacco built on the sweetness of dark Virginia leaves, carrying a light Burley spiciness and a woody depth; sources mention a subtle caramel note. The slices are pressed to a firmness that rubs out easily. With its medium body and low flavoring level, it can be smoked over long periods throughout the day. Because the pressed Virginia character deepens over time, it's considered suitable for tin aging. It's one of the starting points for smokers wanting to get acquainted with the classic, unflavored English flake style.
j-f-germain-son-germains-brown-flake.o: Leaves a woody, lightly caramel aroma along with dried-fruit sweetness.

peter-stokkebye-dansk-passion.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Dansk Passion in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

pipesandcigars-com-chocolate-covered-esp.z: No independent source material could be found sufficient to fill out a specification for the pipesandcigars.com blend called Chocolate Covered Espresso Bean.

g-l-pease-childhoods-end.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Childhood's End.

lane-limited-holiday-excursion.z: Holiday Excursion is an American-style blend registered under Lane Limited; not enough sources could be found to describe its content and character.
lane-limited-holiday-excursion.o: Reportedly leaves a sweet, spicy room note.

lane-limited-hs-3.z: One of Lane Limited's bulk ribbon-cut aromatic blends, part of the code-named Lane series. Since no independent source could be found for its leaf composition and casing, the related fields have been left blank.

cornell-diehl-star-of-the-east.z: Star of the East is a full-bodied English mixture built on Cyprus Latakia, which makes up half the blend. Latakia is joined generously by Turkish leaf; sweetness comes from stoved red Virginia, added so the colors darken and the flavor deepens. It's one of the blends Cornell & Diehl has kept in its catalogue for many years. Despite the high Latakia proportion, the maker's description notes it burns cool and offers a deep flavor layer. Turkish leaf's resinous spice and Virginia's dark sweetness balance the smoky base. Prepared for smokers accustomed to heavy smoky blends; the room note is strong and clings to fabric.
cornell-diehl-star-of-the-east.o: Leaves an intense, lingering smoke reminiscent of wood fire and tarred rope.

ohm-mint.z: OHM Mint is the menthol-flavored member of the OHM line, produced in the United States. Like the other OHM blends, it is built from American-grown Virginia and Burley leaf and prepared as a ribbon cut; the difference is the mint-menthol casing applied to the leaf. The line also includes a milder menthol option. In the smoke, menthol's cooling effect stands out and partly masks the tobacco's own taste. The smoke leaves a cold sensation in the mouth, and the room note is pronounced. Suitable for those accustomed to menthol products and for those wanting a cooling smoke in hot weather.
ohm-mint.o: Leaves a cooling mint and menthol aroma.

peter-stokkebye-black-coffee.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Black Coffee could be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-lincoln-a.z: The cavendish-based aromatic version of the Lincoln brand in Scandinavian Tobacco Group's portfolio; no independent source describing the blend's composition could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-lincoln-a.o: No detailed description of the room note could be found in the records.

friedman-pease-fools-cap.z: This is the first blend Friedman & Pease introduced in 1998 and is considered the brand's flagship; due to the company's short life it went out of production, and no reliable source describing its composition could be found.

super-value-ultra-mild.z: Super Value Ultra Mild is a burley-and-cavendish mixture presented as the line's mildest member. Heavy aromatic top flavorings are avoided; only a light sweet top note is applied. With its low nicotine strength and straightforward flavor profile, it functions as an unassuming everyday blend that can be smoked over long stretches.
super-value-ultra-mild.o: Leaves a lightly sugared scent of dry hay and nutty leaf.

faders-turkish-knights.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for the Fader's brand's Turkish Knights pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

bentley-la-dolce-vita-the-planters-sweet.z: An aromatic blend from the German Bentley brand, sold under two different names in different markets; no reliable source verifying its composition and flavoring could be found.
bentley-la-dolce-vita-the-planters-sweet.o: No recorded recipe could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-dulce-de-leche-d.z: D58 Dulce de Leche is a ribbon-cut aromatic made from burley and Virginia leaves. The sauce is caramel-heavy with vanilla tones underneath. The dry-leaning cut recalls traditional American shop blends; it lights easily and burns evenly. Body is light and flavor is soft. Suited to those seeking a low-nicotine, all-day aromatic in the caramel line.
sutliff-tobacco-company-dulce-de-leche-d.o: Leaves a scent of caramelized sugar and light vanilla.

b-b-tobacconists-tribute.z: A small-scale tobacconist's blend; no independent source describing its content could be found, leaving the profile blank.

lane-limited-four-monks.z: Not enough independent sources could be found documenting the contents and character of American blender Lane Limited's blend called Four Monks.

peterson-nightcap.z: Nightcap is a classic English blend carried over from the Dunhill era and today continued under the Peterson name. A generous amount of Cyprus Latakia and Oriental leaf sit atop a Virginia base, with a small proportion of Perique added. It is a ribbon cut; under a smoky, earthy main body there is a creamy sweetness from the Virginia and a peppery sharpness from the Perique. As its name suggests, it is designed for the last pipe of the day: a blend heavy in nicotine that lingers long on the palate. It suits smokers accustomed to heavy Latakia and seeking depth in English blends; it is heavy going for new smokers starting out with aromatic tobacco. The room note is pronounced and needs care indoors.
peterson-nightcap.o: Leaves a heavy, smoky wood aroma recalling a campfire that clings to fabric and curtains.

mac-baren-capstan-original-navy-cut.z: Capstan Original Navy Cut is an unflavored flake made by pressing and slicing mature Virginia leaves selected from various regions; records indicate a small amount of dark leaf is also present in the blend. It's the darker, fuller-bodied counterpart to the Gold version. It's effortless to pack and light, offering a cool, long smoke. Flavor intensity dips at times, but it retains the classic Virginia flake structure; a product designed for those seeking pure Virginia taste in daily smoking.
mac-baren-capstan-original-navy-cut.o: Leaves a dry-hay and lightly woody tobacco room note.

golden-harvest-natural.z: Golden Harvest Natural is the unflavored version of the same series. US-grown Virginia and Burley leaf are finely cut and blended, with no flavoring or topping used in the product. It is sold in six-ounce pouches and one-pound bags. The taste rests on the leaf's own character: Burley's dry, bready, nutty base mixes with Virginia's light sweetness. Being unflavored, the room note is also plain and stays close to the tobacco's natural aroma. Suited to smokers wanting to steer clear of flavored blends and looking for an economical, simple American mixture for all-day smoking.
golden-harvest-natural.o: The burning leaf's own aroma, in tones of dry hay and bread crust.

republic-tobacco-co-4aces-mellow-gold.z: 4Aces Mellow is the mild member of Republic Tobacco's economy line, sold in large-volume bags. It is a shag-cut American blend built from Burley and Virginia leaf; compared to the red-labeled Regular, its body and nicotine are kept noticeably lower. The profile is plain and straightforward; no strong flavoring comes through, with Virginia's light sweetness working alongside Burley's nutty dryness. It suits smokers looking for an uncomplicated, cheap, all-day tobacco. It is produced in the US by Illinois-based Republic Tobacco and distributed in resealable bags.
republic-tobacco-co-4aces-mellow-gold.o: Leaves a dry hay and lightly nutty aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-ts1r-red-virgini.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Sutliff Tobacco Company's TS1R Red Virginia Ribbon pipe tobacco could be found.

park-lane-tobacconist-london-fog.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of London Fog, one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

paul-olsen-no-907.z: One of the aromatic blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

milan-tobacconists-buddys-blend.z: Buddy's Blend is a light aromatic among Milan Tobacconists' house blends. It takes its name from the shop owners' Labrador dog. Select virginia leaves are combined with cavendish; according to the maker's description this gives a soft, lightly sweet taste, hints in the direction of chocolate and coffee, and a nutty finish. Since ribbon cut is used instead of flake, it packs easily and gives a cool burn that doesn't bite the tongue. Being light in nicotine, it forms an entry suited both to those new to the pipe and to experienced smokers looking for a soft everyday aromatic.
milan-tobacconists-buddys-blend.o: Leaves a sweetish, nutty aroma in the direction of cocoa and fresh coffee.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-kentucky.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Kentucky blend.

peterson-summertime-2011.z: Summertime 2011 is a limited edition blend released as part of Peterson's Summertime series specific to that year; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient first-hand sources confirming its content and character could be found.

rattray-winter-edition-2015.z: Winter Edition 2015 is a one-year edition in Rattray's winter series, prepared in Kohlhase & Kopp's Danish-style aromatic approach. The blend combines various Virginia leaf with black Cavendish, with Burley added to fill out the body. Compared to the previous year's caramel-almond profile, it has a darker fruit side: cherry and fruitcake notes come forward. Nicotine stays low, making it suitable for long sessions. It suits smokers looking for a sweet, bakery-like winter aromatic; being a limited edition, it is no longer in current production.
rattray-winter-edition-2015.o: Leaves a cherry fruitcake and spiced-pastry aroma.

consolidated-burley-black.z: No verifiable sourcing could be found for this blend sold under the Consolidated name, so its content and character cannot be described.

wellauer-co-irish-whiskey.z: Irish Whiskey is a ready-rubbed blend from Swiss maker Wellauer, tied to the Irish tradition. According to retailer records, the base is selected Virginia leaf, joined by fire-cured Kentucky and leaves mostly described as "Indian cured" and Thai Burley. A casing evoking Irish whiskey is applied on top. Virginia gives natural sugar and a light toast taste, while Kentucky brings a core-like depth and a roasted tone; Burley completes the body and nutty dryness. As a result, the blend is fuller and more structured than pure Virginias. The whiskey casing sits as a dry, warm frame rather than a cake-like sweetness. The ready-rubbed cut makes packing easy, and the burn stays even on a slow draw. It suits those seeking a medium-bodied blend with casing that doesn't lose the tobacco taste.
wellauer-co-irish-whiskey.o: Leaves a warm, sweetish whiskey scent settling over toasted tobacco.

edwards-sebring.z: No sufficient independent sourcing could be reached to document the composition and character of Sebring, a pipe tobacco from Edward's.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-blend-no-1.z: Not enough manufacturer or retailer record information could be reached about Kohlhase & Kopp's blend called Blend No.1.

foggy-fox-owls-haunted-hollow.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Foggy Fox's Owl's Haunted Hollow blend.

pcca-equinox.z: Equinox is one of the limited club tins PCCA (the Pipe Collectors Club of America) had McClelland produce in the 1980s and 1990s. The blend's defining component is Syrian latakia, joined by Virginia and oriental leaf. Broken flake pieces appear among the coarse, short-cut leaf, and the color ranges from dark brown to black. From the first draw, latakia and oriental leaf come forward, giving an intense taste dominated by smoke and wood char. Syrian latakia leaves a drier, spicier, less sweet smoke than Cyprian latakia, so the blend speaks to smokers accustomed to heavy Latakia mixtures. With the Syrian latakia supply having dried up and McClelland's 2018 closure, the blend has passed entirely into history.
pcca-equinox.o: A heavy scent of smoke, leather, and dry grass fills the room.

peter-stokkebye-natural-no-1.z: Natural is one of Stokkebye's most straightforward Cavendish-based records. Sweet Virginias and soft Burley leaf are layered, given a very light alcohol-based top flavoring, and after pressing and slicing, fully opened out into a loose cut. The result is a light aromatic in which the flavoring is hard to notice, one that lets the tobacco's own taste come forward. Its body is low; a grassy sweetness from the Virginia and golden Cavendish runs alongside honey and citrus associations. It suits smokers seeking a straightforward blend for all-day smoking and those wanting to move from aromatics toward unflavored tobacco. Some sources indicate the product has been discontinued.
peter-stokkebye-natural-no-1.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, grassy tobacco aroma.

erik-stokkebye-night-slice.z: No reliable source could be found for the Night Slice blend registered under the Erik Stokkebye name.
erik-stokkebye-night-slice.o: Could not be described due to lack of sourcing.

sutliff-tobacco-company-cherry-cavendish.z: 12 Cherry Cavendish is a classic American aromatic built by adding soft burley and bright Virginia alongside cavendish-processed leaves, topped with a cherry-liqueur-direction flavoring. It's ribbon cut and sold in bulk. It's a blend with low nicotine, limited tongue bite, and measured flavor intensity; the defining element is the cherry topping. An entry-level mixture for smokers who enjoy fruity aromatics and for those new to the pipe.

paul-olsen-heimdal.z: A blend from the My Own Blend line that originated at the Paul Olsen shop in Copenhagen; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

g-l-pease-elf-weed.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Elf Weed.

cornell-diehl-trinidad.z: No listing documenting the composition of Trinidad, a Cornell & Diehl blend, could be found in the maker's current catalogue or reliable retailer pages.

cornell-diehl-warped-kings-stride.z: Kings Stride is a blend built jointly by Warped founder Kyle Gellis and Cornell & Diehl head blender Jeremy Reeves, introduced at the end of 2019 alongside Cloud Hopper. Its composition combines Louisiana Perique with five-year-aged Burley and Virginia leaf, rounded out by a special black Cavendish made by pressing and steaming cigar leaf. The mixture is pressed and presented as a crumble cake, which the smoker breaks apart to whatever fineness they prefer. It's an unflavored blend, and its profile is described as reaching toward dark fruit and chocolate. Perique's spice, the earthy texture of aged Burley, and the leathery note of cigar leaf sit together. Aimed at smokers wanting a full, complex smoke without Latakia, comfortable working with cake-form tobaccos.
cornell-diehl-warped-kings-stride.o: Leaves an intense trace of dark fruit and cocoa, smelling of leather and earth.

david-cigarpipe-midnight-in-persepolis.z: No adequate sources were found documenting the composition or character of the David CigarPipe Midnight in Persepolis blend.

motzek-dark-side-alpha.z: Since neither the manufacturer's own description nor two independent reliable sources could be found for the Motzek blend called Dark Side Alpha, its composition, cut, and character could not be documented here.

briarworks-international-petes-beards-bl.z: Pete's Beard's Blend is the ribbon-cut blend in BriarWorks's English-mixture line. It is made by pairing light Virginias with smoky Latakia and is offered in a two-ounce glass jar. Since the Latakia share is not kept heavy, the smoke gives a measured woody layer instead of dense smokiness; the Virginias form a lightly sweet base underneath. The body is medium, flavor medium-to-full; a balance suited for smoking throughout the day is the aim. A blend aimed at those who don't want the intensity of heavily Latakia-laden mixtures but still want to preserve an English character.
briarworks-international-petes-beards-bl.o: Leaves a fine aroma combining light wood smoke with dry-hay sweetness.

king-smoking-pipes-and-cigars-king-of-ci.z: A blend sold by the American retailer King Smoking Pipes and Cigars under its own name, understood from its name to be cigar-leaf based; no verifiable source could be found for its content and character.
king-smoking-pipes-and-cigars-king-of-ci.o: Reportedly close to the woody, sharp tobacco note left by cigar-leaf-forward blends.

ministry-of-food-industry-of-rsfsr-kapit.z: Kapitanskiy, whose name means "belonging to the captain" in Russian, is a pipe tobacco produced during the Soviet era at factories under the RSFSR Ministry of the Food Industry; records indicate Leningrad's Tobacco Factory No. 2 was among its main producers, and the brand lasted from at least the 1950s into the 1990s. The Soviet pipe-tobacco tradition doesn't use Latakia; instead it relies on Oriental leaves grown domestically and around the Caucasus and Crimea, along with Virginia-Oriental blends. Kapitanskiy is noted as following this line, a mixture lightly sweetened with rum essence. It is not in production today; tins circulating on the market are old stock in collectors' hands. With its dry, dusty Oriental character and measured rum casing, it draws the interest of those looking for a historical palate different from Western English mixtures. Standard codes on the packaging indicate some tins were printed between 1974 and 1983.
ministry-of-food-industry-of-rsfsr-kapit.o: Leaves a light rum and floral aroma sitting over the dry Oriental leaf.

grants-tobacconist-custom-blend-no-9131.z: One of Grant's Tobacconist's numbered custom blends; there is no independent sourcing on its composition.

hu-tobacco-cervantes.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Cervantes, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

cornell-diehl-consolation.z: Consolation is an English blend built on Latakia, Oriental leaves, and bright Virginia. Per the manufacturer's description, black cavendish and cube-cut burley are also part of the composition; these two leaves soften the finish, leaving a lightly sweet tail. It is packaged as a ribbon cut. Because smoke, woody taste, and light sweetness sit in balanced proportion, the blend traces a more measured English profile than the heavy Latakia bombs. It suits those looking for a medium-strength blend that works for daytime smoking as well as evening pipes, and newcomers to the English family.
cornell-diehl-consolation.o: Leaves a smoky, woody, campfire-like aroma with the Latakia.

e-a-carey-soft-aromatic-mixture.z: An aromatic blend registered under the E. A. Carey name; it does not appear on the maker's current list, and not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition.

mclintock-orange-dream.z: Orange Dream is one of the very light-bodied aromatics in the McLintock line. A sweet, deep, lightly tart orange flavoring is applied over a black Cavendish and Virginia base. The ribbon cut gives the blend a structure that packs and lights easily. The low nicotine load and the prominence of the citrus flavoring make this blend suitable for those new to the pipe or looking for a light smoke during the day. It is produced at Kohlhase & Kopp's facilities in Germany.
mclintock-orange-dream.o: Leaves an aroma of orange peel and candied citrus.

cornell-diehl-old-grove.z: Old Grove is Cornell & Diehl's ribbon-cut aromatic blend. Bright and red Virginia, dark burley, Katerini Turkish leaf, black cavendish, and granulated perique come together, topped with a light pomegranate flavoring. Because the flavoring level is kept low, the leaves' own herbal and sweet notes remain distinguishable within the smoke. It takes its name from the Old Grove area of New Orleans, known for its moss-draped old oaks. It suits those avoiding heavy aromatics and looking for a lightly flavored blend that keeps its tobacco character intact. According to the maker, it ages well over long periods, with a peak maturation window given as ten to fifteen years.
cornell-diehl-old-grove.o: A dry-grass and hay aroma layers over the pomegranate sweetness.

planta-farmer-tabak.z: Farmer Tabak is an unflavored mixture that has long been part of Planta's catalogue. It consists of a balanced combination of US-origin Virginia leaf and Kentucky-Burley tobaccos; its taste is full and spicy. Its fibers are thicker and longer than other pipe tobaccos, and its cut is broad. Because of this broad cut, it is used not only in pipes but also for roll-your-own cigarettes. Nicotine is pronounced, making it suited to smokers used to full-bodied, unflavored tobacco. It is sold in 50- and 160-gram tins; after the brand's Berlin production ended, production continued under Mac Baren.
planta-farmer-tabak.o: Leaves a lightly woody tobacco aroma along with dry hay and nuts.

schurch-zaffiro-129.z: No sufficient source describing the content of this English-style mixture, which carries one of the gemstone names given to Schürch blends, could be found.

clan-shaw-southern-nights.z: No reliable, independent sourcing could be found regarding Clan Shaw Southern Nights, so a detailed profile could not be compiled.

dunhill-standard-mixture-mild.z: A record referred to as the light rung of the Dunhill Standard Mixture family, not currently in production; no independent source verifying its component ratios could be found, so a detailed record couldn't be compiled.
dunhill-standard-mixture-mild.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

schurch-mogano-146.z: One of the Swiss Schürch blends; the distinguishing trait noted for Mogano is Havana-origin cigar leaf, but no sufficient source giving the blend's full composition and cut could be found.

sillems-mayor-1814-flake.z: Mayor 1814 Flake is the Sillem's series' entry on the straight-Virginia wing, produced by Kohlhase & Kopp. Selected mature Virginia leaves are pressed for a long time to form a flake; the tin holds thin slices stuck to one another. On the smoke, the citrusy, herbal sweetness of light Virginia leads; a fine honey-and-orange-like casing rounds off this base, though the blend stays measured enough not to be called aromatic. Smoked slowly and cool, it gives a balanced, full flavor; nicotine is in the medium range. Suited to those interested in straight Virginia flakes and accustomed to rubbing and airing tobacco.
sillems-mayor-1814-flake.o: Leaves a baked-bread scent mixed with honey and orange peel.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-railroad-station.z: Railroad Station is the mixture among Boswell's English blends where Latakia is clearly dominant. The manufacturer's description characterizes the blend as Latakia-forward, full in flavor and cool-burning. Because of its unflavored structure and high Latakia proportion, it offers a smoky, sooty profile; aimed more at smokers accustomed to the traditional English style than at aromatic fans. Its room aroma is pronounced, so its smoking is noticeable indoors.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-railroad-station.o: Leaves a heavy smoke, tar and campfire aroma.

mac-baren-brigg-regular.z: Brigg Regular is the most measured-casing member of the Brigg line; like the rest of the series, it was first prepared in Germany by Planta and, following the brand's change of hands, by Mac Baren in Denmark. In the blend, light Virginia leaf is combined with cavendish, with a small amount of burley added for balance; a fine Jamaican rum note is applied on top. The taste largely comes from the natural tobacco; the rum casing stays in the background and complements Virginia's sweetness. Its body is medium; the ribbon cut lights easily and burns evenly. Suited to smokers seeking a lightly sweetened everyday blend where tobacco character leads, rather than strong fruit flavors.
mac-baren-brigg-regular.o: Leaves a warm tobacco note with a fine rum scent.

brebbia-balkan-mixture-no-10.z: Balkan, in Brebbia's numbered mixture series, is a Latakia-forward blend prepared under the Italian pipe manufacturer's name; per records it was manufactured at the German DTM workshop. Its composition keeps Latakia at a high proportion, with a small amount of kentucky and perique added to increase body and strength. Because the Virginia share is kept low, instead of the familiar sweet base, salty, smoky tones and the tart notes brought by the Oriental leaf come forward. The body is between medium and full. Suitable for experienced smokers who want Latakia in its unsoftened form and seek smoke and spice over sweetness.
brebbia-balkan-mixture-no-10.o: Leaves a sharp aroma reminiscent of wood-fire smoke, tar and salty sea air.

lane-limited-hazelnut.z: Hazelnut is one of Lane Limited's bulk ribbon-cut aromatics. Virginia and burley leaf are combined with toasted cavendish, with a hazelnut-direction casing applied on top. Nicotine is low, taste is soft and one-directional; the casing carries the same line throughout the bowl. A blend for those seeking a nut-toned, light and cool aromatic.
lane-limited-hazelnut.o: Leaves a roasted-hazelnut and sweet-pastry room note.

paul-olsen-sirius.z: A Paul Olsen blend records show was available, alongside Kong Frederik and Dannebrog, up until 2006; no independent source describing its composition could be found.

my-smoking-shop-golden-honey.z: Golden Honey is an American-style bulk blend prepared by topping a cavendish-forward body with a honey sauce. It is sold under the Century name in the UK and is also known as Golden H following the 2017 naming change. Its ribbon cut and high moisture give a cool burn. It has a light-to-medium strength, low nicotine, and a pronounced sweet taste; the honey note leads the smoke. Suited to smokers who like sweet, single-note aromatics and want a soft smoke that won't bite the tongue.
my-smoking-shop-golden-honey.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of warmed honey and candle wax.

wessex-classic-virginia.z: Brigade Classic Virginia is a blend combining dark red pressed Virginia leaf with Louisiana Perique. Although only Virginia appears in the name, since it contains Perique it belongs to the Virginia/Perique family. It's offered as broken flake, at a moisture level ready to pack without further rubbing out. Its taste is rounded rather than sharp or grassy; Perique's spicy, lightly fruity tone layers over Virginia's bready sweetness. Since nicotine stays in the mild-to-medium band, it's considered suitable for all-day smoking. This is a record for those seeking a Virginia blend with Perique used in moderation.
wessex-classic-virginia.o: Leaves a sweetish, dry-grass and lightly peppery warm tobacco scent.

john-middleton-inc-kentucky-club-mild.z: A lighter version of the Kentucky Club line; not enough sources could be found on its contents, cut, and character.
john-middleton-inc-kentucky-club-mild.o: Leaves a light, dry tobacco aroma.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-spiced-turk.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Spiced Turk blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

g-l-pease-stonehenge-flake.z: Stonehenge Flake is a Virginia-Perique flake G. L. Pease developed in 2001 together with John Gawith of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. The blend uses bright flue-cured and sun-cured leaves of Brazilian, Zimbabwean, and Malawian origin; some burley is added for body and flavour intensity, and genuine St. James Parish perique is added for spiced topping. The blended leaf is steamed and compressed into blocks under hot press and left to mature; the matured blocks are cut into thin flakes and separated into pieces about five centimetres long. It first launched in a limited number of tins and was later put into regular production. It is aimed at smokers seeking the ripe, lightly tart sweetness of pressed Virginia blends; records note production was subsequently discontinued.
g-l-pease-stonehenge-flake.o: Leaves a tartish, sweet dry-grass and fermented-fruit aroma.

buckhorn-smooth.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Smooth under the Buckhorn brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

robert-mcconnell-turkish-izmir.z: Turkish Izmir is an Oriental tobacco from Robert McConnell's blending-tobacco line. Reports indicate the product is built on small-leaf Turkish tobacco sourced from Izmir and Samsun. These leaves are sun-cured, a process that gives the tobacco an intense, dry aroma and a lightly tart, spicy character. Smoked alone it offers a medium-mild nicotine experience with an intense flavor. Its main use is in blending: added to Virginia-heavy mixtures it reduces the tendency to bite the tongue and brings a creamy sweetness with a spicy top note. It also serves as a bridge in Latakia-based English and Balkan-style mixtures. The brand is Belfast in origin; production today is carried out in Germany.
robert-mcconnell-turkish-izmir.o: Leaves a dry, spicy aroma reminiscent of sun-dried grass and incense.

hu-tobacco-kelvins-silent-secret.z: Kelvin's Silent Secret is a medium-strength, lightly flavored blend from HU Tobacco. A small amount of dark-fired Kentucky and black Cavendish is added to a base built from different Virginia grades; a measured flavoring is applied on top. The idea behind the blend is to achieve a structure where the flavoring doesn't dominate and all components work together; the Virginia character is preserved as a result. It holds an in-between position for smokers avoiding the intensity of flavored blends but not wanting a fully unflavored tobacco either. The blend takes its name from a young pipe maker met at the 2010 Lohmar pipe show.
hu-tobacco-kelvins-silent-secret.o: A faint candy-like thread mixes into a sweet, lightly smoky tobacco aroma.

house-of-windsor-classic-cavendish-t411.z: Records indicate this is a bulk aromatic in which a vanilla flavoring is applied over Cavendish obtained by steam-processing Green River Burley leaf until black; no sufficient source verifying the details could be found.

tabakfabrik-roth-jabuca-vanilla.z: Also known as Jabuca Vanille, this blend is the vanilla aromatic in Tabakfabrik Roth's Jabuca series. According to the maker, specially fermented Virginia leaf is rounded out with some black Cavendish and sweetened with a light Danish-style vanilla casing, so the tobacco's own taste is preserved while a vanilla note settles into the finish. It is filled at a medium cut (about 3.5 mm) and offered in a resealable freshness pouch. It suits smokers looking for a vanilla aromatic who don't want the essence to overpower the tobacco; with its light body, it's also a mixture new pipe smokers can approach.
tabakfabrik-roth-jabuca-vanilla.o: Leaves a scent of sweet vanilla and baked pastry.

peterson-irish-flake.z: Irish Flake is an unflavored blend prepared by pressing and slicing Kentucky, Burley, and Virginia leaf. The slices come out of the tin at a smokable moisture level; they can be packed folded without breaking them apart, or rubbed out. When rubbed out and loosely packed, it tends to burn fast. Nicotine strength is very high and the flavor is intense from the first draws. Virginia's light sweetness stays underneath the bitter, dark body of Kentucky and Burley; as the smoke progresses a bright, fresh taste comes forward. It suits smokers accustomed to strong tobaccos who are willing to put effort into preparation and lighting; it is heavy going for beginners.
peterson-irish-flake.o: Fills the room with an intense, sharp, woody, burnt-tobacco aroma.

fincks-cigar-company-fincks-whiskey.z: As its name suggests, this is a whisky-topped, burley-heavy shop aromatic from Finck Cigar Company; no reliable source describing its composition and character could be found.

holger-danske-golden-harmony.z: Golden Harmony is a renamed version, with an updated recipe, of the product previously known as "Mango and Vanilla." While the old version contained only Virginia and Burley, black Cavendish and Turkish (Oriental) tobacco have been added to the new blend. The structure is still Virginia-forward; Burley and Turkish tobacco remain in trace amounts. The cut is ribbon, the flavoring is built on mango and vanilla, and toward the end of the smoke a toasted-Cavendish tone becomes pronounced. The Holger Danske name is tied to Danish aromatic tradition; it's recorded that this product is produced in Germany under Danish license and sold with tax stamps. It's noted that it has no retail distribution in Turkey. Flavor intensity is moderate, and strength stays between light and medium; it suits aromatic-blend smokers looking for a fruit-vanilla pairing.
holger-danske-golden-harmony.o: Leaves an aroma of ripe mango and vanilla, with a lightly toasted Cavendish tone lingering behind it.

cornell-diehl-mixture-monster-iv-rise-of.z: Mixture Monster is Cornell & Diehl's seasonal aromatic series released each year for Halloween, and MMIV: Rise of the Mixture Monster is the fourth entry in that line. Where earlier years used four separate tin artworks, this release settles on a single label design. The blend is built on black and light cavendish, joined by Virginia and burley, all cut as ribbon. On the palate, caramel, apple, and chocolate notes take the lead, giving an autumn-themed, distinctly flavored aromatic profile. Nicotine strength is moderate, making it suitable for extended sessions. It is designed for smokers who enjoy aromatic blends and are looking for a sweet, confectionery-leaning profile; it is a limited seasonal release.
cornell-diehl-mixture-monster-iv-rise-of.o: Leaves a sweet aroma of caramel, baked apple, and cocoa.

peterson-holiday-season-2019.z: This is the 2019 edition of Peterson's Christmas series, produced only for that season; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient sources specifying that year's flavoring and leaf mix could be found.
peterson-holiday-season-2019.o: Leaves the sweet, spicy aroma typical of aromatic Christmas mixtures.

james-fox-anniversary-mixture.z: Anniversary Mixture is a house blend James J. Fox tobacconist, founded in Dublin in 1881, prepared for its founding anniversary. It's part of the 50-gram tin series the Grafton Street shop sells under its own name, and is described as a ready-rubbed mixture combining Virginia and Oriental leaf. According to the maker's description, what sets the blend apart is a mango note layered over the leaf base — giving the classic Virginia-Oriental skeleton a lightly fruity coating. Body is kept medium. Since it contains no Latakia, it suits smokers who aren't after the smoky character of English blends but want more leaf taste than a plain aromatic offers.
james-fox-anniversary-mixture.o: Leaves a ripe tropical-fruit sweetness together with a dry-hay aroma.

cornell-diehl-crooner.z: Crooner is an American classic pairing cube-cut burley with deertongue herb. Per Cornell & Diehl, the blend is a reconstruction of a private mixture prepared for singer Bing Crosby; the recipe comes from Bob Runowski, who blended for Crosby. The cube-cut burley burns slowly, giving a nutty, dry body; deertongue adds a sweetish aroma and flavor layer somewhere between vanilla and hay. It suits smokers who love nearly-unflavored, single-axis burley blends and are curious about the classic American style.
cornell-diehl-crooner.o: Leaves a sweetish, hay-like room aroma reminiscent of dry grass and coumarin.

peter-stokkebye-proper-english-no-52.z: Proper English is described as the brand's highest-Latakia blend. It is built up with a generous amount of Cyprus Latakia, Old Belt bright Virginias, and Oriental leaf. The cut is fine ribbon; color ranges from light brown to black. On the palate, Latakia's smoky, woody, earthy side leads, Orientals add a dry, grassy, lightly tart seasoning, and Virginia carries sweetness at the base. The smoke is dense and creamy; the body sits between medium and full. It suits smokers who enjoy classic English blends and want a pronounced smokiness.
peter-stokkebye-proper-english-no-52.o: Fills the room with an intense aroma recalling smoke, burnt wood, and a campfire.

koltoma-tets.z: One of the cigar-leaf-based blends from Russian manufacturer Koltoma; no verifiable content information from the manufacturer or a retailer could be found.

cornell-diehl-orient-express.z: Orient Express is a layered mixture named after the historic train line that ran between Istanbul and Paris. Per Cornell & Diehl's listing, Virginia, Latakia, Oriental leaves, Perique, and black Cavendish are used together. While the Oriental leaves' grassy-tart line and Latakia's smoke stay up front, black Cavendish adds a rounding sweetness and Perique a measured spice. The ribbon cut lights easily and burns evenly. With nicotine in the medium band, it's well suited to long smokes. Designed for smokers who like an Oriental-heavy Balkan line and want Latakia within a mixture rather than on its own.
cornell-diehl-orient-express.o: Leaves an incense-like smoky scent with a lightly sweetish layer.

sillems-linea-epoque-antique.z: Linea Epoque Antique is part of the Sillem's brand's aromatic line built in the Danish style and produced in Germany by Kohlhase & Kopp. Its body is built from black cavendish and light Virginia leaf; the cut is loose and fluffy, allowing for a short airing burn when needed. The flavoring is built on vanilla, mirabelle plum, and cappuccino; a citrusy undertone balances the sweetness. Nicotine is light, the smoke stays cool, and the room note is noticeable. Suited to smokers who enjoy creamy-sweet aromatics centered on coffee and vanilla.
sillems-linea-epoque-antique.o: Leaves a scent of vanilla latte and ripe yellow plum.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-mick-mcqu.z: Mick McQuaid Ready Rubbed is the pre-rubbed form of the same-named Irish-origin pressed Virginia blend. Since it removes the step of rubbing the plug slice by hand, it is ready for direct packing. The leaf composition and character match the plug format: pressed Virginia's deepened sugar, a sour-fruit direction, and a pronounced body. It is not light on nicotine. Suited to smokers who want the pressed-Virginia taste without bothering with preparation steps.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-mick-mcqu.o: Leaves a dark, sourish, lightly smoky tobacco scent.

vauen-auenland-the-shire.z: Auenland is an aromatic blend the German maker Vauen, founded in 1848, positions alongside its churchwarden pipe series of the same name; the name comes from the German rendering of the Shire from J. R. R. Tolkien's works. The ribbon-cut blend contains Virginia, black Cavendish and Burley leaf, cased with a fruity casing toward peach and orange. Nicotine is notably light and the body of flavor is moderate; the blend's center of gravity is the fruit casing. Since it arrives with high moisture from the tin, airing it out briefly before packing helps regulate the burn. A fitting profile for smokers after a low-strength, distinctly fruity European-style aromatic.
vauen-auenland-the-shire.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity aroma reminiscent of peach and orange peel.

svendborg-mild-mixture.z: A product listed as one of the Svendborg brand's mild-profile mixtures; no independent source describing the blend's content and character could be found.

samuel-gawith-cob-plug.z: Cob Plug is the pressed plug form of Samuel Gawith's 1792 Flake blend. It is listed in catalogs in the dark-leaf family under plug cut; thin slices are cut from the plug and rubbed for packing. Because of the plug presentation, moisture is preserved longer and the flavor is described as more intense than the flake form. A perfumed scent from tonka bean sits alongside the fire-cured leaf's smoky character; nicotine level is high. Suited to smokers accustomed to cutting plug and to strong tobaccos.
samuel-gawith-cob-plug.o: Leaves a perfumed sweetness from tonka bean together with a smoky tobacco scent.

borkum-riff-bourbon-whiskey.z: Borkum Riff Bourbon Whiskey is a ribbon-cut aromatic blend built mainly on Virginia and black Cavendish with some Burley, named for its Kentucky bourbon topping. According to sources, the mix uses Virginias of Brazilian and African origin along with black Cavendish sourced from Africa, Europe, and the Philippines. The blend of light and dark leaf gives a moderate whiskey impression on opening the pack; in the smoke the topping stays in the background, following a flat course alongside Virginia sweetness. Borkum Riff launched in Sweden in 1962, taking its name from a lighthouse in the North Sea; the blends, originally produced for Swedish Match, are now prepared in Denmark under Scandinavian Tobacco Group. This blend was added in the early 1960s with the American palate in mind. Its low moisture means it can be packed straight from the pouch; its light nicotine and mild smoke suit smokers in their early pipe years as well as those seeking a simple all-day aromatic.
borkum-riff-bourbon-whiskey.o: Leaves a sweet room note with hints of oak and whiskey.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-mixed-shag-aro.z: Kendal Mixed is the second of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s shag-cut main bodies. Unlike Kendal Gold's pure-Virginia structure, this body is built by adding Malawi-origin dark leaf and some fire-cured Kentucky to golden Virginia; because of this, its color is more mottled and its taste more earthy. This is the aromatic version under the series' general name; a Lakeland-style floral flavoring is applied to the Kendal Mixed body. Body is medium-full, and the smoke is cool and easy; since the fine cut burns fast, it calls for a slow draw. Suited to those seeking an introduction to Lakeland aromatics.

gbd-mariner-flake.z: Mariner Flake, tinned under the GBD brand, is, according to records, an old English flake tobacco that has been out of production for a long time; there is not enough independent sourcing documenting the blend's composition.
gbd-mariner-flake.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

edwards-buccaneer.z: This is one of Edward's Pipe & Tobacco's in-house aromatic blends prepared in the shop; not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition and character.
edwards-buccaneer.o: Could not be described due to insufficient records.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-coconut.z: Kendal Gold is the umbrella name for the shag-cut tobacco family Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. produces in the town of Kendal in England's Lake District. The family's body is built from Brazilian- and Indian-origin, heat-cured light Virginia leaf; largely stripped of stem, it's cut into fine golden strands. The producer steams and softens the tobacco, cuts it, toasts it on a hot cylinder, and then applies the top flavoring — so the family's members are versions of the same body offered with different scents. Entry No. 9 in the series (CCN) carries a coconut flavoring over the Virginia body.
