The use of perique sets this tobacco apart from ordinary sweet aromatics: beneath the sweetness lies a tart layer close to black plum and fig. It is light to medium in nicotine, burning cool all the way to the bottom of the bowl. It suits those who love an aromatic smoke but want more than plain sugar taste, and those wanting to sample perique in a low dose.
east-india-trading-co-cellar-reserve.o: Leaves a sweet trace carrying rum, vanilla and dried fig and plum scents together.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-wynne.z: A Danish-style aromatic in Kohlhase & Kopp's Caribbean Blue series; no verifiable source could be found detailing the blend's contents and casing profile.

burlington-on-whyte-tobacconist-festival.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named Festival 2017 under the Burlington on Whyte Tobacconist brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

peter-stokkebye-luxury-bullseye-flake-no.z: Luxury Bullseye Flake is made by spicing ripe Virginias with Louisiana Perique, pressing them into thin layers, and then wrapping them tightly around a pressed black Cavendish rod. When cut into medallion rounds, a dark core appears in the center surrounded by light-colored blend, which is where the name comes from. According to brand records, it replaced Luxury Curly Cut in the line in 2006. On the palate, Virginia's natural sweetness is balanced by Perique's nose-tickling peppery sharpness, while the Cavendish at the center smooths the transitions. The body is medium and the flavor full; it burns evenly and packs easily. It suits smokers who enjoy working with rolled cuts and are seeking an unflavored Virginia-Perique taste.
peter-stokkebye-luxury-bullseye-flake-no.o: A bready sweet tobacco aroma is mixed with a light peppery trace from the Perique.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-faulkner-.z: Faulkner Flake is The Country Squire tobacconist's unflavored flake blend, named for Mississippi author William Faulkner. It is made from natural Virginia, burley, and Oriental leaf, aged and then cut into soft, crumbly flakes. The Virginia lends the blend grassy notes and light sugary sweetness, the burley gives a nutty, earthy body, and the Oriental adds dry spice and an incense-like tone. With no casing, the flavor comes entirely from the balance of the leaves. The soft cut makes the flake easy to rub out for packing. It suits those interested in Latakia-free natural blends who are used to smoking flake.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-faulkner-.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay, bread, and lightly spiced leaf.

uhles-blend-114.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend Blend 114 has been found.

peter-stokkebye-virginia-q.z: This is a blend known under the Peter Stokkebye name; no sufficient first-hand sources documenting its content and character could be found.
peter-stokkebye-virginia-q.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

larus-brother-company-inc-edgeworth-cave.z: Recorded as the gold-labeled Cavendish aromatic of the Edgeworth line; no reliable source could be found describing the blend's contents.

rattray-wallace-flake.z: Wallace Flake is a flake blend made by pressing Virginia leaf ranging in color from golden to chocolate-brown together with sun-cured leaf of Indian origin. After pressing, the slices can be easily rubbed out for packing; it burns slow and cool. A very light plum casing is applied, kept light enough not to overwhelm the blend's natural tobacco character. Its taste combines Virginia's sweet, faintly tangy structure with the dark leaf's nutty fullness; nicotine is medium. Reports indicate the blend continues under a new name after the production rights to Rattray's previously released University Flake changed hands. It suits smokers used to flake cuts and medium-bodied Virginia character who want an unflavored or very lightly flavored blend.
rattray-wallace-flake.o: Leaves a tobacco-forward aroma carrying dry hay and dark plum sweetness.

drew-estate-meat-pie.z: Meat Pie is Drew Estate's English-style, latakia-heavy blend. It contains Cyprus latakia, Virginia leaf from America's Old Belt district, and oriental tobaccos. As the name suggests, the blend's character brings out baking spices, hickory smoke and a meaty, smoked tone; latakia takes the lead role in this picture while Virginia provides a measured sweetness in the background. Though the body stays light to medium, the flavor intensity is pronounced; the smoke finishes with a creamy, roasted close. It's a blend for latakia lovers, particularly those wanting to taste the smoky character without it going overboard. Per records, production was limited to 2013, and the blend was later withdrawn from the market.
drew-estate-meat-pie.o: Leaves a smoky, spicy scent evoking wood fire and smoked meat.

gawith-hoggarth-co-bobs-chocolate-plug.z: Bob's Chocolate Plug is the pressed plug form of the same house's Bob's Chocolate Flake blend. The body is built from Virginia leaves sourced from Brazil, Zimbabwe, and Malawi, with a small proportion of Latakia and Malawi burley added. A cocoa bowl note and a measured touch of vanilla give the tobacco sweetness, but the topping is kept restrained so it doesn't overtake the leaf. Because it comes as a plug, the smoker decides the slice thickness: a thin slice burns quickly and brings out the sweetness, while a thick slice or cube cut slows the burn. The presence of Latakia keeps the blend from being a pure sweet aromatic; it gives a medium-bodied smoke that moves back and forth between cocoa and smoke. It suits smokers used to working with plug tobacco who want a flavoured but not sugary taste.
gawith-hoggarth-co-bobs-chocolate-plug.o: A thin smokiness passes beneath the cocoa and light vanilla aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-academy.z: A mixture called Academy in Sutliff's Private Stock line; since sufficient sources describing its composition and character could not be found, this record is kept limited.

d-r-tobacco-windsail-silver-blend.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of D & R Tobacco's Windsail Silver Blend were found.

peter-stokkebye-whiskey-no-2.z: This is a whiskey-flavored blend numbered 2 in Peter Stokkebye's numbered bulk series; no sufficient first-hand sources detailing its character could be found.
peter-stokkebye-whiskey-no-2.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

gawith-hoggarth-co-bosun-cut-plug-unscen.z: This is the untopped version of Bosun Cut Plug. It is sold as broken flake pieces from a pressed plug; burley and dark fire-cured leaf are added alongside the Virginia leaf. The Kendal-style clove-like bowl note found in the aromatic version is absent here, so the taste comes directly from the leaf itself. Since pressing fuses the leaves together, the pieces need to be rubbed apart; moisture generally runs high, and airing for a while before filling makes lighting easier. Nicotine is above medium. It suits an experienced smoker who dislikes the floral scent of Kendal-style topped tobaccos but is looking for the dry, earthy character of English plug tobaccos.
gawith-hoggarth-co-bosun-cut-plug-unscen.o: Leaves an aroma of dry grass, sour bread, and woodsmoke.

reiner-professional.z: Professional is recorded as the first in-house blend Kohlhase & Kopp released under the Reiner line. Its base of Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish leaf is rested for weeks in whisky casks, a stage during which the tobacco naturally picks up oak and whisky notes. Fresh Virginia is then added and a tropical-fruit-and-nut casing is applied on top. The ribbon cut makes packing and burning easy. In the smoke, nicotine stays low-to-medium while the flavor balances the sweetness from the casing against the tobacco's own tart-sweet structure. It suits fans of flavored blends who want a more layered profile from cask resting rather than a one-dimensional sugary casing.
reiner-professional.o: Fills the room with an oak cask, sweet fruit, and roasted hazelnut aroma.

f-j-burrus-s-a-d-r-picayune.z: F.J. Burrus S.A. is a tobacco company with Swiss origins; no verifiable source could be found regarding the composition and character of this blend.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrugs-west-minster.z: Surbrug's West Minster is the Latakia-and-Virginia-centered record of the Surbrug line Wilke carries on. Virginia builds the base with grass, citrus, and light dark-fruit notes; smoky, distinctly woody, sweetish, lightly musty Cyprian Latakia moves to the front of the profile. The structure is plain and balanced; it carries no spice or casing load. Strength only just reaches the medium band, flavor sits right in the middle, and nicotine is mild to medium. It burns cool and clean without biting the tongue. It suits smokers who want the classic English framework at low intensity and are looking for a Latakia blend suited to long bowls.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrugs-west-minster.o: Leaves a sweetish wood-smoke scent, with a light grassy tone lingering behind.

good-stuff-gold.z: Good Stuff is a tobacco series made in the US by Privateer Tobacco and sold in resealable bags. The series consists of Red, Gold, Silver, and menthol variants. Gold is the milder-end variant, weighted toward US-grown flue-cured Virginia and supported by Burley; it has a very finely shredded cut. In the taste, Virginia's honeyed, natural sweetness stands out, while Burley supplies a dry body in the background. Nicotine is noticeably lower than in Red, and the smoke stays mild. Because of the fine cut, it needs to be packed loosely and drawn slowly, or it can bite the tongue. Suited to those wanting an unpretentious, mild everyday tobacco in a large-gram package.
good-stuff-gold.o: Leaves a lightly honeyed, sweet trace close to dry hay.

sutliff-tobacco-company-vanilla-maple-13.z: Vanilla Maple #131 is one of Sutliff's long-running bulk aromatics. Its base contains bright Virginia grades, natural Cavendish, and sun-cured dark leaf of Brazilian origin. A dark casing is applied to the blend; this both darkens the leaf's color and raises its sugar content, letting the vanilla and maple syrup top note settle in. The resulting profile is sweet but not heavy: maple syrup's caramel-like side and vanilla's creamy side lead, while the tobacco's own taste stays in the background. Nicotine is light. It is a good option for those looking for a sweet, distinctly flavored tobacco and for those starting out on pipes with aromatics. Because of the moisture from the casing, drying it before smoking reduces tongue bite.
sutliff-tobacco-company-vanilla-maple-13.o: Leaves a sweet, sugary scent of maple syrup and vanilla.

dan-tobacco-bulldog-medium-cut.z: Bulldog Medium Cut is a medium-cut blend inspired by Irish tobacco tradition, prepared at German maker Dan Tobacco's (DTM) workshop in Lauenburg. Alongside light golden Virginia leaf it contains dark Virginia, brown Kentucky, and a small amount of Latakia; rubbed flake pieces added in measured amount give the mixture body and sweetness. The casing is a floral-fruity touch the maker calls "Bulldog aroma," kept restrained enough not to mask the tobacco flavor. This makes the blend suitable for pipe smokers who don't want the sugar intensity of full aromatics but want something a bit sweeter and rounder than a straight Virginia mixture. With Latakia kept low, the smoky character isn't dominant — just a background spice element.
dan-tobacco-bulldog-medium-cut.o: Leaves a dry-leaf scent alongside a light fruity, floral sweetness.

sutliff-tobacco-company-dark-decadence-z.z: Z93 Dark Decadence is a blend made entirely from burley leaf converted into black cavendish. Green River burley is flavored, fire-cured, and steamed before being processed with a sauce carrying maple, vanilla, cherry, and whiskey notes. On the palate, a whiskey-like base runs beneath vanilla and dark-fruit sweetness; flavor holds through to the bottom of the bowl. Given the high moisture content, it calls for slow smoking. Suited to smokers seeking dark, sweet, heavily sauced aromatics.
sutliff-tobacco-company-dark-decadence-z.o: A sweet scent reminiscent of vanilla, dark fruit, and whiskey fills the room.

planta-full-english.z: Planta Full English is a pipe tobacco blend for which there is not enough independent source material.
planta-full-english.o: Not enough records could be found on the room note.

blatter-blatter-escudo.z: No reliable source documenting the composition of this Virginia-Perique entry listed under the Blatter & Blatter name could be found.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-1992.z: Christmas Cheer is the name of the limited series McClelland prepared each year from unflavored flue-cured Virginia leaf selected from a single harvest. The 1992-dated tin is the series' first release; per its label, it's made from mottled Virginia leaves of the 1989 Old Belt harvest. The leaf is pressed into cake and presented as broken flake. The series was designed to show unflavored Virginia character through year-to-year harvest differences and to be invested in for long cellaring. The brand's characteristic tangy-sweet tin note is pronounced; in the smoke, natural sugar sweetness, hay, and dried-fruit tones stand out. Nicotine level is medium and no flavoring is used. Suited to smokers seeking aged, unflavored Virginia.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-1992.o: Leaves a sweet hay, dried-fruit, and faintly tangy vinegar aroma.

pfeifendepot-flake-cut-070.z: No. 070 Flake Cut is one of the numbered house blends of the Hamburg-based house Gerd Jansens Pfeifendepot, produced by KOPP Tobaccos. Per the maker's description it is an unflavored flake made from three distinct sweet, soft Virginia leaves; the leaves are rested in zinc barrels for two years before pressing. It can be smoked as slices or rubbed out; fully rubbed out it delivers a full, lightly sweet Virginia taste. Its light nicotine makes it suitable for all-day smoking. Carrying no flavoring, it is aimed at smokers seeking a straightforward Virginia taste who are used to working with flakes. It is sold in 50, 100, 200, and 500 gram packages.
pfeifendepot-flake-cut-070.o: Leaves a lightly sweet tobacco aroma recalling dry hay and baked bread.

von-eicken-wild-geese.z: Wild Geese is a blend counted among the aromatic line of German maker Joh. von Eicken; no reliable source could be found regarding its composition and character.

century-columbian-coffee.z: A blend in the Century line known for a coffee aroma; no sufficient source could be found to document its content and character.

tabac-turc-turk-pipo-tutunu.z: Tabac Turc's Türk Pipo Tütünü is, according to records, a blend whose recipe dates back nearly a century and which served for years as the staple tobacco of pipe smokers in Turkey. It is made from Yayladağı, Bitlis, İzmir, and Adıyaman leaf; the product is prepared and packed at the facility in Menemen, İzmir. It is offered as dark-colored flake slices. Though the label lists casing elements such as cavendish, plum, rum, licorice root, carob, fig extract, and honey, their proportions are low, and what stands out on the smoke is the plain tobacco taste. Its character directly conveys the oily, exotic, sweet, and spicy side of Turkish tobacco, with a carob-like sweetness sitting in the background. Airing the tobacco for a while helps balance these flavors and makes it easier to light. It burns slowly, gives a long, cool smoke, and leaves a clean white ash in the bowl. Nicotine is above medium. It is a blend for those curious about the unflavored taste of domestic Oriental tobaccos and for smokers used to packing flake; since the scent it gives off in a room is pronounced, smoking it indoors calls for some care on that front.
tabac-turc-turk-pipo-tutunu.o: Leaves a sharp, burnt-leaf scent typical of oily, spicy Turkish tobacco that permeates a room.

pipesandcigars-com-south-vacherie.z: This is a blend offered under the American retailer pipesandcigars.com's name; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-lavish-english-1.z: Coded SPS-17 in Sutliff's Private Stock line, Lavish English is a ribbon-cut English blend that combines Cyprus latakia and perique with Virginia, black cavendish, oriental, and white burley leaf. Latakia forms the blend's backbone but doesn't dominate the ratio; cavendish and a light vanilla topping add a rounded sweetness to the smoke, while perique leaves a spicy twist in the background. Its character is medium-bodied and cool-burning; suited to smokers seeking smoky flavor without the intensity of heavy latakia blends, and to those wanting a balanced English blend for all-day smoking. Because of the topping's presence, it sits apart from what those expecting a fully unflavored English blend might anticipate.
sutliff-tobacco-company-lavish-english-1.o: Leaves a scent where latakia's woody smoke mixes with a light vanilla sweetness.

mac-baren-fireside-danish-blend-aromatic.z: Cited as the aromatic version of the short-lived line Mac Baren produced for its distributor Fireside; no verifiable source could be found for its contents or character.

bufflehead-canvasback-decoy.z: One of the discontinued waterfowl-named blends from the Bufflehead shop; tins dated 2005 circulate among collectors, but no source regarding its composition could be found.

kadewe-mischung-no-20.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for KaDeWe's Mischung No 20, so the profile is left incomplete.

castro-brothers-raku.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Raku under the Castro Brothers brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

seattle-pipe-club-narrows-bridge.z: Narrows Bridge is one of the American-style aromatics in the Seattle Pipe Club series. A Burley-based body, drawing its fullness from Burley, is joined by black cavendish as a softener; the blend is flavored with the sweet-tart taste of ripe cherry and creamy vanilla. It is ribbon cut. Nicotine is low, flavor intensity is medium; the Burley gives a nutty body that balances the cherry's sweetness. Suited to newcomers to aromatic blends and to those seeking a light, flavored mixture they can smoke all day.
seattle-pipe-club-narrows-bridge.o: Leaves a scent of ripe cherry and creamy vanilla, with a light baked-sweet trace behind it.

j-j-moll-tabaksfabriek-mixture-no-2.z: This is a product from the numbered mixture line of the Dutch J.J. Moll tobacco factory; no reliable source describing its content and character could be found.

watch-city-cigar-simply-red.z: Watch City Cigar's blend called Simply Red is, according to records, one of the house blends of the Waltham, Massachusetts tobacconist shop; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

robert-mcconnell-cruise-line-original.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of Robert McConnell Cruise Line Original.

john-aylesbury-mixture-no-888.z: 888 is the fullest-bodied step in John Aylesbury's numbered aromatic series. The blend, built from Virginia and black Cavendish leaf, is prepared as a fine-cut mixture and offered in 50- and 200-gram packages. Its casing carries cherry and vanilla notes. The maker describes the blend as an everyday tobacco running light to medium-bodied, balanced, and burning evenly. The casing is kept measured enough not to bury the tobacco's own taste. Suited to smokers who like the classic Danish aromatic style and want to avoid heavily cased tobaccos.
john-aylesbury-mixture-no-888.o: Leaves a cherry and vanilla aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-ts2-carolina-fla.z: TS2 Carolina Flake is a Virginia slice in Sutliff's unflavored-leaf series. No casing is applied; the tobacco's character comes entirely from the leaf's own sugar and from pressing and slicing. The leaf used leans toward bright Virginia rather than dark red, giving the taste a lemony tartness and hay-like sweetness. Thanks to its slice structure, the burn is slow and gives fullness. The blend is used in two ways: smoked directly, or rubbed out and added to other blends to build volume and Virginia sweetness. Records note it has been used together with Oriental leaves, such as Yenidje ribbons. For those new to unflavored Virginia, drying the slices thoroughly and packing loosely is a practical way to reduce tongue bite.
sutliff-tobacco-company-ts2-carolina-fla.o: Leaves a sweetish scent of dry hay with a light baked note.

de-la-concha-sir-henry-morgan.z: Named after the pirate Henry Morgan, this is a De La Concha shop blend; no independent source describing its type and composition could be found.
de-la-concha-sir-henry-morgan.o: No reliable record could be found for the room note.

dan-tobacco-rainer-barbi.z: A pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source on the blend's composition or character was found, so no further detail is given.

astleys-no-33-rubbed-virginia-flake.z: A Virginia leaf blend referred to within the London-origin Astley's numbered series; composition information for this number could not be found in sources, leaving the profile blank.

milan-tobacconists-sportsman.z: Sportsman is an aromatic blend in which black cavendish and bright and dark burley tobaccos' sweetness meets in a body drawn from virginia. The casing profile is described in the direction of vanilla, walnut, and cherry. It is presented as a slow, cool-burning mixture; because of its burley proportion it carries a fuller tobacco taste than purely cavendish-based aromatics. Aimed at those looking for fruity and nutty aromatics together.
milan-tobacconists-sportsman.o: A toasted-walnut tone mixes into the vanilla and cherry aroma.

planta-koniglich-preuisches-tabakskolleg.z: Königlich-Preußisches Tabakskollegium 1720 Blau is a medium-strength mixture named after the tobacco council of King Frederick William I's era, based on a recipe referencing that period. Double-fermented black Cavendish is combined with golden Virginia leaf, with a fruity casing carrying vanilla and faint caramel notes applied on top. The variable-width cut makes the tobacco easy to pack and even-burning. It is usually sold in a 100-gram tin to preserve freshness. It suits smokers looking for a measured, classic German-style Cavendish mixture; production reportedly continues today under Mac Baren's German division.
planta-koniglich-preuisches-tabakskolleg.o: Leaves a mellow sweet vanilla and burnt-sugar aroma in the room.

smokers-pride-natural-blend.z: No independent source detailing the composition and character of Natural Blend, referred to as the burley-based unflavored record in the Smoker's Pride line, could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-hearth-of-galway.z: Hearth of Galway is a private blend Wilke Pipe Tobacco prepared for the Pipe Smokers of Ireland club. The brand has kept up its tradition of producing shop and club blends since its founding; this record is among the members of that line where the Latakia character weighs heaviest. Cyprian Latakia makes up roughly half the composition, joined by a notable Tennessee Burley share, a small amount of natural cavendish and black cavendish, with Virginia at the base. The Latakia intensity brings a layer of soot, tar, and burnt wood forward, while Burley gives a dry, nutty body and cavendish adds a softening sweetness. Body and flavor are high, and the room note is strong. It suits experienced smokers seeking high-Latakia mixtures.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-hearth-of-galway.o: Leaves a powerful, smoky scent reminiscent of a hearth wood fire.

f-k-sterling-balkan-759.z: Sterling Balkan 759 is a full-bodied Balkan blend previously sold in the Charles Fairmorn line, later offered in bulk under the F & K brand. Its composition includes matured Virginia leaves, sharp Oriental leaves, and a heavy amount of Latakia; the cut is ribbon. As the Balkan designation indicates, the Oriental leaf share is higher than in classic English blends; this adds a dry-grass, spicy, tart sharpness to the smoky Latakia base. The smoke is dark and full, and it is not light in nicotine either. It suits smokers accustomed to Latakia-heavy blends; it contains no flavouring.
f-k-sterling-balkan-759.o: Leaves an aroma of dry grass and spice within a heavy woodsmoke.

mccranies-my-reserve.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found on My Reserve, one of McCranie's Pipe Shop's house blends.
mccranies-my-reserve.o: No reliable description of the aroma could be found.

pipesandcigars-com-scottys-salmon-river.z: This is a blend offered under the American retailer pipesandcigars.com's name; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

emerson-southern-forged-walais.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing could be found for Walais, a blend from Emerson Southern Forged, so the record has been left open; according to available listings it is classified in the Virginia Based family.

samuel-gawith-cabbies-uncut.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Cabbies Uncut, according to records a Virginia-Perique blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-golden-sliced-.z: Golden Sliced Vintage is the long-pressed, extended-aging version of Golden Sliced, Orlik's best-known product line. Matured American Virginia leaves are slowly pressed and held under pressure; the resulting thin, light-brown slices are presented in the tin with paper interleaving. Its moisture is at a directly smokable level, needing no long drying. Being unflavored, it draws its sweetness from the leaf itself, and its tendency to bite the tongue stays low.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-golden-sliced-.o: Leaves a sweetish tobacco scent toned with bread crust, dry grass, and honey.

black-anchor-black-anchor.z: No manufacturer or retailer source for this blend could be found.
black-anchor-black-anchor.o: No verified information on the room note could be found.

john-patton-quadruple-virginia.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Patton's Quadruple Virginia blend.

mr-bs-110-mr-bs-anniversary-blend.z: Reportedly a pressed-and-sliced blend prepared for Canadian Brigham's Mr. B's line to mark the company's anniversary; no independent source confirming its composition could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-erinmore-m.z: Erinmore Mixture Match is an aromatic in Sutliff's Match line based on the Irish-origin Erinmore Mixture. Bright Virginia with pronounced natural sweetness is paired with cool-burning black cavendish as the base; a pronounced tropical-citrus-character casing leaning toward lemon, orange, peach, and pear is applied over it. This sharp fruitiness of the casing is the blend's most defining trait and sits ahead of the leaf character. The body stays light, and the burn is slow and cool. It suits smokers looking for fruity-tart aromatics who are familiar with the profile of traditional Irish-style mixtures; production ended with Sutliff's closure.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-erinmore-m.o: Leaves a sharp, sweet-tart scent recalling citrus and ripe stone fruit.

von-eicken-lucky-star-mild-granulated.z: Lucky Star Mild Granulated is one of Von Eicken's American-style mixtures. Its weight comes from granulated (cube-cut) Burley, joined by a smaller amount of shag-cut Virginia. It was sold in 50- and 100-gram tins and is no longer in production. The granulated Burley burns slow and cool, giving a nutty, dry taste; the Virginia leaves a light sweetness behind it. True to the "mild" in its name, nicotine is kept low. A record worth noting for smokers curious about how cube-cut tobacco burns, or after mild Burley mixtures.
von-eicken-lucky-star-mild-granulated.o: Leaves a nutty, lightly sweet, dry tobacco aroma.

rattray-winter-edition-2017.z: Winter Edition 2017 is the edition of Rattray's winter series that came in a copper-colored tin, its lid decorated with three black nutcracker figures. The blend consists of black Cavendish, Burley, Virginia, and finely cut (mini-cut) Burley. The flavor line is built around crema catalana: macadamia nut provides a measured background while caramel taste is kept up front, rounded out with vanilla. On the maker's own scale, flavoring, room note, and nicotine are all shown as medium. It suits smokers looking for a sweet but not overdone winter aromatic.
rattray-winter-edition-2017.o: Leaves a caramel and vanilla aroma reminiscent of a burnt sugar custard dessert.

house-of-windsor-honey-t424.z: This is a blend among House of Windsor's T-series bulk aromatics, flavored, as the name suggests, with honey; no verifiable source describing its content could be found.

abenaki-tobacco-co-coco-creme.z: Coco Creme is Abenaki Tobacco's cocoa-direction aromatic. Per the maker's recipe, black Cavendish and dark Burley are brought together, with cocoa and vanilla essence added over it. The cocoa flavoring is the blend's main axis, with vanilla setting a creamy mellowness in the background. Using dark Burley brings a fuller nicotine and a thicker smoke body compared to the same brand's light aromatics. It suits those looking for a sweet but not syrupy aromatic aimed at evening hours. Abenaki Tobacco operated in Conway, New Hampshire; since its own sales site isn't live today, the blend's current status is unclear.
abenaki-tobacco-co-coco-creme.o: Leaves a warm cocoa and vanilla-cream room note.

e-a-carey-rum-flake.z: As the name suggests, this is a rum-flavored, flake-cut E. A. Carey blend; it does not appear on the maker's current list, and not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition.

cornell-diehl-burley-straight.z: This product, referred to as a burley-based component tobacco from Cornell & Diehl, could not have its content and character verified, as it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog.

pipe-and-pint-magnolia-avenue.z: No sources describing the content of Magnolia Avenue, recorded as a house blend of the American tobacconist Pipe and Pint, could be found.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-henrys.z: Henry's is listed as McGahey The Tobacconist's broad-cut burley blend; it is noted to consist of a combination of golden and brown leaves. No detailed source about its character and casing could be found.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-henrys.o: No detailed record regarding its room note could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-vanilla-custard-.z: Vanilla Custard is among the most widely distributed members of Sutliff Tobacco Company's bulk aromatic line; the Z92 code number belongs to the maker's own blend numbering. It is a black-cavendish-forward, ribbon-cut blend; Virginia and Burley leaves add base sweetness and fullness to the body.
sutliff-tobacco-company-vanilla-custard-.o: Leaves a scent of vanilla cream and baked pastry.

uhles-uhles-irish-aromatic.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend called Uhle's Irish Aromatic has been found.
uhles-uhles-irish-aromatic.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

diamond-crown-cherry-blossom.z: A Diamond Crown pipe blend whose name points to cherry aroma; no independent source documenting its composition and character could be found.

john-middleton-inc-sugar-barrel.z: Sugar Barrel is one of John Middleton's Burley-forward blends; not enough sources could be found to describe its contents and character.

jacks-tobacco-firehouse-dog.z: This is a blend under the Jack's Tobacco name; no accessible source describing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
jacks-tobacco-firehouse-dog.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-warped-until-the-end.z: Until The End is a joint effort between Warped founder Kyle Gellis and Cornell & Diehl head blender Jeremy Reeves; its name refers to one of Gellis' wine labels. Its composition includes top-grade sun-grown Ecuadorian cigar leaf, Virginia leaf, the same cigar-leaf Cavendish used in Kings Stride, and a dark fire-cured Kentucky selected to be less smoky than usual. The mixture is offered as broken flake. It's an unflavored blend; its profile is described as deep, earthy, and full. Since Kentucky's smokiness is deliberately kept in the background, cigar leaf and Virginia sweetness come forward. Aimed at smokers wanting to get to know cigar-leaf-based blends and looking for a medium-full smoke.
cornell-diehl-warped-until-the-end.o: A light smoke and dark sweetness mingle with a scent of earth and wood.

sutliff-tobacco-company-lord-of-the-mano.z: Lord of the Manor, part of Sutliff's Private Stock line, is a medium-bodied English blend. Cyprus latakia stands at the forefront of the mixture, followed by Virginia's sweetness and the orientals' floral, dry tones. Being unflavored and latakia-forward in construction, it is aimed at smokers accustomed to smoky blends. While its flavor is intense, it doesn't push nicotine to an extreme; a typical example for those seeking the balance of the classic latakia-Virginia-oriental trio.
sutliff-tobacco-company-lord-of-the-mano.o: Leaves an intense wood-smoke scent with a light floral trace behind it.

cornell-diehl-raspberry-cordial.z: No verifiable product description could be found for this Cornell & Diehl blend named Raspberry Cordial; the brand's blend named Cordial is a separate, differently structured mixture.

cornell-diehl-warped-scarecrow-2021.z: Scarecrow is the blend series Warped and Cornell & Diehl release in limited quantity each autumn; the 2021 release is that year's edition of the series. Its composition includes a special red Virginia Cavendish made from 2017-harvest dark red and 2019-harvest orange-red flue-cured leaf, rounded out with 2014-harvest white Burley and old-style air-cured dark leaf. After being pressed for days, the mixture is sliced into old-fashioned crumble cake. The flavoring is measured: a light top note leaning toward chocolate, vanilla, and caramel sits over the natural tobacco character. The result is a smoke where malty cocoa and warming spice come forward, sitting between aromatic and unflavored. Its pressed structure makes it well suited to aging; being a seasonal limited run, it's only available during its release period.
cornell-diehl-warped-scarecrow-2021.o: Leaves a scent where cocoa and caramel sweetness mingle with bread yeast and autumn spice.

gawith-hoggarth-co-best-brown-unscented.z: Best Brown Unscented is Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s flaked record that, unlike the firm's essenced Lakeland lines, carries no flavouring at all. It contains various Virginia leaves, Malawi burley, and a measured amount of African-sourced dark fire-cured leaf; the mixture is steam-cooked and pressed into the traditional flake form. Without a topping, the taste comes directly from the leaf itself: Virginia's bread-like sweetness, burley's nutty, earthy tone, and the fire-cured leaf's light smoke in the background all sit together. It is a full-bodied record in terms of nicotine; aimed at those seeking essence-free English flakes and a slow smoke.
gawith-hoggarth-co-best-brown-unscented.o: Leaves an aroma of dry grass, bread crust, and light fire smoke.

mostex-stanislaw-black-cavendish.z: No independent, verifiable source describing the composition of this blend, released under the Stanislaw brand of the Brno-based maker Mostex, could be found.

sir-william-english-classic.z: An English-style blend recorded under the Sir William name, said to contain Latakia; no source confirming the brand's identity and the blend's composition could be found.
sir-william-english-classic.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

peretti-ultra-lite.z: Ultra-Lite is described as a house blend belonging to L.J. Peretti's light aromatic line; however, no sufficient sources describing its content and character could be found.
peretti-ultra-lite.o: No documented recipe could be found in the records.

mcclelland-legends-collector-series.z: Legends is an unflavored English mixture in McClelland's collector series. Its composition holds Latakia, Oriental/Turkish leaf, and Virginia; the cut is ribbon. Latakia builds the blend's frame but isn't kept in a dominant position; what stands out is the spicy Oriental leaf and the Virginia's plain sweetness. Body stays light to medium while flavor intensity is high, making it suitable for those wanting a layered smoke without raising the soot load. Moisture straight out of the pack is balanced enough to smoke directly, and the burn is mild. Like the rest of the series, this blend was discontinued when McClelland ceased operations in 2018.
mcclelland-legends-collector-series.o: Leaves a spiced tobacco aroma with measured wood smoke.

g-l-pease-triple-play.z: Triple Play is a blend that brings together ripe red and bright flue-cured Virginias with Acadian perique and a measured amount of dark fire-cured Kentucky. Once the leaf is pressed and matured in cakes, it is cut into two-ounce bars; the smoker separates the slice to whatever thickness they like. The name references the three leaf types making up the blend. According to the producer, the dark fire-cured Kentucky content is notably lower than in JackKnife Plug and is used only to add dimension. It is aimed at smokers wanting a touch of smokiness added to the Virginia-Perique structure.
g-l-pease-triple-play.o: Leaves a mix of smoky wood and sweet, dry-grass aroma.

ruddells-blarney-twist.z: Referred to as a rope-format tobacco produced by the Dublin-based Wm. Ruddell Ltd.; no reliable source describing the blend's content could be found.

old-virginia-tobacco-co-el-dorado.z: El Dorado is one of the aromatic blends Old Virginia Tobacco Co. sells under its house label; no published description of its composition could be found.

d-r-tobacco-vengeur-regular-blend.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of D & R Tobacco's Vengeur Regular Blend were found.

pfeifen-huber-georg-der-erste.z: Georg der Erste is one of Pfeifen Huber's aromatic house blends, its name a reference to the founder. The loose-cut blend is built on the contrast between light, orange-toned Virginia leaf and dark Virginia, joined by nougat-leaning Burley and black Cavendish. On the flavoring side there is a pronounced but not sharp citrus-and-almond-cream note. The blend is light in nicotine, intensely aromatic, and has a fresh character; Virginia's sugar meets the citrus topping while Burley adds fullness to the body. The smoke is soft and sweet. It suits smokers who like sweet aromatics but want a fruity, fresh direction rather than the classic vanilla-and-chocolate axis.
pfeifen-huber-georg-der-erste.o: Leaves an almond-paste sweetness together with a citrus-peel aroma.

cornell-diehl-gray-ghost.z: Gray Ghost is one of Cornell & Diehl's blends containing cigar leaf. Virginia leaf forms the core, joined by fragrant cigar leaf and black cavendish. The cut is ribbon. Cigar leaf gives the blend an earthy, lightly salty body and a pronounced nicotine load; Virginia and cavendish pull that body toward the sweet side. It is a blend aimed at experienced smokers seeking an unflavored, hearty smoke and curious about what cigar tobacco brings to a pipe.
cornell-diehl-gray-ghost.o: Leaves an earthy, sweetish cigar-leaf aroma.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-limited-edition-.z: No manufacturer or retailer record could be found documenting the contents of Kohlhase & Kopp's 2013 annual limited series.

gawith-hoggarth-co-ennerdale-mixture.z: Ennerdale is one of the best-known examples of Kendal tradition (Lakeland) and is the crumbled, broken-flake presentation of the brand's flake-form Ennerdale product. African- and South American-origin Virginia leaf and Malawi Burley are selected for their sweetness and ability to absorb the topping; air-cured dark leaf cools the smoke and adds a woody, creamy texture. The topping side is a compound top sauce made of rum, vanilla, citrus, almond, and floral essences; because of this, the blend's aroma is strong and lingering. Suited to smokers wanting a moderate-nicotine but flavor-intense blend, and to those wanting to get to know classic Lakeland style. Since it clings noticeably to jar and pipe, smoking it in a dedicated pipe is common practice.
gawith-hoggarth-co-ennerdale-mixture.o: Leaves a heavy aroma combining soapy florals, citrus, and almond, lingering in fabric and the room for a long time.

danneman-sweet-mango.z: Sweet Mango is the best-known blend in Dannemann's pipe tobacco line; for a long time it appeared on packaging as "Dannemann Original (Sweet Mango)." It is built from Maryland, Virginia, and Burley leaf. According to the maker's own account, the different tobacco types are processed and flavored separately before being combined with a heavy mango casing, producing a fruity, sweet profile. Nicotine stays mild, making it suitable for smokers new to aromatic blends as well as those wanting a light smoke during the day. The brand originated in Brazil and is now run under the Switzerland-based Burger Söhne group, with pipe tobacco production carried out in Europe. Records indicate the blend has in recent years been offered under the name W.Ø. Larsen Standard Mixture No. 1, in new packaging but with the same mixture preserved.
danneman-sweet-mango.o: Leaves a pronounced ripe-mango and sweet-fruit scent.

ken-byron-ventures-meadow-lark.z: Meadow Lark is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

pfiefen-tesch-hamburger-mischung.z: No sources documenting the content and character of Hamburger Mischung, recorded as a house blend of the German tobacconist Tesch, could be found.

crofts-1.z: Recorded as a member of the numbered Crofts house-blend series; no source documenting its composition and character was found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-196.z: Wilke No. 196 is a Virginia-Burley mixture in the maker's 190 series. Lightly flavored black cavendish, prepared with Wilke's own roasting method, is added to natural Virginia and Burley leaves. While the cavendish addition raises the blend's sweetness, the mixture's backbone stays in the unflavored leaf; body and nicotine are medium. With no Latakia present, it suits smokers seeking a smoke-free, lightly sweet everyday smoke.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-196.o: Leaves a mild scent reminiscent of toasted bread and light caramel.

astleys-no-55-elizabethan.z: Astley's No.55 Elizabethan is a flake blend carrying on the unflavored Virginia tradition. The pressed leaves are sliced and tinned; preparing it requires rubbing out and airing the flakes. In the smoke, dark fruit, citrus, an earthy base, and a faintly tangy sharpness all appear together. Since citrus notes are subdued, the leaf's buttery mellowness comes forward, and a grassy lightness rounds out the blend's complexity. Body is medium. It suits smokers who enjoy following the narrow but layered flavor range of unflavored Virginia.
astleys-no-55-elizabethan.o: Leaves a mellow room note leaning toward dry hay and a light citrus peel.

e-a-carey-vintage-estate.z: Vintage Estate is E. A. Carey's golden-cavendish-based blend. Per the maker's description, golden cavendish forms the mixture's backbone; a small amount of fire-cured dark leaf is added inside for a light depth. The result is a lightly flavored tobacco leaving a lasting scent. Production takes place in Denmark. The nicotine load is low and the flavor body is moderate. It's a record for those seeking a lightly aromatic, all-day tobacco far from heavy flavorings. It appears on the brand's current list and is also offered with a personalized tobacco tin option.
e-a-carey-vintage-estate.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, lasting, woody scent.

cornell-diehl-carolina-red-flake-with-pe.z: This limited-production flake, the 2021 edition of the Carolina Red Flake series with perique added, could not have its content and character verified, as it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog.

tres-cajones-tobacco-dragons-drool.z: No sufficient source verifiable from the maker or retailer side has been found for Tres Cajones Tobacco's blend Dragon's Drool.
tres-cajones-tobacco-dragons-drool.o: No reliable source describing the room note has been found.

mac-baren-navy-plug.z: Navy Plug is the block-form version of Mac Baren's well-known Navy Flake blend. Select Virginia and Burley leaves are combined with the brand's own Cavendish, pressed, rested for weeks, and then packaged unsliced as a block; the smoker cuts the block to whatever thickness they want. In keeping with sailors' tradition, a rum note is applied on top. At the front of the taste sits the Burley leaf's earthy, woody, distinctly nutty and oat-like character, joined by a fine molasses trace. The Virginia leaf adds tangy citrus, bread, and dry-hay notes along with dark-fruit sweetness. The rum topping binds these tastes together rather than masking them. Body and nicotine are medium; it burns cool, clean, and slow. Suited to smokers wanting to get to know plug tobaccos or who prefer to decide the cut thickness themselves.
mac-baren-navy-plug.o: Leaves a sweet rum and baked-bread aroma in the room.

john-middleton-inc-bin-56.z: An American-style blend from Philadelphia-based John Middleton; no verifiable information on its profile could be found.
john-middleton-inc-bin-56.o: No verifiable information on its room note could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-peach-mixed.z: Kendal Mixed is the second of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s shag-cut main bodies. Unlike Kendal Gold's pure-Virginia structure, this body is built by adding Malawi-origin dark leaf and some fire-cured Kentucky to golden Virginia; because of this, its color is more mottled and its taste more earthy. Peach Mixed is the peach-flavored version of this body. The dark leaf's nutty, earthy base continues beneath the fruit flavoring, giving a fuller, higher-nicotine smoke than the Kendal Gold-based peach version. The fine shag cut lights easily and calls for a slow draw. Suited to smokers wanting an aromatic smoke without sacrificing body.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-peach-mixed.o: Leaves an aroma of ripe peach and a light nuttiness.

john-cotton-john-cottons-double-pressed-.z: A pipe tobacco blend released under the John Cotton name; not enough independent sources could be found to document its contents and character.
john-cotton-john-cottons-double-pressed-.o: No source could be found on the room note.

iwan-ries-international.z: Records indicate this is a Virginia-and-Burley-based Iwan Ries blend; no independent source verifying its composition could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
iwan-ries-international.o: No room note described in the records could be found.

smokin-g-pipe-tobacco-turkish-straight-b.z: A blend from the Smokin' G brand stated to be built on oriental leaf; no source confirming its composition could be found.

hu-tobacco-imagine.z: Imagine is a medium-strength ready-rubbed flake from HU Tobacco that brings together different Virginia grades. A small proportion of Perique is added to a sweet Virginia base; the Perique brings a plummy sweetness and light spice, but isn't the dominant component. The blend's distinguishing feature is a subtle citrus aroma that doesn't mask the tobacco's natural taste. It's described as burning slowly and cool, needing fewer relights than a typical flake. It suits those looking for a much more measured flavoring, in the Virginia-Perique vein, than flavored blends.
hu-tobacco-imagine.o: Leaves a tart aroma where dried-fruit sweetness meets a light lemon-peel coolness.

sutliff-tobacco-company-paradoxical.z: Paradoxical arrived in the summer of 2023 as the closing entry in the Birds of a Feather line bearing Per Georg Jensen's signature. Red and stoved Virginia are added to a burley-forward base, along with rustica, the line's signature leaf. It is offered pressed into plug form, giving the smoker the option to slice, rub out, or fold it directly for packing. On the taste, a nutty, cocoa-leaning base from the burley is balanced by a measured sweetness from the Virginia leaves; the rustica brings a spicy, earthy sharpness and a pronounced nicotine load. It is a blend prepared for experienced smokers looking for an unflavored, full-bodied smoke.
sutliff-tobacco-company-paradoxical.o: Leaves a dark leaf scent dominated by earth, nuts, and spice.

cornell-diehl-constellation-no-411.z: Constellation is, according to available records, one of Cornell & Diehl's older blends also referred to by a catalog number. Per the manufacturer's description, ribbon-cut Virginia, coarse-cut burley, unsweetened black cavendish, and Latakia are brought together. Latakia's smoke and burley's earthy, nutty heartiness form the blend's backbone; Virginia adds a light sweetness, while cavendish gives a soft finish. It suits experienced smokers looking for a hearty English blend, with nicotine that could be called above medium.
cornell-diehl-constellation-no-411.o: Leaves an aroma of smoky Latakia and earthy burley.

john-brumfit-and-radford-tobacco-limited.z: An aromatic blend from the JBR brand, rooted in the English tobacconist tradition; no verifiable information on its contents could be found.
john-brumfit-and-radford-tobacco-limited.o: No verifiable information on its room note could be found.

kleinlagel-aplicious.z: Aplicious is a Golden Delicious apple-themed aromatic blend from small-scale German workshop Kleinlagel. Virginia leaves are lightly pressed and rested, then rubbed out; the apple aroma is rounded off with a pinch of vanilla. It was offered in a 50-gram tin and a 250-gram package. Nicotine is low, flavor load is medium. Since it burns dry and clean, it suits smokers avoiding the wetness common in aromatic blends. A blend for those seeking a fruity aromatic and for short daytime smokes; per retailer records, it's now been delisted.
kleinlagel-aplicious.o: Leaves a scent of freshly cut green apple with a fine vanilla note behind it.

peter-heinrichs-reserve-crue-no-2.z: Reserve Crue No. 2 is a pressed long-slice blend belonging to Peter Heinrichs' hand-processed Reserve Crue series, built from pure Virginia leaf. Since the leaves are cold-pressed into blocks and then sliced, the burn stays slow and cool; the slices need to be rubbed out before packing. A measured flavoring recalling vanilla, honey, and orange is added over the natural Virginia sweetness. The flavoring is kept at a level that doesn't mask the leaf's own sugar; nicotine strength stays light. It suits smokers seeking a flavored Virginia flake who enjoy the slow smoke of pressed tobaccos.
peter-heinrichs-reserve-crue-no-2.o: Leaves a sweet trace of vanilla, honey, and orange peel.

brookfield-aromatic-no-1.z: Brookfield No. 1 is a distinctly aromatic blend combining Virginia, burley and Java leaf, topped with a sweet vanilla casing. Its strength is low; on the flavor side a fruity sweetness comes forward, with the tobacco's own character staying in the background. Because of its low nicotine and soft smoke, it is positioned as one of the first blends for those new to the pipe. The brand is manufactured by Pöschl Tabak, founded in 1902 in Geisenhausen near Landshut, Bavaria, and run today by the fourth generation.
brookfield-aromatic-no-1.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of sweet vanilla and ripe fruit.

planta-anno-mmx-after-dinner-mixture.z: Anno MMX is the 2010 edition of the annual limited year-tobacco series from Planta Tabak-Manufaktur, founded in Berlin in 1956, carried under the subtitle After Dinner Mixture. A casing evoking chocolate and smoky Scotch whisky is applied to a body of honey-colored Virginias and black Cavendish; the blend is hand-prepared. It is designed as a full-bodied aromatic set aside for after dinner: the casing is pronounced, while the Cavendish base mellows the smoke. Being a limited edition, it is not in continuous production. It suits those wanting sweet and smoky notes together, looking for a blend set aside for evening smoking.
planta-anno-mmx-after-dinner-mixture.o: Leaves a cocoa and smoky-whisky aroma in the room.

paul-olsen-no-222-flake.z: For Paul Olsen's blend called No. 222 Flake, no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

pfeifen-huber-munchner-rauch-huber.z: Münchner Rauch is one of Pfeifen Huber's aromatic house blends named after the city. The base of the loose-cut mixture is soft brown Cavendish; golden Virginia leaf and a small amount of black Cavendish are added to it. The flavoring is built around coconut, pineapple, and vanilla. The body is light and nicotine is low; the smoke is soft and sweet, the tropical fruit note persists throughout the smoke and closes with a long finish. Thanks to the Cavendish structure, bite is minimal and it packs easily. It suits smokers who like fruity, creamy aromatics and want a light, evenly burning everyday blend.
pfeifen-huber-munchner-rauch-huber.o: Leaves a tropical fruit aroma dominated by coconut and pineapple, with vanilla behind it.

cornell-diehl-da-vinci.z: Da Vinci is one of the blends where Cornell & Diehl pushes the Latakia ratio to an extreme: per available sources, roughly 75 percent of the mixture is aged Cyprus Latakia. The remainder is made up of coarse-cut burley and light Virginia flake. The leaf is mostly black, with brown and beige pieces mixed in; it is dry but supple, needing no extra preparation. The taste runs along smoky wood, earth, and incense; burley carries the body, while Virginia adds a thin sweetness. No flavoring is used. It suits smokers looking for Latakia not as spice but as the main ingredient, accustomed to heavy English mixtures.
cornell-diehl-da-vinci.o: Leaves a strong, long-lasting smoke aroma in the room reminiscent of campfire and incense.

outwest-tobacco-western-sunrise.z: Western Sunrise is one of the house blends from Outwest Tobacco of Idaho. Golden-yellow Virginia leaf forms the base, joined by a small amount of fire-cured leaf, golden Burley, and black Cavendish. Per the maker's recipe, the mixture burns cool and slow. With its light nicotine level and measured sweetness, it's positioned as a mellow blend smokable all day; it suits those wanting a straightforward, calm tobacco rather than a heavy Latakia mixture.
outwest-tobacco-western-sunrise.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly smoky scent recalling baked bread.

cornell-diehl-morleys-best.z: Morley's Best is a burley-forward English mixture bearing the signature of Cornell & Diehl blender Bob Runowski. According to the manufacturer's description, three distinct burley types — white burley, cube-cut burley, and coarse-cut burley — come together with Virginia flake and Cyprus Latakia. It is offered as a ribbon cut; the Latakia level is pronounced enough to place the blend in the English category, yet restrained enough not to overpower burley's nutty, earthy taste. The smoke runs cool and even, with no sharp heat or tongue bite reported. Nicotine strength sits in the medium range, suiting smokers who want an all-day blend with Latakia present but not heavy-handed. It also serves as a good introduction for those wanting to get to know burley-based American mixtures.
cornell-diehl-morleys-best.o: Leaves a nutty aroma of dry leaf mingled with light wood smoke.

milan-tobacconists-cherry-bon-bon.z: Cherry Bon Bon is recorded as a cherry-and-chocolate-cased, very light-bodied aromatic house blend from Milan Tobacconists; no verifiable source regarding its leaf composition could be found.
milan-tobacconists-cherry-bon-bon.o: Leaves a cherry and chocolate aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-modern-english-3.z: Modern English #310 is a lightly cased English mixture from Sutliff's numbered bulk line. Burley and Virginia leaf form the body, with a small amount of latakia added for a smoky edge. What sets it apart from classic English mixtures is a light topping applied over the tobacco; records indicate this casing leans toward red wine, with a hint of cinnamon here and there. Because the latakia ratio is kept low, smoke is not dominated by smokiness; the blend runs mostly on burley's nutty base. Nicotine strength is below average. Suited to smokers who want the smoky character of English mixtures in moderation while also caring that the room note isn't harsh.
sutliff-tobacco-company-modern-english-3.o: A faint sweet-spicy scent accompanies a light smoky tobacco aroma.

planta-old-french-cognac.z: This is cited as a brandy-flavored mixture bearing the Planta name; there is not enough independent source material on its content, cut, or production status.
planta-old-french-cognac.o: Leaves a sweetish aroma evoking brandy.

cobblestone-chess-queen.z: A Virginia-heavy, broken-flake-cut blend in Cobblestone's Chess series; not enough independent sourcing could be found for detailed composition information.

rauch-rauch-pfeifentabak-aus-osterreich.z: This is a pipe tobacco from Weinhof Rauch, which farms on volcanic soil in Austria's Styria region; the family business grows tobacco on small plots alongside its vineyards. The product is prepared from one hundred percent natural Austrian tobacco with no additives, and every stage from cultivation to processing takes place within the country. The operation states it uses no pesticides and relies heavily on manual labor. Being unflavored, it is positioned as a natural (natur) tobacco rather than an aromatic. Under Austria's tobacco monopoly regulations it cannot be sold directly and is only available through licensed dealers called Trafik. The maker has not published a detailed specification of the blend's leaf composition or cut.
rauch-rauch-pfeifentabak-aus-osterreich.o: Leaves the earth and hay aroma of unflavored dry leaf.

super-value-black-cavendish.z: Super Value Black Cavendish is a single-component aromatic blend built from cavendish leaf slowly steamed to blacken it. Its ribbon-cut structure packs easily into the pipe; per the catalog description it carries a vanilla-and-citrus-direction flavor and offers a medium fullness. The topping doesn't overpower the tobacco, giving a straightforward, uncomplicated smoke. The blend is a typical example of the inexpensive bulk-tobacco class meant for all-day smoking; suited to those not seeking complex leaf character beyond black cavendish's natural sweetness, and to those new to the aromatic category. It can also serve as a base to soften harsher blends.
super-value-black-cavendish.o: A trace of light citrus peel mixes into vanilla sweetness.

tinder-box-special.z: No reliable source has been found for the Tinder Box pipe blend called Special.

d-r-tobacco-athey.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the D & R Tobacco brand as Athey; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

1776-tobacco-co-golden-eagle.z: One of 1776 Tobacco Co.'s Virginia-Burley-centered blends; no adequate source could be reached to fill in the profile.

campbells-smoke-shop-2000-blend-iii.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named 2000 Blend III under the Campbell's Smoke Shop brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

sutliff-tobacco-company-golden-cavendish.z: J6 Golden Cavendish is a light-bodied aromatic in Sutliff's letter-and-number-coded bulk line. Select red and golden Virginia leaves are combined with burley; a light aromatic coating is applied on top. The ribbon cut has a golden-yellow appearance. Pouch aroma is sweet and hay-like. On the palate, flavor stays low-intensity, with no tendency to bite the tongue and a slow burn. A record for those wanting a light sweetness rather than a heavy topping in aromatics, or for smokers new to the pipe; distributed in bulk by weight.
sutliff-tobacco-company-golden-cavendish.o: Leaves a scent of sweet vanilla and dry hay.

pipesandcigars-com-grand-point.z: Grand Point is one of the house blends sold under its own name by the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com; no sufficient independent sources documenting its content and character could be found.

richs-grandpas.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of Rich's Grandpa's.

peter-heinrichs-dark-strong-flake.z: Dark Strong Flake is a dark, full-bodied pressed-leaf blend in Peter Heinrichs' Special Selection line. The mixture's backbone is built from full-bodied black Cavendish with its characteristic roasted scent; naturally sweet Virginia joins it, and the mixture is pressed and sliced. A plum flavoring applied on top adds a fruity top note to the blend. As its name suggests, it is a dark tobacco in both color and body; nicotine and flavor intensity are above medium. It suits people seeking a satisfying smoke that has an aromatic touch but stays away from light, sugary blends. Being pressed, the slices need to be opened and, if necessary, aired briefly.
peter-heinrichs-dark-strong-flake.o: Leaves a roasted dark-tobacco and stewed-plum aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-backwoods-4x4-ru.z: Backwoods 4x4 Rugged Cut is a Sutliff aromatic prepared, as the "rugged cut" in its name suggests, with a coarse, irregular-piece cut rather than neat ribbon. A burley-forward base is joined by Virginia and black cavendish; its defining topping is vanilla. Because of the coarse cut, it packs more loosely into the pipe and gives a slow, cool burn. The vanilla topping is heavy but doesn't completely mask the tobacco flavor beneath it; nicotine level is low. Suited to smokers who like vanilla aromatics and prefer working with a coarser-textured tobacco rather than fine ribbon. The blend is no longer in production.

mcclelland-top-hat.z: Top Hat is a Virginia-Perique blend built by adding a pronounced amount of Perique to McClelland's characteristic red and orange Virginias. Red and stoved Virginias give a sharp, tangy-sweet, dark-fruited base, underlaid with a faint herbal, earthy sweetness from fermentation. Here, the Perique brings forward its raisin-and-fig side rather than sharp peppery spice; the spice note becomes more pronounced as the smoke progresses. The brand's vinegary aroma noticeable on opening largely fades after the first few puffs. Since its sweetness balances its body, it stays at a sustainable intensity all day for smokers used to Virginia-Perique blends. Production ended in 2018.
mcclelland-top-hat.o: Leaves a dark-fruit and tangy-sweet aroma.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2005.z: Christmas Cheer 2005 is the 2005 release of the series in which McClelland presented a single Virginia harvest as a separate tin each year. Select, matured orange-red flue-cured Virginia leaves are pressed into cake, aged, sliced, and partly broken up before going into the tin as broken flake; this form eases packing. The blend is unflavored; taste comes from the leaf's own sugar and maturation. The sharp tang in the tin note is a known trait of the brand's Virginias. Since each year's crop differs, character shifts between releases, and tins continue to change as they're cellared. Suited to smokers following the unflavored Virginia line who know how to work with flake form. The maker ceased operations in 2018.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2005.o: Leaves a tangy, vinegary sweetness along with a toasted-bread aroma.

uhles-black-stoker.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend Black Stoker has been found.

stephen-mitchell-son-tam-o-shanter.z: Tam O' Shanter is a tobacco released by Stephen Mitchell & Son, founded in Linlithgow in 1723 and operating in Glasgow after 1825, taking its name from Robert Burns's poem of the same name; the company merged with W. D. & H. O. Wills in 1901, becoming part of Imperial Tobacco, and no detailed record of the blend's composition could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-verge-engine-2020.z: The 2020 release of Verge Engine is reported to be classified as straight Virginia; no independent source could be found to detail its contents.
ken-byron-ventures-verge-engine-2020.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

watch-city-cigar-original-crumb-cut.z: This is Watch City Cigar's Burley-based crumb-cut blend; no sufficient source could be found for details of its composition.
watch-city-cigar-original-crumb-cut.o: Records note it leaves a nutty, earthy scent typical of Burley-forward blends.

mission-pipe-shop-circus-candy.z: Circus Candy is among Mission Pipe Shop's aromatic house blends named to evoke confectionery; no accessible source describing its composition could be found.

dream-castle-tobacco-company-natural-cav.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of Natural Cavendish, a blend from Dream Castle Tobacco Company.

dunhill-my-mixture-34596.z: A discontinued mixture belonging to Dunhill's My Mixture line, for which no verifiable source on its composition could be found.

cornell-diehl-sun-bear-black-locust.z: No current maker or retailer record documenting the composition of this limited release, part of Cornell & Diehl's honey-themed Sun Bear series, could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-court-of-st-jame.z: Court of St. James is an unflavored blend in Sutliff's Private Stock line. Louisiana perique is added to a broken-flake, long-ribbon Virginia base, with a small amount of latakia sprinkled on top. Though latakia's scent is noticeable on opening the tin, its share on the palate stays limited; the blend carries a primarily Virginia-perique character. The Virginias are full, herbal, and earthy; perique is peppery and sweet. The cut packs easily into the bowl and requires few relights. Suited to smokers who enjoy unflavored blends and want a subtle smoky touch within a Virginia-perique frame.
sutliff-tobacco-company-court-of-st-jame.o: Leaves a scent of pepper and thin wood smoke over tangy sweet Virginia.

mostex-stanislaw-blackberry-blend.z: No independent, verifiable source describing the composition of this blend, released under the Stanislaw brand of the Brno-based maker Mostex, could be found.

cult-abacus.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the Cult brand as Abacus; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

mcclelland-no-600-special-black.z: A blend in McClelland's numbered bulk series, reportedly black-Cavendish-based; no sufficient source documenting its composition could be found.

rattray-marlin-flake.z: Marlin Flake is a blend in which Virginia, black Cavendish, and Perique are pressed and cut into long slices. The slices are coiled into the tin; the color is a mottled dark brown, and the flakes are brittle. In the tin note, Cavendish's tangy sweetness overtakes Virginia. It causes no trouble in packing or lighting, and burns evenly throughout the smoke. In the first half, Cavendish-driven sweetness dominates; in the second half Virginia's character becomes pronounced. Here Perique stays more a background depth element than a pronounced pepper accent. It suits smokers looking for a sweet Virginia-Perique flake with a high Cavendish share.
rattray-marlin-flake.o: Leaves a sharp, tangy sweet, dark tobacco aroma.

park-lane-tobacconist-park-lane-no-14.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Park-Lane No. 14, one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

pipesandcigars-com-civic-duty.z: No independent source material could be found sufficient to fill out a specification for the pipesandcigars.com blend called Civic Duty.

sutliff-tobacco-company-vanilla-honey-17.z: An aromatic from Sutliff's bulk catalog, carrying, as its name indicates, a vanilla and honey top note; no independent source detailing the blend's content and character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-vanilla-honey-17.o: Leaves a scent of vanilla and honey.

g-l-pease-25th-anniversary-silver-jubile.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for G. L. Pease's 25th Anniversary Silver Jubilee blend; records place it in the Virginia-heavy class.

douwe-egberts-amphora-extra-mild-cavendi.z: Amphora is a pipe tobacco brand with roots in the Netherlands; per records, its current blends are produced in Denmark by Mac Baren. Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Extra Mild Cavendish.

chief-catoonah-tobacconist-princes-stree.z: Princes Street Mixture is an English mixture reconstructed from a twenty-eight-year-old sample of John Cotton 1&2 Medium. Latakia is used in measured amounts, with Virginia base and Oriental leaf brought to the front; the smoke is smooth and leaves no harshness on the tongue. The blend was prepared by Dick Silverman, a tobacconist in Ridgefield, Connecticut for over thirty years, and was chosen first place in the John Cotton recreation contest at the 2012 Chicago Pipe Show. The name comes from the street where the shop is located. Suitable for smokers seeking measured English mixtures without heavy Latakia.
chief-catoonah-tobacconist-princes-stree.o: Leaves a trace of dry hay and spicy Oriental over a measured smoky aroma.

peterson-craftsmans-reserve-2017.z: Craftsman's Reserve 2017 is a limited-production mixture Peterson released specifically for that year. Golden Virginia and black Cavendish are combined with hand-rubbed Virginia flake, topped with a cream-caramel flavoring. It is presented in a 100 gram tin.
peterson-craftsmans-reserve-2017.o: Leaves a creamy caramel and burnt-sugar aroma.

4noggins-chipman-hill.z: Chipman Hill sits among 4noggins' English-style blends. Per the manufacturer's description, it's a dark, thin, long-cut tobacco built on a balanced footing of Latakia and Oriental leaves, with no topping applied. Strength and flavor are kept at a moderate level, positioning it as a choice that can be smoked all day without the heaviness of Latakia-forward blends weighing on the smoker. It suits those moving on from aromatics into the English style, and anyone seeking a measured Oriental-Latakia balance.
4noggins-chipman-hill.o: Leaves a burnt-wood and dry-spice aroma of moderate sharpness.

vauen-lounge-blend-no-1.z: Lounge Blend No. 1 is the first entry in Vauen's numbered series and follows a Danish-style aromatic approach. Black Cavendish, Virginia, Burley and pieces of Virginia flake are used together; the varying cut widths keep the burn even. The blend is cased with plum, vanilla and rum flavoring; the taste stays on a sweet, fruity line while nicotine is low. The room note is fruity without being overpowering. Suited to those new to aromatic tobacco and to anyone after an easy, everyday smoke.
vauen-lounge-blend-no-1.o: Leaves a ripe plum and vanilla-rum aroma.

house-of-calabash-canadian-maple.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for House of Calabash's Canadian Maple blend, so its content and character could not be recorded.

hearth-home-sweet-cask.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for this blend, said to contain Virginia and Burley, from the Hearth & Home brand.

mcclelland-no-805-carolina-deluxe.z: A blend in McClelland's bulk series, discontinued when the firm closed in 2018; no sufficient source documenting its contents and character could be found.

hearth-home-vischer-ferry.z: Vischer Ferry is a blend in Hearth & Home's Landmark line, inspired by place names in New York state; no sufficient source describing its composition could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-count-pulaski.z: Sutliff's Count Pulaski takes its name from Kazimierz Pulaski, the Polish soldier who organized cavalry units during the American Revolutionary War; the tin text references Benjamin Franklin's letter recommending Pulaski and his role at the Battle of Brandywine. The blend itself is not a single piece: per the maker's description, it's a combination of four separate sub-blends. The composition brings together burley in shag, plug, and cube-cut forms along with Carolina flake, Virginia, and latakia; over this base, an essence of select Syrian latakia along with rum and anise flavoring is applied. The result is a layered blend with high fullness due to its burley-forward body, where latakia's smoke and spiced sweetness intertwine. Aimed at experienced smokers seeking an unusual, intense structure that combines different cuts.
sutliff-tobacco-company-count-pulaski.o: Rum sweetness and anise spice mix into a smoky latakia scent.

butera-latakia-no-1.z: Latakia No.1 is the Balkan-style blend in Butera's Royal Vintage line. Its composition uses generous mountain-grown Cyprus Latakia, joined by a notable proportion of Turkish basma leaf, bright North Carolina and red virginia. In the blend Oriental leaf sits slightly ahead of the Latakia, so the smoke is soft while the woody, dry-spice side is more pronounced. The body is medium. Suitable for smokers who want Latakia as a carrying rather than a masking element, seeking Oriental-forward Balkan blends.
butera-latakia-no-1.o: Leaves a woody smoke, dry spice and light resin aroma.

super-value-bourbon-whiskey.z: Super Value Bourbon Whiskey is a budget aromatic where a bourbon-whiskey-style top flavoring is applied to a cavendish-forward base. The burley, cavendish, and Virginia leaves used in the line are prepared with a coarse cut; the blend is produced in the US and sold in both large bags and small pouches. It gives a pronouncedly sweet, low-nicotine smoke. Suited to smokers who enjoy liquor-themed flavors and consume large quantities of everyday tobacco.
super-value-bourbon-whiskey.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly alcohol-tinged scent of oak and caramel.

robert-mcconnell-scottish-flake.z: Scottish Flake is an unflavored flake blend of Virginia leaf with Kentucky and Perique added, then pressed. The slices are dark and oily in appearance; because tin moisture runs high, letting it rest balances moisture and flavor. It packs and burns without trouble. It offers a cool smoke. Alongside quality Virginia sweetness there is a spicy layer pointing to the Oriental leaf in the blend. The Kentucky and Burley character is hard to distinguish individually but adds fullness to the body. Strength and flavor sit in the medium range. It suits smokers looking for an unflavored, pressed, full-bodied Virginia blend.
robert-mcconnell-scottish-flake.o: Leaves a sweet-tart aroma of raw tobacco close to dried fig.

esoterica-tobacciana-ramsgate.z: Ramsgate is listed in the aromatic family among ribbon-cut blends in the Esoterica line, produced by J. F. Germain & Son in Jersey. Its flavouring is light; according to sources it sits at the edge of the aromatic class, with a measured sweetness. Virginia leaf's natural sweetness and the dark leaves' soft body lead, with the topping not overtaking the leaf. It suits smokers steering clear of heavily flavoured aromatics but finding fully untopped blends too dry.
esoterica-tobacciana-ramsgate.o: Leaves a warm, lightly sweet, fruity tobacco aroma.

smokers-pride-mellow-taste.z: Smoker's Pride Mellow Taste is an American bulk blend that could be called essentially unflavored, combining light-colored sweet golden Virginia leaves with soft burley. Per the maker's description, it carries no noticeable top flavoring, so what stays in the mouth is limited to the leaves' natural sugar and nutty notes. The ribbon cut ensures easy packing and even burning. The blend's positioning matches the "mellow" descriptor the line takes its name from: a profile that doesn't tire the palate, has low nicotine, and can be smoked all day is the goal. Designed for smokers who don't want the sweet residue flavored tobaccos leave but also aren't looking for a heavy Virginia flake's acidity or a dark burley's fullness. Sold in large bags, it's a product meant for everyday use.
smokers-pride-mellow-taste.o: Leaves a plain tobacco scent reminiscent of dry hay and grain.

drew-estate-harvest-on-hudson.z: Harvest on Hudson is an aromatic blend in Drew Estate's pipe tobacco series. Golden Virginia leaves, burley and Danish-style black cavendish are brought together; a dark-colored, ribbon-cut mixture results. The topping is built on a fruity sweetness evoking green apple, combined with the softness cavendish brings. The body stays light to medium, so it draws the interest of newcomers to aromatic blends or those seeking a low-nicotine tobacco smokable all day. Per records, Drew Estate's pipe tobacco line has been withdrawn from the market; the blend can now only be found in old tins.
drew-estate-harvest-on-hudson.o: Leaves a fruity, sweetish scent evoking freshly cut apple.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-saratoga.z: Saratoga is a house blend The Country Squire tobacconist presents with a candied cherry flavoring. A pronounced cherry top flavoring is applied over a soft, Cavendish-forward base. The cherry comes through clearly on the smoke, with the tobacco's own taste staying in the background. It stays light on the palate, nicotine load is low, and the room note is sweet. Aimed at those seeking classic fruity aromatics and cherry flavoring in particular; a structure that newcomers to the pipe can also smoke comfortably.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-saratoga.o: Leaves a scent of candied cherry.

borkum-riff-mixture-with-cherry-cavendis.z: Borkum Riff Cherry Cavendish is a ribbon-cut aromatic where black Cavendish and Virginia meet in equal weight, topped with sweet cherry flavoring. The topping is apparent from the first opening and stays up front throughout the smoke; the leaf base itself stays light and sugary, keeping nicotine low. Borkum Riff launched in Sweden in 1962, taking its name from a lighthouse in the North Sea; the blends, originally produced for Swedish Match, are now prepared in Denmark under Scandinavian Tobacco Group. It's one of the brand's most widely available versions and remains in production. It suits smokers looking for a fruit-flavored, low-nicotine, easy-burning blend, as well as pipe beginners; its flavoring level is high compared to what smokers accustomed to unflavored Virginia or Latakia blends are used to.
borkum-riff-mixture-with-cherry-cavendis.o: Leaves a pronounced sweet cherry room note.

peretti-yuletide-2015.z: Yuletide is the name of the seasonal blend L.J. Peretti prepares in limited quantities every December; since the recipe changes each year, editions are not identical to one another. Records indicate the 2015 edition was built almost entirely on Virginia leaf, with a light plum note worked in on top. This construction keeps Virginia's bready, lemony sweetness at the center; the plum flavoring is measured enough that it doesn't push the blend into the aromatic category. It suits smokers who love near-unflavored Virginia blends and want to age seasonal editions.
peretti-yuletide-2015.o: Leaves a dried plum and baked grain aroma.

cornell-diehl-carolina-red-flake-2022.z: This straight Virginia flake, the 2022 edition of Cornell & Diehl's limited Carolina Red Flake series, could not have its content and character verified, as it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog.

pipesandcigars-com-cinnamon-roll.z: No independent source material could be found sufficient to fill out a specification for the pipesandcigars.com blend called Cinnamon Roll.
