barclay-rex-vincents.z: One of Barclay Rex's unflavored shop blends, named after Vincent, of the Nastri family who ran the business across generations; no adequate source describing its content could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-cherry-cream-f.z: Referred to as a cherry-topped, pressed and sliced aromatic from Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.; no reliable sourcing on its composition and production status could be found.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-cherry-cream-f.o: Leaves a cherry and cream aroma.

paul-olsen-sif.z: A Paul Olsen aromatic taking its name from Scandinavian mythology; no independent source describing its composition could be found.

dan-tobacco-bibo-biker-und-bolzer.z: One of Dan Tobacco's limited-distribution aromatic blends known under the BiBo name; no adequate source documenting its composition and character was found.

richs-maple-steamer.z: Maple Steamer is one of Rich's Cigar Store's house blends referred to as aromatic; no verifiable source could be found on its composition or flavoring.
richs-maple-steamer.o: No reliable information could be found on the room note.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-special-d.z: No independent source describing the content and cut of the light variety of the Special Dublin series could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-special-d.o: Recorded as leaving a light, sweet scent.

bufflehead-goldeneye-decoy.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Goldeneye Decoy under the Bufflehead brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

dan-tobacco-sligo-bay.z: Sligo Bay belongs to Dan Tobacco's Treasures of Ireland line, built on a high-natural-sugar Virginia leaf. After pressing, the leaf is hand-rubbed out and presented ready rubbed; a light, floral-direction topping is brushed over it. Because the topping is measured, Virginia's bready, grassy sweetness stays in front. It's light in nicotine, and the smoke is cool. It suits those seeking a tobacco somewhere between straight Virginia and aromatic, smokable throughout the day. It's distributed in 50-gram tins.
dan-tobacco-sligo-bay.o: Leaves a floral, lightly honeyed and sweet scent.

tobacco-trader-mild-cherry.z: A blend listed as a mild cherry-flavored house blend from the tobacconist Tobacco Trader; no leaf composition or production information has been found.
tobacco-trader-mild-cherry.o: Recorded as leaving a fruity aroma tied to cherry essence.

wesleys-no-24-black-cavendish.z: No. 24 Black Cavendish is an aromatic product South African tobacconist Wesley's offers under the Scandinavian and American type blends heading. As the name suggests, its foundation is black cavendish; cavendish is a preparation method where the leaf is darkened under steam, heat, and pressure, bringing its natural sugar to the fore. According to the maker's description, it's a dark-colored, smooth, easy-lighting, and distinctly aromatic tobacco aiming for a cool, not-too-full smoke. The cut is American-style granulated, which makes packing and lighting easy. It's not heavy in nicotine. It's a suitable option for smokers who enjoy sweet, fragrant tobaccos and seek a light everyday smoke that doesn't bite the mouth, as well as for newcomers to the pipe.
wesleys-no-24-black-cavendish.o: Leaves a sweet, dark-sugary, lightly toasted scent.

doctor-pipe-vanilla-cream.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Vanilla Cream, a pipe tobacco from Doctor Pipe.
doctor-pipe-vanilla-cream.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

4noggins-imagine.z: This is one of 4noggins' house blends; there is not enough available source material documenting its composition.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-captain-earles-p.z: Private Stock is an English mixture reportedly built by selecting and combining eight separate tobaccos. Latakia and stoved red Virginia come forward; Oriental leaves, Cavendish, and Perique join them. The mixture is pressed and presented as a crumble cake, opened by hand before filling. Here, Latakia smoke stands less as a dominant note and more as a layer balanced by Virginia's dark sweetness; Perique plays a spicy role, and Cavendish a softening one. Because it traces a more moderate profile than the line's other members, it's considered suitable for all-day smoking. On the taste side, tones evoking smoked meat and toasted wheat bread are noted. It carries no flavoring. It suits those looking for a complex but measured English mixture, and smokers seeking a starting point before moving to the line's heavier Latakia blends.
hermit-tobacco-works-co-captain-earles-p.o: Leaves an aroma of freshly baked bread, cut dry hay, and light leather.

argento-vanilla-mixture.z: Argento Vanilla Mixture is the vanilla-flavored blend in the Argento line, produced in Argentina. Its base holds Virginia and Burley leaf; the flavoring is built on vanilla, and it's sold in 50-gram pouches. With its low nicotine load and pronounced vanilla note, the blend is the line's most clearly aromatic product. It suits those new to aromatic blends as well as smokers looking for a sweet tobacco with an obviously perceptible flavoring.
argento-vanilla-mixture.o: Leaves a pronounced vanilla and sweet-dough room note.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrugs-best-make.z: Surbrug's Best Make is a blend counted among Wilke's oldest recipes, carried under the name of Surbrug, one of New York's long-established tobacconists. According to the maker's account, Virginia and Burley leaves are combined with unflavored black cavendish, topped with a generous amount of Latakia. The result is a medium-strength, soft, and full mixture in the English tradition; since no flavoring is added, the taste comes entirely from the leaf itself. It suits smokers used to medium nicotine who seek classic blends centered on Latakia smoke.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrugs-best-make.o: Leaves a heavy scent reminiscent of wood smoke and wet earth.

just-for-him-bombadil.z: One of the house blends the Just For Him tobacconist prepares at its own counter; no independent source could be found on its contents or character.

tabac-turc-yayladag-cikolatali.z: Yayladağ Çikolatalı (Chocolate) is Tabac Turc's Oriental blend prepared with a chocolate casing. Its content includes Yayladağı, Bitlis, and İzmir leaf along with a trace amount of latakia. It is offered as flake; the slices are heavily fermented, with surfaces that look close to sugared. The moisture level is suitable for packing and needs no additional airing. Opening the pack releases an intense cocoa and chocolate scent, though the chocolate taste on the smoke is milder than that scent suggests. Nicotine is very light and the taste is low in intensity. In a wide-bowled pipe suited to flake packing, a full bowl gives two and a half to three hours of smoking. It suits smokers who enjoy mild tobaccos and want to try flavored domestic products.
tabac-turc-yayladag-cikolatali.o: Leaves a scent of cocoa and sweet fermented leaf in the room.

cornell-diehl-midnight-orchard.z: Midnight Orchard is the first aromatic blend released in Cornell & Diehl's Small Batch series. Its composition includes 2023-harvest darkened bright Virginias, 2019- and 2023-harvest lemon-colored bright Virginias, 2019- and 2022-harvest Old Belt red Virginias, and real St. James Perique from 31 Farms. Head blender Jeremy Reeves traces the blend's starting point to the orangey, floral scent the kumquat tree in front of his house leaves on summer nights. In the profile, dark fruit and citrus notes intertwine with an earthy base and warm spice; traces of vanilla and forest fruit are kept measured enough to highlight the tobaccos' own taste rather than mask it. Despite being aromatic, since the Virginia-and-Perique structure is preserved, it's aimed at smokers who don't expect heavy sugar from cased blends and want natural tobacco character.
cornell-diehl-midnight-orchard.o: Leaves a scent of garden fruit, citrus, and warm spice.

peterson-sunset-breeze.z: Sunset Breeze is an aromatic built from Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish leaf. It is given an amaretto, or almond-based, topping; Burley's natural nutty taste works in the same direction as the almond note, producing a lightly tart sweetness. It is moderate in nicotine, a blend suited to after-dinner smoking. It suits those looking for sweet, nutty aromatics as well as newcomers to the pipe; those seeking an unflavored tobacco taste will find the topping pronounced. It is grouped with Sweet Killarney in Peterson's aromatic line.
peterson-sunset-breeze.o: Leaves a sweet almond liqueur and marzipan aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-happy-brown-bogie-uns.z: This product, referred to as Happy Bogie or Brown Bogie, is a traditional rope tobacco where fire-cured and air-cured dark leaves are twisted and pressed into rope form. Sold unsliced in this form, the smoker cuts the rope to their own thickness, rubs it out, and airs it. The smoke is full, smoky, and woody; nicotine is very high. It carries no flavoring essence, with the taste coming entirely from the leaf's curing method. Suited to those with rope-tobacco experience accustomed to smoking slowly and in small amounts; heavy going for a beginner smoker.
gawith-hoggarth-co-happy-brown-bogie-uns.o: Leaves the smoke-and-wood aroma of fire-cured leaf in the room.

drucquer-sons-levant-mixture.z: Levant Mixture is the fullest blend in the Drucquer & Sons line and designed in Balkan style. Plenty of small-leaf Turkish tobacco and Cyprus latakia are combined with aged red Virginia and a bit of light Virginia for sweetness. It's ribbon cut, so the blend can be smoked straight from the tin. Latakia's woody, smoky sootiness builds the flavor core; the orientals add a buttery, dry, spicy layer, while Virginia lays a measured sweetness beneath this weight. It's not merely a latakia pile but a balanced, if high-dosed, mixture; it suits smokers accustomed to heavy English and Balkan blends. The blend is among the most cited of the recipes reorganized from the Drucquer archive.
drucquer-sons-levant-mixture.o: A heavy incense, pine-wood smoke and spice scent spreads through the room and lingers long.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-188.z: Wilke No. 188 is an English-style blend the maker states it re-created from old Surbrug ledgers; no verifiable details could be found regarding its composition and cut.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-188.o: No confirmed description of the room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-irish-blessing.z: Irish Blessing is an all-black, ribbon-cut aromatic prepared on a Green River black cavendish base, flavored with honey and the Irish Mist liqueur aroma Cornell & Diehl frequently uses. Honey's sweetness and the liqueur's herbal, sharp edge hold through to the end of the smoke. The texture is oily and creamy, leaving a full feeling in the mouth; nicotine is low. It suits those looking for a pronouncedly flavored, sweet, liqueur-themed blend.
cornell-diehl-irish-blessing.o: Leaves a honeyed, liqueur-like, lightly herbal sweet aroma.

tordenskjold-special-blend.z: No sufficient source documenting the composition and character of Tordenskjold Special Blend has been found.
tordenskjold-special-blend.o: No reliable source describing the room note has been found.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-richmond-navy-.z: Richmond Navy Cut is a light-colored flake blend prepared entirely from matured Virginia leaves left in their natural state. The pressed leaf is cut into thin slices; no flavoring is applied. It has long been available in the European market in 50-gram packs. Its taste rests on Virginia's own sweetness; sugar and herbal sides come forward, with strength staying moderate. Being a flake, it needs rubbing out or folding before packing and rewards a slow smoking pace. It's aimed at smokers who love unflavored Virginia flake and want a straightforward leaf taste.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-richmond-navy-.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay and baked bread on a sweetish base.

straus-tobacco-88.z: One of the house blends from Straus Tobacconist, operating in Cincinnati since 1880; no verifiable source describing its composition could be found.

house-of-calabash-first-smoke-of-the-day.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for House of Calabash's First Smoke of the Day - Reserve Blend, so its content and character could not be recorded.

tabac-turc-blackship-chery-blend.z: Blackship Chery Blend is an aromatic blend released under the Blackship name and, according to records, produced by Tabac Turc. Its body is built on Oriental, i.e., Turkish, tobacco, cut as broken flake. Alongside a light cherry essence closer to sour cherry, it carries a caramel and liqueur- or whisky-leaning flavoring, giving a taste that shifts between tart and sweet.
tabac-turc-blackship-chery-blend.o: Leaves the spicy, sweetish scent of Oriental tobacco alongside a light sour-cherry essence.

john-cotton-john-cottons-number-1-mild-r.z: John Cotton's No. 1 is a light English blend built from matured bright Virginias, small-leaved Orientals, and a small amount of Cyprian Latakia. The original line was withdrawn from the market years ago; the blend was recreated by Russ Ouellette based on examination of old tins and the remembered character of the 1970s version. Here Latakia isn't dominant — it's kept at a woody, lightly smoky seasoning level, letting Virginia's sweetness and the Oriental's dry spice come forward. Strength is low and the smoke is moderate. A middle-ground profile for those looking for something between bright Virginia flake and a Latakia-heavy English blend, and suited to a morning pipe or all-day smoking.
john-cotton-john-cottons-number-1-mild-r.o: Leaves a measured smoke mixing light woody char with dry hay.

per-g-jensen-three-swords.z: Three Swords is a Virginia-perique blend within the Viking Collection series released under Per G. Jensen's name. Its base is built from select red and light-colored Virginia leaves, topped with genuine perique from Louisiana's St. James parish. To expand on the classic VaPer mold, the blender also added rustica and fire-cured Kentucky leaf to the mixture. The Virginia leaf carries a bready, fruity sweetness from natural sugar, over which the perique layers a spice line toward pepper and dried plum. Rustica and Kentucky pull both the body and the nicotine load upward, adding a measured smokiness to the blend. It suits smokers seeking the familiar Virginia-perique structure in a fuller, smokier form.
per-g-jensen-three-swords.o: Leaves a peppery, lightly smoky scent following dried-fruit sweetness.

hearth-home-latham-circle.z: Latham Circle is an aromatic blend in Hearth & Home's Mid-Town series, named after places around Albany. Quality Burley's mild, nutty taste is paired with Virginia's sweetness, topped with a maple-syrup note and a small amount of rum. A ribbon-cut, light-to-medium bodied recipe where the topping is kept light enough not to mask the leaf. Suited to smokers who like the maple-and-rum combination and want a measured aromatic for everyday smoking. The Mid-Town series was created to offer more affordably priced options.
hearth-home-latham-circle.o: Leaves a sweet, warm aroma of maple syrup and light rum.

b-b-tobacconists-llc-carolina-home-blend.z: One of the bulk-sold house blends from B&B Tobacconists in Asheville, North Carolina; no adequate source on its content could be found.

mcclelland-emperor-leopaldos-special-vir.z: No sufficient independent source describing the contents of this Virginia blend, apparently prepared in a limited run, could be found.
mcclelland-emperor-leopaldos-special-vir.o: Records indicate it leaves a mildly sweet aroma typical of Virginia blends.

cornell-diehl-oriental-silk.z: Oriental Silk is a blend Cornell & Diehl prepared as a Latakia-free Oriental mixture. Per the maker's listing, Perique, bright Virginia flake, Oriental (Turkish) flake, and bright Virginia ribbon are brought together; using different cuts together gives the mixture textural variety. Since there's no Latakia, the Oriental leaves' grassy, lightly tart, spicy character is felt directly; Virginia builds the sweet base, while Perique sharpens the edges with a plum-and-pepper accent. Room note stays light. Suited to smokers avoiding smoky blends who want to follow the Oriental leaf's own taste.
cornell-diehl-oriental-silk.o: Leaves a dry, spicy, lightly tart leaf scent.

barclay-rex-hampton-bay.z: Listed among Barclay Rex's shop blends as an English-style mixture; no independent source detailing its composition could be found.
barclay-rex-hampton-bay.o: According to records it leaves a wood- and spice-forward room note.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-kraken-.z: Kraken Plug is produced by stemming rested red Virginia leaf and pressing it into a plug, then dressing it with dark rum. It's sold as a roughly 50-gram bulk plug and is part of Ken Byron Ventures' nautical-themed lineup. Because plug tobacco is prepared by slicing and rubbing out, it leaves the smoker in control of the cut, and its tight structure gives a slow, cool burn. Red Virginia's dark-fruit, molasses-like line stands out, and the rum deepens that sweetness. Aimed at smokers willing to work with plug and slice cuts who want a medium-bodied Virginia.
ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-kraken-.o: Leaves a dense tobacco aroma mixed with dark rum and molasses-like fruit.

mac-baren-halberg-green.z: Not enough information could be found in the manufacturer's current catalog or verifiable independent sources about this member of the Halberg series.

ashton-consummate-gentleman.z: Consummate Gentleman is Ashton's ribbon-cut English mixture. A touch of Latakia is added alongside Virginia, Maryland, and Burley leaf; the maker's description also notes unflavored Cavendish in the blend. Here Latakia isn't the main character but a seasoning element. Body is medium, and it conveys the traditional English style without drowning it in smoky intensity; Burley and Maryland set a dry, nutty base while Virginia's sweetness comes forward. It suits those new to Latakia blends or looking for a measured English mixture for everyday smoking. It's produced for Ashton by Kohlhase & Kopp.
ashton-consummate-gentleman.o: Leaves a measured, lightly smoky room note close to dry leaf and baked bread.

fribourg-treyer-golden-mixture.z: Golden Mixture is the untopped Virginia blend of the Fribourg & Treyer series, presented as a ribbon cut. The blend, which uses light and matured Virginia leaves together, brings out bread, dry-grass, and meadow sweetness, accompanied by a tart citrus edge reminiscent of orange peel and a lightly spiced finish. Thanks to the ribbon cut, it is easy to fill and light, making this untopped Virginia accessible even to those unaccustomed to plug and flake forms. The nicotine load is below medium; it suits smokers wanting to get to know the untopped Virginia character in a plain way, looking for a blend suitable for all-day smoking.
fribourg-treyer-golden-mixture.o: Leaves an aroma of dry grass, fresh bread, and a lightly tart orange peel.

iwan-ries-british-full.z: This blend, part of Iwan Ries's English-style line, does not appear in the shop's current British Blends listing, and no verifiable source about its composition could be found.

de-la-concha-old-faithful.z: This is a shop blend from the De La Concha tobacconist, noted as straight Virginia type; no independent source stating the Virginia grades used could be found.
de-la-concha-old-faithful.o: No reliable record could be found for the room note.

clan-shaw-big-apple.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Big Apple.

robert-mcconnell-red-roses.z: There is not enough independent source material on Red Roses, cited among Robert McConnell's aromatic blends.

tabakfabrik-roth-jabuca-danish-blend.z: Jabuca Danish Blend is the Danish-style aromatic member of Tabakfabrik Roth's Jabuca series, built with Cavendish tobaccos. The maker describes the blend as fruity, fragrant, fresh, and soft; the Virginia body is mellowed with black Cavendish and sweetened with a light fruit essence. It is filled at a medium cut (about 3.5 mm) and offered in a resealable freshness pouch. It suits smokers looking for low-nicotine, sweet, easy-burning aromatics who don't mind a pronounced room note.
tabakfabrik-roth-jabuca-danish-blend.o: Leaves a fruity, sweet, and fresh scent.

f-j-burrus-s-a-clever.z: F.J. Burrus S.A. is a tobacco company with Swiss origins; no verifiable source could be found regarding the composition and character of this blend.

schneiderwind-aachen-2012.z: The 2012 edition of Schneiderwind's annual blend series released under the Aachen name; no sufficient source documenting its content could be found.
schneiderwind-aachen-2012.o: Recorded as leaving a sweetly cased scent.

gallaher-limited-condor-black-xx.z: This is a blend called Condor Black XX among the pipe tobaccos of Gallaher Limited, founded by Tom Gallaher in Derry in 1857 and later absorbed into Japan Tobacco; no reliable source could be found on the blend's composition and character.

iwan-ries-irc-virginia-flake.z: IRC Virginia Flake is a single-varietal Virginia blend, part of Iwan Ries & Co.'s own-name flake line. Per the maker's description, it's prepared from untoasted Virginia leaves and has a mild, lightly sweet character. Since it's pressed and sliced, it gives smokers the freedom to fill it either rubbed out or folded. In this type of unflavored Virginia flake, the taste comes from the leaf's own sugar; because it can sting the tongue if smoked too fast over a hot bowl, it calls for a slow, cool pace. It's aimed at smokers looking for a plain Virginia, free of Latakia or flavoring, that rewards aging.
iwan-ries-irc-virginia-flake.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of dry straw and baked bread crust.

iwan-ries-budget-green.z: No verifiable source could be found for this aromatic blend registered under the Iwan Ries name.

cobblestone-limited-pressed-no-22-crumbl.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Cobblestone pipe tobacco named Limited Pressed No. 22 Crumble Kake, so the blend's content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

just-for-him-wifes-bane.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Just For Him's Wife's Bane blend.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-erinmore-.z: Erinmore Mixture is the ribbon-cut aromatic counterpart of the same brand's flake. It is built on black cavendish and virginia; the producer does not disclose the recipe, and it is presented in 100-gram tins. Like Erinmore Flake, this blend too is produced by Scandinavian Tobacco Group. Packing, lighting, and smoking it are effortless; it burns slowly and gives long bowls. The casing is fruity in the direction of citrus and pineapple, leaving an easily recognizable taste distinctive to the brand. Nicotine load is low. Suited to smokers seeking a light, classic aromatic they can smoke all day.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-erinmore-.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity scent in the direction of citrus and pineapple.

samuel-gawith-chocolate-flake.z: Chocolate Flake is one of Samuel Gawith's Virginia-forward flakes; burley and a small amount of latakia also feature in the blend, with a chocolate casing applied on top. As with other SG flakes, tin moisture is high; airing before smoking directly affects ease of lighting and flavor. The smoke is rich, medium in flavor and nicotine. The chocolate casing is pronounced enough to move ahead of the tobacco's natural taste. Even smoked slowly it can cause moisture buildup at the pipe bottom, so keeping a pipe cleaner on hand is advised. Suited to smokers accustomed to cased flake smoking who seek a chocolate-evoking sweetness.
samuel-gawith-chocolate-flake.o: Leaves a scent evoking cocoa and sweet dough.

7-20-4-dexters-secret.z: Dexter's Secret is the English-style entry in the 7-20-4 Briary Blends line. Virginia and Burley leaf, along with Perique from the St. James region, are added over a generous amount of Cyprus Latakia. The mixture is pressed, cut into flake, and put into tins as broken flake, so it only needs to be rubbed out by hand before packing. The line was introduced in 2023. In the taste description, cream, soot, and citrus tones are followed by a dark, fig-like fruit sweetness; the Perique adds a spicy edge to that sweetness. Body is medium, so it isn't on the heavy end among Latakia blends. It suits those looking for a balanced English mixture smokable any time of day and those just warming up to Latakia.
7-20-4-dexters-secret.o: Leaves a sharp, woody room note reminiscent of pine smoke, soot, and leather.

former-birds-eye-flake.z: Bird's Eye Flake is part of the tobacco line carrying the name of the Danish pipe maker Former (Hans Nielsen), who has made pipes since 1956. Names in the line come from the grain patterns in briar burl; the bird's-eye figure is one of the names carrying on this tradition. The blend's backbone is built from selected Virginia leaves, with perique added as a spicy accent colour. The leaves are pressed in traditional layer-by-layer fashion, rested, and cut into flakes.
former-birds-eye-flake.o: Leaves an aroma of dry grass and light tart fruit.

cornell-diehl-firebird-flake.z: Firebird Flake is a pressed blend from Cornell & Diehl's Small Batch series, periodically reprinted. It contains three separate red Virginias, aged Samsun- and Izmir-type Oriental leaves, and two different fire-cured Kentucky varieties. Per the manufacturer's data, Orientals make up roughly forty-three percent of the blend, with fire-cured Kentucky accounting for close to five percent; the name itself references the fire-curing method. The flavor profile leads with citrus, wood smoke, and green peppercorn traces, carrying a tangy, herbal, salty-spiced character. Thanks to the balance struck between the fire-cured leaf's smoke and the sun-cured Orientals' spice, no single component overwhelms the others. Ranking high in both nicotine and flavor intensity, it suits experienced smokers and those seeking full-bodied, unflavored blends.
cornell-diehl-firebird-flake.o: Leaves an aroma of wood smoke and spiced grass.

a-c-petersen-caledonian-virginia-flake.z: Caledonian Virginia Flake is the straight Virginia slice in A & C Petersen's Caledonian line. It's obtained by pressing and slicing unflavored Virginia leaf; its sweetness comes entirely from the leaf itself and the maturation during pressing. Since it's a flake cut, it's packed by rubbing out or folding, and it burns slowly. Its production has ended; examples found on the market today are mostly aged old tins — indeed, tins dated 1992 appear in records. It's a blend aimed at users who like unflavored Virginia flakes and enjoy patient, slow smoking.
a-c-petersen-caledonian-virginia-flake.o: Leaves a sweetish room note leaning toward dry hay and baked bread.

philip-morris-bond-street.z: This is one of the pipe tobaccos Philip Morris sold in the twentieth century that has since gone out of production; no sufficient sources documenting the blend's content could be found.

drucquer-sons-kings-fool.z: King's Fool is an English mixture where light-colored warm-air-cured leaf and full red Virginia build the backbone, with a small amount of latakia added on top. The mixture also includes a small proportion of burley, cavendish and St. James perique; the blend is pressed and then sliced into flake. Because the latakia proportion is kept low, the taste line brings forward Virginia sweetness and burley's dry, nutty texture, while the smoke stays as a fine layer in the background. Like the rest of the line, this mixture was also reorganized from old Drucquer recipes, and per records is produced at Cornell & Diehl through Gregory Pease's work. Because it's light in nicotine, it suits those newly moving into latakia-containing mixtures and those who enjoy preparing sliced tobacco, seeking an all-day English mixture.
drucquer-sons-kings-fool.o: Gives off a scent carrying bready sweetness, with a fine trace of smoke and spice behind it.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-no-6-shag-coco.z: A cocoa-flavored ribbon-cut blend belonging to Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s numbered Kendal shag series; no independent sourcing detailing its composition and character could be found.

bufflehead-mottled-duck.z: Bufflehead was a brand producing small batches in the United States in the early 2000s, naming its blends after waterfowl; since no independent source describing this blend's content and character could be found, the entry has been left incomplete.

lane-limited-captain-black-black-sea.z: Recorded as a blend tied to Lane Limited's Captain Black package series; not enough sources could be found to document its composition.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrugs-jackson.z: Surbrug's Jackson is a Latakia-based Wilke record topped with black cavendish and Yenidje Turkish leaf. The composition includes black cavendish, Burley, Latakia, Yenidje Oriental, Perique, and Virginia. Smoky, woody, and lightly musty-sweet Cyprian Latakia is the most prominent element; Tennessee Burley, giving roasted-walnut and nut tones, plays a supporting role. Spicy, plummy, raisin-noted Perique is a significant seasoning. Due to its unflavored construction and high Latakia ratio, it offers a full-bodied, smoke-forward smoke. It suits smokers accustomed to the English and Balkan style who seek a spicy layer. Wilke carries this record in bulk; stock status varies seasonally.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrugs-jackson.o: A dried-plum and spice tone mixes into the wood-smoke and soot scent.

torben-dansk-syrian-latakia.z: No sufficient source documenting the composition and character of Syrian Latakia registered under the Torben Dansk name has been found.
torben-dansk-syrian-latakia.o: No reliable source describing the room note has been found.

peter-heinrichs-club-tabak-gelb.z: Peter Heinrichs Club Tabak Gelb is reportedly counted among the firm's aromatic group; no accessible manufacturer or retailer description documenting its content, cut, and flavoring could be found.

lane-limited-captain-black-midnight-gold.z: Recorded as an aromatic blend tied to the Captain Black series; not enough sources could be found about its contents.

p-lorillard-peter-weinig-no-9.z: A pipe tobacco registered under the P. Lorillard name, long out of production; no usable source describing the blend's composition and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-sliced-brown-m.z: A malt-whisky-flavored sliced blend belonging to Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Kendal series; no independent sourcing detailing its composition and character could be found.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-sliced-brown-m.o: Leaves a dry, sweet aroma reminiscent of oak and malt whisky.

jacks-tobacco-old-brookfield.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of Old Brookfield, under the Jack's Tobacco name, could be found.
jacks-tobacco-old-brookfield.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

brigham-enterprises-inc-tudor-mixture.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named Tudor Mixture under the Brigham Enterprises Inc. brand could be found.

mac-baren-brigg-coco-ananas.z: Brigg is a pipe tobacco line prepared for many years by the German manufacturer Planta; with the brand's move to Mac Baren, production shifted to Denmark. Coco-Ananas has appeared on shelves under the short name "Brigg CA" following EU regulations restricting the use of flavor names on tobacco packaging. The blend is made by combining yellow and golden Virginia leaves from Brazil and Zimbabwe with black cavendish twice fermented by the traditional method; the cut is a long-fiber ribbon. The coconut and pineapple casing is the blend's defining note; beneath it sits the Virginia leaf's own sugary sweetness. Its body is medium and its taste is soft, suitable for any pipe size. A blend for smokers seeking an easy-smoking, exotic-fruit-flavored Danish-style aromatic.
mac-baren-brigg-coco-ananas.o: Leaves a coconut and ripe pineapple room note.

w-d-h-o-wills-capstan-navy-cut-full.z: No independent source sufficient to complete a record could be found regarding W.D. & H.O. Wills's Capstan Navy Cut Full blend, so this entry remains incomplete.

lane-limited-edgeworth-ready-rubbed.z: Edgeworth Ready-Rubbed is a classic burley-based blend produced in the US for many years; in its final period of production it was made by Lane Limited. Its recipe rests on mature burley and selected light golden Virginia leaf; a measured casing is applied on top, with the old recipe reportedly including Jamaican rum. Since the pressed leaf is cut ready to be rubbed by hand, it gets its name from this preparation and packs easily into a pipe. In the smoke, cocoa, molasses and nutty sides come forward; nicotine is medium, and the casing doesn't override tobacco character. A blend for those seeking a cased but not aromatic burley to smoke all day. The brand went out of production in 2004; once Lane lost the rights to the name, it carried on a similar blend under the name Lane Limited Ready Rubbed.
lane-limited-edgeworth-ready-rubbed.o: Leaves a roasted-nut, cocoa and light-rum room note.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-pom-holiday.z: Pom Holiday is an aromatic prepared by J. M. Boswell in 2009, taking its name from pomegranate. Per records, the blend was born from the manufacturer's idea of carrying a favorite fruit into tobacco; the pomegranate aroma is set over a cavendish-forward base. The blend is light-bodied, its aroma pronounced. Nicotine stays low, and it burns cool. A distinctive option for smokers seeking a flavor line less common among fruity aromatics.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-pom-holiday.o: A tart pomegranate aroma spreads into the room together with a sweet cavendish note.

sobranie-of-london-balkan-sobranie-reser.z: A pure Virginia blend from Sobranie of London's Reserve Blend line, presented in a rubbed-leaf form. Like the rest of the line, it has long been out of production, and no source giving a detailed description of the blend could be found.

georgetown-tobacco-reverie.z: Reverie is the best-selling mixture among Georgetown Tobacco's loose-sold aromatic house blends. According to the maker's description, it brings together dark Cavendish pieces, light-colored Virginia leaf, and smoothing Burley; its sweetness is pronounced but kept subtle enough not to be pinned to a single topping. The Cavendish-and-Burley combination keeps nicotine at a moderate-to-light level, while Virginia leaves a light fruity tartness in the background. Suited to smokers who steer away from heavy syrupy aromatics but still want a sweet line, as well as anyone wanting a mild shop blend for all-day smoking.
georgetown-tobacco-reverie.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, caramel-like, mild tobacco aroma.

von-eicken-private-club-vanilla.z: Private Club Vanilla is a blend in German producer Joh. von Eicken's light aromatic line. Its base is soft black Cavendish obtained by fermenting sweet Brazilian Virginia; this is joined by bright Zimbabwean Virginia, and the mixture is flavored with vanilla extract. Because the vanilla dosing is kept measured, the sweetness does not overpower the leaf; the blend offers a low-nicotine smoke with little bite on the tongue. This makes it an all-day aromatic, appealing to smokers who don't expect heavy syrupy sweetness from an aromatic but haven't moved to unflavored tobacco either. The ribbon cut makes for easy lighting and burning; records note that Von Eicken blends are sensitive to moisture balance, so storage conditions noticeably affect the smoke.
von-eicken-private-club-vanilla.o: Leaves a lightly vanilla, sweetish pastry-like aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-old-vienna.z: Records present this as a Sutliff aromatic built on burley and black cavendish, flavored in multiple stages; no sufficient independent source detailing its casing could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-old-vienna.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly caramel scent.

mcclelland-st-james-woods.z: St. James Woods is a Virginia-Perique blend in McClelland's Personal Reserve line. Red and stoved Virginia leaves are presented as broken flake; the Louisiana Perique share in the mixture is considerable. Turkish-language sources note that resting the tin for two to three days after opening settles the moisture and flavor. In the smoke, mature Virginia's sweetness interweaves with Perique's dark-fruit, spicy sharpness; body runs medium to full. The high Perique share can weigh on you with repeated, long smoking sessions. Suited to smokers wanting a pronounced Perique presence along the Virginia-Perique axis. McClelland stopped production in 2018.
mcclelland-st-james-woods.o: Leaves a sharp, tangy, and spicy aroma, with a dark-fruit note behind it.

players-navy-cut-flake.z: Navy Cut Flake is a classic navy-cut flake in which light and dark Virginia leaf are combined with nutty Burley and cold-pressed. The slices carry golden veins over a brown ground; a small amount of rum is used during pressing, leaving a dark sugar-like sweetness without overtaking the tobacco. On the taste side, Virginia's herbal, tangy, cooked-fruit-like character leads, while Burley fills the gaps and rounds off the texture. Nicotine stays more measured than expected; it offers a cool, plain smoke, so even those unaccustomed to preparing flake can use it without difficulty. It suits smokers looking for a Virginia-heavy, very lightly flavored everyday flake, and those wanting to get to know pressed tobaccos in the English-navy tradition. The navy-cut name historically comes from sailors rolling and slicing tobacco into a rope.
players-navy-cut-flake.o: Leaves a light brown-sugar trace beneath a herbal, citrusy tobacco aroma.

milan-tobacconists-cherry-velvet.z: Cherry Velvet is a house blend among Milan Tobacconists' cherry aromatics. Toasted black cavendish, soft burley, and sweet light-colored virginia leaves are brought together; according to the maker's description the mixture is flavored with a generous amount of cherry extract. The leaf selection builds a light, soft base, with the cherry casing defining the character. An entry geared toward those looking for classic American cherry aromatics who don't mind a pronounced casing.
milan-tobacconists-cherry-velvet.o: Leaves a pronounced ripe-cherry aroma, with a sweet sugary trace lingering behind.

a-c-petersen-jubilee.z: No adequate source describing the content and character of A & C Petersen's blend called Jubilee could be found.

milan-tobacconists-single-malt.z: Single Malt is an aromatic in which a body combining bright and dark tobaccos is flavored with whisky from Scotland's Highland region. The casing is the blend's most defining feature. The tobacco's own sweetness runs alongside the grainy, lightly smoky association of the whisky. A shop blend prepared for smokers experimenting with alcohol-cased aromatics.
milan-tobacconists-single-malt.o: Leaves a grainy, lightly alcoholic aroma reminiscent of malt whisky.

cornell-diehl-bright-virginia-ribbon.z: Bright Virginia Ribbon is a single-varietal component tobacco: high-quality golden Virginia leaf from North Carolina's "Old Belt" region, cut as ribbon. The leaf's natural sugar content is high, its oil content relatively low; this gives a pronounced sweetness accompanied by a light citrus accent. It is both a Virginia that can be smoked on its own and a leaf that can be used as a base or sweetening component in home blends, commonly paired with burley in particular. It suits smokers wanting to get to know unflavored, straight Virginia taste and those building their own blends. As with high-sugar bright leaves generally, it needs to be smoked slowly and cool.
cornell-diehl-bright-virginia-ribbon.o: Leaves a sweet-hay aroma with a light orange-peel note.

gettysburg-cigar-company-general-chamber.z: Belongs to the series of shop blends named after generals from the battle, produced by the Gettysburg Cigar Company in Gettysburg, Pennsylvania; no verifiable sourcing describing its composition could be found.
gettysburg-cigar-company-general-chamber.o: No record of the room aroma could be found.

westgate-yellow.z: No confirmed composition description from maker or retailer could be found for Yellow, referred to as the plain Virginia-character member of the Westgate series; according to records, the Westgate name was used on tobaccos produced by McConnell for a Danish importer.
westgate-yellow.o: According to the records, the room note has not been documented.

sutliff-tobacco-company-appalachian-trai.z: Appalachian Trail is an aromatic blend from Sutliff's long-running Private Stock line. Per the maker's description, its base rests on Virginia leaves and the composition includes perique; a rum-and-peach-direction flavoring is applied on top. As with the rest of the line, it's presented ribbon cut and sold in bulk. The blend is described as a medium-intensity aromatic where the topping is pronounced in scent and taste, while the Virginia sweetness and perique's fruity sharpness beneath it are still perceptible. Nicotine stays light. Suited to smokers who smoke aromatics but don't want to stick solely to the vanilla-cherry axis, and who want to try fruit and liquor notes alongside perique. Like most of Sutliff's Private Stock line, this blend has been discontinued.
sutliff-tobacco-company-appalachian-trai.o: Leaves a scent of sweet peach and rum.

paul-olsen-special-blend-33-lakrids-liqu.z: A Paul Olsen aromatic flavored with licorice root, as indicated by the Danish word "lakrids" in its name; no independent source documenting its tobacco composition could be found.

smokers-haven-american-best-blend.z: A blend appearing in the catalog of the Ohio-based Smokers' Haven tobacconist; sufficient sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

mission-pipe-shop-barrister.z: Barrister is one of the house blends prepared at Mission Pipe Shop's San Jose store; no accessible source describing its composition could be found.

tobacco-merchant-twilight.z: The Twilight blend, classed as English-style, from the tobacconist Tobacco Merchant; no verifiable source on its Latakia proportion, cut, or production period has been found.
tobacco-merchant-twilight.o: Thought to leave a smoky aroma typical of English-style blends; a detailed description has not been found in records.

hearth-home-virginia-spice.z: Virginia Spice is a blend based on the clean, sweet spice of matured Virginia leaves, adding Perique's plum-and-pepper seasoning to it. The component that sets it apart from an ordinary Virginia-Perique mixture is the maduro cigar leaf added to give it body and a creamy texture. There's also a light sweet top note. The cigar leaf thickens the thin, flat smoke typical of Virginia-Perique blends; because of this, the blend is a variation built for smokers who find the classic VaPer style lacking body. It suits those not unfamiliar with cigar tobacco's earthy taste.
hearth-home-virginia-spice.o: An earthy layer from the cigar leaf is added to the sweet Virginia aroma.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-mick-mcqu.z: The cube-cut version of the Mick McQuaid brand; the brand's origin traces to the P. J. Carroll firm in Dundalk in 1889 and takes its name from the pipe-smoking character in Lynam's stories. No sufficient primary source describing the blend's composition and flavor character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-no-6-unscented.z: The unscented version within Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s numbered Kendal shag series; records indicate it is Virginia-forward, but no independent sourcing to confirm the blend's composition could be found.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-no-6-unscented.o: Leaves a dry-hay and burnt-leaf aroma.

old-virginia-tobacco-co-manassas.z: Manassas is one of the aromatic bulk blends from Old Virginia Tobacco Co.; no published source describing its composition could be found.

bennington-tobacconist-no-05-english-lux.z: No. 05 English Luxury is one of Bennington Tobacconist's shop blends. Golden-brown Burley of Kentucky and Tennessee origin is combined with heat-cured Virginia ribbon and Cyprus Latakia. This sets a Latakia-based skeleton over Burley's dry, earthy body. Per the maker's description, the blend's distinguishing trait is that despite having a pleasant aroma, it smokes fuller-bodied and cooler than most aromatics. It can serve as a middle step for smokers wanting to move away from heavily flavored tobaccos but not yet ready for a full Latakia bomb. Its ribbon cut makes packing and lighting easy.
bennington-tobacconist-no-05-english-lux.o: Roasted hazelnut and dry bread notes layer over a faint smoky room note.

motzek-p-cones.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called P-Cones could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-blue-danube.z: Blue Danube is a Sutliff Private Stock blend named after Johann Strauss's famous waltz. Its composition includes bright golden cavendish, white burley, and sweet Virginia leaves; a rum-and-vanilla-direction flavoring is applied on top. Like the whole Private Stock line, this blend is built on the work of Carl McAllister, the brand's longtime master blender. Using golden cavendish instead of black sets the blend's color and taste apart from classic dark aromatics: the sweetness stays lighter and brighter, while white burley adds a dry body. With low nicotine, it's structured for all-day smoking. Suited to smokers seeking a non-heavy rum-vanilla aromatic. It was sold as ribbon-cut bulk and is no longer in production.
sutliff-tobacco-company-blue-danube.o: Leaves a scent of sweet vanilla and rum.

bosphorus-english-mixture.z: Bosphorus English Mixture is a ribbon-cut English mixture where Turkish tobaccos are added to a Virginia and Cyprus Latakia base. In the blend's first release, a light whiskey aroma accompanied the Virginia, Turkish tobaccos and Latakia; the recipe was completely reworked in 2016. In the new version the Latakia proportion is kept around 30%, burley is not used, and additions such as flavored cavendish are not included. Strength is between light and medium, flavor between medium and intense; it gives a cool smoke at a slow pace. Its moisture level is ready for direct filling, and the smoke becomes cooler when rested. Suited to smokers who want Latakia in moderation and want to experience Turkish tobacco's spicy sweetness together with Latakia, and to those new to Latakia blends.
bosphorus-english-mixture.o: A sharp smoke and burnt-wood aroma from the Latakia settles into the room.

charatan-flake.z: Charatan Flake is a light-colored Virginia flake prepared in the line as the counterpart to Dunhill's Light Flake. After pressing and slicing, the leaf keeps its golden-straw tones; no casing is used. A lemony tartness sits alongside a baked-bread note in the flavor; sweetness builds as the bowl progresses. Nicotine is in the medium range. The flakes want to be rubbed out and smoked slowly. Suitable for smokers who enjoy unflavored light Virginia flakes and want a blend for daytime smoking.
charatan-flake.o: Leaves a baked bread and dry hay room note.

vogels-tabakstube-der-block.z: Der Block is one of the signature house blends from the German tobacconist Vogel's Tabakstube. It is prepared from dark Virginia, Kentucky and Perique leaf and sold as a 100-gram plug. The block is pressed relatively firm and is prepared by slicing and rubbing out. The dark Virginia leaf carries a honey-like sweetness; the Perique adds a tangy, plum-like note that becomes more pronounced as the bowl progresses. The Kentucky thickens the body, bringing a spicy, walnut-like dryness. The mixture is unflavored, gives light-to-medium body, and shows no tendency to bite. Suited to smokers unfazed by plug preparation who enjoy an unflavored Virginia-Perique structure.
vogels-tabakstube-der-block.o: Leaves a woody, faintly sour-plum, smoky tobacco aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-nessmuk-navy-flake.z: Nessmuk Navy Flake is the flake version of the plug product of the same name. The "Navy" name refers to the traditional sailor's-tobacco style where Virginia and Burley leaf are pressed and flavored with rum; the name also draws on the "Nessmuk" pen name of 19th-century American nature writer George W. Sears. The Virginia leaf gives a dark dried-fruit sweetness and an earthy note, while Burley adds a nutty depth and a light molasses taste; the rum topping brings out this base and softens the perceived nicotine. Given its pressed structure, it burns slowly and cool. Suited to smokers who love classic rum-topped navy flakes and want a medium-bodied tobacco.
gawith-hoggarth-co-nessmuk-navy-flake.o: Leaves an aroma carrying rum, molasses, and dried-fruit sweetness.

sutliff-tobacco-company-maraschino-702.z: Coded 702, Maraschino is a cherry-themed blend in Sutliff's bulk aromatic line. A sauce reminiscent of maraschino cherry is applied over a ribbon-cut base of burley, Virginia, and black cavendish leaves; the blend is prepared to minimize tongue bite. Body is light and nicotine is low; on the flavor side, the leaves' own character stays in the background while cherry sweetness comes forward. Following the classic line of cherry-flavored American bulk tobaccos, this blend suits smokers who enjoy a sweet, fruity profile as well as those seeking a light tobacco in their early pipe years.
sutliff-tobacco-company-maraschino-702.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity scent reminiscent of cherries steeped in syrup.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-bohemian-mixture.z: No verifiable composition and character information could be compiled for Wilke Pipe Tobacco's aromatic blend Bohemian Mixture.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-bohemian-mixture.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-captain-log.z: A blend from Tabacos Wilder Finamore said to be cavendish-based; no independent source describing its content and character could be found.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-captain-log.o: Records suggest it leaves a sweet cavendish scent.

robert-mcconnell-notting-hill.z: Notting Hill is the Robert McConnell Heritage line's English blend with a noticeable Oriental weight. Latakia and Oriental leaves are combined with Virginia; lightly toasting the leaves gives the blend depth and a sweet undertone. The balance between Latakia's smoke and the Oriental's spicy, dry-hay character is the blend's defining trait. Flavor intensity is high, nicotine load medium; presented ribbon cut in a 50-gram tin. Aimed at those familiar with classic English mixtures seeking an unflavored, smoky smoke. The brand is London-rooted, with current production carried out in Germany.
robert-mcconnell-notting-hill.o: A spicy, lightly sweet trace mixes into the incense and wood-smoke scent.

cornell-diehl-bayou-morning.z: Cornell & Diehl Bayou Morning is an unflavored mixture built by combining red and bright Virginia leaves with Louisiana perique at roughly a quarter proportion. Keeping the perique level high turns the blend into one of the more full-bodied examples of its type. The cut is ribbon. On the flavor channel, the Virginias' bready, dried-fruit-leaning sweetness interweaves with perique's plum, fig, and black pepper notes. Nicotine and flavor intensity run high; it calls for slow smoking. It suits experienced smokers looking for a full-bodied Virginia mixture centered on perique's spicy character.
cornell-diehl-bayou-morning.o: Leaves a tangy dark-fruit and black-pepper aroma in the room, with a bready tobacco scent beneath.

stone-pine-tobacco-company-blue-angel.z: One of the blends from Stone Pine Tobacco Company; no verifiable source describing its composition and character could be found.

synjeco-bad-nun-ii.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Synjeco's Bad Nun II pipe tobacco could be found.

carmel-pipe-shop-ocean-blend.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Ocean Blend under the Carmel Pipe Shop brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

up-down-mr-keiths-vanilla-creme.z: Noted as a vanilla-flavored aromatic house blend from Up Down Tobacco; no independent source documenting its base leaves and cut has been found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-chocolate-suprem.z: D54 Chocolate Supreme is an aromatic where a generous chocolate topping is applied over a ribbon-cut combination of bright Virginia, nutty burley, and black cavendish leaves. The topping gives a soft, creamy cocoa direction, with tobacco flavor staying measured beneath it. It's noted that the tobacco can be moist out of the package and should be aired before smoking. Suited to smokers seeking chocolatey, sweet aromatics.
sutliff-tobacco-company-chocolate-suprem.o: Leaves a scent of creamy chocolate and cocoa.

ken-byron-ventures-verge-engine-2022.z: Recorded as the 2022 edition of Verge Engine, classed as pure Virginia; not enough independent sources could be found to detail its contents.
ken-byron-ventures-verge-engine-2022.o: No reliable record could be found regarding the room note.

havanezas-1864.z: A house blend carrying a tobacconist's founding year; there is not enough sourcing on the brand, composition, and character.
havanezas-1864.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

seattle-pipe-club-yakima-valley.z: Yakima Valley is one of the Seattle Pipe Club series' Latakia-bearing blends. A base of sweet Virginia, nutty Burley, and soft black cavendish is joined by a noticeable share of Latakia; the dark leaf comes forward but does not overpower the other components. It is ribbon cut. Nicotine is kept low, the smoke draws cool, and it leaves a nutty aftertaste. Suited to smokers wanting to sample Latakia's flavor in a measured dose and to those seeking a light English mixture.
seattle-pipe-club-yakima-valley.o: A warm, sweet, nutty note mixes into the smoky wood aroma.

peter-stokkebye-black-cherry-cavendish-n.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Black Cherry Cavendish (No.302) could be found.

former-cross-grain-flake.z: The Former brand carries the name of Danish pipe maker Hans "Former" Nielsen. Cross Grain Flake is an untopped flake prepared by adding a small proportion of perique to select Virginia leaf, then pressing and maturing it. Virginia's natural sweetness leads; perique leaves a fine accent of spice and fruit. It follows a milder, cooler course than the same line's Straight Grain Flake. It suits smokers newly approaching the pressed Virginia type or looking for a low-nicotine everyday flake.
former-cross-grain-flake.o: Leaves an aroma of dry hay and warm, lightly fruity tobacco.

wesleys-no-19-pure-latakia.z: No. 19 Pure Latakia is a single-varietal product South African tobacconist Wesley's offers under a "for blending" heading; it's not a mixture but straight Latakia leaf. Latakia is a leaf processed by smoking over fire, taking its distinctive smoky character from that process. The maker states this tobacco is used within a blend to cut the weight of flavoring and reduce an overly sugary impression, typically making up at most fifteen percent of the mixture. Smoked on its own, the taste consists entirely of soot, wood, leather, and resinous tones; natural sugar is nearly absent, so smoking it alone isn't common. It's a building block for smokers preparing their own blends who want to adjust the smoky component directly.
wesleys-no-19-pure-latakia.o: Leaves a dense scent of campfire, pine smoke, and leather.

peretti-no-8-slice.z: No.8 Slice is a Virginia/perique mixture that Peretti blended and pressed specially for a club. Per the maker's description, several distinct full-bodied Virginia varieties are pressed together with perique; today it is offered as a plug rather than slices. The plug lets the smoker cut slices to their own thickness, giving control over burn rate. The profile is spicy and layered; with a pronounced share of perique, flavor intensity and satisfaction run high. It's aimed at smokers accustomed to pressed Virginia blends who want a full-bodied tobacco with a slow, cool smoke. In plug form it is well suited to long-term storage.
peretti-no-8-slice.o: Leaves a spiced trace mingling with dark fruit and warm bread aromas.

g-l-pease-aragorn.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Aragorn.

r-j-reynolds-george-washington-cut-plug.z: George Washington Cut Plug is an American pipe tobacco produced since the early twentieth century at R.J. Reynolds' Winston-Salem factory, also known for its tins. Burley forms its core; some Virginia and Cavendish are added, along with a light molasses- or caramel-type flavoring. Despite its name, its cut comes ready-rubbed rather than as a plug.
r-j-reynolds-george-washington-cut-plug.o: Leaves a sweetish aroma reminiscent of burnt sugar and dry nuts.

cornell-diehl-bluegrass.z: Bluegrass is a ribbon-cut mixture built by adding perique and fire-cured Kentucky to bright and red Virginia leaves. Cornell & Diehl describes the blend as a spiced melody where perique and Kentucky accompany the steady rhythm of the Virginias. Its name connects to the region the Kentucky leaf comes from and to that region's music. The Virginias' bready sweetness forms the foundation; fire-cured Kentucky adds a smoky, salty body, while perique brings a plum-and-black-pepper spice. Nicotine strength is medium, but the blend sharpens when smoked quickly, so packing tight and drawing slowly changes its character. It suits those who love unflavored Virginia blends and want a bit more smoke and spice.
cornell-diehl-bluegrass.o: Leaves a smoky, sweet aroma reminiscent of wood-fire-cooked meat and dried fruit.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-pigtail-e-s.z: Brown Pigtail is the thin-to-medium gauge of the four thicknesses of twisted rope Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. produces; the "brown" designation shows that the rope is left as it comes off the twisting machine, without further pressing or cooking. The E/S version's body is built from strong Virginia leaves and treated with sweet maple sugar; the topping does more to bring out the leaf's own sweetness than to build a distinct flavour layer. Uncut, the rope smells woody and sharp; once sliced thin and rubbed out, the peaty, smoky character deepens. The product tends to be quite moist, so it wants a fairly long airing before loading, otherwise it needs frequent relighting. With high nicotine and flavour intensity, it suits smokers familiar with rope tobaccos and fire-cured leaf.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-pigtail-e-s.o: Leaves a peat- and smoke-dominant, sharply woody aroma, with a lightly sugary note behind it.

intertabak-perique-po-20.z: No verifiable source could be found for this Perique tobacco registered under the INTERTABAK name.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-golden-sliced-.z: Golden Sliced is Orlik's navy-cut flake known for its red tin. It's made by pressing fire-cured Virginia leaves and cutting them into thin slices; a small amount of perique is added. The slices range in color between copper-red and oak brown. It's counted among the best-known examples of the Virginia-perique type. Before lighting it gives off a natural sweet scent recalling tea and citrus; on the smoke, herbal, sweet Virginia taste leads, accompanied by a raisin-like depth and a spicy touch from the perique. It's unflavored and rewards aging. It's described as a starting point for those wanting to get to know the Virginia-perique type.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-golden-sliced-.o: Leaves a scent of dry grass, tea, and citrus peel.

timm-no-name-schwarz.z: The black variety in the Timm No Name series is an aromatic built on Virginia and black Cavendish. Vanilla and a fruit flavoring evoking red currant are used as the casing; the proportion of Cavendish determines the blend's sweetness and moisture. Nicotine is low and the smoke is mellow. Prepared for smokers who enjoy fruit-and-vanilla aromatics and want an affordable everyday tobacco in a large package.
timm-no-name-schwarz.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of vanilla and red-berry syrup.

volker-bier-bier-plug.z: Bier Plug is a pressed block tobacco bearing the name of German blender Volker Bier. Its composition includes Virginia, Kentucky and Perique; the block is sliced and rubbed out before being loaded into the bowl. Virginia takes the lead role in the mix, offering natural sugary sweetness, a grassy, hay-like character and a lemony tangy top note. The Perique adds a plummy, spicy layer on top, while the Kentucky brings body and a light smokiness. It is unflavored and carries moderate strength. Aimed at those used to plug preparation who enjoy an unflavored Virginia-Perique structure.
volker-bier-bier-plug.o: Leaves a dry hay, lemon peel, and lightly smoky wood aroma.

j-f-germain-son-royal-jersey-perique-mix.z: Royal Jersey Perique Mixture is the Virginia-Perique (VaPer) blend in J. F. Germain & Son's Royal Jersey line. Perique of Louisiana origin is added atop the sugary base of Virginia leaves; the Perique lends the blend depth in the direction of peppery spice and dried fruit. The product is presented already rubbed out. It contains no flavoring; the flavor comes entirely from the interaction of the two leaves. As the Perique proportion increases, the spice becomes more pronounced, so slow smoking and moderate packing make it easier to distinguish the flavors. It suits smokers looking for an unflavored, spicy Virginia blend that deepens over time.
j-f-germain-son-royal-jersey-perique-mix.o: Leaves a spicy, sweetish aroma reminiscent of dried figs and black pepper.

bugler-pipe-tobacco-blue.z: Bugler is a brand that launched in the United States in 1932, known for many years for its roll-your-own tobacco; per records, Lane Limited, which runs the brand, joined the Scandinavian Tobacco Group in 2011. Blue is the base blend in the brand's pipe tobacco line, built on combining long-fiber light-colored Virginia leaf with dark, mahogany-toned Burley. The cut is wide ribbon, and because the tobacco's moisture is kept low it catches quickly once loaded into the pipe. Its character is plain and tobacco-forward: Burley's dry, nutty, earthy tone sits over a lightly sweet-tart base from the Virginia. Casing use is kept to a minimum, so no aromatic profile should be expected. Nicotine is on par with similar American blends sold over the counter. A blend aimed at smokers seeking a plain, inexpensive, everyday Virginia-Burley they can smoke for long stretches.
bugler-pipe-tobacco-blue.o: Leaves a slightly sharp smoke trail with a dry hay and nutty tobacco aroma.

synjeco-oxenfisl-twist.z: Oxenfisl Twist, a pipe tobacco from Synjeco; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-black-cavendish.z: Wilke Black Cavendish is an unsugared black cavendish record. The leaf, steam-processed and darkened with heat, gains a soft, dark character as its natural sugars caramelize; since no casing is applied either, the flavor comes from the processing itself. It can be smoked on its own, or used as a blending component to soften the harshness of other tobaccos or bulk up their body. The flavor carries a soft sweetness reminiscent of brown sugar and a light toasted-bread note. Body and nicotine are low; it burns cool and clean, leaves little moisture in the chamber, and the flavor stays consistent throughout. Since it tends not to bite the tongue, it's a convenient option for newcomers to the pipe and those seeking a light all-day tobacco; it also serves as a base component for those blending their own mixtures.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-black-cavendish.o: Leaves a scent of light toasted bread and brown sugar.

mac-baren-honey-chocolate.z: Honey & Chocolate is a fine loose-cut aromatic blend from Mac Baren based on leaf that has undergone a special cavendish process. Records indicate the blend's foundation is a Brazilian Virginia that is hot-air cured and then fermented like cigar leaf; this process removes the leaf's sharpness and turns it into a softer expression. After a long, slow cavendish process, the blend is given a top flavor of honey and chocolate. In the smoke, the tobacco character stays in the background; the flavor that stands out is honey sweetness and cocoa tones. Nicotine is low and it burns cool. Suited to those starting out on pipes with flavored blends and to those seeking sweet top notes. Since the product's moisture can run high, airing it a while before packing regulates the burn.
mac-baren-honey-chocolate.o: Leaves a sweet room note reminiscent of honey and cocoa, with a light burnt-sugar tone.

peretti-original-mixture.z: One of the house blends from L. J. Peretti's shop in Boston; it appears under the burley blends heading in the maker's listing. No published description of the blend's composition and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.

savinelli-essenza-cipriota.z: Savinelli's ribbon-cut blend, classified as English-aromatic, taking its name from Cyprus Latakia; no sufficient source describing its leaf proportions and casing could be found.

mac-baren-golden-dice.z: Not enough information could be found in the manufacturer's current catalog or verifiable independent sources about this Mac Baren blend, which is described as cavendish-based.

borkum-riff-copper-highland-malt-whisky.z: A Scotch malt whisky-flavored version in Borkum Riff's color-named series. No reliable source on its leaf composition and cut could be found, leaving the profile incomplete.
borkum-riff-copper-highland-malt-whisky.o: According to records it leaves a room note reminiscent of malt whisky.

bosphorus-navy-flake.z: Navy Flake is an unflavored flake where Virginia and burley are balanced. Virginia gives the blend sweetness, while burley adds fullness and a nicotine effect that becomes pronounced toward the end of the fill; strength and flavor are medium. The slices can be filled either pulled apart in strips or intact, and the smoke stays even either way. The blend carries a trace resembling the slick, floral note known in the English tradition as Lakeland soap taste; it lingers in the mouth for a while. Per records, its character changes when rested for a few weeks. Suitable for smokers seeking an unflavored, balanced Virginia-burley flake.
bosphorus-navy-flake.o: Leaves an aroma carrying dry-hay sweetness with a lightly soapy, floral trace.

craftsman-black-aromatic-supreme.z: Recorded as a bulk aromatic blend sold under the Craftsman name; no source confirming its composition and production status was found.

mcclelland-no-24.z: No. 24 is a Virginia-based flake blend in McClelland's "Matured Virginias" series. Turkish-language sources indicate it contains Oriental leaf alongside Virginia, with Drama tobacco among the elements defining the blend's character. The small flake slices can also be smoked unrubbed after airing; this method demands experience to control the burn, but raises flavor intensity. In the smoke, a pure, sweet Virginia character comes through with a moderate nicotine dose; it doesn't harden toward the bottom of the bowl. Aimed at smokers wanting a slow smoking pace and an unflavored Virginia taste. Withdrawn from the market when McClelland stopped production in 2018.
mcclelland-no-24.o: Leaves a sharp, tangy, earthy tobacco aroma.

bufflehead-wood-duck.z: One of the discontinued blends from the Bufflehead shop; no source documenting its composition could be found.

dan-tobacco-stars-and-stripes-original-a.z: This is an aromatic blend Dan Tobacco calls an American-style mixture; not enough sourcing could be found about its composition and character.
dan-tobacco-stars-and-stripes-original-a.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-perle-mellow-t.z: A Virginia-burley-based blend listed as the mellow-smoking version of the Perle line; no independent source describing its character could be found.

peretti-blend-no-333.z: Blend No. 333 is a cube-cut Burley blend from Boston's L.J. Peretti and is counted among the firm's best-known records. The leaves come in pieces ranging from medium to dark brown; the maker describes the blend as a non-aromatic, full, sweet, slow-burning tobacco. The sweetness in the pouch scent suggests a measured topping has been applied. The cube cut simplifies packing: the pipe is filled, lightly pressed, and lit. On the palate, natural Burley character, roasted nut, and dark wheat notes come forward, with a fine spice sensed in the background. The smoke is cool and slow, and the sense of nicotine is pronounced. It suits smokers seeking a near-unflavored, full-bodied Burley.
peretti-blend-no-333.o: Leaves a roasted nut and dark bread aroma.

park-lane-tobacconist-fireside.z: No reliable source could be found for the Park brand pipe tobacco called Lane Tobacconist-Fireside, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

ken-byron-ventures-red-forest-phenomenon.z: A Virginia-forward blend released as a limited batch in 2019; not enough sources could be found to describe its composition.

karl-erik-private-blend-no-20.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to fill in the profile of Karl Erik's Private Blend No.20.

4noggins-alamosa.z: Alamosa is a blend in the 4noggins catalog made from high-quality Virginia leaf pressed into flakes. According to the manufacturer's description, the leaf is pressed into Cornell & Diehl's signature flake/chip cut, a process that locks in the natural sweetness the leaf develops during pressing. No additives are reported, so the sweetness comes entirely from the Virginia's own sugars. The blend ships at a moisture level ready to pack straight from the pouch, while also being well suited to long-term aging; as expected with pressed Virginias, the flavor profile deepens the longer it rests. Nicotine and flavor sit at a moderate level. It's aimed at smokers who enjoy unadulterated Virginia flavor, the density of pressed leaf, and the practice of cellaring tobacco.
4noggins-alamosa.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of an orange cake fresh from the oven.

wattsons-special-mixture-green.z: Wattsons is a pipe tobacco brand sold under the Denmark-based Scandinavian Tobacco Group; no maker or retailer record describing the composition of the green-packaged version of Special Mixture could be found.
wattsons-special-mixture-green.o: No description could be found as no source was available.

danske-club-cherry.z: Cherry is the cherry-cased aromatic blend from the Danish brand Danske Club. It is made of Burley, Cavendish, and Virginia leaf, ribbon cut. Nicotine sits a little above mild, flavor intensity is medium, and the casing itself turns out more restrained than expected. What stands out is its smoking behavior: the tin can hold tobacco that's quite dry, making it hard to light and keep lit. Records note a sharp, peppery bite in the first half of the smoke that fades by the second half, when cherry notes come forward. Prone to overheating and needing careful moisture management, it calls for a slow pace — not a beginner's tin, but a fitting one for smokers experienced with aromatic blends.
danske-club-cherry.o: Leaves a sweetish fruit scent reminiscent of cherry candy.

sutliff-tobacco-company-kentucky-blizzar.z: Coded 705, Kentucky Blizzard is a Sutliff bulk aromatic named after the cocktail of the same name. The cocktail's components — bourbon, cranberry juice, lime, and grenadine — are applied as a sauce over a base built from six separate tobacco types, which include burley, Virginia, black cavendish, and Kentucky leaf. The result is a medium-bodied blend where a fruity, tart sweetness meets a bourbon note. With the Kentucky leaf's contribution, nicotine and fullness sit a notch above typical light American aromatics. Suited to smokers who like fruited sauces but don't want an entirely sugary profile. With Sutliff's production having ended, the blend now depends on remaining stock.
sutliff-tobacco-company-kentucky-blizzar.o: Leaves a sweetish scent reminiscent of tart red fruit and whiskey.

cobblestone-sangria.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Cobblestone pipe tobacco named Sangria, so the blend's content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

iwan-ries-three-star-royale.z: Three Star Royale is a mixture in Iwan Ries & Co.'s Three Star line, described by the maker as a "transition blend." Its base is made up of white Burley, Virginia, and Turkish (Oriental) leaf, with a light share of Perique and Latakia added, topped off with a house-specific flavoring. The Oriental leaf's dry spiciness and the Burley's nutty fullness stand out; the Latakia smokiness stays in the background as a subtle seasoning. Since the flavoring level is kept low, the tobacco's natural taste is preserved. It's aimed at smokers wanting to move from aromatic toward English or American styles, looking for a medium-strength, versatile blend.
iwan-ries-three-star-royale.o: Leaves a lightly spicy, sweet layer over a nutty tobacco aroma.

comptons-of-galashiels-mixture-14.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Compton's of Galashiels pipe tobacco named Mixture #14, so the blend's content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-911.z: Wilke No. 911 is an English blend with moderate smokiness, built on a Virginia and cavendish base with added Oriental leaf and Cyprian Latakia. According to the records, the cavendish component receives a light brandy casing; this addition isn't heavy enough to push the blend into the aromatic class, functioning more as a softener that smooths the Oriental leaf's sour, floral edges. The Oriental leaf lends an earthy, herbal, lightly smoky dimension, while the Latakia supplies the wood-smoke side. The burn rate is moderate and occasional relights are needed. Mild to medium in nicotine and slightly below medium in flavor intensity, this profile makes it an English blend suitable for all-day smoking among experienced pipe smokers.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-911.o: Leaves a scent of campfire smoke, dry grass, and a faint grape-liqueur note in the background.

frederick-tranter-circus-spin-cut.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Frederick Tranter's Circus Spin cut blend; records place it in the Virginia-Perique class.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-brown-bogie-ar.z: Sliced Brown Bogie Aromatic is the lightly flavored, factory-sliced version of the producer's brown bogie rope, twisted from fire-cured leaf. Structurally it rests on the same base as the unflavored bogie; the difference is the sweet topping applied to the leaf during production. On the smoke, the smoky, earthy, leather-reminiscent core of the fire-curing is preserved, with a fine sugary sweetness layered on top. Nicotine stays high; it needs to be thinly sliced and smoked slowly. An entry for those familiar with the bogie style who want a somewhat sweeter version. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. is one of the English producers that continues traditional twist (rope) production at its Kendal factory, hand-twisting fire-cured leaves into rope form. Because twist tobaccos don't go through a pressure-cooking stage, they stay intense in nicotine; records indicate these ropes are sold for both chewing and pipe smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-brown-bogie-ar.o: Leaves an aroma adding a fine sugary sweetness over wood smoke and earth.

robert-mcconnell-celebrated-sovereign.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of Robert McConnell Celebrated Sovereign.

esoterica-tobacciana-and-so-to-bed.z: And So To Bed is the only blend in the Esoterica line not named for an English coastal town. It is made by combining aged virginia and maryland leaves with Greek orientals and Cyprus latakia; after blending, the mixture undergoes an additional aging process. It is ribbon cut. Latakia is clearly present but stays measured compared to the series' more soot-forward blends; the orientals' spicy, dry-herbal tone and virginia sweetness come through. As its name suggests, it suits those seeking a slow-smoked, medium-bodied English mixture for the day's last bowl.
esoterica-tobacciana-and-so-to-bed.o: Leaves a lightly sweet tobacco trace alongside woody soot and dry spice.

cornell-diehl-chenets-cake.z: Chenet's Cake takes its name from Pierre Chenet, the farmer credited with discovering, in 1824, the process for turning burley leaf into perique. Part of Cornell & Diehl's Cellar Series, the blend is prepared by adding a very high proportion of perique to a red-Virginia-heavy base and pressing it into an old-style crumble cake. According to available sources, the perique share exceeds a third of the blend. Young, it delivers an intense, spicy, heavy taste; with age, sweetness reminiscent of plum and jam is reported to come forward. It suits experienced smokers who want perique not as a secondary spice but as the blend's main character, and who plan to cellar it for an extended period.
cornell-diehl-chenets-cake.o: Leaves a spicy, sweetish aroma reminiscent of plum and black pepper.

sutliff-tobacco-company-presbyterian-ref.z: A record listed in Sutliff's catalogs as an aromatic; no sufficient source on its content and character could be found.

motzek-michas-cake.z: Micha's Cake is a cake tobacco made by curing select toasted Virginia leaves with twelve-year-old rum and then pressing them. It is sold in block form; it is cut into thin slices with a sharp knife and rubbed by hand before being loaded into the pipe. The casing is natural and measured, so this entry sits somewhere between straight tobacco and aromatic. In the taste, Virginia's citrusy tartness runs alongside the rum's resinous sweetness; pressing concentrates Virginia's sugars and slows the burn. The maker describes its strength as three out of five, i.e. medium-bodied. A fitting entry for smokers accustomed to pressed Virginia construction and light-level flavoring, who don't mind the effort of slicing and rubbing.
motzek-michas-cake.o: Leaves a resinous, sweet rum aroma over the dry tobacco scent.

g-l-pease-varoom.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of the G. L. Pease pipe tobacco Varoom!.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-indian-su.z: An aromatic blend produced under Scandinavian Tobacco Group; no reliable detail on its composition could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-indian-su.o: Recorded as leaving a sweet, casing-forward scent.

cest-la-vie-chocolate-eclair.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named Chocolate Éclair under the C'est La Vie brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

house-of-calabash-craven-legion-of-honor.z: This is reportedly an unflavored Virginia-Perique blend in the Craven line of House of Calabash, operated by Steven Books in Oregon City; no sufficient source verifying the details could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-ready-rubb.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the content and character of Match Ready Rubbed, one of the bulk blends from Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company, could be found.

wessex-burley-broadcut.z: Burley Broadcut is the Burley-forward member of the Wessex series. As the name indicates, it's offered in a broadly cut, broken-flake structure, suited to being rubbed out by hand before packing into the pipe. Burley leaf carries the structure, while Virginia provides sweetness and burn balance.
