The taste revolves around nut, dry cocoa, and earthy tones; due to Burley's low sugar content, the smoke runs dry and plain, with little tendency to bite the tongue. According to records, a light flavoring accompanies the cut, but the character leans toward natural tobacco rather than aromatic. It suits those seeking a slow-burning, lightly cased everyday blend.
wessex-burley-broadcut.o: Leaves a lightly sweet scent leaning toward nuts and toasted bread.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-vintage-aged-g.z: Vintage Aged Golden Sliced is the long-matured version of Orlik's Golden Sliced line. Perique is added to sun-matured golden-yellow Virginia leaves; the mixture is held under heat and pressure into a cake, which is then sliced into flake. Per the maker's recipe, a light natural citrus-based casing is applied to the cake before slicing, with no other flavoring involved.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-vintage-aged-g.o: Leaves a scent of dry grass, honey, and light citrus peel.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-banana-gold.z: Kendal Banana Gold is the banana-topped member of the Kendal Gold family. Light-yellow, flue-cured Virginia leaf is cut into fine shag strands; the tobacco is fluffy and moist but not sticky. The banana aroma sits closer to fresh fruit than an artificial candy note. On the smoke, Virginia's toasted sugar sweetness stands out, with banana remaining as a fine layer on top. Nicotine is low and tongue bite is minimal. Suited to those new to aromatic shag tobaccos and anyone wanting a cool, sweet smoke.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-banana-gold.o: Leaves an aroma of freshly peeled banana with a light candy scent.

ohm-silver.z: OHM Silver is the mildest member of the OHM line, produced in the United States. The line's shared base of American-grown Virginia and Burley leaf is prepared as a ribbon cut. Silver is positioned below Bold and Blue, at the lowest strength step in the line. In the smoke, both taste and nicotine follow a flat course; the leaf's own sweetness stays faint. Being ribbon cut, it lights easily. Suitable for those looking for short, light sessions and an everyday blend with low strength.
ohm-silver.o: Leaves a faint, lightly hay-like tobacco aroma.

affordable-pipes-morning-watch.z: One of the house blends from the American seller Affordable Pipes; no accessible source describing its content could be found.

w-o-larsen-a-true-delight.z: No independent source sufficient to complete a record could be found regarding W.O. Larsen's A True Delight blend, so this entry remains incomplete.

tinder-box-blend-no-2.z: Tinder Box is the name of an American tobacconist chain founded in 1928 that sells blends prepared for its own shops under its own name; Blend No. 2 is one of these house blends, though no sufficient independent source describing its composition and character has been found.

vauen-tradition-no-2.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Vauen pipe tobacco called Tradition No 2 to record the blend's composition and character.

lane-limited-black-and-brown.z: Black and Brown is a blend in Lane Limited's bulk aromatic line. It takes its name from its appearance: the dark tone of flavored black cavendish leaves sits alongside the brown of light Virginia and Burley leaves in the same cut. The cavendish base stays close to the sweet line of the brand's BCA record. Being a ribbon cut, it packs easily and burns evenly. Sugar load is pronounced, nicotine load is low; the smoke is creamy and sweet. Suited to those new to aromatic tobaccos and those seeking an everyday blend that leaves a pronounced sweet scent in the room. As a result of contraction in Lane's bulk catalog, it's not commonly found today.
lane-limited-black-and-brown.o: Leaves a dark sugar room note reminiscent of sweet vanilla and molasses.

planta-van-halteren-black-and-mild.z: Van Halteren Black and Mild is a heavily cased, black-Cavendish-heavy aromatic from the Berlin house Planta. Double-fermented black Cavendish forms the blend's body; the vanilla, licorice-root, and ripe-plum notes layered on top are pronounced both in the tin note and the smoke. Nicotine is low, and the tobacco taste stays beneath the casing. Reports indicate its moist structure calls for a slow, patient smoke, and drawing quickly overheats the pipe. It suits smokers used to black-Cavendish-based, heavily cased tobaccos, and those looking for sweetness over tobacco taste in aromatics; for those coming from English or straight Virginia blends, its character stays too sweet.
planta-van-halteren-black-and-mild.o: Fills the room with a vanilla, licorice-root, and ripe-plum aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-plug-aromatic.z: Dark Plug is built from an equal combination of Malawi-origin fire-cured leaf and Indian-origin air-cured dark leaf; the former gives a smoky taste, the latter a sweetish, cigar-like one. The cake is cold-pressed for more than a week and sold as plug. In the aromatic version, a top flavoring characteristic of Kendal tradition is added to this dark body. It's prepared by slicing with a knife and rubbing out. Both nicotine and taste sit at the top of the catalog; it gives a deep, earthy, smoky smoke. Suited to smokers accustomed to pressed dark tobaccos wanting a sweet essence layer added on top.
gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-plug-aromatic.o: A floral-sweet essence layer sits above a heavy smoke and leather aroma.

motzek-dad-n-tobak.z: Since neither the manufacturer's own description nor two independent reliable sources could be found for the Motzek blend called Dad'n Tobak, its composition, cut, and character could not be documented here.

srensen-srensen-flake.z: SØRENSEN Flake is one of two house blends bearing the name of Sørensen Tobakk, which has operated on Bergen's Torgallmenningen square since 1905. Dark Virginia and fire-cured dark leaves are pressed and sliced, with Perique grown in a small region of Louisiana giving the blend Kentucky-style spice. It offers an unflavored, intense taste born of pressing; the retailer's scale rates its strength four out of five. Once the slices are rubbed out and aired before packing, dark Virginia sweetness, Kentucky's smoky tone, and Perique's peppery fruitiness come through in sequence. It suits smokers who like strong, unflavored flake and are used to a heavy nicotine load.
srensen-srensen-flake.o: A peppery, lightly tart grain scent mixes into the woody smoke of the fire-cured leaf.

hu-tobacco-white-dog.z: White Dog is a blend that brings together Virginia leaves of different origins in a ribbon cut. In the leaf profile, earth, fresh herb and dry hay, citrus peel, and a slowly cooked dark-fruit sweetness come forward; light-colored Virginia adds a small spicy edge. The measured woody coating applied to the blend gives a light spice evoking cedar shavings and rounds out the tobacco without making it fully aromatic. It suits those looking to get accustomed to Virginia, or those wanting a mild leaf for all-day smoking.
hu-tobacco-white-dog.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of dry hay and cedar shavings.

clan-shaw-bali-hai.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Bali Hai.

sutliff-tobacco-company-top-shelf.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Sutliff Tobacco Company's Top Shelf pipe tobacco could be found.

mcclelland-blending-virginia.z: Blending Virginia is the unflavored flue-cured Virginia leaf McClelland sold as a component in its bulk line. It's prepared for smokers building their own recipe to add a sweet Virginia base to their blend; it's ribbon cut and carries no flavoring. Smoked on its own, it gives a sweet, herbal, plain profile from its natural sugar; nicotine level is low to medium. Given Virginia leaf's tendency to mature in long storage, it's considered suitable for aging. McClelland was founded in 1977, known for its Virginia and Oriental blends, and stopped production in 2018.
mcclelland-blending-virginia.o: Leaves a sweet hay and dry-grass aroma.

paul-olsen-plantagenet.z: One of the Virginia-perique-based blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

wesleys-no-58-perique-navy-cut.z: Perique Navy Cut is a navy cut blend made from pressed leaf that's been rubbed out. According to the maker's description, the Perique ratio in the mixture is kept high, creating a fruity, spicy flavor line. Strength is medium, and the burn is slow.
wesleys-no-58-perique-navy-cut.o: Leaves a dark, spicy tobacco scent reminiscent of plum, fig, and date.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-jamaica-inn.z: Jamaica Inn is listed as one of McGahey The Tobacconist's Virginia-based house blends; no reliable source about its composition and character could be found.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-jamaica-inn.o: No reliable record regarding its room note could be found.

tinder-box-mayor-pete.z: Mayor Pete is an aromatic house blend sold at Tinder Box stores; no verifiable source on which leaves it is built from or what its casing is has been found.
tinder-box-mayor-pete.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

cornell-diehl-warped-sarto.z: Sarto is the first Latakia-containing pipe blend from the Warped and Cornell & Diehl partnership. Aged Virginia leaf, fine Orientals, and Perique are topped with a measured amount of Latakia and dark fire-cured Kentucky; the result is a balanced English mixture where smoke and spice don't jump to the front. The cut is broken flake — pressed leaf boxed in a broken-apart state. On the flavor side, Virginia's mature sweetness and Perique's peppery sharpness stand out; Latakia builds more of a smoky texture in the background. Nicotine load is medium. Suited to those looking for a measured, steadily smokable English mixture rather than a heavy Latakia bomb. The blend is named after the Cane Corso dog belonging to Warped founder Kyle Gellis and was designed as a companion to the brand's Until The End release.
cornell-diehl-warped-sarto.o: Leaves a dried-fruit sweetness behind a light smoke and leather scent.

uhles-perfection-plug-burley.z: Perfection Plug Burley is a bulk tobacco from Uhle Tobacco Company combining two different Burley cuts. Both cube-cut and ribbon-cut Burley are used together in the blend; it is offered in 1.5, 7 and 14-ounce measures. The maker's description characterizes the taste as a sweet, nutty tobacco line. Because the slow, cool burn of the cube cut works together with the easy lighting of the ribbon cut, the burn balance spreads evenly across a wide bowl; since no flavoring is added, the sweetness comes from the leaf itself. Nicotine sits in the medium range. A fitting record for smokers after unflavored Burley character and the cube-cut experience.
uhles-perfection-plug-burley.o: Leaves a plain, sweetish tobacco aroma leaning toward nuts and dry cocoa.

pcca-full-balkan-reserve-syrian.z: For PCCA's blend called Full Balkan Reserve - Syrian, no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

john-aylesbury-summerhill.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to document the contents and character of John Aylesbury's Summerhill.

robert-mcconnell-special-london-fine-cut.z: Special London Fine Cut is an unflavored blend of Virginia leaf from Robert McConnell's Special London line. As the name suggests, the cut is very fine, using a shag cut similar to cigarette tobacco in consistency. Reports note the tobacco is at a mature, ready-to-smoke moisture level when the tin is opened, needing no further resting. The fine cut brings quick lighting and fast burning; because it heats the pipe easily it calls for a loose pack and slow draw, which requires some experience to protect the pipe's wood. Nicotine runs above medium and flavor stays in the medium range, carrying the character of quality red Virginia. It suits smokers who prefer unflavored tobacco and are used to working with a fine cut.
robert-mcconnell-special-london-fine-cut.o: Leaves a clean, sweetish Virginia aroma reminiscent of dry hay.

ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-hey-wire.z: Referred to as a pure-Virginia-axis small-batch blend tied to Ken Byron Ventures' Yoshimi's line; not enough sources could be found to document its composition.
ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-hey-wire.o: Could not be described due to lack of accessible records.

ken-byron-ventures-goblin-city-2022.z: The 2022 release of Goblin City; no independent source could be found to document that year's blend ratios.
ken-byron-ventures-goblin-city-2022.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-palmetto-balkan.z: A blend, no longer in Cornell & Diehl's current catalogue, referred to as Balkan style; no adequate source documenting its composition was found.
cornell-diehl-palmetto-balkan.o: No adequate information for a description could be found in records.

peter-stokkebye-english-opulence.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend English Opulence could be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-burrus-bl.z: Burrus Bleu is the most common of the three Burrus pipe tobaccos originating from the Burrus tobacco house in Switzerland's Jura region. The brand is now under Scandinavian Tobacco Group and the product is made in Denmark for the Swiss market. The blend is entirely burley leaf: part air-cured, part sun-cured, then given a light fermentation. It contains no flavor casing whatsoever; the sweetness comes only from curing and fermentation. Its character is built on dry, toasted-walnut, and earthy tones; smoked slowly it leaves a light peppery trace on the tongue. Its fullness is pronounced but not aggressively harsh. Suited to those seeking an unflavored, traditional Continental European burley smoke.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-burrus-bl.o: Leaves a scent of toasted walnut, dry hay, and light earthiness.

just-for-him-the-bearded-lady.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for Just For Him's The Bearded Lady, so the profile is left incomplete; per catalog records, the blend is classified as "Virginia/Perique."

w-d-h-o-wills-sweet-chestnut.z: Sweet Chestnut is one of the discontinued blends from English maker W.D. & H.O. Wills, described as Burley-forward; no sufficient source could be found regarding its composition and character.
w-d-h-o-wills-sweet-chestnut.o: No reliable information could be found regarding the room note.

robert-mcconnell-black-parrot.z: Black Parrot is an unflavored Virginia-Perique blend made by pressing aged Virginia leaf together with Perique and slicing it into tight flakes. The slices can be rubbed out for packing or folded in whole, the latter method slowing the burn further. In the smoke, Virginia's sweet, tangy structure runs alongside Perique's dark fruit and pepper spice; as the bowl progresses, notes of raisin, fig, and bread become more pronounced. It burns cool and slow, offering medium fullness. It suits smokers familiar with pressed Virginia-Perique blends who want an unflavored tobacco that develops over time.
robert-mcconnell-black-parrot.o: Leaves a baked bread and dried fig aroma.

abenaki-tobacco-co-turkish-balkan.z: A blend Abenaki Tobacco Co. lists among Balkan-style mixtures in its own catalog; no adequate source on its ratios and smoke could be found.

mcclelland-drama-reserve.z: Drama Reserve belongs to McClelland's Grand Orientals series, which spotlights single-region Orientals, and takes its name from Greece's Drama region. Alongside the Oriental leaf is matured Virginia; the cut is ribbon, presented in small 50-gram tins. No flavoring is used. In the smoke, the dry, cigarette-like, spicy line typical of Orientals dominates, joined by a sweet-tart undertone from the brand's Virginias. Records indicate it leaves an oily trace reminiscent of olive oil on the palate. The tobacco burns easily and evenly without overheating; nicotine dose is medium and the ash stays light-colored. Suited to smokers wanting to hear the Oriental leaf in the lead role. The brand closed in 2018.
mcclelland-drama-reserve.o: A sweet-tart undertone accompanies a dry, cigarette-like tobacco aroma.

black-river-cigar-company-degudchit.z: No reliable source documenting the content of DeGudchit, a blend from Black River Cigar Company, could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-bobs-chocolate-flake.z: Bob's Chocolate Flake is a pressed flake blend made by combining Virginia leaves of Brazilian, Zimbabwean, and Malawian origin with some Malawi Burley and a small proportion of Latakia. It carries a cocoa-based sauce with chocolate and vanilla additions, accompanied by the distinctive floral Lakeland note characteristic of Gawith, Hoggarth production. The flakes rub out relatively easily, and since the moisture content tends to run high, a short airing before lighting helps. In the smoke, a soft cocoa layer sits atop a sweet Virginia base; the Latakia does not give a dominant smokiness but instead builds a thin, woody frame that balances the sweetness. It is a cool, slow-burning blend with a below-average nicotine load. It suits smokers who want an aromatic tobacco but wish to avoid sugar-laden, heavy aromatics, as well as those who want to sample the Lakeland style in a moderate example.
gawith-hoggarth-co-bobs-chocolate-flake.o: Leaves cocoa and vanilla topped with a thin smokiness from the Latakia and a floral Lakeland twist.

dan-tobacco-mikes-ready-rubbed.z: M.A. Mike's Ready Rubbed is an aromatic blend in Dan Tobacco's Michael Apitz-signed series. Its body is built from black Cavendish prepared by pressing and then crumbling, joined by Virginia leaf. The casing on top is described as leaning fruity and floral. The ready-rubbed preparation is achieved by pressing the flake and rubbing it by hand, which makes packing easier and slows the burn. It's a blend with moderate nicotine and pronounced sweetness. Suited to those wanting to stay on the aromatic side without moving into heavy English blends, and smokers who like flake texture but don't want the extra prep work.
dan-tobacco-mikes-ready-rubbed.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity, lightly floral scent.

just-for-him-dark-star.z: One of the house blends the Just For Him tobacconist prepares at its own counter; no independent source could be found on its contents or character.

bufflehead-bufflehead-decoy.z: One of the discontinued mixtures, dating from the mid-2000s, from the Bufflehead shop known for blends named after waterfowl; no source documenting its composition could be found.

grants-tobacconist-camelot.z: One of Grant's Tobacconist's house blends; there is no independent sourcing on its composition and character.

dunhill-a-25000.z: A discontinued mixture referred to by its code number under the Dunhill name, for which no verifiable source on its composition could be found.

mac-baren-amphora-black-cavendish-specia.z: The black cavendish member of the Amphora Special Reserve series is built on Virginia leaf that Mac Baren ferments twice; burley and oriental leaf round out the blend. It's presented as a loose cut. The double fermentation gives the cavendish a dark, natural sweetness without needing heavy applied syrups later; in the smoke, tones toward caramelized sugar and dried fruit come forward. Nicotine sits between light and medium. Suited to smokers seeking cavendish character without heavy casing.
mac-baren-amphora-black-cavendish-specia.o: Leaves a dark, sweet, lightly caramelized room note.

bufflehead-greater-scaup.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Greater Scaup under the Bufflehead brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

reiver-pipes-tobacco-gilnockie-gloamin.z: This is a blend from Reiver Pipes & Tobacco listed as Scottish style, named after border reiver Johnnie Armstrong's Gilnockie tower; there is not enough source material on its content.
reiver-pipes-tobacco-gilnockie-gloamin.o: No source could be found describing its aroma.

sentimiento-nacional-macedonia-ii.z: The second blend in Sentimiento Nacional's Macedonia series; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

john-aylesbury-mixture-no-666.z: 666 is the first step in John Aylesbury's Danish-style numbered aromatic series. Its composition is built on aromatic Virginia and twice-fermented black Cavendish, and it's offered in 50- and 200-gram packages. The maker describes the blend as delicately and measuredly sweet. Nicotine is low and the burn is cool; its casing intensity is more measured than the other members of the numbered series. Directly aimed by the maker at pipe newcomers, it's suited to those seeking a light aromatic that won't bite the tongue.
john-aylesbury-mixture-no-666.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, caramel-like tobacco aroma.

seattle-pipe-club-christmas-spirit-2023.z: Christmas Spirit 2023, signed by Seattle Pipe Club, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-the-english-fragrant.z: The English Fragrant is a blend in which Ken Byron Ventures deliberately marries classic English blend structure with the Lakeland tradition. Its body contains Virginia, Oriental, Kentucky, Perique, and Latakia, over which fruit and floral extracts are applied. The maker describes the concept as an experiment in what would happen if a blender working in the London school turned toward Lakeland scenting. The smoky, woody base of Latakia and Kentucky and the floral scenting are perceptible at the same time, while the Perique adds a spicy, tangy twist. Nicotine and flavor intensity run above medium, making for a full-bodied smoke. It's built for experienced smokers who know English blends and Lakeland scenting separately and are curious about their intersection; those unfamiliar with floral scenting may find it unusual. The room note is pronounced and tends to cling to clothing.
ken-byron-ventures-the-english-fragrant.o: Leaves a woody, smoky aroma overlaid with floral extracts and fruit.

hu-tobacco-aus-dem-krater-nr-5.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Aus dem Krater Nr. 5, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

stanwell-guarana.z: A guarana-themed aromatic blend from the Stanwell brand; though it's referenced in 40-gram pouches as well as 50- and 125-gram packaging, sufficient independent sources describing its composition could not be found.
stanwell-guarana.o: No description is available in records.

mcclelland-townsman-cavendish-silver.z: No sufficient source detailing the contents and character of this aromatic entry from McClelland's Townsman Cavendish series could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-great-outdoors.z: Great Outdoors is one of the bulk blends from the Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

just-for-him-whiskey-biscuit-gravy.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Just For Him's Whiskey Biscuit Gravy blend.

pipesandcigars-com-scottys-university-de.z: University Dean is a listing connected to the family of university-named English blends in pipesandcigars.com's Scotty's line; no source could be found verifying its composition, so no detailed specification is given.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-troost-sp.z: Troost Special Cavendish is one of the Dutch Troost brand's cavendish-centered aromatic blends. Despite its Dutch origin, the brand's aromatics follow a sweetness line close to the Danish style; virginia and mild burley leaf are combined with tobacco darkened through the cavendish process. The current version is, according to records, remade by Scandinavian Tobacco Group based on the original recipe and is found largely in the Dutch market. Suited to those seeking a warm, sweet, non-heavy-bodied aromatic.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-troost-sp.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly caramel-like tobacco scent.

samuel-gawith-special-flake-no-5.z: A pressed flake known as the most intensely flavored member of Samuel Gawith's numbered Special Flake series; no sufficient independent source confirming its leaf content could be found.
samuel-gawith-special-flake-no-5.o: Leaves an intense floral Lakeland scent along with a sweet fruit note evoking apricot.

campbells-smoke-shop-11-scottish-tweed.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named # 11 (Scottish Tweed) under the Campbell's Smoke Shop brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

mac-baren-royal-box.z: Remembered as an aromatic blend attributed to Mac Baren; since no independent source documenting its contents and character could be found, the record is left incomplete.
mac-baren-royal-box.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

panama-jack-melon.z: Melon is an aromatic blend within Panama Jack's tropical pipe tobacco line. A ripe-melon-direction flavoring is applied to a base built from burley, Virginia, and cavendish leaves; it's among the more moderately flavored blends in the line. It is ribbon cut and offered in fifty-gram tins. The smoke is cool and mellow, with nicotine load low. The sweetness cavendish brings sits together with burley's nutty base, and the melon note layers thinly over them. It's aimed at those wanting a light-bodied, fruity blend smokable all day.
panama-jack-melon.o: Leaves a scent of ripe melon and light sugary sweetness.

milan-tobacconists-our-walnut.z: Referred to as an American mixture from Milan Tobacconists' "Our" line, whose name references walnut; since it doesn't appear in the maker's current catalogue and no source describing its composition could be obtained, no further detail can be given.

just-for-him-longbottom-leaf.z: Longbottom Leaf is the first entry in the Middle-earth Pipeweed series from Just For Him, a tobacconist in Springfield, Missouri. The series comprises five blends inspired by the pipeweed names in Tolkien's books, and its design is credited to Bob Schafer. The blend's backbone is scented Virginia leaf, over which a light vanilla casing is applied. As with the series overall, the flavoring is measured and never intense enough to override the tobacco taste. Because it stays light on nicotine and is well suited to all-day smoking, it's a good fit for newcomers to aromatics and for those wanting a break from heavy Latakia blends.
just-for-him-longbottom-leaf.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and dry-hay aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-new-prince.z: New Prince is an aromatic Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. tobacco built mainly on light golden Virginia leaf, with a few dark flue-cured strands mixed in. The topping sits on a maple-and-vanilla axis; the sweetness is pronounced, but maple's salty-syrupy edge keeps the topping from being a one-note sugar. The cut sits between shag and ribbon, slightly thicker than a classic shag, which eases packing and lighting. Body and taste stay light to medium, burning cool with a patient draw. Suited to smokers seeking a Virginia aromatic whose topping is clearly audible but not heavy.
gawith-hoggarth-co-new-prince.o: Leaves a trace reminiscent of sweet baking, carrying maple syrup and vanilla.

robert-lewis-tree-mixture.z: Tree Mixture is a medium-bodied English blend weighted toward Oriental tobaccos, with a small amount of Latakia and a touch of black Cavendish and Virginia added. Sources also note the blend was produced from a Virginia-and-Latakia-containing cake and then broken into flake; the retail presentation is a fine ribbon cut. No flavoring is applied. Reports indicate the mixture was originally prepared exclusively for a Robert Lewis customer named Colonel Tree, and was sold only to him for roughly fifty years before going on general sale at the end of the 20th century. In the smoke, the Oriental leaf's gentle spice comes forward, Latakia builds a smoky ground, and Cavendish rounds off the sweetness. It offers a cool, rich smoke. It suits fans of classic, Oriental-forward English blends.
robert-lewis-tree-mixture.o: Leaves a campfire-like soot aroma alongside spicy Oriental leaf.

7-20-4-queen-city.z: Queen City is a Virginia-Perique blend released under the 7-20-4 brand's Briary Blends line. Per the promotional texts, it's based on dark red Virginia Cavendish, with a pronounced proportion of St. James Parish Perique added over it. The resulting taste moves toward dark cocoa, earth, and plum; the spicy sharpness brought by the Perique forms the blend's backbone. It carries no added flavoring, relying on the leaf's own sugar. The brand's name comes from the historical number referencing 1724, the founding year of Manchester, New Hampshire in the US; "Queen City" is that same city's recorded nickname. The blend is cut out for smokers accustomed to unflavored blends who are looking for the balance between Virginia sweetness and Perique spice. Since the Perique ratio isn't low, it may be heavy for those looking for an entirely mild everyday smoke.
7-20-4-queen-city.o: Leaves a sweetish room note dominated by dark cocoa and plum, carrying a peppery sharpness.

georgetown-tobacco-hastings.z: Referred to as one of Georgetown Tobacco's shop blends in the Virginia-Perique line; no published detail on its composition could be found.
georgetown-tobacco-hastings.o: No record of the room aroma could be found.

mccranies-black-lace.z: Black Lace is one of the aromatics sold under its own name by McCranie's pipe shop in Charlotte, North Carolina. A measured topping is applied over a dark, full-bodied Cavendish leaf, resulting in a cool-smoking, very light-nicotine smoke. The fine cut packs and lights easily, with balanced moisture. Suited to those new to aromatics and to those wanting a light, all-day smoke. As with sweet, Cavendish-heavy blends generally, small-to-medium-capacity pipes reduce the risk of tongue bite and flavor loss.
mccranies-black-lace.o: Leaves a sweet, faintly caramel-like aroma.

craven-craven-aromatic-original.z: Craven Aromatic is the aromatic product of the brand named after the mixture nineteenth-century London tobacconist Carreras prepared for the third Earl of Craven. Today it's sold in the UK in 25-gram packs under the name Craven Original. The ribbon-cut blend is built on Burley and Virginia leaf; it's flavored with a casing the maker doesn't disclose, and its description notes a sweet top note. Strength and flavor intensity are low, with a measured casing; Burley's dry texture, close to milky cocoa, comes to the front. Aimed at smokers looking for a light, cased everyday blend, away from heavy aromatics. Its character is recorded as changing noticeably depending on the pack's moisture level.
craven-craven-aromatic-original.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, soft scent close to cocoa.

criss-cross-vanilla-blend.z: Criss Cross is a budget-class tobacco brand sold in large bags in the US. Per the brand's own marketing, the base blend is built from air-cured Burley and Virginia leaf, presented in a fine, shag-like cut, and described as containing fewer stems than competitors. Though the product is sold under the name pipe tobacco, its structure is close to roll-your-own cigarette use. Vanilla Blend is the version with a vanilla-style casing added to this base. The smoke carries a sweet, creamy top note, with the tobacco's own taste falling behind the casing. Aimed at users looking for a heavily flavored, fast-burning, low-cost tobacco; not suited to those expecting a layered pipe smoke.
criss-cross-vanilla-blend.o: Leaves a scent of sweet vanilla and roasted tobacco.

g-l-pease-windjammer.z: Windjammer is a fine-flake blend that brings together ripe Virginias, nutty burley, untopped roasted black cavendish, and a generous measure of perique. A small amount of dark rum is added to the mix as a binder and sweetener. It burns slow and clean, and is noted to carry flavours reminiscent of cocoa, black walnut, and dried fruit, leaving a full body on the palate. It is aimed at smokers wanting to try the Virginia-Perique structure alongside a light spirits topping.
g-l-pease-windjammer.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of raisins, cocoa, and rum.

watch-city-cigar-capn-boomers.z: This is described as an American-type house mixture linked to Watch City Cigar's Moby Dick-themed blend series; no published maker record could be found.
watch-city-cigar-capn-boomers.o: Could not be determined from the records.

g-l-pease-haddos-delight.z: Haddo's Delight is a full-bodied G. L. Pease blend combining various Virginia leaves with long-cut perique. Untopped Green River black cavendish and a small amount of air-cured white burley add fullness and extra body to the blend. The producer's own processing darkens the mixture and brings the components closer together; cocoa and dried-fruit facets appear in the tin aroma. Full in nicotine, this blend suits experienced smokers who lean toward a perique-forward, dark Virginia character.
g-l-pease-haddos-delight.o: Leaves a dark, sweetish aroma reminiscent of cocoa and dried fruit.

backwoods-black-n-gold.z: Black 'N Gold is one of the aromatic blends in the pipe tobacco line of Backwoods, the American brand known for its cigar papers. Coarse, irregularly cut Burley and Virginia leaf is used together with dark Cavendish; a vanilla-and-caramel-forward flavoring is applied over it. The topping is also described as carrying notes of honey, citrus, and herbs. Body sits between light and medium; since nicotine load is kept low, it doesn't weigh even over long smokes, while the sweetness stays pronounced. It's aimed at smokers looking for the familiar sugar profile of cheap bulk aromatics, who want scent and sweetness more than tobacco character. The line is also notable for carrying the brand's cigar-side flavor names over to its pipe tobacco.
backwoods-black-n-gold.o: Vanilla caramel and honey fill the room, trailed by a light citrus-peel note.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-singleton.z: Referred to under the Scandinavian Tobacco Group umbrella, according to records a burley-forward blend; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

captain-black-cherry.z: Captain Black is the best-known brand of mass-produced aromatic pipe tobacco sold in American supermarkets and tobacco outlets. Cherry is the cherry-flavored member of the line; a strong cherry casing is applied over a black-Cavendish-forward base. The cut is ribbon and the tobacco is packed as a sticky mass. It is extremely light in nicotine; the casing itself, rather than the tobacco flavor, comes to the fore in the smoke. The cherry aroma carries a synthetic, intense character, and the room note is pronounced in the same direction. Because moisture content is high, it needs to be aired before filling, otherwise it burns wet and leaves residue in the bowl. A blend aimed at smokers seeking a strong fruit aroma rather than tobacco character.
captain-black-cherry.o: Leaves a heavy, sugary cherry-syrup aroma.

rivertown-tobacco-works-crimson-shadow.z: Crimson Shadow is a balanced blend from Rivertown Tobacco Works' bulk line, built on stoved red Virginia and black Cavendish. The red Virginia gives the blend its lead flavor: a tart citrus, bread, dark fruit, and light wood character. Black Cavendish forms an earthy, nutty, molasses-like creamy base. The ribbon cut burns cool and even; flavor intensity is kept at a medium level. The brand also positions this line as components tobacconists can use for their own house blends, so it works both smoked alone and as a mixing ingredient. It suits smokers looking for an unflavored, plain Virginia-Cavendish profile.
rivertown-tobacco-works-crimson-shadow.o: Leaves a warm trace where bready sweetness meets a light molasses aroma.

lane-limited-royal-canadian.z: Not enough independent sources could be found documenting the contents and character of American blender Lane Limited's blend called Royal Canadian.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-golden-mixture.z: Golden Mixture is a light-colored Orlik mixture built mainly on pressed Virginia leaf. Loose-cut Virginia, toasted burley, and black cavendish are added to it, resulting in a structure that combines different cuts together. The top note applied is limited, used to bring out the blend's natural sweetness. It packs easily and smokes cool; nicotine level stays low. The taste is balanced between Virginia's fresh, sweet side and cavendish's mellowness, with the topping not dominant. It forms a stepping stone for smokers wanting to move from heavy aromatics toward unflavored Virginia blends.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-golden-mixture.o: Leaves a fresh, sweetish, lightly bready scent.

ken-byron-ventures-burlington-arcade.z: A blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches, listed in catalogs as an English mixture; since the maker's own page carries no current profile, no verifiable information on its contents and character could be compiled.

cornell-diehl-spencer-house.z: No current listing for Cornell & Diehl's Spencer House blend could be found in the maker's own catalogue or major retailer pages; its composition and character could not be confirmed.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2009.z: Christmas Cheer 2009 is the 2009 release of McClelland's single-crop annual Virginia series. Flue-cured Virginia leaves picked at peak maturity are pressed into cake, matured, sliced, and partly broken up before being tinned as broken flake. It's an unflavored blend; the taste comes from the leaf's own sugar, following a bready, fruity line. On opening the tin, the brand's characteristic sharp, vinegary aroma is pronounced. Since each year's crop is separate, releases are treated as distinct records from one another. Aimed at smokers used to working with flake form who seek unflavored Virginia. The maker halted operations in early 2018.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2009.o: Leaves a tangy, vinegary sweetness along with a toasted-bread aroma.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-imperial-english.z: Imperial English is a traditional mixture combining red Virginia, Turkish tobacco and burley with Latakia and perique. Virginia sweetness forms the base while Latakia's smoke and perique add a peppery-fruity sharpness; the manufacturer describes the blend as medium strength. A suitable starting point for smokers wanting to enter the classic English style while avoiding too heavy a Latakia proportion. It carries no flavor casing.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-imperial-english.o: Leaves a lightly peppery trace along with a smoke and wood-smoke aroma.

hu-tobacco-aus-dem-krater-nr-1.z: The Aus dem Krater line is HU Tobacco's special series referencing the Nördlinger Ries crater region. Nr. 1 is a flake in which Virginia and Burley leaves are combined with black Cavendish; the maker's description highlights unusual spicy and toasted notes.
hu-tobacco-aus-dem-krater-nr-1.o: Leaves a peppery, lightly smoky tobacco aroma following dried-fruit sweetness.

motzek-yamyam-no-17.z: A blend mentioned among the products of the Kiel-based TAK workshop; no independent source confirming its composition and character could be found.

house-of-calabash-wild-rose.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for House of Calabash's Wild Rose blend, so its content and character could not be recorded.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.z: This is the coffee-flavored version of the Cândido Giovanella line. The Brazilian maker Imigrantes Fumos's shared base applies here too: Virginia and Burley leaf are joined by black Cavendish, and the tobacco is packed in ribbon cut. In the smoke, roasted coffee's lightly burnt, sweetish taste is pronounced; Burley adds a dry, nutty body while Cavendish balances the sweetness. The smoke is cool, and the nicotine load is moderate. It suits those looking for an aromatic that pairs with coffee for a morning smoke.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.o: Leaves an aroma of freshly brewed coffee and roasted beans.

holger-danske-original-tobacco.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for Holger Danske's Original Tobacco blend, so its content and character could not be recorded.

alfie-turmeaus-mystery-mix-a.z: One of the unnamed experimental mixtures from Turmeaus tobacconist; no accessible source documenting its content or character could be found.

peter-heinrichs-no-127.z: Peter Heinrichs No. 127 is an aromatic blend built by combining broadly cut, light-colored Virginia leaves with slices that have gone through the Cavendish process. Per the maker's account, this structure gives a slow, cool burn; the blend is rounded out with some black Cavendish. What determines its character is the special peach essence added to the blend; a fruity, soft flavor profile results. Nicotine sits in the light band, while the flavoring level is pronounced. It is a suitable record for smokers seeking fruit-flavored, light-nicotine everyday blends.
peter-heinrichs-no-127.o: Leaves a ripe peach and candied fruit aroma.

mac-baren-amphora-burley-blend.z: Amphora Burley Blend represents the burley-forward line within Mac Baren's long-running Amphora series. Most of the blend is burley; a small amount of Virginia leaf is added for balance. It's presented ready rubbed — hand-rubbed and ready to pack. Burley's nutty, dry and earthy character sits at the center of the blend; Virginia leaves a measured sweetness in the background. Casing is not pronounced. Nicotine is medium and it offers a filling smoke. Suited to those who love unflavored or lightly flavored burley blends and want to follow the tobacco taste rather than sweetness.
mac-baren-amphora-burley-blend.o: Leaves a room note reminiscent of nuts, lightly earthy and mildly sweet.

georgetown-tobacco-berkebile-special-res.z: A shop blend carrying the name of Georgetown Tobacco's founder, David Berkebile, said to be based on pure Virginia; since it doesn't appear in the producer's current catalog, its composition and production status could not be confirmed.
georgetown-tobacco-berkebile-special-res.o: No record of the room aroma could be found.

paul-olsen-dark-flake.z: Dark Flake is the classic flake tobacco of the Copenhagen-based My Own Blend line. Its body is built from matured dark Virginia leaves, joined by fire-cured Kentucky and a share of cavendish, then pressed and sliced. The Kentucky share gives the blend an earthy, lightly smoky depth, while Virginia provides a bready, dried-fruit-like natural sweetness. Rubbed between the fingers before lighting, the slices burn slowly and coolly. Flavoring is next to none, so it's aimed at smokers accustomed to flake tobaccos who want a straightforward Virginia character. The brand descends from the personal-blending tradition Paul Olsen began at his Copenhagen shop in 1939, and the blends are now offered through The Danish Pipe Shop in Copenhagen.
paul-olsen-dark-flake.o: Leaves a dark, tartly sweet tobacco scent mingling with dry hay and light smoke.

paul-olsen-no-45.z: One of the Virginia-forward blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

cornell-diehl-carolina-red-flake-w-periq.z: Carolina Red Flake w/Perique is the perique-added version of the red Virginia flake Cornell & Diehl releases in its yearly Small Batch series; the 2025 edition is among the final entries of that cycle. The base leaf is ripe red Virginia, pressed and sliced; Louisiana perique adds a spicy, fruity layer to the blend. The blend is unflavored, meaning no added flavoring. Virginia's bready sweetness balances against perique's pepper-and-dried-fig side; nicotine sits at medium, and the body becomes more pronounced as the perique ratio rises. Being a flake, it calls for slow, cool smoking; it is aimed at smokers familiar with the VaPer style and accustomed to unflavored leaf taste. Being limited production, after its release season it remained available only in aged stashes.
cornell-diehl-carolina-red-flake-w-periq.o: Leaves a trace where black pepper and dried fig aroma mix into a bready sweetness.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-boswells-black-che.z: Black Cherry is an aromatic where cherry aroma is applied over black cavendish. The manufacturer describes the blend as one whose taste and aroma stay very close to black cherry itself; it is noted for its dry burn and even lighting. Dating back to the early 1980s, this blend is one of the Boswell workshop's early signatures. Suitable for smokers who want the fruit note in aromatic tobaccos to be clear and single-note, and who don't mind a pronounced room aroma.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-boswells-black-che.o: Leaves a ripe black cherry aroma, with sweet cavendish sugar sensed underneath.

danske-club-black-virginia.z: A blend from the Danish brand Danske Club said to be aromatic; there isn't enough reliable source material to confirm its composition and character.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-riversmeet-flake.z: Riversmeet Flake is an unflavored flake made from pure, pressed-and-sliced Virginia leaves. Pressing and resting bring out the leaf's natural sugar; once the slices are rubbed and loosened, it gives a slow, cool burn. Its strength ranges from light toward medium.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-riversmeet-flake.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of dry hay and honey.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-troost-ar.z: Troost is a Dutch brand that began production under the van Rossem company in Rotterdam, passed to Theodorus Niemeyer after 1991, and from there to Scandinavian Tobacco Group. Aromatic Cavendish continues the brand's traditional Dutch-style cavendish direction: Virginia sweetness, mild burley, and a small amount of Oriental leaf are put through a special process to achieve a round, smooth taste.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-troost-ar.o: Leaves a sweetish, mild, and lightly floral tobacco scent.

century-vanilla.z: Century Vanilla is the most straightforward aromatic record in the line. Per the seller's description, light-colored cavendish and virginia leaf are added to a base of toasted black cavendish; the blend is topped with a rich vanilla-bean flavoring. Its pre-rubbed cut allows it to be loaded directly into the pipe. Sweetness is kept measured, aiming for a cool-burning tobacco; though vanilla is the dominant note, cavendish's own sugar can be sensed. Nicotine stays light. Suitable for those new to the pipe and smokers seeking a classic vanilla aromatic.
century-vanilla.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough aroma.

blenders-gold-natural-cavendish.z: Natural Cavendish is a Cavendish-based blend in Sutliff's Blender's Gold line, aimed at the American tobacco maker's bulk market. Per the product description it's made from imported and domestic leaf, offers a fine-cut leaf put through the classic Cavendish process, and is kept very mild so it won't bite the tongue. The line was sold for a long time in pouch packaging on drugstore-chain shelves, later moving to 3.5-ounce tins. In character it's a plain, straightforward tobacco: aside from the mild sweetness the Cavendish process brings, it carries no pronounced flavor layer, burns cool and dry, and — thanks to low tin moisture — packs and lights easily. Its low nicotine makes it suitable for pipe beginners and for smokers wanting a mild background tobacco to smoke throughout the day; those wanting more intense flavor usually use it as a component mixed into other blends. According to records, similarly composed blends can also be found in the same maker's Super Value and Admiral's Choice lines.
blenders-gold-natural-cavendish.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, baked-grain room note.

doctor-pipe-english-mixture.z: Representing Doctor Pipe's traditional English mixture branch, this blend is built from Latakia, Oriental leaves, red Virginia and Perique. Since no flavoring is added, the taste comes entirely from the leaves' own character.
doctor-pipe-english-mixture.o: Leaves a lightly spicy trace along with soot and resinous wood scent.

iwan-ries-dr-bradley.z: Dr. Bradley is one of the long-running house blends of Iwan Ries & Co., which has operated in Chicago since 1857. Per the maker's description, it's a full, sweet tobacco; though it carries an aromatic hint, it doesn't give a dominant aromatic flavor or aroma. In that respect, it sits at a crossing point between American-style "codger" blends and more unflavored mixtures. Its base is built on Burley and Virginia leaves; black Cavendish adds sweetness, and a measured Latakia share adds a light smoky layer as well. Records indicate the fine top flavoring leans toward plum-like dried fruit and doesn't mask the tobacco's natural taste. It suits smokers looking for a medium-strength, lightly flavored American blend that can be smoked all day.
iwan-ries-dr-bradley.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, dried-fruit-like aroma with a subtle wood smoke.

charatan-charatan-no-4.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the British pipe maker Charatan.

city-cigar-company-sweet-seymour.z: Sweet Seymour, a house blend from the tobacconist City Cigar Company, is referred to in available records as an aromatic; not enough sourcing could be found to document its content.
city-cigar-company-sweet-seymour.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-don-carlos.z: One of Cornell & Diehl's older English-style blends; it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog, and not enough sourcing could be found to verify its composition.

seattle-pipe-club-columbia-river.z: Columbia River, signed by Seattle Pipe Club, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

alfie-turmeaus-morrison-blend.z: Morrison Blend is one of the Latakia-based mixtures presented by Turmeaus tobacconist under its own name in 50-gram tins. Its recipe is built on sweet golden Virginia leaf and a roughly equal share of smoky Latakia; a small amount of black Cavendish completing the composition adds a dark, lightly sugary base. Keeping Virginia and Latakia nearly equal produces a more pronounced smoky layer than usual in this type of mixture. It's a high-flavor-intensity, medium-nicotine smoke; the sweetness brought by the Cavendish softens Latakia's dry smokiness. Records mark it as discontinued in the maker's listing. It suits smokers familiar with smoky English mixtures, looking for a straightforward structure where Virginia sweetness runs alongside Latakia.
alfie-turmeaus-morrison-blend.o: Leaves a smoky-wood and resinous pine-smoke room note along with a sweet bread note.

wessex-aromatic.z: Wessex Aromatic Mixture is the aromatic member of the Wessex series, which carries on the English-style production tradition. Virginia, Burley, and black cavendish leaf are brought together in ribbon cut, topped with a measured flavoring giving cocoa and vanilla notes.
wessex-aromatic.o: Leaves a cocoa-and-vanilla-forward scent with a nutty undertone.

peretti-ampersand-flake.z: A pressed slice tobacco listed among L.J. Peretti's flake-group house blends, still offered in 1 ounce, 8 ounce, and 1 pound sizes; no published source describing its leaf composition and flavor character could be found.

mcclelland-m-40-rum-toddy.z: As the name suggests, a rum-flavored blend in McClelland's bulk aromatic series; no sufficient source documenting its composition could be found.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-captain-earles-t.z: Ten Russians is a full-bodied English mixture built on Latakia, Oriental leaves, and Virginias. It's presented as a pressed crumble cake, opened by hand before filling. Latakia stands pronouncedly in front; the Orientals give a tart-spicy edge, while the Virginias give a measured sweetness that rounds out the smoke. Given its high nicotine and flavor intensity, it calls for slow smoking. The blend's name comes from the story in which Captain James A. M. Earle is said to have rescued ten Russians adrift in a small boat in the Sea of Japan. Like the other Captain Earle's blends, it's produced by Cornell & Diehl for Hermit Tobacco Works. It suits smokers familiar with heavy Latakia mixtures.
hermit-tobacco-works-co-captain-earles-t.o: Heavy wood smoke and smoked-leather aroma settles into the room.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-john-cottons-n.z: John Cotton's numbered mixtures are the best-known products of the brand's Edinburgh-rooted history. This record, a medium-strength combination of the No. 1 and No. 2 blends, is noted alongside 'No. 1 Mild' in a 1986 Gallaher document; the brand's trail is lost after that date, and in the years production rights changed hands the product was listed under the Orlik Tobacco Company A/S name. The blend is a classic latakia-built English-type mixture: Virginia leaves supply the base body, latakia the smoky, incense-like layer, and oriental leaves the tart spice. Its ribbon cut and medium strength strike a balance a smoker new to latakia mixtures can also follow; records note that extended tin aging pulls the latakia's sharpness back and lets the orientals come forward.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-john-cottons-n.o: Leaves a smoky scent dominated by charred wood and incense.

b-b-tobacconists-llc-scotts-companion.z: One of the shop blends from B&B Tobacconists in Asheville; according to records it's a Virginia-Perique-centered mixture, though no adequate source verifying its content could be found.

hearth-home-delta-days.z: Delta Days is an unflavored blend that combines the toasted sweetness of aged red Virginia with dark mahogany Burley and a substantial portion of Perique. Perique is a pressure-fermented tobacco produced in Louisiana's Mississippi delta, and it lends the blend a plummy, peppery bite. The Burley's presence gives it a fuller body and nutty depth than typical Virginia-Perique blends, yet the taste stays even rather than jagged. Well suited to smokers who want Perique's spice but are after something heartier than a blend leaning solely on Virginia sweetness.
hearth-home-delta-days.o: Leaves a dark tobacco aroma reminiscent of dried figs and black pepper.

gambler-regular.z: Gambler Regular is a blend sold in bulk bags, produced by Republic Tobacco in the United States. It consists of flue-cured Virginia and Burley leaf, is a fine-to-medium ribbon cut, and is not classified as aromatic. Its body is light to medium; Burley's dry, nutty taste and Virginia's light sweetness lead, with no complex flavour construction intended. Since it is sold in large bags, it is used as an everyday blend among heavier smokers; the cut suits pipe use as well as rolling papers and tubes. It suits those seeking a plain, untopped, American-style everyday tobacco.
gambler-regular.o: Leaves a plain, dry, woody tobacco aroma.

milan-tobacconists-jefferson-street.z: Jefferson Street is one of the house blends Roanoke, Virginia-based Milan Tobacconists sells under its own name. A sliced burley-forward body is joined by some Turkish tobacco and cavendish, topped with a sauce evoking rum and raisin. It gives a medium-strength, nutty, sweetish profile. Because it combines burley's dry, nutty base with a light aromatic dressing, it's a fitting option for smokers who avoid heavily sugared aromatics but aren't drawn to fully unflavored blends either. The blend's name comes from South Jefferson Street, where the shop has stood since 1912.
milan-tobacconists-jefferson-street.o: A nutty tobacco base accompanies the sweet rum-and-raisin aroma.

city-cigar-company-citys-own-2655.z: City's Own #2655, a house blend from the tobacconist City Cigar Company, is referred to in available records as an aromatic; not enough sourcing could be found to document its content.
city-cigar-company-citys-own-2655.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

william-p-solomon-presbyterian-mixture.z: Presbyterian Mixture is a ribbon-cut, unflavored English-style blend dominated by Virginia and Oriental leaf. The smoke is cool and mildly sweet, with moderate strength. Whether the blend contains Latakia has long been a point of debate: it gives a smoky, sooty impression, but it's not certain whether this comes from the Oriental leaf or a small proportion of Latakia. This ambiguity has played a part in the blend's reputation among its following. In character it is more restrained than heavy smoky mixtures, making it an entry point for smokers curious about English-style blends but wary of a heavy Latakia content. It also appeals to those who want to experience the Oriental leaf's spicy tones alongside Virginia's sweetness. The ribbon cut makes it easy to pack and light, with an intensity suited to all-day smoking.
william-p-solomon-presbyterian-mixture.o: Leaves a lightly smoky scent reminiscent of dry grass and spicy Oriental leaf.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-portorico.z: A pipe-tobacco brand within Scandinavian Tobacco Group's portfolio; no independent source on the blend's content and character could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-portorico.o: No detailed description of the room note could be found in the records.

robert-mcconnell-shakespeare.z: Shakespeare is one of the replacement blends offered after Dunhill-branded tobaccos ceased production, marketed as a stand-in for Ye Olde Signe, which Dunhill began producing in 1916. It is made under the Robert McConnell name by the German firm Kohlhase & Kopp. The tin holds fine-ribbon Golden Virginia together with bulkier Red Virginia, the two cuts distinguishable by eye; the aroma is sugary, lightly spicy, and suggests fruit. Casing is very light; when rested in a jar, a faint green, tea-like note with a touch of spice and fruit comes forward. It burns slow and steady, the smoke is light and easy-flowing, and strength sits at a medium level; as the bowl progresses the flavor intensifies and tones reminiscent of cigarette tobacco increase. It suits smokers who want to follow the distinction between two Virginia types and prefer a mild, lightly flavored smoke.
robert-mcconnell-shakespeare.o: Leaves a light but distinct tobacco aroma reminiscent of cigarette tobacco.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2007.z: Christmas Cheer 2007 is the 2007 release of the series in which McClelland tinned a separate Virginia harvest each year. The leaf is dried by the flue-cure method, matured pressed into cake, and after slicing, partly broken up and packaged as broken flake. The blend carries no flavoring; sweetness comes entirely from the leaf's own sugar and maturation. The tin note carries the brand's characteristic sharp tang, while the smoke shows a bready, fruity Virginia line. Smokers who collect tins to cellar for aging track the series' years separately. Production ended in 2018.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2007.o: Leaves a tangy, vinegary sweetness along with a toasted-bread aroma.

nat-sherman-527-morningside-golden.z: Among Nat Sherman's numbered aromatic house blends; while it is mentioned in forum records, no independent source explaining its composition could be found.

e-a-carey-desert-island-mixture.z: An aromatic mixture referred to under the E. A. Carey name; no source could be found documenting its composition and character.

dunhill-my-mixture-36166.z: A discontinued mixture belonging to Dunhill's My Mixture line, for which no verifiable source on its composition could be found.

mcclelland-royal-cajun-dark.z: Royal Cajun Dark is the dark member of the three-blend series McClelland built around a component it calls Cajun Black. Cajun Black is made from Virginia-seed leaf grown in Kentucky, smoked and then barrel-pressed and fermented as with Perique. Dark is made by combining five separate red and stoved Virginia leaves with a generous amount of Cajun Black. The tin note carries a Perique-like, woody, and smoky character, with the brand's familiar tanginess also present. In the smoke, woody, smoky, spicy, and herbal layers interweave; a tangy-citrus sharpness balances the Virginia sweetness. Body is medium. Suited to smokers wanting to try a fermented leaf different from the usual Virginia-Perique axis. McClelland stopped production in 2018.
mcclelland-royal-cajun-dark.o: Leaves a woody, smoky, and spicy aroma, with a tangy fruit note behind it.

cornell-diehl-lunchtime-blues.z: Lunchtime Blues is the second blend in Cornell & Diehl's Working Man series, designed to be smoked during the midday break. Virginia and a small amount of Oriental leaf are added to a Burley base; it's ribbon cut, with no casing. On the smoke, Burley's nutty, dry texture leads, Virginia sweetness accompanies it, and Oriental leaf gives a subtle spice in the background. The profile stays soft and balanced throughout the bowl. Suited to those looking for an unflavored, medium-strength Burley blend they can smoke in a short session during the day.
cornell-diehl-lunchtime-blues.o: A light spice mingles with a nutty, dry-grassy tobacco scent.

mcclelland-no-610-caramel.z: A caramel-flavored blend in McClelland's numbered bulk aromatic series; no sufficient source documenting its composition could be found.

mcclelland-orient-996-vintage-2007.z: Orient 996 is a McClelland mixture that puts Oriental leaf at the blend's center. The first batch was prepared in a limited run for the Pipe Club of America in 2007, with a second batch released in 2009 under the maker's Collectors Series banner. The Oriental tobaccos' dry, spicy, faintly tangy character is joined by Virginia sweetness, while Syrian Latakia stays like a shadow without pushing the sooty side forward. The mixture isn't heavy, offering a light smoke with a strong flavor dimension. According to sources, airing the tobacco sharpens its character; after a few hours of airing, the Oriental leaf's fine balance reads more clearly. Suited to those familiar with Oriental tobacco taste who seek Oriental-focused smokes rather than Latakia-heavy English mixtures. Since McClelland halted production entirely in early 2018, the blend survives only in old tins.
mcclelland-orient-996-vintage-2007.o: Leaves a fine, smoky trace of wood mixed into dry hay and spice aromas.

just-for-him-buccaneer-blend.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Just For Him's Buccaneer Blend.

wessex-balkan-supreme.z: Wessex is an English-origin name first used as a pipe brand by Hall & Fitzgerald, later passed on to a tobacco line. Balkan Supreme belongs to the brand's series known as Brigade, and is classified as a ribbon-cut English/Balkan-style mixture. Virginia leaves build the backbone; Latakia's smoky tone and the Oriental leaf's dry, spicy sharpness settle into this foundation. Its smoke carries wood soot, a salty-spicy framework, and a light sweetness from the Virginia in the background. Nicotine sits at a medium level, while the intensity on the palate is pronounced. It suits smokers accustomed to Latakia-forward mixtures who seek unflavored, smoky tobacco; it's not an entry point for those coming from aromatic blends.
wessex-balkan-supreme.o: Leaves a scent of smoky wood and spicy dry grass reminiscent of a campfire.

4noggins-bakerstreet-usa.z: Bakerstreet, USA is an English blend prepared for 4noggins by Matt Robillard. According to the manufacturer's account, the blend came about at the suggestion that Robillard try his hand at an English-style recipe. Its composition includes a measured amount of Latakia, various Oriental leaves, Virginias, and a small portion of Burley; the Latakia is kept in the background rather than dominant. The result is a profile with moderate smokiness underpinned by a light sweetness from the Virginia. No additives are reported. Nicotine is moderate and flavor is medium-to-full-bodied. It suits smokers who find heavy Latakia blends too intense but still want the dry, smoky framework of English-style tobacco; the maker positions it as the day's last pipe.
4noggins-bakerstreet-usa.o: Leaves a lightly smoky, sweetish dry-leaf aroma.

john-b-hayes-tobacconist-revolution.z: One of American tobacconist John B. Hayes' counter blends; no verifiable information on its contents could be found.
john-b-hayes-tobacconist-revolution.o: No verifiable information on its room note could be found.

sentimiento-nacional-centinela.z: One of Sentimiento Nacional's blends named after references to Argentine history; no verifiable source on its content could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-base-15.z: One of the unflavored Virginia-burley mixtures Sutliff sells as base material for blending; sufficient independent sources giving its exact proportions could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-base-15.o: Records indicate it leaves a plain scent of dry hay and nutty leaf.

mcclelland-syrian-super-balkan.z: Syrian Super Balkan is among the fullest-bodied members of McClelland's Syrian-Latakia-based blends. Per the maker's description, dark, cool-smoking Syrian Latakia forms the blend's backbone, joined by Oriental tobaccos, Virginia leaf, and a generous amount of Louisiana Perique. This Perique addition is the key point separating it from its sibling blend in the series. In the smoke, Perique's dark-fruit, spicy sharpness rides atop the smoky Latakia layer; Virginia sweetness balances the pair. Body is full and the nicotine load is pronounced. Aimed at experienced smokers wanting Latakia and Perique together at a high dose. The brand ceased operations in 2018.
mcclelland-syrian-super-balkan.o: A spiced, dark-fruit note mixes into an intense aroma of incense and wood smoke.

kleinlagel-cucumber.z: Cucumber is one of German manufacturer Kleinlagel's unusually themed blends. Dark ready-rubbed flake, some Perique, soft Black Cavendish and wide-cut Virginia are brought together; the mixture is flavored with fresh cucumber and rested dried-fruit aromas. Perique's spice, combined with the cucumber theme, leaves a dill-like line. Nicotine is low, taste is measured; the cucumber note doesn't dominate, and dried-fruit sweetness stays in the background. Suited to those wanting to try an unusual aroma and familiar with the Virginia-Perique structure. It was sold in a 50-gram tin; per retailer records, it's been delisted.
kleinlagel-cucumber.o: A cool, green scent reminiscent of fresh cucumber peel leaves alongside dried fruit's sweet scent.

faders-cherry-vanilla.z: Not enough independent sourcing documenting the composition and character of Cherry Vanilla, one of the house blends of the Baltimore-based Fader's tobacconist, could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-scare-o.z: Scare-O-Matic is an American-style aromatic released under Ken Byron Ventures' budget sub-line, Mr. Christian's. White Burley and black Cavendish are worked in a heavy casing that gives off a creamy licorice-root aroma; the maker describes the blend as a twist on the classic American aromatic. It's offered as 2 oz. bulk. Nicotine is moderate and the smoke is mild; the weight of the sugary casing can make it feel damp, and it may need some airing before smoking. Aimed at smokers looking for a pronounced sweet-spiced aroma rather than plain leaf taste, and who like aromatics with a strong room note. It's part of the brand's autumn seasonal releases.
ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-scare-o.o: Leaves a creamy licorice-root and confectionery aroma.

planta-akropolis.z: Akropolis is a blend, said to be Oriental-heavy, from Planta Tabak-Manufaktur, founded in Berlin in 1956, whose brand portfolio passed to Mac Baren in 2021; no source could be found describing its composition, so no detailed specification is given.

mccranies-red-flake-vintage-1996.z: McCranie's Pipe Shop is a long-established tobacconist in Charlotte, North Carolina; the shop's tinned tobacco line began with red Virginia leaf from a single harvest set aside exclusively for it. This leaf is rested and pressed; the name flake refers to the presentation in which the pressed block is left in slices rather than broken up. Records indicate the year on the tin (1996) marks the leaf's harvest/packing year, and batches stamped with other years circulate under the same name. Being unflavored, single-varietal Virginia, the tobacco's taste comes from the leaf's own sugar: a bready, creamy base with a sweet depth that deepens with age. Nicotine load runs light to medium, making it suitable for all-day smoking. Aimed at smokers seeking an unflavored Virginia who want to smoke slowly and follow the leaf's own taste. The shop no longer continues this line; what's on the market are older batches.
mccranies-red-flake-vintage-1996.o: Leaves a sweetish hay aroma with a faint bready note.

straus-tobacco-buttermilk-pike.z: An aromatic house blend from Straus Tobacconist taking its name from Buttermilk Pike road in Northern Kentucky; no verifiable source describing its composition could be found.

clan-shaw-pennsylvania.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Pennsylvania.

ravenwood-fine-provisions-bison-burley.z: Bison Burley is one of the blends US home blender James Ravenwood prepares in small batches under the name Ravenwood Fine Provisions; the products are distributed through The Briar Fellowship. Most of the blend consists of unprocessed, nutty, straight dark-fired cut Burley, accompanied by Virginia. The blender states that a portion of the Burley and Virginia is lightly sweet-cased and then toasted to caramelize, a step that leaves the leaf with varying color tones and a brown-sugar note. The result is a tobacco in the line of old-school "codger" Burley blends, with light flavoring and pronounced nicotine. It suits experienced smokers looking for natural Burley taste, expecting sweetness from the leaf rather than added flavoring.
ravenwood-fine-provisions-bison-burley.o: Leaves a dry tobacco aroma with roasted walnut and brown sugar.

newminster-no-3b-black-cherry.z: Newminster No. 3B Black Cherry is a bulk aromatic prepared as a ribbon cut of black Cavendish, Burley, and Virginia leaves. The black cherry flavoring that gives the blend its name is highlighted by the manufacturer as its distinguishing feature. The cherry note holds through the pouch aroma and the smoke alike; Cavendish sweetness supports this note, while Burley gives the body a dry base. Nicotine is light. Suitable for those who enjoy fruit-flavored tobaccos and for smokers new to the aromatic world.
newminster-no-3b-black-cherry.o: Leaves a pronounced, sweet cherry aroma in the room.

gq-tobaccos-askwith-kake.z: Askwith Kake is a Virginia-Perique blend that the small English producer GQ Tobaccos prepared for Askwith Pipes. The blend's starting idea was to build a Perique-dominant smoke by raising the Perique ratio from the roughly five percent typical in this style to twenty percent. The product is pressed into a crumble cake; the needed amount is broken off and rubbed out by hand before use. The base is built from two separate Virginias: hot-air-cured leaf gives a herbal but not flat base with a measured citrus-and-honey sweetness, while steamed Virginia leaves a lightly fruity, occasionally vegetal edge. Perique layers plum, raisin, and a measured spiciness on top of these. Nicotine runs above average. Despite the high Perique ratio, the blend stays coherent rather than falling apart. The producer no longer makes this blend, so it is only found in old stock.
gq-tobaccos-askwith-kake.o: Leaves a tart tobacco aroma reminiscent of dried plum and spice.

cascade-cigar-tobbaco-perfect-blend.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Perfect Blend under the Cascade Cigar & Tobbaco brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

straus-tobacco-rookwood.z: Referred to among Straus Tobacconist's aromatic counter blends; no verifiable source describing its composition and character could be found.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-hunting-c.z: Hunting Creek, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an aromatic mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

gawith-hoggarth-co-latakia-cc-blending.z: Latakia CC Blending is the Latakia entry in Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s coarse-cut single-leaf series. Sources indicate the leaf used is of Cyprian origin, cured in smoke to take on a heavy smokiness. No sauce or top note is applied to the product. It isn't intended to be smoked on its own; its real function is to add smoke, depth, and dark color to English- and Balkan-style mixtures. It's a component ingredient for smokers building their own blends — its taste is very intense, and its room note spreads widely.
gawith-hoggarth-co-latakia-cc-blending.o: A heavy pine-smoke and smoked-leather aroma spreads through the room.

clan-shaw-admiral.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Admiral.
clan-shaw-admiral.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-private-blend-no.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Private Blend No8.

peter-stokkebye-virginia-long-cut.z: Virginia Long Cut is Peter Stokkebye's unflavored Virginia blend sold in bulk. Records indicate it is prepared by combining seven distinct grades of flue-cured bright Virginia leaf, presented as long, loosely cut ribbons. No flavoring is used; the tobacco's taste comes entirely from the leaf's own sugar content. On the palate, a lemony tartness and a natural sweetness recalling hay and honey come forward. Nicotine strength is between light and medium, making it suitable for long, cool smoking sessions. It suits smokers wanting to get to know unflavored Virginia character, those interested in single-leaf blends, and those who age tobacco by resting it in a jar.
peter-stokkebye-virginia-long-cut.o: Leaves a thin aroma carrying dry hay and a light bready sweetness.

lane-limited-paladin-black-cherry.z: Recorded as a cherry-flavored blend sold in bulk under Lane Limited's Paladin label; since no independent source detailing its content and character could be reached, the record is left incomplete.
lane-limited-paladin-black-cherry.o: Leaves a cherry-forward sweet fruit room note.

edwards-catalina.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Catalina, a pipe tobacco from Edward's. Edward's is a tobacconist business based in Tampa, Florida.

mcclelland-no-27.z: No. 27 is an unflavored Virginia blend in McClelland's "Matured Virginias" series. Records indicate it's an orange-red toned blend, matured as a cake and then prepared in a very fine (shag) cut. It's related to No. 25 in the series; No. 27 sits on a drier, sharper line. Its taste is dry, clean, and lightly sweet; Virginia's characteristic tangy sharpness makes itself known in the background. Smoked slowly and cool, it doesn't bite the tongue, though the fine cut can turn harsh if smoked quickly. Aimed at smokers seeking an unflavored, unadorned Virginia who want to hear the tobacco's own taste. Discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-no-27.o: Leaves a fine tobacco aroma with faint tang, dry hay, and honey tones.

abenaki-tobacco-co-pipe-dream.z: Pipe Dream is Abenaki Tobacco's vanilla-direction aromatic. Per the maker's recipe, high-grade American Burley, golden Cavendish, and Virginia are brought together; the flavoring is given via vanilla extract. The leaf is presented in a fine, thread-like cut. The fine cut allows quick lighting and easy burning; on the other hand, the pipe needs to be packed loosely. The Burley-Virginia pairing sets a balanced base beneath the flavoring — neither too sweet nor too flat. It's aimed at smokers looking for the classic vanilla aromatic line. Abenaki Tobacco was based in Conway, New Hampshire; the brand's own sales site isn't live today.
abenaki-tobacco-co-pipe-dream.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough room note.

moonshine-pipe-co-mason-jar-blend.z: No reliable manufacturer description could be found for the Mason Jar Blend carrying the Moonshine Pipe Co. name.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-pipemakers-choice.z: Pipemaker's Choice, according to the maker, is a recipe Elliott Nachwalter created for his first pipe shop in Stowe, Vermont; the blend is still carried today in Wilke Pipe Tobacco's bulk catalog. A generous amount of Latakia is added over a Virginia base, and the mixture is rounded out with a variety of cavendish leaves. Described as a medium-bodied English blend, the cavendish addition leaves only a light sweetness; Latakia smoke defines the dominant character. It suits smokers accustomed to smoky blends who want an unflavored smoke that isn't entirely dry.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-pipemakers-choice.o: Leaves a faintly sweet trace beneath the wood-smoke and soot scent.

von-eicken-dark-flake-navy-cut.z: A dark navy cut flake tobacco Von Eicken formerly produced in Hamburg and sold in tins; no sufficient source describing the blend's composition and character has been found.

compagnia-toscana-sigari-cimette-di-mast.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Compagnia Toscana Sigari pipe tobacco named Cimette di Mastro Tornabuoni, so the blend's content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

cornell-diehl-string-duster.z: String Duster is a ribbon-cut blend combining red and bright Virginia leaf with Turkish (Oriental) leaf, topped with a measured rum-and-maple casing. It carries one of Cornell & Diehl's music-referencing names. It sits on the light side in both nicotine and flavor; the casing is kept to a level that doesn't overpower the tobacco. A fitting build for those wanting a mild blend they can smoke over long stretches of the day, or those looking to move from aromatics toward unflavored Virginia blends.
cornell-diehl-string-duster.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay with a light rum-and-maple-syrup sweetness.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-222.z: Wilke No. 222 is a blend where Turkish Yenice leaf is added to a fine-cut Virginia base; a small amount of natural cavendish is mixed in, and Latakia rounds it out on top. The shag cut lets the blend catch quickly and the flavor open fast; Yenice's spice and Latakia's smoke sit above Virginia's sweetness. It's aimed at smokers seeking a balance of Oriental and Latakia, accustomed to fine-cut blends.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-222.o: Leaves a trace of dry hay beneath a scent of wood smoke and spice.

bosphorus-2018-virginia-perique.z: 2018 Virginia & Perique is a Bosphorus product built from golden Virginia and perique leaf, pressed into flake form. Per the manufacturer's description, a very small chocolate touch has been applied to the blend; this casing is barely distinguishable in the smoke, and the blend reads as an unflavored Virginia-perique. It consists entirely of Turkish tobaccos, and the perique too is prepared from Turkish leaf. Perique's tart, woody taste comes forward in the blend, with golden Virginia's sugary base leaving a natural sweetness underneath it. A woody taste lingers in the mouth after smoking. Since moisture is at the right level, the flake does not run wet when broken up and filled; it burns evenly and smokes easily. Suitable for smokers seeking a Virginia blend with pronounced perique taste and an almost imperceptible casing.
bosphorus-2018-virginia-perique.o: Leaves a lightly sweet leaf aroma over a woody, tart base.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-summer-edition-2.z: Summer Edition 2022 is the summer installment of Kohlhase & Kopp's annually renewed seasonal limited series. The blend is built on various golden Virginia leaves and black cavendish.
