The blenders aimed for a fruity profile inspired by summer, combining mirabelle plum and cherry notes with an exotic fruit casing like kiwi. It was offered in 100-gram tins. Black cavendish carries the sweetness; Virginia leaves a lightly tangy, grassy base beneath it. It's an aromatic light in nicotine with a soft body. Being produced in limited numbers, it hasn't returned to the market. Aimed at those interested in fruity, sweet blends and seeking a light all-day smoke.
kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-summer-edition-2.o: Leaves a sweet room note forward in cherry and plum with a lightly exotic fruit tone.

samuel-gawith-palace-gate.z: No sufficient source describing the content and character of this blend, classified as aromatic, from Samuel Gawith could be found.

just-for-him-blending-perique.z: One of the house blends the Just For Him tobacconist prepares at its own counter; no independent source could be found on its contents or character.

the-tobacco-barn-brush-creek.z: No sufficient source describing the leaf composition and character of Brush Creek, listed under "specialty English blend" in the house blend list of the Tobacco Barn tobacconist in Lake Forest, California, has been found.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-santa-f.z: A blend released as part of Ken Byron Ventures' small-batch production; no independent, verifiable source could be found on it.

bufflehead-pintail.z: Bufflehead was a brand producing small batches in the United States in the early 2000s, naming its blends after waterfowl; since no independent source describing this blend's content and character could be found, the entry has been left incomplete.

gallaher-limited-rich-dark-honeydew.z: Rich Dark Honeydew is a shag-cut blend Gallaher produced from dark Virginia leaf. The tobacco is nearly black in colour and was sold fully rubbed out. The "honeydew" in the name points to the light melon flavouring found in English tradition; the topping is not intense enough to give a fruity aromatic impression, and the sweetness stays measured. The taste is strong and spicy, with dark Virginia's natural sugar clearly present; it is considered heavy in nicotine. The Gallaher version is no longer in production; Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. produced a blend of the same name and, due to European Union regulations, renamed it Rich Dark Spring Dew. It is meaningful for those seeking dark, strong, lightly flavoured English-style Virginia blends.
gallaher-limited-rich-dark-honeydew.o: A light melon-like sweet trace mixes into the tartish aroma of the dark Virginia.

uhles-hunt-club-blend.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend called Hunt Club Blend has been found.
uhles-hunt-club-blend.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

schneiderwind-darley-moor.z: Darley Moor is the Schneiderwind house's dark, full-bodied pressed blend. Its foundation is fire-cured, dark-colored Kentucky flakes; these are joined by selected Virginia leaf and a pinch of Louisiana-origin perique. No additives are used; the flavor comes from the leaves' own smoky, spicy, and lightly fruity character. According to records, the blend was built with smokers accustomed to classic English mixtures in mind and is described by the producer as aimed at experienced pipe smokers. Nicotine load is pronounced, not suited to smoking on an empty stomach. The flake structure gives a slow, cool burn; it needs to be rubbed or folded for packing. Sold in 100-gram packages.
schneiderwind-darley-moor.o: Leaves the woody, smoky scent of fire-cured leaf and a hint of dried plum.

sutliff-tobacco-company-rl-english-long-.z: RL English Long Cut is one of the classic English mixtures Sutliff offers in bulk. Its base rests on lemon Virginia leaves and picked burley; latakia, Oriental (Turkish) leaves, and a small amount of perique are added. As its name suggests, it has a long-cut ribbon structure, making for easy packing and an even burn. The blend counts as unflavored; the perceived sweetness comes from the latakia and Virginia leaves' own sugars. The latakia doesn't establish a dominant weight, making it a measured starting point for those new to English mixtures. Nicotine sits light to medium; it suits smokers looking for a smoky but not suffocating smoke they can repeat throughout the day.
sutliff-tobacco-company-rl-english-long-.o: Leaves a scent of woody fire smoke with spicy, lightly sweet leaf.

my-smoking-shop-royal-champagne.z: A champagne-themed aromatic house blend from the tobacconist My Smoking Shop; no independent source documenting its composition and character could be found.
my-smoking-shop-royal-champagne.o: True to its name, it is noted to leave a sweet, fruity aroma reminiscent of sparkling wine.

cornell-diehl-speakeasy.z: Speakeasy Navy Blend is a blend in Cornell & Diehl's Cellar series, built on the traditional navy flake concept. Oriental leaf and dark fire-cured Kentucky are added to a Virginia-and-Perique pairing; a rum top note ties the blend to the navy tradition. It was first released in July 2016. At the center of the smoke is woody, earthy, lightly smoky Kentucky leaf. Virginia builds the base with tangy dark fruit and citrus tones, Perique adds spice, and the rum casing is applied in a measure that doesn't mask the leaves. Being offered in pressed slices, it can be packed either rubbed out or folded; it's full-bodied with a pronounced nicotine load.
cornell-diehl-speakeasy.o: Leaves a dark scent where woody smoke meets a molasses-rum sweetness.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-10.z: No sufficient source could be found documenting the composition and character of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Wilke No. 10.

sutliff-tobacco-company-maple-cavendish-.z: Coded 14, Maple Cavendish is referred to as a maple-syrup-flavored cavendish in Sutliff's bulk line; no independent source detailing its composition and character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-maple-cavendish-.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

mcclelland-no-x-30-pressed-burley.z: One of the pressed Burley components McClelland sold in bulk for blend-building; no sufficient source giving a detailed description could be found.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-lustleigh-coconu.z: Lustleigh Coconut is an aromatic house blend from McGahey The Tobacconist, built on black cavendish and Virginia leaf. It is given a coconut-and-nougat-based flavoring; the tobacco is presented in bulk in a ready-rubbed consistency. The body is light to medium and the nicotine load low. Cavendish's dark sugar and coconut's creamy sweetness work in the same direction, leaving the tobacco's earthy side in the background. Suitable for those looking for a pronouncedly sweet, flavored blend and for those wanting a light option for evening smoking.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-lustleigh-coconu.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of coconut and sugared almond paste.

tinder-box-black-raspberry.z: Black Raspberry is one of the fruit-flavored house blends weighed at Tinder Box stores; no verifiable source on the blend's base and cut has been found.
tinder-box-black-raspberry.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

ken-byron-ventures-sabotage.z: Sabotage is one of Ken Byron Ventures' latakia-containing blends, its name coming from a deliberate blurring of the line between aromatic and English type. Per the manufacturer's description, barrel-fermented Acadian Bright Virginia, matured red Virginia, Turkish (oriental) leaf and latakia are brought together. The distinguishing process is that cognac is soaked directly into the latakia during blending, rather than sprinkled over the tobacco; this places the casing inside the most aromatic component rather than on the surface. In the smoke, latakia's woody, smoky, leather-like side leads; oriental leaf adds a spicy, dry edge, and the Virginias add a bready, lightly fruity sweetness. The cognac isn't perceived as an independent sweet casing but as a grape-like depth sitting beneath the smoky base. Suited to smokers accustomed to latakia-based blends seeking a measured casing on top; for those expecting an unflavored English blend, it's a different structure.
ken-byron-ventures-sabotage.o: Leaves a light cognac and dried-fruit scent over a note toward wood smoke and incense.

rattray-red-rapparee-british-collection.z: Red Rapparee is a broken-flake English blend in Rattray's British Collection line. Red Virginia leaf is spiced with a generous amount of Oriental tobacco, while Latakia is used only at a touch level; the blend also contains black Cavendish. Red Virginia's sugary sweetness is balanced by the Oriental leaf's sweet-firm spice; this spice leaves a trace reminiscent of cinnamon and orange peel, occasionally recalling black pepper. Latakia plays a supporting role in the flavor, adding coolness to the smoke. Nicotine is medium, and toward the end of the bowl the Oriental leaf becomes active and gives a firm finish. It suits smokers looking for a spicy, Oriental-heavy English blend suited to after-dinner smoking. The Rattray name draws on the Scottish pipe-tobacco tradition; the brand's tobaccos are produced today in Germany.
rattray-red-rapparee-british-collection.o: Leaves a sharp aroma dominated by spicy Oriental leaf and a light incense note, filling the room.

house-of-windsor-briggs.z: Briggs Mixture is a plain blend prepared by combining sweet, light-colored Virginia with mild white Burley leaf, without a pronounced flavoring. The aim is to achieve a measured, mild smoke that lets the leaf's natural taste come forward. Because of this, flavor intensity is low, nicotine level moderate, and the burn cool. The brand's history goes back to the P. Lorillard era; in later years it was produced by House of Windsor in tins. Since House of Windsor ceased operations, the original product doesn't exist; match blends prepared in its place are sold. It suits smokers looking for a plain Virginia-Burley base and low flavor intensity, wanting a tobacco that can be smoked all day.
house-of-windsor-briggs.o: Leaves an aroma of dry hay and baked bread.

abenaki-tobacco-co-captain-spice.z: Captain Spice is Abenaki Tobacco's entry on the spicy-aromatics side. Per the maker's recipe, it's entirely black leaf processed with the "Century Black Cavendish" method; cinnamon and nutmeg are applied over it. The spice flavoring is pronounced, pushing the tobacco taste into the background. The black Cavendish base is a process known for high sugar and low tongue bite; so the blend stays mellow and round in the mouth, with a measured nicotine load. It's built for those looking for a spicy aromatic in the cold months and those new to aromatics. Abenaki Tobacco was based in Conway, New Hampshire; since its own sales site is no longer live, the blend's current production status is unclear.
abenaki-tobacco-co-captain-spice.o: Leaves a baked, sweet spice room note where cinnamon and nutmeg lead.

mcclelland-corps-full-balkan-reserve.z: Full Balkan Reserve is among the club blends McClelland produced for the Conclave of Richmond Pipe Smokers, and records indicate it was introduced in 1995. What sets the blend apart is its use of Syrian Latakia, which was growing harder to source at the time; this leaf gives a milder, creamier smoke than Cyprian Latakia. Virginia and Oriental tobaccos sit alongside the Latakia. Despite "full" in the name, its body is described as a medium Balkan mixture; the smoke is round rather than sharp, and the Oriental tobaccos' spice and the Virginia's sweetness can stand out. Nicotine dose is measured, flavor intensity pronounced. A record aimed at smokers curious about Syrian Latakia's texture and wanting a balanced Balkan profile rather than heavy smoke.
mcclelland-corps-full-balkan-reserve.o: Spiced Oriental-tobacco traces mix into a mild, creamy smoke aroma.

owl-shop-harkness-tower.z: No reliable source could be found for the Owl Shop pipe tobacco called Harkness Tower, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-countryside.z: Countryside is Boswell's English blend containing a medium level of Latakia. The manufacturer describes the blend as soft-bodied and non-tongue-biting; Latakia and Oriental leaf accompany a virginia base, and the cut is ribbon. The Latakia proportion is kept at a level that does not overtake the blend; so the smoke note is balanced by virginia's sweetness. It sits on a sweeter line than the brand's other English blend, Northwoods. Suitable for smokers newly moving to English blends or seeking a measured Latakia they can smoke all day.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-countryside.o: Leaves a sweetish tobacco aroma underneath a wood-smoke aroma.

mac-baren-navy-mixture.z: Navy Mixture is Mac Baren's presentation of the Navy line in mixed cut. Per the maker, over thirty raw leaves are used; the tin holds ready-rubbed processed Virginia and Burley, loose-cut Virginia, Burley, the brand's own Cavendish, and small flake pieces together. Having different cuts together lets the burn proceed slow and cool. In the smoke, Virginia's sweetness and Burley's nutty dryness proceed together, with Cavendish adding roundness; the rum-leaning top note typical of the Navy tradition stays at a level that doesn't mask the tobacco taste. Nicotine level is medium. Suited to pipe smokers seeking a complex texture rather than a single cut type and a balanced, all-day blend.
mac-baren-navy-mixture.o: Leaves a measured aroma reminiscent of sweet rum and dried fruit.

peretti-royal-blend.z: Royal is a mixture Peretti offers under its English-type heading, but built on oriental leaf rather than latakia. Per the maker's description, matured Virginia is combined with select oriental tobaccos, with a high proportion of Yenice leaf used in the blend. Yenice sits at the sweeter, more floral end of the oriental group, so the mixture carries a spicy mellowness rather than sharpness. With no smoky component, the profile differs markedly from latakia-heavy English blends. It suits smokers seeking the oriental leaf's character balanced by Virginia sweetness. The ribbon cut and medium moisture level allow it to be packed straight from the tin.
peretti-royal-blend.o: Leaves a spicy, dry-grass, and lightly sweet hay scent.

motzek-motzek-93.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called Motzek #93 could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-no-7-shag-choc.z: A chocolate-flavored blend belonging to Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s numbered Kendal shag series; no independent sourcing describing its composition could be found.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-no-7-shag-choc.o: Leaves a sweet aroma leaning toward dark chocolate.

samuel-gawith-scottish-autumn-flake.z: No sufficient source describing the content and character of this flake referred to under the Samuel Gawith name could be found.

butera-sweet-cavendish.z: Sweet Cavendish is the lightest blend in Butera's Royal Vintage line. Bright red and orange virginia leaves are combined in equal measure with toasted black Green River leaf and cut into ribbon form. A sweet roundness leaning toward chocolate and vanilla comes forward in the smoke; the smoke is creamy and cool, with a low tendency to bite the tongue. It can be smoked with the moisture it comes out of the tin with. Because it can run hot if puffed quickly, it calls for a slow smoke. With a very low nicotine load, suitable for smokers seeking a sweet-tasting cavendish.
butera-sweet-cavendish.o: Leaves a cocoa and sweet cream aroma.

tobacco-lane-london-fog.z: One of the house blends from the tobacconist Tobacco Lane; no verifiable source on its composition and character has been found.
tobacco-lane-london-fog.o: No source describing its aroma has been found.

pauls-pipe-shop-seminole.z: Seminole is a layered aromatic that Paul's Pipe Shop built by combining several sub-blends. Per the maker's recipe, the shop's Post Office mixture, Green River black cavendish, Brandywine, and Virginia flake are brought together; rum, maple, and amaretto are used as the top dressing. The Post Office component contributes golden Virginia and burley to the blend, while the cavendish component brings moisture and sweetness. Having flake pieces alongside ribbon-cut leaf diversifies the fill's texture and slows the burn. The flavor profile is sweet but not one-dimensional; almond, caramelized syrup, and rum notes come forward in turn. It suits smokers who enjoy flavored blends but want several layers of aroma at once.
pauls-pipe-shop-seminole.o: Leaves a scent of maple syrup, rum, and almond.

koltoma-porter-foam.z: One of the burley-forward blends from Russian manufacturer Koltoma; no verifiable content information from the manufacturer or a retailer could be found.

grants-tobacconist-old-drum.z: One of Grant's Tobacconist's house blends; there is no independent sourcing about its composition.

d-r-tobacco-rimboche-s-j.z: Rimboché S.J. is a ribbon-cut VaPer blend from Daughters & Ryan, combining Virginia leaf with real Perique from Louisiana's St. James parish. The S.J. in the name points to that Perique source; the brand's Rimboché series also includes other entries distinguished by Perique type. The Virginia base gives soft grassy and sweet-hay tones, while the Perique adds spice, dark fruit, and body. No casing is used. Flavor is medium-to-full-bodied, with noticeable spice that doesn't overpower the Virginia. Suited to smokers who like unflavored VaPer blends and want a straightforward recipe available in bulk quantity.
d-r-tobacco-rimboche-s-j.o: Leaves a scent reminiscent of dry hay and fig sweetness, with a peppery sharpness at the edge.

hbt-hi-brasil-tobacco-virginia-blend.z: A Virginia entry from a Brazilian producer; there is not enough sourcing on its composition, cut, and production status.
hbt-hi-brasil-tobacco-virginia-blend.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

schneiderwind-black-currant.z: A limited Schneiderwind blend from 2008; described by its fine blackcurrant casing, no additional source documenting its content could be found.

stanwell-lotus.z: Lotus is an aromatic blend from the Denmark-based Stanwell brand combining Danish-style black cavendish, brown cavendish, and fine Virginia leaves. It's presented in a loose cut, which allows the tobacco to pack easily and burn evenly. Though the Stanwell brand is best known for its pipes, its tobacco line has long continued within the Danish production tradition and is today produced under the Scandinavian Tobacco Group. The blend's distinguishing trait is the combined use of coconut and vanilla flavors; the cavendish base's natural sweetness gathers these two notes into a creamy axis. In the maker's classification, strength is light-to-medium, flavoring is at the top level, and room note is given as intense. A tobacco that suits smokers seeking a pronounced sweet aroma rather than unflavored leaf taste, particularly those who favor tropical and sweet notes.
stanwell-lotus.o: Leaves a sweet, creamy scent reminiscent of coconut and vanilla.

ken-byron-ventures-king-black.z: King Black is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

levin-pipes-international-ringlow.z: Ringlow is a latakia-containing mixture McClelland produced in limited batches, built on oriental leaves specifically selected by Barry Levin. The oriental and latakia components form the blend's backbone, with Virginia acting more as a binding base. For smokers accustomed to unflavored blends seeking Syrian latakia and a pronounced oriental character. After Levin's death, McClelland carried on the recipe in its own catalog under a separate version called Ringlow Syrian Reserve; both versions are now discontinued.
levin-pipes-international-ringlow.o: Leaves a resinous latakia smoke reminiscent of incense, with a tangy-spicy oriental scent.

affordable-pipes-very-cherry.z: A cherry-themed house blend from the American seller Affordable Pipes; no accessible source describing its content could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-pensioners-mixture.z: Pensioners Mixture is a medium-strength Lakeland aromatic. Records indicate the leaf composition has changed from time to time, while the fruit-and-Kendal-style-flower sauce has stayed unchanged; this top note is what defines the blend's identity. The fruit sweetness and floral essence support each other, while the tobacco base provides a nutty, bready foundation. Suited to smokers wanting to get to know the Kendal style through a strong fruit side; the aroma lingers strongly.
gawith-hoggarth-co-pensioners-mixture.o: Leaves a fruity, floral, soapy Kendal-style aroma.

motzek-motzek-7.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called Motzek #7 could be found.

stanwell-fruit-vanilla.z: No verifiable source could be found for the composition of this blend, which from its name appears to be a fruit-and-vanilla-flavored aromatic.

dan-tobacco-bill-baileys-best-blend.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of Dan Tobacco's Bill Bailey's Best Blend were found.

sobranie-of-london-the-balkan-sobranie.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Sobranie of London blend called The Balkan Sobranie could not be found.

hu-tobacco-flanagan.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Flanagan, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

gallaher-limited-condor-long-cut-brown.z: Condor is a British brand tracing its origin to the tobacco house Thomas Gallaher founded. Long Cut is a long-cut flake, previously sold under the name Condor Flake, pressed from dark and light Virginia leaves. A traditional Lakeland-style essence carrying floral, fruity, and alcoholic notes is applied over it. Earthy, woody, citrus, and dark fruit tastes coming from the Virginias are sensed beneath this pronounced topping. It is a slow-burning tobacco with a medium nicotine level, aimed at smokers curious about the traditional essenced blends that have long sat on shelves in the United Kingdom.
gallaher-limited-condor-long-cut-brown.o: Leaves a mix of soapy floral essence and dark fruit aroma.

ken-byron-ventures-sakura.z: Sakura is a blend in Ken Byron Ventures' aromatic line, named after the Japanese cherry blossom. Per the maker's description, cherry blossom and fruit notes are worked into a base of red Virginia, Oriental, and Cavendish leaf. The casing's direction departs from classic cherry aromatics: what dominates is not ripe cherry sugar but a floral, lightly perfumed top note. The red Virginia lends breadlike sweetness, the Oriental leaf a dry, lightly spiced edge, and the Cavendish a soft body with a moist smoke. Nicotine is low and flavor intensity moderate. Suited to aromatic smokers who don't want the casing to fully bury the tobacco, and who are after a floral, restrained cherry character.
ken-byron-ventures-sakura.o: Leaves a floral cherry aroma with a hint of sweet fruit.

peretti-bpc-burley-plug-cut.z: BPC, short for Burley Plug Cut, is the plug-cut Burley blend of L.J. Peretti, which has operated in Boston since 1870. Per the firm's own account, this tobacco is the base leaf on which all its other Burley blends are built; Peretti's Burleys have been a fixed part of the catalog since the 1930s. The first taste is Burley's nutty character; a measured sweetness soon enters and this balance is maintained down to the bottom of the bowl. Its burning qualities are even, leaving no harshness or sharpness, requiring an average number of relights and leaving little residue. It suits smokers seeking an unflavored, straightforward Burley for all-day smoking.
peretti-bpc-burley-plug-cut.o: Leaves a roasted nut and dry hay aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-country-do.z: Match Country Doctor is a coarse-cut American mixture Sutliff produced modeled after the old blend of the same name. Burley is at the blend's center; its earthy, nutty structure with a light molasses sweetness is joined by Virginia leaf's grassy, bready tone. A small amount of latakia and perique appear as side notes, with a fine liqueur casing applied on top. It is medium-bodied with a cool burn. It is aimed at smokers who enjoy burley-centered, lightly cased classic American blends; the coarse-cut leaf needs a bit of care in packing and lighting.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-country-do.o: Leaves an earthy tobacco scent carrying a molasses-like sweetness.

cornell-diehl-ghost-of-christmas-future.z: Ghost of Christmas Future is the aromatic entry in a trio Cornell & Diehl released in its 2022 Wintertime Reserve series, inspired by the three ghosts in Charles Dickens's A Christmas Carol. Its base is bright Virginia leaves and cavendish, topped with a stone-fruit, vanilla, and caramel flavoring. On the smoke, vanilla and caramel are pronounced in both taste and aroma, with an apricot-like tangy-sweet fruit note standing out as the most prominent flavoring; even so, Virginia's citrusy, grassy base remains unmasked. It is light in nicotine and medium in flavor, described as a cool-smoking blend. It suits those looking for winter blends that are flavored yet don't entirely abandon tobacco character; being a limited release, it is not in continuous production.
cornell-diehl-ghost-of-christmas-future.o: Leaves an aroma of vanilla, caramel, and stone fruit.

sutliff-tobacco-company-jamestowne-tradi.z: Jamestowne Tradition Aromatic Mixture is an aromatic blend in Sutliff's Jamestowne Tradition line; independent sources do not provide sufficient information on its composition and production status.

pipesandcigars-com-a-few-too-many.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of the pipesandcigars.com blend called A Few Too Many.

samuel-gawith-pensioners-mixture-dark-fi.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Pensioners Mixture - Dark Fired Off Cuts, according to records a Virginia-Burley blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

rattray-tower-bridge.z: This is a flavored blend sold under the Rattray name; it is not part of the brand's current product list, and no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.
rattray-tower-bridge.o: There is not enough source material to describe its aroma.

paul-olsen-royal-danish.z: Recorded as a sweet, fruity Paul Olsen aromatic later continued under the name Royal Blend within the My Own Blend line; no second independent source detailing its composition could be found.

abenaki-tobacco-co-vanilla-maple.z: Counted among Abenaki Tobacco Co.'s aromatics, a blend that, as its name suggests, is vanilla-and-maple-syrup themed; no adequate source on its tobacco content could be found.

schurch-moschita-408.z: Moschita 408, signed by Schürch, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

charles-fairmorn-lancers-slices.z: Charles Fairmorn Lancer's Slices is a nearly black flake obtained by maturing Virginia leaf, known for its natural sweetness, together with smoked Latakia under pressure and then slicing it. It is produced as a long flake, folded in two and packed; the slices can run longer than 30 centimeters. On opening, it leaves a dark, cake-like tobacco aroma in the tin. For smoking, the flake is rubbed out or folded and packed into the bowl; it lights easily and keeps burning with the occasional light tamp. In the flavor profile it starts soft and sweet, intensifying toward the end of the bowl with a light peppery top note. Suitable for smokers who like Latakia blends and want an unflavored, full-bodied flake.
charles-fairmorn-lancers-slices.o: Leaves a smoky wood and incense aroma with a lightly sweet tobacco note underneath.

ashton-guilty-pleasure.z: Guilty Pleasure is Ashton's ribbon-cut aromatic blend. Tangy Virginias, mellow Carolina Burley, and some silky black Cavendish are brought together; a top note based on vanilla, mango, and exotic citrus is worked over it. The flavoring is pronounced but doesn't fully mask the tobacco base; Burley's dry nuttiness and Virginia sweetness can be heard beneath the fruity notes. It's a light-to-medium blend on nicotine. It suits smokers who like fruited, vanilla aromatics, looking for a low-burn-temperature everyday blend.
ashton-guilty-pleasure.o: Leaves a tropical fruit room note leaning toward vanilla, mango, and citrus.

lane-limited-rc-1.z: Not enough independent sources could be found documenting the contents and character of American blender Lane Limited's blend called RC-1.

tobacco-land-rum-and-honey.z: Tobacco Land Rum and Honey is noted as an aromatic with rum and honey essence; no verifiable source on its composition or maker has been found.
tobacco-land-rum-and-honey.o: Recorded as leaving a sweet aroma tied to rum and honey essences.

barling-royal-hunt.z: An old English blend once sold under the Barling name; no reliable source describing its content and character could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-whimsical.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Sutliff Tobacco Company's Whimsical pipe tobacco could be found.

solani-127-green-label.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Solani blend 127: Green Label could not be found.

vauen-bavarian-blend-no-3.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Vauen blend called Bavarian Blend No. 3 has been found.
vauen-bavarian-blend-no-3.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

e-a-carey-cinnamon.z: This is listed in catalogs as E. A. Carey's Virginia-based, cinnamon-flavored aromatic; it does not appear in current production, and no source giving a detailed description could be found.

de-la-concha-666.z: This is one of the shop blends from De La Concha, a tobacconist founded in New York in 1964; no independent source describing its composition could be found.
de-la-concha-666.o: No reliable record could be found for the room note.

cornell-diehl-nutty-irishman.z: Nutty Irishman is an aromatic mixture named after the cocktail of the same name. Per Cornell & Diehl's recipe, a base of burley, Virginia, and black cavendish is worked with a Frangelico-like hazelnut flavor and a honeyed, spiced liqueur note reminiscent of Irish Mist. The ribbon cut takes on a dark, mottled look thanks to the black cavendish. While the flavoring level is pronounced, nicotine stays low, keeping the smoke light; as with many aromatics prone to excess moisture, a short airing before packing helps. It is intended for new smokers wanting to start with sweet, scented blends, and for anyone seeking a hazelnut-liqueur flavor profile.
cornell-diehl-nutty-irishman.o: Leaves an aroma of toasted hazelnut and honeyed liqueur, with a faint cinnamon sweetness behind it.

ken-byron-ventures-mycroft-2023.z: A blend released as part of Ken Byron Ventures' small-batch production; no independent, verifiable source could be found on it.

jons-pipe-shop-lord-melbourne.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Jon's Pipe Shop's Lord Melbourne pipe tobacco.

w-d-h-o-wills-capstan-navy-cut-medium-re.z: No independent source sufficient to complete a record could be found regarding W.D. & H.O. Wills's Capstan Navy Cut Medium Ready Rubbed blend, so this entry remains incomplete.

pauls-pipe-shop-iapsc-tobacco.z: IAPSC is a house blend named after the international pipe smokers' club Paul's Pipe Shop belongs to. Per the maker's recipe, vanilla and chocolate essence are given to cube-cut burley leaf. Cube cut is a traditional American preparation method that gives burley a slow, cool burn. The burley base gives the blend a dry, nutty, earthy body; the topping adds a sweet layer over that body rather than masking it. Nicotine load runs more pronounced than in aromatics generally. It suits smokers accustomed to cube-cut burley, or those wanting a lightly flavored blend where the tobacco taste still leads.
pauls-pipe-shop-iapsc-tobacco.o: Leaves a scent of cocoa and vanilla.

poschl-tabak-allegro-gusto-delicato.z: This is a product in Pöschl Tabak's Allegro line, described as light-bodied; no source could be found documenting its content.

g-l-pease-navigator.z: Navigator is a blend in the Old London Series line. Bright and red Virginia leaves are pressed and matured together with a drop of rum; dark fire-cured Kentucky is added to give the taste a smoky, spicy dimension. It is presented in broken-flake form, with the red-brown leaves rubbing out easily. In the smoke, Virginia's natural sweetness, notes close to dried fruit and caramel, and Kentucky's pronounced smokiness, savoury body, and peppery spice come to the fore. The rum leaves a thin warmth underneath, not pulling the blend into the aromatic class. Nicotine is medium-to-high; it is aimed at smokers seeking a smoky, full Virginia.
g-l-pease-navigator.o: Leaves a fine rum aroma behind the smoky wood and dried fruit.

iwan-ries-three-star-ebony.z: This is a blend from the Three Star line prepared over the counter by the Chicago-based tobacconist Iwan Ries & Co.; no independent source detailing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
iwan-ries-three-star-ebony.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

barclay-rex-alkazar.z: One of the shop blends from Barclay Rex, the New York tobacconist founded in 1910, sold in the aromatic class; no adequate source describing its composition could be found.

e-a-carey-celebrity-blend.z: Celebrity Blend is one of the aromatics E. A. Carey has produced in Denmark and sold under its own name. Per the maker's description, aged Virginia leaves, sweet fire-cured dark tobaccos and a soft burley are brought together; the blend is flavored with a core of pure rum and vanilla. The smoke is cool and soft, staying light in nicotine; because the topping is pronounced, the flavor profile follows a sweet direction. It suits smokers seeking the classic Danish-style aromatic approach, an all-day blend that doesn't tire the palate. Though the brand is American, this blend's production takes place in Denmark.
e-a-carey-celebrity-blend.o: Leaves a sweet, lasting scent evoking rum and a vanilla core.

uhles-bishops-move.z: No current source documenting the composition and character of the blend called Bishop's Move, attributed to the Uhle's tobacconist in Milwaukee, has been found.

ken-byron-ventures-nakatomi.z: A blend Ken Byron Ventures released as part of its small-batch production; no independent and verifiable source could be found about it.

john-middleton-inc-wine-berry.z: One of the blends from John Middleton, a company founded in Philadelphia in 1856 that has made pipe tobacco since the 1950s; the entry is left incomplete because not enough sources could be found to document the blend's contents and character.
john-middleton-inc-wine-berry.o: No source could be found on the room note.

campbells-smoke-shop-2-full-english-natu.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named #2 Full English (Natural) under the Campbell's Smoke Shop brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

cornell-diehl-cross-eyed-cricket.z: Cross-Eyed Cricket is one of Cornell & Diehl's blends sitting between the aromatic and English molds. An unsweetened black cavendish base is joined by Turkish leaf, Latakia, and a small amount of perique; it is topped with a rum-punch-style flavoring. Cavendish's soft sweetness, the Oriental's earthy tone, Latakia's smokiness, and perique's spice all sit together; the flavoring adds a light fruit-and-rum layer on top. The maker describes the blend as a structure that could be counted as both English and aromatic; it suits smokers curious to try the intersection of the two categories.
cornell-diehl-cross-eyed-cricket.o: Leaves a lightly smoky aroma in the room mixed with a rum-fruit-punch-like sweetness.

peter-stokkebye-royal-guard-rum.z: This is a Peter Stokkebye blend whose name suggests a rum flavoring; no sufficient first-hand sources documenting its content and character could be found.
peter-stokkebye-royal-guard-rum.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

mcclelland-no-100-tropical.z: A tropical-fruit-flavored blend in McClelland's numbered bulk aromatic series; no sufficient source documenting its composition could be found.

the-smoker-pine-hills.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the The Smoker pipe tobacco called Pine Hills to record the blend's composition and character.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-coffee.z: Referred to as a coffee-flavored version within the Kendal Gold shag series; no reliable sourcing giving details specific to this version's composition and character could be found.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-coffee.o: Leaves a roasted-coffee and tobacco aroma.

tinder-box-wilshire.z: Wilshire is an aromatic pipe tobacco American retail chain Tinder Box, founded in 1928, has blended under its own name and sells only in its own stores. Selected Virginia and Burley leaves are added to a ribbon-cut black Cavendish core; a light casing carrying vanilla and caramel notes is applied on top. Per the company's own description, the brand considers it the flagship aromatic among the recipes it has developed since its founding. Sweetness comes forward in the smoke but the sugar load isn't heavy; the ribbon-cut leaf gives an even, controlled burn. Nicotine is light and the flavor body is moderate, giving it a structure suited to repeated bowls throughout the day. A fitting profile for those new to aromatics and for anyone after a low-strength, ribbon-cut classic American aromatic.
tinder-box-wilshire.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly spiced aroma leaning toward vanilla and caramel.

peterson-signature-flake.z: Signature Flake is a pressed flake made of unflavored Virginia leaf. The blend uses light-colored leaf sourced from Africa and Brazil; only very light casing is applied in production, a step that leaves no noticeable contribution to the taste. The slices are mottled yellowish, cinnamon-toned, and dark brown, and being moisture-balanced, they crumble easily by hand. The taste carries tart citrus, dry hay, honey, and baked-dough notes, along with a peppery sharpness noticeable in the nose. It burns slowly and needs few relights. It suits smokers accustomed to Virginia flakes who are seeking the natural sugar-acid balance of an unflavored tobacco; since it requires preparation and slow smoking, it doesn't suit hurried moments.
peterson-signature-flake.o: Leaves a dry hay, bread-crust, and light citrus-peel aroma.

petersen-sorensen-cadillac.z: Cadillac is a mixture built from Virginia leaf of African and South American origin, drawing most of its sweetness from the leaf's own sugar. According to manufacturer records, only botanical extracts are used to support the taste, which sets the blend apart from heavily flavored products.
petersen-sorensen-cadillac.o: Leaves a lightly sweet hay and dry-grass aroma.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-royal-admiral.z: Royal Admiral is among Wilke's semi-aromatic English records. Cyprian Latakia leads with smoke, earth, wood, grass, and light spice; Yenidje Oriental leaf adds a floral, herbal, dry-sour layer. Bright Virginia carries the sweet side with tart citrus, grass, and bread notes, while black cavendish and a Jamaican rum addition leave a creamy, measured sweetness. Strength and nicotine run a little above medium; the blend burns slowly, cool, and clean. It suits smokers wanting a Latakia-forward body with a light addition alongside it. The room note is more pronounced than the taste in the smoker's mouth; Wilke offers this blend in bulk, and it can occasionally go out of stock.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-royal-admiral.o: A sweet rum trace mixes into a wood-smoke scent reminiscent of a campfire.

tabaqueria-xian-turkish-delight.z: One of Tabaquería Xian's house blends; no accessible source describing its content and character could be found.

lane-limited-edgeworth-cavendish-natural.z: Not enough independent sources could be found documenting the contents and character of American blender Lane Limited's blend called Edgeworth Cavendish Natural (Brown).

lane-limited-golden-honey.z: Not enough independent sources could be found documenting the contents and character of American blender Lane Limited's blend called Golden Honey.

mcclelland-corps-vanilla-ice.z: Vanilla Ice is an aromatic among the club blends McClelland prepared for the Conclave of Richmond Pipe Smokers. Its structure has two layers: slowly steam-processed black Cavendish forms the base, joined by bright, naturally sweet yellow Virginia; a mild vanilla flavoring is applied over it. In the smoke, the tobacco's own character stays in the background, with creamy vanilla taking the lead. Nicotine dose and flavor intensity are low to medium, making it suitable for long, cool smokes; as with high-Cavendish aromatics generally, moisture balance and even tamping matter. A record aimed at smokers who like aromatics and want a light, everyday tobacco.
mcclelland-corps-vanilla-ice.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and sugared-cream aroma.

peter-stokkebye-peaches-cream-no-303.z: Peaches & Cream is a coarse-cut aromatic built from bright Virginias, nutty Burley, and velvety black Cavendish leaf. The blend is given a pronounced peach flavoring with a softening touch of vanilla; within the cut, black Cavendish is visibly dominant to the eye. The body sits between light and medium; the taste is fruity and sweet, carrying a creamy softness. It suits smokers seeking a pronounced fruit flavoring in an aromatic that doesn't sit heavy on the palate.
peter-stokkebye-peaches-cream-no-303.o: Fills the room with a ripe peach and creamy vanilla aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-scotch-flake.z: Scotch Flake is an all-Virginia flake weighted toward Brazilian and Zimbabwean flue-cured Virginias, with a small amount of sun-cured leaf added for body and sweetness. It carries a light cocoa sauce and is sliced after pressing; this pressing gives it a darker appearance than the same house's Broken Scotch Cake product. Bread, dry hay, and ripe-fruit tones lead the flavor palette with a lightly spiced finish; the cocoa essence doesn't override the leaf. Nicotine is moderate. Suited to smokers seeking a near-unflavored, pressed Virginia.
gawith-hoggarth-co-scotch-flake.o: Leaves an aroma where a fine trace of cocoa falls over dry hay and baked bread.

richs-lord-nelson.z: Lord Nelson is listed among Rich's Cigar Store's house blends referred to as English type; no verifiable source could be found describing its content.
richs-lord-nelson.o: No reliable information could be found on the room note.

cornell-diehl-turkish.z: No listing documenting the composition of Turkish, understood to belong to Cornell & Diehl's single-component leaf series, could be found in the maker's current catalogue or reliable retailer pages.

lane-limited-almond.z: Lane Limited's record called Almond is, as its name suggests, an almond-flavored blend; since no independent source could be found to confirm its tobacco composition and cut, the record is left incomplete.

black-cat-cigar-company-danish-cherry.z: Danish Cherry is a Cavendish-based cherry aromatic from Black Cat Cigar Company, prepared in the Danish style. Sold in bulk, this mixture is calibrated per the maker's recipe to burn cool. In the flavor profile, Cavendish's dark sweetness leads; the cherry topping stays medium and isn't intense enough to overpower the tobacco's own taste. It stays light in both nicotine and body. It suits smokers looking for a low-intensity cherry aromatic that can be smoked over long stretches during the day.
black-cat-cigar-company-danish-cherry.o: Leaves a cherry and sweet Cavendish room note.

mac-baren-amphora-special-reserve-no-8.z: Amphora Special Reserve No.8 is the series' ready-rubbed member. Per the manufacturer's description, Virginia, burley and cavendish leaves from three continents are blended; the post-pressing rubbed-out structure keeps both the density of pressed tobaccos and the easy packability of a loose cut. The brand is Dutch-rooted, produced in Denmark. Though it comes from the same leaf family as No.2, the ready-rubbed preparation makes the smoke a bit more compact and slower. Virginia's sweetness and burley's earthy body lead, with cavendish adding a softening layer. Casing is at a level that won't leave a pronounced perfume. Suited to smokers curious about the character of pressed tobaccos but who don't want to bother slicing flakes.
mac-baren-amphora-special-reserve-no-8.o: Leaves a sweet dried-fruit and lightly toasted bread room note.

pipes-pleasures-old-english.z: No sufficient sources were found documenting the content and character of Pipes & Pleasures' blend Old English.

peterson-special-reserve-2014.z: Special Reserve 2014 is a limited edition blend released as part of Peterson's Special Reserve series specific to that year; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient first-hand sources confirming its content and character could be found.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-bellamy.z: Bellamy is one of six Danish-style aromatics in Hamburg-based Kohlhase & Kopp's Caribbean Blue line. The series' names are taken from pirates and pirate captains; the blend is offered in a 50-gram, sailor-illustrated tin. The leaf structure rests on the Virginia, Burley and black cavendish trio; Burley gives a cooling body, while cavendish provides a sugary base. The top casing consists of melon, banana and orange extracts, giving a pronounced tropical fruit direction. Since nicotine load is measured, it suits smokers who love aromatics and prefer fruity casings over alcohol or vanilla tones. The ribbon cut is easy to pack directly; due to the cavendish proportion, a slow smoke is needed to keep the bowl dry.
kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-bellamy.o: Leaves a tropical fruit room note combining melon and banana peel with orange peel.

bentley-the-royal-vanilla.z: The Royal Vanilla is the vanilla-centered aromatic in the Bentley line. Its base holds selected Virginia grades, some Burley, and mellow black Cavendish matured under press; over this a Madagascar vanilla and a notable amount of honey are applied. The black Cavendish gives the blend a dark sweetness and moist texture, while the Burley supports body and burn balance. The topping is pronounced but calibrated so as not to fully mask the tobacco's own taste; nicotine load is below medium. It's aimed at those who like classic vanilla aromatics and want a mellow blend they can smoke all day.
bentley-the-royal-vanilla.o: Sweet vanilla and honey fill the room.

faders-porter.z: Not enough independent sourcing documenting the composition and character of Porter, one of the house blends of the Baltimore-based Fader's tobacconist, could be found.

peterson-summertime-2016.z: This is the 2016 edition of Peterson's limited-production Summertime series, released with a distinct composition each summer; no sufficient primary sources giving this year's composition details could be found.

spednova-virginia.z: As its name suggests, a Virginia-forward blend from the Spednova brand; sufficient independent sources describing the blend's composition and character could not be found.
spednova-virginia.o: No description is available in records.

with-pipe-and-book-olympic-blend.z: This is a house blend from the With Pipe and Book shop in Lake Placid, a town that has twice hosted the Winter Olympics; its name draws on the town's Olympic history. After the shop closed, the blend also became unavailable, and no reliable record of its composition exists.
with-pipe-and-book-olympic-blend.o: No description of its room note could be found in the records.

charatan-black-aromatic.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the British pipe maker Charatan.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-kentucky-c.z: An aromatic blend in Sutliff's Match line prepared to correspond to the mild version of Kentucky Club; no independent source detailing its content could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-kentucky-c.o: Records suggest it leaves a lightly sweet scent.

hu-tobacco-anniversary-blend.z: HU Tobacco is a German maker practicing hand blending, founded by Hans Wiedemann in the Bavarian town of Reimlingen. Anniversary Blend is the blend the brand prepared for its anniversary, built by bringing together red and light Virginia leaves in both ready-rubbed flake and cross-cut form.
hu-tobacco-anniversary-blend.o: Leaves a woody, smoky tobacco aroma along with a resinous, balsamic sweetness.

gq-tobaccos-peak-park.z: One of GQ Tobaccos's own blends; there is not enough independent sourcing describing its composition and character.

mcclelland-crisp-apple.z: One of three apple blends in McClelland's bulk aromatic line; no sufficient independent source describing its detailed contents could be found.

wellauer-co-wellauers-best.z: Wellauer & Co's Wellauer's Best is, according to records, one of the blends carrying the Swiss tobacconist house's name; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-skandinav.z: One of the aromatic members of the Danish-origin Skandinavik series; no sufficient source describing the blend's composition and casing could be found.

vincenzo-red.z: Vincenzo Red is an aromatic mixture built from red, orange and gold Virginia leaf joined with a touch of black Cavendish and a small measure of Burley. According to sources, the blend carries a light fruit-and-nut casing. The Virginia weight lends the tobacco a natural sugary sweetness, the Burley adds body and dryness, and the Cavendish smooths the smoke. Nicotine sits between mild and medium; the flavoring is kept restrained enough not to mask the tobacco's own taste. Suited to smokers who steer clear of heavily scented aromatics but still want a sweet smoke.
vincenzo-red.o: Leaves a roasted hazelnut and ripe-fruit aroma.

mcclelland-gkcpc-syrian-star.z: A blend among McClelland's club selections, as the name suggests built on Syrian Latakia; no sufficient source documenting its composition could be found.

peter-stokkebye-sweet-vanilla-no-6.z: Sweet Vanilla is an aromatic combining ripe orange flue-cured Virginias with loose-cut Burley and black Cavendish, topped with a flavoring prepared from pure vanilla bean. The roasted Cavendish's natural sweetness runs alongside the vanilla. The body is very light, leaves no harshness on the tongue, and needs few relights. It suits smokers seeking a mild, sweet blend for all-day smoking and newcomers to the pipe.
peter-stokkebye-sweet-vanilla-no-6.o: Fills the room with a sweet vanilla and roasted sugar aroma.

theodorus-niemeijer-ltd-dutch-heerenbaai.z: Heerenbaai is one of the names in the Netherlands' classic pipe tobacco tradition. The term "baai tabak" describes North American leaf shipped to the Netherlands via Chesapeake Bay starting in the 17th century; Groningen-based Theodorus Niemeijer was among the makers who carried on this tradition. The blend has a finely cut, freely burning structure and, per records, is composed mainly of air-cured Maryland-type leaf with some flue-cured tobacco. Its character is unflavored and dry: with no sugar casing or flavoring added, the leaf's own tangy, grassy taste comes forward. Nicotine load stays below medium, while the fine cut means the flavor opens quickly, so it needs to be smoked slowly. A historical example for smokers curious about the old Continental European pipe tobacco style and who enjoy plain, unflavored blends. The brand today sits under Imperial Tobacco, and production under this name has not continued.
theodorus-niemeijer-ltd-dutch-heerenbaai.o: Leaves a dry hay and lightly tangy leaf aroma in the room.

gatlin-burlier-gatlin-burley.z: Gatlin-Burley is the house blend carrying the name of the Tennessee tobacconist Gatlinburlier, referred to in the shop as "the Burlier's best." Its base is selected burley leaf; a small amount of Latakia and a light shop-specific topping are added. Burley's dominant character defines the blend, Latakia leaves a measured smokiness in the background, and the topping gives a light vanilla-like sweetness. Since the moisture is kept low, it can be smoked straight from the pouch. It is aimed at those seeking a Burley-forward, American-style smoke standing between aromatic and English blends.
gatlin-burlier-gatlin-burley.o: Leaves a nutty tobacco aroma with a light smokiness and sweet vanilla.

joseph-martin-semois-lux-no-3.z: A blend from the Joseph Martin house, known for Belgian Semois tobacco; not enough independent sources could be found on its contents and character.

mostex-stanislaw-pilot-blend.z: No independent, verifiable source describing the composition of this blend, released under the Stanislaw brand of the Brno-based maker Mostex, could be found.

planta-mccormick-selection-cherry.z: The Cherry mixture in the McCormick Selection line is an aromatic with a whisky-rested cherry-evoking casing applied over an American-style body. Virginia and Burley leaf are joined by black Cavendish; the cherry note is pronounced both in the cold scent and the smoke. The second member of the line is whisky-flavored, and the two flavors are offered within the same line. Nicotine is measured and the smoke mellow; it suits fans of classic cherry aromatics. It is sold in 50-gram packages.
planta-mccormick-selection-cherry.o: Leaves a sweet cherry-liqueur and light malt aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-coffee-203.z: 203 Coffee is a coffee-flavored aromatic in Sutliff's bulk line; sufficient independent sources documenting its leaf composition and character could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-coffee-203.o: Records did not provide sufficient information for a description.

dunhill-golden-hours.z: A discontinued mixture referred to under the Dunhill name, for which no verifiable source on its composition could be found.

vegassmokes-five-star-legend.z: A VegasSmokes blend described as English-style; no independent source documenting its composition has been found.

rattray-winter-edition-2014.z: Winter Edition 2014 is an installment in the limited series Rattray releases every winter, produced at the Kohlhase & Kopp facility in Germany. Its body contains various loose Virginia leaf, ready-rubbed Virginia flake, Burley, and black Cavendish. The top note is built around caramel and almond, giving the blend a sweet, bakery-like character suited to the winter months. The mix of different cuts balances the burn rate. Nicotine stays light, making it suitable for all-day smoking; it is designed for aromatic fans and smokers who steer clear of English blends.
rattray-winter-edition-2014.o: Leaves a roasted almond and caramelized sugar aroma.

f-k-lancer-slices.z: Lancer Slices is one of the blends previously sold under the name Charles Fairmorn, later gathered under the F & K brand. It is obtained by pressing and slicing Virginia leaves with Latakia and Oriental leaf; the rubbed-out form of the same blend is presented as broken flake under the name Lancer Ready Rubbed. Records indicate production takes place in Germany. The Latakia proportion is kept more measured than in full-bodied English blends; the smoke taste doesn't mask Virginia's bread-like sweetness, and the smoke proceeds creamy and mild. Since pressing intensifies the leaf's taste, the flakes need to be rubbed out and aired for a while before lighting. It suits an English-blend smoker wanting to get used to flake cutting who doesn't want a heavy Latakia load.
f-k-lancer-slices.o: Leaves a measured woodsmoke aroma with bread-like Virginia sweetness underneath.

chieftain-roberts-mixture.z: No reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Chieftain blend Roberts Mixture, so the profile has been left incomplete.

dan-tobacco-bulldog-chili-chocolate.z: A ready-rubbed aromatic blend that was part of Dan Tobacco's Bulldog series, carrying a chocolate-and-chili-leaning flavoring; no adequate source documenting its ratios was found. It is no longer in production.
dan-tobacco-bulldog-chili-chocolate.o: Records indicate a stinging spice mingles with cocoa sweetness.

sail-london-dock.z: Sail is a brand resting on a century-old Dutch cavendish tradition, known for its aromatic blends prepared with leaves from various regions of the world. London Dock is one of the brand's short-lived members; it is described as a mixture combining Virginia with cavendish leaf, carrying floral essence and sugar-based flavoring. Its cut is ribbon form, and it stays light on nicotine. Blends of this type appeal to those seeking a mild smoke where the flavoring stands out more than the tobacco taste, and to pipe newcomers. The name "London Dock" has been used by multiple producers with different formulas over the years; so it should not be confused with other blends bearing the same name. The Sail version is no longer in production.
sail-london-dock.o: Leaves a sugary, lightly floral, sweet scent.

drucquer-sons-the-devils-own.z: The Devil's Own is among the fuller English mixtures in the Drucquer & Sons line. The proportion of golden Virginia leaves and the amount of Cyprus latakia are kept higher than in the brand's Inns of Court blend, giving both a sweeter and fuller-bodied smoke. A small amount of burley and unsweetened black cavendish add weight and texture to the smoke. It's ribbon cut, showing yellow-tan, light brown, brown and black leaves together. Latakia is the component that defines the blend's identity; the soot is balanced by Virginia sweetness and holds its intensity through the smoke. It's medium in nicotine, with above-medium flavor intensity. It suits smokers seeking smoky English mixtures for evening smoking or long sittings, unbothered by a strong latakia character.
drucquer-sons-the-devils-own.o: Leaves a heavy soot scent evoking wood fire, with a lightly sweet tobacco note lingering underneath.

low-country-pipe-cigar-carolina-christma.z: One of the house blends of South Carolina-based Low Country Pipe & Cigar; described as a limited edition from 2008, but not enough sources could be found to describe its character.

iwan-ries-2035-flake.z: This flake registered under the Iwan Ries name does not appear in the maker's current flake lineup, and no verifiable source about its content could be found.

newminster-no-24-imperial-nougat.z: Newminster No. 24 Imperial Nougat is an aromatic blend prepared by combining sweet Virginia leaves with soft Burley and light-colored Cavendish. A vanilla note and a rounded chocolate taste are added on top; the name comes from this nougat-like combination. In the tin note, a fruity sharpness and a very faint vanilla can be sensed beneath the caramel sweetness. The cut is ribbon, and it is sold in bulk. Nicotine is light to medium, and the flavor intensity is set by the sweetness carried in the casing. Suitable for those looking for sweet, confectionery-style aromatics, and for smokers new to aromatics.
newminster-no-24-imperial-nougat.o: Leaves a lightly nutty, smoky aroma sitting on top of chocolate and vanilla in the room.

borkum-riff-limited-edition-11-mixture-w.z: This is a limited-run blend Borkum Riff released in 2013. Its base holds red- and mahogany-toned Virginias along with dark black Cavendish, joined by some Burley and fire-cured leaf, topped off with Trinidad rum and fruit flavoring. The fire-cured leaf gives the blend a drier, smokier backbone compared to the brand's usual aromatics. Borkum Riff launched in Sweden in 1962, taking its name from a lighthouse in the North Sea; the blends, originally produced for Swedish Match, are now prepared in Denmark under Scandinavian Tobacco Group. Being a limited run, it's not currently available on the market. It suits smokers who like rum-flavored aromatics but don't want an entirely sugary smoke, accustomed to medium-bodied blends.
borkum-riff-limited-edition-11-mixture-w.o: Sweet rum and ripe fruit are accompanied by a faintly smoky base note.

ilsted-special-london-flake.z: This is a pressed flake in the line prepared under the Poul Ilsted name; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

cup-o-joes-6-skookum.z: One of the Cup O' Joes tobacco shop's numbered house blends, classed as Virginia-heavy; no source documenting its composition was found.

erik-stokkebye-twilight.z: Twilight Mixture is a lightly pressed blend combining aged Virginia leaves with lively orientals and perique from the St. James district. After pressing, it is presented as broken flake; this structure slows the burn and lets the flavors meld. Virginia's sweetness meets perique's plum and spice tones, with the orientals bridging the gap. It suits those who love unadulterated Virginia-perique mixtures and want a more compact, intensely sweet smoke in the evening hours.
erik-stokkebye-twilight.o: Leaves a slightly tart tobacco scent carrying dried fruit and a hint of pepper.

gambler-gold.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of the Gambler brand's Gold pipe tobacco could be found.

mcclelland-organically-grown-flake.z: This was an unflavored, flake-cut McClelland entry made from organically grown Virginia leaf; production was halted by the firm's own decision before it closed altogether, and no second independent source documenting its character in detail could be found.

samuel-gawith-lakeland-dark.z: No sufficient source describing the content and character of this blend referred to under the Samuel Gawith name could be found.

bufflehead-cinnamon-teal.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Cinnamon Teal under the Bufflehead brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

cornell-diehl-steamworks.z: No listing documenting the composition of Steamworks, a Cornell & Diehl blend, could be found in the maker's current catalogue or reliable retailer pages.

walgreens-peach-melba.z: This is a cheap, cavendish-forward aromatic sold in large bags on Walgreens shelves, described in records as peach-flavored; no published maker record could be found regarding the blend's composition.

dunhill-my-mixture-221b-baker-street.z: My Mixture 221B Baker Street is a Virginia- and burley-based blend from Dunhill's "My Mixture" line. Per the tin description, alongside Virginia it contains fire-cured and sun-cured tobaccos; the leaf is cut fine ribbon. A very light topping is applied, echoing the line seen in Royal Yacht and Three Year Matured Virginia but more measured. Wood, smoke, nut and a light background spice stand out in the taste; despite its measured aroma, the nicotine load is pronounced, so it suits smokers accustomed to full-bodied tobaccos. The blend was sold exclusively at Dunhill shops for a long time, was later reissued for a limited period, and left the list when Dunhill pipe tobacco production ended.
dunhill-my-mixture-221b-baker-street.o: Leaves a woody scent of roasted hazelnut with a light smokiness.

robert-mcconnell-the-original-pure-black.z: Pure Black Cavendish is a member of Robert McConnell's single-varietal "Pure" series. Rather than offering a finished blend, the series consists of pure leaves meant for smokers to build their own mixtures or modify a ready-made one. This leaf is Cavendish processed and darkened under steam and pressure; its natural sugars caramelize, giving it a sweet, mellow character. Nicotine is low and it does not bite the tongue. Smoked on its own its flavor range is narrow; its real purpose is adding sweetness, moisture, and body to Virginia- or Burley-heavy blends and slowing the burn rate. It serves as a base component for smokers building their own mixtures. The brand is Belfast in origin; production today takes place in Germany.
robert-mcconnell-the-original-pure-black.o: Leaves a light molasses and cooked-sugar aroma.

jim-mate-pipe-and-tobacco-shop-aromatic-.z: No reliable source documenting the content and character of Jim Mate Pipe and Tobacco Shop's Aromatic Pipe Mixture blend could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-bright-.z: Bright Side brings together bright Virginia with some of the lightest-colored Oriental tobaccos, such as Basma and Yenice. The maker states the blend is prepared with an unsweetened lemon and elderflower casing, giving it a smooth smoke without sweetness, and that the blend carries no characterizing flavor of its own; it's offered as 2 oz. bulk. The dry, tangy, spicy line of the Oriental leaf and Virginia's light sweetness stand out; rather than masking this structure, the casing softens its edges. Aimed at those who like light-bodied Oriental mixtures without Latakia, and at those looking for a low-intensity blend for warm weather.
ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-bright-.o: Leaves a dry tobacco aroma mixed with lemon peel and a floral freshness.

smokers-haven-25th-anniversary-mixture.z: One of the limited-run tinned series Smokers' Haven released for its founding anniversaries; while the 20th-anniversary mixture's composition is documented, no independent source on this blend's composition could be found.

fribourg-treyer-waterloo-no-2-mixture.z: Waterloo No. 2 is regarded as one of the oldest recorded blends in the line continued under the Fribourg & Treyer name. Its structure is simple: Virginia leaves and latakia are brought together in a ribbon cut; no other flavouring tobacco is used. Since the latakia proportion is kept low, the smoke sits as a thin layer over Virginia's bright, lightly sweet taste. It suits smokers wanting to smoke the classic English style without heavy Balkan intensity and who like working with light blends.
fribourg-treyer-waterloo-no-2-mixture.o: Leaves an aroma of fine woodsmoke and dry leaf.

chonowitsch-t-17.z: T 17 is a full-bodied blend in which a pronounced Latakia share is combined with soft, sweet Oriental leaves, with Virginia set behind them as the chosen backbone. Despite carrying Latakia weight, the roundness of the Oriental leaves brings the blend closer to the Balkan type. The series consists of small-batch productions Danish pipe maker Jess Chonowitsch had prepared to accompany his own pipes; each blend is prepared and rested in small quantity. This is an entry aimed at those looking for mixtures where Latakia and Oriental leaf stand out together.
chonowitsch-t-17.o: The Oriental leaf's dry, spicy scent is noticeable alongside a heavy smoky aroma.

bufflehead-ruddy-duck.z: Bufflehead was a brand producing small batches in the United States in the early 2000s, naming its blends after waterfowl; since no independent source describing this blend's content and character could be found, the entry has been left incomplete.

van-erkoms-assegai-cloudy.z: Van Erkoms is a South African firm producing pipe and snuff tobacco in Mokopane (formerly Potgietersrus), Limpopo, and it supplies the Virginia base used by many blenders in the country. No independent source describing this version's composition and cut in the Assegai series has been found, so the record is left incomplete.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-holiday-blend-20.z: Holiday Blend 2003 is part of Hermit Tobacco Works Co.'s annual holiday series; there is not enough sourcing to describe its composition and character.

peter-heinrichs-no-169.z: This is one of the pipe tobaccos of the Cologne-based house Peter Heinrichs; the profile is left incomplete, as no reliable sources describing the blend's content and character could be found.

hu-tobacco-aus-dem-krater-plug.z: Aus dem Krater Plug is the same series's Virginia tobacco pressed into a block and left uncut; it needs to be sliced and rubbed out before smoking. The maker's description calls it a blend with balanced sweet and spicy sides. It sits between light and medium in strength, with no flavoring applied. It suits smokers accustomed to preparing plugs as well as those wanting to get acquainted with pressed Virginia texture; it's presented in a 100-gram tin.
hu-tobacco-aus-dem-krater-plug.o: Leaves an aroma of damp wood and dried fruit reminiscent of an autumn forest.

ash-ember-fat-man.z: No adequate independent source could be found for Fat Man, a house blend from the Ash & Ember shop.
ash-ember-fat-man.o: No reliable information on the room note could be found.

affordable-pipes-wall-street.z: One of the house blends from the American seller Affordable Pipes; no accessible source describing its content could be found.

emerson-southern-forged-kilmallock.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing was found for the Emerson Southern Forged brand's Kilmallock blend, so the entry has been left open; records place it in the English family.

mcclelland-avenue-blend-tq.z: Avenue Blend TQ is a medium-intensity blend in McClelland's bulk aromatic series. A ribbon-cut mixture of Burley, Cavendish, and Virginia leaves is topped with a vanilla-and-cocoa-forward flavoring; a light coconut note is also detectable in the aroma. It's an aromatic with low nicotine and a mild, near-uniform flavor, falling into the same category as classic American bulk aromatics like Lane 1-Q. Suited to those starting the pipe with aromatic blends and those seeking a light, all-day tobacco. Since the brand stopped production in 2018, it's found only in old stock.
mcclelland-avenue-blend-tq.o: Leaves an aroma of vanilla, milk chocolate, and light coconut.

peterson-sherlock-holmes.z: Sherlock Holmes is a ribbon-cut blend that gives its name to the series Peterson dedicated to the literary character. Its content is based on Virginia and Burley leaf, with a very light, citrus-leaning fruity topping applied on top. The tin's scent is sweet and appetizing, and the tobacco burns evenly after a short airing. Its strength sits between light and medium, and its flavor carries a spicy sweetness. It suits smokers seeking a balanced starting point before moving into heavy Latakia blends or intense aromatics; those looking for strength and fullness may find it plain.
peterson-sherlock-holmes.o: Leaves a light citrus and baked-grain aroma.

mcclelland-no-2050-oriental-cavendish-mi.z: No. 2050 Oriental Cavendish Mix is a mixture in McClelland's bulk series pairing Oriental leaf with Cavendish-processed tobaccos. Per the catalog description, the blend uses Orientals, Virginia Cavendish, and black Cavendish together. Black Cavendish works here as a component that boosts sweetness and mildness; the blend is built not as a heavily flavored tobacco but as a softened take on the Oriental character. In the smoke, the Oriental's spicy tang sits alongside the Cavendish's dark, lightly sugary tone. Body and nicotine are moderate. Suited to smokers seeking a Latakia-free Oriental mixture who also want a mild base. Discontinued when the brand closed in 2018.
mcclelland-no-2050-oriental-cavendish-mi.o: Leaves a sweetish dark tobacco aroma with a faint spice.

watch-city-cigar-eureka.z: Eureka! is one of the house blends Massachusetts-based Watch City Cigar & Pipe prepares at its own facility. According to the maker's description, it's a light-bodied aromatic mixture built from golden and black Cavendish leaves; the sweetness brought by the Cavendish processing comes forward, and nicotine load is kept low. It has a structure suited to smokers seeking an all-day aromatic that doesn't tire the tongue, and to newcomers to the pipe. Since it's ribbon cut, it's easy to pack and light, and the burn temperature is measured. Watch City blends are produced to the shop's own recipes; repackaging of ready-made blends is not involved.
watch-city-cigar-eureka.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly caramel Cavendish scent.

mac-baren-royal-twist.z: Royal Twist is one of Mac Baren's blends built on the rope (spun cut) tradition. Select Virginia leaves, dark-fire-cured Kentucky, and Perique are hand-twisted into a rope, rested for weeks, and sliced into thin coin shapes; the naturally sweet whole-leaf Virginia is used as the outer wrap. The brand name dropped off the list in the 1960s due to joint trademark issues, and was later reintroduced in a limited run in 100-gram tins, said to be based on the original recipe. In the smoke, Virginia's sweet, tangy base, Kentucky's smoky, woody tone, and Perique's spice evoking dried plum and pepper follow one another. Suited to those seeking an unflavored, full but not excessive character, and to experienced smokers used to rubbing out and drying coin cuts before smoking.
mac-baren-royal-twist.o: Leaves a dark tobacco aroma with a lightly smoky trace of dried fruit and spice.

watch-city-cigar-hampton-roads.z: This is a house blend from Watch City Cigar counted among its Virginia-Perique group, for which no sufficient source could be found.
watch-city-cigar-hampton-roads.o: Records note it leaves a tart-sweet scent typical of Virginia-Perique blends.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-coconut-twist.z: Sweet Coconut Twist is one of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s old-style rope (twist) tobaccos. The leaves are twisted and wound like rope and left to mature, producing a dark-colored, oily-looking, tightly wound roll. A light coconut-based flavoring is applied over the roll. According to sources, this flavoring doesn't mask the tobacco's own heavy, fire-cured character — it's more noticeable in the aroma than in the smoke's taste, and recedes as the smoking progresses. The general rule for rope tobaccos applies here too: the roll burns evenly when very thinly sliced and rubbed out, but is hard to light and needs a lot of relighting when cut thick. Nicotine is high, giving a hearty fullness. Not for those expecting a mild aromatic; suited to smokers familiar with dark, strong, traditional English rope tobaccos who are willing to do the slicing and preparation work.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-coconut-twist.o: Leaves a sweet coconut aroma mixed with heavy fire-cured leaf smoke.

clan-shaw-albany.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Albany.
clan-shaw-albany.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

red-bull-red-bull-aromatic.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of the Red Bull Aromatic blend.

richs-alder-street.z: Alder Street is one of the house blends Rich's Cigar Store in Portland prepares in-house. It is built on dark-fired leaf and golden Cavendish, described as a light-bodied, distinctly scented mixture. It takes its name from the street where the shop is located. Its Cavendish-heavy structure gives a sweetish, mellow smoke that burns without biting the tongue. It suits smokers looking for a blend on the aromatic side that isn't weighed down by fruit flavoring. It is available only in bulk at Rich's stores; most of these house blends were created over thirty years ago by the shop's head blender.
richs-alder-street.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly smoky Cavendish aroma.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-cornishma.z: Cornishman, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an American-type mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

hearth-home-black-house.z: Black House is a mixture Russ Ouellette prepared as a tribute to a great Balkan blend of the past, produced for a 2011 blending competition; records indicate it was judged the closest entry to the dark Balkan style it took as its model. Its composition includes quality Virginia leaf, Latakia, Perique, and dark fire-cured Kentucky. What sets the blend apart is its use of various Oriental leaves, including Yenidje; these add a dry-hay, spicy, tart depth to the smoke. The overall character is spicy, full-bodied, and smoky, with an earthy sweetness in the background. It is unflavored. Suited to smokers familiar with dark Balkan mixtures who want a layered blend with Latakia used at a high dose.
hearth-home-black-house.o: Leaves a heavy aroma of wood smoke, spice, and dry earth.

samuel-gawith-1792-flake.z: 1792 Flake is one of the best-known Samuel Gawith blends produced in Kendal. It is obtained by pressing steam-processed (stoved) Virginia leaf together with fire-cured Kentucky into flake form; a casing evoking tonka bean and whiskey is applied on top. The tin yields dark-colored, often high-moisture, partly broken flakes; airing is needed before smoking. On the smoke, tonka's floral, spicy scent comes forward, with an intense tobacco taste carrying a smoky, woody, near-caramel sweetness beneath it. Nicotine is, according to records, very high and tends to bite the tongue as pace increases; hence it is used in small-chambered pipes with a slow smoke. Suited to experienced smokers familiar with strong, intense, and unusually flavored tobaccos; not a blend that would be a pipe newcomer's first choice.
samuel-gawith-1792-flake.o: Spreads a scent of tonka's floral, perfumed note along with smoky tobacco and coffee echoes through the room.

frederick-tranter-persimmons-mixture.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Frederick Tranter's Persimmons Mixture blend; records place it in the Virginia-heavy class.

the-smoker-olde-virginia.z: Olde Virginia is recorded as one of the hand-prepared house blends from The Smoker, a tobacconist that operated in Albany from the 1930s until 2011; no independent source describing the blend's composition has been found.

bosphorus-bitter-almond.z: Bitter Almond is a ribbon-cut aromatic blend built from Turkish tobaccos of the Adıyaman and Bitlis regions, flavored with bitter almond aroma. The light bitterness the aroma brings is distinguishable in the smoke but not to a degree that covers the tobacco's own taste; strength and flavor are medium. Among domestically produced aromatics, this blend has an intensity suited to all-day consumption. Appeals to smokers seeking a moderately flavored product that preserves the spicy character of Turkish tobacco.
bosphorus-bitter-almond.o: Leaves a sweet almond aroma reminiscent of bitter-almond confection in the room.

ken-byron-ventures-meditations.z: Meditations is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

mcclelland-blending-turkish.z: Blending Turkish is an unflavored Turkish tobacco McClelland sold only in bulk. As the name suggests, its main function is to serve as a component for smokers building their own blends; it's ribbon cut and carries no flavoring. It has an oily, sweet character reminiscent of cigarette flavor; the spicy, exotic taste typical of Oriental tobacco is pronounced. Nicotine level runs above medium, so it suits slow smoking. Smoked on its own, it offers a uniform profile; the room note is sharp and lingers a long time indoors.
mcclelland-blending-turkish.o: Leaves a sharp, oily tobacco aroma reminiscent of cigarettes that fills the room.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-flake-vanilla.z: This is the vanilla-topped version of the Brown Flake family. The same base is used: burley accompanies Virginia leaf that has been hot-pressed and darkened. The topping replaces the floral and liquorice line of the family's other versions with a single-direction vanilla sweetness. The flake is tight and burns slowly once rubbed out; when moisture runs high, a short airing regulates the burn. In the taste, Virginia's bread-like sweetness and vanilla's creamy note layer on top of each other, while the burley leaves an earthy body in the background.
