It suits a smoker who doesn't want to approach the heavy floral scents of the Kendal style but is looking for a flaked, flavoured English tobacco.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-flake-vanilla.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked dough aroma.

robert-mcconnell-the-original-pure-orien.z: Pure Orient is a product from Robert McConnell's single-varietal series made of small-leaf Oriental tobaccos. The brand's blending Oriental leaf is reported to be sourced from Izmir and Samsun; being sun-cured, it carries a distinctive dry, tart, spicy aroma. Nicotine sits below medium, while the flavor range is wide. Used in mixtures, it reduces Virginia's tendency to bite the tongue and adds a creamy sweetness and a spice layer to the blend. It is one of the core components for smokers building English and Balkan-style mixtures; smoked alone it offers an intense, unusual taste. The brand is Belfast in origin; production takes place in Germany.
robert-mcconnell-the-original-pure-orien.o: Leaves an aroma of dry hay, incense, and a light spice.

rattray-caribbean-dream.z: Caribbean Dream is a blend in Rattray's aromatic line. Its composition includes Virginia leaf, cube-cut Virginia, black Cavendish, and some Burley. Its flavoring is coconut-forward, rounded out with tropical fruit and vanilla notes. The brand is Scottish in origin; production today takes place in Germany. The slow burn the cube cut brings sits alongside the Cavendish's sweetness; the Burley share gives the smoke a light body. Nicotine is measured, and the taste stays on a fruity, creamy line. It appeals to those looking for a light, sweet summer aromatic, especially fans of the coconut note.
rattray-caribbean-dream.o: Leaves a sweet aroma dominated by coconut and vanilla, carrying a tropical-fruit freshness.

tabacos-cisne-branco-finamore-ltda-wilde.z: A product in the Wilder line from Juiz de Fora-based Tabacos Cisne Branco Finamore, whose name points to being unflavored; no independent source describing its content and character could be found.
tabacos-cisne-branco-finamore-ltda-wilde.o: Records suggest it leaves an unflavored, dry tobacco scent.

alfie-turmeaus-mystery-mix-b.z: One of the unnamed experimental mixtures from Turmeaus tobacconist; no accessible source documenting its content or character could be found.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-pink-champagne.z: There is not enough independent sourcing available for this Hermit Tobacco Works Co. blend, which is described as aromatic.

van-erkoms-black-cavendish.z: A tobacco South African maker Van Erkoms offers under the name black Cavendish, noted as one of the bulk products made at the brand's Mokopane facility. No independent source documenting its flavoring, cut, and leaf source has been found, so the record is incomplete.

the-ridge-pipe-tobacco-elementary-blend.z: No reliable source could be found on The Ridge Pipe Tobacco's Elementary Blend.

thepiperoom-com-midnight-vigil.z: Midnight Vigil, one of ThePipeRoom.com's house blends, is noted as a dark-character mixture; since no independent source detailing its composition has been found, the record is left incomplete.
thepiperoom-com-midnight-vigil.o: Records describe it as leaving a smoky, dark tobacco aroma.

astleys-no-1-medium-latakia-mixture.z: Astley's No. 1 Medium Latakia Mixture is a classic London blend sold under the name of Astley's, the pipe house on Jermyn Street in London. It contains red Virginia, Latakia, Turkish tobacco, and black Cavendish in balanced proportions. It carries no flavoring and is sold in 50-gram tins. Latakia gives the blend an earthy, smoky character, while the dominant Virginias add measured sweetness, and the black Cavendish adds a walnut-like mellowness. Body is light-to-medium, flavor intensity is medium; it burns evenly with a mild smoke temperature. It suits those wanting to get into English blends with a moderate dose of Latakia, and those looking for an unflavored mixture to smoke all day.
astleys-no-1-medium-latakia-mixture.o: Leaves a sweetish tobacco room note beneath a woody, smoky scent.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrugs-golden-scept.z: Surbrug's Golden Sceptre is among the Surbrug recipes Wilke carries with the widest leaf variety. According to the maker's recipe, two different Burleys, red Virginia, and long-cut Virginia are brought together, topped with Latakia. In the smoke, Cyprian Latakia's profile opens up, Burley carries the nutty, spicy body, the Virginias leave a fruity, tart edge, and Perique adds a subtle spice layer. It's a complex record that stays in the medium strength band and burns cool and clean. It suits smokers who love unflavored blends and want Latakia and Burley balanced together; due to its intensity, it's meant for particular sessions rather than repeated all-day bowls.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrugs-golden-scept.o: A light spice mixes into the roasted-nut and wood-smoke scent.

vauen-no-22-english-blend.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Vauen pipe tobacco called No. 22 English Blend to record the blend's composition and character.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-irish-twist-liq.z: This is a product of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s old-fashioned rope (twist) production in Kendal. Dark fire-cured leaves are twisted into rope; within the Brown Irish Twist family, this body carries the natural smoky, earthy character of fire curing untouched. In the Liquorice Plum version, the rope is finished with a liquorice-root and plum-based flavouring, so alongside the sharpness of the raw leaf, a dark fruit sweetness also appears. The rope is sliced coin-thin and rubbed out; since moisture runs high, airing it before loading the pipe is standard practice. It is a full-bodied tobacco sitting at the upper end for nicotine; it may be heavy for anyone not accustomed to ropes built on dark Virginia and fire-cured leaf. Records note that part of this rope family has traditionally also been consumed as chewing tobacco. It is aimed at those seeking a slow-smoking, long-lasting, strong rope softened with a sweet top note.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-irish-twist-liq.o: A heavy smoky, cured-leather aroma is topped with a sweet liquorice and stewed-plum note.

w-o-larsen-flake-cut.z: No reliable source could be found regarding the composition and character of this Danish blend bearing the W.Ø. Larsen name.
w-o-larsen-flake-cut.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

iwan-ries-gourmet-aromatic.z: No verifiable source about the composition of this aromatic blend, part of Iwan Ries's Gourmet line established in 1997, could be found.

hu-tobacco-the-bullet.z: The Bullet is a pressed-and-rubbed-out flake built by adding a touch of Perique and a small amount of Havana and Brazilian leaf atop dark red Virginia leaves. The cigar leaf pulls the blend toward an earthy, spicy side, while the Perique adds a sharp turn. The sweet, fruity coating applied on top reportedly carries an unusual tomato-evoking note; in this respect the blend counts as neither fully aromatic nor a straight Virginia. It's medium strength and aimed at smokers looking for spicy, pressed leaf.
hu-tobacco-the-bullet.o: Leaves an aroma of sweetish fruit and lightly spiced leaf.

dunhill-aromatic.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of this aromatic blend referred to under the Dunhill name.
dunhill-aromatic.o: Leaves a sweetly sauced tobacco scent.

peretti-dundee.z: This is one of the house blends of the L. J. Peretti shop in Boston; it appears under the English blends heading in the maker's list. The profile is left incomplete, as no published description of the blend's content and character could be found.

hu-tobacco-casablanca-feeling.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Casablanca Feeling, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

karl-erik-private-blend-no-16.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Karl Erik's Private Blend No.16.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2002.z: Christmas Cheer is McClelland's unflavored Virginia series presenting one harvest as a separate tin each year; 2002 is a release from the series' earlier years. In the series, matured orange-red Virginia leaves dried by the flue-cure method are pressed into cake, aged, sliced, and then partly broken up before being tinned as broken flake. What sets the series apart is that each year comes from a separate crop and the tins change as they age. The tin note carries a sharp, tangy vinegar-like acidity characteristic of McClelland Virginias; in the smoke, the leaf's natural sweetness and a bready line stand out, with no flavoring added. A record kept for smokers wanting to track unflavored Virginia and the effect of aging. Since the brand closed in 2018, no new release has come out.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2002.o: Leaves a tangy, vinegary sweetness along with a toasted-bread aroma.

friedman-pease-fez.z: This is one of two blends put into production, alongside Fool's Cap, in Friedman & Pease's line inspired by hat names; since the company closed around 2000, its production ended and no reliable source describing its composition could be found.

criss-cross-smooth-blend.z: Criss Cross is a budget-class tobacco brand sold in large bags in the US market. Per the brand's marketing, the blend is made of air-cured Burley and Virginia leaf, presented in a fine, shag-like cut; though sold under the name pipe tobacco, its structure leans more toward roll-your-own cigarette use. Smooth Blend is a softened version of the series' original red-bag product. While keeping the same cut, body and sharpness are reduced, aiming for a flatter, lighter smoke. It carries no pronounced flavoring; taste rests on the tobacco's own toasted base. Aimed at those looking for a low-cost, light, undemanding smoke.
criss-cross-smooth-blend.o: Leaves a scent of roasted tobacco and lightly sweet hay.

dobies-four-square-mild-navy-cut-yellow.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of Four Square Mild Navy Cut (Yellow), a blend from Dobie's.

the-eastern-company-4-aces.z: 4 Aces is a bulk pipe tobacco produced by Eastern Company S.A.E., Egypt's largely state-run tobacco concern founded in 1920. Alongside cigarettes, shisha tobacco and cigars, the company also runs a limited pipe tobacco line. The blend is composed mainly of Oriental (Turkish) leaf, giving it a dry, spicy, grassy taste line reminiscent of Oriental-forward cigarette blends. There is no record of any casing being used. A product with limited international distribution, aimed at those curious about the plain character of Oriental leaf and those seeking a blending base.
the-eastern-company-4-aces.o: Leaves a dry, spicy, faintly tangy Oriental-tobacco aroma.

motzek-typ-3-2-danish-blend.z: A numbered blend from the Motzek workshop's Danish-style aromatic line; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and flavoring could not be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-balkan-i-510.z: The first entry in Sutliff's Balkan series; the later Balkan II, with its heavier oriental and latakia load, was built on top of this blend. Sufficient independent sources detailing its own composition could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-balkan-i-510.o: Records indicate it leaves a scent of woody latakia smoke and dry spice.

watch-city-cigar-justice-mixture.z: This is one of the house blends of the Watch City Cigar shop; it does not appear in the current catalog, and no source could be found documenting its composition.

d-r-tobacco-value-pipe-blend.z: Value Pipe Blend is Daughters & Ryan's budget-line American-style mixture. It's built on sweet Virginia and soft Burley leaf, offered in versions distinguished by tin color names: the red version is full and flavorful, the blue version a softened take on the same blend, and the green version has a menthol character. It's ribbon cut, with moisture suited to smoking straight from the pouch. An uncomplicated blend sold in large packagings for everyday consumption; nicotine and flavor intensity sit below the medium band. Built for smokers who don't expect a showy aromatic or a layered English mixture but want a plain American taste for steady, everyday smoking.
d-r-tobacco-value-pipe-blend.o: Leaves a plain trace where sweetish Virginia and dry Burley scent mingle.

paul-olsen-players-white.z: A Virginia blend recorded as one of the house blends from the Danish Paul Olsen (My Own Blend) house; no independent source about its composition and character could be found.

bosphorus-chocolate-cake.z: Chocolate Cake is a chocolate-flavored flake built from Eastern-region tobaccos, Yenice, Latakia and cavendish. For a flavored product, the Latakia proportion is measured and does not show itself too much; the blend's true color comes from the spicy taste characteristic of Turkish tobaccos. Sugar content is kept low, so the chocolate note does not turn into a pronounced sweetness. Suitable for smokers seeking a lightly sugared, spicy-structured chocolate aromatic.
bosphorus-chocolate-cake.o: Leaves a trace where light cocoa sweetness mixes into the spicy Turkish tobacco aroma.

dunhill-nightcap.z: Nightcap is a ribbon-cut English mixture made of latakia, Turkish orientals, perique and Virginia leaves. The tin name is seen written both as one word and two across different periods, though the blend's structure stays the same. Latakia is the dominant component, with perique sharpening the spice. The nicotine level is high, and its weight increases from the second half of the smoke onward; it is therefore not a blend for an empty stomach or a fast smoke. The smoke is satisfying and dense. It suits smokers experienced with strong, latakia-heavy blends seeking an evening smoke. Production under the Dunhill name has ended.
dunhill-nightcap.o: Heavy wood soot and spicy tobacco scent fills the room.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-black-jack.z: Black Jack is a coarse-cut burley and cavendish mixture from the Boswell workshop in Pennsylvania. The thick cut gives a slow, cool burn; burley's nutty, bready base is softened with cavendish's measured sweetness. The manufacturer describes it as a blend that can be smoked all day. Suitable for smokers who stay away from heavy flavoring, feel an affinity for the classic American burley character, and prefer smoking a single tobacco for long stretches.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-black-jack.o: Leaves a plain tobacco aroma, not tart, with a dry-leaf and light molasses smell.

robert-mcconnell-kentucky.z: Kentucky is an unflavored product from Robert McConnell's single-varietal line, made entirely of Kentucky tobacco. This dark-fired Burley type is known for its smoke, soot, and earthy-spice tones; it has no sweet side, and its taste is dry and deep. Nicotine is high, so smoking it on its own calls for experience. Its main use is as a body and strength component in the hands of home blenders: added to Virginia-heavy mixtures, it balances the sweetness and adds fullness to the smoke. The brand was founded in London in 1848; production continues today in Germany.
robert-mcconnell-kentucky.o: Leaves the wood-smoke and soot aroma of dark-fired leaf.

koiki-kizami.z: Koiki Kizami is a traditional kiseru tobacco produced from Virginia leaf grown in Japan. The name "Kizami" describes the leaf being sliced as fine as hair; though classed as shag, its fibers are far finer than usual shag cuts. It's unflavored and sold in small 10-gram pouches. Records indicate it's sold only within Japan, with export outside the country restricted by regulation. The smoking method differs from Western pipe smoking: a pinch of tobacco is rolled between the fingers into a small ball and placed in the bowl of a kiseru, a pipe usually with a bamboo body, metal mouthpiece and a very small metal bowl. Since the bowl holds about an eighth of a teaspoon, the smoke finishes in a few puffs. The pouch note carries grassy freshness with light earth, wood and hay; once lit, lemony citrus and fresh grass come forward. Nicotine is notably filling; of interest to those interested in unflavored Virginia and traditional Japanese smoking practice.
koiki-kizami.o: A lemony sharpness mixes into the scent of freshly cut grass and dry hay.

brigadier-black-bull-run.z: Bull Run is the classic vanilla aromatic in the Brigadier Black line. A measured vanilla casing is applied over a combination of black cavendish and golden burley leaf. Burley forms the blend's dry, nutty base; cavendish carries the sweetness and moisture. Since the casing is not applied heavily, the tobacco's own taste is not entirely covered. Nicotine is low, flavor soft. A profile suited to those wanting vanilla aromatics at an intensity fit for all-day smoking, and to those new to pipe tobacco.
brigadier-black-bull-run.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough aroma.

samuel-gawith-kendal-cream-flake.z: Kendal Cream Flake is a flake tobacco Samuel Gawith presses and slices at its Kendal facility, built from Virginia and Burley leaves. The substance used as casing is not explicitly stated; the amount used is very low and does not cover the leaf's own taste. The resulting flavor is creamy and full in structure, which the "cream" designation in the name references. Its nicotine is above medium, so it may be heavy for those not accustomed to full tobaccos. A suitable record for those seeking a small variation within a familiar plain-Virginia flavor frame, especially those accustomed to slow smoking with flake cut.
samuel-gawith-kendal-cream-flake.o: Leaves a creamy, lightly sweet, and oily tobacco scent.

j-f-germain-son-goldleaf-r-r.z: Virginia Goldleaf Ready Rubbed is a straight blend made up solely of flue-cured Virginia leaf. Golden and brown leaves are selected and lightly pressed, then rubbed out — so it has a loose, broken-flake-like ribbon structure that can be filled straight from the tin. The light pressing slows the burn rate, allowing the Virginia's natural sugar and sour-citrus-tinged flavors to come forward. Flavor-wise it's intense but unflavored, and moderate in nicotine; smoked cool, its bready sweetness and light citrus sharpness become more pronounced. It suits smokers who enjoy unflavored Virginia and don't want the hassle of preparing flakes themselves. Records indicate it's cut from the same leaf as Peacehaven, which goes to the US market under the Esoterica name.
j-f-germain-son-goldleaf-r-r.o: Leaves an aroma of dry hay, stale bread, and a hint of lemon peel.

mac-baren-hh-old-dark-fired-ready-rubbed.z: HH Old Dark Fired Ready Rubbed is the rubbed-out version of the same-named flake. The blend still rests on Virginias and fire-cured dark Kentucky burley; the leaves are pressed with heat and steam to mature, then sliced, and these slices are rubbed out before packing. The tin doesn't contain whole flakes; it comes as short, thin and relatively dry strands. Being pre-rubbed speeds up packing and lets the tobacco arrive ready to light; in exchange, instead of the slow-opening smoke of a pressed slice, a faster-burning character emerges. The flavor profile is in line with the flake version: it carries the smoky, earthy Kentucky blend, while the Virginias' ripe-fruit sweetness balances that weight. Nicotine load is notable. A presentation meant for those wanting the same character without the bother of preparing a flake.
mac-baren-hh-old-dark-fired-ready-rubbed.o: Leaves a leathery scent reminiscent of meat cooked over wood fire and smoke.

paul-olsen-no-4.z: One of the Virginia-forward blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

seattle-pipe-club-mississippi-river-spec.z: Mississippi River Special Reserve is a longer-aged, tinned version of the Virginia blend of the same name. The ingredient list matches the main record: a pressed Virginia body accompanied by Oriental leaf, a small amount of Latakia, and Perique. What sets it apart is the extra maturation period the blend undergoes before tinning. Aging lets the Virginia sugars turn into a deeper, rounder taste; the sharp edges of the accent leaves are filed down and the blend becomes a more integrated whole. Considered a series set aside for smokers who know the main version and want to compare it against the matured take on the same recipe, and for those seeking cellar-worthy records.
seattle-pipe-club-mississippi-river-spec.o: A fine wood smoke accompanies a mature-hay and dried-fruit scent.

cornell-diehl-big-n-burley.z: Big n' Burley is one of Cornell & Diehl's burley-centered mixtures. A sweet, long-cut burley leaf forms the body; a small amount of Latakia, Turkish leaf, and a pinch of perique are added on top. The maker describes it as "an English blend for burley lovers"; the Latakia level is enough to nudge the blend toward the English family but doesn't mask burley's nutty, earthy core. Nicotine strength runs high, so smoking on an empty stomach or at a fast pace noticeably increases the harshness. Taken slowly, it burns cool, with a light perique-derived spice emerging toward the middle of the bowl. It suits smokers looking for burley's natural taste along with a smoky edge, accustomed to unflavored blends; it is not a suitable starting point for someone expecting an aromatic.
cornell-diehl-big-n-burley.o: A thin layer of wood smoke sits over an earthy aroma reminiscent of roasted nuts.

tabakfabrik-roth-jabuca-english-blend.z: Jabuca English Blend is the mixture within Tabakfabrik Roth's Jabuca series reserved for the English style. According to the maker, black Cavendish and richly flavored Latakia are added to a balanced Virginia-Burley base; a touch of vanilla adds depth to the mixture. The result is a structure with smoky and spicy facets that is nonetheless not entirely dry. It is filled at a medium cut and offered in a resealable pouch. It suits smokers who like Latakia but find fully unflavored English blends too harsh, and who want a sweet edge.
tabakfabrik-roth-jabuca-english-blend.o: A light, sweet trace of vanilla mixes into Latakia's smoky scent.

watch-city-cigar-waltham-broken-cake.z: Watch City Cigar's blend called Waltham Broken Cake is, according to records, one of the house blends of the Waltham, Massachusetts tobacconist shop; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

4noggins-nutty-professor.z: Nutty Professor is one of the house blends US-based 4noggins sells in bulk. Its backbone is built from stoved Virginia leaves and Burley, with a small amount of Cyprus Latakia, Turkish tobacco, and St. James Parish Perique added. As the name suggests, the dominant character is Burley's nutty, lightly molasses-like tone; Perique here leans more toward a raisin-like sweetness than a peppery bite, while the Latakia and Oriental only draw a thin frame around the blend. Being ribbon cut, it packs and lights easily; it's described as a cool, slow-burning tobacco with moderate nicotine. It carries no flavoring — it's an unadulterated blend. It suits smokers who enjoy Burley-based American-style blends, don't mind a light touch of Latakia, and want a balanced tobacco smokable all day.
4noggins-nutty-professor.o: Leaves a nutty, lightly molasses-like scent with a thin trace of smoke from the Latakia.

mcclelland-take-6.z: One of the blends in McClelland's aromatic series; no sufficient source describing its contents and character could be found.

gurkha-retribution.z: Retribution is a dark English blend in the pipe tobacco line of Gurkha, a brand known for cigars. Its composition includes Turkish-origin Oriental leaf and a high proportion of Latakia; Virginia is used just enough to balance these two components. The ribbon cut ensures an even, cool burn in the pipe. The blend's character is set by Latakia's smoky, resinous tone; the Oriental leaf adds a spicy, lightly tart layer on top of that base, while Virginia leaves a measured sweetness in the background. Its unflavored makeup and heavy smoke make it suited to smokers accustomed to dark English blends; it is not considered a starting blend for someone coming from aromatics.
gurkha-retribution.o: Leaves a heavy room aroma evoking smoke, burnt wood, and incense.

hearth-home-smoky-mountain.z: Smoky Mountain belongs to Hearth & Home's Slow-Aged line, a blend where fire-cured (dark fired) leaf comes forward. The tobaccos are pressed into a cake and then held in an aging press for roughly a month; this process deepens the flavors and softens the sharp edges. In the smoke, an intense, easily flowing draw is found, along with an initial peppery sharpness followed by a sustained, meaty, herbal depth. It suits smokers looking for smokiness without Latakia and able to handle the nicotine load of dark leaves.
hearth-home-smoky-mountain.o: Leaves an intense aroma reminiscent of wood smoke and smoked meat.

sutliff-tobacco-company-tobacco-galleria.z: Simplicity is a blend in Sutliff's Tobacco Galleria line; no sufficient source describing this product's content and character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-tobacco-galleria.o: No reliable record of a room note could be found.

michael-apitz-private-blend-blue-canary.z: Blue Canary is one of the aromatic varieties in the Michael Apitz line under Dan Tobacco. The blend's body is built from soft black cavendish matured by traditional methods; its dark appearance is loosened by golden flake fragments. The flavoring rests on apple and vanilla, leaving a subtle cinnamon trace behind. The blend's name is a reference to the song "Blue Canary," recorded by Dinah Shore in 1953, chosen by Michael Apitz for its inspiration from the contrast of mountain, sun, wind, and water on the Canary Islands. It is a tobacco with low nicotine strength and a pronounced sweetness; suitable for those looking for a sweet, spiced profile in aromatic style.
michael-apitz-private-blend-blue-canary.o: Leaves an aroma of baked apple, vanilla, and cinnamon.

sentimiento-nacional-don-alfonso.z: A blend under the Sentimiento Nacional name; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

paul-olsen-atlantic.z: One of the aromatic house blends from Danish tobacconist Poul Olsen; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.

paul-olsen-freja.z: A blend from the My Own Blend line that originated at the Paul Olsen shop in Copenhagen; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

borkum-riff-mellow-breeze-full-aromatic.z: An option presented as a heavily flavored offering in the Borkum Riff line; no adequate source on its composition and flavor profile could be found.

consolidated-507-c-virginia-slices-matur.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Consolidated blend 507-C: Virginia Slices (Matured).

century-american-blueberry.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named American Blueberry under the Century brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

mcclelland-townsman-cavendish-blue.z: Townsman Cavendish Blue is a Cavendish blend in McClelland's bulk aromatic series, said to be flavored in a 19th-century maple style; it was discontinued when the maker closed in 2018. No reliable source on the blend's leaf composition could be found, so no detailed description is given here.
mcclelland-townsman-cavendish-blue.o: Leaves a sweet, sugary aroma reminiscent of maple syrup.

a-c-petersen-the-chiefs-own-mixture-no-3.z: A numbered mixture belonging to A & C Petersen's "The Chief's Own" line; no adequate source documenting its content could be found.

mac-baren-24-karat.z: No verifiable information could be found in the manufacturer's own catalog or in two independent sources about Mac Baren's aromatic blend known as 24 Karat.

hearth-home-louisiana-red.z: Louisiana Red is a Virginia-Perique blend where two separate red Virginia leaves are combined with a generous amount of Acadian Perique. It is a medium-brown ribbon cut, and the tin releases a sweet aroma reminiscent of dried fruit. The Virginias give a round, dark sweetness with a light tart-fruit tone, while Perique adds plum and black-pepper seasoning. The smoke is cool and full; the balance between sweetness and spice is the blend's defining trait. Being unflavored, it is aimed not at aromatic seekers but at smokers looking for the classic style of the Virginia-Perique family. It is counted among the brand's fully original, non-imitation blends.
hearth-home-louisiana-red.o: Leaves an aroma where dried-fruit sweetness mingles with peppery spice.

mcclelland-no-22.z: No. 22 is a cake tobacco in McClelland's "Matured Virginias" series. Records indicate Eastern and Middle Belt Virginias are rested as a cake to develop their natural sugars; within the series, blends numbered 22 and 24 take a bit of Oriental alongside red and yellow Virginias. The cut is coarsely prepared and can be rubbed out by hand to the desired fineness. In the flavor profile, Virginia's tangy-sweet, sharp side stands out; the Oriental addition adds spiced depth to that tang. The coarse cut suits smoking outdoors in windy weather. Smoked slowly, it's a blend close to pure Virginia character that leaves no harshness on the tongue. Production ended when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-no-22.o: Leaves a sharp, sweet tobacco aroma reminiscent of tart fruit vinegar.

owl-shop-black-magic.z: Black Magic is one of the house mixtures from the Owl Shop, a tobacconist operating in New Haven since 1934. It's a sweet, pronouncedly flavored blend based on black Cavendish; the shop's description mentions traces of dark chocolate, raisin, and crème brûlée. Being light in nicotine, it counts among the blends smokable all day. It's an option for those seeking sweet aromatics with a heavy room note, and those wanting a taste different from straight Virginia or Latakia mixtures.
owl-shop-black-magic.o: Leaves a scent of dark chocolate, raisin, and burnt-sugar cream.

samuel-gawith-christmas-mixture-2007.z: A limited-run edition Samuel Gawith released for the 2007 holiday season; no independent source documenting that year's specific blend content could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-r-blend.z: R-Blend is a multi-component American blend produced at Sutliff's facilities in Virginia. Its base contains burley and Virginia leaf; a small amount of latakia and perique along with pressed leaf are added to build a layered structure. Records indicate the blend brings together a number of taste elements that are hard to pick apart individually; none overpowers the others, so its character is built on a balanced whole rather than one dominant note. The smoke is soft and measured; nicotine strength stays below medium, and the taste sits close to medium. Because the latakia and perique proportions are kept low, it's also an easy entry point for smokers unfamiliar with English blends. It suits smokers looking for an unflavored blend that can be smoked all day without becoming monotonous. It has been removed from Sutliff's catalog and is not currently in production.
sutliff-tobacco-company-r-blend.o: Leaves a woody, smoky tobacco scent alongside a light fruity sweetness.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-1995.z: Christmas Cheer 1995 is a member of McClelland's annual unflavored Virginia series. Per its label, it's made with lemon-orange-colored Carolina leaves selected from the Piedmont region's 1992 harvest. The leaf is pressed and presented as broken flake. Like other light-Virginia-forward years, it gives a sweet, tangy-citrus profile; the brand's well-known tangy-sweet tin note is pronounced. No flavoring, and nicotine is medium. Like the whole series, it's produced for long-term storage and suits smokers seeking unflavored Virginia.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-1995.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of sweet hay and lemon peel.

ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-out-shine.z: Yoshimi's Out Shine is a light-bowl Virginia-oriental blend in Ken Byron Ventures' Yoshimi's line. A honeysuckle-and-melon casing is applied to the tobacco skeleton; the casing isn't masking, kept at a level that complements the tobacco's own taste. In the smoke, Virginia's lemony, tangy side comes forward, the oriental leaf brings a dry musk and spice, and the melon note appears lightly in the background. Nicotine load isn't heavy; built for daytime and outdoor bowls. Suited to smokers seeking a light-bowl oriental blend without latakia. Due to small-batch production, it isn't constantly on the market.
ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-out-shine.o: Floral honeysuckle and cool melon are underlaid by a hay-like tobacco trace.

motzek-black-twist.z: Since neither the manufacturer's own description nor two independent reliable sources could be found for the Motzek blend called Black Twist, its composition, cut, and character could not be documented here.

cao-first-colony.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named First Colony under the CAO brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

alfie-turmeaus-orchant-seleccion.z: Orchant Seleccion is a store-exclusive mixture from the tobacconist that carries the founding name of the Turmeaus and C.Gars Ltd. umbrella. Its structure rests on combining a generous amount of Latakia and Turkish-origin Oriental leaf with selected Virginias; the blend is rounded out with Havana-origin cigar leaf and black Cavendish. Adding cigar leaf gives the classic English mixture an earthy, salty depth rarely found in pipe tobaccos. The smoke is cool and slow-burning, sitting in the medium-strong band; as the palate adjusts, it leaves an aftertaste that shifts between oak and smoked walnut. Because of its unflavored structure and the nicotine load from the cigar leaf, it's aimed at experienced smokers; it suits those who know Latakia mixtures and want to add a cigar-leaf dimension to them.
alfie-turmeaus-orchant-seleccion.o: Leaves an intense cigar-smoke trace in the room, mixed with burnt oak and roasted hazelnut.

peterson-petersons-perfect-plug.z: Peterson's Perfect Plug is a blend in which ripe African Virginia leaf and spicy Brazilian- and Malawi-origin Burley leaf are pressed into a plug. It is sold as a molded block; before smoking it needs to be sliced and rubbed out. Peterson is an Irish brand, and the blend appears in the current Peterson tobacco line under the name 3 P's Peterson's Perfect Plug. It carries a medium-strong nicotine level and an intense flavor; a fruity sweetness rounds out the blend's character. Pressing intensifies the tobacco's flavor while also giving a slow, cool smoke. It suits smokers accustomed to preparing plug tobacco who are seeking a full-bodied Virginia-Burley mixture.
peterson-petersons-perfect-plug.o: Leaves an intense tobacco aroma mixed with fruity sweetness.

park-lane-tobacconist-milk-and-honey.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Milk and Honey, one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

e-a-carey-imported-light-vanilla.z: Imported Light Vanilla is a light-colored aromatic E. A. Carey has produced in Denmark and sold under its own name. Per the maker's description, a Danish-style vanilla topping along with real vanilla extract is applied over a rested burley base. The blend is built very light; its nicotine load is low and it doesn't harshen the tongue. It is therefore a suitable all-day choice for newcomers to the pipe and smokers bothered by sharp blends. Though the brand is American, this blend's production takes place in Denmark.
e-a-carey-imported-light-vanilla.o: Leaves a soft vanilla and sweet bakery scent.

e-hoffman-company-distinguished-gentlema.z: Distinguished Gentleman is a blend in the E. Hoffman Company line bringing together burley, Virginia, black cavendish and Cyprus latakia. The Virginia leaves provide natural sweetness and body; burley and cavendish add a nutty roundness to the mixture, while latakia leaves a measured smokiness in the background. A light aromatic topping is applied on top. With medium body, earthy and nutty tones combined with a sweet top note, this structure places the blend in the transitional zone between aromatic and unadulterated. It suits smokers coming from aromatics who want to get to know latakia, or conversely, those looking for a lightly topped American mixture.
e-hoffman-company-distinguished-gentlema.o: Leaves a sweetish, nutty scent with a fine wood smoke in the background.

rivertown-tobacco-works-mystic-moor.z: Mystic Moor is the English-style blend in Rivertown Tobacco Works' bulk line. Latakia takes the lead role in this ribbon-cut mixture, joined by black Cavendish for a soft sweetness and Virginia for a bright, fresh base. Latakia's smoke, incense, floral, and herbal tones come forward alongside dark fruit and leather associations, while Cavendish's natural sweetness rounds off the blend's sharp edges. Flavor intensity is high and nicotine medium. It is a blend Latakia lovers can smoke through the day, carrying the weight of classic English mixtures while also holding a sweet side thanks to the Virginia and Cavendish. Since it is sold in bulk, it also works as a smoky component in house blends.
rivertown-tobacco-works-mystic-moor.o: Leaves a lightly sweet trace beneath the wood-fire smoke, incense, and leather aroma.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.z: Cândido Giovanella is a pipe tobacco line produced by Imigrantes Indústria e Comércio de Fumos, operating in Brazil's Paraná state, and has long been available domestically. The backbone of the line is built on sun-dried Virginia leaf grown in Brazil, along with Burley and black Cavendish; the leaves are ribbon cut and usually presented in 45-50 gram resealable packs. Baunilha is the vanilla-flavored version of this base. In the smoke, vanilla's creamy sweetness leads, while the tobacco's own bready, lightly earthy taste stays in the background. Nicotine load is moderate, the smoke is cool, and thanks to the even cut it lights and stays lit without trouble. It's a suitable entry for those new to aromatic blends and those looking for a light, sweet smoke during the day.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.o: Leaves an aroma of sweet vanilla and sugared dough.

cornell-diehl-first-responders.z: First Responders is a Virginia blend released in memory of the first responders to the September 11 attacks. Per the maker's recipe, red, bright, and stoved Virginia leaves are joined by a small amount of perique and toasted cavendish; the cut is ribbon. Stoved Virginia gives the blend a dark, molasses-like depth, while the bright leaf preserves a tangy sweetness; perique steps in with a plum-and-spice note. Nicotine is medium, flavor intensity is pronounced. It suits smokers who love the Virginia-Perique family and are looking for a blend with dark sweetness.
cornell-diehl-first-responders.o: Leaves a dried-fruit sweetness with a lightly spiced, bready aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-mixed-coconut-.z: Kendal Mixed is the second of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s shag-cut main bodies. Unlike Kendal Gold's pure-Virginia structure, this body is built by adding Malawi-origin dark leaf and some fire-cured Kentucky to golden Virginia; because of this, its color is more mottled and its taste more earthy. This member is prepared by adding a coconut flavoring to the Kendal Mixed body; the "medium" designation indicates the series' medium-intensity flavoring setting. The fine shag cut lights easily and calls for a slow draw to avoid burning too fast. Suited to smokers wanting a sweet flavoring over the dark leaf's earthy base.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-mixed-coconut-.o: Leaves a roasted-coconut and sweet-milk aroma.

just-for-him-dusk.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Just For Him's Dusk blend.

samuel-gawith-bright-virginia.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Bright Virginia, according to records a pure Virginia blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

admirals-choice-black-gold-cavendish.z: Black & Gold Cavendish is the classic American-style Cavendish blend of the Admiral's Choice line, produced by the Dream Castle Tobacco Company under Sutliff. It takes its name from its appearance: a mixture of slow-steamed black Cavendish and golden-brown light-colored leaves. It has a sweet, mellow smoke standing out with toasted vanilla notes, described as not putting strength on the tongue. Its ribbon cut makes packing easy. It suits smokers looking for an inexpensive, widely available aromatic who want a sweet, flat profile rather than strong nicotine.
admirals-choice-black-gold-cavendish.o: Leaves a toasted vanilla and sweet-dough room note.

van-erkoms-exclusive-mix.z: Van Erkoms' Virginia-based blend sold in bulk in South Africa under the name "Exclusive Mixture"; it can be found at tobacconists within the country. No independent source detailing the blend's leaf proportions and cut has been found, so the record is left incomplete.

koltoma-tets-vintage.z: Referred to as the rested version of Russian manufacturer Koltoma's cigar-leaf-based TETS blend; no verifiable content information could be found.

fincks-cigar-company-dutch-style-cavendi.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for Finck's Cigar Company's Dutch Style Cavendish pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

mac-baren-scaferlati-caporal-vert.z: Vert is the light end of the Scaferlati Caporal series. The series, one of the classic names in French pipe smoking, was long produced by Seita and is continued today under the Mac Baren umbrella. The blend combines dark-fire-cured Kentucky with bright Virginia leaf; it's loose cut, and no flavoring is applied. Compared to the Bleu and red-labeled releases, it gives a lower-nicotine, milder smoke; records position it within the series as the reduced-nicotine release. The taste is dry, earthy, and lightly spiced, with no sweetness sought. Suited to those curious about unflavored French-style tobacco who don't want a full blend's nicotine load, and to daytime use.
mac-baren-scaferlati-caporal-vert.o: Leaves a dry hay and faintly earthy aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-black-kathy.z: Black Kathy is an aromatic blend listed as code 101 in the Sutliff catalog. Its distinguishing trait is that the black cavendish used is not bought ready-made but produced specifically for this blend: both burley and Virginia leaves are steamed to blacken them, then rested and matured for a week. This method gives a base carrying the character of two different leaves rather than a single cavendish type. The resulting tobacco is soft, creamy, and sweet; vanilla is used as the topping. The burley base adds an earthy body while Virginia brings light sweetness. Nicotine is low and the burn is even. Suited to smokers who like vanilla-centered aromatics and want a soft, cavendish-forward smoke. It's ribbon cut and sold in bulk.
sutliff-tobacco-company-black-kathy.o: Leaves a scent of creamy vanilla and sweet pastry.

schurch-don-carlos-195.z: Don Carlos 195, signed by Schürch, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

niall-of-nine-long-neck-demon.z: Long Neck Demon is a blend under the Niall of Nine signature, produced in small batches in the US. Records indicate it is made of 2022-harvest Kentucky leaf, darkened and heat-pressed burleys from 2016 and 2022, 2014 St. James Parish perique, and a small amount of Cyprian latakia and Macedonian oriental. No additives are used; sweetness comes from the tobacco's own processing. Its character is dark and earthy: perique's plum-and-pepper sharpness and a smoky line from the latakia layer over the pressed burley's bready, nutty body. It's a full-bodied blend in nicotine terms; it suits smokers accustomed to burley- and perique-forward, unflavored tobaccos wanting a long pipe toward day's end. The brand's blends come out in vacuum-sealed 50-gram jars in limited numbers, so availability is periodic.
niall-of-nine-long-neck-demon.o: Leaves a dark tobacco scent thickened by wood smoke, carrying a tart-fruit and peppery sharpness.

mac-baren-7-seas-red-blend.z: 7 Seas Red Blend is the fruity member of the line Mac Baren established for American-style aromatics. Per the manufacturer, the structure shared across the series applies here too: a Virginia base, burley for balance, and modern cavendish. It's presented as a loose cut with high moisture. The flavor direction leans toward a sweet red-fruit profile; the tobacco taste stays as a soft base beneath the flavoring. It's light in nicotine and soft in body. Suited to those who enjoy fruity aromatics and want a low-strength blend to smoke all day; slow smoking and pre-airing are needed to avoid tongue bite.
mac-baren-7-seas-red-blend.o: Leaves a sweet room note toward ripe red fruit.

days-work-days-work.z: This is a burley-based blend of American origin; not enough sourcing could be reached to verify its composition and character.

torben-dansk-blue-note.z: The Torben Dansk blend called Blue Note is noted in records as an aromatic; no reliable source documenting its composition and character has been found.

e-a-carey-mediterranean-blend.z: Mediterranean is one of the blends sold under its own name by E. A. Carey, a Chicago-based mail-order house. Per the maker's description, it is a golden-colored mixture of air-cured burley and Virginia leaves, presented ribbon cut. Its flavoring runs on soft vanilla. With a low nicotine load and a moderate flavor body, the blend falls into the light aromatic class, suited to all-day smoking. It draws the interest of newcomers to aromatics or those seeking a low-bite tobacco. It is no longer on Carey's current blend list; per records, it has been discontinued.
e-a-carey-mediterranean-blend.o: Leaves a soft vanilla and lightly sweet tobacco scent.

century-picaroon-1690-plug.z: Picaroon 1690 is the Latakia-forward pressed-plug record in the Century line. Per the seller's description, latakia, Turkish orientals, virginia, cavendish and perique from Louisiana's St. James district are brought together; the leaf is rested for thirty days in Kentucky bourbon barrels. The name comes from the Spanish word "picaroon," referring to seventeenth-century pirates. The plug form lets the tobacco undergo additional fermentation during pressing; the result is a full-bodied, smoky and spicy smoke. Perique brings dark fruit and pepper notes, the orientals a dry, herbal sharpness, and the barrel rest a lightly sweet background. Given its heavy nicotine and flavor load, this is a record aimed at experienced smokers.
century-picaroon-1690-plug.o: Leaves smoke, leather and spice together with a light whiskey-barrel aroma.

iwan-ries-british-rich.z: British Rich is an unflavored Latakia mixture among Iwan Ries & Co.'s English-style house blends. The ribbon-cut tobacco is made up of Virginia, Latakia, and Oriental leaves; the Virginia's natural sugar meets smoky Latakia, while the Oriental leaves trace a spicy, resinous edge. On the maker's scale it counts as medium strength. It's a mixture meant for smokers looking for a profile matching the classic definition of an English blend, staying away from flavored tobaccos. Because of its unflavored composition, the taste comes from the leaves' own character. The blend is produced in Denmark.
iwan-ries-british-rich.o: Leaves the room with a mix of resinous Oriental and smoky aroma.

cup-o-joes-high-peaks-white.z: An aromatic blend in Cup O' Joes' bulk High Peaks line; no adequate source describing its composition and character was found.

clan-shaw-new-hampshire.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend New Hampshire.

greenfield-winther-champagne-blend.z: One of the mid-twentieth-century blends from San Francisco-based Greenfield & Winther; there is no independent sourcing describing its composition.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-scotch-cake.z: Kendal Scotch Cake is one of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s pressed cake products and is usually offered broken up into large pieces. Its weight comes mainly from flame-cured Virginia; some sun-cured leaf is added to cool and sweeten the smoke. No essence or heavy sweetening is used. The coarsely broken cake burns slowly and keeps the bowl cool; nicotine is low and the flavor structure mild and even. This makes it suitable for those new to the pipe, as well as for use as a blending base to soften blends considered heavier.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-scotch-cake.o: Leaves an aroma of warm bread and dry hay.

comptons-of-galashiels-commonweal-mixtur.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Compton's of Galashiels blend Commonweal Mixture.

caminetto-umbria.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named Umbria under the Caminetto brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-10-downing-street.z: 10 Downing Street is among the unflavored blends of Wilke Pipe Tobacco, a New York house tracing its roots to 1872. Structurally it's Burley-based; Virginia flake is added on top, and it's finished with Latakia and Perique. This construction sets the blend apart from classic English mixtures: Latakia smoke and Perique spice sit atop Burley's nutty, dry body instead of the Virginia usually found in English mixtures. When Burley's fullness meets Perique's plummy spice, a medium-to-high body results; Virginia flake provides a measured sweetness and sugar balance. Since there's no casing, the flavor is entirely leaf-derived. It suits smokers accustomed to Latakia mixtures who also want Burley's dry, full character; it's not for those seeking a light everyday tobacco.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-10-downing-street.o: Leaves a smoky scent reminiscent of burnt wood and dry-leaf smoke.

caminetto-lombardo.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named Lombardo under the Caminetto brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

lane-limited-black-cordial.z: Black Cordial is one of the aromatic blends registered under Lane Limited; since it doesn't appear in the manufacturer's or retailers' current listings, not enough sources could be found to describe its content and character.

peter-stokkebye-no-313-oriental.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name No. 313 Oriental in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

panama-jack-pina-colada.z: Pina Colada is one of the aromatic blends in Panama Jack's tropically themed pipe tobacco line. Referencing the cocktail it's named for, it carries a pineapple, coconut, and rum-direction flavoring; as is common across the line, the base rests on the trio of mild burley, bright Virginia, and black cavendish. It is ribbon cut and sold in fifty-gram tins. It's among the most pronouncedly flavored blends in the line; the smoke is cool, sweet, and creamy, with nicotine load staying low. It's aimed at pipe smokers who lean toward aromatic tobacco and want the flavoring, rather than the leaf character, to lead the smoke.
panama-jack-pina-colada.o: Leaves a scent of coconut cream and pineapple.

wellauer-co-special.z: Special is one of the lightest blends in Swiss maker Wellauer's product line. Its foundation is selected black cavendish, joined by broadly cut Virginia. It's stated to be kept low in nicotine, positioning it as a calm starting point for frequent daytime smoking or for newcomers to the pipe. Cavendish gives a soft, creamy smoke texture while the broad-cut Virginia adds a natural, open sweetness and freshness. The result is not flat but a rounded, balanced smoke; the casing level is measured enough not to create a pronounced candy-like effect. The cut is a loose mixture and easy to pack. It's an everyday option for smokers avoiding heavy Latakia or high-nicotine blends.
wellauer-co-special.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, creamy, tobacco-forward scent.

ash-ember-burley-bear.z: No adequate independent source could be found for Burley Bear, a house blend from the Ash & Ember shop.
ash-ember-burley-bear.o: No reliable information on the room note could be found.

mcclelland-no-900-refined-tennessee-ribb.z: A blend in McClelland's bulk series, discontinued when the firm closed in 2018; no sufficient source documenting its contents and character could be found.

dan-tobacco-ropers-roundels.z: A pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source on the blend's composition or character was found, so no further detail is given.

dan-tobacco-the-jolly-joker.z: The Jolly Joker is a blend in Dan Tobacco's sweet aromatic line. Black cavendish forms the body, with Virginia and burley added. The topping applied on top is described in the direction of marzipan, nuts and vanilla. Burley provides an earthy base holding the topping, black cavendish gives softness and natural sweetness, and Virginia adds coolness. It's light to medium in nicotine. It suits smokers seeking sweet, confectionery-evoking aromatics. Distributed in 100-gram tins.
dan-tobacco-the-jolly-joker.o: Leaves a sweet trace evoking marzipan and vanilla cake.

paul-bugge-pfeifentabak-virginia-honey-d.z: Virginia Honey-Dew Flake is a Virginia flake in the house-blend line carrying the name of Paul Bugge, a German pipe and tobacco retailer. As has long been the tradition in Germany, shop brands have their blends prepared by contract manufacturers; this blend, too, is sold under the shop's own label. The "honey-dew" in the name points to a light honey casing given to the leaf. On the palate, tart, lemony, naturally sugared Virginia leaf leads; the honey casing layers a thin sweetness and a faint licorice suggestion over it, though not intensely enough to mask the leaf's own taste. Offered as a pressed, sliced flake, it needs rubbing out before packing and keeps its character when smoked slowly. Though flavored, it isn't fully aromatic; it occupies a middle ground for smokers interested in Virginia blends who find fully unflavored tobacco too dry.
paul-bugge-pfeifentabak-virginia-honey-d.o: Leaves a scent recalling honey and dry grass, close to warm bread crust.

g-l-pease-fillmore.z: Fillmore is a G. L. Pease blend prepared using the Scottish tradition's sliced-and-broken flake method. Ripe red Virginia leaves are combined with Louisiana perique, pressed, sliced, and lightly rubbed out before boxing. Perique adds a spicy edge reminiscent of plum, fig, and pepper to the Virginia sweetness. Part of the Fog City Selection line, the blend burns slowly and smokes cool. It suits smokers seeking the classic Virginia-perique structure in flake form.
g-l-pease-fillmore.o: Leaves a dried-fruit and bread-like sweetness with a fine peppery aroma.

barclay-rex-virginia-flake.z: Referred to as Barclay Rex's unflavored Virginia flake; no adequate source on its pressing and leaf selection could be found.
barclay-rex-virginia-flake.o: According to records it leaves a room note reminiscent of dry hay and bread crust.

up-down-queen-mary.z: One of the aromatic house blends from the Up Down Tobacco shop in Chicago; no verifiable source on its composition and flavoring has been found.

cult-anonymous.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the Cult brand as Anonymous; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-buckland-curlies.z: Buckland Curlies is part of the bulk blend line of Exeter-based McGahey The Tobacconist. According to the seller's description it consists of twisted Virginia, Cavendish, and Perique leaves and is sold as coin-shaped pieces obtained by slicing tobacco wound into a rope. This cut preserves the leaf's own sugar for a long time and produces a structure meant to be deliberately smoked slowly. The perique share layers a spice reminiscent of plum and pepper over the virginia sweetness; the body is medium. Suitable for smokers accustomed to rubbing the coins apart between their fingers or loading them whole into the bowl, who are looking for an unflavored Virginia-Perique character. Records indicate McGahey's bulk blends are named after place names in the Dartmoor region, and the shop's history goes back to the 1880s.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-buckland-curlies.o: Leaves a dry-hay, bread-crust aroma with a lightly peppery spice.

cornell-diehl-stanhope.z: Stanhope is one of the Atlas blends Cornell & Diehl took over. It's a ribbon-cut English mixture built from a composition of Burley, Perique, Oriental, and Latakia; the maker's description notes it's full in flavor but light in nicotine. The Burley base gives the blend a dry, nutty body, while Perique adds spice and Latakia together with Oriental take on a smoky, tangy layer. On the maker's scale, strength is low, flavor high, and room note medium. Suited to smokers wanting intense flavor without high nicotine, drawn to Burley-focused English mixtures.
cornell-diehl-stanhope.o: Leaves a scent where smoky Latakia mingles with dry spice and nutty tones.

samuel-gawith-celtic-talisman.z: Celtic Talisman is an aromatic prepared by combining Virginia and burley leaves with black cavendish and flavoring with kirsch, a cherry liqueur, and vanilla. It carries a fruity, sweet top aroma; black cavendish adds mildness and sugar direction to the blend while burley balances the burn. Suited to smokers seeking a light-bodied, distinctly flavored tobacco and to those newly getting acquainted with aromatic blends.
samuel-gawith-celtic-talisman.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity scent evoking cherry liqueur and vanilla.

milan-tobacconists-appalachian-gold.z: Appalachian Gold is one of the house blends Roanoke, Virginia-based Milan Tobacconists prepares at its own counter. It is built by combining soft, lightly sweet black cavendish with burley and virginia leaves; according to the maker's description it gives vanilla, toasted marshmallow, and a light sweet, nutty taste at the finish. The ribbon cut allows for an easy-lighting, evenly burning pack. The nicotine load is measured, and the flavor stays in the medium band where the casing stands out. Suitable for smokers looking for a soft aromatic they can smoke at any hour, who want cavendish sweetness balanced by burley's dry body. Milan has been a tobacconist shop in business since 1912, and these blends are sold under the shop's own name.
milan-tobacconists-appalachian-gold.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly nutty aroma in the direction of vanilla and toasted marshmallow.

tabac-manil-coupe-fine.z: Coupe Fine, a pipe tobacco from Tabac Manil; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

amphora-original-blend.z: Amphora Original Blend is a Burley-heavy blend also containing Cavendish, Kentucky, Oriental/Turkish tobacco, and Virginia. Even after passing into Mac Baren's hands, it continues to be sold as a ribbon cut in 50-gram pouches. The moisture of the tobacco straight from the pack is pack-ready. Its flavoring shows itself as a light chocolate taste coming from deep within; it's slightly sweeter than its namesake, Full Aroma. The Turkish tobacco listed in the contents reportedly stays well in the background, with Burley dominant. It doesn't give burning trouble, leaves gray ash, and can be smoked without going out; on the other hand it noticeably heats the pipe and tends toward bitterness late in the smoke. It suits smokers looking for an everyday blend where tobacco flavor dominates and flavoring stays low.
amphora-original-blend.o: Leaves a lightly chocolatey, sweetish tobacco room note.

motzek-virginia-cake.z: Virginia Cake is the straight virginia blend from the Kiel-based TAK workshop, presented in pressed block (cake) form. Mature virginia leaves' notes of dry hay, light citrus, and natural sugar lead; no flavoring is added to the blend, yet the leaf's own sweetness makes it seem soft. The block tobacco is cut with a knife into thin strips, chopped into cubes, and loaded with its top layer lightly rubbed.
motzek-virginia-cake.o: Leaves a plain tobacco aroma carrying dry hay and a fine citrus sweetness.

mac-baren-vanilla-roll-cake-classic-roll.z: Vanilla Roll Cake is a product in which Mac Baren combines the rope-cut tradition with an aromatic approach. The outer wrap consists of whole Virginia leaves; inside are Virginia and whole-leaf Burley. After the spun rope rests, it's cut into coins. A measured Madagascar-vanilla topping is applied to support the leaves' natural sweetness. The flavoring is milder and less spiced than the maker's flake-form vanilla products; on the other hand, the tobacco body is more pronounced. The coins burn slowly and need to be rubbed out before packing. The taste is built between Virginia's bready sweetness and Burley's nutty base, with vanilla adding a creamy layer on top. Suited to smokers seeking a balance between aromatic and natural leaf taste.
mac-baren-vanilla-roll-cake-classic-roll.o: Leaves a creamy vanilla and sweet dry-hay aroma.

park-lane-tobacconist-park-lane-no-12.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Park-Lane No. 12, one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-blackthorn-shill.z: Blackthorn Shillelagh, named after the traditional Irish walking stick, is a limited-production aromatic Sutliff released for St. Patrick's Day in early 2024. The ribbon-cut blend brings together tart Virginia, nutty burley, and sweet black cavendish, topped with an Irish whiskey flavoring. On the palate, fruity sweetness, oak, barley, and light tartness stand out; vanilla and floral notes stay in the background. Nicotine strength is light-to-medium, leaning slightly toward medium. With its cool, even burn and low need for relighting, it suits long smoking sessions. Sold in eight-ounce tins.
sutliff-tobacco-company-blackthorn-shill.o: A sweet trace where vanilla and nuts mix into Irish whiskey, oak, and barley scent.

ken-byron-ventures-moriarty-2023.z: Moriarty 2023 is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

cornell-diehl-black-dawg.z: Black Dawg was a mixture built by adding Syrian Latakia and perique to an unsweetened black cavendish base. Cavendish's round sweetness forms the body, Latakia brings a smoky, resinous layer, and perique leaves a light spice and plum direction in the background. As no sugar is added, the sweetness comes from the leaf's own processing. The blend went out of production in its original form once the supply of Syrian Latakia was cut off; according to available records, Cornell & Diehl rebuilt the same structure with Cyprus Latakia and continued it under a different name. It is a medium-strength smoke, not the kind whose smoke fills the mouth. It falls within the interest of those seeking the Latakia-and-cavendish pairing on a soft foundation.
cornell-diehl-black-dawg.o: Smoke and resinous wood aroma are noticeable over a sweetish base.

east-india-trading-co-royal-challenge.z: Royal Challenge is an aromatic blend in the East India Trading Co. line built on a spicy rum character. Black cavendish, steamed after fire-curing, is added alongside American burley and Virginia; the mixture is aged in rum and given cinnamon and nutmeg notes. It smokes cool, carrying a pronounced spice layer alongside the sweetness. Its nicotine is light to medium. It suits smokers looking beyond the classic vanilla aromatics for a spicy, rum-forward profile, and those wanting a cool-burning tobacco for long smokes over conversation.
east-india-trading-co-royal-challenge.o: Leaves a scent of spiced rum, cinnamon and nutmeg; a sweet, warm trace settles into the room.

planta-yin-yang.z: Yin Yang is an English-style blend from Planta combining Syrian Latakia, black Cavendish, and light Virginia tips with Oriental tobaccos. The blend's distinguishing feature is a light flavoring with Calvados, the Normandy apple brandy; this note is carried by the black Cavendish and leaves an apple-like sweetness over the smoky base. Here Syrian Latakia builds a woody, measured smoky, lightly spicy frame; the Orientals give a tart sharpness, while Virginia supplies a sugary ground in the background. It suits those interested in Latakia blends who want a lightly flavored take rather than a fully unflavored English mixture. Nicotine is medium.
planta-yin-yang.o: A sweetish aroma evoking apple brandy layers over smoky Latakia smoke.

milan-tobacconists-star-city-delight.z: Star City Delight is a vanilla-forward, peach-toned aromatic built on virginia tobaccos and black cavendish. It takes its name from Roanoke's nickname, 'Star City.' With its low nicotine load and soft smoke, it stands as a light everyday aromatic. Suitable for those who enjoy fruity flavorings and want a smoke where the body doesn't stand out.
milan-tobacconists-star-city-delight.o: Leaves a fruity aroma reminiscent of vanilla and peach.

ken-byron-ventures-holly-jolly-goblin.z: A holiday-themed limited release in the Goblin series; no independent source could be found to document its contents.
ken-byron-ventures-holly-jolly-goblin.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

smokers-haven-65th-anniversary-blend.z: A limited-run mixture Smokers' Haven prepared for the 65th anniversary of its 1940 founding; per records it's assessed in the unflavored Virginia line, but no independent source confirming this could be found.

peter-stokkebye-cinnamon-no-46.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Cinnamon (No.46) could be found.

mclintock-wild-cherry.z: Wild Cherry is one of the cherry-flavored aromatics in Kohlhase & Kopp's McLintock line. According to the seller's description, a ripe wild-cherry flavoring is added to a base of processed black Cavendish, oriental and Turkish leaf, and Virginia. The oriental share gives a lightly smoky, dry background rarely seen in aromatic blends. Body is light to medium; what stands out is the intensity of the cherry flavoring. Aimed at smokers who enjoy fruity aromatics but want a construction that isn't purely Cavendish sweetness. It has a different flavoring construction from the Black Cherry blend in the same line and is sold under the name "Wild C." in some markets.
mclintock-wild-cherry.o: Leaves an aroma of ripe cherry and candied fruit.

iwan-ries-irc-slices.z: IRC Slices is a flake-cut blend made up of Virginia and Perique leaves, produced in Denmark under the Iwan Ries name. The Virginia base gives the blend a hay-and-baked-dough sweetness, while the Perique adds a plummy, peppery spice layer, as expected in classic Virginia-Perique mixtures. The maker classifies the blend as medium-bodied, and its balanced structure is considered suitable for smoking throughout the day. The slices need to be rubbed out or folded before filling; it's also a suitable starting point for smokers new to unflavored Virginia blends.
iwan-ries-irc-slices.o: A plummy spice trace accompanies the aroma of dry hay and baked bread.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-no-88-virginia-f.z: Not enough independent sources could be reached to fill out the record for Kohlhase, Kopp und Co. KG's blend called No. 88: Virginia Flake.

john-middleton-inc-royal-comfort.z: One of the blends from John Middleton, a company founded in Philadelphia in 1856 that has made pipe tobacco since the 1950s; the entry is left incomplete because not enough sources could be found to document the blend's contents and character.
john-middleton-inc-royal-comfort.o: No source could be found on the room note.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-riverboat.z: No reliable source has been found for The Country Squire Tobacconist pipe blend called Riverboat Queen.

peter-stokkebye-irresistable-chocolate.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Irresistable Chocolate in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-hines-mixt.z: Match Hines Mixture T426 is a mild American aromatic in which Virginia and burley leaf are combined with black cavendish. Like the other entries in Sutliff's "Match" line, it was prepared to reinterpret a market blend that had gone out of production or become hard to find; most of the line was created by Sutliff blender Carl McAllister. On the smoke, vanilla from the black cavendish leads; Virginia's sweetness and burley's nutty tone occasionally appear beneath this casing. Nicotine is low and the taste structure is plain and straightforward. It suits smokers looking for a lightly flavored classic aromatic they can smoke all day.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-hines-mixt.o: Leaves a sweet, vanilla-forward scent with a light nutty note behind it.

peretti-cherry-cavendish.z: Cherry Cavendish is Peretti's classic cherry-flavored Cavendish blend. Per the maker's recipe, it is arranged for those seeking a sweet cherry taste and is flavored to leave a pronounced scent. Cherry essence is worked into black Cavendish's sugary, soft body; nicotine is low and the taste is built directly through the flavoring. It is designed for smokers accustomed to fruit aromatics and newcomers to the pipe, an easy-to-smoke blend during the day.

old-virginia-tobacco-co-shiloh.z: Shiloh is one of the aromatic labeled blends from Old Virginia Tobacco Co.; no published description of its composition could be found.

craven-craven-ready-rubbed.z: This is the ready-rubbed version of the Craven brand; one retailer's marketing states it's built from Virginia, Latakia, and Oriental tobaccos, but no second independent source confirming its composition was found.

mac-baren-capstan-original-navy-cut-read.z: The ready-rubbed version of Capstan Original is prepared by pressing and slicing the mature Virginia cake, then rubbing it at the factory; it comes out of the tin in a texture between broken flake and ribbon, so it packs more easily than the flake version. On opening, a distinct tangy casing scent can be noticed, which lessens with airing. Its strength is at a medium level, flavor intensity is medium, and its filling power in terms of nicotine is limited. A presentation for those wanting to smoke Virginia without the bother of separating flakes.
mac-baren-capstan-original-navy-cut-read.o: Leaves a trace where tangy fruit and dry tobacco scents mix.

robert-mcconnell-ripe-honeydew.z: Ripe Honeydew is made by applying a light honey casing over a plain Virginia blend, the aim being to support the leaf's own natural sugar. The cut is described as broken flake, though it is reported to come out of the tin closer to a ribbon or fine-cut texture. The tin note carries lemongrass and dry-hay associations. The honey addition is not overpowering; the blend reads more as a lightly sweetened Virginia than a true aromatic. It is reported to want a loose pack and occasional relighting. It suits smokers who don't want heavy aromatic intensity but do want a subtle sweetness added to a straight Virginia.
robert-mcconnell-ripe-honeydew.o: Leaves a lightly honeyed aroma carrying dry-hay and lemongrass tones.

ken-byron-ventures-fireside-chat.z: Fireside Chat is a blend that looks back to the aromatics of the old American drugstore-counter tradition. A Burley-forward body is softened with Virginia and black Cavendish; the cut is ribbon. Rather than the wet, sharp casing of heavy modern aromatics, its sweetness is built on a more measured level. Nicotine runs light to medium, giving it a structure well suited to all-day smoking. Aimed at smokers seeking the classic American aromatic style in an easy-lighting texture that doesn't bite the tongue. Since the brand works in small batches, availability is seasonal.
ken-byron-ventures-fireside-chat.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly toasted, nutty aroma.

j-f-germain-son-century.z: Century is a limited-run English mixture from J. F. Germain & Son. It's made up of Cyprus Latakia, spicy Oriental leaves, and flue-cured Virginia that retains its natural sweetness. Latakia builds a smoky, leathery backbone, while the Oriental gives a sharp spiciness and the Virginia a bready sweetness in the background. Because it was a limited production, it has been withdrawn from the market, and today only old tins circulate hand to hand. It suits smokers accustomed to traditional Latakia mixtures, looking for an unflavored, smoky profile. The Germain family has produced tobacco on the island of Jersey since 1820, and releases such periodic blends under its own name.
j-f-germain-son-century.o: Leaves an aroma of wood smoke, tar, and spicy leather.

tinder-box-20-year-matured-virginia.z: Tinder Box is an American chain of pipe and tobacco shops that has sold blends under its own name since 1928. 20 Year Matured Virginia was an unflavored Virginia blend in the chain's old catalog; presented in a dark-colored cut rubbed almost to shag fineness, it was described as made from long-aged leaf. Records indicate it left the catalog in the late 1970s and today can only be found in old stock. It was aimed at smokers seeking aged Virginia's dark, tangy-sweet line; being unflavored, the taste came entirely from the leaf itself.
tinder-box-20-year-matured-virginia.o: Leaves a tangy-sweet aroma reminiscent of dark bread and dried fruit.

mac-baren-amphora-golden.z: Amphora is a pipe tobacco brand with roots in the Netherlands, now produced under Danish Mac Baren. The Golden Blend member of the Amphora line is a pre-rubbed (ready rubbed) blend where matured burley leaves are forward, with a small amount of golden Virginia added. Casing is kept very limited; the taste largely comes from the natural tobacco. Over a nutty, grainy body there's a fine citrus note. It burns clean and dry, with the character staying fairly consistent from the start to the end of the bowl; it lights easily. A blend suited to smokers seeking a burley-centered, unpretentious tobacco to smoke all day.
mac-baren-amphora-golden.o: Leaves a room note of dry hazelnut and roasted grain.

pfeifen-huber-danish-mixture.z: Danish Mixture is one of the house blends sold under its own name by Pfeifen Huber, a house operating in Munich since 1863. A loose-cut mixture, the tobacco builds broken Virginia and bright Virginia leaf on a base of black Cavendish; on the flavoring side there is a measured touch of whiskey, a faint plum sweetness, and a thin veil of vanilla. As the name suggests, it stays true to the classic Danish approach to aromatics. The blend is light in nicotine and mildly sweet; because flavoring intensity is kept low, the tobacco's own taste isn't masked and the smoke stays dry. Cavendish gives the body depth and sweetness while Virginia lightens the blend. It suits smokers who want to avoid heavy aromatics but aren't after a fully natural tobacco either, as well as those seeking a light mixture for long, all-day sessions.
pfeifen-huber-danish-mixture.o: Leaves a light plum sweetness with whiskey and vanilla behind it.

lane-limited-vip.z: Referred to as an aromatic blend carrying the Lane Limited name; not enough sources could be found to confirm its content and character.

nassau-street-bachelors-ribbon.z: From its name and the limited information available, it appears to be a ribbon-cut Virginia-Burley blend; no independent source documenting the brand and blend could be found.

riegels-balkan-sobranie-black.z: Balkan Sobranie Black, registered under the Riegel's name, is referred to as a tobacconist's adaptation of the classic Balkan Sobranie mixture; no verifiable source could be found on its maker, composition, or character.
riegels-balkan-sobranie-black.o: No reliable information could be found on the room note.

samuel-gawith-brown-rope-no-4-rum.z: Brown Rope No. 4 Rum is the rum-cased version of Samuel Gawith's thick rope series. Virginia and burley leaf are twisted into rope and matured; a rum-based casing is applied during production. The product is sold in wheel form; the smoker cuts and crumbles a slice. The rum casing leaves a sweet background but does not cover the tobacco's dark, earthy taste; nicotine load is high. It requires slow smoking and thorough drying. Suited to smokers seeking the naval-tradition rope cut together with rummy sweetness.
samuel-gawith-brown-rope-no-4-rum.o: Leaves a scent of rum and brown sugar over dark tobacco.

mcclelland-smyrna-no-1-grand-orientals.z: Smyrna No.1 is one of the entries in which McClelland's Grand Orientals series spotlights a single region's Oriental tobacco. As the name suggests, the blend's backbone is İzmir-region tobacco, with Virginia in a supporting role. The cut is ribbon; on opening the tin, the brand's usual tangy aroma is noticeable, and a whole leaf is laid over the blend as presentation. Since the tin's moisture content is high, airing it for a while settles the flavor. It lights very easily; the first tastes are Virginia sweetness, followed by the familiar Turkish-tobacco character. Smoked quickly it can run hot and turn bitter, so it calls for a slow smoke. A light-to-medium-strength, unflavored blend for those curious about Oriental tobacco taste. The maker closed in 2018, so the product is no longer produced.
mcclelland-smyrna-no-1-grand-orientals.o: A faintly tangy sweetness mixes into the dry Oriental tobacco's hay and spice aroma.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-princeton.z: Listed as an American-type Orlik blend based on dark Virginia, light burley, and black cavendish; not enough independent source material confirming its composition could be found.

american-tobacco-co-weymans-cutty-pipe.z: Cutty Pipe is a historic American pipe tobacco originally released by the Pittsburgh-based Weyman & Bros., passing to the American Tobacco Company in 1905. Promotional texts of the era emphasize that the blend was prepared from Kentucky Burley leaf using a new processing method. It was sold in large tins and pouch packaging, and per records was discontinued around the 1980s. Its single-leaf-type structure places the blend at the plain end of the American Burley tradition: a nutty, dry, earthy taste is delivered without pronounced sweetness or added flavoring. Its coarse, granular cut packs loosely into the bowl and burns slowly; nicotine load is medium. It's considered a historical example for those curious about the everyday, unflavored Burley tobacco of the past; today it can only be traced through collector's tins.
american-tobacco-co-weymans-cutty-pipe.o: Leaves a room note of dry walnut meat and roasted grain.

holland-house-holland-house-regular.z: Holland House Regular is the brand's original blend: it's built from a combination of sweet Virginia, full-bodied Burley, and golden-colored Cavendish leaves. As a slow-burning, measuredly flavored aromatic, it was developed in the Netherlands and has been maintained along the same line for a long time. In the smoke, caramel and mild tobacco taste come forward; the sweetness stays measured enough not to override the smoke. With its light-to-medium nicotine range and low tendency for tongue bite, it suits those looking for a mild aromatic for everyday smoking and those new to the pipe.
