gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-black-aromatic.z: Sliced Black Aromatic is the factory-sliced, coin-shaped presentation of the brand's dark rope tobacco; the product is also known as Sliced Black Twist. The base leaf is stoved dark Virginia and fire-cured leaf, topped with a rum flavoring. Being pre-sliced, it can be packed directly after a short airing. Nicotine and flavor intensity are high; it calls for slow smoking. Suited to smokers wanting the body of rope tobaccos without the hassle of cutting.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-black-aromatic.o: Leaves a heavy tobacco aroma leaning toward dark sugar and rum.

sutliff-tobacco-company-frosty-mint-2008.z: Frosty Mint 2008 is one of the bulk blends from the Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-holiday-blend-20.z: Holiday Blend 2007 is part of Hermit Tobacco Works Co.'s annual holiday series; there is not enough sourcing to document the blend's composition.

peretti-boylston-cavendish-blends.z: Boylston is a blend in L.J. Peretti's Cavendish-based aromatic line. Per the maker's recipe, amaretto's nutty, almond-like sweetness is worked into a soft, mellow Cavendish body. It takes its name from Boylston Street in Boston, where the firm was founded. Nicotine strength is kept low, with the taste side left to the flavoring; the aim is a cool burn that doesn't bite the tongue. It suits smokers seeking a light aromatic for all-day smoking or those starting the pipe from the aromatic side. The ribbon cut makes packing easy.
peretti-boylston-cavendish-blends.o: Leaves a roasted almond and sugared liqueur aroma.

cornell-diehl-carolina-red-flake.z: Carolina Red Flake is an unflavored Virginia flake Cornell & Diehl prepared as a tribute to the old American tobacco belt. The blend is built from heirloom red Virginia varieties of the Old Belt region and is reformulated each year with that season's leaf; according to available records, the sugar levels of the batches used are selected individually. The pressed and sliced leaves show a range of colors from light orange to dark brown. The flavor profile sits between grassy dryness and natural sweetness with a tangy sharpness; tones reminiscent of dried fruit and citrus are described. It suits smokers accustomed to unflavored Virginia flake, comfortable rubbing out the slices themselves, and intending to cellar the tobacco.
cornell-diehl-carolina-red-flake.o: Leaves an aroma in the room reminiscent of dry grass and baked-bread sweetness.

gawith-hoggarth-co-red.z: Red is the brand's air-cured blend, also offered in a 50-gram tin; it rests on the same composition as the product known as Gawith Red. It contains Burley, Kentucky, Oriental, and Virginia, topped with a very light floral essence. A nutty, bready, earthy base stands out on the flavor palette; sweetness is kept low. Records indicate it was developed as a replacement for the air-cured tin blends once common in England. Suited to smokers seeking an everyday, lightly sauced blend.
gawith-hoggarth-co-red.o: A light floral note mingles with a nutty tobacco aroma.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-1994.z: Christmas Cheer 1994 is the third tin in McClelland's annual Virginia series. Per its label, it's prepared from select mature, mottled lemon-orange-colored Carolina leaves of the 1991 Middle Belt harvest. Unflavored flue-cured Virginia is pressed and presented as broken flake. As expected of light-colored Virginias, sweetness and citrusy tang lead; it gives a brighter profile than years with dark red harvests. No flavoring is used, and nicotine is medium. Since the series is explicitly made for cellaring, the leaf's sugars are expected to mature with age; suited to smokers used to unflavored Virginia and flake smoking.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-1994.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of sweet hay and citrus peel.

pfeifen-schilde-spun-flake-no-32.z: No sufficient sources confirming the content and character of Spun Flake No. 32, recorded as a house blend of the German tobacconist Pfeifen Schilde, could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-aged-maduro-cave.z: Aged Maduro Cavendish is a bulk Sutliff mixture made from cavendish leaf blackened through slow steaming. Flavoring is applied with a light hand; vanilla and chocolate notes are kept measured enough not to overpower the leaf's own sweetness. It's a soft, non-biting, easy-smoking tobacco. Suited to smokers who enjoy black cavendish character but want to avoid heavy flavoring.
sutliff-tobacco-company-aged-maduro-cave.o: Leaves a warm scent of vanilla and cocoa.

samuel-gawith-cannon-plug.z: Cannon Plug is a plug produced by pressing and aging Virginia leaves; a traditional casing called honeydew is applied on top. According to records it is among the brand's oldest still-produced blends. Thin slices are cut from the tightly pressed plug and rubbed for packing. When the plug is opened, the casing scent comes forward with citrus and woody echoes, with the Virginia leaf's own scent beneath. The smoke is cool and sweet; the casing lingers long on the palate. Suited to those who enjoy working with a pressed presentation and seek a notably cased but medium-bodied tobacco.
samuel-gawith-cannon-plug.o: Leaves a pronounced casing scent carrying citrus and woody sweetness.

austria-tabak-gmbh-landtabak.z: Recorded under the name Austria Tabak GmbH, Landtabak is a Burley-forward blend produced in Austria since 1949, and is the same product as the Landtabak described in the previous entry, listed under a different manufacturer credit. It contains Burley, golden Virginia, Paraguayan, and Oriental leaf; the brand is blended today within the Japan Tobacco International group. It's a fine-ribbon cut, coming out of the pack quite dry, though the leaf retains its internal moisture. The pack scent carries Paraguayan tobacco's strong scent first, followed by a measured note of sugar, cocoa, spice, and fruit after airing. Strength is medium, flavor is intense. It suits smokers looking for a full-bodied Burley blend where flavoring stays in the background.
austria-tabak-gmbh-landtabak.o: Leaves a full-bodied tobacco room note beneath a bakery-like scent of sugar, cocoa, and spice.

mcclelland-virginia-no-25-matured-virgin.z: Virginia No. 25 is one of McClelland's straight Virginia entries in the Matured Virginias series. It comes as a fine ribbon cut rather than a tin flake, with fairly high moisture, and carries the brand's familiar tangy aroma. The fine cut dries quickly when aired out, packs easily, and lights readily. On the first few puffs the fine cut gives a cigarette-like impression; past the first third of the bowl, the sweet tobacco taste typical of matured Virginia settles in. Letting it go out after the first light and resting it a bit makes the flavor more settled on the relight. Full-bodied but light on nicotine, it suits those looking for an unflavored, mellow Virginia. Production ended in 2018.
mcclelland-virginia-no-25-matured-virgin.o: Leaves a sweet, mature tobacco aroma.

pauls-pipe-shop-blend-2120.z: Blend 2120 is recorded as a burley-forward mixture blended at Paul's Pipe Shop's store in Flint; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found.
pauls-pipe-shop-blend-2120.o: No source could be found to describe the room note.

pipesworld-old-spook-english.z: Old Spook English appears among the English-type blends of the seller known as PipesWorld; no source could be found verifying its composition or maker.

g-l-pease-tribute.z: Tribute is a limited-production blend G. L. Pease prepared following the September 11, 2001 attacks. Its composition includes red and lemon Virginias, stoved red Virginia, perique, and untopped roasted black cavendish; all selected from American leaf. Released in sealed two-ounce tins, records indicate proceeds from the tobacco's sale were donated to the "Families of Freedom Scholarship Fund." It was never put into regular production; today it is known only through old tins.
g-l-pease-tribute.o: Leaves a sweet, dry-grass aroma with a light bread-like, dark-sugar note.

cornell-diehl-plum-duff.z: No composition description published by the maker or retailers could be found for this Cornell & Diehl blend named Plum Duff.

van-erkoms-fox.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of Van Erkoms' blend called Fox has been found.
van-erkoms-fox.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

admirals-choice-cherry-cavendish.z: Cherry Cavendish is the cherry-flavored blend of the Admiral's Choice line. Mellow black Cavendish is added alongside Burley and Virginia leaf; a pronounced cherry coating is applied over these. The line is produced by the Dream Castle Tobacco Company under Sutliff. It offers a light-to-medium fullness; the cherry note reads clearly in both scent and taste. It's built for those looking for a fruited, sweet, direct aromatic and smokers who prefer tobaccos with a pronounced scent.
admirals-choice-cherry-cavendish.o: A pronounced, bright cherry note fills the room.

sutliff-tobacco-company-h-gray-rcaf.z: H. Gray RCAF, mentioned among Sutliff's custom special-order productions, lacks independent sources documenting its composition and character.
sutliff-tobacco-company-h-gray-rcaf.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

robert-lewis-123-mixture.z: 123 Mixture is a ribbon-cut blend from Robert Lewis, classified as cigar-leaf based. It contains Havana-origin cigar leaf alongside Cyprus Latakia, Turkish-Oriental tobaccos, Virginia, and black Cavendish. No flavoring is applied. Robert Lewis is a London-based tobacconist founded in 1787. The cigar leaf's share stays limited in the smoke; Latakia, Oriental, and Virginia proportions balance one another, with black Cavendish giving a light sweetness underneath. Flavor starts at a medium level and intensifies toward the end of the bowl, leaving a full finish. It burns hot, so it calls for slow smoking. It suits smokers accustomed to English blends who are curious about what cigar leaf adds.
robert-lewis-123-mixture.o: Leaves a heavy soot and burnt-leaf aroma, carrying a sharp trace reminiscent of cigar ash.

baraccini-clasico.z: Clasico is an unflavored English mixture blended at Scandinavian Tobacco Group under the Italian pipe brand Baraccini. Turkish-Oriental leaf and a measured amount of Latakia are added to a Virginia base. Since the Latakia share is deliberately kept low, the smoky note doesn't coat the palate, leaving the Oriental's spicy-tangy tone and Virginia's sweetness up front. Body is light-to-medium and not tiring on nicotine. It suits smokers transitioning into English mixtures or those who find heavy Latakia blends too much; its ribbon cut makes packing easy, and the burn runs cool.
baraccini-clasico.o: Leaves a thin woodsmoke note reminiscent of a campfire, along with dry hay.

sutliff-tobacco-company-lord-fairfax.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of Lord Fairfax, listed among Sutliff's English-style blends, could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-lord-fairfax.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

mcclelland-maple-supreme.z: No sufficient independent source describing the contents of this maple-flavored blend from the bulk aromatic series could be found.
mcclelland-maple-supreme.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of maple syrup.

new-york-pipe-club-bowling-green.z: Bowling Green is the straight Virginia entry in the series of blends the New York Pipe Club has had prepared exclusively for its members. The club bases its blends on classic tobacco recipes free of casing and embellishment; this tobacco too is built entirely from Virginia leaf and presented as a pressed cake. Pressing lets the flavors of the different Virginia grades meld together inside the tin. The tin note shows fruity notes of plum, apricot, and peach; in the smoke it leaves a taste that swings between sweet and tangy sharpness, reminiscent of dried apricot. A fitting recipe for smokers who enjoy drawing out unflavored Virginia character through a slow smoke and who are accustomed to cake tobaccos. It takes its name from the Bowling Green neighborhood at the southern tip of Manhattan.
new-york-pipe-club-bowling-green.o: Leaves a sweet-tart, doughy aroma reminiscent of dried apricot and canned peach.

iwan-ries-three-star-bronze.z: This is a blend from the Three Star line prepared over the counter by the Chicago-based tobacconist Iwan Ries & Co.; no independent source detailing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
iwan-ries-three-star-bronze.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

clan-shaw-placer.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Placer.

reiver-pipes-tobacco-mangerton-morn.z: This is a blend from Reiver Pipes & Tobacco listed as Scottish style, named after Mangerton in the Scottish border region; there is not enough source material on its content.
reiver-pipes-tobacco-mangerton-morn.o: No source could be found describing its aroma.

peter-stokkebye-aromatic-dutch-slices-no.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Aromatic Dutch Slices (No.308) could be found.

kramers-pipe-and-tobacco-shop-new-mix.z: Referred to as an English-type bulk blend carrying the shop's own name; no independent source could be found to document its composition.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.z: This is an aromatic record flavored with cocoa essence in Imigrantes Fumos's Cândido Giovanella line; the catalog appears to list the same flavor under different names. The base is built on Brazilian-grown Virginia leaf with black Cavendish and Burley, cut in ribbon. In the smoke, cocoa's dry, lightly bitter sweetness leads; Cavendish gives a sugary depth, and Virginia a bready base. Nicotine and fullness are moderate, and the smoke stays cool. It suits those who enjoy dark, sweet aromatics and want a low-nicotine smoke.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.o: Leaves an aroma of dry cocoa powder and sweet tobacco.

paul-olsen-fethry-duck.z: A blend from the My Own Blend line that originated at the Paul Olsen shop in Copenhagen; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

the-smoker-red-virginia-supreme.z: Red Virginia Supreme is recorded as one of the hand-prepared house blends from The Smoker, a tobacconist that operated in Albany from the 1930s until 2011; no independent source describing the blend's composition has been found.

clan-shaw-new-orleans.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend New Orleans.

tabaqueria-xian-gimlis-beard.z: A house blend from Tabaquería Xian listed as Virginia-Perique; no independent source documenting its content could be found.

hearth-home-distinguished-penguin.z: Distinguished Penguin is a blend in the Hearth & Home series linked to the Scottish style. Its composition includes bright Virginia along with Carolina-grown flake-cut leaf, steamed-and-heat-treated (stoved) dark Virginia, Latakia, and black Cavendish. The stoved Virginia lends the blend a depth of cooked fruit and caramel. Latakia is kept at a low proportion, sitting in the background rather than overriding the sweetness. This positions the blend somewhere between English mixtures and straight Virginias. It carries no topping. Well suited to smokers who want Latakia as a subtle hint of spice with Virginia sweetness at the center, as well as those wanting to sample the Scottish style.
hearth-home-distinguished-penguin.o: Leaves a fine wood-smoke aroma mingled with caramelized hay sweetness.

paul-olsen-3-nuns-my-own-blend.z: No reliable source could be found for the Paul Olsen pipe tobacco called 3 Nuns (My Own Blend), so a detailed profile could not be produced.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-cremon-mixture.z: Not enough independent sources could be reached to fill out the record for Kohlhase, Kopp und Co. KG's blend called Cremon Mixture.

mastro-de-paja-roma.z: Remembered as a blend attributed to Mastro de Paja, founded in Pesaro in 1972 and known for pipe-making; since no source documenting its composition could be found, the profile is left incomplete.
mastro-de-paja-roma.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

tabacum-h5.z: No reliable source describing the composition of this Tabacum blend, recorded as based on cigar leaf, could be found.

ravenwood-fine-provisions-moose-marmalad.z: Moose Marmalade is the citrus-themed aromatic blend in the Ravenwood Fine Provisions line. As its name suggests, it is built around orange and tangerine notes reminiscent of classic marmalade; some descriptions also mention lemon. Its body is built from Burley and Virginia, with toasted Cavendish contributing sweetness; the blender states the goal is to keep the tobacco taste intact despite the flavoring. Nicotine stays light. It suits smokers looking for a fruity-citrus aromatic who don't want the leaf's own taste fully masked. It is produced in small batches.
ravenwood-fine-provisions-moose-marmalad.o: Leaves an orange-peel and sugar aroma reminiscent of orange marmalade.

p-lorillard-union-leader.z: Union Leader is one of the grocery-shelf classics P. Lorillard — founded in 1760 and considered America's oldest continuously operating tobacco manufacturer — sold throughout the twentieth century. Its body is built from burley, joined by bright Virginia, and the blend was sold ribbon cut, in two-ounce pouches at times and fourteen-ounce large tins at others. Records indicate the leaf received a light maple-direction flavoring; this topping isn't pronounced enough to place the blend in the aromatic class, and mainly rounds off burley's nutty, earthy taste.
p-lorillard-union-leader.o: A thin trace of toasted sugar mingles with a nutty, lightly sweet tobacco scent.

tavern-tobacco-co-rusty-hinge-flake.z: Rusty Hinge Flake, a pipe tobacco from Tavern Tobacco Co.; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

chacom-2.z: Chacom #2 is the fruity aromatic in the line the French pipe brand has manufactured by Kohlhase & Kopp in Germany. Various high-natural-sugar Virginias form the body along with broken Virginia; a small proportion of burley and a thin share of black cavendish round out the blend. A yellow-plum and sweet vanilla casing is applied on top. The flavor is fruity and creamy, giving a tone reminiscent of fruit cake and custard. Nicotine is in the low-to-medium range and does not turn harsh on the tongue. Because the fine shag cut burns quickly, it calls for a slow smoke. Suitable for those who find heavily sugared aromatics too much and want a measured fruit note.
chacom-2.o: Leaves a yellow plum and vanilla cream aroma.

dan-tobacco-gordon-pym.z: Gordon Pym is a traditional English mixture in which a base of golden Virginia and Maryland leaf, with a small amount of fire-cured dark Virginia added, is combined with select Oriental leaf and Syrian Latakia. It takes its name from the protagonist of Edgar Allan Poe's only full-length novel. Syrian Latakia gives a less tarry, more incense-like smokiness than Cyprus Latakia; the Oriental leaf adds a soft, tangy sharpness. Its broad cut means it burns slowly and evenly, and the maker notes that its character shows better in larger-chambered bowls. Suited to smokers looking for a classic, measured smoky English mixture.
dan-tobacco-gordon-pym.o: Leaves a smoky but not heavy scent reminiscent of dry spice and incense sticks.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-skandinav.z: Skandinavik Navy is the Danish-origin Skandinavik series' aromatic member referencing naval tradition. Matured virginia leaves are brought together with toasted burley, and the blend is given a sweet, rum-character casing. Thanks to its ribbon cut, it packs easily into the pipe and gives a slow burn. On the flavor side, burley's bready fullness is balanced by virginia sugar; nicotine load stays below medium. A suitable option for newcomers to aromatic blends and those seeking a mild tobacco they can smoke all day. The Skandinavik brand comes from the Peter Stokkebye tradition and is produced today under the Scandinavian Tobacco Group umbrella.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-skandinav.o: Leaves a sweet, rum-like scent evoking lightly toasted nuts.

mcclelland-2008-holiday-spirit.z: Holiday Spirit is the 2008 release of McClelland's limited-run seasonal aromatic series for the year-end holidays. Since the Kansas City-based maker ceased operations in 2018, the blend is no longer produced. The mixture consists of Burley, Virginia, and Cavendish leaves, topped with a dark-rum, pecan, and cocoa-based flavoring. True to its name, the tin note carries a sweet character evoking year-end baking. The smoke is cool and mild, nicotine load is low, and tendency to bite the tongue stays limited. Cocoa and walnut tones form the flavor's backbone, with rum adding a sharp accent to them. A historical record for those interested in seasonal aromatics and McClelland's now-ended production lines.
mcclelland-2008-holiday-spirit.o: Leaves an aroma of cocoa, toasted walnut, and sweet pastry.

cornell-diehl-interlude.z: Interlude is a blend where Cornell & Diehl presses dark red Virginia leaf, lightly sweetened with a touch of honey to bring out the leaf's own sweetness, and slices it into flake. The slices are neat and relatively moist; they can be packed rubbed out or folded and stuffed into the chamber, the latter giving a slower, more intense smoke. The profile leads with dried fruit, bread, and grass notes; the honey theme is kept from overpowering the tobacco. The richness expected from red Virginia is somewhat softened by the flavoring, while nicotine sits at medium. The ash can come out coarse, and airing before packing helps regulate the burn. It suits those looking for a lightly sweetened Virginia flake.
cornell-diehl-interlude.o: Leaves an aroma of honeyed bread and dry grass.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-black-diamond.z: Black Diamond is an aromatic blend referred to under the Orlik Tobacco Company A/S label from Assens, Denmark; no published description of its composition could be found.

low-country-pipe-cigar-strawberry.z: Low Country Pipe & Cigar is a tobacconist based in Little River, South Carolina; it prepares its blends by hand and sells most of them in bulk. Strawberry is one of the most directly fruit-flavored members of this bulk aromatic line. The body of this fine ribbon-cut blend is carried by Virginia leaf, accompanied in a smaller proportion by black cavendish; the strawberry casing is the dominant note both in the pouch and in the burn. Nicotine is low and the smoke is soft; thanks to the fine cut it lights easily even when moist and needs no long drying. Aimed at smokers seeking a pronounced fruit note rather than natural tobacco character and wanting a light aromatic to smoke all day. Compared to the harsher-on-the-tongue type of aromatics, it offers a smooth, calm burn.
low-country-pipe-cigar-strawberry.o: Leaves a pronounced, candy-like ripe strawberry room note.

dan-tobacco-jubilee-40-dan-pipe.z: Referred to as a limited blend released for Dan Pipe's founding anniversary; no adequate independent sources were found describing its composition.

w-o-larsen-fresh-elegant.z: No independent source sufficient to complete a record could be found regarding W.O. Larsen's Fresh & Elegant blend, so this entry remains incomplete.

torben-dansk-latakia-cypern.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Torben Dansk blend Latakia Cypern has been found.

magne-falkum-tullagreme-house-12.z: Tullagreme House 12 is an unflavored flake in Tabakhaus Falkum's house series. Its composition rests on Kentucky and White Burley. The leaves are matured very slowly, toasted, pressed, and heat-treated before storage; the series is produced by Kohlhase & Kopp. Pressing and toasting slow the burn and leave a dark, sweetish taste reminiscent of licorice root. Burley's dry, nutty structure proceeds together with Kentucky's smoky aroma, with no topping applied. Nicotine load is high. Suited to smokers used to packing a pipe who seek unflavored dark tobacco and a slow-burning flake.
magne-falkum-tullagreme-house-12.o: Leaves a dark aroma reminiscent of soot, dry wood, and licorice root.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-twist-sweet-map.z: This is the maple-topped version of the Kendal-style brown twist. Dark fire-cured and air-cured leaves are twisted into rope; the topping is applied while the rope is being made. According to sources the topping is medium in strength; it does not leave a sticky sweetness but the maple source is identifiably present. As with all members of this family, nicotine is high; while the topping adds sweetness, it doesn't lighten the body. The rope is sliced coin-thin and rubbed out for filling; smoked slowly, the taste stays in balance. It suits a smoker who knows the weight of rope tobacco and wants a measured sweet topping on top of it.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-twist-sweet-map.o: Burnt sugar and maple syrup aromas mix with woodsmoke.

blatter-blatter-danish-slices-tranches-d.z: A Virginia flake blend sold under its own name by the Blatter & Blatter shop in Montreal, also known by the French name Tranches Danoises; according to records it carries a light honey-and-nut topping, though no verified source for its recipe could be found.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-brazilian-coffee.z: Brazilian Coffee is a coffee-flavored cavendish blend from McGahey The Tobacconist. Its body rests on a combination of golden and black cavendish leaves; the two cavendish types together give a dark-sugar sweetness and a soft smoke. Brazilian coffee flavoring is added on top. The coffee note is pronounced in the dry tobacco and stays in the foreground throughout the smoke; because of its cavendish-forward construction the nicotine strength stays low. Given cavendish's tendency to hold moisture, airing it briefly before lighting is common practice. An entry geared toward smokers looking for sweet and roasted notes together who want to stay on the aromatic side.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-brazilian-coffee.o: Leaves an aroma of freshly roasted coffee beans and caramelized sugar.

alfie-turmeaus-the-reggae-man.z: One of Turmeaus tobacconist's house mixtures noted as aromatic; no accessible source documenting its content could be found.

wolfway-brown-green-river.z: This is a Wolfway product said to be Burley-dominant; no verifiable source could be found describing its composition and character.

cobblestone-fishing.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Cobblestone pipe tobacco named Fishing, so the blend's content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

g-l-pease-ranger.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Ranger.

gawith-hoggarth-co-ennerdale-plug.z: Ennerdale Plug is the pressed plug form of Ennerdale, Gawith Hoggarth's best-known Lakeland blend. Malawi Burley is added to African- and South American-origin Virginia leaf; the share of air-cured dark leaf cools the smoke and leaves a woody, creamy texture. The plug comes as a block, and smokers slice and rub it out for packing. The blend's defining trait is the intense floral flavoring known as Lakeland essence; rum, vanilla, citrus, and almond notes layer on top of it. The aroma is so dominant that it easily clings to jar and pipe, so smoking it in a dedicated pipe is common practice. Suited to smokers curious about the classic English Lakeland style who don't shy away from heavily topped tobaccos.
gawith-hoggarth-co-ennerdale-plug.o: Soapy floral essence, vanilla, and rum aroma spread through the room, with almond and citrus lingering behind.

danish-import-skandinavik-regular.z: Skandinavik Regular is a ribbon-cut mixture built on select Burley and Virginia leaf, in keeping with the Danish blending tradition. The series traces back to the Danish production line known under the Peter Stokkebye name and has long been sold in the United States as imported tobacco. "Regular" is the most modestly cased member of the series. The fine cut makes for easy lighting; nicotine sits between mild and medium. It offers a middle option for smokers who don't want the sugar load of heavy aromatics but aren't ready to move fully to unflavored blends either. It's built with everyday, extended smoking in mind.
danish-import-skandinavik-regular.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, warm tobacco scent.

peterson-summertime-2020.z: Summertime 2020 is the 2020 entry in Peterson's limited-production series prepared for the summer season. The blend is built from a balanced combination of lightly pressed black Cavendish with hand-rubbed Virginia and Burley leaf; a measured blackcurrant-and-apple flavoring is applied on top. The brand is Irish in origin, while tobacco production is carried out in Germany. The smoke is light-bodied, sweet-leaning, and low in nicotine; Burley dries and levels out the blend while Cavendish adds roundness and Virginia supplies natural sugar. The fruit flavoring is noticeable but doesn't overwhelm the tobacco's own taste. It suits smokers seeking a light aromatic with a tart fruit note for all-day smoking. As a limited production, it was not remade once the season passed.
peterson-summertime-2020.o: Leaves a tart, cranberry-like fruit aroma alongside baked apple.

rocky-patel-prohibition-pure-simple.z: Prohibition Pure & Simple is an aromatic blend from the pipe-tobacco line of Rocky Patel, known primarily as a cigar maker. The mixture is built from black Cavendish, Burley, and Virginia leaf, over which vanilla and caramel essences are applied. Cavendish supplies sweetness and moisture, Burley the carrying body, and Virginia a light fruity sweetness in the background. Nicotine ranges from low to medium, the smoke is mellow, and the flavoring is pronounced. The ribbon cut packs easily, though the tin runs moist and may need airing before smoking. It suits newcomers to aromatics and smokers looking for a sweet, fragrant smoke; it will disappoint those looking for an unflavored blend. The product comes in large packaging such as a 12-ounce glass jar.
rocky-patel-prohibition-pure-simple.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of sweet vanilla and burnt sugar caramel.

sutliff-tobacco-company-pipe-force-episo.z: The Pipe Force line consists of limited blends Per Georg Jensen prepared for Sutliff; the fourth episode was released in the summer of 2023 in a production run of 7,500 units. This Oriental-forward English mixture uses red Virginia, latakia, and the series' signature leaves — stoved rustica and Katerini. On the taste, grassy, floral, and spicy layers from the Orientals lead; the red Virginia gives a toasted sweetness, and the latakia adds a measured smokiness. Katerini and rustica bring both a peppery sharpness and a pronounced nicotine load. Since it is offered pressed into plug form, how to prepare it is left up to the smoker.
sutliff-tobacco-company-pipe-force-episo.o: Leaves a spicy, grassy, lightly smoky scent.

synjeco-synjecos-balkan.z: Synjeco's Balkan, a pipe tobacco from Synjeco; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

chief-catoonah-tobacconist-baileys-supre.z: The entry has been left incomplete as no reliable source could be found for Chief Catoonah Tobacconist's Bailey's Supreme blend.

mcclelland-no-2015-virginia-perique-flak.z: No. 2015 Virginia Perique Flake is a flake blend sliced from a dark, mature cake built by adding St. James-region Perique to orange and red Virginias. The Perique share is kept at a level that gives the smoke depth and a spiced edge without overpowering the Virginia's sweetness; the maker's description likens the blend to the Maritime flakes of the past. Aimed at smokers who like the Virginia-Perique combination and are used to working with unflavored, pressed tobaccos. The slices need to be rubbed out or folded before packing; smoked slowly it burns cool. Discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-no-2015-virginia-perique-flak.o: A dried-fig and plum-bread aroma comes through with a light spice.

cienfuegos-black-aromatic-mixture.z: Black Aromatic Mixture, recorded under the Cienfuegos name, is referred to as Virginia-and-Latakia-based; not enough sourcing could be found to document the blend.
cienfuegos-black-aromatic-mixture.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

schurch-champion-mixture-v.z: Champion Mixture V, signed by Schürch, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-rumcake.z: No sufficient source could be found documenting the composition and character of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Rumcake.

ole-shenandoah-appalachian-harvest.z: Appalachian Harvest is one of the aromatic members of the Ole Shenandoah line aimed at the American market. Mild black cavendish makes up the bulk, joined by bright Virginia, topped with a fruity, forest-fruit-direction flavoring. The cut is loose, described as smoking-ready straight from the tin. Nicotine level is low and the taste mild; the topping largely defines the blend's character. Its slow, cool burn suits long sessions. It's a blend designed not for those seeking the tobacco leaf's own taste to lead, but for smokers who love sweet, fruity aromatics and those new to the pipe. Records indicate the line is no longer in production.
ole-shenandoah-appalachian-harvest.o: Spreads a scent of sweet forest fruit and sugary cavendish through the room.

theodorus-niemeyer-hollandia.z: Hollandia was a blend the Groningen-based Theodorus Niemeyer house produced in its Dutch-style aromatic Cavendish line. Woody, earthy, nutty Burley forms the body, joined by Kentucky and Cavendish-processed Virginia, with a small amount of Oriental leaf reportedly also present. The top note is described as a dark, sugary casing evoking Dutch liqueurs. The taste is not intense but measured; the casing sits in the background without overpowering the leaf, and the smoke is medium-bodied. A typical example for smokers wanting to get to know classic Continental European shop aromatics and after a blend without exaggerated sweetness. The Niemeyer brand today sits under Imperial Tobacco, and production under this name has not continued.
theodorus-niemeyer-hollandia.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma in the room reminiscent of dark sugar and liqueur.

mccranies-first-light.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found on First Light, one of McCranie's Pipe Shop's house blends.
mccranies-first-light.o: No reliable description of the aroma could be found.

king-street-coffee-tobacco-emporium-moun.z: Mountaineer is a blend King Street Emporium credits as a Burley-forward aromatic. Per the manufacturer's description, toasted cavendish is added to golden Virginia and Burley leaves; the result is a lively, lightly sharp character, with the taste reportedly opening up over the course of the day. It sits at a medium nicotine level; sugar load is kept low, in a mixture that brings forward Burley's dry, nutty side. Suited to smokers avoiding heavy aromatics but still wanting a sweet layer behind. Prepared only in-house.
king-street-coffee-tobacco-emporium-moun.o: Leaves toasted cavendish's sweet scent together with Burley's nutty, lightly tangy scent.

ascorti-toscana.z: No adequate independent source documenting the content of the Toscana blend, carrying the Ascorti name, could be found.
ascorti-toscana.o: No reliable information on the room note could be found.

golden-harvest-mild.z: Golden Harvest is a pipe tobacco series made from leaf grown in the United States and sold in large-gram bags. The series consists of five variants — Mild, Light, Natural, Robust, and Mint — with Mild sitting at the mildest end. Finely cut Virginia and Burley leaf are used, and the tobacco is packed in resealable bags. Its character is simple: Burley's dry, nutty base is joined by Virginia's measured sweetness, with no pronounced flavoring beyond a light topping. Nicotine is low and the smoke is mild. Suited to those wanting an unpretentious, economical everyday tobacco that can be smoked all day, as well as newcomers.
golden-harvest-mild.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma in tones of dry hay and nuts.

grants-tobacconist-my-mellow-blend.z: One of Grant's Tobacconist's house blends; there is no independent sourcing about its composition.

savinelli-juno.z: Juno is an unflavored Virginia blend. A stoved red Virginia base is joined by light-colored Virginia, the mixture is stoved once more, and finished with unprocessed red Virginia. This process sequence forms the blend's dark, sugary character. Its flavor is built on the sweetness coming from Virginia's natural sugar; it carries sour-fruit and baked-bread directions. It is measured in nicotine. Suited to those seeking plain Virginia blends progressing on a single leaf type and to those wanting a flake they can smoke all day. Though the brand is Italian, it is produced in the United States.
savinelli-juno.o: Leaves a scent of sweet hay and light bread crust.

borkum-riff-vanilla-cavendish-sungold.z: Vanilla Cavendish is an aromatic blend in which dark Kentucky and Burley leaf are put through the Cavendish process and finished with a vanilla-heavy topping. The leaf is heavily fermented, giving the blend a balanced, mellow, easy-approach structure. Alongside the vanilla, the topping also carries a faint boozy note. Due to naming regulations in EU countries, it's sold in these markets under the name Sungold. It's a ribbon-cut tobacco with medium-light nicotine. It suits smokers looking for classic vanilla aromatics who want the sweetness to be pronounced.
borkum-riff-vanilla-cavendish-sungold.o: Leaves a warm room note of heavy vanilla reminiscent of sweet baked pastry.

sutliff-tobacco-company-walnut-knoll-lan.z: An aromatic recorded under the Sutliff name, apparently walnut-themed based on its title; no independent source describing the blend's content, cut, and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-curly-cut-sliced.z: Curly Cut consists of round medallions obtained by rolling twisted rope tobacco, pressing it, and then slicing it. Unlike ropes made entirely of dark leaf, this roll uses light-colored Virginia as the outer wrap; this both makes the tobacco milder and creates a look of light and dark rings in the slice. The medallions are packed by rubbing them out and spreading them in the palm. It carries an unflavored Virginia character: a bready, sweet base with a measured smokiness from the fire-cured leaf. Aimed at smokers who love pressed, rolled Virginia forms and want an unflavored smoke.
gawith-hoggarth-co-curly-cut-sliced.o: Leaves a lightly smoky tobacco aroma carrying bready sweetness.

peter-stokkebye-english-luxury-no-17.z: English Luxury is one of the blends carried over into today's line from the production Peter Stokkebye founded in the 1970s. Soft Georgia Virginias, black Cavendish, Mexican Burley, and Cyprus Latakia are all used together. The Latakia proportion is kept measured enough that its smoky taste doesn't overwhelm the blend; Cavendish adds a light sweetness and a cool burn to the base. Its body sits between light and medium; Latakia's earthy, mushroomy side is noticeable but stays milder than in classic English blends. It is a good entry-level record for those trying Latakia for the first time and those who find heavy smoky blends tiring.
peter-stokkebye-english-luxury-no-17.o: A light, sweet background accompanies a smoky wood and burnt-brush aroma.

iwan-ries-three-star-dutch.z: Three Star Dutch is a light aromatic in Iwan Ries & Co.'s decades-running Three Star line. Per the maker's description, the blend is built on toasted Burley and cut thick; this cut allows the tobacco to burn slowly and evenly, leaving little ash behind. The flavoring is kept light enough not to mask the Burley's nutty taste. With its low nicotine load, it suits smokers looking for an all-day tobacco, and those who value a pipe that lights easily and burns without trouble. It's produced in the United States.
iwan-ries-three-star-dutch.o: Leaves an aroma of toasted nuts and a lightly sweet baked note.

peter-stokkebye-london-export-no-96.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name London Export No.96 in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-royal-yach.z: Match Royal Yacht is a single-leaf Virginia-based record prepared to correspond to the famous Royal Yacht blend made by Gawith Hoggarth. A special vanilla-forward casing is applied over a base close to Sutliff's own Virginia Slices #507-C blend. Unlike the original blend, it contains no perique. On the smoke, Virginia's grain and honey sweetness leads; the casing pulls this base toward a caramelized direction. Nicotine is medium, and the taste is full but not sharp. It lights easily and leaves grayish speckled ash. It suits those looking for a softened, sweetened Virginia rather than the original Royal Yacht's dark, spicy character.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-royal-yach.o: Leaves a scent of caramelized grain and light vanilla.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrugs-71st-street.z: Surbrug's 71st Street is a sweet aromatic from Wilke's Surbrug recipes. According to the maker's description, sugared and unsugared cavendish are used together, with Burley and Virginia added. The casing layout consists of a touch of Irish whiskey with old-fashioned nougat and chocolate. Burley builds the blend's nutty, bready foundation while Virginia adds a light tartness; cavendish carries the casing. It suits smokers seeking a bowl with a pronounced dessert-sweet character who prefer low-nicotine aromatics.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrugs-71st-street.o: A light whiskey tone accompanies the cocoa and nougat scent.

gawith-hoggarth-co-curly-cut.z: Curly Cut is produced by twisting Virginia leaves into rope form, then rolling and pressing them, and cutting them into round coins. Light-coloured Virginia is used as the outer wrapper leaf; this both creates a noticeable colour contrast in the coins and softens the smoke. The coins are prepared either rubbed out or folded to fit the bowl. This is an untopped blend, carrying only a very fine Lakeland trace from the production line. In the smoke, Virginia's malty sweetness, reminiscent of bread dough and dry grass, leads. The tightly pressed structure gives a slow, cool burn, with a medium nicotine load. This is a good record for those wanting to get to know rope- and coin-cut tobaccos, staying close to an untopped Virginia taste.
gawith-hoggarth-co-curly-cut.o: An aroma of bread dough and dry grass is mixed with a very light floral trace.

players-navy-cut-deluxe.z: Player's Navy Cut Deluxe is a pipe tobacco blend for which there is not enough independent source material.
players-navy-cut-deluxe.o: Not enough records could be found on the room note.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-cherry-an.z: Kendal Gold is the umbrella name for the shag-cut tobacco family Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. produces in the town of Kendal in England's Lake District. The family's body is built from Brazilian- and Indian-origin, heat-cured light Virginia leaf; largely stripped of stem, it's cut into fine golden strands. The producer steams and softens the tobacco, cuts it, toasts it on a hot cylinder, and then applies the top flavoring — so the family's members are versions of the same body offered with different scents. Entry No. 8 in the series carries a cherry-and-vanilla flavoring over the Virginia body. The two scents balance each other: vanilla is creamy and round, cherry sharper and fruitier; underneath, the leaf's own herbal, honeyed sweetness can be sensed. The fine shag cut is packed with the fingertips, lights immediately, and resists going out; since it burns fast, slow smoking is needed. Nicotine is measured. Suited to smokers wanting a tobacco on the aromatic side that can be smoked all day.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-cherry-an.o: Leaves a creamy vanilla and ripe-cherry aroma.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-private-stock.z: J.M.'s Private Stock is a Virginia-perique blend combining Virginia flake with perique. Virginia's grassy, dried-fruit sweetness forms the base; perique adds a peppery, tart-fruited depth. Because the flake structure takes time to prepare, the blend has long been available only in the shop. The blend is described as J.M. Boswell's personal mixture of more than fifteen years. It carries no flavor casing; suitable for those seeking intense, unflavored Virginia sweetness and accustomed to a slow smoke.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-private-stock.o: Leaves a light pepper trace along with a dry hay and tart fruit aroma.

pipesandcigars-com-perique-blend-p-37.z: Perique Blend P-37 is one of the house blends sold under its own name by the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com; no sufficient independent sources documenting its content and character could be found.

dan-tobacco-mona-lisa.z: Mona Lisa is an aromatic blend built on Dan Tobacco's own house-made black Cavendish. The maker states the Cavendish is heat-fermented under press, yielding a leaf that stays soft despite its pronounced sweetness. The blend is prepared as ready-rubbed flake; a small amount of light-colored Mysore Virginia is added to lighten the appearance. The casing is described as fruity and fresh, kept light enough not to mask the tobacco's own sweetness. Nicotine is low, giving a cool smoke. Suited to smokers who lean aromatic but want to avoid heavy syrupy blends, and who like flake texture. Distributed in 100- and 250-gram packagings.
dan-tobacco-mona-lisa.o: Leaves a lightly caramel scent with fresh-fruit sweetness.

cornell-diehl-warped-midsommar.z: Midsommar is one of the limited releases jointly prepared by Warped Cigars founder Kyle Gellis and Cornell & Diehl head blender Jeremy Reeves. Per the maker's description, the blend uses 2019-harvest Canadian bright Virginia, 2014-harvest white Burley, and aged Basma along with Izmir Oriental together; a light rum-and-molasses casing ties the components together. The leaf is pressed into cake form, which allows both slice-and-fill packing and further aging. On the character side, the earthy and nutty tones Burley and Oriental bring are balanced by Virginia's natural sweetness; the casing isn't dominant, sitting instead as a background-level sweetness. Nicotine load is close to medium-high, making it suited to smokers looking for texture and body rather than an aromatic. The name comes from the blend being designed with summer evenings in mind. Being a limited release, it isn't in regular production.
cornell-diehl-warped-midsommar.o: A light molasses sweetness can be sensed beneath a scent of dry hay and nutty tobacco.

comoys-of-london-cask-11-british-strengt.z: Blend No. 11 in Comoy's of London's Cask series is an unflavored English mixture built in the Balkan style. Its composition includes hazy-character Oriental leaves, bright Virginias, and dark, full Latakia. Though Latakia is pronounced, the blend's center of gravity is left to the Oriental leaves' spicy, dry notes. On the flavor channel it follows a smoky, spicy line; the Virginias supply a light sweetness in the background to establish balance. Since nicotine stays at a medium level, it can be used in long sessions by smokers accustomed to Latakia blends. According to available records, Comoy's Cask series has not been in production for some time.
comoys-of-london-cask-11-british-strengt.o: Leaves a smoky wood aroma reminiscent of campfire in the room, topped with a dry, spicy Oriental scent.

up-down-barnyard-too.z: No sufficient source documenting the composition of the Up Down house blend Barnyard Too has been found.
up-down-barnyard-too.o: No reliable source describing the room note has been found.

charatan-1992-mixture.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the British pipe maker Charatan.

per-g-jensen-dark-fired-kentucky.z: Dark Fired Kentucky is the Blender's Collection member devoted to fire-cured Kentucky leaf. Being an unflavored single-leaf presentation, it lacks top-note flavoring like the series' other members and comes as a ready-rubbed cut. Fire curing gives the leaf a smoky, woody character, so the tobacco can be smoked either on its own or used in measured proportions to add smoke and body to other blends. The smoke carries earth, wood, smoke, and herbal notes alongside light spice and floral edges; it burns cool and clean with a medium nicotine load. It suits those who love a smoky character and want an intense leaf for particular moments rather than a flat everyday tobacco, as well as blenders building their own mixtures.
per-g-jensen-dark-fired-kentucky.o: Leaves a scent of wood smoke and cured leaf.

torben-dansk-latakia-special.z: Torben Dansk Latakia Special is a single-varietal Latakia product in the brand's blending-component line. Latakia is obtained by smoke-curing Oriental leaf; this DTM product is unflavored and presented with a more pronounced smoke character than the line's standard Cyprus Latakia. Its nicotine is medium, but flavor intensity is very high, so it is used more as a spice leaf in English and Balkan blends than smoked on its own. Suited to home blenders wanting to raise the smoke character.
torben-dansk-latakia-special.o: A campfire, pine-smoke and soot aroma spreads through the room and lingers for a long time.

james-b-russell-bengal-slices.z: Bengal Slices is a blend prepared at the Sobranie factory for the James B. Russell company, launched around 1977. Its method of production is based on the "krumble kake" technique developed for Smoker's Haven in the late 1960s: shredded leaves are pressed and rested into a cake form, then sliced. This produces a stubbier but easily crumbled shape, distinct from a classic flake cut from whole leaf. It has long been said that the product is a pressed version of the Balkan Sobranie mixture. The backbone of the blend is generous Latakia, Oriental leaves, and Virginia; the aroma and flavor are smoky, spicy, and deep, accompanied by a subtle top flavoring. Production changed hands in the 1980s and stopped for a time; in 2015, the Standard Tobacco Company of Pennsylvania, which took over the brand, had blender Russ Ouellette reinterpret it and restarted production. It's aimed at smokers with an interest in heavily Latakia-forward, pressed blends.
james-b-russell-bengal-slices.o: A thin sweet layer sits atop heavy wood smoke, cedar, and spice.

virginia-gold-natural.z: Virginia Gold Natural is the unflavored blend in the same budget line. Its base is a grassy, citrusy, lightly toasted Virginia, with earthy, nutty Burley used as the secondary leaf. It is ribbon cut and sold in bags. Nicotine is low and the smoke does not tire the tongue unless puffed too fast. It burns clean and somewhat quickly, leaves little moisture at the bottom of the bowl, and shows no marked change in taste throughout. A record aimed at those seeking an unflavored, everyday, plain Virginia-Burley mixture.
virginia-gold-natural.o: Leaves an aroma of dry hay and toasted bread.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-brown-twist-u-.z: Sliced Brown Twist U/S, as the abbreviation in the name indicates, is the factory-sliced form of unscented brown Burma. It's produced by hand-twisting dark fire-cured leaf into rope and carries no flavoring at all. On the smoke, earth, wood smoke, leather, and a bready sweetness stand out; the taste comes entirely from the leaf itself. Since it doesn't go through a pressure-cooking stage, it's intense in nicotine and needs to be thinly sliced and smoked slowly. An entry for those wanting to try the unflavored, strong English Burma tradition. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. is one of the English producers that continues traditional twist (rope) production at its Kendal factory, hand-twisting fire-cured leaves into rope form. Because twist tobaccos don't go through a pressure-cooking stage, they stay intense in nicotine; records indicate these ropes are sold for both chewing and pipe smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-brown-twist-u-.o: Leaves an unflavored tobacco aroma weighted toward wood smoke and dry earth.

john-aylesbury-brown-yellow.z: No reliable source documenting the content and character of John Aylesbury's Brown & Yellow blend could be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-drexel-ii.z: A blend referred to as aromatic; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

brigham-enterprises-inc-virginia-flake.z: Mr. B's Virginia Flake is an unflavored flake obtained by blending and pressing red, lemon (light yellow) and dark Virginia leaves together. Having different Virginia grades together gives a broader flavor range than flakes based on a single leaf class. Sugars concentrate due to pressing; smoked slowly, it gives a grassy, tart-sweet profile that deepens over time. It calls for a measured pace since fast smoking can cause tongue bite. A structure suited to fans of unflavored Virginia and to cellaring (long-term aging).
brigham-enterprises-inc-virginia-flake.o: Leaves a trace reminiscent of dry hay and warmed bread.

samuel-gawith-bothy-flake.z: Bothy Flake is produced by pressing Virginia and latakia leaves into flake form and then flavoring with Scotch Highland malt whisky. The blend was prepared for the Kearvaig Pipe Club, founded in 2012 at the Kearvaig bothy on Scotland's north coast. It is a product falling into the flavored-English-blend class, with a fine whisky casing riding atop the smoky latakia character. Suited to smokers who love Latakia-bearing blends and want a light top note over it; because of the flake presentation, packing and lighting call for care.
samuel-gawith-bothy-flake.o: A malt whisky's grainy, sweetish scent mixes into the smoky latakia scent.

cornell-diehl-chocolate-cavendish.z: Chocolate Cavendish is a ribbon-cut aromatic formed by adding the company's own special flavoring mix, prepared from natural chocolate and cocoa nibs, to Cornell & Diehl's traditional cavendish base. The blend also contains burley and Virginia leaf alongside the black cavendish. Nicotine sits on the light side; what stands out most is the sweet, roasted character imparted by the chocolate flavoring. It can be smoked on its own or used as a flavoring component in homemade blends. It suits those looking for a chocolate-forward aromatic and newcomers to the pipe.
cornell-diehl-chocolate-cavendish.o: Leaves an aroma of cocoa and sweet dough fresh from the oven.

cult-embassy.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the Cult brand as Embassy; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

dan-tobacco-american-line-flake-and-cave.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of Dan Tobacco's American Line Flake and Cavendish blend were found.

alfie-turmeaus-mystery-mix-c.z: One of the unnamed experimental mixtures from Turmeaus tobacconist; no accessible source documenting its content or character could be found.

dan-tobacco-london-blend-no-750.z: No adequate independent sources were found documenting the composition of this blend, listed as Virginia-based in Dan Tobacco's numbered London Blend series.

pipe-republic-blackpool.z: No reliable sources on Pipe Republic's blend Blackpool could be found, so its content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

anthony-cranswick-blue-castle.z: No verifiable source could be found for content and character information on the Blue Castle version in Anthony Cranswick's Castle line.

seattle-pipe-club-mississippi-river-spec.z: Mississippi River Special Reserve Flake is the version presenting Seattle Pipe Club's Mississippi River recipe in flake cut and enriched with matured accent tobaccos. Whole-leaf virginias with a sour character are layered and pressed; latakia, matured Turkish tobacco, and genuine St. James perique are then added and the blend is pressed again and sliced into thin leaves. St. James leaf adds a fruity spice, while sun-cured mature tobaccos add a peppery nuance; latakia builds the blend's smoky backbone. The flake cut both keeps preparation orderly and suits long aging. Suited to smokers accustomed to full-bodied English mixtures and flake preparation.
seattle-pipe-club-mississippi-river-spec.o: A spicy, lightly fruity edge accompanies an intense smoky wood scent.

intertabak-orientale-po-1.z: No verifiable source could be found for this Oriental tobacco registered under the INTERTABAK name.

e-a-carey-peach-brandy.z: An aromatic blend registered under the E. A. Carey name; it does not appear on the maker's current list, and not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition.

villiger-english-export.z: No sufficient independent source could be found regarding Villiger's pipe tobacco called English Export, so the blend's composition and character could not be recorded.

decatur-soft-and-mellow.z: This is one of the aromatic blends in the Decatur bulk series prepared for a soft smoke; no independent source stating its composition and topping could be found.
decatur-soft-and-mellow.o: No reliable record could be found for the room note.

planta-caribbean-black-pearl.z: The Black Pearl mixture in the Caribbean line is an aromatic built entirely from black Cavendish and cased with tropical fruit flavoring. There is not enough independent source material for detailed content and cut information.
planta-caribbean-black-pearl.o: Leaves a sweet tropical fruit aroma.

milan-tobacconists-old-dominion.z: Old Dominion, one of Milan Tobacconists' house blends, is reportedly a coarse-cut mixture built mainly on burley leaf; since it doesn't appear on the maker's current list, its detailed profile could not be verified.

iwan-ries-gourmet-english.z: This is one of the English-style house blends of Iwan Ries & Co.; no sufficient source describing its content and proportions could be found.
iwan-ries-gourmet-english.o: Records note it leaves the smoky wood aroma typical of Latakia-containing English blends.

house-of-calabash-for-meerschaums-only.z: This is a small-scale House of Calabash blend prepared, as the name suggests, for meerschaum pipes; no verifiable source describing its content could be found.

players-no-name.z: This is a straight Virginia blend carried under the Player's name; no independent source could be found verifying its content and character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-sangria-201.z: Sangria #201 is a blend in Sutliff's bulk aromatic line. The maker states that the blend uses the same base and process as its wine-cased product, with a sangria-character top casing applied over it. The base is built from Virginia and cavendish leaf; being ribbon cut, it lights easily and burns evenly. What defines the character is the combination of mature wine sweetness with selected citrus extracts; the leaf's own taste stays behind this casing. Since it sits light in nicotine, it is a good option both for all-day smoking and for those new to aromatic blends. Sutliff is a well-established American maker based in Richmond, Virginia.
sutliff-tobacco-company-sangria-201.o: Leaves a scent of winey red fruit and sweet citrus peel.

the-seasons-summertime.z: No reliable source could be found on the Summertime blend from The Seasons series.

g-l-pease-cairo-original-mixtures.z: Cairo is an untopped blend combining Virginia and Oriental leaves in a ribbon cut, with a small amount of Perique added. It sits on the Virginia-Oriental axis within G. L. Pease's Original Mixtures line. The tin's moisture level is directly suited to filling and burns without issue. The flavour is built on Virginia's natural sweetness and the Oriental leaf's spicy, oily character; the Perique topping adds a peppery depth, which may stand out to a smoker unfamiliar with this leaf. Loose loading gives a smoky, cool smoke, while tight loading gives a longer, more flavour-intense one. It suits those wanting to get to know untopped Virginia-Oriental mixtures.
g-l-pease-cairo-original-mixtures.o: Leaves a sweetish tobacco aroma dominated by dry grass and spice.

petersen-sorensen-sweet-cherries-cube-cu.z: This is a cube-cut, cherry-flavored mixture reported to come out of the tin at a near-dry moisture level. The profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient independent sources detailing the leaf composition could be found.

tinder-box-aalborg.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Tinder Box pipe tobacco called Aalborg to record the blend's composition and character.

lane-limited-captain-black-original-regu.z: Captain Black Original is the brand's core blend, in production since 1956. Steam-processed black cavendish, soft burley and golden Virginia leaves are combined to build depth; the cut is ribbon. Known for its white packaging, it's one of the few pipe tobaccos also widely sold at non-tobacconist outlets in the US. The taste is lightly sweet with a vanilla direction on top; nicotine is low, the smoke is cool. It offers no complex development, proceeding along the same line throughout the bowl. It has long been the go-to blend for newcomers to pipes and those seeking a familiar aromatic.
lane-limited-captain-black-original-regu.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough room note.

my-smoking-shop-columbian-coffee.z: Columbian Coffee is an American-style bulk blend built from bright and black cavendish leaves, topped with a sweet coffee sauce. It is sold under the Century name in the UK; following the 2017 naming change it also appears on shelves as Colombian C. It is ribbon cut, high in moisture, and burns cool. Nicotine is low, the smoke soft; the coffee note sits over a smoky sweetness and leads from start to finish. Suited to smokers looking for a sweet, coffee-scented aromatic.
my-smoking-shop-columbian-coffee.o: Leaves an aroma of freshly brewed coffee and roasted beans.

seattle-pipe-club-mississippi-river.z: Mississippi River is among the best known of Seattle Pipe Club's Virginia-forward entries. Rich Virginia leaves are pressed into a cake; Oriental leaf, a pinch of Latakia, and Perique are added as accents. The Latakia share is not high enough to place the blend in the English class, only adding a smoky shade; the Perique opens up a plum-and-spice direction. According to the brand's account, the recipe's main line is based on a draft blendmaster Joe Lankford jotted down one night. The intense flavor that emerges after pressing preserves the Virginia base while also bringing out the layers of the accent leaves. Suited to smokers who love the sweetness of Virginia blends and want a measured smokiness and spice alongside it.
seattle-pipe-club-mississippi-river.o: Leaves a fine wood smoke and a trace of plum behind a sweet hay scent.

john-patton-robusto-royale.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Patton's Robusto Royale pipe tobacco.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-racing-green.z: Racing Green is Orlik's aromatic blend built on contrasts. Its base holds bright Virginia leaves from the US Old Belt region, burley sourced from Mexico and Malawi, and a share of black cavendish. A topping recalling citrus, fruit, and cream is used for the top note. The smoke is mild and sweet; citrus, vanilla, and cream notes are pronounced, and the nicotine sensation is low. Because of this structure, it's described as a light aromatic smokable all day. It suits smokers avoiding heavily topped blends who want a moderately sweet aromatic.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-racing-green.o: Leaves a scent of vanilla cream and citrus.

mcclelland-beacon-extra.z: Beacon Extra is the version of McClelland's Beacon blend with a raised Perique proportion. Records indicate the two blends share the same base; the difference lies in the share of Louisiana Perique in the mixture. The broken-slice structure and matured Virginia body are preserved, but the Perique's peppery-fruity push comes forward noticeably. This carries both taste and satiety above Beacon's. Falls within the territory of those used to Perique intensity who seek strong, spicy Virginia smokes; may run heavy for those new to Perique.
mcclelland-beacon-extra.o: Leaves an aroma mixing dark fruit, pepper, and tangy ferment.

savinelli-english-mixture.z: English Mixture is one of Savinelli's longest-produced blends. A high proportion of latakia is added to sweet virginia and light burley leaf; some Oriental also adds spice and floral depth. The coarsely cut, partly granulated leaf is prepared for an even burn; no top-note flavoring is applied, and it is sold in 50-gram tins. On the smoke, latakia's grassy-woody soot and burley's spicy, dry taste lead; virginia's sweetness is sensed at the start and recedes as the bowl progresses. The burn is very slow and the tobacco does not overheat, though it is noted the pipe bottom can gurgle. Suited to smokers seeking latakia against a burley foundation, wanting a medium-strength, unflavored English-style mixture.
savinelli-english-mixture.o: Leaves a trace of dry hay and spice alongside a scent of wood smoke and leather.

charles-fairmorn-blantyre-mild-blend.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the Charles Fairmorn name.

mcclelland-tawny-flake.z: Tawny Flake is a Virginia flake in McClelland's line presented under the Blakeney's Best name. Per its description, it consists of small, sun-matured, sweet flue-cured Virginia leaves with a tangy sharpness. The line's distinguishing point is the toasting process applied to the leaf, which files down flue-cured leaf's sharp edge and leaves a rounder sweetness. In the smoke, a bready, caramel-like sweetness stands out, and the tang is more measured than in typical Virginia flakes. Body is light to medium. Suited to smokers wanting to get used to flake smoking or who find sharp Virginia too harsh. McClelland closed in 2018, so the blend is no longer produced.
mcclelland-tawny-flake.o: Leaves an aroma of toasted bread and dry hay, with a sweet trace behind it.

mac-baren-uncle-louie-rum.z: Uncle Louie Rum is a member of Mac Baren's drink-themed Bar Selection series. The blend brings together sweet Virginia, full Burley, and the brand's own Cavendish; rum flavoring is applied over this base. It's distributed as loose ribbon cut in large-capacity tins. In the smoke, the Cavendish's mild sweetness stands out along with the rum's brown-sugar, faintly oaky tone; the Burley adds body to the blend's smoke. Suited to smokers who like a pronounced flavoring, low nicotine, and tobaccos that leave a trace in the room. Records indicate the product was distributed especially for the North American market.
mac-baren-uncle-louie-rum.o: Leaves an aroma of sweet rum, brown sugar, and light oak.

john-aylesbury-copenhagen.z: No reliable source could be found to document the contents and character of John Aylesbury's Copenhagen blend.

hearth-home-capitol-stairs.z: Capitol Stairs is an American mixture in the Hearth & Home series built on a trio of Burley, Virginia, and Perique. In its original form, the blend included deer tongue, an herb used in the tobacco industry as a flavoring plant; this herb gives the smoke a coumarin-derived vanilla-like, herbal sweetness. Records indicate the blender changed this component around 2014 due to regulatory uncertainty. The flavor profile runs along a sweet, nutty line where the tobacco's own character stays in front, often compared to cinnamon French toast. Perique provides a spicy, fruity counterpoint. It carries no heavy top note. Suited to smokers wanting a sweetish Burley mixture without tipping into aromatic territory, who love the American style of all-day smoking.
hearth-home-capitol-stairs.o: Leaves a sweet, nutty aroma reminiscent of cinnamon French toast.

planta-empire-perique.z: Planta Empire Perique is a pipe tobacco blend for which there is not enough independent source material.
planta-empire-perique.o: Not enough records could be found on the room note.

just-for-him-grey-flannel.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for Just For Him's Grey Flannel, so the profile is left incomplete.

dobies-four-square-curlies-original.z: The "curly" designation in the name refers to tobaccos rolled and sliced into coin shapes. The Four Square series began in 1922 with George Dobie & Son in Paisley; no independent source documenting this particular blend's leaf composition could be found.

borkum-riff-mixture-with-bourbon-whiskey.z: Bourbon Whiskey is an aromatic blend in which ripe, sweet Virginia leaf and mellow Burley are combined through the Cavendish process, then topped with a coating evoking eight-year-aged bourbon whiskey. The whiskey note arrives warm and sharpish, without masking the tobacco's own sweetness. It's ribbon cut. In some markets it's sold as Bronze; the brand's whiskey-flavored product was reportedly renamed under this name. Nicotine stays medium-light. It suits smokers looking for a classic, non-fruited, liquor-flavored aromatic. The blend is produced in Denmark under Scandinavian Tobacco Group.
borkum-riff-mixture-with-bourbon-whiskey.o: Leaves a sweet, faintly sharp room note reminiscent of oak-aged whiskey.

a-c-petersen-caledonian-melange-no-10-hi.z: Caledonian Melange No.10 Highland Cream is the aromatic member of the Caledonian line produced for the Danish A & C Petersen. It's a ribbon-cut blend built from Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish; as a top layer it carries a creamy sweetness leaning toward whisky and vanilla. After the company passed to Orlik in 2000, the brand has continued under Scandinavian Tobacco Group and is distributed in 50-gram tins. Strength and flavor intensity are kept low, designed as a light Danish aromatic with a clear creamy side. It suits those getting acquainted with aromatic blends and those looking for a non-heavy, sweet everyday smoke.
a-c-petersen-caledonian-melange-no-10-hi.o: Leaves a sweet, faintly boozy room note reminiscent of vanilla cream and whisky.

buoy-mint.z: Buoy Mint is the green-coded branch of Rouseco's Buoy line produced in North Carolina, prepared by adding mint and menthol casing to American leaf. The fine-cut mixture gives a pronounced coolness in the smoke while keeping the leaf's dry, full-bodied taste underneath. A product aimed at those accustomed to menthol tobacco and seeking a cooling smoke. Because the casing is intense, when used in a pipe the bowl is expected to hold the mint aroma for a long time.
buoy-mint.o: Leaves a cool mint and menthol aroma with dry tobacco behind it.

john-middleton-inc-carter-hall.z: Carter Hall is one of the best-known American over-the-counter (OTC) classics. It's a ribbon-cut blend combining air-cured, cross-cut Burley with Virginia leaf, flavored just enough to stop short of being called an aromatic. The brand dates back to 1895; John Middleton has continued production since acquiring it from R.J. Reynolds in 1987. It packs and lights easily and burns cool. The start of the smoke gives a lightly sweet, fruity entry, with a nutty Burley taste emerging further in. Strength is kept low, making it suited to all-day smoking. A good fit for pipe newcomers, those wanting an easy-to-find, economical everyday tobacco, and anyone wanting to get to know plain Burley character.
john-middleton-inc-carter-hall.o: Leaves a nutty, lightly sweet, dry tobacco aroma.

sentimiento-nacional-el-restaurador-de-l.z: A Sentimiento Nacional blend named after a figure from Argentine history; no verifiable source on its content could be found.

mcclelland-black-parrot.z: Black Parrot is a Virginia-Perique mixture McClelland produced by reconstructing an old club blend. With its red-Virginia-forward body, it sits close to the same maker's slice-form Virginias. On first opening the tin, the Perique aroma comes forward, but the peppery push in the bowl stays measured; in this respect it offers a milder smoke than Perique-heavy blends. The smoke is full, the taste mild and balanced. Falls within the territory of those wanting Perique as a complementary element rather than a dominant one. Discontinued when McClelland closed; cellared tins have become a collector's item.
mcclelland-black-parrot.o: Leaves a spiced, faintly tangy fruit aroma.

peterson-holiday-season-2009.z: No sufficient sources giving composition information for the 2009 edition of Peterson's annual Holiday Season series could be found; the series' documented tins begin with the year 2010.

cornell-diehl-bijou.z: Bijou is a flake-cut Virginia mixture Cornell & Diehl prepares using vintage leaf. Its base is 2003-crop red Virginia grown in eastern North Carolina; light bright leaf and small-leafed Katerini Oriental are added. It is given a light honey casing on top, so the blend cannot be called unflavored, though it isn't aromatic either. Red Virginia's bready, fruity sweetness and Katerini's dry, incense-leaning spice form the blend's two axes; the honey casing leaves a thin sweetness that binds the two together. Nicotine strength is medium-to-high. The flake slices are noted as being amenable to aging, with long-term storage said to develop the character further. It suits smokers who want to trace the Virginia-Oriental relationship in a simple composition.
cornell-diehl-bijou.o: A honeyed sweetness accompanies an aroma reminiscent of dry grass and incense.

savinelli-brunello-flake.z: Brunello Flake is Savinelli's Virginia-based pressed blend. Sweet virginias are joined by burley and some Macedonian Oriental; the leaves are rested together before being pressed into flake so the flavors merge. Sold in 100-gram tins; the flakes are thick, even, and easily crumbled. The smoke opens with virginia's honeyed, lightly sour sweetness; the Oriental's spicy tone shows itself now and then, and the burley adds an oily body and a slow burn. The tin note brings out chestnut-brown spice and cooked-fruit notes. It can also be packed in ribbon form by crumbling. Suited to smokers seeking an unflavored or lightly flavored, medium-strength daily flake.
savinelli-brunello-flake.o: A light spicy hay note mixes into a honey-and-cooked-fruit scent.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-blackcurr.z: Referred to as a blackcurrant-flavored version within the Kendal Gold shag series; no reliable sourcing giving details specific to this version's composition and character could be found.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-blackcurr.o: Leaves a dark-fruit and sweet tobacco aroma.

chris-morgan-white-rabbit.z: Chris Morgan's White Rabbit is referred to in available records as an English-style mixture; not enough independent sourcing could be found to document its content and character.
chris-morgan-white-rabbit.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

brigadier-black-shermans-march.z: Sherman's March is the member of the Brigadier Black line that ties back to the American-type blend tradition. A casing evoking rum and maple is applied over a combination of soft, nutty burley and sweet Virginia leaf. The burley proportion gives the blend a dry body and medium nicotine; Virginia's sugar and the casing add a dark sweetness on top. The flavoring is kept at a level meant to frame rather than mask the tobacco's own taste. Suitable for fans of American-style burley blends seeking a lightly flavored everyday smoke.
brigadier-black-shermans-march.o: Leaves a dark, sugary aroma reminiscent of maple syrup and rum.

karl-erik-private-blend-no-12.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Karl Erik's Private Blend No.12.

gawith-hoggarth-co-lr3-coarse-cut.z: No verifiable sourcing could be found for this code-named product, said to be Virginia-based and part of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s coarse-cut line.
gawith-hoggarth-co-lr3-coarse-cut.o: Records indicate it leaves a plain, herbal tobacco aroma.

gladora-tobacco-blue-pearl.z: Blue Pearl is an aromatic flake in the Pesse Canoe series from Turkish producer Gladora. The brand states that all the Virginia, Oriental, and Latakia leaf it uses in its blends is sourced from tobacco grown in Turkey; the products were once available only in the Asia-Pacific market before entering US and European distribution in 2025, with European distribution handled through Germany's Kopp Tobaccos. A measured topping of vanilla, chocolate, and walnut is applied to a base built from Turkish Virginia, Oriental leaf, and Burley; the flake structure gives a slow, cool burn, letting the Oriental's dry spice show through beneath the topping. Suited to smokers who avoid heavy syrupy aromatics but still want to hear the Oriental character, and who are accustomed to preparing flake.
gladora-tobacco-blue-pearl.o: A creamy vanilla, cocoa, and roasted-walnut aroma mingles with the Oriental leaf's dry spice.

the-smoker-saratoga.z: A house blend called Saratoga from the American tobacconist The Smoker; records note it as Virginia-forward, but no independent source confirming its composition and character has been found.

erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-1931.z: The 4th Generation series uses the birth years of four generations in Erik Stokkebye's family (1855, 1897, 1931, 1957) as blend names; 1931 carries his father's year. This flake, sliced after pressing, is built mainly on American burley and aged American virginia with a small amount of black cavendish. The maker states the blend offers an unadulterated, natural smoke. Its character sits between burley's nutty, bready fullness and virginia's measured sweetness; the black cavendish acts as a cushion softening the edge. It suits smokers who enjoy rubbing out and loosening the flake, prefer a slow smoke, and want to get close to an unadulterated burley palate.
erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-1931.o: Leaves a slightly earthy scent reminiscent of dry walnut shell and baked bread crust.

larus-brother-company-inc-hi-plane.z: Hi-Plane is one of Larus & Brother Company's blends combining Virginia and Burley leaves. Records indicate deer tongue, a plant often used in old American pipe tobaccos, was added to the mix; since this plant contains coumarin, it gives the blend a natural sweetness reminiscent of vanilla and freshly cut grass. This achieves a lightly flavored character without becoming a syrupy aromatic. On the flavor axis, Burley's nutty, bready base sits alongside Virginia's sugar; body is medium. The blend was discontinued long ago and today is found only among the rare records in old stock tins. Of interest to those curious about the palate of mid-20th-century American shop blends.
larus-brother-company-inc-hi-plane.o: Leaves a sweet, hay-like room note with dry grass and a coumarin-derived vanilla tone.

mac-baren-roll-cake.z: Roll Cake is one of Mac Baren's rope-spun and sliced products. Whole Virginia leaves are used as the outer wrap; inside, a Virginia-forward core is set along with the maker's own Cavendish and a small, balancing amount of Burley. After the spun rope rests for a while, it's cut into thin coin shapes. This preparation method makes the tobacco slow-burning and dense; the coins need rubbing out before packing. The taste is built on Virginia's bready sweetness with the Cavendish's dark tones riding atop it.
