As with Mac Baren's rope products generally, only a thin maple-sugar topping is present, so the natural leaf taste leads rather than an aromatic character. Suited to patient smokers used to flake and coin cuts.
mac-baren-roll-cake.o: Leaves a sweetish hay and baked-bread aroma.

james-barber-wharfdale-mixture.z: A James Barber aromatic named after Wharfedale, the Yorkshire valley the brand originates from; no independent source could be found to document its composition.

gq-tobaccos-rum-honey.z: Rum & Honey is an aromatic carried by rum-steeped brown Burma tobacco. Alongside the Burma leaf come sweet golden Cavendish and black Cavendish; these two add a creamy texture and a light vanilla trace to the blend. Rum is also added to the mix, with honey sitting further back as a secondary topping. Spices such as cinnamon and nutmeg keep the sweetness from staying flat. Because of the Burma tobacco, it burns slowly and works more comfortably in wide-chambered pipes. Despite smoking cool, it sits high on nicotine — a blend that might look mild going by its sweet aroma but carries noticeable strength. Suited to smokers accustomed to nicotine who want to try aromatic flavors alongside the English Burma tradition.
gq-tobaccos-rum-honey.o: Leaves a warm aroma where rum-and-honey sweetness mixes with cinnamon and nutmeg spice.

peretti-park-square.z: Park Square is among Peretti's Virginia-forward blends and takes its name from the shop's Park Square address in Boston. Per the maker's description, red Virginia, matured Virginia, and steamed Virginia are used together, with a measured share of perique added on top to give the blend spice and depth. Having three distinct Virginia types side by side builds a layered sweetness no single Virginia could provide alone. The profile moves between the dark, bready side of stoved Virginia and the fruity side of red Virginia. It suits smokers who love unflavored Va-Per blends and want perique in a supporting rather than dominant role. Being ribbon cut, it needs no preparation.
peretti-park-square.o: Leaves a lightly peppery trace mingling with dried fruit and honey aromas.

samuel-gawith-traveller-s-dream.z: A Samuel Gawith product listed as Virginia-forward; no sufficient independent source describing its content, cut, and character could be found.
samuel-gawith-traveller-s-dream.o: No reliable description of its scent could be found.

paul-olsen-dark-plug.z: Dark Plug is the My Own Blend line's dark blend offered in pressed plug form. It contains Virginia, burley, and cavendish leaves along with a share of fire-cured Kentucky; the mixture is rested and compressed into rectangular blocks. Thin slices are cut from the plug with a knife and rubbed out in the palm before packing. Pressing and resting fuse the flavors together: burley gives an earthy, nutty base, Kentucky a smoky frame, and Virginia dark sweetness. In nicotine and fullness it sits above the mild blends; it suits those unafraid of working with plug tobaccos who want a slow, cool smoke.
paul-olsen-dark-plug.o: Leaves a dark, tartly sweet, lightly smoky scent recalling baked bread crust.

rona-obester-cavendish.z: A pipe tobacco recorded in Rona's Obester series, classified as aromatic; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

hu-tobacco-my-special-one.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the My Special One blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

king-street-coffee-tobacco-emporium-221-.z: One of the blends prepared over the counter at King Street Emporium in Martinsburg, West Virginia; no accessible source could be found describing its composition.
king-street-coffee-tobacco-emporium-221-.o: No verifiable information could be found regarding its scent.

petersen-sorensen-scottish-blend.z: This is one of the blends released under the Petersen & Sorensen name; no sufficient first-hand sources documenting its content and character could be found.
petersen-sorensen-scottish-blend.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

peter-stokkebye-black-cherry.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Black Cherry could be found.

briar-patch-king-solomons-mines.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named King Solomon's Mines under the Briar Patch brand could be found.

lane-limited-cherry-cavendish.z: A cherry-essence-flavored, cavendish-forward bulk aromatic. The cavendish process gives the tobacco a dark color, high moisture and a natural sweetness; the cherry note sits clearly atop this base. Nicotine is low, the smoke is cool and soft. It represents one of the best-known molds of the American bulk-aromatic tradition and is one of Lane Limited's staple products of this type. Suited to those wanting a sweet, easy-smoking blend rather than heavy latakia or sharp Virginia character; due to high moisture, airing it a while before lighting improves the burn.
lane-limited-cherry-cavendish.o: Leaves a sweet cherry and candied-fruit room note.

borkum-riff-genuine-pure-tobacco.z: Listed as one of Borkum Riff's seemingly unflavored versions; no adequate source on its composition and character could be found, leaving the profile incomplete.
borkum-riff-genuine-pure-tobacco.o: According to records it leaves a room note close to plain tobacco.

mcclelland-no-2040-cyprian-mixture.z: No. 2040 Cyprian Mixture is a full-bodied English mixture named for the Cyprian Latakia within it. Per McClelland's bulk catalog, the blend is built on a high proportion of Latakia, Oriental leaves, and Carolina Virginia. Latakia is the dominant component here; the Orientals give a spicy edge, and Virginia provides a faint sweetness underneath. Flavor intensity is high and the smoke is heavy. Nicotine runs above medium. Designed for smokers seeking traditional Latakia-forward English mixtures, using pipes reserved for long, slow smokes; it may prove heavy for smokers unaccustomed to Latakia. Unavailable since the brand closed in 2018.
mcclelland-no-2040-cyprian-mixture.o: Leaves an intense pine-smoke and soot aroma that lingers in the room.

park-lane-tobacconist-mr-mikes-blend.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Mr. Mike's Blend, one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

garfinkels-orient-express.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of Garfinkel's Orient Express pipe tobacco could be found.

cornell-diehl-bob-bushman.z: Bob Bushman takes its name from a private blend Cornell & Diehl prepared for a longtime customer. A ribbon-cut composition of black cavendish, burley, Oriental, perique, and Virginia leaf is topped with a flavoring evoking coconut and other tropical fruits. Per the manufacturer's classification, it belongs to the aromatic family. The flavoring is kept from overpowering the tobacco composition beneath it: perique lends a spicy accent, Oriental leaf a dry, grassy background, and burley provides body. Sitting on the light side for nicotine, it suits those looking for an all-day aromatic and smokers with an interest in tropically flavored blends.
cornell-diehl-bob-bushman.o: A light tobacco base accompanies the aroma of coconut and ripe tropical fruit.

synjeco-swiss-chocolate.z: Swiss Chocolate is a blend in Synjeco's own line, recorded as produced in England by Samuel Gawith. Roughly three percent Latakia and a chocolate flavoring are added over high-quality Virginias; small flake pieces appear within the ribbon cut. Because the latakia proportion is kept low, the smoke stays on the mild end of English blends; Virginia sweetness, the cocoa casing, and a fine smokiness proceed together. It suits smokers looking for a light English blend that can be smoked throughout the day, wanting a middle ground between aromatic and unflavored.
synjeco-swiss-chocolate.o: A light woody smoke accompanies a scent of cocoa and raisins.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-pennsylvania-dutch.z: Pennsylvania Dutch Treat is one of the oldest recipes of the Boswell family, who blend in their own shop in Chambersburg, Pennsylvania. Cavendish and burley leaf form the body; a measured cherry casing is applied on top. Per the manufacturer's description, J. M. Boswell built this blend at age twenty, and it has remained a fixture of the shop ever since. The burley base gives a nutty, satisfying foundation, while the cherry casing sits distinctly on top of it. Since moisture is not kept heavy, it lights easily and stays lit, leaving no wetness at the bottom of the bowl. Suits smokers who want an aromatic smoke while avoiding a syrupy texture, seeking a medium-bodied, evenly burning blend.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-pennsylvania-dutch.o: Leaves a light roasted-nut trace beneath a sweet cherry and baked dried-fruit aroma.

dobies-four-square-ready-rubbed-flake.z: This is a Four Square product presented rubbed out after being pressed and sliced; the series was launched in 1922 by George Dobie & Son in Paisley, Scotland. No independent source documenting this blend's leaf composition and character could be found.

cornell-diehl-plum-rum.z: No verifiable product description could be found for this Cornell & Diehl blend named Plum & Rum.

mcclelland-anniversary-1977-2017.z: Anniversary is a blend McClelland released in limited numbers for its founding anniversaries. The first batch was produced for the firm's 25th year in 2002 in roughly 3,000 tins, reissued in 2005 and 2010, and the fourth batch, stamped 1977-2017, was prepared for the 40th anniversary. Its contents hold red and stoved Virginia along with Cyprian Latakia; the cut is ribbon. On opening the tin, a light Latakia aroma stands out; the tangy tin note seen in the brand's other Virginia blends isn't pronounced in this product. In the smoke, Virginia's sweetness dominates, with Latakia giving a measured woody-herbal background; citrus and faintly spiced touches appear at the start, closing with a tangy-spiced finish. Strength is light-to-medium at first, rising to medium as the smoke proceeds. It produces plenty of smoke and tends toward tongue wetness with frequent puffing; given the low Latakia proportion, it's considered suitable for aging.
mcclelland-anniversary-1977-2017.o: A light, sooty Latakia aroma mixes with sweet Virginia and plentiful smoke.

vauen-tab21-piemont-blend.z: Piemont Blend is the aromatic blend that sits at number 21 in Vauen's numbered series, previously sold under the name red wine tobacco in the Horst Lichter collection; the named chef has also lent his name to several of the brand's pipe models. The composition includes golden Virginia, dark black Cavendish and Burley. The varying cut widths give a mellow, even burn. What sets the blend apart is its full-bodied red wine flavoring; sweetness is measured and nicotine is low. Suited to smokers after an aromatic along a wine-and-grape line.
vauen-tab21-piemont-blend.o: Leaves a sweetish aroma reminiscent of full-bodied red wine and raisins.

sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-maya.z: According to records, an aromatic blend in which Sentimiento Nacional flavors a Burley base with bitter cocoa; detailed composition information could not be substantiated with a verifiable source.

watch-city-cigar-stubbs-pipe.z: Watch City Cigar's blend called Stubb's Pipe is, according to records, one of the house blends of the Waltham, Massachusetts tobacconist shop; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

lane-limited-hoyo-de-monterrey.z: Not enough independent sources could be found documenting the contents and character of American blender Lane Limited's blend called Hoyo de Monterrey.

tsuge-premium-pipe-tobacco-raijin-the-th.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Tsuge Premium Pipe Tobacco blend Raijin - The Thunder God has been found.

mcclelland-oriental-mixture-no-12.z: Oriental Mixture No. 12 is among the higher numbers in McClelland's green-label Oriental series. Per retailer descriptions, it's built by adding a pronounced amount of Turkish tobacco and Latakia over matured Virginia leaves, making it one of the fuller-bodied entries in the series. The cut is ribbon, and it packs and burns without trouble. In the smoke, Virginia's sweetness comes first, followed by a woody, tangy-citrus layer and a faint note reminiscent of licorice root. The Latakia gives smoke but doesn't cover the blend; throughout the series, the Latakia weight is kept limited. Aimed at smokers seeking Oriental tobacco alongside measured Latakia, avoiding the heavy Latakia end of English blends. Discontinued when the brand closed in 2018.
mcclelland-oriental-mixture-no-12.o: A campfire-like sooty aroma is joined by citrus peel and a sweet caramel note.

gawith-hoggarth-co-black-cherry-twist.z: Sweet Black Cherry Twist is a rope-form tobacco Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. prepares by hand-twisting stoved Virginia leaf. It is essentially built on the twist called Brown Irish; black cherry essence is applied over it, an application that darkens the rope's colour. About five-millimetre coin slices are cut from the rope, rubbed out, and usually left to dry overnight. The smoke sits on top of a dark, earthy tobacco taste; the cherry topping stays light. Nicotine is moderate at first and rises noticeably toward the bottom of the bowl. It is aimed at smokers familiar with rope tobaccos and high-nicotine English twists.
gawith-hoggarth-co-black-cherry-twist.o: Leaves a light cherry aroma over dark, earthy tobacco.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-royal-p.z: An aromatic blend released under Ken Byron Ventures' Mr. Christian's line; no accessible source could be found to document its contents.

sutliff-tobacco-company-tobacco-galleria.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Sutliff Tobacco Company's Tobacco Galleria - Wild Cherry pipe tobacco could be found.

karl-erik-private-blend-no-17.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Karl Erik's Private Blend No.17.

rattray-brown-clunee.z: Brown Clunee is a blend combining fire-cured Virginia leaf with Kentucky and Perique, presented as broken flake. Its color is dark; the tin holds pieces in dark brown, brown, and lighter tan tones together. No casing or flavoring is used. Despite its dark appearance, its taste stays measured; the tin note is described as raisin, spice, and ripe plum. Rather than a sharp peppery accent, Perique deepens Virginia's sweetness, while Kentucky adds an earthy weight to the body. It suits smokers looking for an unflavored, medium-bodied Virginia-Perique flake.
rattray-brown-clunee.o: Leaves a dark tobacco aroma dominated by raisin and spice.

savinelli-jupiter.z: Jupiter is a mixture modeled on old-style burley blends. White and dark burley leaves are joined by red and light Virginia and some fire-cured Kentucky; a light dark-rum-and-molasses sauce is applied on top. Its character is nutty, earthy, and lightly spicy; Kentucky carries the smoke direction, molasses the sweetness. The blend's fullness is noticeable in nicotine. Suited to those seeking classic American-style mixtures built on burley with a measured casing. It is produced in the United States.
savinelli-jupiter.o: Leaves a scent of toasted hazelnut, molasses, and light rum.

robert-mcconnell-oxford-street.z: Oxford Street is an English blend built to traditional proportions. Latakia and Oriental leaf are layered onto a Virginia base; the leaves are lightly toasted during curing, which gives the blend a round, balanced flavor. The Latakia ratio is measured, so the smoke remains an accompanying note rather than a dominant one. This is a ribbon-cut, medium-bodied smoke with moderate nicotine and flavor, and a relatively light room note. It suits newcomers to English blends as well as those looking for a measured Latakia mixture they can smoke all day. Like the rest of the Heritage line, it is produced in Germany by Kohlhase & Kopp.
robert-mcconnell-oxford-street.o: Leaves a light wood-smoke and dry-spice aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-b-o-a-rum-aka-ha.z: Referred to as one of the rum-flavored private blends Sutliff produces to retailer order; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-b-o-a-rum-aka-ha.o: Records indicate it leaves a scent of rum and sugared oak.

torben-dansk-no-13-italian-style.z: Torben Dansk No.13 Italian Style is an aromatic blend called Italian-style in the brand's numbered series; no sufficient independent source describing its composition has been found.
torben-dansk-no-13-italian-style.o: Records describe it as leaving a sweetish aromatic aroma.

clan-shaw-honey-bee.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Honey Bee.

fincks-cigar-company-danish-black-gold.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for Finck's Cigar Company's Danish Black & Gold pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

cornell-diehl-spice-nut.z: No listing for Cornell & Diehl's Spice Nut blend could be found in the maker's current catalogue or in major retailer listings; its composition and character could not be confirmed.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-mixed-shag-aro.z: Kendal Mixed is the second of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s shag-cut main bodies. Unlike Kendal Gold's pure-Virginia structure, this body is built by adding Malawi-origin dark leaf and some fire-cured Kentucky to golden Virginia; because of this, its color is more mottled and its taste more earthy. This is the rose-flavored version of the Kendal Mixed body. Records indicate the floral taste gives a sweet impression reminiscent of Turkish delight, and is a typical example of the floral flavoring that defines Lakeland tradition. The fine cut burns fast, calling for a measured draw. Aimed at those curious about Lakeland-style floral blends.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-mixed-shag-aro.o: Leaves a floral aroma reminiscent of rosewater and Turkish delight.

cornell-diehl-sunday-picnic.z: Sunday Picnic is a pressed and sliced blend combining golden Virginia leaf with Louisiana Perique and Turkish Izmir tobacco. The tin note is full; the slices can be packed either rubbed out or folded. The smoke follows a complex path: sometimes the Izmir leaf's spicy, fig-like tone leads, sometimes Virginia sweetness dominates the base. Perique adds measured sharpness and body to the blend. It burns evenly and cool, with medium body. Suited to smokers looking for spicy-sweet Virginia mixtures.
cornell-diehl-sunday-picnic.o: Leaves a tangy tobacco scent carrying dried-fig and spice tones.

james-b-russell-ambassador.z: Ambassador is a mild blend in the tinned pipe tobacco line of James B. Russell, a company that operated in New Jersey for many years. Its composition includes Virginia leaf, Oriental (Turkish) tobaccos, and black Cavendish; because the black Cavendish share raises the blend's sugar balance, the flavor leans sweet without drifting into heavy aromatic territory. Nicotine load is low, and the smoke stays mild. The company operated as a tobacco importer and distributor in the United States, first based in New York and later in New Jersey; when it ceased operations, the blends in this line were withdrawn from the market as well. Ambassador suits those looking for a light, balanced tin tobacco that can be smoked all day, as well as newcomers wanting to get acquainted with the aroma of Oriental leaf. Today it can only be found via old tins.
james-b-russell-ambassador.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma of dry hay and baked bread.

the-smoker-civil-war.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the content and character of The Smoker's Civil War pipe tobacco could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-black-whiskey-51.z: Referred to as a tobacco-forward Sutliff aromatic where whiskey is processed into the leaf itself rather than applied as a top flavoring; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-black-whiskey-51.o: Records indicate it leaves a scent of whiskey and dark oak.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-peaches-and-crea.z: Peaches and Cream is an aromatic mixture referred to among the house blends of the McGahey tobacconist; no verifiable source regarding its composition and cut could be found.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-peaches-and-crea.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet aroma in the direction of peach and cream.

thepiperoom-com-black-watch.z: No independent source confirming the composition of ThePipeRoom.com's Scottish-style blend Black Watch has been found; the brand's own site is no longer online.
thepiperoom-com-black-watch.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

hu-tobacco-chinas-heaven.z: China's Heaven is a flavored blend in HU Tobacco's The Blender's Pride line. Medium-bodied Virginia leaves are prepared ready-rubbed, backed by Burley, and flavored with a mandarin-and-coconut-forward aroma; the described aroma notes also include vanilla, cinnamon, and floral accents. The blend builds a structure suited to everyday smoking, where the floral, fruity flavoring doesn't suppress the tobacco base. It's an uncomplicated option for those who smoke flavored blends but avoid heavy syrupiness. Records indicate it was sold in 100-gram tins.
hu-tobacco-chinas-heaven.o: A light floral tail accompanies the aroma of sweet coconut and citrus peel.

the-tobacco-barn-butter-rum.z: No sufficient source describing the composition and character of this aromatic, listed as "Black Velvet - Butter Rum" in the medium-to-dark toasted Cavendish group of Tobacco Barn's house blend list, has been found.

dan-tobacco-midnight-ride.z: Midnight Ride is the English blend in Dan Tobacco's series referencing American history, named for Paul Revere's 1775 night ride. Virginia grades from three separate growing regions are combined with Oriental tobaccos and Cyprus Latakia, topped with a small amount of Perique. The Latakia proportion is noticeable; the blend gives a slow-burning, cool, smoky-spicy smoke. The Virginia's sweetness forms a base beneath the Latakia and Oriental tobaccos, while the Perique adds a peppery sharpness. No casing is used, so the flavor comes entirely from the leaf composition. Suited to smokers accustomed to classic Latakia-heavy English blends looking for one long smoke during the day; not considered a starter blend for those unfamiliar with the scent of Latakia.
dan-tobacco-midnight-ride.o: Leaves a long-lingering scent where wood-fire smoke mingles with spicy Oriental tobacco.

cornell-diehl-mild-english.z: No adequate source documenting the composition and character of Cornell & Diehl's Mild English blend could be found; the blend isn't in the maker's current catalogue.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-lanes-blen.z: Match Lane's Blend 11 was prepared to correspond to Lane Limited's classic aromatic of the same name. Burley, Virginia, and Green River black cavendish are used together; a marshmallow-forward light casing with a small whisky note is applied over them. Burley gives a toasted, nutty base with a light molasses tone; Virginia carries a somewhat grassy, citrusy edge, and the black cavendish provides a very soft vanilla. The casing isn't dominant, and the tastes intertwine. It burns cool with low tendency to leave sediment at the bottom of the bowl. It suits smokers looking for a light, trouble-free everyday aromatic.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-lanes-blen.o: Leaves a scent of sweet marshmallow and vanilla.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-derby-s.z: Derby Shag is a blend prepared from bright Virginia leaf rested for over a decade, cut into a very fine shag. The maker states the leaf is matured with a casing of Woodford Reserve bourbon, floral honey, and a touch of mint, that the product is offered moist for ease of storage, and that its fine cut means it needs to be dried out before smoking. The brand notes it's the series' last aged shag and that the blend isn't an aromatic aimed at a particular room note; it was offered as 2 oz. bulk. The long rest settles Virginia's tang and brings a dark-fruit and honey line to the front; the bourbon and mint stay in the background of that structure. The shag cut burns fast, so it calls for a slow draw and a small bowl. Aimed at smokers interested in aged Virginia who are used to working with a fine cut.
ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-derby-s.o: Leaves a tobacco aroma carrying a cool mint trace alongside honey and bourbon.

reiver-pipes-tobacco-heather-braes.z: Heather Braes is an unflavored mixture weighted toward Izmir Oriental leaf, rounded out with red Virginia, white Burley, and Louisiana Perique. The Oriental leaf sits at the center of the blend, building a dry, floral-spicy frame; Virginia adds sweetness, Burley body, and Perique a twist of pepper and dried fruit. With no Latakia present, the result is a spicy rather than smoky profile. It appeals to fans of Oriental-forward blends who want something more complex than a straight Virginia without Latakia. Reiver Pipes & Tobacco is a small-scale blending operation; its mixtures are prepared by Dan Armstrong and carry names referencing the border reiver tradition.
reiver-pipes-tobacco-heather-braes.o: Leaves a dry-hay and spice aroma with a light floral note.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-christmas-cookie.z: Christmas Cookie is one of Dan Boswell's earliest blends, completed in November 2002. Per the manufacturer's account, the blend was released for Christmas 2002 after seven months of trials, and despite being planned as a seasonal product, it turned into a year-round item due to demand. The blend is prepared by hand, with care taken for each leaf to keep its own character. Its body is light, the smoke soft; no tongue bite is reported. True to its name, the casing is built in a direction evoking sweet baked goods. Suitable for smokers seeking a light, sweet aromatic with a pronounced room aroma.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-christmas-cookie.o: Leaves an aroma of cinnamon cookies fresh out of the oven.

gawith-hoggarth-co-burley-bright.z: Burley & Bright is a thin-ribbon-cut blend prepared by adding nutty Burley to a base heavy in light-coloured Virginia. It carries a light vanilla-based sauce and a fine cocoa-like tone; since the topping dose is kept low, the blend sits somewhere between topped and untopped tobaccos. The cut is finer than average, which makes it easy to fill. The presence of Burley makes the smoke cooler than pure Virginia and reduces the tendency to bite the tongue. The taste is flat and mild; light Virginia's grassy sweetness and Burley's dry, nutty base run side by side. The nicotine load is light to medium and suits all-day smoking. This is a good record for those steering clear of heavy topped aromatics but still wanting a subtle sweetness, as well as those new to the pipe.
gawith-hoggarth-co-burley-bright.o: A light cocoa and vanilla aroma is accompanied by a dry-grass note.

the-danish-pipe-shop-pure-virginia-flake.z: Pure Virginia Flake is the unflavored Virginia flake The Danish Pipe Shop releases under its own name. The scent of the slices carries typical Virginia character: a lively, bright, citrus-leaning air. On the smoke, a grassy, hay-like base is reported, joined by a measured sweetness with a subtle cedar note in the background. No casing is used; the taste comes entirely from the leaf itself. It sits on the same line as plain Virginia slices like Samuel Gawith Full Virginia Flake or Dunhill Flake, so it suits those used to preparing flake and to unflavored Virginia smoking.
the-danish-pipe-shop-pure-virginia-flake.o: Leaves a dry, sweetish aroma leaning toward dry hay and lemon peel.

exclusiv-wild-mango.z: Wild Mango is one of the fruity members of the Exclusiv aromatic line prepared by Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. in Kendal. Like the line's other blends, it is built on a base of Virginia leaf and black cavendish; the cavendish process softens the leaf and lets the flavouring take hold. The flavouring centres on mango and stays clearly within the tropical-fruit line; the tobacco's own taste stays in the background as a sweet base. Nicotine load is light while the aroma intensity is high. It is sold in the United Kingdom loose by weight, in 25- and 50-gram packs. It suits smokers looking for a fruit beyond the usual vanilla and cherry flavourings.
exclusiv-wild-mango.o: Leaves a tropical, ripe-mango aroma with a lightly sweet toasted-leaf note behind it.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.z: This is the honey-flavored version of the Cândido Giovanella line, produced by Imigrantes Fumos in Brazil. The blend is built on Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish; it's presented ribbon cut in small resealable packs. In the smoke, honey's floral, intense sweetness brings out the Virginia's natural sugar; Burley establishes a dry balance in the background. The smoke is cool, the nicotine load low. It suits those looking for a mild, distinctly sweet aromatic, and those new to aromatic blends.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.o: Leaves an aroma of honey and warm sugar.

w-o-larsen-larsens-choice.z: No reliable source could be found regarding the composition and character of this Danish blend bearing the W.Ø. Larsen name.
w-o-larsen-larsens-choice.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

ashton-rainy-day.z: Rainy Day is a ribbon-cut aromatic built from Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish leaf. The blend's distinguishing feature is that after preparation it's rested for about a month in whiskey barrels; this process gives the tobacco a woody, sweet layer from the barrel. In the flavor description, tropical fruit, toasted nuts, and notes close to barrel wood stand out. The dry body from the Burley keeps the blend from being purely a sweet aromatic and pulls its strength to medium. It suits smokers looking for barrel-rested aromatics with relatively measured flavoring.
ashton-rainy-day.o: Leaves a room note leaning toward tropical fruit, oak barrel, and toasted nuts.

sutliff-tobacco-company-spicey-vanilla-z.z: Z91 Spicey Vanilla is a vanilla- and spice-cased blend among Sutliff's Z-series aromatics; no reliable source on its leaf composition and cut could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-spicey-vanilla-z.o: Leaves a scent of vanilla and spice.

peretti-ebony.z: This is one of the house blends of the L. J. Peretti shop in Boston; it appears under the Cavendish blends heading in the maker's list. The profile is left incomplete, as no published description of the blend's content and character could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-504c-aromatic-en.z: Sutliff 504C Aromatic English is a ribbon-cut bulk blend combining the softness of an aromatic built on black cavendish and burley with the smoky depth latakia provides. The maker's description characterizes it as both an "aromatic English" and a "leathery aromatic," describing it as standing at the intersection of the two categories. The latakia ratio isn't high enough to turn the blend into a heavy English mixture; black cavendish's sweetness remains felt beneath the smoke throughout. Suited to those wanting a soft entry point into latakia blends and to those trying to move from aromatics into the English category. Since moisture runs high, letting it sit before packing changes the burning balance.
sutliff-tobacco-company-504c-aromatic-en.o: A light sweet undertone accompanies a smoky scent reminiscent of smoke and leather.

samuel-gawith-black-xx-twist-rope.z: Black XX Twist (Rope) is an unflavored Kendal product produced by twisting dark Virginia leaf into rope form. Thin coins cut from the rope are packed into the pipe after airing; the burn is finicky and requires a very slow smoke. Nicotine level is, according to records, very high; by contrast the smoke is cool, intense, and the tobacco flavor full. A few coin-loads are enough in small-chambered pipes. Suited to experienced smokers accustomed to high-nicotine, unflavored, rope-cut tobaccos.
samuel-gawith-black-xx-twist-rope.o: Fills the room with a sharp, smoky, heavy tobacco scent.

sutliff-tobacco-company-raspberry-burley.z: Raspberry Burley is an unusual aromatic in Sutliff's bulk line: sharp Latakia is added alongside selected burley leaf, with a sweet raspberry essence applied over the mixture. This brings a fruity topping and a smoky base together in the same blend. Burley's nutty dryness and Latakia's smoke balance the fruit sweetness, carrying the blend to a fuller place than most aromatics. It is aimed at smokers who like cased tobacco but want a smoke that isn't fully sugary.
sutliff-tobacco-company-raspberry-burley.o: A light smoky, dry-earth scent can be sensed beneath the raspberry sweetness.

w-o-larsen-collectors-blend.z: Collectors Blend, part of the series W.Ø. Larsen offers in collector's tins, is described as a light aromatic made by adding black cavendish and a small amount of Kentucky to light Virginias; sources on the blend's details are limited.
w-o-larsen-collectors-blend.o: No reliable information could be found regarding the room note.

two-friends-deacons-downfall.z: Deacon's Downfall is a ribbon-cut English blend sitting on the dark side of the Two Friends line. Turkish Latakia, black Cavendish, toasted Virginia leaves and Oriental leaf are joined by pure St. James Perique; this setup gives the blend a dark body and a sharp spicy edge. The Perique cuts through Latakia's smoky weight and lends the blend a plummy, peppery liveliness; the toasted Virginia leaves a dark sweetness underneath. Nicotine stays medium while flavor intensity is high, making it better suited to a slower pace and long sittings. A profile aimed at smokers who know the Latakia-Perique pairing and want a full-bodied English blend.
two-friends-deacons-downfall.o: A peppery, sharp edge cuts through the heavy wood-smoke and leather aroma.

l-l-bean-tobacco-beans-special-blend.z: Tobacco Beans Special Blend is a record left over from the years when Maine-based L.L. Bean sold pipes and tobacco in its catalog. Per the recipe on the box, the medium-cut blend consists of nine measures of white Burley and three measures of flavored Burley; it contains no other tobacco type. Given its Burley-forward makeup, the smoke carries a dry, low-sugar, slow-burning character, with a low tendency to bite the tongue. Nicotine and flavor intensity are moderate, making it a plain American blend suited to smoking all day. Since the brand stopped selling tobacco, the product is no longer in production and appears only in collector tins today.
l-l-bean-tobacco-beans-special-blend.o: Leaves a warm tobacco room note toward dry hay and light cocoa.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-sail-green.z: Match Sail Green was prepared to correspond to the green-packaged version of the Dutch-origin Sail line. Bright Virginia leaf is combined with Oriental tobaccos, burley, and black cavendish; a small amount of latakia is added over it. The blend is given a light anise note, positioning it as a cased English mixture. Because the latakia proportion is kept low, the smoke stays in the background; the Oriental's spicy edge and Virginia's sweetness lead. Nicotine is light and taste intensity is medium. It suits those wanting to get to know the English style without moving to heavy Balkan mixtures, or looking for a balanced blend to smoke all day.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-sail-green.o: Leaves a faint anise scent mixed into a lightly smoky tobacco aroma.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-cherry-cavendish.z: No sufficient source could be found documenting the composition and character of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Cherry Cavendish.

bengal-slices-bengal-slices-white.z: Bengal Slices is a Latakia-forward crumble-cake blend dating back to the late 1970s. Records say the original product was pressed by Sobranie for James B. Russell, with the matured cakes cut into slices; the blend was withdrawn from the market in the mid-1980s. The name and recipe were revived in 2015 by Standard Tobacco Company of Pennsylvania, and the blend was rebuilt by Russ Ouellette. The White version, joining the family in 2019, carries less Latakia than the original recipe and contains no added flavoring. Sweet golden Virginia leaf and Oriental seasoning form the blend's backbone; Latakia here isn't dominant, standing instead as a layer providing smoky, woody depth. Black Cavendish rounds out the sweetness. Since it comes as a pressed cake, the slice is rubbed out before packing; moisture control and slow smoking bring out the leaf's sugary tones. It suits smokers who want Latakia in moderation and follow unflavored English-style blends.
bengal-slices-bengal-slices-white.o: Leaves a room note of smoky wood and dry spice.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-drexel-vi.z: Drexel is a series of affordably priced pouch tobaccos; no reliable detail on the composition of blend VIII could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-drexel-vi.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay and light spice.

hausmarken-no-21-elizabeth.z: Elizabeth, entry No. 21 in the Special Line series, is a medium-bodied mixture modeled on English blending tradition. Sweet Virginia and broken Virginia carrying a citrusy note form the body; full black Cavendish adds softness, Oriental leaf brings spice, and a small amount of Latakia adds measured smokiness. The blend is described as similar in construction to the discontinued Dunhill Elizabethan Mixture. Since Latakia is kept low, it stays far from the weight of dark English blends; suited to smokers seeking the balance between Virginia sweetness and light smoke, in an everyday blend where the topping remains subtle.
hausmarken-no-21-elizabeth.o: Leaves a lemon-peel and sweet-tobacco aroma over a lightly smoky base.

missouri-meerschaum-creeper-of-the-corn.z: Creeper of the Corn is a limited-production aromatic Missouri Meerschaum prepared for the Halloween season. A burley and black cavendish base is topped with a sauce evoking rum and cinnamon-raisin. The blend is mostly ribbon cut, with the black cavendish present in a coarser cut. It comes out of the tin with high moisture and needs to be aired out before smoking. Since its nicotine load stays below medium, it's geared toward those looking for a seasonal, sweet aromatic.
missouri-meerschaum-creeper-of-the-corn.o: Leaves an aroma of cinnamon-raisin bun and rum.

tordenskjold-extra-light.z: Tordenskjold Extra Light is described as a light aromatic in the Danish tradition; no independent source confirming the blend's composition has been found.
tordenskjold-extra-light.o: No reliable source describing the room note has been found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-special-d.z: No sufficient primary source describing Special Dublin Danish Mixture's composition and character could be found.

watch-city-cigar-persian-slipper.z: Watch City Cigar's blend called Persian Slipper is, according to records, one of the house blends of the Waltham, Massachusetts tobacconist shop; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

cornell-diehl-star-of-the-east-flake.z: Star of the East Flake is the pressed, sliced form of the ribbon-cut blend of the same name. The recipe again rests on half Cyprus Latakia; Turkish Izmir leaf adds spice, and lightly stoved red Virginia adds dark sweetness. Pressing lets the leaves' flavors meld over time, giving a slower, more intense smoke once the slices are rubbed out or folded for packing. It has a full-bodied, unflavored, distinctly smoky character; aimed at smokers accustomed to Latakia who know how to work with flake tobacco.
cornell-diehl-star-of-the-east-flake.o: A dry spice and sweet tobacco tone mingle with an intense wood-smoke scent.

sutliff-tobacco-company-archduke-ferdina.z: Archduke Ferdinand, part of Sutliff's Private Stock line, is described as a light-to-medium-strength aromatic. Named after Austro-Hungarian history, the blend is one of the line's Central European-themed names. It's ribbon cut and prepared for bulk sale. Records indicate a layered structure was aimed for rather than a one-dimensional sweetness; cavendish sweetness is set over a Virginia and burley base. Nicotine level is low. Suited to smokers who smoke aromatics but want a measured topping. The blend is no longer in production.
sutliff-tobacco-company-archduke-ferdina.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, lightly spiced tobacco scent.

straus-tobacco-ault-park.z: An aromatic house blend from Straus Tobacconist taking its name from Ault Park in Cincinnati; records describe it as full-bodied with a vanilla-cream taste, but no detailed source describing the leaf composition could be found.
straus-tobacco-ault-park.o: Leaves a sweet scent reminiscent of vanilla cream.

bennington-tobacconist-no-46-strawberry-.z: No. 46 Strawberry Fields is one of Bennington Tobacconist's aromatic shop blends. As the name suggests, the dominant topping is strawberry; the base, as with the brand's other aromatics, rests on flavored black Cavendish along with mellow Virginia and Burley leaf. In blends of this type, the tobacco's own taste stays in the background, with the fruit topping and Cavendish's sugar taking the lead. Nicotine and body are kept low, allowing for long smoking sessions. It's aimed at smokers looking for fruited aromatics or those new to the pipe. Since heavily topped tobaccos can run moist, it should be aired for a while before packing and smoked slowly.
bennington-tobacconist-no-46-strawberry-.o: A pronounced strawberry-jam note is joined by a sweet Cavendish syrup.

mcclelland-rsvp-invitation.z: RSVP Invitation is one of the aromatic blends McClelland supplied to retailers in bulk under the Avenue Blend heading. Its Cavendish-forward body is flavored, but the topping level is kept measured enough not to fully mask the tobacco taste; sources describe it as a mild aromatic that preserves the tobacco flavor. Strength is low, and the ribbon cut makes packing and lighting easy. Suited to those who don't want heavy Latakia or intense Virginia smokes and who want a light aromatic at any time of day. The blend was discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018. A detailed content breakdown isn't given explicitly in the records.

de-la-concha-marbella.z: This is one of the aromatic shop blends from the De La Concha tobacconist; no independent source describing its composition could be found.
de-la-concha-marbella.o: No reliable record could be found for the room note.

cornell-diehl-golden-days-of-yore.z: Golden Days of Yore is a mixture first released as Cornell & Diehl's Christmas blend in 2015 and periodically reissued since. Its base contains burley, fire-cured Kentucky, red and bright Virginia, black cavendish, and Greek Katerini leaf, topped with notes of cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, chocolate, and dark rum. Though the flavoring list is long, the application is light, so the blend leans closer to a spiced natural-tobacco profile than a heavy aromatic. On the smoke, citrus tang, woody and sweet-grass notes, a background of toast and dried fruit, and a measured peppery edge on the retrohale all appear. It suits those looking for a spice-forward seasonal blend where the flavoring stays understated.
cornell-diehl-golden-days-of-yore.o: Leaves a warm, spiced sweet aroma mixing cinnamon, nutmeg, and chocolate.

borkum-riff-red-cavendish.z: One of Borkum Riff's regional Cavendish-based offerings referred to by color names; no adequate source on its content and flavoring could be found.

newminster-no-48-danish-gold.z: Newminster No. 48 Danish Gold is a Danish-style aromatic prepared by combining bright Virginia leaves with soft black Cavendish. The blend is given a warm, sweet caramel note with a subtle fruit combination layered beneath it. The ribbon-cut, bulk-sold blend offers a light-bodied, low-nicotine smoke. The caramel's sweetness is kept measured enough not to cover Virginia's natural sugar. Suitable for those looking for a moderately flavored Danish aromatic that can be smoked throughout the day.
newminster-no-48-danish-gold.o: Leaves a warm caramel and light fruit aroma in the room.

cornell-diehl-junkyard-dawg.z: Junkyard Dawg is a reinterpretation following in the footsteps of the old American counter blend Barking Dog. Bright Virginia and Latakia are added to a Burley base, presented in broken flake form; it carries no casing. On the smoke, Burley's cool, nutty texture, Virginia's sweetness, and a light background Latakia smoke move together in balance. Body sits between mild and medium. Suited to those not wanting intense Latakia but looking for a classic American Burley smoke with a smoky touch.
cornell-diehl-junkyard-dawg.o: A measured Latakia smoke mingles with a nutty Burley scent.

wellauer-co-latakia-mixture.z: Wellauer & Co's Latakia Mixture is, according to records, one of the blends carrying the Swiss tobacconist house's name; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

clan-shaw-casablanca.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of Clan Shaw's Casablanca blend could be found.

vauen-no-20-italian-blend.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Vauen pipe tobacco called No. 20 Italian Blend to record the blend's composition and character.

fribourg-treyer-cut-virginia-plug.z: Cut Virginia Plug is a pure Virginia blend prepared under the British Fribourg & Treyer name by the German producer Kohlhase & Kopp. The plug, matured under pressure, is cut into mottled slices ranging from light yellow to dark brown; records indicate the leaves used are drawn from Brazilian, Indian, and African Virginias. A very light fruit-citrus-and-vanilla sauce is applied over it; this topping is more noticeable in the tin aroma than in the smoke, so the blend does not count as fully aromatic.
fribourg-treyer-cut-virginia-plug.o: Leaves a tart dry-grass aroma mixed with light citrus and sweet cream.

ken-byron-ventures-mycroft-2021.z: A blend released as part of Ken Byron Ventures' small-batch production; no independent, verifiable source could be found on it.

peretti-yuletide-2018.z: The 2018 edition of Yuletide brings back the plum note seen in earlier years of the series. Records indicate the flavoring is applied with a noticeably heavier hand onto a base of Virginia and Cavendish leaf; in this respect it is a more sweetened blend than the 2015 edition. The Cavendish proportion softens the smoke and increases sweetness, while Virginia holds the acid balance underneath. It suits smokers seeking a plum-forward, seasonal, medium-intensity aromatic.
peretti-yuletide-2018.o: Leaves a stewed plum and dark sugar aroma.

iwan-ries-old-colonial.z: This is an aromatic blend that appears in Iwan Ries catalogs; no independent source describing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
iwan-ries-old-colonial.o: No room note described in the records could be found.

peterson-special-reserve-2012.z: Special Reserve 2012 is a limited edition blend released as part of Peterson's Special Reserve series specific to that year; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient first-hand sources confirming its content and character could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-pina-colada-2009.z: Pina Colada is an aromatic listed under the code SPS-2009 in Sutliff's SPS bulk series. Like the cocktail it is named after, it carries a casing leaning toward pineapple, coconut, and rum; records indicate the base is black-cavendish-forward, softened with Virginia and burley, and ribbon cut. It is aimed at aromatic smokers looking for a low-nicotine, sweet, fruity summer smoke. Because the series number became part of the blend's name, it is also listed in catalogs as "Pina Colada 2009."
sutliff-tobacco-company-pina-colada-2009.o: Leaves a tropical trace of pineapple, coconut, and a light rum scent.

hu-tobacco-khoisaan.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Khoisaan, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

sir-william-sweet.z: A record of a flavored aromatic blend referred to under the name Sir William Sweet; no source specifying the toppings used could be found.
sir-william-sweet.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

e-a-carey-old-town-vanilla-flake.z: As the name suggests, this is a vanilla-flavored, flake-cut E. A. Carey blend; it does not appear on the maker's current list, and not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition.

hu-tobacco-jerry-saronno.z: Jerry Saronno is a pronouncedly flavored blend in HU Tobacco's United Passion line. Its base is a ready-rubbed flake prepared from Philippine-origin Virginia leaves; the flavoring is built on cherry and amaretto. On opening the tin, ripe cherry is the first thing noticed; amaretto adds a bitter-almond layer. The medium-bodied Virginia base carries the flavoring while not letting the tobacco taste disappear entirely. It's aimed at those looking for a fruity, liqueur-evoking flavored blend. Records indicate it's presented in 50-gram tins.
hu-tobacco-jerry-saronno.o: Leaves an intense sweet aroma reminiscent of ripe cherry and amaretto liqueur.

peterson-nutty-cut.z: Nutty Cut is a ribbon-cut aromatic produced in Germany. Gold, red, and dark Virginia leaves are combined in different cuts, with the blend rounded out by Burley and black Cavendish. It is topped with a flavoring giving coconut, macadamia, and rum notes. The blend was reportedly later released on the market under the name Peterson Special Cut. It has a moderate nicotine strength and a sweetness-forward structure; it is aimed at smokers seeking nutty, creamy aromatics and wanting a mild blend for long smoking sessions through the day.
peterson-nutty-cut.o: A sweet coconut and toasted hazelnut aroma is joined by a light rum note.

pfeifen-huber-earl-grey-mixture-huber.z: Sold under the Pfeifen Huber name, this is an aromatic house blend that, judging by its name, carries a bergamot-leaning Earl Grey flavoring; no sufficient sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

cornell-diehl-virginia-oriental.z: No listing for Cornell & Diehl's Virginia Oriental blend could be found in the maker's current catalogue or in major retailer listings; its ratios and character could not be confirmed.

just-for-him-reeds-weed.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Just For Him's Reed's Weed blend.

robert-mcconnell-pure-100-cuba.z: There is not enough independent source material on Pure 100% Cuba, cited as one of Robert McConnell's cigar-leaf-based blends.

affordable-pipes-orient-express.z: No reliable source sufficient to establish the content and character of Orient Express, a blend from Affordable Pipes, could be found.

doctor-xious-blends-no-30-midnight-strol.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of No.30 Midnight Stroll, a pipe tobacco from Doctor Xious Blends.
doctor-xious-blends-no-30-midnight-strol.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

cornell-diehl-christmas-blend-2015-golde.z: This is Cornell & Diehl's limited-quantity 2015 holiday blend; though noted as Virginia-forward, not enough sourcing could be found to verify its composition.

mac-baren-7-seas-royal-blend.z: 7 Seas Royal Blend is the member of Mac Baren's American-style aromatic series that uses both golden and dark leaves together. Steam-processed black cavendish is added alongside yellow Virginias and soft burley; the blend is loose-cut. On the flavor side, vanilla, honey and light fruit notes stand out; these casings support rather than suppress Virginia's natural sugar. It offers a smoke that's light in nicotine and soft yet not flat in body. Suited to smokers who stay on the aromatic side but want a blend where the tobacco taste can still be followed.
mac-baren-7-seas-royal-blend.o: Leaves a sweet room note toward vanilla, honey and light fruit.

mike-russ-the-mind-meld-sweet-english.z: Sweet English is a member of the Mind Meld line, prepared jointly by Mike McNiel of McClelland and blender Russ Ouellette. According to the seller's description, matured Virginia leaves, soft Cavendish, and Cyprus latakia come together to build a structure balanced between sweet and smoky. The line was designed around the idea of bringing the aromatic and English mixture traditions together in the same blend; Sweet English therefore forms common ground for aromatic smokers taking their first step toward latakia blends and English-mixture smokers looking for a sweeter smoke. Its body is medium. The line was withdrawn from the market after McClelland closed in 2018.
mike-russ-the-mind-meld-sweet-english.o: Leaves a wood-smoke aroma alongside a sweet undertone.

van-erkoms-navy-cut-aromatic-flake.z: A navy cut flake bearing the Van Erkoms name, produced in South Africa's Limpopo region, apparently flavored as its name suggests; no independent source documenting the blend's composition and character has been found, so the record is left incomplete.

mcclelland-vanilla-black-cavendish.z: Vanilla Black Cavendish is one of McClelland's simply structured aromatics sold in bulk. Its base is black Cavendish darkened by steam processing, topped with vanilla flavoring; the blend contains no heavy leaves like Latakia or Oriental. Discontinued when the company closed in 2018. Nicotine load is low, the smoke is mild, and the burn is cool; the flavor consists largely of vanilla and Cavendish's sugary roundness, with the leaf character staying in the background. Suited to smokers new to the pipe and to those seeking a mild, sweet, distinctly scented aromatic.
mcclelland-vanilla-black-cavendish.o: Leaves a sweet, bakery-like aroma reminiscent of vanilla homemade cookies.

two-friends-bed-breakfast.z: Two Friends is an American blend line jointly founded by Cornell & Diehl's founder Craig Tarler and G.L. Pease; Bed & Breakfast sits in the line's English wing. In the ribbon-cut blend, red and light Virginia leaves are the carrier; Oriental leaf, toasted Cavendish and a small amount of Latakia are added on top. Because the Latakia proportion is kept low, the smoke side isn't dominant, acting instead as an accompaniment that frames the Virginia sweetness. Nicotine and flavor intensity stay in the medium range, making it suited to smoking spread through the day rather than leaning on a single sitting. A measured entry point for smokers new to Latakia or after a light English character.
two-friends-bed-breakfast.o: Gives an aroma that moves between wood smoke and dry hay, leaving a sweetish dried-fruit trace behind.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-pigtail.z: Sweet Pigtail is a pigtail-type Burma tobacco produced by twisting dark fire-cured leaves into a fine rope. It's traditionally sold both as chewing tobacco and for pipe smoking; because of its thin diameter it's used cut into small discs, and the cut surface shows a dark reddish-brown color in direct light. The pouch aroma is oily and spicy. On the smoke, the earthy, smoky core of the fire-curing runs alongside the sweet topping applied during production. Since it doesn't go through a pressure-cooking stage, it stays intense in nicotine; it needs to be thinly sliced and smoked slowly. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. is one of the English producers that continues traditional twist (rope) production at its Kendal factory, hand-twisting fire-cured leaves into rope form. Because twist tobaccos don't go through a pressure-cooking stage, they stay intense in nicotine; records indicate these ropes are sold for both chewing and pipe smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-pigtail.o: Leaves an aroma adding a fine sugary sweetness over spicy, oily tobacco.

savorys-oxford-oxford-memory.z: According to records, an old English blend connected to the Oxford branch of H. L. Savory & Co., founded in London in 1885; no sufficient independent source describing its content and character could be found.
savorys-oxford-oxford-memory.o: No reliable description of its scent could be found.

bosphorus-virginia-perique-flake.z: Virginia & Perique Flake is Bosphorus's flake-cut blend built from golden virginia and perique. The slices are cut thicker than usual, and the product is offered moist; drying it briefly before smoking, and using the Z-fold method when filling flake, gives a balanced smoke. Its character rests on the balance between a sweet, lightly tart virginia base and perique's spicy, grassy, woody note. The perique proportion is pronounced but does not cover the virginia; the two components take turns coming forward through the smoke. Suitable for smokers accustomed to flake filling, seeking a Virginia/Perique with no casing or one barely perceptible.
bosphorus-virginia-perique-flake.o: Leaves a lightly woody tobacco aroma accompanied by dried fruit and spice.

exclusiv-black-cherry.z: Exclusiv Black Cherry belongs to the Exclusiv aromatic line of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. in Kendal. Its base is double-fermented black cavendish; this process darkens the leaf's own sugar and gives a soft base for the flavouring to hold onto. A heavy cherry flavouring is applied on top. The product is sold as Exclusiv Black Cherry in the United Kingdom and as Top Black Cherry in the American market; in recent years the line's naming has been shortened to Exclusiv BC. Unlike many examples in the aromatic market, the cherry flavouring doesn't lean toward candy and almond; it carries a darker, riper, lightly bitter black-cherry character instead. It is not heavy in nicotine, though the taste is perceived as full due to the intensity of the flavouring. It suits aromatic lovers who want to avoid overly sugary flavourings.
exclusiv-black-cherry.o: Leaves a dark, tart black-cherry aroma that doesn't slip into almond sweetness.

paul-olsen-kong-frederik-mellow.z: For Paul Olsen's blend called Kong Frederik Mellow, no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

edwards-sweet-vanilla.z: No sufficient independent sourcing could be reached to document the composition and character of Sweet Vanilla, a pipe tobacco from Edward's.

mclintock-creme-de-cassis.z: Creme de Cassis is an intensely flavored blend in Kohlhase & Kopp's McLintock line. Its base, built from black Cavendish and Virginia leaves, is worked with a sauce evoking the blackcurrant liqueur that gives it its name; it is ribbon cut and in some markets is sold under the shortened name "Creme de C." Since the nicotine load stays light, the blend's standout feature is its casing intensity rather than its body. Geared toward smokers looking for a pronounced fruity taste who are used to high sugar and moisture levels in aromatic blends. Its moist structure calls for a slow, controlled burn.
mclintock-creme-de-cassis.o: Leaves a sweet, sharp fruity aroma reminiscent of dark blackcurrant syrup.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-irish-twist.z: Brown Irish Twist is a thicker-gauge twisted version of Brown Bogie. Dark fire-cured and air-cured leaves are wound like rope, left to rest under their own weight for a long time, and sliced for smoking. According to sources it has a floral, sweet leaf character; the taste is reminiscent of cigar leaf. Once lit, the smoke begins medium-bodied and grows noticeably heavier as the bowl progresses, sharpening on the tongue in the final quarter. Nicotine is high. Thick slices burn slow, thin ones burn fast, so slice thickness directly shapes the character of the smoke. It is aimed at smokers experienced with rope tobaccos.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-irish-twist.o: Leaves a heavy woodsmoke and a sharp aroma reminiscent of cigar leaf.

blatter-blatter-executive-executif.z: One of the aromatic house blends prepared at the counter of the Blatter & Blatter shop in Montreal; no reliable source on its composition or character could be found.

pipesandcigars-com-connecticut-yankee.z: No sufficient sources were found documenting the content and character of pipesandcigars.com's blend Connecticut Yankee.

mcclelland-deep-hollow.z: Deep Hollow is one of McClelland's Virginia-based aromatics. Its base holds red Virginia and steam-processed (stoved) black Virginia; a light topping in the direction of apple and vanilla is applied over it. The name comes from Deephallow, a settlement in J. R. R. Tolkien's fictional geography. Despite being an aromatic, its moisture is measured; it burns cool and clean, with low tendency to bite the tongue. While the flavoring gives a pronounced caramel sweetness, the tobacco's own Virginia line can still be read in the smoke, making the blend a followable aromatic even for smokers used to unflavored mixtures. Body is light and nicotine dose stays low. The maker halted production in early 2018.
mcclelland-deep-hollow.o: Leaves a caramel sweetness along with a baked-apple aroma.

dan-tobacco-christmas-tobacco-2000.z: A limited annual Christmas blend prepared by Dan Tobacco for the year 2000; no adequate independent sources were found describing its composition.

james-fox-harrods-cabinet-blend.z: Recorded as one of the house blends James J. Fox prepared for the Harrods shop; not enough sources could be found on its composition.

ken-byron-ventures-sandy-row.z: A limited release in the unflavored Virginia line; not enough sources could be found to describe its composition.

the-smoker-fred-goldring-special.z: A house blend Mel Feldman, owner of Albany's The Smoker, prepared for collector Fred Goldring, reportedly made using only McClelland leaf; no independent source detailing its composition has been found.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-perique.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Perique blend.

planta-anno-mmxiv-fruity-and-fragrant.z: Anno MMXIV is Planta's 2014 limited edition. A soft, creamy body built from double-fermented black Cavendish, lively Virginia leaf, and cooling white Burley is topped with a sweet casing led by mango and lychee. The mixture is a typical example of the aromatic class: fruit sweetness stays up front throughout the smoke, while the tobacco's own earthy taste remains in the background. It suits smokers looking for a low-nicotine, sweet, fruity tobacco, as well as newcomers to the pipe. Being an annual edition, it was not reproduced once stock ran out.
planta-anno-mmxiv-fruity-and-fragrant.o: Fills the room with a sweet mango and floral lychee aroma over a creamy background.

mac-baren-halberg-yellow.z: Not enough information could be found in the manufacturer's current catalog or verifiable independent sources about this member of the Halberg series.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2010.z: Christmas Cheer is the straight Virginia series that Kansas City-based McClelland released once a year, in limited numbers, from the 1980s until the company's closure in early 2018. The series' idea is to present a single Virginia batch selected from that year's harvest on its own; each year is thus considered a separate record, and the year on the tin defines the blend's identity. The 2010 release was prepared the same way, with selected matured Virginia leaf pressed into cake and tinned as broken flake. Records indicate it was prepared from a batch selected from the 2010 harvest. Unflavored Virginia character dominates the smoke: natural leaf sweetness over a bready, herbal base, with a faint tang and a lemony sharpness in the background. Nicotine dose is measured, while flavor intensity is pronounced; it burns cool when smoked slowly, but tends to bite the tongue when rushed. Since the flake's moisture can run high straight from the tin, airing it before packing is common practice. A record aimed at smokers seeking unflavored Virginia who are considering cellaring the tin; not suitable for those expecting an aromatic.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2010.o: A tangy, sharp trace characteristic of McClelland tins mixes into an aroma of dry hay and toasted bread.

peter-stokkebye-1882-mixture.z: This is a blend belonging to the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no reliable sources describing its content and character could be found.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-john-cottons-s.z: Taking its name from Smyrna, the old name for Izmir, this mixture is the oriental-forward product of the John Cotton line. The brand traces its origin to a tobacconist's shop opened in Edinburgh in the late 18th century; the company changed hands throughout the 20th century, with production moving first to London and then to Denmark, and the blend was listed under the Orlik Tobacco Company A/S name. The product was later discontinued, and in the 2010s the name was revived by a different manufacturer in the United States. Anatolian-origin oriental leaves form the blend's body, joined by a substantial amount of latakia and a Virginia that balances the sweetness. The result is a medium-to-full-bodied smoke, with a dry, faintly tart spice layer sitting atop a smoky, earthy core. It's a record aimed at smokers accustomed to oriental-forward Balkan-type mixtures who want an unflavored, smoky tobacco.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-john-cottons-s.o: Leaves a smoky, dry-spice scent recalling incense sticks.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-belmont.z: Belmont comes from Wilke Pipe Tobacco's tradition of preparing private blends for retailers; according to the records, it was produced specifically for Abercrombie and Fitch stores. This type of shop blend was a common practice in 20th-century American tobacco retailing, and Wilke has carried a number of them into the present. Structurally Tennessee-cut Burley forms the base; Virginia adds balance and sweetness, topped with Latakia and black cavendish. The Latakia amount isn't enough to turn the blend into an English mixture; it mainly adds a light smoky layer to Burley's nutty body. Cavendish, meanwhile, provides a creamy sweetness that softens the harder edges. It suits smokers seeking an American-style, moderately smoky, essentially unflavored everyday blend.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-belmont.o: Leaves a scent combining light wood smoke with baked walnut.

cornell-diehl-virginia-flake.z: Virginia Flake is an unflavored Virginia blend Cornell & Diehl produces by pressing high-grade Virginia leaf into its own flake/chip cut. Per the maker's description, the leaf's natural sugar comes forward; on the smoke there's citrus tartness, dry hay, light earth, woody tones, and dried-fruit flavors. It carries no casing — the character comes entirely from the flue-cured leaf itself. The pressed leaf can be packed straight from the pouch or rubbed out first; records indicate it's well suited to long aging. Built for smokers who enjoy unflavored Virginia and want to watch the flavor develop in a single-varietal blend. Nicotine and flavor intensity sit at a medium level.
cornell-diehl-virginia-flake.o: Leaves a sweetish trace reminiscent of orange cake fresh from the oven.

samuel-gawith-balkan-flake.z: Balkan Flake is an unflavored English blend produced by pressing Virginia and latakia leaves into flake form. The tin yields high-moisture, thickly cut flakes; airing before lighting and packing without compressing into the pipe are needed. Smoked at a calm pace, latakia's smoky flavor and Virginia's mature sweetness separate out distinctly; as the pace picks up, a spicy, bitterish direction comes forward, and the tendency to go out and gurgle at the bottom increases. A single bowl can take over an hour. Suited to smokers accustomed to Latakia-bearing blends and flake smoking who can spare the time.
samuel-gawith-balkan-flake.o: The campfire-and-soot scent from latakia lingers in the room for a long time.

samuel-gawith-squadron-leader-special-ed.z: No sufficient source describing where this variant, referred to as a special edition of Squadron Leader, departs from the standard blend could be found.

dan-tobacco-gold-of-mysore.z: A pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source on the blend's composition or character was found, so no further detail is given.

paul-olsen-river-plug.z: A Paul Olsen blend whose name indicates it is offered in plug form; no independent source documenting its composition could be found.

lane-limited-captain-black-dark.z: Captain Black Dark is a blend built entirely from black cavendish leaf. The manufacturer states the leaf is processed using the steaming method developed by Herman G. Lane; this process darkens the leaf and brings out its natural sugar. The cut is ribbon, offered in pouch and tin. The flavor profile is deep and sweet, with a light vanilla direction on top. Nicotine is measured, the smoke is cool; suited to those seeking a single-leaf, sweet and plain aromatic, or those wanting a bowl that isn't heavy at the end of the day.
lane-limited-captain-black-dark.o: Leaves a dark, syrupy-sweet vanilla room note.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-john-cottons-l.z: A latakia-forward English-type mixture that came to market under the John Cotton name; not enough independent source material detailing the blend's composition could be found.

w-o-larsen-black-diamond.z: No independent source sufficient to complete a record could be found regarding W.O. Larsen's Black Diamond blend, so this entry remains incomplete.

kadewe-mischung-n50.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for KaDeWe's Mischung n°50, so the profile is left incomplete.

old-virginia-tobacco-co-old-dominion.z: Old Dominion is a mixture referred to among Old Virginia Tobacco Co.'s labeled blends as straight Virginia; no independent source confirming its composition could be found.

smoke-inn-cuban-coffee.z: Recorded as a coffee-flavored house blend bearing the name of the Florida-based Smoke Inn tobacconist; no source specifying the leaf composition could be found.
smoke-inn-cuban-coffee.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

g-l-pease-maltese-falcon.z: Maltese Falcon is an English blend in Pease's Heirloom series, built from sweet Virginias, quality Oriental leaves, and Cyprus latakia. It is coarse cut. Latakia takes the lead role in the overall flavour but does not rise to a proportion that masks the other leaves; Virginia's sweetness and the Oriental tobacco's spicy, oily texture are felt throughout the smoke. Strength is light to medium, and there is no flavour additive. Records note it has a long-lasting finish on the palate. It is a record aimed at those wanting to smoke classic English blends with a balanced latakia proportion.
g-l-pease-maltese-falcon.o: Leaves a heavy smoke and burnt-wood aroma that clings to the room.

vauen-no-14-virginia-flake.z: No. 14 Virginia Flake is the plain Virginia flake German maker Vauen offers in 50-gram tins. Only Virginia leaf is used in the blend; no other tobacco type is added. Per the maker's own description, the leaf receives a very light top casing that leaves the blend with a nutty edge and a faint trace of vanilla. The taste is built between the Virginia leaf's own sweetness and this subtle casing; the flake structure gives a slow, cool burn. Nicotine sits in the medium range and flavor intensity is moderate. Since tin moisture runs high, separating the flakes and letting them dry briefly before packing helps regulate the burn. A fitting record for smokers wanting to get used to plain Virginia flake, or after a very lightly cased European-style flake.
vauen-no-14-virginia-flake.o: A faint trace of vanilla sits atop a scent of dry hay and baked bread.

clan-shaw-natural-cavendish.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Natural Cavendish.

bennington-tobacconist-connoisseurs-choi.z: One of the recorded mixtures hand-blended in-shop at Bennington Tobacconist in Florida; no reliable source documenting its content and character could be found.
bennington-tobacconist-connoisseurs-choi.o: No recorded recipe could be found.

savinelli-140th-anniversary.z: A limited-production, Virginia-forward blend Savinelli released for its 140th founding anniversary; no sufficient source detailing its content could be found.

bbb-green-label-mild-english-aromatic-mi.z: Referred to as BBB's green-labeled, lightly flavored English mixture; no adequate source documenting its composition and flavoring could be found.
bbb-green-label-mild-english-aromatic-mi.o: Leaves a lightly smoky, sweetish room note.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-regul.z: This is the unflavored, or minimally flavored, base version of the Cândido Giovanella line, produced by Imigrantes Fumos in Brazil and sold domestically in 45-gram resealable packs. The blend is built on domestically grown Virginia leaf with Burley, processed in ribbon cut. In the smoke, the Virginia's hay-like, lightly sugary taste and the Burley's dry, nutty tone come forward; the flavoring is not pronounced. Nicotine load is moderate, the burn even. It's a suitable record for those looking for a non-aromatic, everyday, plain tobacco.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-regul.o: Leaves an aroma of dry hay and burning leaf.

dan-tobacco-london-blend-no-1000.z: London Blend No. 1000 is a full-bodied English mixture with a high Latakia content. The maker positions it as an "after-dinner mixture." Its composition includes Cyprus Latakia, Izmir-origin Oriental leaf, and Zimbabwe-origin Virginia; ribbon cut. On the smoke, Latakia's meaty, smoky flavor forms the blend's backbone; the Oriental leaf adds a tangy, spicy contrast, while the earthy African Virginia keeps the blend from drying out and holds the body together. Despite its intensity, it's noted to burn cool and dry. A fitting choice for smokers accustomed to heavy Latakia blends looking for a filling mixture for evening smoking.
dan-tobacco-london-blend-no-1000.o: A heavy scent of wood smoke and roasted spice spreads through the room.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-1928-pr.z: 1928 Preserve is built on red and bright Virginia, white Burley, and dark-fired Burley leaf, topped with a small amount of cocoa and cream aroma. The maker describes the blend as an American-Danish-style mixture made in memory of the discontinued McClelland product 1928 Reserve; it's offered as 2 oz. bulk and reissued seasonally in winter. Rather than a complex structure, the goal is a flat, balanced smoke that can be enjoyed without much attention. Suited to indoor smokers who don't want to leave a heavy scent in the room and who want a lightly sweet background note.
ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-1928-pr.o: Leaves a lightly sweet trace of cocoa and cream.

petersen-sorensen-english-blend.z: This is one of the blends released under the Petersen & Sorensen name; no sufficient first-hand sources documenting its content and character could be found.
petersen-sorensen-english-blend.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

lane-limited-captain-black-round-taste.z: Captain Black Round Taste is an aromatic blend tied to the Captain Black series; not enough sources could be found to describe its content and character.
lane-limited-captain-black-round-taste.o: Reportedly leaves a sweet cavendish room note.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-john-cottons-m.z: The John Cotton name traces back to a tobacconist's shop opened in Edinburgh in the late 18th century; the company was registered in 1905 and, changing hands over the following decades, moved its production off the islands. A 1972 company document records a 'Rich Mellow Virginia' produced in Denmark among the tobaccos sold under the John Cotton name; the line was later associated with Orlik Tobacco Company A/S. As its name indicates, this is a single-leaf Virginia preparation: unflavored, offered as a ready-rubbed cut, made of light- and medium-toned Virginia leaves. The same product was later continued in the UK market under the name 'Special Virginia'. With its mild sweetness and low nicotine load, it is regarded as a record aimed at smokers wanting an unflavored Virginia suitable for all-day smoking.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-john-cottons-m.o: Leaves a straightforward tobacco scent carrying dry hay and light caramel sweetness.

dan-tobacco-bill-baileys-bowling-blend.z: Referred to as a limited-distribution blend in Dan Tobacco's Bill Bailey's series; no adequate source documenting its composition and character was found.

mostex-krakonosova-smes.z: No independent, verifiable source describing the composition of this blend, released under the Stanislaw brand of the Brno-based maker Mostex, could be found.

hu-tobacco-zulu.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the Zulu blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

jacks-tobacco-12th-anniversary.z: This is a blend under the Jack's Tobacco name; no accessible source describing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
jacks-tobacco-12th-anniversary.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-luigi-radice.z: A blend Cornell & Diehl prepared for Italian pipe maker Luigi Radice, not in current catalogues; no adequate source on its composition and character was found.
cornell-diehl-luigi-radice.o: Records indicate it leaves a tobacco-forward, lightly spiced scent.

gawith-hoggarth-co-rum-flake.z: Rum Flake is a flake made by pressing and slicing Virginia and Burley leaf, rounded out with light rum and maple sugar sauces. It has also been offered in some markets under the name Jamaican Flake. The slices burn evenly once crumbled and aired. The essence topping is pronounced but measured; Virginia's bready sweetness and Burley's nutty tone are still distinguishable on the smoke. Nicotine is moderate. Suited to those wanting to try an aromatic flake while avoiding heavily sugared tobaccos.
gawith-hoggarth-co-rum-flake.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly spirit-touched aroma reminiscent of rum and burnt sugar.

with-pipe-and-book-black-cherry.z: Black Cherry is one of the house blends from With Pipe and Book, a bookshop and tobacconist in Lake Placid, New York, that remained open until 2006; no verifiable source could be found regarding its composition.
with-pipe-and-book-black-cherry.o: No confirmed description of the room note could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-sunrise.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the content and character of Match Sunrise, one of the bulk blends from Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company, could be found.

robert-mcconnell-special-london-mature.z: Although this blend from Robert McConnell's Special London line is said to share the same leaf selection as Mature, there is not enough independent source material describing it in detail.

cornell-diehl-levant.z: No adequate source documenting the composition and character of the Levant blend, referred to as Cornell & Diehl's English type, could be found; the blend isn't in the maker's current catalogue.

alsbo-gold.z: Alsbo Gold is based on blending golden Virginia leaf with aged Burley; black Cavendish is added for contrast. It's a ribbon-cut aromatic with a top layer leaning toward vanilla and pistachio. Hay, earth, and citrus notes from the Virginia combine with the creamy vanilla flavoring, while the Burley leaves a nutty taste reminiscent of nougat in the background.
