Nicotine and strength levels are low; the tobacco is lightly moist straight out of the pack. It suits those looking for a mellow, clean-burning Danish aromatic.
alsbo-gold.o: Leaves a sweet trace close to creamy vanilla and roasted pistachio.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-wine-berry.z: An aromatic record in Sutliff's Match line prepared to correspond to Middleton's discontinued fruit-flavored blend called Wine Berry; no independent source detailing its content could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-wine-berry.o: Records suggest it leaves a scent of wine and red fruit.

g-l-pease-southlinch.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Southlinch.

chacom-grand-cru.z: Grand Cru is one of the blends offered under its own name by Chacom, the French pipe manufacturer dating back to 1825; though the brand's origin is France, tobacco production is carried out in other countries. Per the seller's description, steamed red and bright virginia leaves are combined with sugared and unsugared black cavendish; a small amount of perique is added, with molasses and vanilla used as the top flavoring. The result is a record sitting between aromatic and Virginia, where virginia's bready sweetness and vanilla's pronounced top note stand together. The perique share is small and leaves a dark-fruited, lightly spicy depth; nicotine stays moderate. Suitable for those seeking a sweet everyday smoke where the tobacco taste is still present, without turning to heavy English blends.
chacom-grand-cru.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and dark, molasses-like sugar aroma.

randys-tobacco-shop-pirates-cove.z: This is an aromatic house blend registered under the name Randy's Tobacco Shop; no source could be found documenting its content.

edwards-special-balkan.z: No reliable source could be found for Special Balkan, a blend from Edward's; the name points to a Balkan-style mixture.
edwards-special-balkan.o: Could not be described due to lack of sourcing.

tabak-trennt-78er.z: 78er is one of the house blends from Tabak Trennt, a shop founded in Kiel in 1870, taking its name from the year it was prepared, 1978. Like other Trennt blends bearing Karl-Heinrich Trennt's signature, it is an unflavored mixture made purely of natural tobacco leaf; according to the shop's records, production continues unchanged at the Walter Wehde tobacco factory in Hamburg, to the original recipe. Being a house blend, it has no wide distribution and is obtained largely through the Kiel shop. It suits smokers who enjoy unflavored English-style mixtures and look for tobacco's own natural taste — a product of a business tradition opposed to artificial flavoring.
tabak-trennt-78er.o: Leaves a dry, heavy scent leaning toward soot and wood smoke.

planta-anno-mmvi-sweet-pear-mixture.z: This is a blend in the German maker Planta's limited-production Anno series, named after a year; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

mccranies-balkan-supreme.z: Balkan Supreme is an unflavored Balkan blend rooted in the old Balkan Sobranie tradition. It's built on a generous helping of Latakia, select Oriental leaves, and matured Virginias, rounded out with Samsun-type Turkish tobacco and a small amount of black Cavendish. On the tin note, Latakia's smokiness dominates, but the Orientals' herbal spice and the fine sweetness from the Cavendish balance that smokiness. No flavoring is used.
mccranies-balkan-supreme.o: Leaves a smoky aroma reminiscent of campfire smoke, with a trace of dry hay and faint sweetness behind it.

samuel-gawith-beginners-luck-second-chan.z: No reliable source could be found for this record, referred to as the second version of Samuel Gawith's Beginner's Luck blend.

flandria-florina.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Flandria's Florina blend; records place it in the aromatic class.

mcclelland-blending-oriental.z: Blending Oriental is among the component tobaccos McClelland sold in bulk. Prepared for those wanting to add an Oriental layer to their own recipe when building a mixed blend, it's a ribbon-cut product made of unflavored Oriental leaf. Smoked on its own, it gives a single-plane flavor; it has a spicy, faintly tangy, dry character. Its real use is as a supporting component in Latakia-forward English and Balkan recipes or in Virginia blends. Since the brand stopped production in 2018, the product is found only in old stock.
mcclelland-blending-oriental.o: Leaves a spicy, faintly tangy aroma reminiscent of cigarette tobacco.

mac-baren-hh-balkan-blend.z: HH Balkan Blend is a loose-cut English-style blend in Mac Baren's HH line. The base rests on Virginia and burley; oriental leaves and matured latakia are added on top. As with the rest of the series, there is no applied essence, and casing is kept to a minimum. Latakia defines the smoky side of the blend and adds a spicy, tangy layer, while oriental contributes; Virginia carries the sweetness. The ribbon cut makes packing easy and it burns evenly. A medium-bodied product for smokers seeking latakia-containing blends.
mac-baren-hh-balkan-blend.o: Leaves a note of wood-fire smoke and leather-like smokiness.

cornell-diehl-shelbyton.z: Shelbyton is a blend in Cornell & Diehl's natural-aromatic wing. A significant amount of light Virginia leaf is added on top of a soft Cavendish and black Cavendish base; some dark fire-cured Kentucky is used to strengthen the body. It's ribbon cut, offered both in bulk and tinned. The topping is tawny port wine, leaving a measured undertone reminiscent of raisin and stone fruit. Thanks to the fire-cured leaf, the smoke moves away from pure sweetness into something creamy and full-bodied. Suited to smokers avoiding heavy syrupy aromatics who want naturally flavored blends that preserve tobacco taste.
cornell-diehl-shelbyton.o: Leaves a sweet, wine-leaning scent mingling with raisin and stone fruit.

abenaki-tobacco-co-colombian-coffee.z: This blend, listed as "Columbian Coffee" in Abenaki Tobacco's catalog, is made from a combination of golden and black Cavendish leaf; Brazilian coffee flavoring is applied over it. The flavoring is pronounced, and the coffee side defines the blend's identity. Using two types of Cavendish together sets the blend on both a sweet and low-acid base; this lets the coffee flavoring carry through without biting the tongue. It's cut out for those looking for an aromatic to smoke with coffee in the morning and those who like a sweet-toasted taste line. Abenaki Tobacco was based in Conway, New Hampshire; the brand's own sales site isn't live today.
abenaki-tobacco-co-colombian-coffee.o: Leaves a fresh-brewed coffee and roasted-bean room note.

chief-catoonah-tobacconist-york-street-m.z: The entry has been left incomplete as no reliable source could be found for Chief Catoonah Tobacconist's York Street Mixture blend.

super-value-black-gold.z: Black & Gold, a mixture in the Super Value line, takes its name from the combination of dark black cavendish and golden-yellow Virginia leaf within it. It's prepared as a coarse-cut, lightly flavored aromatic, made, like the rest of the line, from a combination of domestic and imported leaf. It gives a low-nicotine, soft smoke where tobacco sweetness stands out. Suited to smokers who use large bags of everyday tobacco and seek measured sweetness rather than a heavy topping.
super-value-black-gold.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly caramel-like scent.

bayside-virginia-blend.z: A straight Virginia blend sold under the name Bayside; no adequate source verifying its maker and composition could be found.

mac-baren-cube-gold.z: Cube Gold is a ribbon-cut Danish aromatic prepared by bringing together up to twenty-seven different component tobaccos. Its base is loose-cut golden Virginia, rubbed-out Burley, and the brand's characteristic Virginia Cavendish. A measured fruit flavoring is applied over it, resulting in a balanced, lightly sweet smoke consistent from batch to batch. Nicotine stays light. A blend accessible to those wanting a sweet smoke without finding the flavoring overwhelming, and to those new to the pipe.
mac-baren-cube-gold.o: Leaves a lightly fruity, creamy sweet aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-peach-twist.z: Sweet Peach Twist is Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s peach-topped version of its brown Burma base. Fire-cured leaves are twisted into a fine rope; the tobacco arrives as a dense mass that yields small coin-like slices when cut. The pouch aroma is oily and spicy; on the smoke, the earthy, smoky core of the fire-curing is preserved while the sweet topping and inverted sugar worked into the leaf during production add a sweet top layer to the smoke. Since it isn't steam-cooked under pressure, it stays intense in nicotine; it needs to be thinly sliced and smoked slowly. An entry for those wanting a topped but still strong Burma tobacco. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. is one of the English producers that continues traditional twist (rope) production at its Kendal factory, hand-twisting fire-cured leaves into rope form. Because twist tobaccos don't go through a pressure-cooking stage, they stay intense in nicotine; records indicate these ropes are sold for both chewing and pipe smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-peach-twist.o: Leaves an aroma combining peach-and-sugar scent with the tobacco's woody aroma.

samuel-gawith-special-flake-no-3.z: A member of Samuel Gawith's small-batch numbered Special Flake series; besides being a pressed flake carrying Lakeland-style floral flavoring, no sufficient independent source confirming its content could be found.
samuel-gawith-special-flake-no-3.o: Leaves a floral, soapy scent characteristic of Lakeland tradition.

motzek-sweet-crushed-twist.z: Sweet Crushed Twist belongs to the Motzek workshop's twist line known as Tom's Twists. The tobacco is hand-twisted into rope form, rested, and before smoking it is sliced and rubbed into flakes before loading; the "crushed" name comes from this rubbed presentation. At its core are sweet virginias, joined by perique, which records say raises the spice. The tight winding of the twist format lets the tobacco burn cool and long, giving a profile that swings between sweetness and peppery spice throughout the bowl. The nicotine load sits at medium. Suitable for smokers willing to spend time cutting and preparing rope and twist tobaccos, and who are looking for an unflavored sweet virginia character.
motzek-sweet-crushed-twist.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of dry hay and dark-fruit sweetness.

pipesandcigars-com-scottys-pancake.z: This is a blend offered under the American retailer pipesandcigars.com's name; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

stanwell-housemark-sungold.z: Sungold is the classic vanilla aromatic in the Denmark-based Stanwell brand's housemark line. The mixture is built on Virginia leaves, joined by black cavendish and burley, and presented in a mixture cut. Sold in 50- and 125-gram tins, the tobacco counts among Stanwell's easy-lighting, moisture-balanced everyday aromatics. The brand originates in Denmark; tobacco production today is carried out under the Scandinavian Tobacco Group. On the aroma side, a sweet, fruity, fresh vanilla line stands out. The aroma dose is pronounced, and the room note is given at the maker's own top level, meaning the scent lingers in the room for a long time. With nicotine kept low, the blend suits those who spend long sessions with their pipe or are new to aromatics. It's a guiding example for those seeking a structure where the topping, rather than leaf flavor, is the defining factor.
stanwell-housemark-sungold.o: An intense vanilla and sweet-bakery scent fills the room for a long time.

bengal-slices-bengal-slices-re-release.z: Bengal Slices was a Latakia-forward blend, originally produced by House of Sobranie, pressed into a crumble-cake form. It gained a wide following in the 1970s, then was quietly withdrawn from the market. In 2015, rights to the brand were acquired by Standard Tobacco Company of Pennsylvania, and blender Russ Ouellette was brought on to re-create the blend. The reissued version adds premium Orientals, Virginias, and some black Cavendish over the Latakia base; a single, measured top note is worked into the blend. Since it comes as a cake, it needs to be rubbed out before smoking. It's aimed at smokers looking for smoky, sweetish, deep English mixtures, as well as those chasing the trail of the original blend.
bengal-slices-bengal-slices-re-release.o: Leaves a room note with a sweetish top note detectable beneath smoky Latakia.

peter-stokkebye-black-vanilla-no-21.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Black Vanilla (No.21) could be found.

john-middleton-inc-prince-albert.z: Prince Albert is a Burley-based blend launched by R.J. Reynolds in 1907 that became one of the best-selling names in American pipe tobacco history. It's named after Edward VII, who was known as Prince Albert before taking the throne. When Reynolds divested its pipe tobacco line, the brand passed to John Middleton in 1987; Middleton's roots trace to a tobacconist shop opened in Philadelphia in 1856. The blend is built from crimp-cut ribbon Burley combined with bright leaf and black Cavendish, topped with a light flavoring along cocoa and molasses lines. For that reason, it counts as a lightly flavored Burley rather than a full aromatic. It gives a nutty, cocoa-leaning, cool-burning smoke with low tongue bite. Suited to those wanting a fuss-free, classic American blend for all-day smoking and to those looking to get used to Burley character.
john-middleton-inc-prince-albert.o: Leaves a dry, sweet smoke reminiscent of nuts, cocoa, and a touch of molasses.

alsbo-mango.z: The mango-flavored aromatic member of the Alsbo line produced by the Danish Orlik Tobacco Company; beyond the black-Cavendish-heavy Alsbo base, no accessible source giving content information specific to this variant could be found.

lane-limited-black-silk.z: Black Silk is referred to as one of Lane Limited's black-cavendish-forward aromatic records; since no independent source could confirm its composition, the record is left incomplete.

borkum-riff-admirals-flake-vanilla.z: Admiral's Flake Vanilla is one of Borkum Riff's aromatic offerings presented in flake form. According to records, a vanilla topping is added to a body built on Burley and Kentucky leaf; once the flakes are rubbed out and packed, the topping's sweetness comes through alongside the dark leaf's dry, earthy base. Pressing produces a slower-burning, fuller smoke compared to the same brand's ribbon-cut blends. Borkum Riff launched in Sweden in 1962, taking its name from a lighthouse in the North Sea; the blends, originally produced for Swedish Match, are now prepared in Denmark under Scandinavian Tobacco Group. It suits flake smokers who want a mellow sweetness rather than the tangy taste of unflavored Virginia flakes. Nicotine-wise it's a notch more noticeable than the brand's ribbon-cut aromatics.
borkum-riff-admirals-flake-vanilla.o: Leaves a dry, faintly smoky leaf note alongside vanilla sweetness.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-mettowee.z: Mettowee is the vanilla-flavored blend in Wilke Pipe Tobacco's bulk aromatic line. According to the maker's account, a base obtained by converting flue-cured leaf into black cavendish is generously flavored with vanilla, resulting in a sweet taste and a pronounced scent. While rich in flavor, the blend stays extremely smooth in the smoke; nicotine is light. This makes it suitable for those seeking an all-day aromatic that leaves no harshness on the tongue, and for newcomers to the pipe. It is a record in the classic American bulk-aromatic tradition where vanilla takes the lead.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-mettowee.o: Fills the room with a sweet vanilla and sugary-cake scent.

g-l-pease-laurel-heights.z: Laurel Heights is a blend in Pease's Fog City Selection line, built on ripe, dark red Virginias. A very small amount of latakia is mixed into the base; this leaf is used not to build a smoky layer but to add depth to the Virginias. Records note it was designed for smokers who love unstoved dark Virginia. The smoke carries a natural sweetness; notes of orange peel, toasted oats, leather, and something turf-like are reported. The smoke grows richer as the bowl progresses, leaving a malt- and grapefruit-like sharpness at the finish. It is a good record for those wanting a straightforward Virginia character that doesn't veer into syrupy intensity.
g-l-pease-laurel-heights.o: Leaves a light trace of smoke beneath a dry-grass and baked-grain aroma.

david-cigarpipe-virginia-breeze.z: No adequate sources were found documenting the composition or character of the David CigarPipe Virginia Breeze blend.

mac-baren-golden-extra.z: Not enough first-hand sources could be reached to confirm the contents and character of the Mac Baren-branded Golden Extra blend.
mac-baren-golden-extra.o: The room note description for this record could not be confirmed.

greenfield-winther-edward-g-robinsons-pi.z: This blend arose from a partnership in the latter half of the 1940s between San Francisco's Greenfield & Winther firm and actor Edward G. Robinson; Robinson allowed the use of his name only after the final recipe had been agreed upon. It is an old-style American Burley mixture built on a ribbon-cut Burley base, joined by black Cavendish, a small amount of Latakia, and a measured plum top note. Its character sits closer to the lightly flavored classic Burley line than to heavy aromatics: a nutty, earthy body, a fine smokiness from the Latakia, and a fruity sweetness left in the background. Suited to smokers wanting a medium-bodied everyday blend that can be smoked all day, and to anyone curious about the palate of old American shop blends. Rights to the recipe passed to Sutliff in 1969, and the tobacco has continued to be made under that company since.
greenfield-winther-edward-g-robinsons-pi.o: Leaves a light plum sweetness and a fine woody-smoke aroma over nutty Burley.

chacom-6.z: One of the numbered blends offered under its own name by French pipe manufacturer Chacom; no sufficient source could be found to document its content.

abenaki-tobacco-co-irish-cream.z: Irish Cream is one of Abenaki Tobacco's base aromatics. Per the maker's recipe, a base of domestic and imported light-colored leaf is used, with imported Irish cream flavoring applied over it. The light-Virginia-heavy base sets a light, sweet ground that doesn't compete with the flavoring. The cream-liqueur axis is the blend's defining feature; the tobacco taste stays secondary beneath this flavoring. It has a structure suited to those looking for a light-nicotine, sweet aromatic as well as pipe beginners. Abenaki Tobacco was based in Conway, New Hampshire; since its own sales site isn't live today, the blend's current production status is unclear.
abenaki-tobacco-co-irish-cream.o: Leaves a creamy liqueur, vanilla, and light cocoa room note.

pipesandcigars-com-scottys-stonewall.z: This is a blend offered under the American retailer pipesandcigars.com's name; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

nording-fox-hound-hunting-2025.z: Fox Hound belongs to the tobacco wing of the Hunting series Erik Nørding has continued since 1995. The 2025 edition was produced in collaboration with American blender Cornell & Diehl; although the brand is Danish in origin, this tobacco is manufactured in the US. A small amount of latakia is added as seasoning to a blend built from cube-cut burley, matured red and light Virginias, cavendish, and St. James perique. Since the latakia proportion is kept low, the blend gives a profile that leans on Virginia rather than reading as a classic English mixture, with the smoke staying in the background. Cube-cut burley gives the blend a creamy texture and a nicotine strength slightly higher than expected in English mixtures; perique leaves a dried-fruit-and-spice line. It suits smokers wanting to get to know smoky tobacco without diving into heavy Balkan mixtures, or those seeking a naturally sweet mixture for a morning pipe.
nording-fox-hound-hunting-2025.o: Leaves a thin wood-smoke and dried-fruit scent atop a bready sweetness.

sutliff-tobacco-company-ambrosia-j8.z: A blend appearing in Sutliff's bulk aromatic coded series; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-ambrosia-j8.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet, fruity scent.

sutliff-tobacco-company-jamestowne-tradi.z: Jamestowne Tradition Black Mixture is a black-cavendish-forward blend in Sutliff's Jamestowne Tradition line; independent sources do not provide sufficient information on its composition and production status.

mcclelland-gkcpc-scout.z: As the name suggests, this blend was prepared for the Greater Kansas City Pipe Club; no sufficient independent source describing its contents could be found.
mcclelland-gkcpc-scout.o: Records indicate it leaves a smoky aroma typical of Latakia-containing blends.

hu-tobacco-darkwood-scenery.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Darkwood Scenery, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

war-horse-war-horse-ready-cut.z: No reliable source could be found regarding this version of the War Horse brand, so its details could not be recorded.

gawith-hoggarth-co-american-blend-cherry.z: Cherry & Vanilla is a double-flavoured aromatic in Kendal's Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s bulk American Blend line. A mix of black cavendish, Virginia, and burley is prepared as a ribbon cut; cherry and vanilla flavouring are applied together on top. It is a topping-forward record with a light nicotine load, aimed at those seeking mild aromatics that can be smoked at any time of day.
gawith-hoggarth-co-american-blend-cherry.o: Leaves a sweet aroma combining vanilla cream with cherry candy.

sutliff-tobacco-company-bananas-creme-d5.z: A banana-and-cream-flavored blend appearing in Sutliff's D-coded bulk aromatic line; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-bananas-creme-d5.o: Records indicate it leaves a scent of banana and cream.

4noggins-weybridge.z: Weybridge is a blend 4noggins prepares by stoving Burley and Virginia together. The heat treatment darkens the leaves' sugars and gives the blend a nutty, faintly sweet aroma; as a distinguishing touch, some Perique is added. Since no topping is applied, the flavor comes directly from the leaf: grainy sweetness with dry notes of oak and leather stand out. It suits smokers looking for an unflavored, medium-strength American-style blend who enjoy the rounded character of stoved tobaccos.
4noggins-weybridge.o: Leaves a nutty, lightly sweet aroma along with a dry trace reminiscent of old paper and leather.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-private-blend-no.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Private Blend No.57 Summer 2016.

vcpo-selection-nr-5-aromatic-mixture.z: The fifth blend in the VCPÖ Selection series, presented as an aromatic mixture; since it was not distributed outside Austria, no independent source describing its composition and character has been found.

warped-the-haunting.z: The Haunting is among Warped's blends that put cigar leaf front and center. Its composition includes AA-grade Dominican Criollo cigar leaf along with selected Virginia leaves; the aim is to bring together the flavor worlds of cigar and pipe smoking. Alongside ribbon cut, a pressed cake form is also offered.
warped-the-haunting.o: Leaves a dark, earthy, nutty scent reminiscent of cigar smoke.

sutliff-tobacco-company-mild-burley-j4.z: Mild Burley J4 is one of the bulk blends from the Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-boswells-premium-b.z: Premium Burley is a blend J. M. Boswell created in 2007, based entirely on Kentucky burley. The manufacturer states the leaves are held until fully matured and the blend is kept in a balanced structure; the cut is ribbon. Burley's nutty, dry, lightly bready sweetness stands as the blend's main axis; nicotine level is low for this leaf type, and no tongue bite is reported. Suitable for smokers wanting a near-unflavored, soft burley and seeking a plain taste they can smoke all day.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-boswells-premium-b.o: Leaves a dry tobacco aroma reminiscent of nuts and stale bread.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-sailor-jack.z: Sailor Jack is a Latakia-forward English blend Wilke Pipe Tobacco named with a nautical theme. According to the maker's recipe, Latakia dominates the blend, joined by a small amount of Virginia and Perique, with the mixture rounded out by maduro cigar leaf. The addition of cigar leaf gives the blend an earthy, heavy body, while Perique leaves a spicy edge. This is an unflavored mixture aimed at smokers accustomed to high-smoke, high-nicotine blends; it will be heavy for those seeking a light smoke.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-sailor-jack.o: Fills the room with a dense scent of wood smoke and cigar tobacco.

g-l-pease-the-virginia-cream.z: The Virginia Cream is a blend in G. L. Pease's aromatic wing. At its core lie red and golden flue-cured Virginia leaves, joined by rare complementary leaves, with the mix sweetened by a measured vanilla-and-bourbon-based top note. The topping is kept at a level that doesn't suppress the natural sweetness of the Virginias, and it's noted not to leave a lingering foreign taste in the pipe. It is aimed at smokers wanting a sweeter smoke without giving up the Virginia character, or aromatic smokers looking to transition into Virginias.
g-l-pease-the-virginia-cream.o: Leaves a sweet, creamy aroma reminiscent of vanilla and a bourbon cask.

cup-o-joes-1-windigo.z: One of the numbered house blends from the Cup O' Joes tobacco shop in New York state, named after legendary creatures, and classed as an English mixture; no source describing its composition was found.

larus-brother-company-inc-four-seasons.z: Not enough sources could be found about this blend, described as aromatic, from Larus & Brother Company, based in Richmond, Virginia.

uhles-karen-club.z: Karen Club is one of the aromatic blends Uhle Tobacco Company prepares at its Milwaukee shop. Per the maker's description, dark, full-bodied Burley is combined with Cavendish; the flavor direction is built on dark coffee enriched with fruit. The Burley weight gives the blend a relatively full body among aromatics; though the casing sweetness is pronounced, it doesn't smother the tobacco's earthy side. Because the flavor layers become more distinct when smoked slowly, it suits those who enjoy a dark-coffee-and-fruit pairing and don't want a watery-light aromatic smoke. Sold only through the maker's own channels.
uhles-karen-club.o: Leaves an aroma where brewed coffee and red-berry sweetness are noticed together.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-skandinav.z: The vanilla-cased cavendish version of the Skandinavik series; besides the name, no sufficient primary source describing the blend's composition could be found.

frederick-tranter-elizabethan-mixtue.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Frederick Tranter's Elizabethan Mixtue blend; records place it in the Virginia-heavy class.

peter-stokkebye-natural-dutch-cavendish-.z: Natural Dutch Cavendish is a loose-cut, ready-rubbed blend produced by processing selected flue-cured Virginias together with Burley leaf using the traditional Cavendish method. Per the maker's description, the blend was prepared to match the character of Dutch-made Cavendish tobaccos no longer available in the United States. Its flavoring is not perceptible; the taste is clean, lightly sweet, and tobacco-forward. The body is moderate, making it a base tobacco suitable for all-day smoking. It suits those seeking an unflavored Cavendish taste and smokers who blend their own mixtures.
peter-stokkebye-natural-dutch-cavendish-.o: Leaves a dry tobacco aroma with a light sweetness recalling paper and bread.

pipes-pleasures-randys-mix.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of the Pipes & Pleasures blend called Randy's Mix.

de-la-concha-barbados-gold.z: This is on record as one of the aromatic shop blends from the De La Concha tobacconist; no independent source describing its composition and topping could be found.
de-la-concha-barbados-gold.o: No reliable record could be found for the room note.

pete-brothers-exchange.z: Pete Brothers Exchange is reportedly regarded as a Virginia-forward blend; however, no independent source describing its content, cut, and character could be found.

philip-morris-field-stream.z: This pipe tobacco is recorded under the Philip Morris name and is no longer produced; no sources documenting its content and character could be found.

gq-tobaccos-classic-balkan-izmir.z: Classic Balkan is a Balkan blend that, as the parenthetical in its name states, centers Turkish tobacco of Izmir origin. Izmir stands out alongside Virginia leaf; Latakia and Kentucky are present but sit in the background as framing components. The result is a smoke where the Virginias' creamy sweetness and the Oriental's woody, sourish tang keep trading places beneath a veil of smoke. Since the Latakia ratio is kept low, the blend offers an Oriental-forward reading rather than a heavy, smoky Balkan. In smoking behavior it is dry and even: it gives plenty of smoke, causes no moisture problems, and needs little relighting. Since flavor intensity, sharpness, and complexity are all pronounced, it is heavy going for those new to the pipe; it's a blend designed for experienced smokers deliberately seeking the sour-smoky side of Oriental tobacco. It carries no topping and runs on leaf taste alone.
gq-tobaccos-classic-balkan-izmir.o: A fine campfire smokiness accompanies the woody, sourish aroma of Turkish tobacco.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-shag-blac.z: Kendal Gold is one of the shag-cut main bodies produced at Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Kendal workshop in Cumbria. Its base is a fine golden-hued cut of flame-cured bright Virginia leaf; the producer states it uses no other tobacco type in this series, only cleanly cut Virginia. The Kendal Gold body is offered with numerous different flavorings, and Kendal Gold Shag Black Cherry is this family's black-cherry-flavored member. An intense black cherry flavoring is added to Kendal Gold's bright Virginia body; the jar aroma is more pronounced than on the smoke. The fine shag cut lights easily and tends to burn fast. Aimed at smokers who love fruity aromatics and want a low-nicotine blend.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-shag-blac.o: Leaves a dark cherry and candied-fruit aroma.

cornell-diehl-black-cherry.z: Black Cherry is a single-direction aromatic Cornell & Diehl offers in bulk. The base is entirely black cavendish; the same wild-cherry essence used in the brand's Cherry Jubilee blend is applied on top. Since there is only one leaf type, the flavoring largely determines the blend's character, with the tobacco itself staying in the background. The black cavendish base is low in acidity and soft, so the smoke rarely causes tongue burn, and nicotine strength stays light. The smoke carries a sweet, jammy direction, with a pronounced room note. It suits newcomers to aromatics and anyone looking for a single-note, strong fruit-flavored blend; it is not for someone looking for a mixture that lets the leaf's own taste come through.
cornell-diehl-black-cherry.o: A heavy, sugary wild-cherry aroma spreads through the room.

dan-tobacco-milonga.z: Milonga is an aromatic blend named after a traditional musical style common in and around Argentina. Sweet Virginia grades — some of Argentine origin — are combined with soft black Cavendish, topped with a caramel and vanilla casing. It's ribbon cut, and the same blend is offered both in tins and in large vacuum-sealed packs. In the tin note, caramel and vanilla can be picked out separately. It has a mild-to-medium body and a medium level of casing. Once given a short drying period and packed loosely, it lights easily and burns evenly; smoked too fast, it tends to overheat. Suited to smokers wanting a cased but not syrupy aromatic, and to those new to the pipe.
dan-tobacco-milonga.o: Leaves a sweet scent of burnt sugar and vanilla.

holland-house-holland-house-black-cavend.z: Holland House Black Cavendish is an aromatic blend whose weight is made up of black Cavendish, with light-colored Virginia added for balance. In the pouch aroma, almond, caramel, licorice root, and liqueur notes come forward; in the smoke, caramel taste dominates, with licorice and almond-liqueur-evoking notes staying in the background. Starting very mild in the first third, the blend gains body as the bowl progresses. The creamy texture typical of Cavendish and low nicotine suit smokers wanting an intense aromatic taste without a harsh smoke. The brand is Dutch in origin and sold in many countries.
holland-house-holland-house-black-cavend.o: Leaves a sweet aroma of caramel and light licorice root evoking incense.

abenaki-tobacco-co-stonehenge-english.z: A blend the New Hampshire-based Abenaki Tobacco Co. lists among its English mixtures in its own catalog; no adequate source on its content and character could be found.

the-tobacco-barn-treasure-chest.z: Treasure Chest is a house blend in the light-aromatic line of American retailer and blender The Tobacco Barn. It is prepared by combining light and dark Cavendish leaves with golden Cavendish and some fire-cured tobacco; the cut is a loose shag that can be packed freely. The casing stays on a measured sugar-vanilla line that highlights the Cavendish's own sweetness without smothering the leaf. The smoke is cool and low in nicotine; suited to those after a mellow aromatic that can be smoked all day, and to newcomers to the pipe. The maker presents this blend among those smokable in company on the grounds that its scent doesn't cause discomfort in a room. Since it contains no Latakia or spicy Oriental, it may read as plain to palates used to English blends.
the-tobacco-barn-treasure-chest.o: Leaves a warm, sweet, candy-like Cavendish aroma in the room.

holts-cigar-company-crown-royale.z: This is an aromatic mixture recorded as one of the house blends of the Philadelphia-based Holt's Cigar Company; no independent source describing its composition could be found.
holts-cigar-company-crown-royale.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

milan-tobacconists-joes-blend.z: Joe's Blend is a house blend linked to Joe, the eldest son of Milan Tobacconists founder J. H. Milan. Records indicate Joe created his own mixture in the 1950s; the recipe sold today is a new formulation carrying that name. It combines a small amount of latakia with burley and virginia leaves. Since the latakia share is kept low, it sits at the light end of English mixtures; per the maker's description it gives a soft, satisfying, lightly sweet smoke with notes of walnut, hickory, and a measured spice. Suitable for those newly moving into English mixtures or smokers who want the smokiness kept in the background.
milan-tobacconists-joes-blend.o: Leaves a faint wood-smoke and hickory aroma, with a nutty trace beneath it.

cornell-diehl-intercourse.z: Intercourse is a lightly aromatic blend in Cornell & Diehl's bulk catalog. It consists of black cavendish along with soft, sweet burley leaves, topped with an apricot brandy flavoring. The name references both the Pennsylvania town of the same name and the word's meaning of 'conversation.' On the smoke, apricot's fruity sweetness and brandy's soft warmth stand out, while burley builds a nutty foundation. It sits on the light side for nicotine and flavor, leaving no harshness on the tongue. It suits newcomers to aromatics and anyone looking for a light, sweet, long-lasting smoke.
cornell-diehl-intercourse.o: Leaves an aroma of apricot and brandy.

emerson-southern-forged-fairbourne.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing was found for the Emerson Southern Forged brand's Fairbourne blend, so the entry has been left open; records place it in the Virginia/Perique family.

peterson-gold-blend.z: Gold Blend is a ribbon-cut aromatic built from jet-black Cavendish, light and dark Virginia leaf, and Burley. Its flavoring uses a nut-recalling note, vanilla, and a small amount of cinnamon; the tin gives off a sweet, nutty, spiced scent. Nicotine strength is between light and medium. Nutty and vanilla notes from the topping are pronounced on the first light and recede as the smoke progresses, leaving room for Burley's earthy body. It suits smokers wanting to get to know spicy, nutty aromatics.
peterson-gold-blend.o: Leaves a toasted hazelnut, vanilla, and light cinnamon aroma.

davidoff-blue-mixture.z: Blue Mixture is a member of Davidoff's aromatic trio distinguished by color names (Red, Green, Blue). It is ready-rubbed cut; its weight is black cavendish, with burley and Virginia present in smaller proportions. A high-sugar topping has been applied. On opening the pack, an intense scent evoking coconut and raisin cake emerges. On the smoke the flavor intensity is high, and the fullness sits a little above light; Turkish-language sources note a light, undesired bitterness in the blend. It suits those seeking a pronounced-topping, sweet cavendish blend.
davidoff-blue-mixture.o: Leaves a sweet scent evoking coconut and raisin cake.

frederick-tranter-scholars-mixture.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Frederick Tranter's Scholar's Mixture blend; records place it in the "other" class.

the-smoke-shop-finest-balkan.z: No reliable source could be found on Finest Balkan, the house blend from the tobacconist The Smoke Shop.

smoker-friendly-jamaican-rum.z: The rum-flavored product in the Smoker Friendly private-label line; no independent source describing the blend's leaf composition could be found.

villiger-late-night.z: No sufficient independent source could be found regarding Villiger's pipe tobacco called Late Night, so the blend's composition and character could not be recorded.

tinder-box-blend-no-33.z: Blend No. 33 is a member of the numbered house blend series Tinder Box put together in the 1970s; the same series includes blends numbered 1, 19, Special and Vintage. Records indicate the whole series is Burley-based and continues to be sold loose by weight in the chain's stores. Burley's nutty, dry, earthy taste forms the blend's backbone; Virginia and Cavendish leaves add sweetness and burn balance. Any casing present is kept light. Suited to those after an everyday tobacco that doesn't bite the tongue and burns calmly, and to anyone wanting to get to know Burley character in a plain form.
tinder-box-blend-no-33.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of nuts and toasted bread.

radfords-opus-one.z: No independent source could be found documenting the content and character of the Opus One blend sold under the Radfords name.

cigar-connoisseur-rvr-flake.z: RVR Flake is a pure Virginia flake tobacco the Cigar Connoisseur shop sells in bulk. The slices come out of the pack loose but unbroken, with a fairly high moisture content. Airing time determines the character of the smoke: smoked moist, the burn is comfortable but can run hot; smoked drier, the flavor clarifies but the risk of tongue bite increases. Packing without breaking up the slice structure is the method preferred in available records. It burns quite comfortably and reveals its flavor from the first puffs; Virginia's pure, sweet taste holds its line throughout the bowl. If the smoking pace speeds up, harshness and flavor breakdown can appear in the final quarter, so it calls for a controlled tempo. Nicotine strength isn't low, though it may feel limited to those seeking very high nicotine. It is a blend suited to those accustomed to unflavored Virginia slices who smoke their tobacco slowly.
cigar-connoisseur-rvr-flake.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly tangy aroma of dry grass and baked fruit in the room.

schermerhorn-bestoval.z: Bestoval is an American-tradition plug tobacco sold by the Chicago-based Schermerhorn Cigar Stores. It is made by pressing white burley leaf and breaking it into cubes; it is described on packaging as a "crushed plug." Casing level is low, the taste largely relying on burley's own nutty, dry character. The cube cut burns slowly and cool, and is easy to pack; nicotine is at medium level. Suited to those seeking a plain, dry American smoke without aromatic flavoring. The brand was later transferred to Swisher, and its pipe-tobacco line was discontinued; today Bestoval is seen only in the collector market via old tins.
schermerhorn-bestoval.o: Leaves a scent of dry nuts and toasted bread.

lane-limited-foundry.z: Lane Limited's Foundry blend is an English-type mixture prepared by combining selected burley, Virginia, black cavendish and latakia leaves in a ribbon cut. The latakia proportion forms the blend's backbone; burley gives fullness and a nutty base, Virginia sweetness, and black cavendish softness. Retail listings state it's offered in 1.75-ounce metal tins. Since the mixture carries a more balanced latakia dose than heavy Balkan blends, it suits smokers new to the English type or wanting a measured smoky taste for daily smoking. The ribbon cut eases pipe packing and ensures an even burn. Lane Limited is, per records, a long-established blender manufacturing in Tucker, Georgia, USA.
lane-limited-foundry.o: Latakia's woody, smoky, campfire scent is accompanied by a lightly sweet base.

watch-city-cigar-none-of-your-business-r.z: This is Watch City Cigar's house blend described as an English-aromatic hybrid built on a black-and-golden Cavendish base; no sufficient source could be found regarding the casing details.
watch-city-cigar-none-of-your-business-r.o: Leaves a light smoky trace alongside a sweet Cavendish scent.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.z: This is the cognac-flavored version of the Cândido Giovanella line, produced by Imigrantes Fumos in Brazil. The base consists of domestically grown Virginia and Burley leaf with black Cavendish, cut in ribbon. In the smoke, cognac's grapey, lightly burnt sugary taste leads; Burley gives a dry body while Virginia adds bready sweetness. Nicotine is moderate, the smoke cool. It suits those who enjoy liqueur-flavored aromatics and are looking for a darker taste for evening smoking.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.o: Leaves an alcoholic, fruity, lightly woody aroma reminiscent of cognac.

dunhill-blenders-own.z: A discontinued mixture referred to under the Dunhill name, for which no verifiable source on its composition could be found.

pcca-constantinople.z: Constantinople is a blend McClelland tinned in limited numbers for the PCCA club, noted in records as sitting on the Virginia-perique line; no independent source describing its composition could be found.
pcca-constantinople.o: No source could be found to describe the room note.

cornell-diehl-blenheim.z: A blend bearing the Cornell & Diehl name, recorded as an aromatic; as it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog, no verifiable information about its content and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-glengarry-flake.z: Glengarry Flake is an all-Virginia flake built from Brazilian, Zimbabwean, and Malawian flue-cured leaf. After pressing and slicing, the slices show a color between dark gold and brown; crumbled and aired before smoking, they burn evenly. On the flavor palette, Virginia's bready-herbal sweetness stands out along with a light tart-fruit tone. Nicotine is moderate. Suited to smokers accustomed to slow smoking who want an unflavored or very lightly essenced plain Virginia flake.
gawith-hoggarth-co-glengarry-flake.o: Leaves a lightly sweet tobacco aroma reminiscent of dry hay and baked bread.

uhles-white-cavendish-blend.z: White Cavendish is one of Uhle Tobacco Company's simply constructed aromatics. Per the maker's description, the blend is built on a single component, white Cavendish leaf directly, with a bourbon touch added to the taste. The single-leaf setup keeps the blend light and straightforward; nicotine load is low and the flavor direction is defined by the sweetness the casing brings. Suited to those after an uncomplicated aromatic that doesn't bite the tongue, and to newcomers to the pipe. The blend is prepared at the Milwaukee shop and offered in 1.5, 7 and 14-ounce bulk measures.
uhles-white-cavendish-blend.o: Leaves a soft aroma of sweet, lightly burnt sugar evoking bourbon.

grants-tobacconist-barbary-coast.z: A Grant's house blend named after San Francisco's old Barbary Coast neighborhood; there is no independent sourcing on its composition.

wellauer-co-standard-mixture.z: Standard Mixture is Swiss tobacconist Wellauer's classic blend tied to the English school. It consists of Latakia, Oriental leaves, and processed Virginia; according to retailer records, these leaves are also roasted. It contains no flavoring casing, so the taste comes entirely from the leaves themselves. On opening the tin, a pronounced Latakia scent and a spicy depth come forward. In the smoke, Latakia builds a woody, smoky, lightly leathery base; the Oriental leaf adds a dry, grassy, occasionally sharp spice; Virginia holds a measured natural sugar and a warm toast tone underneath. As the smoke progresses, the spicy opening gives way to a fuller, rounder character. The loose-mixture cut makes packing easy, and the burn stays even. It can be considered an evening pipe for smokers seeking a traditional, unflavored Latakia mixture.
wellauer-co-standard-mixture.o: Leaves a smoky, woody, tobacco-forward scent typical of classic English mixtures.

cornell-diehl-guilford-flake.z: Not enough primary sourcing could be found regarding the composition and character of Guilford Flake, one of Cornell & Diehl's flake-cut products.

dunhill-my-mixture-rum-truffle.z: As the name suggests, rum- and cocoa-flavored; a record tied to Dunhill's custom blending program, not currently in production; no independent source giving detailed composition information could be found.
dunhill-my-mixture-rum-truffle.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

james-barber-old-jamaican.z: A James Barber aromatic whose name nods to the rum tradition; no independent source could be found to confirm its contents and casing.

park-lane-tobacconist-park-lane-no-8.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Park-Lane No. 8, one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

two-friends-english-chocolate.z: English Chocolate sits in the aromatic-English wing of the Two Friends line. Turkish Latakia is added to red and light Virginia leaves and the blend is pressed, then broken into flake; this cut makes packing easier while retaining the density the pressing gives. The maker's description highlights creamy cocoa notes. On the smoke, the chocolate casing layers over Latakia's smoke; the result is a profile that is neither a plain aromatic nor a full English blend. Nicotine is low and the flavor body is medium. A fitting structure for smokers wanting to try Latakia smoke alongside a sweet casing, or to get used to flake cut.
two-friends-english-chocolate.o: Leaves a sweet aroma where cocoa dough mixes with light wood smoke.

smokers-haven-sids-mello-mix-17.z: A numbered edition of the Mello-Mix line produced outside for Smokers' Haven; sufficient sources documenting its composition could not be found.

mac-baren-cube-bronze.z: Cube Bronze is one of the members of Mac Baren's cube-cut Cube family. As with the series' other members, its base is golden Virginia with a small amount of Burley, while black Cavendish adds a sweet layer. Turkish-language sources list its contents as Virginia, Burley, and Cavendish; the cut is described as close to loose ribbon. The cube-cut structure eases the tobacco's cool burn by letting air through. Flavoring level is low; the sweetness doesn't push the smoke to a cloying point, and the tobacco taste stays up front. It's in a very light band for nicotine, suiting long, calm smokes. Suited to smokers who like flavored blends but don't want the flavoring to mask the leaf.
mac-baren-cube-bronze.o: Leaves a measured aroma leaning lightly sweet and reminiscent of toasted grain.

4noggins-button-bay.z: Button Bay is, in 4noggins' own description, a "very American English" blend: Turkish leaf, Perique, and Latakia are added on top of an American body of Burley and Virginia. It takes its name from Vermont's Button Bay area. The composition aims to hold together the smoky framework of English blends and the nutty base of American ones. Burley contributes nuttiness, Virginia sweetness, Perique a spicy, plummy tang, and Latakia adds smoke; the maker describes this balance as its sweet, spicy, and smoky trio. No additives are reported. Being ribbon cut, it packs easily and needs few relights. It suits smokers seeking a middle path between full English and full American styles.
4noggins-button-bay.o: Leaves a lightly smoky, spicy scent reminiscent of nuts.

robert-mcconnell-carolina-gold.z: Carolina Gold is a light blend combining pale-colored Virginia and Carolina-region leaf with select Burley varieties. Flavoring is measured; the aim is to smooth the smoke without masking the leaf's natural sweetness. Burley adds a dry body and nutty undertone to the blend, while Virginia builds the dominant sweet-herbal character. Nicotine and flavor intensity are low; it lights easily, packs light, and burns for a long time. It suits smokers looking for a mellow, all-day blend. Reports indicate this line was prepared for Robert McConnell in Denmark; the brand itself traces back to 1848 London.
robert-mcconnell-carolina-gold.o: Leaves a lightly sweet hay and dried-fruit aroma.

mcclelland-no-105-chocolate-mint.z: A blend flavored toward chocolate and mint within McClelland's numbered bulk aromatic series; no sufficient source documenting its composition could be found.

e-a-carey-europe-careys-peach-brandy.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Carey's Peach Brandy, a pipe tobacco from E. A. Carey (Europe).

ken-byron-ventures-festivus-gt.z: Festivus GT is the straight-Virginia member of Ken Byron Ventures' holiday-season Festivus trio. The GT in its name stands for "Grand Tour"; the blend is built on the idea of bringing together Virginia leaf from different growing regions around the world. It carries no flavoring. On the taste side, Virginia's characteristic hay, bread, and sugary fruit notes are decisive; strength sits around medium. Aimed at smokers who enjoy unflavored Virginia and want to follow a single leaf family's own sweetness. Being a limited-batch release, it isn't continuously available.
ken-byron-ventures-festivus-gt.o: Leaves a sweetish aroma reminiscent of dry straw and bread crust.

middle-earth-tobacco-mordor.z: The Balkan-style blend in the Middle Earth Tobacco line; since no verifiable source could be found, no detail can be given.

peter-stokkebye-belle-epoque.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Belle Epoque could be found.

comptons-of-galashiels-york-full-mixture.z: Compton's of Galashiels York Full Mixture is one of the brand's fullest-bodied members among its old-style English mixtures. In keeping with the brand series' general structure, multiple Virginia types, unflavored cavendish, Latakia, and Oriental leaves are used; the result is a body with more intense sweetness and higher nicotine than its modern counterparts. On the flavor channel, Latakia-derived smokiness runs together with Virginia sweetness, and the Orientals add a spicy layer on top. It suits experienced smokers accustomed to classic heavy English mixtures who are looking for an unflavored, hearty smoke. The brand is a small series produced in limited numbers; its current production status could not be clearly established from available records.
comptons-of-galashiels-york-full-mixture.o: Leaves a heavy smoky wood aroma in the room, with a dark, sweetish tobacco scent beneath.

cobblestone-cherry-delight.z: Cobblestone's Cherry Delight blend is, per available records, a ribbon-cut, flavored mixture, though not enough independent sourcing could be found to detail its composition.

lane-limited-vanilla-black-cavendish.z: As its name suggests, a black-cavendish-based, vanilla-flavored Lane Limited blend; not enough sources could be found for detailed composition.

pcca-syrian-star.z: A blend produced by McClelland within the PCCA club series, apparently built around Syrian latakia judging by its name; not enough source material giving detailed composition information could be found.

dan-tobacco-cavendish.z: A Virginia-based Cavendish blend registered under the Dan Tobacco name; no adequate independent source detailing its composition and processing was found.

w-o-larsen-mellow-tasty.z: This is an aromatic blend known under the Copenhagen-based W.O. Larsen name; no reliable source could be found documenting its composition and character.

cornell-diehl-warped-the-red-hunt.z: The Red Hunt is one of the few blends from the Warped and Cornell & Diehl partnership that contains no cigar leaf. Its composition includes red, mahogany, and light-colored Virginia leaf alongside aged Basma and Izmir Oriental tobaccos and well-fermented Perique. The mixture is pressed, cut into broken flake, and offered in a 60-gram tin. It's an unflavored blend, built on Virginia's breadlike sweetness, the Oriental tobaccos' dry spice, and Perique's fermented-fruit edge. Its pressed, Virginia-heavy structure makes it well suited to long-term storage. Aimed at smokers wanting a complex Virginia-Perique-Oriental trio without Latakia.
cornell-diehl-warped-the-red-hunt.o: Breadlike Virginia sweetness is accompanied by a scent of dry hay, spice, and a lightly resinous Oriental tobacco.

doctor-pipe-old-dark-fired.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Old Dark Fired, a pipe tobacco from Doctor Pipe.
doctor-pipe-old-dark-fired.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

robert-mcconnell-carolina-black.z: Carolina Black is a light aromatic blend bringing together Carolina-origin black Cavendish with golden Virginia leaf. A subtle vanilla scent applied to the Cavendish, along with accompanying spice notes, is the blend's defining feature; Virginia supports the base with natural sugar. Reports place the blend within an aromatic line prepared for Robert McConnell in Denmark. Nicotine is light and the smoke is mellow. It suits smokers avoiding heavy casing who want a low-key, all-day aromatic, as well as newcomers to the pipe. The Robert McConnell brand was founded in London in 1848 and continues today under Kohlhase & Kopp in Germany.
robert-mcconnell-carolina-black.o: Leaves a soft vanilla and sweet-spice aroma.

w-o-larsen-classic.z: No reliable source could be found regarding this blend bearing the W.O. Larsen name, so its details could not be recorded.

war-horse-war-horse-bar.z: No reliable source could be found regarding this version of the War Horse brand, so its details could not be recorded.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-peace-edition.z: Peace Edition is one of Kohlhase & Kopp's themed limited series. The mixture sits dark black cavendish, coarsely broken Virginia, naturally sweet Virginia and nutty Burley side by side; the different cuts together also give the tin a mottled appearance. The casing runs along a fruit axis: raspberry, peachy cream and fruit yogurt tones define the blend's top taste. The cavendish base carries this sweetness, while the Burley share adds a bit of weight to the body, so the smoke doesn't stay purely sugary. Suited to smokers seeking a fruity aromatic who want to move away from an alcohol or vanilla line. Being a limited run, it's found today only in old stock.
kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-peace-edition.o: Leaves a note reminiscent of raspberry and peach along with a milky dessert.

planta-anno-mmxi-caribbean-mixture.z: Anno MMXI is the 2011 edition of Planta Tabak-Manufaktur's year-tobacco series, a limited aromatic carried under the subtitle Caribbean Mixture; no source could be found documenting the blend's leaf composition and flavoring, so no detailed specification is given.

low-country-pipe-cigar-natural-virginia-.z: One of the house blends of South Carolina-based Low Country Pipe & Cigar; described as Virginia-forward, but not enough sources could be found to describe its character.

a-c-petersen-caledonian-melange-no-499-o.z: A long-discontinued navy cut blend belonging to the Danish A & C Petersen's Caledonian line; no reliable description of its content could be found.
a-c-petersen-caledonian-melange-no-499-o.o: No adequate description of its scent could be found in records.

cornell-diehl-sun-bear.z: Sun Bear is a Virginia-Oriental sliced tobacco released in Cornell & Diehl's limited Small Batch series. Red and bright Virginia leaf are joined by Basma and Izmir Orientals. Honey taken from head blender Jeremy Reeves' own hives in South Carolina, along with a small amount of silver tequila and elderflower, is used as the casing. Despite being cased, the blend isn't classed as aromatic; the casing serves to bring out the fruity, floral side of the Oriental and Virginia leaf. The smoke follows a bright, fresh line, finishing creamy and round. In later years of the series, versions with different casings such as Tupelo and Bourbon Cask were released.
cornell-diehl-sun-bear.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay over a floral, honeyed sweetness.

imperial-tobacco-group-plc-amphora-cesar.z: This is an aromatic blend released under the Amphora umbrella; no independent source describing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
imperial-tobacco-group-plc-amphora-cesar.o: No room note described in the records could be found.

andreas-mon-ami.z: No source documenting the content and character of the blend called Andrea's Mon Ami could be found.

john-patton-dark-horse.z: One of the small-scale blends released under the John Patton name; not enough independent sources could be found to document its contents and character.
john-patton-dark-horse.o: No source could be found on the room note.

sutliff-tobacco-company-pressed-burley.z: A Sutliff blend whose name suggests it is prepared by pressing burley leaf; no independent source documenting its composition and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-seasonal-reserve-2020.z: Seasonal Reserve is Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s series of limited holiday blends released each year; the 2020 edition is that year's entry in the series, later replaced by new editions in following years. The base is built from bright flue-cured Virginia, dark fire-cured Cavendish Virginia, and naturally sweet sun-cured Burley leaf. The topping sits on a cherry-and-almond axis, accompanied by a vanilla trace that adds creaminess. Body stays light, and no tongue bite is reported. An entry aimed at smokers wanting a Christmas-themed aromatic with a pronounced topping but a light body, as well as collectors of the annual limited editions.
gawith-hoggarth-co-seasonal-reserve-2020.o: A creamy vanilla trace accompanies the aroma of morello cherry and marzipan.

james-barber-best-shag.z: Best Shag is a fine shag-cut house blend traced back to the English tobacconist house James Barber, founded in Otley in 1867; no independent source documenting its composition could be found.
james-barber-best-shag.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

e-a-carey-careys-soft-black-aromatic.z: This appears to belong to E. A. Carey's black-cavendish-based aromatic line and does not appear in the current catalog; no detailed primary source could be found.

doctor-pipe-black-diamond.z: Doctor Pipe is a series blended in Brazil that features imported leaves such as Latakia, Oriental, Perique and Kentucky. Black Diamond is an unadulterated, ribbon-cut English mixture putting Virginia, black Cavendish, dark fire-cured Kentucky and Perique alongside Latakia.
doctor-pipe-black-diamond.o: Leaves a scent of wood smoke, soot and dark roasted leaf.

admirals-choice-natural-cavendish.z: Admiral's Choice is a bulk pipe tobacco line sold for a long time as the store brand of a major American drugstore chain, later handed to catalog and online sales when the chain stopped carrying tobacco products. Natural Cavendish is the unflavored wing of this line: its weight is set by nutty Burley, with some Virginia added, and the mixture is put through the Cavendish process. No further flavoring is applied; the sweetness comes from the process itself. The smoke is cool and dry, burning slowly; the tobacco taste is flat and low-pitched, with nicotine measured. This low profile makes it usable both as a standalone everyday tobacco and as a blending component added to other blends for body and sweetness. It suits smokers looking for an unflavored but not harsh Cavendish, and pipe beginners.
admirals-choice-natural-cavendish.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, dry-hay, nutty tobacco room note.

alsbo-black.z: Alsbo Black is the black-Cavendish-forward aromatic of the Danish-origin Alsbo brand. It's built from a combination of Cavendish and Virginia; the top layer gives a sweet, round character while leaving a thin spice line behind. Per records, the brand has produced blends within the Danish aromatic tradition for over a century, and its products are mostly distributed in 50-gram packs. Strength is low, flavor intensity is medium; its ribbon cut is suited to packing straight from the pouch. It suits those who like dark, sweet Danish aromatics and those wanting a cool, mellow smoke.
alsbo-black.o: Leaves a lightly spiced room note with a dark, syrupy sweetness.

planta-original-danish-black-vanilla-mix.z: Danish Black Vanilla is one of Planta's best-known aromatic blends. Burley and Virginia are added to a black-Cavendish-heavy body, with an intense vanilla flavoring applied on top. The cut is ribbon and the tobacco arrives moist. The "Danish" designation in the name references the Danish-style steamed sweet Cavendish tradition; production takes place in Germany. Nicotine stays very light, while the aroma intensity in the mouth and the room note it leaves are both at a high level. It suits smokers looking for a profile where vanilla leads and tobacco character stays behind; it also circulates among newcomers to the pipe drawn to low-nicotine, distinctly sweet blends. For smokers bothered by an intense casing scent, it feels heavy.
planta-original-danish-black-vanilla-mix.o: Leaves an intense vanilla and sweet-confection aroma that fills the room.

doctor-pipe-virginia-perique.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Virginia & Perique, a pipe tobacco from Doctor Pipe.
doctor-pipe-virginia-perique.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

vauen-zeppelin.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Vauen pipe tobacco called Zeppelin to record the blend's composition and character.

backwoods-all-natural-tobacco.z: Corresponds to the unnamed base version in Backwoods' pipe tobacco line, marketed with an emphasis on natural leaf; no adequate source detailing the blend's composition could be found.

mccranies-watsons-glen.z: Watson's Glen is McCranie's shop's composite Virginia blend. Rather than settling for a single leaf type, it brings together differently prepared Virginias; according to the shop's recipe the mixture includes Rattray's black Virginia, Marlin Flake, dark aromatic Virginias, and the shop's own Red Ribbon red leaf. This structure is a typical example of shop mixtures built by rubbing out and recombining ready-made blends. The resulting profile is more layered than a straight Virginia: the tangy dried-fruit quality of the red leaf, the dark sugar depth of the black Virginia, and the intense body from the flake all sit together. It carries no casing. An entry geared toward smokers who know Virginia blends and are looking for a mixed Virginia rather than a single leaf type.
mccranies-watsons-glen.o: Leaves a lightly tangy trace where dark dried fruit mixes with sweet bread aroma.

tabaqueria-xian-221b-baker-street.z: An English-type house blend from Tabaquería Xian in Xalapa; no independent source describing its composition could be found.

cornell-diehl-john-marr.z: John Marr is a Virginia blend built by adding a significant proportion of Oriental leaf, measured Perique, and black Cavendish to bright and red Virginias, lightly flavored with bourbon and vanilla. It takes its name from Herman Melville's sailor poem of the same title and is presented ribbon cut. On the smoke, Virginia leads, with the other components accompanying it in balance: Oriental leaf and Perique together provide depth and spice, while the casing stays light enough to sit in harmony with Virginia's dry-hay scent. Strength is medium. Suited to those looking for a blend sitting between unflavored Virginia and aromatic that can be smoked all day.
cornell-diehl-john-marr.o: Leaves a scent where vanilla and whisky sweetness mingle with dry hay.

bosphorus-red-devil.z: Red Devil is the blend Bosphorus founder Birol Salman considers his own masterwork. It is prepared by soaking red Turkish tobaccos and burley in wine, fermenting them, and then blending with perique; a very small mango casing is applied on top. The cut is ribbon, flavoring level medium. In the first half of the smoke, the tart grape taste from the wine and abundant spice lead; nicotine does not show itself much at first. Past the halfway point the tartness recedes, giving way to the Oriental tobacco's spicy character and a noticeable nicotine presence. Because of fermentation the leaves are moist, requiring brief airing before smoking. Suitable for those seeking a medium-strength blend that is flavored yet keeps its tobacco taste.
bosphorus-red-devil.o: Leaves a sweetish tobacco aroma accompanied by tart grape and spice.

robert-mcconnell-boutique-blend.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of Robert McConnell Boutique Blend.

bosphorus-venice-nights.z: Venice Nights is one of Bosphorus's Virginia/Perique-structured blends. Per records it contains about 50% golden virginia, 30% perique and 20% burley; it is ribbon cut and prepared by leaving it to ferment for a long time in an oak barrel. No top-layer casing is applied to the blend; the sweet, fruity impression comes largely from this process and from golden virginia's sugar. In the first half of the smoke a sweet layer evoking fig, carob and plum leads; as it progresses this layer recedes, and burley's spicy fullness together with virginia's sweetness become pronounced. The woody, lightly tart taste from the oak lingers in the mouth for a while after smoking. Since it is offered at high moisture, it needs airing. Suitable for smokers seeking an unusual Virginia/Perique character.
bosphorus-venice-nights.o: A sweetish tobacco aroma sits over an oak wood and dried-fruit aroma.

samuel-gawith-special-flake-no-4.z: A dark-colored, lightly Lakeland-style flavored flake from Samuel Gawith's numbered Special Flake series; no sufficient independent source confirming its content could be found.
samuel-gawith-special-flake-no-4.o: Leaves a resinous, lavender-like scent alongside a honeyed sweetness.

tinder-box-3-cherry.z: One of the cherry-flavored house blends from the Tinder Box chain; no source documenting its composition and current status has been found.
tinder-box-3-cherry.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of cherry syrup.

charatan-rolls.z: Rolls is a roll blend prepared in the Charatan line as the counterpart to Dunhill's De Luxe Navy Rolls. Virginia leaves are wound into a roll, pressed, and then sliced into coin-shaped pieces; Perique is included. Perique lends a spicy depth toward plum and raisin, while Virginia carries a dark, bready sweetness. Rubbing out the coins and airing them briefly eases the smoke. Nicotine sits in the high range. Suitable for experienced smokers accustomed to roll-cut VaPer blends who want a slow, long smoke.
charatan-rolls.o: Leaves a plum, raisin and dark bread room note.

per-g-jensen-bold-strong.z: Bold & Strong is the stoutest member of the Blender's Collection series bearing the name of Danish blender Per Georg Jensen. The series consists of tobaccos carrying no top-note flavoring and given almost no casing, aiming to offer pure leaf that can be smoked on its own or mixed into personal blends. This blend sets rustica leaf — whose nicotine content runs markedly higher than traditional tobaccos — alongside Virginia and burley leaf, and is presented as a loosened ready-rubbed cut. Although the brand's name draws on Danish pipe tradition, the series is produced in the US at Sutliff's facilities. The taste runs along the leaf's own salty, earthy, herbal line unflavored; rustica pulls both fullness and sharpness markedly upward. It suits experienced smokers seeking a nicotine-resistant, strong tobacco, and those wanting to build their own blend and give it strength; it's a hard one to recommend as a beginner's first tobacco.
per-g-jensen-bold-strong.o: Leaves a sharp, earthy, herbal leaf scent.

peterson-st-patricks-day-2017.z: This is the 2017 tobacco edition of Peterson's St. Patrick's Day series, released every March; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient sources documenting that year's leaf mix and topping could be found.
peterson-st-patricks-day-2017.o: Leaves the sweet aroma typical of aromatic blends.

pipesandcigars-com-scottys-butternut-bur.z: Butternut Burley is one of the earliest examples in the Scotty's line, born from pipesandcigars.com founder Scott Bendett's effort to produce blends unique to his own shop. A casing giving butter, a small amount of vanilla, and honey notes is applied to a Burley-heavy body; Burley's natural nutty taste combines with this sweetness. It is sold in bulk, is a ribbon cut, and stays measured in nicotine. It suits smokers looking for a mellow, all-day aromatic that leaves no bitterness on the palate, as well as newcomers to the pipe. The same line also includes blends such as Trout Stream, Milk & Honey, and University Professor.
pipesandcigars-com-scottys-butternut-bur.o: Leaves a melted-butter and honeyed-nut aroma.

peter-heinrichs-no-223.z: No. 223 is a flake blend from Peter Heinrichs aimed at building a spicy character without using Latakia. The maker presents it as the house's first Latakia-free spicy flake; the composition is built on Virginia and fire-cured Kentucky leaf. Its pressed and sliced structure gives a slow, cool burn, and it needs to be rubbed out before packing. Virginia carries a light sweetness recalling honey and dry hay, while Kentucky adds an earthy, woody, smoky depth. Sources indicate the aim was a character that doesn't bite the tongue. It is a suitable record for smokers seeking a full-bodied, spicy natural blend who want to avoid Latakia's smoky weight, and for those accustomed to smoking flake.
peter-heinrichs-no-223.o: Leaves a dry hay, fire-cured leaf, and light woody-smoke aroma.

low-country-pipe-cigar-natural-virginia.z: One of the house blends of South Carolina-based Low Country Pipe & Cigar; described as pure Virginia, but not enough sources could be found to describe its character.

tinder-box-rum-runner.z: Tinder Box is the name of an American tobacconist chain founded in 1928 that sells blends prepared for its own shops under its own name; Rum Runner is one of these house blends, though no sufficient independent source describing its composition and character has been found.

g-l-pease-ellipsis-flake.z: Ellipsis Flake is the fourth entry in G. L. Pease's Zeitgeist series. Oriental leaf and a small amount of Perique are added to a Virginia-heavy base; white Burley, which gives the blend strength, and Cavendish, which softens the texture, also enter the mix. The leaves are pressed and cut into flakes, a process that lets the flavours meld and intensify. It is a medium-bodied, untopped blend; sweetness, spice, and a nutty background sit together. Whether the flake is rubbed out or loaded folded determines the pace of the smoke. It suits smokers interested in pressed Virginia flakes and ageing.
g-l-pease-ellipsis-flake.o: Leaves a spicy tobacco aroma reminiscent of baked dough and dried fruit.

straus-tobacco-mercantile.z: Mercantile is one of the counter blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; records indicate the shop was founded in 1880 and that most of its house blends were named after Cincinnati neighborhoods and landmark buildings. Since no independent source on the blend's composition and character could be found, this record is kept at listing level only.

dan-tobacco-buddies-bi-bo.z: One of Dan Tobacco's limited-distribution aromatic blends known under the Bi-Bo name; no adequate source documenting its composition and character was found.

grand-river-enterprises-le-baron-gusto-c.z: Records indicate Le Baron Gusto Classico is a plain everyday mixture built from Virginia, Burley, and Oriental leaf, said to carry no sauce or top note. Its profile has been left incomplete since it rests on a single independent source.

pcca-quantum.z: For PCCA's blend called Quantum, no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-blacksburg.z: Blacksburg is a Sutliff aromatic that appears entirely black, made from cavendish and burley leaves. It takes its name from the town of Blacksburg in Virginia; since the brand is based in Richmond, the naming carries a local reference. Light notes of fig, prune, and rum are used as the topping. The blend's defining trait is its dryness: despite belonging to the aromatic category, moisture and sugar load are kept low, which is why it's referred to as the "driest aromatic." Its sweetness is measured, nicotine is light; burley adds an earthy body. Suited to smokers who want an aromatic character while avoiding sticky, heavily sugared tobaccos, and who want a blend ready to pack straight into the pipe. It's ribbon cut.
sutliff-tobacco-company-blacksburg.o: A dark tobacco scent mixes into dried fruit and rum.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2001.z: Christmas Cheer is the straight Virginia series that Kansas City-based McClelland released once a year, in limited numbers, from the 1980s until the company's closure in early 2018. The series' idea is to present a single Virginia batch selected from that year's harvest on its own; each year is thus considered a separate record, and the year on the tin defines the blend's identity. The 2001 release was prepared the same way, with selected matured Virginia leaf pressed into cake and tinned as broken flake. Records indicate it's among the series' earlier releases, and tins that have been cellared long hold collector value. Unflavored Virginia character dominates the smoke: natural leaf sweetness over a bready, herbal base, with a faint tang and a lemony sharpness in the background. Nicotine dose is measured, while flavor intensity is pronounced; it burns cool when smoked slowly, but tends to bite the tongue when rushed. Since the flake's moisture can run high straight from the tin, airing it before packing is common practice. A record aimed at smokers seeking unflavored Virginia who are considering cellaring the tin; not suitable for those expecting an aromatic.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2001.o: A tangy, sharp trace characteristic of McClelland tins mixes into an aroma of dry hay and toasted bread.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-sir-walte.z: Sir Walter Raleigh Aromatic is the cased version of the classic American brand of the same name. A casing giving a fine sweetness is added to a blend balancing burley and virginia leaf; this preserves burley's nutty body while softening the smoke. Described as an evenly burning, cool tobacco. Suited to those seeking all-day-smokable aromatics and to pipe newcomers, staying in the light-to-medium nicotine range.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-sir-walte.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly creamy tobacco scent.

brigham-enterprises-inc-sweet-pleasure.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named Sweet Pleasure under the Brigham Enterprises Inc. brand could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-tobacco-galleria.z: This is the tinned product in Sutliff's Tobacco Galleria line sharing its name with the bulk Rum & Maple blend; no accessible source could be found showing whether the two blends are exactly identical.

american-tobacco-co-bowl-of-roses.z: Bowl of Roses is, per records, an American aromatic blend sold in pocket tins in the mid-twentieth century; since it can only be traced today through collector's tins, its content and cut could not be verified.

gawith-hoggarth-co-bourbon-flake.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Bourbon Flake blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

w-o-larsen-virginia-flowers.z: W.Ø. Larsen Virginia Flowers is one of the blends from the Copenhagen-based Larsen name carrying on the Danish aromatic tradition. Its composition includes Virginia, Burley, and black cavendish leaves, prepared in a loose, broad cut. A light caramel-leaning casing is applied on top, so the tin gives off a sweet scent when opened. The brand originates from Denmark, not Ireland or Germany; today its products are prepared under the Scandinavian Tobacco Group umbrella. It's a blend that stays very light in nicotine; the flavor also runs mainly on Virginia sweetness and cavendish softness, with Burley filling out the body a little. The casing level is measured, not intense enough to leave a sugary film in the mouth. It suits those newly moving toward the aromatic side or seeking a light, all-day-sustainable tobacco; those who favor strong, tobacco-focused blends may find it too plain.
w-o-larsen-virginia-flowers.o: Leaves a sweetish caramel scent leaning toward burnt sugar.

pipesandcigars-com-virginia-sundown.z: Virginia Sundown is a listing cited among pipesandcigars.com's bulk Virginia blends; no source could be found sufficient to document its leaf composition and cut, so no detailed specification is given.

sutliff-tobacco-company-buckheads-best.z: Referred to as one of the Virginia-burley-based private blends Sutliff produces under a retailer's name; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-buckheads-best.o: Records indicate it leaves a nutty, lightly sweet leaf scent.

erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-1982.z: 1982 Centennial Blend is an aromatic prepared for the Stokkebye family's hundredth year in the tobacco business. Golden Virginia leaves are joined by soft black cavendish and light Burley; small navy-pressed flake pieces are also mixed in, so the cut is not a uniform ribbon but a mixed look. French vanilla and blackberry notes are used in the topping. Because its fruity, creamy topping is pronounced, the scent lingers in the room for a long time.
