It suits smokers seeking a sweet aromatic blend where the added flavoring is clearly noticeable, while also wanting a low nicotine load that can be smoked all day.
erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-1982.o: Leaves a scent combining vanilla cream and dark forest berries.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-1999.z: Christmas Cheer 1999 is a tin in McClelland's annual Virginia series. Per its label, it's prepared with mature, orange-colored flue-cured Virginias selected from the Carolina Border Belt region's 1994 harvest. The unflavored leaf is pressed and presented as broken flake. Orange-colored Virginias give a medium-bodied profile where sweetness and tang are balanced. No flavoring is used, and nicotine is medium. Since the series is produced for cellaring, the leaf is expected to mature with age; suited to those who love smoking a single-varietal Virginia.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-1999.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of sweet hay and ripe orange.

leavitt-peirce-balkan-no-1.z: Sold as the first number of the Balkan series at Leavitt & Peirce's Harvard Square shop; no source could be found describing the blend's composition.

samuel-gawith-grousemoor.z: Grousemoor is one of Samuel Gawith's aromatics tied to the Lakeland tradition. Its base is flame-cured light Virginia leaf; the leaf is first steamed and cut, then stoved and flavored by the producer with an essence blend. Its name comes from grouse hunting practiced on English moors. The cut is ribbon form and the tin carries a pronounced perfume scent. On the smoke, Virginia's sweetness proceeds together with a floral, lightly soapy Lakeland essence; the flavor level is high and tends to linger in the pipe, so it is usually reserved for a pipe set aside for this style. Nicotine and flavor intensity are medium. A blend for smokers wanting to get to know the classic English aromatic and Lakeland style; not suitable for those seeking unflavored Virginia.
samuel-gawith-grousemoor.o: Spreads a soapy floral essence and a lavender-like perfume trace through the room.

brookfield-black-vanilla-no-2.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Black Vanilla (No. 2) under the Brookfield brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

faders-oxford.z: Not enough independent sourcing documenting the composition and character of Oxford, one of the house blends of the Baltimore-based Fader's tobacconist, could be found.

seattle-pipe-club-give-me-liberty.z: Give Me Liberty is an unflavored blend built mainly from red Virginia leaf sourced from North Carolina's Old Belt region. A lightly stoved Brazilian Virginia is added to this; after aging, the mixture is pressed into a plug. The dark, bready sweetness of the red Virginia runs alongside the lemony tartness of the flue-cured leaf; the pressing softens and rounds off both sides. Nicotine load is medium. Suited to those willing to slice and rub the plug for preparation, seeking an unflavored Virginia they can smoke all day.
seattle-pipe-club-give-me-liberty.o: Leaves a bready sweetness alongside a lightly sour, hay-like scent.

niall-of-nine-hellmouth.z: One of the blends prepared in very small batches under the Niall of Nine signature; not enough independent source material documenting its composition and character could be found.

mccranies-southern-cream.z: Southern Cream is one of the cream-leaning aromatic bulk blends from McCranie's shop; sufficient sources describing its composition could not be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-ts9-maryland.z: TS9 Maryland is a Burley-Virginia mixture among Sutliff's unflavored base tobaccos. The Maryland in its name refers historically to a leaf type that burns very well, with a mild taste but good fullness. The blend carries no flavoring; the taste is flat, dry, and calm, while the burn qualities are quite stable. The main function of a tobacco like this is to serve as a base. Smokers who build their own blends turn to a neutral leaf like this to dilute strong Latakia, Perique, or heavily flavored components and to fix a mixture's burn. Smoked on its own, nicotine is light-medium and the taste profile is plain; it doesn't suit smokers looking for intense taste, but rather those wanting a calm profile they can smoke all day.
sutliff-tobacco-company-ts9-maryland.o: Leaves a dry-leaf scent with a light nutty, papery note.

j-f-germain-son-germains-medium-flake.z: Medium Flake is J. F. Germain & Son's pressed blend built solely on Virginia leaf. Per the maker's description, red, brown, and golden Virginia grades are pressed together and sliced to rub out easily; the aim is to let the leaf's natural flavor come forward. Body is light to medium, and it smokes cool. The flavor comes directly from the leaf's sugar and carries a pronounced sweetness; sources note that it can sting the tongue if smoked too fast. It suits smokers who want an unflavored, single-varietal Virginia and who are accustomed to smoking slowly; like other pressed Virginias, it takes well to aging.
j-f-germain-son-germains-medium-flake.o: Leaves a lightly sweet trace reminiscent of straw, dried hay, and honey.

bosphorus-balkan-flake.z: Balkan Flake is an unflavored blend built by adding Latakia and Turkish Oriental leaf over a Virginia base, pressed into flake form. It belongs to the Latakia branch of the Bosphorus series produced in Istanbul; the Oriental leaf the brand uses is of Adıyaman origin, while some of the Latakia comes from Syria. The blend is considered full in nicotine. Latakia's smoky, resinous taste comes forward, with the Oriental's spicy tartness and Virginia's sweetness sitting underneath it. Because of its pressed structure, the slices need to be crumbled before filling, and aired if needed. Suitable for experienced smokers seeking an unflavored, full-bodied, smoky Balkan blend.
bosphorus-balkan-flake.o: Leaves a sharp smoke aroma leaning into spicy Oriental over smoky Latakia.

bufflehead-harlequin-duck.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Harlequin Duck under the Bufflehead brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

lane-limited-tgb-1.z: Not enough independent sources could be found documenting the contents and character of American blender Lane Limited's blend called TGB-1.

motzek-morning-1975.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called Morning 1975 could be found.

pipe-republic-pink-villa.z: No reliable sources on Pipe Republic's blend Pink Villa could be found, so its content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

sutliff-tobacco-company-casanova-b37.z: Casanova B37 is a Sutliff bulk aromatic dominated by flavored black cavendish, supported by burley and Virginia. The high cavendish ratio gives the blend a measured vanilla sweetness; burley and Virginia sit at equal weight, building a fruity, molasses-leaning background. It's a cool-burning blend with low tongue bite; nicotine strength is light. The ribbon cut makes packing and lighting easy. A record for those seeking a balanced-sweetness, everyday-smokable aromatic.
sutliff-tobacco-company-casanova-b37.o: Leaves a scent carrying soft vanilla and molasses sweetness.

mcclelland-front-runner.z: No sufficient independent source describing the contents and character of this blend could be found.
mcclelland-front-runner.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet aroma typical of aromatic blends.

my-smoking-shop-old-fashioned.z: One of the Virginia-based blends My Smoking Shop sells in bulk; sufficient sources describing its composition and character could not be found.

ken-byron-ventures-moonlit-trail.z: Moonlit Trail is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

seattle-pipe-club-plum-pudding-special-r.z: Plum Pudding Special Reserve is a longer-aged, then-tinned version of the brand's Balkan blend. The leaf list matches the main record: Cyprus Latakia, Turkish Orientals, Virginia, Perique, and black cavendish. What sets the special series apart is the extra maturation applied before tinning. This period rounds off Latakia's sharp smoke and unites the Virginia sugars and Oriental spice into a single whole; the dried-fruit direction reads deeper. The blend remains a full-bodied, intensely sweet Balkan record. Aimed at smokers who know the main version and want to smoke the matured take of the same recipe comparatively, and at those seeking cellar-worthy records.
seattle-pipe-club-plum-pudding-special-r.o: Leaves a deepened pine-smoke scent along with dried plum and leather.

dunhill-my-mixture-10.z: A discontinued mixture belonging to Dunhill's My Mixture line, for which no verifiable source on its composition could be found.

dan-tobacco-galway.z: Galway is an aromatic blend in Dan Tobacco's "Treasures of Ireland" series. A base of sweet Virginia and very soft black Cavendish is flavored with blackberry and vanilla; it belongs to the series' "Black and Bright" leaf line. The casing is kept light enough not to mask the leaf: in the background there's soft vanilla and a light tart blackberry note, while up front the Virginia's grassy sweetness and the Cavendish's creamy texture come through. It lights easily, giving a cool, dry smoke. Suited to smokers who like a moderate fruity aromatic or are new to aromatics.
dan-tobacco-galway.o: Leaves a sweet scent reminiscent of blackberry jam and vanilla cream.

charutaria-cruzeiro-ltda-tabaco-blend-ce.z: The entry has been left incomplete as no reliable source could be found for Charutaria Cruzeiro Ltda.'s Tabaco Blend Cereja (Cherry) blend.

cornell-diehl-corinthian.z: One of Cornell & Diehl's older English-style blends; it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog, and not enough sourcing could be found to verify its composition.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-tc-ebony.z: TC Ebony is a blend appearing in the Wilke Pipe Tobacco catalog; no verifiable source could be found regarding its composition, cut, and character.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-tc-ebony.o: No confirmed description of the room note could be found.

bulwark-flake.z: Bulwark Flake is one of the old names in the English pipe tobacco tradition. Per records it was manufactured for a long time by Imperial Tobacco and later continued by Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. in Kendal. It is a pressed and sliced, dark-colored Virginia flake, said to carry a light fruity top flavoring. The slices are dense and moist, needing to be rubbed out and aired before filling. In the smoke, dark bread, dried plum and sugared Virginia tones come forward; the flavoring stays at a level that does not overtake the tobacco. It carries above-medium nicotine and burns slowly. Appeals to smokers familiar with classic English flakes like Digger, Walnut Flake or Original Virginia Flake, seeking a traditional, satisfying Virginia.
bulwark-flake.o: Leaves a heavy, tobacco-forward trace with dark bread crust and dried fruit aroma.

george-karelias-and-sons-hand-rolling.z: Hand-Rolling is the flagship product of Greek tobacco company Karelia's rolling-tobacco line and is also widely distributed in our own market. Virginia forms its base; Burley is used as filler, with a small amount of dark fire-cured Burley used as seasoning. It sits close to the "American type" shag blends of Dutch tradition. The small 25-gram pack yields a very finely cut, medium-to-dark brown mass with reddish tones; because generous amounts of humectant are added to prevent quick drying, the tobacco stays wet by hand. The casing is pronounced: on opening, a wine-like aroma with spice and red-fruit associations comes through, intense enough to sting the nose. When spread on paper and aired for about half an hour, notes of red fruit, sugar, spice, and cocoa blend together. The burn is light and steady, and burn regulators are balanced; by contrast, the smoke is dense and sharp. On the palate, Virginia's very light sugar and the casing's acidity are noticeable, and as the smoke progresses, an accumulating tar taste brings the product closer to an ordinary cigarette smoke. It's a rolling tobacco, not a pipe tobacco, and a product that stands out more for its aroma than for its tobacco taste.
george-karelias-and-sons-hand-rolling.o: Leaves a wine-like aroma with spice and red-fruit associations, along with a heavy, sharp smoke scent.

lane-limited-buttered-rum.z: Buttered Rum is one of Lane Limited's bulk, coarse-cut aromatics. Its base is cut cavendish and burley leaf; some recipes note Virginia is also added. The applied casing is built around buttered rum and vanilla; the smoke starts with a sweet, buttery entry, with rum and a light almond side coming forward past the middle of the bowl. It's a light-to-medium-nicotine, open and single-note blend; suited to those not seeking complex development but wanting a sweet aromatic to smoke all day. Lane is among the most widespread manufacturers of bulk aromatic tobacco in the US market and has been under the Scandinavian Tobacco Group since 2011.
lane-limited-buttered-rum.o: Leaves a sweet rum, melted butter and light almond room note.

bufflehead-shoveler.z: Bufflehead was a brand producing small batches in the United States in the early 2000s, naming its blends after waterfowl; since no independent source describing this blend's content and character could be found, the entry has been left incomplete.

cornell-diehl-haunted-bookshop-cake.z: Haunted Bookshop Cake is the pressed form of Haunted Bookshop, Cornell & Diehl's burley-forward classic. The blend, made of burley, Virginia, and perique, is pressed into a cake and offered as a crumble cake. Pressing lets the flavors meld together and makes the tobacco more amenable to aging; the smoker can break off a piece from the cake and pack it with little preparation. Burley's dry, nutty body is joined by perique's spice and plum tone. It suits smokers wanting an unflavored blend of medium strength and the depth that pressed tobaccos offer.
cornell-diehl-haunted-bookshop-cake.o: Leaves a dark tobacco aroma reminiscent of nuts and tangy bread dough.

stanislaw-driver-mixture.z: A Virginia-forward blend released by the Czech firm Mostex under its Stanislaw brand, part of the "Cars Collection" line produced by the German house Kohlhase & Kopp; sufficient independent sources describing its composition could not be found.
stanislaw-driver-mixture.o: No description is available in records.

gawith-hoggarth-co-exclusive-black-cherr.z: Exclusive Black Cherry is an aromatic blend where double-fermented, sweetened black Cavendish meets flue-cured Virginia in a ribbon cut. The black cherry topping is pronounced; behind it there's a fine vanilla trace and a hint of the brand's classic Lakeland tones. The smoke is thick and cool, and nicotine is low. Suited to smokers who love fruity aromatics and want a low-bite, easy-smoking blend. Among Gawith Hoggarth's cherry-themed products, it's in the same family as Kendal Black Cherry, and has recently been packaged under abbreviated names.
gawith-hoggarth-co-exclusive-black-cherr.o: Leaves a ripe black-cherry and light-vanilla aroma.

cornell-diehl-captain-bobs-ships-mate-bl.z: One of the aromatic blends belonging to Cornell & Diehl's Captain Bob's series; it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog, and not enough sourcing could be found to describe its character.

craven-craven-mixture.z: Craven Mixture is a historic English blend based on the mixture London tobacconist Don José Joaquin Carreras prepared for the third Earl of Craven in the 1860s. Its appearance under the name "Arcadia Mixture" in J. M. Barrie's 1890 book My Lady Nicotine introduced it to a wide readership, and it's also referenced as Dr. Watson's tobacco in the Sherlock Holmes stories. The Carreras company was later absorbed into Rothmans, and the blend was subsequently discontinued. Its composition includes Syrian Latakia, Oriental tobaccos, and not-too-light Virginia leaf; records indicate fire-cured leaf was also used. Its profile is described as flat, unified, and full, with pronounced nicotine. It was sold in knife-lid tins. Since it can no longer be found today, attempts have been made to recreate the blend; McClelland's 221b Series Arcadia and Cornell & Diehl's Yale Mixture are cited examples in this direction.
craven-craven-mixture.o: Leaves a scent of smoke, cedar wood, and dry hay reminiscent of a campfire.

solani-333-festival.z: Solani 333 Festival is an aromatic blend in the Solani line from Hamburg-based Kohlhase & Kopp. The body is built from red and golden Virginia leaves along with two separate grades of black cavendish; a small amount of burley is added to keep the burn cool and carry the sweet topping. The coarse-cut ribbon structure gives a scent of plum, blackcurrant, and vanilla when the tin is opened. On the palate there's a light-to-medium fullness, dried-fruit flavors, and a creamy texture; it's noted to burn cool and even. Keeping the aromatic topping measured enough not to overwhelm the Virginia and cavendish base sets the blend apart from heavily flavored aromatics. A suitable blend for smokers seeking a flavored tobacco without losing leaf taste, and for those new to the world of aromatics.
solani-333-festival.o: Leaves a scent where dried plum and forest-fruit sweetness meet a light vanilla trace.

mr-bs-days-end-brunante.z: Days End is part of the D line Brigham introduced under the Mr. B's umbrella in 2009, positioned among the full-bodied English blends. Due to Canada's bilingual labeling requirements, the tin also carries the French name "Brûnante"; the two names refer to the same blend. Its composition includes Virginia sweetness, a sharp-tangy layer from Oriental and perique, and a notable share of Latakia. The blend is designed as an evening tobacco to close out the day: flavor intensity and nicotine level are high, with the smoky side at the blend's center. The ribbon cut makes it easy to pack. It is a recipe geared toward smokers accustomed to Latakia-heavy traditional English mixtures; no flavor casing is used.
mr-bs-days-end-brunante.o: Leaves a heavy wood-smoke and soot aroma, with a sharp spice note lingering behind.

bosphorus-balkan-mixture.z: Balkan Mixture is an unflavored, ribbon-cut blend built from Oriental tobaccos and about thirty percent Syrian Latakia. Latakia's characteristic intense aroma appears immediately when the pack is first opened. The tobacco comes quite dry; it can be filled directly without needing to be aired. It lights and burns easily; it is possible to smoke it at a normal pace from the first light to the last puff with almost no relighting. It does not run wet or bite the tongue. Its strength and flavor intensity are medium. Suitable for smokers seeking an unusual Oriental-Latakia composition built with Syrian Latakia.
bosphorus-balkan-mixture.o: Spreads Latakia's characteristic smoky, sharp smoke aroma into the room.

jacks-tobacco-acadian-coast.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of Acadian Coast, one of the products from the small-scale American blender Jack's Tobacco, could be found.
jacks-tobacco-acadian-coast.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

stanwell-ariston.z: An old blend referred to as Scottish style from the Denmark-based Stanwell brand; it does not appear in current retail channels, and sufficient independent sources describing its composition could not be found.
stanwell-ariston.o: No description is available in records.

john-middleton-inc-walnut.z: Walnut is listed as one of John Middleton's American-style blends; not enough sources could be found to describe its contents and character.

mcclelland-black-sea-sokhoum-grand-orien.z: Black Sea Sokhoum is a member of McClelland's Grand Orientals series, which spotlights single-varietal Oriental tobaccos. The blend's core is Samsun-origin tobacco grown in Georgia, joined by Virginia; the cut is ribbon. From the tin, alongside the brand's familiar tangy-sweet aroma, a pronounced cigarette smell comes through, and this character is reflected in the flavor too. The Oriental tobacco's exotic, spicy side reaches its most intense point when the pipe is half smoked; the Virginia's sweetness sets the overall balance. Strength is medium, flavor medium-intense, and no flavoring is used. Suited to smokers seeking pure Oriental character without Latakia; since the room note is sharp, it leaves a noticeable trace indoors.
mcclelland-black-sea-sokhoum-grand-orien.o: Leaves a sharp, spicy, sweet-tart aroma reminiscent of cigarettes.

richs-city-of-roses.z: City of Roses, named after Portland's "City of Roses" nickname, is a house blend at Rich's Cigar Store described as a natural aromatic. It is built from red Burley, Virginia, and sweet Oriental tobacco; added flavoring is minimal, with sweetness coming largely from the leaf itself. The profile shows a nutty base, a light sweetness suggesting honey and flowers, and a spice that lingers on the finish; the overall character leans dry rather than sugary. It suits smokers avoiding heavily flavored aromatics who want a naturally sweet everyday blend. Reports note the blend was previously sold as Wild Rose at House of Calabash. Its current status is unclear since it doesn't appear on the shop's current list.
richs-city-of-roses.o: Leaves a nutty, lightly honeyed, floral aroma.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-dark-strong-ke.z: Dark Strong Kentucky, known by its abbreviation DSK, is an Orlik blend. Fire-cured Kentucky is added to matured Virginia leaves, and the mixture is pressed and sliced into flake, establishing a pronounced contrast between the light and dark leaves' tastes. A light top dressing recalling maple syrup or brown sugar is noted as applied before pressing, though the blend isn't placed in the aromatic class as a result. The taste combines traces of licorice root and molasses, a smoky backbone from the Kentucky, and Virginia's natural sweetness. Strength is medium to full. It was reintroduced to the market after a long period out of distribution. It suits experienced smokers seeking fire-cured leaf's strength and smoky character.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-dark-strong-ke.o: Leaves a wood-fire-smoke scent alongside a sweet, molasses-like aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-old-professor-52.z: Old Professor is a latakia-forward English mixture among Sutliff's numbered bulk blends. Leaf length is not uniform; shag, fine, and thick ribbon pieces sit together. Latakia is pronounced but used in measured amounts, with the lemony sweetness from the Virginia leaf coming forward in the second half of the bowl. Nicotine stays light, making it easier to smoke than heavy English mixtures. Some sources note a light flavoring can be sensed. It falls within the interest of those looking for a soft entry into the Latakia world and those wanting a lightly smoky blend during the day.
sutliff-tobacco-company-old-professor-52.o: Leaves a smoky, woody scent reminiscent of campfire.

mcclelland-no-m-27-three-cherry-blend.z: No. M-27 Three Cherry Blend is a cherry-flavored blend in McClelland's bulk aromatic line. The brand named some blends in this line after catalog numbers of galaxies and star clusters; the name M-27 refers to the Dumbbell Nebula. The base rests on mild, Cavendish-processed leaves, with three separate cherry essences joined by a vanilla-cream note. Flavor intensity is high; the cherry note is pronounced clearly both in aroma and in the smoke. Nicotine dose is low, it burns evenly, and leaves a light gray ash. Aimed at smokers seeking a pronounced fruity aromatic; too dominant for those wanting an unflavored tobacco taste. Unavailable since McClelland stopped production in 2018.
mcclelland-no-m-27-three-cherry-blend.o: Leaves an intense cherry and vanilla-cream aroma that spreads noticeably through the room.

the-tobacco-barn-el-capitan.z: El Capitan is a house blend built from five separate leaves by the Tobacco Barn tobacconist in Lake Forest, California. Per the maker's description, the composition includes Virginia, Burley, Cavendish and Latakia, with a small amount of Perique added for spice. The shop's online sales later continued under the name CigarSpots. The blend is constructed as a bridge blend that delivers Latakia's smoky backbone together with Cavendish's sweetness: it is aimed at smokers wanting to move toward English mixtures but finding a fully dry, smoky profile too soon. Since Perique is used in a small proportion, the spice sits as a supporting element from the side rather than driving the taste. Strength and flavor are moderate.
the-tobacco-barn-el-capitan.o: Leaves a sweetish trace from dark Cavendish beneath a smoky-leaf aroma.

mac-baren-symphony.z: Symphony is one of Mac Baren's classic-series products, a mixture dominated by select Burley leaves. These are joined in a smaller proportion by golden Virginia and the maker's own Cavendish. The blend is pressed using the traditional Cavendish method, sliced, and then packaged rubbed out ready to pack. The aim is to bring forward the mild sweetness and cocoa association naturally present in Burley; the flavoring is kept at a level that supports this trace, not made dominant as in aromatics. The smoke is cool and even, and thanks to the ready-rubbed structure, packing is easy. A suitable middle stop for those seeking a nutty, earthy, chocolate-leaning taste and smokers wanting to move from aromatics to natural leaf taste.
mac-baren-symphony.o: Leaves an aroma of toasted hazelnut and cocoa.

charatan-light-aromatic.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the British pipe maker Charatan.

mastro-de-paja-venezia.z: No reliable source describing the contents and character of the Venezia blend released under the Italian pipe maker Mastro de Paja could be found; records indicate it's an English-style blend.
mastro-de-paja-venezia.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

barclay-rex-coconut.z: Referred to as a coconut-flavored aromatic among the shop blends of Barclay Rex, New York's longstanding tobacconist; no verifiable source on its content and cut could be found.
barclay-rex-coconut.o: Leaves a sweet room note dominated by coconut.

mccranies-old-master.z: Old Master is one of the Burley-forward house blends from McCranie's tobacconist in Charlotte, North Carolina; since no independent source detailing its composition could be found, no full description is given here.
mccranies-old-master.o: Leaves a nutty tobacco aroma alongside a faint trace of cocoa and vanilla.

cornell-diehl-good-morning.z: Good Morning is a ribbon-cut English mixture Cornell & Diehl prepared years ago for the Chicagoland Pipe Show. Its base is red and bright Virginia; Cyprus Latakia and Oriental leaves play a supporting role, with no added flavoring. Red Virginia's ripe dark-fruit and earthy notes lead, while bright Virginia carries the citrus-and-grass side. Latakia builds a smoky, woody frame, joined by the Orientals with their spicy, dry, buttery sweetness; the Latakia level is kept from overwhelming the blend. This makes it suitable for those new to English mixtures and for anyone wanting a lightly smoky smoke early in the day.
cornell-diehl-good-morning.o: Leaves a dry aroma where spiced Oriental notes layer over woody, smoky Latakia.

stanwell-extra-mild.z: As its name suggests, a low-nicotine, burley-forward light blend from the Stanwell brand; sufficient independent sources describing its composition and flavor profile could not be found.
stanwell-extra-mild.o: No description is available in records.

rain-city-cigar-buttered-rum-reserve.z: This is a house blend from Rain City Cigar, open since 1997 in Seattle's Georgetown neighborhood; there is not enough source material describing its composition and character.

g-l-pease-jackknife-plug.z: JackKnife Plug is the blend that opens G. L. Pease's New World Collection line and is the brand's first plug product. Dark and light Virginia leaves are pressed and matured together with dark fire-cured Kentucky leaf, then presented cut into a block. The plug form lets the smoker cut and rub out the slice at whatever thickness they like, which lets the burn speed and flavour intensity be adjusted. Kentucky's woody, smoky body and high nicotine load direct the blend toward experienced smokers seeking fullness.
g-l-pease-jackknife-plug.o: Leaves a heavy woody smokiness from the fire-cured leaf.

house-of-windsor-model.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for House of Windsor's Model blend, so its content and character could not be recorded.

stanwell-corvado-tequila.z: A tequila-themed aromatic blend from the Stanwell brand; sufficient independent sources describing its composition and character could not be found.
stanwell-corvado-tequila.o: No description is available in records.

cornell-diehl-odessa.z: Odessa is a medium-bodied English mixture Cornell & Diehl builds on a burley base. Per the manufacturer's description, burley, Oriental leaves, Latakia, and perique are used together, with Virginia also present in the mix. The Latakia level is enough to give a smoky character without masking the other leaves. Burley lends the blend a cool, dry body, while perique adds a measured spicy edge. The maker describes it as a blend suited to all-day smoking. It offers a middle-ground option for smokers new to Latakia blends or those who find full-bodied English mixtures too heavy.
cornell-diehl-odessa.o: Leaves a dry, grassy note mingled with a touch of smoke and leather.

seattle-pipe-club-rainier-levant.z: Rainier Levant is Seattle Pipe Club's Balkan-style blend. It consists of red Virginia, Turkish-Oriental leaf, and a generous amount of Cyprus Latakia. According to records, the blend's origin traces to Levant Mixture from Drucquer & Sons, once based in Berkeley, California; Joe Lankford developed his own take on the recipe starting from an old tin. It takes its name from Mount Rainier, which overlooks Seattle. On the smoke, Latakia's smoky, resinous character leads, but it is balanced by the sour-spicy, orange-peel-like sweetness of the Oriental leaf and the bready base of the red Virginia; it is built as a layered Balkan blend rather than a straight pile of Latakia. Nicotine sits in the medium range. Aimed at smokers accustomed to unflavored, smoky blends and interested in classic Balkan recipes.
seattle-pipe-club-rainier-levant.o: Leaves a smoky, resinous, faintly floral scent reminiscent of an incense stick.

vegassmokes-five-star-deluxe.z: The member of the Five Star family described as English-style; no independent source confirming its composition has been found.

iwan-ries-china-black-whiskey.z: China Black Whiskey is a whiskey-flavored blend in Iwan Ries's China Black line, built on fire-cured dark leaf. Fire-curing gives the leaf a smoky, deep base; the whiskey flavoring adds a sweet, sharp layer on top. Like the other members of the line, it's presented coarse-cut and suited to slow burning. It's an option for smokers looking for a darker, smokier base among aromatic blends.
iwan-ries-china-black-whiskey.o: The sweet-sharp aroma of the whiskey flavoring mixes with the smokiness of the fire-cured leaf.

edwards-black-cherry.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Black Cherry, a pipe tobacco from Edward's. Edward's is a tobacconist business based in Tampa, Florida.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-john-bull.z: The English-style blend of the John Bull line; no reliable detail on its composition and production status could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-john-bull.o: Leaves a smoky scent from latakia.

thepiperoom-com-bing-cherry.z: No independent source documenting the composition of ThePipeRoom.com's cherry-flavored blend Bing Cherry has been found; the brand's own site is no longer online.
thepiperoom-com-bing-cherry.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-dark-shag-unsc.z: The unflavored version of Kendal Dark shows Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s dark-leaf approach in its plainest form. Malawi-origin fire-cured leaf and India-origin air-cured Virginia are cut into fine shag; no top flavoring is applied. Records indicate the pressed version of the same leaf mixture is sold under the name Dark Flake. On the taste side, dry hay, bread crust, and earth dominate; a clear peppery sharpness accompanies the smoke. Nicotine is high, so it isn't well suited to smoking on an empty stomach or at a fast pace. Aimed at experienced smokers wanting an unflavored, dark, and full-bodied English tobacco.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-dark-shag-unsc.o: Leaves a smoky, earthy, and sharply scorched-leaf aroma.

samuel-gawith-chocolate-plug.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Chocolate Plug, according to records a Virginia-forward blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

nat-sherman-509-blend-manhattan-twilight.z: 509 Blend is Nat Sherman's dark aromatic, also known by the name Manhattan Twilight. Records indicate it was produced in the US by Lane Limited, sold only at the company's New York store starting in 2007, and reissued in tin form in 2014. It has a jet-black appearance, built mainly around heavily sauced black cavendish, with vanilla and maple syrup standing out in the casing. The smoke is thick and cool, with dense smoke output; the taste shows vanilla, nougat, and toasted nuts, while the sense of nicotine stays low. Because of its pronounced casing and strong room note, it is a blend set aside for evening smoking, geared toward smokers who like dark aromatics. It is out of production since the brand's tobacco operations ended.
nat-sherman-509-blend-manhattan-twilight.o: Leaves an intense aroma of vanilla, caramelized sugar, and nutty nougat.

dan-tobacco-bulldog-curly-cut.z: A blend that was part of Dan Tobacco's Bulldog series, presented in roughly 25-millimeter rolled slices with a black-Cavendish core and containing Perique; no adequate source documenting its ratios was found.
dan-tobacco-bulldog-curly-cut.o: Records indicate it leaves a dark scent leaning toward dried fruit.

house-of-calabash-ancient-imperial-ancie.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for House of Calabash's Ancient Imperial - Ancient Blend, so its content and character could not be recorded.

cornell-diehl-dark-burley.z: Dark Burley is a blending tobacco in which Cornell & Diehl offers air-cured dark burley leaf from Kentucky fields on its own. It is packaged as a ribbon cut, and the brand describes it as both a tobacco that can be smoked on its own and a base leaf for home mixtures. The taste is naturally sweet, nutty, and earthy; a sweetness coming from the leaf itself rather than sugar, alongside a cigar-like dry body, is described. It suits users looking for the full expression of unflavored burley and wanting a hearty, nicotine-rich smoke, as well as those building their own blends.
cornell-diehl-dark-burley.o: Leaves a dry, earthy, lightly tangy room aroma reminiscent of cigar.

american-club-classic.z: No reliable source describing the content and character of American Club Classic could be found.

davis-and-son-tobacconists-english-supre.z: English Supreme is a latakia-containing mixture among the house blends of Davis & Son Tobacconists in Wilmington. The shop lists such blends separately under an "English" heading. The blend consists of aged virginia combined with oriental tobaccos from Smyrna, Dubec and Macedonia, and latakia; structurally it falls under the Balkan mixture definition, meaning the oriental share is pronounced. Latakia gives a smoky, woody layer, the oriental leaves a tart, spicy top note, and virginia a measured sweetness in the background. It's unadulterated. It suits smokers accustomed to smoky, unadulterated blends, for long evening smokes.
davis-and-son-tobacconists-english-supre.o: Leaves a sharp, smoky scent evoking pine smoke and fire-cured leaf.

the-storytellers-pipe-cockeyed-kilt.z: Cockeyed Kilt is one of the house blends the Illinois-based The Story Teller's Pipe tobacconist prepares at its own counter. Per the maker's description, Latakia and Oriental leaf are first balanced against each other, then soft Cavendish, Burley and Virginia are added to the mix; it is sold ribbon cut. While Latakia's smoky backbone is preserved, a light citrus and fruit flavoring is layered on top, which is why the maker describes the blend as a bridge point between English mixtures and aromatics. It is medium in strength and flavor; it acts neither as a pure Latakia bomb nor as a casing-forward aromatic. Suited to smokers wanting to get used to English mixtures but finding a fully dry, unflavored profile too soon, as well as those coming from the aromatic side wanting to get acquainted with smoky leaf. A house blend sold loose by the ounce rather than in tins.
the-storytellers-pipe-cockeyed-kilt.o: Leaves an aroma where a light citrus sweetness can be sensed beneath wood smoke and spiced leaf.

the-tobacco-barn-danish-virginia.z: A Virginia blend the Tobacco Barn tobacconist calls Danish style; no verifiable source describing its composition and character has been found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-balkan-sa.z: Balkan Sasieni is a Balkan mixture with roughly a century of history. The blend was born in London; according to records it is produced today in Denmark and sold mainly in the American market. Its structure holds Macedonian and Black Sea Orientals, red virginia, and plenty of Cyprus latakia. It is presented ribbon cut in 50-gram tins, with no casing applied. On opening the tin, the latakia scent dominates; the tobacco arrives moist and may need airing. On the smoke, latakia is abundant and pronounced but does not cover the other leaves: behind it come the virginia's sweetness and the orientals' bitter, spicy tone. Packing and lighting are easy, the ash stays light gray; harshness increases as the bowl progresses and may cause slight tongue bite in sensitive smokers. Suited to smokers seeking the classic Balkan structure where latakia leads without upsetting the balance.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-balkan-sa.o: Heavy latakia soot and tar scent fills the room, with a spicy Oriental-tobacco trace underneath.

peter-stokkebye-black-currant-cavendish-.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Black Currant Cavendish (No.45) could be found.

vauen-auenland-morning-mixture.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Vauen blend called Auenland Morning Mixture has been found.
vauen-auenland-morning-mixture.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

watch-city-cigar-balkan-mild.z: This is described as a house blend from Watch City Cigar, an Oriental-forward Balkan mixture kept mild; no published maker record could be found.
watch-city-cigar-balkan-mild.o: Could not be determined from the records.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-baker-str.z: Baker Street, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an English-type mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

dan-tobacco-the-mallard-flake-plus-periq.z: This is a blend from the German maker Dan Tobacco, noted as Virginia- and Perique-based; not enough sourcing could be reached to verify its composition and character.

exclusiv-no-6-sherry-cherry.z: Sherry & Cherry is a member of the Exclusiv aromatic line produced by the house of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. in Kendal; after the line's naming was simplified it is also known as Exclusiv SC. The blend's base is built from Virginia leaf and black cavendish, prepared soft enough to carry the flavouring. Two flavourings named in the blend are used together: a dark, raisin-like note reminiscent of sherry wine, and cherry essence. Despite the intensity of the flavouring, the smoke stays light in nicotine; the taste runs sweet and full. It suits smokers seeking a fruity, wine-noted aromatic; it contains no Latakia or Oriental leaf.
exclusiv-no-6-sherry-cherry.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly alcoholic aroma reminiscent of a wine cask together with cherry.

torben-dansk-no-14-navy-cut.z: Torben Dansk No.14 Navy Cut is a Danish-style flake. It is made by pressing several varieties of Virginia; it gives a full, aromatic taste while noted for staying particularly mellow when smoked. The light flavoring on top sits alongside Virginia's own natural sugar. The flake slices are broken up by hand or folded before lighting, giving a slow, cool burn. Suited to those after a Virginia flake on the sweet side without harshness, and to those newly moving into flake smoking.
torben-dansk-no-14-navy-cut.o: Leaves a sweet dry-hay and light caramel aroma.

blatter-blatter-baker-street.z: One of the house blends prepared at the counter of the Blatter & Blatter shop in Montreal; no reliable source documenting its content could be found.

poul-winslow-poul-winslow-no-1.z: This is one of the numbered blends in the line carrying the name of Danish pipe maker Poul Winslow; no verifiable source could be found on its content or flavoring.
poul-winslow-poul-winslow-no-1.o: It is recorded as a flavored blend; there is not enough source material to describe its aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-sambuca-747.z: A Sutliff aromatic named after the anise-flavored Italian liqueur sambuca; no independent source documenting the tobacco's composition and character could be found.

kramers-pipe-and-tobacco-shop-blend-for-.z: One of the blends prepared by Kramer's Pipe and Tobacco Shop in Beverly Hills for its customer, actor Cary Grant, this ribbon-cut blend is classed in the English aromatic family; not enough sources could be found to detail its contents.

watch-city-cigar-masshole-flake.z: Masshole Flake is Watch City Cigar's Burley-forward house blend in flake form. According to records, it's built from Burley leaves of African and Brazilian origin; a light cocoa casing supports the base's nutty, earthy, and molasses-like tones. Since the long flake slices retain their moisture, they can be rubbed out by hand into whatever fill form is desired. Flavor intensity is pronounced, and the burn is cool and slow; its structure suits smokers seeking Burley's tart sharpness and its grassy, woody tones over Virginia sweetness. Nicotine load is medium, making it suitable for those wanting a full-bodied everyday Burley.
watch-city-cigar-masshole-flake.o: Leaves a cocoa-tinged, nutty, lightly earthy scent.

gallaher-limited-golden-bar.z: This is a blend called Golden Bar among the pipe tobaccos of Gallaher Limited, founded by Tom Gallaher in Derry in 1857 and later absorbed into Japan Tobacco; no reliable source could be found on the blend's composition and character.

smokers-haven-owens-blend.z: An American-style blend appearing in the Smokers' Haven catalog; sufficient sources describing its composition could not be found.

samuel-gawith-kendal-plug.z: A plug in Samuel Gawith's plug-tobacco line, referred to in records as natural tobacco carrying no essence casing; no sufficient source confirming its leaf composition and character could be found.

torben-dansk-louisiana-perique-u-s-a.z: Torben Dansk Louisiana Perique U.S.A is a single-varietal blending component consisting of Perique leaf fermented under pressure in Louisiana's St. James region. Perique is described as the leaf that gives blends a pronounced spice and black-pepper sharpness; it also carries dried-fruit notes. Nicotine and flavor intensity are very high, so it is generally used at proportions not exceeding ten percent in blends. Suited to experienced home blenders wanting to sharpen their Virginia-forward mixtures.
torben-dansk-louisiana-perique-u-s-a.o: Leaves a peppery, vinegary-sharp aroma of dried fig and plum.

peterson-holiday-season-2012.z: Holiday Season is Peterson's limited-edition, Christmas-themed aromatic tin series released each year; the 2012 edition was presented in a 100 gram tin. In this edition, various Virginia leaves are blended with three distinct black Cavendishes, bringing forward hazelnut, caramel, and baked apple notes. Peterson is an Irish brand, but the blending and production of these special tins is outsourced; records indicate they were made by Kohlhase, Kopp & Co. to a recipe specified by Peterson. The cut is described as broadly cut. Because the recipe changes each year, every edition of the series counts as a distinct blend; the 2012 tin was likewise prepared for its release year and never reprinted. It is a notable record for smokers seeking flavored, sweet-profile tins and for those who collect the annual limited editions.
peterson-holiday-season-2012.o: Leaves a baked apple and caramel aroma.

sobranie-of-london-the-balkan-sobranie-7.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Sobranie of London blend called The Balkan Sobranie 759 could not be found.

hearth-home-daybreak.z: Daybreak was designed as a light English blend in the Hearth & Home signature series, meant for all-day smoking. Its base is sweet Virginia leaf, joined by a measured amount of Oriental and a small hand-added portion of Cyprian Latakia, keeping the smoke layer from overtaking the Virginia sweetness. According to the maker, the blend was developed at the request of the New York Pipe Club during a period when Dunhill tobaccos were unavailable in the United States. Body runs light to medium, nicotine is low, and the blend is unflavored. Well suited to smokers new to English blends, as well as those looking for a Latakia mixture light enough for morning smokes or long sessions.
hearth-home-daybreak.o: Leaves a light wood-smoke aroma along with dry hay and bready sweetness.

magne-falkum-falkums-wintertabak.z: Falkums Wintertabak is a Danish-style aromatic blend Miltenberg-based Tabakhaus Falkum prepared for the winter season. Its composition holds twice-fermented Black Cavendish, Maryland Burley, and golden and red Virginia leaves from Zimbabwe. It's loose cut; a flavoring blend of rhubarb, vanilla, orange, and cinnamon is applied over it. The smoke is sweet and spicy; the Cavendish's dark sugary taste proceeds together with the Virginia's fruity acidity and the sharpness of cinnamon and orange. Nicotine load is kept low, suiting long sittings. Suited to smokers who like pronouncedly flavored tobaccos and seek seasonal, sweet blends; doesn't match the expectations of those seeking unflavored tobacco.
magne-falkum-falkums-wintertabak.o: Leaves a sweet, spicy aroma in which cinnamon, orange peel, and vanilla stand out.

pauls-pipe-shop-louisiana-coffee-tobacco.z: Louisiana Coffee is a Paul's Pipe Shop blend taking its name from Louisiana cuisine's chicory-laced coffee tradition. Per the maker's recipe, Virginia leaf given a cappuccino essence is joined by some of the shop's Arrowhead blend and coffee-flavored burley. The Arrowhead component brings cavendish, Virginia flake, and a small amount of spicy leaf to the blend. The result is a medium-bodied aromatic where Virginia's sweetness and burley's dry body come together under a coffee note. The smoke is cool, and the topping is pronounced but not enough to entirely mask the tobacco taste. It suits those wanting a single-note sweetness alongside their morning coffee.
pauls-pipe-shop-louisiana-coffee-tobacco.o: Leaves a scent of coffee with milk and roasted beans.

hu-tobacco-nashville-county.z: Nashville County is a blend from German blender Hans Wiedemann, prepared under the HU Tobacco umbrella, that positions Burley not as a carrier but as the main ingredient. Per the maker's description, roughly sixty percent of the mixture is made up of strong, sweet Kentucky-Burley grades of Tennessee origin; these are joined by malty red Virginia leaves and a very small touch of Perique. With a structure carrying a light toastiness and a licorice-root trace, it's presented in ready-rubbed flake form, and the tobacco can be filled straight from the tin. In the cold tin aroma, nutty toasted notes, a light chocolatey layer, and a herbal sweetness come forward; in the smoke, Burley's earthy fullness is balanced by Virginia's malty sweetness. Being on the full side for nicotine, it's aimed at smokers accustomed to heavy Burley blends, looking for an unflavored or nearly unflavored American style; it isn't suited to smoking on an empty stomach.
hu-tobacco-nashville-county.o: Leaves an aroma of toasted hazelnut, light cocoa, and licorice root.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-maple-twist.z: Sweet Maple Twist is another product from Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s rope series. Its composition rests on Burley and dark fire-cured Kentucky leaf, topped with a light maple flavoring. Because the leaves are twisted and wound into a roll, the tobacco takes on a dense, oily, tight structure. On the smoke, earthy, woody, and spicy notes stand out; a cocoa-like sweetness remains in the background, and the overall character leans toward cigar leaf. Sources indicate it isn't at the strongest end among rope tobaccos, but it's still considered strong. It needs to be thinly sliced and rubbed out before use. Suited to those who love the weight of fire-cured leaf as well as smokers wanting to try a lightly flavored, traditional English rope tobacco.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-maple-twist.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of maple syrup alongside woody smoke.

clan-shaw-bear-claw.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Bear Claw.

lane-limited-10-downing-st.z: One of Lane Limited's bulk-sold English-type blends; not enough sources could be found for its proportions and character.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-sticky-.z: A blend released as part of Ken Byron Ventures' small-batch production; no independent, verifiable source could be found on it.

paul-olsen-pure-virginia.z: A Paul Olsen house blend apparently built on unflavored Virginia judging by its name; no independent source confirming its details could be found.

timm-no-name-violett.z: The purple variety in the Timm No Name series is an intense aromatic blend built on black Cavendish and Virginia leaf. The defining casing is cherry; the mixture is kept on a distinctly sweet line. It is very light in nicotine and mellow to smoke. An everyday blend, sold in a large package, aimed at those seeking cherry-flavored tobaccos and newcomers to the pipe.
timm-no-name-violett.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of ripe cherry and candy.

brebbia-latakia-flake-mixture-no-9.z: Latakia Flake No. 9, in Brebbia's numbered series, is a pressed flake tobacco built on Virginia and Syrian Latakia. The Latakia proportion is kept noticeably lower than the same brand's Balkan blend; the blend is calibrated to bring out the Syrian leaf's finer tones. The slices come dry and crumble easily by hand, so keeping them whole is difficult. In the smoke, Virginia's sweetness and Latakia's woody smoke run in balance; the blend is not a heavy Latakia bomb. Suitable for smokers experienced with working flake tobacco and seeking a measured dose of smoke.
brebbia-latakia-flake-mixture-no-9.o: Leaves a light wood smoke together with dried grass and spice aroma.

drucquer-sons-cooks-5.z: A mixture tied to Drucquer & Sons, for which no verifiable source on its composition and character could be found.

peter-stokkebye-heather-raspberry.z: This is one of Peter Stokkebye's flavored blends; no sufficient first-hand sources documenting its content and character could be found.
peter-stokkebye-heather-raspberry.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

mac-baren-halberg-red.z: Not enough information could be found in the manufacturer's current catalog or verifiable independent sources about this member of the Halberg series.

astleys-no-99-royal-tudor-full-latakia-m.z: Astley's No.99 Royal Tudor is a traditional English mixture combining Virginia and Turkish-Oriental leaf with a high proportion of Latakia. The phrase "full latakia" in its name points to the prominence of the Latakia share in the blend. In the smoke, a balance is struck between Latakia's deep, smoky character and the spiciness of sun-cured Orientals; sweetness from the Virginias keeps the blend from becoming too heavy and rounds out the taste. Body is full, with no added flavoring. It suits smokers who prefer dark English mixtures as an evening smoke and aren't put off by Latakia intensity.
astleys-no-99-royal-tudor-full-latakia-m.o: Fills the room with a spicy, incense-like scent dominated by woodsmoke and soot.

bbb-blue-label-mild-english-mixture.z: This BBB blend, presented with a blue label as a light English mixture, is known to keep its Latakia share low; no adequate source for a detailed composition could be found.
bbb-blue-label-mild-english-mixture.o: Leaves a lightly smoky, woody room note.

spednova-olandese-puro-pure-dutch.z: A blend from the Italian-market-focused Spednova brand aimed at recreating the classic Dutch style; due to insufficient independent sources, its composition and character are not detailed in this record.
spednova-olandese-puro-pure-dutch.o: Records do not provide detail describing this blend's room note.

peterson-3-years-cask-aged-virginia-mixt.z: In this mixture, high-sugar Virginia leaves along with some black Cavendish are rested for at least three years in old oak casks. The long rest brings out the leaf's own sweetness, while vanilla and caramel tones from the cask wood round out the blend. Rum from the Danish distillery Braunstein is used as the top flavoring.
peterson-3-years-cask-aged-virginia-mixt.o: Leaves a sweet rum, vanilla, and cask-wood aroma.

owl-shop-mr-greens.z: Referred to among the Owl Shop's unflavored blends as a full-bodied mixture carrying numerous leaf varieties; no second source detailing its composition could be found.
owl-shop-mr-greens.o: No description could be found in the records.

mr-bs-golden-virginia-flake.z: Golden Virginia Flake is the Virginia blend Canadian Brigham presents in traditional pressed-and-sliced flake form within its Mr. B's line. Virginia leaves ranging in tone from golden to medium brown are used; the taste rests on the sweetness of natural sugar, and the blend is considered light-bodied. The usual preparation is to rub the flake leaf apart and fold it, or fold and load it whole into the bowl.
mr-bs-golden-virginia-flake.o: Leaves a light tobacco aroma carrying dry hay and honeyed sweetness.

schurch-corona.z: Corona, signed by Schürch, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

houston-pipe-club-the-heights.z: This is a limited-circulation, English-style club blend prepared for the Houston Pipe Club; no verifiable source describing its content could be found.

mac-baren-hh-rustica-ready-rubbed.z: HH Rustica takes its name from Nicotiana rustica, the variety that forms the backbone of the blend; this species carries far more nicotine than the Nicotiana tabacum usual in pipe tobaccos. Mac Baren combines this leaf with dark Virginia and burley, applies hot pressing and matures it with light fermentation. Long sold only as slices, the blend has since also been offered as a pre-rubbed (ready rubbed) loose form. The taste is spicy, earthy, woody and grassy; behind it are notes of tangy citrus, tea, smoke, toasted bread and leather, carrying a sharpness close to cigar tobacco. It's the heaviest blend in Mac Baren's catalog in terms of nicotine, and it isn't suited to smoking on an empty stomach. Aimed at very experienced smokers seeking an unflavored, harsh and intense tobacco.
mac-baren-hh-rustica-ready-rubbed.o: Leaves a sharp, cigar-like smoky and earthy room note.

richs-cravens-claw.z: Craven's Claw is one of the Virginia-Perique blends Rich's Cigar Store in Portland prepares in-house. Reports indicate it combines long-rested Virginia leaf with Louisiana Perique aged several years, adding Perique's plum and pepper layer to the blend's tart-sweet Virginia body. Being an unflavored, natural blend, the tobacco's own sugar and fermentation flavors come forward. It deepens when smoked slowly, making it suited to midday and late-afternoon smoking; it appeals to smokers familiar with the Virginia-Perique idiom looking for unflavored tobacco. It is available only in bulk at Rich's stores.
richs-cravens-claw.o: Leaves a light peppery trace along with a tart dried-fruit and stale-bread aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-rum-twist.z: Sweet Rum Twist is Kendal's rope-tobacco tradition rendered in a rum-flavored example. Sources indicate the word "sweet" was dropped from current packaging due to English labeling regulations; the tobacco today is mostly referred to simply as Rum Twist. The twisted, wound dark leaf matures in rope form and needs to be thinly sliced and rubbed out before smoking. The rum flavoring is more pronounced here than in the house's other rope tobaccos, and softens the tobacco's raw, tar-like edge. A light smoky taste remains in the background. Being heavy in nicotine, it gives a hearty smoke. Suited to smokers new to rope tobaccos who want to avoid some of the harshness of plain rolls, as well as those seeking the traditional English twist style.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-rum-twist.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of rum candy along with a fine trace of smoke.

smokinjoescigars-com-joes-easy-mild-blen.z: A bulk blend referred to as a light aromatic signed by the retailer; no source about it could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-tobacco-galleria.z: One of the aromatic blends in Sutliff's Tobacco Galleria line; no accessible source documenting its content could be found.

paul-olsen-old-belt.z: One of the Virginia-forward blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

consolidated-205-peach.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Consolidated blend 205: Peach.

mac-baren-golden-ambrosia.z: Golden Ambrosia is a Danish aromatic with a ready-rubbed cut. The blend combines brown burley tobaccos with Mac Baren's modern cavendish, made by processing golden Virginia leaf into black cavendish. The burley gives the blend a nutty base while the cavendish carries sweetness and softness. Nicotine stays light and the flavor is medium. Since the ready-rubbed structure makes packing easy, it's aimed at those wanting a low-maintenance, sweet-leaning everyday blend.
mac-baren-golden-ambrosia.o: Leaves a honeyed, vanilla-like room note reminiscent of baked pastry.

gawith-hoggarth-co-blonde-bogie.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Blonde Bogie blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

john-cotton-john-cottons-double-pressed-.z: A pressed, Burley-forward blend released under the historic Scottish brand John Cotton; no verifiable information on its current production profile could be found.
john-cotton-john-cottons-double-pressed-.o: No verifiable information on its room note could be found.

lane-limited-danish-cherry.z: Lane Limited's cherry-flavored aromatic blend; not enough sources could be found to detail its composition.

mcclelland-frog-morton-on-the-bayou.z: Frog Morton on the Bayou is a blend built by adding Louisiana Perique to the series' Latakia-Oriental body, and given its high Oriental share, it lands on the Balkan line. The Perique raises the blend's nicotine load and spice output, layering a tangy note reminiscent of pepper, fig, and plum atop the Virginia's sweetness. Named after the Louisiana bayous, the blend is among the fullest-bodied members of the series and is aimed at smokers used to the pairing of Latakia and Perique. Its ribbon cut burns quickly, suiting a heavy smoking pace. Production stopped after the brand closed in 2018.
mcclelland-frog-morton-on-the-bayou.o: A spicy, faintly tangy plum aroma can be sensed beneath the sooty wood.

georgetown-tobacco-jabberwock.z: Referred to as one of Georgetown Tobacco's shop blends; no verifiable sourcing on its composition, cut, and character could be found.
georgetown-tobacco-jabberwock.o: No record of the room aroma could be found.

tinder-box-black-tie.z: Black Tie is Tinder Box's English-type blend exclusive to its own catalog. Cyprus Latakia comes forward, joined by Oriental leaves and flue-cured Virginia that set the blend's sweet, spicy foundation. No casing is used; the taste comes entirely from the leaves themselves. The smoke is smoky, leathery and salty; Virginia's sweetness balances Latakia's weight. Nicotine sits at a medium level. Suited to smokers moving from aromatics into English blends, and to those who want Latakia in measured amounts.
tinder-box-black-tie.o: Leaves a smoky aroma evoking leather and tar, reminiscent of a wood fire.

de-la-concha-turkish-delight.z: This is a De La Concha shop blend whose name points to oriental leaf; no independent source verifying its composition could be found.
de-la-concha-turkish-delight.o: No reliable record could be found for the room note.

watch-city-cigar-stardust.z: Stardust is Watch City Cigar's hybrid house blend combining aromatic and English styles. According to the maker's description, a broadly cut aromatic Cavendish base is supported by Latakia and bright Virginia ribbon, adding a smoky, woody layer over the sweet base. It's a cool-burning blend with a measured nicotine load. It serves as a middle step for smokers who find full aromatics' sugary taste too much but aren't ready to move to a heavy Latakia blend either. The broad cut requires the tobacco to be rubbed out somewhat before packing.
watch-city-cigar-stardust.o: Leaves a scent where a smoky Latakia trace mixes into sweet Cavendish.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-24.z: Wilke No. 24 is a multi-component American blend built on a matured Burley base. According to the recipe, granulated-cut Virginia, Latakia, natural Virginia cavendish, a small amount of Perique, and a pinch of Wilke's lightly flavored Royal Scot blend are added to this base. The maker describes the blend as light and slow-burning. Burley's dry, nutty base is layered with Latakia smoke and Perique spice, while the Royal Scot leaves a light sweetness at the finish. It suits smokers seeking a slow smoke, low nicotine, and a layered blend structure.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-24.o: Leaves a nutty, lightly smoky scent with a sweetish trace at the finish.

ken-byron-ventures-kellems-mixture.z: One of Ken Byron Ventures' limited-release blends; no independent source could be found to document its contents.
ken-byron-ventures-kellems-mixture.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

paul-olsen-tobacco-of-two-decades-1939-1.z: A commemorative blend whose name references the first twenty years of the blending shop Poul Olsen opened in 1939 at Østerport in Copenhagen; no independent source documenting its composition could be found.

gambler-silver.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of the Gambler brand's Silver pipe tobacco could be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-skandinav.z: Skandinavik White is one of the series' contemporary-styled aromatics. Virginia and burley leaves are combined with cavendish-processed tobaccos; the result is a mild yet full flavor. The ribbon cut makes packing and lighting easy. The casing is kept more measured than the series' other members; the tobacco taste does not get lost behind the casing. Nicotine stays light, so it suits those seeking a blend for long sessions or any time of day. The Skandinavik name rests on the Peter Stokkebye tradition in Denmark and is continued today by Scandinavian Tobacco Group.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-skandinav.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and lightly creamy scent.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-lancaster.z: Lancaster is The Country Squire tobacconist's aromatic house blend, bringing together chopped black cavendish with ribbon-cut Virginia leaf. The top note is built on soft caramel, with a light coffee tone added on top. The cavendish gives the blend dark sweetness and a moist burn, while the Virginia provides a grassy base and natural sugar. Nicotine is low, and the taste stays sweet without turning syrupy. It suits those who like a caramel-coffee pairing and want a light aromatic for everyday smoking.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-lancaster.o: Leaves a scent of caramel sweetness with lightly roasted coffee.

lambert-butlers-log-cabin.z: Log Cabin is one of the tinned pipe tobaccos of the British firm Lambert & Butler from the early twentieth century; it's no longer in production and not enough sources could be found to confirm the blend's composition.

pipesandcigars-com-falling-leaves.z: No sufficient sources were found documenting the content and character of pipesandcigars.com's blend Falling Leaves.

austria-tabak-landtabak.z: Landtabak is an old German term for unflavored, full-bodied folk-style tobaccos. Sold under this name in Austria, it has been produced since 1949; it's blended within the Japan Tobacco International group under the Austria Tabak brand. It contains Burley, golden Virginia, Paraguayan, and Oriental leaf. It's a fine-ribbon cut, coming out of the pack quite dry, though the ribbons keep their flexibility and internal moisture. On opening the pack, Paraguayan tobacco's strong, intense scent is noticed first; after airing, a measured note reminiscent of sugar, cocoa, spice, and fruit comes forward. Strength is medium, flavor is intense. It suits smokers looking for a Burley-heavy, full-bodied everyday tobacco where flavoring stays in the background.
austria-tabak-landtabak.o: Leaves a full-bodied tobacco room note beneath a bakery-like scent of sugar, cocoa, and spice.

cigar-tobacco-world-chocolate.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content of Chocolate, an aromatic blend from the retailer Cigar & Tobacco World.
cigar-tobacco-world-chocolate.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

dan-tobacco-blend-number-3.z: A Virginia-and-Latakia-focused English-style mixture from Dan Tobacco, no longer in production; no adequate source documenting its ratios and cut was found.
dan-tobacco-blend-number-3.o: Records indicate it leaves a woody, smoky scent.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-192.z: Wilke No. 192, in the maker's description, is a Burley-based blend built for all-day smoking. The brand's 190-number series generally centers on Wilke's own roasted black cavendish; 192, within that series, leans toward Burley's dry body rather than sweetness. The Burley-forward structure gives the blend a character that burns cool, leaves no harshness on the tongue, and stays full in the mouth. Nicotine is at a medium level. It offers a middle option for smokers who find aromatics' sugar load heavy but don't want to lean into the tartness of fully unflavored Virginia blends either.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-192.o: Leaves a scent of roasted nut and light cocoa.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-sweet-dreams.z: Sweet Dreams consists of a combination of dark cavendish and flame-cured light Virginia leaves. A mix of sweet food flavorings developed through J. M. Boswell's experiments is added on top; the result is a light, fresh and distinctly sweet blend. Nicotine and flavor body stay at a low level, while the aroma left in the room is strong. A mixture prepared for those who enjoy sweet aromatics and smoke their pipe indoors.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-sweet-dreams.o: A sugary, sweet bakery aroma spreads into the room.

cornell-diehl-st-patricks-day-reserve.z: No verifiable listing could be found in the maker's current catalogue or retailer listings for St Patrick's Day Reserve, referred to as a seasonal Cornell & Diehl release.

wessex-rich-aroma.z: No sufficient independent source could be found documenting the composition of the Wessex Rich Aroma blend.
wessex-rich-aroma.o: According to the records, no scent description has been documented.

pipesandcigars-com-russ-bold-rum.z: Russ' Bold Rum is one of the blends the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com sells under its own name; there is not enough independent source material documenting its content and character.

gawith-hoggarth-co-exmoor-mixture.z: Exmoor Mixture is an unflavored English blend prepared by combining Indian- and Brazilian-origin light Virginia leaf with Latakia. The light leaf gives a natural sweetness and citrusy sharpness, while Latakia adds depth, an earthy base, and a measured smokiness. Since the Latakia ratio is kept restrained compared to heavy Balkan blends, the overall structure stays medium-bodied and cool. Suited to smokers new to Latakia or wanting a balanced English blend for all-day smoking; since its cut lights easily, no preparation is needed.
gawith-hoggarth-co-exmoor-mixture.o: Leaves a lightly smoky aroma reminiscent of wood and campfire.

kaptn-barsdorfs-bester-bright-virginia.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for Kapt'n Barsdorf's Bester's Bright Virginia, so the profile is left incomplete; per catalog records, the blend is classified as "Virginia Based."

boswell-pipes-tobacco-sweet-tea.z: Sweet Tea is a light black-cavendish blend taking its name from the sugared iced tea drunk in the American South. The casing carries a lemon-leaning tart citrus tone together with sweetness. In the smoke, sweet dry grass and lemon appear first, followed by a round taste reminiscent of sugared tea. It burns cool and leaves no pronounced aftertaste. Being very light in nicotine, suitable for those seeking a refreshing aromatic for summer months or long smoking sessions.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-sweet-tea.o: Leaves a dry grass trace behind a sugared iced tea and lemon peel aroma.

pipesandcigars-com-perique-blend-sv-23.z: Perique Blend SV-23 is one of the house blends sold under its own name by the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com; no sufficient independent sources documenting its content and character could be found.

g-l-pease-union-square.z: Union Square is a Virginia blend made entirely from flue-cured leaf, presented sliced in plug form. The composition uses a wide range spanning sweet bright leaves to dark, earthy red leaves. The added sugars, sauces, and top dressings seen in many Virginia flakes are absent from this blend. On the palate it stands out with an intense, natural tobacco sweetness and a long finish. It is aimed at smokers seeking an untopped Virginia smoke who want to follow how the taste changes as the pressed leaf matures. It is part of the Fog City Selection line.
g-l-pease-union-square.o: Leaves an aroma of sweet dry grass and a light bread-like grain note.

affordable-pipes-fishermans-friend.z: One of the house blends from the American seller Affordable Pipes; no accessible source describing its content could be found.

bosphorus-vanilla.z: Vanilla is Bosphorus's classic vanilla-cased aromatic blend. It is ribbon cut, and the casing bearing its name is the blend's defining element. Per records, the product's recipe has been reworked over time, so batches sourced from different periods may differ. As with this class of aromatic blends, the casing's sweetness leads rather than the tobacco's own taste. Suitable for smokers wanting to start with flavored blends or seeking a familiar vanilla note; no detailed breakdown of its content has been published.

american-tobacco-co-london-dock.z: London Dock is an old American blend, per records originally released by the St. Louis-based Christian Peper Tobacco Company, later passing to Bloch Brothers and then to John Middleton. In the blend list published during Middleton's era, the product is described as a rum-flavored, rubbed cake cut made of Burley and Virginia leaf. The original product was discontinued in the early 2000s. Its character follows the familiar line of American cake tobaccos: Burley's nutty, earthy base combines with Virginia's bready sweetness; the rum flavoring adds a measured sweetness and a light boozy depth over this base. The leaf, rubbed from the cake, burns slow and cool. The name is carried on today under a different manufacturer, with a new interpretation prepared using Burley, Virginia, Oriental, and Perique along with rum and coumarin sold under the same name. It's a historical reference point for smokers wanting to get to know the cake-cut, measured-sweetness American style.
american-tobacco-co-london-dock.o: Leaves a warm trace leaning toward sweet rum and toasted sugar.

hu-tobacco-my-red-fox.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the My Red Fox blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

dan-tobacco-olda-jirsas-magister-kellys-.z: An aromatic blend from one of Dan Tobacco's blender-signature series; no adequate source on its composition or character was found.
dan-tobacco-olda-jirsas-magister-kellys-.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

mcclelland-tudor-castle-collector-series.z: Tudor Castle is a blend McClelland released under its Collector Series heading, adding Oriental tobacco and Perique to a Virginia base. It's ribbon cut. The brand's characteristic sweet-tart character is pronounced here too; Yenice-sourced Oriental leaf adds a sweet-spiced richness to the smoke, while Perique sets a measured firmness against the sweetness. Packing and lighting are effortless, requiring no special technique. Nicotine level is medium, and the balance between body and sweetness is the blend's defining feature. Suited to those who get along with Perique-containing Virginia blends and want an unflavored, true tobacco taste. Discontinued with McClelland's 2018 closure.
mcclelland-tudor-castle-collector-series.o: Leaves a sharp aroma mixing tangy sweetness and spice.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-mistura-ext.z: This is the mint-cased version of Wilder Mistura Extra, prepared by Tabacos Wilder Finamore in Juiz de Fora, Brazil, using the maker's stated handmade process built on Virginia and Burley leaf. Since no independent source detailing the blend's composition ratios and smoking character could be found, the record is kept limited.

edwards-toasted-cherry.z: No sufficient independent sourcing could be reached to document the composition and character of Toasted Cherry, a pipe tobacco from Edward's.

d-r-tobacco-ramback-regular.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of D & R Tobacco's Ramback Regular blend were found.

arango-balkan-supreme.z: Balkan Supreme is Arango's Latakia-forward bulk blend. Alongside Latakia, Oriental leaf, Virginias, some black Cavendish, and Samsun-type Turkish tobacco are added; no top flavoring is applied to the blend. At first, wood and soot notes stand out; as it progresses, creamy, grassy, peppery, and leathery layers appear along with a woody sweetness reminiscent of cinnamon. It belongs to the full-bodied English-Balkan family; it suits experienced smokers accustomed to Latakia, looking for an intense, unflavored smoke.
arango-balkan-supreme.o: Leaves an intense room note dominated by woodsmoke and soot, with traces of leather and spice.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-dunhills-l.z: Match Dunhill's London Mixture is an unflavored English mixture modeled after Dunhill's blend called London Mixture. Cyprus latakia gives a woody, sweetish smoke; Turkish leaf adds a dry, woody, lightly buttery tone; and Virginia rounds out the blend with a grassy, light citrus tartness. Strength and taste sit light to medium, and it burns cool and even. It suits smokers looking for a measured English blend where latakia makes its presence felt without taking over the body.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-dunhills-l.o: Leaves a dry, woody scent with a light wood smoke.

clan-shaw-dutch.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of Clan Shaw's Dutch blend could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-blueberry.z: Kendal Blueberry is a shag-cut aromatic where a blueberry topping is applied to light-colored Virginia leaf. The tobacco is close to medium brown, made of fine strands, kept at a moisture level suited to packing. On the smoke, fruity sweetness leads, with Virginia's herbal, lightly sweet base staying underneath. Nicotine is low, the smoke cool, and it tends to burn fast; smoking slowly reduces tongue bite. Suited to smokers wanting a fruity aromatic in a fine cut.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-blueberry.o: Leaves a sweet blueberry and fruity candy aroma.

villiger-weber-aromatischer-teetabak.z: Weber Aromatischer Teetabak is an aromatic pipe tobacco in Villiger's Weber line, aimed at the Swiss domestic market. It's prepared predominantly from Burley leaf grown in Switzerland, cut in a short shag, and flavored with a fruity casing evocative of tea, which also gives the tobacco its name. Its smoke is soft; a low-level sweetness sits atop a lightly nutty body, and nicotine load stays limited. Thanks to the short cut it catches quickly, so a brisk draw should be avoided for a cool, even smoke. It suits those seeking a plain, low-intensity aromatic suitable for all-day smoking; it's sold in 80-gram pouches.
villiger-weber-aromatischer-teetabak.o: Leaves a lightly fruity, sweetish scent reminiscent of brewed tea.

ken-byron-ventures-embrys-christmas-bisc.z: A limited aromatic from Ken Byron Ventures' Embry's line, timed to the holiday season; no accessible maker's profile could be found to document its contents.

peretti-crown.z: This is a shop mixture L.J. Peretti lists in its English blends group and continues to produce in three package sizes; no published source on its content and flavor profile could be found.

century-black-and-brown.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Black And Brown under the Century brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

bosphorus-coffee-mate.z: Coffee Mate is a coffee-flavored, ribbon-cut blend built from Turkish tobacco, red Virginia, golden cavendish and black cavendish. The coffee aroma is pronounced when the pack is opened, while in the smoke the aroma stays more measured and does not mask the tobacco's own taste. Its strength is between light and medium, flavor between medium and intense. Per records no flavor degradation or bitterness is observed through the smoke, and no tongue bite or overheating is reported. Its intensity suits after-breakfast and daytime use; the Turkish tobacco within it forms the blend's body.
bosphorus-coffee-mate.o: A freshly roasted coffee aroma spreads into the room.

sutliff-tobacco-company-taste-of-autumn.z: Taste of Autumn is the autumn member of Sutliff's season-named aromatic line; it is said to apply a pumpkin- and pie-spice-based casing over black and golden cavendish with Virginia. Since no verifiable maker source could be found, the composition details are not certain.
sutliff-tobacco-company-taste-of-autumn.o: Leaves a scent of pumpkin pie and cinnamon-nutmeg spice.

mcclelland-pebblecut.z: Pebblecut is among the blends McClelland produced for Ashton. Per its description, the mixture contains Carolina's mottled red leaf, small-leaved Oriental tobaccos from Macedonia, nutty-character bright Virginia, and Louisiana Perique. The leaf is pressed and broken into small pieces, giving it a pebble-like look somewhere between flake and ribbon. In the smoke, Virginia's tangy-sweet axis is pronounced; the Oriental tobaccos add a spicy sharpness, and the Perique adds a dark-fruit depth. Body is medium.
