Suited to smokers who find straight Virginia insufficiently layered and want Oriental tobacco alongside a Virginia-Perique axis. Records indicate the blend was occasionally sold in bulk as well. McClelland stopped production in 2018.
mcclelland-pebblecut.o: Leaves a tangy fruit and spice aroma, with a dry-hay note behind it.

nice-ash-cigars-vanilla-custard.z: An aromatic record among Nice Ash Cigars' house blends, flavored with vanilla cream; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.
nice-ash-cigars-vanilla-custard.o: No description could be found in the records.

motzek-pure-burley.z: An unflavored burley blend from the Motzek workshop; beyond its name, sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

grants-tobacconist-balkan-light.z: One of Grant's Tobacconist's house blends; though its name points to the Balkan style, there is no independent sourcing to confirm its composition.

castello-optimo.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Optimo under the Castello brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

liberty-tobacco-entertainer.z: Entertainer is an aromatic house blend carrying the name of San Diego-based tobacconist Liberty Tobacco; not enough sources could be found for its composition and character.
liberty-tobacco-entertainer.o: Leaves a sweetish aromatic room note.

g-l-pease-samugweeg.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Samugweeg.

samuel-gawith-full-virginia-flake-burnt-.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Full Virginia Flake Burnt Ends, according to records a pure Virginia blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

dunhill-black-aromatic.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of this black-cavendish-based aromatic blend referred to under the Dunhill name.
dunhill-black-aromatic.o: Leaves a sweet, dark, sauced tobacco scent.

sobranie-of-london-virginian-no-10.z: Virginian No.10 is one of the long-discontinued Virginia-forward blends from the London-based Sobranie brand; sufficient sources on its composition and character could not be found.
sobranie-of-london-virginian-no-10.o: Records did not describe the room note.

gladora-tobacco-oriental-flake.z: Oriental Flake is a flake tobacco in the Pesse Canoe line from Izmir-based Gladora. The blend is built from Turkish-grown Virginia and Oriental leaf; after pressing and slicing, it's tinned as thin plates that can be rubbed out by hand. The brand was long available only in the European market before expanding into North America through its distribution network. Its character is floral and lightly sweet; the Oriental leaf's dry-hay and spice association combines with a fruity depth giving impressions of fig and raisin. The fig seasoning applied to the leaf is felt less as a pronounced flavoring layer and more as a subtle sweetness in the background. Nicotine is moderate, and the burn stays even when the slices are aired sufficiently. Suited to smokers wanting an Oriental-forward, near-unflavored flake tobacco without Latakia.
gladora-tobacco-oriental-flake.o: Leaves a floral, lightly sweet tobacco aroma reminiscent of dry hay.

fdb-cigar-no-221b-baker-street.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for the FDB Cigar brand's No. 221B Baker Street pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

sutliff-tobacco-company-cabaret-rouge.z: Cabaret Rouge is an aromatic made from a combination of Virginia and black cavendish leaves. Dark fruit directions reminiscent of citrus, cherry, fig, and date stand out on the palate, along with a molasses-like sweetness; the vanilla trace from cavendish is kept thin, while Virginia forms a cooling base. Because it burns slowly when moist, airing it out for a while before smoking is advised. Suited to smokers seeking a sweet, fruity blend of the sort typically smoked after dessert.
sutliff-tobacco-company-cabaret-rouge.o: Leaves a scent carrying dark fruit and molasses sweetness.

mcclelland-corps-sophisticate.z: A club blend McClelland released for the Conclave of Richmond Pipe Smokers, reportedly in 1993; no sufficient source describing its contents and character could be found.

benjamin-hartwell-chesdin-mixture.z: Chesdin Mixture is a ribbon-cut English-type blend built by adding Latakia over a Virginia base. Latakia's smoky, resinous taste forms the blend's backbone, while the Virginia leaf leaves a grassy, lightly sweet foundation; there is no added flavoring. The tobacco's name comes from the narrative built around the Benjamin Hartwell brand: in the brand's story, Chesdin is mentioned as a riverside resting place. Records indicate the blend was produced first by McClelland and later under Altadis U.S.A. It suits smokers accustomed to the smoky character of Latakia-based blends, looking for an unflavored, medium-bodied evening tobacco; because of its Latakia intensity, it can be a rough transition for someone coming from aromatic tobaccos.
benjamin-hartwell-chesdin-mixture.o: Leaves a smoke that lingers in the room, reminiscent of a campfire, with Latakia's soot and tar.

von-eicken-barsdorfs-kaptn-bester-cherry.z: Käpt'n Barsdorf's Bester is Von Eicken's long-running pipe tobacco line in Germany, drawing on the Lübeck-based company's nearly two-and-a-half centuries of blending history. The Cherry version of the series is prepared by casing a base of sun-cured Virginia leaf and dark Cavendish toward cherry. The cherry note is pronounced throughout the smoke; the Cavendish lays a soft, sugary base beneath it, while the Virginia leaves a light acidic edge that keeps it from becoming too heavy. Nicotine is low and flavor intensity is moderate. A record aimed at those new to aromatic tobaccos or after fruity scents.
von-eicken-barsdorfs-kaptn-bester-cherry.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of ripe cherry and candy.

benson-hedges-gold-flake.z: Gold Flake is a straight Virginia flake blend presented in tins under the Benson & Hedges name. The flakes are neatly cut; once rubbed out and packed, they burn without trouble and smoke cool. Strength sits between light and medium, with medium flavor intensity. The blend carries a very light flavoring. This topping sits over the leaf's own natural sweetness and can partly mask the Virginia character over a long smoke. It suits smokers looking for a middle point between an unflavored Virginia flake and an aromatic, wanting a mild flake they can smoke all day.
benson-hedges-gold-flake.o: Leaves a dry-hay, faintly sweet leaf room note.

peter-stokkebye-vanilla-creme-no-9.z: This is a vanilla-flavored blend numbered 9 in Peter Stokkebye's numbered bulk series; no sufficient first-hand sources detailing its character could be found.
peter-stokkebye-vanilla-creme-no-9.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

barclay-rex-no-4.z: Referred to as one of Barclay Rex's Cavendish-based shop blends; no adequate source on its composition and character could be found.
barclay-rex-no-4.o: According to records it leaves a sweetish, lightly toasted room note.

ogden-ogdens-mixture.z: A blend carrying the name of the Liverpool-based Ogden brand; sufficient independent sources describing its composition and character could not be found.

friedman-pease-templar.z: This is one of the blends Friedman & Pease released during its roughly eighteen months of activity; today it is known only through tins in collectors' hands, and no reliable source describing its composition could be found.

mcclelland-corps-cyprian-star.z: Cyprian Star is among the club blends McClelland prepared for the Richmond-based pipe club Conclave of Richmond Pipe Smokers (CORPS), and records indicate it was introduced in 1996. As the name suggests, the blend's signature is Cyprian Latakia, laid over a Virginia base and Oriental tobaccos. Since club blends were released in small tins and limited numbers, it's found today only in old stock. Its character sits in the classic English mixture line: soot and wood smoke lead, but the Latakia proportion is kept measured enough not to overwhelm the Virginia's sweetness, so body stays medium-to-full rather than fully loaded. Records describe a cool-burning smoke that leaves a dry, spiced trace on the palate. Aimed at smokers used to Latakia mixtures who don't want the smoke to crush the rest of the tobacco.
mcclelland-corps-cyprian-star.o: Leaves a dry, herbal, faintly resinous layer over an aroma of wood smoke and soot.

motzek-m74.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called M74 could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-byronic-slices.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to fill in the profile of Ken Byron Ventures' Byronic Slices.

super-value-whiskey-cavendish.z: Super Value Whiskey Cavendish is a budget aromatic where a whiskey-style flavoring is applied to a black-cavendish-forward base. Like the rest of the line, it's coarse cut and produced in the US from a combination of domestic and imported leaf. It gives a sweet, soft, low-nicotine smoke. Suited to smokers who enjoy liquor-flavored mixtures and want a bulky tobacco for everyday use.
super-value-whiskey-cavendish.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly alcohol-tinged scent of grain and caramel.

peterson-connemara-black.z: Connemara Black is a ribbon-cut aromatic blend that combines ripe Virginia leaf with soft black Cavendish, topped with a pronounced cherry flavoring. It takes its name from the Connemara region on Ireland's west coast. Being ribbon cut, it packs easily. The smoke is medium-bodied; Cavendish's sweetness and Virginia's freshly cut hay quality run together underneath the cherry note. Nicotine strength stays low, making it suitable for long smokes. It suits smokers interested in fruit-flavored tobaccos and those seeking a pronounced room note.
peterson-connemara-black.o: Fills the room with a ripe cherry and sugared fruit aroma.

john-cotton-john-cottons-sweet-english.z: An English-style blend from the historic Scottish brand John Cotton; no verifiable information could be found on its current production profile.
john-cotton-john-cottons-sweet-english.o: No verifiable information on its room note could be found.

bennington-tobacconist-no-15-balkan-mix.z: No. 15 Balkan Mix is a shop blend Bennington Tobacconist developed with the legendary Balkan Sobranie White Label as its model. Per the company's history, founder William E. Bennington spent an evening dividing a 230-gram batch into Turkish, Latakia, and Virginia components with tweezers and a scale, working out the ratio this way. The blend uses a high proportion of Turkish Yenidje leaf, accompanied by heat-cured golden Virginia and Cyprus Latakia. The maker states the mixture is free of artificial flavoring. The result is a medium-bodied Balkan type where Latakia doesn't leap forward, and the Orientals' smoky, resinous character is what defines it. It suits smokers looking for the classic Balkan line.
bennington-tobacconist-no-15-balkan-mix.o: Incense and dry-hay notes are joined by soot and a resinous spice note.

fincks-cigar-company-english-supreme.z: English Supreme is among the bulk pipe tobaccos of Finck Cigar Company, founded in San Antonio in 1893 and one of America's oldest family businesses; no producer record explaining the blend's composition could be found.
fincks-cigar-company-english-supreme.o: Records do not contain enough information for a description.

holger-danske-original-orange-mellow-ori.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for Holger Danske's Original Orange Mellow (Original Mild Orange) blend, so its content and character could not be recorded.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-captain-earles-n.z: Nightwatch is one of the high-Latakia English mixtures in the Captain Earle's line. Latakia, Oriental leaves, Virginias, and Perique are pressed into a crumble cake; the cake is rubbed out by hand before filling. Latakia smoke builds the blend's backbone, the Orientals add a dry, herbal edge, and Perique gives a spicy-plummy accent. It's a structure meant for sitting and following the smoke rather than all-day smoking. Like the rest of the line, this blend is also produced at Cornell & Diehl's facilities for Hermit Tobacco Works, and takes its name from the 19th-century whaling ship captain James A. M. Earle's maritime background. It carries no flavoring. It suits smokers looking for Latakia intensity, accustomed to English mixtures; it may be heavy for those encountering Latakia for the first time.
hermit-tobacco-works-co-captain-earles-n.o: Leaves an aroma of campfire smoke and smoky pine, with a light dried-fruit trace lingering behind it.

paul-olsen-hipster.z: A blend from the My Own Blend line that originated at the Paul Olsen shop in Copenhagen; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

the-pipe-shop-superieur-caporal-pipe.z: Superieur Caporal is a blend unique to The Pipe Shop on Leith Walk in Edinburgh, prepared to replace the Scaferlati the shop previously sold. It follows the dry, unflavored tobacco tradition of French caporal blends and is built from dark Virginia leaf. It is full-bodied with high nicotine; the taste is described as earthy and malty, with an association to dark beer. No casing is used. It is meant for smokers accustomed to dry, strong, straightforward tobaccos, well beyond the level of anyone looking for a mild or sweet blend.
the-pipe-shop-superieur-caporal-pipe.o: Leaves a dry, earthy, malty, sharp tobacco scent.

cornell-diehl-kellys-coin.z: Kelly's Coin is a Burley-heavy, full-bodied Cornell & Diehl blend named after Australian outlaw Ned Kelly. Alongside Burley, it holds Virginia and black Cavendish; ribbon cut. Burley gives the blend a dry, cocoa-like, earthy body along with a pronounced nicotine load; Virginia and Cavendish pull that structure toward sweetness and smooth out the smoke. Suited to experienced smokers wanting a filling, unflavored, strong tobacco in a single bowl.
cornell-diehl-kellys-coin.o: Leaves a dark, dry tobacco scent reminiscent of cocoa and damp earth.

milan-tobacconists-sultans-blend.z: Sultan's Blend is one of the fullest among Milan Tobacconists' English-style house blends. According to the maker's profile, cube-cut and coarse-cut burley, Turkish leaf, light-colored Virginia ribbon, toasted cavendish, long-cut latakia, a touch of perique, and a small amount of black cavendish are all used together. The side-by-side different cuts give a mottled look in the jar and a layered, progressive taste in the smoke. Because of its medium-to-full body and pronounced latakia share, it's geared toward smokers accustomed to smoky mixtures. Since the burley proportion raises the sense of nicotine, it's better suited to a filling evening pipe than to smoking on an empty stomach.
milan-tobacconists-sultans-blend.o: Leaves a sharp aroma reminiscent of pine soot and spicy dry leaf.

ole-shenandoah-barrel-edition.z: Barrel Edition is one of the aromatic blends in the American Ole Shenandoah line working the barrel theme. It uses burley, light-colored Virginia, and dark cavendish together; the flavor direction given rests on chocolatey, nutty notes with hints of caramel. Smoke body is medium and nicotine load low; a balance is aimed for between burley's dryness and cavendish's sweetness. It suits smokers avoiding heavily essenced aromatics who still want a sweet frame, and works well as an evening pipe. The Ole Shenandoah line was prepared for American retail chains and is not on the market today.
ole-shenandoah-barrel-edition.o: Leaves a cocoa-and-caramel-forward scent of lightly toasted hazelnut.

argento-nougat.z: Nougat is an aromatic blend where walnut-hazelnut-type nut notes and cinnamon are worked over a body built from Argentine tobaccos. It takes its name from the confection it evokes: the sweetness comes not from syrup but from toasted nuts and spice. It's ribbon cut and sold in 50-gram pouch packaging. The flavoring level is noticeable but not heavy enough to mask the tobacco; it suits smokers drawn to spiced aromatics who want to step outside the usual fruit-and-vanilla classics. It's among the limited-distribution blends produced for the Argentine domestic market.
argento-nougat.o: Leaves a roasted hazelnut and cinnamon room note.

sterling-tobacco-co-bargain-blend.z: No verifiable source describing the composition of this blend, understood to be part of Sterling Tobacco's budget line, could be found.

milan-tobacconists-our-carter-hall.z: One of the house blends from Milan Tobacconists, in business in Roanoke, Virginia since 1912. It is a traditional American burley mixture built by adding some Virginia flake over crosscut burley leaves, with its casing kept barely perceptible. The brand states it developed this blend to fill the gap left by Middleton's Carter Hall, discontinued in the early 2020s, and gave it its final form after evaluating trials by customers who had smoked the original product for years. It has a structure that is easy to pack and light, burns cool, and doesn't bite the tongue; its sweetness comes from burley's own nutty base and Virginia's sugar. Suitable for those looking for a low-nicotine, straightforward tobacco to smoke throughout the day and for smokers accustomed to classic American code blends.
milan-tobacconists-our-carter-hall.o: Leaves a subtle tobacco aroma carrying dry hay and a light bready sweetness.

georgetown-tobacco-southern-cross.z: Referred to as one of Georgetown Tobacco's aromatic shop blends; no verifiable sourcing on its composition could be found.
georgetown-tobacco-southern-cross.o: No record of the room aroma could be found.

consolidated-b-21-black-spice.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Consolidated blend B-21: Black Spice.

e-a-carey-europe-careys-wild-cherry.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Carey's Wild Cherry, a pipe tobacco from E. A. Carey (Europe).

timm-no-name-gold.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Timm pipe tobacco called No Name Gold to record the blend's composition and character.

peretti-boston-slices.z: This is a shop tobacco L.J. Peretti lists in its flake group, presented as pressed slices and still in production; no published source on the leaf composition and flavor character could be found.

james-fox-honeydew-flake.z: A flake-cut Fox blend reported to be Virginia-based, drawing on the honeydew flavoring tradition; no detailed maker's description could be found.

unknown-please-use-with-restraint-studen.z: No verifiable source has been found for the blend Students' Club, whose maker is unclear.
unknown-please-use-with-restraint-studen.o: No reliable source describing the room note has been found.

gq-tobaccos-balkan-full-no-1.z: Balkan (Full) No. 1 is one of the Balkan-style blends from small English producer GQ Tobaccos; there is not enough sourcing describing its composition, cut, and character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-golden-dream-d63.z: Golden Dream D63 is a plain burley blend supported by a touch of Virginia; the leaves are pressed and then crumbled. Flavor is nutty and lightly sweet, largely drawn from the leaf's own character. Body and nicotine are low, and the smoke is soft and smooth. Records indicate it was previously sold as Altadis Golden Dream. A record for those wanting an undemanding burley they can smoke comfortably throughout the day.
sutliff-tobacco-company-golden-dream-d63.o: Leaves a nutty, lightly sweet bakery scent.

billow-the-yeoman.z: One of the blends prepared in the Virginia-Perique line at the Billow lounge; no adequate source on its content could be found.
billow-the-yeoman.o: No verified information on the room note could be found.

peter-stokkebye-vanilla-gold.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Vanilla Gold in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

stanwell-full-aroma.z: Referred to as a vanilla-and-cocoa-direction aromatic blend from Stanwell that brings together matured Virginia and roasted burley leaves in pressed form; a second independent source confirming this information could not be found.
stanwell-full-aroma.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet scent reminiscent of vanilla and cocoa.

douwe-egberts-nord-sund-extra-mild-scand.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Nord-Sund Extra Mild Scandinavian Blend, a pipe tobacco from Douwe Egberts.
douwe-egberts-nord-sund-extra-mild-scand.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

peter-stokkebye-b-b-no-23.z: PS23 B&B is one of the classic Danish-style aromatics in Peter Stokkebye's bulk line. The blend's backbone is black Cavendish, joined by pressed Burley; this pairing balances Cavendish's sweetness against Burley's nutty, cool-burning base. A pronounced vanilla flavoring applied on top gives the blend its distinguishing side. The smoke is mild and low in nicotine, offering a sweet profile that doesn't sit heavy on the tongue. Being ribbon cut, it packs directly, though as is typical with aromatics, a brief airing improves the burn if moisture is high. It suits people starting out with aromatic blends or seeking a light tobacco for all-day smoking.
peter-stokkebye-b-b-no-23.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough aroma.

paul-olsen-winter-special-2014.z: A limited seasonal blend the Paul Olsen house released for winter 2014; no independent source documenting its composition could be found.

old-virginia-tobacco-co-antietam.z: Antietam is one of the aromatic bulk blends sold under its own name by Old Virginia Tobacco Co., a retailer in the state of Virginia; no detailed published description of its composition could be found.

w-o-larsen-danish-choice.z: Danish Choice is among W.Ø. Larsen's aromatic blends, said to be based on an old company recipe. Its foundation is mature Virginia tobaccos; black cavendish is added to soften the body, and the mixture is flavored with coffee and a small amount of chocolate. While the flavoring intensity is pronounced, the smoke stays soft with limited impact on the tongue. The coffee note is the taste that comes forward throughout the smoke, with chocolate sitting behind it as a subtle layer; according to records, a note reminiscent of malt whisky also appears toward the end of the bowl when smoked slowly. Nicotine runs from light toward medium. This is a blend aimed at smokers who love sweet, fragrant Danish aromatics and seek flavor over strength.
w-o-larsen-danish-choice.o: Leaves a scent of freshly brewed coffee and dark chocolate.

bufflehead-virginia-ruddy-duck.z: One of the discontinued Bufflehead shop blends, whose name suggests a Virginia-forward composition; no source documenting its content could be found.

wolfway-blue-xanthi-basma.z: As the name suggests, this is a single-varietal product based on Basma-type Oriental leaf from the Xanthi region; no verifiable source could be found regarding the blend.

faders-e-b.z: Not enough independent sourcing documenting the composition and character of E.B., one of the house blends of the Baltimore-based Fader's tobacconist, could be found.

pipa-vanilla-cavendish.z: No sufficient sources from the manufacturer or a reliable product page could be found for Pipa Vanilla Cavendish.

sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-regular-i.z: The first blend in the brand's Regular series aimed at everyday use; although said to be Virginia- and Burley-forward, no independent source confirming its composition could be found.
sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-regular-i.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

pipesandcigars-com-mountain-pass.z: Mountain Pass is one of the house blends sold under its own name by the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com; no sufficient independent sources documenting its content and character could be found.

4-aces-turkish.z: There is not enough independent source material documenting the composition and character of 4 Aces' blend called Turkish.

chief-catoonah-tobacconist-sugar-hollow-.z: The entry has been left incomplete as no reliable source could be found for Chief Catoonah Tobacconist's Sugar Hollow Blend blend.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-holiday-blend-20.z: Holiday Blend 2000 is part of Hermit Tobacco Works Co.'s annual holiday series; records indicate the early years of the series were Virginia or Virginia-Perique in structure, but there is not enough sourcing to detail this particular year's blend.

georgetown-tobacco-his-masters-choice.z: Referred to as one of Georgetown Tobacco's shop blends in the pure-Virginia line; no verifiable sourcing describing its composition could be found.
georgetown-tobacco-his-masters-choice.o: No record of the room aroma could be found.

schurch-sangstone.z: Sangstone, signed by Schürch, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

samuel-gawith-almond.z: No sufficient source could be found for this blend among Samuel Gawith's bulk aromatics, understood from its name to contain almond casing.

cellini-classico-riserva.z: Cellini is a tobacco line from German manufacturer Planta that nods to Italian style; Classico Riserva is the line's main aromatic. Light yellow Virginias selected from Tuscan and Umbrian leaf are combined in the blend with the dark tones of black cavendish, joined by burley. An orange-forward casing is applied on top. Orange leads the flavor, with vanilla in the background; a light herbal tone sits underneath. Nicotine is low and the smoke is cool. Suitable for those seeking a citrus-forward aromatic. The blend was discontinued when Planta ended its tobacco production.
cellini-classico-riserva.o: Leaves an orange peel and light vanilla room note.

borkum-riff-cherry-cavendish-ruby.z: Cherry Cavendish is a fruited aromatic prepared by heavily coating and fermenting dark Kentucky, cool-smoking Burley, and light Virginia leaf in wooden casks. Sweet cherry and vanilla are used together in the topping, with the cherry note being the blend's most prominent feature. In some markets it's sold as Ruby, and it's one of the brand's most widely available products in the Scandinavian countries. The blend is ribbon cut and stays light on nicotine. It suits smokers looking for classic cherry-flavored aromatics, wanting a pronounced fruit sweetness ahead of the tobacco's own taste. The brand is produced in Denmark under Scandinavian Tobacco Group.
borkum-riff-cherry-cavendish-ruby.o: Leaves a sweet, candy-like room note where ripe cherry and vanilla meet.

d-r-tobacco-rowland-platinum-blend.z: A blend in Daughters & Ryan's Rowland series; no adequate source describing its composition and character was found.

samuel-gawith-b-s-flake-brown-sugar-flak.z: B.S. Flake is a Virginia flake prepared through collaboration between Samuel Gawith and the Danish Pipe Shop in Denmark. Matured Virginia leaves are compressed in a hot press together with unflavored cavendish; the blend also contains a small amount of burley and Oriental leaf. The hot press caramelizes Virginia's own sugar, producing a dark-colored, full-bodied flake with pronounced natural sweetness. Nicotine is, according to records, medium. Suited to smokers accustomed to packing flake who seek unflavored or lightly cased, pressed Virginia character.
samuel-gawith-b-s-flake-brown-sugar-flak.o: Leaves a lightly sweet tobacco scent evoking toasted bread and burnt sugar.

edwards-e-r-s-mixture-no-88.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of E.R.'s Mixture No.88, a pipe tobacco from Edward's. Edward's is a tobacconist business based in Tampa, Florida.

g-l-pease-jackknife-ready-rubbed.z: JackKnife Ready Rubbed is the ready-rubbed form of the plug blend of the same name. Dark fire-cured Kentucky leaf and ripe red Virginias are layered over a golden flue-cured Virginia core sitting in the middle; the mix is pressed, matured into a cake, then sliced and turned into broken flake. This process preserves the deep, smoky character of the plug form while making it easier to fill; the light Virginia layer at the core places a thin sweetness among the dark flavours. It suits smokers leaning toward Kentucky-heavy, highly full-bodied blends.
g-l-pease-jackknife-ready-rubbed.o: Leaves a light, sweet leaf aroma alongside the woody smokiness.

borkum-riff-rum.z: A rum-flavored Virginia-Burley blend once offered in the Borkum Riff line, reportedly no longer in production; no adequate source for detailed content information could be found.

pauls-pipe-shop-columbus-day-blend.z: Columbus Day Blend belongs to the series of blends Paul's Pipe Shop devotes to calendar days. Per the maker's recipe, it combines several kinds of cavendish with straight Virginia and burley leaf, topped with coffee and vanilla. Burley's dry, nutty base is balanced by Virginia's light sweetness, while cavendish adds mellowness to the smoke. Described as burning cool and smokable all day, this mixture sits among the middle-ground aromatics where, despite being flavored, the leaf taste isn't entirely masked. It suits smokers who love the coffee-and-vanilla pairing but want to avoid heavily syrupy blends. It's prepared in bulk at the shop's own counter.
pauls-pipe-shop-columbus-day-blend.o: Leaves a scent of freshly brewed coffee and vanilla.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-cisne-branc.z: Cisne Branco is the classic Brazilian pipe tobacco produced under the Tabacos Cisne Branco Finamore banner in Juiz de Fora, Minas Gerais, and the blend that gave the brand its name. According to the product description, its pipe blends are prepared by bringing together sugar, plant extracts, and flavoring agents; the body is built on Virginia and Burley leaf. It is widely distributed domestically in 45-gram packs. Taste intensity is described as medium to high; while the flavoring is pronounced, the tobacco's own sharpness still makes itself felt in the smoke. It appeals to smokers wanting to get to know Brazil's traditional, affordable everyday blends, looking for a medium-bodied, flavored smoke.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-cisne-branc.o: Leaves the heavy, sugary scent of flavored tobacco.

seattle-pipe-club-plum-pudding-bourbon-b.z: Plum Pudding Bourbon Barrel Aged is a version of the brand's Balkan blend prepared by aging it in a bourbon barrel. The recipe carries the same leaves as the main record: Latakia, Oriental, Virginia, Perique, and black cavendish. The distinction comes from the maturation period the blend undergoes in a bourbon barrel before tinning. The time spent in the barrel adds a layer of oak, vanilla, and sweet-spirit echo to the smoky body; this layer is not a flavoring applied afterward but a trace picked up through contact. The result is a Balkan record that is rounder and more distinctly sweet than the main version. Set aside for smokers who know Plum Pudding and want to see how the same skeleton changes with a different maturation.
seattle-pipe-club-plum-pudding-bourbon-b.o: Oak-barrel and sweet-spirit traces mix into the pine-smoke and dried-fruit scent.

gq-tobaccos-swamp-flower.z: Swamp Flower is built on a heavy base formed by fire-cured Kentucky and Virginia leaf. This base is joined by air-cured Virginias, a hefty share of Perique, and a very small amount of Izmir-origin Turkish tobacco. The geranium topping applied on top, tied to Lakeland tradition, is the blend's most recognizable trait — it sets a fine, floral contrast against the dark, smoky body. The smoke is rich, dark, and layered; the high Perique ratio brings a spicy, peppery bite. It sits at the upper end for nicotine, so it isn't suited to smokers avoiding high-nicotine tobaccos. A blend designed for experienced smokers wanting both the Lakeland-style floral topping and the heft of fire-cured leaf together.
gq-tobaccos-swamp-flower.o: A fine trace of geranium flower sits atop the heavy, smoky aroma of fire-cured tobacco.

mccranies-quail-run.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found on Quail Run, one of McCranie's Pipe Shop's house blends.
mccranies-quail-run.o: No reliable description of the aroma could be found.

watch-city-cigar-double-barrel.z: This is described as one of Watch City Cigar's Virginia-and-Burley-based house blends; no published maker record could be found to confirm its composition.
watch-city-cigar-double-barrel.o: Could not be determined from the records.

gawith-hoggarth-co-american-blend-sweet-.z: Sweet Peach is a light aromatic offered with peach flavouring in Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s bulk American Blend line. Its base is flue-cured Virginia and black cavendish, cut as ribbon; the peach flavouring is applied as a light touch. It is a mild, low-nicotine record that steers away from the firm's heavy Lakeland-style essence tradition.
gawith-hoggarth-co-american-blend-sweet-.o: Leaves an aroma of ripe peach and light honey.

sutliff-tobacco-company-usa-600.z: USA #600 was one of Sutliff's plain aromatics sold in bulk. Its base is made of air-cured American Burley and sun-cured bright American Virginia; rather than a heavy casing, only a light sugary top note is applied. The cut is coarse, which supports a slow burn and a cool smoke. The blend served as a middle ground for smokers who don't want a strong flavoring but find fully unflavored tobacco too plain. Nicotine and taste intensity are moderate, and the room note is balanced. Records indicate the product was discontinued by its maker; remaining stock stayed available at some retailers for a while longer.
sutliff-tobacco-company-usa-600.o: Leaves a lightly sugary, warm dry-leaf scent.

mcclelland-fresh-apple-m96.z: An apple-flavored blend in McClelland's bulk aromatic series; no sufficient source describing its contents and character could be found.

teds-pipe-shoppe-colonel-custard.z: One of the house blends prepared at Ted's Pipe Shoppe in Tulsa, Oklahoma; though records show it among the more than forty house blends of the business founded in 1961, no independent source describing the blend's content and character could be found.

mcclelland-avenue-blend-p-m.z: No sufficient independent source describing the contents of this English-type blend, apparently prepared for a tobacconist, could be found.
mcclelland-avenue-blend-p-m.o: Records indicate it leaves a smoky aroma typical of Latakia-containing blends.

vegassmokes-five-star-luxury.z: A VegasSmokes blend described as a Virginia and Latakia combination; no independent source confirming its proportions has been found.

mcclelland-no-715-raspberries-in-cream.z: A blend in McClelland's bulk aromatic series, discontinued when the firm closed in 2018; no sufficient source documenting its contents and character could be found.

barclay-rex-no-6.z: One of Barclay Rex's numbered shop blends; no adequate source describing its composition could be found.

milan-tobacconists-our-royal-comfort.z: Referred to as an aromatic blend from Milan Tobacconists' "Our" line; since it doesn't appear in the maker's current catalogue and no source describing its composition could be obtained, no further detail can be given.

cornell-diehl-home-from-the-hills.z: Not enough primary sourcing could be found regarding the composition and character of the Cornell & Diehl blend Home from the Hills.

samuel-gawith-lakeland-special-no-6.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Lakeland Special No.6, according to records a pure Virginia blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

nording-retriever.z: Retriever is an aromatic blend in Erik Nørding's Hunter series, named after the hunting dog breed. It is built from Virginia and cavendish leaf, ribbon cut, and lightly flavored. The line was originally produced by McClelland; since McClelland ceased operations in 2018, that version has ended, and the blend's current status is not consistently reported in sources. The body is light to medium, with hints of toasted nut and caramel in the taste, and the casing is kept moderate compared to heavily sauced aromatics. It can be recommended for smokers looking for a clean, sweetish, low-nicotine blend.
nording-retriever.o: Leaves a caramel and toasted-nut aroma.

peterson-dark-flake.z: Dark Flake is a pressed, sliced blend made from selected dark Virginia leaves with a small amount of Perique added for spicy sharpness. Compared to the same brand's unflavored Virginia called Flake, it is built fuller in both flavor and nicotine; it is just as easy to prepare. Smoked slowly, Perique's tart, peppery side becomes pronounced; fruity and bready notes from the Virginia range broadly from light to dark. Beyond a very light sweetening it carries no heavy flavoring. It suits smokers who like the Virginia-Perique line, who pack by rubbing or folding the slice, and who are considering aging it in the tin.
peterson-dark-flake.o: Leaves an unassertive aroma recalling dried fig and bread dough.

lane-limited-burley-mild.z: A nearly unflavored bulk blend of lightly processed burley leaf. Burley's natural dry, nutty and lightly cocoa-like taste leads; since sugar content is low, the smoke is cool and the tendency to bite the tongue is low. It's a ribbon cut with low moisture, burning steadily once lit. It's a foundational product in Lane Limited's bulk line: smoked both on its own and used to build body in house blends. Suited to those who want no casing and seek a plain tobacco, and to those who blend their own.
lane-limited-burley-mild.o: Leaves a faint room note reminiscent of dry hazelnut and hay.

newminster-no-31-optimal-choice.z: No. 31 Optimal Choice combines hot-air-cured virginia leaves from Zimbabwean and Malawian fields with flavored black cavendish and soft burley. The top casing mixes fruit and vanilla together; cherry and vanilla cream stand out in front, with a light hint of brandy behind. It is one of the line's best-selling numbers and is sold in bulk. The nicotine load is moderate, the smoke sweet; suitable for smokers looking for a classic Danish-style aromatic. It is produced at Mac Baren's facilities in Denmark.
newminster-no-31-optimal-choice.o: Leaves an aroma of cherry liqueur and vanilla cream in the room.

house-of-calabash-grandfathers-own-blend.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for House of Calabash's Grandfather's Own Blend, so its content and character could not be recorded.

sillems-london-blend.z: London Blend is the Sillem's brand's full-bodied English mixture. The blend combines Latakia, Virginia, black cavendish, Kentucky, and Perique. Latakia gives the smoky main color while Virginia sets a sweet foundation; fire-cured Kentucky raises the body and nicotine share, Perique opens a plum-and-pepper-like spice, and black cavendish rounds off the sharp edges. The five-leaf structure makes the blend more layered than classic two- or three-component English mixtures; smoky, earthy, and spicy layers come forward in turn across the smoke. No additives are used. Suited to smokers accustomed to Latakia who want a high-body, complex English blend.
sillems-london-blend.o: Leaves a scent of wood smoke, leather, and dried plum.

bennington-tobacconist-no-31-donegal.z: No. 31 Donegal is the dark, pressed, Burley-centered blend among Bennington's shop blends. Black, twice-heat-fermented Burley from the Green River region is pressed long-cut and rested; the maker states this gives a mellower structure than ordinary black Cavendish. Golden Virginia ribbon and Virginia flake are later added to the mixture, along with air-cured Kentucky white Burley for body. The result is a low-acid tobacco with restrained sweetness, not prone to tongue bite. The Virginia share adds a light sugar layer, while Burley provides a dry, nutty base. It suits smokers avoiding heavy aromatics but not wanting a completely bare Virginia either; the maker also emphasizes that the blend is smokable for beginners.
bennington-tobacconist-no-31-donegal.o: Toasted bread and dark-sugar notes are joined by a faintly earthy undertone.

cornell-diehl-or-lyom-daylight.z: Or L'yom, whose name means "daylight" in Hebrew, is a blend in Cornell & Diehl's Hebraica series. The series grew out of mixtures blender William Serad — who worked for many years with founder Craig Tarler — prepared for Rabbi Ira Stone, who favored Burley-Oriental-Perique compositions; the blend names were given by Stone, referencing the language and concepts of Jewish tradition. The body is built from select red Virginia, dark Burley, and toasted black Cavendish; Oriental and Perique are sprinkled on top. It's a ribbon-cut mixture with medium flavor intensity and measured nicotine; sources note it's kept balanced enough to smoke at any hour of the day. Suited to smokers looking for sweet, salty-spicy, and cocoa-leaning layers together, drawn to unflavored American-type mixtures.
cornell-diehl-or-lyom-daylight.o: Leaves a floral tobacco scent with a light cocoa-and-caramel lean.

mccormick-selection-mango.z: Listed as a mango-flavored aromatic; no sufficient sources could be found to confirm its maker or contents.

cup-o-joes-adirondack-northway-pipe-toba.z: Adirondack Northway is the mint-cased member of the Adirondack line of bulk house blends from Cup O' Joes in New York state. Pressed Virginia ribbon, Burley, and black Cavendish are brought together; records note that mint is the dominant scent when the pack is opened, leaving a cooling effect on the palate throughout the smoke. The blend is low in nicotine, with a build where a pronounced menthol coolness takes precedence over tobacco flavor. Aimed at smokers looking for cased, cooling flavors and wanting a light everyday tobacco. Cup O' Joes' bulk blends are products the retailer released under its own name; the brand was later folded under the Pipes and Cigars umbrella.
cup-o-joes-adirondack-northway-pipe-toba.o: Leaves a scent of cool mint and lightly sweet tobacco.

pipesandcigars-com-russ-tartlet.z: Russ' Tartlet is one of the blends the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com sells under its own name; there is not enough independent source material documenting its content and character.

rona-obester-cherry.z: A pipe tobacco recorded in Rona's Obester series, classified, as its name suggests, as cherry-flavored; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

peretti-whiskey-cavendish.z: Whiskey Cavendish is a Peretti blend prepared by curing Cavendish leaf with Kentucky bourbon. The maker describes the blend as mellow, smooth, and mild; its taste and aroma come directly from this curing process. The flavoring is measured, giving a dry sweetness in the direction of oak and grain rather than the sugar load of fruit aromatics. It suits smokers who enjoy liquor-based flavorings but want to steer clear of heavily scented blends.
peretti-whiskey-cavendish.o: Leaves an oak cask and caramelized grain aroma.

poschl-tabak-brookfield-aromatic-blend.z: This is a flavored pipe tobacco German maker Pöschl Tabak offers under the name Brookfield; no reliable source could be found on the blend's content, cut, or flavoring.
poschl-tabak-brookfield-aromatic-blend.o: Reports indicate it is a flavored blend; there is not enough source material to describe its aroma.

d-r-tobacco-ryback.z: Ryback is a dark-colored blend prepared with Burley smokers in mind, combining Burley with fire-cured Kentucky leaf and Virginia. It's cut very fine (shag) and packaged with low moisture, so it shouldn't be packed too tightly before smoking. On the palate, Burley's nutty, creamy base and the dark-fired leaf's smoky, spicy weight come forward, while Virginia sets up a sweet-tart balance in the background. Nicotine level is above medium. Aimed at smokers wanting an unflavored, smoky, full Burley with the tobacco's own flavor at the front.
d-r-tobacco-ryback.o: Leaves a strong scent reminiscent of smoked meat and smoky wood in wood smoke.

with-pipe-and-book-maple-leaf.z: Maple Leaf is one of the aromatic house blends from the With Pipe and Book shop in Lake Placid; no verifiable source could be found regarding its composition.
with-pipe-and-book-maple-leaf.o: No confirmed description of the room note could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-cringle-flake-20.z: The third entry in the series, Cringle Flake 2021 consists of rested, partly cavendished red Virginia leaves and eighteen-year-old perique. It's pressed and sliced into flake, produced in limited quantity. Sweetness from natural sugars is accompanied by perique's sharp spice; stone fruit, earthy spice, and molasses tones are noted. Aimed at smokers seeking unflavored, intense Virginia-perique blends.
sutliff-tobacco-company-cringle-flake-20.o: Leaves a scent where molasses and stone-fruit sweetness mix with earthy spice.

hearth-home-porch-swing.z: Porch Swing is a blend in the Hearth & Home catalog; there is not enough sourcing to document its composition and flavor profile.

cornell-diehl-happy-hour.z: Happy Hour is a bulk blend among Cornell & Diehl's English mixtures. Its base is built from sweet bright Virginia and darker red Virginia leaves; a thin layer of Oriental and a small amount of perique are added. The manufacturer's description also lists black cavendish and Latakia among the components. It is a ribbon cut. Rather than the heavy English mixtures where Latakia leaps to the front, the blend offers a balanced profile with spice and measured smoke layered over Virginia sweetness; perique adds a plummy, spicy depth. On the manufacturer's scale, strength is medium while flavor intensity is given as above medium. It suits those new to English mixtures and anyone wanting a moderately smoky, all-day blend.
cornell-diehl-happy-hour.o: Leaves a lightly smoky, spicy, sweetish tobacco aroma.

butera-matured-ribbon.z: Matured Ribbon is an unflavored blend in Butera's Royal Vintage line, obtained by pressing lemon-yellow, red and steam-darkened virginia leaves and cutting them into ribbon form. The contribution of the three leaf types can be distinguished separately in the smoke: red virginia is tart and soft, the darkened leaf spicy and cool, the lemon-yellow sweet and hay-like. The blend leans toward the red and darkened leaves in weight. Suitable for smokers seeking a virginia built on leaf variety rather than a single type.
butera-matured-ribbon.o: Leaves a dry hay, tart fruit and light cinnamon aroma.

sobranie-of-london-rich-virginia.z: Rich Virginia is a tinned blend from the London-based Sobranie house, made of unflavored Virginia tobaccos. Though the Sobranie name is mostly associated in the pipe world with latakia-forward mixtures like Balkan Sobranie and 759, the house also released plain, latakia-free Virginia tins during the same period; Rich Virginia belongs to this second line. Records indicate the blend was built by adding stoved dark Virginia alongside lemon-yellow Virginia leaves, presented in ribbon cut. Its character revolves around orange peel, lightly fermented dark fruit, and a grainy sweetness reminiscent of bread crust; nicotine strength sits somewhere between light and medium, making it suited to those seeking a Virginia they can smoke all day. Since Sobranie's pipe tobacco production has ended, the blend is not in production today and is found only in old stock tins. A historical reference point for smokers wanting to know the unflavored Virginia idiom — the balance between sugar sweetness and tartness.
sobranie-of-london-rich-virginia.o: Leaves a lightly tart-sweet tobacco scent reminiscent of dry hay and lemon peel.

nording-seaweed.z: Seaweed is a ready-rubbed, ribbon-cut blend in the aromatic wing of the Nørding brand. Its body is built from golden Virginia and cocoa-brown Burley, with a small amount of black cavendish added. A cream-like caramel sauce is applied on top. It comes in a fifty-gram tin. The sweetness of the caramel is prominent in the smoke, though Burley's nutty, dry body can be felt underneath. Nicotine is light to medium, making it suitable for long sessions. The room note it leaves is strong. A fitting blend for those looking for a Danish-style sweet-sauced aromatic, and suitable for beginning pipe smokers.
nording-seaweed.o: Leaves an aroma of boiled sugar and buttery caramel.

james-fox-the-squires-mixture.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of James Fox's The Squire's Mixture blend could be found.

brigham-peaches-cream.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named Peaches & Cream under the Brigham brand could be found.

uhles-golden-shag-blend.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend called Golden Shag Blend has been found.
uhles-golden-shag-blend.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

dobies-dobies-four-square-cavendish.z: Four Square is a series launched in 1922 by George Dobie & Son in Paisley, Scotland. The brand later passed to Godfrey Phillips; the Greenhill factory on Clark Street closed in 1956, and blending moved first to Denmark, then to the United States. The country field shows the brand's country of origin; current production takes place elsewhere.
dobies-dobies-four-square-cavendish.o: Leaves a lightly sweet scent of dark, sugared leaf and dried fruit.

w-o-larsen-155th-anniversary.z: 155th Anniversary is a release prepared for the 155th year of the W.Ø. Larsen name, tied to the brand's Craftsmans Edition series. Each of these blends, referencing the company's Danish pipe tobacco tradition dating to 1864, is designed for a specific year. Virginia leaves make up the bulk of the blend, joined by Burley of African and Central American origin. Most of the Virginias are pressed into flake and then rubbed out, offered as ready-rubbed, giving a slower, more even burn. The light-colored Virginia pieces and dark Burley leaves create contrast both in appearance and taste: Virginia brings sweet and tart, Burley a dry, nutty side. Flavoring isn't pronounced. Nicotine runs at a medium level; despite being a Danish product, it's aimed at smokers seeking a profile closer to unflavored Virginia-Burley blends than aromatics.
w-o-larsen-155th-anniversary.o: Leaves a warm grain scent reminiscent of dry grass and stale bread.

grants-tobacconist-roanoake.z: One of Grant's Tobacconist's house blends; there is no independent sourcing describing its composition.

cavallini-sobranity.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Sobranity under the Cavallini brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

barclay-rex-vanilla.z: Listed as a vanilla-flavored Barclay Rex shop blend; no verifiable source on its leaf composition and cut could be found.

gatlin-burlier-mountain-mall-mix.z: Mountain Mall Mix is one of the shop blends of the Gatlinburlier tobacconist in Gatlinburg. Per the producer's description, lemon Virginia flakes are mixed into roasted cavendish and burley leaf; the blend's aroma is associated with caramel popcorn flavouring.
gatlin-burlier-mountain-mall-mix.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of caramel popcorn and nut candy.

peter-stokkebye-black-beauty.z: Black Beauty is a Peter Stokkebye blend obtained by putting ripened Virginia, Java, and Burley leaf through a black Cavendish process. The process gives the leaf a dark, near-black appearance and a pronounced softness; the medium-loose cut packs easily and burns cool. On the palate a soft sweetness recalling sugar and light caramel leads; nicotine strength is low and bite is kept minimal. This structure suits newcomers to the pipe, those seeking a not-too-heavy sweet smoke, and those wanting a sweet base for their own blends.
peter-stokkebye-black-beauty.o: Leaves an aroma with a sweet, lightly caramelized, roasted-sugar association.

seattle-pipe-club-mississippi-river-rum-.z: Mississippi River Rum Barrel Aged is a barrel-aged version of Seattle Pipe Club's classic Mississippi River recipe. The blend's skeleton is built on a balance of virginia, Oriental, latakia, and perique; after mixing, the tobacco is rested for thirty days in a used rum barrel. During this time, the leaf picks up traces of the rum and the oak. The result is an English mixture that has gained a sweet depth while keeping the smoky Latakia together with Perique's plum-spice sharpness. Presented as a crumble cake, it is easy to prepare; a rum-barrel stave is added to the tin to help preserve the aromas. Aimed at experienced smokers seeking a full-bodied, smoky, lightly sweet mixture.
seattle-pipe-club-mississippi-river-rum-.o: Sweet rum and oak-barrel notes mix into the smoky Latakia scent.

mcclelland-katerini-classic.z: Katerini Classic is a member of McClelland's Grand Orientals series, which spotlights single-region Orientals. Oriental leaf grown in Greece's Katerini district, supported by a small amount of Virginia, is presented as ribbon cut; no flavoring is used. In the smoke, a deep, fine sweetness can be heard, along with a cigarette-like line and a spicy texture reminiscent of olive oil. It's related to Samsun and Black Sea Orientals, which come from the same seed stock grown in different regions; records indicate it draws a lighter body than those. A product for those wanting to get to know a single Oriental variety's character. Discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-katerini-classic.o: Leaves a dry hay, spice, and faintly olive-oil-like aroma.

cornell-diehl-americana.z: Americana is a ribbon-cut mixture Cornell & Diehl builds around American leaves. A small amount of Latakia and black cavendish are added to a Virginia-and-burley body; the maker describes the blend as a recipe carrying old-style American mixture taste to the modern smoker. Burley forms an earthy, nutty base, Virginia brings light sweetness, and Latakia leaves a non-dominant smoky layer. It suits those looking for a medium-strength blend, smokable at any time of day, with an understated flavoring.
cornell-diehl-americana.o: A sweetish tobacco aroma accompanies a light smoke and dry-hay scent.

john-patton-storm-front.z: Storm Front is a blend carrying the signature of blender John Patton, classified as cigar-leaf-based; not enough sources could be found to detail its contents.

mcclelland-2015-holiday-spirit.z: 2015 Holiday Spirit is that year's tin of the limited-edition aromatic McClelland released for year-end. Its composition holds Burley, Virginia, and Cavendish, sweetened with dark rum, walnut, and cocoa. The cut is irregular: stem pieces, large Burley leaves, dried Virginia bits, and Cavendish of every size sit together, making an even burn through the smoke difficult to maintain. In the first half, the rum-and-chocolate combination is pronounced; as the smoke proceeds, an ashy tone comes forward. Nicotine is low and body stays thin. Suited to smokers seeking a sweet holiday-season aromatic who don't mind dealing with an irregular cut. The brand stopped production in 2018.
mcclelland-2015-holiday-spirit.o: Leaves a sugar-and-rum aroma that lingers in fabric for a long time.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-captain-earles-d.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for this blend, part of the Captain Earle's line, described as English type.

faders-black-flake.z: Fader's is a line of house blends offered under its own name by a long-established Baltimore tobacconist; no verifiable source could be found regarding this blend's composition and character.

pipe-republic-northforeland.z: No reliable sources on Pipe Republic's blend Northforeland could be found, so its content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

borkum-riff-cherry-liqueur.z: Cherry Liqueur is a loose-cut aromatic combining roughly forty percent black Cavendish with sixty percent Virginia-seed leaf, finished with a cherry-and-liqueur topping. The leaf is gathered from batches sourced across different continents. The topping is kept more restrained than in Cherry Cavendish; a liqueur note alongside the cherry adds a slight tang to the sweetness. Nicotine is light and the smoke is mild. It suits smokers who like fruited aromatics but want to avoid heavily sugary toppings. The blend belongs to the Borkum Riff line, produced in Denmark under Scandinavian Tobacco Group.
borkum-riff-cherry-liqueur.o: Leaves a sweet, faintly boozy fruit note reminiscent of cherry liqueur.

schurch-rubelite-366.z: Rubelite 366, signed by Schürch, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

bosphorus-plumcake.z: A blend carrying the Bosphorus name, classified as aromatic in catalog records; no reliable source regarding its content and smoking character could be found.
bosphorus-plumcake.o: No sufficient description of its aroma could be found in the records.

cornell-diehl-joie-de-vivre.z: Joie de Vivre is a Cornell & Diehl English blend inspired by New Orleans' festive atmosphere, presented in pressed plug form. Equal proportions of Perique and Katerini Oriental tobacco are added to fragrant Latakia and sweet red Virginia; unsweetened black Cavendish rounds it out to soften the smoke. The pressed structure lets the flavors meld together; Latakia's smoke-and-leather character layers with Perique's spice and Katerini's dry, grassy tone. With high nicotine load and flavor intensity, it's aimed at smokers accustomed to Latakia looking for a full evening bowl.
cornell-diehl-joie-de-vivre.o: A spicy background accompanies a scent of smoke, leather, and smoked wood.

consolidated-14-maple.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Consolidated blend 14: Maple.

faders-lanyard.z: Not enough independent sourcing documenting the composition and character of Lanyard, one of the house blends of the Baltimore-based Fader's tobacconist, could be found.

cornell-diehl-izmir-turkish.z: Izmir Turkish is a member of Cornell & Diehl's single-varietal leaf series, consisting solely of unflavored, ribbon-cut Izmir leaf. This sun-cured, small-leafed Oriental tobacco is low in nicotine and intense in flavor, and is cut to the company's own blending specifications. Its profile has a woody base, a pronounced peppery spice, and just enough fruity tang to keep things balanced; on the retrohale, a perfumed black-pepper note with a hint of sweetness appears. The body is light. It is intended primarily as a blending component, though it can be smoked on its own; it suits those wanting to get to know Oriental tobacco's character in its pure form.
cornell-diehl-izmir-turkish.o: Leaves a dry-grass and spicy, perfumed tobacco aroma.

gatlin-burlier-mellow-moonshine.z: Mellow Moonshine is one of the house blends the Gatlinburlier tobacconist in Gatlinburg, Tennessee, prepares at its own counter. Per the producer's description, a touch of peach brandy flavouring is added over cavendish-processed burley leaf; the "moonshine" reference in the name relates to this alcoholic fruit flavouring.
gatlin-burlier-mellow-moonshine.o: Leaves a sweet peach and lightly alcoholic fruit aroma.

comoys-of-london-cask-2-portwood.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Comoy's of London blend Cask #2 Portwood.

uhles-par-shooter-blend.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend called Par Shooter Blend has been found.
uhles-par-shooter-blend.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

samuel-gawith-english-summer-flake.z: English Summer Flake is a member of the limited-run Four Seasons series prepared through collaboration between Samuel Gawith, Stanislaw, and DTM. The series' other members are Irish Spring Time Flake, Scottish Autumn Flake, and Winter Time Flake. It is a Virginia-forward, pressed flake; a light citrus-echoing top flavoring is applied. Its body is measured, its sweetness fresh. Suited to those seeking a lightly cased Virginia flake; being a limited production, it is not constantly available on the market.
samuel-gawith-english-summer-flake.o: Leaves a fresh sweetness evoking lemon peel with a grassy tobacco scent.

ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-scented-plug.z: Referred to as a small-batch blend in Ken Byron Ventures' Yoshimi's line, presented as its name suggests in a cased, pressed plug form; not enough sources could be found to document its composition.
ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-scented-plug.o: Could not be described due to lack of accessible records.

poschl-tabak-tilbury-cherry-cream.z: Tilbury Cherry Cream is the aromatic in Pöschl Tabak's Tilbury line flavored with a cherry-and-cream casing. Its base is built from Virginia and Burley; the ribbon-cut structure ensures an even burn. Nicotine is low and the tobacco flavor measured. The casing's weight is maintained throughout the smoke and stays ahead of the tobacco's own character. It is the type smokers looking for a light-bodied, sweet-cased everyday aromatic, including newcomers to the pipe, tend toward. The line is continued by Pöschl in 40-gram packs.
poschl-tabak-tilbury-cherry-cream.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of ripe cherry and milk cream.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-cherokee.z: Cherokee, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an aromatic mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

b-b-tobacconists-llc-country-gentleman.z: A tobacconist-signed blend; no verifiable source on its content could be found, leaving the profile blank.

mac-baren-hh-bold-kentucky.z: HH Bold Kentucky Flake is built mainly from dark fire-cured Kentucky leaf sourced from the US and Africa, with a small amount of light Virginia added for balance. The tobaccos are pressed into a cake and then sliced into flake form. There is no applied top flavor and casing is minimal, letting the leaf's own smoky, earthy taste come through. Nicotine and flavor intensity are high, so it's best smoked slowly on a full stomach. A blend for smokers accustomed to dark fire-cured leaf.
mac-baren-hh-bold-kentucky.o: Leaves the sharp smoky note of wood smoke and fire-cured leaf.

sutliff-tobacco-company-pipe-force-episo.z: The second episode of the Pipe Force series continues Per Georg Jensen's experiments built around Katerini leaf. Its base is made of bright, red, and stoved Virginias; over this, smoky Latakia, floral Kentucky, stoved Katerini, and Katerini Perique — the series' distinguishing component — are added. It is an unflavored, layered mixture in which Virginia sweetness carries Latakia's smoke and Perique's red-fruit-and-spice accent. It is aimed at smokers familiar with English mixtures who don't shy away from high nicotine. It was produced in limited numbers.
sutliff-tobacco-company-pipe-force-episo.o: Leaves a scent combining smoke, dried fruit, and spice.

the-smoker-proctors.z: Proctors is recorded as one of the hand-prepared house blends from The Smoker, a tobacconist that operated in Albany from the 1930s until 2011; no independent source describing the blend's composition has been found.

peter-heinrichs-no-30.z: This is one of the pipe tobaccos of the Cologne-based house Peter Heinrichs; the profile is left incomplete, as no reliable sources describing the blend's content and character could be found.

ilsted-own-mixture-black-light.z: This is a mixture in the Own Mixture line bearing the name of Danish pipe maker Poul Ilsted; no sufficient source verifying its content and character could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-194.z: Wilke No. 194 is an aromatic belonging to the brand's 190-number series. According to the maker's recipe, Wilke's long-used Royal Scot leaf is combined with the house's own roasted black cavendish. The resulting smoke has a sweet side, though the sugar load isn't dominant; the dark, lightly scorched sweetness coming from the roasted cavendish is the blend's most distinctive trait. Since the casing level is kept measured, the tobacco's own flavor isn't masked, which sets the blend apart from heavily fruity or liqueur-style aromatics. It's light in nicotine and burns slowly. It suits smokers wanting a sweet background without a syrupy texture, seeking an aromatic suitable for all-day smoking.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-194.o: Leaves a scent of toasted sugar and dried fruit.

amsterdam-tabaco-amsterdam.z: No reliable source documenting the content and character of this blend sold under the name Amsterdam Tabaco could be found.

robert-mcconnell-st-james-park.z: St. James Park is a ribbon-cut blend from Robert McConnell's English-style line. Golden Virginia leaf is combined with smoky Latakia; Oriental tobacco adds a spicy layer while black Cavendish builds the sweet, mellow side of the mixture. The result is a medium-bodied, layered taste that is neither purely smoky nor purely sweet. The cut lights quickly when dry and burns evenly in medium-sized bowls. The brand was founded in Belfast in 1848; production today is carried out by the German blender Kohlhase & Kopp, though the brand identity remains Irish. With nicotine and flavor intensity both staying medium, it serves as an entry point for those new to Latakia blends and as an all-day option for experienced smokers. Its unflavored composition makes it a poor fit for those looking for aromatic tobacco.
robert-mcconnell-st-james-park.o: Leaves an aroma dominated by wood smoke and incense, with a faint sweetness underneath.

newminster-no-23-blackberry-brandy.z: No. 23 Blackberry Brandy is one of the fruity aromatics in the Newminster line. Its base contains Mexican air-cured burley along with Brazilian and US fire-cured virginia leaves; a portion of these is converted to black cavendish. The top casing combines blackberry's fruity sweetness with brandy's sharp note. The cut is a mix of loose shag and cake cuts, and the tobacco is moist but not sticky. The smoke stays cool; the blackberry note holds from the start of the bowl to the end, with a nutty, creamy base from the burley perceptible in the background. Given its pronounced casing, this tobacco naturally leaves a scent behind; it is commonly smoked in a pipe or corn cob set aside for fruity aromatics. Suitable for smokers looking for a fruity, sweet aromatic.
newminster-no-23-blackberry-brandy.o: Leaves an aroma of blackberry jam and snifter brandy.

randys-tobacco-shop-balkan-supreme.z: This is a Balkan Supreme listing sold under a tobacconist's own label; no independent source could be found to distinguish it from other makers' blends of the same name.

petersen-sorensen-premium-blend.z: This is one of the blends released under the Petersen & Sorensen name; no sufficient first-hand sources documenting its content and character could be found.
petersen-sorensen-premium-blend.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

john-middleton-inc-hickory.z: One of the blends from John Middleton, a company founded in Philadelphia in 1856 that has made pipe tobacco since the 1950s; the entry is left incomplete because not enough sources could be found to document the blend's contents and character.
john-middleton-inc-hickory.o: No source could be found on the room note.

hu-tobacco-sissinghurst.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the Sissinghurst blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

cornell-diehl-guilford-courthouse.z: Guilford Courthouse is a ribbon-cut, unflavored Cornell & Diehl blend built on Virginia leaf with Izmir tobacco added. It is named for the Battle of Guilford Court House in the American Revolutionary War; its current production status is unclear since it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog. The smoke is cool and smooth, burning easily. Virginia's sweetness and Izmir tobacco's spicy, lightly tangy character stand out as the blend's two axes. It suits those wanting to get to know an unflavored Virginia-Oriental composition, particularly the place of Turkish tobacco in a pipe blend.
cornell-diehl-guilford-courthouse.o: Leaves the sharp, heavy scent of spicy Oriental tobacco and sweet Virginia.

john-middleton-inc-prince-albert-soft-va.z: The vanilla-flavored Cavendish version in the Prince Albert line; not enough sources could be found on the blend's full contents and cut.
john-middleton-inc-prince-albert-soft-va.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough aroma.

robert-mcconnell-oriental-square.z: Oriental Square is a ribbon-cut blend combining matured dark and yellow Virginia leaves with latakia and Oriental tobaccos. The producer's description states the blend gives a balanced smoke with fine floral tones coming forward alongside the smokiness. The Oriental share is pronounced, as the name suggests; in this respect the blend leans toward the classic Balkan style. Suited to smokers who don't want Latakia's smokiness to be overpowering and who seek the Oriental's sour, spicy side. It stays in the medium range for nicotine and flavor, making it suitable for long smoking sessions. The Robert McConnell name rests on an old English tobacco house; production is carried out today at the Kohlhase & Kopp facilities in Germany.
robert-mcconnell-oriental-square.o: Leaves a fine, smoky tobacco scent in the room carrying floral tones.

sutliff-tobacco-company-vanilla-cavendis.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Sutliff Tobacco Company's Vanilla Cavendish pipe tobacco could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-festivus-mixture.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents of this blend from Ken Byron Ventures' Festivus series.
ken-byron-ventures-festivus-mixture.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-dark-thick-cut.z: The Kendal Dark family represents the brand's dark, unflavored leaf approach. In this product, fire-cured Malawi leaf and air-cured Indian leaf stand out; the result is a dark-colored, intense, earthy flavor palette. The name "Thick Cut" describes a cut kept thicker than the usual fine shag. It's on the high side for nicotine and calls for slow smoking. Suited to experienced smokers wanting an unflavored, dark, and full English style without a sweet sauce; it isn't a blend suited to smoking on an empty stomach or at a fast draw.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-dark-thick-cut.o: Leaves a dark, smoky, woody tobacco aroma.

mac-baren-club-blend.z: Club Blend's recipe dates back to 1955. Specially selected whole Virginia leaves are used as the wrap; Mac Baren's own Cavendish and Virginia tobaccos are placed inside and spun whole, then sliced and presented in rolled form. This structure requires the slices to be rubbed out before packing and gives a slow, cool burn. Its character is built between Virginia's sweetness and Cavendish's mildness; suited to smokers who like the texture of pressed and spun tobaccos and who keep their distance from heavy aromatics.
mac-baren-club-blend.o: Leaves a sweetish, faintly caramel tobacco aroma.

dan-tobacco-bill-baileys-balkan-blend.z: Bill Bailey's Balkan Blend is a full-bodied Balkan mixture with Latakia kept above forty percent. Per the maker's recipe, alongside Virginia and Oriental leaf it contains roughly ten percent fire-cured Kentucky and a small amount of Perique; ribbon cut. The weight of Latakia is the blend's most defining trait. The smoke opens with smoky, creamy, woody Latakia tones; as it progresses, the Oriental leaf's tangy, grassy, spicy contribution comes forward. Kentucky and Perique pull up the body and the sense of nicotine. A fitting choice for smokers accustomed to heavy Latakia blends looking for a strong, complex smoke; too heavy for beginners.
dan-tobacco-bill-baileys-balkan-blend.o: A heavy scent of pine smoke and burnt leather spreads through the room and clings to clothing.

g-l-pease-penny-farthing.z: Penny Farthing is a blend built by spicing bright and red Virginia leaves with Louisiana perique and a small amount of dark fire-cured Kentucky. It is the first shag cut offered in the brand's line; this fine cut, at about thirty-two cuts per inch, is easy to fill. The smoke opens with a measured sweetness and gains depth as the bowl progresses. Red Virginias build an earthy, tartish base, light Virginias add a grassy brightness; perique adds its fermented spice, and Kentucky adds a fine oak-smoke layer. Clove, leather, and light floral notes are reported. It suits smokers seeking the Virginia-perique structure together with a smoky layer.
g-l-pease-penny-farthing.o: Leaves an aroma of sweet hay, dried fruit, and a fine oak smoke.

hearth-home-cherry.z: A Burley-based, cherry-flavored blend from Hearth & Home; there is not enough independent sourcing available for it.

svendborg-danish-mixture.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Svendborg's Danish Mixture pipe tobacco could be found.

rocks-vanilla-cigar.z: Rocks Vanilla is recorded not as a pipe tobacco but as a cheap vanilla-flavored cigarillo, sold as a low-priced product in the Turkish market. No reliable information could be found on its blend content or place of production.
rocks-vanilla-cigar.o: Leaves a cigar-smoke aroma dominated by the vanilla flavoring.

dan-tobacco-sud-brasilien-sweet-and-mild.z: This is a blend in Dan Tobacco's Ocean Liner series dedicated to ocean-line ships, marketed as sweet and mild; not enough sourcing could be found about its composition.
dan-tobacco-sud-brasilien-sweet-and-mild.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

solani-369-blue-label.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Solani blend 369: Blue Label could not be found.

cornell-diehl-super-balkan.z: Super Balkan is one of Cornell & Diehl's oldest recipes. Perique, Latakia, and Burley are added to a base weighted toward bright Virginia slices, with high-quality Turkish leaf sprinkled on top. Its Latakia proportion is higher than the same house's Atlas Balkan blend. Despite "Balkan" in the name, the blend isn't purely Oriental-focused — Perique and Burley have a clear say. On the smoke, Latakia's smoke leads, Perique adds sharpness, while Burley and Oriental leaf balance the dusty, leathery base with floral-citrus tones. Its body is full and the room note strong.
cornell-diehl-super-balkan.o: Leaves a heavy smoky scent reminiscent of leather, orange peel, and tar.

ken-byron-ventures-van-gogh-2020.z: The 2020 release of Van Gogh is reported to be classified as Virginia and Perique; no independent source could be found to document that year's specific contents.
ken-byron-ventures-van-gogh-2020.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

just-for-him-old-toby.z: Old Toby is one of the blends in Just For Him's Middle-earth Pipeweed series. The series takes its names from the pipeweed varieties in Tolkien's works; Old Toby refers to the leaf named as the Southfarthing's well-known weed in the books. The blend is Virginia-based with Perique added in. The Perique lends Virginia's sweetness a spicy, lightly fruity edge, giving a drier, more tobacco-forward smoke compared to the series' distinctly vanilla-scented entries. Flavoring is either very light or absent entirely. Suited to those who like the Virginia-Perique structure and want the aromatic side kept measured.
just-for-him-old-toby.o: Leaves a lightly peppery edge alongside a tangy, dry-hay aroma.

cornell-diehl-stratfordshire.z: Stratfordshire is a ribbon-cut mixture in Cornell & Diehl's English blend family. Latakia and Turkish leaf are added to a Virginia body; Burley and black Cavendish also balance the blend's texture and sweetness. It takes its name from the English region of the same name, and the brand's marketing highlights this rural association. On the flavor side it offers a medium-to-full English profile: Latakia's smoke is noticeable but doesn't take over the blend alone, sitting alongside Virginia's sweetness and the Oriental's dry spice. Suited to smokers who like unflavored blends and want a balanced Latakia mixture they can smoke all day.
cornell-diehl-stratfordshire.o: Leaves a scent of woody smoke reminiscent of a campfire alongside dry hay.

e-a-carey-careys-cavendish-mixture.z: Per available records from the E. A. Carey catalog, this is referred to as a cavendish-forward aromatic blend; no primary source could be found documenting its composition and character.

black-river-cigar-company-fire-cured-twi.z: No independent, reliable source could be found on Fire Cured Twist, a twist of rope tobacco made from fire-cured leaf as the name suggests.

hearth-home-summer-harvest.z: Summer Harvest is an aromatic mixture in Hearth & Home's Signature line; no sufficient source stating its composition and flavoring could be found.

borkum-riff-ruby.z: Ruby is a heavily flavored blend built from Kentucky, Burley, and Cavendish leaf, with cherry flavoring rounded out by a touch of vanilla. Borkum Riff's cherry-centered product is sold under this name in Northern European markets; in terms of content and topping it stands in line with the brand's Cherry Cavendish product. It's ribbon cut and light on nicotine. It suits smokers looking for the cherry side of fruited aromatics, wanting a mild, sweet everyday bowl. The brand is produced in Denmark under Scandinavian Tobacco Group.
borkum-riff-ruby.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity room note of ripe cherry with a touch of vanilla.

planta-jacaranda.z: Planta Jacaranda is a pipe tobacco blend for which there is not enough independent source material.
planta-jacaranda.o: Not enough records could be found on the room note.

warped-kings-stride.z: Kings Stride is the Virginia-forward member of the series Warped founder Kyle Gellis prepared together with Cornell & Diehl blender Jeremy Reeves. Its foundation is selected Virginia leaves and five-year-aged Burley; on top, a special cavendish obtained by pressing and steaming St. James Perique and Dominican cigar leaf is added. The mixture is pressed and offered in crumble-cake form.
warped-kings-stride.o: Leaves a tart dried-fruit and baked-dough scent with a light earthy trace.

peter-stokkebye-toasted-burley-no-312.z: This is a Burley-forward blend in Peter Stokkebye's numbered bulk series; no sufficient first-hand sources detailing its content could be found.
peter-stokkebye-toasted-burley-no-312.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

sutliff-tobacco-company-no-150-mark-twai.z: A blend within Sutliff Tobacco Company's bulk aromatic line; since no accessible source documenting its content and character could be found, no further detail is given here.

cornell-diehl-organic-pipe-dreams.z: A blend, no longer in Cornell & Diehl's catalogue, referred to as aromatic; no adequate source documenting its composition and character was found.
cornell-diehl-organic-pipe-dreams.o: No adequate information for a description could be found in records.

mcclelland-arcadia-221b-series.z: Arcadia is a blend in McClelland's Sherlock Holmes-themed 221B series; per the maker's account, it's a reconstruction, based on old sources, of the tobacco favored by Dr. Watson. It's a ribbon-cut mixture of Virginia and Oriental (Turkish) tobaccos; the tin label doesn't list Latakia, though records show assessments suggesting a trace amount is present. The cut and moisture balance ease packing and burning, giving a cool smoke.
