The Oriental tobaccos' sweet-spiced, faintly tangy character sits at the blend's center, with Virginia building a sweet base under it. Strength is light-to-medium, flavor medium. Suited to smokers seeking a pronounced Oriental character rather than a Latakia-forward mixture.
mcclelland-arcadia-221b-series.o: Leaves a sharp aroma reminiscent of spiced Oriental tobacco and cigarette tobacco.

peter-heinrichs-chateau-henri-no-51.z: Chateau Henri No. 51 is an English mixture formed by blending golden and chocolate-coffee-toned Virginia leaves with Macedonian-origin Oriental tobaccos, rounded out with some Latakia. The Latakia proportion is not kept high enough to dominate the blend; the main body is built by Virginia's sweetness and the Oriental's dry, tart spice. Given this structure, flavor intensity is pronounced while nicotine sits in the medium band. It is a suitable record for smokers wanting to taste Latakia's smoky character in a measured way over a Virginia base, who lean toward the classic English mixture tradition. The series takes its name from Peter Heinrichs' shop called Chateau Henri in Bergheim.
peter-heinrichs-chateau-henri-no-51.o: A heavy aroma recalling smoke and leather leaves a dry-hay note underneath.

bosphorus-mocha.z: Mocha is a ribbon-cut aromatic built on red Virginia and burley. The flavor casings are bitter chocolate, caramel, vanilla and various fruit extracts. In the smoke, cocoa taste comes forward slightly more than the other notes; vanilla and fruit extracts show themselves more in the aroma. Sugar content is kept low relative to the variety of flavors, and the tobacco taste stays distinguishable throughout the smoke. The combination of red Virginia and burley gives the blend strength and fullness; flavor intensity is high. Aimed at smokers seeking an intensely flavored but not syrupy aromatic.
bosphorus-mocha.o: Leaves a dark, sweet aroma dominated by caramel and cocoa.

japan-tobacco-asuka-new.z: No reliable source documenting the content and character of Japan Tobacco's Asuka (new) blend could be found.

planta-anno-mmxv-brazilian-mixture.z: This is a blend in Planta's limited-production Anno series, named after a year; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

faders-renaissance.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for the Fader's brand's Renaissance pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

gawith-hoggarth-co-seasonal-reserve-chri.z: Seasonal Reserve is the 2019 edition of the Christmas blend within Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s limited annual seasonal series. It's made by combining bright flue-cured Virginia and fire-cured Cavendish Virginia with sweet sun-cured Burley leaf; according to the maker's description, the mixture is light and shows little tongue bite. The topping is built on a cherry-and-almond axis, with vanilla added for a creamy texture; a marzipan and fruitcake association stands out both when the tin is opened and throughout the smoke. Since it was produced in a limited run and withdrawn from the market once that year's edition sold out, it's found today only in old tins. An entry aimed at those wanting a distinctly flavored seasonal aromatic kept light on nicotine.
gawith-hoggarth-co-seasonal-reserve-chri.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of marzipan, cherry, and spiced cake.

solani-633-virginia-flake.z: Solani 633 is the unflavored Virginia-Perique flake in Kohlhase & Kopp's Solani line. The slices are pressed tight and firm; airing them for a while before packing eases both packing and burning. On opening the tin, a strong tobacco scent is noticeable; the blend carries no flavoring. The smoke is slow and cool. Virginia's sweet base is surrounded by perique's spice, so smoking pace matters: puffed too fast, the perique can turn bitter. It's a full-nicotine tobacco, appealing to Virginia smokers who know how to work with flake tobaccos and want to keep the same character going all day.
solani-633-virginia-flake.o: Perique's spicy, lightly peppery trace mixes into a tangy-sweet Virginia scent.

cobblestone-chess-knight.z: A blend noted as Virginia-based, belonging to Cobblestone's Chess series; not enough independent sourcing could be found regarding it.

milan-tobacconists-anniversary.z: A blend from Milan Tobacconists' aromatic line carrying the shop's own name. African-origin golden Virginia leaves, burley, and soft black cavendish are brought together; a vanilla-and-cocoa-leaning casing is applied on top. It is a mixture with low nicotine and a soft, sweet taste. Suitable for smokers who like aromatics, want a tobacco that doesn't bite the tongue and leaves a pronounced room note, and for those new to the pipe.
milan-tobacconists-anniversary.o: Leaves a warm, sweet-dough aroma carrying vanilla and cocoa sweetness.

planta-burberry.z: Planta Burberry is a pipe tobacco blend for which there is not enough independent source material.
planta-burberry.o: Not enough records could be found on the room note.

wessex-tradition.z: Tradition is the English mixture in the Wessex series known by its red packaging, presented in ribbon cut. Latakia and Oriental sit atop a base dominated by red Virginia leaf; it contains no flavoring additive. In the smoke, red Virginia's dark, bready sweetness runs alongside Latakia's smoky tone; the Oriental leaves a dry spice line in the background. Nicotine and intensity are medium. It suits smokers seeking the classic English blend framework with the Virginia side more pronounced.
wessex-tradition.o: Leaves a scent of smoky wood and dry spice.

mac-baren-classic-amber.z: Classic Amber is the name of the aromatic blend Mac Baren offers as Vanilla Toffee in some markets. Per the maker's description, select, rested Virginia leaves are combined with the brand's modern black Cavendish; small plug pieces are mixed into the loose-cut tobacco to complete the blend. This mixed structure gives a texture that's both easy to pack and burns slower. As the name suggests, the topping is built along a vanilla-and-confectionery axis; the Cavendish deepens this sweetness, while the Virginia leaves a fruity base behind it. Nicotine dose stays on the low side. Suited to those who like pronouncedly flavored, sweet blends whose smoke lingers in the room, and to smokers in their early pipe years.
mac-baren-classic-amber.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of sweet vanilla and sugared butter.

ken-byron-ventures-hand-of-gotz.z: One of Ken Byron Ventures' limited-release blends; no independent source could be found to document its contents.
ken-byron-ventures-hand-of-gotz.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

peter-stokkebye-mellow-mocha.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Mellow Mocha in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

super-value-vanilla-cavendish.z: Super Value's vanilla cavendish blend is a ribbon-cut aromatic made from soft cavendish leaves topped with vanilla flavoring. The catalog description describes it as an easy-lighting, smooth-smoking tobacco; it's undemanding for beginners in moisture balance and burning behavior. Its character is plain and single-note: it offers nothing beyond vanilla scent and cavendish sweetness. Worth considering for those seeking an inexpensive, everyday aromatic favored for its scent, and for those new to aromatic blends.

gawith-hoggarth-co-black-pigtail.z: Black Pipe Pigtail is the dark record in Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s fine-cut pigtail line. The rope is pressed and steam-cooked until it turns fully black; the resulting tobacco gives a cool, mild smoke with a leathery undertone reminiscent of unsweetened cavendish. The firm's twist tobaccos are traditionally made for both pipe smoking and chewing. According to records this line carries a light touch of anise flavouring, though the leaf itself still defines the main character. Since it is sold in rope form, thin coins are cut off and rubbed out for filling; it is aimed at smokers who want a slow smoke and are used to working with dark leaf.
gawith-hoggarth-co-black-pigtail.o: Leaves a sweetish aroma reminiscent of aniseed candy together with the leather and earth notes of the dark leaf.

pauls-pipe-shop-english-toffee.z: English Toffee is an aromatic mixture named among Paul's Pipe Shop's house blends; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.
pauls-pipe-shop-english-toffee.o: No source could be found to describe the room note.

gawith-hoggarth-co-deluxe-twist-xxx.z: Deluxe Twist XXX is a thick hand-twisted rope tobacco from Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. in Kendal. It's produced by rolling and pressing fire-cured and air-cured dark leaves together with Virginia; it's a notably thicker cut than the brand's fine ropes called Pigtail and Bogie. Before smoking, fine slices are cut from the rope, rubbed out, and usually aired for a while. On the taste side, unflavored Virginia character leads: it gives a sharp, herbal sweetness occasionally approaching dried fig. Nicotine is high, so it suits smokers accustomed to rope tobaccos and to fullness; it's heavy going for a beginner. Records indicate it's among the fullest of the rope tobaccos that carry on Gawith Hoggarth's Kendal tradition dating back to 1792.
gawith-hoggarth-co-deluxe-twist-xxx.o: A light dried-fruit sweetness mingles with the smoky, woody aroma of fire-cured leaf.

alsbo-silver.z: Alsbo is a Scandinavian-style aromatic line produced under the Orlik Tobacco Company in Denmark, but no verifiable source for content and character information on the version called Silver could be found.

john-patton-winter-heartbeat.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Patton's Winter Heartbeat blend.

tavern-tobacco-co-rose-of-zanzibar.z: A blend under the Tavern Tobacco Co. name listed as English-type; no accessible source describing its composition could be found.

missouri-meerschaum-great-dane.z: Great Dane represents the Danish-style aromatic among Missouri Meerschaum's bagged blends; it takes its name from the company's pipe model of the same name, inspired by Danish designs. Its base is a dark, sweet cavendish, and the blend is flavored with dark cherry and vanilla notes. The nicotine load is low and the smoke soft; the taste comes largely from the top-level flavoring, with the leaf character staying in the background. Suitable for those drawn to sweet, distinctly scented aromatics and for those new to the pipe.
missouri-meerschaum-great-dane.o: Leaves a sweet, cake-like aroma reminiscent of dark cherry and vanilla.

milan-tobacconists-evening-stroll.z: An aromatic listed among Milan Tobacconists' shop blends; sufficient sources describing its composition could not be found.

andreas-75th-anniversary.z: No source documenting the content and character of the blend called Andrea's 75th Anniversary could be found.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-cndid.z: This is a record in the Brazilian maker Imigrantes Fumos's Cândido Giovanella line, whose name points to aged leaf; no sufficient source to establish its content and character could be found.

john-sinclair-highland-sliced-ready-rubb.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Sinclair's Highland Sliced Ready Rubbed pipe tobacco.

tsuge-premium-pipe-tobacco-the-mystery-o.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Tsuge Premium Pipe Tobacco blend The Mystery of Autumn has been found.

milan-tobacconists-presidential.z: Presidential is among Milan Tobacconists' aromatic house blends. According to the maker's profile, hot-air-cured leaves from Zimbabwe and Malawi are combined with sweet black cavendish and soft burley; a measured fruit-and-vanilla casing is applied on top. African-origin flue-cured leaf carries a plainer, drier sweetness than classic American Virginia. Suitable for those looking for a light-bodied aromatic where the casing stands out without overpowering the leaf. Its low nicotine load makes it suited to extended smoking sessions.
milan-tobacconists-presidential.o: Leaves an aroma of vanilla and light fruit candy.

just-for-him-blue-balls.z: One of the house blends the Just For Him tobacconist prepares at its own counter; no independent source could be found on its contents or character.

wessex-premier.z: Premier is a ribbon-cut blend on the aromatic side of the Wessex series, also known according to records as the International Mixture. Black Cavendish is added to a Virginia base to provide sweetness and softness, topped with a measured flavor casing. The smoke is soft, sweetish, and low in sharpness; nicotine stays on the light side. Since the casing intensity is limited compared to heavy aromatics, the tobacco flavor isn't entirely masked. It suits those seeking a middle ground between aromatic and unflavored blends, wanting a light, all-day-smokable tobacco.
wessex-premier.o: Leaves a sweet scent, lightly fruity, reminiscent of sugared nuts.

murray-sons-co-ltd-murrays-1a-linfield.z: One of the discontinued English-type blends from the Belfast-based Murray Sons & Co factory; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition could not be found.

straus-tobacco-calumet.z: Calumet is one of the counter blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; records indicate the shop was founded in 1880 and that most of its house blends were named after Cincinnati neighborhoods and landmark buildings. Since no independent source on the blend's composition and character could be found, this record is kept at listing level only.

cobblestone-amaretto.z: Cobblestone's Amaretto blend is, per available records, a ribbon-cut, flavored mixture, though not enough independent sourcing could be found to detail its composition.

danneman-rose-of-latakia.z: No adequate sources were found documenting the composition or character of the Rose of Latakia blend registered under Dannemann.

dan-tobacco-bpk-175th-year-edition.z: A Dan Tobacco blend produced as a limited anniversary edition for a pipe club and distributed in small quantities; no adequate source documenting its composition was found.

john-aylesbury-english-mixture.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to document the contents and character of John Aylesbury's English Mixture.

ilsted-virginia-plug.z: Virginia Plug is the unflavored Virginia member of the Ilsted line. The leaf is pressed into a block and presented as a plug; it needs to be sliced and rubbed out before smoking, but in return the long pressing gives a slow, cool burn and lets the Virginia's hay-and-bread sweetness deepen. It carries no coating or flavoring. It's aimed at smokers who enjoy working with pressed leaf and want a plain Virginia taste. Records indicate it has been on the market since 2014, produced by Kopp Tobaccos in Germany; it appears to have been out of stock at retailers for a long time.
ilsted-virginia-plug.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of dry hay and baked bread.

georgetown-tobacco-curmudgeon-blend.z: Referred to as one of Georgetown Tobacco's Virginia-and-Perique-based shop blends; no verifiable sourcing describing its ratios and character could be found.
georgetown-tobacco-curmudgeon-blend.o: No record of the room aroma could be found.

sterling-tobacco-co-hunnicut.z: Hunnicut is the blend Sterling Tobacco Company classifies as "natural" (unflavored). Per the maker's description, it's built from aged and fermented leaves; using different cuts together lets the blend settle easily into the bowl. The mixed-cut structure helps air channels form naturally when packing and keeps the burn even. Since no flavoring is used, the leading flavors come from the leaf itself: Virginia's bready sweetness and burley's dry, walnut-like base. Nicotine is medium. Suited to smokers seeking an unflavored everyday blend and wanting to follow the natural taste of unflavored American leaf.
sterling-tobacco-co-hunnicut.o: Leaves a tobacco scent reminiscent of dry hay and baked bread.

robert-mcconnell-black-and-gold.z: Black & Gold is a ribbon-cut flavored blend prepared from Virginia leaf and vanilla-cased black Cavendish, with Turkish-Oriental tobacco and Louisiana Perique added. Reports place it among the brand's earliest recipes dating back to 1848, and it is one of McConnell's few flavored products. The brand is produced in Germany today. The vanilla flavoring is pronounced but does not fully mask the tobacco base; Virginia's sweetness and the plum and pepper notes from Perique show through beneath the casing, while the Oriental leaf adds a light spice layer. Nicotine is low, and the smoke is light and sweet. It suits smokers who enjoy flavored blends but still want real tobacco flavor to come through.
robert-mcconnell-black-and-gold.o: Leaves vanilla sweetness in the room along with a light plum and spice aroma.

cup-o-joes-adirondack-tiger-slices-pipe-.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the Cup O' Joes brand as Adirondack Tiger Slices Pipe Tobacco; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

gambler-mellow.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of the Gambler brand's Mellow pipe tobacco could be found.

avrasya-pipo-tutunu-chocolate-cake.z: Chocolate Cake is a pressed blend prepared by Eurasia Pipe Tobacco from Virginia, Burley, and Oriental leaf. It's presented in flake form, with a light chocolate flavoring applied to the blend. In terms of blend type it sits on the Virginia-Oriental axis. The smoke is cool and light; the chocolate note stays measured enough not to override the tobacco, leaving a light sweetness on the palate. Strength is light-to-medium, flavor intensity is medium. It's aimed at those looking for a domestically produced aromatic flake and wanting a low-nicotine blend suited to short smokes.
avrasya-pipo-tutunu-chocolate-cake.o: Leaves a light chocolate and sweet tobacco room note.

uptowns-smoke-shop-cullodens-harvest.z: One of the English-style house blends from Nashville's Uptown's Smoke Shop; production ended when the shop closed, and no source describing its composition has been found.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-cherry-and-vanil.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Cherry and Vanilla blend.

reiner-yellow-star-blend.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of Reiner Yellow Star Blend.

james-fox-provost-mixture.z: Provost Mixture is James J. Fox's black-Cavendish-forward blend. American Cavendish gives the blend body and sweetness, while select bright Virginias dilute that sweetness for a cool smoke. It's presented in a ribbon cut; opening the tin gives off an aroma reminiscent of plum, raisin, and fig. On the smoke, sweetness is felt from the start but never reaches a syrupy weight. Strength is low and the smoke is full-bodied. A profile suited to those wanting a lightly aromatic, easy-lighting blend for all-day smoking, and to those new to Cavendish-based mixtures. James J. Fox's St. James Street shop in London and its Dublin branch carry the brand's long history.
james-fox-provost-mixture.o: Leaves a dried-fruit and dark-sugar aroma with distinct plum and fig notes.

ilsted-own-mixture-cedros.z: Cedros sits at the aromatic end of the Own Mixture line prepared under the Poul Ilsted name. Ripe Virginia leaves and black Cavendish are joined by lightly pressed Burley, and the blend is coated with a cognac-and-honey flavoring. The Cavendish provides a soft sweetness and a cool smoke, while the Burley rounds out the body. It suits smokers looking for a mild, Danish-style aromatic that doesn't sting the mouth. The line was introduced in 2006, named after the Danish pipe maker Poul Ilsted, who has worked since the late 1960s; production is handled by Kopp Tobaccos in Germany.
ilsted-own-mixture-cedros.o: Leaves a warm, lightly alcoholic aroma evoking cognac alongside honeyed sweetness.

wellauer-co-erste-mischung.z: This blend from St. Gallen tobacconist Wellauer does not appear in current product listings, and no source could be found documenting its composition.
wellauer-co-erste-mischung.o: No description could be found as no source was available.

j-p-couvert-vallee-du-mont-dor.z: This is a blend under the French J.P. Couvert name, taking its name from a valley; no reliable source describing its content and character could be found.

lane-limited-andullo.z: A blend named after andullo, a tobacco fermented wrapped in palm leaf in the Dominican Republic; not enough sources could be found about its composition.

e-a-carey-soft-black-aromatic.z: This belongs to E. A. Carey's black-cavendish-based aromatic line; it does not appear on the maker's current list, and not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition.

kentuckys-best-original.z: Kentucky's Best Original is a blend produced by Farmers Tobacco Co. in Cynthiana, Kentucky, sold in large packages. Its composition includes flue-cured leaf, toasted Burley and oriental tobaccos; the manufacturer describes it as a whole-leaf mix called "KB2." The cut is a distinctly thicker ribbon than comparable products. Its character is built on Burley's toasted, nutty, earthy taste; Virginia adds a light sweetness and oriental a dry spice casing. Nicotine sits fuller than the brand's other lines. This product group is traditionally sold in cheap, large-volume packaging, so it's positioned as an economical, all-day option rather than a complex tin blend. Because of the thick cut and low moisture, airing the leaf before packing is common practice.
kentuckys-best-original.o: Leaves an earthy, cigarette-like trace with roasted nut and dry-hay scent.

john-middleton-inc-prince-alberts-cherry.z: Prince Albert's Cherry Vanilla is described as a cherry-and-vanilla-flavored blend released under the Prince Albert umbrella by the American company John Middleton; no reliable source could be found to detail the blend's contents and character.
john-middleton-inc-prince-alberts-cherry.o: Leaves a cherry and vanilla aroma.

rain-city-cigar-mild-burley.z: This is a house blend from Rain City Cigar, open since 1997 in Seattle's Georgetown neighborhood; there is not enough source material describing its composition and character.

tabakfabrik-roth-brasilianer.z: Brasilianer is one of the aromatic blends from Tabakfabrik Roth in Beinwil am See, marketed as Switzerland's only active tobacco factory. It is prepared entirely from Swiss-grown Burley and Virginia leaf; coffee, brandy, and chocolate essences are added over a honey and molasses casing. The maker describes the blend as having cigar-like, spicy, and floral facets. The factory offers the tobacco hand-filled to order in three cuts — fine (about 1.5 mm), medium (about 3.5 mm), and coarse (about 9 mm). It suits smokers looking for the cigar-toned character its name suggests, who enjoy balanced, sweetly cased aromatics where no single essence dominates.
tabakfabrik-roth-brasilianer.o: Leaves a sweet, faintly cigar-like scent leaning toward coffee and cocoa.

turk-pipo-tutunu-tabac-turc-tekel.z: Türk Pipo Tütünü is the domestic pipe tobacco produced by Turkey's Tekel monopoly since 1933, also known as Tabac Turc. It is built on Oriental leaf and presented as a flake; per its official description, the leaf is shaped by pressing with aged wooden blocks set into cast-iron molds. Along with Yayladağ Pipo Tütünü, it was one of two pipe tobaccos long produced in Turkey; records indicate production was later discontinued. Its flavoring carries a sweet line leaning toward honey and carob, with strength between light and medium and flavor intensity moderate. Since it arrives with high moisture and its leaves stuck together straight out of the pack, it needs to be separated and left to air out for proper burning. A key record for smokers curious about the Oriental leaf's characteristic sweet-spicy character and the history of domestic production.
turk-pipo-tutunu-tabac-turc-tekel.o: Leaves a sweet, honey-and-carob-leaning spicy aroma, at times reminiscent of mesir paste.

havana-house-ralph-allen.z: One of the Virginia-forward house blends from the Havana House tobacconist in England; there is not enough sourcing on the details of its composition.
havana-house-ralph-allen.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

east-india-trading-co-officers-club.z: Officer's Club is the sweet aromatic wing of the East India Trading Co. line. A ribbon-cut base of American burley, Virginia and black cavendish is given a rum and spice-forward topping. Compared to Cellar Reserve in the same line, both its body and topping intensity are more measured. It is light in nicotine, burns cool, and can be smoked all day. It suits those wanting a soft, sweet smoke and those newly moving into aromatic tobaccos; it is not aimed at smokers accustomed to unadulterated English mixtures.
east-india-trading-co-officers-club.o: Leaves a scent of sweet rum and warm spice, with a light vanilla tone lingering afterward.

nice-ash-cigars-night-cap.z: One of Nice Ash Cigars' house blends, taking its name from the day's last bowl; not enough source material describing its composition could be found. It should not be confused with the identically named Peterson blend.
nice-ash-cigars-night-cap.o: No description could be found in the records.

mac-baren-hh-old-dark-fired-plug-cut.z: The HH line is known as Mac Baren's unflavored, pressed-tobacco arm. Old Dark Fired is prepared by combining fire-cured Kentucky burley with hot-air-cured Virginia leaf and steam-pressing them; this process lets the flavors meld and settle through light fermentation. In this Plug Cut version, the tobacco is left as a whole block rather than sliced; the smoker cuts the block to whatever thickness they like. The weight is carried by the fire-cured Kentucky leaf: it gives an earthy, woody, nutty, smoky taste, with floral and tangy spice notes behind it. The Virginia leaf adds a measured sugary sweetness to this dark body. It's medium to heavy in nicotine and fullness, and burns slowly and coolly. Aimed at experienced smokers seeking an unflavored, full-bodied tobacco.
mac-baren-hh-old-dark-fired-plug-cut.o: Leaves a room note of wood-smoked meat and charred lumber.

hearth-home-sweet-smoky.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for this blend, described as American type, from the Hearth & Home brand.

cornell-diehl-bourbon-bleu.z: Bourbon Bleu takes its name from Bourbon Street, known for its blue shutters, in New Orleans's French Quarter. Bright and red Virginia leaves are joined by a measured amount of fire-cured Kentucky and long-cut perique; the mixture is combined with bourbon, then pressed and cut into a cake. Here bourbon isn't a prominent flavoring as in aromatics, but rather a binder pulling Virginia's sweetness toward oak and vanilla. Perique brings a plummy spice, Kentucky a smoky saltiness; as the bowl progresses a thin, honey-like sweetness emerges. Nicotine strength is medium. According to available records, aging brings the components closer together over time. It suits those looking for the Virginia-perique structure with a lightly boozy preparation.
cornell-diehl-bourbon-bleu.o: A smoky, spiced edge accompanies a sweet aroma reminiscent of an oak barrel.

stanwell-honey-caramel-sepia.z: Sold under the name Sepia in Stanwell's color-named aromatic series, this blend carries honey, caramel, and vanilla toppings together. Presented as a loosely cut mixture in 40-gram pouch packaging, its body consists of Virginia, burley, and black cavendish. The topping level is pronounced and keeps the blend's flavor line on the sweet side; nicotine strength stays light. Suited to those seeking a long, cool, sweet smoke and an aromatic that won't feel heavy during the day. The Stanwell brand originates in Denmark; tobacco production is carried out at facilities within the Scandinavian Tobacco Group.
stanwell-honey-caramel-sepia.o: Leaves a scent of caramelized sugar, honey, and vanilla in the room.

g-l-pease-embarcadero-fog-city-selection.z: Embarcadero is an untopped blend in G. L. Pease's Fog City Selection line, built from Virginia and Turkish Oriental leaf. After pressing, it is presented in broken-flake form. The producer states the Oriental leaf in the blend is of Izmir origin. Virginia stands out with both sweet and pronounced tobacco taste; Izmir leaf's oily, sweet character sits alongside it without overpowering it, keeping the sweet and spicy notes in balance. Records note it arrives moist from the tin; airing it thoroughly both lengthens the smoke and opens up the flavours. It suits smokers wanting to focus on the Oriental leaf up front, who smoke untopped blends.
g-l-pease-embarcadero-fog-city-selection.o: Leaves a sweetish hay and lightly oily Oriental leaf aroma.

peter-stokkebye-imperial-english.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Imperial English in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

hu-tobacco-manyara.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the Manyara blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

tabac-manil-le-petit-robin.z: One of Tabac Manil's burley-based blends; no accessible source could be found to fill out the profile.

rattray-malcolm-flake-flake-collection.z: Malcolm Flake, in Rattray's Flake Collection line, is a dark-colored, flavored flake tobacco prepared from Virginia, Burley, and Kentucky leaf. The slices are carefully cut and packed moist; its scent is reminiscent of pineapple-forward tropical fruit. It lights easily even when moist; breaking up the slices and airing them makes the burn more even. One bowl lasts a long time, and the flavor becomes more pronounced as the pipe nears the bottom. Strength is medium and flavor intensity high. It suits smokers interested in fruit-flavored blends who are used to packing flake. The Rattray name draws on the Scottish pipe-tobacco tradition; the brand's tobaccos are produced today in Germany.
rattray-malcolm-flake-flake-collection.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of pineapple and mixed tropical fruit juice.

schurch-azurite-407.z: One of Schürch's English mixtures bearing gemstone names; no sufficient source documenting its content could be found.
schurch-azurite-407.o: Recorded as leaving a smoky, woody scent.

charles-fairmorn-sterling-balkan.z: Sterling Balkan is a full-bodied English/Balkan-type blend carrying a generous share of Latakia. Despite the smoky weight of the Latakia, the smoke stays smooth and cool; a faint sweetness from the Virginia base softens the edges of the smoke. No casing is used. The blend was released under the German firm Charles Fairmorn; some of the same blends were also distributed under the F&K name. Suitable for smokers who regularly smoke Latakia-forward blends and want a full mixture reserved for evening hours.
charles-fairmorn-sterling-balkan.o: Latakia's heavy, tar-like aroma, reminiscent of tent smoke, lingers in the room for a long time.

e-a-carey-amaretto.z: E. A. Carey's Amaretto is an aromatic where cavendish-processed virginia leaf is given an almond and amaretto-liqueur-direction topping. Per the maker's page, the blend is produced in Denmark; the brand itself is a US-based pipe house operating since 1948. On the taste side, sweetness and a nutty note move together, with the tobacco's own sharpness staying in the background. It's noted as very light in nicotine; it therefore suits those seeking a long-burning, non-harsh smoke or newcomers to aromatic tobacco. Since the cut is a loose cavendish mixture, it packs easily.
e-a-carey-amaretto.o: Leaves a sweet, nutty scent evoking marzipan.

john-cotton-john-cottons-double-pressed-.z: John Cotton's Double Pressed Virginia takes its name from its production method: unflavored Virginia is first pressed into flake, fully rubbed out and aired, then re-pressed into a crumble cake. The double pressing aims to strip away the leaf's sharp edges and deepen its flavor. The brand name comes from an old tobacconist shop in Edinburgh; the line was later brought back into production in America. The resulting tobacco gives a fuller-bodied smoke than straight Virginias, with the tongue bite commonly found in Virginia leaf noticeably reduced. Sweetness gathers along honey and breadlike lines. It's noted as smokable straight from the tin without needing a long rest, suiting those who want to smoke Virginia without waiting. It took first place in the 2019 Chicago Bowl selection.
john-cotton-john-cottons-double-pressed-.o: Leaves a dark, sweet aroma reminiscent of honey and toasted bread.

war-horse-war-horse-green.z: No reliable source could be found regarding this version of the War Horse brand, so its details could not be recorded.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-coffee-ca.z: Kendal Gold is the umbrella name for the shag-cut tobacco family Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. produces in the town of Kendal in England's Lake District. The family's body is built from Brazilian- and Indian-origin, heat-cured light Virginia leaf; largely stripped of stem, it's cut into fine golden strands. The producer steams and softens the tobacco, cuts it, toasts it on a hot cylinder, and then applies the top flavoring — so the family's members are versions of the same body offered with different scents. This version adds a coffee-and-caramel flavoring to the series' Virginia body; it's listed under the name Coffee Caramel in the producer's bulk-tobacco list. The roasted-coffee scent combines with caramel's sugary roundness, with the leaf's own herbal, honeyed sweetness underneath. The fine shag cut lights quickly and resists going out; since it burns fast, slow smoking is needed. Nicotine is measured. Aimed at aromatic smokers wanting sweet and roasted aromas together.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-coffee-ca.o: Leaves an aroma of roasted coffee and burnt-sugar caramel.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-rackham.z: Rackham is one of the aromatics in Kohlhase & Kopp's Caribbean Blue line, released in a 50-gram, sailor-themed tin. The whole series is blended in Germany; the names are taken from pirates and pirate captains. The leaf structure rests on the Virginia, black cavendish and Burley trio. The casing list is one of the series' most crowded: mango, passion fruit, strawberry, mirabelle plum and cherry are used together. As a result, the blend's fruity top tone is pronounced and the tobacco taste stays in the background. The coarse cut supports a slow burn. With a low nicotine load, it suits daytime smoking and smokers seeking an intensely fruity aromatic.
kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-rackham.o: Leaves an intense fruit-syrup room note where mango, strawberry and cherry sit together.

argento-natural.z: No adequate independent source detailing the content and character of Natural, a blend from the Argentine brand Argento, could be found.
argento-natural.o: No reliable information on the room note could be found.

watch-city-cigar-4q.z: 4-Q is a house mixture Watch City Cigar of Massachusetts prepared as a counterpart to the best-selling aromatic blend in the US. According to the shop's account, instead of heavily sugar-coated leaf, pressed-cut Burley and stoved cavendish are used, aiming for a cooler, more measured aromatic smoke.
watch-city-cigar-4q.o: Leaves a soft vanilla and flavored-tobacco scent.

mclintock-armagnac.z: McLintock Armagnac is one of the brand's liqueur- and brandy-themed aromatic varieties; no verifiable source regarding its composition and cut could be found.
mclintock-armagnac.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweetish aroma reminiscent of grape brandy.

sutliff-tobacco-company-county-cork.z: County Cork is an aromatic in Sutliff's Private Stock (SPS) line. Its base contains burley and Virginia leaves, topped with Irish cream and a light whiskey sauce. The short ribbon cut lights easily and burns cool and even. On the palate, the creamy texture and whiskey's sweet-spicy trace lead; as the topping fades, burley's bready and Virginia's lightly sweet base emerge. Records note it carries a touch more fullness than many aromatics in the same line. Suited to those seeking an all-day aromatic where the topping doesn't overpower.
sutliff-tobacco-company-county-cork.o: Leaves a bready trace along with creamy sweetness and a light whiskey scent.

missouri-meerschaum-american-patriot.z: American Patriot is the latakia-containing member of the tobacco line Missouri Meerschaum, known for its corn cob pipes, launched in 2013. Blender Russ Ouellette built the line around the idea of old American-style blends designed to be smoked in a corn cob pipe; the blends' names come from the company's pipe models. This blend has an English-American construction, with a touch of bourbon note accompanying the latakia. The latakia proportion isn't high enough to count the blend as a heavy English mixture; virginia sweetness and burley's dry body can be picked out over the smoky base, and the bourbon casing is only barely perceptible. Suitable for those newly moving into latakia blends and for those looking for a smoky character in bagged tobaccos.
missouri-meerschaum-american-patriot.o: Leaves a subtle whiskey sweetness beneath the aroma of wood smoke.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-irish-sweet-che.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Brown Irish Sweet Cherry Cream blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

paul-olsen-no-333.z: For Paul Olsen's blend called No. 333, no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

cornell-diehl-xxv-reserve-dusk.z: XXV Reserve: Dusk is the dark wing of the two-blend series Cornell & Diehl prepared for Smokingpipes' twenty-fifth anniversary. The series was introduced as a joint effort between Smokingpipes founder Sykes Wilford and Cornell & Diehl head blender Jeremy Reeves, using twenty-five-year-aged Virginia leaf set aside for this project. Compared to sibling blend Dawn, Dusk is built on darker Virginia grades, 31 Farms Perique, and dark fire-cured Kentucky; it's offered in flake form. Records indicate only a one-time run of ten thousand tins was produced before it was withdrawn from the market. Its character is a Virginia-focused but full VaPer: Perique's plum-and-spice accent combines with Kentucky's smoky, dry base and mature Virginia's breadlike sweetness. Medium-high in nicotine and body, it offers an intense smoke best saved for the end of the day. It carries no added flavoring; aimed at smokers accustomed to dark Virginia blends and Perique, comfortable preparing flake. Strength stays high for beginners.
cornell-diehl-xxv-reserve-dusk.o: Leaves a scent of tart plummy tobacco and woody smoke.

edwards-peach-blossom.z: No sufficient independent sourcing could be reached to document the composition and character of Peach Blossom, a pipe tobacco from Edward's.

appalachian-customs-navel-slices.z: No adequate independent source could be found on Navel Slices, a blend from the small-scale maker Appalachian Customs.
appalachian-customs-navel-slices.o: No reliable information on the room note could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-samsun-and-delilah-20.z: The 2023 release of Samsun and Delilah is, per the maker's description, a blend built on Virginia, Oriental, and Cavendish leaf. The "Samsun" in the name refers to the Turkish-origin Oriental tobacco variety, and much of the blend's dry, herbal, lightly spiced identity comes from this leaf. The Virginia base supplies a breadlike, faintly fruity sweetness, while the black Cavendish adds a dark, cocoa-leaning, soft body. Records note that no casing is used, with the sweetness coming instead from the processed Cavendish. Nicotine runs light to moderate, and flavor intensity is measured. Suited to smokers seeking an Oriental-forward blend without Latakia.
ken-byron-ventures-samsun-and-delilah-20.o: Leaves a sweet, cocoa-leaning tobacco aroma with dry hay.

amphora-rich-aroma.z: Amphora Rich Aroma is an aromatic built on Burley and Cavendish, in a ready-rubbed cut. Despite what its name suggests, the flavoring level is medium for an aromatic product and doesn't mask the tobacco's taste. Its toppings include notes of coffee, rum, and nuts; records note this note leans more toward walnut than hazelnut. The toasted-Cavendish taste is accompanied by a coffee note; a barely perceptible bitterness from the rum is felt. Burley makes itself known late in the smoke, giving a sense of fullness. Strength is medium, flavor is above medium. It suits smokers looking for a measured-flavor blend they can smoke all day, as well as those new to the pipe.
amphora-rich-aroma.o: Leaves a sweet room note of coffee and walnut over toasted Cavendish.

sutliff-tobacco-company-crumble-kake-red.z: Sutliff Crumble Kake Red Virginia is an easily crumbled cake blend pressed solely from red Virginia leaves of different ages. Using multiple age groups together adds depth and nuance to a structure based on a single leaf type; the blend nonetheless stays a straightforward, uncomplicated pure Virginia line. Per the maker's description, flavor runs along dry hay, bread, tart fruit, and a measured sweetness. Because the cake crumbles easily, it can be packed rubbed out or in pieces. Suited to those seeking unflavored Virginia and a balanced intensity for all-day smoking.
sutliff-tobacco-company-crumble-kake-red.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay, baked bread, and tart fruit.

sutliff-tobacco-company-amaretto-777.z: 777 Amaretto is part of Sutliff's numbered bulk aromatics; burley and black cavendish are ribbon-cut blended and flavored with Italian almond liqueur, amaretto. Despite its intense scent, the flavoring is calibrated to stay measured on the palate. Body is light, nicotine is low, and tendency to bite the tongue is minimal. Suited to smokers who enjoy almond and marzipan tones and seek a pronounced room note.
sutliff-tobacco-company-amaretto-777.o: Leaves a sweet almond scent reminiscent of marzipan.

pipesandcigars-com-locked-out.z: No independent sources sufficient to complete a full profile of pipesandcigars.com's blend Locked Out could be found.

burlington-on-whyte-tobacconist-roanoke-.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named Roanoke Island under the Burlington on Whyte Tobacconist brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

the-grey-fox-old-macrae.z: Old MacRae is recorded as a blend from a small maker known as The Grey Fox; no source documenting its composition, cut, and character has been found.
the-grey-fox-old-macrae.o: No described room note has been found in records.

d-r-tobacco-raccoons-accent.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the D & R Tobacco brand as Raccoon's Accent; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

samuel-gawith-black-vanilla.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Black Vanilla, according to records a flavored blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

samuel-gawith-cigar-leaf.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Cigar Leaf, according to records a cigar-leaf-forward blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

shpc-vr-blend.z: VR Blend is one of the limited-distribution club blends prepared for the Sherlock Holmes Pipe Club; no sufficient source on its content and character could be found.
shpc-vr-blend.o: No description of the room note has been recorded in the sources.

d-r-tobacco-williams-delight.z: Referred to as an American-style blend under the Daughters & Ryan (D & R Tobacco) name; no reliable source on its composition and character was found.

pipe-club-no-3.z: No sources documenting the content or maker of the No.3 blend recorded under the Pipe Club name could be found.

samuel-gawith-navy-flake.z: Navy Flake is one of the pressed slice tobaccos Samuel Gawith produces in Kendal. Retailer records classify it in the English blend family under flake cut; its foundation is Virginia leaf, with Latakia serving as the smoky component. The "navy" tradition behind its name rests on the practice, during the age of sail, of pressing tobacco into blocks. On the smoke, Virginia's sweetness proceeds together with Latakia's woody, smoky line; because of pressing, the burn is slow, and crumbling the slices or airing them briefly before packing eases the burn. Nicotine and flavor intensity are medium. Fits flake smokers who don't want the intensity of heavy Latakia blends but seek a smoky line.
samuel-gawith-navy-flake.o: Leaves a trace combining wood smoke with sweetish Virginia scent.

radfords-scottish-blend.z: This is a pipe tobacco sold under the Radfords brand, named after the Scottish blending tradition; no verifiable source could be found on its content, cut, or character.
radfords-scottish-blend.o: There is not enough source material to describe its aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-pipe-force-episo.z: The sixth episode of the Pipe Force series centers on sweet, citrusy Virginias. Alongside them, to soften the strength and deepen the taste, stoved Katerini Orientals, dark fire-cured Kentucky, and genuine Perique from Louisiana's St. James region are added. The Perique gives a red-fruit-and-pepper accent, the Kentucky a woody body, and the Katerini a grassy background. It is aimed at smokers who like spicy Virginia-Perique-axis blends without Latakia. It was produced in limited numbers.
sutliff-tobacco-company-pipe-force-episo.o: Leaves a scent of dried fig, black pepper, and a light wood smoke.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-184.z: Wilke No. 184 is a blend obtained by working black cavendish into Turkish Yenice leaf. Yenice stands out among Oriental leaves for its tart-spicy, dry-grassy character; the cavendish layer adds a measured sweetness to this structure. The maker describes the blend as suitable for all-day smoking; body and nicotine stay moderate. It suits those seeking an Oriental-based smoke that isn't entirely dry, with a light sweetness. The blend is listed in Wilke's bulk aromatic line.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-184.o: A sweetish cavendish trace mixes into the dry-grass and spice scent.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2016.z: Christmas Cheer is the straight Virginia series that Kansas City-based McClelland released once a year, in limited numbers, from the 1980s until the company's closure in early 2018. The series' idea is to present a single Virginia batch selected from that year's harvest on its own; each year is thus considered a separate record, and the year on the tin defines the blend's identity. The 2016 release was prepared the same way, with selected matured Virginia leaf pressed into cake and tinned as broken flake. Records indicate it was prepared from a batch selected from the 2016 harvest. Unflavored Virginia character dominates the smoke: natural leaf sweetness over a bready, herbal base, with a faint tang and a lemony sharpness in the background. Nicotine dose is measured, while flavor intensity is pronounced; it burns cool when smoked slowly, but tends to bite the tongue when rushed. Since the flake's moisture can run high straight from the tin, airing it before packing is common practice. A record aimed at smokers seeking unflavored Virginia who are considering cellaring the tin; not suitable for those expecting an aromatic.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2016.o: A tangy, sharp trace characteristic of McClelland tins mixes into an aroma of dry hay and toasted bread.

cornell-diehl-billy-budd-blonde.z: Billy Budd Blonde is a sweeter variation Cornell & Diehl prepared starting from its Billy Budd blend. It contains light-colored Virginia flake, white burley, chopped cigar leaf, and a small amount of perique; it is presented as a ribbon cut. Cigar leaf gives the blend an earthy, cocoa-like, nutty character along with a pronounced nicotine load; Virginia's sweetness and perique keep the spice in balance. It suits smokers accustomed to cigars who are looking for a similar body in a pipe; because nicotine runs high, it can be demanding to smoke on an empty stomach.
cornell-diehl-billy-budd-blonde.o: Leaves an earthy, dry-leaf aroma reminiscent of cigar smoke.

w-d-h-o-wills-capstan-mild-navy-cut.z: Capstan is a family of flakes pressed from unflavored Virginia leaves, launched by Bristol-based W.D. & H.O. Wills more than a century ago. Mild Navy Cut represents the softer wing of this family and over time became identified with the version known by its "blue" label; during pressing, the leaf's own sugars come forward, with no outside flavoring casing added. Its character stays tied to the plain-Virginia tradition: a bready, grassy, lightly fruity sweetness comes together with a measured nicotine load. Since it arrives as flake, the leaf needs to be rubbed out or folded before packing; smoked slowly, it holds its balance. This is a suitable starting point for smokers wanting to acclimate to unflavored Virginia's palate or seeking a plain, long-lasting everyday tobacco.
w-d-h-o-wills-capstan-mild-navy-cut.o: Leaves a subtle scent carrying dry grass and light bready sweetness.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-bogie-sweet-rum.z: Brown Bogie is a traditional Kendal product made by twisting dark fire-cured and air-cured leaf into rope form; this version applies a rum bowl note to the rope. The rope is sliced coin-thin and rubbed out for smoking. According to sources, alongside the black twist versions, the brown twist is also considered high in nicotine, and the rum sweetness doesn't fully mask the weight of the leaf. The taste is spicy, oily, and earthy; the rum only becomes distinct in the second half of the bowl. In terms of nicotine it sits at the very top end of pipe tobaccos, so it is not suited to smoking on an empty stomach or a fast smoke. It suits an experienced smoker who knows how to work with rope tobacco and doesn't shy away from strength; it is a direct continuation of the old Kendal tradition of sailors cutting and chewing pieces off a rope.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-bogie-sweet-rum.o: A heavy woodsmoke is mixed with a sweet, syrupy rum aroma.

mcclelland-dominican-glory.z: Dominican Glory is a blend in which McClelland combines Dominican Republic cigar leaf with matured red Virginia. The mixture is pressed into cakes; after resting to let the oils among the leaves meld, the cakes are sliced into flake. The cigar leaf gives the blend an earthy, spicy, full-bodied character, while the Virginia provides a sweet base; there's no added flavoring. Nicotine dose is high, as expected for cigar-leaf blends, so it's not suited to smoking on an empty stomach or at a fast pace. A record for smokers seeking cigar taste in a pipe. Discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-dominican-glory.o: Leaves a dark, earthy, and spicy aroma reminiscent of cigar smoke.

gatlin-burlier-danish-luxury.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of the Gatlin brand's Burlier-Danish Luxury pipe tobacco could be found.

leonard-dingler-ltd-nineteen-ofour-origi.z: Not enough sources could be found about Leonard Dingler's Nineteen O'Four Original blend.

d-r-tobacco-don-giovanni-sigaro.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the D & R Tobacco brand as Don Giovanni Sigaro; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

vauen-jubilaums-jubilee-edition.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Vauen blend called Jubiläums [Jubilee] Edition has been found.
vauen-jubilaums-jubilee-edition.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

g-l-pease-chelsea-morning.z: Chelsea Morning is a traditionally structured blend in G. L. Pease's Old London Series. Light and red Virginia leaves build the base; Oriental leaf adds spice, while a very small amount of Cyprus latakia and a touch of perique add fine depth in the background. Since the latakia proportion is kept low, the blend sits at the light end of the smoky mixtures. It suits an early smoke in the day, or those wanting a light English mixture and smokers newly approaching latakia.
g-l-pease-chelsea-morning.o: Leaves a fine aroma mixing light woodsmoke and dry grass.

st-basils-tobacco-peter-the-great.z: Referred to as St. Basil's Tobacco's unusual aromatic that adds a high proportion of perique to a maple-syrup-flavored black cavendish base; since sufficient independent sources confirming the blend could not be found, this record is left incomplete.
st-basils-tobacco-peter-the-great.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet scent reminiscent of maple syrup.

planta-cellini-forte.z: Planta Cellini Forte is a pipe tobacco blend for which there is not enough independent source material.
planta-cellini-forte.o: Not enough records could be found on the room note.

peretti-blend-no-101.z: This is one of Peretti's numbered Burley blends and remains in production; records indicate the hundred-series numbers date to the company's early ledgers, though this blend's composition has not been published.

cornell-diehl-ridin-the-raid.z: A blend, no longer in Cornell & Diehl's current catalogue, referred to as a straight Virginia; no adequate source documenting its composition was found.
cornell-diehl-ridin-the-raid.o: No adequate information for a description could be found in records.

burlington-on-whyte-tobacconist-black-ch.z: Black Cherry is one of the house blends sold in bulk by Burlington on Whyte, a tobacconist located on Whyte Avenue in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada; from its name and the shop's catalog description it can be understood to be a cherry-flavored, cavendish-forward mixture. The entry has been left incomplete as no independent source giving a detailed account of the blend's content and smoking character could be found.

tobacco-world-light-and-mild.z: Tobacco World is a tobacconist in Wisconsin that prepares its own aromatic and English-style blends. The light blend called Light and Mild does not appear on the shop's current list, and no verifiable information on its composition has been found.
tobacco-world-light-and-mild.o: No source describing its aroma has been found.

samuel-gawith-kendal-cream-deluxe-flake.z: Kendal Cream Deluxe Flake, now labeled KC Deluxe Flake, is Samuel Gawith's medium-intensity flake bringing together sweet Virginia and Burley leaf. The slices are not tightly pressed, so they crumble easily by hand and pack effortlessly. As with most Lakeland blends, it is flavored by the producer with an essence blend, though the flavor level is more measured than the brand's heavier aromatics like Grousemoor. On the smoke, Burley's creamy, nutty body is balanced by Virginia's sweetness; the flavor line stays mild, while nicotine fullness becomes noticeable toward the middle of the bowl. Fits smokers wanting to know the Lakeland style in a light dose or seeking a crumbly flake.
samuel-gawith-kendal-cream-deluxe-flake.o: Leaves a creamy, lightly floral, and nutty scent.

sutliff-tobacco-company-tropical-sunset-.z: 706 Tropical Sunset is a mango-cased blend in Sutliff's bulk aromatic line. The base is built from a combination of burley, Virginia, and black cavendish leaf; the cut is ribbon. The casing gives a fruity sweetness leaning toward mango and tangerine; alongside this sweetness there is a light tartness and a spicy liveliness. It isn't a sugary structure — the tobacco's own taste can be sensed beneath the fruit. Nicotine is on the light side. It suits smokers looking for a fruity but not overly sugary aromatic.
sutliff-tobacco-company-tropical-sunset-.o: Leaves a floral, lightly tart scent reminiscent of mango and tangerine peel.

lewis-tobacco-black-bird.z: Black Bird is an aromatic pipe blend referred to under the Lewis Tobacco name; no reliable source could be found about its manufacturer, composition or character.
lewis-tobacco-black-bird.o: Leaves a sweetish aromatic room note.

smokers-paradise-clearwater-black-knight.z: One of the shop blends from the Smoker's Paradise tobacconist in Clearwater; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found.

imperial-tobacco-group-plc-coopvaert.z: Coopvaert is a pipe tobacco built on an old recipe tied to the classic Dutch "baai" tradition. The product comes from the tobacco line known in the Netherlands under the Douwe Egberts name; this line is today under the London-based Imperial Tobacco Group umbrella, with production continuing in the Netherlands. The blend uses natural Virginia along with Java and Maryland leaves, with American Burley added to slow the burn. Because the tobacco is presented in fine ribbons in an air-permeable pouch, it feels dry; despite this it smokes cool. The taste shows a light sweetness alongside a spicy, cigar-like earthiness. It's suited to smoking in wide-bowled pipes; it's aimed at those looking for an unflavored, plain, traditional Dutch-style blend.
imperial-tobacco-group-plc-coopvaert.o: Leaves an earthy aroma reminiscent of dry leaf and a light cigar.

hearth-home-country-lane.z: A Virginia and Burley based Hearth & Home blend; there is not enough independent sourcing available for it.
hearth-home-country-lane.o: Leaves a bready, nutty tobacco aroma.

old-holborn-yellow.z: Old Holborn Yellow is the yellow-pack version of the English-rooted Old Holborn line. It's prepared from golden Virginia leaf in a very fine shag cut; its moisture is high and its color dark. Compared to the line's better-known green-pack version, it's described as fuller in nicotine and more pronouncedly flavored, with a wine-like topping direction. The fine cut and high moisture require careful packing and a slow pace in a pipe. Its taste is intense while its harshness on the throat stays measured relative to its nicotine level. A marked divergence is noted between the topping aroma on opening the pack and the taste on the smoke. It's a product aimed at those seeking a full, dominant-character everyday tobacco with limited flavoring; because its room note is heavy, it lingers a long time indoors.
old-holborn-yellow.o: Leaves a heavy scent, sharp and smoky, recalling burnt charcoal.

mccranies-hells-gate.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found on Hell's Gate, one of McCranie's Pipe Shop's house blends.
mccranies-hells-gate.o: No reliable description of the aroma could be found.

schurch-tuli-bc.z: Tuli (BC), signed by Schürch, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

erik-stokkebye-evening-flake.z: Evening Flake is an unadulterated flake prepared by adding a measure of perique to golden virginia leaves. The mixture is left to warm-press for a week and then sliced into flake; this process lets the leaves' flavors meld together. On the smoke, virginia's dry-grass and citrus-peel echoes are joined by a darker, fruitier intensity leaning toward plum and fig, occasionally approaching cocoa. The perique share stands out more here than in similar blends in the series. It suits smokers seeking a long, slow evening bowl, familiar with the VaPer palate.
erik-stokkebye-evening-flake.o: Leaves a slightly spicy scent reminiscent of dry grass and dark fruit preserve.

peretti-black-virginia.z: A house blend L.J. Peretti lists in its cavendish group, apparently based on darkened Virginia leaf judging by its name; no published source describing its flavoring and character could be found.

ravenwood-fine-provisions-leaves-of-athe.z: Leaves of Athelas is a blend in the Ravenwood Fine Provisions line made entirely of Oriental leaf; it is built by bringing together different Oriental classes and contains neither Latakia nor Virginia. The blender's description lists soft herbal notes, tea, cedar, and earth as prominent; the smoke is cool with an oily texture and carries light traces reminiscent of olive oil and incense. There is no flavoring. Being built on a single leaf type, its nuances become clearer with slow smoking; it is designed for experienced smokers who want to get to know Oriental leaf's own character.
ravenwood-fine-provisions-leaves-of-athe.o: Leaves aromas reminiscent of dry hay, tea leaf, and incense.

gatlin-burlier-mountain-vine-wine.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of the Gatlin brand's Burlier-Mountain Vine Wine pipe tobacco could be found.

house-of-calabash-seven-of-nine.z: Records indicate this is a House of Calabash blend built on Virginia and Perique with a small proportion of Turkish tobacco added, stated to use no propylene glycol; no sufficient source verifying the details could be found.

former-private-blend.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Former's Private Blend; records place it in the Virginia-heavy class.

mcclelland-venture-forth.z: No sufficient independent source describing the contents and character of the McClelland-branded Venture Forth blend could be found.

ashton-type-4.z: Ashton Type 4 is referred to as a Virginia-based blend in the brand's numbered series; no adequate independent source verifying its content and character could be found.
ashton-type-4.o: According to records, not enough information could be found to describe it.

house-of-windsor-bond-street.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for House of Windsor's Bond Street blend, so its content and character could not be recorded.

doctor-pipe-mixture-888.z: This is an unadulterated mixture built from golden Virginia, Oriental leaves, Latakia and Perique. Per sources, the Oriental leaf is measured to stay ahead of the Latakia; a taste axis leaning toward dry grass and citrus is described, along with a heavily smoky body.
doctor-pipe-mixture-888.o: A dry-grass and citrus-peel scent is accompanied by soot.

cult-conspiracy-theory.z: This blend in the Cult series is recorded under the name Conspiracy and was released in the mid-2010s. A base of golden Virginia, black Cavendish, Burley, and Cyprus Latakia is topped with a vanilla and clover-honey-style flavoring. It's described as a transitional blend sitting between aromatic and English mixture, carrying traces of both styles. The smoke moves over a creamy, sweet base; Latakia's smoke isn't dominant, sitting instead as a thin layer balancing the sweetness. Body is medium, and it's not demanding in nicotine. Suited to smokers wanting to move from aromatics into Latakia blends, or looking for a sweet top note in smoky tobaccos. Since the brand has withdrawn from distribution, the product isn't regularly available today.
cult-conspiracy-theory.o: Leaves a scent where sweet, vanilla-laced smoke mingles with a light smokiness.

mcclelland-no-710-colombian-mocha.z: No. 710 Colombian Mocha is a blend in McClelland's bulk aromatic line. Per the maker's description, a mild, medium-bodied mixture of black Cavendish and Virginia leaves is flavored with dark chocolate and Colombian coffee aroma. The brand named some of its bulk aromatics after celestial bodies. In the smoke, coffee and cocoa notes are pronounced in the aroma, while the taste on the palate is balanced by the Cavendish's mild sweetness. Nicotine dose is low and it lights easily. A blend meant for smokers seeking aromatic tobacco who like sweet-toasted profiles, and for those new to the pipe. Discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-no-710-colombian-mocha.o: Leaves an aroma of dark chocolate and freshly brewed coffee.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-late-eveni.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the content and character of Match Late Evening, one of the bulk blends from Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company, could be found.

pauls-pipe-shop-late-night-smoke.z: Late Night Smoke is referred to as an English-style mixture among Paul's Pipe Shop's house blends; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.
pauls-pipe-shop-late-night-smoke.o: No source could be found to describe the room note.

gawith-hoggarth-co-no-7-broken-flake.z: No. 7 Broken Flake is built by adding a small amount of light flue-cured leaf to sun- and wood-fire-cured Virginias. Since the pressed slab is sliced and then broken up for sale, the cut carries a look somewhere between flake and ribbon; golden pieces show against the dark base. The taste is earthy, smoky, and dry; it carries no essence. Nicotine is high. Suited to smokers seeking the pressed form of the same house's Kendal No.7 blend, who love dark, full-bodied Virginia.
gawith-hoggarth-co-no-7-broken-flake.o: Leaves a dark tobacco aroma reminiscent of wood smoke and dry leather.

charatan-royal-ensign-mixture.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the British pipe maker Charatan.

4noggins-essence-of-vermont.z: Essence of Vermont is among 4noggins' blends referencing the state of Vermont. It's based on a broad-cut Burley leaf flavored with maple essence, to which St. James Parish Perique is added, lending a sweetness and spicy dried-fruit note similar to aged tobaccos. Burley's earthy, nutty character and Perique's peppery-plum edge are balanced so as not to overwhelm the maple topping; the blend isn't a full aromatic but stands as an American style carrying a topping. It suits those looking for a moderately sweetened, full-bodied Burley.
4noggins-essence-of-vermont.o: Leaves a maple-syrup and toasted-nut aroma with a faint spicy dried-fruit trace behind it.

rain-city-cigar-vanilla.z: This is a house blend from Rain City Cigar, open since 1997 in Seattle's Georgetown neighborhood; there is not enough source material describing its composition and character.

missouri-meerschaum-orchard-mist-2022.z: No verifiable composition information could be found for Missouri Meerschaum's 2022 Orchard Mist release.

clan-shaw-italiano.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Italiano.

brigadier-black-gettysburg.z: Gettysburg is a fruit-cased aromatic in the Brigadier Black line. A light fresh-peach casing is applied over a combination of nutty burley and bright, tart Virginia leaf. Virginia gives the blend a bright, lightly tart sweetness, while burley provides a dry, earthy body; the casing sits atop this base as a fine fruit layer. Nicotine is low, flavor medium. A blend aimed at those seeking a drier, more tobacco-forward fruity profile rather than heavily syrupy aromatics.
brigadier-black-gettysburg.o: Leaves a lightly fruity, sweet aroma reminiscent of fresh peach skin.

mcclelland-no-x-90-american-cavendish-bu.z: One of McClelland's X-series bulk Burley entries, discontinued when the firm closed in 2018; no sufficient source documenting its contents and character could be found.

seattle-pipe-club-pioneer-square.z: Pioneer Square is a mild aromatic named after Seattle's historic square. A base obtained by cavendish-processing golden Virginia leaves preserves the leaf's own bright sweetness; floral honey and vanilla notes are added on top. It is ribbon cut. Nicotine and flavor intensity are kept low, the smoke stays cool and mild. The casing is noticeable but does not reach a heavy syrupy structure. Suited to newcomers to the pipe and to those seeking a light, sweet, low-nicotine daily blend.
seattle-pipe-club-pioneer-square.o: Leaves a scent of floral honey and soft vanilla, with the tobacco scent staying in the background.

dan-tobacco-china-japan-ready-rubbed.z: Referred to as one of Dan Tobacco's ready-rubbed aromatic blends; no adequate independent source documenting its composition was found.

cherokee-mellow-blend.z: The entry has been left incomplete as no reliable source could be found for Cherokee's Mellow Blend blend.

hearth-home-knotty-pine.z: Knotty Pine is the only English mixture in Hearth & Home's Slow-Aged series. Tobacco composed of Latakia, Virginia, Oriental, and some Burley for body is first cut into broken flake, then re-pressed into a crumble cake and left in the press for a month to let the leaves mature. This process melds the blend's flavors together and softens and settles Latakia's smoky, resinous character. Aimed at smokers accustomed to hand-crumbling cake tobacco who love dark, smoky mixtures; it falls into the class of heavier-bodied recipes favored in cooler seasons.
hearth-home-knotty-pine.o: Leaves a smoky, resinous aroma reminiscent of campfire smoke.

sutliff-tobacco-company-black-cherry-b23.z: Black Cherry B23 is a cherry-flavored blend in Sutliff's bulk "B" line. Its structure relies on Virginia leaves placed over a roasted black cavendish base; the cherry topping is kept measured, its fruit flavor not pushed to a syrupy intensity. The cavendish base slows the burn and gives the tobacco a soft sweetness; Virginia establishes a light tart balance behind it. Nicotine is low, with little tendency to bite the tongue. Cherry aromatics have a long tradition in pipe tobacco, and B23 is a bulk-sold, everyday-use example of that tradition. It's ribbon cut.
sutliff-tobacco-company-black-cherry-b23.o: Leaves a scent of sweet cherry and sugared fruit.

radfords-blend-no-55-wild-honey.z: No source could be found documenting the content and flavoring of Blend No. 55 Wild Honey, part of Radfords' numbered blend series.
radfords-blend-no-55-wild-honey.o: No information describing the room note could be found in available records.

samuel-gawith-lakeland-mixed.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Lakeland Mixed, according to records a Virginia-forward blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

john-aylesbury-mini-cut.z: Mini Cut is an aromatic blend produced for John Aylesbury by Kopp Tobaccos, known for its fine-grained cut. Its composition includes Burley, bright Virginia, and black Cavendish; its casing is vanilla-based. It's offered in 50- and 150-gram packages. The fine-grained cut makes the tobacco easy to pack into a pipe and gives a cool burn. Because the vanilla casing is kept measured, its sweetness doesn't overwhelm the tobacco taste. Suited to smokers seeking a light-bodied aromatic for all-day smoking who are used to working with finely cut tobaccos.
john-aylesbury-mini-cut.o: Leaves a light vanilla and sweet tobacco aroma.

shockoe-valley-tobaccos-red-virginia-cak.z: Recorded as a Shockoe Valley Tobaccos product in which red Virginia leaf is pressed into a cake; no independent source describing the production details and character could be found.
shockoe-valley-tobaccos-red-virginia-cak.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

peretti-holiday-1951.z: Holiday 1951 is a limited reissue of Bob Peretti's original 1951 Yuletide blend. Per the maker's account, burley, Virginia, and Turkish leaf are joined by a lightly sweet aromatic component that adds both body and mellowness to the blend. It is a classic American-style construction: a burley base, Virginia's sweetness, and the oriental's dry spice work together. The topping is not heavy enough to create a pronounced aromatic impression. It's aimed at smokers interested in the firm's history and fond of moderately sweetened American blends.
peretti-holiday-1951.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly spiced scent of baked bread.

century-buttered-rum.z: A blend in the Century line known for a buttered-rum aroma; no sufficient source could be found to document its content.

mostex-stanislaw-balkan-latakia.z: Balkan Latakia is an unflavored, ribbon-cut latakia mixture offered under the Stanislaw brand by Czech maker Mostex. Records indicate the blend is roughly forty percent latakia and ten percent dark Kentucky; the remainder consists of select virginia and oriental tobaccos along with a very small amount of Louisiana perique. The high latakia proportion gives the blend a smoky, full body; Kentucky raises the nicotine load, while perique adds a spicy sharpness at the finish. Aimed at those accustomed to heavy Balkan mixtures who are looking for an intense, unsauced smoke.
mostex-stanislaw-balkan-latakia.o: Leaves an intense aroma of soot, tar, and burnt wood.

hearth-home-ambassadors-blend.z: Ambassador's Blend is a Latakia-forward English mixture in Hearth & Home's Signature series. According to the maker's description, the blend was designed as a counterpart to Dunhill's richer Latakia mixtures. In its composition, Latakia sits just ahead of Virginia, while Oriental leaf forms the supporting layer. The smoke carries notes of wood smoke, leather, toasted bread, and cream, alongside tart-fruit and lemon-peel traces from the Oriental leaf; no top note is used. Body sits between medium and full. Suited to smokers familiar with classic English mixtures who want a blend where the Latakia dose isn't kept low but doesn't override spice and Virginia sweetness either.
hearth-home-ambassadors-blend.o: Leaves a heavy aroma of wood smoke, leather, and toasted bread.

paul-olsen-no-55.z: One of the burley-forward blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-ruins-of-.z: There is not enough independent documentation on The Country Squire Tobacconist pipe tobacco called Ruins of Windsor to record the blend's composition and character.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-pigtail-sweet-r.z: This is the sugared rum version of Brown Pigtail. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. produces its rope by twisting fire-cured leaves; in this product the rope is given rum flavouring together with invert sugars, so the sweetness stands out a notch more than the plain rum version. Over time the brand has also listed this tobacco under names like "S Type Brown Twist RM." Preparation is the same as with other ropes: a thin slice, thorough rubbing, and airing before filling. In terms of nicotine it is above medium. It is aimed at those wanting a strong rope body together with a sweet top note.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-pigtail-sweet-r.o: Leaves a molasses and rum sweetness with smoky tobacco underneath.

cornell-diehl-081-balkan.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Cornell & Diehl blend #081 Balkan.

mac-baren-mixture-scottish-blend.z: Mixture: Scottish Blend, per the product description, was introduced in 1958 and is prepared from over thirty-five leaves sourced from different regions of the world. It contains Virginia, Burley, and Cavendish; the cut is mixed, made up mostly of ready-rubbed and broken flake pieces. An intense honey-forward topping is applied over the blend. The sharp, faintly bitter base typical of Scottish-type blends is pronounced in this product; the honey topping is used to balance that sharpness. The firmness felt in the mouth on the first light eases as the smoke progresses, letting the honey sweetness come forward. Since flavor intensity is high, the natural leaf taste stays in the background; toward the bottom, body and nicotine from the Burley become pronounced. A blend aimed at those seeking an intensely flavored, full-bodied smoke.
mac-baren-mixture-scottish-blend.o: A sharp, heavily sweet honey aroma mixes with a burnt tobacco tone.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-tc-black-gold.z: TC Black & Gold is a blend in Wilke Pipe Tobacco's bulk aromatic series. According to the maker's recipe, a small amount of Latakia is added over Burley and Virginia leaf, finished with a casing that leaves a subtle vanilla note. This construction sets the blend apart from straightforward aromatics: sweetness stays on the surface, while the tobacco's own bready, woody base comes forward. Wilke is a blending house founded in New York in the late 19th century and now operating out of Fall River, Massachusetts. TC Black & Gold offers a middle ground for smokers wanting a lightly smoky backdrop while avoiding heavy aromatics, and for those wanting to try Latakia for the first time in a small dose. Nicotine strength is moderate, and it suits all-day smoking.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-tc-black-gold.o: Leaves a subtle vanilla sweetness over a lightly smoky wood scent.

peretti-rctr.z: One of the house blends from L. J. Peretti's shop in Boston; it appears under the English blends heading in the maker's listing. No published description of the blend's composition and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.

newminster-no-6-vanilla-delight.z: Newminster No. 6 Vanilla Delight is a classic Danish-style Cavendish blend built from bright Virginia, soft Burley, and sweet black Cavendish. The blend is finished with a measured, smooth vanilla flavoring. It is sold in bulk and is ribbon cut. Nicotine is low and the smoke is soft; the vanilla note is kept from overpowering the tobacco. Suitable for smokers looking for a classic vanilla aromatic.
newminster-no-6-vanilla-delight.o: Leaves a soft, creamy vanilla aroma in the room.

nat-sherman-584-uptown-highstone.z: Reportedly a Nat Sherman house blend built from Burley and Virginia, light in body and very lightly flavored; no independent source giving further detail could be found.

lane-limited-coco-creme.z: A Lane aromatic whose name points to a cocoa or coconut-and-cream note; not enough sources could be found to document its contents.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-twist-sweet-rum.z: This is the rum-topped version of brown twist; the brand once listed it under the name S Type Brown Twist RM. Dark leaves are twisted into rope form, and the rum topping adds sweetness to the tobacco. According to sources, the rum note stays in the background in the first half and becomes noticeable as the bowl progresses; nicotine sits somewhere between medium and strong. Rubbing out the slices and airing them for a while regulates the burn, since rope tobacco generally arrives moist. The taste sits atop an earthy, spicy base; the rum leaves a sweet edge rather than masking that base. It suits someone accustomed to working with rope tobacco who wants a flavoured but heavy-bodied smoke.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-twist-sweet-rum.o: A sweet rum and molasses aroma is accompanied by dark woodsmoke.

tobacco-lane-harvest-moon.z: One of the house blends from the tobacconist Tobacco Lane; no verifiable source on its composition and character has been found.
tobacco-lane-harvest-moon.o: No source describing its aroma has been found.

paul-olsen-tudor.z: One of the house blends from the Paul Olsen house; no independent source describing its composition could be found.

mac-baren-cube.z: Cube is a Danish-style aromatic bringing together Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish leaves. The blend contains both pressed and loose-cut tobaccos; this mixed structure eases packing and gives a slow, cool burn. In the taste, a deep, sweet, and fruity line stands out; caramel and toasted-sugar sides are pronounced. Burley gives the blend a creamy body, while nicotine level stays measured. A product aimed at those seeking a sweet aromatic and wanting a long smoking time.
mac-baren-cube.o: Leaves an aroma leaning toward caramel, toasted sugar, and sweet fruit.

smokers-haven-deelicious.z: An American-style blend signed by Smokers' Haven; no reliable source describing its composition could be found.
