cobblestone-cafe-hot-chocolate.z: Cobblestone's Cafe Hot Chocolate blend is, per available records, a ribbon-cut, flavored mixture, though not enough independent sourcing could be found to detail its composition.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-crown-achi.z: Crown Achievement Match is a Virginia-burley mixture in Sutliff's Match line based on the old Crown Achievement blend. It carries a very light bourbon casing that doesn't overshadow the burley and Virginia leaf; in that sense it counts more as a lightly cased everyday blend than a true aromatic. Its body ranges from light to medium, it burns cool, and gives a consistent taste through the bowl. Not leaving sediment and not drifting into cigarette-like notes give it a suitability for long sessions. It was designed for those looking for a plain, balanced American blend to smoke all day. Production ended with Sutliff's closure.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-crown-achi.o: Leaves a scent of toasted nuts and bready tobacco alongside a faint whisky sweetness.

mac-baren-st-bruno-flake.z: St. Bruno is an English classic created by Thomas Ogden in Liverpool in the 1890s. Its production was taken over by Mac Baren starting in 2006, and the brand transferred fully to this company in 2015. The blend's body is built by mild Virginia leaves and dark-fire-cured Kentucky; the mixture is steam-pressed and cut into thin slices. The topping applied over it is a floral-and-fruit sauce tied to English Lakeland tradition; rose geranium and tonka are two well-known components of this style. In the smoke, the flavoring's floral side and Kentucky's smoky, dry body sit side by side; the balance between the two is the blend's defining trait. The flake burns slow and cool, giving a long smoke; the taste intensifies especially past the middle of the bowl. Nicotine load isn't to be taken lightly. A historical reference point for smokers interested in the Lakeland style and pressed English tobaccos.
mac-baren-st-bruno-flake.o: Leaves a trace where a floral, soap-like aroma sits alongside a smoky leaf aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-whiskey-twist.z: Sweet Whiskey Twist is a product in Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s traditional rope (twist) line. Stoved Virginia leaf is hand-twisted into rope form, then flavored with whiskey. Stoving deepens Virginia's natural sugars, giving the leaf a dark color and a bready depth; the whiskey topping layers a grainy, lightly barrel-toned sweetness on top of that. The rope is sold either pre-sliced or whole, letting the smoker cut their own thickness when bought whole. Despite the sweetness in its name, the smoke is full and hearty: since pressing and twisting compress the leaf, the smoke is dense and nicotine runs high. As is typical for rope tobaccos, the slices need to be thoroughly rubbed out and aired for a while, or lighting becomes difficult. Suited to those wanting a topped aromatic where the tobacco taste stays in front rather than tipping into candy, and to smokers accustomed to strong smokes.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-whiskey-twist.o: Leaves a sweet, spirit-touched aroma reminiscent of grain and barrel, along with dark tobacco smoke.

davids-blend-burly-blend.z: This is a burley-forward shop blend from David's Fine Tobaccos; no verifiable description of its composition and character could be found.

vauen-n5-oxford-blend.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Vauen pipe tobacco called N°5 Oxford Blend to record the blend's composition and character.

ravenwood-fine-provisions-vanilla-deku-n.z: This is a vanilla aromatic blend Ravenwood Fine Provisions produces in small batches, described by the seller as a tribute to Mac Baren Vanilla Roll Cake; no independent source could be found on its content or cut.

tinder-box-buttered-rum.z: Buttered Rum is an aromatic house blend from Tinder Box combining golden Virginia leaves with soft white Burley. The casing follows the buttered-rum drink its name suggests, leaving a spicy tail. Its body is light, yet flavor intensity is not low; on retrohale, Burley's nutty softness comes through. Nicotine load is low, so it can be smoked all day. Suited to smokers who enjoy sweet aromatics and want a blend that doesn't bite the tongue.
tinder-box-buttered-rum.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of buttered rum and warm spice.

cornell-diehl-pennington-gap.z: Pennington Gap is a bourbon-flavored mixture Cornell & Diehl built on cube-cut Burley. Per the maker's listing, nutty Kentucky cube-cut Burley is combined with dark black Cavendish, Louisiana Perique is added, and the blend is finished with bourbon. The maker describes the blend as an American mixture with a southern accent. The cube cut supports a slow, cool burn; Perique adds a spicy sharpness, and bourbon a sweetness evoking oak and caramel. The casing is pronounced but doesn't mask the leaf's taste. Suited to smokers looking for a middle ground between cased blends and unflavored Burley mixtures.
cornell-diehl-pennington-gap.o: Leaves a sweet, nutty tobacco note mingling with a bourbon scent reminiscent of an oak barrel.

low-country-pipe-cigar-edisto.z: One of the house blends of South Carolina-based Low Country Pipe & Cigar; described as pure Virginia, but not enough sources could be found to describe its character.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-maple-leaf.z: Maple Leaf is a Boswell aromatic where the maple flavor named in its title comes to the fore. Per the manufacturer's description, maple's soft, full taste sits at the blend's center; a small vanilla touch added to it does not replace the maple aroma, only gives it an extra layer. Thanks to its cavendish-forward structure, nicotine load is low and the burn is cool. Since the flavor casing is pronounced, it appeals more to smokers who lean toward sweet, scented mixtures than to those seeking the tobacco leaf's own taste. It is one of Boswell's long-standing aromatics in the catalog.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-maple-leaf.o: Leaves a maple syrup and light vanilla aroma.

john-aylesbury-mixture-no-777.z: 777 is the middle step in John Aylesbury's numbered aromatic series. Its composition includes twice-fermented Virginia and Burley leaf; it's described as a dark, fruit-forward blend with a pineapple note standing out in its casing. It's offered in 50- and 200-gram packages, supplied through Kopp Tobaccos. The double fermentation gives the smoke smoothness and a dark sweetness; the Burley share gives a more pronounced body than 666. Suited to smokers who enjoy fruity aromatics and want a medium-bodied everyday tobacco.
john-aylesbury-mixture-no-777.o: Leaves a fruity, sweet aroma reminiscent of pineapple.

alsbo-cherry-ruby.z: Alsbo Cherry is a cherry-flavored Danish blend later sold under the name Ruby. It's built from Virginia and Burley leaf combined with a light Cavendish base; the top layer leans toward cherry. The cherry note has a fresh, tangy character rather than a syrupy candy one, so the smoke proceeds without weighing heavy. Strength and flavor intensity are low. It suits those getting acquainted with fruit-flavored blends and those looking for a light cherry aromatic.
alsbo-cherry-ruby.o: Leaves a fresh, tangy cherry room note, closer to fruit than candy.

kleinlagel-maiway.z: Maiway is an aromatic pipe tobacco from the German house Kleinlagel, offered in a 50-gram tin. Its body is built from Virginia leaves; the casing the blend's name comes from is an essence of woodruff, called Waldmeister in German. Since this casing gives a vanilla-like sweet, herbaceous tone, the blend is shown in retailer records as light in strength and sweetish in taste. The cut is a fine strand suited to packing directly from the tin, requiring no preparation. Since nicotine load is low, it suits all-day smoking and fits the roster of those new to aromatic tobacco. Records indicate the blend has been delisted from production and is now seen only in old stock.
kleinlagel-maiway.o: Leaves a scent reminiscent of freshly cut grass and sweet woodruff syrup.

ken-byron-ventures-re-animated-english.z: One of the limited-run English-type blends Ken Byron Ventures released; not enough reliable sources could be found to document its content and character.

g-l-pease-charing-cross.z: Charing Cross is a G. L. Pease blend built in the traditional Balkan style. Selected Virginia leaves are enriched with a generous measure of smoky Cyprus latakia, with a spicy layer of Oriental tobaccos added on top. According to the producer's own comparison, the Orientals in this blend are sharper and more upfront than in Abingdon; the result is a full-bodied, dark, layered smoke. It is aimed at smokers accustomed to classic latakia-heavy mixtures who want a full-bodied tobacco.
g-l-pease-charing-cross.o: Leaves an aroma of heavy woodsmoke and spiced leather.

woodlands-fine-cigars-mr-henry.z: This is one of the bulk house blends sold by Woodlands Fine Cigars, a family-run tobacconist in The Woodlands, Texas; no source could be found describing its composition and character.
woodlands-fine-cigars-mr-henry.o: No description of its room note could be found in the records.

reiner-blend-51.z: Reiner Blend 51 is a light English mixture built from light and dark Virginias, Burley, black Cavendish, and a small amount of Latakia. With the Latakia proportion kept low, the smoke acts as a spicy frame rather than overwhelming the blend; the thick-cut Latakia burns slowly and the Virginia base carries the whole. Body is medium-light and nicotine measured, which suits smokers looking for an all-day Latakia blend and those new to English mixtures. It is produced in Germany by Kohlhase & Kopp and, like the rest of the Reiner line, is based on Rüdiger L. Will's recipes. It is also listed as Red Blend 51 in some markets.
reiner-blend-51.o: Leaves a lightly smoky aroma reminiscent of wood fire.

synjeco-broken-perique-flake.z: A blend produced under the Synjeco name that, based on its title, appears to be a broken-flake product containing Perique; no independent source describing its content and character could be found.

john-patton-hannays-danube-blend.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Patton's Hannay's Danube Blend pipe tobacco.

g-l-pease-shelobs-lair.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Shelob's Lair.

middle-earth-tobacco-ettenmoors.z: The Scottish-style member of the Tolkien-referencing blend series released under the Middle Earth Tobacco name; since no reliable source could be found, no detail can be given regarding its composition and character.

cornell-diehl-blockade-runner.z: Blockade Runner is a straight Virginia mixture prepared using the traditional navy cavendish method. Baked red Virginia and golden Virginia are rested in rum for seven days, then pressed and cut into a cake. The seven-day period references the length of the voyage ships made from the Caribbean to New England; carrying tobacco preserved in rum was standard naval practice of the period. The ship on the label is the Advance, a Civil War blockade runner. The tin note is noticeably boozy, but on the smoke the rum doesn't present as an aromatic; it stays more as a molasses-like undertone deepening Virginia's sweetness. Nicotine and flavor intensity are medium, with no harsh sharpness. It suits smokers wanting to keep Virginia blends simple, looking for the rum treatment's effect kept understated.
cornell-diehl-blockade-runner.o: A lightly boozy rum aroma is noticeable alongside a molasses-like dark sweetness.

sutliff-tobacco-company-taste-of-summer.z: Taste of Summer is the summer member of Sutliff's season-named aromatic line; no reliable source on its content and character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-taste-of-summer.o: No reliable record of a room note could be found.

briar-patch-trafalgar-square.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named Trafalgar Square under the Briar Patch brand could be found.

coronation-squires-irish-mixture.z: Recorded as an aromatic pipe tobacco under the Coronation brand; no reliable source on its composition, cut, and production status was found.

garfinkels-oriental-express.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of Garfinkel's Oriental Express pipe tobacco could be found.

motzek-kieler-foerde.z: Kieler Foerde is a blend named after the Kiel fjord, representing the Latakia-heavy wing of the Motzek workshop. Records indicate roughly two-thirds of the composition is Latakia; the remainder consists of fine Oriental leaves and perique. The blend's distinguishing feature is that it contains no Virginia: the base sweetness layer typical of British-origin Balkan mixtures is absent here, so the smoky, spicy side comes forward directly. Perique adds a fruity, peppery depth to the Oriental leaf's dry spice; in the absence of Virginia the blend builds a dry, smoky, sharp profile. Though nicotine stays at a medium level, flavor intensity is high, making this an entry geared toward smokers accustomed to Latakia. The product is released in 100-gram tins and pouches; a later revised version under the name 2.0 also entered the catalogue.
motzek-kieler-foerde.o: Leaves an intense pine-smoke and soot aroma, with a sharp spice note layered on top.

wessex-sovereign-curly-cut-brigade.z: Sovereign Curly Cut is the Virginia-Perique blend in Wessex's Brigade series. It's presented in a coin (curly cut) preparation; on opening the tin, part is in curled disc form and part is loose. The moisture level is directly suited to filling, and the tobacco gives off a light fruity scent. A cider casing is applied to the blend; this casing leaves a distinct sharpness and burning sensation in the mouth during the first third of the smoke. Once this alcohol-driven effect burns off, Virginia's sweetness and Perique's spicy tartness come forward in the smoke, and the blend gains a satisfying body. It suits smokers familiar with coin-cut preparation and cased Virginia-Perique structure who can tolerate the sharpness in the first third.
wessex-sovereign-curly-cut-brigade.o: Leaves a lightly fruity, tart-sweet scent reminiscent of cider.

john-patton-candy-apple.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Patton's Candy Apple pipe tobacco.

sutliff-tobacco-company-mango-4.z: Coded SPS-4, Mango is a tropical-fruit-themed blend in Sutliff's bulk aromatic line. A mango-and-vanilla sauce is applied over a ribbon-cut base of black cavendish, burley, and Virginia leaves; it has been sold in bulk packaging ranging from two ounces to five pounds. The blend is light-bodied and low in nicotine; with a high proportion of black cavendish, the burn is cool and the flavor soft. Leaf character recedes, with fruity sweetness taking the lead. Suited to smokers seeking a light, fruit-flavored tobacco who don't mind a sweet scent lingering in the room.
sutliff-tobacco-company-mango-4.o: Leaves a sweet scent reminiscent of ripe tropical fruit and vanilla.

middle-earth-tobacco-buckleberry-ferry.z: Buckleberry Ferry is referred to as Middle Earth Tobacco's only cavendish-based aromatic variety; sufficient sources describing the blend's composition and cut could not be found.
middle-earth-tobacco-buckleberry-ferry.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet, cavendish-forward aroma.

mcclelland-no-x-9-blended-light-burley-r.z: A light-colored Burley ribbon component McClelland sold in bulk for smokers building their own blends; no sufficient source giving a detailed description could be found.

john-patton-soulmates-kiss.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Patton's Soulmate's Kiss pipe tobacco.

schneiderwind-no-100.z: No. 100 is the Schneiderwind house's plain Virginia blend built from light-colored leaves. The producer describes this tobacco as aimed at those who enjoy thin, bright blends; since no additive is used, the flavor comes entirely from the Virginia leaf's natural sugar and grassy character. The smoke is light to medium; drawn slowly it gives a lemony freshness, while a faster pace can bring sharpness to the tongue. Suited to smokers who avoid Latakia and heavy casing and want a clean leaf taste during the day. Blended by the house in Aachen and distributed in 100-gram packages.
schneiderwind-no-100.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay and baked bread.

caminetto-como.z: One of Caminetto's discontinued aromatic blends; the entry has been left incomplete as no independent source documenting its content could be found.
caminetto-como.o: Leaves a red fruit and nut aroma.

holland-house-cherry-cavendish.z: Cherry Cavendish is the cherry-flavored aromatic blend of the Dutch brand Holland House. A cherry flavoring is applied to a base built from sweet Virginia, full-bodied Burley, and Cavendish leaves; the tobacco is ribbon cut, mostly presented in pouch packaging. Thanks to the leaf softened by the Cavendish process, the smoke stays creamy and cool, with the cherry note standing in front of the smoke. Being light in nicotine and slow-burning makes it suitable for smokers who love intense aromatics and those new to the pipe. The brand is one of the old aromatic lines that has found shelf space in many markets around the world.
holland-house-cherry-cavendish.o: Leaves a pronounced aroma of ripe cherry and sweet sugar.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-515-double-s.z: Wilke No. 515 Double Shot is a more heavily cased version of 515, the brand's best-known blend. The base blend rests on ribbon-cut Virginia leaf and Wilke's own roasted black cavendish, flavored with Jamaican rum; the name Double Shot comes from giving the same blend a double dose of rum. As a result, the rum note stands out clearly in the smoke, while the tobacco's own flavor recedes somewhat. According to Wilke's records, 515 was among the blends smoked by actor Basil Rathbone during the shop's New York era, and it is considered the brand's signature. The Double Shot version offers a mild-nicotine, slow-burning smoke with pronounced sweetness; it is aimed at smokers who favor liqueur-style aromatics or who find 515 itself not intense enough.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-515-double-s.o: Leaves a scent of dark rum, molasses, and caramelized sugar.

c-b-mller-co-a-s-osborne-62.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named Osborne 62 under the C.B. Møller & Co. A/S brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

century-black-cavendish.z: Century is the brand American pipe tobacco manufacturer Sutliff prepares for the UK market; as a name, the line ties back to American tobacco tradition. Black Cavendish, as its name suggests, is a single-leaf record: it consists entirely of black cavendish, and per the seller's description the leaf is lightly fire-cured to gain an earthy character. It comes pre-rubbed, ready to be loaded straight into the pipe. Its character is described as a cool-burning, low-nicotine tobacco with its natural sweetness to the fore; no heavy flavor casing has been layered on top. Suitable for smokers who want to experience Cavendish's sugary sweetness in its unflavored form, or who want a sweet base for their own blend. Aimed at those who don't want a harsh bite from the pipe and want a soft tobacco to smoke all day.
century-black-cavendish.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly smoky aroma reminiscent of dried fruit.

cornell-diehl-billy-budd.z: Billy Budd is a ribbon-cut mixture built by adding burley, bright Virginia flake, and a considerable amount of natural-cut cigar leaf to a Latakia-heavy body. Cornell & Diehl released the blend as a tribute to a friend nicknamed Sailorman Jack. The presence of cigar leaf sets it apart from classic English mixtures: earth and fermented cigar taste join the smoke and leather notes. Flavor intensity and room-note strength both rank high; the smoke is heavy and lingers in the room for a long time. Nicotine strength is also high, making it a blend intended for particular occasions rather than continuous all-day smoking. It suits those looking for tastes where Latakia and cigar leaf sit together, accustomed to unflavored, hearty smokes.
cornell-diehl-billy-budd.o: Leaves a heavy, clinging smoke carrying the aroma of a spent campfire and burnt cigar together.

milan-tobacconists-poochies-blend.z: Poochie's Blend is an aromatic in which virginia and Green River burley tobaccos are combined with quality black cavendish. The casing profile is described in the direction of toasted marshmallow, maple syrup, and vanilla. With its low nicotine level and soft smoke, it's the kind of light mixture that can be smoked throughout the day. Prepared for those who enjoy sweet aromatics and want a cool smoke that won't bite the tongue.
milan-tobacconists-poochies-blend.o: Leaves an aroma of toasted sugar, maple syrup, and vanilla.

ken-byron-ventures-jupiter-slices.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to fill in the profile of Ken Byron Ventures' Jupiter Slices.

tavern-tobacco-co-laurel-flake.z: Laurel Flake, a pipe tobacco from Tavern Tobacco Co.; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

e-a-carey-spritzer.z: An aromatic blend registered under the E. A. Carey name; it does not appear on the maker's current list, and not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-chesapeak.z: Chesapeake is The Country Squire tobacconist's mild aromatic house blend, carrying a nutty top note with light vanilla; no detailed source on its leaf composition could be found.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-chesapeak.o: Leaves a scent of nutty sweetness with light vanilla.

mcclelland-aurora.z: Aurora is a straight Virginia blend in McClelland's Collector series. It was originally prepared for a pipe collectors' club; later printings dropped the club abbreviation from the label. The blend uses bright yellow, red, and stoved black Virginia together, gathering a wide taste range of Virginia in the bowl rather than a single leaf class. It's fine ribbon cut, and the tin carries McClelland's characteristic tangy-fruity fermentation aroma. The taste turns sometimes sweet, sometimes earthy and herbal; body stays measured enough for all-day smoking. Falls within the territory of those wanting to trace unflavored Virginia's layers. Difficulty sourcing the red Virginia leaf such blends depend on has been cited as one reason for the firm's closure.
mcclelland-aurora.o: Leaves a tangy fruit-ferment and sweet hay aroma.

g-l-pease-maltese-falcon-heirloom-collec.z: Maltese Falcon is a coarse-cut English blend in G. L. Pease's Heirloom Collection line. High-quality Oriental leaves and a measured amount of Latakia are added over sweet Virginia leaves; no additive is used in the blend. Latakia takes the lead role in the overall taste, but not to a degree that masks the other leaves' flavour; the Oriental leaf's silky, oily, spicy character and Virginia's sweetness remain identifiable in the background. Strength is light-to-medium and it leaves a long-lasting taste on the palate. It suits those wanting to smoke Latakia in a balanced rather than heavy dose.
g-l-pease-maltese-falcon-heirloom-collec.o: Leaves a woody incense aroma with a sweetish, spicy trace behind it.

intertabak-pure-virginia-po-5.z: No verifiable source could be found for this straight Virginia registered under the INTERTABAK name.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-widecombe-aromat.z: Widecombe Aromatic is a McGahey blend taking its name from the village of Widecombe-in-the-Moor in Dartmoor. A measured share of latakia is added over Virginia and cavendish sweetness, so that aromatic softness and smoky depth sit side by side. It is presented as a ready-rubbed ribbon cut and has a medium strength.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-widecombe-aromat.o: Leaves a fine wood-smoke aroma over sweet cavendish.

smokers-haven-pure-pleasure.z: Pure Pleasure is one of Smokers' Haven's bulk-sold American mixtures close to the English style. Per the maker's account, white burley forms its base; a flavoring-level proportion of latakia and a limited amount of golden Virginia are added on top. Its medium-thick cut is well suited to slow burning and leaves a dry, powdery ash.
smokers-haven-pure-pleasure.o: Leaves a lightly smoky, dry wood scent sitting over nutty burley.

carroll-p-j-co-ltd-old-road.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Old Road under the Carroll P. J. & Co. Ltd. brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

bufflehead-redhead-decoy.z: Bufflehead was a brand producing small batches in the United States in the early 2000s, naming its blends after waterfowl; since no independent source describing this blend's content and character could be found, the entry has been left incomplete.

danske-club-white.z: White is the blend in the Danske Club series' classic line, previously listed on packaging under the name White Luxury. As with the rest of the series, Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish leaf form the base, ribbon cut. Casing is kept more restrained than the series' fruited members. Strength sits between mild and medium. Suited to smokers who aren't looking for a pronounced fruit or liqueur note and want a smooth, straightforward aromatic. Distributed in 50-gram pouches and 100-gram tins.
danske-club-white.o: Leaves a soft, creamy-sweet tobacco scent.

philip-morris-kilta.z: This pipe tobacco is recorded under the Philip Morris name and is no longer produced; no sources describing the blend could be found.

motzek-plug-no-4.z: Plug No. 4 is the milder entry in the Motzek workshop's numbered plug series. Records indicate it consists of roughly 80 percent virginia and 20 percent black cavendish; it is released after resting for at least a year under vacuum. It is sold in block form and is sliced and rubbed out before smoking. It carries no artificial flavoring; the taste rests on Virginia's own sweetness and the dark tones softened by the cavendish. It carries a more measured nicotine load than the line's other plugs, burns cool, and can be smoked for a long time without heating up the pipe. Suitable for those looking for a plain pressed tobacco to smoke throughout the day and for those new to the plug format.
motzek-plug-no-4.o: Leaves a plain, bready tobacco aroma.

clan-shaw-rummy.z: No reliable, independent sourcing could be found regarding Clan Shaw Rummy, so a detailed profile could not be compiled.

mac-baren-gold-block.z: Gold Block is a blend rooted in the English pipe tobacco tradition, produced today under the Mac Baren umbrella alongside the St. Bruno line. Virginia tobaccos selected from two continents form the body of the blend, balanced by a small amount of burley. Its loose cut makes it easy to pack and it burns evenly. The character is Virginia-forward; there is a light casing sweetness, but the blend does not fall into the heavy aromatic class. Suited to those looking for a plain, everyday, low-maintenance smoke.
mac-baren-gold-block.o: Leaves a soft, lightly sweet, floral tobacco room note.

cornell-diehl-house-reserve.z: Not enough primary sourcing could be found regarding the composition and character of the Cornell & Diehl blend House Reserve.

owl-shop-bancroft-tower.z: Recorded as one of the Owl Shop's house blends, flake cut and Virginia-based; no second source detailing its composition could be found.
owl-shop-bancroft-tower.o: No description could be found in the records.

windels-half-grove-semois.z: This blend is recorded as being produced from local tobacco grown in Belgium's Semois valley; no sufficient source could be found for detailed composition and character information.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-holiday-blend-19.z: Holiday Blend 1997 is part of Hermit Tobacco Works Co.'s series of limited annual holiday-season releases; there is not enough sourcing to document this particular year's composition.

uhles-pride-o-wisconsin.z: Pride O' Wisconsin is a blend Uhle Tobacco Company prepares under its own name, built on a pairing of Virginia and Burley. Per the maker's description, a small amount of peach brandy adding a soft note accompanies a woody, clean base. Because the amount of flavoring is kept limited, the blend cannot be fully classed as aromatic; Virginia sweetness and Burley's dry, nutty side stay in front. Suited to smokers who steer away from heavy aromatics but still want a light fruit touch in a plain Virginia-Burley blend. The blend has been prepared at the shop operating in Milwaukee since 1939, and its distribution is limited to the maker's own channels.
uhles-pride-o-wisconsin.o: Leaves an aroma of light peach sweetness over a dry hay and woody base.

bosphorus-dark-cherry.z: Dark Cherry is a cherry-flavored, ribbon-cut blend built from yellow Virginia, burley and cavendish. It is one of the products the brand released in 2015. Virginia's sweetness and cherry's tartness complement each other; toward the end of the smoke, burley becomes more pronounced, giving the blend body and making the nicotine level satisfying. Its strength is slightly above medium, and its flavor balance stays at a medium level. Suitable for smokers seeking a fruit-flavored aromatic that does not grow heavy and wanting to fill the bowl more than once during the day.
bosphorus-dark-cherry.o: Leaves a sweet cherry and sugared-fruit aroma.

borkum-riff-black-cavendish.z: Borkum Riff Black Cavendish is an aromatic built on dark Kentucky and cool-smoking Burley leaf with some light Virginia added, heavily coated and fermented in wooden casks. This process gives the leaf its black Cavendish color and a mellow, sweet base. Notes reminiscent of truffle, nougat, and hazelnut stand out in the topping. Borkum Riff emerged in Sweden in the 1960s and is now produced in Denmark under the Scandinavian Tobacco Group umbrella. This blend suits smokers looking for a nuttier, sweeter direction than heavily fruited aromatics, wanting a medium-to-light-bodied everyday tobacco.
borkum-riff-black-cavendish.o: Leaves a room note reminiscent of roasted hazelnut, nougat, and a dark, sugary sweet.

esoterica-tobacciana-penzance.z: Penzance is the most sought-after blend in the Esoterica line, and its recipe is not disclosed. Per the maker's description, select virginia leaves, Turkish and oriental tobaccos and Cyprus latakia are hand-blended, pressed hard, and cut into wide, thick flake slices. It is produced by J. F. Germain & Son in Jersey. The pressing binds latakia's soot and the orientals' spice together within the sweetness of aged virginia; the result is a medium-strength profile in the English-Balkan line but with its edges softened. The flake needs to be rubbed out and smoked slowly. Due to limited production it appears in the market only periodically.
esoterica-tobacciana-penzance.o: Leaves a scent of campfire soot, cedar and dry spice.

g-l-pease-piccadilly.z: Piccadilly is a blend in the Classic Collection built by spicing several Virginias with a small amount of latakia and rounding it out with Louisiana perique. It is lighter and sweeter than other records in the series; latakia smoke does not lead but sits as a thin layer between the Virginia and Oriental-like spice. The flavours open layer by layer through the smoke; notes reminiscent of cinnamon and citrus are reported. It is noted to be notably affected by ageing. It is a record aimed at smokers seeking a light English blend for the day's first pipes.
g-l-pease-piccadilly.o: Leaves a light smokiness and a sweetish, cinnamon-like woody aroma.

tavern-tobacco-co-mccraigans-flake.z: McCraigan's Flake, a pipe tobacco from Tavern Tobacco Co.; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

faders-unique.z: Unique is one of the house blends of the Baltimore-based Fader's tobacconist; not enough sourcing explaining the blend's composition and character could be found.
faders-unique.o: Records do not contain enough information for a description.

torben-dansk-burley-maduro.z: Torben Dansk Burley Maduro is a darker, longer-aged form of the standard Burley. Sources describe it as a strong, spicy Burley with earthy and walnut-like notes coming forward and low sweetness. It is heavier than the brand's plain Burley in both nicotine and body, so it is not suited to smoking on an empty stomach. Suited to those wanting to add darkness and strength to their blends, and to experienced smokers after an unflavored, full-bodied dark tobacco.
torben-dansk-burley-maduro.o: Leaves a dark, earthy aroma reminiscent of dry bark.

cornell-diehl-habana-daydream.z: Habana Daydream is a blend built on a base of Virginia, perique, and unsweetened black cavendish, with a small amount of Latakia and a pronounced proportion of cigar leaf added. It is a ribbon cut and is built on the idea of bringing the cigar-smoking experience into a pipe. The tin note interweaves molasses, aged leather, banana bread, and cedar notes. On the smoke, the smoke is dense and creamy; the body is full but doesn't hit the tongue hard, with perique's spice and Latakia's smoke framing the cigar leaf's earthy, leathery character. It suits those looking for an unflavored, full-bodied smoke leaning toward the cigar side.
cornell-diehl-habana-daydream.o: Leaves an aroma of leather, cedar, and molasses reminiscent of cigar smoke.

schneiderwind-banbridge-flake.z: Banbridge Flake is one of the pressed blends the Aachen-based Schneiderwind house offers under its own name. It is built by bringing together various Virginia and burley leaves; a spicy pinch of Louisiana-origin perique is added on top. A noticeable but not overpowering nougat casing rounds off the blend's sweet side; according to records, the producer positions this tobacco as a mild counterpart to the house's darker, harsher flakes. The flake format lets the tobacco burn slowly and cool; the leaves need to be rubbed or folded for packing before use. Nicotine load stays between low and medium. Suited to smokers getting acquainted with pressed tobaccos who want a full-bodied leaf taste without heavy Kentucky or Latakia; distributed in 100-gram packages.
schneiderwind-banbridge-flake.o: Leaves a nutty nougat sweetness together with a dry hay scent.

pfeifen-huber-no-15.z: This blend is one of Pfeifen Huber's numbered house blends, reportedly regarded as a light introductory tobacco to English-Scottish blends; no sufficient sources documenting its composition could be found.

friedman-pease-oasis.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Friedman & Pease's Oasis blend; records place it in the English-mixture class.

john-aylesbury-finest-british.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to document the contents and character of John Aylesbury's Finest British.

jons-pipe-shop-october-crimson.z: One of the house blends Jon's Pipe Shop sells under its own name; no independent source could be found on its contents or character.

echte-friesche-heerenbaai-echte-friesche.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of the pipe tobacco called Echte Friesche Heerenbaai, from the brand Echte Friesche Heerenbaai.

cascadia-pipe-co-downwind.z: Downwind is the Burley-forward member of Cascadia Pipe Co.'s five-blend, nature-themed series. Like the other members it is offered in pressed-cake form; the cake structure preserves the tobacco's moisture and requires it to be sliced before filling. Nutty, dry, earthy Burley forms the body of the blend; Virginia leaf provides a faint sweet-tart balance in the background. No flavor casing is used. Nicotine sits at the upper end of the series and it burns slow and cool. Aimed at smokers seeking an unflavored Burley character with body, wanting a non-aromatic everyday blend.
cascadia-pipe-co-downwind.o: Leaves a roasted-nut and dry-earth aroma.

house-of-windsor-2005-cube-burley.z: House of Windsor's bulk-sold blend numbered 2005 is, as the name suggests, an unflavored mixture prepared with cube-cut single-varietal Burley leaf. Records indicate it's formed by combining light and medium-colored cubes in equal proportions; because the pieces are small, it's recommended to fill the bowl by gravity rather than tamping. Its moisture is kept at a level suited for smoking straight from the tin.
house-of-windsor-2005-cube-burley.o: Leaves a dry tobacco aroma carrying toasted-nut and light-molasses sweetness.

mcclelland-old-dog.z: Old Dog is one of McClelland's full-bodied English mixtures. Per the product description, the blend is deepened with Cyprian Latakia and spiced with Macedonian-sourced Xanthi Oriental; its liveliness comes from rested flue-cured Virginias and black Cavendish. Here, black Cavendish isn't used for flavoring but as a dark, mellow base element. Latakia's smoke sits at the blend's center; the Oriental's spice and the Virginia's sweetness frame that smoke, while the Cavendish softens the mouthfeel. Flavor intensity and nicotine dose run high. A blend meant for evening pipes among smokers used to heavy English mixtures. Discontinued when the brand closed in 2018.
mcclelland-old-dog.o: Leaves a dark wood-smoke and spiced-soot aroma.

nording-labrador.z: Labrador is the aromatic blend in Erik Nørding's Hunter series, named after hunting dog breeds. It's built from scented black cavendish, mild burley, and sweet Virginia leaves, and burns slowly since it's loose cut. The line's first production was made by McClelland; later production passed to Cornell & Diehl. The topping brings forward nutty, coffee, and whisky notes along with a pronounced caramel sweetness; on opening the tin, the scent is intense enough to be noticed from several steps away. The smoke stays cool and the nicotine sensation low. It suits smokers seeking a sweet, flavored cavendish character and those newly getting acquainted with aromatic blends.
nording-labrador.o: Leaves a scent of baking cinnamon roll and caramel.

mac-baren-special-fine-cut.z: Remembered as a fine-cut Virginia blend; since no maker or retailer page documenting its contents could be found, the record is left incomplete.
mac-baren-special-fine-cut.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-coniston-plug.z: Coniston is a product of the pressing tradition Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. carries on in Kendal. Light-coloured and fire-cured Virginias are blended with Burley; the leaves are steamed, the topping added by hand, then placed in a mould, left under press overnight, and cooked in the press. The resulting cake is sold as a plug or sliced; before smoking it is sliced with a knife and rubbed out. Its body is medium; the floral top note of the Lakeland style is kept measured here. For this reason it is one of the products smokers new to Lakeland-essenced tobaccos often start with. It suits those willing to work with pressed tobacco and smoke slowly.
gawith-hoggarth-co-coniston-plug.o: A light floral-soapy Lakeland note accompanies the pressed tobacco's sweetness.

mcclelland-gkcpc-chocolate-silk.z: Chocolate Silk sits at the aromatic end of the selection McClelland prepared for the Greater Kansas City Pipe Club (GKCPC). Its base combines black Cavendish with golden Virginia leaves; a chocolate-and-nougat topping is applied over it. The Cavendish share softens the burn, while the Virginia leaves a sugary base in the background.
mcclelland-gkcpc-chocolate-silk.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of cocoa and sweetened nut paste.

tabacos-catarinenses-ltda-havana-pequi.z: A pipe tobacco in Tabacos Catarinenses' Havana line, known for its flavoring after the Brazilian pequi fruit; no independent source describing the blend's content and character could be found.
tabacos-catarinenses-ltda-havana-pequi.o: Records suggest it leaves a tropical scent reminiscent of pequi fruit.

cornell-diehl-coffee.z: This blend, referred to as one of Cornell & Diehl's coffee-flavored aromatics, could not have its content and character verified, as it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog.

doctor-pipe-vanilla-flake.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Vanilla Flake, a pipe tobacco from Doctor Pipe.
doctor-pipe-vanilla-flake.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-wattsons-speci.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of this blend tied to the Wattson's line could be found.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-wattsons-speci.o: No description could be found in the records.

rona-black-gold-special.z: No independent source documenting the content and character of Rona Black Gold Special could be found; according to records it is a cavendish-forward blend.

cornell-diehl-burley-flake-3.z: Burley Flake #3 is the series member distinguished by fire-cured Kentucky. Cool-burning burley leaf is joined by rich dark-fired Kentucky; Virginia provides natural sweetness and aroma, while a pinch of perique adds extra nuance. The mixture is pressed and sliced, presented as flake. The presence of Kentucky adds a smoky, salty direction to the blend; as a result it carries a smoky impression despite the series containing no Latakia. Burley keeps the body dry and nutty, Virginia's sweetness balances that dryness, and perique leaves a plummy spice in the background. Nicotine strength runs high, and the smoke is heavy. It suits those looking for an unflavored, smoky, hearty flake.
cornell-diehl-burley-flake-3.o: A smoked-wood aroma is noticeable together with a nutty scent.

newminster-no-306-english-oriental.z: No. 306 English Oriental brings together Cyprus latakia with select hot-air-cured virginia leaves and spicy samsun tobacco from Turkey. Burley is added for body and to slow the burn, and black cavendish is added to soften the texture. There is no top-flavoring; the oriental leaf's spice sits alongside latakia's smoky tone. It is a ribbon-cut blend sold in bulk. Suitable for those who like oriental-forward English mixtures where latakia is present but not overwhelming. It is produced at Mac Baren's facilities in Denmark.
newminster-no-306-english-oriental.o: Leaves a smoky wood and spicy dry-herb aroma in the room.

gq-tobaccos-nottingham-lace-noir.z: Noir, the dark member of the Nottingham Lace series, is built on English-style black Cavendish. This base is joined by golden-hued Virginia leaf, Izmir-origin Turkish tobacco, and Perique. The Virginia side gives a herbal, lightly citrusy base; the black Cavendish supplies sweetness without resorting to a vanilla-like topping; the Izmir draws a smoky, woody line; and the Perique sharpens the blend's edges with raisin, plum, and pepper notes. The result is a smoke that flows smoothly but isn't flat — all four components remain individually distinguishable. Suited to smokers who steer away from the heavy sweetness of topped aromatics and seek natural Cavendish sweetness, as well as those curious about the balance between Oriental and Perique. Since it stays at a moderate level for nicotine, it has an intensity suited to smoking at different times of day.
gq-tobaccos-nottingham-lace-noir.o: Leaves a dark, lightly smoky sweetness along with a raisin-and-plum aroma.

dan-tobacco-caro-mio.z: Caro Mio is Dan Tobacco's caramel-focused aromatic blend. Its body is largely black Cavendish, with only a small proportion of rubbed Virginia flake added. The casing, per the maker's description, is a creamy toffee-caramel note, and the idea behind the name is a nod to Italian desserts like panna cotta or crème caramel. The Cavendish weight makes the blend low in nicotine, soft, and cool-burning. Suited to smokers who like sweet aromatics and want a light mixture they can smoke any time of day, as well as those new to the pipe. If a spicy or smoky character is what's wanted, this blend doesn't offer it.
dan-tobacco-caro-mio.o: Leaves a sweet, milky trace with a scent of burnt sugar and buttery caramel.

borkum-riff-authentic.z: Borkum Riff Authentic is made from a combination of black Cavendish, flue-cured Virginia, and Burley leaf. After blending, the mixture is pressed into cakes under warm pressure; the rested cakes are then sliced into flakes and rubbed out for packing. This preparation gives it a denser, slower-burning structure than the loose-cut blends common in the line. The Borkum Riff brand was born in Sweden in 1962, taking its name from a lighthouse in the North Sea; the blends are now produced at Scandinavian Tobacco Group's Assens factory in Denmark. Authentic is the line's option that avoids heavy flavoring and lets the tobacco's own taste lead; it suits smokers accustomed to Cavendish sweetness who want less topping, and those looking for an all-day smoke.
borkum-riff-authentic.o: Leaves a lightly sweet room note of dry hay and baked tobacco.

samuel-gawith-winter-time-flake.z: Winter Time Flake is the Latakia-forward link in English producer Samuel Gawith's limited Four Seasons series. According to records, the blend is the product of collaboration with Dr. Josef Stanislav; it is built by combining selected latakias with pressed virginias and is presented in dark-colored flake leaves in 50-gram tins. Virginia's high sugar content sits alongside latakia's spicy, smoky character; the result is a slow-burning, cool yet full smoke. No casing is applied. It is noted that this series, unlike Samuel Gawith's other products, is packed drier, which eases packing and lighting. Suited to experienced smokers accustomed to Latakia who want a medium-to-above-medium strength flake.
samuel-gawith-winter-time-flake.o: Leaves a scent forward with leather and burnt wood smoke, carrying a light sweet trace underneath.

charles-fairmorn-belmore-cross-cut.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the Charles Fairmorn name.

lane-limited-hayward-mixture.z: An American-style Lane Limited mixture; not enough sources could be found to describe its contents and character.

benson-hedges-original-virginia-flake.z: A Virginia flake blend presented in tins by Benson & Hedges under its Old Bond Street address; according to records it was on the market in the 1970s, and no reliable source on its recipe and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-american-blend-whiske.z: American Blend Whiskey is a record offered with whisky flavouring in Kendal's Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s bulk aromatic line. A mix of Virginia, burley, and black cavendish is prepared as a ribbon cut and topped with whisky flavouring. Related to the same firm's American Irish Spice, it is a topping-forward blend that is light on nicotine.
gawith-hoggarth-co-american-blend-whiske.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly alcoholic aroma reminiscent of oak-aged whisky.

fincks-cigar-company-imperial-chocolate.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for Finck's Cigar Company's Imperial Chocolate pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

spectre-spectre.z: No verifiable information from a maker or retailer source could be found about this blend, which is stated to be built on cigar leaf.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-balkan-sob.z: This Sutliff blend is a Balkan mixture modeled on the 1970s version of Balkan Sobranie. It's built on smoky latakia, a broad share of orientals, and bright Virginia leaf; the orientals' spicy, floral tone defines the blend's identity. Records indicate that compared to the version it models, the orientals lean a touch spicier, the latakia share is a bit lower, and the creamy sweetness is a bit more pronounced. Aimed at experienced smokers seeking classic Balkan mixtures that are unflavored, richly sweet, and smoky.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-balkan-sob.o: Leaves a scent of wood smoke mixed with spice, reminiscent of incense.

hu-tobacco-haymaker.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Haymaker, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

esoterica-tobacciana-margate.z: Margate is the Esoterica line's classic English mixture; a ribbon-cut tobacco built on the virginia-oriental-Cyprus latakia trio, following old-school English blending tradition. It is produced by J. F. Germain & Son in Jersey. The latakia smoke is pronounced, with the orientals' spicy, herbal tones running underneath it, while virginia provides a sweet base. The same blend flavored with cognac is offered under the name Pembroke. It suits those seeking an unadulterated, soot-forward English mixture.
esoterica-tobacciana-margate.o: Leaves a heavy woody scent evoking pine soot and dry leather.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-poniatows.z: Poniatowski is Scandinavian Tobacco Group's aromatic pipe-tobacco line produced solely for the Polish market; no independent source on the content of the Full Aroma version could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-poniatows.o: No detailed description of the room note could be found in the records.

cornell-diehl-crooked-lane.z: Crooked Lane is a full-bodied English blend named after an old London street. Per the manufacturer's description, a Virginia base is joined by a pronounced share of Latakia, Oriental leaves, and a small amount of perique; black cavendish is also present in the composition. It is a ribbon cut. The flavor side is layered with Latakia's smoke, the Oriental's tangy spice, and perique's plum-and-pepper note; Virginia lays a sweet foundation beneath these layers. Nicotine stays medium while flavor intensity is high, so it suits smokers who love dark, complex English blends.
cornell-diehl-crooked-lane.o: Leaves a smoky trace reminiscent of leather and wood.

paul-olsen-the-mixture.z: One of the house blends from the Paul Olsen house; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found.

tsuge-premium-pipe-tobacco-gunjin-the-sa.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Tsuge Premium Pipe Tobacco blend Gunjin - The Samurai God has been found.

motzek-16-5-der-neue.z: 16/5 Der Neue is a Virginia-Burley-Perique blend listed in the catalogue of the Motzek workshop in Kiel (TAK, Tabak aus Kiel). Curly rings prepared from bright and dark-fired Virginia leaves are joined with ribbon-cut burley and dark flake pieces carrying perique. The maker states it uses only natural additives; the blend's light honey note is given by this means as well. In the taste profile, earthy and herbal tones, burley's nutty side, and a measured peppery point from the perique stand out. Records indicate the blend carries the name "Der Neue" ("The New One") because it was the first new blend added to the catalogue after Thomas Darasz took over the business from Herbert Motzek. Nicotine and body sit between light and medium; it can therefore be considered a recipe for smokers who want something smokable throughout the day and aren't looking for heavy Latakia or heavily flavored blends. Because of the cut's mixed structure, the curly rings and flake pieces need to be rubbed by hand before loading.
motzek-16-5-der-neue.o: Leaves a fine honey sweetness beneath the aroma of dry hay and baked tobacco.

rattray-3-noggins.z: 3 Noggins is a Scottish-style mixture in which aged Virginia leaf is mellowed with black Cavendish, with a touch of Latakia and a small amount of Oriental tobacco added. The ribbon cut packs easily and burns evenly; the Cavendish share smooths off Virginia's sharp edges, while Latakia sketches a smoky frame without sitting at the blend's center. Reports indicate the blend was developed from a wish to keep the same maker's 7 Reserve's aroma while building up its body, so a kinship is felt between the two. It suits smokers new to Latakia blends who aren't yet ready for the weight of a full-bodied English mixture, as well as those looking for a sweet-smoky balance.
rattray-3-noggins.o: Leaves a trace where wood smoke and sweet dark tobacco interweave.

ken-byron-ventures-the-dread-planet-2019.z: Ken Byron Ventures' Dread Planet, in its limited 2019 release, is reported to be Virginia- and Perique-forward; no independent source could be found to document its contents and character in detail.
ken-byron-ventures-the-dread-planet-2019.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

watch-city-cigar-reindeer-droppings.z: This is one of Watch City Cigar's seasonal releases, for which no sufficient source could be found.
watch-city-cigar-reindeer-droppings.o: No record could be found regarding the room note.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-lowland-p.z: Lowland Pine is one of The Country Squire tobacconist's house blends; no reliable source on its content and character could be found.

cornell-diehl-halav-udvash-milk-honey.z: Halav U'Dvash is a member of Cornell & Diehl's Hebraica series. The series grew out of blends prepared for Rabbi Ira Stone, a fan of burley, Oriental, and perique mixtures; Stone gave the blends their names using the language of Jewish tradition. The blend pairs a black-and-red Virginia cavendish base with burley and fire-cured Kentucky, joined by a small amount of perique and Oriental leaf; it is topped with a light honey-and-milk theme, and the cut is ribbon. It comes out of the tin on the moist side and needs airing; smoked quickly, it can burn hot. As the smoke progresses the profile grows more complex, turning in the second half toward something reminiscent of spice cake. Thanks to the fire-cured Kentucky, nicotine runs above what's typical for aromatics; it suits those looking for a lightly flavored but full-bodied blend.
cornell-diehl-halav-udvash-milk-honey.o: A light smoky note from the fire-cured leaf can be sensed beneath the honeyed, spiced-cake aroma.

intertabak-bright-virginia-n-3750.z: No verifiable source could be found for this light-colored Virginia registered under the INTERTABAK name.

sobranie-of-london-626-old-tradition.z: A blend referenced by number in the old catalog of the Sobranie house, founded in London in 1879, that is not produced today; no source documenting its composition could be found.

motzek-toms-plug.z: Tom's Plug is the pressed tobacco carrying the name of Tom Darasz, who took over the Motzek workshop. Virginias, some black cavendish, and burley are joined by a measured but character-defining dose of perique and latakia, then pressed into block form. When fresh, it is left to air out for a while; after that it can be broken up like bread and rubbed into the bowl. It is a natural blend carrying no artificial flavoring. At the core of the taste is a subtle undertone of sweetness from the virginia and cavendish, along with the piquant, lightly smoky character brought by the latakia-perique pairing; the strength doesn't build through the bowl but stays balanced. Suitable for smokers wanting to try the English style in pressed format, who find the plug convenient to carry while traveling, and who are considering long-term storage.
motzek-toms-plug.o: Leaves a plain, lightly smoky tobacco aroma that doesn't linger in the room.

bergerac-affine.z: Recorded as a mixture of unflavored dark tobaccos in the French scaferlati tradition; detailed content information could not be verified.
bergerac-affine.o: Leaves a dark, earthy, sharp tobacco room note.

watch-city-cigar-fat-bastard.z: This is one of the house blends of the Watch City Cigar shop; it does not appear in the current catalog, and no source could be found documenting its composition.

sutliff-tobacco-company-307-mocha-strips.z: Sutliff's mixture number 307, Mocha Strips, is a flake-cut aromatic prepared by pressing and slicing burley, Virginia, and Turkish leaf. Pressing lets the applied Dutch-style flavoring work into the leaf; cocoa leads the top note, accompanied by light coffee and dark fruit tones. On the palate, the chocolate character is more pronounced than the fruit note in the flavoring, with burley's body felt behind it. Suited to those accustomed to flake cut who seek a medium-intensity, non-biting aromatic.
sutliff-tobacco-company-307-mocha-strips.o: Leaves a scent of cocoa and coffee with a light dark fruit note.

rotary-rotary-superior.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the Rotary brand, classified as aromatic; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

bentley-old-london-the-london-pine.z: Bentley's The London Pine, also known as Old London, is the German maker's English-style blend. The defining component is a generous share of smoky Latakia, accompanied by Virginia leaf serving as the base. The maker describes the blend as having a pronounced body without being unpleasantly strong. The Latakia share keeps the blend on the axis of soot, tar, and resinous wood; underneath, Virginia leaves a measured sweetness that softens the smoke. The same tobacco appearing under two names is one of the brand's products that changes name by market. It's aimed at those familiar with classic Latakia mixtures, wanting a medium-to-full-bodied, unflavored smoke.
bentley-old-london-the-london-pine.o: Resinous woodsmoke and soot are accompanied by a dry spice edge.

gawith-hoggarth-co-ultimum.z: Ultimum is a blend in Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s aromatic line labeled "American type." Black Cavendish forms the base, joined by aged Virginia and mild Burley. Cherry and caramel flavoring is applied on top. The product was previously sold as Cherry & Caramel before taking on the name Ultimum. The cut is ribbon; moisture is high, and the color is dark due to the black Cavendish weight. Its character is markedly sweet and mild. Black Cavendish gives the body a thick, sugary base, while Virginia adds light fruitiness and Burley a nutty dryness; the cherry-and-caramel topping leads in both aroma and taste. Nicotine is low and tongue bite stays limited, so it's counted among the blends that even those new to the pipe can comfortably smoke. A product aimed less at those seeking unflavored tobacco taste and more at those wanting a sweet, fragrant smoke.
gawith-hoggarth-co-ultimum.o: Leaves an aroma of boiled sugar, caramel, and ripe cherry.

mac-baren-cherry-ambrosia.z: Cherry Ambrosia, also known as Red Ambrosia in some markets, is a ready-rubbed Danish aromatic. The blend is built from roughly equal proportions of brown Burley and Mac Baren's modern Cavendish; this Cavendish is obtained by processing golden Virginia leaf into black Cavendish. As the name suggests, the main flavoring is cherry, and the aroma stands out pronouncedly. The Burley base gives the blend a nut-leaning body while the Cavendish balances the sweetness. Being light on nicotine, it suits smokers who like aromatics and don't want the tobacco taste too far forward.
mac-baren-cherry-ambrosia.o: Spreads a sweet cherry and sugared-fruit aroma through the room.

lane-limited-blend-eleven.z: One of Lane Limited's numbered bulk aromatics; not enough sources could be found about its contents.

barclay-rex-bits-of-gold.z: One of the shop blends from Barclay Rex, the tobacconist open in New York since 1910; no composition record for this name could be found, leaving the profile blank.

the-smoker-fire-side.z: Fire Side is recorded as one of the hand-prepared house blends from The Smoker, a tobacconist that operated in Albany from the 1930s until 2011; no independent source describing the blend's composition has been found.

levin-pipes-international-scottish-woods.z: Scottish Woods is a matured oriental mixture McClelland prepared exclusively for Levin Pipes International. In the dark-colored, fine shag cut, oriental/Turkish tobaccos and Syrian latakia come forward, with Virginia staying in the background. Its four-ounce tins from the early 1990s appear on the collector market. Aimed at those seeking latakia- and oriental-forward blends with low sweetness. Production ended after Barry Levin's death.
levin-pipes-international-scottish-woods.o: Leaves a resinous, incense-like latakia scent with a thyme-like dry oriental note.

g-l-pease-samarra.z: Samarra is a mixture in which matured red Virginia carries the structure and a fine sweetness, joined by a generous measure of Cyprus latakia for smoky richness, fragrant Oriental leaf for fullness, and a small amount of perique. It is among the first blends offered under the G. L. Pease name, described as a reworking of the Sublime Porte blend Pease produced while working at Drucquer & Sons. Despite the high latakia proportion, the blend is not a latakia showcase; the weight is shared between Virginia's structure and the Oriental leaf's exotic aroma. In the smoke, notes of earth, bread, smoky wood, tart lemongrass, floral, and dry grass are reported. It suits smokers seeking the classic structure with a not-too-heavy body.
g-l-pease-samarra.o: Leaves an aroma of smoky wood and dry spice.

dan-tobacco-bill-baileys-birthday-blend.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of Dan Tobacco's Bill Bailey's Birthday Blend were found.

royal-cigar-no-12-black-raspberry.z: No reliable source could be found for No.12 Black Raspberry, signed Royal Cigar and, as its name suggests, understood to be raspberry-flavored.

kontor-tabak-no-4.z: Kontor-Tabak No. 4 is, per the manufacturer's description, a full-bodied flake prepared for smokers who love matured natural tobaccos. The blend brings together golden and red Virginia leaves, Kentucky and a small amount of Perique. The pressed slices burn very slowly, evenly and cool. The floral sweetness from golden Virginia, Kentucky's toasted-leaf scent and Perique's measured spice come through layer by layer. Since it's above medium in nicotine, it's aimed at experienced smokers seeking a full body; whether the flake is rubbed or folded before packing determines the burn pattern.
kontor-tabak-no-4.o: A floral sweetness accompanies the toasted-leaf and lightly smoky wood scent.

paul-olsen-njord.z: One of the aromatic blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-continental.z: No reliable sourcing describing the composition and character of this blend, part of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Kendal-named tobacco family, could be found.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-peans.z: No reliable source describing the content and character of this blend, listed as a product of the Brazilian maker Imigrantes Fumos, could be found.

j-f-germain-son-eighteen-twenty.z: This is an English-style blend taking its name from 1820, the year J. F. Germain & Son was founded on the island of Jersey; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.
j-f-germain-son-eighteen-twenty.o: Records indicate it carries the smoky aroma typical of Latakia-containing English blends.

peterson-wild-atlantic.z: Wild Atlantic is an English blend built on Virginia and Oriental leaf with a smaller proportion of Latakia added on top. It is a ribbon cut, presented in 40 gram pouches; the difference in leaf color and cut is visible to the naked eye. When the pouch is first opened it gives off an intense, Oriental-dominant scent; as it airs, a note recalling dried fig comes forward. It is moisture-balanced enough to smoke without going out. Its strength is between light and medium, and its flavor is between medium and intense. It suits smokers seeking English blends where Latakia is kept in modest amount and the Oriental character comes through. The room note is strong and needs care indoors.
peterson-wild-atlantic.o: A sharp, smoky Latakia scent fills the room and lingers for a long time.

rain-city-cigar-golden-cavendish.z: This is a house blend from Rain City Cigar, open since 1997 in Seattle's Georgetown neighborhood; there is not enough source material describing its composition and character.

ken-byron-ventures-fat-old-sun.z: Fat Old Sun is one of the Virginia-forward blends from Ken Byron Ventures, a small-batch producer based in Tennessee. Records indicate bright and dark Virginia leaf are used together; on the tongue, citrus, dry hay, and dark fruit stand out. The cut is ribbon, and the blend is reported to burn cool. Nicotine is said to run slightly below medium, without pronounced tongue bite. Suited to smokers seeking Virginia's sweet-tart balance in a plain form, away from heavily cased blends. Since the brand works in limited batches, it isn't continuously available.
ken-byron-ventures-fat-old-sun.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of dry hay and citrus peel.

sutliff-tobacco-company-south-seas.z: South Seas is a blend among Sutliff's tropical-themed aromatics, offered in bulk. Its base is burley-forward and softened with black cavendish; a mango-based flavoring is applied over it. Records indicate the fruit casing is the blend's dominant element and can overshadow the tobacco notes. Burley builds a lightly sweet, nutty background and carries most of the blend's body. It sits light in nicotine and medium in taste. It suits those who enjoy sweet, fruity aromatics and are looking for a smoke that can stand in for dessert at the end of the day.
sutliff-tobacco-company-south-seas.o: Leaves a scent of ripe mango and tropical fruit.

radfords-nut-berry.z: No source could be found documenting the content and flavoring of Radfords Nut & Berry.
radfords-nut-berry.o: No information describing the room note could be found in available records.

holts-cigar-company-mocha-black.z: This is a house blend of Holt's Cigar Company carrying, as the name suggests, a coffee-themed flavoring; no independent source detailing its composition could be found.
holts-cigar-company-mocha-black.o: No detailed record of its aroma could be found.

blatter-blatter-black-cherry-cerise-noir.z: A cherry-flavored Blatter & Blatter house blend, as the name suggests; no reliable source documenting its content could be found.

just-for-him-ruins-of-isengard.z: Ruins of Isengard is one of the two Latakia-bearing blends in Just For Him's Middle-earth Pipeweed series. The name refers to the ruins left behind after Isengard's destruction in Tolkien's narrative. The blend is built on a Virginia base with a measured amount of Latakia added. Records indicate its smoky side is pronounced, though, true to the series' general character, it also carries a light sweetness. It therefore sits somewhere between a pure English blend and an aromatic. Suited to smokers wanting to get used to Latakia, or those looking for a presentation where the smoky taste isn't overwhelming.
just-for-him-ruins-of-isengard.o: Leaves a lightly sweet layer beneath an aroma of wood smoke and soot.

comptons-of-galashiels-macedonian-mixtur.z: Compton's of Galashiels is a blend series described as prepared in Scotland based on original recipes from the turn of the century; the series' general structure uses various Virginias, unflavored cavendish, Latakia, and Izmir-origin Orientals, along with rare Oriental leaves such as Yenidje and Dubec. Macedonian Mixture is the Balkan-style member of this series. What defines the blend's character is its Oriental leaves, Yenidje in particular; Latakia builds the smoky frame, while the Virginias leave a sweet base beneath. It offers an unflavored, intensely sweet, and nicotine-heavy profile. It suits smokers wanting to get to know old-style Balkan mixtures, accustomed to hearty, Oriental-heavy smokes.
comptons-of-galashiels-macedonian-mixtur.o: Leaves an incense-like smoky aroma in the room, topped with dry grass and spice.

lane-limited-1-q.z: 1-Q is a ribbon-cut aromatic blend from the American firm Lane Limited. Golden Virginia and dark cavendish form the backbone; a vanilla-forward casing opening into caramel and honey directions is applied on top. It's long been considered the best-selling bulk pipe tobacco in the US and is sold both in bulk and in tins. Since the smoke tends to arrive moist, airing it a while before lighting makes it burn more evenly; otherwise gurgling and wetness can occur. It's very light in nicotine, doesn't bite the tongue, and holds its vanilla-and-caramel line throughout the burn. Suited to those new to the aromatic side and those seeking a light, sweet, all-day blend; conversely, due to its flavoring and low fullness, it comes across as plain to smokers seeking a dark, complex taste.
lane-limited-1-q.o: Fills the room quickly with a sweet vanilla and caramel scent.

sutliff-tobacco-company-crumble-kake-lim.z: Rustica, the fifth limited edition in the Crumble Kake Barrel Aged series, combines sun-cured Nicotiana rustica leaf with lively Virginias and nutty burley. After barrel-resting, it's pressed and sliced into a crumbly cake form. The rustica variety carries markedly higher nicotine than the customary Nicotiana tabacum, giving the blend a very full body; it's prepared for experienced smokers. On the palate, earthy, herbal, and sharp tones lead. Being a limited edition, it is not in continuous production.
sutliff-tobacco-company-crumble-kake-lim.o: Leaves a sharp, earthy, herbal scorched-leaf scent.

cornell-diehl-pashas-dream.z: Pasha's Dream is a light blend Cornell & Diehl classes as English-aromatic. Caramel and vanilla casing is applied over Turkish leaf, Latakia, red Virginia, Kentucky Burley, and light-colored strands; it's a long ribbon cut. This structure brings smoky English character and sweet aromatic casing together in one bowl: Latakia's smoky base and the Oriental's dry spice sit beneath the caramel-vanilla sweetness. On the maker's scale, strength is light, flavor and room note medium. Suited to smokers wanting to move from aromatics to Latakia, or looking for a sweet layer over a smoky base.
cornell-diehl-pashas-dream.o: Leaves a scent where caramel-and-vanilla sweetness intertwines with Latakia's woody smoke.

mac-baren-latakia-rolls-limited-edition.z: Not enough information could be found in the manufacturer's current catalog or verifiable independent sources about this latakia-containing blend, which is described as a limited edition.

republic-tobacco-co-largo.z: Largo is Republic Tobacco's economy-segment line of traditional American blends built from Burley and Virginia leaf. It is described as unflavored, with options ranging from light-medium to full strength. Virginia supplies sweetness and a light spice angle, while Burley brings a nutty, earthy base. Alongside plain options like Original and the milder Mellow, the line also includes a minted variant. The shag-cut leaf is sold in resealable bags of roughly 170 grams and 450 grams. It suits smokers looking for an unflavored, uncomplicated, low-cost, all-day tobacco.
republic-tobacco-co-largo.o: Leaves a dry hay, walnut-meat, and earth aroma.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-no-11-honey-rum-.z: No source could be found documenting the leaf composition of this numbered Kohlhase & Kopp blend, understood from its name to carry honey, rum and plum casings.

gq-tobaccos-christmas-blend-2015.z: GQ Tobaccos's limited holiday blend released specially for the year 2015; there is no sourcing documenting its composition.
gq-tobaccos-christmas-blend-2015.o: No record of its aroma could be found.

mac-baren-burley-london-blend.z: Burley London Blend is a burley-forward Mac Baren blend balanced with Virginia. Its partly rubbed, ribbon-like structure of flake pieces eases packing and burning; on the flip side, since it tends to burn fast, it stays cool if smoked at a slow pace. The light cocoa and chocolate touch applied to the blend is kept to a level that doesn't mask burley's own nutty, earthy taste. With nicotine and flavor intensity between light and medium, it's a blend suited for daytime use — something habitual Virginia smokers might turn to for a change of pace.
mac-baren-burley-london-blend.o: Leaves a cocoa and roasted-tobacco mix, lightly sweetish room note.

gallaher-limited-special-virginia-rubbed.z: This is a Virginia-heavy blend Gallaher offered in rubbed-out form; not enough independent sourcing could be found regarding its composition and character.
gallaher-limited-special-virginia-rubbed.o: Leaves an aroma of dry grass and lightly sweet Virginia.

fincks-cigar-company-vintage-english.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for Finck's Cigar Company's Vintage English pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

cup-o-joes-anniversary-blend-no-23.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the Cup O' Joes brand as Anniversary Blend No. 23; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

consolidated-no-306-black-cherry.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Consolidated blend No.306 Black Cherry.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore-re.z: Finamore Regular is the plain version of the brand's base blend, also known under the name Tradicional. It is prepared from Burley and Virginia leaf at the Juiz de Fora facility; it is described as a light-colored mixture with low nicotine. In Brazil it is available in packs and tins. It carries no pronounced flavoring; on the smoke, Virginia's light sweetness and Burley's dry side lead. It suits smokers who want to steer clear of aromatics and are looking for a plain blend they can smoke throughout the day.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore-re.o: Leaves a plain tobacco scent reminiscent of dry hay and nuts.

sutliff-tobacco-company-jamestowne-tradi.z: Jamestowne Tradition Rum Mixture is a rum-flavored aromatic in Sutliff's Jamestowne Tradition line; independent sources do not provide sufficient information on its composition and production status.
sutliff-tobacco-company-jamestowne-tradi.o: Leaves the sweet scent of the rum topping.

cornell-diehl-eight-state-burley-2022.z: One of Cornell & Diehl's burley-based, vintage-dated limited releases; details are left blank as it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog and no source verifying its composition could be found.

cornell-diehl-acpc-heady-doctrine.z: This Cornell & Diehl blend, prepared in limited quantity as a club order, does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog; details cannot be given as not enough sourcing could be found to describe its content.

mcclelland-tudor-castle.z: Tudor Castle is one of McClelland's Virginia-forward flake blends. High-sugar bright Virginia and red Virginia are joined by top-quality Yenidje Oriental and Louisiana-sourced St. James Perique. The maker closed in 2018, so the blend is no longer produced. After a brief drying, the crumbled flake burns slow and cool; the Virginias' cola-and-sweet-tea-like sweetness is joined by the Oriental's salty-tangy edge and Perique's occasional peppery, ginger-like spice. Suited to those wanting an unflavored Virginia-Perique structure paired with Oriental, comfortable with flake smoking; records indicate the blend was designed for cellar aging.
mcclelland-tudor-castle.o: Leaves a dried-fruit-sweet, lightly spiced and tangy tobacco aroma.

tavern-tobacco-co-thunder-road.z: Thunder Road, a pipe tobacco from Tavern Tobacco Co.; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

comptons-of-galashiels-cuban-style-cigar.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Compton's of Galashiels blend Cuban Style Cigar Blend.

richs-retro-grandpas.z: Retro-Grandpas is a Burley-based blend from Rich's Cigar Store, a nod to old-generation pipe tobaccos. The smoke opens with a dry sweetness, and as it progresses cocoa and cinnamon notes become clearer, turning into a lightly aromatic character. The flavoring is kept light enough not to mask Burley's nutty body, which keeps the blend close to smokers familiar with the language of classic American drugstore tobaccos. Nicotine is medium, and it is sold in bulk at Rich's Portland stores.
richs-retro-grandpas.o: Leaves a trace where cocoa and cinnamon aroma meet dry, nutty tobacco.

mission-pipe-shop-shag.z: No reliable manufacturer or retailer description could be found for the blend called Shag, sold under Mission Pipe Shop's own name.

w-o-larsen-the-masters-blend-28.z: No reliable source could be found regarding the composition and character of this entry in W.Ø. Larsen's Master's Blend series; the series as a whole generally consists of light, fruit-cased blends.
w-o-larsen-the-masters-blend-28.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

peterson-special-reserve-2017.z: Special Reserve is Peterson's limited edition tin series, reworked each year. The 2017 edition tops a base of Virginia, Burley, and Cavendish leaf with a vanilla and caramel flavoring, producing a sweet mixture that could be called lightly aromatic. Nicotine strength is kept low, making it suitable for all-day smoking, and it is presented in a 100 gram tin.
peterson-special-reserve-2017.o: Leaves a vanilla and burnt-sugar caramel aroma.

the-smoker-black-noble.z: Black Noble is recorded as one of the hand-prepared house blends from The Smoker, a tobacconist that operated in Albany from the 1930s until 2011; no independent source describing the blend's composition could be found.

4noggins-prairie-wind.z: Prairie Wind is 4noggins' Virginia-Perique (VaPer) style blend. It's built by adding a notable proportion of Perique to three separate Virginia leaves; no topping is applied, and the sweetness comes entirely from the Virginia's own sugars. It offers a structure where Perique's peppery, plummy character sits on top of a cool, even-burning, tangy-sweet Virginia base. Smokers have noted it responds well to jar-aging. It suits those looking for an unflavored, all-day-smokable VaPer.
4noggins-prairie-wind.o: A thin spicy line accompanies the aroma of dry hay and baked bread.

owl-shop-bay-state.z: Referred to as one of the house blends from the Owl Shop in New Haven; no reliable source describing its composition could be found.
owl-shop-bay-state.o: No description could be found in the records.

james-barber-charlies-mixture.z: No independent source could be found to document the composition and character of Charlies Mixture, one of the aromatic house blends from the James Barber tobacconist house.
james-barber-charlies-mixture.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

stanwell-kir-apple.z: This Stanwell blend, also sold under the name Green & Indigo, combines a blackcurrant (cassis) topping — named after the Kir cocktail — with a fresh apple note. It's a mixture-cut aromatic sold in 40- and 50-gram packaging; its body is built from Virginia, burley, and black cavendish. The fruit topping is pronounced and nicotine level is low. With its thin, fruity line, it suits those seeking a light option among heavier English blends, or those who smoke aromatics exclusively. The brand originates in Denmark; part of the tobacco is produced at Scandinavian facilities in Europe.
stanwell-kir-apple.o: Leaves a scent of fresh apple and blackcurrant.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-middletons.z: Match Middleton's Cherry was prepared to correspond to John Middleton's classic cherry-flavored blend called Cherry Blend. The same blend has also been distributed by some retailers under the name Mid-Town Cherry. Virginia and black cavendish are added to a burley-forward base, with a cherry-based casing applied over it. The cherry casing is more pronounced than in the original version, with burley sitting a bit further back. Nicotine is below medium and taste intensity is medium. It burns cool and leaves a sweet trace in the mouth. It suits smokers looking for a straightforward, uncomplicated fruit-flavored aromatic.
