sutliff-tobacco-company-match-middletons.o: Leaves a pronounced cherry scent with a sweet tobacco note behind it.

new-york-pipe-club-jacks-shanty.z: Jack's Shanty is a cigar-leaf blend prepared for the New York Pipe Club, based on the personal recipe of the club's founder, Sailorman Jack. Its base is built from lemony and red Virginia leaves; a considerable share of Latakia and Perique is added on top, and the blend is rounded out with shredded cigar leaf. The dry jar aroma is sweet in a way reminiscent of English and Balkan-style mixtures, and the cut is classic ribbon. In the smoke, Virginia and Latakia lead, while the cigar leaf adds a dark, meaty undertone that pulls the blend toward a salty, smoky direction. The smoke is dense and full; nicotine and flavor sit above medium. Suitable for smokers accustomed to Latakia blends who are looking for the heavy tones of cigar leaf; it will be too strong for beginners. The blend is an example of the tradition of limited-production club blends prepared for club members.
new-york-pipe-club-jacks-shanty.o: Leaves the room with Latakia's smoky scent alongside the heavy, earthy, leather-like aroma of cigar leaf.

john-middleton-inc-prince-alberts-mellow.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Middleton, Inc's Prince Albert's Mellow Whiskey pipe tobacco.

gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-virgina-cavendis.z: Recorded as an aromatic blend from Kendal-based Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. where a chocolate topping is applied to dark Virginia and Cavendish leaf. Since no detailed independent sourcing could be found, the ratios and cut form aren't specified here.
gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-virgina-cavendis.o: Leaves a cocoa and dark-sugar aroma.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-old-port.z: A blend referred to as aromatic; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-lizzie-blood-red-engl.z: No verifiable composition and character information could be compiled for Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Lizzie Blood Red English.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-lizzie-blood-red-engl.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

e-a-carey-balkan-special.z: A record referred to as one of E. A. Carey's house blends in the Balkan line; since it does not appear in the maker's current catalog, no source could be found describing its component ratios.
e-a-carey-balkan-special.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

holger-danske-emerald-isle.z: Emerald Isle is the new name for a Holger Danske blend previously sold as Sherry and Whiskey (S.W.). Its composition includes Virginia, Burley, black Cavendish, and Oriental leaves; a honey-like sweet flavoring along with a whiskey note is applied on top. It's prepared in a wide, irregular (wild cut) cut. The light smokiness and spice brought by the Oriental leaf ties together the whiskey aroma and the black Cavendish's sweetness; Burley carries the body. Being light in nicotine, the blend suits those looking for a liqueur-flavored but not heavy aromatic. The brand is Danish in origin, with production today handled by Mac Baren.
holger-danske-emerald-isle.o: Leaves a lightly smoky aroma reminiscent of whiskey beneath honeyed sweetness.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-bright-.z: Bright Flek is a bulk flake prepared from rested bright Virginia leaf. The maker notes that the color darkens with the leaf's maturity, that no flavoring is added to the blend, and that the profile stays light to medium. It's sold as 2 oz. bulk. The brand deliberately spells its products "flek" rather than "flake" because the bulk slices don't have the pristine look of factory-boxed flakes and can arrive as broken pieces. The taste develops along unflavored Virginia's tangy-sweet, herbal, breadlike line. Because the slice is compact, it needs to be crumbled and aired out before smoking; in return it burns slow and cool. A pick for lovers of plain Virginia and those who like to cellar tobacco for extended periods.
ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-bright-.o: Leaves an unflavored tobacco aroma reminiscent of dry hay and stale bread.

bufflehead-blue-goose.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Blue Goose under the Bufflehead brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

murray-sons-co-ltd-murrays-1921-cunningh.z: One of the discontinued Virginia-Perique-centered blends from the Belfast-based Murray Sons & Co factory; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition could not be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-light-english-30.z: Sutliff 302 Light English is a ribbon-cut English blend built on Virginia leaf with oriental varieties and a small amount of Cyprus latakia added. As the name suggests, the latakia ratio is kept low; rather than taking over the blend, the smoke accompanies Virginia's bready sweetness and the orientals' dry, lightly spicy tones. With its light body and low nicotine density, it serves as an entry point for smokers new to the English mixture category, and as a mild option experienced smokers can slot in between heavier latakia blends. Being unflavored, the tobacco's own taste stays in front.
sutliff-tobacco-company-light-english-30.o: Leaves a scent of diluted wood smoke and dry grass.

fribourg-treyer-evans-blend.z: Evans Blend is a Virginia blend in the untopped wing of the Fribourg & Treyer line. Pure Virginia and unsweetened black cavendish are combined in roughly equal proportion; no other flavouring tobacco is used, and the blend is presented ribbon cut. Virginia's bright, grassy side and black cavendish's creamy softness sit side by side; the sweetness comes not from a top sauce but from the leaf's own sugar. It suits smokers who don't want Latakia or spicy toppings and are looking for a plain but full-bodied Virginia.
fribourg-treyer-evans-blend.o: Leaves a sweetish dry-grass and lightly toasted bread aroma.

motzek-scottish-blend.z: A blend the Motzek workshop calls Scottish-style; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

hickey-nicholson-classic-reserve.z: This is an aromatic mixture recorded as one of Hickey & Nicholson's house blends; no independent source describing its composition could be found.
hickey-nicholson-classic-reserve.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

campbells-smoke-shop-7-cherries-jubilee.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named #7 Cherries Jubilee under the Campbell's Smoke Shop brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

robert-mcconnell-regent-street.z: Regent Street is a Virginia-Perique blend built from long-cut dark Virginia leaf with a small amount of Perique added, presented as a ribbon cut. Because the Perique share is kept low, the blend delivers a peppery finish over an otherwise smooth, easy-flowing smoke. The tin note is sweet, almost fruity, though that sugary sweetness does not really come through in the smoking. It suits smokers entering the Virginia-Perique family or looking for Perique in moderate measure. Its mild-to-medium nicotine makes it suitable for long smoking sessions. The brand is currently produced in Germany by Kohlhase & Kopp.
robert-mcconnell-regent-street.o: Leaves a lightly peppery tobacco aroma reminiscent of dried fruit.

vantas-tabak-sir-william-aromatic.z: The aromatic option from Vantas Tabak's Sir William series; records indicate it has been discontinued, and no sufficient independent source describing the blend's composition has been found, so the record is left incomplete.

cornell-diehl-old-college.z: Not enough sourcing could be located to document the composition and character of Cornell & Diehl's Old College blend; it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog.

players-whiskey-ready-rubbed-highland-mi.z: Player's Whiskey Ready Rubbed (Highland Mixture) is a pipe tobacco blend for which there is not enough independent source material.
players-whiskey-ready-rubbed-highland-mi.o: Not enough records could be found on the room note.

cornell-diehl-jolly-old-st-nicholas-2022.z: No adequate firsthand source on the composition of this blend, the 2022 release of Cornell & Diehl's annual year-end series, could be found.

mcclelland-blending-perique.z: A single-component Louisiana Perique tobacco McClelland sold in bulk for those building their own blends; since no detailed, independent source could be found, the record is left incomplete.

mcclelland-nutty-hazel.z: Records indicate this was an aromatic within McClelland's Avenue Blend series, and it had already been placed among the products not to be restocked before the firm closed; no sufficient source documenting its contents could be found.

peretti-blend-no-52.z: Blend No.52 is a Burley blend Robert Peretti created in 1947 after returning from naval service following World War II. It stayed on sale until roughly 1960, then dropped from the catalog, and years later was brought back into production when the shop's old formula ledgers were revisited. Its composition consists of Burley, red Virginia, and a Turkish tobacco called Dubeck. Per the maker's recipe, the blend's backbone is built from Burley's deep, nutty taste; red Virginia adds a natural sweetness that softens this taste, while Dubeck, used in a small amount, being the mildest form of Turkish tobacco since it comes from the plant's top leaves, adds a fine sharpness to the mixture. With its unflavored body ranging from light to medium, it suits newcomers to Burley blends and those seeking a low-nicotine but flavor-full everyday tobacco.
peretti-blend-no-52.o: Leaves a measured aroma where a lightly sweet dried fruit and a warm grassy trace accompany the nutty Burley scent.

bennington-tobacconist-pirates-gold.z: Pirates Gold is a blend prepared by Bennington Tobacconist using the traditional rope method. Golden Virginia is combined with black Cavendish; the mixture is wrapped in whole tobacco leaves and twisted by hand, rested in cake form, then cut into very thin discs. Since this preparation compresses and matures the tobacco, the taste turns out more intense and rounder than ribbon-cut equivalents. Virginia's natural sugar and Cavendish's dark sweetness set a medium-bodied profile that could be called essentially unflavored. Since it comes as thin discs, it needs to be rubbed out or coiled into place before packing. It's aimed at smokers familiar with rope and coin-cut tobaccos.
bennington-tobacconist-pirates-gold.o: Dry hay and molasses-bread notes are joined by a faint yeasty note.

tinder-box-amaretto.z: Amaretto is one of the house blends from Tinder Box, the American tobacconist chain that has blended under its own name since 1928. Almond-based amaretto flavoring is cased over a sweetened black-Cavendish-forward body; records indicate the blend is ribbon cut and kept at average moisture. Nicotine load is low and the smoke is mellow; the almond sweetness of the casing comes forward in the mouth more than the tobacco's own taste. Suited to those new to aromatic blends and to anyone after a light tobacco to smoke all day. Tinder Box blends are mainly sold loose by weight in the chain's own stores.
tinder-box-amaretto.o: Leaves a lightly toasted-nut aroma reminiscent of sweet almond liqueur.

poschl-tabak-tilbury-full-aroma.z: Tilbury Full Aroma is positioned as the most heavily cased member of Pöschl Tabak's Tilbury line. Black Cavendish is added to a Virginia and Burley base; the ribbon-cut structure makes packing and even burning easy. Compared to other variants in the line, its flavoring load is higher, while nicotine stays light. It suits smokers who prefer a pronounced casing intensity but don't want a strong tobacco. The product is continued in 40-gram packs.
poschl-tabak-tilbury-full-aroma.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly fruity, creamy aroma.

ken-byron-ventures-mona-lisa-overdrive.z: Mona Lisa Overdrive is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

peter-heinrichs-no-78.z: No. 78 is a dark-character Peter Heinrichs blend built from a select composition of Tennessee leaf, Burley, and Oriental tobaccos. Per the maker's account, the leaves are matured under pressure for two weeks and then cut to a Cavendish width of about 1.5 millimeters. This process gives a slow, even burn and allows the pipe to be set aside and relit later without trouble. On the palate, Burley's nutty, earthy base is determining, the fire-cured leaf brings a light smoky edge, and Oriental leaf adds dry spice. Nicotine and fullness reach medium levels. It suits smokers seeking a dark, natural, full-bodied Burley smoke.
peter-heinrichs-no-78.o: Leaves a dark, nutty, and lightly smoky dry-leaf aroma.

fribourg-treyer-cut-blended-plug.z: Cut Blended Plug is the pressed Virginia blend in the Fribourg & Treyer line as continued by Kohlhase & Kopp. Pressed into plug form and sliced, the maturation during pressing gives the leaf a natural fruitiness. The body is fuller than many flue-cured blends; the untopped tobacco taste runs together with dark fruit and bread-like tones. It carries a fuller, sweeter structure than the line's Cut Virginia Plug. It suits smokers who love pressed Virginia and want a slow, long bowl.
fribourg-treyer-cut-blended-plug.o: Leaves a dark fruit and baked bread aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-windsor-80.z: Match Windsor 805 is a heavily aromatic blend built entirely of black cavendish. The casing rests on a trio of licorice root, chocolate, and walnut. Records indicate it was prepared to correspond to one of the House of Windsor brand's blends; documented information on the original blend is limited. Because it is built from a single leaf type, the tobacco character is plain and soft; the casing is what stands out. Nicotine is very low, while taste and aroma intensity are pronounced. It suits lovers of dark, sweet cavendish-based aromatics and those new to pipes; as with high-moisture blends generally, it may call for slow smoking and relighting.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-windsor-80.o: Leaves a scent at licorice and chocolate sweetness carrying a nutty note behind it.

villiger-early-day.z: Villiger's blend called Early Day is referred to in records as English-style; no reliable source could be found documenting its composition and character.

peterson-aran.z: Aran Mixture is a ribbon-cut aromatic blend that brings together ripe Virginia leaf and black Cavendish. The applied topping brings vanilla and floral notes forward; in cross-section, pieces of black Cavendish are visible among light brown ribbons. It takes its name from the Aran Islands off the west coast of Ireland. The smoke is light; nicotine strength is low and flavor intensity is moderate. Cavendish lays down a sugary, creamy base while Virginia adds a light tartness. It suits newcomers to aromatic blends, those who want to keep the risk of tongue bite low, and smokers seeking a mild tobacco for all-day smoking.
peterson-aran.o: Leaves a sweet aroma recalling vanilla pastry and floral water.

peter-heinrichs-no-35.z: No. 35 is Peter Heinrichs' aromatic house blend built on Virginia and black Cavendish. Virginia leaf provides natural sweetness and lightness, while black Cavendish adds a dark color, moisture, and a soft body; the result is a mixture that goes gently on the tongue and lights easily. On the palate a sugary, creamy base is noticeable, and nicotine strength stays low. This structure suits newcomers to the pipe and those seeking a not-too-heavy sweet smoke through the day. Since the flavoring level isn't excessively high, the leaf's taste isn't fully masked.
peter-heinrichs-no-35.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and roasted sugar aroma.

dan-tobacco-shamrock.z: This is a pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source about the blend's composition and character could be found, so no detail is given.

cornell-diehl-black-satin.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Cornell & Diehl blend Black Satin.

cornell-diehl-uss-nassau-lha-4.z: No verifiable listing could be found in the maker's current catalogue or retailer listings for this blend, referred to as one of Cornell & Diehl's entries dedicated to navy ships.

w-o-larsen-aromatica.z: Aromatica is one of the aromatic blends known under the Danish-origin W.Ø. Larsen name; no sufficient source could be found regarding its composition and character.
w-o-larsen-aromatica.o: No reliable information could be found regarding the room note.

gawith-hoggarth-co-black-brown.z: Black & Brown is a record in Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s bulk line, also known as "Mixture No. 5." Its structure is simple: brown Virginia leaf is combined side by side with black cavendish, with no heavy flavouring applied. The smoke is described as cool and creamy; it is not, however, light in nicotine, being a full-bodied Kendal-style tobacco. This is a good record for those who like a plain cavendish-Virginia line and want to stay away from heavily essenced Lakeland blends.
gawith-hoggarth-co-black-brown.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, faintly toasted-sugar and dry-tobacco aroma.

peter-stokkebye-turkish-export-no-84.z: Turkish Export is built by blending sun-cured Samsun-type Turkish tobacco with ripe Virginias, and is one of the best-known records of the line Peter Stokkebye established in the 1970s. It carries no flavoring. Sources indicate it is offered in two cuts: a fine ribbon sold in bulk and a fine shag sold in pouches. On the palate, the Turkish tobacco's spicy, dry, lightly tart taste leads; Virginia stays in the background as a faint sweetness. It burns comfortably and gives plenty of smoke; because of its fine cut, it smokes fast and the bowl is prone to overheating. It is used both by those seeking Oriental taste on its own and by those blending their own mixtures as a base or seasoning leaf.
peter-stokkebye-turkish-export-no-84.o: Fills the room with a pronounced, spicy, dry-grass-like Turkish tobacco aroma.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-escudo-na.z: Escudo Navy De Luxe is one of the best-known coin-cut Virginia-perique blends. Virginia leaves are rolled together with perique into a rope and aged, then sliced into thin coins; hence the cut is also called bullseye or spun cut. No casing is applied. Long produced under the A&C Petersen name, it is now continued under the Scandinavian Tobacco Group umbrella. On the smoke, virginia's full, sweet taste leads by a few steps; perique builds a sharp, black-pepper-like layer in the background. Moisture is reasonable, the burn even and cool. Suited to smokers seeking a medium-strength, unflavored, pure virginia-perique structure.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-escudo-na.o: A sharp black-pepper trace mixes into a sweet-and-sour, dry-hay scent.

lane-limited-up-all-night.z: Referred to as an aromatic blend registered under Lane Limited; no reliable source describing its contents or character could be found.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore-bu.z: Finamore's cherry-flavored version is prepared by working a cherry essence into the Burley and Virginia body the brand uses at its Juiz de Fora production. As its name indicates, the blend's skeleton is unchanged — what distinguishes it is the flavoring. On the smoke, the cherry note is pronounced, while the tobacco's dry side forms a light backdrop; nicotine is low. It suits smokers who like fruity aromatics and want a blend that isn't heavy-bodied.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore-bu.o: Leaves a sweet fruity scent reminiscent of cherry liqueur.

thomas-radford-daily-dream.z: One of the aromatic blends in the Thomas Radford line, prepared for London's Harrow-based Radford Tobacco Limited; per the practice of the period, the tobacco was blended in Germany. Today only old tins are seen in the collectors' market; no primary source detailing its composition has been found, so the record is left incomplete.
thomas-radford-daily-dream.o: Records describe it as leaving a sweetish, fruity aroma.

motzek-am7b5.z: Since neither the manufacturer's own description nor two independent reliable sources could be found for the Motzek blend called Am7b5, its composition, cut, and character could not be documented here.

fincks-cigar-company-fincks-golden-caven.z: This is a cavendish-based blend Finck Cigar Company sells under its own name in its San Antonio shops; no reliable source describing its composition could be found.

planta-planta-number-1.z: Planta Number 1, carrying the production house's own name, is a mellow aromatic and one of the best-known members of its catalogue. Most of its body is built from double-fermented black Cavendish rested in a special casing of red wine, fruit extracts, and spices; golden Virginia joins it. In the flavor line, vanilla and rum notes stand out alongside the wine-fruit-spice trio. Nicotine is low and the smoke mellow. It suits smokers looking for sweet, spicy German-Danish-style Cavendish mixtures, as well as newcomers to the pipe; it is sold in various package sizes.
planta-planta-number-1.o: Leaves a sweet red wine, vanilla, and dried-fruit aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-eastfarthing.z: Eastfarthing, part of Sutliff's Private Stock line, is a mixture that blends the aromatic and English blending traditions. A base of stoved burley, mature red Virginia, and rested Cyprus latakia is rounded out with a light vanilla-based top note. The ribbon cut consists predominantly of brown, dark brown, and black leaves, with bright golden strands appearing here and there. Its name comes from the eastern region of the Shire in J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings. The smoke carries a sweet, soft body; because the latakia ratio is kept low, the smoky character stays at the level of a noticeable wood-smoke hint, and the vanilla note recedes in the final third of the bowl. With its light nicotine strength, it serves as a suitable stepping stone for smokers wanting to transition into latakia blends or move past aromatics into smoky flavors.
sutliff-tobacco-company-eastfarthing.o: Leaves a thin wood-smoke scent beneath a vanilla sweetness.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-celtic-twilight.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Celtic Twilight blend.

smokers-pride-rum-cured.z: Rum Cured is the rum-flavored record in the Smoker's Pride line. Burley and black cavendish lead the body; the Virginia share establishes a sweet base. The leaf is processed with a rum-direction casing, producing a sweetness reminiscent of brown sugar. The blend is presented in ribbon cut in large packaging. Thanks to the burley share, the taste doesn't stay entirely on a sugary line; a roasted, nutty base sits beneath it. Nicotine is in the medium-low band, and the smoke is cool. Suited to smokers seeking a rum interpretation of classic American everyday aromatics and wanting a soft blend for all-day smoking.
smokers-pride-rum-cured.o: Leaves a scent of sweet rum and brown sugar.

chief-catoonah-tobacconist-charlottesvil.z: The entry has been left incomplete as no reliable source could be found for Chief Catoonah Tobacconist's Charlottesville Mixture blend.

century-black-cherry.z: A cherry-flavored blend in the Century line; details of content, cut and character have been left blank as no sufficient independent source could be found.
century-black-cherry.o: Reported to carry a cherry aroma.

hearth-home-fleet-commander.z: Fleet Commander is a classically structured English mixture in Hearth & Home's Marquee series. It is built from Cyprian Latakia, salty-spicy Orientals, and select Virginia leaf, with no topping used. The blend keeps the traditional English balance between smoke and sweetness: Latakia provides body and woody smoke, the Orientals carry spice and dry-hay tones, and the Virginia supplies background sweetness. Aimed at smokers accustomed to Latakia mixtures who want a balanced English blend suitable for all-day smoking. The brand is US-based and the blend is offered as a ribbon cut.
hearth-home-fleet-commander.o: Leaves an aroma of pine smoke and dry spice.

cornell-diehl-warped-the-haunting.z: The Haunting is a cigar-leaf-based blend Warped founder Kyle Gellis and Cornell & Diehl head blender Jeremy Reeves introduced in 2019. Its weight is carried by AA-grade Dominican Criollo cigar leaf, joined by Virginia leaf and black Cavendish made from Dominican cigar leaf. It contains no Latakia; it's offered both ribbon cut and pressed into crumble cake. Its profile is described as a dark one, with Virginia's natural sweetness layered over leather and measured spice notes, carrying earthy and tangy edges. Nicotine sits below medium. Aimed at cigar smokers looking for a similar texture in a pipe, or those leaning toward intense Latakia-free blends.
cornell-diehl-warped-the-haunting.o: Leaves a leather-and-spice-heavy cigar scent with a dark sweetness behind it.

old-virginia-tobacco-co-london-night.z: London Night is among Old Virginia Tobacco Co.'s labeled blends and is classified in records as an English-style mixture; no detailed source about its composition could be found.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-senior-ch.z: Senior Chief is noted among the house blends of The Country Squire Tobacconist in Jackson, Mississippi, as an aromatic mixture; since no source documenting its composition and character has been found, no further detail is given.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-senior-ch.o: No described room note has been found in records.

gawith-hoggarth-co-rum-and-maple-r-m.z: Rum and Maple is a Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. aromatic sold under the abbreviation "R & M" following naming regulations in the United Kingdom. The base is built from Virginia and Cavendish leaf; after the mixture is pressed, it's offered as broken flake, topped with a rum-and-maple axis flavoring. The rum topping is dark and syrupy, while maple brings a rounder sweetness; given the pressed structure, the burn is slow and cool. Suited to smokers who love classic English rum aromatics and want a tobacco with a pronounced topping that still keeps its flake texture. The same producer's product called Rum Flake also carries a rum-and-maple sauce; these two entries are closely related.
gawith-hoggarth-co-rum-and-maple-r-m.o: Leaves a dark aroma carrying rum and maple syrup sweetness.

chris-morgan-jackalope.z: Jackalope is an unflavored blend prepared by slowly toasting light Virginia leaves to darken them and then pressing them into a cake. The heat treatment caramelizes the leaf's own sugars; the result brings together caramel sweetness with dark fruit, giving an intense but not sharp taste. The cake is dark chocolate in color and can be broken apart by hand, though a portion still needs to be cut and rubbed out. It burns slow and cool. The blend belongs to the series pipe maker Chris Morgan prepared with the Sutliff Tobacco Company and is tinned as two cake slices. It is aimed at those wanting to follow the toasted, darkened form of unsauced Virginia over a long smoke.
chris-morgan-jackalope.o: A light grassy trace accompanies an aroma of caramelized sugar and fig.

james-b-russell-diplomat.z: Records indicate Diplomat was one of the premium tinned tobaccos from the New Jersey-based tobacco importer James B. Russell; no independent source documenting the blend's composition could be found.
james-b-russell-diplomat.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

mullins-westley-ltd-mullins-mixture.z: One of the blends sold under its own name by the Mullins & Westley tobacconist in London's Covent Garden; sufficient sources describing its composition and character could not be found.

national-tobacco-red-cap.z: For National Tobacco's blend called Red Cap, sufficient independent sources describing its composition and character could not be found.

pipes-pleasures-black-treasure.z: Pipes & Pleasures is a tobacconist shop opened in Columbus, Ohio, in 1977; Black Treasure is one of the blends the shop offers under its own name, though no sufficient sources describing the blend's content and character could be found.

mission-pipe-shop-english-oriental.z: English Oriental is a house blend in Mission Pipe Shop's English-style line, with the Oriental share brought forward; no accessible source documenting its detailed composition could be found.

tewksbury-company-hobbits-weed.z: No reliable source could be found on Tewksbury & Company's Hobbit's Weed pipe blend.

tinder-box-connoisseur.z: Connoisseur is one of the catalog-exclusive blends sold at Tinder Box stores; no verifiable source on its composition and character has been found.
tinder-box-connoisseur.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

house-of-calabash-for-meershaums-only-re.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for House of Calabash's For Meershaums Only - Reserve Blend, so its content and character could not be recorded.

mac-baren-modern-virginia-flake.z: Modern Virginia Flake is Mac Baren's product presenting its Virginia-forward blend in pressed slice form. Per the stated ratio, roughly seventy percent of the blend is made up of two Virginia types: light-colored and dark leaves from different countries. To this, twenty percent black Cavendish made by the maker from Virginia leaf, called "Modern Cavendish," and ten percent Burley are added. Burley is used to balance the sweetness and cut Virginia's tendency to burn hot. The blend carries a light top note reminiscent of ripe fruit. For the slices, the tobacco is pressed into a block and rested for at least thirty days before cutting; the cut flakes are hand-packed so they don't break. In the smoke, hay and dried-fruit tones like raisin and fig come forward. Nicotine level is measured and the burn is cool. Suited to those who like Virginia character but want a somewhat milder smoke than fully unflavored blends.
mac-baren-modern-virginia-flake.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of dry hay and raisin.

gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-flake-aromatic.z: Dark Flake Aromatic is a strong flake blend where Malawi- and Indian-origin fire-cured dark leaves are combined in equal proportions and pressed. It rests on the same body as unflavored Dark Flake; the difference is the application of traditional English sauces based on licorice root, maple, and tonka bean. The slices are dark-colored, heavy, and oily. On the smoke, the fire-cured leaf's smoky, spicy taste leads; the topping doesn't mask it but lays a measured sweetness underneath. Nicotine is among the brand's highest examples, and the smoke is filling. It burns slowly, and the slices need to be rubbed out and aired. An entry suited to experienced smokers who love dark, strong tobaccos and want a light sweetness added to them.
gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-flake-aromatic.o: The sweet, spicy tone of licorice root and maple layers over a heavy smoke aroma.

watch-city-cigar-santas-sack.z: This is one of Watch City Cigar's seasonal blends timed to the holiday season; no sufficient source could be found regarding its composition.
watch-city-cigar-santas-sack.o: No record could be found regarding the room note.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-mellow-mixture.z: Mellow Mixture is a loose-cut Orlik blend combining matured golden Virginia leaf with two distinct types of black cavendish. Toasted burley also goes into the mixture. It's given a chocolate-and-caramel-direction topping. Using two different cavendishes layers the blend's sweet side; Virginia leaves a light tartness behind it, while burley leaves a mellow body. The topping is pronounced but described as not entirely masking the leaf's taste. Nicotine is low and the smoke cool. It's aimed at those who love chocolate-caramel aromatics and want a mellow everyday blend.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-mellow-mixture.o: Leaves a cocoa-and-caramel scent on a sweet cavendish base.

sentimiento-nacional-regular-ii.z: The second blend in Sentimiento Nacional's Regular series; no independent source describing its content and character could be found.
sentimiento-nacional-regular-ii.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-ts-20-louisiana-.z: TS-20 is the pure Louisiana perique product Sutliff sells as a blending component. Perique is a tobacco grown in and unique to the St. James Parish region of Louisiana; after harvest it is packed under pressure in barrels and undergoes heat and fermentation. This process gives the leaf its distinctive peppery, fruity character. Sutliff offers this tobacco ribbon cut. It is not designed to be smoked on its own; its nicotine and taste intensity are very high. It is generally added in small proportions to Virginia-based blends to bring in spice, plum, and fig notes. It is one of the essential components for smokers who prepare their own blends.
sutliff-tobacco-company-ts-20-louisiana-.o: Leaves a sharp scent of black pepper, vinegary plum, and fermented fruit.

benson-hedges-special-mellow-virginia.z: Sold for a long time as Mellow Virginia before later taking the name Special Virginia, this blend contains air-cured Burley and Kentucky alongside Virginia leaf. It's presented ready rubbed, meaning it needs no further rubbing out before packing. A light topping evoking honey, citrus, and vanilla is applied over it, bringing out Virginia's natural sweetness while softening any sharpness. It's an everyday blend widely found in 50-gram pouches on the UK market. It suits smokers looking for a grassy, lightly sweet, medium-bodied smoke who want a straightforward Virginia character without turning to complex English blends. The Burley and Kentucky component gives the blend a more pronounced fullness than a purely Virginia-based tobacco.
benson-hedges-special-mellow-virginia.o: Leaves a dry-hay room note carrying a light citrus-and-honey sweetness.

w-o-larsen-limited-edition-2009.z: No independent source sufficient to complete a record could be found regarding W.O. Larsen's Limited Edition 2009 blend, so this entry remains incomplete.

theodorus-niemeyer-neptune.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Theodorus Niemeyer pipe tobacco called Neptune to record the blend's composition and character.

e-a-carey-black-aromatic.z: This blend, sold under the name Classic Black Aromatic, is the aromatic E. A. Carey developed in the 1970s and has kept at the center of its catalog for many years. Per the maker's page, the blend is prepared by resting two distinct toasted black cavendish leaves together in their own natural juices; this process gives the leaf a deep, nearly all-black color. On the smoke side, cavendish sweetness is pronounced while nicotine is kept light. Due to the leaf's moist, dark structure, it burns slowly, requiring patient packing and occasional relighting. It suits smokers who don't want heavy nicotine but want a sweet, strongly scented everyday tobacco.
e-a-carey-black-aromatic.o: Leaves a dark scent evoking sweet, lightly burnt sugar and dried fruit.

uhles-old-shoe-blend.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend called Old Shoe Blend has been found.
uhles-old-shoe-blend.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

e-a-carey-english-oriental-supreme.z: English Oriental Supreme is E. A. Carey's moderate English mixture in the catalog. Per the maker's description, Georgia Virginias, black cavendish, imported burley leaves and Cyprus latakia are combined; the cut is described as medium cavendish and loose cut. The blend is unadulterated; while latakia is present, its proportion stays below classic heavy English mixtures, so the smoky taste is balanced by cavendish sweetness. It is light to medium in nicotine. It suits those seeking a measured entry to latakia blends and those wanting an everyday English mixture where smoke isn't the main feature.
e-a-carey-english-oriental-supreme.o: Leaves a sweetish trace alongside light soot and toasted wood scent.

sutliff-tobacco-company-smoker-friendly-.z: Jamaican Rum is one of the bulk aromatics Sutliff produces for the Smoker Friendly retail chain. Sources list it in the aromatic class and note that its base rests predominantly on dark burley, with a Jamaican-rum-character casing applied over it. It is ribbon cut. The rum casing stands out in the first puffs, after which the dark burley's nutty, earthy taste becomes dominant; because of this it is positioned as an aromatic with a pronounced tobacco taste rather than a sugary one. Nicotine runs on the high side because of the burley weight. Being sold in bulk, it can carry excess moisture; sources recommend airing it for a while before lighting.
sutliff-tobacco-company-smoker-friendly-.o: Leaves a dark, baked tobacco scent sitting atop rum and molasses sweetness.

paul-olsen-blue-queen.z: No reliable source could be found for the Paul Olsen pipe tobacco called Blue Queen, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

solani-131-red-label.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Solani blend 131: Red Label could not be found.

milan-tobacconists-sheiks-delight.z: Sheik's Delight is an unflavored mixture in Milan Tobacconists' English-style line. According to the maker's profile, a generous amount of Virginia, latakia, and perique come together, joined by a pinch of burley, a small amount of Turkish leaf, and toasted black cavendish. Latakia's smokiness and perique's spicy fruit tone sit over the virginia sweetness, while the cavendish share smooths the transitions. With its light-to-medium body, it can serve as an entry point for those newly moving into latakia blends, while also appealing to those wanting a complex but not heavy English mixture. Nicotine sits at a medium level.
milan-tobacconists-sheiks-delight.o: Leaves a faint wood-smoke and dry-leaf aroma.

hearth-home-bright-night.z: Bright Night is an unflavored Virginia blend prepared under Hearth & Home, signed by blender Russ Ouellette. It contains only a single type of tobacco: different Virginia leaves are pressed, rested in a press for about a month, and then offered as a crumble cake. This production method concentrates the leaves' sugars and gathers the flavor onto a single line. The blend is aimed at those wanting Virginia's bready, fruity sweetness without any topping. Since the cake tobacco can be rubbed out by hand to the desired thickness, moisture and burn speed can be adjusted to the smoker's preference. The Hearth & Home brand is produced in the US at Sutliff facilities.
hearth-home-bright-night.o: Leaves a sweetish tobacco aroma reminiscent of dry hay and honey.

mcclelland-celebrated-sovereign.z: Celebrated Sovereign is an English-type blend in the Revival series McClelland produced for Ashton. Records indicate its contents hold Syrian Latakia, an Oriental tobacco known as Dubec, black Cavendish, and Carolina and red Virginia. Syrian Latakia gives a milder, more spiced smokiness than Cyprian Latakia; the Cavendish and Virginia build a sweet base beneath this smoky layer. Suited to smokers who love Latakia-forward blends but want a rounder profile rather than a sharp smokiness. Since Syrian Latakia supply became difficult and the brand halted production in 2018, it's found only in old stock.
mcclelland-celebrated-sovereign.o: A lightly sweet background accompanies an aroma of smoked wood and spice.

milan-tobacconists-reflections.z: Reflections is among Milan Tobacconists' heavily cased aromatics. According to the maker's profile, a light-to-medium-bodied base of burley, Virginia, and black cavendish leaves is topped with a casing in the direction of vanilla, caramel, sweet cream, nutmeg, and a light spice. The burley share leaves a dry, nutty base beneath the sugared casing. Suitable for those looking for a complex but not harsh aromatic where sweet and spiced casings run together. Because of its spice note, it's a character particularly suited to cooler-season smoking.
milan-tobacconists-reflections.o: Leaves a sweet aroma of caramel, sweet cream, and nutmeg.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-butterf.z: An aromatic blend released under Ken Byron Ventures' Mr. Christian's line; no accessible source could be found to document its contents.

peterson-summertime-2012.z: Summertime 2012 is a limited edition blend released as part of Peterson's Summertime series specific to that year; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient first-hand sources confirming its content and character could be found.

with-pipe-and-book-brecks-mixture.z: Breck's Mixture is a house blend named after Breck Turner, founder of the With Pipe and Book shop in Lake Placid; no verifiable source could be found regarding its composition and character.
with-pipe-and-book-brecks-mixture.o: No confirmed description of the room note could be found.

ravenwood-fine-provisions-twilight-rever.z: This is a tobacco in the Ravenwood Fine Provisions line, offered in a 50-gram tin and marketed by the maker as a mellowed, Oriental-heavy English blend; a detailed specification of the ingredient proportions and cut has not been published.

uhles-raider-blend.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend called Raider Blend has been found.
uhles-raider-blend.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

mac-baren-virginia-no-1.z: Virginia No. 1 is a blend Mac Baren introduced in 1955 and counts among its classics. Its contents consist solely of Virginia leaves; it's presented ready-rubbed, so it can be packed directly straight from the tin. Moisture is set to a smoke-ready level, it lights easily, and leaves a light gray ash. Despite being pure Virginia, it carries a honey-and-sugar-based sweetening; this flavoring adds a sweetness distinguishable from the leaf's own natural sugar. Nicotine load is low, flavor intensity limited, and a faintly bitter edge can appear in the first part of the smoke. It's also prone to running hot quickly, so it needs to be smoked slowly. Suited to those seeking a light, flavored, non-fatiguing Virginia and to those new to the pipe.
mac-baren-virginia-no-1.o: Leaves a mild tobacco aroma carrying a light honey sweetness.

gawith-hoggarth-co-coniston-cut-plug.z: Coniston Cut Plug is one of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s classic plug tobaccos built on fire-cured leaf. Records indicate roughly three-quarters of the mix is dark fire-cured leaf, with the remainder split equally between Malawi Burley and Virginia. After the mixture is pressed and cut, it is broken into broken-flake form; this coarse structure gives a slow, cool burn. A light Lakeland topping reminiscent of clove is applied; the topping doesn't mask the tobacco taste but adds a sweet, floral edge to it. In the smoke, the smoky, woody body of the fire-cured leaf leads. Within the brand's dark trio, it carries a more measured strength than Dark Flake and Bosun, so it can be seen as a gateway into blends built on fire-cured leaf. Still, the nicotine load is notable and may be heavy for newcomers.
gawith-hoggarth-co-coniston-cut-plug.o: A clove-scented, floral, soapy tone settles over the smoky, woody aroma.

mac-baren-red-velvet.z: No content or character information could be found for the Red Velvet blend attributed to Mac Baren, either on the maker's own product pages or in reliable retailer records.
mac-baren-red-velvet.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-english-gold-y.z: English Gold is a blend produced under the Orlik label, classified in records as straight Virginia and known by its yellow pack; no published description of its composition could be found.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.z: This is a blend in the Brazilian maker Imigrantes's Candido Giovanella line, presented, as the name suggests, unflavored; no independent source verifying its content could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.o: No room note described in the records could be found.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-winter-tobacco.z: A name referred to among Kohlhase & Kopp's winter aromatic releases; no verifiable source could be found documenting the contents and character of the blend sold under this name.

karl-erik-private-blend-no-14.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Karl Erik's Private Blend No.14.

dan-tobacco-salty-dogs.z: Salty Dogs is a classic plug blend tied to seafaring tradition. Selected sweet Virginia grades and a small amount of perique are flavored with Caribbean rum and pressed into pocket-sized blocks, aged for a long time under press. The result is a dark brown, tightly textured tobacco. The smoke is cool and soft; Virginia's sweetness combines with the dark sugar tone from the rum, while perique adds a peppery spice. Being plug, it needs to be sliced and rubbed out before packing, meaning extra work before filling. It suits those seeking the pressed Virginia/perique structure and lightly flavored navy-style tobaccos.
dan-tobacco-salty-dogs.o: Leaves a trace where dark sugar and rum scent meet a tart tobacco scent.

comoys-of-london-irish-mixture.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Comoy's of London blend Irish Mixture.

abenaki-tobacco-co-vanilla-custard.z: A vanilla-themed aromatic blend registered under the Abenaki Tobacco Co. name; no adequate source verifying its content could be found.

borkum-riff-limited-edition-36-mixture-c.z: A California-wine-flavored version in Borkum Riff's limited-run numbered blend series. No reliable source on its composition could be found, leaving the profile incomplete.
borkum-riff-limited-edition-36-mixture-c.o: According to records it leaves a sweetish room note reminiscent of wine.

roland-after-dark.z: After Dark is one of the Latakia-containing blends from the Japanese Roland brand. Here Latakia is used in measured proportion rather than raw and sharp; instead of pushing the smoky layer forward, the mixture balances it with Virginia sweetness and Oriental leaf spice. As the name suggests, it is meant for evening smoking, building a character that is not heavy but calm and cohesive. It sits stronger than the brand's blend called Before Dark. The Roland brand belongs to the Fukashiro company, whose roots go back to 1924, built on a tradition associated with the Ginza Kikusui house in Tokyo and pipe maker Fukashiro Tsutomu. It suits fans of Latakia blends who don't want the smoke load to dominate. Its unflavored composition means it doesn't appeal to aromatic seekers.
roland-after-dark.o: Leaves a soft aroma of wood smoke and incense.

pipa-whiskey.z: No sources documenting the content or maker of the Whiskey blend recorded under the Pipa name could be found.

mostex-stanislaw-danish-blend.z: No independent, verifiable source describing the composition of this blend, released under the Stanislaw brand of the Brno-based maker Mostex, could be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-pipa-vani.z: Pipa is a starter kit prepared by Lane, Scandinavian Tobacco Group's US arm, to introduce cigarette and cigar smokers to the pipe. The box yields roughly 40 grams of vanilla cavendish blend, a corncob pipe, and a short guide on smoking a pipe. The blend is a flavored, black-cavendish-forward, ribbon-cut aromatic; vanilla is applied on top. Its nicotine is low and it does not bite the tongue, designed for a first pipe try. No longer distributed as a set.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-pipa-vani.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough scent.

the-smoker-new-york-new-york.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the The Smoker pipe tobacco called New York, New York to record the blend's composition and character.

emerson-southern-forged-kilkenny.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing was found for the Emerson Southern Forged brand's Kilkenny blend, so the entry has been left open; records place it in the Straight Virginia family.

american-tobacco-co-blue-boar-rough-cut.z: Blue Boar is a classic American mass-market blend produced by the American Tobacco Company for much of the twentieth century. Its coarse-cut namesake version is based on combining differently processed Burley leaves with light Virginia; a very small amount of Latakia is added to give a smoky edge. This structure exemplifies the era's in-between type known as "American-style English": body comes from the Burley, with Latakia decorative rather than dominant. The coarse-cut leaf, packed loosely into the bowl, allows generous airflow and gives a cool smoke. The taste is medium-intense; Burley's nutty, bready base is balanced by Virginia's measured sweetness. Per records the brand was discontinued long ago; today's products carrying the same name are imitation mixtures prepared to stand in for the original blend. It's considered a measured option for everyday smoking, suited to smokers cautious about smoky blends.
american-tobacco-co-blue-boar-rough-cut.o: Leaves a room note of toasted bread and lightly smoky wood.

davidoff-argentina-cavendish.z: Argentina Cavendish is an aromatic blend in Davidoff's Discovery series. It consists of very finely cut black Cavendish and bright-toned Virginia ribbons, ribbon cut. On opening the pack, a sharp, intense scent evoking artificial fruit candy stands out; the tobacco is at a suitable moisture for smoking and catches easily. It gives a cool smoke and doesn't bite the tongue; the nicotine load stays light while the sugary taste lingers in the mouth. Airflow and jar-resting notably change the blend. The synthetic sugar bouquet recedes, replaced by an aroma evoking honey; the soft Virginia taste balanced by the Cavendish, along with mango, papaya-like citrus and floral tones, become distinguishable. It suits those seeking a sweet, direct aromatic rather than a nuanced Virginia experience, and those drawn to Danish-type Cavendish blends.
davidoff-argentina-cavendish.o: Leaves a sweet scent evoking sugary fruit candy and floral honey tones.

tinder-box-cherry-almond.z: Tinder Box is the name of an American tobacconist chain founded in 1928 that sells blends prepared for its own shops under its own name; Cherry Almond is one of these house blends, though no sufficient independent source describing its composition and character has been found.

charatan-purple.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the British pipe maker Charatan.

fincks-cigar-company-istanbul.z: This is an English-style mixture among Finck Cigar Company's shop blends, its name referencing Istanbul; no reliable source describing its composition could be found.

paul-olsen-no-d2771.z: One of the Virginia-forward blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

mccranies-old-syrian.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found on Old Syrian, one of McCranie's Pipe Shop's house blends.
mccranies-old-syrian.o: No reliable description of the aroma could be found.

dunhill-a-21000.z: A-21000 is a vanilla-sauced cavendish mixture among Dunhill's shop blends. Its base is burley and black cavendish, with Virginia staying in the background. The pouch carries a scent evoking raisin, vanilla and caramel; on the smoke, vanilla and woody tobacco taste move side by side. It's a cool-burning blend that doesn't harshen the tongue and stays light in nicotine; this makes it suitable for any hour of the day. It suits those who love vanilla aromatics but avoid heavy, sticky sauces. Per records, the blend was sold only through Dunhill shops; it remained available in London for a while after the brand's tobacco production ended.
dunhill-a-21000.o: Vanilla and light caramel scent is accompanied by a woody tobacco note.

rattray-terry-red.z: Terry Red is an aromatic blend carried under the Rattray name; no reliable source could be found on its content and character, so no detailed specification is given.
rattray-terry-red.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity tobacco aroma.

telfords-pipes-cigars-nob-hill.z: One of roughly forty house blends prepared by Telford's Pipe & Cigar shop in Mill Valley, California; no accessible source describing the blend's composition and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-cherry-br.z: Referred to as a cherry-and-brandy-flavored version within the Kendal Gold shag series; no reliable sourcing giving details specific to this version's composition and character could be found.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-cherry-br.o: Leaves a cherry and spirit-touched fruit aroma.

e-a-carey-buttercream-delight.z: Buttercream Delight (listed in the maker's catalog with the spelling "Buttercreame Delight") is a mild aromatic within the eponymous blend line of E. A. Carey, an Ohio-based American tobacco and pipe retailer. Per the maker's description, it is flavored with a soft, buttery topping and presented flake cut; this cut makes it easy to pack into a pipe and ensures an even burn. The nicotine load is low and the flavor profile is sweet and creamy; because the topping is pronounced, the blend sits in the upper-middle rung of the aromatic world. It suits those seeking a light, sweet, all-day aromatic and newcomers to the pipe. Like some Carey blends, it is prepared from imported leaf and sold in bulk and small tin sizes.
e-a-carey-buttercream-delight.o: Leaves a sweet, milky scent evoking butter.

sterling-tobacco-co-double-eagle.z: Double Eagle is a blend in Sterling Tobacco's light aromatic wing, based on air-cured cube-cut burley. Its structure is described as reminiscent of older-generation American codex tobaccos, particularly the Prince Albert and Edgeworth line. The cube cut gives a slow, cool burn; the topping consists of just a light flavoring evoking an after-dinner liqueur. Nicotine level is low and the flavor line stays straightforward, built on burley's nutty character. A suitable everyday blend for those seeking a cool smoke while steering clear of heavily topped aromatics.
sterling-tobacco-co-double-eagle.o: A light sweet liqueur trace accompanies a nutty burley scent.

owl-shop-mystique.z: Listed as the Owl Shop's best-selling house blend; though described as a full-bodied aromatic, no source stating its leaf composition could be found.
owl-shop-mystique.o: Leaves a pronounced, sweet aromatic scent.

lane-limited-black-raspberry.z: Black Raspberry is Lane Limited's fruit-flavored ribbon-cut blend. A sweet, baked dark cavendish core is accompanied by Virginia and softened burley; a black raspberry essence is applied on top. The casing is pronounced and stands out both in the pack scent and in the smoke. Nicotine is light, and it's a cool-burning blend. Suited to smokers who love fruity aromatics and want a sweet presentation that overrides the leaf's own taste; it's far from the line of those seeking unflavored blends.
lane-limited-black-raspberry.o: Leaves a sharp, sweet fruit room note reminiscent of black raspberry jam.

consolidated-b-25-dark-chocolate.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Consolidated blend B-25: Dark Chocolate.

former-private-flake.z: Private Flake is a plug-cut blend in the aromatic wing of the line named after Danish pipe maker Former. It combines various Virginia leaves of US, African, and Indian origin with burley; records indicate the sauce is made from fig, tamarind, hazelnut, truffle, and apple syrup extracts as a top aroma. The topping is kept at a level that adds a fruity base to the leaf's own taste rather than masking it, so the blend behaves less like a classic heavy aromatic and more like a lightly sauced Virginia-burley plug. It suits smokers who enjoy rubbing out and filling a plug, who don't want full aromatic intensity but aren't looking for a fully untopped tobacco either.
former-private-flake.o: Leaves an aroma of dried fruit and sweet pastry dough.

super-value-natural-cavendish.z: Super Value Natural Cavendish is a mixture in the line without a pronounced fruit or liqueur flavoring, relying on the cavendish-processed leaf's own sweetness. It consists of coarse-cut burley, Virginia, and cavendish leaf and is produced in the US. It offers a light-bodied, soft, straightforward smoke. Appeals to those seeking a low-topping, plain everyday tobacco.
super-value-natural-cavendish.o: Leaves a plain, lightly sweet tobacco scent.

g-l-pease-mephisto.z: Mephisto is among the first blends offered under the G. L. Pease name. It is a mixed-cut blend combining dark-looking broken flake, ribbon, and coarsely cut pieces. Syrian latakia is used in its composition, joined by Cyprus latakia and Oriental leaves; records also note a light rum top note. The smoke is reported to be rich, sweet, and spicy; Syrian latakia's distinctive aroma stays beneath the Cyprus latakia and Oriental leaves. In a warehouse fire in November 2004, the aged Syrian latakia stock used in the blend was destroyed, and production was halted indefinitely as a result; it has been announced that the blend will return if sufficient quality Syrian leaf becomes available.
g-l-pease-mephisto.o: Leaves a smoky aroma reminiscent of campfire, lightly sweet and spicy.

samuel-gawith-perfection.z: Perfection is a ribbon-cut English blend Samuel Gawith produces in Kendal. Its composition holds Virginia, Izmir-type Oriental leaf, and Latakia; a fine vanilla casing is also applied to the blend. According to the producer's account, the blend was prepared for a local smoker who couldn't find a tobacco to his taste, and satisfaction with the result became the source of the product's name. The Virginia leaf is steam-processed; this treatment preserves the leaf's grassy character while cooling the smoke. At the center of the flavor line sits the Oriental leaf's spicy, creamy tone; Virginia contributes sweetness, and Latakia adds a measured smokiness. The vanilla casing is not dominant enough to place the blend in the aromatic class, only sharpening the sweetness. Nicotine is in the light-to-medium range. Fits smokers newly approaching Latakia or seeking an Oriental-forward, undemanding English blend.
samuel-gawith-perfection.o: Leaves a spicy scent where light smoke meets sweet vanilla.

d-r-tobacco-rimboche-a-p.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of D & R Tobacco's Rimboché A.P. blend were found.

peretti-blend-no-33.z: Blend No.33 is one of L.J. Peretti's numbered Burley blends; since the maker's product page gives no detailed description, no sufficient sources on its content and character could be found.
peretti-blend-no-33.o: No documented recipe could be found in the records.

iwan-ries-private-blend.z: This is an aromatic blend that appears in Iwan Ries catalogs; no independent source describing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
iwan-ries-private-blend.o: No room note described in the records could be found.

paul-olsen-no-51.z: One of the blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

ilsted-own-mixture-no-100.z: No.100, one of the numbered house blends sold under the Ilsted name, is reportedly an aromatic mixture; no source verifying its content could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
ilsted-own-mixture-no-100.o: No room note described in the records could be found.

lane-limited-bright-virginia.z: Not enough independent sources could be found documenting the contents and character of American blender Lane Limited's blend called Bright Virginia.

sturks-tobacconists-nutty-unscented.z: An unflavored house blend drawn from the under-counter notebooks of Sturk's Tobacconists in Cape Town; no independent source on its composition could be found.
sturks-tobacconists-nutty-unscented.o: Records indicate it leaves an unflavored leaf scent.

torben-dansk-no-8-midnight-special.z: Torben Dansk No.8 Midnight Special is a mixture combining a high Latakia proportion with various Virginia types. The maker's description mentions an understated sweet, full spicy aroma; the leaf's high essential-oil content gives a mellow smoke and a slow, cool burn. Thanks to the varying cut widths, it is noted as burning mild and dry. Suited to smokers after a smoky blend designed for nighttime smoking that isn't too heavy.
torben-dansk-no-8-midnight-special.o: A light sweet note runs through the smoky wood aroma.

dunhill-aperitif.z: Aperitif is a medium-bodied blend classified as Scottish style in the Dunhill line. It consists of unsweetened black cavendish, latakia, Turkish tobaccos and Virginia leaves. Cavendish keeps the smoke cool and soft while latakia adds a smoky, leathery depth, the orientals a dry spicy sharpness, and Virginia a meadow-and-citrus brightness. The name points to a lightness suited to smoking before a meal. Despite its latakia content, the blend stays measured; this makes it well suited to smokers wanting to move toward English mixtures without seeking heavy smokiness. Dunhill pipe tobaccos have gone out of production; part of the line has continued under other brands.
dunhill-aperitif.o: Leaves a sweetish scent evoking light smoky wood and brown sugar.

gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-virginia-cavendi.z: This product, referred to by the abbreviation DVC, is produced by darkening light hot-air-cured Virginia leaf through extended processing under ample steam. The process largely removes the leaf's sharper elements and leaves a velvety, cool-burning tobacco. This is the unflavored version; the taste comes entirely from the processed leaf itself. On the smoke, a very measured Virginia character comes through: lightly bright, lightly citrusy, lightly herbal, and lightly sweet. Nicotine is low. Suited to those wanting an unflavored but mild tobacco, smokers looking to move from aromatics to unflavored blends, and anyone wanting a plain Cavendish for all-day smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-virginia-cavendi.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, bready, cool tobacco aroma.

thompson-cigar-co-orange.z: An orange-flavored blend in Thompson Cigar's bulk aromatic line; no source describing its composition has been found.
thompson-cigar-co-orange.o: Leaves a citrus aroma reminiscent of orange peel.

von-eicken-three-stars.z: Three Stars is a German aromatic from Joh. von Eicken, described as made from hand-blended tobaccos produced for many years. Its presentation differs from the usual ribbon cut: dark brown, tightly pressed discs sit alongside lighter-toned, thick-cut strips; this twisted-and-sliced structure resembles the curly cut tobaccos of Escudo or Gawith & Hoggarth. In the smoke, Burley's nutty, earthy, molasses-reminiscent sweetness appears lightly ahead of the Virginias; a fruity sweetness typical of the German aromatic tradition layers on top, forming the blend's character. Nicotine sits at a medium level, and despite being aromatic, the leaf taste can still be traced. Since the discs need to be rubbed out, preparation takes more time than with ribbon-cut tobaccos. The blend is not currently in production.
von-eicken-three-stars.o: Leaves a dark scent reminiscent of sweet fruit and molasses.

smokers-pride-vanilla-cavendish.z: Vanilla Cavendish is the vanilla-flavored record in the Smoker's Pride line. The base rests on black cavendish, with burley and Virginia shares rounding out the body. The vanilla flavor worked into the leaf is defining both in tin aroma and throughout the smoke; the tobacco base stays in the background. The ribbon cut makes packing easy; cavendish's moisture slows the burn and keeps the smoke cool. Nicotine share is low. Suited to smokers seeking a classic, sweet everyday aromatic in the vanilla line, wanting an economical option in large packaging, and to those new to the aromatic category.
smokers-pride-vanilla-cavendish.o: Leaves a scent of sweet vanilla and baked dough.

charatan-gray.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the British pipe maker Charatan.

tabaqueria-xian-sweet-ebenezer.z: A house blend from Tabaquería Xian listed as an aromatic; no accessible source describing its composition could be found.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-choctaw.z: Choctaw, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an aromatic mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

sutliff-tobacco-company-crumble-kake-va-.z: Sutliff Crumble Kake Va. Perique is a pressed, crumbly cake blend combining red Virginia leaves with some perique and unflavored black cavendish. The Virginias give a dark-fruit-leaning tart sweetness and a bready-herbal base, while perique adds the tingling spice expected of Virginia-perique blends. The blend carries no top flavoring; since the black cavendish is unflavored, it leaves only a creamy sweetness in the background, letting the Virginias lead. Suited to those seeking an unflavored but not entirely dry Virginia-perique, and those wanting to use the cake cut's packing flexibility.
sutliff-tobacco-company-crumble-kake-va-.o: Perique's spicy sharpness mixes into a scent of dark fruit and bread.

dunhill-my-mixture-rum-cherry.z: As the name suggests, rum- and cherry-flavored; a record tied to Dunhill's custom blending program, not currently in production; no independent source giving detailed composition information could be found.
dunhill-my-mixture-rum-cherry.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-tombigbee.z: No reliable source has been found for The Country Squire Tobacconist pipe blend called Tombigbee.

david-p-ehrlich-company-navy-flake.z: This is a flake-cut shop blend from Boston's David P. Ehrlich Company; no verifiable source describing its composition and character could be found.

milan-tobacconists-milans-balkan-blend.z: Milan's Balkan Blend is Milan Tobacconists' latakia-forward house blend. The recipe is built on latakia, joined by oriental leaves and virginia. According to the maker, its body is strong and its taste earthy and spicy; the virginia share leaves a measured sweetness in the background. It carries no casing and sits at the full end of Balkan-type mixtures. Suitable for smokers accustomed to latakia who are looking for an intense taste in the direction of soot, leather, and spice; it may be too heavy for those coming from light mixtures.
milan-tobacconists-milans-balkan-blend.o: Leaves an intense wood-smoke, leather, and soot aroma that lingers in the room a long time.

mac-baren-brigg-honigmelone.z: Honigmelone, the honeydew-melon-flavored member of the Brigg line, was launched in 2008. Born under German manufacturer Planta, the line has been produced in Denmark since the brand moved to Mac Baren; the package name has been shortened to "Brigg H" due to EU regulations. The blend is made by traditionally processing Virginia leaves ranging from yellow to golden brown, cutting them in a long fiber, and completing with twice-fermented black cavendish. Its body is medium. The casing brings out the melon's cool, juicy side; beneath it, the Virginia leaf's own tobacco sweetness can be sensed. Its taste is soft, suited to any pipe size. Aimed at smokers seeking a fresh, fruit-noted, light blend rather than heavy syrupy aromatics.
mac-baren-brigg-honigmelone.o: Leaves a cool, juicy honeydew melon room note.

dan-tobacco-bill-baileys-black-blend.z: Referred to as a dark-leaf blend in Dan Tobacco's Bill Bailey's series; no adequate source documenting its composition and character was found.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.z: This is the strawberry-flavored record in Imigrantes Fumos's Cândido Giovanella line. The brand's fruit versions (strawberry, cherry, peach) share the same base: Brazilian-grown Virginia and Burley leaf joined by black Cavendish, processed in ribbon cut. In the smoke, strawberry's fruity, sugary taste is pronounced; it combines with the Virginia's natural sweetness, while Burley adds a light body. Nicotine is low, the smoke cool. It's a suitable blend for those who enjoy fruity aromatics and are looking for light smokes.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.o: Leaves a fruity aroma reminiscent of ripe strawberry and candy.

4noggins-covered-bridges.z: Covered Bridges, named after Vermont's covered wooden bridges, is a mild-to-medium aromatic. Per the manufacturer's recipe, the flavoring leans whiskey, occasionally showing a chocolate-like edge. The body is built from black Cavendish along with Zimbabwean and Carolina Virginias. It's relatively dry among aromatics, which makes packing and lighting easier. The higher proportion of Virginia gives the blend a tobacco body that goes beyond mere topping. Nicotine and flavor sit between mild and moderate. It offers a drier alternative for smokers who find damp, heavily topped aromatics hard to keep lit.
4noggins-covered-bridges.o: Leaves a sweetish aroma reminiscent of whiskey and cocoa.

j-paul-tuckers-oxmoor-smoke-shoppe-holy-.z: This is a house blend sold under a small American tobacconist's own name; no reliable source describing its content and character could be found.

tinder-box-epicurean.z: Epicurean is an English-type mixture noted among Tinder Box house blends; no verifiable source describing its composition and character has been found.
tinder-box-epicurean.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

cup-o-joes-25th-anniversary-vabur-blend.z: A house blend the Cup O' Joes tobacco shop prepared for its twenty-fifth anniversary, understood from its name to be Virginia-and-Burley-based; no source describing its ratios and character was found.

affordable-pipes-top-hat.z: One of the house blends from the American seller Affordable Pipes; no accessible source describing its content could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-irish-sweet-cho.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Brown Irish Sweet Chocolate Rose blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

p-g-c-hajenius-hajenius-759.z: Hajenius 759 is a Balkan mixture from the "My Own Blend" house line of P.G.C. Hajenius, the Amsterdam tobacconist open since 1826. Records indicate the blend was built to replace the discontinued Balkan Sobranie: generous Cyprian latakia, spicy oriental leaves, and the Virginia body carrying them all sit together. It is ribbon cut and typically sold in hundred-gram tins. The smoke follows a smoky, leather-and-wood-leaning, unflavored, full line; latakia stays up front, though Virginia's sweetness lingers all the way to the end. It's aimed at pipe smokers accustomed to Balkan and English mixtures who want a satisfying midday or evening smoke; it would be heavy going for someone starting out with aromatic tobacco.
p-g-c-hajenius-hajenius-759.o: Leaves the room with a scent of smoky pine char, leather, and dry grass.

fribourg-treyer-34th-mixture.z: 34th Mixture is one of the English-style blends in the line tracing its roots to Fribourg & Treyer, the tobacconist founded in 1720 on Haymarket in London. Latakia and black cavendish are added to Virginia leaves, and it is presented in a fairly coarse ribbon cut. Because the latakia amount is kept measured, the smoke taste doesn't overtake the blend; the black cavendish gives a sweet base that softens the smoky side. Without venturing into heavy Balkan mixtures, it has a structure suitable for all-day smoking for smokers wanting to get to know the English style.
fribourg-treyer-34th-mixture.o: Leaves an aroma of woodsmoke with a light sweet smokiness.

w-o-larsen-premium.z: No reliable source could be found regarding the composition and character of this Danish blend bearing the W.Ø. Larsen name.
w-o-larsen-premium.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

cup-o-joes-high-peaks-gold.z: An aromatic blend from Cup O' Joes' bulk High Peaks line; records indicate a very mild build, though no adequate source detailing its composition was found.

just-for-him-riptide.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for Just For Him's Riptide, so the profile is left incomplete; per catalog records, the blend is classified as "Aromatic."

sentimiento-nacional-libertador.z: Libertador is one of the blends from Sentimiento Nacional, an Argentine handmade pipe-tobacco producer; no reliable source on its content and character could be found.
sentimiento-nacional-libertador.o: No description of the room note has been recorded in the sources.

mclintock-batida-de-coco.z: An aromatic blend in Kohlhase & Kopp's McLintock line, taking its name from coconut liqueur; no detailed source regarding its composition could be found.
mclintock-batida-de-coco.o: Leaves a sweet, creamy coconut aroma.

b-b-tobacconists-llc-orthodox-mixture.z: A tobacconist-signed mixture; no independent source describing its content could be found, leaving the profile blank.

hill-hill-tobacconists-danish-slices.z: Danish Slices is a Virginia-forward blend sold at the Hill & Hill Tobacconists shop in Grosse Pointe, Michigan. Its weight is made up of bright Virginia leaf; a light honey-like flavoring is applied on top to bring out the leaf's own sugar. As the name indicates, it's presented in flake form. Keeping the flavoring measured brings the blend closer to the lightly sweetened Virginias of European tradition rather than heavily syrupy American-style aromatics. It suits those who love Virginia's tart-sweet, herbal taste and don't want an intense flavoring, and those comfortable rubbing out or folding flake tobacco to fill a pipe.
hill-hill-tobacconists-danish-slices.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of honey and baked bread crust.

bosphorus-burley-flake.z: Bosphorus Burley Flake is an unflavored, single-type flake prepared from burley leaf grown in the Black Sea region. Its nicotine content and the tobacco's own intrinsic aroma are high; its strength is very pronounced and its taste stays close to traditional Turkish pipe tobacco. No tongue bite is observed. The slices come moist and can be difficult to light and prone to going out even after airing for a few days. It is a full, satisfying tobacco not suited to smoking on an empty stomach, meant for evenings. Per records, the product's name was later changed to Black Stone Flake.
bosphorus-burley-flake.o: Leaves a nutty, tart and sharp burnt-tobacco aroma.

tinder-box-black-vanilla-cavendish.z: Tinder Box is the name of an American tobacconist chain founded in 1928 that sells blends prepared for its own shops under its own name; Black Vanilla Cavendish is one of these house blends, though no sufficient independent source describing its composition and character has been found.

pipesworld-wilsons-virginia-flake.z: Wilson's Virginia Flake appears among the sliced-cut Virginia listings of the seller known as PipesWorld; no source could be found documenting its leaf composition and production.

peter-heinrichs-no-110.z: Peter Heinrichs No. 110 is, per the maker's description, a blend whose backbone is built from Virginia varieties sourced from the world's select growing regions, joined by a pinch of Kentucky and Burley gathered from quality sources. Virginia's sweetness runs alongside Burley's dry, nutty earthiness, while fire-cured Kentucky adds a smoky, full base underneath. Since it is an unflavored structure, the taste comes from the leaves' own character; nicotine sits above medium. It is a record aimed at smokers seeking unflavored Virginia-Burley mixtures who want a full-bodied smoke.
peter-heinrichs-no-110.o: Leaves a dry leaf and light smoky-nut aroma.

ken-byron-ventures-uzumaki-2019.z: The 2019 release of Ken Byron Ventures' Uzumaki; no independent source could be found to document its contents and character.
ken-byron-ventures-uzumaki-2019.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

rattray-black-mallory.z: Black Mallory is the mixture among Rattray's dark English blends where the Latakia share is felt most clearly. Virginia, Oriental tobacco, and black Cavendish are combined with a generous amount of Latakia in ribbon cut. It lights easily, needs no extra care to stay lit, and leaves a dark trace that lingers long on the palate. Strength is medium; smoked at a slow pace the smoke thickens, while a fast pace leaves it prone to heating up. It suits smokers looking for a classic English blend centered on a smoky-woody character, where sweetness stays only in the background.
rattray-black-mallory.o: Leaves a thick, smoky wood aroma that lingers in the room for a long time.

paul-olsen-po.z: One of the house blends from the Paul Olsen house tied to the Scottish style; no independent source documenting its composition could be found.

consolidated-c-b-f.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Consolidated blend C.B.F.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-titus-blend.z: Titus Blend, listed among Boswell's English mixtures, is a blend built from light-cavendish-processed Virginias, burley, Latakia and Perique. The Latakia proportion is kept measured, and the manufacturer describes the blend as full-bodied but not harsh. The dried-fruit and spice tone Perique brings takes on a balancing role between Latakia's smoky taste and burley's earthy base. Being an unflavored mixture, suitable for smokers seeking the tobacco leaf's own taste and familiar with the English style.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-titus-blend.o: A dried fruit and spice tone accompanies a light smoky aroma.

imperial-tobacco-amphora-regular.z: Amphora Regular is a light-bodied aromatic blend in which Burley, Cavendish, Kentucky, Oriental, and Virginia leaves are brought together in a fine ribbon cut. On the flavoring side, cocoa and chocolate notes come forward; flavor intensity is low and nicotine strength limited, so it's described as an all-day tobacco. The Amphora name is Dutch in origin, and the brand has a long history; the blend is today produced in Denmark by Mac Baren, with the brand operating under the Imperial Tobacco umbrella. It suits smokers who want an aromatic that isn't syrupy and has a distinctive cocoa character.
imperial-tobacco-amphora-regular.o: Spreads a pronounced aroma of cocoa and sweetened toasted leaf through the room.

borkum-riff-orange-honey.z: Orange & Honey is an aromatic built from light Virginia, dark aromatic Kentucky, and cool-smoking Burley leaf. Orange and honey are used together in the topping; the citrus note is kept measured, balanced by honey's round, creamy sweetness. It's a ribbon-cut blend with medium-light nicotine. It suits smokers looking for a citrus-based sweetness outside the usual vanilla- and cherry-centered classic aromatics. The Borkum Riff line is produced in Denmark under Scandinavian Tobacco Group.
borkum-riff-orange-honey.o: Leaves a creamy, citrus room note where orange peel and honey meet.

the-grey-fox-st-augustine.z: St. Augustine is recorded as a blend from a small maker known as The Grey Fox; no source documenting its composition, cut, and character has been found.
the-grey-fox-st-augustine.o: No described room note has been found in records.

hu-tobacco-take-five.z: Take Five is one of HU Tobacco's lighter-leaning mixtures. Perique and black Cavendish are added atop a Virginia-and-Burley base; the Cavendish carries sweetness, while the Perique opens a spicy turn in the background. The leaf is prepared rubbed out into small clumps, meaning it needs no separating before smoking.
hu-tobacco-take-five.o: Leaves a soft, lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of cooked fruit.
