gawith-hoggarth-co-bosun-cut-plug.z: Bosun Cut Plug is a broken-flake blend produced by pressing and cutting dark-fired Virginia together with light Virginia, then breaking the result. The pressed plug tobacco is finished with a fine Lakeland topping based on clove essence. Within Gawith, Hoggarth's classic trio built on dark-fired leaf, it sits somewhere between Coniston Cut Plug and Dark Flake. In the smoke, the smoky, woody flavour of the dark-fired leaf leads; the light Virginia lays a bread-like sweetness beneath it, and the clove draws a spicy edge without masking the taste. It burns slow and cool with a heavy nicotine load. The thick broken pieces want a bit of airing before lighting. It suits smokers accustomed to dark, strong, lightly topped English tobaccos; it may be heavy for those new to the pipe.
gawith-hoggarth-co-bosun-cut-plug.o: A spicy, sharp clove aroma settles over a smoky, woody base.

paul-olsen-b93.z: No reliable source could be found for the Paul Olsen pipe tobacco called B93, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

mac-baren-plumcake.z: Plumcake is one of Mac Baren's old blends, dating back to 1957. Its base holds matured light Virginia leaves; Burley, the maker's own black Cavendish, and a small amount of Latakia are added to these. The blend is ribbon cut, and once the mixture is complete, it's flavored with dark Jamaican rum. So it isn't a pure aromatic but a hybrid structure with a smoky leaf slipped in. In the smoke, Virginia's matured sugar and a tangy sweetness from the rum come forward first; the plum association comes from this. Though the Latakia proportion is low, the smoky trace is noticeably felt, and the Cavendish builds a spiced base. Moisture is high straight out of the tin, requiring some airing. Falls to those coming from aromatics who want a bit more leaf character, or those wanting to try English blends in softened form; smoked quickly it's prone to running hot and biting the tongue.
mac-baren-plumcake.o: A fine soot aroma sits atop a sweet plum-and-rum aroma.

house-of-windsor-cappucino-t418.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for House of Windsor's Cappucino T418 blend, so its content and character could not be recorded.

kontor-tabak-no-13.z: Kontor-Tabak No. 13 is a dark Virginia flake in the Leipzig-based Tabak-Kontor's namesake series. Per the manufacturer's description, the blend is built by adding dark fired Kentucky and full-bodied Perique to selected Virginia leaves; the result is a spicy, long-lasting smoke that leans on old English tradition. The pressed, sliced leaf burns slowly, suiting smokers accustomed to rubbing tobacco before packing. Nicotine load and flavor intensity are above medium; the plum-and-pepper-level spice from the Perique and Kentucky's smoky tone are aimed at those seeking natural, i.e. unflavored, tobacco. For someone coming from aromatic blends, it counts as a harsh start.
kontor-tabak-no-13.o: Leaves a room note where smoky wood-fire aroma mixes with dark fruit sweetness.

montes-old-reserve.z: No verifiable source could be found regarding the maker and composition of the blend known as Monte's Old Reserve.

dan-tobacco-hollys-discovery.z: Holly's Discovery is a ready-rubbed blend in which select bright Virginia leaf is matured under pressure together with Latakia. The maker's description notes it is lightly scented with soft vanilla, placing it somewhere between unflavored English mixtures and aromatics. The smoke is cool and light. The Virginia's sweetness meets Latakia's measured smokiness, while vanilla stays in the background as a rounding layer. Nicotine level is low. Suited to smokers looking for a not-too-heavy blend combining smoke and sweetness, or wanting a gentle introduction to Latakia.
dan-tobacco-hollys-discovery.o: Leaves a sweetish scent where light smoke and soft vanilla appear together.

hu-tobacco-ju-52.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of JU 52, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

paul-olsen-kbenhavn-800-v.z: A blend from the My Own Blend line that originated at the Paul Olsen shop in Copenhagen; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

kinnickinnick-kinnickinnick.z: Kinnickinnick is a generic term in the Algonquian language meaning "that which is mixed," describing Native North American pipe mixtures; tobacco is sometimes combined with plants such as bearberry leaf and red willow bark. The composition of the single branded product carrying this name could not be confirmed.
kinnickinnick-kinnickinnick.o: Close to the grassy, woody scent left by mixtures forward in plant leaf and tree bark.

pete-brothers-grand-national.z: Pete Brothers Grand National is reportedly recorded as an American-style mixture; no accessible source documenting the blend's composition and smoking character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-cherry-menthol.z: Kendal Cherry Menthol is the cherry-and-menthol-topped member of the Kendal shag family. Virginia and Burley leaf are cut into fine strands; the blend itself offers an earthy base with a dry-hay association, over which the topping is layered. The product has in recent years been packaged under the abbreviation "CHM." Menthol's cooling effect is notably strong in this line and sits dominant on the palate together with the cherry sweetness. Nicotine is light to moderate. Suited to smokers seeking menthol tobacco who enjoy a fine cut; not for those seeking unflavored tobacco taste.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-cherry-menthol.o: Leaves a cooling menthol and black-cherry aroma.

newminster-no-35-french-champagne.z: Newminster No. 35 French Champagne is an aromatic bulk tobacco made by blending Brazilian-origin Virginia leaves with Mexican Burley and adding sweet black Cavendish on top. It takes its name from the fruity aroma given to the blend, evoking the champagne reference. The smoke stays soft and light; fruity sweetness dominates, and it may leave a light sharpness at the finish. Nicotine is low. Suitable for smokers looking for a light-bodied, fruit-flavored aromatic.
newminster-no-35-french-champagne.o: Leaves a light red-berry and sweet-grape aroma in the room.

mac-baren-brigg-vanilla.z: The vanilla member of the Brigg line is also referred to on packages as "Brigg V." The blend is prepared by combining Virginia, burley and black cavendish leaves in a ribbon cut. Virginia and cavendish carry the blend's character and sweetness, while burley balances the body and prevents it from tipping into an overly syrupy structure. The applied casing is a measured vanilla note, with a fine fruit touch alongside it. Nicotine is low and the smoke is soft, lighting easily. Suited to smokers who love classic Danish-style vanilla aromatics and want a blend where the scent stands out more than the tobacco itself. Like the rest of the line, this blend too was first produced in Germany by Planta and later in Denmark by Mac Baren.
mac-baren-brigg-vanilla.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and lightly fruity, bakery-like room note.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-flying-.z: Flying Dutchman Flek is a broken-flake presentation of Dutch-style Cavendish made from Virginia, Oriental, and Burley leaf. The maker explains that Dutch Cavendish generally refers to a slice-cut tobacco blend converted into brown Cavendish and dressed with fruit-inclusive aromatic casings; it's sold as 2 oz. bulk. The Cavendish process strips the leaf's sharpness and brings sweetness forward, while the slice structure slows the burn. Suited to those seeking a classic continental European-style slice that's flavored but not heavy on sugar, and who are used to working with slice-cut tobacco.
ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-flying-.o: Leaves a dark Cavendish aroma mixed with dried-fruit sweetness.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2006.z: Christmas Cheer 2006 is the release made from the 2006 crop in McClelland's annual Virginia series. The leaf used in this release is orange-red flue-cured Virginia picked at peak maturity; it's matured pressed into cake, sliced, and tinned as broken flake. In the smoke, unflavored Virginia's natural sweetness proceeds over a bready, faintly fruity base; no flavoring is used. Nicotine dose is medium. The sharp tin note characteristic of the series is present in this release as well. Since it comes from a single crop, the release is considered a separate record from other years in the same series. Not reproduced since the brand closed in 2018.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2006.o: Leaves a tangy, vinegary sweetness along with a toasted-bread aroma.

4noggins-butternut-burley.z: Butternut Burley is a Burley-based aromatic offered in bulk by 4noggins under the Hearth & Home label. According to the manufacturer's recipe, the profile is built on melted butter with a small addition of vanilla and honey; Burley's own nutty flavor complements this sweetness. The flavoring is noticeable but not heavy enough to mask the tobacco. Because nicotine stays mild, it's counted among the all-day-smokable blends; the maker notes it leaves no aftertaste bitterness. Burley's tongue-friendly nature and the measured topping make this a blend both newcomers to the pipe and those seeking a mild aromatic can use.
4noggins-butternut-burley.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of warm butter, vanilla, and nuts.

cornell-diehl-nutty-virginia.z: No reliable product description from the manufacturer or retailers could be found for this Cornell & Diehl blend.

imperial-tobacco-group-plc-dr-pat-irish-.z: Dr. Pat is a pipe tobacco brand with a history of roughly a century. It was originally produced by the William Butler Tobacco Company, later taken over by Imperial Tobacco's Australian arm; today it's sold only in Australia and New Zealand, and is one of the few classic pipe tobaccos still surviving in those markets. It's recognized by its round tins with black and green enamel lids. The blend is built on finely cut Virginia, Burley, and Cavendish, and flavored with a light liqueur note. On opening the tin, a pronounced aroma reminiscent of fruit cake comes through; in the smoke, though, the flavoring stays much further in the background, and the tobacco's own mild, lightly sweet taste comes forward. Nicotine load is low. It suits those looking for a plain, light, traditional everyday tobacco.
imperial-tobacco-group-plc-dr-pat-irish-.o: Leaves an aroma of fruit cake and light liqueur.

thepiperoom-com-king-arthur-blend.z: No reliable source has been found for the ThePipeRoom.com pipe blend called King Arthur Blend.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-lighthous.z: Lighthouse Keeper is one of The Country Squire's lightly flavored house blends. Grassy, lightly citrusy Virginia, nutty burley, perique contributing plum and spice, and black cavendish carrying brown-sugar sweetness are combined; a measured maple and vanilla top note is applied over them. The flavoring doesn't overwhelm the leaf, so the blend sits somewhere between an aromatic and a natural mixture. The burn is cool and even, leaves little moisture in the bowl, and needs relighting only rarely. Nicotine is light to medium. It suits those looking for a subtly flavored, balanced everyday blend.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-lighthous.o: Leaves a scent of sweet maple and vanilla over a smoky base.

national-tobacco-red-cap-no-7.z: For the No.7 version of the Red Cap line, sufficient independent sources describing its composition and character could not be found.

cornell-diehl-warped-scarecrow-2022.z: This is the September 30, 2022 release of Scarecrow, the autumn series from Warped and Cornell & Diehl. The composition follows the same skeleton as the previous release: a special red Virginia Cavendish made from 2017 dark red and 2019 orange-red flue-cured leaf, 2014-harvest aged white Burley, and old-style air-cured dark leaf. The mixture is pressed for days and sliced into crumble cake; it's lightly moist straight from the tin. The chocolate, vanilla, and caramel-leaning top note is again kept measured in this release; records note the aged white Burley is a touch more pronounced than in the 2021 release, with nicotine at a medium level. Its pressed structure makes the blend well suited to aging. Being released in limited quantity, it isn't in continuous production.
cornell-diehl-warped-scarecrow-2022.o: A dry spice and earthy edge accompany the scent of malty cocoa and caramel.

house-of-windsor-union-leader.z: Union Leader is a classic over-the-counter (OTC) blend based mainly on Burley leaf. It's ribbon cut with a light top flavoring added; sources note its smoke carries a cigarette-like, dry, sharp character. The Virginia share adds a limited sweetness to the Burley's earthy taste. Nicotine level counts as above the medium band. It was one of the cheap, widely distributed tobaccos in America for many years; in its later period it was produced by House of Windsor and was withdrawn from the market when the company closed. Today it's mostly remembered through collectible tins and as an example of the era's pipe culture.
house-of-windsor-union-leader.o: Leaves a dry, sharp burnt-leaf aroma.

blatter-blatter-virginia.z: A straight Virginia house blend from Blatter & Blatter; no reliable source documenting its composition or character could be found.

mostex-stanislaw-london-mixture.z: London Mixture is the classic English-style mixture in Mostex's Stanislaw series. It is built on a virginia base with Basma and Izmir orientals along with Cyprus latakia added, and it carries no casing. Since the latakia proportion is kept measured, the body doesn't become heavy; the blend stays at an intensity smokable throughout the day. Suitable for smokers looking for the structure of traditional London-style mixtures while avoiding heavy smokiness.
mostex-stanislaw-london-mixture.o: Dry hay and spice tones sit beneath a measured smoky-wood aroma.

cornell-diehl-stovepipe.z: Stovepipe is one of Cornell & Diehl's ribbon-cut aromatic blends. Its body is built from bright and red Virginia leaf; on top, cocoa, caramel, and vanilla sauce is applied. Beneath the blend sit layers of dark Burley and Perique, which add an earthy base and spicy sharpness under the sweet sauce. This structure sets the blend apart from classic light aromatics: though sweetness is pronounced, the body rises to a medium level thanks to Perique and Burley. Built for those wanting an aromatic smoke where tobacco character comes through alongside the sugary taste rather than instead of it. The room note stays measured compared to typical aromatic blends.
cornell-diehl-stovepipe.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, bakery-like scent where cocoa and caramel mingle with vanilla.

rain-city-cigar-classic.z: This is a house blend from Rain City Cigar, open since 1997 in Seattle's Georgetown neighborhood; there is not enough source material describing its composition and character.

dan-tobacco-sweet-georgia-brown.z: Sweet Georgia Brown is one of Dan Tobacco's burley-forward aromatic blends. The broadly cut leaf carries plenty of coated burley cavendish, accompanied by a small amount of Virginia. The topping is described in the direction of brown sugar and maple syrup, and is pronounced in the tin scent. Burley's earthy, nutty structure carries the syrupy sweetness of the topping, while Virginia leaves a light coolness behind. Nicotine is medium. It suits smokers seeking American-style sweet burley aromatics; it doesn't answer an expectation for oriental or latakia.
dan-tobacco-sweet-georgia-brown.o: Leaves a dark, sweet scent leaning toward brown sugar and maple syrup.

4noggins-killington.z: Killington, named after the mountain region in Vermont, is an aromatic. Per the manufacturer's recipe, the blend is built from golden Cavendish leaves with a small amount of Burley added; in the pouch, the mix of gold and black tones gives a ribbon-cut appearance. The flavoring sits somewhere between nutty and berry-like. Nicotine runs mild-to-moderate, and flavor sits in the same range; the topping level is reported as moderate. Keeping the Burley ratio low leaves the blend on the gentle side. It's aimed at smokers who enjoy fruity, nutty aromatics but don't want a heavy tobacco body.
4noggins-killington.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of nuts and berries.

sutliff-tobacco-company-vanilla-latte-d5.z: Vanilla Latte is among Sutliff's coffee-themed aromatics. Its base is built from black Cavendish, Burley, and Virginia; a vanilla and coffee top note is applied over it. The black Cavendish carries the sweetness and moisture, the Burley holds the casing, and the Virginia adds a light sugar note in the background. The cut is ribbon. The blend tries to build the impression of the drink it's named after: rather than roasted coffee bitterness, a milky, sweet, and creamy side leads. Nicotine is light, making for a profile that can be smoked for long stretches during the day. It suits those new to aromatic tobacco or looking for a coffee note alongside their tobacco. As with cased tobaccos generally, airing it briefly before packing makes for an easier light.
sutliff-tobacco-company-vanilla-latte-d5.o: Leaves a scent of milky coffee and vanilla.

dunhill-mild-blend.z: Referred to as a light blend from Dunhill built on Virginia and cavendish; not enough independent sourcing exists to document its composition and character.
dunhill-mild-blend.o: Leaves a lightly sweet tobacco scent.

sullivan-powell-sullivans-special-mixtur.z: Sullivan's Special Mixture is one of the classic English mixtures from the Sullivan & Powell house, established in London's Burlington Arcade. It's a medium-cut blend built by adding Macedonian-origin oriental leaves and latakia to a Virginia body. No flavoring is used; the spicy and lightly sweet layers in the taste come from the leaf itself and its fermentation.
sullivan-powell-sullivans-special-mixtur.o: Leaves a faint trace where woody latakia smoke mixes with dry spice.

ken-byron-ventures-diogenes-club-2023.z: The 2023 batch of Diogenes Club; no accessible maker's profile could be found to document its contents.

pipesandcigars-com-scottys-university-pr.z: This is a blend offered under the American retailer pipesandcigars.com's name; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

douwe-egberts-monza.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Monza, a pipe tobacco from Douwe Egberts.
douwe-egberts-monza.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

samuel-gawith-st-james-flake.z: St. James Flake is Samuel Gawith's pressed slice tobacco bringing together Virginia and Perique. Its name references the St. James region of Louisiana where the Perique leaf is grown. It is tinned with the high moisture typical of the brand's flakes; drying it thoroughly before packing eases the burn and gives an even burn throughout the bowl. The Perique share in the blend is pronounced; although Virginia's sweetness is felt at the start of the bowl, Perique's peppery, astringent line takes over shortly after and becomes dominant in the final portions. Nicotine fullness and flavor intensity are high, sharpening with a fast smoke. Aimed at experienced smokers who want to know the Perique character in high dose; not suitable for those expecting a mild, pure Virginia. The ash is light gray and clean.
samuel-gawith-st-james-flake.o: Leaves a sharp trace evoking plum and cracked pepper over a sweet Virginia scent.

clan-shaw-madrid.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Madrid.

mcclelland-dominican-glory-maduro.z: Dominican Glory Maduro is the version of the blend built with dark maduro cigar leaf. Dominican-sourced maduro cigar leaves are balanced with matured red and stoved Virginias; after being pressed into cake form and aged, the mixture is sliced as flake. In the smoke, a spicy-sweet opening continues into dark tones close to espresso and cocoa; the upper part of the bowl carries a mild, chocolate-like line. There's no added flavoring. Body and nicotine dose are high; the blend is aimed at smokers seeking maduro cigar taste in a pipe and runs heavy for beginners. The maker ceased operations in early 2018.
mcclelland-dominican-glory-maduro.o: Leaves a heavy aroma in the direction of dark cigar smoke, coffee, and cocoa.

up-down-moms-norwegian-pipe.z: One of the blends prepared at Up Down Tobacco's shop in Chicago; since no reliable source on its composition has been found, the record has been left unfilled.

dunhill-mr-alfreds-own.z: Mr. Alfred's Own is among the Dunhill blends sold exclusively from the London shop. It stands apart within the English blending scheme by adding cigar leaf: its original version, sold in gold tins, is on record as containing Havana leaf, which gives the blend a sweetish, sharp edge. Latakia is kept balanced, not overpowering the other components. The smoke is smooth and full, with moderate nicotine. With aging, the sharpness from the cigar leaf softens. Shop blends went out of production when the Murray's factory closed; today the blend can only be found in old tins. It's an intriguing record for smokers familiar with classic English mixtures curious about the difference cigar leaf makes.
dunhill-mr-alfreds-own.o: Smoky latakia scent is mixed with the earthy, sweetish note of cigar leaf.

abenaki-tobacco-co-georgia-peach.z: Georgia Peach is among Abenaki Tobacco's fruited aromatics. Per the maker's recipe, Burley, Virginia, and flavored black Cavendish are pressed and cut into ribbon; peach and honey are applied over it. The pressing stage is a step that lets the flavoring settle into the leaf. The honey addition softens the peach's sharpness and sets the blend into a round sweetness. Nicotine load is measured, suiting those looking for a fruited aromatic to smoke midday. Abenaki Tobacco was founded in Conway, New Hampshire; the brand's own sales site isn't live today.
abenaki-tobacco-co-georgia-peach.o: Leaves a honeyed-peach and cooked-fruit room note.

ken-byron-ventures-van-gogh-2022.z: Van Gogh is an all-Virginia blend from Ken Byron Ventures, a small-scale producer based in Pennsylvania. Per the maker's description, domestic and imported Virginias are brought together and, after pressing, presented as broken flake with a mottled, dark-toned appearance. The leaf goes through a light casing; no dominant flavoring or heavy sweetening is added, so the taste comes largely from Virginia's own breadlike, dried-fruit character. KBV re-blends its offerings every year and releases them in limited numbers under a year stamp, so leaf sourcing and aging can differ between years of the same name. The broken-flake structure calls for rubbing out between the fingers before packing and rewards a slow smoke. Suited to smokers who want to follow unflavored Virginia's natural sweetness and its development in the jar over time, and to those already used to flake form.
ken-byron-ventures-van-gogh-2022.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma of dry hay and cooked fruit.

peter-heinrichs-sir-henry-no-ii.z: Sir Henry No. II is a Virginia, Burley, and Maryland leaf composition in Peter Heinrichs' Sir Henry series. Per the maker's description, the blend offers a mild smoke that is gentle on the tongue, with a measured room note. The ribbon cut allows easy packing and an even burn. Maryland leaf gives the blend lightness and an even burn, Burley a bready base, and Virginia natural sweetness. Flavoring is kept at a low level and nicotine strength is light. It suits smokers seeking a mild, unassuming blend for all-day smoking as well as newcomers to the pipe.
peter-heinrichs-sir-henry-no-ii.o: Leaves a thin aroma with light sweetness recalling bread and dry hay.

paul-olsen-silke-2.z: One of the numbered house blends from the Paul Olsen house; no independent source documenting its composition could be found.

hausmarken-danish-mixture-ruby-cherry.z: Ruby, the red-tin member of the Danish Mixture series, is a topped mixture prepared in the Danish style. Sun-ripened Virginia leaf builds a citrusy, herbal base; Burley adds a nutty, earthy, lightly sharp layer, while unflavored black Cavendish brings a soft brown-sugar tone. A fruity topping reminiscent of wild cherry is applied to the blend. The ribbon cut makes it easy to light and gives an even burn. Nicotine stays moderate to light, while the cherry topping is pronounced in the taste, making it suitable for smokers wanting a fruity aromatic in a large everyday-size package. Records place it as part of a house-brand series aimed at the German market, offered in 50- and 200-gram packages.
hausmarken-danish-mixture-ruby-cherry.o: Leaves a room aroma of ripe cherry and light caramel sugar.

consolidated-s-p-s.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Consolidated blend S.P.S.

cornell-diehl-solace.z: A blend not in Cornell & Diehl's current catalogue, referred to as American style; no adequate source documenting its composition was found.
cornell-diehl-solace.o: No adequate information for a description could be found in records.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-irish-sweet-app.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Brown Irish Sweet Apple blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

richs-real-irish.z: Real Irish is a blend Rich's Cigar Store describes as a "natural aromatic." Maryland Burley and Carolina bright Virginia form the base, with a very small amount of fruit flavoring and a touch of Perique added. Because the flavoring dose is kept low, the tobacco's own dry sweetness stays in front, while Perique leaves a light spice and plum trace in the background. It is an all-day mixture suited to smokers who avoid heavy, syrupy aromatics but also keep some distance from fully unflavored blends.
richs-real-irish.o: Leaves a trace where a light fruity sweetness meets a dry, nutty grain aroma.

hearth-home-stogie.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for this blend, said to contain cigar leaf, from the Hearth & Home brand.

john-patton-virginia-squire.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Patton's Virginia Squire blend.

smokers-haven-cognac-mixture.z: Cognac Mixture is a discontinued mixture prepared for Smokers' Haven; sufficient sources on its composition and character could not be found.
smokers-haven-cognac-mixture.o: Records did not describe the room note.

exclusiv-no-5-special-whisky.z: No verifiable source could be found regarding the producer, composition, and character of this pipe tobacco marketed under the Exclusiv name.

peter-stokkebye-burley-no-702.z: PS702 is Peter Stokkebye's unflavored Burley leaf. The leaf is processed by the Cavendish method, but no sweetening is applied on top; the taste therefore comes entirely from Burley's own character. The cut is ribbon and moisture is kept low. The profile runs along a nutty, dry, plain line; flavor intensity is low while nicotine is medium, typical of Burley. Given its cool, slow burn, its main function is as a blending component: it lowers the burn temperature of the mixture it's added to and softens sharp tastes. It suits those preparing their own blends and those seeking an unflavored, straightforward Burley smoke.
peter-stokkebye-burley-no-702.o: Leaves a plain tobacco aroma leaning toward nuts and dry straw.

levin-pipes-international-klenderwood.z: Not enough sources could be found about this blend, described as oriental-forward.

motzek-little-snake.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called Little Snake could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-john-rolfe.z: Match John Rolfe is a blend modeled after Lane's mixture called John Rolfe. Golden-yellow Virginia leaves are combined with white burley, with a peach-brandy casing applied over them. Virginia leads, giving sweet, grassy, fig-like, bready tones, while burley adds depth and structure to the body. The casing is noticeable but not intense enough to mask the tobacco's taste. Nicotine is low and the burn is soft; it suits smokers looking for a mixture sitting somewhere between a lightly fruity aromatic and a Virginia-forward blend, one they can smoke all day.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-john-rolfe.o: Leaves a fruity scent carrying peach and brandy sweetness.

erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-black-dot.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing could be found for 4th Generation Black Dot, a blend from Erik Stokkebye, so the record has been left open; according to available listings it is classified in the Virginia/Perique family.

g-l-pease-telegraph-hill.z: Telegraph Hill belongs to G. L. Pease's Fog City Selection line, named after San Francisco neighbourhoods. Small flake pieces of perique are added to a Virginia base, giving the ribbon-cut blend a spicy, lingering finish. With its untopped Virginia-Perique structure, it is aimed at smokers seeking a medium-bodied option for everyday use.
g-l-pease-telegraph-hill.o: Leaves a dry-grass and lightly fruity tobacco aroma.

peretti-tashkent.z: Tashkent, named after the city of Tashkent in Central Asia, is one of Peretti's spicy, full-flavored English mixtures. Per the maker's description, the blend is built from Izmir and Turkish leaf together with Latakia; that is, instead of Virginia sweetness, the Oriental leaf's resinous, tart character is set directly against Latakia's smoke. This structure keeps flavor intensity high and the profile dry. Being Oriental-forward, it offers a sharper, less sweet smoke than classic Virginia-based English mixtures. It is aimed at smokers accustomed to Latakia and Oriental leaf who are seeking spicy intensity. It is a ribbon cut.
peretti-tashkent.o: Leaves an intense aroma of smoke, leather, and spice.

peterson-special-reserve-2019.z: Special Reserve 2019 is a limited edition blend released as part of Peterson's Special Reserve series specific to that year; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient first-hand sources confirming its content and character could be found.

mac-baren-hh-old-dark-fired.z: HH Old Dark Fired is an unflavored flake combining selected Virginias with fire-cured dark Kentucky burley. The leaves are tightly pressed under heat and steam to mature, then sliced. Casing is minimized and no top flavor is used. Opening the tin releases an earthy, smoky, leather-toned scent; the cooked-fruit sweetness of the Virginias is followed by the cocoa-like depth of the dark Kentucky. In the smoke, the smoky, tangy Kentucky character carries the blend, with Virginia sweetness softening this weight; toward the finish, the burley's body becomes more pronounced. Nicotine is high and it offers a filling smoke, so it suits pipe smokers already acquainted with strong, smoky leaf more than newcomers. It packs easily and burns evenly.
mac-baren-hh-old-dark-fired.o: Leaves a leathery scent reminiscent of meat cooked over wood fire and smoke.

cornell-diehl-mississippi-mud.z: Mississippi Mud is an unusual English blend built on unsweetened black Cavendish, Cyprus Latakia, and Perique, containing no Virginia. Toasted Cavendish gives the blend its dark color and rounded sweetness. In the pouch note, sweet, smoky Latakia leads, while Perique leaves a subtle peppery edge in the background. On the smoke, a creamy texture, a nutty base, notes reminiscent of black coffee and chocolate, and measured spice appear; it burns cool. Suited to those looking for a Latakia-heavy but non-Virginia, unusual smoky blend.
cornell-diehl-mississippi-mud.o: A light peppery edge mingles with a sweetish, pronouncedly smoky Latakia scent.

milan-tobacconists-christmas-blend.z: Christmas Blend is referred to among the seasonal aromatic house blends Milan Tobacconists prepares; no verifiable source regarding its composition, cut, and flavor construction could be found.
milan-tobacconists-christmas-blend.o: No source describing its room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-longevity.z: No adequate source documenting the composition and character of Cornell & Diehl's Longevity blend could be found; the blend isn't in the maker's current catalogue.

j-f-germain-son-celebration.z: This is a blend released by J. F. Germain & Son on the island of Jersey, today encountered only via empty tins; no reliable source describing its content and character could be found.

hearth-home-patroon-island.z: Patroon Island is counted among Hearth & Home's Burley-based blends; there is not enough sourcing to document its recipe and character.

porter-house-mellow-mixture.z: This is a light-bodied mixture carried under the name Porter House; no source could be found verifying its content.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore-bu.z: Finamore's peach-flavored version is prepared by working a peach essence into the Burley and Virginia body the brand produces in Juiz de Fora. The blend's skeleton is the same as the line's other flavored products — the distinction lies in the flavoring. The peach note stands out on the smoke, while the tobacco's own taste remains a soft base; nicotine is kept low. It suits smokers looking for fruity, light-bodied aromatics.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore-bu.o: Leaves a sweet fruity scent reminiscent of stewed peach.

ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-burley-hot-m.z: Referred to as a Burley-forward aromatic small-batch blend in Ken Byron Ventures' Yoshimi's line; not enough sources could be found to document its composition.
ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-burley-hot-m.o: Could not be described due to lack of accessible records.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrug-white-label.z: Surbrug White Label is a lightly aromatic record inherited from the Surbrug legacy and carried on by Wilke. An earthy, nutty Burley base governs the blend; Cyprian Latakia adds depth and light smoke without overpowering the Burley. Virginia carries the sweet side with tart citrus, honey, and dark-fruit tones. A casing of brandy, chocolate, and vanilla is applied very sparingly. Strength and nicotine sit just below medium, and flavor intensity is at the edge of the medium band. It burns cool and clean without biting the tongue. It suits smokers who want both a casing and Latakia at low intensity, and those seeking long bowls.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrug-white-label.o: A subtle vanilla-cocoa tone mixes into a nutty, lightly smoky scent.

ken-byron-ventures-exhumed-virginia.z: West's Best Exhumed Virginia is a blend combining Virginia and stoved Virginia leaf with Perique, over which a licorice-root casing is applied. The Perique gives the blend a spicy, dried-fruit-leaning direction, while the licorice-root casing deepens its sweetness. The 2019 batch was sold in its original sealed packaging and later moved as a cellar item.
ken-byron-ventures-exhumed-virginia.o: Leaves an earthy aroma accompanied by dark fruit and licorice root.

park-lane-tobacconist-doctors-mix.z: One of Park-Lane Tobacconist's American-type house blends; no usable source could be found to confirm its composition.

sutliff-tobacco-company-jamestowne-tradi.z: Jamestowne Tradition English Mixture is a latakia-based English mixture in Sutliff's Jamestowne Tradition line; independent sources do not provide sufficient information on its composition and production status.

the-smoker-washington-ave.z: A house blend called Washington Ave. from the American tobacconist The Smoker; it is noted as English-style, but no verifiable source describing its composition has been found.

mac-baren-three-nuns-pouch-version.z: The pouch version of Three Nuns is the form presented as loose cut instead of coin cut. The composition base is the same as the tinned version: Virginia as wrap and body, dark-fire-cured Kentucky as the core, Burley as balance. The difference is that the rope, once cut, is rubbed out and packed into the pouch, removing the step of rubbing out coins. The loose cut lets the tobacco burn faster and more easily, though the pressed form's slowly unfolding flavor development is shortened. Virginia's bready sweetness and Kentucky's fine smoke remain the taste's two axes. Suited to smokers seeking everyday practicality and wanting to try the classic blend in ready-cut form.
mac-baren-three-nuns-pouch-version.o: Leaves a fine wood-smoke aroma behind a dry-hay sweetness.

teds-pipe-shoppe-british-imperial.z: One of Ted's Pipe Shoppe's house blends; no accessible source describing its content and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-twist-sliced.z: Brown Twist Sliced is the factory-sliced, coin-thin form of the brown rope tobacco; records indicate it comes from the same production line also known in Kendal as "Happy Bogie." The wrapper leaf is dark fire-cured, while the filler is predominantly fire-cured leaf with a small proportion of air-cured dark Indian leaf. The brown form does not go through the pressure-cooling stage the black ropes undergo. The sliced presentation removes the trouble of cutting individual pieces from a rope; the pieces are rubbed out and aired before filling. In the smoke, a sweetness reminiscent of caramelised sugar and dark chocolate is layered under a strong, earthy, oaky, smoky body; the character is close to that of a cigar. Nicotine is very high. This is a good record for those who love rope tobaccos and prefer short, slow smokes.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-twist-sliced.o: A sharp smoke, burnt wood, and leather aroma fills the room.

bennington-tobacconist-no-40-erebus.z: No. 40 Erebus is Bennington Tobacconist's shop blend built entirely on Burley. Air-cured Kentucky Burleys are twice heat-fermented; this process takes off the leaf's harshness for a mellower smoke. Fermentation preserves Burley's typical dry, nutty, earthy taste while reducing sharpness. The maker states the blend doesn't bite the tongue and burns at a balanced pace. It's aimed at smokers avoiding sugary aromatics, looking for a plain, straightforward Burley character. Since Burley is low in sugar, it lights easily in the pipe and is considered suitable for all-day smoking.
bennington-tobacconist-no-40-erebus.o: Leaves a room note of dry hazelnut, cocoa husk, and faint earthiness.

hu-tobacco-maclochain.z: MacLochain is a Latakia blend in the Clans of Scotland line, distinguished by its floral flavoring. A geranium aroma along with a touch of vanilla and honey is added to a mix of Virginia, Latakia, and English-style black Cavendish. The blend references the wild geraniums growing along the banks of the River Tweed near Kelso. In the smoke, pronounced smokiness runs alongside sharp floral notes and a bitter-orange association. It's aimed at those wanting to try the unusual combination of Latakia with a floral flavoring. Records indicate it's presented in 50-gram tins.
hu-tobacco-maclochain.o: Orange peel and a sharp floral layer accompany the aroma of toasted bread and smoke.

nording-no-3.z: One of the numbered blends tied to the Nording name; no reliable source describing its composition and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-american-blend-delite.z: American Delite is a blend prepared by Kendal's Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. in imitation of American-style aromatics. Its composition includes Virginia, burley, and black cavendish, topped with a flavouring carrying vanilla, caramel, and fresh fruit notes. The presence of burley keeps the smoke cool and mild, while the topping provides pronounced sweetness. Records indicate the producer developed this blend as a response to the well-known sweet aromatics of the American market. With its low nicotine level and straightforwardly sweet character, it suits smokers seeking an aromatic or those new to the pipe.
gawith-hoggarth-co-american-blend-delite.o: Leaves a sweet, candy-like aroma of caramel and vanilla.

dan-tobacco-tumblin-dice.z: A blend from the German manufacturer Dan Tobacco said to be built on Virginia and Perique; there isn't enough reliable source material to confirm its composition and character.

brigham-klondike-gold.z: Klondike Gold is a pure virginia flake prepared for the Canadian Brigham brand; per records the blend was built by German blender Reiner Will. Leaves ranging from golden yellow to light brown are pressed and cut in classic flake form; no casing is applied to the blend. The flavor comes entirely from the leaf itself: citrus tartness, ripe fruit, dry grass and a woody base. Its moisture, as it comes out of the tin, is ready for smoking. Suitable for smokers who love unflavored virginia flakes and expect the blend's sweetness from the leaf itself rather than sugaring. The blend has been discontinued in the US market; a similar product is sold in Canada under the Legend line.
brigham-klondike-gold.o: Leaves a honey, dry hay and light citrus aroma.

ken-byron-ventures-crimson-guard.z: Crimson Guard is a plug tobacco pressed from red Virginia leaf, given a light, colorless rum casing. The 2019 batch was sold in its original sealed packaging and later moved as a cellar item.
ken-byron-ventures-crimson-guard.o: A fine rum and dried-fruit aroma layers over the sugary tobacco.

gawith-hoggarth-co-no-20-latakia-mixture.z: No. 20 Latakia Mixture is a Balkan-style blend built by adding Oriental and Turkish leaf along with a high proportion of Latakia to a Virginia base. Since the Latakia share is pronounced, smoke, leather, and resinous wood lead on the flavor palette; Virginia sweetness plays a balancing role in the background. It is referred to as one of the brand's best-known Latakia blends in Europe. Suited to smokers accustomed to Latakia seeking an unflavored, smoky, salty-spicy profile; since the cut is on the dry side, it packs readily straight from the tin.
gawith-hoggarth-co-no-20-latakia-mixture.o: Leaves a heavy aroma reminiscent of smoke, pine smoke, and leather.

john-patton-crossroads.z: One of the small-scale blends released under the John Patton name; not enough independent sources could be found to document its contents and character.
john-patton-crossroads.o: No source could be found on the room note.

sutliff-tobacco-company-spinnaker.z: Spinnaker is a blend from Sutliff's bulk aromatic line, built on burley and black cavendish. The casing sits on a fruity line that shifts between sweet and tart. No complex structure is aimed for; the blend's defining trait is a consistent taste profile that doesn't change through the bowl. Burley builds the blend's body, while black cavendish adds a sugary, soft base. It sits light to medium in nicotine and medium in taste. It suits smokers looking for a plain aromatic that stays the same from start to finish rather than a shifting, layered structure. It is not currently in Sutliff's catalog.
sutliff-tobacco-company-spinnaker.o: Leaves a sweet fruity, lightly tart scent.

peterson-flake.z: Flake is an unflavored Virginia blend obtained by pressing and slicing selected lemon and bronze Virginia leaf. The blend comes from the Dunhill catalog; after Dunhill stopped producing pipe tobacco, Peterson continued making it with the recipe and tin artwork preserved. Its sweetness is not pushed forward, giving it a measured Virginia character; the smoke proceeds slowly and cool, with a low tendency to bite. Nicotine strength is medium. It suits smokers who love unflavored Virginia flakes, who age tobacco in the tin over long periods, and who like tracking flavor through a single leaf type.
peterson-flake.o: Leaves a thin trace recalling dry hay and stale bread.

hearth-home-vermont-meat-candy.z: Vermont Meat Candy is an aromatic where Cavendish deeply flavored with maple syrup aroma meets dark Kentucky leaf fire-cured over hickory wood. Its name comes from these two axes as well: sweetness is carried by the Cavendish, while the smoky, salty smoke taste is carried by the fire-cured Kentucky. Though the flavoring level is high, because of the fire-cured leaf, the body and nicotine weight are heavier than most aromatics. It's aimed at smokers looking for the sweet-smoky contrast, wanting to try something different from classic fruit or vanilla aromatics. The room note is pronounced and lingers in the space for a long time.
hearth-home-vermont-meat-candy.o: Leaves a pronounced aroma where maple syrup sweetness combines with the smell of meat cooked in wood smoke.

e-a-carey-classic-black-aromatic.z: Classic Black Aromatic is a house blend created by the American tobacconist E. A. Carey in the 1970s following customer trials. It is built from two distinct toasted black cavendish leaves; the leaves are left to rest in bulk in their own sugary sap, taking on a dark, almost black color. It is a moist, soft-textured aromatic. It offers a smoke that is light in nicotine and sweetness-forward in taste, and has long been the line's best-selling entry. It suits those seeking the natural sweetness from cavendish processing rather than heavy chemical additives in aromatic tobaccos, and those wanting a soft start in their early years with the pipe.
e-a-carey-classic-black-aromatic.o: Leaves a dark scent evoking sweet, lightly burnt sugar.

sutliff-tobacco-company-tiramisu-j9.z: Tiramisu J9 is a blend listed within Sutliff's bulk aromatic code series; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-tiramisu-j9.o: No reliable record of a room note could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-aromatic-brown.z: Kendal Aromatic Brown Bogie is a hand-twisted rope tobacco slightly over a centimeter thick. Its body is mostly fire-cured dark leaf, with a small proportion of Indian-origin air-cured dark leaf added. The brand's classic Lakeland-style floral essence is applied on top, so the tin aroma is strongly floral. On the smoke, the smoky, earthy rope character sits together with a sweet floral note. Nicotine is high and the smoke full; suited to experienced smokers wanting a hearty smoke. Slicing and airing for a while before packing is common practice.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-aromatic-brown.o: An intense floral Lakeland aroma spreads through the room together with smoky dark leaf.

davidoff-brazil-virginia.z: Brazil Virginia is the third blend in Davidoff's Discovery series. Per the product description, it's a mixture of double-fermented black Cavendish and the Brazilian Virginias that give the blend its name; however, Cavendish is clearly dominant in the blend, with yellow-brown Virginia ribbons remaining sparse among the dark leaves. It's ribbon cut and comes out of the pack nearly dry; it has a floral-topped, sugary and fruity scent. It catches easily and its smoke disperses quickly. Due to the topping load it's prone to hot burning and tongue bite, so it calls for a slow pace. Rather than giving a sugary taste, it leaves a bitterish taste combined with a vanilla-evoking aroma; the Virginia's contribution is hard to distinguish. Despite a light nicotine load, its body is heavy, and toward the end of the smoke it turns toward tones reminiscent of Burley, even Kentucky, blends. It's a record for those curious about Danish-type Cavendish blends, offering intensity rather than nuance.
davidoff-brazil-virginia.o: Leaves a heavy tobacco scent evoking oiliness and something synthetic.

david-cigarpipe-winter-solstice.z: No verifiable maker or retailer description could be found for this blend, so the record has been left incomplete.

g-l-pease-temple-bar.z: Temple Bar is a Virginia-Oriental blend in G. L. Pease's Old London Series. Ripe red and sweet golden Virginias are heavily spiced with fragrant Oriental leaf; a small amount of perique is added for depth. Whole leaf strips are layered and pressed into large cakes for about two weeks, then cut into bars and boxed. The smoker cuts the slice to whatever thickness they like and rubs it out as often as they wish. It is aimed at smokers seeking a Latakia-free, Oriental-forward, slow-burning blend.
g-l-pease-temple-bar.o: Leaves a spicy, smoky-tinged Oriental leaf aroma over dry grass.

paul-olsen-no-3005.z: For Paul Olsen's blend called No. 3005, no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

cigar-connoisseur-full-virginia-flake.z: Full Virginia Flake is a pure Virginia blend the Cigar Connoisseur shop sells in bulk. The slices come out long and moist; because drying time noticeably changes the flavor, airing is considered a separate stage with this tobacco. According to available records, it doesn't cause burn problems even moist, but roughly forty-five minutes of airing in warm conditions clarifies the slices' taste. Flavor sets in from the first puffs: alongside natural Virginia sweetness, this leaf's characteristic tangy, pure tobacco taste is pronounced. It allows a smoke with generous smoke output without heating the pipe and gives long bowls. Harshness only begins toward the end of the bowl; nicotine content is more measured than many pure Virginias. It suits smokers who love unflavored Virginia character and packing flake tobacco, and who can give their tobacco time.
cigar-connoisseur-full-virginia-flake.o: Leaves an aroma of dry hay and tangy sweet tobacco in the room.

blatter-blatter-coffee.z: A coffee-flavored Blatter & Blatter house blend; no reliable source documenting its composition could be found.

sterling-tobacco-co-maple-leaf.z: Maple Leaf is Sterling Tobacco Company's maple-syrup-flavored blend. Per the maker's description, the base is a plain mixture built directly from burley leaf; the flavoring is added on top of this base. The burley-forward structure gives the blend a dry, walnut-like body and, due to low sugar content, a cool burn; the maple note is felt more as scent than sweetness on the palate. Nicotine is medium. Suited to smokers avoiding heavily syrupy aromatics but seeking a lightly flavored burley.
sterling-tobacco-co-maple-leaf.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly caramel-like scent reminiscent of maple syrup.

motzek-dark-orion.z: Since neither the manufacturer's own description nor two independent reliable sources could be found for the Motzek blend called Dark Orion, its composition, cut, and character could not be documented here.

drew-estate-heirloom-cherry.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of Heirloom Cherry, a blend from Drew Estate.

mr-bs-whiskey.z: Reportedly a whiskey-flavored blend in Canadian Brigham's Mr. B's line; no independent source confirming its composition and current name could be found.

cornell-diehl-tranquility.z: No listing documenting the composition of Tranquility, a Cornell & Diehl blend, could be found in the maker's current catalogue or reliable retailer pages.

ken-byron-ventures-orange-thunder.z: Orange Thunder, one of Ken Byron Ventures' small-batch productions, is recorded as a Virginia-forward blend; no independent source could be found to detail its character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-sugar-bucket-sug.z: Sugar Bucket is a Virginia-burley-based product Sutliff prepared to correspond to another maker's Sugar Barrel blend; no sufficient source for detailed composition and character information could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-sugar-bucket-sug.o: No reliable record of a room note could be found.

synjeco-clegir-rope.z: Clegir Rope is one of the rope tobaccos released under its own name by the Cadenazzo-based Swiss firm Synjeco. Records indicate the firm's rope products were twisted at the Gawith Hoggarth facilities in England; Clegir, a thinner-diameter version of the house's thicker rope Oxenfisl, is prepared from different Virginia leaves. It is an unflavored Virginia rope, sliced into discs and rubbed out for packing. The leaf, tightly twisted into rope form and matured, gives a concentrated taste and a pronounced nicotine load. Smoked slowly, a sweet Virginia core comes through; smoked fast, it can bite the tongue. It suits smokers used to rope and twist tobaccos looking for a strong, unflavored Virginia; it's a heavy smoke for beginners.
synjeco-clegir-rope.o: Leaves a scent of dark, smoked leaf with a light tart fruit note.

blenders-gold-mellow-blend.z: One of the aromatic blends in Sutliff's Blender's Gold line; no reliable source on its composition or character could be found.

samuel-gawith-skiff-mixture.z: Skiff Mixture is one of Samuel Gawith's ribbon-cut English blends. Its composition holds flame-cured Virginia, Turkish-origin Oriental leaf, and Latakia; the Oriental leaf forms the blend's center of gravity. Its name comes from "skiff," meaning a small one-person boat. On the smoke, the Oriental leaf's dry, spicy, lightly sour line comes forward; Latakia persists throughout the bowl but stays in the background and does not weigh the blend down. Virginia sweetness serves as the binder. Nicotine and flavor intensity are medium. Fits smokers seeking an Oriental-forward, more measured English blend rather than a heavy Latakia-dominated mixture.
samuel-gawith-skiff-mixture.o: Leaves a light wood smoke together with a dry spice scent.

watch-city-cigar-deluxe-crumb-cut.z: Deluxe Crumb Cut is a Burley-forward blend Watch City Cigar of Massachusetts prepares at its own facility. According to the maker's account, the blend is the product of seeking a middle path between ribbon cut's overly hot burn and cube cut's difficulty catching, so the leaf is processed into a crumbled "crumb" form. Its character sits on the unflavored Burley line: a nutty, lightly cocoa-like, earthy base comes with measured sweetness. Nicotine load is medium. Thanks to the cut, it sits loose in the bowl and is suited to a cool burn. It's a defining example for smokers seeking an unflavored, everyday-suitable American Burley.
watch-city-cigar-deluxe-crumb-cut.o: Leaves a nutty, earthy, dry scent.

jack-schwartz-importer-traders-blend.z: This is one of the house blends sold under its own name by the Chicago tobacconist Jack Schwartz Importer; no reliable source describing its content could be found.

racine-laramie-burley-english.z: Burley English is one of the house blends from Racine & Laramie, the tobacconist founded in 1869 in San Diego's Old Town neighborhood. It rebuilds the classic English blend mold around Burley: the smoky, spicy core of Latakia and Oriental leaf is mellowed with plug-cut Burley and toasted Cavendish. This structure pulls the Latakia intensity back somewhat and puts a bready, earthy ground in its place. It suits people who want to get to know smoky blends without diving straight into a heavy Balkan mixture, as well as those looking for English character with a Burley texture.
racine-laramie-burley-english.o: Leaves a trace where burnt wood and incense aroma mix with a bready sweetness.

mac-baren-virginia-flake.z: Virginia Flake is one of Mac Baren's Virginia-forward classics. The blend's foundation rests on flame-cured leaves selected from three separate continents; a small amount of specially selected Burley is added to set the balance. The mixture is pressed and cut into slices, finished with a fine topping to bring the natural sugar forward. In the taste, a bright, citrus-leaning top note and a honey-like sweetness lead; the Burley builds a nutty base behind it. Thanks to the flake structure, it burns slow and even, giving a long smoke. The slices need rubbing out, and moisture needs adjusting; rushed, it's prone to running hot. Suited to those wanting to start with Virginia blends and smokers seeking balance in pressed tobaccos.
mac-baren-virginia-flake.o: Leaves a sweetish trace leaning toward honey and dried fruit.

david-p-ehrlich-company-judges-mixture.z: Judge's Mixture is one of the shop blends sold under the name of David P. Ehrlich Company, a long-standing Boston tobacconist. Founded in 1868 and taking its current name in 1916, the firm has long been known both for pipe-making and its own tobacco blends; per records, its most recent production was done by Sutliff and offered jointly with the related Leavitt & Peirce shop. The blend is built on a black-cavendish-forward body and flavored with a light mango topping. It's light to medium in nicotine, with a soft smoke. It suits smokers not seeking a burnt or sharp taste but a sweet, fruity aromatic, and it fits any hour of the day.
david-p-ehrlich-company-judges-mixture.o: Leaves a lightly sugary scent carrying tropical fruit sweetness.

richs-lord-cravens-havana-blend.z: Lord Craven's Havana Blend is one of Rich's Cigar Store's house blends, said to contain cigar leaf; no verifiable source could be found describing its composition.
richs-lord-cravens-havana-blend.o: No reliable information could be found on the room note.

pipesandcigars-com-blending-perique.z: Blending Perique is not a standalone blend but a single-varietal leaf sold in bulk for use in blending. Fermented under pressure in a barrel in Louisiana's St. James region, Perique is known for its distinctive plum, fig, and pepper associations; the batch pipesandcigars.com sells is reportedly Sutliff's Louisiana Perique coded TS-20. The leaf is extremely intense and full, so it is usually used as a small percentage of a mixture; it is most often paired with Virginia to build the frame called VA-Per. It serves as an intermediate ingredient for home blenders; smoked alone, its nicotine and flavor intensity are at the top end.
pipesandcigars-com-blending-perique.o: Leaves a sharp, tangy aroma reminiscent of vinegary plum and pepper.

edwards-quick-draw.z: No sufficient independent sourcing could be reached to document the composition and character of Quick Draw, a pipe tobacco from Edward's.

paul-olsen-no-42.z: One of the Virginia-and-burley-based blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

tom-eltang-sweet-mellow.z: Sweet & Mellow is the aromatic member of the tobacco line bearing the name of Danish pipe maker Tom Eltang. The series was developed according to Eltang's own palate preferences together with American maker Cornell & Diehl and produced in North Carolina; the brand's identity, however, rests on the Danish pipe tradition. In the blend, black Cavendish joins Burley and Virginia leaves in a ribbon cut. On opening the jar there is a sweet aroma leaning toward fermented apple and raisin; on the smoke, notes evoking chocolate and maple syrup come forward. Nicotine is moderate and the burn is cool; aimed at those who steer away from heavy syrupy aromatics but still want a sweet everyday smoke that doesn't fully mask the tobacco's natural taste.
tom-eltang-sweet-mellow.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly chocolatey aroma reminiscent of fermented apple and raisin.

robert-mcconnell-virginia-5-year-matured.z: Robert McConnell is an English brand rooted in London, now produced in Germany by Kohlhase & Kopp. Virginia 5 Year Matured, as its name suggests, is an unflavored single-varietal blend of long-aged Virginia leaf, pressed and then sliced into flake. Its character rests on the bready sweetness of Virginia's own sugars, along with dry-hay and light fruit tones. Nicotine is measured; smoked slowly it leaves no sharpness on the tongue. It is a good fit for fans of unflavored Virginia and smokers accustomed to flake tobacco; reports note the sweetness increases with jar aging.
robert-mcconnell-virginia-5-year-matured.o: Leaves a dry-hay aroma with a hint of bread crust.

samuel-gawith-golden-glow-bulk.z: Golden Glow's bulk presentation is the same blend as the tinned product; the difference is in packaging. The tobacco consists solely of Virginia leaf, comes as broken flake pieces, and carries no flavor casing. Since moisture in bulk batches can vary depending on packaging, the habit of airing before packing applies here too. In character it follows a mild, straightforward Virginia line: sweetness is measured, nicotine fullness low, and no sharpening is expected during the smoke. It suits those seeking an undemanding, long-smokable Virginia; it may read as light for smokers expecting the intensity of dark pressed Virginias.
samuel-gawith-golden-glow-bulk.o: Leaves a light, fine trace evoking dry hay and honey.

newminster-no-81-denmark-pipe-cut.z: Newminster No. 81 Denmark Pipe Cut is a loosely cut bulk tobacco built from African and American flue-cured Virginia leaves. The blend is given an almost imperceptibly light top-flavoring, so it sits somewhere between aromatic and unflavored. The smoke is soft and light; Virginia's natural sweetness leads, and nicotine is low. Suitable for smokers looking for an easy-lighting, light Virginia that can be smoked throughout the day.
newminster-no-81-denmark-pipe-cut.o: Leaves a faint, lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of dry hay in the room.

john-aylesbury-virginia-blend.z: A Virginia-forward blend from John Aylesbury; no detailed, verifiable information on its contents could be found.
john-aylesbury-virginia-blend.o: No verifiable information on its room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-engine-611.z: Engine #611 is part of Cornell & Diehl's railroad-themed bulk blend series, named after the last of the Norfolk and Western Railway's Class J steam locomotives. It is composed of black cavendish, Virginia, and burley leaves, topped with a light coumarin-vanilla flavoring. It is a ribbon cut, offered in bulk. The blend sits at a measured aromatic level that doesn't mask the leaf's own taste: the vanilla's sweetness is balanced by burley's nutty dryness and Virginia's sugary tone. With nicotine sitting in the light-to-medium range, it makes a good option for long, everyday smoking and for anyone transitioning from aromatics toward natural tobacco tastes.
cornell-diehl-engine-611.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla aroma with a hint of dry grass.

murray-sons-co-ltd-parsons-pleasure.z: One of the discontinued straight Virginia blends from the Belfast-based Murray Sons & Co factory; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition could not be found.

cornell-diehl-luxurious.z: A blend from Cornell & Diehl referred to as Virginia-and-Latakia-based, not in current catalogues; no adequate source on its composition and character was found.
cornell-diehl-luxurious.o: Records indicate it leaves a smoky tobacco scent.

wessex-brown-virginia-flake.z: This is, according to records, a flake-cut blend belonging to the Virginia family of the Wessex series; no sufficient source could be found to detail its character.

dunhill-elizabethan-mixture.z: Elizabethan Mixture is a ribbon-cut blend where Virginia leaves meet perique. It burns steadily, leaving white ash in the bowl; this even burn allows the tobacco to be smoked slowly. Aging notably transforms the blend: perique's sharp spice mellows over time, and the Virginia side matures and comes forward. Its strength runs medium to strong, and its flavor intensity is above average; it is not an all-day blend but rather a choice for particular occasions. It suits smokers familiar with Virginia-perique mixtures, comfortable with nicotine load, and interested in tobaccos that reward cellaring. Production under the Dunhill name has ended.
dunhill-elizabethan-mixture.o: Leaves a trace of the tart Virginia and spicy perique scent lingering in the room.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-1.z: Wilke No. 1 sits at the head of the brand's numbered blend series as a light, everyday smoke. According to the maker's recipe, its base is unsugared black cavendish, joined by a small amount of dark Burley and the leaf Wilke calls Royal Scot. Since the casing load is kept low, the blend gives a dry, plain profile far from the syrupy structure we're used to in sweet aromatics with black cavendish. The blend's slow-burning, non-harsh structure makes it suitable for mornings or long sessions. Nicotine is low and flavor intensity is measured, making it a stepping stone for smokers wanting to move toward unflavored blends but wary of Virginia's sharp tartness. Wilke is a blending house tracing its roots to 1870s New York, and most of these numbered blends come from the brand's old ledgers.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-1.o: Leaves a scent of dry bread crust and dark tobacco, carrying no sweet trace.

7-20-4-boston-tea-party.z: Boston Tea Party is the unflavored American-type mixture in the 7-20-4 Briary Blends line. White and dark Burley, bright and red Virginia, and Turkish Oriental leaf are brought together; the line was introduced in 2023, with blending done at the Cornell & Diehl workshop. Its name references the brand's New England origin and the region's history. The smoke starts medium-bodied at the top of the bowl, rising to a medium-full intensity toward the bottom. Cedar and nutty tones arrive together with sweet hay and citrus; at the finish, a caramel-close nutty sweetness and a black-tea taste appear. Since no flavoring is used, it suits smokers accustomed to unflavored Burley-Virginia character who want the Oriental spice in moderation.
7-20-4-boston-tea-party.o: Leaves a room note of cedar shavings, dry hay, and roasted hazelnut.

uhles-blend-232.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend Blend 232 has been found.

james-barber-golden-coconut.z: A coconut-flavored house blend from the James Barber tobacconist house; no independent source could be found to document its composition and character.
james-barber-golden-coconut.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

mcclelland-tudor-castle-arcade.z: Tudor Castle Arcade is a Collector Series entry that keeps the same-family Tudor Castle's Virginia-Perique backbone while adding Katerini-sourced Oriental leaf and Syrian Latakia. The Virginias give high, wine-like notes and a sweet, cola-like aftertaste; the Katerini adds a floral top note, while the Latakia keeps the smoke measured. When the flake structure is rubbed out and packed, it burns cool and even. Through the smoke, a sweetness reminiscent of cola nut, sweet tea, and candied walnut sits alongside the Oriental leaf's faintly salty-tangy edge; the Perique occasionally gives a peppery touch. The dry, tin-note aroma and taste are likened to a spiced fruitcake. The blend was discontinued as Syrian Latakia stocks ran out and the firm closed in 2018.
mcclelland-tudor-castle-arcade.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of spiced fruitcake and fine wood smoke.

peterson-summertime-2013.z: Summertime 2013 is a limited edition blend released as part of Peterson's Summertime series specific to that year; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient first-hand sources confirming its content and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold.z: Kendal Gold is a blend offering golden flue-cured Virginia leaf in a very fine shag cut. Moisture is high, so airing it for a while before smoking is common. The smoke is cool, and records note it doesn't easily heat up even when pushed. On the flavor palette, Virginia's herbal-honeyed sweetness stands out, with nicotine at a low-to-moderate level. Suited to those who like a fine cut and want a light Virginia that can be smoked all day.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold.o: Leaves a fine tobacco aroma reminiscent of dry hay and light honey.

reiner-light-english.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of Reiner Light English.

doc-james-yorktown.z: No reliable source could be found identifying the maker, composition, or character of this blend referred to under the Doc James name.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-five-brothers.z: Five Brothers, according to records, is a blend created over a century ago by the Finzer brothers, made entirely of air-cured burley leaf. Its cut is a very fine ribbon close to shag. It is produced today in Denmark and imported into the United States by Lane Limited. The blend is unflavored; its taste carries a nutty, earthy, sharp burley character. It is heavy in nicotine with a pronounced fullness. Suited to experienced smokers seeking unflavored, strong classic shelf (OTC) burley blends; because of its fine cut, it needs to be packed loosely.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-five-brothers.o: Leaves a sharp, earthy, intense tobacco scent dominated by burnt grass.

gq-tobaccos-no-2-dutch-halfzware.z: GQ Tobaccos's fine-cut blend offered under the name Dutch-style halfzware; there is no sourcing documenting its composition and character.
gq-tobaccos-no-2-dutch-halfzware.o: No record of its aroma could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-kings-ramson-2021.z: King's Ramson 2021 is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

barclay-rex-royal-scott.z: Counted among Barclay Rex's longtime aromatic shop blends; no adequate source describing its composition could be found.
barclay-rex-royal-scott.o: According to records it leaves a sweet, lightly smoky room note.

pipes-pleasures-johnny-mocha.z: Pipes & Pleasures is a tobacconist shop opened in Columbus, Ohio, in 1977; Johnny Mocha is one of the blends the shop offers under its own name, though no sufficient sources describing the blend's content and character could be found.

cornell-diehl-engine-113.z: Engine #113 is a member of Cornell & Diehl's Engine series, dedicated to steam locomotives; it is named after CNJ #113, a locomotive that worked for thirty years at the Reading Anthracite company in Pennsylvania. Per the manufacturer's description, red and bright Virginia, cube-cut burley, and fire-cured Kentucky are brought together, then topped with brandy and vanilla notes. It is a ribbon cut. The Kentucky leaf sets the blend apart from an ordinary aromatic, grounding it in a smoky, hearty base; vanilla and brandy leave a measured sweetness over that base. Nicotine is medium. It suits smokers wanting aromatic flavor together with real tobacco body.
cornell-diehl-engine-113.o: Leaves a lightly smoky, boozy aroma along with vanilla sweetness.

samuel-gawith-finest-kendal-twist-black.z: Finest Kendal Twist Black is the dark-colored member of the twist tradition Samuel Gawith continues in Kendal. The leaf is twisted into rope, aged for a long time to darken, and sold in wheel form; the smoker cuts coin-thick slices and crumbles them. Its smoke is intense, earthy, and structured to bring forward the tobacco's own taste; nicotine load is high. It requires good drying and slow smoking. Suited to smokers accustomed to twist and rope cuts who seek a strong English-style tobacco.
samuel-gawith-finest-kendal-twist-black.o: Leaves a dark, smoky, earthy tobacco scent.

brigham-enterprises-inc-aurora-borealis.z: Aurora Borealis is the English mixture in Brigham's Legend series. The leaf carries a nearly black, dark appearance; the composition includes generous spicy Latakia, matured Virginia and shag-cut stoved black Virginia. Despite the high Latakia proportion, thanks to the softening sweetness of the stoved Virginia the smoke runs cool and does not turn harsh on the tongue. Flavor is intense, the room note pronounced; nicotine stays medium. Designed for smokers who love Latakia-forward blends and seek a dark, smoky profile. Offered in a 50-gram tin.
brigham-enterprises-inc-aurora-borealis.o: A light sweetness accompanies a heavy wood smoke and soot aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-rosedale-cherr.z: A cherry-flavored aromatic blend belonging to Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Kendal series; no independent sourcing documenting its composition and cut could be found.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-rosedale-cherr.o: Leaves a sweet cherry and floral aroma.

iwan-ries-balkan-supreme.z: Balkan Supreme is a ribbon-cut English-Balkan blend produced in Denmark for Iwan Ries & Co. of Chicago. Its composition includes Virginia, Latakia, Oriental, and natural Cavendish; the Latakia proportion gives the blend a heavy, smoky, salty body, with the Oriental leaves laying a spicy layer beneath it. Classified by the maker as full-bodied, the blend sits at the high end for both nicotine and flavor intensity. It's aimed at pipe smokers accustomed to classic Latakia-heavy mixtures, looking for a long, slow smoke at certain times of day; it carries no flavoring.
iwan-ries-balkan-supreme.o: The wood smoke and smokiness from the Latakia settle into the room for a long time.

butera-dark-stoved-royal-vintage.z: Dark Stoved in Butera's Royal Vintage series is an unflavored flake tobacco built entirely on Virginia leaf. Per records the blend was prepared by McClelland. Flue-cured Virginia leaf is darkened through an additional heat treatment, then pressed into flake form. The slices are dark-colored and are rubbed out for filling. Because the heavy heat treatment converts much of the leaf's sugar, a flat, dry profile emerges in the smoke; the sweet-spicy intensity expected of dark Virginia flakes is limited. Nicotine is medium, and it can bite the tongue if smoked quickly. It carries no flavor casing. It is no longer in production today and is found only in old stock.
butera-dark-stoved-royal-vintage.o: Leaves a faint trace reminiscent of toasted bread and dry wood.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-menthol.z: Kendal Gold is the umbrella name for the shag-cut tobacco family Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. produces in the town of Kendal in England's Lake District. The family's body is built from Brazilian- and Indian-origin, heat-cured light Virginia leaf; largely stripped of stem, it's cut into fine golden strands. The producer steams and softens the tobacco, cuts it, toasts it on a hot cylinder, and then applies the top flavoring — so the family's members are versions of the same body offered with different scents. Entry No. 22 in the series carries menthol over the Virginia body. Menthol leaves a cooling, lightly sharp sensation on the smoke; underneath, the leaf's herbal, hay, and light-lemon sweetness remains. A cherry-menthol version of the same body is also produced. The fine shag cut lights immediately and resists going out; since it burns fast, it calls for a slow tempo. Nicotine is measured. Suited to smokers wanting a cool-smoking, light-bodied tobacco.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-menthol.o: Leaves a cool menthol and lightly sweet tobacco aroma.

cornell-diehl-anthology-2023.z: This blend, part of Cornell & Diehl's yearly limited-production series, does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog; details cannot be given as not enough sourcing could be found to describe its content.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-rum-and-ma.z: Match Rum and Maple is Sutliff's counterpart to the long-standing classic aromatic called Rum & Maple. Virginia and black cavendish are added to a burley-forward base; a rum- and maple-syrup-based casing is applied over it. The blend has been distributed both in bulk and, under the Tobacco Galleria name, in pouch form. The casing is more pronounced than in the Lane version it corresponds to; maple leads over the rum. Nicotine is light to medium and taste intensity is medium. It suits smokers wanting a sweet, straightforward aromatic who don't mind the casing sitting ahead of the tobacco.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-rum-and-ma.o: Leaves maple syrup sweetness in front with a rum scent behind it.

hearth-home-slice-o-gold.z: Slice O' Gold is an American-type mixture prepared by Russ Ouellette under the Hearth & Home brand; no reliable source detailing the blend's composition and character could be found.

georgetown-tobacco-raven.z: Referred to as one of Georgetown Tobacco's aromatic shop blends; no verifiable sourcing describing its composition and topping could be found.
georgetown-tobacco-raven.o: No record of the room aroma could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-vanilla.z: Vanilla is Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s long-running classic vanilla aromatic; under the brand's latest naming scheme it's also sold as American V. The blend consists of a combination of black Cavendish and flue-cured Virginia leaf, offered as a ribbon cut. The vanilla topping gives a soft, velvety sweetness; the Virginia base adds coolness and lightness to the smoke. It stays light to medium in nicotine, making it suitable for long sessions. An entry for those new to aromatics and anyone wanting a sweet blend that can be smoked all day.
gawith-hoggarth-co-vanilla.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and creamy dough aroma.

cornell-diehl-exhausted-rooster.z: Exhausted Rooster is a Virginia-Burley blend Cornell & Diehl prepared for the Chicagoland Pipe Show, offered as broken flake. Virginia's sweetness, fire-cured burley's body, and a small amount of perique's spice come together, with no added flavoring. Since the flakes come out of the tin relatively dry, they need little airing, pack easily, and burn slow and cool. The flavor profile leads with dark fruit notes recalling plum and raisin, an earthy sweetness, and a fine peppery edge from the perique. Strength is medium: burley provides genuine tobacco texture and nicotine, while perique isn't dominant enough to throw off the balance. It makes a suitable everyday flake for those seeking unflavored blends along the Virginia-perique and burley axis.
cornell-diehl-exhausted-rooster.o: Leaves a dried-fruit and earthy tobacco aroma along with a light smoky trace from the fire-cured leaf.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-coffee-pigtail.z: Sweet Coffee Pigtail is the coffee-topped version of 'pigtail'-type Burma tobacco, made by twisting fire-cured leaves into a very fine rope. Because the rope's diameter is small, cutting it produces small, coin-sized slices; the cut surface shows a dark reddish-brown color. The pouch aroma is oily and spicy, topped with a roasted-coffee association. On the smoke, the earthy, smoky core combines with coffee's sweetness. These fine ropes are traditionally sold for both chewing and pipe smoking; they run intense in nicotine and call for slow smoking. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. is one of the English producers that continues traditional twist (rope) production at its Kendal factory, hand-twisting fire-cured leaves into rope form. Because twist tobaccos don't go through a pressure-cooking stage, they stay intense in nicotine; records indicate these ropes are sold for both chewing and pipe smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-coffee-pigtail.o: Leaves an aroma combining roasted coffee and woody tobacco scents.

paul-olsen-vester-voldgade-92-vv92.z: A Paul Olsen Virginia blend taking its name from the pipe shop at Vester Voldgade 92 in Copenhagen; no independent source describing its composition could be found.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-irlandez-ex.z: This is stated to be the export-prepared version of the Irlandez line; no independent source describing its content and character could be found.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-irlandez-ex.o: Records suggest it leaves a sweetish cavendish scent.

american-tobacco-co-dills-best.z: Dill's Best is a historic American pipe tobacco carrying the name of the J. G. Dill company, founded in Richmond, Virginia. Packaging information traces the brand's origins to the second half of the nineteenth century; a 1946 trademark filing lists the name's first use as 1885, though some tins bear the date 1848. The product changed hands over time, carried on first by the U.S. Tobacco Company and later by major firms in the American tobacco industry. The blend follows the classic mold of American house-style tobaccos: a Burley-heavy base is mellowed with a measured amount of Virginia. It was sold in several cuts — granulated plug, slice, and rubbed — with the leaf rubbed from the plug retaining moisture for a long time. The taste is nutty, dry, and lightly sweet, carrying no pronounced flavoring. With the decline of pipe smoking in America, the brand was withdrawn from the market and today is only of historical interest.
