american-tobacco-co-dills-best.o: Leaves a plain tobacco room note leaning toward dry hay and nutshell.

savinelli-black-cavendish.z: Black Cavendish is the black-cavendish-forward member of Savinelli's classic aromatic line. Most of the blend is made up of mild black cavendish; fine-cut, fruity virginia and nutty burley accompany it. It is ribbon cut and sold in 50-gram tins. A measured vanilla-and-chocolate flavoring is applied as the top layer; the casing is noticeable but does not fully cover the tobacco's own taste. Nicotine load is low, the smoke cool and straightforward. Suited to pipe newcomers or smokers seeking a light, sweet blend that leaves a strong scent in the room.
savinelli-black-cavendish.o: Spreads a scent of vanilla cream and cocoa through the room.

my-smoking-shop-christmas-cheer.z: One of the seasonal aromatics My Smoking Shop sells in bulk; sufficient sources describing its composition could not be found.

ole-shenandoah-fuzzy-schnapps.z: Fuzzy Schnapps is an American-made aromatic blend taking its name from peach liqueur. A clear peach essence is given to mild burley, sweet Virginia, and silky-textured black cavendish leaves; the flavor direction concentrates on a single fruit, with no complex construction sought. Nicotine load is low and the smoke body light. It suits those seeking a pronouncedly fruit-flavored tobacco with little bite, and newcomers to the pipe. The Ole Shenandoah line was sold in 50-gram tins and bulk packs; the blend is not produced today.
ole-shenandoah-fuzzy-schnapps.o: Leaves a scent of ripe peach and lightly sugared fruit.

mastro-de-paja-milano.z: No reliable source describing the contents and character of the Milano blend released under the Italian pipe maker Mastro de Paja could be found; records indicate it's a blend within the unflavored Virginia line.
mastro-de-paja-milano.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

paul-olsen-brown-plug.z: A Virginia-based blend from the Poul Olsen shop, apparently offered in pressed plug form judging by its name; not enough source material documenting its details could be found.

1776-tobacco-co-bostonian.z: One of 1776 Tobacco Co.'s blends; per records it's referred to as a mixture close to English style, but no adequate source verifying its composition could be reached.

milan-tobacconists-chartwell.z: Chartwell is a light-bodied blend in Milan Tobacconists' English mixtures group. According to the shop's description, sliced Burley, latakia, and Turkish leaf come together in balanced fashion; it leaves a light sweetness reminiscent of plum at the finish. Because the latakia proportion is kept limited, the smoke is smoky but not heavy; the taste holds through the whole bowl and doesn't leave sharpness on the tongue. A construction suited to smokers newly approaching English mixtures or looking for a light latakia dose during the day. Its name references Winston Churchill's home.
milan-tobacconists-chartwell.o: Leaves a light wood-smoke and dried-fruit aroma.

quintessence-no-2.z: No reliable source could be found documenting the maker, content, and character of the Quintessence No.2 blend.
quintessence-no-2.o: No information describing the room note could be found in available records.

newminster-no-84-oriental-pipe-cut.z: No. 84 Oriental Pipe Cut combines small-leaved sun-cured Oriental tobaccos with mature virginia leaves from Africa's fertile regions. No pronounced top-flavoring is used; the natural scent comes from the leaf itself. Turkish tobacco's mild spice sits over Virginia's sweetness. Like No. 80, it is a fine ribbon cut at near-dry moisture, lights easily, and keeps a measured flavor profile. Since it contains no Latakia, it leaves the Oriental character exposed; suitable for those wanting to get to know Oriental tobaccos on their own and for those looking for a blending tobacco. It is produced at Mac Baren's facilities in Denmark.
newminster-no-84-oriental-pipe-cut.o: Leaves a spicy dry-herb and lightly sweet tobacco aroma in the room.

per-g-jensen-port-guardian.z: For Per G. Jensen's blend called Port Guardian, no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-richmond-mixtu.z: A Virginia-based mixture registered under the Orlik Tobacco Company A/S name; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

levin-pipes-international-trollshaws.z: Trollshaws is an extremely rare-today blend, its name taken from Tolkien's geography, built by Barry Levin on matured Virginia; not enough sources could be found for its cut and exact composition.
levin-pipes-international-trollshaws.o: Leaves a room note reminiscent of dry hay and lightly tangy fruit.

mcclelland-2009-holiday-spirit.z: Holiday Spirit is a member of the aromatic series McClelland began in 2008 and released in limited numbers each year for the holiday season; the 2009 release is the second entry in this tradition. The series' basic structure rests on a trio of nutty Burley, tangy Virginia, and black Cavendish; this base is flavored with dark rum, walnut praline, and cocoa aroma. On opening the tin, chocolate and sugared walnut aroma stand out, followed by the rum's tone. The smoke is mild and low in nicotine. As with the series generally, the cut is irregular, with leaf pieces of different sizes mixed together. Prepared for smokers seeking sweet, non-spiced aromatics typical of the holiday season. Since McClelland stopped production in 2018, the series is no longer made.
mcclelland-2009-holiday-spirit.o: Leaves a sweet trace with aromas of cocoa, brown sugar, and rum.

edwards-drury-lane.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Drury Lane, a pipe tobacco from Edward's. Edward's is a tobacconist business based in Tampa, Florida.

just-for-him-black-magic-woman.z: One of the house blends the Just For Him tobacconist prepares at its own counter; no independent source could be found on its contents or character.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.z: This is a peach-flavored blend in the Brazilian maker Imigrantes's Candido Giovanella line; no independent source describing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.o: No room note described in the records could be found.

clan-shaw-trade-winds.z: No reliable, independent sourcing could be found regarding Clan Shaw Trade Winds, so a detailed profile could not be compiled.

gawith-hoggarth-co-american-irish-spice.z: American Irish Spice is the whisky-flavoured member of the American Blend family sold in bulk by Kendal's Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. Its base of black cavendish, burley, and Virginia leaf is ribbon cut; the whisky flavouring applied over it is felt at a medium-to-strong level. Nicotine stays light, and flavour intensity is medium.
gawith-hoggarth-co-american-irish-spice.o: Leaves a sweet whisky and caramel-like cavendish aroma.

gq-tobaccos-sugar-spice.z: One of GQ Tobaccos's small-batch blends marketed as a spiced aromatic; no detailed profile could be produced since there is no independent sourcing to confirm its composition and character.

cargo-hold-yankee-clipper.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Yankee Clipper under the Cargo Hold brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

cornell-diehl-from-beyond-2025.z: From Beyond is an English mixture from Cornell & Diehl's The Old Ones series, dedicated to H. P. Lovecraft, inspired by the 1920s story of the same name; it is presented as the only blend from that series brought into the Small Batch line and is reissued year by year with the vintage noted. The 2025 edition uses Eastern North Carolina red Virginias (2017), bright Canadian Virginias (2022), Thai Izmir (2019), Turkish Latakia, Greek Basma (2022), and 2004-crop Cyprus Latakia. Head blender Jeremy Reeves describes the blend as his answer to an impression he took from an aged 1990s tin of Dunhill Nightcap. The flavor profile is dark, dense, and sweet in the background, carrying an incense-like, smoky air. Red and bright Virginias build a sweet, earthy foundation, while Izmir and Basma add a spiced, lightly floral layer; the two separate Latakias — one classically smoky, the other darker and more resinous — round out the body. It is prepared for smokers accustomed to full-bodied, multi-component English mixtures.
cornell-diehl-from-beyond-2025.o: Leaves a dense aroma of wood smoke and incense.

my-smoking-shop-autumn-sun.z: One of the blends sold in bulk by British tobacconist My Smoking Shop; sufficient sources describing its composition could not be found.

dan-tobacco-alter-pinnas.z: Alter Pinnas is one of Dan Tobacco's Virginia-and-Burley-focused, coarse-cut blends. Its composition includes Virginia, Burley, smoke-cured Kentucky leaf, and Cavendish. The coarse cut makes it easy to pack and light, and it comes with a moisture level balanced enough to keep it burning evenly throughout the smoke. On the smoke, Virginia's sweetness and Kentucky's spicy, woody sharpness are the defining notes; Cavendish adds an aromatic texture in the background and leaves a very faint fruity trace. Though body appears mild to medium, it's satisfying in nicotine, so it's described as a blend suited to all-day smoking without feeling thin. Suited to those looking for German-style mixtures where casing doesn't take the lead and leaf flavor stays dominant.
dan-tobacco-alter-pinnas.o: A faint fruity sweetness mingles with a scent of roasted leaf and woody smoke.

mcclelland-no-x-40-burley-by-the-slice.z: Records indicate this was a Burley product presented in thick, loose slices, its leaf noticeably darkened from cellaring since 1992; discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018.

vauen-no-09-himalaya-blend.z: No. 09 Himalaya Blend is a mellow aromatic representing the fruity wing of Vauen's numbered series. Velvety black Cavendish makes up the bulk of the blend, joined by sweet golden Virginia; different cuts are combined to aim for a cool, balanced burn. Its aroma is built on ripe cherry, goji berry and a subtle citrus note. Nicotine is light and the taste is sweet and fruity. Aimed at those not seeking Latakia or high nicotine, who want a light, fragrant smoke during the day.
vauen-no-09-himalaya-blend.o: Leaves a scent of ripe cherry, red berries, and a subtle citrus peel.

john-patton-harvest-home.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Patton's Harvest Home pipe tobacco.

mcclelland-dark-star.z: Dark Star is an unflavored flake blend of darkened Virginia leaves in McClelland's Personal Reserve series. The slices come quite moist and tightly packed; separating and packing them into a pipe takes experience. Records indicate that airing the slices thoroughly and partially rubbing them out before packing significantly eases both loading and burning. In the smoke, the near-black leaf's mild sweetness stands out along with spiced touches; the tobacco burns cool and long. Though nicotine dose looks light in a small pipe, it reaches a satisfying level in a medium-sized bowl. Given the preparation difficulty, it isn't a blend for those new to the pipe; it's aimed at smokers who know how to handle dark Virginia flakes. The brand closed in 2018.
mcclelland-dark-star.o: Leaves a heavy, tangy, sharp tobacco aroma.

cornell-diehl-father-the-flame-straight-.z: This is a Cornell & Diehl blend recorded as an English type and known under two names; details are left blank as it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog and no reliable source giving its composition could be found.

tsuge-premium-pipe-tobacco-ryujin-the-dr.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Tsuge Premium Pipe Tobacco blend Ryujin - The Dragon God has been found.

cornell-diehl-burley-flake-4.z: Burley Flake #4 is the series member containing Latakia. Light and dark burley leaves form the body, red Virginia provides sweetness, and a small amount of Latakia is added on top. After pressing and slicing it is presented as flake; there is no added flavoring. Here Latakia isn't present in a proportion that turns the mixture into an English blend; it more casts a smoky shadow over burley's nutty, earthy core. This structure is positioned as an example within the series of how burley and Latakia sit together. Nicotine strength is high, and the smoke retains its burley-derived heaviness. It suits those accustomed to unflavored burley who want a small amount of smoke.
cornell-diehl-burley-flake-4.o: A noticeable wood-smoke trace lingers at the edge of a nutty aroma.

cornell-diehl-shaare-orah-gates-of-light.z: Sha'are Orah is a blend in Cornell & Diehl's Hebraica series. Its name comes from the book of the same title by Rabbi Yosef ben Avraham Gikatilla, considered one of the foundational texts of the Kabbalah tradition. The series' origin traces back to mixtures blender William Serad prepared for Rabbi Ira Stone, who favored Burley-Oriental-Perique compositions. The blend is built on a base of cube-cut Burley and stoved red Virginia; touches of Perique and Oriental leaf strike a balance between sweetness and spice. The cut is coarse and textured. As expected of Burley-Perique compositions, it's full-bodied in both nicotine and smoke intensity; suited to experienced smokers looking for unflavored, filling, spicy blends.
cornell-diehl-shaare-orah-gates-of-light.o: Leaves a dark, spicy tobacco scent reminiscent of nuts.

ashton-type-6.z: Ashton Type 6 is referred to as an aromatic blend in the brand's numbered series; no adequate independent source verifying its content and character could be found.
ashton-type-6.o: According to records, not enough information could be found to describe it.

st-basils-tobacco-miyagis-mindfulness.z: A blend classified as American-style from St. Basil's Tobacco; sufficient independent sources describing its composition and character could not be found.
st-basils-tobacco-miyagis-mindfulness.o: No description is available in records.

gawith-hoggarth-co-grasmere-flake.z: Grasmere Flake is a Lakeland flake where Kendal-style floral essences are used pronouncedly. The essence line rests on rose and geranium; because of this it's considered a relative of the same house's Kendal Flake, though records indicate it's fuller in both taste and nicotine. The slices are moist and dark, smoked after airing. Beneath the floral essence sits the earthy fullness of dark fired leaves; nicotine becomes noticeable as the smoke progresses. Suited to smokers familiar with Lakeland style who want a high-nicotine flake.
gawith-hoggarth-co-grasmere-flake.o: Leaves an intense floral aroma reminiscent of rose and geranium leaf.

e-a-carey-careys-10.z: Carey's 10+ is one of E. A. Carey's older blends, kept in the catalog since 1984. Per the maker's description, it brings together a light burley, toasted cavendish and light-colored Virginia; the burley's rough edges are smoothed during processing while the tobacco's own taste is preserved. The result is a cool-burning, easy-smoking aromatic where the topping doesn't stand out too much. It is light to medium in nicotine. It is an in-between choice for smokers seeking the tobacco's own toasted taste rather than heavy flavoring, but who aren't ready to move to fully unadulterated blends either.
e-a-carey-careys-10.o: Leaves a lightly sweet scent of toasted tobacco and nutty dried fruit.

charatan-royal-escape-mixture.z: Royal Escape Mixture is built on a single leaf family, bringing together a selection ranging from light, pale-lemon Virginias to heavy-bodied dark Virginias. The thick-cut ribbon leaf burns slowly and cool; a light plum-like topping added to the blend gives it a sharp turn reminiscent of Perique. It runs above typical Virginia blends in nicotine. The Charatan brand was taken over by Tor Imports to keep the name alive after Dunhill withdrew from pipe tobacco and handmade cigars in 2017; Royal Escape is offered as the counterpart to take the place of Dunhill's Royal Yacht. The brand is British in origin, with production now carried out in continental Europe. Suitable for smokers seeking dark, full Virginia blends with a barely perceptible topping, wanting a satisfying smoke at certain times of day.
charatan-royal-escape-mixture.o: Leaves a tart, dark-Virginia sweetness with a plum-like fruity trace.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-dark-menthol.z: Kendal Dark is Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s dark-bodied shag family. The body is built from Malawi-origin fire-cured leaf and India-origin air-cured Virginia; the mixture is cut into fine shag. The menthol version carries a menthol top flavoring over this dark body. The fine cut lights quickly and resists going out; on the other hand, since it burns fast, it calls for a slow tempo. It's a full-bodied tobacco for nicotine; the menthol's coolness doesn't mask the dark leaf's earthy, peppery base but layers on top of it. Suited to smokers familiar with dark English shag tobaccos who want a menthol version.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-dark-menthol.o: Leaves a dark, smoky tobacco aroma along with a cool mint-menthol scent.

ken-byron-ventures-the-endless-void-2020.z: The 2020 release of The Endless Void is reported to be built on cigar leaf; no independent source could be found to detail its contents.
ken-byron-ventures-the-endless-void-2020.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-burley-flake-2.z: Burley Flake #2 is the member of the series without perique. Light and dark burley leaves are used together for the body, with red Virginia added for sweetness; the manufacturer's records also list fire-cured Kentucky among the components. The mixture is pressed and sliced, presented as flake, and carries no added flavoring. Bringing together two different burley types is the blend's distinguishing feature: light burley builds a dry, lightly papery base, while dark burley brings a depth leaning toward cocoa and earth. Red Virginia provides the sweetness that balances this dry foundation. Nicotine strength is high, and smoking it slowly noticeably changes its character. It suits those looking for a plain, unspiced burley flake.
cornell-diehl-burley-flake-2.o: A thin sweetness sits over an aroma of dry wood and toasted nuts.

affordable-pipes-maple-crown.z: One of the house blends from the American seller Affordable Pipes; no accessible source describing its content could be found.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-fleur-de-.z: Fleur-de-Lis is a blend The Country Squire prepared as a nod to New Orleans and Deep South culture, presented as the official blend of the first New Orleans Pipe Show. Grassy, flue-cured Virginia leaves are joined by fire-cured burley and a generous measure of Louisiana perique. On the smoke, Virginia's grassy, bready sweetness comes together with the smoky earthiness of the dark-fired burley and the plum-and-pepper spice of the perique. The body is full and the burn is smooth. It suits lovers of unflavored blends with a spicy, smoky side.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-fleur-de-.o: Leaves a scent of fire-cured leaf smoke and plum.

mccranies-red-flake-vintage-2008.z: McCranie's Pipe Shop is a long-established tobacconist in Charlotte, North Carolina; the shop's tinned tobacco line began with red Virginia leaf from a single harvest set aside exclusively for it. This leaf is rested and pressed; the name flake refers to the presentation in which the pressed block is left in slices rather than broken up. Records indicate the year on the tin (2008) marks the leaf's harvest/packing year, and batches stamped with other years circulate under the same name. Being unflavored, single-varietal Virginia, the tobacco's taste comes from the leaf's own sugar: a bready, creamy base with a sweet depth that deepens with age. Nicotine load runs light to medium, making it suitable for all-day smoking. Aimed at smokers seeking an unflavored Virginia who want to smoke slowly and follow the leaf's own taste. The shop no longer continues this line; what's on the market are older batches.
mccranies-red-flake-vintage-2008.o: Leaves a sweetish hay aroma with a faint bready note.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-blue-ribb.z: Blue Ribbon, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an aromatic mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

just-for-him-sailors-mix.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for Just For Him's Sailor's Mix, so the profile is left incomplete.

peterson-balkan-delight.z: Balkan Delight is a ribbon-cut Latakia blend built by adding a generous amount of Cyprus Latakia and a small amount of Louisiana Perique to Virginia leaf. Records indicate the blend was later continued under the name Balkan Mixture, with the Balkan Delight name discontinued; the composition is described along the same lines. Latakia's smoky, woody taste shows itself on the first draw, but not so heavily as to overwhelm Virginia's sugar; Perique leaves a peppery sharpness in the background. Nicotine strength is medium. It suits smokers familiar with English and Balkan-type blends who are seeking an unflavored, smoky smoke.
peterson-balkan-delight.o: Leaves a sharp aroma recalling wood smoke and soot that lingers in a room for a long time.

cup-o-joes-4-yeti-flake.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the Cup O' Joes brand as #4 Yeti Flake; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

4noggins-otter-creek.z: Otter Creek is a simply constructed blend in 4noggins' bulk aromatic lineup. A vanilla-based topping is applied over a trio of Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish; rather than a stack of elaborate layers, it targets a single-note, straightforward sweetness. It burns at a low, steady, even temperature; nicotine is mild and flavor mild-to-moderate. It suits newcomers to aromatics, those looking for a gentle tobacco that won't feel heavy in the morning, and smokers who want the vanilla topping noticeable but not overwhelming.
4noggins-otter-creek.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and lightly caramelized-sugar aroma.

paul-olsen-bs-hvid-balkan.z: No reliable source could be found for the Paul Olsen pipe tobacco called BS Hvid Balkan, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-dark-holl.z: Dark Holler is a pressed American blend that The Country Squire releases in small batches. Burley, Virginia, black cavendish, and Louisiana perique are brought together, pressed under weight, and aged. The blend is said to have been created by Quinn Crawford. The generous perique and the pressing give the blend an intense flavor profile: alongside vanilla, almond, coconut, and cane sugar, notes of bittersweet chocolate, dark fruit, anise, and spiced blackberry come through. The body is full and the sweetness measured, without harshness. It is aimed at experienced smokers looking for a pressed, richly sweet burley-perique profile. Being produced in limited quantities, it is not consistently available.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-dark-holl.o: Leaves a scent of baking spice, caramel, and dark fruit.

sahte-puro-sahte-pipo-tutunu.z: This record is not a blend; it corresponds to a warning piece about counterfeit products sold in the Turkish market under well-known brand packaging with unrelated tobacco inside, along with the sale of counterfeit cigars.

dunhill-early-morning-pipe.z: Early Morning Pipe, as its name suggests, is a classic English mixture built for the day's first bowls. Oriental tobaccos and a measured amount of latakia are added over Virginia leaves; the ribbon cut packs easily and burns evenly. The latakia proportion is enough to establish a smoky frame without covering the other components. Its strength stays light to medium, while its flavor intensity is above medium; this balance suits it to morning and daytime smoking. Aged in the tin, the transitions between the leaves soften further. It suits smokers wanting to enter English mixtures or seeking a smoky smoke without a heavy latakia load. Production under the Dunhill name has ended.
dunhill-early-morning-pipe.o: Leaves a trace mixing light soot and dry-grass scent.

mcclelland-no-910-kentucky-cavendish.z: A blend in McClelland's bulk series, discontinued when the firm closed in 2018; no sufficient source documenting its contents and character could be found.

orlik-golden-sliced.z: Golden Sliced is Orlik's best-known product and counted among the most widely smoked Virginia-based flake blends in the world. A small amount of perique is added to pressed, thinly sliced golden Virginia leaf; no flavoring is applied. The slices go into the tin partly rubbed (broken flake), and a ribbon-cut version also exists. Its taste is sweet, its texture clean, and its strength light to medium. Virginia's natural sweetness comes forward in the first half of the smoke, and the leaf's own fullness in the second half; smoked at a slow pace, the taste quality is preserved without degrading. It's a widely recommended blend for those wanting to enter the world of unflavored Virginia, and smokers learning to pack flake.
orlik-golden-sliced.o: Leaves a sweetish tobacco scent recalling toasted bread and hay.

the-smoker-legacy.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the The Smoker pipe tobacco called Legacy to record the blend's composition and character.

stanislaw-fire-mixture.z: A blend offered by the Czech firm Mostex under its Stanislaw brand, said to be built on dark burley and high-sugar light Virginia and flavored with licorice root and a light pepper note; a second independent source confirming this information could not be found.
stanislaw-fire-mixture.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweetish scent reminiscent of licorice root.

virginia-gold-vanilla.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Virginia Gold pipe tobacco called Vanilla to record the blend's composition and character.

mac-baren-scaferlati-caporal-rouge.z: Scaferlati Caporal is one of the most common names in French pipe tobacco tradition. Its name is traced to the Napoleonic era's soldier tobacco rations; it was among the country's best-selling tobaccos for many years. The brand belongs to Mac Baren today. The Rouge release's body is built from Virginia and Kentucky leaves; Paraguayan leaf, characteristic of French tobaccos, adds a distinctive trace to the character. No flavoring is used, and the air-cured, fermented leaves give the well-known strong profile. The cut is loose and fine, packing easily into a pipe; on the other hand, since moisture is low, care is needed while packing. The taste moves between herbal and woody tones, with a smoky base underneath. Nicotine load is high. Aimed at experienced smokers seeking unflavored, strong, traditional European tobaccos.
mac-baren-scaferlati-caporal-rouge.o: Leaves a sharp, herbal, and woody tobacco aroma.

w-d-h-o-wills-the-three-castles-tobacco.z: No independent source sufficient to complete a record could be found regarding W.D. & H.O. Wills's The Three Castles Tobacco blend, so this entry remains incomplete.

mac-baren-mixture-flake.z: Mixture Flake is the pressed-slice version of Mac Baren's classic Mixture blend. Its foundation is Virginia, burley and the brand's own black cavendish; the manufacturer states over thirty-five leaves from different parts of the world are brought together in the blend. The leaves are pressed, rested a while and cut into slices. A lightly sweet top note is applied, so it's classed as a light aromatic. In the smoke, Virginia sweetness and burley's nutty dryness form a balanced base, cavendish adds softness, and the top flavor stays within a range that doesn't mask the tobacco taste. Being pressed, it burns slowly and coolly, suited to smoking throughout the day. Suited to pipe smokers seeking a middle path between flavored and unflavored, who don't mind preparing a flake.
mac-baren-mixture-flake.o: Leaves a measured note reminiscent of light sweetness, dry straw and caramelized sugar.

japan-tobacco-momoyama.z: Momoyama is a Virginia-based pipe tobacco, supported by Burley and Oriental leaf, produced by Japan Tobacco for the Japanese domestic market. Records indicate it was launched in 1934, and, in keeping with Japanese pipe tradition, it's presented in a very fine, kizami-style cut. It carries a light flavoring in the direction of rum-like liqueur, caramel, and fruit. Because of the fine cut, it smokes fast and cool; the initial sweet, aromatic character gives way to a more classic tobacco taste as the bowl progresses. Strength is kept low. It's a profile suited to smokers wanting to step outside Western-style blends, looking for a lightly flavored, short smoke. Since it isn't exported, it's hard to find outside Japan.
japan-tobacco-momoyama.o: Leaves a sweetish smoke with notes of caramelized sugar and a light liqueur aroma.

cornell-diehl-xx-flake-dark.z: XX Flake Dark is the dark version of the commemorative blends Cornell & Diehl released in 2020 for Smokingpipes.com's twentieth anniversary. Its composition includes select Virginia leaf and aged Perique; like its sibling product XX Flake, eighteen-year-aged Perique is used. The mixture is pressed and cut into broken flake, and records indicate it was limited to five thousand numbered tins. Its profile is described as dark and deep, with pronounced spice sitting alongside a measured sweetness. Its high Virginia proportion and pressed structure make it well suited to long-term storage. Being a limited run, it isn't an ongoing product on the market.
cornell-diehl-xx-flake-dark.o: Leaves a scent where dark bread and dried-fruit sweetness mingle with a spice edge.

harrods-english-mixture.z: A house blend prepared for the tobacco counter of London's Harrods department store; records indicate it was manufactured by James J. Fox, but there is not enough sourcing to confirm its composition.
harrods-english-mixture.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

hearth-home-victorian-stroll.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for this blend, described as English type, from the Hearth & Home brand.

peter-heinrichs-reserve-crue-no-9.z: Reserve Crue No. 9 is a hand-packed flake blend in which Peter Heinrichs puts Perique at the center. Per the maker's description, six distinct fire-cured Virginia leaves and a pinch of Oriental tobacco are added alongside the Perique; the mixture is pressed and sliced for sale. Perique brings the blend a dark fruit sweetness recalling plum and fig along with a peppery spice; the fire-cured Virginia leaves add a woody, smoky base to that. Body and nicotine strength sit above medium. It suits experienced smokers who know the Virginia-Perique tradition and are seeking an intense, spicy smoke.
peter-heinrichs-reserve-crue-no-9.o: A light pepper and smoke mix into a dark fruit aroma recalling plum and fig.

john-brumfit-limited-london-blend.z: A blend London tobacconist John Brumfit prepared under his own name; no verifiable information on its contents could be found.
john-brumfit-limited-london-blend.o: No verifiable information on its room note could be found.

vincenzo-green.z: Vincenzo Green is the Latakia-led mixture from the Italian Vincenzo brand. Cyprus Latakia serves as the main leaf, joined by select golden Virginia, sweetening black Cavendish, and Basma-type Oriental tobacco. It is ribbon cut and sold in tins. Smoke, resinous wood and leather come to the front on the smoke; the Virginia and Cavendish soften this core, carrying the blend to a rounder place than classic English mixtures. Nicotine and flavor intensity stay in the middle range. It can be considered a fitting starting point for smokers who want to get acquainted with Latakia character without diving into a heavy Balkan blend.
vincenzo-green.o: Leaves wood smoke and soot with a faint sweet layer underneath.

sutliff-tobacco-company-vanilla-d40.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Sutliff Tobacco Company's Vanilla D40 pipe tobacco could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-exclusive-peach-brand.z: Exclusive Peach Brandy is a ribbon-cut aromatic blend built from selected Burley and mild Virginia leaf. The fresh peach topping leads; the brandy note stays more measured underneath it and balances the sweetness. The Burley's share keeps the smoke cool and dry, while Virginia adds a light sweetness. Nicotine is moderate, and the smoke is mild. Suited to smokers who love fruity aromatics but avoid a syrupy heaviness. Gawith Hoggarth's Exclusive series consists of this style of single-theme aromatics.
gawith-hoggarth-co-exclusive-peach-brand.o: Leaves a fresh peach aroma with a light brandy scent behind it.

walgreens-burley-light.z: This is one of the bulk blends sold under the Walgreens pharmacy chain's own name; no reliable source could be found documenting its composition.

teds-pipe-shoppe-blend-1.z: One of the numbered house blends from Ted's Pipe Shoppe; no accessible source documenting its content could be found.

tabaqueria-xian-suenos-canadienses.z: One of Tabaquería Xian's Cavendish-based house blends; no accessible source documenting its content could be found.

jack-lee-blend-beowulf.z: Beowulf is one of the English-style mixtures from the small-scale American blender Jack Lee Blend. Latakia forms the smoky backbone, and Virginia carries sweetness; past the middle of the bowl, a sweet-spicy clove note appears, along with hints of ripe plum and dark chocolate, backed by a light honey sweetness. The burn is cool, and it's considered mild in terms of tongue bite. It's noted as one of the blender's late-period products, with production said to have stopped after US tobacco regulations changed; there is no new production today. It's a profile likely to interest smokers seeking an unflavored, Latakia-forward but not harsh mixture. As the information relies mainly on community reviews, details are limited.
jack-lee-blend-beowulf.o: Leaves an aroma of wood smoke, sweet spice, and dark fruit.

milan-tobacconists-centenary.z: Centenary is a house blend among Milan Tobacconists' traditional English mixtures. According to the maker's description it is built by bringing together fifteen separate tobaccos, including latakia; it carries a smoky taste in the direction of hickory wood, walnut and woody undertones, and a pronounced spice share. It is a mixture without casing, with body ranging between medium and full. Suitable for smokers who like latakia's smokiness and are drawn to multi-component classic English constructions. The blend's name references the shop's hundredth anniversary; Milan was founded in 1912.
milan-tobacconists-centenary.o: Leaves an aroma of wood smoke and smoky oak, with a dry spice trace on top.

mcclelland-cpcc-rich-virginia-ribbon.z: A ribbon-cut straight Virginia blend, as the name suggests, McClelland released for the Chicagoland Pipe Collectors Club, reportedly in 2009; no sufficient source describing its character in detail could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-plug.z: Dark Plug is an unflavored plug tobacco produced by combining Malawi-origin fire-cured leaf and Indian-origin air-cured dark leaf in equal proportions and cold-pressing them for more than a week. The plug shape keeps the tobacco's natural oils inside; because of this, it can be stored for a long time and matures faster. Cutting only as much as needed to smoke lets the remaining piece keep its moisture. The same blend is also offered in sliced form. It's a near-black tobacco; its aroma is deep, earthy, and carries a sharp smokiness. On the smoke, the fire-cured leaf's leather- and cigar-like smoky taste combines with the air-cured leaf's earthy, woody, and spicy tones. Nicotine is very high. An entry for experienced smokers accustomed to preparing plug tobacco who want a dark, strong smoke.
gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-plug.o: A heavy aroma of sharp smoke, earth, and cigar-like leaf fills the room.

hearth-home-whiteknight.z: WhiteKnight is a Balkan blend built on bright Virginia, select Oriental varieties — particularly Yenidje — and smoky Latakia. It's a 2012 work by blender Russ Ouellette, prepared as a tribute to the late-1970s Balkan Sobranie Original Smoking Mixture, and built along the same axis of leaf types used in that blend. Its aroma is reminiscent of incense; on the taste side there's a sharp, clear edge and a short, clean finish not seen in most Latakia blends. It's aimed at smokers familiar with the classic Balkan style or tracing its lineage. It's part of the brand's Marquee line; records indicate a separate edition was also released for the tenth anniversary.
hearth-home-whiteknight.o: Leaves a pronounced aroma reminiscent of incense, spreading through the room with smoke and resinous wood.

sutliff-tobacco-company-mixture-no-79-ch.z: Mixture No.79 Cherry & Brandy is a cherry-and-brandy variant of Sutliff's best-known counter blend, Mixture No. 79. The base blend is burley-based, known for its anise-heavy sauce, and this version layers dark cherry and brandy notes on top of that character. Records indicate it has not been in regular production for some time and is only found through old stock on the market. The cut is uneven, mixing large chunks with fragments almost as fine as snuff, a structure that leads to hot burning if not packed carefully. The cherry addition leans dark and jam-like rather than raw and sweet. Nicotine strength is moderate. It appeals to those wanting to sample heavily flavored, traditional American aromatics.
sutliff-tobacco-company-mixture-no-79-ch.o: Dark cherry and anise fill the room, carrying a brandied sweetness behind them.

brookfield-black-bourbon-no-4.z: Brookfield No. 4 is an American-type blend built from Virginia and burley leaf; a bourbon-whiskey aroma is applied on top. Burley's nutty, dry base and Virginia's sweetness combine with the caramel-oaky note of the bourbon. While the flavor casing is pronounced, it is more measured than sugared aromatics; the tobacco character remains legible. Suitable for those seeking a cased but not overly sweet everyday blend. Like the other Brookfield blends, it is manufactured by Pöschl Tabak in Germany.
brookfield-black-bourbon-no-4.o: Leaves a sweetish aroma reminiscent of an oak barrel and whiskey.

dan-tobacco-killarney.z: A pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source on the blend's composition or character was found, so no further detail is given.

san-antonio-pipe-club-smooth-syrian.z: Smooth Syrian is one of the small-batch products from the blending workshop San Antonio Pipe Club founded in 2018. The blend's backbone is built by Syrian latakia; red and yellow virginias, dark-fire-cured Kentucky leaf, and cavendish accompany it. The mixture is given a sweetish casing and pressed and rested for at least four weeks. Syrian latakia gives a milder, more buttery smoke than Cyprus latakia; Kentucky adds fullness, and cavendish raises the roundness. The resulting profile is a light sweetness sitting on a smoky foundation, with nicotine staying in the medium range. Suited to smokers who love latakia but don't seek the harshness of sharp English mixtures.
san-antonio-pipe-club-smooth-syrian.o: Leaves a scent evoking wood smoke, cured meat, and sweetish maple syrup.

samuel-gawith-dixie-pride.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Dixie Pride, according to records a pure Virginia blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

bufflehead-masked-duck.z: One of the discontinued blends from the Bufflehead shop; no source documenting its composition could be found.

hu-tobacco-olafs-favourite-english.z: Olaf's Favourite English is a high-Latakia HU Tobacco blend that leans close to Balkan style. Records indicate roughly forty percent Syrian Latakia along with ten percent Cyprus Latakia, Perique, a notable amount of Izmir Oriental tobacco, fire-cured leaf, and English-style black Cavendish are added atop a sweet Virginia base. The fire-cured leaf's woody, dry, spicy character supports the Latakia's silky smokiness, building a layered smoky taste; sweet, salty, sour, and leathery notes run interwoven. It's ribbon cut, carries medium-to-full nicotine, and the components meld further with aging. Because it uses Syrian Latakia, it's hard to find today in the described original form.
hu-tobacco-olafs-favourite-english.o: Heavy smoke, leather, and burnt wood fill the room for a long time.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-irish-aniseed.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Brown Irish Aniseed blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

mr-bs-chocolate.z: Mr. B's Chocolate is an aromatic blend in Canadian Brigham's line, made from fire-cured black cavendish and dark burley leaves flavored with chocolate. The blend was later sold under the name Mr. B's Ancient Secrets; it is presented in 50-gram pouches and 400-gram bags. Burley's bready, earthy base gives body to the cocoa casing.
mr-bs-chocolate.o: Leaves an aroma of bitter chocolate and roasted cocoa.

just-for-him-hornblowers-blend.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for Just For Him's Hornblower's Blend, so the profile is left incomplete; per catalog records, the blend is classified as "Aromatic."

e-a-carey-old-english-ready-rubbed.z: A blend registered under the E. A. Carey name, said to be Virginia-forward; it does not appear on the maker's current list, and not enough sourcing exists to describe its character.

villiger-burley.z: This is a Burley-forward pipe tobacco from Villiger, taking its name directly from the leaf type; no independent source giving detailed composition and cut information could be found.

peretti-wild-cherry-blend.z: Wild Cherry Blend is a cherry-flavored blend in Peretti's Burley-based line. The maker states the blend is distinguished by its pronounced wild cherry taste; this note leans closer to a tart side than the sugary sweetness of garden cherry. The Burley base gives the blend a drier body and somewhat more strength than Cavendish-forward cherry aromatics. It suits smokers who love cherry flavoring but don't want a syrupy taste.
peretti-wild-cherry-blend.o: Leaves a tart wild cherry aroma.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-187.z: Wilke No. 187 is a blend in the brand's bulk aromatic series. According to the maker's recipe, it's built by adding Virginia to black cavendish and dark Burley, and it carries a pronounced sweet side in the smoke. The sweetness comes from both the cavendish processing and the casing applied to the blend; Burley, meanwhile, provides a dry base that keeps the sugar from dominating on its own. The blend burns slowly and leaves no harshness on the tongue, with nicotine sitting mild to medium. It suits newcomers to aromatic blends or those seeking a sweet but not-too-heavy option for all-day smoking. Wilke's 180 and 190 series generally consist of this style of cavendish-centered aromatics.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-187.o: Leaves a scent of sweet caramel and baked dough.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-nappa-val.z: A blend referred to as aromatic; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

dan-tobacco-your-sundays-pleasure.z: A blend from German manufacturer Dan Tobacco said to be aromatic; there isn't enough reliable source material to confirm its composition and character.

beehive-fillmore-beaver.z: One of the bulk aromatic blends sold under its own name by Beehive Cigars in Salt Lake City; the name is a reference specific to Utah. No adequate source on its content could be found.

orlik-park-lane-no-7.z: Park Lane No. 7 is a flake blend carrying the name of the old Dixon & Hamilton brand, whose production later passed to Orlik. It's offered in a 50-gram pack as long, dark slices running the length of the package. It contains Virginia and burley; no heavy flavoring is applied, and a thin, sweetish direction is noted. Its burn and smoke are even, with a tendency to run hot when smoked quickly. The tangy taste from burley increases as the smoke progresses, but the blend doesn't turn harsh; overall it stays mild. It's a convenient example for those wanting to learn flake packing and get to know burley character at a low strength. Records indicate its production has stopped and it is hard to find.
orlik-park-lane-no-7.o: Leaves a lightly sweet scent recalling dry hay and nut shell.

astleys-no-44-dark-virginia-flake.z: Astley's No.44 Dark Virginia Flake is a flake tobacco made by resting dark Virginia leaf under press before slicing. The brand traces its origins to the Astley's tobacconist founded in 1862 at 109 Jermyn Street, London; the blend is produced today by Kohlhase & Kopp. Since the leaf's sugars concentrate during pressing, the smoke brings out dark dried fruit, cooked sugar, and a tangy depth. Its body and flavor intensity are markedly higher than the brand's light-colored Virginia flakes. It's aimed at those who like dark Virginia flakes and are accustomed to smoking slowly, airing and resting the tobacco.
astleys-no-44-dark-virginia-flake.o: Leaves a deep tobacco room note leaning toward dark dried fruit and cooked sugar.

milan-tobacconists-black-forest.z: Black Forest is one of the shop blends from Milan Tobacconists in Roanoke, Virginia. According to the shop's description it consists of a measured combination of matured Maduro Cavendish, black Cavendish, and toasted Cavendish leaves; its flavoring shows an impression of vanilla, caramel, and buttered walnut. Because of its cavendish-forward construction the body stays light, and the smoke is soft and sweet. Aimed at smokers looking for a slow-burning, sweet aromatic that doesn't leave heaviness on the tongue. Milan Tobacconists has been operating for over a hundred years and offers its own blends in bulk.
milan-tobacconists-black-forest.o: Leaves an aroma of vanilla, caramel, and toasted hazelnut.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-huccaby-dane.z: Huccaby Dane is listed as McGahey The Tobacconist's Danish-style aromatic house blend and is reported to carry a citrus character; sufficient sources regarding its composition and cut could not be found.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-huccaby-dane.o: Carries a fresh trace reminiscent of citrus peel.

georgetown-tobacco-berkebile-special-res.z: Referred to as an English-style second edition of Georgetown Tobacco's Berkebile Special Reserve blend; no verifiable sourcing on its composition could be found.
georgetown-tobacco-berkebile-special-res.o: No record of the room aroma could be found.

imp-aiden.z: This is one of four English blends released by IMP USA in 2013; production ended when the company changed hands in 2015. No sufficient independent source detailing the blend's character could be found.

bufflehead-american-widgeon.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named American Widgeon under the Bufflehead brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

sutliff-tobacco-company-charlemagne.z: Charlemagne, part of Sutliff's Private Stock line, is a burley-based aromatic. Black cavendish and a small amount of Virginia are added alongside it; a light rum-and-plum-direction topping is applied on top. Burley's sweet side comes forward more than its nutty side, with Virginia playing a supporting role via dry-hay traces. It's a mixture low in strength and flavor intensity with little bite. Suited to smokers seeking a long, slow-smoking aromatic with a measured topping.
sutliff-tobacco-company-charlemagne.o: Leaves a soft scent carrying light plum and vanilla sweetness.

gladora-tobacco-latakia-flake-40.z: Latakia Flake-40 is a Turkish-made blend from Gladora Tobacco using leaf grown and processed on the company's own fields. Virginia, Latakia, and Turkish Orientals are pressed and sliced into flake; the 40 in the name refers to the blend's Latakia ratio. The version distributed in the European market under the name Pesse Canoe carries the same composition. A woody smokiness leads on the smoke; the Virginia's natural sweetness, reminiscent of plum and dried fruit, and the Orientals' spicy dryness balance that smoke. There is no flavoring. Nicotine and flavor intensity are moderate, making it suitable both for smokers wanting to get used to Latakia flakes and for those seeking an everyday English mixture. Being a flake, it needs to be rubbed out and aired for a while before smoking.
gladora-tobacco-latakia-flake-40.o: Leaves a light dried-fruit tone beneath the aroma of pine smoke and smoked wood.

pipesandcigars-com-scottys-hpcs-owls-hea.z: This is a blend offered under the American retailer pipesandcigars.com's name; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

brigham-enterprises-inc-hudsons-bay.z: Hudson's Bay is an unflavored Virginia blend in Brigham's Legend line. Matured medium- and dark-brown Virginia leaves are offered in English-style thick-cut broken flake form; stoved black Virginia is added to the blend to give a dark, deep tobacco taste with its own inherent sweetness. Per the manufacturer's description, strength and flavor sit in the light-to-medium band; this makes it suitable for those seeking a Virginia without a heavy nicotine load that can be smoked all day, and for those wanting to get used to flake cuts. Thanks to the broken flake structure, the leaf crumbles easily in the palm, giving a long, slow smoke. The name refers to Canada's historic fur-trading company, Hudson's Bay.
brigham-enterprises-inc-hudsons-bay.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, earthy tobacco aroma reminiscent of dark bread crust.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-bulls-eye-flak.z: Bull's Eye Flake is a Virginia-perique press produced at Orlik's facilities in Denmark, also marketed under the Peter Stokkebye label. Matured Virginia leaves from different sources are blended with Louisiana perique, then pressed around an unessenced cavendish core; the finished block is sliced into coins. It takes its name from this ringed, target-like cross-section. The cavendish core softens the sharpness between Virginia and perique; as perique's spice and Virginia's natural sweetness combine, the taste takes on a citrus-leaning direction. Body stays medium. It's an entry-level tobacco for those wanting to get to know the coin cut and the Virginia-perique family, calling for patient lighting and rubbing out the slices before packing.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-bulls-eye-flak.o: Leaves a scent of sweet hay alongside a tart dried-fruit and peppery-spice aroma.

niall-of-nine-aberdeen-orange-english.z: One of the blends prepared in very small batches under the Niall of Nine signature; not enough independent source material documenting its composition and character could be found.

mclintock-black-cherry-black-c.z: Black Cherry is an aromatic from the McLintock line German maker Kohlhase & Kopp established in the late 1960s; in some markets, due to restrictions on using the fruit's name on packaging, it is sold under the name Black C. Its base is black cavendish, joined by golden virginia in various cuts; black cherry, coffee, and whisky notes are applied as the top layer. Thanks to the cavendish weight, the smoke is soft and moist, with the nicotine load measured; in the taste, alongside the cherry sweetness, coffee's roasted edge and whisky's light sharpness can be distinguished. Suitable for smokers drawn to fruity aromatics who favor the top-level flavoring over the tobacco character.
mclintock-black-cherry-black-c.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly liqueur-like aroma reminiscent of ripe cherry and roasted coffee.

w-o-larsen-craftmans-edition.z: Craftmans Edition is W.Ø. Larsen's annual release series referencing the Danish pipe tobacco tradition dating to 1864; a separate blend is prepared for each year and offered in numbered tins. The series' common line is a medium-bodied aromatic structure built on Virginia, Burley, and fermented black cavendish. Part of the tobaccos are pressed, rested, and then rubbed out; this preparation, combining ribbon cut with rubbed-out flake, gives a slower, more even burn. In flavoring, vanilla and caramel establish Larsen's known sweet signature, while nutty notes like almond add creamy depth. Nicotine level is light. This is a series of interest to smokers who want to follow Danish-style aromatics and enjoy comparing versions that change from year to year.
w-o-larsen-craftmans-edition.o: Leaves a scent of vanilla caramel and roasted nuts.

lane-limited-hgl.z: HGL is the only latakia-containing blend in Lane Limited's bulk line. A measured amount of mountain latakia is added to toasted cavendish leaf, accompanied by white burley and golden Virginia; the cut is ribbon. Here latakia isn't used as a dominant building block but as a seasoning. The result is a full-bodied yet cool, slow-burning smoke carrying a fine layer of smoke over a sweet cavendish base. Nicotine is medium. Suited to smokers seeking a bridge between aromatics and English blends, wanting latakia measured rather than intense.
lane-limited-hgl.o: Leaves a fine smoke and wood scent over a sweet cavendish base.

motzek-tom-a-hawk.z: Tom-A-Hawk is among the Motzek workshop's blends built on a virginia-perique core. Records indicate it combines Ugandan and Malawian-origin virginias with dark-fired virginias from India, joined by roughly 20 percent perique and a very small amount of latakia. Unlike the workshop's mostly plug- and twist-focused product range, it is presented as a loose ribbon cut. In the cold scent, the smokiness of latakia and dark-fired leaf is faintly perceptible. In the smoke, Virginia's sweetness stays dominant while perique adds pepper and a light fruit acidity; since the latakia proportion is far below that of an English blend, it adds depth without taking over the profile. Strength sits in the light-to-medium band. Suitable for smokers looking for a virginia-perique blend with a smoky touch that doesn't push latakia to the forefront.
motzek-tom-a-hawk.o: Leaves an aroma that mixes light smoky wood with peppery sweetness.

argento-whisky-chocolate.z: Whisky & Chocolate is an aromatic blend where whiskey and chocolate flavoring are worked into selected Argentine tobaccos. In the balance of the pair, chocolate leads; the whiskey stays more in the background, as a dry, lightly boozy trace. It's ribbon cut, listed as number 2 in the brand's numbering, and distributed in 50-gram pouches. Because it stays mild on nicotine and its flavoring is pronounced, it's counted among the first blends for those new to the pipe. For those who don't like heavy aromatics, the flavoring level may seem high; on the other hand, for those looking for a sweet, well-defined profile, the blend's character is clear from start to finish.
argento-whisky-chocolate.o: Leaves a cocoa-dominant room note carrying a faintly boozy sweetness behind it.

sillems-copenhagen-blend.z: Copenhagen Blend is the Sillem's brand's aromatic entry referencing the Danish style. Virginia, burley, and black cavendish are used together in the blend; Virginia sets a sweet foundation while burley gives a toasted, nutty base, and cavendish softens the smoke and adds a moist, dark sweetness. Over this, a flavoring in the direction of amaretto and toasted hazelnut is applied. The casing is kept light enough not to cover the tobacco base; the almond-liqueur echo works in the same direction as burley's natural nuttiness. Nicotine share is low, the smoke stays cool and mild. Aimed at smokers who lean toward Danish-style sweet aromatics, seek a sweet-nutty line, and want a light entry they can smoke all day.
sillems-copenhagen-blend.o: Leaves a scent of toasted hazelnut and almond liqueur.

j-f-germain-son-bridge-old-brown-flake.z: This is a blend under the J. F. Germain & Son name, produced on the island of Jersey; no accessible source verifying its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
j-f-germain-son-bridge-old-brown-flake.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-plug.z: This is one of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s pressed plug products; not enough independent records could be found to establish the blend's composition and character.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-plug.o: Beyond the pressed tobacco's own smell, not enough records were found for a distinguishing description.

sutliff-tobacco-company-natural-cavendis.z: Natural Cavendish #10 is one of the base blends in Sutliff's numbered bulk line. Aged American burley leaf is combined with imported flue-cured Virginia; a small amount of cognac is applied on top to open up the taste. The "Natural" name signals that no heavy flavoring is used. The smoke is soft and straightforward; it carries no sharp casing or pronounced fruit note. Nicotine is below medium. It can be smoked on its own, but it is also used as a base tobacco in house blends to add sweetness and body. It suits smokers looking for a plain, subtly flavored everyday blend, as well as those building their own mixtures.
sutliff-tobacco-company-natural-cavendis.o: Leaves a soft, lightly sweet tobacco scent.

davidoff-year-of-the-rat.z: Year of the Rat is the 2020 entry in Davidoff's yearly limited-edition series based on the Chinese zodiac. It was released in red-lacquered, gold-embroidered tins, limited worldwide to five thousand numbered tins. The Swiss-origin brand has its pipe tobaccos produced in Germany. The blend is built on black cavendish and bride-cut virginia, with the addition of Indonesian-origin fire-cured Kentucky leaf; it's flavored with rose petal and lychee notes. On the smoke, dried fruit, cream and lychee tastes appear with a floral top note, while Kentucky leaves a dry smokiness in the background. It suits smokers who love the aromatic structure but also want body alongside the sweetness.
davidoff-year-of-the-rat.o: Behind the floral rose and lychee sweetness, a lightly smoky scent lingers.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-new-ripples.z: A blend registered under the Orlik Tobacco Company A/S name, Virginia-burley based; no independent source confirming its details could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-dark-shag-blac.z: This is the cherry-flavored version of the Kendal Dark family. The body is a fine shag cut of Malawi-origin fire-cured leaf and India-origin air-cured Virginia, topped with the dark cherry flavoring known in Kendal tradition. Although it falls into the aromatic category, its body isn't light: the earthy, peppery base of the fire-cured leaf shows through beneath the cherry, and nicotine runs high. The fine cut lights quickly, so it needs to be smoked slowly. Aimed at smokers wanting a flavored but full-bodied English shag tobacco.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-dark-shag-blac.o: Leaves a smoky, heavy tobacco aroma along with dark cherry scent.

mcclelland-oldchurch.z: This was one of McClelland's aromatic entries, discontinued when the firm closed in 2018; no sufficient source documenting its contents and character could be found.

mcclelland-bombay-court.z: Bombay Court is one of McClelland's Latakia-containing mixtures centered on Oriental tobaccos. In the recipe, sun-cured exotic Oriental leaves lead; Latakia is used at a level where it's noticeable but not dominant. McClelland's matured red Virginia sets the balance and gives the blend sweetness. It's ribbon cut. The overall profile runs sweet, floral, and lightly smoky, with body kept measured. It falls within the territory of those seeking a milder smoke where Oriental tobacco leads, rather than heavy Latakia-forward English mixtures. A richer version of the blend, with darker Virginias, added Perique, and a higher Latakia share, was produced under the name Bombay Extra.
mcclelland-bombay-court.o: Leaves an aroma mixing floral Oriental tobacco with a fine trace of soot.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-brown-bogie.z: Sliced Brown Bogie is the sliced form of the producer's brown Burma, also known as 'Happy Bogie'. Fire-cured leaf is used for the wrapper; the inner filler is mostly fire-cured leaf with some air-cured dark Indian leaf. The flavor core carries earth, wood, dark dried fruit, barbecue-like smoke, spice, leather, and tart citrus notes. Nicotine is high and the tobacco arrives moist; sliced thin and smoked slowly it stays balanced, but left thick it goes out frequently. An entry aimed at experienced smokers seeking an unflavored, heavy, and smoky Burma. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. is one of the English producers that continues traditional twist (rope) production at its Kendal factory, hand-twisting fire-cured leaves into rope form. Because twist tobaccos don't go through a pressure-cooking stage, they stay intense in nicotine; records indicate these ropes are sold for both chewing and pipe smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-brown-bogie.o: Leaves a sharp aroma weighted toward wood smoke, earth, and leather.

peter-stokkebye-english-oriental-supreme.z: English Oriental Supreme is an unflavored blend that combines soft Georgia Virginias, black Cavendish, Mexican Burley, Turkish Oriental, and Cyprus Latakia. Compared to English Luxury, the Oriental leaf's share is pronounced, giving the blend a dry, grassy, spicy frame. The body sits between light and medium. On the palate, oak, toasted bread, and the tobacco's own taste come forward, leaving a lightly sweet, woody trace behind. It suits smokers who like Latakia blends but don't want heavy smoke, and who are seeking the dry spiciness of Oriental leaf.
peter-stokkebye-english-oriental-supreme.o: A smoky wood aroma is mixed with toasted bread and a spicy dryness.

cornell-diehl-mild-turkish.z: A light-character Oriental tobacco from Cornell & Diehl, also used as a casing leaf in blending; no adequate source for detailed composition and smoking information was found.
cornell-diehl-mild-turkish.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay and light spice.

ravenwood-fine-provisions-brandywine-bri.z: Brandywine Bridge is described as thoroughly aromatic within the Ravenwood Fine Provisions line. The blender states he uses a Natures Flavors brand Japanese plum casing; the resulting taste rests on sweet plum and light caramel. According to the blender's own description, this plum note differs from blends like Plum Cake or Royal Yacht that carry a wine-like character; the goal is a fresh, ripe fruit taste without the tartness of the skin. Flavoring is pronounced and nicotine low; it suits smokers looking for a fruity aromatic who focus more on the top note than the body. Being small-batch production, stock is replenished intermittently.
ravenwood-fine-provisions-brandywine-bri.o: Leaves a ripe plum and light caramel aroma.

schurch-unakit-jak.z: Unakit (Jak), signed by Schürch, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

robert-mcconnell-brasil.z: Brasil belongs to Robert McConnell's single-varietal line and is made entirely of Brazilian cigar leaf. The coarsely cut, dark brown leaf is unflavored; the taste rests on the earthy, tart, faintly sweet tones characteristic of cigar tobacco. Reports note that opening the tin gives an aroma reminiscent of aged Virginia and Perique. Nicotine is pronounced and flavor intensity high; it tends to burn fast and hot, so it calls for slow smoking. It is used mainly by home blenders as a body-deepening component, and smoked alone it appeals to experienced smokers. The brand was founded in London in 1848; production today is carried out in Germany by Kohlhase & Kopp.
robert-mcconnell-brasil.o: Leaves the sharp, earthy, faintly salty aroma of burnt cigar leaf.

dan-tobacco-wappen-von-hamburg.z: Wappen von Hamburg is one of the long-standing older brands in the catalogue of German manufacturer Dan Tobacco (DTM). The blend combines black Cavendish with coarsely cut Virginia flake ribbons; the broad cut means it burns slowly and evenly. The casing is a hard-to-pin-down fruity flavoring, kept modest by the maker's own account: it lifts the Virginia's natural sweetness without overpowering the tobacco's character. Given this profile, available records point to wide-chambered pipes as the better fit; the coarse cut can make packing narrow bowls difficult. Nicotine sits between mild and medium, making it suitable for all-day smoking for those wanting noticeable but not dominant flavoring. It can serve as a starting point for smokers looking for a middle ground between aromatics and straight Virginias.
dan-tobacco-wappen-von-hamburg.o: Leaves a room note of baked tobacco with a light fruity sweetness.

dobies-dobies-four-square-english.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of Dobie's Four Square-English, a blend from Dobie's.

tabac-benden-the-eagle.z: The Eagle is Tabac Benden's blend bringing the intensely floral-essenced tobacco tradition specific to England's Lakeland region to the German market. A base of ready-rubbed flake made from fully matured Virginias is joined by a spicy measure of Burley and a very small share of Kentucky. The Lakeland essence is the blend's most defining feature: a floral layer reminiscent of rose, lavender, and soap sits over the Virginia's bready sweetness. The body is medium, with Kentucky giving a light smokiness from behind. It suits smokers who know or are curious about the Lakeland style; for those unfamiliar with this essence it can feel overpowering, and rotating it with another blend in the same pipe is difficult.
tabac-benden-the-eagle.o: Leaves an intense scent reminiscent of soapy floral essence, leaning toward rose and lavender.

levin-pipes-international-turkish-woods-.z: Turkish Woods Flake is a dark-colored, heavily pressed broken flake McClelland prepared for Levin Pipes International, built on latakia and a wide range of oriental leaves. Pressing and maturation followed McClelland's usual method, with the leaf rested long in the tin. Aimed at those seeking oriental-forward, pressed English-style blends. After Barry Levin's death, this recipe was not carried into McClelland's catalog and production ended.
levin-pipes-international-turkish-woods-.o: A smoky latakia scent reminiscent of an incense stick comes with a dry spice note.

g-l-pease-montgomery.z: Montgomery is a blend built by bringing together several grades of flue-cured Virginia leaf, from light gold to dark red, with a small amount of dark fire-cured Kentucky added. It is ribbon cut and carries no flavour additive. The smoke is naturally sweet, tartish, and grassy; notes reminiscent of bread and sweet corn are reported. Kentucky leaf adds weight to the body without turning the blend smoky. It is noted to burn cool and not bite the tongue; it is a good record for those seeking a not-too-heavy but complex Virginia blend, and one suited to ageing.
g-l-pease-montgomery.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of sweet hay, fresh bread, and sweet corn.

lane-limited-irish-cream.z: One of Lane Limited's aromatic blends; not enough sources could be found to document its composition.

sutliff-tobacco-company-french-quarter.z: French Quarter is a honey-and-vanilla aromatic from Sutliff's Private Stock line. It contains burley, black cavendish, and Virginia, presented in large-cut pieces. It takes its name from New Orleans' historic French Quarter. Tin aroma carries heavy honey sweetness, while on the palate cavendish's soft, sugary texture comes forward and the sweetness persists throughout the bowl. Nicotine strength is low, with little tendency to bite the tongue. A record for those seeking a pronounced-topping, soft-bodied aromatic.
sutliff-tobacco-company-french-quarter.o: Leaves a sweet, confection-like scent dominated by honey and vanilla.

peter-stokkebye-bb-v.z: No reliable sources confirming the content and character of the BB-V blend recorded under the Peter Stokkebye name could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-hot-chocolate-b2.z: Hot Chocolate B28 is a cocoa-flavored blend in Sutliff's letter-and-number-coded bulk aromatic line; independent sources do not provide sufficient information on its composition and cut.
sutliff-tobacco-company-hot-chocolate-b2.o: Leaves a sweet scent dominated by cocoa.

ashton-type-5.z: No manufacturer or retailer record describing the composition of this Ashton-affiliated blend could be found, leaving the profile blank.

synjeco-virginia-perique-slices.z: Virginia Perique Slices is recorded as a slice-form Virginia-Perique product in Synjeco's pressed Virginia line; no sufficient independent source for detailed content and character information could be found.
synjeco-virginia-perique-slices.o: No reliable record of a room note could be found.

gatlin-burlier-cascades-cavendish.z: Cascades Cavendish is one of the house blends of the Gatlinburlier tobacconist in Gatlinburg. It is prepared by applying a fruity flavouring over cavendish leaf, and per the shop's description, is built to be light enough to smoke all day. The tobacco taste stays in the background; the topping determines the blend's character, and nicotine level is low. It suits smokers just getting acquainted with the pipe through aromatic blends, or those seeking a light, sweet everyday tobacco.
gatlin-burlier-cascades-cavendish.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity, sugary aroma.

fribourg-treyer-vanners-mixture.z: Vanners Mixture is one of the mild Virginia blends in the line produced under the name of Fribourg & Treyer, the London tobacconist dating to 1720. Some black cavendish is added to red and golden Virginia leaves for body, and the blend is prepared as a ribbon cut. Red Virginia brings a bread-like, dark sweetness, while golden Virginia adds a brighter, grassier top tone; cavendish is the soft texture binding the two together. It suits smokers seeking a cool-burning, low-nicotine everyday blend, who don't want the smoky taste of the English style.
fribourg-treyer-vanners-mixture.o: Leaves an aroma of light sweet hay and dried fruit.

cornell-diehl-dark-fired-kentucky.z: Dark Fired Kentucky is less a blend than a single leaf variety: fire-cured Kentucky burley is offered as a ribbon cut. Cornell & Diehl lists it both as a tobacco that can be smoked on its own and as a blending leaf the smoker can use in their own mixtures. Fire-curing gives the leaf a pronounced smoky, woody sharpness while also keeping nicotine high. Smoked on its own it draws a hearty, direct profile; added in small amounts to Virginia- or burley-based mixtures it adds depth. It suits smokers accustomed to strong tobaccos and those building their own blends.
cornell-diehl-dark-fired-kentucky.o: Leaves a sharp aroma reminiscent of wood-smoked meat and smoke.

jewel-of-st-james-perique.z: No reliable source documenting the content and character of Jewel of St James's Perique blend could be found.

mcclelland-arcadia.z: Arcadia is the second blend, after Black Shag, in McClelland's 221b series, which it linked to the Sherlock Holmes universe. Its name is based on the legendary mixture mentioned in J. M. Barrie's "My Lady Nicotine"; the maker stated it reconstructed this recipe, known as Dr. Watson's tobacco, drawing on old samples. Its contents feature Virginia and Oriental tobaccos up front; though the tin label doesn't list Latakia, whether the blend contains a trace amount is a point often debated in reviews. The ribbon cut and balanced moisture make packing and burning easy. The smoke is cool; the Oriental tobaccos' sweet-spiced character stays pronounced through the bowl, with strength in the light-to-medium band. Falls within the territory of those seeking an Oriental-tobacco-centered mixture that isn't Latakia-forward.
mcclelland-arcadia.o: Leaves an aroma mixing spiced Oriental tobacco and a light trace of soot.

milan-tobacconists-lucky-leaf.z: Lucky Leaf is one of Milan Tobacconists' plainest house aromatics. According to the maker's description it is cavendish-based with a golden color, giving a soft taste; the ribbon cut provides an easy-lighting, evenly burning light smoke. Because its nicotine load and flavor casing are both kept low, it forms a mixture smokable throughout the day. Suitable for those new to the pipe and for smokers who avoid heavy flavoring but still want a soft cavendish taste.
milan-tobacconists-lucky-leaf.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, subtle cavendish aroma.

rona-primus-red-yellow.z: A pipe tobacco recorded in Rona's Primus series, classified as aromatic; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

mccranies-currituck.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found on Currituck, one of McCranie's Pipe Shop's house blends.
mccranies-currituck.o: No reliable description of the aroma could be found.

pipesandcigars-com-fireworks.z: No sufficient sources were found documenting the content and character of pipesandcigars.com's blend Fireworks.

samuel-gawith-turkish-blend.z: A Samuel Gawith mixture listed as Oriental-leaf-forward; no sufficient independent source describing its content and character could be found.
samuel-gawith-turkish-blend.o: No reliable description of its scent could be found.

uhles-b-js-cavendish.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend B&J's Cavendish has been found.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-raspberry-cream.z: Raspberry Cream is a light, sweet aromatic built by scattering a touch of golden cavendish over toasted raspberry cavendish. In the tin, black cavendish is mostly visible, with a few light-brown leaf pieces distinguishable among it. In the smoke raspberry and vanilla move together, giving a creamy, round taste. It burns cool with a low tendency to bite the tongue. With a very light nicotine load, suitable for smokers seeking a fruity aromatic they can smoke for long stretches during the day, or for those new to the pipe.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-raspberry-cream.o: Leaves a raspberry jam and creamy vanilla aroma.

brebbia-70-anniversary-25-06-2017.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named 70° ANNIVERSARY 25.06.2017 under the Brebbia brand could be found.

republic-tobacco-co-4aces-turkish-blue.z: 4Aces Turkish is the option in Republic Tobacco's economy line that puts Oriental leaf front and center. Added to a Burley-and-Virginia base, the Oriental tobacco gives an unusually spicy and dry profile for the line; the cut remains shag. The Oriental addition brings the blend closer to the spicy side of pricier mixtures, though the structure stays plain and body stays medium. It suits smokers looking for a spicy angle beyond the straightforward American profile in a cheap tobacco. It is produced in the US and distributed in large resealable bags.
republic-tobacco-co-4aces-turkish-blue.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of dry spice and incense.

von-eicken-piccolo-honey-and-rum.z: The Piccolo series comprises small plugs Von Eicken designed to match a single bowlful: pressed Cavendish is cut into broken flake and each piece individually wrapped in paper. Honey and Rum is the member of this series flavored toward honey and rum. Honey and rum notes stay pronounced from start to finish; the Cavendish base carries that sweetness, with the Virginia leaving a light acidic edge behind it. Nicotine is low. A product aimed at those wanting an aromatic tobacco suited to measured portions for smoking outdoors or on the go.
von-eicken-piccolo-honey-and-rum.o: Leaves a dark, sweet aroma reminiscent of honey and rum candy.

faders-14k.z: Fader's is a line of house blends offered under its own name by a long-established Baltimore tobacconist; no verifiable source could be found regarding this blend's composition and character.

john-middleton-inc-saga.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Middleton, Inc's Saga pipe tobacco.

pipesandcigars-com-snow-drift.z: This is a blend offered under the American retailer pipesandcigars.com's name; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

mcclelland-grey-havens.z: Grey Havens is a McClelland blend that sits close to Danish-style light aromatic mixtures. Bright Virginia, mild Burley, and black Cavendish are topped with a subtle top note; what sets the blend apart is the addition of Perique. Perique brings a dark fruitiness and a fine spiced edge to the mixture. Suited to smokers who steer clear of heavily syrupy aromatics yet still want a sweet line, and to easy daytime smokes; nicotine load stays light. Released within the Craftsbury series, the blend was discontinued when the brand closed in 2018.
mcclelland-grey-havens.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma of dried fruit and baked dough.

g-l-pease-fellowship-ii.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Fellowship II.

mars-cigars-pipes-arts-endeavor.z: Remembered as a house blend from the retailer Mars Cigars & Pipes; since no source documenting its contents could be found, the profile is left incomplete.
mars-cigars-pipes-arts-endeavor.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-whitehall-black-.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Sutliff Tobacco Company's Whitehall Black Tie pipe tobacco could be found.

mr-bs-brighams-own.z: Brigham's Own sits in the aromatic wing of the tobacco line Canadian pipe maker Brigham offers under the Mr. B's name. The composition's base is a black cavendish known as Green River, joined by burley and Virginia leaves. The manufacturer does not disclose the casing recipe that defines the blend's taste and aroma. The black cavendish-heavy structure gives the blend a sweet, soft, low-nicotine profile; burley balances the burn, while Virginia carries a light sweetness in the background. The ribbon cut makes packing easy. Suitable for smokers new to aromatic tobaccos or looking for a soft blend they can smoke all day. Distributed in fifty-gram pouches and in bulk.
mr-bs-brighams-own.o: Leaves a dark, sweet, confectionery-like aroma.

tres-cajones-tobacco-gnome-gnuggets.z: No sufficient source has been found for Tres Cajones Tobacco's blend Gnome Gnuggets.
tres-cajones-tobacco-gnome-gnuggets.o: No reliable source describing the room note has been found.

james-b-russell-bengal-slices-aromatic.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of James B. Russell's Bengal Slices Aromatic blend could be found.

planta-anno-mmvii-black-mixture.z: Anno MMVII is the 2007 installment of the limited Anno series the Berlin house Planta releases every year; no verifiable source could be found on the blend's composition and casing.

gawith-hoggarth-co-black-irish-x-unslice.z: Black Irish X is a tobacco produced by the traditional rope method at Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Kendal facility. Predominantly dark fire-cured leaf, joined by a small amount of air-cured dark Indian leaf, is hand-twisted with the wrapper leaf into rope form. The difference here lies in the cooking stage: because the rope is cooled and blackened under pressure, the tobacco softens and offers a more measured strength than its sibling Brown Irish X. The "Unsliced" designation indicates the product is sold as a whole, uncut rope; the smoker cuts coin-shaped pieces at whatever thickness they like and rubs them out.
