In the smoke, the smoky, woody, leather-like taste of the fire-cured leaf leads; cooking adds a caramelised sweetness and a lightly spiced tone. Nicotine is high, so it is not suited to an empty stomach or a fast smoke. This is a record that can serve as an entry point for smokers curious about rope tobaccos but wary of the strongest examples like Brown Irish X; it appeals to those who enjoy dark, satisfying, slow-smoking tobaccos.
gawith-hoggarth-co-black-irish-x-unslice.o: A light sweet undertone accompanies the smoke and leather aroma of the fire-cured leaf.

cornell-diehl-chick-magnet.z: One of Cornell & Diehl's aromatic blends; it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog, and not enough sourcing could be found to document its character.

mac-baren-amphora-virginia.z: Amphora Virginia is a blend built solely from Virginia leaves; the manufacturer states the leaves used are gathered from three separate continents. It's presented rubbed out, ready to pack. Since it contains no other leaf type, the blend's character is entirely defined by Virginia's natural sugar and grassy tones; in the smoke, sweetness toward hay, baked bread and light citrus comes forward. There's no applied casing. Nicotine is light, but tongue bite common in Virginia blends can appear if smoked quickly. Suited to those seeking an unflavored Virginia smoke and to those new to this type.
mac-baren-amphora-virginia.o: Leaves a sweetish room note toward dry hay and baked bread.

samuel-gawith-x-blend-limited-edition.z: A limited-run Samuel Gawith blend classified as Cavendish-based; no sufficient source describing its composition could be found.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-widecombe-mixtur.z: Widecombe Mixture is a bulk mixture arising from blending select Virginia leaf with cavendish and latakia. Virginia gives the body and sweetness while latakia builds a smoky backbone; the cavendish share smooths the transition. It is sold as a bulk ribbon cut.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-widecombe-mixtur.o: Leaves an aroma where woody latakia smoke mixes with sweet leaf scent.

peter-heinrichs-no-15.z: Peter Heinrichs No. 15 is a hand-rubbed slice tobacco in the English mixture tradition. Per the maker's account, Louisiana Perique and Oriental leaves are enriched with pitch-black Latakia; the blend is hand-rubbed and then cut into 2.1-millimeter slices. The high proportion of Latakia determines the blend's character; the Oriental adds dry spice, while Perique adds a sharpness recalling plum and pepper. Flavor intensity sits at the top band, and nicotine is pronounced too. It is a record aimed at experienced smokers familiar with heavy Latakia structures and pressed slices.
peter-heinrichs-no-15.o: Leaves an intense aroma dominated by tar and smoked wood.

hu-tobacco-sunset.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the Sunset blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

hu-tobacco-haddes-best-irish.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Hadde's Best Irish, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-p-s-blend.z: P.S. Blend, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an aromatic mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

pcca-tudor.z: A blend produced by McClelland within the PCCA club series; it should not be confused with the identically named Tudor Castle series, and not enough source material describing its composition could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-mellow-peach-205.z: Mellow Peach #205 is a fruit-flavored blend in Sutliff's numbered bulk line. It is built by combining Virginia-based golden cavendish with flavored black cavendish; the casing focuses on peach. Thanks to the cavendish-forward structure, nicotine is low and the smoke is soft. The tobacco's own taste stays in the background, and peach sweetness is what stands out. It lights easily and burns cool. It suits those looking for a single-note, pronouncedly fruity blend and those wanting a soft start in their early years of pipe smoking.
sutliff-tobacco-company-mellow-peach-205.o: Leaves a pronounced peach scent with a sweet, clean trace behind it.

dan-tobacco-solway-blend.z: This is referred to in the Dan Tobacco catalog as a Virginia and perique-based blend; not enough sourcing exists for detailed composition, cut, and character information.
dan-tobacco-solway-blend.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

holger-danske-double-fermented.z: Double Fermented is an aromatic blend under the Holger Danske name that takes its name from its composition. Its weight is made up of twice-fermented black Cavendish; a small amount of loose-cut Burley is added for balance. Light vanilla, fruit, and rum flavoring are applied on top, and the tobacco is presented ribbon cut. Because the second fermentation lowers the leaf's harshness, the smoke stays cool and mild. The moist, tacky black Cavendish prepared in the Danish-American style gives the blend a sweet body leaving an oak-like aftertaste. Being light in nicotine makes it suitable for newcomers who enjoy aromatics and those not wanting a heavy tobacco during the day. Records indicate the brand was previously blended in Germany by Planta; today it's produced in Denmark by Mac Baren.
holger-danske-double-fermented.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of nougat, chocolate, and raisins.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-524.z: No verifiable source could be found documenting the composition and character of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Wilke No. 524.

paul-olsen-english-virginia-g965.z: A blend from the My Own Blend line that originated at the Paul Olsen shop in Copenhagen; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

esoterica-tobacciana-brighton.z: Brighton is a fine shag-cut blend bringing together six distinct Virginia leaves. A light apricot-like topping is applied over them, kept light enough not to suppress the tobacco's own sugar. The brand is run in the US under Arango Cigar Co, while production takes place in England by J. F. Germain & Son, and the blends are rested before release. It is light in color and body; the fine cut lets it catch quickly and leaves little residue. It suits those seeking a fruity but not overdone Virginia, a mild blend smokable at any hour of the day.
esoterica-tobacciana-brighton.o: Leaves apricot sweetness together with a dry-grass scent.

alfie-turmeaus-sweet-leaf.z: Sweet Leaf was one of the special mixtures Turmeaus stores prepared at the counter. It was built by combining sweetly sauced aromatic tobaccos with smoky Latakia and shredded Havana cigar leaf; this brought an aromatic top taste together with the cigar leaf's dry, earthy body in the same bowl. This contrast between the sweet and smoky extremes was the blend's distinguishing trait. With changes in UK regulations on tobacco product composition, using shredded cigar leaf in the store's own recipe became impossible, and Sweet Leaf was removed from the list along with Wavecrest; per records, the maker has stated that a similar recipe could return in a different form. It appealed to smokers wanting to try aromatic sweetness together with Latakia and cigar leaf.
alfie-turmeaus-sweet-leaf.o: Leaves a room note of soot and dry cigar leaf emerging beneath a sweet, sugary top scent.

samuel-gawith-golden-glow.z: Golden Glow is one of Samuel Gawith's blends made solely from Virginia leaf, found in the tin as broken flake, meaning crumbled leaf slices. On opening the tin, large leaf pieces and intact flake fragments are seen among bright-yellow shredded pieces; it carries no casing scent, only Virginia's own scent. Since the tobacco is tinned with high moisture, airing before packing noticeably eases the burn. On the smoke, Virginia's sweetness stays measured; flavor intensity and nicotine fullness are low, with no hardening or sharpening seen across the bowl, and the ash stays light-colored and mild. In this respect it is a Virginia suited to the day's first bowls or long, undemanding smokes; it may read as limited to smokers seeking a dark, full Virginia character or expecting higher nicotine.
samuel-gawith-golden-glow.o: Leaves a light, fine trace evoking dry hay and honey.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-seersucke.z: Seersucker is an aromatic house blend from The Country Squire tobacconist combining Burley and Cavendish leaves with a raspberry-cream top flavoring. The name references the American South's summer fabric. Burley gives the blend a nutty, lightly earthy base, while the Cavendish adds dark sweetness and a moist burn; raspberry and cream sit distinctly on top of these. Nicotine load is low and the taste is mellow. Prepared for smokers who enjoy fruity, creamy aromatics.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-seersucke.o: Leaves a scent of raspberry cream and sugary fruit.

cornell-diehl-christmas-blend-2014-we-th.z: We Three Kings was released as Cornell & Diehl's 2014 holiday blend and was later added permanently to the catalog. It takes its name from the American Christmas carol written in 1857. One measure of black cavendish is joined by equal measures of red Virginia, light Virginia, and Katerini Oriental; it is topped with a light flavoring along the lines of allspice, cinnamon, and vanilla. It is a lightly flavored Virginia-Oriental mixture that lets the natural sweetness and spice of the flue-cured and sun-cured leaves come through; on the palate, tones reminiscent of brown sugar and baked goods sit alongside an earthy, floral background. It suits smokers who avoid heavy aromatics but want a seasonal, spiced sweetness.
cornell-diehl-christmas-blend-2014-we-th.o: Leaves a sweet, spiced room aroma reminiscent of cinnamon cookies and vanilla.

marcovitch-co-black-white-smoking-mixtur.z: Remembered as a pipe blend released under the name Black & White by Marcovitch & Co., founded in London in 1867 and known for its black-and-white-striped tins; since no source documenting its composition could be found, the profile is left incomplete.
marcovitch-co-black-white-smoking-mixtur.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

motzek-no-name.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called No Name could be found.

georgetown-tobacco-berkeburley.z: As its name suggests, one of Georgetown Tobacco's Burley-forward shop blends; no published sourcing on its leaf ratios and character could be found.
georgetown-tobacco-berkeburley.o: No record of the room aroma could be found.

robert-mcconnell-the-original-pure-kentu.z: Pure Kentucky is a product from Robert McConnell's "Pure" series made entirely of Kentucky leaf. Kentucky comes from the Burley family and is prepared by dark-fire curing, a process that gives the leaf a smoky, sooty, spicy character and considerable fullness. It is among the heaviest members of the series in nicotine; it is not well suited to smoking on an empty stomach or at a fast pace. It can be smoked alone, but reports indicate its main purpose is blending: added in small amounts, it lends depth, smoke, and body to Virginia- or Oriental-heavy blends. The brand is Belfast in origin; production today takes place in Germany.
robert-mcconnell-the-original-pure-kentu.o: Leaves the sharp aroma of dark-fired leaf, heavy with soot and wood smoke.

bosphorus-full-virginia-flake.z: Full Virginia Flake is an unflavored flake prepared from Syrian Virginia, fermented in oak barrels. Its strength is light, flavor intensity low. The product has been discontinued and replaced by New Virginia Flake. It stands on record as one of the brand's early Virginia experiments.
bosphorus-full-virginia-flake.o: Leaves a faint trace of dry grass and lightly tart hay aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-extra-sweet-br.z: Brown Pigtail is one of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s hand-twisted fine rope (pigtail) tobaccos. Strong Virginia leaf is twisted into rope and flavored with maple sugars; the name "extra sweet" denotes the version where this flavoring is applied more intensely. Fine slices are cut from the rope and rubbed out before packing the pipe. The fine twist gives a more intense taste than the thick Irish twist; on the other hand, it's more of a chore to cut. On the smoke, a peppery sharpness and an earthy, musk-reminiscent base stand out; the sugar doesn't turn this into an aromatic, just rounds off its edge. Nicotine is very high. Aimed at smokers accustomed to rope tobaccos wanting a strong smoke; historically, these fine ropes were also used as chewing tobacco among sailors and miners.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-extra-sweet-br.o: Leaves a heavy, earthy tobacco aroma along with burnt-sugar sweetness.

magne-falkum-tullagreme-house-no-3.z: Tullagreme House no.3 is a release in Falkum's flake series that reads darker than the series' lighter members like No. 2 and No. 6. A small amount of Perique is added to the Virginia-forward composition; records indicate this leaf is the source of the blend's mild tang. The pressing is loose and the slices break up easily, so it can be packed as if already rubbed out. On opening, dried-fruit and dark-bread notes stand out. Virginia sweetness stays measured, and the spice from the Perique proceeds without overtaking it. It's cited as the fullest-smoking flake in the series, yet stays medium in nicotine. Suited to smokers new to Perique-containing flakes or wanting measured spice.
magne-falkum-tullagreme-house-no-3.o: Leaves a dark aroma reminiscent of dried fruit and dark bread.

vauen-no-15-english-blend.z: No. 15 English Blend is an English-style mixture on Vauen's unflavored side. Classic Virginia forms the body; Burley, Latakia, Oriental leaves and a pinch of Perique are added on top to give a spicy structure. No additional flavoring is used in production or processing, so the taste comes from the tobacco's own aroma. The Latakia proportion is not kept at a level that would turn the blend into a heavy Balkan mixture; smoke and spice are pronounced, yet Virginia sweetness is still felt. Suited to those looking for an entry point into unflavored English mixtures and to smokers moving from aromatics to unflavored tobacco.
vauen-no-15-english-blend.o: Leaves a smoky aroma reminiscent of soot, dry wood and spice.

sutliff-tobacco-company-tabac-noir.z: Tabac Noir is listed as a dark-leaf-forward blend within Sutliff's aromatic line; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-tabac-noir.o: No reliable record of a room note could be found.

amphora-burley.z: Amphora Burley is a semi-aromatic Burley blend in the Dutch-origin Amphora brand's line, carried on today by Mac Baren. Alongside Burley it contains Kentucky and Virginia; its cut is ready rubbed, meaning it looks like broken flake. The color is medium-to-dark brown, and though it looks dry on the outside, the leaf retains its internal moisture. In the pack scent, the Amphora line's base topping — sugary, with fruit and fruit-brandy notes — stands out; after airing, chocolate and hazelnut notes become more apparent. The blend lights easily and gives an intense but quickly dissipating smoke; records note it burns warmer than typical Burley blends. Strength is medium, flavor is intense. It suits smokers looking for a tobacco that presents Burley character without drowning it in flavoring, and those wanting a mixing tobacco to mellow the Amphora line's more intensely flavored blends.
amphora-burley.o: Leaves a chocolate-and-hazelnut room note over a faintly smoky tobacco base.

leavitt-peirce-dark-honey.z: An aromatic record among Leavitt & Peirce's house blends; no source could be found describing its composition and character.

frederick-tranter-gaelic-mixture.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Frederick Tranter's Gaelic Mixture blend; records place it in the Virginia-heavy class.

paul-olsen-haddock.z: A blend from the My Own Blend line that originated at the Paul Olsen shop in Copenhagen; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-majestic-586.z: Majestic 586 is one of the blends the Boswell workshop in Pennsylvania blends in-house. A toasted cavendish core is joined by some burley and wide-cut Virginia leaf; Virginia's golden yellow is clearly visible among the dark leaves. Per the manufacturer's description, the flavor softens as the bowl progresses, yet stays full without losing its character to the end, and holds up through relights. Its sweetness comes more from the cavendish processing than from casing, making it a measured aromatic. Nicotine load is low, flavor body medium; suitable for smokers seeking a mixture they can smoke all day without turning to heavy English blends. Since Boswell tobaccos are distributed mainly through the manufacturer's own shops, freshness and moisture level can vary by batch.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-majestic-586.o: Leaves a sweetish aroma reminiscent of toasted walnut and fresh bread.

the-pipe-shop-southern-star.z: Southern Star is one of the house blends from The Pipe Shop in Edinburgh. It is made from a mix of broken flake pieces and ribbon-cut leaf, and this combination of cuts shapes both how the blend packs and how it burns. A measured amount of whisky, vanilla, and marshmallow flavoring has been added on top; the taste is described as a light, cool-smoking aromatic. It suits smokers looking for a sweet but not overpowering mixture that stays more restrained than heavily cased aromatics.
the-pipe-shop-southern-star.o: Leaves a scent of vanilla candy with a light hint of whisky.

gawith-hoggarth-co-black-cavendish-cc-bl.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Black Cavendish CC Blending blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

walgreens-black-cavendish.z: This is one of the bulk blends sold under the Walgreens pharmacy chain's own name; no reliable source could be found documenting its composition.

pipesandcigars-com-scottys-milk-and-hone.z: This is a blend offered under the American retailer pipesandcigars.com's name; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

d-r-tobacco-ryback-gold.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of D & R Tobacco's Ryback Gold blend were found.

the-smoke-shop-amarillo-tx-summer-deligh.z: No reliable source could be found on Summer Delight, the house blend from the tobacconist The Smoke Shop (Amarillo, TX).

peretti-british-blend.z: British is one of the house blends produced by L.J. Peretti Co. in Boston and, per the maker's own description, is counted among the house's fuller-bodied mixtures. Latakia and Perique are placed together on top of Virginia and Oriental leaf; using this pair together gives the blend both a smoky depth and a spicy edge. The cut is ribbon, as is customary in the shop's counter blends, and it is well suited to aging in a jar. The blend is aimed at smokers whose palates are accustomed to Latakia and who are seeking full-bodied English mixtures. It is not light in nicotine, so it can be demanding on an empty stomach or as the first pipe of the day. Peretti was founded in 1870 and reportedly began blending pipe tobacco around 1915; the majority of the house's more than eighty blends came from third-generation Robert Peretti.
peretti-british-blend.o: Leaves a woody, dry-leaf-dominant aroma leaning toward smoke.

peterson-irish-whiskey.z: Irish Whiskey is a ribbon-cut blend built from Virginia, Burley, and Kentucky leaf, topped with a flavoring recalling Irish whiskey. Being ribbon cut, it packs easily and burns evenly. Nicotine strength is medium; flavor intensity sits between medium and high. It is recorded as wanting a slow, controlled smoking pace, since it overheats and loses flavor if rushed. It suits smokers seeking whiskey flavoring alongside their tobacco who aren't put off by a Burley-Kentucky body.
peterson-irish-whiskey.o: Fills the room noticeably with a whiskey and sharp burnt-tobacco aroma.

just-for-him-berts-blend.z: One of the house blends the Just For Him tobacconist prepares at its own counter; no independent source could be found on its contents or character.

cornell-diehl-virginia-gentleman.z: Virginia Gentleman is a ribbon-cut blend combining Virginia leaf with Burley, topped with a small amount of Turkish (Oriental) leaf. Per the maker's description, the aim is to offer a softer option to smokers who love Virginia blends but feel tongue bite over an all-day smoke. The pouch note carries raisin, oat, grass, and sweet-bread notes. On the smoke, Virginia carries the weight; toward the end Burley builds an earthy, nutty base, while the Oriental leaf gives occasional spicy sharpness. No casing is used. Suited to smokers looking for a Virginia that's not one-dimensional but not tiring either, smokable all day.
cornell-diehl-virginia-gentleman.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, breadlike scent reminiscent of dry hay and oatmeal.

poul-winslow-poul-winslow-no-3.z: Poul Winslow No. 3 belongs to the aromatic line prepared under the name of Danish pipe maker Poul Winsløw. The blend brings together orange-toned broad-cut Virginia leaf, hand-rubbed soft Virginia flake, and double-fermented black Cavendish; these three components are presented in the same tin as a mix of different cuts. The casing uses notes recalling champagne, vanilla cream, and light almond. Sweetness is carried by the black Cavendish, while the Virginia base builds a tart balance in the background. Nicotine falls between light and medium; it fits the territory of those interested in Danish-style aromatics with pronounced casing that still doesn't fully mask the tobacco taste. The tin lid carries a print from Winsløw's own drawings.
poul-winslow-poul-winslow-no-3.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of vanilla cream and almond candy.

mcclelland-black-shag.z: Black Shag is the first blend in McClelland's Sherlock Holmes-themed 221b series, introduced at a 1997 Sherlock Holmes gathering. Its name nods to the thick-cut dark tobacco tradition mentioned in the Holmes stories. The blend is built from unflavored Virginia: stoved black Virginia is used together with flue-cured red Virginia. It looks predominantly black, with dark yellow and red threads among it. The very fine cut eases packing and even burning, the tobacco lights easily, and needs few relights. The taste rests on stoved Virginia's mild sweetness, and nicotine is low; it can bite the tongue if smoked quickly. Falls within the territory of those who know how to work with fine-cut tobacco and want a straight Virginia.
mcclelland-black-shag.o: Leaves a fine, lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of toasted bread crust.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-pigtail-sweet-b.z: This is a product from Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s twisted-rope family, finished with sweet brandy. The body rests on strong Virginia leaves; the brandy topping gives a sweetness closer to dried fruit rather than the sharp, harsh taste often found in alcohol-flavoured blends. The rope is filled by slicing thin and rubbing out, and wants airing due to its high moisture. Fullness and flavour intensity are above medium. It is aimed at those wanting a product that keeps the body of rope tobaccos while the topping stays measured.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-pigtail-sweet-b.o: Leaves a dried-fruit sweetness mixed with a light alcohol aroma over smoky tobacco.

frederick-tranter-comfort-of-bath.z: This is one of the bulk-sold house blends of Frederick Tranter, a Bath tobacconist who opened his first shop in 1870; no reliable source describing its composition and character could be found.

pipesandcigars-com-scottys-university-st.z: This is a blend offered under the American retailer pipesandcigars.com's name; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

cornell-diehl-mad-fiddler-flake.z: Mad Fiddler Flake is a pressed flake starring Indonesian-origin Kasturi cigar leaf, rounded out with red Virginia, Perique, and black Cavendish. As in Cornell & Diehl's other blends using cigar leaf, Kasturi gives the smoke body and texture. On the smoke, a spice reminiscent of dry cinnamon and clove comes forward alongside dark fruit notes and a measured sweetness; Perique's spice sharpens Kasturi's earthy character. Body sits between medium and full, and nicotine is noticeable. Aimed at those interested in full-bodied flakes containing cigar leaf.
cornell-diehl-mad-fiddler-flake.o: Cigar leaf's earthy scent accompanies dark fruit and cinnamon-spice notes.

tobacconist-reserve-ltd-virginia-blend.z: Tobacconist Reserve Virginia Blend is an unflavored Virginia blend prepared by pressing and slicing aged red Virginia leaves sourced from three separate continents. It is tinned as a crumble cake; the smoker crumbles off a slice by hand and prepares it to the fullness desired. The red Virginia weight gives the blend a dark, bready, lightly fruity sweetness; rather than the sharp acidity of bright Virginia blends, a rounder, deeper taste line comes forward. Because the pressed structure gives a slow, cool burn, it suits smokers accustomed to unflavored Virginia and willing to work with sliced tobacco. It was distributed in 1.75-ounce tins.
tobacconist-reserve-ltd-virginia-blend.o: Leaves a warm, sweetish tobacco aroma reminiscent of dry hay and stale bread crust.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-dark-oriental.z: Dark Oriental is among Wilke Pipe Tobacco's unflavored records that put Oriental leaf front and center. Turkish tobacco and Macedonian Prilep leaf take the lead role in the composition, joined by maduro cigar leaf and oven-dried bright Virginia. Though it contains no Latakia, the dark leaves' contribution produces a notable body and depth. The flavor combines earth, wood, dry grass, herbal notes, a floral edge, dry tartness, tingling spice, and measured sweetness; the maduro leaf adds toast, cocoa, coffee, and dark-fruit traces. Body runs medium to full, flavor a notch more intense than that, and nicotine sits just below body strength. It burns cool and clean, needing an average number of relights. The room note is sharp. This is a blend aimed less at all-day smoking and more at experienced smokers who want to taste the Oriental character intensely.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-dark-oriental.o: Leaves a sharp scent reminiscent of earth, dry grass, and dark cigar leaf.

charatan-mild-flake.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the British pipe maker Charatan.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-granger.z: Granger is a ribbon-cut, mild-nicotine American burley blend produced for generations; no second independent source on its composition could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-granger.o: Leaves a nutty, lightly sweet burley scent.

motzek-vb-twist.z: Referred to as one of the virginia-and-burley-based twist-form products of the Kiel-based TAK workshop; no independent source describing the blend's composition could be found.

pcca-cyprian-star-3.z: For PCCA's blend called Cyprian Star 3, no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

park-lane-tobacconist-christmas-morning.z: One of Park-Lane Tobacconist's New Year-themed aromatic house blends; no usable source describing its composition could be found.

brigham-enterprises-inc-benedict-brandy.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named Benedict Brandy under the Brigham Enterprises Inc. brand could be found.

cornell-diehl-evergreen.z: Evergreen is a Virginia-Perique blend prepared in limited quantity under Wintertime Reserve, the winter-season extension of Cornell & Diehl's Small Batch series. The composition includes both stoved and unstoved red Virginia leaves, unflavored black cavendish, and a small amount of perique; the mixture is pressed into flake. It is hand-produced in small batches, following recipes selected by head blender Jeremy Reeves. The tin note leads with dry grass and dried fruit. On the smoke, Virginia's sugary sweetness combines with black cavendish's soft body, while perique stays in the background as a spicy, plummy trace. It is unflavored, not heavy, and well suited to slow smoking; it is aimed at those seeking natural Virginia sweetness with an understated touch of perique. Being a limited production run, it is not consistently available on the market.
cornell-diehl-evergreen.o: A light, tangy tobacco tone accompanies the aroma of dry grass and dried fruit.

john-surrey-ltd-snow-apple-blend-no-549.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Surrey, Ltd.'s Snow Apple (Blend No. 549) pipe tobacco.

sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-oriental.z: Recorded as an Oriental-leaf blend from Sentimiento Nacional, the brand founded in 2003 by Argentine blender Antonio Petti; no independent source describing the blend's composition and character could be found, so no further detail is given.
sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-oriental.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-pigtail-rum.z: This is the rum-topped version of the old-fashioned twisted-rope tradition. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. produces its rope by twisting fire-cured leaves; in Brown Pigtail Rum the dominant figure is Virginia leaf, while the rum builds a sweet layer in the background. The topping level is measured and does not mask the leaf's own character. The rope is sliced coin-thin and rubbed out for filling. Given the high moisture, airing it for a while first is common practice. In terms of nicotine it is above medium; it is aimed at those wanting to try a classic English rope tobacco with a light sugared top note.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-pigtail-rum.o: A sweet, sugared rum note is heard over the smoky tobacco aroma.

sobranie-of-london-reserve-blend-aromati.z: The aromatic number in Sobranie of London's Reserve Blend line; records indicate it was sold in its own tin, and the line as a whole has gone out of production. No reliable source on its composition and topping could be found.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-sweet-and-mild.z: Sweet and Mild is an aromatic formed by adding toasted cherry notes over a golden cavendish base. Per records, the blend took its final form in 1998 through the joint work of Dan Boswell and Russ Hess, a regular customer of the shop. The smoke is soft, nicotine load low; the sweet aroma it leaves in the room is pronounced. The cherry aroma is kept more measured than Boswell's more intense cherry blends, making it suited to those seeking a light aromatic to smoke all day.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-sweet-and-mild.o: A toasted cherry and sweet cavendish aroma spreads into the room.

douwe-egberts-house-blend-aromatic.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of House Blend Aromatic, a pipe tobacco from Douwe Egberts.
douwe-egberts-house-blend-aromatic.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

kendal-rodeo-shag.z: Rodeo Shag is an unflavored blend produced by Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. in the town of Kendal in England's Lake District. Its composition combines flue-cured and dark-fired Virginia leaves with Burley; sources indicate some of the leaves are sourced from Brazil, India and Indonesia. As the name suggests, it's presented in a very fine shag cut. No essence or syrup is applied; sweetness comes only from the leaf's own sugars. In the smoke, a round Virginia taste without pronounced tang, dominated by grass and hay, is supported by an earthy, woody body from the dark-fired leaf and Burley. It's medium-bodied and suited to smoking all day. Since the fine cut lights and burns quickly, lightly moistening it and packing it loosely is the usual practice. Suited to smokers seeking an unflavored, plain, English-made everyday blend.
kendal-rodeo-shag.o: Leaves an earthy, low-sharpness trace with dry hay and burnt-wood scent.

planta-pergamon.z: Planta Pergamon is a pipe tobacco blend for which there is not enough independent source material.
planta-pergamon.o: Not enough records could be found on the room note.

g-l-pease-sextant.z: Sextant is the fifth entry in the Old London Series, combining a classic mixture with the navy flake tradition. Ripe Virginia leaves are first blended with Cyprus latakia, quality Oriental tobaccos, and a small amount of dark fire-cured Kentucky; a touch of dark rum is then infused, and the mix is lightly pressed, matured, and sliced. The smoke is full and satisfying. The rum infusion, combined with the dark fire-cured Kentucky, pressing, and fermentation, gives the blend its own distinctive sweetness and aroma; even so, the structure stays within the classic mixture line and does not cross into the aromatic class. It is a record aimed at smokers wanting to try a navy-style flake together with a Latakia mixture.
g-l-pease-sextant.o: Leaves a sweet rum aroma passing through the woodsmoke.

lane-limited-anniversary.z: Lane Limited's record called Anniversary is a name that could be confused with the limited blends the brand releases for its anniversaries; since no independent source could be found to confirm this record's composition, it's left incomplete.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2017.z: Christmas Cheer is the straight Virginia series that Kansas City-based McClelland released once a year, in limited numbers, from the 1980s until the company's closure in early 2018. The series' idea is to present a single Virginia batch selected from that year's harvest on its own; each year is thus considered a separate record, and the year on the tin defines the blend's identity. The 2017 release was prepared the same way, with selected matured Virginia leaf pressed into cake and tinned as broken flake. The 2017 release became the series' final entry, as the company closed in February 2018. Unflavored Virginia character dominates the smoke: natural leaf sweetness over a bready, herbal base, with a faint tang and a lemony sharpness in the background. Nicotine dose is measured, while flavor intensity is pronounced; it burns cool when smoked slowly, but tends to bite the tongue when rushed. Since the flake's moisture can run high straight from the tin, airing it before packing is common practice. A record aimed at smokers seeking unflavored Virginia who are considering cellaring the tin; not suitable for those expecting an aromatic.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2017.o: A tangy, sharp trace characteristic of McClelland tins mixes into an aroma of dry hay and toasted bread.

olaf-poulsson-extra-light.z: A blend tied to Dan Tobacco's Olaf Poulsson line; no record under this name in current product listings, and no reliable source describing its composition, could be found.

lane-limited-vanilla.z: Lane Limited's vanilla-flavored aromatic blend; not enough independent sources could be found for its composition.

gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-honeydew.z: A lively aromatic that combines mature Virginias' and Burley's natural sweetness with a honey-and-maple-based flavoring. A measured floral Lakeland trace from Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Kendal tradition also sits behind the blend; this sets it apart from Continental European aromatics. Records indicate the product is sold under the name "Rich Dark Spring Dew" in some countries due to European Union regulations. Nicotine is moderate; sweetness is pronounced and the smoke is generous. Aimed at those who love aromatic tobacco but want a blend where the tobacco taste is still audible rather than an all-sugar product.
gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-honeydew.o: A light floral Lakeland trace mingles with the aroma of honey and maple syrup.

cornell-diehl-o-harim.z: No verified description of the contents could be found from the manufacturer or retailers for this entry, associated with Cornell & Diehl's Hebraica series.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-san-val.z: An aromatic blend released for Valentine's Day under Ken Byron Ventures' Mr. Christian's line; no accessible source could be found to document its contents.

planta-cutty-sark.z: Cutty Sark is a mellow mixture in which Planta gives its own Scottish-style interpretation. Lighter-colored tobaccos are scattered among the dark brown leaves; the casing isn't heavy and doesn't mask the tobacco's own taste. A subtle flavor line is aimed for with a light casing evoking the Scotch whisky the name references. Nicotine is measured, giving it a structure suitable for all-day smoking. It suits smokers who avoid heavy aromatics but also keep some distance from fully unflavored tobaccos. It was sold in 100-gram tins.
planta-cutty-sark.o: A light malt-and-whisky association mixes into a dry tobacco aroma.

james-b-russell-monarch.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of James B. Russell's Monarch blend could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-no-12-mixture.z: No. 12 Mixture is a traditional English blend where the Latakia ratio is kept noticeably high. Latakia's smoky, incense-laden character is joined by sweet Virginias; the ribbon cut packs easily. The flavor line carries smoke, dry wood, and a light fruity sweetness in the background. Nicotine is moderate. Suited to smokers who love Latakia-forward, unflavored English mixtures.
gawith-hoggarth-co-no-12-mixture.o: Leaves a sharp smoke aroma reminiscent of pine wood and incense.

sturks-tobacconists-balkan.z: A house blend called Balkan from the tobacconist Sturk's Tobacconists; since sufficient sources documenting its composition and character could not be found, this record is kept limited.
sturks-tobacconists-balkan.o: Leaves a smoky, woody scent typical of Balkan-style mixtures.

van-erkoms-rum-and-honey.z: An aromatic blend from Van Erkoms whose name points to rum and honey flavoring; no independent source documenting the tobacco composition and smoking character has been found, so the record is left incomplete.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-amphora-re.z: This blend, also known as Euphoria in Sutliff's Match line, is a Dutch-style cavendish mixture modeled on the aromatic version of Amphora. A sweet Virginia and nutty burley base is accompanied by a light topping of orange, red fruit, and floral essences. It's a cool, evenly burning blend, low in nicotine, with flavor that changes little over the course of the bowl. Aimed at smokers who like light Dutch-style aromatics and want a soft mixture suitable for all-day smoking. The Match line was created to offer approximations of blends that have been discontinued or become hard to find.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-amphora-re.o: Leaves a soft scent carrying orange peel and light fruit sweetness.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2000.z: Christmas Cheer 2000 is a member of McClelland's annual unflavored Virginia series. Per its label, it's prepared with mature, orange-red flue-cured Virginias selected from the 1996 harvest grown near Danville. The leaf is pressed and presented as broken flake. Redder leaves give a darker profile leaning toward dried fruit and bready sweetness. No flavoring is used, and nicotine is medium. The series was produced in limited numbers each year from a single harvest and designed for long-term storage; suited to smokers seeking unflavored Virginia flake.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2000.o: Leaves a sweet hay, dried-fig, and faintly tangy aroma.

chacom-3.z: Chacom #3 is the sweetest aromatic in the line. Double-fermented black cavendish forms the body of the blend; golden-yellow and red Virginia along with a pinch of burley are added alongside it. A generous bourbon-vanilla casing is applied on top. The flavor is creamy and soft, with vanilla staying dominant through the bowl. Nicotine is low, and the tobacco's own taste stays behind the casing. The moist fine cut calls for careful lighting. Suitable for those seeking a heavily vanilla-flavored, low-strength aromatic and wanting to leave a strong sweet aroma in the room.
chacom-3.o: Leaves a bourbon-vanilla and honeycomb room note.

g-smith-sons-old-london-100-virginia.z: Old London 100% Virginia is an untopped broken flake, entirely Virginia leaf, from the series named after the G. Smith & Sons tobacconist on Charing Cross Road in London. The shop was founded in 1869 and is considered the street's first licensed tobacconist; it offers around fifty bulk blends under its own name. The leaf is matured and dark in colour, giving a full taste that grows heavier toward the bottom of the bowl as the smoke progresses; no flavouring is used at all. It suits smokers seeking old-fashioned, dark, plain Virginia blends.
g-smith-sons-old-london-100-virginia.o: Leaves a dark, slightly tart, woody tobacco aroma.

robert-mcconnell-three-kings.z: This is a blend carried under the Robert McConnell name, said to belong to the aromatic class; there is not enough source material describing its content and character.
robert-mcconnell-three-kings.o: Could not be determined from available sources.

wesleys-no-15-three-quarter-flake.z: No. 15 Three Quarter Flake is listed among South African Wesley's house blends under the English-type mixtures heading. According to the maker's description, it consists of a combination of matured, full flakes, offered ready-rubbed. The "three quarter" in the name refers to its strength level, kept a bit above medium. Its ready-rubbed structure makes packing easy and aims for a cool smoke. The matured leaf, together with the compressed texture of the flake cut, gives a bready, measured sweetness; the leaf's own character comes forward rather than casing. It's intended for smokers accustomed to the slow pace of flake cut who want above-medium body without leaning into heavy Latakia mixtures.
wesleys-no-15-three-quarter-flake.o: Leaves a bready, lightly sweet, dry-grassy scent.

lane-limited-a-100.z: One of Lane Limited's code-named bulk blends; not enough sources could be found to document its contents.

ken-byron-ventures-the-candela-effect.z: As the name suggests, this blend is built on Candela cigar leaf, harvested early and dried to preserve its green color; not enough sources could be found to document its proportions or other components.

peterson-special-reserve-2006.z: Peterson's 2006 special tin is known only as the brand's 140th-anniversary tin; no sufficient sources on the blend's composition exist.

g-l-pease-cumberland.z: Cumberland is a G. L. Pease blend built solely from leaves of American continental origin. At its centre lies matured, dark fire-cured Kentucky leaf; this leaf is rounded out with various Virginias and a small amount of Louisiana perique. Kentucky's woody, smoky body balances Virginia's sweetness, while perique adds a plum-and-spice edge. Its fullness is above medium. It suits smokers seeking a dark, full-bodied smoke without Latakia, one leaning close to the Virginia-perique tradition.
g-l-pease-cumberland.o: Leaves the woody, smoky aroma of the fire-cured leaf together with dried-fruit sweetness.

peretti-yuletide-2025-version.z: The 2025 edition of Yuletide is the latest entry in Peretti's annual seasonal tradition, offered from December 1 until stock runs out. Per the maker's description, this Cavendish-based blend carries cognac, chocolate, and mint notes. Using three flavorings together creates a more layered taste than single-fruit editions: mint gives coolness, cocoa depth, and cognac a boozy sweetness. Cavendish's soft body carries this load and keeps the burn cool. It suits smokers seeking a pronounced, flavored blend for the winter months.
peretti-yuletide-2025-version.o: Leaves a trace where mint, cocoa, and cognac aromas sit together.

cornell-diehl-old-hollywood.z: Old Hollywood is, per available records, an American mixture from Cornell & Diehl containing red Virginia, Latakia, red Virginia cavendish, Oriental leaf, and cube-cut burley; it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog, and its details could not be verified due to a lack of sufficient primary sourcing.
cornell-diehl-old-hollywood.o: Leaves a lightly smoky, sweetish tobacco aroma.

charatan-no-63.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the British pipe maker Charatan.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-blend-35.z: Blend 35 is a blend Boswell prepared in 2015 for its thirty-fifth anniversary. It consists of loosely cut burley combined with golden cavendish, with a small amount of fire-cured cavendish added. The result is a slow-burning, light-bodied, lightly sweet smoke; there is no casing amounting to a sugary flavor. Boswell is a family business that prepares its blends in its own shop in Chambersburg, Pennsylvania. This blend suits fans of the burley-based American style and smokers seeking a transition from aromatic to unflavored blends; nicotine is measured and it has a soft profile in terms of tongue bite.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-blend-35.o: Leaves a nut-like, lightly sweet and soft aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-peach.z: Kendal Gold is one of the shag-cut main bodies produced at Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Kendal workshop in Cumbria. Its base is a fine golden-hued cut of flame-cured bright Virginia leaf; the producer states it uses no other tobacco type in this series, only cleanly cut Virginia. The Kendal Gold body is offered with numerous different flavorings, and Kendal Gold Peach is this family's member flavored with peach essence. Since the shag cut is fine and dry, it lights quickly; a slow draw is needed so the bowl doesn't burn too fast. The peach flavoring is layered over the Virginia base's citrusy sweetness, while nicotine stays moderate. Suited to those wanting a fine-cut, fruity everyday blend that isn't too heavy; also suited to use in small-chambered pipes.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-peach.o: Leaves an aroma of ripe peach and light honey.

gawith-hoggarth-co-revor-plug.z: Revor Plug is a plug tobacco with a long history, made by different producers over the years and today continued by Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. The glossy-surfaced plug is made of fire-cured Virginia and Kentucky leaf, carrying a light floral essence from the house's Lakeland style on top. Being sold in plug form, the smoker slices and rubs out their own portion, which allows adjusting the burn speed. The taste is smoky, earthy, and full, while nicotine is very high. Suited to those with plug tobacco experience wanting a strong smoke.
gawith-hoggarth-co-revor-plug.o: Leaves a heavy tobacco aroma with a light floral trace over the smoky dark leaf.

dunhill-royal-yacht.z: Royal Yacht's name refers to King George V's 1911 voyage to the Delhi Durbar aboard the RMS Medina; when Alfred Dunhill launched his pre-packaged blends in 1912, he named one Royal Yacht and another Durbar in commemoration of the event. The tobacco was produced in London for many years before production moved to the Assens factory in Denmark. The tin contains short, bulky ribbon-cut Virginia leaves in various colors; its appearance recalls a ready-rubbed texture. The blend carries a serious sauce: a complex topping combining light spicy fruit aroma, tart notes and coumarin. It catches easily and sustains its burn. It's strong in nicotine and intense in taste; it's heavy for those seeking light smokes. With aging, the sauce's sharpness fades and the aroma concentrates. It's a long-lived classic built for smokers seeking strong Virginia blends together with a pronounced sauce.
dunhill-royal-yacht.o: A sweet scent of spicy fruit and coumarin lingers, together with a tart tobacco note.

just-for-him-privateer.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Just For Him's Privateer blend.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-latakia.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Latakia blend.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-flake-u-s.z: The "U/S" in the name stands for "unscented," meaning untopped. Brown Flake U/S is a traditional flake blend produced by combining various Virginia leaves with Malawi Burley and a measured amount of African dark fire-cured leaf, then stoving and pressing the mix. No heavy sauce or top dressing is applied; only a very fine Lakeland trace from the production line remains. In the smoke, the dark sweetness of the stoved Virginia and Burley's dry, nutty, earthy taste run together; the fire-cured leaf adds a light smokiness in the background. It is a medium-bodied, cool-burning blend with a medium nicotine load. This is a good record for smokers seeking an untopped pressed tobacco who want to stay away from the floral side of the Lakeland style.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-flake-u-s.o: A bread-like, earthy tobacco aroma is accompanied by a very light floral trace.

bennington-tobacconist-no-24-baffra.z: No. 24 Baffra is one of the longest-lived among Bennington's numbered shop blends kept since 1965. At its base, Kentucky white Burley is hand-combined with a darker, cube-cut Georgia Burley; a small amount of Cyprus Latakia and St. James Perique is sprinkled in, and finally one hundred percent Old Belt Virginia is added. The Burley-heavy structure gives the blend a dry, nutty, earthy base; Latakia and Perique stay only at the edges, not dominant enough to turn the mixture into an English type. This opens a middle ground for smokers accustomed to both Latakia mixtures and aromatics. The presence of cube-cut Burley slows the burn, allowing for long smokes.
bennington-tobacconist-no-24-baffra.o: Dry walnut and roasted-grain notes are joined by a thin line of woodsmoke.

hu-tobacco-port-latakia.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the Port Latakia blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

mccranies-st-albans-best.z: St. Alban's is one of the shop blends from McCranie's Pipe Shop in Charlotte, North Carolina. According to the store's own description, the blend's core is mountain latakia, joined by golden Virginia, white Burley, and toasted Cavendish. Its latakia-forward construction places the blend in the classic English mixtures family, while the Cavendish and Virginia share puts a measured sweetness underneath the smoky taste. The burley leaf carries the blend's body and nicotine load to a medium level, making it a fitting option for smokers who like latakia but don't want an entirely dry, sharp mixture. McCranie's is a shop that has been operating since 1979, preparing its bulk blends at its own counter; this blend too is distributed mainly through the shop.
mccranies-st-albans-best.o: Leaves an aroma dominated by wood smoke and soot, with a lightly sweet toasted-leaf scent underneath.

dan-tobacco-da-vinci.z: Da Vinci is a ribbon-cut aromatic blend in which golden Virginia and soft black Cavendish are flavored with Tuscan red wine. It is produced at Dan Tobacco's facility in the German town of Lauenburg. The casing recipe is presented alongside the Renaissance theme that gives the blend its name. Up front there's a soft vanilla sweetness, and behind it a tannic, lightly sour trace of the wine; both are kept restrained enough not to mask the leaf's own flavor. Nicotine sits between mild and medium, burning cool and even. Suited to smokers looking for a moderately flavored aromatic without a heavy sauce.
dan-tobacco-da-vinci.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla scent alongside a lightly sour, fruity note reminiscent of a wine barrel.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-boswells-best.z: Boswell's Best is J. M. Boswell's personal blend, prepared in 1975 and bearing the brand's name. Per the manufacturer's breakdown, vanilla-flavored black cavendish is added to complement a base built from cavendish and ribbon-cut virginia. The casing is measured; virginia's sweetness and cavendish's softness come forward, with nicotine level staying low. The manufacturer describes the blend as suited to all-day smoking. Suitable for smokers seeking a lightly flavored, balanced American-style aromatic, including those new to the pipe.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-boswells-best.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-pastry aroma.

ilsted-own-mixture-dark-fired-plug.z: Dark Fired Plug is the fullest-bodied member of the Ilsted line. It's built from fire-cured Kentucky along with leaves of Malawian and Indian origin; the blend is pressed into a block and sold as a plug, a cut that's rarely encountered today. The plug needs to be sliced and rubbed out before smoking, but in return gives a slow, cool burn. Smokiness, wood smoke, and earthy taste lead, with sweetness staying in the background. Given its full nicotine strength, it's aimed at experienced smokers. It appears to have been out of stock at retailers for a long time.
ilsted-own-mixture-dark-fired-plug.o: The wood smoke and smokiness of fire-cured leaf are pronounced.

sutliff-tobacco-company-sps-701-virginia.z: SPS-701 Virginia Longcut is a straight Virginia product in Sutliff's bulk line, cut as long ribbon. According to the maker's description, it is prepared from pressed Virginia leaf, with a light casing applied that sweetens and darkens the tobacco; it carries no flavoring layer. The taste is earthy and moderately sweet, softer than straight Virginias generally and with less tendency toward tongue bite. Its strength stays on the low side. It is positioned primarily as a component used for a blend's base or to add natural sweetness to another mixture; those looking for a plain, soft Virginia can also smoke it on its own.
sutliff-tobacco-company-sps-701-virginia.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay and lightly caramelized sugar.

cornell-diehl-poplar-camp.z: Poplar Camp is a Virginia-Perique mixture in which Cornell & Diehl keeps the Perique proportion high. Per the maker's listing, Perique at close to twenty percent and a small amount of unflavored black Cavendish are added to Yorktown Virginia. This proportion makes Perique's plum-and-pepper-evoking spice the mixture's main line. Black Cavendish softens the sharpness and adds richness to the body, while Virginia builds the sweet base. Nicotine sits in the upper band and calls for a slow pace. Prepared for smokers wanting Perique in a heavy rather than measured dose, accustomed to the VaPer line.
cornell-diehl-poplar-camp.o: Leaves a sharp, sweetish tobacco scent reminiscent of ripe plum and black pepper.

hu-tobacco-dark-moor.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Dark Moor, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

rattray-hal-o-the-wynd.z: Hal O' the Wynd is a blend presented as broken flake, built on a Virginia-heavy base with a small amount of Kentucky and Perique added. It arrives moist from the tin; packed without airing it burns unevenly and wets the pipe, while used near dry the flavor line settles into place. On the first light, a sharp, lightly tart taste comes forward; as the smoke progresses this sharpness gives way to Virginia's plain sweetness, and intensity increases. The Kentucky and Perique proportion is kept low, so the blend largely carries a pure Virginia character. Nicotine is high; this makes it demanding for pipe newcomers but a straightforward choice for those looking for a filling Virginia flake.
rattray-hal-o-the-wynd.o: Leaves a dark, tart, woody tobacco aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-mans-best-friend.z: Man's Best Friend Blend is one of the bulk blends from the Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

mostex-stanislaw-water-mixture.z: Since neither the manufacturer's own description nor two independent reliable sources could be found for the Mostex blend called Stanislaw Water Mixture, its composition, cut, and character could not be documented here.

hu-tobacco-indaba.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Indaba, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

vantas-tabak-sir-william-virginia-flake.z: Sir William Virginia Flake is a flake product from Vantas Tabak pressed and sliced from golden Virginia leaf. Virginia forms the backbone of the blend; a measured pinch of Louisiana Perique is added on top, giving the structure a peppery, dried-fruit twist. As no flavoring is used, the taste comes from the tobacco's own natural sugars and fermentation; the smoke stays light and straightforward.
vantas-tabak-sir-william-virginia-flake.o: Leaves a subtle tobacco aroma reminiscent of dry hay and faintly tangy fruit.

hu-tobacco-tillerman.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the Tillerman blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

cup-o-joes-anniversary-blend-no-24-balka.z: Anniversary Blend No. 24 Balkan Kake is the anniversary blend Cup O' Joes prepared for its twenty-fourth year. Cyprus Latakia, Oriental leaf, and fermented Virginias are pressed into a crumbly kake (krumble kake) that breaks apart easily by hand into ribbon form. Its appearance is mottled, carrying brown, dark brown, black, and a small amount of light tones. In character, Latakia leads: it sets a smoky, woody, earthy, faintly leathery base. The Virginias add a tangy dark fruit, bread, sugar, and citrus tone, while the Orientals contribute dry spice and herbal notes. With nicotine and body staying at a medium level, it's a build usable both by those new to Balkan blends and experienced smokers wanting an all-day smoke.
cup-o-joes-anniversary-blend-no-24-balka.o: Leaves a dry-leaf smoke reminiscent of wood fire and smokiness.

john-aylesbury-limited-edition-2023.z: The 2023 entry in John Aylesbury's annual limited-run Limited Edition series; since the maker's current catalog only lists later years' editions, no verifiable source could be found on this release's composition.

lane-limited-captain-black-platinum.z: Captain Black Platinum is the light-colored, lighter-side member of the series. A measured cavendish sweetness and a faint vanilla note accompany a Virginia-and-burley-forward body; the casing stays more in the background than the series' fruity members. It's ribbon cut, with regulated moisture and low nicotine. It's a widely available everyday tobacco sold in pouches. Suited to smokers who find heavily essenced blends too much but aren't ready to move to fully unflavored tobacco, and to newcomers to pipes.
lane-limited-captain-black-platinum.o: Leaves a light vanilla and sweet-hay room note.

g-l-pease-meridian.z: Meridian is a balanced mixture within the Old London Series. Red and orange Virginias, small-leaved Oriental tobaccos, and a generous but not overwhelming measure of Cyprus latakia are brought together; the blend is pressed and sliced, then rubbed into ribbon form for boxing. The smoke is medium-bodied and leans savoury rather than sweet; latakia smoke layers with the Oriental leaf's spice and Virginia's sweetness. It is a record aimed at smokers seeking the classic structure with a latakia proportion that doesn't go to excess.
g-l-pease-meridian.o: Leaves an aroma of smoky wood and incense.

chief-catoonah-tobacconist-joes-morning-.z: The entry has been left incomplete as no reliable source could be found for Chief Catoonah Tobacconist's Joe's Morning Pipe blend.

richs-boars-head.z: Boar's Head is one of Rich's Cigar Store's English-style house blends. It is built on red Carolina leaf and Latakia and flavored with golden Virginia, creating a profile that shifts between sweet and tart, carried along by smoke. An oily texture from the Oriental leaf and a yeast-bread association are reported. It is medium-bodied, and its cut is said to stand apart from the shop's other blends with a coarser leaf appearance. It suits fans of classic English mixtures who steer clear of full-bodied Latakia bombs. Its current status is unclear since it does not appear on the shop's current list.
richs-boars-head.o: Leaves an aroma where soot, tangy bread yeast, and sweet leaf mix together.

hu-tobacco-the-untouchables-special-mixt.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for The Untouchables Special Mixture blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-black-arr.z: Black Arrow, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an aromatic mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

mac-baren-three-nuns.z: Three Nuns is a Scottish classic released by J & F Bell in Glasgow over a century ago. Production rights transferred to Mac Baren in 2013. The blend is a rope in which a select Virginia leaf is used as the wrap; its core holds dark-fire-cured Kentucky, and after resting, the rope is cut into coins. Burley sets the balance in the Virginia-dominant structure. An important historical detail is that the original formula contained Perique, while today's release uses dark-fire-cured Kentucky in its place; this change shifts the taste's spicy-fruity side toward a smoky tone. The coins burn slowly, with a fine soot layer riding atop Virginia's bready, herbal sweetness. Suited to patient smokers interested in classic English and Scottish cuts.
mac-baren-three-nuns.o: Leaves a fine wood-smoke aroma behind a dry-hay sweetness.

campbells-smoke-shop-chateau.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Chateau under the Campbell's Smoke Shop brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

exclusiv-no-1-royal.z: No sufficient information confirming the composition of Exclusiv No. 1 (Royal) could be found in producer or retailer sources.
exclusiv-no-1-royal.o: Records do not contain enough information for a description.

rattray-stirling-flake.z: Stirling Flake is a full-bodied blend where Burley, Virginia, and fire-cured Kentucky leaf are pressed tightly and sliced. The slices are prepared to crumble easily, which shortens flake preparation. The blend contains neither Latakia nor Perique; its smoky character comes entirely from the Kentucky. Burley builds a nutty, dry ground, Virginia adds a limited sweetness, and Kentucky pulls up both body and nicotine. It suits experienced smokers looking for an unflavored, strong, filling pressed tobacco; it may feel heavy for those unaccustomed to nicotine.
rattray-stirling-flake.o: Leaves a dry, smoky tobacco aroma roasted over wood fire.

timm-timms-own-blend-no-66.z: The Th. Timm's Own Blend series consists of blends the Timm pipe shops, widespread in northern Germany and especially Hamburg, have Dan Tobacco prepare under their own name. Blend No. 66 is a black-Cavendish-based aromatic; it is joined by Virginia and Burley, cased with creamy vanilla and honey flavoring. Nicotine is moderate, and the taste is sweet and round. Sold in 100-gram tins, this blend is aimed at those seeking the sweet line of classic German aromatics in an everyday tobacco.
timm-timms-own-blend-no-66.o: Leaves a creamy vanilla and honey aroma.

house-of-windsor-chocolate-cream-t417.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for House of Windsor's Chocolate Cream T417 blend, so its content and character could not be recorded.

brebbia-english-mixture-no-80.z: English Mixture No. 80, in Italian manufacturer Brebbia's numbered blend series, is an English mixture built from small-leaf Syrian Latakia, matured spicy burley and bright Virginia leaf. Its cut is ribbon; the blend's identity is set largely by Latakia, burley carries the body and medium strength, while Virginia stays in the background. Per records it carries a very light anise touch. With Syrian Latakia's withdrawal from the market, this mixture was dropped from the catalog and replaced by Serenata (Mixture No. 28). It was aimed at smokers seeking a resinous, smoky Latakia profile and enjoying a traditional English mix with almost no perceptible flavor casing.
brebbia-english-mixture-no-80.o: Syrian Latakia's resinous, smoky, heavy aroma lingers in the room for a long time.

von-eicken-black-gold-mixture.z: Black & Gold Mixture is one of Von Eicken's now-discontinued Latakia mixtures. The black, gold and brown-toned leaf is cut extremely fine, almost fine enough to resemble cigarette tobacco. On the smoke, Cyprus Latakia lays down a woody, earthy, lightly sweet layer of smoke, set against grassy, citrusy light Virginia. Neither leaf group overtakes the other. Nicotine is medium, and due to the fine cut the bowl tends to burn quickly. A record that appeals to fans of classic English mixtures and today can only be found in old stock.
von-eicken-black-gold-mixture.o: Leaves a smoky, burnt-wood aroma with a faint grassy tobacco undertone.

mcclelland-best-of-show.z: Best of Show is a 50-gram tinned aromatic in McClelland's Premium Aromatic line. The maker described it as a full, sweet, mild mixture built from select classes of American leaf. A nougat-based casing builds the aromatic character, joined by caramel-leaning tones. It's ribbon cut, burns even and cool, and a full bowl lasts long. Being light on nicotine, it falls within the territory of those who prefer sweet-scented, flavored blends. Among the later-period products in the McClelland line, discontinued when the firm closed.
mcclelland-best-of-show.o: Leaves a sweet, sugary aroma leaning toward nougat and caramel.

cornell-diehl-manhattan-afternoon.z: Manhattan Afternoon is a single-varietal blend in which naturally sweet golden Virginia leaf is lightly honey-flavored and pressed into sliced flake. The slices are medium brown, easy to prepare, and can be packed rubbed out or folded. On the smoke, Virginia's citrus and grassy sweetness leads; the honey theme is applied at a level that doesn't overshadow the leaf. It burns cool and even, with a low tendency to bite the tongue, and nicotine is light. Suited to those looking for a plain, lightly flavored Virginia flake, and to those new to the Virginia type.
cornell-diehl-manhattan-afternoon.o: Leaves a sweet scent of dry hay and honeyed bread.

schurch-snowflake-132.z: One of the Swiss Schürch house's Virginia-forward blends; no sufficient source detailing its content and character could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-special.z: A blend released as part of Ken Byron Ventures' small-batch production; no independent, verifiable source could be found on it.

w-o-larsen-belle-epoque-carte-noire.z: No independent source sufficient to complete a record could be found regarding W.O. Larsen's Belle Epoque - Carte Noire blend, so this entry remains incomplete.

rattray-union-jack.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of the Rattray blend called Union Jack.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-mild-english.z: Mild English is a mixture built by adding a small amount of Latakia to burley, golden Virginia and cavendish. Since the Latakia proportion is kept low, the blend carries classic English mixtures' smoky identity while staying away from their weight; per the manufacturer's description, it burns cool and slowly. The sweetness cavendish brings forms a bridge between smoky Latakia and burley's nutty taste. This structure makes it an entry point for smokers newly moving into English-style blends or not wanting a heavy Latakia dose during the day. It is listed among Boswell's products under the English-blends heading.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-mild-english.o: A lightly woody, smoky aroma is accompanied by a sweetish undertone.

sutliff-tobacco-company-golden-age.z: Golden Age is a Virginia-perique blend from Sutliff's Private Stock line. Its coarse-ribbon cut shows beige, chocolate-brown, and black tones together. The tin note carries perique's sharp, liqueur-like trace along with earth and light fruit notes. On the palate, perique leans more toward plum and raisin than pepper, asserting itself throughout the bowl without overwhelming Virginia's hay-like sweetness. Nicotine strength is light, and the blend doesn't turn harsh as it heats up. A record for those seeking the classic Virginia-perique structure found in the Dunhill Elizabethan line.
sutliff-tobacco-company-golden-age.o: Leaves a fruity scent of dry hay sweetness along with plum and raisin.

friedman-pease-winters-tale.z: Winter's Tale is among the limited-production final blends of Friedman & Pease, the brand Greg Pease and Irwin Friedman founded in 1998. Records indicate the blend's backbone is dark Virginia processed at the company's own facility, with latakia and some perique added. The stoved Virginia gives a deep sweetness reminiscent of bread and molasses, while the latakia carries woody smoke and the perique carries plummy spice. After the company closed, Pease agreed not to use the formulas and names he had developed, so the blend was never produced again, and its limited run has made it a collector's item.
friedman-pease-winters-tale.o: Leaves an aroma of sweet woodsmoke and dark dried fruit.

samuel-gawith-beginners-luck.z: No reliable source could be found for Samuel Gawith's aromatic blend called Beginner's Luck.

john-patton-honeymoon.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Patton's Honeymoon pipe tobacco.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-skandinav.z: Considered one of the more intensely flavored members of the Skandinavik series, a blend hard to find on the market today; no sufficient source documenting its composition could be found.

teds-pipe-shoppe-county-cork.z: One of the house blends prepared at Ted's Pipe Shoppe in Tulsa, Oklahoma; though records show it among the more than forty house blends of the business founded in 1961, no independent source describing the blend's content and character could be found.

cornell-diehl-ghost-of-christmas-present.z: Ghost of Christmas Present is the straight Virginia blend in Cornell & Diehl's 2022 Wintertime Reserve series. It consists of red and bright Virginia leaves, topped with a light holiday-themed casing (sugar flavoring), making it not entirely unflavored but rather a lightly sweetened Virginia. Both the tin note and the smoke lead with sugar-and-biscuit sweetness, citrusy tang, and fresh-bread notes. It is a medium-bodied blend with generous smoke output and measured nicotine. It suits smokers seeking Virginia's natural sweetness while avoiding heavy aromatics. Being a seasonal, limited series, it is not in continuous production.
cornell-diehl-ghost-of-christmas-present.o: Leaves a fresh-baked bread and sugary pastry aroma.

tabakhaus-buttner-nr-801.z: One of the numbered house blends from Tabakhaus Büttner in Frankfurt; no accessible source describing its content and character could be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-schippers.z: According to records, a Dutch-origin blend produced in Rotterdam that has long been unavailable in the United States; no sufficient source documenting its current content could be found.

per-g-jensen-kings-watch.z: For Per G. Jensen's blend called King's Watch, no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

mccranies-my-reserve-ii.z: My Reserve II is one of McCranie's Virginia-and-Latakia-based bulk blends; no sufficient sources could be found on its ratios or character.

cigar-connoisseur-circus-spun.z: Circus Spun is one of the house blends the England-based Cigar Connoisseur tobacco shop sells in bulk. As its name suggests, it is prepared using the spun method: small oval medallions with Virginia as the outer wrapper and perique leaf at the core. The medallions come out of the tin somewhat moist, so airing time directly determines the smoke; moist, perique comes through more dominant and the burn runs hot, while as it dries, Virginia's sweetness moves to the front. When packing, stacking the medallions vertically keeps the Virginia wrapper on top. On the smoke, pure Virginia sweetness and perique's black-pepper sharpness alternate in the lead; sugar and spice balance each other. It is sensitive to burn speed, and smoked quickly it can turn into a harsh burn on the tongue and palate. It therefore suits smokers accustomed to slow, controlled smoking who know the perique-Virginia character; it isn't a structure that would be a newcomer's first choice.
cigar-connoisseur-circus-spun.o: Leaves a tangy tobacco and peppery dryness aroma in the room.

pipesandcigars-com-bluegill-lake.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of the pipesandcigars.com blend called Bluegill Lake.

peter-heinrichs-reserve-crue-no-4.z: This is one of the pipe tobaccos of the Cologne-based house Peter Heinrichs; the profile is left incomplete, as no reliable sources describing the blend's content and character could be found.

von-eicken-bayside-mixed-blend.z: There is not enough independent documentation on Von Eicken's Bayside Mixed Blend to fill out the record, so it has been left incomplete.

american-tobacco-co-buckingham-cut-plug.z: Buckingham Bright Cut Plug is a cake-cut tobacco sold in pocket tins in the first half of the twentieth century, first by John J. Bagley & Co. and later by the American Tobacco Company; no detailed source describing the blend's leaf composition and flavor character could be found.

smokers-pride-classic-blend.z: Smoker's Pride Classic Blend is a blend representing the inexpensive, high-volume wing of large-scale American pipe tobacco production. Nutty, earthy burley and sweet golden Virginia leaves are brought together in ribbon cut; only a very light top flavoring is applied, so the leading taste in the mouth is the unprocessed leaf itself. Being sold in 340-gram (12 oz) resealable bags indicates the blend is designed for everyday, ongoing use. It sits between light and medium for nicotine and fullness; it doesn't tire the tongue and suits long sessions. It occupies a middle ground for smokers who don't want the syrupy sweetness of aromatic blends but also don't want to go into the intensity of a fully unflavored Virginia or burley. A typical American bulk tobacco used as a break-in tobacco for those new to the pipe and as an everyday bowl-filler for experienced smokers.
smokers-pride-classic-blend.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, dry-hay and nutty tobacco scent.

uhles-crushed-white-burley.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend called Crushed White Burley has been found.
uhles-crushed-white-burley.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-virginia-cavendi.z: Dark Virginia Cavendish, listed as DVC for short in the brand's catalog, is obtained by darkening light hot-air-cured Virginia leaf through an extended Cavendish process using ample steam. This process removes a significant portion of the leaf's harsher elements and leaves a mild, cool-burning base. In the Liquorice version, a licorice-root-based flavoring is added to this base. It's ribbon cut, easy to pack and light. Nicotine is light; the taste is built between the mild Virginia sweetness and licorice's dark, sweetish note. Suited to those wanting a mild, sweet everyday tobacco, and to smokers in their early years with the pipe.
gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-virginia-cavendi.o: Leaves a sweet licorice-root and candied-tobacco aroma.

cornell-diehl-yaller-dawg.z: An English blend not in Cornell & Diehl's current catalogue, said to contain Syrian Latakia; no independent source confirming its composition was found.

alfie-turmeaus-1817-blend.z: Turmeaus is a tobacconist house founded in Liverpool in 1817; the name 1817 given to the blend also references this founding year. Selected Virginia leaves form the mixture's body, with smoky Latakia and a smaller proportion of Turkish-origin Oriental added. This produces a measured interpretation of the classic English mixture scheme: Virginia sweetness sets the base, Latakia smoke provides the frame, and the Oriental gives a spicy, tangy top note. Even before lighting, the smoke scent is noticeable on opening; the smoke is mild, with nicotine at light-to-medium, making it suitable for those looking for a Latakia mixture they can smoke all day. Since the Latakia ratio isn't as high as in heavy Balkan-style blends, it can also serve as an entry point for smokers new to English mixtures. It's presented in a 50-gram tin.
alfie-turmeaus-1817-blend.o: Leaves a smoky room note reminiscent of a mix of soot, cedar wood, and dry hay.

bufflehead-common-teal.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Common Teal under the Bufflehead brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

low-country-pipe-cigar-guendalose.z: One of the house blends of South Carolina-based Low Country Pipe & Cigar; described as cigar-leaf based, but not enough sources could be found to describe its character.

burlington-on-whyte-tobacconist-lapis-la.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named Lapis Lazuli under the Burlington on Whyte Tobacconist brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

affordable-pipes-blue-grass-melody.z: A bulk blend noted as Burley-forward, for which no adequate independent source could be found.
affordable-pipes-blue-grass-melody.o: No adequate description of its scent could be found in records.

mcclelland-no-620-mocha-black.z: No. 620 Mocha Black is a blend in McClelland's numbered bulk aromatic series, built entirely on black Cavendish. The cut is ribbon, and the leaf looks dark, nearly coal-black. On opening the pouch, an intense bakery aroma leaning toward coffee, cocoa, and chocolate comes through; the tobacco's own smell stays behind this topping. Though moisture appears high straight from the pack, it lights easily and resists going out in the pipe. The taste follows the nose: a smoke running along coffee, cocoa, and warm chocolate lines, with the leaf character kept in the background. Structured for smokers seeking aromatics with a pronounced flavoring. Production ended when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-no-620-mocha-black.o: Leaves a bakery aroma reminiscent of coffee, cocoa, and warm chocolate.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-captain-earles-s.z: Stimulus Package is one of the highest-Latakia members of the Captain Earle's line. The mixture, made up of Latakia, Oriental leaves, and Virginias, is pressed into a crumble cake; it contains no Cavendish. Sources describe it as a version of Nightwatch with increased Latakia and Cavendish removed. This structure makes the smoke drier, smokier, and fuller; the Virginia's sugar stays only in the background. It falls into the full-bodied English mixture category, and its nicotine side is also considered pronounced. It suits experienced smokers looking for Latakia as the main taste; it will be heavy for those accustomed to light blends. It carries no flavoring.
hermit-tobacco-works-co-captain-earles-s.o: Heavy campfire and tar-and-smoke aroma spreads through the room, leaving a dry-wood tone behind.

good-stuff-red-robust.z: Good Stuff Red is the full-bodied variant of the series made in the US by Privateer Tobacco. US-grown sun-cured Burley leaf forms the blend's body, while sweet Virginias are added as a balancer. It is sold very finely shredded, in resealable six-ounce and one-pound bags. The taste is Burley-forward: it carries a dry, nutty, earthy character, with the Virginia's sweetness staying in the background. Nicotine is higher than the series' other variants.
