The fine cut calls for loose packing and slow drawing. Suited to smokers accustomed to Burley character who want a strong, plain, and economical everyday tobacco.
good-stuff-red-robust.o: Leaves a lightly sharp aroma reminiscent of dry nuts and earth.

a-c-petersen-the-chiefs-own-curly-cut-no.z: A numbered curly-cut blend belonging to A & C Petersen's "The Chief's Own" line; no adequate source documenting its content could be found.

faders-mo-goodrick-heavy.z: Not enough independent sourcing documenting the composition and character of Mo' Goodrick Heavy, one of the house blends of the Baltimore-based Fader's tobacconist, could be found.

dunhill-ready-rubbed.z: Ready Rubbed is a blend where aged flue-cured Virginia leaves are combined with oriental tobaccos. A light cavendish process and a fine fruity sauce are applied to the leaves; after the mixture is steamed and pressed, it's cut and, true to its name, rubbed out into ribbon. This lets the smoker pack it directly with no extra preparation. Though classed as aromatic, the sauce level is low; the tobacco's own taste leads in the smoke. Its strength is light and its flavor intensity is medium. It suits those who want the texture of pressed tobaccos without wanting to deal with crumbling flake. The blend was discontinued for a time, was one of the Dunhill blends reintroduced in 2015, and production under this name ended with the brand's exit from pipe tobacco.
dunhill-ready-rubbed.o: Leaves a dry tobacco scent carrying a light fruity sweetness.

sutliff-tobacco-company-maple-walnut-z88.z: Z88 Maple Walnut is a ribbon-cut aromatic Sutliff builds by adding burley and Virginia leaf to a black cavendish base. The topping combines maple syrup sweetness with walnut's oily, nutty tone; burley forms an earthy base beneath that sweetness. Nicotine density is low and the burn is cool. Suited to smokers seeking a pronounced sweet-flavored tobacco that leaves a strong scent in the room, and to those new to the aromatic category; it falls outside the interest of those seeking unflavored tobacco taste.
sutliff-tobacco-company-maple-walnut-z88.o: Leaves a scent of maple syrup and roasted walnut.

frederick-tranter-st-johns-mixture.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Frederick Tranter's St. John's Mixture blend; records place it in the English-mixture class.

pipesandcigars-com-acadian-english.z: Acadian English belongs among pipesandcigars.com's own RO Series blends, built on the dark Virginia base of the same line's Acadian Gold. The orange-toned Virginia leaf's bready sweetness is balanced by Latakia's smoky layer and Cavendish's rounding texture; the blend thus settles into a more measured, English-leaning frame than the straight Virginia version. Its ribbon-cut structure makes lighting and even burning easy. It offers a suitable frame for those looking for a medium-bodied English blend that uses smoky leaf as spice rather than the main taste, as well as those wanting to move from Virginia-heavy to Latakia blends. Reports indicate the blend's flavor profile changes during storage, thanks to a Virginia base the maker states is suited to aging.
pipesandcigars-com-acadian-english.o: Leaves a smoky, resinous aroma reminiscent of wood fire.

blatter-blatter-mild-english-anglais-leg.z: A light English-style mix among the house blends of the Blatter & Blatter shop in Montreal; no reliable source on its composition or character could be found.

clan-shaw-yorkshire.z: No reliable, independent sourcing could be found regarding Clan Shaw Yorkshire, so a detailed profile could not be compiled.

planta-marc-de-champagne.z: Marc de Champagne is a light-colored aromatic built by combining golden Virginia with fully ripened black Cavendish in set proportions. It takes its name from marc, distilled from grape pomace in the Champagne region; its casing uses that spirit's note together with a creamy truffle association. Its smoke is creamy and mellow, packing and lighting cause no trouble, and it burns evenly. Nicotine is low. It suits smokers looking for sweet but not syrupy aromatics with an alcoholic-pastry association.
planta-marc-de-champagne.o: Leaves a creamy cocoa and light grape-spirit aroma.

pfeifen-huber-kurt-eisner.z: Kurt Eisner is Pfeifen Huber's unflavored Virginia-Burley blend, known by a name referencing Bavarian history, reportedly prepared by blender Hans Wiedemann. The tobacco is presented ready-rubbed, obtained by hand-rubbing a pressed flake; beyond its topping it carries no added flavoring. It has no wide distribution outside the Munich shop and the brand's own sales channel. On the palate a sweetness recalling bread dough and milk-bitter chocolate comes forward, alongside a grassy nuttiness and a dried-fruit background. The body sits between light and medium while the flavor is intense and layered; its creamy texture keeps spice and sweetness in balance. It can be smoked straight from the tin, though a brief airing improves the burn. It suits smokers seeking an unflavored, all-day natural tobacco and those wanting to get to know Burley character.
pfeifen-huber-kurt-eisner.o: Leaves a plain tobacco aroma leaning toward fresh bread and cocoa.

cao-eileens-dream.z: CAO Eileen's Dream is a multilayered aromatic built on a virginia and black cavendish base. The casing is built on a cream base enriched with Irish whiskey and coconut milk, combined with a sweet composition of hazelnut paste, white chocolate, almond, cocoa and vanilla extracts. The cut is ribbon; the tobacco comes moist. The blend has a low-nicotine structure that does not turn harsh on the tongue; a cake-like sweet casing rather than the leaf character leads the flavor. Suitable for smokers seeking a heavily flavored, sweet-profile blend and for fans of this creamy branch of aromatics. It is manufactured in the US as part of the CAO aromatic line.
cao-eileens-dream.o: Leaves a creamy white chocolate, hazelnut and coconut aroma with a light whiskey note.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-midnight-lace.z: There is not enough independent sourcing available for this Hermit Tobacco Works Co. blend.

sutliff-tobacco-company-christmas-spice.z: Christmas Spice is a spice-flavored aromatic listed in the Sutliff catalog; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-christmas-spice.o: Records did not provide sufficient information for a description.

samuel-gawith-pure-izmir-turkish-leaf.z: Pure Izmir Turkish Leaf is, as the name suggests, a single-leaf product: Izmir Oriental tobacco grown in the Aegean region, presented in a coarse ribbon cut. Samuel Gawith offers this leaf not as a blend but as raw material; it contains no virginia, latakia, or casing. Its character carries the Oriental leaf's typical traits: dry hay, spice, and a lightly sour citrus tone, low nicotine, a cool burn. Smoked alone it stays thin and light-bodied; its main function is to supply the Oriental component for those building their own blends. It is the type used by those wanting to add spice and depth to an English or Balkan-type mixture.
samuel-gawith-pure-izmir-turkish-leaf.o: Leaves a sharpish scent of dry hay, sour citrus, and cigarette-tobacco-like notes.

havana-house-windsor-breeze.z: One of the Virginia-forward house blends from the Havana House tobacconist; there is not enough sourcing on its composition and character.
havana-house-windsor-breeze.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

ashton-old-london-pebble-cut.z: Ashton Old London Pebble Cut is an unflavored, Virginia-based flake blend. Alongside Virginia, it contains Cavendish, Perique, and Macedonian Oriental. The long flakes in the tin are brittle and high in moisture; if packed without airing, they're difficult to light. Records indicate this blend, remaining from Ashton's collaboration period with McClelland, is not currently in production. The smoke is long and generous. The flavor sits on a sweet-tangy base; the Perique adds a bitterness that isn't overly high in dose. The Cavendish share is felt in the blend. The Oriental listed in the contents is hard to distinguish in the tasting. It suits smokers accustomed to packing flakes, wanting to try unflavored Virginia blends with a sweet direction.
ashton-old-london-pebble-cut.o: Leaves a tangy, sharp tobacco room note that settles into the room.

dan-tobacco-patriot-flake.z: Patriot Flake is the straight-Virginia blend in Dan Tobacco's American history series. US- and India-origin Virginia varieties are fermented, pressed, and after aging sliced into flake. No other leaf type or flavoring enters the mixture. The pressure-aging gives an intense yet cool smoke; beneath the sweetness lies a light spicy undertone. Body sits medium. Being flake, it needs rubbing or folding before packing and calls for a slow draw. Suited to smokers looking for unflavored Virginia character and the aging potential of a pressed tobacco.
dan-tobacco-patriot-flake.o: Leaves a subtle scent reminiscent of dry hay and stale-bread sweetness.

straus-tobacco-coliseum.z: Coliseum is one of the counter blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; records indicate the shop was founded in 1880 and that most of its house blends were named after Cincinnati neighborhoods and landmark buildings. Since no independent source on the blend's composition and character could be found, this record is kept at listing level only.

cobblestone-hiking.z: Hiking is a flake-cut blend from Cobblestone's Outdoors series, built almost entirely on burley. The tin note carries the typical line of European-style burley blends: cocoa, raisin, and sweet bread. Burley character stays consistent throughout the smoke; the blend doesn't offer a many-layered development, resting instead on the taste of a single leaf family. The Outdoors and Chess series are blended and produced for the Cobblestone name in Germany by Kohlhase & Kopp. It is aimed at smokers looking for European-style burley flakes and wanting a single-direction, settled taste.
cobblestone-hiking.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of cocoa, raisin, and sweet bun dough.

mac-baren-capstan-gold-navy-cut.z: Capstan Gold Navy Cut is an unflavored Virginia flake obtained by pressing light-colored Virginia leaves gathered from three continents into a cake and slicing them. The Capstan name comes from an old brand in the English pipe tobacco tradition; the product is produced today by Mac Baren in Denmark. Since moisture in the tin can run high, airing the slices for a while eases the smoke. Filled without breaking the flake up too much, it gives a long, cool and sweet smoke; nicotine dosage isn't high, making it suited to all-day smoking and to those seeking pure Virginia taste.
mac-baren-capstan-gold-navy-cut.o: Leaves a lightly fruity room note reminiscent of sweet hay and bread crust.

lane-limited-a-few-too-many.z: A Few Too Many, registered under Lane Limited, is referred to as an aromatic blend; since no independent source could be found to confirm its composition and character, the record is left incomplete.

mars-cigars-pipes-sangria-201.z: Remembered as a sangria-themed aromatic house blend from the retailer Mars Cigars & Pipes; since no source documenting its contents could be found, the profile is left incomplete.
mars-cigars-pipes-sangria-201.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

peterson-holiday-season-2013.z: Holiday Season is Peterson's limited-edition, Christmas-themed aromatic tin series released each year; the 2013 edition was presented in a 100 gram tin. A mixture of black Cavendish, Burley, and Virginia is flavored with honey, plum, and cinnamon. Peterson is an Irish brand, but the blending and production of these special tins is outsourced; records indicate they were made by Kohlhase, Kopp & Co. to a recipe specified by Peterson. The cut is described as ribbon. Because the recipe changes each year, every edition of the series counts as a distinct blend; the 2013 tin was likewise prepared for its release year and never reprinted. It is a notable record for smokers seeking flavored, sweet-profile tins and for those who collect the annual limited editions.
peterson-holiday-season-2013.o: Leaves a honeyed plum and cinnamon aroma.

pipesandcigars-com-apple-fritter.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of the pipesandcigars.com blend called Apple Fritter.

sutliff-tobacco-company-voodoo-queen-523.z: A blend in Sutliff's numbered bulk line recorded as containing latakia; no accessible source confirming its composition could be found.

cornell-diehl-black-bourbon.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Cornell & Diehl blend Black Bourbon.

petersen-sorensen-kolibri-tropic-mixture.z: Kolibri Tropic Mixture is an aromatic mixture built on a black-Cavendish-forward body with Burley and Virginia added. Cognac is used as the top flavoring, giving the blend a dark, boozy sweetness. It is presented in 50 and 80 gram tins. Thanks to the Cavendish weight, nicotine strength stays low, making it suitable for smokers new to aromatic mixtures.
petersen-sorensen-kolibri-tropic-mixture.o: Leaves a boozy sweetness recalling cognac along with a dark fruit aroma.

iwan-ries-three-star-gold.z: This is a blend from the Three Star line prepared over the counter by the Chicago-based tobacconist Iwan Ries & Co.; no independent source detailing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
iwan-ries-three-star-gold.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-blend-7.z: One of Cornell & Diehl's older burley-heavy blends; it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog, and not enough sourcing could be found to document its composition.

tobacco-lane-tolkiens-wreath.z: One of the house blends from the tobacconist Tobacco Lane; no verifiable source on its composition and character has been found.
tobacco-lane-tolkiens-wreath.o: No source describing its aroma has been found.

cornell-diehl-cavendish-cut-burley.z: Cavendish Cut Burley is a ribbon-cut, unflavored blend pairing high-quality bright Virginia leaf with white burley. Virginia leaf carries a natural sugar-derived sweetness and a light citrus accent, while burley contributes nutty dryness and body. The pairing of these two leaves is one of the foundational structures of American pipe tobacco tradition; burley keeps the blend burning cool while Virginia adds sweetness to the taste. It suits those looking for a classic, unflavored, all-day Virginia-burley mixture, as well as anyone building a full-bodied base for homemade blends.
cornell-diehl-cavendish-cut-burley.o: Leaves a nutty, lightly sweet, dry-grass tobacco aroma.

newminster-no-702-light-burley.z: The Burley-forward numbered blend in the Newminster line; reportedly a light burley kept low in nicotine load, though sufficient independent sources confirming processing and casing details could not be found.

hu-tobacco-cochmondt.z: Cochmondt is one of the flavored Latakia blends in the Clans of Scotland line. Its base is medium-strength cube-cut Virginia, rounded out with black Cavendish and Latakia; in the flavoring, caramel and vanilla stand out, with tonka staying as a small accent in the background. The series's shared idea, a reference to Scottish confectionery, is built in this blend through caramel sweetness standing alongside Latakia's smoky saltiness. The cube cut provides a slow, cool burn; it's designed for smokers looking for sweet flavoring alongside a smoky base. Records indicate it's presented in 50-gram tins.
hu-tobacco-cochmondt.o: A smoky undertone mixes into the aroma of burnt sugar and vanilla candy.

straus-tobacco-johns-blend.z: John's Blend is one of the counter blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; records indicate the shop was founded in 1880 and that most of its house blends were named after Cincinnati neighborhoods and landmark buildings. Since no independent source on the blend's composition and character could be found, this record is kept at listing level only.

cornell-diehl-smooth-english.z: Smooth English is an English-type mixture Cornell & Diehl offers in bulk. Its composition includes Burley leaf, unflavored black Cavendish, and Latakia; having Burley take the carrying role instead of Virginia sets this blend apart from similar ones. Over the warm, nutty base Burley provides, Latakia adds a layer of leather and wood smoke; it carries no sharp or spicy edge, moving flat and balanced. It's described as a fitting option for morning smokes or for those newly moving into English-type blends. It serves as an intermediate step for smokers wanting to move from aromatics to Latakia blends.
cornell-diehl-smooth-english.o: Leaves a nutty scent reminiscent of leather and wood smoke.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-angry-cor.z: Angry Cornishman, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an English-type mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

hearth-home-larrys-blend.z: Larry's Blend is a full-bodied Balkan mixture built from Latakia, Oriental, and Virginia leaf. It is unflavored; sweetness comes from the Virginia, while a creamy, oily depth comes from the selected Oriental varieties. The Latakia ratio is kept higher than in the brand's Ten to Midnight blend, giving the smoke a thicker, smokier character. The blend's origin traces to shop customer Larry Loerzel asking for a fuller English-Balkan mixture; the blender responded by changing the Oriental selection and increasing the Latakia. It comes out of the tin at a moisture level ready to smoke directly. Suited to smokers accustomed to Latakia-heavy blends looking for an evening smoke.
hearth-home-larrys-blend.o: Leaves a buttery, dry-spice trace alongside heavy smoke and incense aroma.

john-aylesbury-london.z: John Aylesbury London is recorded as one of the brand's city-named blends; no verifiable source could be found on its composition and character.

e-a-carey-50th-anniversary.z: E. A. Carey is an American-origin house brand that has sold pipes and pipe tobacco since 1948; 50th Anniversary is a custom aromatic blend prepared for the firm's fiftieth year. Per the maker's page, the blend is built from golden African virginias, imported burley and black cavendish leaf, and produced in Denmark. So while the origin brand is American, the tobacco itself is processed and delivered Danish-style. In character it sits close to the brand's long-selling Classic Black Aromatic line: cavendish sweetness stands out, burley holds the body, and virginia gives a light sugar behind it. It's noted as light in nicotine. It suits newcomers to aromatic tobacco or those seeking a sweet blend that isn't heavy for all-day smoking.
e-a-carey-50th-anniversary.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly caramel-like cavendish scent.

ken-byron-ventures-plague-bringer-2020.z: A blend Ken Byron Ventures released as part of its small-batch production; no independent and verifiable source could be found about it.

g-l-pease-cumberland-original-mixtures.z: Cumberland is an untopped, ribbon-cut American blend that combines matured Virginia leaves with dark Kentucky and Perique. It belongs to G. L. Pease's Original Mixtures line and adds weight to the Virginia-Perique line with dark leaf. The flavour is intense and layered; Virginia's ripe sweetness, Kentucky's smoky fullness, and Perique's peppery sharpness can each be picked out separately throughout the smoke. Nicotine dose is considered high, so it is not a blend suited to an empty stomach or a fast smoke. It is easy to prepare and burns easily. It suits experienced smokers accustomed to dark, strong, untopped blends.
g-l-pease-cumberland-original-mixtures.o: An earthy, smoky aroma from the fire-cured leaf is accompanied by a dark, plum-like sweetness.

paul-olsen-2015-ltd-edition.z: A house blend the Copenhagen-based Danish tobacconist Poul Olsen released in limited numbers in 2015; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.

doctor-pipe-scottish-mixture.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Scottish Mixture, a pipe tobacco from Doctor Pipe.
doctor-pipe-scottish-mixture.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

davis-and-son-tobacconists-evening-rum.z: This is referred to as one of the rum-flavored house blends of Davis & Son Tobacconists; since it doesn't appear on the current list, its composition couldn't be verified.

king-street-coffee-tobacco-emporium-ol-t.z: Ol' Trapper is a ribbon-cut blend King Street Emporium prepares from golden Virginia leaves. Per the manufacturer's description, only a very light aromatic essence is added to the mix; its main character is defined by Virginia's own sugar and tangy fruity taste. Nicotine is low, taste sits on the plain side. A suitable intermediate step for smokers of unflavored Virginia or those moving from aromatics to Virginia. Smoked slowly, its tendency to bite the tongue lessens. Sold only in-shop, with stock changing regularly.
king-street-coffee-tobacco-emporium-ol-t.o: Leaves a lightly sweet room note reminiscent of dry hay and baked bread.

vauen-tab-170-jubilaum.z: TAB 170 is the limited jubilee blend Vauen released in 2018 for its 170th anniversary, presented that same year alongside three separate jubilee pipe models. The composition contains a high proportion of golden Virginia, joined by some cube cut, nutty Burley and full-bodied black Cavendish. The flavoring departs from the usual sweet aromatics: a herbal structure evoking rosemary, lavender and lemon is used. Nicotine stays at a medium level, and the room note leans herbal rather than sweet. Suited to those after a flavor direction outside fruit and vanilla.
vauen-tab-170-jubilaum.o: Leaves an herbal aroma evoking rosemary, lavender and lemon peel.

century-black-kathy.z: An aromatic blend within the Century line; no sufficient source could be found to determine its content and character.

pipesandcigars-com-paulina.z: No independent sources sufficient to complete a full profile of pipesandcigars.com's blend Paulina could be found.

jack-lee-blend-blackstrap.z: This is an aromatic-line blend from the now-closed American blender Jack Lee Blend, taking its name from dark molasses; no reliable source describing its content could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-rum-maple.z: Rum & Maple is among Sutliff Tobacco Company's classic American aromatics offered in bulk. Burley and Virginia are added to a black-cavendish-forward body, ribbon cut; the rum and maple syrup flavoring the name refers to is pronounced enough to keep the leaves' own taste in the background. Moisture is at the level customary for aromatics, so a brief airing after opening the pack makes for an easier burn.
sutliff-tobacco-company-rum-maple.o: Leaves a scent of syrupy maple sweetness alongside dark, toasted sugar and rum.

century-charleston-blockade.z: Charleston Blockade is the unflavored virginia record in the Century line. Per the seller's description it is blended solely from aged red virginia leaf and offered in what is called Krumble Kake form — pressed under heat but easily crumbled by hand. The name refers to the blockade imposed on Charleston harbor during the American Civil War. When red virginia is held under pressure its sugars concentrate, producing a bready, dark-fruited, sweet-leaning flavor. With no top flavoring applied, the taste comes entirely from the leaf itself, and it is a record that needs to be smoked slowly to avoid tongue bite. Suitable for smokers who want no flavor casing and are interested in pure virginia in pressed form.
century-charleston-blockade.o: Leaves a dry hay and cooked-fruit aroma leaning sweet.

pipa-cherry-cavendish.z: No sources documenting the content or maker of the Cherry Cavendish blend recorded under the Pipa name could be found.

casey-jones-last-ride.z: Last Ride is the fruity wing of the Casey Jones line. Black cavendish made from Green River burley forms the main body; natural burley and Virginia are added alongside it. A topping combining dark cherry and vanilla is applied on top, so fruit stands out in both flavor and aroma. The blend is built to burn cool and has a structure that does not turn harsh on the tongue. Nicotine is low, flavor intensity is in the medium range. Suitable for those seeking a classic American aromatic on the cherry-vanilla axis and wanting to start the day with a sweet blend.
casey-jones-last-ride.o: Leaves a dark cherry and vanilla room note.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-irlandez-bl.z: Irlandez Black Chocolate is the version of the Irlandez line's Black Cavendish- and Virginia-based body flavored with chocolate. The product is prepared at the Juiz de Fora facility and, like the other members of the line, distributed in flavor-sealing packs. It sits in the same lineup as the variant listed in catalogs under the name Chocolate Alpino. Thanks to the cavendish processing, the smoke is soft; the chocolate note leads while the Virginia forms a base with its light sweetness. Nicotine is low. It suits smokers looking for sweet, cocoa-leaning aromatics.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-irlandez-bl.o: Leaves a scent of milk chocolate and cocoa.

charatan-fc-1863-mixture.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the British pipe maker Charatan.

peretti-blend-no-102.z: This is one of the numbered blends L.J. Peretti lists in its Burley group and continues to produce in three package sizes; no published details on its content could be found.

uhles-blend-303.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend called Blend 303 has been found.
uhles-blend-303.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

rattray-summer-edition-2014.z: Summer Edition 2014 is the summer installment of the seasonal limited series Rattray releases every year. Its base holds black Cavendish, select Virginia leaf, and broken flake; a flavoring built from raspberry, hibiscus, honey, and creme caramel notes is applied on top. Being a limited edition, its production has ended. Despite the texture the broken-flake share brings, the blend produces a smoke that lights easily and stays sweet; nicotine is low. It suits smokers looking for a light, fruity, floral summer aromatic, as well as collectors of seasonal editions.
rattray-summer-edition-2014.o: Leaves a sweet aroma mixing raspberry jam, honey, and creamy caramel.

torben-dansk-no-6-english-delight.z: Torben Dansk No.6 English Delight is noted in brand marketing as the number aimed at those wanting a natural blend without Latakia; no sufficient independent source giving detail on its composition has been found.
torben-dansk-no-6-english-delight.o: Records describe it as leaving a dry, non-smoky tobacco aroma.

ole-shenandoah-bootlegged.z: Bootlegged is the aromatic blend of the Ole Shenandoah line carrying a bootleg-liquor-themed name. Burley, black cavendish, and Virginia are used together, topped with a sweet dark-fruit-and-cherry-direction flavoring. The cut is loose ribbon, defined by a slow, cool burn. Under the sweet topping, burley builds an earthy, nutty body, while cavendish carries the sugary side. Nicotine runs from light to medium, while the taste is pronounced depending on the topping's intensity. It's aimed at smokers who love fruity aromatics and want some tobacco body beneath the sweet topping. Records indicate this line is no longer produced.
ole-shenandoah-bootlegged.o: A dark fruit scent recalling cherry liqueur is joined by a sugary cavendish base.

diamond-crown-kentucky-nougat.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of Kentucky Nougat, a blend from Diamond Crown.

davidoff-45-years.z: 45 Years is a limited-edition commemorative blend Davidoff prepared for its forty-fifth year in pipe tobacco. The Swiss-origin brand has its pipe tobaccos produced in Germany; this edition was released in numbered 100-gram tins, limited to six thousand pieces. The leaves are stated to be sourced from Brazil, Cyprus, Turkey and Malawi. The blend consists of burley, black cavendish, latakia, dark leaf of Zairean origin and oriental tobaccos, flavored with cherry, vanilla and rum. On the smoke, cherry and plum notes stand out along with traces of spice, vanilla and honey, while latakia and light virginia leave a fine smoky layer in the background. It suits smokers who love the aromatic structure but also want to taste tobacco character, interested in transitional blends where latakia is used sparingly.
davidoff-45-years.o: Beneath the cherry and vanilla sweetness, a fine woody soot scent can be sensed.

carmel-pipe-shop-bay-fog.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Bay Fog under the Carmel Pipe Shop brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

my-smoking-shop-buttered-rum.z: As its name suggests, a bulk aromatic flavored with a rum-and-butter sauce; sufficient sources describing its leaf composition could not be found.

murray-sons-co-ltd-erinmore-mild-mellow.z: A now-discontinued version from Murray, Sons & Co's Erinmore series; sufficient sources describing its composition and character could not be found.

robert-mcconnell-river-thames.z: River Thames is a blend of dark and light Virginia leaf combined with spicy Perique, cut into round medallions. The recipe emphasizes a distinct raisin note; when lit, Virginia's sweet, faintly chocolatey, herbal tones come forward while Perique remains present from the first bowl to the last. The medallion cut allows the leaf to be rubbed out or packed whole, and lets the flavor unfold slowly. Nicotine is moderate and flavor intensity high. It suits fans of the Virginia-Perique line who want a blend where fruity sweetness and spice sit side by side. It is offered in a 50-gram tin as part of the Heritage line.
robert-mcconnell-river-thames.o: A faintly sweet, chocolatey aroma layers over raisin and meadow-grass notes.

john-aylesbury-sweet-dreams.z: John Aylesbury Sweet Dreams is recorded as one of the brand's sweetly cased aromatic blends; since it doesn't appear in the maker's current listing, no verifiable source could be found on its composition and flavor profile.

john-cotton-john-cottons-double-pressed-.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to document the contents and character of John Cotton's John Cotton's Double Pressed Burley.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-dunhills-s.z: This blend in Sutliff's Match line is based on the English mixture known as Dunhill's Standard Mixture Medium. It is an unflavored composition where latakia, Oriental, and Virginia leaves come together; it aims for a medium-bodied, smoky but not overwhelming profile. Compared with the original blend, it is noted to burn a bit cooler, sit a touch sweeter and creamier, and have the tart-woody sharpness of the Orientals come through more faintly. It suits smokers looking for latakia's smoke without the intensity of heavy Balkan blends. With Sutliff's production stopping, the blend has become dependent on remaining stock.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-dunhills-s.o: Leaves a woody, smoky campfire scent alongside a spicy tobacco note.

golden-blend-tobacco-co-wild-honey.z: Beyond being a honey-flavored pipe tobacco under the Golden Blend Tobacco Co. name, there is no independent sourcing documenting the blend's composition and character.
golden-blend-tobacco-co-wild-honey.o: Said to leave a honey-sweet aroma.

ashton-winding-road.z: Winding Road is a ribbon-cut blend of golden and dark brown Virginia leaf flecked with black Cavendish. It aims for a structure between aromatic and English style, with flavoring kept noticeably measured. The top note carries caramel and apricot, but at an intensity that doesn't override the tobacco's natural scent. Strength is low, flavor is light, and the room note stays faint. It suits smokers avoiding heavily syruped aromatics who want sweetness kept in the background and are looking for a low-nicotine everyday blend.
ashton-winding-road.o: Leaves a light room note leaning toward caramel and apricot, with the natural tobacco scent staying up front.

sutliff-tobacco-company-sps-41-cube-cut.z: SPS-41 Cube Cut is a cube-cut burley product in Sutliff's bulk line. The leaf is pressed and cut into small cubes; this cut allows for easy pipe packing and an even burn. According to the maker's description, it is built from selected domestic and imported leaf, with a light casing applied that sweetens and darkens the tobacco. The taste runs along a nutty, bready, earthy line; there is no pronounced flavoring layer. It is one of the products blenders often use as a base tobacco, but it is also smoked on its own. It suits smokers looking for a slow, cool burn from the cube cut who enjoy a plain burley character.
sutliff-tobacco-company-sps-41-cube-cut.o: Leaves a plain tobacco trace with a scent of dry bread and roasted walnut.

sutliff-tobacco-company-burley-j4.z: J4 Burley is a semi-aromatic blend where a light vanilla topping is applied to a ribbon-cut combination of burley and fire-cured Kentucky leaf. The casing softens burley's harshness; the topping is kept measured enough not to mask the leaf's own flavor. A blend long present in Sutliff's bulk line, records indicate it was also originally used as blending material and as a base tobacco packaged by retailers under their own names. Suited to those seeking a low-nicotine, lightly sweet burley for all-day smoking.
sutliff-tobacco-company-burley-j4.o: Leaves a trace where soft vanilla mixes with a nutty tobacco scent.

d-r-tobacco-three-sails.z: Three Sails is a light-bodied, English-style blend made purely of flue-cured Virginia leaf. Its distinguishing feature is a very fine cut, which allows for a tighter pack in the bowl. Per the maker's description, careful leaf selection and processing method shape the blend's character. On the palate, citrus tartness and dry-hay sweetness lead; the profile stays consistent throughout the smoke, and the leaf ashes down with minimal relighting. It carries no casing. Suited to smokers wanting a light, clean, unflavored Virginia they can smoke all day; it also serves as a base tobacco in other blends.
d-r-tobacco-three-sails.o: Leaves a light, clean tobacco scent reminiscent of dry hay and lemon peel.

samuel-gawith-pensioners-mixture-fvf-bbf.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Pensioners Mixture - FVF & BBF Off Cuts, according to records a straight Virginia blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

1776-tobacco-co-boston-whaler-aromatic.z: One of 1776 Tobacco Co.'s aromatic blends; no adequate source documenting its content and character could be reached.

ken-byron-ventures-bright-star.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Ken Byron Ventures' Bright Star blend.

peter-stokkebye-golden-dawn.z: This is a Peter Stokkebye blend reported to be Burley-forward; no sufficient first-hand sources documenting its content and character could be found.
peter-stokkebye-golden-dawn.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

consolidated-305-black-brown.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Consolidated blend 305: Black & Brown.

hearth-home-freight-train.z: Freight Train is an unflavored American blend made up of red Virginia, dark Burley, fire-cured Kentucky, a small amount of unflavored black Cavendish, and Perique. Since all the components lean toward dark leaf, the taste develops along a nutty, earthy line, with Perique leaving a spicy backbone. It is noted for burning cool and producing a heavy volume of smoke. Suited to those wanting a full-bodied blend without Latakia; nicotine is not light, so it calls for slow smoking.
hearth-home-freight-train.o: Leaves an earthy, nutty tobacco aroma with a light pepper edge.

holger-danske-amber-magic.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for this blend, described as aromatic, from the Danish brand Holger Danske.

gq-tobaccos-cherry-menthol.z: GQ Tobaccos's cherry-and-menthol flavored blend; there is no sourcing documenting the tobacco composition.
gq-tobaccos-cherry-menthol.o: The name implies it leaves a cherry-and-menthol aroma.

batavia-1628-no-3-premium-vanilla.z: No manufacturer or retailer source could be found for this product, which appears from its name to be a vanilla-flavored blend.

gawith-hoggarth-co-broken-scotch-cake.z: Broken Scotch Cake is prepared by combining hot-air-cured Virginia leaf, predominantly, with sun-cured leaf added to cool and sweeten the smoke, then pressing the mix. Because the pressed mass is broken into coarse pieces, the tobacco has a large, irregular appearance; this coarse cut gives a slow, cool burn. It is an untopped blend and stays on the light side in flavour. Virginia's grassy sweetness leads, and the sun-cured leaf adds a dry, faintly tart frame to it. The nicotine load is low. It is a good record for those new to the pipe as well as those looking for a blending tobacco to mellow out blends they find too heavy.
gawith-hoggarth-co-broken-scotch-cake.o: Leaves an aroma of dry grass and slightly sweet hay.

affordable-pipes-fox-hound.z: One of the house blends from the American seller Affordable Pipes; no accessible source describing its content could be found.

schurch-marcassite-245.z: Marcassite 245, signed by Schürch, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

emersons-mississippi-morning.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing could be found for Mississippi Morning, a blend from Emersons, so the record has been left open; according to available listings it is classified in the Aromatic family.

house-of-windsor-barking-dog.z: Barking Dog is considered one of the typical examples of American-style English mixtures. Cube-cut Burley forms the body of the blend; smoky Latakia and a small amount of light-colored Virginia are added to it. The cube-cut Burley burns slowly and gives a nutty, dry taste, while the Latakia stands only as a smoke layer; because of this, the blend sits in the medium range of English mixtures rather than the heavy end. The blend was produced by House of Windsor during the period in the second half of the twentieth century when over-the-counter (OTC) tobaccos were common in America. Since House of Windsor ceased operations, the original product is no longer made; match blends prepared by different makers exist. It's a structure aimed at smokers looking for a classic American profile, Burley-based with measured Latakia.
house-of-windsor-barking-dog.o: A nutty, dry tone accompanies the light wood-smoke aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-english-toffee-1.z: English Toffee #16 is, despite its name, a latakia-free aromatic; toffee and caramel flavoring is applied to a ribbon-cut base of burley and Virginia leaves. The name refers not to the blend type but to the English confection the topping evokes. It's among the lightest of Sutliff's bulk aromatics; nicotine strength is low and the smoke is soft. Sold in bulk from one-ounce up to five-pound packaging. A record for those seeking a sweet but not heavy aromatic.
sutliff-tobacco-company-english-toffee-1.o: Leaves a scent of buttery caramel and sugared nuts.

tinder-box-reserve-1928.z: No reliable source has been found for the Tinder Box pipe blend called Reserve 1928.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-wilder-frut.z: This Wilder blend, whose name refers to dried fruit, is an aromatic product flavored with plum-forward dried-fruit essences. The maker, Tabacos Wilder Finamore, has prepared handmade Virginia- and Burley-based blends in Juiz de Fora since 1949; since no independent source for a detailed description of the blend could be found, the record is kept limited.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-wilder-frut.o: Leaves a scent of dried fruit and plum.

white-elephant-sahara.z: Sahara is a member of the Afrika aromatic tobacco line introduced in 2023 by White Elephant, a brand founded in 1945 as a small briar-pipe workshop in Bavaria. The brand takes its name from the Tanzanian meerschaum it used in its early pipe bowls; since 2019 it has been among the brands under the Kopp umbrella, keeping the blend tied to the German tobacco tradition. The composition combines black cavendish, broken Virginia, cube-cut Virginia, and Burley, topped with a date and honey-based casing. The mixed cut, offering both slow-burning cube pieces and quick-catching broken leaf, means little pressing is needed while packing. On the flavor side, cavendish's dark sugary base leads; Burley adds a nutty body and slight dryness. Nicotine level is measured. This blend suits smokers who love heavy aromatics and want the sweet casing pronounced enough to override the tobacco character, as well as newcomers to the pipe. It's offered in a 50-gram tin.
white-elephant-sahara.o: Leaves a dark, sugary scent reminiscent of honey and dried dates.

richs-sunday-morning.z: Sunday Morning is one of Rich's Cigar Store's house blends referred to as aromatic; no verifiable source could be found describing its composition or character.
richs-sunday-morning.o: No reliable information could be found on the room note.

reiner-blend-25.z: Reiner Blend 25 is a German aromatic blend combining bright Virginia, black Cavendish, and Burley leaf, flavored with cocoa and hazelnut notes. It is produced at the Hamburg house Kohlhase & Kopp, based on the historical recipes of Rüdiger L. Will. The flavoring load is not heavy; it is designed as a light-to-medium-bodied aromatic, steering away from a sugar-bomb style. The Burley component builds a dry, nutty base while Virginia's sweetness and Cavendish's mellowness carry the flavoring. Straight from the tin, its moisture is ready for smoking. It suits smokers looking for an all-day aromatic with measured nicotine, avoiding fruity, intensely sweet blends. The Reiner line, along with Solani, is a product of the same blending tradition.
reiner-blend-25.o: Leaves a sweetish aroma dominated by cocoa and roasted hazelnut.

sutliff-tobacco-company-crumble-kake-lim.z: The fourth limited edition in the Crumble Kake Barrel Aged series combines fire-cured, hot-pressed burley leaves with lively Virginias. The blend is rested in a freshly emptied bourbon barrel to pick up oak and whiskey traces, then re-pressed into a crumbly cake form. The smoke and earth tones from fire-curing combine with Virginia's tangy sweetness and the oaky depth from the barrel. Body sits on the full side. For smokers seeking near-unflavored, full-bodied blends with barrel character; being a limited edition, it is not in continuous production.
sutliff-tobacco-company-crumble-kake-lim.o: Leaves a sweet, oaky scent of wood smoke and bourbon barrel.

clan-shaw-delaware.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of Clan Shaw's Delaware blend could be found.

tinder-box-chocolate-treat.z: Tinder Box is the name of an American tobacconist chain founded in 1928 that sells blends prepared for its own shops under its own name; Chocolate Treat is one of these house blends, though no sufficient independent source describing its composition and character has been found.

peter-stokkebye-luxury-navy-flake.z: Luxury Navy Flake is produced by pressing and slicing ripe Old Belt flue-cured Virginias with a small amount of Louisiana Perique. In keeping with the classic navy flake recipe, a very light rum flavoring is applied to the blend; this flavoring is measured to the point of being hard to notice. When the slices are rubbed out for packing, they light easily. On the palate, Virginia's sweet side, recalling citrus and dried fruit, leads; Perique stays well in the background, a faint spicy trace. Body and nicotine are low. It suits smokers seeking a mild entry into the Virginia-Perique category; for those expecting an intense example of the category, it stays measured in both flavor and strength.
peter-stokkebye-luxury-navy-flake.o: A dry hay and ripe fruit aroma is joined by a very faint trace of rum.

tabac-turc-tekel.z: Türk Pipo Tütünü (Turkish Pipe Tobacco) is a domestic product long produced under the Tekel state monopoly and, according to records, on the market since 1933. It is made from Oriental leaf, pressed and packed as flake; per the product description, the pressing is done in cast-iron molds using aged wood. Its flavoring is light, carrying a sweetish trace of honey and carob.
tabac-turc-tekel.o: Leaves a heavy, lingering Oriental tobacco scent beneath a honeyed, carob-like sweetness.

gawith-hoggarth-co-no-27-perique-flake.z: No. 27 Perique Flake is an unflavored Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. product where flue-cured Virginia leaf is combined with Louisiana Perique and pressed. It comes out of the tin as long, dark slices carrying sparse sugar crystals; sources indicate the 25-gram pack contains only a few long flakes. Perique lends the blend spice, body, and coolness, while Virginia holds a measured sweetness underneath. There is no sauce or topping, so the taste comes entirely from the leaf and pressing. Suited to smokers who love unflavored Virginia-Perique flakes and are accustomed to rubbing out slices and smoking slowly.
gawith-hoggarth-co-no-27-perique-flake.o: Leaves a peppery, spicy aroma alongside dried-plum sweetness.

watch-city-cigar-rhythm-blues.z: Watch City Cigar's blend called Rhythm & Blues is, according to records, one of the house blends of the Waltham, Massachusetts tobacconist shop; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

samuel-gawith-finest-kendal-twist-black-.z: Finest Kendal Twist Black XX is the product of the rope-twisting tradition Samuel Gawith continues in Kendal. Dark Virginia leaf is tightly twisted into rope, with no casing applied; it is listed in catalogs in the Virginia family under rope cut. Thin coins cut from the rope are crumbled and aired before packing; the burn is finicky and requires a very slow smoke. Nicotine level is very high according to records, the smoke cool and the tobacco flavor full. A product aimed at experienced smokers, smoked in small quantities in small-chambered pipes.
samuel-gawith-finest-kendal-twist-black-.o: Fills the room with a sharp, smoky, heavy tobacco scent.

royal-cigar-no-11-black-cordial.z: No reliable source could be found for No.11 Black Cordial, referred to as an aromatic pipe tobacco signed Royal Cigar.

black-cat-cigar-company-black-raspberry.z: A raspberry-flavored bulk aromatic from Black Cat Cigar Company; no manufacturer recipe for its content could be found.
black-cat-cigar-company-black-raspberry.o: Leaves a sweet raspberry room note.

lane-limited-bs-005.z: BS-005 is listed as one of Lane Limited's code-named bulk blends and is classed in the English family; since it's absent from the manufacturer's current listings, not enough sources could be found for its contents.

mcclelland-no-800-black-and-lemon.z: No. 800 Black and Lemon was a Cavendish-Virginia blend in the aromatic wing of McClelland's numbered bulk series. Its name comes from the contrast it builds: dark black Cavendish and light, lemon-toned Carolina Virginia ribbon cut sit side by side in the same pouch. Rather than being sprayed directly onto the surface, the flavoring is worked into the leaf via McClelland's English-style heat-maturation method; the resulting taste runs along vanilla and caramel lines. While the black Cavendish gives the blend mildness and a syrupy base, the light Virginia leaf balances it with tangy sweetness. It's a light-on-nicotine record with limited tongue bite; the kind used by those starting out with aromatic tobacco or those seeking a sweet but light everyday blend. The blend was withdrawn from the market when McClelland stopped production in 2018.
mcclelland-no-800-black-and-lemon.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and burnt-sugar aroma along with a light lemony freshness.

erik-stokkebye-jubilaeums-flake-small-ba.z: Small Batch Jubilæums Flake is a limited-run product from 4th Generation's flake series; not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition.
erik-stokkebye-jubilaeums-flake-small-ba.o: Could not be described due to insufficient sourcing.

mcclelland-brindle-flake.z: Brindle Flake is an unflavored Virginia blend obtained by pressing flue-cured Virginia leaves into cake, aging them, and then slicing. Since the cakes are partly broken up before going into the tin, it comes as broken flake, which makes packing and lighting easier and lets the tobacco burn evenly. Rather than complex layers, the smoke follows a plain, direct line: Virginia's natural sweetness and pure leaf taste stand out, with no flavoring added. Nicotine dose is kept at a medium level, not fatiguing. A suitable record for smokers wanting to get to know unflavored Virginia character who are used to working with flake form. McClelland Tobacco Company halted production in early 2018, so the blend is no longer made.
mcclelland-brindle-flake.o: Leaves a dry hay and tangy sweet-fruit aroma.

dunhill-a-22000.z: A discontinued mixture referred to by its code number under the Dunhill name, for which no verifiable source on its composition could be found.

peretti-belmont-burley-blends.z: A house blend L.J. Peretti lists in its burley group and continues to sell in three separate weights; its record is incomplete since no detailed composition and flavor description has been published.

samuel-gawith-brown-no-4.z: Brown No. 4 is an unflavored tobacco produced in Kendal by twisting Virginia leaf into rope form. It is listed in catalogs in the Virginia family under rope cut; coins cut from the rope are smoked after crumbling and airing. Along with the brand's other rope products like Black XX, it is counted among the high-nicotine tobaccos; it offers the intense, smoky, and woody flavor of unflavored leaf. A product aimed at experienced smokers requiring slow smoking and small packing.
samuel-gawith-brown-no-4.o: Leaves an intense, smoky, woody tobacco scent.

affordable-pipes-old-fashioned.z: Old Fashioned is one of the Virginia- and Burley-based blends from Affordable Pipes, with other leaves also joining them. As its name suggests, an old-style, mellow sweet profile is the goal. Its taste and scent are noticeable, but strength stays low. Its topping doesn't come forward as much as in heavy aromatics; it's used more to support the leaf's own taste. It's aimed at those looking for an old-style, mild, inexpensive everyday blend.
affordable-pipes-old-fashioned.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly spicy, dry tobacco room note.

bjarne-viking-saint-olaf.z: One of the blends listed alongside Eric the Red and William the Conqueror in Bjarne's Viking line; no reliable source on its composition and character could be found.

d-r-tobacco-raccoons-friend.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of D & R Tobacco's Raccoon's Friend blend were found.

mcclelland-no-2020-matured-cake.z: No. 2020 Matured Cake is a pressed bulk blend bringing together matured Virginia's sweet, tangy line with the Oriental mixture's mild, nutty, aromatic structure. Aging it as a cake lets the flavors meld; in the smoke, Virginia's citrus side and the Oriental's spicy depth alternate in the foreground. Being unflavored and Oriental-forward, it suits those seeking Latakia-free Eastern-style mixtures. The cake structure needs to be rubbed out before packing. Discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-no-2020-matured-cake.o: Leaves a nutty, spiced, and lightly tangy aroma.

diamond-crown-optimum.z: No reliable source could be found documenting the composition and character of this pipe blend sold under the Diamond Crown name.

rattray-charles-mixture.z: Charles Mixture is a lightly flavored Rattray mixture bringing together Cavendish and Virginia leaf with broad-leaf Carolina tobacco. It is a ribbon cut, said to be blended in a measured way that doesn't tire the palate; its scent is pronounced but not overpowering. Body and nicotine stay on the light side, making it suitable for long smokes and daytime use. Reports indicate the blend is not part of the current production list. It suits smokers looking for a classic, not-heavy aromatic.
rattray-charles-mixture.o: Leaves a soft, lightly sweet, dry tobacco aroma.

ken-byron-ventures-spaghetti-western-201.z: A blend released as a limited batch in 2019; not enough sources could be found to describe its composition.

poschl-tabak-allegro.z: This is the Allegro blend from the Bavaria-based house Pöschl Tabak; no source could be found describing its content.

james-barber-broken-scotch-cake-chocolat.z: A chocolate-flavored, Virginia-based house blend from the James Barber tobacconist house, presented as a pressed and broken cake; no independent source could be found to detail its character.
james-barber-broken-scotch-cake-chocolat.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

koltoma-winter-night.z: Koltoma's Winter Night is referred to in records as an English-type blend; since no independent source could confirm its content and character, the record is left incomplete.

sterling-tobacco-co-my-buddy.z: My Buddy is the blend Sterling Tobacco Company classifies as a light English mixture. Per the maker's description, only a touch of latakia is added to what is otherwise a naturally aromatic Virginia-and-burley mixture; the goal is to give the latakia flavor without its heavy room note. Keeping the latakia ratio low moves the blend away from the smoke wall of English mixtures; Virginia's sweetness and burley's dry body come forward, with smoke remaining only a background line. Records indicate the blend also contains a small amount of cigar leaf along with a light casing. Nicotine is medium. A stepping stone for smokers wanting to try English mixtures while avoiding a heavy latakia scent.
sterling-tobacco-co-my-buddy.o: Leaves a soft tobacco scent, lightly sweet with barely perceptible smoke.

mission-pipe-shop-bobs-best.z: Bob's Best is advertised as the best-selling among the house blends Mission Pipe Shop prepares at its San Jose counter. According to the maker's description, it is a cavendish-forward mixture combining domestic and imported leaf, topped with a light almond casing. In business at the same address for over fifty years, the shop sells more than sixty blends loose by weight. Suitable for those looking for a measured aromatic in the direction of dried fruit and nuts; its nicotine load is low and the smoke soft. Since the blend is distributed only through the shop, it isn't found in the wider retail network.
mission-pipe-shop-bobs-best.o: Leaves an aroma of toasted almond and sweet dough.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2011.z: Christmas Cheer 2011 is the release prepared from the 2011 crop of McClelland's annual Virginia series. The method used in the series is kept the same each year: flue-cure-dried orange-red Virginia is matured pressed into cake, sliced, and tinned as broken flake. No flavoring is used; in the smoke, the leaf's natural sweetness proceeds along with bready and faintly fruity tones. Nicotine dose is medium, and the tobacco burns evenly. That the release comes from a single crop is a distinguishing feature for smokers who collect the series year by year. Not reproduced since McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2011.o: Leaves a tangy, vinegary sweetness along with a toasted-bread aroma.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-yachtsman.z: Yachtsman Plug is a classic plug tobacco continuing the Irish pipe-tobacco tradition; the brand is Irish in origin and is produced today under Scandinavian Tobacco Group. The blend's body is built from full-bodied, flue-cured Virginia leaf of African and Brazilian origin; burley is added to provide balance and mildness. The moistened mixture is slowly pressed for days in large steam presses, then divided into plugs. Due to its presentation, the tobacco is a hard, tight block; it is sliced with a sharp knife and rubbed according to the smoker's preference. The sugars concentrated during pressing give a dark, bready, lightly fruity taste; nicotine load is above medium. Suited to smokers accustomed to preparing plug tobacco who want a full-bodied, measured-casing virginia-burley.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-yachtsman.o: Leaves a dark, bready tobacco scent carrying a light fruity sweetness.

bengal-slices-bengal-slices-single-barre.z: Bengal Slices Single Barrel is a limited version that keeps the brand's classic skeleton: sweet, bright Virginias, fragrant Oriental leaves, and a measured amount of Cyprus Latakia come together. Its difference lies in the preparation stage; records say the blend is rested for about a month in a single freshly-emptied bourbon barrel, then pressed and turned into a crumble cake. As a result, the tobacco carries a sweet top note sourced from oak and grain rather than the liquor itself. In the smoke, Latakia's soot-and-leather axis is balanced by Virginia's sugary taste; the Orientals open a dry, spicy layer in the middle. The barrel history doesn't make the blend aromatic — it only adds a sweet frame without disturbing the English character. It suits smokers familiar with English blends who are curious about adding a distilled-spirit-derived nuance to the familiar smoke-and-Virginia equation. Since it comes in cake form, it needs to be rubbed out before smoking, and aired for a while depending on moisture.
bengal-slices-bengal-slices-single-barre.o: Latakia's soot and tar note is joined by a sweetish oak-barrel and whiskey-vapor character.

mars-cigars-pipes-miners-blend.z: Remembered as a house blend from the retailer Mars Cigars & Pipes; since no source documenting its contents could be found, the profile is left incomplete.
mars-cigars-pipes-miners-blend.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

shockoe-valley-tobaccos-proper-english.z: Referred to as a Latakia-bearing English-style shop blend from Shockoe Valley Tobaccos, based in Richmond, Virginia; no independent source confirming its content could be found.
shockoe-valley-tobaccos-proper-english.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

mcclelland-rose-of-latakia.z: Rose of Latakia is a McClelland blend in which, despite its name, Latakia doesn't take the lead. The dry leaf consists of short ribbons ranging from dark brown to black; the tin note carries the brand's usual tangy, vinegary sharpness. In the mixture, stoved and matured Virginia leaves sit atop a measured amount of Oriental tobacco, with Syrian Latakia staying in the background. The smoke sits on the lighter side of medium; it runs along a sweet-and-tart axis, occasionally giving notes reminiscent of toasted sourdough bread, orange peel, and oolong tea. Suited to smokers who find Latakia-heavy English blends too much and who like a tangy Virginia character. McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-rose-of-latakia.o: A fine trace of incense and orange peel accompanies a tangy tobacco aroma.

cornell-diehl-comfort.z: Comfort is a Virginia-Perique blend Cornell & Diehl places within its Virginia family. Per the manufacturer's description, bright Virginia leaves are combined with perique; cube-cut burley and unsweetened black cavendish slow the burn and soften the texture. It is offered as a ribbon cut, making it easy to pack and light. Its character sits between perique's plummy spice and Virginia's bready sweetness; because the cavendish component files down the sharp edges, the blend remains at a manageable intensity even for smokers newly getting used to perique. It suits smokers looking for medium nicotine and a moderate room note, who smoke a pipe over long stretches during the day.
cornell-diehl-comfort.o: Leaves a lightly spiced aroma leaning toward dry-hay sweetness.

dream-castle-tobacco-company-vintage-but.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of Vintage Buttered Rum, a blend from Dream Castle Tobacco Company.

dan-tobacco-holmer-knudsens.z: A pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source on the blend's composition or character was found, so no further detail is given.

peterson-special-reserve-2009.z: Special Reserve is Peterson's limited tin series, released each year with a different recipe; the 2009 edition was presented in a 100 gram tin. Gold, red, and dark Virginia are combined with black Cavendish and given a white-wine flavoring. Peterson is an Irish brand; these special tins are reportedly prepared to Peterson's recipe by the German manufacturer Kohlhase, Kopp & Co. The cut is described as ribbon. Since each year of the series is a distinct blend, the tin was produced only in its release year and never repeated. It is a notable record for smokers seeking a lightly flavored, Virginia-forward aromatic and for those who collect the annual releases.
peterson-special-reserve-2009.o: Leaves a lightly wine-like, sweet tobacco aroma.

ken-byron-ventures-goblin-city-2023.z: Goblin City is a blend Ken Byron Ventures built along the lines of the Perth-tradition Scottish mixture. The body is made of matured red Virginia, joined by Oriental leaf from North Macedonia's Prilep region. Latakia isn't a dominant component here — it's used only at a seasoning level. This structure keeps Virginia's sweetness at the center while layering the Oriental's dry-tangy spice and Latakia's measured smoke on top. Suited to smokers who don't want the smoke density of heavy English blends but want Latakia present as a hint. The blend was released in limited numbers in collaboration with Eldritch Pipes.
ken-byron-ventures-goblin-city-2023.o: Leaves a sweetish tobacco aroma mixed with wood smoke and dry hay.

briarworks-international-sweet-tea.z: Sweet Tea is a lightly flavored blend in BriarWorks's line evoking the American South. Sweet Virginias, black cavendish and Oriental leaf are brought together; a fine flavoring evoking sugared tea is applied on top. Oriental leaf gives the blend a dry, lightly grassy edge and keeps the casing from becoming dominant on its own. Black cavendish carries the sweetness while the Virginias form a bright base. The body is medium, flavor medium-to-full. Worth considering for those who don't want the syrupy intensity of heavy aromatics but still seek a sweet profile; offered in a two-ounce glass jar.
briarworks-international-sweet-tea.o: Leaves a lightly grassy, sweet aroma reminiscent of sugared iced tea.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-pirates-a.z: Pirate's Alley is a Perique-forward Virginia-Perique blend taking its name from the narrow passage in New Orleans's French Quarter. The tobacconist describes the blend as full-bodied and strong; it is ribbon cut. The grassy, sugary side of the Virginia base is covered over by the plum, fig and peppery spice of the high proportion of Louisiana Perique. Nicotine load and flavor intensity are high, so it suits smoking in small pipes and on a full stomach. Meant for experienced smokers after high-Perique blends.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-pirates-a.o: Leaves a sharp spice, plum and tangy tobacco aroma.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-pipers-pleasure.z: Piper's Pleasure is a sweet cavendish blend in the Boswell shop's aromatic wing. Per records, golden cavendish is brought together with black and fire-cured cavendish leaf, topped with a vanilla-and-cherry-based casing. Chocolate is dominant in the smoke; vanilla and a faint coffee tone accompany it, and at the intersection of the two sweet casings a caramel-like taste appears. It is a light-bodied blend that burns slow and cool. Suitable for those seeking an aromatic with a perceptible casing yet a low nicotine load.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-pipers-pleasure.o: Leaves a cocoa, vanilla cream and light coffee aroma behind it.

blatter-blatter-blatter-1981.z: One of the Cavendish-based house blends from the Blatter & Blatter shop in Montreal; no reliable source documenting its content could be found.

cornell-diehl-merlins-choice.z: An American-type blend that formerly appeared in Cornell & Diehl's bulk catalogue; no adequate source on its composition and character was found.
cornell-diehl-merlins-choice.o: Records indicate it leaves a nutty, tobacco-forward scent.

mcclelland-virginia-woods.z: Virginia Woods is one of the blends McClelland classed as semi-aromatic Virginias. At its base is stoved Virginia, a process that lends the blend a woody, smoky edge. A small amount of topping is applied over it, which according to records leaves a resinous aroma reminiscent of a high-altitude pine forest. Production ended when the company closed in 2018. In the smoke, Virginia's natural, non-sugary sweetness and the brand's familiar tangy Virginia character are preserved; the topping isn't heavy enough to make this a full aromatic. Burns cool when smoked slowly. Suited to those wanting a light-to-medium, all-day blend that sits somewhere between an unflavored Virginia and an aromatic.
mcclelland-virginia-woods.o: Leaves a cool, woody aroma reminiscent of a resinous pine forest, along with a faint sweet tobacco trace.

thepiperoom-com-dr-watsons-mixture.z: No independent source documenting the composition of the ThePipeRoom.com house blend Dr. Watson's Mixture has been found; the brand's own site is no longer online.
thepiperoom-com-dr-watsons-mixture.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

brebbia-rondo-mixture-no-27.z: An English-style mixture in Brebbia's numbered series, noted to contain Latakia and Perique; no sufficient source could be found to verify its detailed content.

missouri-meerschaum-timeless.z: No reliable composition information could be found for the Timeless blend released under the Missouri Meerschaum name.

sutliff-tobacco-company-cinnamon-delight.z: D67 Cinnamon Delight is a cinnamon-flavored aromatic in Sutliff's bulk line; sufficient independent sources documenting its leaf composition and character could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-cinnamon-delight.o: Records did not provide sufficient information for a description.

mccranies-moorsgate.z: Moorsgate is McCranie's English blend built with a low Latakia share. Per the shop's recipe, it's based on light Oriental leaves and matured Virginias that build a mild, sweet body, with Latakia added over them only in a small proportion. As a result, the smoky note stays in the background rather than covering the blend. This structure makes it a middle step for smokers who want the English blends' smoky character without a heavy Latakia dose. Since it carries no flavoring, the sweetness comes from the Virginia's own sugar; the Oriental leaf adds a tangy-spiced edge too. It's positioned as a starting point for those wanting to move from aromatic blends toward the English side.
mccranies-moorsgate.o: Leaves a fine trace reminiscent of pine tar, mixing light wood smoke with sweet dried-fruit aroma.

paul-olsen-arabica-melange.z: One of the Poul Olsen house blends; although its name points to a coffee-direction flavoring, not enough source material describing its composition could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-hill-of-slane.z: Hill of Slane is an aromatic blend released in limited quantity within Sutliff's Private Stock line in March 2023 for St. Patrick's Day. A sauce carrying notes of Irish cream, whiskey, vanilla, and caramel is applied over Virginia, burley, and black cavendish leaves; the name comes from the Hill of Slane in Ireland. The ribbon cut offers an easy-lighting, cool, slow-burning smoke. It stays light in nicotine, while on the flavor side the sauce's creamy sweetness takes precedence over the leaf character. A blend for aromatic lovers who favor sweet, liqueur-like profiles. Being a limited production, and with Sutliff's operations ending in 2025, it is only found in remaining stock.
sutliff-tobacco-company-hill-of-slane.o: Fills the room with a pronounced scent of sweet cream, vanilla, and caramel candy.

schurch-lapis-406.z: Lapis 406, signed by Schürch, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

tabacos-catarinenses-ltda-chocolate-e-ho.z: Chocolate e Hortelã is recorded as a chocolate- and mint-flavored tin tobacco from the Brazilian maker Tabacos Catarinenses; no sufficient independent source describing its content and character could be found.
tabacos-catarinenses-ltda-chocolate-e-ho.o: No reliable record of a room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-vieux-carre.z: Vieux Carré is a pressed flake English blend introduced by Cornell & Diehl for its Cellar Series in July 2016. It's named after New Orleans' historic French Quarter. Its composition includes Virginia, Latakia, and Oriental leaf; there is no casing. Its flake structure and composition make the blend well suited to long aging; the maker states the most mature flavor emerges after roughly fifteen years of rest. On the flavor side it offers an intense profile with medium body. Built for those accustomed to breaking down flakes who enjoy cellaring unflavored Latakia blends.
cornell-diehl-vieux-carre.o: Leaves a scent where woody smoke mingles with dry spice and breadlike sweetness.

middle-earth-tobacco-the-shire.z: The Virginia-Perique-centered blend in the Middle Earth Tobacco line; since no verifiable source could be found, no detail can be given.

sutliff-tobacco-company-aberrant.z: Aberrant is an unflavored mixture prepared by Per Georg Jensen under Sutliff's Signature Series umbrella. What makes the blend unusual is the use of Nicotiana rustica leaf, which carries far higher nicotine than the customary Nicotiana tabacum, instead of it; red and light Virginias and dark fire-cured Kentucky accompany it. On the palate, earth, wood, spice, and smoke notes are pronounced; the Virginias add a tangy-sweet citrus and dark-fruit tone, while Kentucky adds a smoky, walnut-like depth. Given the high nicotine strength, it's a record for experienced smokers accustomed to full-bodied mixtures.
sutliff-tobacco-company-aberrant.o: Leaves a spicy, herbal scent along with earth, wood, and smoke.

james-fox-the-bankers.z: The Bankers is a house blend from the James Fox cigar and pipe shop on Grafton Street in Dublin. According to shop staff, the bulk of the blend is made up of Havana (Cuban) leaf, rounded out with a small amount of Latakia. It's ribbon cut; on opening the tin, an aroma reminiscent of a dried Cuban cigar comes through, lightly veiled by the Latakia. The smoke isn't heavy; with its unflavored composition, it's aimed at smokers coming from cigar culture who look for similar earthy, leaf-forward flavors in a pipe. It carries no aromatic additive, and its strength and flavor sit at a moderate level. As the product is exclusive to the shop's own shelves, it reportedly has no wide distribution.
james-fox-the-bankers.o: Leaves an earthy aroma reminiscent of dried cigar leaf, with the smoky tone of Latakia layered on top.

d-r-tobacco-taps-vip.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of D & R Tobacco's TAPS VIP blend were found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-left-bank.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of Left Bank, listed as an aromatic in Sutliff catalogs, could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-left-bank.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

john-patton-cool-hand-fluke.z: One of the small-scale blends released under the John Patton name; not enough independent sources could be found to document its contents and character.
john-patton-cool-hand-fluke.o: No source could be found on the room note.

gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-flake-scented.z: Dark Flake Scented is the floral-topped version of the dark Gawith, Hoggarth flakes built on fire-cured Malawi and Indian leaf. In the firm's naming, "unscented" products are only sauced, while "scented" ones have a top note added on top of that. The topping here is among the most pronounced floral examples of Lakeland style, carrying an intense aroma reminiscent of geranium and rose. The slices are thick-cut, dark brown, and oily. On the smoke, the fire-cured leaf's smoky, earthy body sits side by side with the floral topping. Nicotine is very high, and the burn is slow and cool thanks to the pressed structure. Since the topping lingers strongly, dedicating a separate pipe to this type of blend is common practice. An entry for experienced smokers wanting to try the Lakeland floral style at its most intense, on a strong tobacco.
gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-flake-scented.o: A sharp floral aroma reminiscent of geranium settles over a heavy smoke scent.

bennington-tobacconist-knightsbridge.z: Knightsbridge is a dark English mixture prepared at Bennington Tobacconist's own counter. Rested golden Virginia ribbon-cut tobacco is combined with a notable share of Oriental leaf and high-grade Latakia. No flavoring is used; the taste comes entirely from the leaves themselves. The high Latakia share keeps the blend on the axis of soot, tar, and leather; the Orientals add a dry spice layer, while Virginia leaves a thin sweetness underneath. Being ribbon cut, it can be packed directly and burns evenly. It suits smokers accustomed to Latakia-forward, full-bodied mixtures; it may be heavy for those unfamiliar with smoky tobaccos.
bennington-tobacconist-knightsbridge.o: Heavy woodsmoke, burnt pine, and leather notes linger in the room for a long time.

reiver-pipes-tobacco-invictus-ember.z: This is a blend listed as aromatic in Reiver Pipes & Tobacco's Invictus line; there is not enough source material on its content and character.
reiver-pipes-tobacco-invictus-ember.o: No source could be found describing its aroma.

erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-1882-found.z: 1882 Founder's Blend is the first English mixture in Erik Stokkebye's 4th Generation line. It contains latakia, orientals, aged Virginia leaf and full-bodied burley, cut as ribbon. The latakia builds a smoky core, the orientals add a spicy, smoky layer on top, the Virginia contributes toasted bread notes and measured sweetness, and the burley provides body and a nutty base. The result is a full-bodied, distinctly smoky blend that also carries a fullness from the burley weight alongside the classic English mixture profile. It suits smokers seeking a heavy latakia and oriental character. The name refers to 1882, the year the Stokkebye family entered the tobacco business.
erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-1882-found.o: Leaves a heavy scent combining incense, wood smoke and dry spice.

milan-tobacconists-peaches-cream.z: Peaches & Cream is one of the aromatic house blends Milan Tobacconists prepares at its Roanoke shop. According to the maker's description, a thick-ribbon-cut body of black cavendish, Virginia, and burley leaves is finished with a vanilla-cream and Georgia-peach flavoring. The cavendish share gives the blend its sugar load, while burley provides body and burn balance. Suitable for smokers who enjoy fruity aromatics and want a low-nicotine, sweet everyday blend. Because the flavor level is pronounced, it's geared toward those willing to dedicate a pipe to this type of mixture. The aroma it leaves in the room is fruity and creamy-sweet.
milan-tobacconists-peaches-cream.o: Leaves an aroma of ripe peach and vanilla cream.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-north-p.z: North Pole is Ken Byron Ventures' reworking of Sutliff's limited-release holiday aromatic, North Pole Peppermint Mocha. The maker states they added Virginia leaf to the blend and pulled the mint intensity back a notch with marshmallow, and that there's no major difference between the two versions; it also notes the product has no characterizing flavor of its own and that the described tastes refer to the product's aroma. It's offered as 2 oz. bulk. Mint and a cocoa-coffee pairing stand out in the aroma; the added Virginia gives the blend a dry sweetness and a bit more body. Aimed at winter smokers who like aromatics with a pronounced room note.
ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-north-p.o: Leaves an aroma of mint, cocoa, and marshmallow.

bufflehead-three-oaks.z: Bufflehead was a brand producing small batches in the United States in the early 2000s, naming its blends after waterfowl; since no independent source describing this blend's content and character could be found, the entry has been left incomplete.

murray-sons-co-ltd-murrays-mellow-mixtur.z: One of the discontinued Virginia-Latakia-centered blends from the Belfast-based Murray Sons & Co factory; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition could not be found.

ohm-natural.z: OHM Natural is the unflavored member of the OHM line, produced in the United States. It is built from the line's common base of American-grown Virginia and Burley leaf, prepared as a ribbon cut, and sold in large-gram packaging. According to the manufacturer, no flavor casing is applied to this blend. In the smoke, Burley's dry, nutty body and Virginia's light sweetness come through directly, without the mediation of a casing. Nicotine is medium. Suitable for smokers who don't want a casing and are looking for the leaf's own taste.
ohm-natural.o: Leaves the earthy, hay-like aroma of unflavored dry leaf.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-haunted.z: Mr. Christian's Haunted Virginia is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

kaptn-brammers-frische-brise.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for Kapt'n Brammers' Frische Brise, so the profile is left incomplete; per catalog records, the blend is classified as "Aromatic."

gauntleys-of-nottingham-african-virginia.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's African Virginia blend.

stanwell-green-indigo.z: Green & Indigo is a mixture in the Denmark-based Stanwell brand's aromatic line, matching the color pair in its name with a fruit selection. Its base is a balanced black cavendish, joined by pressed and fermented ready-rubbed Virginia and burley along with light-colored wildcut Virginia leaves. The blend is presented in a 40-gram pouch and a 50-gram tin; Stanwell tobaccos are today produced under the Scandinavian Tobacco Group. Flavoring runs along blackcurrant and fresh apple; while the topping dose is pronounced, nicotine strength stays modest since the leaf base is kept light. In the maker's classification, flavor intensity is given as two-fifths, while aroma dose and room note are given as three-fifths. A suitable option for smokers who enjoy the fruity aromatic idiom but want to steer clear of a heavy vanilla-and-sugar load; the easy-lighting mixture cut means the pipe doesn't need frequent relighting.
stanwell-green-indigo.o: Leaves a fruity scent between sweet and tart, reminiscent of blackcurrant and fresh green apple.

nice-ash-cigars-aromatic-english.z: One of the house blends from Nice Ash Cigars, a tobacconist in Depew, New York; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.
nice-ash-cigars-aromatic-english.o: No description could be found in the records.

mac-baren-hh-vintage-latakia.z: HH Vintage Latakia belongs to the HH line Mac Baren launched in 2006. The series' shared principle is minimal casing on the tobacco and no applied top flavor.
