Per the manufacturer's description, the blend rests mainly on Virginia and burley, to which oriental leaves and latakia are added, yielding a loose-cut English-style mixture. Latakia's woody, smoky, leather-like line defines the blend; Virginia underneath gives measured sweetness, burley provides body and dryness, and oriental leaf draws a spicy edge. Because it's unflavored, the taste comes directly from the leaves themselves and intensifies as the smoke progresses. It sits in the medium band for nicotine. Suited to those wanting to get acquainted with smoky English and Balkan mixtures, and to smokers accustomed to blends with a high latakia proportion.
mac-baren-hh-vintage-latakia.o: Leaves a sharp, smoky note reminiscent of campfire and smoky leather.

sutliff-tobacco-company-ts19-turkish.z: TS-19 Turkish is the Oriental tobacco product in Sutliff's blending-component line. According to the maker's description, it is prepared ribbon cut from Smyrna-grade leaves, with a dark casing applied that sweetens and darkens the tobacco. Sources indicate it is one of the main Oriental options accessible to small-scale blenders. The taste runs along a line of dry hay, spice, and tangy smoke; nicotine stays low while taste intensity is high. It is generally used to add a spicy, dry layer to mixtures containing Virginia and latakia. It suits smokers who prepare their own blends and want to get to know the Oriental character in a pure form.
sutliff-tobacco-company-ts19-turkish.o: Leaves a sharp, tangy scent reminiscent of dry hay, spice, and smoke.

1776-tobacco-co-old-dominion.z: Old Dominion is a black blend made entirely from Virginia leaf, in the light aromatic group of 1776 Tobacco Company. Per the maker's recipe, the leaf is darkened through charcoal toasting and given a light flavoring; the catalog presents it as the country's first fully black blend. Since only one leaf type is used, its character rests on the caramelization of Virginia's natural sugar during toasting. The blend is notably low on nicotine; the maker describes it as an option for those transitioning from cigarettes to the pipe. Its ribbon cut makes packing and lighting easy. It can be considered a suitable starting point for smokers wanting to get to know the pipe's basic taste before turning to heavy English mixtures or heavily sauced aromatics.
1776-tobacco-co-old-dominion.o: Leaves a mellow, lightly sweet room note reminiscent of charcoal-toasted leaf.

peterson-special-reserve-2008.z: Special Reserve is Peterson's limited tin series, released each year with a different recipe; the 2008 edition was presented in a 100 gram tin. Bright orange and dark Virginia leaves are joined by black Cavendish and a nutty burley, carrying notes of bitter orange and almond. Peterson is an Irish brand; these special tins are reportedly prepared to Peterson's recipe by the German manufacturer Kohlhase, Kopp & Co. The cut is described as ribbon. Since each year of the series is a distinct blend, the tin was produced only in its release year and never repeated. It is a notable record for smokers seeking a lightly flavored, Virginia-forward aromatic and for those who collect the annual releases.
peterson-special-reserve-2008.o: Leaves a scent of almond and orange peel.

torben-dansk-jubilee-40-danish-blend.z: Torben Dansk Jubilee 40 Danish Blend is a Danish-style blend in the brand's fortieth-anniversary line; no independent source giving detail on its composition has been found.
torben-dansk-jubilee-40-danish-blend.o: Records describe it as leaving a sweet, Danish-style aromatic aroma.

john-aylesbury-corsario.z: Corsario (also labeled Corsario Island on the tin) is an aromatic blend produced for John Aylesbury by Kopp Tobaccos. Its composition includes Virginia, African Burley, South American-origin Virginia, and twice-fermented black Cavendish. The casing is built on rum, vanilla, and a subtle apricot note; the maker describes the blend as full-bodied and balanced at a four-out-of-five intensity. The tobacco is sold in a 100-gram tin. Its character is distinctly sweet and fruity; the black Cavendish share gives the smoke a creamy texture, while the Burley adds weight. Suited to smokers who enjoy flavored blends but aren't looking for something entirely light on nicotine. Given its high casing intensity, it isn't a good transition tobacco for a palate used to unflavored Virginia or English blends.
john-aylesbury-corsario.o: Leaves an aroma of rum, creamy vanilla, and a light apricot note.

tabak-trennt-smok-mi.z: Smök mi is a Tabak Trennt house blend whose name comes from a North German dialect expression; shop records state it was prepared by Karl-Heinrich Trennt in 1975. It is described as an unflavored mixture of natural tobaccos, with Latakia and Oriental leaf set over a Virginia base. Like the business's other blends, production continues at the Walter Wehde tobacco factory in Hamburg to an unchanged recipe. It is aimed at smokers seeking an unflavored English blend who value smoky and spicy notes; distribution is largely limited to the Kiel shop.
tabak-trennt-smok-mi.o: Leaves a dry trace leaning toward wood fire and smoke.

park-lane-tobacconist-christmas-kake-201.z: A one-off New Year blend Park-Lane Tobacconist released specially for 2011; no usable source describing its composition could be found.

robert-mcconnell-limited-reserve.z: Limited Reserve is an aromatic referencing the English afternoon-tea tradition. Different Virginia grades are joined by dark black cavendish and a pinch of burley; honey, vanilla, and orange lead the flavoring, with cream and scone echoes also emphasized in the recipe. The cavendish builds the blend's sweet, mild texture, while burley adds a dry body to the smoke. It is light in nicotine and pronounced in flavoring; sold in a 100-gram tin. Aimed at those who enjoy sweet, fruity aromatics and those seeking a low-tension tobacco for long, calm sessions. It is produced at the Kohlhase & Kopp facilities in Germany.
robert-mcconnell-limited-reserve.o: Evokes a scent of orange marmalade, honey, and a freshly baked scone.

smokers-haven-in-b-tween-mixture.z: IN-B-TWEEN Mixture is a discontinued mixture prepared for Smokers' Haven; sufficient sources on its composition and character could not be found.
smokers-haven-in-b-tween-mixture.o: Records did not describe the room note.

buoy-mild-blue.z: Buoy Mild is the blue-coded, mild branch of the Buoy line produced by Rouseco in North Carolina. It is prepared as a fine cut from American leaf, and calibrated to give lower strength and a softer flavor next to the line's red-coded, full-bodied branch. Suitable for those seeking an everyday, unpretentious smoke who want to keep nicotine strength low. Being a fine cut, it wants a loose fill and a slow draw.
buoy-mild-blue.o: Leaves a light, dry tobacco and hay aroma.

the-tobacco-cellar-old-toby-stash.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the blend called Old Toby Stash from the shop The Tobacco Cellar has been found.
the-tobacco-cellar-old-toby-stash.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

gbd-london-mixture.z: There is not enough independent sourcing documenting the composition and character of London Mixture, sold under the GBD name.
gbd-london-mixture.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-lipc-dehavilind.z: LIPC Dehavilind is a club blend Wilke Pipe Tobacco prepared for the Long Island Pipe Club, said to be based on an old Wilke recipe. Its construction fits what's called the American-English line: the smoky backbone of English mixtures combined with the body of American Burley. The composition includes selected Cyprian Latakia, cube-cut white Burley, Virginia, and a small amount of creamy sweet black cavendish. The cube-cut Burley burns slowly and cool, building a nutty, earthy base; Latakia adds a layer of soot and wood; Virginia provides balancing sweetness, and cavendish a soft edge. Body is medium. It suits smokers who love smoky mixtures but want a Burley-forward, evenly burning structure.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-lipc-dehavilind.o: Leaves a scent reminiscent of smoky wood, nuts, and light cream.

virginia-gold-black-and-gold.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Virginia Gold pipe tobacco called Black and Gold to record the blend's composition and character.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-tabac-du-.z: There is not enough independent documentation on The Country Squire Tobacconist pipe tobacco called Tabac du Chocolat to record the blend's composition and character.

blatter-blatter-london.z: One of Blatter & Blatter's English-style house blends; no reliable source documenting its composition could be found.

pipesandcigars-com-mark-twain.z: Mark Twain is one of the house blends sold under its own name by the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com; no sufficient independent sources documenting its content and character could be found.

erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-max-eriks-.z: Max Erik 1989 is an unadulterated Virginia blend named for the birth year of Erik Stokkebye's son, marking the family's fifth generation. Aged Virginia leaves from Georgia and North and South Carolina are pressed into cakes for a week, then sliced and presented as flake. Since no additives are used, the taste comes entirely from the leaf's own sugars; grass, light fruit and bready tones stand out. It suits Virginia enthusiasts accustomed to rubbing or folding the flake for a slow, patient smoke. Thanks to its pressed structure, the taste is expected to settle further with jar time.
erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-max-eriks-.o: Leaves a plain tobacco scent reminiscent of dry grass and baked bread crust.

players-digger-flake.z: Player's Digger Flake is a pipe tobacco blend for which there is not enough independent source material.
players-digger-flake.o: Not enough records could be found on the room note.

hearth-home-egg-nog.z: Egg Nog is regarded as the first true aromatic in the Hearth & Home series. It takes its name from the traditional winter drink made with eggs, milk, sugar, and spice, and carries a matching flavor profile of vanilla, rum, cinnamon, and nutmeg. The leaf base leans heavily on black Cavendish, well suited to carrying the topping. The blend has a low tendency to bite the tongue and burns cool. The sweetness in the tin aroma is complex but restrained; on the smoke, the spice notes come through more prominently than the vanilla. Nicotine is light. Well suited to smokers who enjoy spiced winter aromatics and want something sweet without being heavy.
hearth-home-egg-nog.o: Leaves a sweet room note reminiscent of vanilla, rum, and cinnamon-nutmeg spice.

g-l-pease-area-51.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Area 51.

grants-tobacconist-emperor-norton.z: A Grant's house blend named after Joshua Norton, San Francisco's famous local eccentric figure; there is no independent sourcing describing its composition.

exclusiv-apricot.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing was found for the Exclusiv brand's Apricot blend, so the entry has been left open; records place it in the Aromatic family.

rain-city-cigar-midnight-reserve.z: This is a house blend from Rain City Cigar, open since 1997 in Seattle's Georgetown neighborhood; there is not enough source material describing its composition and character.

tinder-box-anniversary.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Tinder Box pipe tobacco called Anniversary to record the blend's composition and character.

just-for-him-black-denim.z: One of the house blends the Just For Him tobacconist prepares at its own counter; no independent source could be found on its contents or character.

motzek-p7-cake.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called P7 Cake could be found.

jacks-tobacco-virginia-1010.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of Virginia 1010, under the Jack's Tobacco name, could be found.
jacks-tobacco-virginia-1010.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

mccranies-red-virginia-vintage-2011.z: Red Virginia is the continuation of McCranie's shop's dated, unflavored red Virginia series and follows the same logic as the Red Ribbon line: North Carolina leaf from a single harvest year, fermented and tinned as ribbon cut. The 2011 batch is among the later releases in this series, and the tins were produced by McClelland. Its profile sits on the typical axis of single-leaf Virginia blends: dark sugar and dried-fruit sweetness accompanied by a pronounced tartness. In younger tins the herbal, hay note is more upfront, shifting toward bread and jam with age. Since no other leaf or flavoring enters the mix, Virginia carries the full weight of the flavor, making the blend a reference point for those wanting to track how a single leaf type changes over the years. The series ended when the maker closed in 2018.
mccranies-red-virginia-vintage-2011.o: Leaves a faintly yeasty trace where tart dried fruit and sweet hay aromas mix.

mac-baren-amphora-original-blend.z: Amphora Original Blend is the blend that carries the series' name and has long been present on the international market. Virginia and oriental leaves are added to a burley base; presented rubbed out, ready to pack. Burley's nutty, dry character forms the body, Virginia adds measured sweetness, and oriental leaves a spicy curl in the background. Casing is light and doesn't mask the tobacco taste. Nicotine is at a medium level. Suited to smokers wanting to step away from heavily flavored blends and seeking a traditional European-style everyday smoke.
mac-baren-amphora-original-blend.o: Leaves a dry tobacco room note toward nuts and light spice.

mcclelland-oriental-mixture-no-8.z: Oriental Mixture No. 8 is from McClelland's green-label Oriental series. Per its description, leaf obtained by fully breaking up a matured red Virginia cake is combined with a generous amount of Oriental tobacco. It's one of the numbers in the series where Latakia stays furthest in the background, running along an Oriental-Virginia axis. The smoke is mild, lightly sweet, and full-bodied; the Orientals' tangy, herbal character sits atop the Virginia sweetness. Nicotine load is low-to-medium, suitable for all-day smoking. Suited to smokers wanting an Oriental blend with little or no Latakia. The brand stopped production in 2018.
mcclelland-oriental-mixture-no-8.o: Leaves a sweet hay and dried-fruit aroma, with almost no soot.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.z: This is the cocoa-flavored version of the Cândido Giovanella line, prepared by the Brazilian maker Imigrantes Fumos. Records indicate the blend uses sun-dried, lightly toasted Brazilian Virginia leaf with black Cavendish, topped with cocoa essence; the cut is ribbon. In the smoke, dark cocoa's lightly bitter sweetness combines with the Cavendish's sugary, dark tone; the Virginia base lays a bready foundation in the background. The burn is light and cool, and the nicotine load is between low and moderate. It suits smokers looking for a chocolate-flavored aromatic and a mild blend that can be smoked all day.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.o: Leaves an aroma of roasted cocoa and sweet bakery.

kramers-pipe-and-tobacco-shop-blend-for-.z: Not enough independent sources could be reached to fill out the record for Kramer's Pipe and Tobacco Shop's blend called Blend for Danny Kaye.

torben-dansk-burley.z: Torben Dansk Burley is a member of the brand's single-varietal blending-component line. It consists of unflavored Burley leaf; it is described as carrying grassy, earthy and nutty notes together with a light sweetness reminiscent of milk chocolate. It is a broad ribbon cut and burns dry. Burley is a leaf with more pronounced nicotine than Virginia and lower sugar; because of this it smokes plain and full, with little tendency to bite the tongue. Suited to home blenders wanting to add body and a carrier base to their blend, and to those after unflavored tobacco.
torben-dansk-burley.o: Leaves a dry, nutty and earthy aroma with a hint of cocoa.

mcclelland-blackwoods-flake.z: Blackwoods Flake is a slice tobacco McClelland built from only two Virginia types, pressed a second time after blending and then matured. It's counted within the firm's Personal Reserve line and presented as broken slice. In the blend, mild red Virginia's natural sweetness interweaves with stoved black Virginia's dark, spiced aroma. Double aging rounds off the flavors; the result is a profile leaning toward sweet-tart fruit, dark bread, and spice. Strength is medium, flavor intense. A record falling within the territory of those used to preparing slice tobacco who seek an unflavored, matured Virginia smoke.
mcclelland-blackwoods-flake.o: Leaves a sweet-tart fruit and spiced, lightly sooty aroma.

consolidated-502-medium-english.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Consolidated blend 502: Medium English.

paul-olsen-vanilla-snow.z: A Paul Olsen aromatic flavored with vanilla, as its name indicates; no independent source documenting its tobacco composition could be found.

wesleys-no-13-golden-flake.z: No. 13 Golden Flake is among the house blends of Wesley's, a South African tobacconist tracing its roots to the 1920s that opened its first shop in Johannesburg in 1971. The maker presents the blend under the English-type mixtures heading. It's prepared by combining medium-strength leaf flakes with Turkish (Oriental) leaf, relying on the leaf's own scent rather than casing. It's a slow-burning, not overly full blend; the maker states it's suited to outdoor smoking. The Virginia flake base gives dry hay and a measured natural sugar, while the Oriental leaf adds a grassy, woody, lightly spicy layer; this combination holds a buttery sweetness together with a dry, tart edge. It suits smokers not seeking high nicotine who lean toward the slow pace of flake cut and unflavored leaf taste.
wesleys-no-13-golden-flake.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay, wood, and a light grassy spice.

pipesandcigars-com-perique-blend-gp-11.z: No independent sources sufficient to complete a full profile of pipesandcigars.com's blend Perique Blend GP-11 could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-banana.z: Kendal Banana belongs to Gawith Hoggarth's fine shag-cut aromatic series. A banana topping is applied to light-colored Virginia leaf; the tobacco is made of fine, springy strands, kept at a moisture level suited to packing. On the smoke, banana aroma is pronounced, with the leaf taste staying light and sweet underneath. Nicotine is low and the smoke cool. Suited to smokers seeking aromatic, fine-cut tobacco. Records indicate part of this shag series began being sold under abbreviated names after packaging regulation changes in England.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-banana.o: Leaves the aroma of freshly peeled ripe banana.

robert-mcconnell-the-fragrant-blend.z: There is not enough independent source material on The Fragrant Blend, associated with the Robert McConnell name.

smokers-haven-40th-anniversary.z: A limited-run mixture among Smokers' Haven's anniversary tins; no independent source describing its composition could be found.

gatlin-burlier-black-jack-bourbon.z: Black Jack's Bourbon is one of the house blends from the Gatlinburlier tobacconist in Gatlinburg, Tennessee. It is built on Cavendish leaves prepared according to Danish tradition and flavoured with whisky; Burley is added to the mix to give body, and vanilla sweetness accompanies the bourbon note. It is a thick-textured aromatic producing plentiful, heavy smoke. Nicotine level is low, tuned so as not to leave sharpness on the palate. It suits smokers interested in aromatic blends and whisky flavouring who want to try a shop blend.
gatlin-burlier-black-jack-bourbon.o: Leaves an aroma of cooked spirits, buttery sugar, and sweet spice.

gawith-hoggarth-co-top-black-cherry.z: Top Black Cherry is Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s black-cherry-based aromatic. According to the maker's description, the blend's foundation is sweet black Cavendish put through a special double-fermentation process, joined by a ripe black-cherry flavoring. The leaf in the tin is nearly all jet black, with the rest a very dark brown; it's a medium-thick ribbon cut, and since moisture is high it arrives clumped, requiring airing before smoking. Unlike many cherry tobaccos, the aroma evokes not candy but a more bitter, dark cherry liqueur, and it becomes more pronounced on the smoke as the bowl progresses. Among the Kendal house's aromatics, it's not an example that's light on nicotine. Suited to aromatic smokers who want to feel the tobacco itself alongside an intense fruit aroma. Records indicate the same blend has been distributed as Exclusiv Black Cherry in the United Kingdom and as Top Black Cherry in North America.
gawith-hoggarth-co-top-black-cherry.o: Leaves a heavy, sweet-yet-bitter fruit aroma reminiscent of dark cherry liqueur.

mac-baren-st-bruno-ready-rubbed.z: St. Bruno Ready Rubbed is the rubbed-out version of the flake of the same name. Ogden's released this form in the 1920s, creating a directly packable option for smokers who didn't want to slice and rub out pressed tobacco. Its contents rest on the same base as the flake: mild Virginia leaves, dark-fire-cured Kentucky, and the Lakeland-style floral-fruit topping. The difference is in the preparation stage; the slices are rubbed out before packaging. The rubbed-out structure lets the tobacco burn faster and a bit quicker, though the flake version's slowly unfolding development is shortened. In the taste profile, Kentucky's smoke and the topping's rose-geranium trace again sit side by side. Nicotine level is above medium. Suited to those wanting to try the Lakeland style in ready-cut form and those seeking a practical English classic for everyday use.
mac-baren-st-bruno-ready-rubbed.o: Leaves a trace where a floral, soap-like aroma sits alongside a smoky leaf aroma.

chieftain-shipwrights-mixture.z: The Chieftain blend Shipwrights Mixture is referred to in available records as an aromatic; not enough sourcing could be found to document its content and character.
chieftain-shipwrights-mixture.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

mccranies-sharons-crossing.z: Sharon's Crossing is an unflavored Virginia blend prepared for McCranie's shop; records indicate it emerged from a McClelland-produced recipe renamed under the shop's name, but no sufficient source describing its composition could be found.

cornell-diehl-sun-bear-mountain-flower.z: No current maker or retailer record documenting the composition of this limited release, part of Cornell & Diehl's honey-themed Sun Bear series, could be found.

cornell-diehl-folklore.z: This is a Cornell & Diehl blend recorded as Virginia-based; details are left blank as it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog and no independent source could be found.

tobacco-world-contentment.z: Tobacco World is a tobacconist that has long prepared house blends in the Milwaukee area of Wisconsin. The English-style mixture called Contentment does not appear on the shop's current blend list, and no verifiable source on its composition has been found.
tobacco-world-contentment.o: No source describing its aroma has been found.

admirals-choice-gold-burley.z: Gold Burley is the Burley-centered blend of the Admiral's Choice line. The line is produced by the Dream Castle Tobacco Company under Sutliff, largely consisting of affordable, everyday-use blends. In this blend, Burley stands out with its nutty, dry, earthy character; Virginia sets the sweetness balance. Unlike the aromatic line, it carries no heavy coating; the profile relies on the leaf's own taste. Because of the fullness typical of Burley, nicotine perception is higher than its aromatic siblings. It's aimed at smokers looking for a low-flavoring, plain, American-style smoke they can repeat throughout the day.
admirals-choice-gold-burley.o: Leaves a nutty, lightly sweet, dry tobacco room note.

blenders-gold-golden-burley.z: Golden Burley is a Burley Cavendish blend from the Blender's Gold line, produced by Sutliff. Like the rest of the line, it was sold under its own brand on drugstore-chain shelves, and the same recipe was also distributed under other store brands. According to records it is now discontinued. The blend's base is vanilla-flavored Burley Cavendish. Burley's dry, nutty taste is balanced by the vanilla's sweetness; it burns cool and even, with moderate moisture in the pouch. Its nicotine is below medium, and the flavoring is noticeable but not heavy — suited to those looking for a simple Burley aromatic to smoke all day.
blenders-gold-golden-burley.o: Leaves a vanilla, faintly nutty room note.

the-eastern-company-captain.z: Captain is a product noted in the pipe tobacco line of Egypt's Eastern Company S.A.E.; since no source describing its composition and character has been found, no further detail is given.
the-eastern-company-captain.o: No described room note has been found in records.

b-b-tobacconists-llc-smokers-forums-ince.z: A limited blend prepared for a forum community; no source on its content could be found, leaving the profile blank.

e-a-carey-broad-cut-english-mixture.z: A record referred to as E. A. Carey's broad-cut English mixture; since it does not appear in the maker's current catalog, no source could be found describing its component ratios.
e-a-carey-broad-cut-english-mixture.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

lane-limited-captain-black-royal.z: Captain Black Royal is a blend using both black and golden cavendish leaves together. Per the manufacturer's description, the forward note is a pronounced vanilla aroma; the cut is ribbon, offered in pouch and tin. The smoke is soft and cool, nicotine is low. It offers a sweet profile determined more by the casing than by tobacco character; suited to smokers within the series seeking a middle ground between light and dark cavendish and wanting a pronounced room scent.
lane-limited-captain-black-royal.o: Leaves a pronounced vanilla, pastry-like sweet room note.

samuel-gawith-irish-spring-flake.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of this blend, produced by Samuel Gawith in Kendal and, according to records, a Virginia-forward flake containing Perique, could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-dwarven-mine.z: Dwarven Mine is the first blend in the maker's Sword & Board series. About a third of the mixture is Latakia, joined by steamed Virginia, toasted Burley, black Cavendish, Oriental leaf, and Danish-style casings. Despite the high Latakia share, the blend sits on the milder side of medium for smokers accustomed to smoky mixtures.
ken-byron-ventures-dwarven-mine.o: Leaves a heavy aroma of soot and pine smoke with a lightly sweet casing note layered on top.

sentimiento-nacional-soberania-de-las-is.z: A Sentimiento Nacional blend named after the sovereignty discourse over the Malvinas/Falkland Islands; no independent source describing its composition could be found.
sentimiento-nacional-soberania-de-las-is.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

borkum-riff-yellow-cavendish.z: One of Borkum Riff's regional Cavendish-based offerings referred to by color names; no adequate source on its content and flavoring could be found.

straus-tobacco-losantiville.z: No verifiable source describing the composition of this Straus house blend, which takes its name from Cincinnati's original name, could be found.

hearth-home-steamroller.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for this blend, described as Virginia-forward, from the Hearth & Home brand.

cornell-diehl-sweet-english.z: Sweet English is, as its name suggests, a blend that combines two worlds: Latakia is added to a traditional American Cavendish base of Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish, then a caramel-and-vanilla sauce is applied. It's presented ribbon cut. This places Latakia's woody, smoky character within a sweet sauce; the blend counts less as an unflavored English mixture than as an English style sitting on the aromatic wing. Nicotine stays light. Designed for smokers curious about Latakia but who find unflavored English blends too harsh, as well as those wanting to add a smoky layer to sweet aromatics.
cornell-diehl-sweet-english.o: Leaves a scent where a light wood smoke can be sensed behind vanilla-and-caramel sweetness.

ilsted-own-mixture-no-55.z: No.55, one of the numbered house blends sold under the Ilsted name, is reportedly an aromatic mixture; no source verifying its content could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
ilsted-own-mixture-no-55.o: No room note described in the records could be found.

peretti-blend-no-100.z: Blend No.100 is one of the Burley-forward house blends L.J. Peretti prepares at its Boston shop; while it appears in the maker's product list, no sufficient sources describing its content and character could be found.
peretti-blend-no-100.o: No documented recipe could be found in the records.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-john-bull.z: John Bull is a pipe-tobacco name rooted in England; its blends are produced today at Scandinavian Tobacco Group's Lane facilities in the US. Fragrant English is the line's softened Latakia version. Its composition holds Cyprus latakia, Virginia, burley, and a small amount of black cavendish; a measured top note is applied. The addition of burley and cavendish pulls the blend away from a classic English mixture toward an American-English style: there is smoke, but alongside it sits a round, lightly sweet foundation. Suited to smokers who want Latakia but find a fully dry English blend too much.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-john-bull.o: A lightly sweet cavendish scent can be detected beneath the wood smoke.

paul-olsen-honeydew.z: A blend from the My Own Blend line that originated at the Paul Olsen shop in Copenhagen; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

john-aylesbury-coconut.z: No reliable source could be found to document the contents and character of John Aylesbury's Coconut blend.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-barclay-mixture.z: No verifiable composition and character information could be compiled for Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Barclay Mixture.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-barclay-mixture.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

charles-fairmorn-golden-delight-mild-and.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the Charles Fairmorn name.

rain-city-cigar-rain-city-reserve.z: This is a house blend from Rain City Cigar, open since 1997 in Seattle's Georgetown neighborhood; there is not enough source material describing its composition and character.

danish-import-blue.z: No adequate sources were found documenting the composition or character of Danish Import Blue.

rattray-40-virginia.z: 40 Virginia is one of Rattray's unflavored, full-bodied blends. It is prepared by combining Virginia leaf ranging from bright gold to nut-brown with Burley; the tin holds a mix of ribbon cut, broken flake, and cube-cut pieces together. This mixed-cut structure keeps the burn even and builds layers of flavor at different intensities through the smoke. The blend's taste rests on natural Virginia sweetness reminiscent of honey and dry hay; Burley adds an earthy body and fullness to that sweetness. It carries no flavoring. It suits smokers curious about unflavored Virginia taste who find straight Virginia blends too thin on their own, as well as those looking for a balanced all-day blend. The Rattray name draws on the Scottish pipe-tobacco tradition; the brand's tobaccos are produced today in Germany.
rattray-40-virginia.o: Leaves a lightly sweetish tobacco aroma reminiscent of dry hay and honey.

sutliff-tobacco-company-julius-orange-j1.z: Coded J11, Julius Orange is referred to as an orange-flavored blend in Sutliff's bulk aromatic line; no independent source detailing its composition and character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-julius-orange-j1.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

richs-old-fashioned-759.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of Rich's Old Fashioned 759.

ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-vizmir.z: Yoshimi's Vizmir is a light-bowl blend in Ken Byron Ventures' Yoshimi's line. Its name comes from its two main components: soft yellow Virginia and light-colored Izmir oriental from Turkey. Cream, strawberry and rose essences are added to this skeleton. The casings aren't applied heavily; they're kept at a level that settles alongside the tobacco taste rather than masking it. The blend combines the oriental's dry, spicy, lightly musky side with Virginia's grass-and-sugar side into a floral-fruity bowl. It's not heavy in nicotine, built for long outdoor bowls. Suited to smokers seeking a fine-bowled, oriental-forward light blend rather than heavy Latakia or syrupy aromatics. Due to small-batch production, it isn't constantly on the market.
ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-vizmir.o: A creamy strawberry and rosewater scent is topped by a trace of hay-like tobacco.

peretti-1072.z: For Peretti's blend called 1072, no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

cornell-diehl-brandy-station.z: One of Cornell & Diehl's older blends noted to contain Virginia and Latakia; it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog, and not enough sourcing could be found to verify its composition.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-meriwethe.z: Meriwether, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an aromatic mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

mcclelland-no-m-93-topper.z: A blend in McClelland's M-series bulk aromatics, discontinued when the firm closed in 2018; no sufficient source documenting its contents and character could be found.

grants-tobacconist-royal-reserve.z: One of Grant's Tobacconist's house blends; there is no independent sourcing about its composition.

w-o-larsen-simply-unique.z: No reliable source could be found regarding this blend bearing the W.O. Larsen name, so its details could not be recorded.

straus-tobacco-blue-chip.z: One of the house blends classified as an English mixture from Straus Tobacconist; no verifiable source describing its composition could be found.

sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-del-rey.z: According to records, one of Sentimiento Nacional's Latakia-forward blends; no source documenting its proportions and full composition could be found.

planta-fishermans-love-navy.z: The navy-tinned member of Planta's Fisherman's Love line is a flavored blend combining coarsely cut golden Virginia leaf with a small amount of broken Burley flake. The cut isn't uniform: ribbon and broken flake sit together, and the distribution of components in the tin may not be even, with Burley usually concentrated toward the bottom. Opening the tin, the dominant scent leans toward honey and citrus; since it arrives quite moist, airing before smoking draws back some of both the scent and the moisture. In the smoke, the first puffs are distinctly sweet, recalling a honey-and-orange combination; after a few puffs Burley kicks in, subduing the sweetness and adding a dry, lightly bitter body to the blend. Strength falls between light and medium, but it carries more nicotine than its sweet aroma suggests. It suits smokers who want tobacco body within a sweet aromatic profile, rather than those looking for a plain, strong tobacco character.
planta-fishermans-love-navy.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity aroma reminiscent of honey and orange peel.

mcclelland-pal-o-mine.z: Pal O' Mine is a blend in McClelland's aromatic line called Premium Aromatics. The maker's description positions it as a calm, mellow, everyday smoke without harsh or coarse edges. The flavoring axis is peach; sources liken the aroma to baked peach dessert. Body is light, and nicotine load is low. The ribbon cut makes packing and lighting easy. Suited to smokers within the aromatic category who want a fruity, cool smoke without a heavy syrupy topping, and who especially favor a light tobacco in warm weather. Discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-pal-o-mine.o: Leaves a fruity, sweet aroma reminiscent of baked peach dessert.

ken-byron-ventures-fore-glory-2023.z: Ken Byron Ventures' 2023 limited release; though reported to be Virginia-forward, no independent source could be found to document its contents.
ken-byron-ventures-fore-glory-2023.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

chonowitsch-t-13.z: T 13 is a soft blend bringing together Kentucky, Virginia, and Maryland leaves, topped with a special Danish cavendish. The cavendish is coated in a light sweet sauce; as a result, the blend sits on the aromatic side, though the sauce is kept from masking the leaf's own taste. The body is light. The series consists of small-batch blends Danish pipe maker Jess Chonowitsch had prepared for his own pipes. It is aimed at those wanting to smoke a moderately sweet Danish mixture, without heavy sauce, throughout the day.
chonowitsch-t-13.o: A dry-grass and lightly nutty trace lies beneath the sweet cavendish aroma.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.z: This is the chocolate-flavored aromatic in Imigrantes Fumos's Cândido Giovanella line, and one of the brand's most widely available flavors in the Brazilian market. The blend includes sun-dried, lightly toasted Brazilian Virginia leaf with black Cavendish, topped with chocolate essence; the cut is ribbon and the packs run around 45 grams. In the smoke, milk chocolate's soft sweetness travels alongside the Cavendish's dark sugary tone; the burn is light and the smoke cool. Nicotine load is low. It's a suitable record for those new to sweet aromatics and those looking for a low-nicotine, long smoke.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.o: Leaves an aroma of milk chocolate and sweet dough.

mccranies-mcarris.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found on McArris, one of McCranie's Pipe Shop's house blends.
mccranies-mcarris.o: No reliable description of the aroma could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-cringle-flake-20.z: Cringle Flake is Sutliff's seasonal series released specifically for the holiday period; the 2022 edition is the fourth entry in the series. The blend is built from partly fire-cured 21-year-old red Virginia and 19-year-old perique. The flame-cured leaf undergoes a secondary fermentation via an hour of steaming before being combined with the perique, then pressed and cut into flake. Per the maker's description, the result is a layered profile carrying spicy, sharp undertones alongside natural sweetness; stone fruit, earthy spice, and molasses are the leading flavor notes. The tin includes "To / From" fields for gifting. Being a limited edition tied to a specific year, it is not in current production; it appeals to those wanting to sample the aged Virginia-perique structure.
sutliff-tobacco-company-cringle-flake-20.o: A spicy trace mixes into tart stone-fruit and molasses sweetness.

tsuge-premium-pipe-tobacco-winters-embra.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Tsuge Premium Pipe Tobacco blend Winter's Embrace has been found.

g-l-pease-caravan.z: Caravan is a G. L. Pease blend that puts Oriental leaf at the centre. A large portion made up of Turkish and Greek Oriental tobaccos is supported by Cyprus latakia's leathery, smoky flavours; New World Virginias build the blend's sweet base. In this Balkan-style mixture, the Oriental character is pronounced enough to overtake the latakia. It is prepared for smokers seeking Oriental tobacco's sharp, dry, spicy side, accustomed to full-bodied mixtures; records indicate its availability is seasonal.
g-l-pease-caravan.o: Leaves an aroma of leather, smoky wood, and dry spice.

abenaki-tobacco-co-sea-breeze.z: Sea Breeze is Abenaki Tobacco's very mild Virginia blend. Per the maker's recipe, light and dark fire-cured Virginia leaves are selected for low nicotine content; the blend's aim is to give a cool, dry smoke. The catalog makes no mention of added flavoring. Low nicotine and low flavor intensity make the blend usable all day or for long smokes. Though Virginia's natural sugar gives a measured sweetness, its structure may read as flat to those seeking intense flavor. Abenaki Tobacco was founded in Conway, New Hampshire; since its own sales site isn't live today, the blend's current status is unclear.
abenaki-tobacco-co-sea-breeze.o: Leaves a dry hay and lightly bready tobacco room note.

clan-shaw-calm-seas.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Calm Seas.

mac-baren-three-nuns-green.z: Three Nuns Green is one of the branches of the Three Nuns name, dating back to the 19th century, continued by Mac Baren. It's prepared per the curly-cut tradition: the interior holds Virginia, dark-fire-cured Kentucky, and Perique, with hand-selected Virginia leaves used as the outer wrap; the rope is sliced and presented as spiral-patterned coins. In taste, Virginia's natural sweetness and herbal, citrusy tang form the base; Kentucky adds a smoky, dry woodiness, while the Perique adds depth with plum and spice tones. Aimed at pipe smokers who like unflavored blends, pack coin cuts by rubbing out or folding, and seek a medium-strength, complex smoke.
mac-baren-three-nuns-green.o: Leaves a tobacco aroma with smoky wood, dried plum, and a faint citrus association.

pipe-republic-manston.z: No reliable sources on Pipe Republic's blend Manston could be found, so its content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

mcclelland-bayou-slice.z: Bayou Slice is a Virginia-Perique slice McClelland put into production in 2005 within the Blakeney's Best series. The name nods to the Louisiana bayou region where Perique is grown. The blend uses a generous proportion of cake-pressed and rested Louisiana Perique, joined by sweet, mild red Virginia. The dense, dark brown broken slices carry lighter-toned veins; the tin note runs earthy and spiced, reminiscent of fermenting fruit. Since it's moist straight from the tin, the slices need rubbing out and some airing. Falls within the territory of those seeking smokes that spotlight Perique's peppery and plum side.
mcclelland-bayou-slice.o: Leaves an earthy, spiced aroma reminiscent of fermenting fruit.

motzek-sunny-virgi.z: A straight blend from the Motzek workshop built on light-colored virginias; sufficient independent sources for detailed composition and character information could not be found.

motzek-night-twist.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called Night Twist could be found.

hu-tobacco-khartoum.z: Khartoum is a Latakia-forward blend in HU Tobacco's African Line. Its base is ready-rubbed Virginia, rounded out with Kentucky, Perique, black Cavendish, Caribbean-origin cigar leaf, and Cyprus Latakia. The line's starting point is to shift the usual weight distribution of English blends and produce English-style mixtures that step outside the classic mold. In Khartoum, smoky Latakia notes stand alongside the cigar leaves' spicy-sweet character; the result is a full, intensely sweet smoke. It's aimed at smokers accustomed to heavy Latakia blends.
hu-tobacco-khartoum.o: A spicy, lightly sweet tail accompanies the heavy smoke and toasted-wood aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-heines-blend.z: Heine's Blend is a burley blend whose origin predates Sutliff and which, according to records, was acquired by Sutliff Tobacco Company in 1963 and added alongside Mixture 79. The cube cut consists of light and dark burley pieces, with bright yellow Virginia flecks visible among them. A light citrus-fruit topping is applied on top. The burley side carries notes of cocoa, molasses, wood, bread, and earth along with a distinct nuttiness; the topping adds a measured, pineapple-like sweetness and tang. The cube cut burns slow and cool. A record for those seeking a body-forward American classic that sits between aromatic and unflavored burley.
sutliff-tobacco-company-heines-blend.o: Leaves a combined scent of roasted nuts and light tropical fruit.

smoke-king-avro-mixture.z: A mixture listed under the name Smoke King, classified as English style; no source about its maker and composition could be found.
smoke-king-avro-mixture.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-black-spice-b21.z: Black Spice B21 is a spiced aromatic in Sutliff's bulk "B" line, built entirely on a black cavendish base. The leaf goes through the same steaming and maturing process as the line's core blend B20; the difference lies in the topping. Cinnamon and nutmeg are used instead of vanilla. As a result, the blend places a dry, warm spice tone over a sweet cavendish base; it belongs to the family of spiced blends favored in autumn and winter. Nicotine is low, the burn is slow. Useful for smokers seeking a direction different from the classic vanilla-cherry axis of aromatics, or wanting to add a spice layer to their own blend. It's ribbon cut and sold in bulk.
sutliff-tobacco-company-black-spice-b21.o: A sweet bakery scent mixes into cinnamon and nutmeg.

sutliff-tobacco-company-matured-red-virg.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the content and character of Matured Red Virginia 515 RC-1, one of the bulk blends from Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company, could be found.

affordable-pipes-cobblestone.z: One of the bulk blends presented under its own name by the American seller Affordable Pipes; no accessible source describing its content could be found.

mcclelland-jubilee.z: Jubilee is a complex blend built from bright and matured Virginias, Turkish leaf, a small Perique share, and a small Latakia proportion. In the broken-ribbon-looking mixture, brown, chestnut, black, and light tones sit together. In the smoke, sugared walnut, dried apricot, marmalade, and woody notes come forward in turn; the Orientals often stay in front while the Perique occasionally brings a tangy edge. A structure for those who love an Oriental-forward English line where Latakia is used only as a seasoning. Discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-jubilee.o: Leaves a nutty, caramel-like, faintly smoky aroma.

tavern-tobacco-co-summit-hill.z: A blend under the Tavern Tobacco Co. name listed as an aromatic; no accessible source describing its content could be found.

chief-catoonah-tobacconist-baileys-reser.z: The entry has been left incomplete as no reliable source could be found for Chief Catoonah Tobacconist's Bailey's Reserve blend.

milan-tobacconists-celebration.z: Celebration is one of the aromatics carrying the signature of Milan Tobacconists' blender David Meyer. According to the shop's description, a processed tobacco unique to the brand is used alongside Virginia and Burley leaves; vanilla, rum, and exotic fruit notes stand out in the flavoring. Its body is kept light, while the flavor intensity is preserved; this makes it a useful option both for those newly moving into aromatic blends and for smokers who consistently prefer sweet casings. It is offered in bulk.
milan-tobacconists-celebration.o: Leaves an aroma of vanilla, rum, and tropical fruit.

peterson-standard-mixture.z: Standard Mixture is an English blend previously produced under the Dunhill name; when Dunhill's tobacco line changed hands it moved to Peterson with the same recipe and tin design. Cyprus Latakia, Turkish-origin Oriental leaf, and fire-cured Virginia are lightly toasted together; it is presented as a ribbon cut in 50 gram tins. It has a medium-bodied, nutty, mellow character; Latakia is present in the blend but not dominant the way it is in Nightcap. It suits smokers looking for a balanced English blend for all-day smoking, and is built fuller than its stablemate Standard Mixture Medium.
peterson-standard-mixture.o: Leaves a smoky wood and roasted nut aroma.

pipesandcigars-com-nations-capital.z: Nation's Capital is one of the house blends sold under its own name by the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com; no sufficient independent sources documenting its content and character could be found.

mccranies-red-ribbon-vintage-1983.z: Red Ribbon is the ribbon-cut version of McCranie's tobacconist's unflavored red Virginia blend. The 1983-stamped batch was produced from that year's harvest and shares the same leaf as Red Flake; the difference is the cut. Being based on a single harvest, it wasn't remade once the batch ran out, and later editions on record came from the 1996 and 2000 harvests. Compared to the flake version, the ribbon cut packs more easily and burns faster; in flavor, red Virginia's dark, bready sweetness stands out along with a creamy roundness from long aging. Suited to those wanting to smoke unflavored Virginia in its aged form.
mccranies-red-ribbon-vintage-1983.o: Leaves a dried-fruit-sweet, faintly creamy and tangy tobacco aroma.

sterling-tobacco-co-royal-london-dock.z: Royal London Dock is Sterling Tobacco's product tied to the English blending tradition. A small amount of cigar leaf is added to a body where latakia is used measuredly; this addition gives the blend a spicy, earthy edge. "London Dock" in the name is a historical term for tobaccos flavored with rum, and the blend does carry a noticeable casing. With this structure, the product sits at a transition point between pure English blends and the flavored American tradition. Suited to smokers wanting both smoke and sweetness together, seeking a profile that departs from the classic English mixture.
sterling-tobacco-co-royal-london-dock.o: A sweetish casing and the earthy trace of cigar leaf mix into latakia's smoke scent.

4noggins-britts-balkan.z: Britt's Balkan is 4noggins' take on the Balkan style. The dominant note comes from Oriental leaves, accompanied by a notable proportion of Latakia, Turkish tobacco, and a base of red, bright, and flake Virginias. Records indicate the blend's creator, Rich Gottlieb, took inspiration from Sam Gawith's Perfection and added a very small amount of vanilla to round out the smoke. Given the weight of Oriental and the Latakia ratio, flavor intensity runs high, while the sweetener contribution is barely perceptible — the blend isn't considered an aromatic. It suits experienced smokers seeking the true Balkan structure, where Latakia stays in the shadow of the Oriental leaf.
4noggins-britts-balkan.o: Leaves a spicy, faintly sweet trace beneath heavy incense and wood-smoke aroma.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-zeal-champagne.z: Zeal Champagne is a light McGahey blend built on black cavendish and Virginia, flavored in the direction of vanilla. The dark cavendish share cools the burn and gives a sweet softness; the nicotine strength is kept low. It comes in ready-rubbed bulk ribbon form and has a construction that those new to aromatic tobacco can comfortably use.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-zeal-champagne.o: Leaves an aroma of sweet vanilla and candied fruit.

pipesandcigars-com-coco-nut.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of the pipesandcigars.com blend called Coco-Nut.

iwan-ries-affinity.z: No verifiable source could be found for this blend registered under the Iwan Ries name.

mac-baren-hh-burley-flake.z: HH Burley Flake is the burley-centered member of the HH line Mac Baren launched in 2006, named after the initials of founder Harald Halberg. Burley leaves gathered from three continents form the body of the blend, accompanied by mature Virginias and a small amount of fire-cured Kentucky. The leaves are pressed into a block and sliced into flake form. As with the rest of the series, casing is kept to a minimum and no top flavor is used. In the smoke, nutty, earthy and woody burley notes lead; the Virginias play a balancing role in the background with a tangy ripe-fruit sweetness, while the Kentucky adds spicy, smoky depth. The nicotine load is notable, making it suited to experienced smokers seeking burley character and a filling body. Since the flake burns slowly, it suits those accustomed to rubbing and drying before packing.
mac-baren-hh-burley-flake.o: Leaves a note of dry walnut shell and woody smoke, with a light molasses sweetness in the background.

mr-bs-buccaneer.z: Buccaneer is an aromatic blend in Canadian Brigham's Mr. B's line. Black cavendish, burley, and virginia leaves are worked with a casing of Barbados rum, chocolate, and raisin; the blend was previously sold under the name Mr. B's Jamaican Rum. The taste sits between medium and full, with cocoa and dark-sugar tones standing out.
mr-bs-buccaneer.o: Leaves a dark, sweet aroma reminiscent of a rum, cocoa, and raisin blend.

4noggins-catamount.z: Catamount is a mild aromatic built by combining mature Virginia leaf with black Cavendish and toasted Cavendish. The name comes from the local word for mountain lion used in Vermont. According to the manufacturer, toasting the Cavendish is meant to lock the leaf's natural sweetness inside. On the flavoring side, vanilla leads while cherry remains only a faint trace in the background. Nicotine sits between mild and moderate, with flavor in the same range. It's a suitable blend for smokers who avoid heavily topped aromatics but still want to sense the sweetness underneath the tobacco.
4noggins-catamount.o: Leaves a sweet, vanilla-forward aroma carrying a thin trace of cherry.

cornell-diehl-reverie.z: Reverie is a member of Cornell & Diehl's four-blend Serenity series; the series splits into Latakia and non-Latakia blends and also includes the blends Repose, Consolation, and Comfort. Reverie is built on black Cavendish and cube-cut Burley; Perique, Latakia, and Turkish tobacco are added as small touches. Per head blender Jeremy Reeves' description, the blend is designed for calm, quiet moments. Thanks to its structure where Oriental leaf is noticeable and natural sugar comes forward, it's well suited to long-term aging. Suited to smokers wanting an unflavored, Burley-focused blend with a small amount of smoke and spice.
cornell-diehl-reverie.o: Leaves a soft, lightly smoky tobacco scent mingling with dry hay and spice notes.

cornell-diehl-woodstock-races.z: No listing for Cornell & Diehl's Woodstock Races blend could be found in the maker's current catalogue or in major retailer listings; its composition could not be confirmed.

reiver-pipes-tobacco-steelcap.z: Steelcap is a traditional Scottish-style mixture in which Latakia builds the smoky backbone while aged red Virginia adds depth and natural sweetness. Izmir Oriental brings dry spice and complexity, and black Cavendish along with a touch of Burley supply body and smoothness. It is a ribbon cut; reports note it burns dry, leaves no residue in the bowl, and requires few relights. Though full-bodied, its structure isn't scattered; it suits people used to Latakia-heavy blends looking for an unflavored, smoky smoke. It is named after the steel cap worn by border reivers. Since Reiver Pipes & Tobacco is a small-scale blender, production is done in batches.
reiver-pipes-tobacco-steelcap.o: Leaves an intense wood-soot and sweet-spice aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-westminster.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Sutliff Tobacco Company's Westminster pipe tobacco could be found.

cornell-diehl-miskatonic-mixture.z: No adequate source documenting the composition and character of Cornell & Diehl's Miskatonic Mixture could be found; the blend isn't in the maker's current catalogue.

bosphorus-istanbul-flake.z: İstanbul Flake is a flake where matured and fermented Oriental tobaccos are combined with cavendish, yellow Virginia and a small amount of burley. A very small hazelnut aroma is added on top; the dominant character is the Oriental's spicy taste, and this makes the Virginia proportion hard to distinguish. Strength and flavor are medium, nicotine satisfying. The slices come moist; when broken up and rested for a few days in an open jar, the tobacco's natural aromas become more pronounced. The recipe has been reworked over time. A blend suited to smokers seeking a low-flavoring, Oriental-forward, genuine tobacco taste.
bosphorus-istanbul-flake.o: A light toasted-hazelnut note accompanies the spicy Oriental tobacco aroma.

mcclelland-master-penman.z: Master Penman is one of McClelland's aromatic blends born within the Greater Kansas City Pipe Club circle. It's named after Mike Sull, a club member and calligrapher who prepared the calligraphy for official White House invitations. The blend's base is the trio of Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish; over it, pecan, cinnamon, and rum essences are applied in a measured balance. The smoke is mild and tongue bite is kept low; drawn through the retrohale, a buttery aroma leaning toward rum and light vanilla appears. Body stays light, placing the blend in a range smokable at any hour of the day. Structured for those on the aromatic side who don't want the flavoring to mask the tobacco. Production ended when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-master-penman.o: Leaves a buttery pastry, cinnamon, and light rum aroma.

ken-byron-ventures-count-shagula.z: One of Ken Byron Ventures' limited releases, its name a nod to a fine shag cut; no accessible maker's profile could be found to document its contents.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-colts-che.z: The cherry-flavored version of the Colts line; no independent source describing the blend's leaf composition could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-colts-che.o: No detailed description of the room note could be found in the records.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-skandinav.z: Referred to as the Skandinavik series member kept with low casing; no sufficient source detailing its content and character could be found.

watch-city-cigar-flake-558.z: No sufficient source could be found regarding this house blend from Watch City Cigar, so its details could not be recorded.

w-o-larsen-limited-edition-2015.z: No independent source sufficient to complete a record could be found regarding W.O. Larsen's Limited Edition 2015 blend, so this entry remains incomplete.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-punchbowl.z: According to records, a medium-bodied blend built on Virginia and latakia, blended by Scandinavian Tobacco Group; no detail is given since no source besides a single community record could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-punchbowl.o: No detailed description of the room note could be found in the records.

wessex-directors-choice.z: No sufficient verifiable information could be found from maker or retailer sources regarding Wessex Director's Choice.
wessex-directors-choice.o: According to the records, no scent description has been documented.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-fancy-pipe-tobac.z: No reliable source giving content and character information could be found for Kohlhase & Kopp's blend registered as Fancy Pipe Tobacco.

hearth-home-fusilers-ration-special-rese.z: Fusilier's Ration is the Marquee series' Latakia-forward blend offered as a crumble cake. Plentiful Cyprian Latakia and the most aromatic Oriental varieties are joined by sweet bright Virginia to lift the flavor; unflavored black Cavendish is used to add body. The finish carries a subtle, old-style light top note. Special Reserve is a specially prepared version of this recipe. According to the blender, the blend was designed as a tribute to Bengal Slices. Bright, smoky flavor and an incense-like aroma stand out; it burns cool with a short finish. Suited to smokers accustomed to crumbling cake tobacco who love classic Latakia-forward English mixtures.
hearth-home-fusilers-ration-special-rese.o: Leaves an incense-like, smoky, and lightly sweet aroma.

georgetown-tobacco-cafe-noisette.z: Referred to as one of Georgetown Tobacco's aromatic shop blends; although its name suggests a coffee-and-hazelnut air, no verifiable sourcing describing its composition could be found.
georgetown-tobacco-cafe-noisette.o: No record of the room aroma could be found.

wessex-wild-cut-supreme.z: Wild Cut Supreme is a black-cavendish-forward aromatic among the English-origin pipe tobaccos gathered under the Wessex name. The Wessex name comes from the pipe brand of Hall & Fitzgerald, whose hallmark was registered in England in the late 19th century; today the name survives only in this tobacco line. Virginia leaf serves as the base, but black cavendish is proportionally more dominant; the cut consists of coarse, moist pieces. The tin gives an impression of chocolate, raisin, and a light nuttiness. The smoke is thick and plentiful, and the burn temperature is low; even drawn quickly, it tends not to bite the tongue. Since nicotine stays light, it suits not so much smokers seeking heft as those wanting a sweet, soft aromatic for long pipe sessions during the day.
wessex-wild-cut-supreme.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly nutty scent reminiscent of cocoa and raisins.

edwards-ambrosia.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Ambrosia, a pipe tobacco from Edward's. Edward's is a tobacconist business based in Tampa, Florida.

cornell-diehl-suwar.z: No listing for Cornell & Diehl's Suwar blend could be found in the maker's current catalogue or in major retailer listings; its composition and character could not be confirmed.

g-l-pease-southfarthing.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Southfarthing.

dan-tobacco-devils-holiday.z: Devil's Holiday is an aromatic blend in which black Cavendish and golden Virginia leaf are flavored with a forest-fruit casing. It takes its name from the 1933 jazz tune of the same title. The fruit aroma is noticeable as soon as the tin is opened; it is ribbon cut. Over the natural tobacco tones sits a sweetness leaning toward red fruit, particularly blackberry and raspberry. On the maker's own scale, strength is rated two out of five; it burns cool and even, without needing frequent relights. Suited to smokers wanting a pronounced fruity aroma in a low-nicotine, easy-to-manage blend.
dan-tobacco-devils-holiday.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity scent reminiscent of a red-forest-fruit herbal tea.

mr-bs-black-cavendish.z: Mr. B's Black Cavendish is a blend built entirely on black cavendish, part of the line Canadian Brigham markets under its own name. It is presented coarse cut in 50-gram pouches; according to the recipe no separate flavoring is added, and the sweetness comes from the character the leaf gains during steam processing.
mr-bs-black-cavendish.o: Leaves a soft aroma carrying dark sugar and a lightly toasted sweetness.

peter-stokkebye-peach-honey.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Peach & Honey in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

paul-olsen-jubilaeums-blandingen.z: A blend from the My Own Blend line that originated at the Paul Olsen shop in Copenhagen; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

drucquer-sons-blend-805.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Blend 805, a pipe tobacco from Drucquer & Sons.
drucquer-sons-blend-805.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

tabacos-cisne-branco-finamore-ltda-irlan.z: Irlandez, a pipe tobacco from Tabacos Cisne Branco Finamore Ltda.; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

von-eicken-piccolo-vanilla.z: Piccolo Vanilla is the vanilla version of Von Eicken's Piccolo plug series. The series is prepared by cutting pressed Cavendish into broken flake, each piece wrapped in paper sized to a single bowlful. A faint vanilla note is noticeable on opening the pack; once lit, it recedes and the Cavendish's own sweetness comes forward. Records describe it as the series' lowest-intensity member in terms of flavoring. Nicotine is low and flavor is moderate. Suited to those after a lightly flavored aromatic without a heavy scent.
von-eicken-piccolo-vanilla.o: Leaves a faint vanilla and sweet Cavendish aroma.

peterson-holiday-season-2016.z: Holiday Season is Peterson's limited-edition, Christmas-themed aromatic tin series released each year; the 2016 edition was presented in a 100 gram tin. Broadly cut and broken-flake Burley, ribbon-cut black Cavendish, and pieces of bright Virginia are combined with an apricot liqueur flavoring. Peterson is an Irish brand, but the blending and production of these special tins is outsourced; records indicate they were made by the Scandinavian Tobacco Group to a recipe specified by Peterson. The cut is described as a mixed cut. Because the recipe changes each year, every edition of the series counts as a distinct blend; the 2016 tin was likewise prepared for its release year and never reprinted. It is a notable record for smokers seeking flavored, sweet-profile tins and for those who collect the annual limited editions.

wellauer-co-kentucky.z: This blend, registered under the Wellauer name and apparently based on fire-cured Kentucky leaf, does not appear in current product listings, and no source could be found documenting its details.
wellauer-co-kentucky.o: No description could be found as no source was available.

rattray-highland-targe.z: Highland Targe is a Scottish-style mixture bringing together Virginia, Oriental tobacco, Latakia, and black Cavendish in ribbon cut. It lights easily, gives plenty of smoke, and stays cool throughout the bowl; the ash stays light and doesn't noticeably wet the pipe. In taste, Virginia's sugary side, the Oriental leaf's fruity-spicy sweetness, and Latakia's smoke form a balanced triangle. In the second half of the bowl the body firms up somewhat, though the coolness doesn't break down. It suits smokers looking for an easy-smoking, all-day mixture with a measured Latakia proportion; smoked quickly it is prone to heating up, so a slow pace is needed.
rattray-highland-targe.o: Leaves a trace where light smoky wood and sweet tobacco aroma mix.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-black-cavendish-.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Black Cavendish (American) blend.

cornell-diehl-sun-bear-tupelo.z: Sun Bear Tupelo is a link in Cornell & Diehl's Sun Bear series, built around varieties of honey. Bright and red Virginia leaf are joined by 2019-harvest Basma and 2018-harvest Izmir Orientals; the blend is presented as flake. It takes its name from tupelo honey gathered from Florida's wetland forests; the casing adds notes of silver tequila and elderflower alongside the honey. On the flavor side it builds an intense but creamy, round profile; the Oriental leaf carries the floral side, Virginia the sweet base. Being a limited-quantity release, it isn't currently available on the market; records indicate production was capped at 20,000 tins. The flake cut and this composition make it well suited to cellaring.
cornell-diehl-sun-bear-tupelo.o: Leaves a lightly herbal scent with a floral honey sweetness.

pipesandcigars-com-nut-cluster.z: Nut Cluster is one of the house blends sold under its own name by the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com; no sufficient independent sources documenting its content and character could be found.

lane-limited-blwb.z: BLWB is Lane Limited's bulk-sold, burley-based blend. Its name comes from the initials of the manufacturer's own promotional phrase "Burley Light Without a Bite"; it's built with the aim of putting burley's known tendency to bite the tongue in the background. The blend adds lightly flavored cavendish to a burley core; cocoa brings burley's own nutty, bready taste forward while softening the smoke. Body stays light, making it suitable for long, all-day smoking. Suited to smokers seeking a balance between aromatic and unflavored blends, wanting to taste burley character without heavy casing.
lane-limited-blwb.o: Leaves a lightly sweet tobacco note toward cocoa and nuts.

cornell-diehl-elegant-emu.z: A blend recorded under the Cornell & Diehl name, noted as an American type; its content and character could not be verified, as it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-brentor-whiskey.z: Brentor Whiskey is one of the house blends prepared for the Exeter-based McGahey The Tobacconist shop. It is a Virginia and cavendish leaf composition that appears entirely brown; the blend is given a malt-whisky-based flavoring. The manufacturer's description notes the blend is kept light and set so as not to bite the tongue. The nicotine strength is low and the flavor level medium; the whisky note accompanies the tobacco's natural sugar without covering it. Suitable for those new to flavored blends and for those looking for a light aromatic they can smoke throughout the day. Records indicate the same blend has occasionally also been listed as Brentor Perique. McGahey has been operating as a tobacconist in Exeter since 1880; the shop on High Street closed in 2019, with sales continuing through the Topsham address.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-brentor-whiskey.o: Leaves a grainy, lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of malt whisky.

sutliff-tobacco-company-tobacco-galleria.z: Classic Chocolate is a chocolate-flavored blend in Sutliff's Tobacco Galleria line. According to the maker's description, top-grade black cavendish and dark burley leaves go through a three-stage blending process and a three-stage flavoring process; the casing uses cocoa together with vanilla essence. The cut is ribbon. On the smoke, cocoa sweetness leads, with the dark burley building an earthy, nutty base beneath it. Nicotine is moderate and taste intensity stays medium. It is a blend for those who like classic sweet American aromatics, especially the cocoa-vanilla line.
sutliff-tobacco-company-tobacco-galleria.o: Leaves a scent of warm cocoa and vanilla pastry.

ken-byron-ventures-mountains-of-madness.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to fill in the profile of Ken Byron Ventures' Mountains of Madness.

peter-heinrichs-no-69.z: No. 69 is a house blend Peter Heinrichs describes as bringing forward the unflavored leaf's own taste. The composition contains Virginia to smooth the smoke, black Cavendish to add softness to the body, Burley for depth, and a small amount of Java and Oriental leaf for spice. The ribbon cut gives an even burn. The profile is close to a medium-bodied Danish-Scottish tradition built without a sweetening topping: the bready Burley base, Virginia's measured sugar, and the Oriental leaf's dry spice are all noticeable together. It offers a middle-ground option for smokers who don't want an aromatic but also don't want to jump into strong English blends.
peter-heinrichs-no-69.o: Leaves a bready, lightly spicy, dry-leaf aroma.

j-p-couvert-cordemoy.z: This is a blend under the French J.P. Couvert name; no reliable source describing its content and character could be found.

century-liquorice-sambuca.z: A blend in the Century line known for a licorice-and-anise sambuca aroma; no sufficient independent source could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-zombie-english.z: A small-batch edition referred to among Ken Byron Ventures' English-type blends; not enough sources could be found to document its composition and character.
ken-byron-ventures-zombie-english.o: Could not be described due to lack of accessible records.

cornell-diehl-opening-night.z: Opening Night is a pressed flake Cornell & Diehl builds purely from Virginia leaf. Per the maker's description, the body is shared between full-bodied red Virginias and fine-structured bright Virginias. Once pressed and sliced, the resulting flake carries the red leaf's breadlike dark sweetness alongside the bright leaf's grassy, citrus line. It carries no casing — all the sweetness comes from the leaf's own sugar. Whether the flake is rubbed out or folded for packing adjusts the burn pace; smoked too fast, it can show the tongue bite typical of Virginias. Suited to smokers wanting to get to know a straight Virginia line and looking for a blend well suited to aging.
cornell-diehl-opening-night.o: Leaves a light citrus note mingling with a scent of dry hay and baked bread.

cascade-cigar-tobbaco-satisfaction.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Satisfaction under the Cascade Cigar & Tobbaco brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

iwan-ries-three-star-blue.z: Three Star Blue is the best-known member of Iwan Ries & Co.'s Three Star line, running since the 1950s, and for many years sold only at the Chicago shop. Over a base of sweet Virginia, nutty Burley, and toasted black Cavendish, a pronounced but measured Latakia share is added along with a very small touch of Perique; it's presented in a coarse cut. The top flavoring brings a fruity sweetness and a single floral note. This places the blend on a middle path between pure aromatic and English style: the flavoring is noticeable, but the smoky, nutty tobacco taste isn't suppressed. It suits smokers wanting to move from aromatic toward unflavored blends, or looking for a lightly smoky aromatic.
iwan-ries-three-star-blue.o: Beneath a lightly fruity, floral sweetness, a subtle smoky aroma can be detected.

faders-hopkins.z: Not enough independent sourcing documenting the composition and character of Hopkins, one of the house blends of the Baltimore-based Fader's tobacconist, could be found.

watch-city-cigar-english-ernie-ental.z: English Ernie-ental is an English mixture with a pronounced Oriental side, built by adding Macedonian Prilep Oriental and Latakia over matured red Virginia and stoved Virginia. Its name is a play on words referencing the shop's blender, Ernie.
watch-city-cigar-english-ernie-ental.o: A tart leaf scent accompanies the wood-smoke and dry-spice aroma.

nording-no-2.z: One of the numbered blends tied to the Nording name; no reliable source describing its composition and character could be found.

peretti-blend-dd.z: This is a shop blend L.J. Peretti lists in its Burley group and continues to produce; no published source describing its composition and flavor character could be found.

mac-baren-navy-flake.z: Navy Flake is a Mac Baren classic continuing the rum-flake concept tied to sailors' tradition. Burley forms the base of the blend, joined by sweet Virginias and the brand's own Cavendish; rum and a small amount of honey are applied to the leaf before pressing. The leaves are pressed and cut into golden-colored slices that break up easily. The tin note carries light rum, honey, and tones reminiscent of plum wine. In the smoke, Burley's body is felt, softened by Virginia's fruity, citrusy sweetness and the rum topping. Nicotine proportion is medium. When airing and packing are handled with care, the burn proceeds without trouble; packed tightly, it gives a slow-burning, cool smoke. Suited to those seeking rum flakes together with Burley body.
mac-baren-navy-flake.o: A light plum tone mixes into a sweet aroma reminiscent of rum and honey.

robert-mcconnell-ready-rubbed.z: Ready Rubbed is a blend of Virginia, Oriental, and African Burley leaf presented as a rubbed, broken-flake cut. Virginia supplies natural sweetness, Oriental a light spiciness, and Burley a dry body. Moisture is kept low so the leaf can be packed straight from the tin. Nicotine is moderate and flavor intensity medium; it lights easily and burns evenly. It is prepared for smokers who want an easy-to-manage, all-day mixture. The brand traces back to 1848 London; production today takes place in Germany.
robert-mcconnell-ready-rubbed.o: Leaves a dry-hay, nutty grain aroma.

cup-o-joes-high-peaks-red.z: High Peaks Red is a cherry-cased aromatic in Cup O' Joes' bulk High Peaks line. A combination of Cavendish and black Cavendish leaf is topped with a heavy cherry sauce; ribbon cut. Nicotine is very low, tobacco flavor stays in the background; what comes forward is the cherry casing. Suited to smokers looking for a heavily cased, low-body tobacco and leaning toward classic fruit aromatics.
cup-o-joes-high-peaks-red.o: Leaves a pronounced cherry and sweet-sugar scent.

park-lane-tobacconist-park-avenue.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Park Avenue, one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

samuel-gawith-pure-latakia.z: Pure Latakia, as the name states, consists of a single leaf type: Cyprus-style smoke-cured Latakia. Latakia is obtained by treating sun-cured Oriental leaf indoors with brush and wood smoke; this process imparts the scent of soot, tar, and resin to the leaf. Its nicotine is low, its flavor extremely intense. Samuel Gawith offers this product not as a stand-alone smoke but as a component blenders add to their own mixtures. Smoked alone the taste stays one-dimensional and sharp; in English and Balkan-style mixtures it is balanced with Virginia and Oriental leaf. A raw-material record for smokers building their own blends.
samuel-gawith-pure-latakia.o: Spreads a scent of wood fire, soot, and cured leather through the room and lingers long.

mac-baren-hh-vintage-syrian.z: HH Vintage Syrian was introduced in 2006, the year Mac Baren launched the HH line; the HH in the series' name stands for founder Harald Halberg's initials. Nearly half the blend's volume is Syrian latakia, and this leaf defines the overall smoky character. Turkish oriental is added for a spicy note, Virginias gathered from three continents for natural sweetness, and a small amount of American fire-cured Kentucky for body and depth. The product is presented as a loose cut, giving an even, cool burn. As Syrian latakia stocks ran out, the blend was discontinued after 2017. Mac Baren introduced HH Vintage Latakia, prepared with Cyprus latakia, in its place; since the two leaves' characters differ, the proportions were also changed. Today it's a record of interest to those seeking latakia-forward Balkan-type blends, findable only in old tins.
mac-baren-hh-vintage-syrian.o: Leaves a heavy, smoke-toned room note reminiscent of smoked wood and spice.

esoterica-tobacciana-st-ives.z: St. Ives is an aromatic-leaning English blend sold under the Esoterica Tobacciana brand, produced at the J.F. Germain & Son house in Jersey. Dark and golden Virginia leaves are combined with black Virginia cavendish; Greek and Cypriot Oriental leaves and Latakia are added on top. In the final step, a light fruit essence is applied, so the record sits somewhere between an English blend and an aromatic. In the smoke, Latakia does not build a pronounced wall; it stands more as a smoke and leather note behind Virginia's sweetness, while the fruit flavouring gives a sharpness close to citrus and apricot. Being light to medium in nicotine, it suits smokers seeking a blend they can smoke all day, who don't want the full weight of English blends. The Esoterica line is prepared for the American market but produced in the British Isles.
esoterica-tobacciana-st-ives.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, dried-apricot-like fruity aroma settling over woodsmoke.
