Being light on nicotine, it suits long sessions; however, given its high sugar content, it can bite the tongue if not smoked slowly. Designed for smokers seeking the fruity aromatic line who favor blends where the top note stands out more than the leaf taste.
hearth-home-berry-nice.o: Leaves a pronounced blackberry-jam aroma and a sugary sweetness.

hu-tobacco-english-breakfast.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of English Breakfast, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

clan-shaw-high-seas.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend High Seas.

von-eicken-bayside-virginia-blend.z: Bayside Virginia Blend is the unflavored Virginia mixture in Von Eicken's Bayside line. It is prepared solely from Virginia leaf using traditional methods, cut to a medium ribbon, and comes in a 100-gram tin. The flavor profile sits on the side of young, light-colored Virginias: sharp citrus, grass and hay notes come forward, with a measured sweetness in the background. Nicotine is low to medium. Suited to smokers wanting to get to know unflavored Virginia character, or seeking a light Virginia for all-day smoking.
von-eicken-bayside-virginia-blend.o: Leaves a fresh aroma reminiscent of dry hay and citrus peel.

frederick-tranter-extravaganza.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Frederick Tranter's Extravaganza blend.

former-straight-grain-flake.z: Straight Grain Flake is a pressed flake in the Virginia-perique wing of the Former line, taking its name from pipe maker Hans "Former" Nielsen's grain-pattern naming. It is untopped and built on the same base as its counterpart in the series, Cross Grain Flake. The perique proportion is notably higher than in Cross Grain Flake, so plum, fig, and peppery spice tones come forward enough to potentially overtake the Virginia sweetness. Its body is fuller and it calls for a slow smoke. It is aimed at experienced VaPer smokers who want a pronounced perique presence.
former-straight-grain-flake.o: Leaves a lightly sharp aroma reminiscent of dried plum and black pepper.

sutliff-tobacco-company-buttered-rum.z: Sutliff Buttered Rum is a ribbon-cut bulk blend combining golden Virginia with soft white burley, topped with a buttery combination of New England and Jamaican rums. The maker's description positions the blend as a "light aromatic"; the topping is noticeable but doesn't overpower the leaf beneath. Nicotine fullness is measured and the smoke follows a straightforward line; it's described as an aromatic suited to all-day smoking. Suited to those seeking a sweet rum-and-butter profile with a lasting room note, as well as those wanting a base tobacco to soften heavier sweet blends.
sutliff-tobacco-company-buttered-rum.o: Leaves a scent of buttered rum and caramel.

sutliff-tobacco-company-medium-english-5.z: Medium English #502, part of Sutliff's numbered bulk line, is, as its name suggests, a medium-strength English mixture; records indicate it combines Virginia, burley, latakia, Oriental, and perique. The blend is also noted to be sold in pouch form in Canada under the Brigham brand. Because of the scarcity of published independent sources, details of its character are limited.
sutliff-tobacco-company-medium-english-5.o: Leaves a woody, smoky scent from the latakia.

motzek-puhwapwap.z: Puhwapwap is a burley twist belonging to the Motzek workshop's rested line, called "aged." In its production, strong burley leaves are held for three to five years, then macerated for about six months in a plant-and-spice liquid based on an old recipe, wound into a twist, and rested for another six months. Rose petals are also placed inside the vacuum pack; these can be loaded into the bowl along with the tobacco. In the dry scent, floral and soapy associations stand out more than tobacco. The smoke has a medium-to-full body with an herbal-spicy sharpness reminiscent of perique, and the nicotine load sits at the upper end of the line. It is a specialty product meant for occasional rather than everyday smoking; suitable for smokers open to the twist format and unusual herbal-floral profiles.
motzek-puhwapwap.o: Leaves a floral aroma reminiscent of a mix of rose and dried herbs.

the-smoker-favorite.z: Favorite is recorded as one of the hand-prepared house blends from The Smoker, a tobacconist that operated in Albany from the 1930s until 2011; no independent source describing the blend's composition could be found.

borkum-riff-classic-pure-tobacco.z: Marketed as one of Borkum Riff's lower-topping versions. No independent source describing its composition and character could be found, leaving the profile incomplete.
borkum-riff-classic-pure-tobacco.o: According to records it leaves a room note close to plain tobacco.

bosphorus-master-grasshoppe.z: Master & Grasshoppe is a ribbon-cut Latakia blend built from golden Virginia, Latakia and cavendish. Flavor casing is low; in the smoke there is a light fruity, tart note whose type is not clearly definable, but this note does not overshadow Latakia's taste. The cavendish proportion is kept measured. Its moisture level is ready for direct filling, it lights easily, and the smoke runs soft. Its strength is medium. Suitable for smokers wanting to try Latakia blends together with the spicy structure of Turkish tobaccos.
bosphorus-master-grasshoppe.o: The Latakia's smoke and burnt-wood aroma settles into the room and lingers.

davidoff-danish-mixture.z: Danish Mixture is a Davidoff blend following the Danish-style aromatic approach. Toasted black cavendish is added to Virginia and burley leaves for a balanced body; the cut is a loose mixture. The topping is kept measured; the tobacco's own taste is preserved enough to stand ahead of the flavoring. Its fullness is light, and the smoke is soft. It suits smokers seeking a Danish-style, lightly flavored blend smokable all day.
davidoff-danish-mixture.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly nutty scent sitting over the toasted tobacco.

drucquer-sons-casbah.z: Casbah is a Balkan-style blend combining red and light Virginia leaves with plenty of small-leaf oriental tobacco and Cyprus latakia. The mixture is pressed into a block and cut into pieces, giving the smoker the option to rub out or slice the leaf before packing the pipe. On the taste line, Virginia's tart sweetness, the orientals' creamy, round texture, and latakia's woody smoke coming from behind all sit side by side. The blend is part of a line reorganized from Drucquer & Sons' old recipes; per records, the line's current form is produced at Cornell & Diehl through Gregory Pease's work. The brand's origin traces to a tobacconist tradition founded in 1841, with production now taking place in the United States. It suits smokers used to preparing block tobacco who want a latakia- and oriental-forward mixture with above-medium fullness in nicotine.
drucquer-sons-casbah.o: Leaves a soot scent dominated by wood smoke, carrying dry grass and a light sweetness underneath.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-holt-blackcherry.z: Holt Blackcherry is the sour-cherry-flavored house blend listed under the Holt name at McGahey The Tobacconist; sufficient sources regarding its leaf composition and cut could not be found.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-holt-blackcherry.o: Leaves a fruity aroma carrying sour-cherry sweetness.

pipesandcigars-com-firestorm.z: No sufficient sources were found documenting the content and character of pipesandcigars.com's blend Firestorm.

cest-la-vie-french-vanilla.z: C'est La Vie French Vanilla is a soft cavendish blend built largely from hot-air-cured leaf. The leaf is lightly pressed and cut using the traditional cavendish method, and in the process is paired with a sweet, creamy casing leaning toward French vanilla. While its aroma spreads noticeably into the room, the flavor stays fainter than expected; the smoke is light and soft on the tongue. It burns cool. Suitable for smokers seeking the familiar vanilla line of pouch aromatics, wanting a low-nicotine, easy-smoking blend.
cest-la-vie-french-vanilla.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and cream aroma that fills the room.

low-country-pipe-cigar-peach.z: Peach is a blend in Low Country Pipe & Cigar's bulk aromatic line, carrying a pronounced peach casing over a ribbon-cut Virginia base. The casing intensity is more forward than other members of the line, and the fruity taste persists throughout the smoke. It's a light, mild blend in terms of nicotine, aimed at those wanting a light, sweet aromatic in the summer months.
low-country-pipe-cigar-peach.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity room note reminiscent of ripe peach.

barclay-rex-rexey.z: One of Barclay Rex's shop blends marketed as a mild aromatic; no independent source documenting its content could be found.
barclay-rex-rexey.o: According to records it leaves a sweet, mellow room note.

tabac-manil-la-volute.z: La Volute, a pipe tobacco from Tabac Manil; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

sullivan-powell-gentlemans-mixture-origi.z: Sullivan & Powell was a tobacconist established in London's Burlington Arcade, blending tobacco, according to records, since the 1880s. Gentleman's Mixture was the house's classic Virginia-oriental mixture; prepared with leaf from various regions, it combined mature Virginia's sweetness with oriental leaf's spicy, sharp character. Though the firm's leaf list did not specify latakia, smokers' accounts point to the presence of a smoky component. The mixture has long been out of production and is now found only in old, sealed tins. It appealed to experienced pipe smokers seeking a medium-bodied, spicy smoke close to the unflavored, oriental-forward English tradition.
sullivan-powell-gentlemans-mixture-origi.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay, spice, and light smoke.

mcclelland-no-2045-oriental-mixture.z: No. 2045 Oriental Mixture appears in McClelland's bulk catalog as the reduced-Latakia counterpart to the No. 2040 Cyprian mixture. Per the maker's description, within a mild, sweet structure, light-colored Orientals and Carolina leaf stand out, with Latakia used only in a supporting tone. This setup makes the blend more an Oriental-forward mixture than an English one. In the smoke, the Oriental's tangy, herbal, and spicy tones are pronounced; the Latakia's smoke draws a frame in the background. Body is medium and nicotine is moderate. Aimed at smokers who want Latakia in measured amounts and who want to hear the Oriental leaf's own character. Production ended when McClelland ceased operations in 2018.
mcclelland-no-2045-oriental-mixture.o: Leaves a dry spice, incense, and faint smoke aroma.

torben-dansk-black-velvet.z: The Torben Dansk blend called Black Velvet is noted in records as an aromatic; no reliable source documenting its composition and character has been found.

w-o-larsen-shamrock.z: This is a blend known under the W.O. Larsen name; no reliable source could be found documenting its composition and character.

dixon-hamilton-burlington-blue-label.z: No reliable source could be found identifying the maker, composition, or character of this blend referred to under the Dixon & Hamilton name.

mcclelland-oriental-mixture-no-6.z: Oriental Mixture No. 6 is from McClelland's green-label Oriental series. Per retailer description, the blend is built by adding a generous amount of Oriental tobacco over orange-toned Virginia leaves, rounded out with only a pinch of Latakia for complexity. It's ribbon cut. Body is medium; the smoke is refreshing, tangy-spicy, with sharp edges. Latakia here isn't the main ingredient but more of an accent. A blend for smokers who want to hear the Oriental tobacco's own character without Latakia stepping forward. McClelland ceased operations in 2018.
mcclelland-oriental-mixture-no-6.o: A very fine trace of soot mixes into an aroma of dry hay and spice.

gawith-hoggarth-co-spirit-of-scotland.z: Spirit of Scotland is the current name of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s aromatic blend previously sold as American Whiskey. It's made by combining sweet Virginia and Burley leaf with double-fermented black Cavendish; the mixture is flavored with a measured whiskey topping. In the coarse-cut, predominantly black-looking tobacco, golden-brown strands appear here and there; since moisture isn't excessive, packing and lighting are easy. On the smoke, vanilla and caramel notes combine with the whiskey to give a soft taste reminiscent of bourbon, with a dried-fruit association in the background. An entry for those wanting an aromatic with measured nicotine, fit for all-day smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-spirit-of-scotland.o: Leaves a sweet, creamy caramel aroma reminiscent of whiskey.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-44.z: Wilke No. 44 is a mixture built outside the usual English blend mold. According to the maker's recipe, black cavendish forms the base, topped with finely cut Yenidje Oriental leaf, Virginia, Latakia, and Perique. Yenidje's spicy, floral character is the blend's most prominent trait; Cyprian Latakia is not a dominant component here, but rather an addition that keeps the smokiness in check. Perique adds a dark, fruity, peppery edge that balances the sweetness of the cavendish base. The fine cut means the blend catches quickly, so it calls for a slow draw. It suits smokers seeking Oriental-forward English blends with controlled smokiness, where Latakia doesn't take the lead.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-44.o: Leaves a scent of wood smoke, dry spice, and light incense.

mccranies-sweet-savannah.z: Sweet Savannah is one of the bulk aromatic blends from McCranie's Pipe Shop. According to the shop's description, fire-cured tobaccos, Burley, and black Cavendish are brought together in balanced fashion; the casing applied on top gives the blend a peachy, sweet impression. The Cavendish share lowers the burn temperature and softens the smoke. Since the nicotine load stays light to medium, it's the kind of aromatic that can be smoked throughout the day; it's constructed for smokers looking for fruity flavorings who want a smoke that doesn't sit heavy on the tongue. The blend is one of roughly seventy-five bulk mixtures prepared at McCranie's shop in Charlotte.
mccranies-sweet-savannah.o: Leaves a pronounced fruity aroma reminiscent of cooked peach and sweet pastry.

borkum-riff-cognac.z: A cognac-flavored option in the Borkum Riff line, reportedly discontinued for a long time; no adequate firsthand source on its composition and character could be found.
borkum-riff-cognac.o: According to records it leaves a sweet, boozy room note reminiscent of cognac.

erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-1966.z: 4th Generation 1966 is a ribbon-cut blend combining aged Virginia leaves with Burley and black cavendish, topped with a touch of latakia. Caribbean rum is used as the topping, placing it somewhere between an aromatic and an English mixture. It is named for the birth year of Erik Stokkebye's younger brother and, like the rest of the series, is produced in Denmark. Because the latakia proportion is kept low, the smoky character isn't dominant, remaining instead as a background element of depth. It suits smokers who enjoy sweetly topped blends but want a bit of a woody, smoky layer alongside, and who find pure aromatics too one-dimensional.
erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-1966.o: Leaves a scent carrying a faint smoky trace beneath the rum sweetness.

cornell-diehl-red-virginia-cavendish.z: Red Virginia Cavendish is obtained by Cornell & Diehl processing red Virginia leaf from the Old Belt region through the Cavendish method at its own facility. It's made of a single leaf variety, carries no casing, and is presented ribbon cut. Since the Cavendish process brings out the leaf's natural sugar, the blend, per the maker's description, carries a sweet character reminiscent of bread fresh from the oven. On the maker's scale, strength, flavor, and room note are medium. It can be smoked on its own or used as a sweetening component in house blends; suited to those looking for unflavored Virginia sweetness.
cornell-diehl-red-virginia-cavendish.o: Leaves a sweet, doughy scent reminiscent of bread fresh from the oven.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore-ca.z: Finamore Café is the version of the brand's Burley- and Virginia-based body flavored with coffee, produced in Juiz de Fora, Minas Gerais. Coffee is a casing frequently used in Brazilian aromatics, and here it becomes the blend's defining trait. Burley's dry, lightly roasted side works in the same direction as the coffee note; the Virginia leaves a light sweetness in the background. Nicotine is low. It suits smokers looking for a roasted-leaning aromatic rather than a sweet one.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore-ca.o: Leaves a roasted scent reminiscent of freshly ground coffee.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-irish-x.z: Brown Irish X is a traditional Lakeland tobacco produced by hand-twisting fire-cured Virginia leaves into rope form. Unlike the black ropes, it does not go through a long cooking stage under pressure, and is left as it comes off the twisting machine. Because of this, the leaf's raw strength and natural oils are largely preserved; the product is sold unsliced in rope form, and the smoker cuts and rubs out coin-shaped pieces themselves. In the smoke, the smoky, woody, leather-like taste of the fire-cured leaf dominates, accompanied by tones reminiscent of caramelised sugar and dark chocolate, with a peppery sharpness. The nicotine load is very high, making this one of the strongest ends of the Gawith, Hoggarth catalogue. It suits small-bowled pipes, a full stomach, and slow smoking; it is a record for experienced smokers accustomed to rope tobaccos.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-irish-x.o: A heavy smoke, leather, and burnt-wood aroma settles into the room and lingers long.

peter-stokkebye-evening-treasure.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Evening Treasure could be found.

gallaher-limited-garryowen-plug.z: This is a blend called Garryowen Plug among the pipe tobaccos of Gallaher Limited, founded by Tom Gallaher in Derry in 1857 and later absorbed into Japan Tobacco; no reliable source could be found on the blend's composition and character.

radfords-caribbean-blend.z: Caribbean Blend is one of the flavored members of the Radford's line under the Pöschl umbrella; it is offered in Germany in 50-gram pouches and 200-gram tins. The blend brings together nutty, cocoa-leaning Burley with sweet Virginia and black Cavendish leaf; its defining character comes from the added real Jamaican rum. Its cut is mixed, nicotine quite light, and its taste leans sweet. Maker data rates flavoring and room note at four out of five. It is a blend for those looking for a light-bodied aromatic loaded with rum flavoring.
radfords-caribbean-blend.o: Leaves a sweet trace reminiscent of candied rum, dry nuts, and cocoa.

lane-limited-lamplighter.z: One of Lane Limited's aromatic blends; not enough independent sources could be found.

exclusiv-amaretto.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing was found for the Exclusiv brand's Amaretto blend, so the entry has been left open; records place it in the Aromatic family.

seattle-pipe-club-galloping-gertie.z: Galloping Gertie is an unflavored blend in which red and stoved dark Virginia leaves are combined with St. James perique, unsweetened black cavendish, and Turkish-Oriental tobaccos and pressed into a crumble cake. The name comes from the nickname attached to the Tacoma Narrows Bridge in Washington State, which famously swayed in the wind and collapsed in 1940. The perique adds a plum-like sweetness and a peppery sharpness to the blend, while the Oriental leaves add a sour-spicy edge; the black cavendish provides richness and roundness rather than sugar. The result is a blend aimed at smokers seeking a layered flavor without added flavoring, who want to try the Virginia-perique family alongside Oriental leaf.
seattle-pipe-club-galloping-gertie.o: Leaves a dried-fruit sweetness with a spicy, faintly earthy tobacco scent.

castello-castello.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Castello under the Castello brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

park-lane-tobacconist-black-forest.z: No reliable source could be found for the Park brand pipe tobacco called Lane Tobacconist-Black Forest, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

a-c-petersen-the-chiefs-own-special-cut-.z: A numbered blend belonging to A & C Petersen's "The Chief's Own" line; no adequate source documenting its content could be found.

dan-tobacco-st-bernard-flake.z: St. Bernard Flake is one of Dan Tobacco's Virginia/perique blends produced pressed and sliced. The tin scent is sweet and tart, carrying a fermented side tone. Being flake cut, the leaves need to be rubbed out or folded before packing. On the smoke there's a deep sweetness accompanied by a light tartness, and a pronounced perique pepperiness spreading through the whole bowl. Fullness is medium. It suits smokers seeking unadulterated pressed Virginia tobaccos that change with aging and perique spice; not for those expecting a sugary aromatic.
dan-tobacco-st-bernard-flake.o: Leaves a peppery tobacco scent mixed with a fermented fruit tartness.

john-cotton-john-cottons-double-pressed-.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to document the contents and character of John Cotton's John Cotton's Double Pressed Creme.

garfinkels-atlas.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of Garfinkel's Atlas pipe tobacco could be found.

dan-tobacco-evening-standard.z: No adequate independent sources were found detailing the composition of this blend, listed as Balkan style in the Dan Tobacco catalogue.

davidoff-year-of-the-tiger.z: Year of the Tiger is the 2022 entry in Davidoff's Chinese zodiac series, released in limited numbers in 100-gram tins. The Swiss-origin brand's pipe tobaccos are produced in Germany; that same year, the maker Kohlhase & Kopp also released a separate lychee-flavored tiger blend under its own name — the two should not be confused. The Davidoff edition is built from latakia, burley and virginia leaves of Chinese, Indian, Malawian and Cypriot origin. The latakia share gives the blend a smoky, woody layer, burley a dry body and medium nicotine, while virginia carries a measured sweetness in the background. It suits smokers seeking a smoky structure with measured sweetness rather than a heavily topped aromatic.
davidoff-year-of-the-tiger.o: Leaves a scent combining woody soot and light fruit sweetness.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-colts-gol.z: Referred to as a variety in the Colts line; no sufficient source documenting this particular blend's content could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-light.z: Kendal Light is an unflavored blend prepared solely from light-colored Virginia leaf, offered as a fine shag cut. Straw, a light lemon tartness, and honeyed sweetness that grows more pronounced as it warms stand out on the flavor palette. Since nicotine stays measured, its structure allows for long sessions throughout the day. Because the fine cut burns fast, it calls for loose packing and a slow draw. Suited to smokers wanting to get to know unflavored Virginia taste from its light end.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-light.o: Leaves a dry-hay and lightly lemony tobacco aroma.

mcclelland-no-x-10-unflavored-burley-rib.z: An unflavored ribbon-cut product from McClelland's X-series bulk Burley entries, discontinued when the firm closed in 2018; no sufficient source documenting its detailed contents could be found.

american-club-light.z: No reliable source describing the content and character of American Club Light could be found.

alfie-turmeaus-the-classic-gentleman.z: The Classic Gentleman was one of the house-recipe mixtures Turmeaus tobacconist prepared in-store. Per records it was made by combining two measures of pressed rope-cake tobacco, one measure of Latakia blending leaf, and one measure of Perique; the rope-cake tobacco brought Virginia and Burley's mature sweetness to the blend, while the Perique added a spice layer leaning toward dried fruit and pepper. Carrying no sweetening sauce and relying only on the leaves' own taste, it's an intense smoke in the medium-strong band. Using Perique and Latakia together makes the blend layered; it suits smokers familiar with unflavored English mixtures and pressed Virginia-Burley tobaccos.
alfie-turmeaus-the-classic-gentleman.o: Leaves a lightly smoky tobacco room note accompanied by dried fig and peppery spice.

sutliff-tobacco-company-tobacco-galleria.z: A blend in Sutliff's Tobacco Galleria line; no accessible source describing its composition could be found.

grand-croupier-bone-yard.z: Bone Yard is the Latakia-forward English blend in the Grand Croupier series. The series rests on the idea of gathering leftover quality tobacco from a producer's various batches; in Bone Yard, these leftovers are drawn from English and Latakia-based mixtures. Because of this, the composition can vary from batch to batch, but the backbone is always built on Latakia's smoke, joined by Virginia and Oriental leaf. The cut is not uniform: alongside ribbon-cut leaf are crumbled flake pieces and larger chunks, with a low proportion of fine dust. This structure calls for some care when packing but burns evenly. Suited to smokers seeking Latakia character rather than a fixed recipe, who are open to small differences from batch to batch.
grand-croupier-bone-yard.o: Leaves a heavy aroma of smoke and resinous wood reminiscent of a campfire.

mcclelland-brindle-flake-ashton-revival.z: Brindle Flake is among the blends McClelland produced for Ashton, offered within the brand's Ashton Revival series. It consists of unflavored Virginia leaf; leaves dried by the flue-cure method are pressed and matured as cake, then presented as broken flake. Packing and lighting are easy. Rather than a complex flavor sequence, it rests on Virginia's natural sweetness and plain tobacco taste; nicotine level is measured. Suited to those seeking unflavored Virginia flake and smokers who want to age their tins.
mcclelland-brindle-flake-ashton-revival.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of sweet hay and toasted bread crust.

century-irish-cream.z: A blend in the Century line known for an Irish cream aroma; no sufficient source could be found to document its content.

cornell-diehl-privateer.z: Privateer is a bright-Virginia-heavy English-type mixture from Cornell & Diehl. Black Cavendish and dark Burley are added on top of a bright Virginia base; Latakia is used in a measured amount. It's ribbon cut, offered both in bulk and tinned. Because the Latakia proportion is kept low, smoke isn't the mixture's main axis but a layer appearing in the background; the flavor up front is Virginia's sweetness and the roundness Cavendish and Burley provide. It sits between mild and medium in both nicotine and body. A fitting entry point for smokers new to Latakia blends or finding heavily smoky mixtures too much.
cornell-diehl-privateer.o: Leaves a sweet, breadlike tobacco scent mingling with light smoky wood.

watch-city-cigar-spillsbane-an-ozark-wiz.z: This is a collaborative release from Watch City Cigar, for which no sufficient source could be found.
watch-city-cigar-spillsbane-an-ozark-wiz.o: No record could be found regarding the room note.

niall-of-nine-meretrix-et-virgo.z: Meretrix et Virgo is a blend Niall of Nine built in Scottish style, taking Dunhill Aperitif as its starting point. It consists of red Virginias' bright tartness, Turkish-oriental leaf's herbal and spicy sharpness, measured Cyprian latakia, and a share of black cavendish that rounds the blend off. True to the Scottish blending tradition, latakia isn't in the lead role here but plays a seasoning part: the smoke stays a thin line behind Virginia's sweetness, while cavendish builds a molasses-like undertone. It's a balanced, medium-strength record smokable all day; it suits smokers who find heavy Balkan mixtures too much, yet find straight Virginia too plain. Production runs in small batches.
niall-of-nine-meretrix-et-virgo.o: A molasses-like sweetness mingles into a thin campfire-smoke scent.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-400.z: No sufficient source could be found documenting the composition and character of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Wilke No. 400.

missouri-meerschaum-taste-of-temptation.z: No verifiable description could be found for Missouri Meerschaum's blend called Taste of Temptation.

the-smoker-smoker.z: A house blend bearing the name of the American tobacconist The Smoker itself; it is noted as English-style, but no verifiable source describing its composition has been found.

solani-763-white-and-black.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Solani blend 763: White and Black could not be found.

ferndown-red-orange.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for the Ferndown brand's Red & Orange pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

sentimiento-nacional-cherry.z: A cherry-flavored entry in Sentimiento Nacional's fruit-essence aromatic line; no source documenting the tobacco composition could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-balkan-sob.z: Match Balkan Sobranie is one of the bulk blends from the Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-winter-edition-2.z: The 2015 installment of Kohlhase & Kopp's winter-season limited series; no verifiable source could be found detailing this edition's contents and casing.

rattray-summer-2018.z: This is the 2018 summer edition of Rattray's seasonally flavored Limited Edition line; reports describe it as a fruity aromatic, but there is not enough source material documenting its composition.

decatur-dark-sweet-rum.z: Decatur is one of the affordable, bulk-sold pipe tobacco lines in the US market. Dark Sweet Rum is an aromatic blend built by adding black cavendish to Virginia and burley leaves, flavored with rum taste and a touch of vanilla. It has a cool-smoking structure with pronounced sweetness; it appeals to those seeking rum-flavored sweetness and newcomers to aromatic tobaccos. Due to regulatory changes in recent years, the blend is offered as a kit the buyer mixes at home to yield roughly a 230-gram batch.
decatur-dark-sweet-rum.o: Leaves a sugary scent mixed with sweet rum and vanilla.

burlington-on-whyte-tobacconist-donnybro.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named Donnybrook under the Burlington on Whyte Tobacconist brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

mcclelland-british-woods.z: British Woods is a medium-to-full-bodied Oriental mixture in McClelland's Personal Reserve series. It's built with a heavy Latakia dose, topped with Macedonia-sourced Oriental leaves and matured sweet Virginias. It's ribbon cut, set to burn slow and cool. In the smoke, the soot-and-wood-smoke line dominates; the Orientals' spicy curl and the Virginia's sweetness proceed beneath it, leaving, per records, a dark taste reminiscent of spiced dark chocolate. No flavoring is used. A blend aimed at smokers used to dark, Latakia-forward mixtures who seek a full-bodied, smoky profile. The maker closed in 2018, so the blend is no longer produced.
mcclelland-british-woods.o: Leaves an aroma of campfire smoke and soot, with a spiced sweetness lingering behind it.

edwards-first-mate.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of First Mate, a pipe tobacco from Edward's. Edward's is a tobacconist business based in Tampa, Florida.

backwoods-buttered-rum.z: Buttered Rum is a rod-cut aromatic in Backwoods' pipe tobacco line, built from a trio of golden Virginia, white Burley, and Cavendish. New England and Jamaican rums are used in the flavoring; since the topping ratio is kept very high, the rum scent overtakes the tobacco scent on opening the pouch. The leaf is dark-colored and noticeably moist, requiring airing before lighting. Nicotine load in the smoke is very low; in contrast, the flavoring intensity largely masks the tobacco's taste and can leave a sharp, bitterish residue on the palate. It's aimed at smokers looking for a strong rum aroma who accept the tobacco character taking a back seat; it isn't a good choice for those seeking natural leaf taste.
backwoods-buttered-rum.o: Leaves a heavy room note of rum and buttered sugar.

sutliff-tobacco-company-state-fair.z: State Fair is one of Sutliff's bulk aromatics named for its fairground theme. It is prepared by bringing together burley, Virginia, and black cavendish leaf; the casing applied over it builds a sweet line reminiscent of sugared apple. It is ribbon cut and offered at a moisture level ready for smoking straight from the pack. The blend sits on the light side; according to the maker's data, its nicotine strength is at the lowest tier, and the taste is also measured. Black cavendish carries the sweetness, burley adds a light body, and Virginia stays in the background. It suits smokers looking for an aromatic with low nicotine and a noticeable but not heavy flavoring.
sutliff-tobacco-company-state-fair.o: Leaves a scent of sugared apple and caramel.

e-a-carey-europe-careys-cavendish-mixtur.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Carey's Cavendish Mixture, a pipe tobacco from E. A. Carey (Europe).

connoisseur-st-james-club-virginia.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Connoisseur blend St. James' Club Virginia.

cornell-diehl-berries-cream.z: Berries & Cream is a ribbon-cut aromatic Cornell & Diehl builds on unsweetened black cavendish. It is flavored with the brand's characteristic Green River vanilla, a cream flavoring, and blackberry brandy; the mixture is dark-colored throughout. Nicotine is very light in the blend, with taste coming mainly from the flavorings; the cavendish base provides a soft, sweet body. It suits smokers who love fruity aromatics and want a low-strength tobacco.
cornell-diehl-berries-cream.o: Leaves an aroma of red berries and sweet cream.

jons-pipe-shop-oak-park.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Jon's Pipe Shop's Oak Park pipe tobacco.

vauen-auenland-sunset-mixture.z: Auenland Sunset Mixture is an aromatic mixture in Nuremberg-based Vauen's Auenland series. Virginia leaves in varying cut widths form the body of the blend, joined by double-fermented black Cavendish and Burley. The variety of cuts slows the burn and keeps it cool. On the flavor side, candied orange, honey and pine resin come forward; a sweet, warm frame is built, while nicotine stays light. Suited to smokers who look for fruit-candy-style sweetness in aromatic tobaccos and want a long, low-strength smoke.
vauen-auenland-sunset-mixture.o: Leaves a scent of candied orange peel, honey and warmed pine resin.

roland-von-bremen-burley-flake.z: This is a Burley-heavy flake blend carried under the Roland von Bremen name; there is not enough source material describing its content and character.
roland-von-bremen-burley-flake.o: Could not be determined from available sources.

cult-militia.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the Cult brand as Militia; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

niall-of-nine-third-cousins.z: Third Cousins is one of Niall of Nine's blends that combines aged cigar leaf stock with pipe tobacco. Records indicate it is built from King Edward cigarillo leaf dating to the 1960s, joined by 2020-harvest red and stoved Virginias, topped with a small amount of 2012 St. James Parish perique. The cigar leaf gives the blend a dark body leaning toward leather and earth, while stoved Virginia gives a dark sweetness in the direction of fig and molasses; perique steps in with a small dose of spice and plum notes. It's a full-bodied tobacco in nicotine terms and appeals to smokers who smoke cigars but also want an intense leaf in a pipe. It was produced in limited numbers in vacuum-sealed jars.
niall-of-nine-third-cousins.o: Leaves a dark, leather-leaning tobacco scent recalling a cigar shop, sitting atop burnt-sugar sweetness.

ken-byron-ventures-byronic-hiro.z: Byronic Hiro is made by stemming matured, stoved red Virginia leaf and pressing it into a very wide, flat cake. The cake is steam-cooked until it darkens, then cut into small bars. It's an unflavored plug tobacco built from a single leaf type.
ken-byron-ventures-byronic-hiro.o: Leaves a dark bread, dried fig, and woody tobacco aroma.

faders-point-iv.z: Point IV is one of the house blends of the Baltimore-based Fader's tobacconist; after the shop closed in 2018, no record documenting the blend's composition could be found.
faders-point-iv.o: Records do not contain enough information for a description.

john-patton-smoked-burley.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Patton's Smoked Burley blend.

h-simmons-aromatic.z: A topped mixture, one of the house blends of H. Simmons, a tobacconist operating in London's Burlington Arcade; there is no reliable sourcing on its composition and cut.
h-simmons-aromatic.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet aroma from the topping.

lane-limited-plc.z: Not enough independent sources could be found documenting the contents and character of American blender Lane Limited's blend called PLC.

hearth-home-saratoga-summer.z: Saratoga Summer is a bulk-sold aromatic mixture prepared by blender Russ Ouellette under the Hearth & Home umbrella. It takes its name from the Saratoga region of New York state, part of the naming tradition referencing the brand's home region. Its distinguishing feature is that the rum flavoring comes to the fore: the rum note sitting atop the leaf base defines the blend's identity. The base is made up of a combination of Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish leaves; being ribbon cut, it's easy to fill and light. With its moderate nicotine load, it's aimed at those looking for a blend that can be smoked over long periods during the day and those who enjoy rum-flavored aromatics. Records indicate Hearth & Home's production ended in the early 2020s, so the blend is no longer on the market today.
hearth-home-saratoga-summer.o: Leaves an aroma of sweet rum and candied dried fruit.

robert-lewis-extra-coarse-cut.z: Extra Coarse Cut is a blend carried under the name of Robert Lewis, the London tobacconist founded in 1787; no reliable source could be found on the blend's content or character.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-knack-m.z: Knack Mixture is built from broken Virginia slices dressed with Latakia, Perique, fire-cured leaf, and cognac. The maker describes the blend as a Scottish-style mixture not tied to the Perth tradition, and states the Virginia component is mostly bright and brown leaf, with no characterizing flavor to the blend; it's offered as 2 oz. bulk. Here Latakia acts less as a dominant body-builder and more as a seasoning that adds smoke and woody depth to the leaf; Perique brings dark fruit and spice, and the fire-cured leaf a molasses-like sweetness. The cognac touch stays in the background. Suited to smokers who want a smoky taste without stepping into heavy English blends, and who are comfortable rubbing out a slice cut.
ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-knack-m.o: Leaves an aroma where woody smoke meets a light cognac sweetness.

wolfway-green-virginia.z: This is a Wolfway product said to be straight Virginia; no verifiable source could be found regarding the blend.

lane-limited-lane-limited-ready-rubbed.z: Lane Limited Ready Rubbed is the tobacco the manufacturer released to continue the same-line burley blend after losing the right to use the Edgeworth name. Mature burley leaf is combined with light Virginia; a measured rum-direction casing is applied on top. After pressing, the leaf is processed ready to be rubbed by hand, easing packing. The taste brings forward cocoa, molasses and nutty sides; the casing doesn't override the tobacco. Nicotine is medium and the burn is even. Suited to those seeking a classic American burley tradition blend to smoke all day.
lane-limited-lane-limited-ready-rubbed.o: Leaves a cocoa, molasses and light-rum room note.

john-patton-eds-home-from-work.z: One of the small-scale blends released under the John Patton name; not enough independent sources could be found to document its contents and character.
john-patton-eds-home-from-work.o: No source could be found on the room note.

royal-collection-aristocrat.z: No reliable source describing the content and character of the Aristocrat blend, released under the Royal Collection name, could be found.

jons-pipe-shop-garveys-balkan.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Jon's Pipe Shop's Garvey's Balkan blend.

samuel-gawith-brown-rope-no-4-aromatic.z: Brown Rope No. 4 is Samuel Gawith's thick-bodied rope series; the No. 4 number denotes the rope's thickness. In the Aromatic version, a light flavoring casing is applied to the twisted virginia-and-burley-based tobacco. It is produced with old rope machines at the Kendal facility and sold in wheel form. Its smoke is thick, tobacco-forward, and nicotine high; the casing does not come forward, serving as a frame that softens the tobacco's dark taste. It needs to be sliced, thoroughly crumbled, and dried. A record for those accustomed to rope smoking who seek a strong blend.
samuel-gawith-brown-rope-no-4-aromatic.o: Leaves a light sweet liqueur scent over dark tobacco.

ravenwood-fine-provisions-olde-burley-be.z: This is a limited-run blend in the Ravenwood Fine Provisions line, presented as a European-style Burley flake; the maker has not published a detailed composition specification.

intertabak-dark-virginia-po-30.z: No verifiable source could be found for this dark Virginia registered under the INTERTABAK name.

peretti-prince-of-wales.z: One of the house blends from L. J. Peretti's shop in Boston; it appears under the English blends heading in the maker's listing. No published description of the blend's composition and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.

erik-stokkebye-small-batch-aged-virginia.z: Small Batch Aged Virginia is an unadulterated Virginia blend born from the collaboration between 4th Generation and Samuel Gawith. All the leaves used were rested for ten years, then warm-pressed, sliced and formed into ribbon. Production took place at the Samuel Gawith facility in northern England, and the product was offered in limited numbers in tin packaging. Because of the long aging, the taste is darker and more concentrated than fresh Virginia blends; the sharpness gives way to a mellow, settled sweetness. It sits high in body and fullness, so it calls for a slow, experienced smoke.
erik-stokkebye-small-batch-aged-virginia.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay, dark bread and a hint of plum.

ken-byron-ventures-belmont-hustle.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Ken Byron Ventures' Belmont Hustle blend.

vcpo-selection-nr-1.z: The first in a five-blend series prepared for VCPÖ, the Austrian trade association for cigars and pipes; due to the country's tobacco monopoly, distribution stayed limited to Austria, and no independent source documenting the composition has been found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-rl-575-large-vir.z: RL-575 is an unflavored blend offered in Sutliff's bulk line as a large-cut Virginia flake. It is made of pure Virginia leaf, pressed and cut into thick slices; records indicate no flavoring casing is applied over it. Thanks to pressing and slicing, Virginia's natural sugar turns into a more intense, bready taste. It is aimed at smokers who like straight Virginia and are used to rubbing out or folding the slices for packing.
sutliff-tobacco-company-rl-575-large-vir.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay and baked bread.

vincenzo-gold.z: Vincenzo Gold is the Virginia-led aromatic from the Italian Vincenzo brand. Red, orange and gold Virginia leaf forms the body of the blend; a small measure of black Cavendish sweetness and a very minor share of Burley provide earthy balance. It is ribbon cut. The casing leans toward stone fruit and nuts, and the smoke is lightly nicotined, soft and sweet. Unlike heavy English blends, it leaves no lasting impression on the palate, suiting those after an easygoing, everyday smoke. Sold in 50-gram tins.
vincenzo-gold.o: Leaves a scent of ripe yellow fruit and roasted hazelnut.

connoisseur-dark-honey.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Connoisseur pipe tobacco named Dark Honey, so the blend's content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

ken-byron-ventures-chichester-road.z: A short-run blend listed in Ken Byron Ventures' catalog as an English mixture; no accessible maker's profile could be found to document its contents.

smokers-pride-cherry-cavendish.z: Cherry Cavendish is the cherry-flavored record in the Smoker's Pride line. The base rests on black cavendish; burley and Virginia shares round out the body. The blend's defining trait is the heavy cherry flavoring worked into the leaf, present up front in both the tin aroma and throughout the smoke. The ribbon cut makes packing easy, while cavendish's moisture slows the burn. Nicotine and tobacco body are kept deliberately low; the emphasis is on the flavoring side. Suited to smokers seeking a fruit-flavored, sweet, light everyday blend, and those wanting an economical aromatic in large packaging.
smokers-pride-cherry-cavendish.o: Leaves a pronounced scent of cherry candy and sweet fruit.

7-20-4-603-roast.z: 603 Roast is an aromatic blend in the 7-20-4 brand's Briary Blends line. Its name comes from the area code of New Hampshire, the state the brand is tied to. It contains traditionally processed black Cavendish and Dominican-origin cigar leaf; the cigar leaf adds an earthy, leathery body unusual for aromatics. The line was introduced in 2023 and sold through a tobacconist channel. The flavor profile is described around smoky sweet cream, dark cocoa, and espresso; the flavoring is pronounced but sits in a darker, more toasted direction than classic fruit-vanilla aromatics. Nicotine sensation is medium. It suits smokers who like aromatics but want a dark sweetness in the coffee-and-chocolate direction rather than a sugary one.
7-20-4-603-roast.o: Fills the room with roasted coffee bean, cocoa, and sweet cream.

affordable-pipes-very-vanilla.z: A vanilla-themed house blend from the American seller Affordable Pipes; no accessible source describing its content could be found.

new-york-pipe-club-hells-kitchen.z: Hell's Kitchen represents the Balkan style among the club blends prepared for the New York Pipe Club. In keeping with the club's general approach, no flavor casing is used; the taste comes entirely from leaf selection: Virginia forms the base, while Latakia and Oriental leaf give it its identity. It takes its name from the Hell's Kitchen neighborhood on Manhattan's west side. In the smoke, Latakia's smokiness is kept restrained, allowing the Oriental leaf's tangy, spicy side to come forward — setting the blend apart from heavy English recipes and closer to the Balkan line. Given its layered structure, it suits smokers looking for nuance in smoky blends rather than those new to Latakia.
new-york-pipe-club-hells-kitchen.o: Leaves a woody, lightly smoky aroma, with the dry-herb and spice scent of Oriental leaf behind it.

bufflehead-black-brant.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Black Brant under the Bufflehead brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

ken-byron-ventures-the-oriental-affair-2.z: The Oriental Affair, part of Ken Byron Ventures' 221-B series, is an unflavored blend combining Turkish-origin Oriental leaf with red Virginia. The maker's description notes that the blend is distinctly aromatic with a faint floral edge, and that this scent comes from the leaf itself rather than an added casing. The Oriental leaf is spicy and dry, while the red Virginia adds body and a measured sweetness. The "221-B" name points to the brand's Sherlock Holmes-referencing sub-series, which draws on the classic English blend tradition. Since it contains no Latakia, it runs on dry spice rather than smoky char. Its moderate nicotine makes it suited to daytime smoking and to those who want to pick out the Oriental leaf's own aroma; for smokers coming from Latakia-heavy blends, it offers a gentler entry point.
ken-byron-ventures-the-oriental-affair-2.o: Leaves a subtle aroma of dry spice and faded flower petals.

clan-shaw-night-watch.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Night Watch.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wall-street.z: Wall Street is one of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's names referencing its New York history, and according to the maker's recipe, it's a special mixture built on Burley and Perique. Burley gives the blend a nutty, earthy, dry base, while Perique raises the plummy-spice edge and the nicotine load. This is a record aimed at experienced smokers seeking unflavored, full-bodied, spicy smokes; it may be heavy for those looking for smoothness on the tongue.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wall-street.o: Leaves an earthy scent reminiscent of nuts, with a sharp spice trace.

w-d-h-o-wills-cut-golden-bar.z: Cut Golden Bar is the unflavored Virginia blend from W.D. & H.O. Wills, manufactured in Bristol and London. According to records, it's been on the market since the 1920s and was widely sold in yellow and red tins through the mid-twentieth century. The blend is built from bright and red Virginia leaves. Its smoke is rich and smooth; it leans toward the sweet side without a grassy or hay-like character, and its impact on the tongue stays measured relative to that fullness. It contains no flavoring; the sweetness comes entirely from Virginia's own sugar. It's no longer produced today; the tins referenced mostly turn up in the collector's market. This is a historical blend of interest to smokers wanting to trace the development of unflavored Virginias and curious about classic examples of English production tradition.
w-d-h-o-wills-cut-golden-bar.o: Leaves a sweetish scent reminiscent of dry hay and baked bread.

milan-tobacconists-our-kentucky-club-mix.z: A blend from Milan Tobacconists based on an old American mixture. White burley, Carolina, and bright Virginia leaves are joined by Turkish tobacco and a small amount of perique; the presence of ribbon, cube, flake, and shag cuts together balances the blend's burn rate. It is a cool-burning mixture kept low in nicotine. The light spice brought by perique and oriental adds depth to burley's nutty base. An in-between option for smokers who don't want an aromatic but also don't want to move into intense English mixtures. Records in the maker's online catalogue indicate it was out of stock for a period.
milan-tobacconists-our-kentucky-club-mix.o: Leaves a dry-hay and lightly spiced tobacco aroma.

john-middleton-inc-prince-albert-choice-.z: A Burley-based version in the Prince Albert line; not enough sources could be found on its contents, cut, and flavoring.
john-middleton-inc-prince-albert-choice-.o: Leaves a dry, nutty, lightly sweet aroma.

ilsted-own-mixture-no-66.z: Own Mixture No.66 is a Danish-style aromatic in which dark and light Virginia leaves are blended with some Burley and Kentucky, then rounded out with a measured amount of dark Cavendish. The coating consists of vanilla and almond; sweetness comes forward, but the Kentucky adds a subtle spice and body to the blend. It's an everyday tobacco for those looking for a mild-smoking, distinctly scented aromatic. The line bears the name of Danish pipe maker Poul Ilsted and is produced by Kopp Tobaccos in Germany.
ilsted-own-mixture-no-66.o: Leaves an aroma of vanilla cake and toasted almond.

ken-byron-ventures-full-metal-balkanist.z: A limited blend from Ken Byron Ventures nodding to the Balkan style; no independent source could be found to document its ratios or contents.
ken-byron-ventures-full-metal-balkanist.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-paradise.z: Paradise is Boswell's black-cavendish-forward aromatic blend. Per the manufacturer's description, a full-bodied cavendish base is joined by a measured vanilla casing felt at the finish. Once lit, the vanilla becomes pronounced and softly complements cavendish's dark sweetness; the smoke is creamy, nicotine low, and no tongue bite is reported. Suitable for smokers seeking a plain, single-note, sweet aromatic.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-paradise.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and dark sugar aroma.

peter-heinrichs-no-116.z: Peter Heinrichs No. 116 is reportedly counted as Virginia-forward among the firm's numbered house blends; however, no accessible manufacturer description documenting its content and cut could be found.

hu-tobacco-daddy-gefftl.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Daddy Gefftl, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

owl-shop-w-b-3.z: No reliable source could be found for the Owl Shop pipe tobacco called W.B. #3, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

bjarne-the-mild-one.z: A member of the light blend line sold under the name Bjarne; according to records it's a mellow, Cavendish-forward Danish blend, though no reliable source on its detailed composition could be found.

larus-brother-company-inc-holiday-pipe-m.z: Holiday Pipe Mixture is one of Larus & Brother Company's multi-component mixtures. Per the tin copy, the blend brings together Louisiana Perique, Carolina's buttery flake leaf, white Kentucky Burley, bright Virginia and Cyprus Latakia; the manufacturer also mentioned an unnamed sixth component. This structure places it in the classic American mixture class. Latakia gives a woody, smoky layer, while Perique adds a plummy, peppery sharpness; Burley and Virginia build a bready, sweet base beneath them. Body is medium, flavor intensity is high. Since Larus's Richmond production ended in 1974, the blend has long been off the market; old tins circulate as collector items.
larus-brother-company-inc-holiday-pipe-m.o: Beneath a woody, lightly smoky scent, dried-fruit and bread notes can be heard.

stone-pine-tobacco-company-acadia-blend.z: A blend from Stone Pine Tobacco Company noted to have a Virginia-Perique structure; no verifiable source describing its composition and character could be found.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2004.z: Christmas Cheer is the straight Virginia series that Kansas City-based McClelland released once a year, in limited numbers, from the 1980s until the company's closure in early 2018. The series' idea is to present a single Virginia batch selected from that year's harvest on its own; each year is thus considered a separate record, and the year on the tin defines the blend's identity. The 2004 release was prepared the same way, with selected matured Virginia leaf pressed into cake and tinned as broken flake. Records indicate it's among the early-2000s harvest releases. Unflavored Virginia character dominates the smoke: natural leaf sweetness over a bready, herbal base, with a faint tang and a lemony sharpness in the background. Nicotine dose is measured, while flavor intensity is pronounced; it burns cool when smoked slowly, but tends to bite the tongue when rushed. Since the flake's moisture can run high straight from the tin, airing it before packing is common practice. A record aimed at smokers seeking unflavored Virginia who are considering cellaring the tin; not suitable for those expecting an aromatic.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2004.o: A tangy, sharp trace characteristic of McClelland tins mixes into an aroma of dry hay and toasted bread.

w-o-larsen-limited-edition-2013.z: This is one of W.Ø. Larsen's annual limited editions; no reliable source could be found regarding its composition and character.
w-o-larsen-limited-edition-2013.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

dan-tobacco-little-wren.z: A pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source on the blend's composition or character was found, so no further detail is given.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-black-cherry.z: Black Cherry is the cherry-flavored blend in the catalogue of McGahey The Tobacconist, founded in 1880 and operating in Devon. Its body is built from Virginia and black cavendish; the cavendish's steam-processed sweetness combines with Virginia's own sugar. A ripe black-cherry flavoring is applied on top, leaving a pronounced fruity scent in the dry tobacco. It is a light-nicotine, soft-smoking aromatic; the cherry note leads throughout the smoke while the tobacco character stays in the background. An entry geared toward those new to aromatic blends and smokers looking for a fruit-forward smoke that doesn't sit heavy on the tongue. McGahey offers the blends carrying its own name largely in bulk through its own shop and online channel.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-black-cherry.o: Leaves an aroma of ripe black cherry and candied fruit.

kontor-tabak-no-33.z: Kontor-Tabak No. 33 is a natural, unflavored tobacco in Tabak-Kontor's unflavored Virginia line. Per the manufacturer's recipe, the cold-tin scent carries dried plum, apricot, honey, bread and malt notes; these notes gradually open up through the smoke. It gives a mild-to-tongue, medium-strength smoke and burns especially slowly in medium and wide bowls. As with Virginia blends of high sugar load, it can bite the tongue if smoked quickly, so a slow rhythm is needed. A record for those seeking plain unflavored Virginia taste and for those wanting a tobacco suited to cellaring.
kontor-tabak-no-33.o: Leaves a warm room note reminiscent of baked bread and dried plum sweetness.

j-f-germain-son-1820-flake.z: This is a blend under the J. F. Germain & Son name, produced on the island of Jersey; no accessible source verifying its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
j-f-germain-son-1820-flake.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

pcca-winter.z: A blend produced by McClelland within the PCCA club series in small batches across different years; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-sweet-muffin.z: An aromatic small-batch blend in Ken Byron Ventures' Yoshimi's line; not enough sources could be found to document its composition and character.
ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-sweet-muffin.o: Could not be described due to lack of accessible records.

dunhill-my-mixture-850.z: A blend tied to Dunhill's My Mixture line, not currently in production; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found, so a detailed record couldn't be compiled.
dunhill-my-mixture-850.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

chonowitsch-t-16.z: T 16 is a full-bodied blend presented as a traditional English mixture. Its composition contains ripe, distinctly smoky Syrian Latakia; this powerful leaf is used at a level that doesn't overwhelm the other components, leaving room for the sweet, spiced Izmir Oriental leaf. Light Virginia adds sweetness and depth to the blend, while perique is added in a small amount. The leaves are aged for an extended period. The blend is among the heartiest members of the series prepared in small batches under Danish pipe maker Jess Chonowitsch's name. It is aimed at smokers looking for classic English mixtures with Syrian Latakia, not shying away from a settled, heavy smoke.
chonowitsch-t-16.o: Syrian Latakia's resinous, sweetish smoky aroma spreads through the room.

hearth-home-magnum-opus.z: Magnum Opus is a full-bodied English blend with Cyprian Latakia as its base, joined by yellow Virginia and select Oriental varieties such as Izmir, Basma, and Yenidje. Records indicate the Latakia ratio runs around forty percent and Perique around eight percent; part of the Virginia is Bulgarian in origin. The smoke is smoky and sweet, with pronounced incense-like, spicy notes from the Oriental leaf. The blend is among the brand's earliest Marquee series products. That series was established for products using costly Oriental leaf, hand-blended in small batches. Aimed at experienced smokers accustomed to intense Latakia and Oriental character who want an evening smoke.
hearth-home-magnum-opus.o: Leaves a heavy aroma of smoke joined by traces of incense and spice.

murray-sons-co-ltd-erinmore-ready-rubbed.z: Erinmore Ready Rubbed is the same blend rested under pressure and then rubbed out, ready to be loaded straight into the pipe. The leaf base consists of mature Virginia, soft Burley, and sweet dark air-cured tobaccos; the series' secret fruity sauce is applied on top. Manufacturer and retailer descriptions note a pineapple note within that sauce. Because it is packed moist, it burns slowly, giving a medium-strength, sweet smoke. The Erinmore name has been associated with Murray, Sons & Co in Belfast since the 1960s; after the company closed in 2005 the brand passed to the Scandinavian Tobacco Group, and production moved to Northern Europe. Suitable for someone who wants a fruity, soft aromatic without having to bother with unfolding flake.
murray-sons-co-ltd-erinmore-ready-rubbed.o: A sweet tropical-fruit and cooked-sugar aroma leaves a light floral trace behind it.

tabak-trennt-abu-riha.z: Abu Riha is Tabak Trennt's oldest house blend; according to the shop's history, the recipe was prepared by Andreas Trennt in 1928 and is built on the classic English style. It is an unflavored mixture with Latakia set over a Virginia body, containing no artificial flavoring. Like the business's later blends, it continues to be produced to its original recipe at the Walter Wehde tobacco factory in Hamburg. It suits smokers who look for Latakia's smoky, leathery sides and are used to unflavored English blends; with roughly a century of continuity, it carries a trace of German tobacco history.
tabak-trennt-abu-riha.o: Latakia's smoky, tarry scent lingers in the room for a long time.

rattray-london-eye.z: This is a flavored blend sold under the Rattray name; it is not part of the brand's current product list, and no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.
rattray-london-eye.o: There is not enough source material to describe its aroma.

cornell-diehl-bradyville.z: Bradyville is a ribbon-cut aromatic blend from Cornell & Diehl's North Carolina production. Its base is soft black cavendish; stoved light Virginia leaves and cube-cut burley join it. Per the manufacturer's description, the blend's top note is brandy; the flavoring is kept at a level that accompanies the tobacco's own sweetness rather than masking it. It sits somewhere between light and medium for nicotine, making it suitable for those wanting an all-day aromatic. It appeals to smokers who love cavendish sweetness and avoid heavy syrupy blends, while also wanting burley's nutty body. Being a ribbon cut, the pipe packs easily and burns evenly.
cornell-diehl-bradyville.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma of soft brandy and toasted sugar.

motzek-sailing-city.z: Sailing City is an American-style blend taking its name from Kiel's identity as a sailing city. Heavily cut virginias and dark-fired virginias are joined by a generous amount of perique and kentucky. It is presented as a coarse cut, in very broad ribbons and sometimes chunk-sized pieces; this coarseness produces a slow, cool burn. At the core of the taste, Virginia's bready sweetness meets kentucky's woody smokiness, while perique pulls the sharpness upward with pepper and dark-fruit acidity. The nicotine load sits above medium. Suitable for smokers who enjoy unflavored, tobacco-focused, spicy blends and are used to packing coarsely cut tobaccos. Motzek is a small Kiel-based workshop that has produced its own tobacco since the late 1970s; after Herbert Motzek's retirement, production passed to Tom Darasz, and the products have continued under the name TAK.
motzek-sailing-city.o: Leaves a peppery sharpness alongside the woody-smoky aroma of dark-fired leaf.

mcclelland-no-m-55-georgia-cream.z: A blend in McClelland's M-series bulk aromatics, discontinued when the firm closed in 2018; no sufficient source documenting its contents and character could be found.

hearth-home-international-pipe-smoking-d.z: There is not enough sourcing to document the composition of this limited edition, said to have been released by Hearth & Home for World Pipe Smoking Day 2011.

watch-city-cigar-blue-ridge-special.z: Blue Ridge Special is a house blend in the Scottish tradition built on mature red Virginia leaf. Latakia is used only at a spicing level, in a measured way; this keeps Virginia sweetness in front while adding a lightly smoky layer to the smoke. It's a mixture with measured body suitable for all-day smoking.
watch-city-cigar-blue-ridge-special.o: A subtle wood-smoke trace mixes into a sweetish dry-grass scent.

payless-pipes-custom-blends-no-526.z: No. 526 is referred to as an aromatic mixture within Payless Pipes' numbered line of custom blends from this American retailer; no independent source describing its composition could be found.
payless-pipes-custom-blends-no-526.o: No source could be found to describe the room note.

just-for-him-golden-cashmere.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Just For Him's Golden Cashmere blend.

king-smoking-pipes-and-cigars-king-of-di.z: A blend King Smoking Pipes and Cigars lists as Virginia- and Burley-based; no verifiable source could be found for its content proportions and cut.
king-smoking-pipes-and-cigars-king-of-di.o: Reportedly close to the nutty, earthy tobacco scent left by Virginia-Burley blends.

john-dengler-black-maria.z: One of the house blends from Dengler tobacconist in Hermann, Missouri; no verifiable information on its contents could be found.
john-dengler-black-maria.o: No verifiable information on its room note could be found.

milan-tobacconists-butter-berry.z: Butter Berry is a house blend in Milan Tobacconists' fruity-aromatics wing. Virginia and burley leaves are combined with black cavendish; according to the maker's description a vanilla-forward taste is built, with a pronounced forest-berry taste left at the finish. The mixture is light-bodied and low in nicotine; the casing, however, is felt at an above-medium intensity. Suitable for smokers looking for sweet, fruity aromatics who don't mind the casing overshadowing the tobacco body.
milan-tobacconists-butter-berry.o: Leaves an aroma of buttery vanilla and ripe red fruit.

d-w-g-cigar-corporation-klompen-kloggen.z: Klompen Kloggen, whose name means "wooden shoe" in Dutch, is an old American blend built in the Dutch-style aromatic tradition. Per its marketing copy, it's hand-mixed from shag-cut Burley, light-colored long-cut Virginia, Carolina leaf, Connecticut shade leaf, and Turkish Yenidje tobacco; the fruit-based flavoring applied during curing is considered the blend's signature. On the smoke, a light cherry or fruit sweetness sits alongside a texture reminiscent of cigar leaf and a dry Oriental spice; body is mild to medium, and it's known for not biting the tongue. The blend was produced by the D.W.G. Cigar Corporation; at the end of 1967, rights to the brand passed to R. G. Dun Corp., and the name was later carried on by other manufacturers. This entry describes the original D.W.G.-era version, which as such is discontinued.
d-w-g-cigar-corporation-klompen-kloggen.o: Leaves a scent where a light cherry-fruit note mingles with cigar leaf and the dry, smoky trace of Oriental tobacco.

hearth-home-dunhill-bb1938-match.z: A matching blend Hearth & Home prepared to stand in for Dunhill's discontinued BB1938 blend; there is not enough independent sourcing to confirm its composition.
hearth-home-dunhill-bb1938-match.o: Leaves a woody, smoky tobacco aroma.

john-middleton-inc-kentucky-club.z: The flagship blend of John Middleton's Burley-based Kentucky Club line; not enough sources could be found on its contents, cut, and character.
john-middleton-inc-kentucky-club.o: Leaves a dry, nutty tobacco aroma.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-deliverance.z: Deliverance is one of the members of the series that Gauntleys, a Nottingham tobacconist founded in 1880, blends by hand in its own shop. At its base sits vanilla-flavoured black cavendish and chocolate-seasoned Virginia leaf; a considerable amount of Latakia, dark fire-cured leaf, and perique is added on top. It is presented partly whole, partly in broken flakes.
gauntleys-of-nottingham-deliverance.o: Leaves a heavy aroma in which woody fire-smoke can be sensed beneath the vanilla and chocolate sweetness.

hearth-home-hall-of-fame.z: There is not enough sourcing to document the composition and character of the Hall of Fame blend from Hearth & Home.

ohm-turkish-red.z: OHM Turkish Red is one of two blends containing oriental leaf within the American-made OHM line. While the line's other members are built solely from American-origin leaf, Turkish Red and Turkish Yellow have Turkish-sourced oriental leaf added. It is prepared as a ribbon cut and offered in large-gram packaging. On the smoke, the oriental leaf's dry, herbal, spicy sharpness is pronounced; Virginia and Burley give body to that sharpness. Between the two Turkish blends, Red sits at the fuller taste level. It suits those seeking the oriental leaf's dry, spicy character without the mediation of a topping.
ohm-turkish-red.o: Leaves a scent recalling dry grass and spice, with a lightly smoky sharpness.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-sir-walte.z: Sir Walter Raleigh, released in 1927, is a burley-forward blend counted among the classics of American shelf pipe tobaccos. The crosscut leaf brings out burley's inherent cocoa and nut tones; a light casing applied to the blend adds a fine sweetness in the direction of anise and molasses. Nicotine is medium, giving a mild, cool smoke on the palate.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-sir-walte.o: Leaves a nutty, cocoa-forward tobacco scent with a light molasses sweetness behind it.

mccranies-red-ribbon-vintage-1996.z: Red Ribbon is McCranie's shop's first tinned blend and its best-known product, produced for the shop by McClelland. It's an unflavored, single-varietal red Virginia, and since each tin is made from North Carolina leaf of a single harvest year, the year appears on the label. The 1996 batch is among the earlier releases in this vintage series. The leaf is fermented and rested, then tinned as ribbon cut; color ranges from bright yellow to dark brown. Its character rests on dried-fruit tartness, dark sugar sweetness, and a yeasty depth from aging. It's often linked to the same maker's well-known red Virginia cake, and, per records, this batch carries a darker profile owing to its single-harvest basis and longer rest. Nicotine satiety is moderate, but its intense flavor and sugar load call for a slow smoke. Aimed at smokers who follow unflavored Virginias and aged tins; the series ended when McClelland stopped production in 2018.
mccranies-red-ribbon-vintage-1996.o: Leaves a trace reminiscent of baked bread crust, where vinegary tart fruit and dry hay aromas meet.

sullivan-powell-no-ox-special-mixture.z: Referred to as one of the English-style mixtures from the Sullivan & Powell shop in London's Burlington Arcade; sufficient independent sources documenting the blend's composition could not be found.
sullivan-powell-no-ox-special-mixture.o: Records indicate it leaves a woody smoke scent dominated by latakia.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-yazoo-wit.z: Yazoo Witch is one of the seasonal blends The Country Squire releases in small batches, timed to the Halloween period. Aged and toasted Virginia leaves form the axis; Turkish tobacco, dark fire-cured Kentucky, a pinch of Latakia and Louisiana Perique darken this base. The 2025 release was rested in a Crittenden Distillery bourbon barrel. The pouch aroma reports a tangy sweetness and a note evoking barbecue sauce; on the smoke, grassy, earthy, spicy, floral, meaty and woody notes sit together. The body is full and nicotine is medium-to-high. Intended for smokers used to unflavored, dark, complex mixtures. The blend bears Quinn Crawford's signature; since it is produced in limited quantity, sales are restricted per person.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-yazoo-wit.o: Leaves a dark trace with a scent of toasted oak and darkened tobacco.

georgetown-tobacco-georgetown-flake.z: A flake blend carrying Georgetown Tobacco's name, reportedly based on pure Virginia; no verifiable sourcing on its composition and current production status could be found.
georgetown-tobacco-georgetown-flake.o: No record of the room aroma could be found.

cornell-diehl-winthrop.z: No listing for Cornell & Diehl's Winthrop blend could be found in the maker's current catalogue or in major retailer listings; its composition could not be confirmed.

pipes-pleasures-danish-cherry.z: Pipes & Pleasures is a tobacconist shop opened in Columbus, Ohio, in 1977; Danish Cherry is one of the blends the shop offers under its own name, though no sufficient sources describing the blend's content and character could be found.

tsuge-premium-pipe-tobacco-fujin-the-win.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Tsuge Premium Pipe Tobacco blend Fujin - The Wind God has been found.

brigadier-black-waterloo.z: Waterloo is a blend in the Brigadier Black line built on golden burley leaf. Only a small amount of vanilla is used as casing; the aim is to lightly sweeten the tobacco without covering its natural taste. The burley-forward composition gives a dry, nutty, earthy taste while carrying medium nicotine. The vanilla casing stays in the background, so the blend sits somewhere between aromatic and unflavored burley. Suitable for smokers who stay away from heavily flavored tobaccos yet still want some sweetness, favoring the burley character.
brigadier-black-waterloo.o: Leaves an aroma carrying a fine vanilla sweetness over roasted nuts.

peter-stokkebye-black-cavendish-no-201.z: PS201 is Peter Stokkebye's bulk tobacco made entirely from black Cavendish leaf. Only a pinch of vanilla bean extract is applied on top; the dark color and sweetness come mainly from the Cavendish process itself, meaning the leaf being matured under heat and pressure. The cut is loose ribbon and moisture is relatively high. Smoked on its own it is a cool, low-nicotine, mild tobacco with flavor intensity kept low. Its main use is as a blending component: added to other mixtures, it contributes sweetness and a cooler burn, softening the harshness of sharper leaves. It is aimed at smokers who blend their own mixtures and those seeking a very light aromatic.
peter-stokkebye-black-cavendish-no-201.o: Leaves an aroma recalling soft vanilla and sweet molasses.

nat-sherman-580-liberty-golden-virginia.z: A blend among the numbered pipe tobaccos of New York-based Nat Sherman; no independent source could be found to fill out its profile, so reliable information about its composition and character cannot be given.

paul-olsen-mrs-nielsen.z: Mrs Nielsen is a My Own Blend special edition put together around 2015 in memory of Inge-Lise Nielsen, wife of The Danish Pipe Shop's founder Steffen Nielsen. It contains matured dark Virginia, light Virginia, and cavendish, topped with almond, vanilla, and a generous amount of chocolate essence. The mixture is hand-pressed and left under pressure for a week, then rubbed out and packed. The pressing lets the essence work into the leaf; the smoke is darkly sweet and creamy, with nicotine load staying low. It suits smokers seeking a pronounced chocolate-vanilla character who enjoy intense aromatics. Like the line's other special editions, it's offered in limited numbers through the shop.
paul-olsen-mrs-nielsen.o: Leaves a dark, sugary scent recalling cocoa, vanilla, and sweet almond paste.

watch-city-cigar-noreaster.z: No sufficient source could be found regarding this house blend from Watch City Cigar, so its details could not be recorded.

sutliff-tobacco-company-african-queen-50.z: Sutliff African Queen #500 is a ribbon-cut bulk blend combining Izmir-origin oriental leaf with Mozambique tobacco and Virginia. It's listed in the catalog under the aromatic category, but the topping level is kept low, leaving the emphasis on the oriental leaf's own spicy, herbal character. The maker describes the blend as appealing both to those accustomed to English-style mixtures and to those used to the native American style. It contains no latakia; as a result it offers a medium-intensity smoke that runs on the oriental leaf's dry spiciness rather than a smoky profile. A stepping stone for those wanting to sample oriental tobacco in the shadow of a topping.
sutliff-tobacco-company-african-queen-50.o: A light sweet undertone accompanies a spicy, herbal oriental leaf scent.

mcclelland-easy-street.z: Easy Street is a blend in McClelland's flavored line, built entirely from black Cavendish leaf. The brand's catalog cites an unusual top note: English walnut; its ribbon cut is known for a slow, cool burn. Since the Cavendish process removes the leaf's natural sharpness and brings its sugar forward, the blend follows a plain, mild taste line and stays light on nicotine. A structure suited to smokers wanting a flavored but non-syrupy, all-day smoke, and to those new to the pipe. Since McClelland halted production entirely in 2018, the blend appears on the market only in old tins.
mcclelland-easy-street.o: Leaves a sweetish walnut-meat and burnt-sugar aroma.

john-cotton-john-cottons-number-3.z: A pipe tobacco blend released under the John Cotton name; not enough independent sources could be found to document its contents and character.
john-cotton-john-cottons-number-3.o: No source could be found on the room note.

d-r-tobacco-london-dock.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the D & R Tobacco brand as London Dock; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

low-country-pipe-cigar-pee-dee.z: Pee Dee is a mixture made by Cornell & Diehl for Low Country Pipe & Cigar in Little River, South Carolina, and is the brand's first burley-based blend. It contains heirloom dark and white burley varieties, matured red and light Virginia, and some St. James Parish perique; the leaf has a semi-rubbed texture with pressed pieces alongside loose ones, and it's ready to smoke straight from the tin. The tin note carries a dark cocoa and bitter-chocolate-like tone. In the smoke, burley's earthy, coarse tastes come first, followed by Virginia's malty, baked-bread sweetness, then perique's dark fruit and spice notes. Body and nicotine sit in the medium to medium-full range; suited to those seeking an unflavored, dark, chocolate-toned burley blend.
low-country-pipe-cigar-pee-dee.o: Leaves a dark room note reminiscent of cocoa, roasted hazelnut and earth.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-el-picante-ameri.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's El Picante Americana blend.
