wilke-pipe-tobacco-shipmate.z: Shipmate comes from the series of blends Wilke prepared for Abercrombie & Fitch, a Latakia-forward English record. According to the maker's description, the Latakia ratio is high, joined by Tennessee Burley and Virginia, with a small amount of Turkish leaf adding a spicy edge. It's unflavored; sweetness comes only from the Virginia, and Burley carries the body. It suits Latakia-accustomed smokers seeking high smoke density and above-medium strength. It's offered in bulk, and stock availability is seasonal.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-shipmate.o: Leaves a heavy wood-smoke and soot scent, with a light spice lingering behind.

gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-flake-rose-geran.z: This is one of the most pronounced examples of Lakeland tradition. This medium-thick flake is built from Indian-origin air-cured dark Virginias and other strong leaf; the cake is pressed in a hot press, rested, and then the top flavoring is applied. The result is a rose-and-geranium-based floral top note running alongside the tobacco's dark body. The slices are packed rubbed out or folded. Nicotine is above medium, and the floral essence is intense, lingering in the pipe for a long time — for this reason, smoking it in a dedicated pipe is common practice. Aimed at those wanting to get to know Lakeland essences or try the darkest end of this style.
gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-flake-rose-geran.o: The floral aroma of rose and geranium leaf sits as a thick layer over the dark tobacco.

dan-tobacco-swatte-deern.z: Swatte Deern is a Hamburg pipe tobacco named after a Low German phrase meaning "dark girl." The maker describes the blend as dark and soft, full-bodied and sweet: flavored black cavendish forms the body, while golden Virginia opens and lightens the mixture. Black cavendish's natural sweetness, together with the applied topping, gives a soft, cool smoke; it stays light in nicotine. It appears alongside the similarly named Lütte Deern in the maker's north-German-themed line. It suits smokers who love the classic Danish-style sweet aromatic. Distributed in 50- and 250-gram packages.
dan-tobacco-swatte-deern.o: Leaves a dark, sweet, soft scent leaning toward vanilla.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-high-hat.z: No sufficient source could be found documenting the composition and character of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend High Hat.

consolidated-777-amaretto.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Consolidated blend 777: Amaretto.

owl-shop-captain-courageous.z: One of the Owl Shop's house blends, described as a broad-cut aromatic mixture leaning toward caramel and chocolate. No independent source stating its leaf composition could be found.
owl-shop-captain-courageous.o: Leaves a sweet scent recalling caramel and chocolate.

just-for-him-ole-doc-byroms.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for Just For Him's Ole Doc Byrom's, so the profile is left incomplete.

carolina-rose-carolina-rose.z: Carolina Rose is known for the single blend bearing its name, an aromatic tobacco sold in an ornate 100-gram tin. Virginia, Burley, black Cavendish and Oriental leaf are used together in its content; the cut sits between broken slice and wide ribbon, and multiple leaf colors are visible in the tin — an appearance unusual for aromatic tobaccos. The tin aroma combines fruity cherry with floral rose tones; in the smoke the aroma stays fainter than in the tin. Nicotine is low, flavor intensity light. Because of its moisture content and sliced structure it can be hard to light, and needs to be rubbed out and aired. The presence of Oriental leaf adds a light dry spice to the base. Aimed at smokers seeking a light, floral aromatic.
carolina-rose-carolina-rose.o: Leaves a sweet floral aroma reminiscent of cherry and rosewater.

w-o-larsen-limited-edition-2019.z: This is one of W.Ø. Larsen's annual limited editions; no reliable source could be found regarding its composition and character.
w-o-larsen-limited-edition-2019.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

iwan-ries-proper-english.z: This is a blend from the Three Star line prepared over the counter by the Chicago-based tobacconist Iwan Ries & Co.; no independent source detailing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
iwan-ries-proper-english.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

bjarne-flake-de-luxe.z: Flake de Luxe is a flake pressed into broad slices from selected sweet, mellow Virginia leaf. The slices range in color from light to medium brown, with occasional darker patches; though relatively dry and crumbly-looking, they hold together tightly. On opening the tin, apricot is the dominant note; the light topping over it is one example of the soft, fruited top-note style referred to as the Danish style. The blend belongs to a line established in memory of Danish pipe maker Bjarne Nielsen and is prepared by the German maker Dan Tobacco (DTM). With its light nicotine, it suits smokers looking for an all-day tobacco sitting somewhere between a lightly topped Virginia flake and a light aromatic. According to records, its distribution is largely limited to the German market.
bjarne-flake-de-luxe.o: Leaves a warm room note reminiscent of apricot and sweet fruit preserves.

campbells-smoke-shop-12-kon-tiki.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named # 12 Kon-Tiki under the Campbell's Smoke Shop brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-chok-lit-pie.z: An aromatic small-batch blend in Ken Byron Ventures' Yoshimi's line; not enough sources could be found to document its composition and character.
ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-chok-lit-pie.o: Could not be described due to lack of accessible records.

peter-stokkebye-black-truffle-no-51.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Black Truffle (No.51) could be found.

murray-sons-co-ltd-barneys.z: One of the Virginia-Latakia-centered blends from the Belfast-based Murray Sons & Co factory; production ended when the factory closed, and sufficient independent sources documenting the blend could not be found.

peterson-summertime-2010.z: This is the 2010 edition of Peterson's Summertime series, released annually for the summer season; while the series overall is said to use Virginia and Burley leaf sourced from Africa and South America, no sufficient sources giving this year's specific composition and topping could be found.
peterson-summertime-2010.o: Leaves a lightly fruity, sweet aroma.

cousins-cigar-custom-blends-cousins.z: Recorded as a house blend a tobacco shop had prepared under its own name; no source documenting its composition and character was found.

hearth-home-lakeland-brickle.z: Lakeland Brickle is a blend that pairs the topping tradition of England's Lakeland district with American manufacturing. The base is mainly red Virginia and dark, sharp Burley, topped with classic Lakeland essences such as rose and tonka bean. Because the essences are applied in moderation, the floral note stays more restrained than the heavy soapy effect often associated with traditional Lakeland blends. Burley adds body, spice, and nicotine to the mix. A stepping-stone for smokers curious about floral toppings but wary of the most intense examples.
hearth-home-lakeland-brickle.o: Leaves a sweet aroma evoking rose and floral soap-perfume.

barclay-rex-diplomat.z: Diplomat is one of the shop blends sold under its own name by Barclay Rex, the family business operating in New York since 1910. It's built from Virginia and Burley leaf paired with toasted Cavendish; this structure gives the blend a lightly sweet taste and a cool-burning character. It suits smokers looking for a moderately sweet everyday blend, away from heavily syruped aromatics. Since the sweetness from toasting isn't dominant, the tobacco leaf's own taste is also felt. Nicotine load is below medium.
barclay-rex-diplomat.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly caramel room note from the toasted Cavendish.

mac-baren-aromatic-choice.z: Aromatic Choice is a ribbon-cut aromatic Mac Baren builds on yellow Virginia, its own cavendish processing and burley. On opening the pack, mixed fruit scents greet you; among these, peach dominates enough to make the others hard to distinguish. Alongside fruit extracts, the casing also carries liqueur-like tones. The casing proportion is high, giving a sugary, fruity smoke; it's very light in nicotine. Smoked slowly it doesn't burn the tongue and behaves less moist than it looks, so it can be smoked without going out; even so, a short airing before packing helps. Suited to smokers seeking an intensely flavored tobacco and to those switching to the aromatic side for variety.
mac-baren-aromatic-choice.o: Leaves an intense mixed-fruit room note, peach foremost.

the-ridge-pipe-tobacco-berkeley-flake.z: No reliable source could be found on The Ridge Pipe Tobacco's Berkeley Flake blend.

hearth-home-stockade.z: Stockade is a blend in the aromatic wing of the Hearth & Home brand; no sufficient source describing its content and flavor structure could be found.

cornell-diehl-hermans-own.z: A blend Cornell & Diehl prepared in memory of Herman G. Lane, a well-known name in the tobacco industry, described as an introduction to English mixtures; not enough independent sourcing could be found for compositional details.
cornell-diehl-hermans-own.o: Leaves a smoky, woody tobacco aroma.

park-lane-tobacconist-dominion.z: One of Park-Lane Tobacconist's Virginia-forward house blends; no usable source describing its composition could be found.

mars-cigars-pipes-turkish-ribbon-cut.z: The name suggests an Oriental-leaf-forward, ribbon-cut house blend; since no source documenting its composition could be found, the profile is left incomplete.
mars-cigars-pipes-turkish-ribbon-cut.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

john-sinclair-highland-sliced.z: Highland Sliced is one of the sliced-presentation aromatic blends from the John Sinclair brand; not enough sources could be found to describe its contents and character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-loire-valley.z: Loire Valley, part of Sutliff's Private Stock line, is a fruited aromatic built on a black cavendish base. Records indicate the dominant flavor is raspberry; the vanilla note stays quite light, mostly serving as a base beneath the fruit. Body sits between light and medium, with low nicotine density. Aimed at smokers seeking a fruited aromatic that doesn't sit heavy on the tongue and leaves a pronounced sweet scent in the room; not a suitable choice for those wanting an unflavored tobacco taste.
sutliff-tobacco-company-loire-valley.o: Leaves a scent of red berry jam and light vanilla.

ole-shenandoah-summer-brandy-berry-appal.z: Summer Brandy Berry is an Ole Shenandoah aromatic also previously known as Appalachian Berry. Green River burley and black cavendish make up the body, topped with a brandy-and-mixed-forest-fruit-direction flavoring. It's described as being at an easily smokable moisture straight from the tin, needing no drying. Nicotine level is very light and the taste mild; the leading direction is the topping's fruity sweetness, described as a blended profile not tied to a single fruit. With easy packing and trouble-free burning, it's a low-threshold option on the aromatic wing; it suits newcomers to the pipe and those seeking a sweet, light blend. Records indicate it is not in production today.
ole-shenandoah-summer-brandy-berry-appal.o: Leaves a mixed forest-fruit scent not tied to a single fruit, on a sweet base.

hearth-home-el-nino-reposado-limited-edi.z: El Nino is the Marquee series' red Virginia and Perique based blend; unflavored black Cavendish forms the body, while fire-cured Kentucky and a very small amount of Latakia add depth. In the Reposado edition, this blend was rested in oak barrels that had held tequila, letting the spirit's aroma transfer directly to the leaf; no liquid alcohol is added to the blend. According to sources, the idea grew out of the tobacco-like tone detectable in aged tequila. The most prominent layers on the smoke are fire-cured leaf and Latakia, followed by Perique's plum-and-pepper note; the overall character is lightly tart and mildly sweet. Records indicate production stayed under 1,800 tins, making it a limited series of interest to smokers seeking unconventional recipes.
hearth-home-el-nino-reposado-limited-edi.o: Leaves a spirit-like aroma reminiscent of tart fruit, light smoke, and barrel wood.

synjeco-kentmere-sliced-twist.z: Kentmere Sliced Twist is a twist tobacco prepared for Synjeco at the Kendal maker. Records indicate the house's Oxenfisl twist forms the base, with roughly seven percent Perique added to the blend's core; the product is twisted into rope form and sliced into thin, coin-like discs. The discs are rubbed out and aired for a while before packing. Virginia's dark sweetness is topped by Perique's peppery, plum-like spice; because of the tight pressing, the taste is intense and the nicotine load pronounced. It suits smokers seeking a strong, unflavored Virginia-Perique profile who are used to twist tobaccos.
synjeco-kentmere-sliced-twist.o: Leaves a scent of darkened leaf, grain, and light pepper.

erik-stokkebye-resolution.z: Small Batch Resolution is the first blend produced by Cornell & Diehl for the 4th Generation label. It combines Carolina mahogany and Canadian bright Virginia leaves with aged orientals from Greece and Turkey; the mixture is pressed and sliced into flake. The flavor profile carries, alongside the sweetness of Virginia sugar, notes of citrus, caramelized sugar, buttery shortbread and light hazelnut; the orientals give this sweetness a dry, spicy balance. It suits those who love unadulterated Virginia-oriental mixtures and the slow smoke of pressed formats.
erik-stokkebye-resolution.o: Leaves a trace close to the scent of caramelized sugar and baked buttery shortbread.

d-r-tobacco-blenders-bench-blonde-burley.z: Blonde Burley is the light-colored Burley leaf sold in Daughters & Ryan's single-leaf Blenders Bench line. Burley is an air-cured tobacco with low sugar content, so it burns cool and has little tendency to bite the tongue. Its flavor structure runs toward nuts, cocoa, and earth, with sweetness staying in the background. In blending it's used as a body-and-nicotine carrier and as a base leaf with high casing absorbency; it's aimed at smokers building their own blends.
d-r-tobacco-blenders-bench-blonde-burley.o: Leaves a scent of dry nutshell and earth.

w-o-larsen-old-belt-ready-rubbed.z: This is a ready-rubbed blend known under the W.O. Larsen name; no reliable source could be found documenting its composition and character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-sunrise-smoke.z: Recorded as one of Sutliff Tobacco Company's English-style blends; since no accessible source describing its content could be found, the profile is incomplete.

peretti-enigma-flake.z: Enigma Flake is a Peretti flake pressed from select burley leaf. Per the maker's description, it carries a measured bouquet: notes recalling dried plum and tart fruit preserves merge with burley's hazelnut-brown depth to give a mild sweetness. The sweetness comes more from the leaf itself and the pressing than from any topping. Peretti states that aged, scarce lots of leaf are used in the blend, which keeps production limited. Being a flake, it needs rubbing out or folding before packing; it suits a burley-based smoker looking for a taste close to unadulterated.
peretti-enigma-flake.o: Leaves a nutty scent recalling dried plum and tart forest-fruit preserves.

john-patton-forgotten-memories.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Patton's Forgotten Memories pipe tobacco.

ken-byron-ventures-plateau-of-leng.z: Not enough independent sources could be reached to fill out the record for Ken Byron Ventures' blend called Plateau of Leng.

mclintock-pipe-smokers-scottish-premium.z: Pipe Smoker's Scottish Premium is a variety that appeared in McLintock's Pipe Smoker's sub-line; sufficient sources regarding the blend's composition and cut could not be found.
mclintock-pipe-smokers-scottish-premium.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet aroma with a light whisky association.

savinelli-145th-anniversary.z: A limited-production blend Savinelli released for its 145th anniversary, according to records built on Virginia and Perique; no sufficient source confirming its composition could be found.

mcclelland-cpcc-scottish-woods.z: Scottish Woods is a Scottish-style mixture McClelland produced for the Chicagoland Pipe Collectors Club. Cyprian Latakia gives the blend a pronounced soot-and-smoke line; Oriental leaves add a lively spice, while matured Virginias provide the sweetness. The element that carries the blend into Scottish style is the addition of steam-processed (stoved) black Virginia, commonly known in Europe as black Cavendish. This structure builds a rounder, sweeter base than Latakia-forward English mixtures; no flavoring is used. A blend aimed at smokers who like smoky mixtures but want a sweet undertone rather than sharpness. The maker ceased operations in early 2018.
mcclelland-cpcc-scottish-woods.o: A sweet, faintly caramel undertone accompanies an intense wood-smoke aroma.

j-f-germain-son-germains-special-latakia.z: Special Latakia Flake is J. F. Germain & Son's product presenting its classic English blend in pressed form. It contains Latakia, Oriental leaves, and Virginia; because the mixture is pressed and sliced, the flavors meld together over time, giving a denser, more cohesive smoke than ribbon-cut versions. The Latakia smokiness is pronounced, but the Oriental's dry, slightly sour spiciness and the Virginia's sweetness keep it in balance. Smoking pace can be adjusted by how much the flake is rubbed out. It's aimed at smokers who know the English style, enjoy pressed formats, and don't shy away from smoky flavors.
j-f-germain-son-germains-special-latakia.o: Beneath the smoky wood and cedar aroma, a trace of dry spice can be detected.

half-half-half-half-light-american.z: The light-line version of the American Half & Half brand, based on Burley and light Virginia and offered in export markets; there is not enough independent sourcing to confirm this particular version's composition and character.

w-o-larsen-selected-blend-no-30.z: No reliable source could be found regarding the composition and character of this entry in W.Ø. Larsen's numbered Selected Blend series; the series as a whole generally consists of light, moderately cased Danish blends.
w-o-larsen-selected-blend-no-30.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

mclintock-syrian-latakia-blend.z: Syrian Latakia Blend is an English-style blend that German maker Kohlhase & Kopp released in its McLintock line, taking its name from its base leaf. It is noted as one of the few blends still using Syrian latakia during a period when Cyprus latakia had become widespread; the latakia is joined by burley and virginia. The leaf is coarse cut and suited to being loaded at the moisture level it comes out of the pack. Syrian latakia gives a less coal-like, sweeter, spicier smoke than the Cyprus version; the burley base adds a nutty body to the blend, while virginia leaves a measured sweetness in the background. Suitable for smokers accustomed to English and Balkan styles who don't mind a heavy tin note.
mclintock-syrian-latakia-blend.o: Leaves a heavy smoke trace reminiscent of smoked wood and smoky leather.

peter-heinrichs-reserve-crue-no-8.z: Reserve Crûe No. 8 is a Peter Heinrichs blend, pressed into a plug, combining Malawi-origin fermented black Cavendish with American Burley leaf. Per the maker's description, Cavendish lays down a soft, deep base while Burley adds a calm, earthy character; a fine chocolate note applied on top ties the components together. The plug structure gives a dense texture, a slow burn, and a flavor that develops steadily through the smoke; it needs to be sliced and rubbed out before packing. Sweetness is measured and the body is medium. It suits smokers with time to prepare pressed tobacco who are seeking a dark, cocoa-toned Burley-Cavendish smoke.
peter-heinrichs-reserve-crue-no-8.o: Leaves a cocoa, roasted hazelnut, and dark bread aroma.

pufferspipes-com-baltimore-harbor-blend.z: This is a house blend an American retailer had prepared under its own name; no source could be found documenting its content.

hu-tobacco-buchstoun.z: Buchstoun is a flavored Latakia blend in HU Tobacco's Clans of Scotland line, referencing Scotland. Its base includes English-style black Cavendish, Mysore-origin ready-rubbed Virginia, and Cyprus Latakia; a flavoring evoking Scottish forest fruits, particularly Glen Coe raspberry, along with forest herbs is applied on top. In the smoke, fruity sweetness leads, while the Latakia builds a smoky, deep base; floral and herbal accents stay in the background. It offers an option stepping outside classic English blends for those wanting to try aromatic sweetness alongside Latakia's smoky structure. Records indicate it's presented in 50-gram tins.
hu-tobacco-buchstoun.o: Leaves an aroma where toasted-raspberry sweetness interweaves with smokiness, with a light herbal line underneath.

james-barber-golden-flake.z: A flake-cut blend from James Barber's tobacconist, reported to be Virginia-forward; not enough sources could be found to describe its composition.

clan-shaw-california.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend California.

casey-jones-heros-blend.z: Casey Jones is a classic American aromatic tobacco line named after Jonathan Luther "Casey" Jones, the American engineer who died at his post in the 1900 crash of his train. Hero's Blend is the line's base blend: Virginia cavendish is brought together with a black cavendish made from Green River burley, topped with a soft vanilla-and-honey-forward casing. The smoke is low in nicotine and soft, with a character that does not turn harsh on the tongue and can be sustained all day. Suitable for those who prefer measured sweetness over heavy sugar in aromatics, and for smokers new to the pipe. The ribbon cut makes it easy to fill and light.
casey-jones-heros-blend.o: Leaves a warm vanilla and honey room note.

doctor-pipe-pure-golden-virginia-flake.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Pure Golden Virginia Flake, a pipe tobacco from Doctor Pipe.
doctor-pipe-pure-golden-virginia-flake.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

brigham-enterprises-inc-king-street.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named King Street under the Brigham Enterprises Inc. brand could be found.

lane-limited-cappuccino.z: Not enough independent sources could be found documenting the contents and character of American blender Lane Limited's blend called Cappuccino.

dream-castle-tobacco-company-vanilla.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of Vanilla, a blend from Dream Castle Tobacco Company.

hu-tobacco-brullende-leeuw.z: Brullende Leeuw is an English-style blend HU Tobacco prepared for a Dutch pipe forum; the name means "roaring lion" in Dutch and symbolizes the Dutch-Flemish connection. Latakia, Oriental tobaccos, some black Cavendish, and a small proportion of Perique are added atop light and red Virginia leaves. Latakia stands at the blend's main axis; the Orientals add a woody, herbal layer, the Virginia leaves ripe fruit and tart sweetness, and the Perique brings dried fruit and spice in the background. With its unflavored structure and medium strength, it's aimed at those looking for a Latakia mixture that can be smoked all day.
hu-tobacco-brullende-leeuw.o: A spicy, sweetish background accompanies the smoky wood aroma reminiscent of a campfire.

villiger-original-export.z: Original Export is the most widely distributed pipe tobacco from Swiss-origin Villiger. Various Virginia leaves, black cavendish, and Burley are brought together, topped with a casing giving vanilla, spice, and a small amount of cocoa notes. The cut is ribbon-style and ready to pack directly as it comes from the pouch. It's an everyday aromatic that stays light in nicotine, with sweetness in front but without weighing heavy in the mouth. It's designed for newcomers to the pipe or smokers seeking a soft blend suitable for long sessions. Villiger is a family company founded in 1888; though known for cigar production, it has carried on its pipe tobacco line for many years.
villiger-original-export.o: Leaves a scent of sweet vanilla, light cocoa, and warm spice.

teds-pipe-shoppe-st-patrick.z: One of the house blends prepared at Ted's Pipe Shoppe in Tulsa, Oklahoma; though records show it among the more than forty house blends of the business founded in 1961, no independent source describing the blend's content and character could be found.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-northwest.z: Northwest Trek, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an English-type mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

barling-garnet.z: Garnet is an unflavored mixture in the tobacco line of Barling, a brand founded in London in 1812; the blend is prepared in Germany by Planta. It contains Syrian Latakia, Burley, Perique, Java, and Virginia leaf; since the Latakia share is kept limited, it's classed as a light English blend. Syrian Latakia gives a drier, spicier smoke than Cyprus Latakia, while the Perique adds a plum-and-pepper depth. The Java leaf and Burley pull the blend toward the earthy side, and Virginia sweetness restores the balance. It offers a medium-bodied, layered but not heavy smoke; it suits smokers wanting to get to know English mixtures without diving into heavy Latakia bombs, or looking for a balanced, unflavored blend to smoke all day.
barling-garnet.o: Leaves a lightly smoky, sweetish wood room note.

milan-tobacconists-wall-street.z: Wall Street is an aromatic in which chocolate-hazelnut and buttercream sauces are applied to a body of virginia and a dark, chocolatey cavendish; a small amount of maduro cigar leaf is also mixed into the blend. The combination of sauces gives a taste reminiscent of nougat. Hazelnut shows mostly in the aroma, while the cigar leaf appears intermittently as a dry, papery layer. Aimed at those looking for an aromatic that isn't overly sugary and whose body is deepened by cigar leaf. Its name, according to records, is a reference to the mingling of pipe and cigar smoke in 1950s bank and business-district lobbies.
milan-tobacconists-wall-street.o: A light cigar-leaf tone mixes into the chocolate-and-hazelnut aroma.

w-o-larsen-w-o-larsen-2015-hand-pressed.z: This is one of W.Ø. Larsen's annual limited editions; no reliable source could be found regarding its composition and character.
w-o-larsen-w-o-larsen-2015-hand-pressed.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

john-aylesbury-major-1814-flake.z: John Aylesbury Major 1814 Flake belongs to the brand's series of pressed flakes named after historical dates; since it doesn't appear in the maker's current listing, no verifiable source could be found on its composition and flavor profile.

the-smoker-woodlands.z: A house blend called Woodlands from the American tobacconist The Smoker; it is noted as English-style, but no verifiable source describing its composition has been found.

paul-olsen-brown-capstan.z: One of the Poul Olsen shop's Virginia-based blends; not enough source material documenting its details could be found.

mac-baren-highland-mixture.z: Not enough information could be found in the manufacturer's current catalog or verifiable independent sources about this Mac Baren blend, which is described as aromatic.

just-for-him-blueberry-hill.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Just For Him's Blueberry Hill blend.

chonowitsch-t-14.z: T 14 belongs to the series prepared in small batches under Danish pipe maker Jess Chonowitsch's name, and is presented as a medium-bodied English mixture; no detailed manufacturer description regarding its composition could be found.

gauloises-gauloises-pipe.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauloises brand's Gauloises Pipe blend.

james-barber-bourbon.z: This is an aromatic house blend from the James Barber tobacconist house, flavored with bourbon whiskey; no independent source documenting its composition and character could be found.
james-barber-bourbon.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-white-lightning.z: White Lightning is one of Cornell & Diehl's ribbon-cut aromatic blends. Its base holds a concentrated mixture of red and light-colored Virginia, joined by Louisiana Perique. On the casing side, applejack forms the foundation, topped with raspberry and vanilla notes. On the maker's scale, strength is low and flavor intensity medium. Since Perique's fermented-fruit spice works in the same direction as the apple and red-fruit casing, the blend stays within the fruited-aromatic band. Aimed at smokers looking for a mild-nicotine, clearly cased everyday blend.
cornell-diehl-white-lightning.o: Leaves a pronounced scent where apple and red-fruit sweetness mingle with vanilla.

ken-byron-ventures-river-of-deceit-2023.z: The 2023-dated version of the same-named blend, distinctly aromatic; not enough sources could be found to describe its casings and composition.

tinder-box-sherlocks-choice.z: No reliable source has been found for the Tinder Box pipe blend called Sherlock's Choice.

faders-vanilla-custard.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for the Fader's brand's Vanilla Custard pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

watch-city-cigar-simply-voriental.z: Watch City Cigar's blend called Simply VOriental is, according to records, one of the house blends of the Waltham, Massachusetts tobacconist shop; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

sutliff-tobacco-company-edward-g-robinso.z: Edward G. Robinson's Pipe Blend is one of the bulk blends from the Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

peter-stokkebye-cherry-no-3.z: Cherry is one of Peter Stokkebye's classic records drawing on the Danish aromatic tradition. Its base is built from flue-cured Virginia and soft Burley leaf; these leaves are pressed and sliced by the Cavendish method and then opened into a loose cut for packaging. A measured cherry flavoring is applied on top; while cherry is pronounced in the scent, the taste in the mouth stays much lighter, letting the tobacco's own sweetness come forward. The blend is light-bodied and low in nicotine; it can be lit at any time of day and gives no trouble in packing or burning. It suits newcomers to aromatic blends and those wanting a fruity scent without a heavy sugary taste in the mouth.
peter-stokkebye-cherry-no-3.o: Fills the room with a ripe cherry and lightly sugared tobacco aroma.

peretti-blend-no-111.z: This is a numbered shop blend Peretti lists in its Burley group; it also appears in the shop's unflavored Burley sample sets, though its composition has not been published.

emerson-southern-forged-strathaven.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing could be found for Strathaven, a blend from Emerson Southern Forged, so the record has been left open; according to available listings it is classified in the Straight Virginia family.

villiger-robi.z: Robi is a Villiger blend that, according to records, combines Virginia leaves of different cuts and colors with Burley grown in Switzerland; no second independent source could be found confirming the details.

schermerhorn-schermerhorns-flake-mixture.z: No sufficient source documenting the content, producer, and character of this blend, understood from its name to be a flake-cut mixture, could be found.

japan-tobacco-asuka.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of Japan Tobacco's Asuka blend could be found.

edwards-coco-creme.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of CoCo Creme, a pipe tobacco from Edward's. Edward's is a tobacconist business based in Tampa, Florida.

peretti-burlington-blend.z: Burlington Blend is a Peretti blend prepared by flavoring selected light golden Green River leaf with honey. Per the maker's account, a slow curing is applied; the aim is a smooth, sweet smoke in which the sugar works its way into the leaf. While the honey flavoring comes forward, it isn't an intensely syrupy aromatic; Burley's nutty, dry base remains noticeable underneath. It suits smokers seeking a moisture-balanced, cool-burning blend who want to avoid heavy fruit flavorings.
peretti-burlington-blend.o: Leaves a warm honey and dry hay aroma.

jerris-tobacco-shop-denver-co-blwb-burle.z: No reliable source documenting the content and character of Jerri's Tobacco Shop Denver, CO's Blwb Burley Light Without Bite blend could be found.

mcclelland-royal-cajun-ebony.z: Royal Cajun Ebony is the darkest member of McClelland's series built around the Cajun Black component. Cajun Black is produced by first smoking Virginia-seed leaf grown in Kentucky, then barrel-pressing and fermenting it as with Perique; per the brand's description, it was the first new component added to pipe tobacco in over forty years. In Ebony, stoved dark Virginia leaves are used alongside this component. In the smoke, smoky, woody, and spicy layers stand out; the tangy sweetness from the Virginia serves as a balancing background. Body runs medium to full, and it calls for a slow smoke. Suited to smokers who find the other series members not dark enough and who seek fermented, smoked leaf character. McClelland ceased operations in 2018.
mcclelland-royal-cajun-ebony.o: Leaves a dark, smoky, and woody aroma, with an earthy weight behind it.

tinder-box-crown-royale.z: Tinder Box is the name of an American tobacconist chain founded in 1928 that sells blends prepared for its own shops under its own name; Crown Royale is one of these house blends, though no sufficient independent source describing its composition and character has been found.

samuel-gawith-full-virginia-flake.z: Full Virginia Flake is an unflavored pressed flake prepared solely from Virginia leaf and one of the brand's best-known products. The tin holds high moisture and sometimes thickly cut, uneven flakes; thick slices can be split lengthwise, and packing and lighting call for care. The intense sugary sweetness attributed to Virginia does not come forward here; instead it offers a full tobacco flavor combining sweetness, bitterness, and coolness. It gives a long, low-smoke, non-souring smoke. Suited to those seeking an unflavored Virginia flake and a balanced blend they can smoke any time of day.
samuel-gawith-full-virginia-flake.o: Leaves a measured-sweetness tobacco scent evoking dry hay and bread.

ashton-platinum.z: A blend referred to as affiliated with the Ashton brand; no independent source documenting its content and character could be found, leaving the profile blank.

imperial-tobacco-group-plc-scaferlati-su.z: Scaferlati Superior, a tobacco belonging to the French scaferlati tradition, was reportedly first produced by Seita, its license passed to Imperial Tobacco for a period, and it was later withdrawn from the market; no reliable source about the blend's composition could be found, so no further detail is given.

cornell-diehl-brigadier.z: Brigadier is a blend bringing together Latakia, cube-cut burley, perique, and toasted brown cavendish, topped with a light fruit flavoring. The maker places the blend in the English family; the leaf, cut short and granulated, makes packing easy and gives a slow burn. The Latakia level isn't high enough to make smoke the dominant note; burley provides body and a nutty dryness, perique adds spice, and the fruit flavoring gives a measured sweetness. This structure suits those newly transitioning to Latakia blends and smokers wanting a smoky taste paired with light sweetening.
cornell-diehl-brigadier.o: A light fruit sweetness mixes into the wood-smoke aroma.

bosphorus-currant.z: Currant is a ribbon-cut aromatic prepared using Çanakkale and Samsun tobaccos with cavendish, flavored with black-currant aroma. Its strength and flavor are medium. Per records the product has been discontinued; today it can only be encountered in old stock. It stands as one of the early examples of domestically produced fruit-flavored blends.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kentucky-cc-blending.z: Kentucky CC Blending isn't a blend but a blending ingredient. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. sells single-leaf varieties unflavored and individually under the "CC" (coarse cut) label; this entry is the standalone offering of dark fire-cured Kentucky leaf. Fire-curing gives the leaf a heavy smokiness, a woody depth, and high nicotine. While it can be smoked on its own, its real use is as a component smokers who build their own blends add in small proportions to give a mixture body, fullness, and a smoky base. It is unflavored; its strength is high, so it's heavy going on its own for a smoker unaccustomed to nicotine.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kentucky-cc-blending.o: Leaves an aroma of wood fire and smoke.

mac-baren-amphora-vintage-malt-whiskey.z: Not enough information could be found in the manufacturer's current catalog or verifiable independent sources about this whisky-flavored blend in the Amphora line.

georgetown-tobacco-night-owl.z: Night Owl is one of the aromatic house blends from Georgetown Tobacco, which has operated in Washington since 1964. Its base contains moist, black, fire-cured Cavendish, joined by light-colored Virginia. Virginia serves a dual purpose: it reduces the moisture that collects at the bottom of the bowl and softens the black Cavendish's weight. The black and golden-yellow leaves sitting side by side also give the blend a visually distinct contrast. Vanilla sets the blend's flavor line — this topping, sitting atop Cavendish's sugary, dark base, leads in both smoke and aroma. Nicotine is low, the smoke is mild, and the ribbon cut makes it easy to pack. A product aimed less at unflavored English blends and more at those wanting a sweet, fragrant everyday smoke, and at those new to the pipe.
georgetown-tobacco-night-owl.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough aroma.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-sweet-street.z: Sweet Street is a Wilke aromatic that puts Burley front and center. Toasted, nutty, earthy, and woody Burley is the blend's star; sugary black cavendish plays a supporting role. The casing layout consists of nougat, chocolate, and vanilla over a heavy rum note; a whiskey tone also appears in the profile. Strength stays mild to medium, and it burns cool and smooth. It suits smokers seeking toasted sweetness alongside a nutty body, and a bowl with pronounced casing that doesn't bite the tongue. Wilke offers it in its bulk listing in various sizes.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-sweet-street.o: A scent of roasted nut, nougat, and rum stands out clearly in the room.

torben-dansk-40-jubilee-smooth-latakia.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Torben Dansk blend called 40 Jubilee Smooth Latakia has been found.

fribourg-treyer-vintage.z: Also known as Vintage Flake, this blend is produced by maturing untopped Virginia leaves under pressure and cutting them into thin flakes. The natural fermentation during pressing darkens the leaf's own sugars; the result brings out honeyed sweetness along with bread-crust and dried-fruit facets. It is a slow-burning flake that can be filled sliced or rubbed out. Since it contains no additive, it is considered well-suited to long tin ageing; it draws the interest of those wanting to observe a plain Virginia structure and how it changes over time.
fribourg-treyer-vintage.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of dry hay and baked bread crust.

park-lane-tobacconist-the-connoisseurs-f.z: No reliable source could be found for the Park brand pipe tobacco called Lane Tobacconist-The Connoisseurs Flake, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

4noggins-bread-loaf.z: Bread Loaf is one of 4noggins' Oriental-forward blends. Per the manufacturer's recipe, alongside the Oriental leaf the composition includes some cigar leaf, Virginia, Burley, and just enough Latakia to lend a hint of smoke. The name references Vermont's Bread Loaf area, continuing 4noggins' tradition, as with most of its house blends, of local naming. The tangy, spicy character of the Oriental leaf forms the blend's main axis, the cigar leaf adds earthy depth, and the very small amount of Latakia leaves a thin line of smoke in the background. Nicotine is moderate, and the maker notes the blend does not bite the tongue. It's aimed at smokers who want Latakia kept measured while the Oriental leaf's spice takes the foreground.
4noggins-bread-loaf.o: Leaves a spicy, lightly smoky, dry, grassy scent.

bufflehead-european-widgeon.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named European Widgeon under the Bufflehead brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

mac-baren-amphora-rich-aroma.z: Amphora Rich Aroma is a blend built by adding Virginia and oriental leaves to a burley base. It's presented rubbed out, ready to pack. The "rich" in its name points more to the fullness of the leaf mix itself than to a heavy sauce layer: burley's dry body, Virginia's sweetness and oriental's spice sit together. Nicotine is at a medium level, offering a balanced smoke. Suited to those seeking a middle path between the flavored and unflavored ends of the Amphora series.
mac-baren-amphora-rich-aroma.o: Leaves a nutty, lightly sweet, warm tobacco room note.

st-basils-tobacco-black-rhino.z: St. Basil's Tobacco is a small American house that has Cornell & Diehl produce its blends and whose distribution stays limited to the Pennsylvania and New Jersey area; though Black Rhino is referred to as English-style, sufficient independent sources describing the blend's composition could not be found.
st-basils-tobacco-black-rhino.o: No description is available in records.

john-dengler-mixture-724.z: One of the house blends from Dengler tobacconist in Hermann, Missouri; no verifiable information on its contents could be found.
john-dengler-mixture-724.o: No verifiable information on its room note could be found.

mac-baren-golden-sweet.z: Not enough information could be found in the manufacturer's current catalog or verifiable independent sources about this Mac Baren blend, which is described as aromatic.

samuel-gawith-squadron-leader.z: Squadron Leader is one of Samuel Gawith's ribbon-cut classic English mixtures. Its composition holds Virginia, Latakia, and Oriental (Turkish) leaf; it carries no casing. The fine, loose cut makes packing easy, and the burn proceeds without trouble. On the smoke, Virginia's sweetness runs alongside Latakia's cool, smoky line; the Oriental leaf's exotic tone stays in the background. Nicotine fullness and flavor intensity are low, so the blend stays light enough to smoke all day. Fits smokers newly starting on English mixtures or avoiding heavy Latakia doses; it may read as measured for those expecting intense smoke and high nicotine.
samuel-gawith-squadron-leader.o: Leaves a fine wood-smoke scent along with a sweetish tobacco trace.

john-aylesbury-latakia-blend.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to document the contents and character of John Aylesbury's Latakia Blend.

danske-club-sungold.z: Sungold is the vanilla-cased blend in the Danske Club series; for a long time it appeared in catalogues directly under the name Vanilla before being renamed. It uses the series' common base of Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish leaf. The ribbon cut allows for easy packing and even burning. Nicotine sits between mild and medium, with clear sweetness. Since vanilla is the most common casing in aromatic pipe tobacco, this blend counts as one of the type's familiar examples and serves as an entry point for those new to aromatics. It comes in 50-gram pouches and 100-gram tins.
danske-club-sungold.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and caramelized-dough scent.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.z: This is the whiskey-flavored aromatic in Imigrantes Fumos's Cândido Giovanella line. The blend is built on Brazilian-grown Virginia and Burley leaf with black Cavendish, and packed in ribbon cut. In the smoke, whiskey's barrel-like woody, lightly smoky, sweetish taste comes forward; Burley gives a dry base while Cavendish adds a dark sugary depth. Nicotine is moderate, the smoke cool. It suits those who enjoy liqueur-flavored aromatics and are looking for a darker profile for evening smoking.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.o: Leaves an alcoholic, lightly smoky, woody aroma reminiscent of whiskey.

park-lane-tobacconist-liebmans-scottish-.z: One of Park-Lane Tobacconist's Virginia-forward, flake-cut house blends; no usable source could be found to confirm its composition.

e-a-carey-cavendish-mixture.z: Referred to as one of E. A. Carey's cavendish-based aromatic mixtures; it does not appear in the current catalog, and no source could be found describing its composition.

dunhill-de-luxe-navy-rolls.z: De Luxe Navy Rolls is a blend where Virginia leaves are pressed into rolls together with perique and sliced into medallion shapes. The tin contains neatly arranged, spiral-patterned round slices. Folding rather than crumbling the slices before packing gives a long, even burn; the blend catches easily and finishes leaving a clean ash in the bowl. On the smoke, Virginia's sweet, fruity base and perique's black-pepper-like sharp spice trade places as the smoke progresses. This sharpness shouldn't be confused with nicotine strength; the blend's strength runs close to medium, with a soft texture. It suits smokers who love Virginia-perique mixtures, especially medallion-cut ones. Since pipe tobacco production under the Dunhill name has ended, the blend is no longer produced under this name.
dunhill-de-luxe-navy-rolls.o: A sharp, tart, spicy tobacco scent lingers in the room for a long time.

telfords-pipes-cigars-parish-1.z: One of roughly forty house blends prepared by Telford's Pipe & Cigar shop in Mill Valley, California; no accessible source describing the blend's composition and character could be found.

cobblestone-cafe-vanilla-latte.z: Cobblestone's Cafe Vanilla Latte blend is, per available records, a ribbon-cut, flavored mixture, though not enough independent sourcing could be found to detail its composition.

schurch-tarek-robusto-197.z: Referred to as one of the Swiss Schürch house's Latakia-bearing, English-style blends; no sufficient source documenting its composition ratios and cut could be found.

emerson-southern-forged-thomas-blend.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing could be found for Thomas' Blend, a blend from Emerson Southern Forged, so the record has been left open; according to available listings it is classified in the English family.

sutliff-tobacco-company-ts-4-white-cube-.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Sutliff Tobacco Company's TS-4 White Cube Burley pipe tobacco could be found.

briarworks-international-smokehouse.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named Smokehouse under the BriarWorks International brand could be found.

samuel-gawith-firedance-flake.z: Fire Dance Flake is produced by taking the brand's unflavored Best Brown Flake blend as a base and flavoring it with blackberry, brandy, and vanilla essences. This preserves the pressed Virginia body while adding a fruity top aroma on top. The smoke is measured in sweetness and mild; Virginia's bready character is felt beneath the casing. A plug form of the same blend is also produced. Suited to those seeking a cased flake that does not entirely cover the tobacco character.
samuel-gawith-firedance-flake.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly alcoholic scent evoking blackberry and vanilla.

thepiperoom-com-cherry-cordial.z: No independent source documenting the composition of ThePipeRoom.com's cherry-liqueur-themed blend Cherry Cordial has been found; the brand's own site is no longer online.
thepiperoom-com-cherry-cordial.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

peter-stokkebye-highland-whiskey-no-38.z: Highland Whiskey is a loose-cut blend that combines Zimbabwe- and Carolina-origin flue-cured Virginias with black Cavendish and roasted Burley, topped with an aged Scotch whiskey flavoring. Since the flavoring is kept measured, it doesn't mask the tobacco's own taste. On the palate a sweet, woody trace recalling whiskey, the Cavendish's toasted sweetness, and a light nuttiness from the Burley proceed together. The body sits between light and medium. It suits smokers seeking a blend with a liquor-based flavoring that stays drier than sugary aromatics.
peter-stokkebye-highland-whiskey-no-38.o: Fills the room with a warm, sweet aroma recalling roasted sugar and a whiskey cask.

erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-freja-loki.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing could be found for 4th Generation Freja & Loki, a blend from Erik Stokkebye, so the record has been left open; according to available listings it is classified in the Virginia Based family.

sutliff-tobacco-company-sutliff-rl-pr-bl.z: RL-PR Blend is Sutliff's cube-cut straight burley product. The letters "PR" in its name refer to the plum and rum extracts used in the blend; it contains no perique. The leaf is pressed and cut into cubes, lightly cased with plum, molasses, and rum extracts. The taste proceeds on a nutty, creamy base, carrying a light cocoa-like sweetness and a tart edge from the plum casing. The casing is measured, so it reads more as a cased classic American burley than as a true aromatic. It suits smokers who enjoy a plain, traditional burley smoke and are looking for the slow burn a cube cut gives.
sutliff-tobacco-company-sutliff-rl-pr-bl.o: Leaves a plain tobacco trace mixed with molasses sweetness and dried-plum scent.

comptons-of-galashiels-scottish-mixture.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Compton's of Galashiels blend Scottish Mixture.

pipesandcigars-com-jeffersonian-mixture.z: Jeffersonian Mixture is one of the house blends sold under its own name by the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com; no sufficient independent sources documenting its content and character could be found.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-no-66.z: Not enough independent sources could be reached to fill out the record for Kohlhase, Kopp und Co. KG's blend called No. 66.

paul-olsen-big-coin.z: No reliable source could be found for the Paul Olsen pipe tobacco called Big Coin, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

sutliff-tobacco-company-erin-go-bragh-ap.z: Erin Go Bragh Apple Crumble is the aromatic member of the Erin Go Bragh line produced by Sutliff Tobacco Company. Its base is formed by sweet, tangy Virginia leaves and soft, nutty burley; ripe apple and baking-spice notes are applied on top. The cut is ribbon. The blend's starting point is the traditional Irish dessert made from apple, oats, and crumbly dough, so its flavor line sits between fruity sweetness and warmed spice. Nicotine strength is kept low, making it a suitable structure for all-day smoking and for those new to aromatic blends.
sutliff-tobacco-company-erin-go-bragh-ap.o: Leaves a scent of freshly baked apple dessert and cinnamon.

poniatowski-sungold.z: This is an aromatic pipe blend carried under the name Poniatowski; no source could be found describing its content and character.

mr-bs-vanilla-maple.z: Vanilla Maple is one of the entries representing the aromatic wing of Brigham's Mr. B's line. Bright Virginia leaves are combined with natural cavendish and Brazilian-origin sun-cured dark tobaccos; a vanilla-and-maple-centered casing is applied on top. The ribbon cut makes packing and lighting easy. The casing level is pronounced and defines the blend's aroma; by contrast, nicotine and flavor intensity are kept low, and the smoke stays cool. A recipe geared toward smokers looking for a sweet, soft profile in aromatic tobaccos who don't want sharpness on the tongue. Distributed in the Canadian market in fifty-gram and bulk packaging.
mr-bs-vanilla-maple.o: Leaves an aroma of sweet vanilla and boiled maple syrup.

cornell-diehl-dancer.z: One of Cornell & Diehl's older Virginia-forward blends; it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog, and not enough sourcing could be found to describe its character.

cornell-diehl-london-squire.z: London Squire is a ribbon-cut English mixture Cornell & Diehl offers in bulk. Its structure holds Cyprus Latakia, sweet Virginia, nutty Burley, and unsweetened black Cavendish; here black Cavendish carries no flavor casing, being used instead to soften the blend and thicken its body. The resulting smoke is smoky but not sharp, with a creamy, full character. Sitting in the medium band for both strength and room note, it suits smokers newly moving into Latakia blends as well as those wanting a balanced English mixture they can smoke all day. Being an unflavored blend, its taste comes from the tobaccos' own balance, offering a profile swinging between Latakia's smoke and Virginia's sweetness. It's produced in the US and is generally found on bulk tobacco shelves rather than in tins.
cornell-diehl-london-squire.o: Leaves a scent dominated by wood smoke and roasted nuts, with a light sweetness underneath.

olaf-poulsson-special-cut-no-42.z: No. 42 Special Cut is a ready-rubbed blend within German manufacturer Dan Tobacco's (DTM) Olaf Poulsson line. Its body is made up of different Virginia varieties; leaf colors range from golden yellow to dark brown. It's offered in a fifty-gram tin and a large two-hundred-fifty-gram package. The applied topping combines vanilla, rum, honey, and fruit notes, making it one of the line's more pronouncedly aromatic members. Its rubbed-out structure eases packing and gives an even burn. It runs from light to medium in nicotine. It suits those seeking a Danish-style blend with a pronounced sweet topping but a Virginia-based body.
olaf-poulsson-special-cut-no-42.o: Leaves a sweet scent mingling honey, vanilla, and rum.

john-middleton-inc-cherry-blend.z: Middleton's Cherry Blend is one of the long-running examples of American over-the-counter aromatics. A pronounced cherry flavoring is applied over a base built from Burley and Virginia leaf; the cut is ribbon and it's offered moist enough to pack directly into a pipe. On the smoke, the cherry note stands out in both taste and aroma, with the tobacco base staying measured underneath it. Strength is low and the smoke is medium in intensity. A profile built for those starting out with aromatic tobaccos and for smokers who value aroma over taste. John Middleton's history, tracing back to a shop founded in Philadelphia in 1856, marks its place in the American pipe tobacco tradition.
john-middleton-inc-cherry-blend.o: Leaves a pronounced cherry-candy aroma; gives a sweet, fruity smoke.

pipe-republic-three-quid-twist-limited-e.z: No reliable sources on Pipe Republic's blend Three Quid Twist - Limited Edition could be found, so its content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

sutliff-tobacco-company-ca-100.z: CA-100 is a ribbon-cut English mixture the Richmond-based Sutliff offers in bulk. Cyprus latakia forms the blend's backbone; oriental leaves add a spicy, lightly floral layer, Virginia gives a warm sweetness, and a small amount of perique adds a peppery sharpness. It offers a dry, smoky, medium-bodied smoke; nicotine strength is medium. A record for those seeking a classic latakia-forward English character in an inexpensive bulk blend. The wide ribbon cut is easy to pack, burns slowly, and may occasionally need relighting. It carries no flavoring; the flavor comes entirely from the leaves themselves.
sutliff-tobacco-company-ca-100.o: Leaves a scent of wood smoke and spicy resin.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-smoky-sweet-chocolate.z: Smoky Sweet Chocolate is a Wilke record that brings together a sweet aromatic with a Latakia-driven body. Creamy, sugary black cavendish forms the blend's base, but the element governing the taste is smoky, woody, earthy, and lightly spicy Cyprian Latakia. Chocolate-cased white Burley adds nut and bread tones; Perique brings pepper and dried fruit, while Virginia contributes a subtle citrus and floral note. It's a medium-strength blend that burns cool and clean. It suits smokers seeking a sweet, smoky, lightly spicy, nutty composition — neither a plain aromatic nor a full English. Wilke offers this record in its bulk aromatic listing.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-smoky-sweet-chocolate.o: A sweet cocoa and roasted-nut tone mixes into the wood-smoke scent.

brobergs-tobakshandel-ab-brobergs-jubile.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named Brobergs Jubileums Mixture under the Brobergs Tobakshandel AB brand could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-louisiana-flake.z: Louisiana Flake is a dark-colored flake made by pressing and slicing Virginia and Perique leaf. A cocoa-chocolate essence is applied on top, accompanied by a floral-soapy trace from the house's Lakeland style. The slices arrive moist; when properly aired, they pack easily and burn evenly throughout the smoke. Nicotine is moderate. Suited to smokers wanting to experience Perique's spicy-plummy tone within an essence-topped frame, and to those interested in Virginia-Perique blends.
gawith-hoggarth-co-louisiana-flake.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of cocoa and dried fruit, carrying a floral trace underneath.

jacks-tobacco-teton-mountain-dog.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of Teton Mountain Dog, part of Jack's Tobacco's "Dog" line, could be found.
jacks-tobacco-teton-mountain-dog.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-spike-hyzer.z: Also known as Golf Spike Hyzer, this blend sits in Ken Byron Ventures' Virginia-Perique line and takes its name from a disc golf throw. Per the maker's description, the base isn't built from a single Virginia variety but from a wide selection of leaf: aged reds, orange and light-yellow Virginias, Carolina leaf, steamed dark Virginia, and both broad-cut and ribbon-cut leaf are all used together. Perique makes up roughly twenty percent. That high Perique share pushes the blend well beyond an ordinary VaPer: alongside plum and fig sweetness, a distinct black-pepper spice and a full body emerge. The mix of different cuts evens out the burn rate and lets the flavor profile shift over the course of the smoke. Nicotine runs medium-plus. Suited to experienced smokers seeking a Perique-forward, unflavored, full-bodied Virginia blend.
ken-byron-ventures-spike-hyzer.o: Leaves a tangy-sweet tobacco aroma with a lightly spiced scent reminiscent of dried plum skin.

paul-olsen-gents.z: A blend from the My Own Blend line that originated at the Paul Olsen shop in Copenhagen; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

black-cat-cigar-company-rum-and-maple.z: A rum-and-maple-syrup-themed bulk aromatic from Black Cat Cigar Company; no manufacturer recipe for its content could be found.
black-cat-cigar-company-rum-and-maple.o: Leaves a rum and maple syrup room note.

cornell-diehl-baileys-front-porch.z: Cornell & Diehl Bailey's Front Porch is an unflavored mixture built by adding bright Virginia, Latakia, and a small amount of perique to a burley-heavy base. Since the Latakia level is kept moderate, the blend takes shape as a soft-end American-English hybrid rather than a heavy English mixture. On the flavor channel, burley's dry, nutty body leads; Virginia adds light sweetness, Latakia a thin smoke, and perique a stinging spicy layer. Nicotine sits at a medium level. It suits smokers wanting to ease into Latakia blends, or looking for an unflavored mixture that doesn't tire in long sessions.
cornell-diehl-baileys-front-porch.o: Leaves a light smoky wood aroma in the room, with a nutty tobacco scent beneath it.

gawith-hoggarth-co-beacon-light-sweet-tw.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Beacon Light Sweet Twist blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

robert-mcconnell-marylebone.z: Marylebone is one of the Robert McConnell brand's ribbon-cut English blends. A Virginia body is joined by latakia and Oriental leaf as well as black cavendish; this fourth component softens the blend's smoky side and gives the smoke a round, lightly sweet foundation. Per the producer's description, the components are balanced so none overpowers the others, and the smoke is cool with a full body. A suitable blend for smokers seeking a daily smoke who like Latakia in moderation; it is neither as smoky as a pure Balkan mixture nor as sweet as an aromatic. The Robert McConnell name rests on an old English tobacco house rooted in London and Belfast; the brand is produced today under the German Kohlhase & Kopp umbrella.
robert-mcconnell-marylebone.o: Leaves a smoky, woody latakia scent in the room with a lightly sweet tobacco scent beneath it.

james-barber-old-judge.z: One of James Barber's American-type house blends; not enough sources could be found on its composition.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-brandy-and-virgi.z: Brandy and Virginia is a brandy-flavored Virginia blend appearing in the McGahey The Tobacconist catalogue; sufficient sources describing its composition and character could not be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-troost-aro.z: Match Troost Aromatic Cavendish is a mixture modeled after the Dutch brand Troost's aromatic cavendish blend. The main component is golden-yellow Virginia cavendish, with a citrus-like tartness and honey-sugar tones; nutty, roasted burley plays a supporting role, and a small amount of Oriental adds a floral, woody twist. The casing consists of a pronounced caramel with a light buttery-sugar note beneath it. The body is light to medium; it suits smokers looking for classic Dutch-style cavendish aromatics.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-troost-aro.o: Leaves a scent of caramel and buttery sugar.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-bright-.z: Recorded as the 2022 batch of Mr. Christian's Bright Side; no accessible source could be found detailing this batch's specific contents and character.

mcclelland-no-815-strawberry-daiquiri.z: As the name suggests, this is a strawberry-and-rum-flavored McClelland aromatic; no sufficient sources could be found to confirm its contents.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-peaches-and-cream.z: Peaches and Cream is a Boswell aromatic built on ripe peach and passion fruit notes. Per the manufacturer's description, the fruit flavor is intense while the aroma spreading into the room is relatively light; the mixture burns soft and cool thanks to its cavendish base. Nicotine load is low, flavor body light. Suitable for fans of fruit-flavored mixtures seeking a soft blend they can smoke for long stretches during the day. It is listed among Boswell's signature aromatics.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-peaches-and-cream.o: A creamy sweetness follows the ripe peach and tropical fruit aroma.

cup-o-joes-3-chuchunaa.z: One of the Cup O' Joes tobacco shop's numbered house blends, classed as aromatic; no source describing its composition was found.

cornell-diehl-gran-marnier-chocolate.z: An aromatic blend flavored with orange liqueur and chocolate that previously appeared in Cornell & Diehl's bulk catalog; not enough sourcing could be found for a detailed composition.
cornell-diehl-gran-marnier-chocolate.o: Leaves an aroma of orange liqueur and chocolate.

sutliff-tobacco-company-royal-viking-105.z: 105 Royal Viking is among Sutliff's bulk aromatics presented as Danish-style. According to the maker's account, it is prepared from four separate base blends, which are stored and fermented individually before being brought together by hand. What gives the mixture its character is a soft roasted-nut aroma. The cool, sweet smoke typical of the Danish school is joined with low nicotine. It is aimed at smokers who enjoy classic Scandinavian-style aromatics and nut-themed toppings. The number 105 in its name is Sutliff's bulk catalog number.
sutliff-tobacco-company-royal-viking-105.o: Leaves a scent of roasted nuts and light sweet wood.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-dummerston.z: No verifiable composition and character information could be compiled for Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Dummerston, which records describe as having a plain Virginia character.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-dummerston.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

w-o-larsen-smooth-tasty.z: No reliable source could be found regarding the composition and character of this Danish blend bearing the W.Ø. Larsen name.
w-o-larsen-smooth-tasty.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

hearth-home-rolandos-own.z: Rolando's Own is a Virginia-Perique blend enlivened with a moderate dose of Perique, in which lemon-yellow, red, and stoved Virginia leaves are used together. The combination of three separate Virginias gives the blend both bright tartness and a dark, caramel-like depth; Perique adds plum and pepper seasoning to this base. It takes its name from, and was prepared for, the Romanian-born pipe maker Rolando Negoita. Being an unflavored, sweet, and high-flavor-intensity mixture, it's an option that smokers familiar with the Virginia-Perique family can smoke all day.
hearth-home-rolandos-own.o: Leaves an aroma where pepper and bread-crust traces mix into dried-fig sweetness.

dan-tobacco-the-raven.z: This is a blend from the German maker Dan Tobacco, noted as English type; not enough sourcing could be reached to verify its composition and character.

lane-limited-mv-1000.z: MV-1000 is a ribbon-cut blend from Lane Limited's bulk line, built on matured golden Virginia leaf. The applied casing is measured and defined as vanilla-direction; some sellers refer to the blend directly as "Golden Virginia." The taste moves between Virginia's bready, lightly fruity sweetness and the casing's subdued vanilla; nicotine is low to medium. For smokers who don't want the syrupy sweetness of heavy aromatics but haven't moved on to unflavored Virginia blends either, it can be considered an intermediate step.
lane-limited-mv-1000.o: Leaves a fine vanilla note over a bready Virginia sweetness.

cornell-diehl-baalbek.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to describe the content of this blend, which does not currently appear in the Cornell & Diehl catalog.

wessex-curly-block.z: Curly Block is the member of the Wessex series produced using the rope technique and pressed into a block. In the English tobacco tradition, rope/roll tobaccos are made by twisting leaf and holding it under pressure for a long time; when sliced, curled medallions emerge. Virginia builds the blend's body, while Perique adds a tart-spicy depth. Since the pressing process concentrates the sugars, the smoke carries a dark-fruit, tart, full character. Nicotine sits on the medium-to-high side; rubbing out and airing the medallions matters for the burn. It suits people accustomed to rope tobaccos and Virginia-Perique balance who are used to slow smoking.
wessex-curly-block.o: Leaves an intense scent leaning toward dark fruit and smoked leaf.

sutliff-tobacco-company-rum-raisin-d57.z: D57 Rum Raisin is one of the long-running blends in Sutliff's bulk aromatic line. Its base contains soft burley, light Virginia, and unflavored black cavendish; some descriptions note a small amount of Turkish leaf added as well. A rum- and raisin-based flavoring is applied over it; the rum note is more pronounced than the raisin. Burley builds the blend's body and gives a molasses-like, near-cocoa depth; Virginia leaves a grassy, citrusy line in the background. Because the flavoring is applied in measured amounts, the tobacco taste isn't erased. It burns cool and even, with nicotine strength a bit above light. It suits smokers looking for a cased aromatic that isn't heavy on sugar.
sutliff-tobacco-company-rum-raisin-d57.o: Leaves a scent of rum-raisin cake and brown sugar.

vcpo-selection-nr-4-scottish-mixture.z: The fourth blend in the VCPÖ Selection series, whose name points to a Scottish-style mixture; since it was not distributed outside Austria, no independent source describing its composition and character has been found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-maple-plum-spice.z: Maple Plum Spice is a blend in Wilke's bulk aromatic line that runs two characters side by side. Its base is earthy, roasted, creamy-sweet black cavendish, topped with a heavy maple-syrup casing. In second place is plum-character Perique, which balances the casing's sweetness with pepper, earth, wood, and fig notes. A small amount of Virginia cavendish adds citrus and bread tones. This is a medium-strength, medium-flavor record that burns cool and clean. Maple and plum progressing together throughout the bowl give the smoke a long, sweet finish. It suits smokers who love aromatics but also want spice and body.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-maple-plum-spice.o: A light pepper trace mixes into the maple-syrup and cooked-plum scent.

drucquer-sons-inns-of-court.z: Inns of Court is Drucquer & Sons' burley-forward, American-style blend. White and brown burley are used alongside Virginia leaves; latakia and perique are added only as an accent. The cut is very fine ribbon, nearly shag-fine; this lets the blend catch easily. Its character is nutty, earthy and lightly toasted; rather than bringing smokiness to the fore, latakia deepens the background. It's an in-between position for smokers who don't like heavy latakia but want the dry taste of English mixtures. Per brand records, the blend was one of the Drucquer shop's best-selling mixtures for decades and even reached the crew of Admiral Richard Byrd's second Antarctic expedition.
drucquer-sons-inns-of-court.o: Leaves a lightly smoky scent dominated by roasted hazelnut and dry earth.

motzek-highland-balls.z: Since neither the manufacturer's own description nor two independent reliable sources could be found for the Motzek blend called Highland Balls, its composition, cut, and character could not be documented here.

pipesandcigars-com-mark-twain-memoir.z: Mark Twain Memoir is one of the house blends sold under its own name by the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com; no sufficient independent sources documenting its content and character could be found.

cornell-diehl-barrister.z: Barrister is a ribbon-cut English mixture in which Cornell & Diehl combines Latakia with Virginia and burley. Named after the courtroom lawyer of English legal tradition, the blend is described by the maker as a rich, layered smoke. Burley's share is pronounced; it gives the blend a leather, earth, and nut-leaning base along with a peppery spice. Latakia builds the smoky frame, while Virginia carries a measured sweetness in the background. It suits those looking for an unflavored, burley-heavy, smoky mixture.
cornell-diehl-barrister.o: Leaves an aroma of leather and dry earth alongside the Latakia smoke.

robert-mcconnell-covent-garden.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of Robert McConnell Covent Garden.

mac-baren-cube-silver.z: Cube Silver also follows the Cube family's twenty-seven-component recipe: loose-cut golden Virginia, a small amount of rubbed-out Burley, and a special Virginia Cavendish are brought together. The cut is ribbon, with some broken flake in it, and the tobacco is tinned at a moisture level ready to smoke directly. In the smoke, creamy sweetness and natural tobacco taste sit side by side; the flavoring reads slightly more fruity than Cube Gold's. Strength is low, flavor intensity medium. A blend prepared for undemanding, everyday aromatic smokes.
mac-baren-cube-silver.o: Leaves a cream and light fruit-sugar aroma.

lane-limited-81-v.z: 81-V is one of the bulk aromatic blends from Lane Limited, founded in Tucker, Georgia. Per the manufacturer's promotion, vanilla casing is combined with selected Virginia, Oriental and soft Burley leaves; the tobacco is pressed into a cake and cut for easy packing and a cool smoke. Its character is close to the sweet, creamy aromatic line that is Lane's signature; nicotine load is low, while flavor intensity is medium thanks to the casing. Designed for smokers who enjoy aromatic tobaccos and don't mind a pronounced room scent. As a result of contraction in Lane's bulk line, it's not commonly found today.
lane-limited-81-v.o: Sweet vanilla scent is accompanied by a lightly toasted-leaf tone.

chieftain-blacksmiths-blend.z: The entry has been left incomplete as no reliable source could be found for Chieftain's Blacksmiths Blend blend.

d-r-tobacco-windsail-original-blend.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of D & R Tobacco's Windsail Original Blend were found.

hearth-home-virginia-memory-10.z: Virginia Memory #10 is Hearth & Home's attempt to reinterpret the long-discontinued Sobranie Virginian #10 blend. Fragrant Orientals are added to mild, sweet Virginia leaves, rounded out with cigar leaf that gives the mixture a creamy texture. The presence of cigar leaf sets the blend apart from a straight Virginia mixture, giving it a rounder, lightly baked base. Being an unflavored blend, the taste comes entirely from the leaf itself; the sweetness of natural sugar, the Oriental's dry spice, and the cigar leaf's earthy softness proceed together. It lights easily and stays at a medium nicotine level. It's aimed at those wanting to get acquainted with classic Sobranie-style Virginia mixtures and those interested in blends carrying cigar leaf.
hearth-home-virginia-memory-10.o: Leaves an aroma of creamy cigar leaf and sweet dry hay.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-dunbar-origina.z: Dunbar Original Dark Flake is a slice tobacco referred to under the Orlik Tobacco Company A/S label, noted in records as burley-forward; no published source confirming its composition could be found.

missouri-meerschaum-drawdown.z: No first-hand manufacturer description regarding the composition of the blend called DrawDown, released under the Missouri Meerschaum name, could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-commander.z: Commander is one of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's records built on a four-component American-English structure: black cavendish, Burley, Virginia, and Latakia. Blends of this type combine the smoky backbone of English mixtures with the body of American Burley and the softness of cavendish. Each component in the blend can be picked out individually, but Latakia governs the dominant character; the layer of soot and burnt wood sits atop Virginia's sweetness and cavendish's creamy edge, while Burley supplies the dry, nutty body. It's said to be blended to burn cool, dry, and without harshening however it's drawn. It suits smokers who love Latakia-based tobaccos but want a bit of sweetness rather than a fully dry English mixture.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-commander.o: Leaves a scent of wood-fire smoke with a lightly sweet background.

ken-byron-ventures-verge-engine-retrodri.z: Verge Engine RetroDrive is a Virginia-Perique blend in Ken Byron Ventures' Verge Engine line. Records indicate the blend shares its skeleton with Verge Engine Overdrive; what sets it apart is the use of a rare, long-rested perique batch called "Decade." The composition is forward in red Virginias aged for many years, with stoved Virginias providing a supporting body, and perique making up roughly a fifth of the blend. The flavor range brings dried plum, fig, raisin, woody and earthy notes alongside Virginia's sugary, tangy, bready side.
ken-byron-ventures-verge-engine-retrodri.o: Leaves a lightly spicy trace with a tangy dried-fruit and baked-bread scent.

mac-baren-green-velvet.z: Not enough information could be found in the manufacturer's current catalog or verifiable independent sources about this Mac Baren blend, which is described as aromatic.

sutliff-tobacco-company-sweet-virginia-7.z: Sweet Virginia #707 is a Virginia blend in Sutliff's numbered bulk line; no reliable source on its composition, cut, and smoking character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-sweet-virginia-7.o: No reliable record of a room note could be found.

hearth-home-sierra-nevada.z: Sierra Nevada is an unflavored mixture Hearth & Home prepared for the 2011 West Coast Pipe Show. It's built by adding Oriental tobaccos, Perique, and a small amount of earthy-tasting Burley atop three separate Virginia leaves; this structure sets it apart from both a straight Virginia and a classic Virginia-Perique. The Virginia's sugary sweetness, the Orientals' dry spice accent, and the Perique's peppery fruit tone proceed together; Burley weighs down the base and balances the burn. It stays in the medium band for nicotine. Because it was prepared in limited quantity for the show, it wasn't in continuous production, and was withdrawn entirely from the market once the brand ceased operations. It's a record for those who love unflavored, layered Virginia mixtures.
hearth-home-sierra-nevada.o: Leaves an aroma of dry hay, tart fruit, and earthy spice.

villiger-maryland-no-333.z: Maryland No. 333 is a light aromatic pipe tobacco from Swiss maker Villiger, taking its name from Maryland leaf. The brand was founded in Pfeffikon in 1888 by Jean Villiger and still keeps its headquarters in Switzerland today; this blend, according to records, is produced in Germany under Villiger's recipe and license. The tobacco is offered in a double-walled, moisture-retaining pouch. Its character is low-nicotine, soft, and geared toward everyday smoking; it suits smokers wanting to steer clear of heavy Latakia or intensely cased blends and seeking a plain, balanced everyday tobacco.
villiger-maryland-no-333.o: Leaves a lightly sweet scent of dry hay and baked bread.

charles-fairmorn-black-delight-mild-trop.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the Charles Fairmorn name.

david-cigarpipe-mountain-sunset.z: No adequate sources were found documenting the composition or character of the David CigarPipe Mountain sunset blend.

mcclelland-black-tie.z: Black Tie is a blend in McClelland's Piper's Choice series, released, per records, in 2014. It consists of Virginia, Perique, and black Cavendish; the Cavendish gives the blend a light sweetness, while the Perique sets the balance with its plum-and-spice character. It's a structure bridging aromatic and unflavored blends: sweetness is measured, and the tin note is close to neutral and lightly sweet. It comes out of the tin at a smokable moisture and lights easily. Suited to smokers seeking a Virginia-Perique structure with a mild sweetness who want an all-day blend.
mcclelland-black-tie.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, plummy, and spiced tobacco aroma.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-polar-x-p.z: Polar X-Press is an aromatic blend The Country Squire prepares for the winter season. Virginia, black Cavendish and Burley leaves are brought together, with the top flavoring set to evoke hot chocolate.
