The Cavendish gives a dark sweetness, the Burley a nutty body, and the Virginia a light grassy base; the cocoa tone sits over all of these. Nicotine load is low and the burn is cool. Prepared for smokers who enjoy sweet, dessert-drink-evoking aromatics; as a seasonal release its availability varies.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-polar-x-p.o: Leaves a scent of hot cocoa and sweet milk.

cornell-diehl-cherry-jubilee.z: Cherry Jubilee is Cornell & Diehl's classic cherry-flavored blend. A black cavendish body is joined by burley and Virginia leaves; it is offered as a ribbon cut. Per the manufacturer, the flavoring leans toward wild cherry rather than the usual sweet-cherry extract, setting the blend apart from other cherry mixtures in the same family. Nicotine is very light; flavor intensity on the palate, by contrast, is pronounced, so smokers seeking flavor rather than body will find their match here. It suits newcomers to the pipe and smokers who enjoy fruity aromatics. The ribbon cut makes the blend easy to pack and gives it an even burn; as often happens with aromatics, if it arrives moist, a brief airing before packing helps.
cornell-diehl-cherry-jubilee.o: Leaves an aroma of sweet wild cherry and sugared fruit.

p-c-rettig-finlandia.z: A pipe tobacco tied to P. C. Rettig, the company founded by Finland's long-established Rettig family of tobacco industrialists; no independent source could be found to confirm the blend's composition and character.

5th-avenue-cigars-petes-legacy.z: This tobacconist house blend lacks sufficient available sources describing its composition.

cornell-diehl-canal-boat.z: Canal Boat is one of Cornell & Diehl's blends built around cube-cut burley. It is constructed by adding Cyprus Latakia and unsweetened black cavendish to a nutty burley base; despite its unflavored structure, the Latakia level gives the blend a pronounced smoky tone. The cube cut burns slowly, while black cavendish adds softness and a light sweetness to the body. Its character sits along a medium-bodied, smoky-sweet line, with tones reminiscent of toasted oats and cocoa described. It suits smokers wanting to get acquainted with Latakia without the intensity of a full English blend, as well as those looking for burley-based, moderately smoky mixtures.
cornell-diehl-canal-boat.o: Leaves a lightly smoky aroma in the room reminiscent of toasted grain.

smokers-haven-sids-m-d-mixture.z: One of the bulk-sold aromatic blends bearing the name of Smokers' Haven co-founder Sid Ritter; no source describing its composition and topping could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-cajun-safari.z: A limited-release blend from Ken Byron Ventures, catalogued as a Virginia/Perique; since the maker no longer has a current profile page, its contents could not be verified.

e-a-carey-mystery-blend.z: Mystery Blend is among the aromatic blends E. A. Carey sells under its own label. Per the maker's description, it is made from a combination of aged golden cavendish and fire-cured leaf; this pairing preserves natural sweetness while adding a light smoky tone to the mixture. The flavoring runs on medium-sweetness vanilla. The tobacco is produced in Denmark, while the brand is US-based. The nicotine load is low and the flavor body is moderate; it is a record aimed at those seeking a soft, all-day aromatic. It continues to appear in Carey's current catalog in various packaging from 2 ounces up to 5 pounds.
e-a-carey-mystery-blend.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla scent with a light woody smokiness.

lane-limited-rum-maple.z: Rum & Maple is a ribbon-cut aromatic blend from Lane Limited built on Virginia and Burley leaves, prepared with a rum-and-maple-syrup themed casing. Structurally it's a light-nicotine, flat-flavor tobacco; much of the flavor load comes not from the leaf itself but from the applied top casing. Turkish records note the tobacco's sweetness is pronounced and that the pipe warms up. The blend offers a suitable starting profile for smokers wanting to get acquainted with cased tobaccos or seeking low nicotine; it doesn't appeal to those looking for the wood and spice character of Latakia- or Oriental-forward mixtures. Lane Limited is a US-based manufacturer known for its code-named bulk aromatics; Rum & Maple is one of the named examples of that tradition. The blend's current production status could not be determined with certainty from the records.
lane-limited-rum-maple.o: Leaves a dark room note reminiscent of maple syrup and a sugary, rum-evoking sweetness when burned.

brebbia-sinfonia-mixture-no-23.z: Sinfonia is an aromatic blend numbered 23 in Brebbia's numbered series. It consists of coarsely cut ribbon leaves; black, medium and light brown tones appear in roughly equal proportion. Yellow-plum sweetness and orange essence are used as casing. In the smoke the orange note comes through more pronounced than the plum, accompanied by an intense confectionery sweetness. Records note it carries somewhat higher nicotine than most aromatics, and shows a tendency to run hot and dry the tongue when puffed quickly. Worth considering for those who can pair the fruity casing with a disciplined slow smoke and seek a taste outside classic vanilla aromatics.
brebbia-sinfonia-mixture-no-23.o: Leaves a fruity aroma carrying orange peel and ripe plum sweetness.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-ocean-queen.z: No reliable source could be found about the contents and character of Kohlhase & Kopp's blend registered as Ocean Queen.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.z: The name "Alemão" means "German" in Portuguese and describes Cândido Giovanella's line modeled on mild German-style aromatics. The German Type version is the near-neutral member of this line, without a pronounced fruit or cocoa coating. Its base is sun-dried Brazilian Virginia leaf and black Cavendish, joined by Burley and a small amount of Oriental leaf. The cut is neat ribbon, the burn is light, and it doesn't leave harshness on the palate. It's aimed at smokers wanting to move from aromatic toward unflavored tobacco, or looking for a mild leaf to smoke all day. It's produced in the Curitiba region of Paraná.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.o: Leaves a measured, lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of dry hay and beeswax.

motzek-warp-17-12.z: Referred to as one of the relatively new virginia-perique products from the Kiel-based TAK workshop; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found.

smokin-g-pipe-tobacco-smooth-platinum.z: A blend referred to as Virginia-and-burley-based from the small-scale Smokin' G brand; no independent source about it could be found.

mccranies-pamlico.z: No sufficient sources could be found on the contents of this aromatic bulk blend, named after North Carolina's Pamlico region.

cornell-diehl-blackberry-brandy.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Cornell & Diehl blend Blackberry Brandy.

dan-tobacco-elwood-flake-no-2.z: A pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source on the blend's composition or character was found, so no further detail is given.

the-tobacco-barn-saddleback-mountain.z: No verifiable source describing the composition and character of the house blend Saddleback Mountain, noted as Burley-based, from the Tobacco Barn tobacconist has been found.

watch-city-cigar-knapdarloch.z: This is a house blend from Watch City Cigar described as Scottish-style, for which no sufficient source could be found.
watch-city-cigar-knapdarloch.o: Records note it leaves a lightly smoky, sweetish scent typical of Scottish-style blends.

pfeifendepot-no-500-kori-flake.z: No. 500 Kori-Flake is a blend in Pfeifendepot's flake line, produced by KOPP Tobaccos. Fully ripened Virginia leaves are kept under the press for three months; the blend takes its name from its defining coriander note. The smoke is described as velvety and balanced; the Virginia's sweetness is joined by coriander's spicy, lightly citrus side. It suits flake smokers who steer clear of heavily flavored blends and want a single spice accent. Sold in a 100 gram package.
pfeifendepot-no-500-kori-flake.o: Leaves the spicy, lightly lemony scent of coriander seed alongside a sweet, hay-like aroma.

nat-sherman-307-mild-cavendish.z: A mild cavendish blend in the numbered pipe tobacco line of New York-based Nat Sherman; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

g-l-pease-smaugweed.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Smaugweed.

petersen-sorensen-danish-mixture.z: This is a Danish-style mixture sold under the Petersen & Sorensen name; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient independent sources describing its composition could be found.
petersen-sorensen-danish-mixture.o: Leaves the lightly sweet aroma typical of Danish-style mixtures.

abenaki-tobacco-co-seaport-rum.z: Seaport Rum is a rum-flavored blend from Abenaki Tobacco Co., a family business based in the White Mountains region of New Hampshire, US. It's a dark brown ribbon cut. At the base is grassy, citrusy golden Virginia; nutty, molasses-sweet Burley edges slightly ahead in proportion. Since both leaves are processed in the Cavendish manner, they carry a drier, lightly toasted character than the usual Cavendish sweetness. Two separate rum flavorings are noted as being used; these bring forward sweetness and a light spice note, softening the leaf's own sharpness. It burns cool and clean, changing little in taste throughout, and nicotine is low. It's a blend aimed at those looking for a non-heavy, sweet aromatic they can smoke all day.
abenaki-tobacco-co-seaport-rum.o: Leaves a sweet rum and light spice room note.

exclusiv-plum-rum.z: Plum & Rum is an aromatic blend in the Exclusiv line of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.; today it is also sold under the name Exclusiv PR. The blend is built on Virginia leaves and black cavendish, pressed into a cake before being flavoured. The top flavouring is made by combining Jamaican rum with natural plum extract; the rum gives a dark, sugary line while the plum adds a fruitier depth. It is a smoke that isn't heavy in nicotine but is sweet and full in taste. It suits an aromatic smoker who likes dark-fruit and spirit-noted flavourings.
exclusiv-plum-rum.o: Leaves dark plum and rum aroma together, sweet and syrupy.

straus-tobacco-412.z: A house blend classified as an English mixture from Straus Tobacconist, operating in Cincinnati since 1880; no verifiable source describing its composition could be found.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-virginia-slice.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named Virginia Slice under the Boswell Pipes & Tobacco brand could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-dark-fired-cherry.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to fill in the profile of Ken Byron Ventures' Dark Fired Cherry.

von-eicken-piccolo-tropical-mango.z: Piccolo Tropical Mango is the mango-flavored member of Von Eicken's Piccolo plug series, designed for a single bowlful. Pressed Cavendish is cut into broken flake, with each piece wrapped individually in paper. The mango aroma is pronounced from the moment it is lit and persists through the bowl; the Cavendish base sets a sweet, soft foundation with the Virginia staying in the background. Nicotine is low. Aimed at users who enjoy fruity, intensely flavored tobaccos and want to smoke in small portions.
von-eicken-piccolo-tropical-mango.o: Leaves a scent of ripe mango and tropical fruit candy.

paul-olsen-gus-goose.z: A blend from the My Own Blend line that originated at the Paul Olsen shop in Copenhagen; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

rattray-westminster-abbey.z: Westminster Abbey is an aromatic blend released under the Rattray name. Its body, built from Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish leaf, is mostly ribbon cut; reports note occasional half-flake pieces mixed in. The dominant tin note is heavy caramel; the blend's flavoring leans toward caramel and cream. In the smoke a sugary, creamy sweetness dominates, and the leaf's own tobacco character stays in the background; a sharp, faintly bitter tone can appear in the first bowls, receding once the tobacco has been aired and rested a while. Nicotine runs a little above light and flavor intensity is high. It suits smokers interested in sugary aromatic blends who are looking for low nicotine.
rattray-westminster-abbey.o: Leaves a sweet, sugary aroma reminiscent of caramel and cream.

smokers-haven-cyrian-limited.z: Recorded as an English-style mixture tinned in limited quantity for Smokers' Haven; the name's relation to Syrian Limited and the blend's composition could not be confirmed by independent sources.

dan-tobacco-old-ironsides.z: Old Ironsides belongs to Dan Tobacco's American history series, named after the nickname of USS Constitution, the oldest ship in the US Navy. It's a high proportion of Cyprus Latakia, rounded out with dark fire-cured Kentucky, Perique, and Virginia leaf. The blend is pressed, aged for twelve weeks, then sliced into flake. The smoke is full-bodied and cool, with a high flavor load: Latakia's smokiness is the defining note, Kentucky adds an earthy, smoky depth, Perique a peppery sharpness, and Virginia an underlying sweetness. Being flake cut, the leaves need rubbing or folding before packing. Aimed at experienced smokers who want a Latakia-heavy profile; too heavy for those expecting a mild blend.
dan-tobacco-old-ironsides.o: Fills the room with a heavy scent of smoke, tar, and campfire.

mccranies-highland-mixture.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found on Highland Mixture, one of McCranie's Pipe Shop's house blends.
mccranies-highland-mixture.o: No reliable description of the aroma could be found.

exclusiv-mild-vanilla.z: No verifiable source could be found regarding the producer, composition, and character of this pipe tobacco marketed under the Exclusiv name.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-model.z: A mixture in Sutliff's Match line said to be modeled after the old burley blend called Model; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

charutaria-cruzeiro-ltda-natural.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the Brazil-based Charutaria Cruzeiro.

mcclelland-cpcc-samovar.z: Samovar is a dark Oriental mixture McClelland prepared for the Chicagoland Pipe Collectors' Club and later folded into the Club Blends series. Records indicate it was first released in April 1995. What sets the mixture apart is its use of rarer Syrian Latakia instead of the more common Cyprian Latakia; this leaf is kept at a non-dominant dose. In the smoke, a line of incense and spice merges with the Oriental leaves' dry curl; the blend's name comes from this dark, tea-evoking character. No flavoring is used. Suited to smokers wanting to trace the difference Syrian Latakia makes and who are used to full-bodied Oriental mixtures. McClelland closed in 2018, so the blend is no longer produced.
mcclelland-cpcc-samovar.o: Leaves an aroma of smoked wood and spice, with a dry trace reminiscent of brewed tea behind it.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-plum-twist.z: Sweet Plum Twist is Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s plum-topped version of its brown Burma base. Fire-cured leaves are twisted into a fine rope; the tobacco arrives as a dense mass that yields small coin-like slices when cut. The pouch aroma is oily and spicy; on the smoke, the earthy, smoky core of the fire-curing is preserved while the sweet topping and inverted sugar worked into the leaf during production add a sweet top layer to the smoke. Since it isn't steam-cooked under pressure, it stays intense in nicotine; it needs to be thinly sliced and smoked slowly. An entry for those wanting a topped but still strong Burma tobacco. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. is one of the English producers that continues traditional twist (rope) production at its Kendal factory, hand-twisting fire-cured leaves into rope form. Because twist tobaccos don't go through a pressure-cooking stage, they stay intense in nicotine; records indicate these ropes are sold for both chewing and pipe smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sweet-plum-twist.o: Leaves an aroma combining dried-plum sweetness with tobacco scent.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-flying-dut.z: Match Flying Dutchman is an aromatic Sutliff produced modeled after the Dutch-style blend of the same name. A soft vanilla casing works together with a light licorice-root-leaning essence; though these two notes lead, they don't fully mask the taste of the various tobacco types. It carries a grassy, spicy background note typical of Dutch-style blends that runs from start to finish. Nicotine is low and the body is light; it is aimed at smokers looking for a measured-sweetness aromatic who want to get to know classic Dutch mixtures.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-flying-dut.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly grassy scent recalling vanilla and licorice root.

peretti-oxford-flake.z: One of the house blends from L. J. Peretti's shop in Boston; it appears under the flake blends heading in the maker's listing. No published description of the blend's composition and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.

ken-byron-ventures-notorious.z: Notorious, one of Ken Byron Ventures' small-batch productions, is described in records as an old-style, dark and richly sweet English blend; no independent source could be found to confirm its contents.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-straw-n.z: A blend released as part of Ken Byron Ventures' small-batch production; no independent, verifiable source could be found on it.

samuel-gawith-full-virginia-plug.z: Full Virginia Plug is a tobacco produced at Samuel Gawith's Kendal facility from flame-cured Virginia leaf alone, hot-pressed into a solid plug. The plug is dark brown and gives the smoker broad freedom in preparation: it can be sliced and used like a flake, or crumbled for packing. According to records, the blend shares the same leaf composition and top note with the same producer's Full Virginia Flake; the only difference is that the pressed plug is presented whole. On the flavor side, dark Virginia's bready sweetness and the depth from pressing come forward; nicotine fullness is pronounced, so it is not a blend for smoking on an empty stomach or fast puffing. Carrying no additives, it is aimed less at smokers seeking flavor than at those wanting to follow pure Virginia character and the slowly unfolding flavor line of pressed tobacco. Since plug moisture can be high, airing it briefly after slicing eases the burn.
samuel-gawith-full-virginia-plug.o: Leaves a sweetish tobacco scent evoking dry hay and stale bread crust.

mac-baren-capstan-gold-navy-cut-ready-ru.z: Capstan is a historic brand rooted in England; its rights passed to Mac Baren in 2015 and production moved to Denmark. Gold Navy Cut Ready Rubbed is obtained by pressing light-colored Virginia leaves gathered from three continents into a block, slicing them and then rubbing them out. It's an unflavored, plain Virginia blend. According to Turkish sources, the strands are unusually thin for a pipe tobacco; this eases packing but can lead to a fast, hot burn, requiring a slow-paced smoke. The taste stays in a plain, refined line based on Virginia's natural sugar, occasionally coming close to a cigarette-like taste. Nicotine dosage is above light-to-medium and accumulates across consecutive smokes. Suited to those wanting to get to know plain Virginia character; for those expecting multi-layered intensity, it stays flat.
mac-baren-capstan-gold-navy-cut-ready-ru.o: Leaves a sharp, cigarette-like, dry and piercing tobacco note.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-special-d.z: Special Dublin is an aromatic pipe-tobacco series Scandinavian Tobacco Group offers to the European market under its umbrella. The series' body is built from Virginia leaf of US, African, and Brazilian origin; these leaves are lightly pressed and cut, then combined with dark black cavendish. The Irish Stout variety stands out by adding a dark-beer- and malt-direction casing evoking an Irish pub to this base. Its character is sweet and mild; nicotine load stays between low and medium, suiting those seeking an all-day-smokable aromatic tobacco. Because of the loose-cut structure, packing the pipe and keeping the burn even requires a bit of practice; according to records, the producer describes this series as aimed at experienced smokers. The product has been distributed in 50-gram pouch and 100-gram tin formats.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-special-d.o: Leaves a scent of toasted malt and dark sugar.

teds-pipe-shoppe-300-the-founders-blend.z: 300 The Founder's Blend, a pipe tobacco from Ted's Pipe Shoppe; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

hu-tobacco-makhuwa.z: Makhuwa is a Burley-forward blend that also contains Virginia and Perique. A light chocolate-cocoa tone appears in the tin aroma and in the smoke, but this flavoring doesn't build a dominant layer, instead accompanying the tobacco's nutty body. Perique adds a spicy, lightly fruity edge, while Virginia gives measured sweetness. The burn is clean and cool; nicotine stays at a moderate level. It's one of the blends HU Tobacco produces in small batches in Germany. It suits smokers looking for a Burley-based, lightly flavored but not quite aromatic structure. It forms an in-between record for those seeking a crossing point between aromatic and plain blends.
hu-tobacco-makhuwa.o: A light cocoa aroma is accompanied by a dry-walnut and hay tone.

rudolph-rudolph-pipe-tobacco.z: No reliable source could be found for this aromatic pipe tobacco known under the Rudolph name.

john-aylesbury-dark-virginia-flake.z: John Aylesbury Dark Virginia Flake is recorded as a pressed, sliced flake in the German John Aylesbury brand's unflavored Virginia line; since it doesn't appear in the maker's current product listing, no verifiable source could be found on its composition and character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-heavy-english-50.z: Heavy English #503 is an unflavored English mixture from Sutliff's numbered bulk line. The blend's backbone is formed by oriental leaves, chiefly Izmir; Cyprus latakia builds a smoky, mustily sweet support layer, while lemon Virginia adds citrusy acidity and herbal freshness. The cut is ribbon. Along the flavor line, smoky cocoa, spiced floral, and citrus notes appear. Despite the "heavy" in its name, the latakia ratio is kept moderate; the smoke stays cool and dry, with a low tendency to bite the tongue. Offered in bulk as an option for those wanting to smoke latakia blends throughout the day.
sutliff-tobacco-company-heavy-english-50.o: Leaves a scent reminiscent of smoky wood, incense, and lemon peel.

john-cotton-john-cottons-numbers-1-2-med.z: A pipe tobacco blend released under the John Cotton name; not enough independent sources could be found to document its contents and character.
john-cotton-john-cottons-numbers-1-2-med.o: No source could be found on the room note.

gawith-hoggarth-co-toffee-brown-pigtail.z: Toffee Brown Pigtail is the toffee-topped version of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s fine pigtail Burma tobaccos. Dark fire-cured leaves are hand-twisted into rope form and cut into small discs for use. Toffee sweetness and a creamy texture dominate the pouch aroma, and this layer carries through into the smoke. Flavor intensity and nicotine level run high, giving a full smoke. An entry for those wanting a strong base paired with a sweet topping. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. is one of the English producers that continues traditional twist (rope) production at its Kendal factory, hand-twisting fire-cured leaves into rope form. Because twist tobaccos don't go through a pressure-cooking stage, they stay intense in nicotine; records indicate these ropes are sold for both chewing and pipe smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-toffee-brown-pigtail.o: Leaves an aroma combining boiled-sugar, buttery toffee scent with tobacco smoke.

torben-dansk-orient-spezialitat.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Torben Dansk blend Orient Spezialitat has been found.

robert-lewis-orcilla-mixture.z: Orcilla Mixture is a ribbon-cut English blend prepared from Turkish-Oriental leaf, Latakia, and Virginia with a small amount of Perique added. No flavoring is applied, letting the tobaccos' own character stand out. The blend is among the classic mixtures of Robert Lewis, the London tobacconist founded in 1787. Because the Latakia proportion is kept measured, the smoky layer does not become dominant; the Oriental leaf's spicy structure and Virginia's sweetness stay in balance, while Perique adds a light sharpness in the background. Nicotine is low-to-medium and it offers a smooth smoke. It suits smokers looking for a light English blend for the first pipe of the day, or those new to the style.
robert-lewis-orcilla-mixture.o: Leaves a light woody-smoke and spice aroma.

ashton-smooth-sailing.z: Smooth Sailing is a ribbon-cut aromatic built on light lemon Virginia, golden Virginia, and generous black Cavendish. The top note is rum, dark chocolate, and maple syrup, joined by a hint of coconut. The cut is a mix of light brown and black tones. Flavoring sits between light and medium. Early in the smoke, coconut is pronounced and resolves quickly, cocoa recedes toward the middle of the bowl, and maple sweetness lingers to the end. It's a slow-burning, low-nicotine blend needing few relights; it's aimed at those who like sweet aromatics and want a cool smoke.
ashton-smooth-sailing.o: Leaves a sweet room note of cocoa, maple syrup, and coconut.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-jester.z: A blend appearing in Scandinavian Tobacco Group records; no independent source documenting its content and character could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-jester.o: No detailed description of the room note could be found in the records.

uhles-blend-33.z: No current source documenting the composition of Blend 33, one of Uhle's numbered house blends, has been found; records indicate the blend does not appear in the maker's current lineup.
uhles-blend-33.o: No reliable source describing the room note has been found.

tinder-box-lazy-edna.z: Lazy Edna is noted as one of the aromatic house blends weighed at Tinder Box stores; no verifiable source on its composition and flavor direction has been found.
tinder-box-lazy-edna.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

dunhill-my-mixture-june-86.z: A record left over from Dunhill's custom blending program, not currently in production; no independent source describing its composition could be found, so a detailed record couldn't be compiled.
dunhill-my-mixture-june-86.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

mcclelland-2011-holiday-spirit.z: Holiday Spirit is the limited-run aromatic series McClelland released for the holiday season each year. A light body made of Virginia, Burley, and Cavendish leaves is topped with dark rum, pecan, and cocoa flavoring. The 2011 release is that year's edition of the series.
mcclelland-2011-holiday-spirit.o: Leaves an aroma of dark rum, cocoa, and toasted walnut.

sutliff-tobacco-company-ts24-blended-tur.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Sutliff Tobacco Company's TS24 Blended Turkish Ribbon pipe tobacco could be found.

poul-winslow-winter-edition.z: This is a seasonal aromatic member of the Poul Winslow line; no source could be found describing its content and casing.

mccranies-dundees-blend.z: Dundee's Blend is one of McCranie's shop's English-class bulk blends; no sufficient sources could be found on its ratios or composition.

hill-hill-tobacconists-haymarket.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for this blend, described as aromatic, from the Hill & Hill Tobacconists brand.

peterson-holiday-season-2014.z: Holiday Season is Peterson's limited-edition, Christmas-themed aromatic tin series released each year; the 2014 edition was presented in a 100 gram tin. A Burley-forward body is joined by Cavendish and Virginia, carrying cocoa and vanilla flavoring. Peterson is an Irish brand, but the blending and production of these special tins is outsourced; records indicate they were made by Kohlhase, Kopp & Co. to a recipe specified by Peterson. The cut is described as ribbon. Because the recipe changes each year, every edition of the series counts as a distinct blend; the 2014 tin was likewise prepared for its release year and never reprinted. It is a notable record for smokers seeking flavored, sweet-profile tins and for those who collect the annual limited editions.
peterson-holiday-season-2014.o: Leaves a cocoa and vanilla aroma.

samuel-gawith-sams-plug.z: Sam's Plug is one of the plug-format products Samuel Gawith produces on its old presses in Kendal. Its weight is on Virginia leaf; Oriental leaf is a secondary component adding spice and depth. Sold in plug form, the smoker slices off the amount needed with a knife and rubs it; this method preserves moisture for a long time. Its smoke is intense with a slow-burning structure, its fullness medium. Its taste is built around Virginia's hay and honey tones, with the Oriental's contribution staying in the background. Suited to smokers accustomed to slicing plug tobacco who seek the natural Virginia character in intensity; it is on record that its profile settles as it is rested, like other pressed tobaccos.
samuel-gawith-sams-plug.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay, honey, and light woody spice.

mcclelland-no-m-34-carnival.z: A blend in McClelland's M-series bulk aromatics, discontinued when the firm closed in 2018; no sufficient source documenting its contents and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-spearmint.z: Kendal Gold is one of the shag-cut main bodies produced at Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Kendal workshop in Cumbria. Its base is a fine golden-hued cut of flame-cured bright Virginia leaf; the producer states it uses no other tobacco type in this series, only cleanly cut Virginia. The Kendal Gold body is offered with numerous different flavorings, and Kendal Gold Spearmint is this family's spearmint-flavored member. The mint flavoring leaves a cooling effect on the mouth and throat, with the Virginia base's sweetness staying beneath that coolness. Since the shag cut burns fast, a measured draw is needed. Aimed at smokers accustomed to mint-topped tobaccos and those wanting a palate-cleansing blend.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-spearmint.o: Leaves a cool mint and herbal aroma.

richs-old-perth.z: Old Perth is a Virginia blend Rich's Cigar Store built in an old-fashioned English style. A mix of different Virginia leaves has a small amount of Turkish-Oriental leaf added; here the Oriental leaf forms a spicy edge without overwhelming the body. With no Latakia present, the smoke load is light and Virginia's bready sweetness stays up front. The maker describes it as a classic mixture intended for afternoon smoking; it suits smokers looking for a light-to-medium-bodied, unflavored Virginia taste.
richs-old-perth.o: Leaves a dry-hay, lightly spicy, tart grain aroma.

milan-tobacconists-our-sugar-barrel.z: Referred to as an aromatic blend from Milan Tobacconists' "Our" line; since it doesn't appear in the maker's current catalogue and no source describing its composition could be obtained, no further detail can be given.

briarworks-international-bacon-old-fashi.z: Bacon Old Fashioned is an aromatic blend Tennessee-based BriarWorks built starting from the cocktail of the same name. Its base holds burley, virginia and black cavendish; a bourbon-and-citrus-based casing is applied on top. What sets the blend apart is hickory-smoked, fire-cured Kentucky leaf added to answer the smoke and salt sense of the cocktail recipe. In the smoke, orange, a salty smoke reminiscent of smoked bacon, and a lightly alcoholic sweetness intertwine. The body is medium. Suitable for smokers wanting to step outside classic fruit aromatics and try smoky, salty tones in an aromatic frame.
briarworks-international-bacon-old-fashi.o: Leaves an orange peel, whiskey-barrel and smoked-meat aroma in wood smoke.

king-smoking-pipes-and-cigars-king-of-sw.z: A blend King Smoking Pipes and Cigars offers as an English mixture; no verifiable source could be found describing its composition.
king-smoking-pipes-and-cigars-king-of-sw.o: Reportedly close to the smoky, spicy tobacco scent left by English mixtures.

cornell-diehl-strawberry-cavendish.z: Strawberry Cavendish is a member of Cornell & Diehl's single-flavor Cavendish series. Strawberry flavoring is applied to a traditional American-style Cavendish base made of Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish; the blend is presented ribbon cut. Nicotine stays light, and on the flavor side, the casing comes forward. Single-note aromatics of this kind are used both by those new to the pipe and by smokers wanting to mix them into other blends to build their own composition. As expected of aromatics, its room note is pronounced.
cornell-diehl-strawberry-cavendish.o: Leaves a scent of fresh strawberry.

smokinjoescigars-com-joes-black-gold-8.z: One of the bulk aromatic blends a retailer numbers under its own name; no source on its composition could be found.

bufflehead-cackling-canada-goose.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Cackling Canada Goose under the Bufflehead brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

samuel-gawith-grousemoor-plug.z: Grousemoor Plug is the pressed plug presentation of the Grousemoor blend; retailer records describe it directly as "the same as Grousemoor." Its base is light Virginia leaf, flavored with the floral essence blend characteristic of the Lakeland style. Because of the plug structure, the smoker can slice it for use like a flake or crumble it. Pressing lets the flavor settle more deeply into the leaf; on the smoke, the floral, sweet essence and Virginia's own sweetness proceed intertwined, and the burn is slower than the ribbon cut. Flavor intensity is high and tends to linger in the pipe. Aimed at those wanting to try Lakeland aromatics in pressed form.
samuel-gawith-grousemoor-plug.o: Spreads a soapy floral essence and a lavender-like perfume trace through the room.

hearth-home-cerberus.z: Cerberus is a Hearth & Home mixture named after the three-headed guard dog of mythology. The name refers to the blend's construction: Latakia, Perique, and dark fire-cured Kentucky are laid over an aged Virginia base in equal weight. Oriental leaf is added to open up the flavor line. Latakia is added to the blend finely cut, so the smoke layer stands out in the taste. Perique brings spice and dark fruit, while Kentucky adds earthy weight. The result is a near full-bodied, layered, and intense English mixture that gives a heavy, creamy smoke when packed loosely. No top note is used. Suited to experienced smokers accustomed to Latakia who want to see more than one character leaf together in a single blend.
hearth-home-cerberus.o: Leaves a heavy aroma of wood smoke, pepper, and dried fruit.

tabac-benden-shamkat-green-label.z: Shamkat Green Label is the version of Tabac Benden's Oriental-forward Shamkat blend with Louisiana Perique added. The Perique joining the Lebanese Oriental and Virginia adds noticeably more spice and complexity to the mixture compared to the classic Shamkat; production takes place at the Dan Tobacco Manufactory, and the tobacco is stored as whole leaf until cutting is needed. The taste strikes a balance between peppery, floral, and earthy notes; the Oriental's dry spice is topped by Perique's plum and pepper side. Body and nicotine sit a notch above the classic Shamkat. It suits smokers who like Oriental blends and want Perique's spice on top.
tabac-benden-shamkat-green-label.o: A peppery, floral note accompanies a spicy, dry-hay scent.

cornell-diehl-sun-bear-navy-cask.z: No current maker or retailer record documenting the composition of this limited release, part of Cornell & Diehl's honey-themed Sun Bear series, could be found.

rattray-accountants-mixture.z: Accountant's Mixture is a dark-colored blend combining aged Virginia leaf with unsweetened black Cavendish, with a measured amount of Latakia added. It doesn't build a complex structure; it follows a direct, full, dark flavor line. Nicotine is described as medium, and its strength never turns sharp. The ribbon cut makes packing and lighting easy, and its structure forgives a relaxed pace during outdoor smoking or long sessions where attention drifts from the tobacco. It suits smokers looking for a dark-bodied but unshowy everyday blend where Latakia remains just a touch.
rattray-accountants-mixture.o: Leaves a dark, smoky tobacco aroma with a light sweet wood note.

peretti-oriental-no-40.z: Oriental No. 40 is Peretti's blend built entirely from Near Eastern-origin leaf. Per the maker's own description, no tobacco from other regions is used in the mixture, so the oriental leaf's distinctive tart, resinous, and spicy character comes through undiluted. It is ribbon cut, and this low-moisture leaf group catches quickly. In terms of body, oriental blends are generally not nicotine-heavy; the fullness here comes from flavor intensity. It's aimed at smokers who want a profile far sharper than plain Virginia, without latakia, and who want to get to know the oriental leaf on its own. Smoked slowly, its tendency to bite the tongue is reduced.
peretti-oriental-no-40.o: Leaves a sharp scent recalling dry grass, spice, and resin.

dobies-four-square-curlies.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of Four Square Curlies, a blend from Dobie's.

faders-cherry-berry.z: Fader's is a line of house blends offered under its own name by a long-established Baltimore tobacconist; no verifiable source could be found regarding this blend's composition and character.

ken-byron-ventures-the-dread-planet-2021.z: The 2021 limited release of Dread Planet is reported to be Virginia- and Perique-forward, but no independent source could be found to document its character.
ken-byron-ventures-the-dread-planet-2021.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

richs-sweet-oriental.z: Sweet Oriental is a blend from Rich's Cigar Store that puts Oriental leaf front and center. The maker describes it as complex, sweet, and smoky; the Oriental tobaccos' tart-spicy taste, reminiscent of dried fruit, combines with Virginia sweetness. Body stays light while flavor intensity is high, which makes the blend suited to smokers who want to get to know the character of Eastern Mediterranean leaf. It is an unflavored composition, sold in bulk at Rich's Portland stores.
richs-sweet-oriental.o: Leaves a spicy, lightly smoky dried-fruit aroma.

hearth-home-lakeland-brickle-fortissimo.z: A blend referred to as a higher-essence version of Lakeland Brickle; there is not enough independent sourcing to confirm the details.
hearth-home-lakeland-brickle-fortissimo.o: Leaves a rose and floral-essence aroma.

pipe-republic-whitstable.z: No reliable sources on Pipe Republic's blend Whitstable could be found, so its content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

paul-olsen-garrick.z: For Paul Olsen's blend called Garrick, no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-victorian.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the content and character of Match Victorian, one of the bulk blends from Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company, could be found.

wellauer-co-mixture-965.z: Mixture 965 is part of the series Swiss tobacconist Wellauer prepared as a counterpart to Dunhill's mixtures; its name and structure are based on the now-discontinued Dunhill My Mixture 965. This ribbon-cut blend contains black or brown cavendish, Latakia, Oriental-Turkish leaf, and Virginia. On opening the tin, Latakia and Oriental's smoky scent arrives together with the Oriental's dry spice and Virginia's fruity note. In the smoke, Latakia appears not as a sharp burst but as a slowly settling woody, leathery layer; the Oriental leaf adds a dry, grassy spice. Cavendish brings a natural sweetness and creamy texture midway through the smoke, balancing the rising strength without turning the blend into a flavored aromatic. A nutty undertone is a typical result of this composition. Being considered full in nicotine, it appeals as an evening or after-dinner pipe for smokers accustomed to classic Latakia-based English mixtures.
wellauer-co-mixture-965.o: A lightly sweet cavendish scent layers over the woody, smoky Latakia smoke.

cornell-diehl-gillingham-mixture.z: Gillingham Mixture is a ribbon-cut blend among Cornell & Diehl's coarser-textured aromatics. Per the manufacturer's description, black cavendish along with red and light Virginia leaves are topped with a small amount of perique; the blend is honey-flavored. The component list also mentions burley and Oriental tobacco. The honey flavoring brings out the blend's Virginia sweetness, while perique leaves a light spice and fruit tone in the background. As the flavoring is kept moderate, the blend suits those who want to avoid heavily syrupy aromatics yet still want a sweet smoke, and who don't want to give up natural tobacco taste entirely.
cornell-diehl-gillingham-mixture.o: Leaves honey sweetness together with the tangy aroma of dry tobacco.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-brown-twist-ci.z: Sliced Brown Twist Cinnamon is Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s cinnamon-topped version of its brown Burma base. Fire-cured leaves are twisted into a fine rope; the tobacco arrives as a dense mass that yields small coin-like slices when cut. The pouch aroma is oily and spicy; on the smoke, the earthy, smoky core of the fire-curing is preserved while the sweet topping and inverted sugar worked into the leaf during production add a sweet top layer to the smoke. Since it isn't steam-cooked under pressure, it stays intense in nicotine; it needs to be thinly sliced and smoked slowly. An entry for those wanting a topped but still strong Burma tobacco. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. is one of the English producers that continues traditional twist (rope) production at its Kendal factory, hand-twisting fire-cured leaves into rope form. Because twist tobaccos don't go through a pressure-cooking stage, they stay intense in nicotine; records indicate these ropes are sold for both chewing and pipe smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-brown-twist-ci.o: Leaves an aroma combining cinnamon spice with woody tobacco scent.

clan-shaw-risha.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Risha.

cornell-diehl-eight-state-burley-2021.z: Eight State Burley is a Small Batch release where Cornell & Diehl blender Jeremy Reeves pays tribute to traditional American burley mixtures; the name references the eight historic American burley-growing states. An air-cured white-and-dark burley base is joined by Canadian light Virginia and SM2-18 red Virginia; 2005-harvest Sokhoum, Samsun, and Katerini Orientals round out the finish. After the leaf is pressed and sliced, it is rubbed out into an old-style ready-rubbed form; it can be lit straight from the tin. The taste moves back and forth between burley's nutty, cocoa-like base and the Orientals' floral, incense-like, cinnamon-reminiscent spice. Being a limited run, it is not continuously in the catalog; it appeals to smokers seeking unflavored, full-bodied burley mixtures.
cornell-diehl-eight-state-burley-2021.o: Leaves a dry room aroma reminiscent of cocoa, nuts, and cinnamon.

radfords-blend-no-77-golden-mystery.z: No source could be found documenting the content and flavoring of Blend No. 77 Golden Mystery, part of Radfords' numbered blend series.
radfords-blend-no-77-golden-mystery.o: No information describing the room note could be found in available records.

park-lane-tobacconist-knightsbridge.z: No reliable source could be found for the Park brand pipe tobacco called Lane Tobacconist-Knightsbridge, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-erinmore-.z: A Balkan-style mixture released under the Erinmore name; no reliable detail on the blend's composition and production history could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-erinmore-.o: Leaves a smoky scent from latakia.

robert-mcconnell-scottish-blend.z: Scottish Blend is an unflavored, full-bodied mixture built on a base of black Cavendish and Virginia, with Latakia, Oriental tobacco, and Perique added. It is presented as a ribbon cut and burns evenly. The flavor profile carries bready, walnut-like dark notes alongside a near-caramel sweetness supplied by the Cavendish and Virginia. Oriental leaf adds a spicy layer, Latakia a measured smokiness, and Perique sharpens the background. Nicotine sits in the upper-medium range. It suits fans of unflavored, full-bodied English blends.
robert-mcconnell-scottish-blend.o: Leaves a bready, walnut-like aroma with a hint of caramel.

black-cat-cigar-company-ultimate-black.z: Ultimate Black is an aromatic blend based on fire-cured black Cavendish, sold under its own name by the Pennsylvania-based Black Cat Cigar Company. Per the maker's description it's a mild tobacco with pronounced sweetness that burns slow and cool; the leaf is dark-colored, finely cut, and high in moisture. It appears in the company's catalog in bulk, in 2-ounce, 8-ounce, and pound packaging. On the flavor side, the Cavendish's own caramelized sweetness stands out, and the vanilla topping applied over it adds a mellow fullness to the smoke. Its low nicotine level suits smokers looking for an all-day tobacco or one to add as a sweetener to other blends; because of its moisture, airing it out before smoking makes it easier to light. For smokers accustomed to English or Latakia-forward blends, its character may read as too sweet.
black-cat-cigar-company-ultimate-black.o: Fills the room with sweet vanilla and burnt-sugar notes.

w-o-larsen-2017-craftmans-edition.z: 2017 Craftmans Edition is the year's entry in W.Ø. Larsen's Craftsmans Edition series, in which a separate blend is prepared each year, offered here in a 3.5-ounce tin. The blend is built on Virginias, Burley, and twice-fermented black cavendish. Part of the tobaccos are pressed, rested, and then rubbed out; this structure, combining ribbon cut with rubbed-out flake, gives a softer burn. In flavoring, vanilla and caramel establish Larsen's known sweet line, and a warm almond note added on top gives the blend a creamy side and a pronounced room note. It's light in nicotine. This is a release aimed at smokers who love sweet Danish-style aromatics and want a low-strength blend suitable for all-day smoking.
w-o-larsen-2017-craftmans-edition.o: Leaves a scent of roasted almond, vanilla, and caramel pastry.

ken-byron-ventures-embrys-banana-bread.z: Banana Bread is an aromatic drawing its body mainly from white Burley and bright Virginia leaf. Its black Cavendish share is kept lower than in similar aromatics, pushing the blend toward a lighter, all-day smoke. The casing is tuned to deliver a warm banana-bread aroma.
ken-byron-ventures-embrys-banana-bread.o: Leaves an aroma of banana bread fresh out of the oven.

sutliff-tobacco-company-chocolate-truffl.z: J12 Chocolate Truffle is an aromatic bringing together six separate tobaccos: a ribbon-cut combination of Virginia, burley, and black cavendish leaves is joined by three different chocolate toppings along with almond, coconut, and a small amount of brandy. The topping builds a sweet, layered direction reminiscent of cocoa. It's a blend low in strength and flavor intensity, with limited tongue bite. Suited to smokers seeking sweet chocolate and nutty notes together.
sutliff-tobacco-company-chocolate-truffl.o: Leaves a sweet trace where cocoa, almond, and coconut scents mix together.

mccranies-new-bedford.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found on New Bedford, one of McCranie's Pipe Shop's house blends.
mccranies-new-bedford.o: No reliable description of the aroma could be found.

newminster-no-201-straight-black.z: No. 201 Straight Black is a traditional Danish-style straight black cavendish. South American-origin virginia leaves are steam-processed and darkened, and the natural tobacco taste is supported with a light vanilla casing. Since it rests on a single leaf type, the flavor profile is plain and sweet, with a low nicotine load. It can be smoked on its own, but is also used as a blending tobacco to soften and sweeten other mixtures. Suitable for those looking for a light, sweet, low-bite smoke, as well as smokers who blend their own mixtures. It is produced at Mac Baren's facilities in Denmark.
newminster-no-201-straight-black.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and steamed-tobacco aroma in the room.

cao-cherry-bomb.z: CAO Cherry Bomb is an aromatic blend where flue-cured virginia leaf and steamed black cavendish are topped with cherry and vanilla flavoring. As its name suggests, the fruity casing is kept pronounced; cherry leads, with vanilla acting as a softening background. It is ribbon cut and packed at a moist consistency. It offers a light-nicotine smoke that runs flat and sweet on the palate. Since the casing rather than the leaf flavor is the determining factor, it appeals to those drawn to fruity aromatics and smokers new to the pipe. Like the rest of the line it is manufactured in the US under the CAO name.
cao-cherry-bomb.o: Leaves a sharp, lightly tart cherry aroma with soft vanilla behind it.

cup-o-joes-adirondack-mardi-gras-pipe-to.z: A tobacco from the Cup O' Joes tobacco shop's Adirondack house-blend series, classed as an English mixture; no source describing its composition was found.

john-aylesbury-sir-johns-curly-cut.z: Sir John's Curly Cut is a blend produced for John Aylesbury by Kopp Tobaccos, rolled into a coil and sliced into coin-shaped pieces. Its composition includes select Virginia and Burley leaf; the leaves are air-cured to help the flavor hold. It's offered in a 100-gram tin. The spiral cut gives the tobacco a slow, even burn. Its character is lightly sweet and balanced, carrying no heavy casing. Suited to smokers who know how to rub out a coin cut and want a slow-smoking blend where the tobacco taste stands forward.
john-aylesbury-sir-johns-curly-cut.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of dry hay and bread crust.

per-g-jensen-brothers-in-arms.z: For Per G. Jensen's blend called Brothers in Arms, no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

house-of-calabash-new-renaissance.z: This is referred to as a Scottish-style House of Calabash blend; no verifiable source describing its content and character could be found.

kleinlagel-valley-lilly.z: Valley Lilly is an aromatic blend Kleinlagel released in a 50-gram tin. Its name comes from two casings noted on the German label: citrus and Maiglöckchen, meaning lily of the valley. The leaf base is Virginia; the casings create a fruity-floral top tone, with the tobacco's own sweetness staying in the background. Thanks to its ready-rubbed cut, it can be packed directly. Retailer records list its strength as light and its taste as sweetish, placing the blend in the low-nicotine, long-smoking aromatic class. Because of its floral casings, it stands apart from the usual vanilla and whisky aromas. Records indicate production has ended.
kleinlagel-valley-lilly.o: Leaves a floral, non-sharp room note reminiscent of lemon peel and lily of the valley.

jacks-tobacco-top-dog.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of Top Dog, part of Jack's Tobacco's "Dog" line, could be found.
jacks-tobacco-top-dog.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

holland-house-holland-house-aromatic.z: Holland House Aromatic is a classic aromatic blend prepared by adding liqueur and citrus essence to a ribbon-cut mix of Burley, Cavendish, and Virginia leaves. Cavendish establishes a sweet, soft base, Burley gives body, and Virginia provides a light sugar contribution. The flavoring is moderate; the smoke is cool and mild. The brand's origin is traced to the early 19th century, and the product is produced today under Orlik. It's widely found in pouch packaging in Europe. It's a structure suited to smokers in aromatic blends looking for a measured liqueur-citrus profile rather than intense sweetness, and to those new to the pipe.
holland-house-holland-house-aromatic.o: Leaves an aroma of sweet liqueur and orange peel.

sutliff-tobacco-company-dutch-masters-wh.z: Dutch Masters Whiskey Cavendish is one of the bulk blends from the Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

mcclelland-stave-aged-virginia-35-ribbon.z: Stave-Aged Virginia 35 Ribbon is the Virginia blend McClelland prepared for its 35th anniversary. It takes its name from the oak barrel stave used to age the tobacco; the package includes a sample piece of that stave, with bourbon aroma worked into the wood. The cut is ribbon and packs easily. In the smoke, a measured bourbon note sits atop stoved Virginia's tea-like, tangy, sweet axis; the flavoring doesn't leap forward, moving instead alongside the tobacco's natural taste. Turkish-language sources note it doesn't bite the tongue but tends to run hot, calling for a slow smoke. Suited to smokers seeking a middle ground between aromatic and straight Virginia. McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-stave-aged-virginia-35-ribbon.o: Leaves a sweet, woody aroma reminiscent of barrel-aged whiskey.

ken-byron-ventures-double-eagle.z: One of Ken Byron Ventures' limited, golf-themed Virginia releases; no accessible maker's profile could be found to document its contents.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-black-tan.z: Black & Tan, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an aromatic mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

smokers-haven-10.z: One of the numbered mixtures from Smokers' Haven, founded in Columbus, Ohio in 1940 and having its blends produced by English makers for many years; no independent source describing this blend's composition could be found.

tinder-box-midnight.z: Tinder Box is the name of an American tobacconist chain founded in 1928 that sells blends prepared for its own shops under its own name; Midnight is one of these house blends, though no sufficient independent source describing its composition and character has been found.

tabac-benden-kluverbaum-marineschnitt.z: Klüverbaum Marineschnitt is a pressed Virginia blend Tabac Benden had prepared with an eye toward the Navy Cut tobaccos of the eighteenth- and nineteenth-century maritime tradition. A measured proportion of Perique is added to selected Virginias, and the mixture is formed into a relatively firm cake using historic English presses located in Koppe. Its name comes from the jib-boom, the spar extending over the bow of a sailing ship to which the headsails are attached. The cake is sliced and rubbed out for packing; the tight pressing intensifies the taste. Virginia's dark, bready sweetness is topped by Perique's pepper and plum side, and the smoke is medium-bodied. It suits smokers who enjoy the unflavored Virginia-Perique style and don't mind working with tobacco in cake form.
tabac-benden-kluverbaum-marineschnitt.o: A peppery, lightly tart note mixes into the dark sweetness of the pressed leaf.

hu-tobacco-out-of-africa.z: Out of Africa is a broken flake in HU Tobacco's The Blender's Pride line. Its base is built on strong Burley grades, joined by dark pressed Virginia and a small amount of Perique. Burley establishes a nutty, molasses-like, earthy base, while the dark Virginia brings cooked-fruit sweetness and a light citrus note; Perique adds depth with a fig-and-raisin-evoking spice. The flavoring is measured; a sweet, lightly floral, woody layer along with pineapple and apricot fruit notes are described. It's aimed at those looking for a full-bodied flake where the flavoring doesn't mask the tobacco. Records indicate it's presented in 100-gram tins.
hu-tobacco-out-of-africa.o: A light tropical-fruit sweetness and woody smoke mix into the aroma of toasted hazelnut and molasses.

mac-baren-amphora-full-aroma.z: Amphora Full Aroma is a blend built by adding burley, fire-cured Kentucky and oriental leaves to a Virginia base. The manufacturer states the leaves are gathered from three continents. Like the rest of the series, it's presented rubbed out, ready to pack. The "full" in the name points more to the fullness of the leaf mix than to a heavy sauce layer: smoke and wood tones from the Kentucky, burley's dry body and the orientals' spice come forward, while Virginia carries the sweetness in the background. It's on the strong end of the series in nicotine. Suited to experienced smokers seeking a dark, smoky and filling smoke.
mac-baren-amphora-full-aroma.o: Leaves a room note toward smoke, wood and dry spice.

faders-danish-flake.z: Not enough independent sourcing documenting the composition and character of Danish Flake, one of the house blends of the Baltimore-based Fader's tobacconist, could be found.

abenaki-tobacco-co-cherokee.z: Cherokee is among Abenaki Tobacco's base aromatics. Per the maker's recipe, selected Green River Burley is combined with black Cavendish, with a light vanilla flavoring applied over it. The flavoring level is kept low; though the blend is counted in the aromatic class, the leaf's own taste stays noticeably present. A balanced structure is built between the dry, nutty base from the Burley and the Cavendish's sweetness. It's a middle option for smokers avoiding heavily syruped aromatics but also finding fully unflavored blends flat. Abenaki Tobacco was a small maker based in Conway, New Hampshire; its own sales site is no longer live today.
abenaki-tobacco-co-cherokee.o: Leaves a light vanilla and dry, nutty Burley room note.

mcclelland-40th-anniversary.z: 40th Anniversary is a straight Virginia slice prepared from a special red Virginia batch McClelland set aside for its fortieth founding anniversary. It was released in 2017 in 100-gram tins, and since the firm closed in 2018, it was produced for only about a year and a half. The blend's body is built on a tangy-sweet, dark-fruited, earthy, and woody red Virginia, joined by a lighter-colored Virginia bringing citrus, faint herbal, and spice tones. Strength runs light to medium, while the taste is intense thanks to the slice-pressing and aging. A record within the territory of those who love unflavored Virginia slices and are used to letting tobacco rest in a jar before smoking.
mcclelland-40th-anniversary.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of dried fruit and tangy bread yeast.

sutliff-tobacco-company-monarch.z: An aromatic bulk blend stated to be part of the Sutliff catalog; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-monarch.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet aromatic scent.

thepiperoom-com-bings-favorite.z: No independent source documenting the composition of the ThePipeRoom.com house blend Bing's Favorite has been found; the brand's own site is no longer online.
thepiperoom-com-bings-favorite.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

samuel-gawith-christmas-mixture-2012.z: A limited-run edition Samuel Gawith released for the 2012 holiday season; no independent source documenting that year's specific blend content could be found.

motzek-kieler-freu-n-de-alte-hasen.z: Since neither the manufacturer's own description nor two independent reliable sources could be found for the Motzek blend called Kieler Freu(n)de "Alte Hasen", its composition, cut, and character could not be documented here.

kaptn-brammers-acht-glasen.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for Kapt'n Brammers' Acht Glasen, so the profile is left incomplete.

sutliff-tobacco-company-crumble-kake-eng.z: Crumble Kake English #1 is the English-character member of Sutliff's pressed, crumbly-cake Crumble Kake series. Alongside latakia are red Virginia, burley, and oriental leaves; no flavoring is used. Leather, earth, and nutty tones carry through the smoke; a light fruity sweetness from Virginia balances the smoke. The cake can be broken by hand into ribbon or larger pieces, allowing burn rate to be adjusted. Suited to smokers accustomed to latakia blends seeking a medium-bodied English mixture.
sutliff-tobacco-company-crumble-kake-eng.o: Wood smoke and smokiness fill the room, leaving a light sweet trace beneath.

teds-pipe-shoppe-the-dubliner.z: One of the house blends prepared at Ted's Pipe Shoppe in Tulsa, Oklahoma; though records show it among the more than forty house blends of the business founded in 1961, no independent source describing the blend's content and character could be found.

watch-city-cigar-ahabs-comfort.z: This is one of the house blends of the Watch City Cigar shop in Massachusetts; it does not appear in the current catalog, and no source could be found documenting its composition.

fincks-cigar-company-black-vanilla.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for Finck's Cigar Company's Black Vanilla pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

the-smoke-shop-seminar.z: No reliable source could be found on Seminar, the house blend from the tobacconist The Smoke Shop.

richs-first-smoke.z: First Smoke is one of the bulk house blends at Rich's Cigar Store in Portland, said to be Burley-heavy; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.
richs-first-smoke.o: No reliable information could be found on the room note.

julius-vesz-virginia-flake.z: A blend bearing the name of Toronto pipe maker Julius Vesz; not enough independent sources could be found on its contents and character.

bosphorus-new-virginia-flake-2021.z: New Virginia Flake is a flake prepared from a single Virginia type, lightly sweetened with lemon and plum notes. It was brought in to replace the brand's discontinued Full Virginia Flake, and has been reworked several times over time. In the 2021 version, sugar content was reduced by about 30% compared to previous versions, yet the smoke is recorded as tasting sweeter; the manufacturer attributes this to changed production techniques. Being offered as fresh flake, its moisture is high; if smoked without being broken up and aired it runs wet, a problem that disappears once rested. Smoked at a slow, even pace, the sweet-tart aroma persists from start to finish, with strength staying medium. Aimed at smokers seeking a Virginia flake suited to all-day consumption.
bosphorus-new-virginia-flake-2021.o: Leaves a sweet-tart citrus and cooked-plum aroma.

torben-dansk-black-cavendish-sweet-aroma.z: Torben Dansk Black Cavendish Sweet Aroma is a single-component product in the brand's blending-component (Mischtabak) line. It consists of steam-processed, darkened black Cavendish leaf and carries a flavored profile; it can be smoked on its own or used as a component leaf to boost the sweetness and moisture of other blends. Nicotine load is low, making for a tobacco that is gentle on the tongue. Records indicate Torben Dansk is a brand known for its Danish-inspired blends, today produced under the Dan Tobacco Manufacturing (DTM) umbrella in Germany. Suited to those who enjoy an aromatic profile or to home blenders.
torben-dansk-black-cavendish-sweet-aroma.o: Leaves a sweet, sugary and lightly caramel-like aroma.

rattray-dark-fragrant.z: Dark Fragrant is a ribbon-cut, black-Cavendish-heavy blend with Perique added. Its color is dark, and the smoke is light and distinctly sweet; here Perique acts as a layer deepening the sweetness rather than giving a sharp pepper taste. It is noted to be prone to moisture even when smoked slowly, so airing before packing and keeping a slow pace helps regulate the burn. It suits smokers who prefer a light-bodied, sweet, Latakia-free smoke, or those wanting an introduction to dark Cavendish-heavy blends.
rattray-dark-fragrant.o: Leaves a sweet, dark, lightly spicy tobacco aroma.

king-street-coffee-tobacco-emporium-almo.z: Almost Heaven is an American-style aromatic blend prepared in-house by King Street Emporium, which has operated in Martinsburg, West Virginia for over thirty years. Per the manufacturer's description, mild-burning golden cavendish is combined with fire-cured leaves and finished with a house-specific flavoring. It's a low-nicotine mixture with medium flavor load; suited to those seeking a light aromatic to smoke at any hour and to smokers moving from aromatics without going to English mixtures. Since the blend is prepared only in the shop, its stock changes regularly and it isn't sold online.
king-street-coffee-tobacco-emporium-almo.o: Leaves the sweet scent of cavendish sugar together with the smoky scent of fire-cured leaf.

edwards-brandywine.z: This is one of Edward's Pipe & Tobacco's in-house blends prepared in the shop; not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition and character.
edwards-brandywine.o: Could not be described due to insufficient records.

drucquer-sons-first-amendment.z: Per records, Drucquer & Sons is a tobacconist house founded in London in 1841 and moved to Berkeley, California in 1928; its house blends were later brought back into production by Greg Pease. First Amendment is described as an English blend built from virginia and latakia leaves, flake cut. Since no independent second source could be reached regarding the blend's ratios, flavoring, or room note, this record has been left incomplete.

g-l-pease-bankside.z: Bankside was released on 8 November 2022 within G. L. Pease's Zeitgeist series, built around avant-garde themes of the modern era. It takes its name from the London district once home to the old Bankside Power Station, now the site of Tate Modern. It is designed as a reinterpretation of the classic Virginia-perique cake: red and bright Virginia build a base with genuine St. James perique, while dark fire-cured Kentucky and latakia add a contrasting smoky undertone. The taste opens with cream and citrus tartness from the Virginia; perique carries plummy spice, while Kentucky and latakia carry the earth and smoke side. Presented in cut-cake plug form, the smoker can adjust their own intensity by rubbing it out or loading it in pieces. It suits smokers who know the Virginia-perique structure and are looking for a measured smoky layer added to it.
g-l-pease-bankside.o: A fine woodsmoke aroma lies beneath the tartish fruit sweetness.

dunhill-light-flake.z: Light Flake is Dunhill's unadulterated Virginia flake. It's made from selected lemon-yellow and bronze Virginia leaves; the word "light" in the name refers to the leaf's color rather than its strength, which stays in the medium band. It's tinned in thin slices, packed either rubbed out or folded. The flavor profile is led by hay, meadow grass and citrus; a sweetness deepening toward honey and dark fruit emerges as it ages. With its slow burn and cool smoke, it suits smokers seeking unadulterated Virginia and those wanting a flake tobacco set aside for cellaring. Due to European packaging regulations the blend was later offered simply as "Flake," and production under the Dunhill name has ended.
dunhill-light-flake.o: Leaves a fine, sweet scent evoking dry grass, hay and citrus peel.

sutliff-tobacco-company-balkan-ii-512.z: Balkan II #512 is the Balkan-style blend in Sutliff's numbered bulk line. Per the maker's description, its composition includes a high proportion of four separate Turkish (oriental) leaves along with a generous amount of latakia and the brand's matured Virginia leaves. Compared to Balkan I in the same line, both the oriental and latakia shares are notably increased; the name reflects this difference. On the palate, latakia's smoke, tar, and wood tones stand at the very front; the orientals' dry, spicy, tart edge emerges from within that smoke, while Virginia provides a measured sweetness in the background. It's unflavored. Flavor intensity is high, while nicotine stays at a medium level. Designed for smokers accustomed to latakia-forward blends; it makes for a harsh introduction for someone coming from aromatics. Sold in bulk as ribbon cut.
sutliff-tobacco-company-balkan-ii-512.o: Leaves an intense scent of smoke, tar, and campfire that fills the room.

sutliff-tobacco-company-roma-vita.z: Roma Vita is an aromatic burley-Virginia mixture Sutliff named after the theme of an Italian evening dinner table. It was offered in small tins and in bulk. According to the maker's description, the blend's purpose is to give a long, unhurried after-dinner smoke, so the leaf selection is built around softness rather than strength. Burley gives the blend a nutty, earthy body, and Virginia adds a light sugary sweetness; the flavoring applied over it is measured and doesn't mask the tobacco's own taste. Thanks to the ribbon cut, it burns cool and even. It suits smokers who enjoy aromatic blends but want to avoid heavy, syrupy tastes. It is not currently in Sutliff's catalog.
sutliff-tobacco-company-roma-vita.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly wine-like aroma alongside a baked tobacco scent.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-matured.z: Mr Christian's Matured Fragrant Virginia is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-tidewater.z: Tidewater is The Country Squire's unflavored Virginia blend, prepared ribbon cut. The pouch aroma carries sweet hay, dried fruit and lemon peel. On the smoke, bright citrus, freshly cut grass, a lightly bready base and the leaf's own natural sugar come forward. Its body is kept light; the structure is built to show the nuances of unflavored Virginia without creating harshness on the palate. This makes it suited to long, all-day smoking and to those wanting to get to know Virginia leaf in its plain form; it is not for those seeking Latakia or aromatic casing.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-tidewater.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma leaning toward dry hay and citrus peel.

uhles-blend-44.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend Blend 44 has been found.

georgetown-tobacco-christmas-morning.z: Christmas Morning is one of the aromatic shop mixtures blended under its own name by Georgetown Tobacco, founded in Washington by David Berkebile in 1964. According to the maker's description, it's a mild aromatic with a raspberry accent added over dark Cavendish; it takes its name from its reference to Christmas morning and is sold loose in 2-ounce and 16-ounce measures. Because of its Cavendish-heavy structure, nicotine is light and the smoke has a round texture; the fruity sweetness is what stands out. Suited to those accustomed to aromatic mixtures wanting a light, sweet all-day smoke, as well as those stocking up on seasonal blends. Given the moist structure typical of aromatic tobaccos, it calls for slow, cool smoking and regular relighting.
georgetown-tobacco-christmas-morning.o: Leaves an aroma of sweet raspberry jam and candied dark tobacco.

dunhill-piping-cool.z: A blend released under the Dunhill name, not currently in production; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found, so a detailed record couldn't be compiled.
dunhill-piping-cool.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

dunhill-my-mixture-27.z: A discontinued mixture belonging to Dunhill's My Mixture line, for which no verifiable source on its composition could be found.

hu-tobacco-scotney.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the Scotney blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

ken-byron-ventures-plague-bringer-2021.z: A blend Ken Byron Ventures released as part of its small-batch production; no independent and verifiable source could be found about it.

4noggins-father-orin.z: Father Orin is an old-style Virginia-Burley blend prepared for 4noggins by Matt Robillard. Per the manufacturer's description, a very small amount of bourbon and honey topping is applied; the topping level is reported as "very light," meaning the blend stays measured enough not to fall into the aromatic category. Virginia's sweetness and Burley's nutty, dry character form the blend's core axis; the honey and bourbon merely round the edges. Nicotine is moderate and flavor is medium-to-full. Though close to unflavored blends, it suits smokers who don't want a completely bare Virginia-Burley but appreciate a light hint of sweetness.
4noggins-father-orin.o: Leaves an aroma of nutty tobacco carrying a thin trace of honey and whiskey.

4noggins-three-blind-moose.z: Three Blind Moose is one of 4noggins' mild aromatics. Alongside Burley, dark, light, and black Cavendish varieties are used together; the topping leans toward caramel and burnt sugar, leaving a buttery-sugar echo behind. Strength and flavor intensity are kept low, with little tendency to bite the tongue. It suits newcomers to the pipe and those looking for a gentle aromatic smokable all day.
4noggins-three-blind-moose.o: Leaves a sweet aroma of burnt sugar and caramel.

clan-shaw-cheyenne.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of Clan Shaw's Cheyenne blend could be found.

cornell-diehl-the-beast.z: The Beast is a limited release in which Cornell & Diehl pushes Perique well beyond the usual limits: roughly half the blend is Perique from the brand's own field in Louisiana. Virginia, fire-cured Kentucky, and black Cavendish are added alongside it; the whole mixture is, per records, rested in rum for seven days so the flavors meld together. It's tinned ribbon cut. The result is a blend extreme in both nicotine and flavor, carrying an intensity the maker describes as umami. Damp earth, sweet stone fruit, mesquite wood, and freshly ground black pepper are the main notes described. It may be heavy for smokers unaccustomed to Perique, and is meant to be smoked in small pipes on a full stomach. Being a limited run, it isn't currently on the market.
cornell-diehl-the-beast.o: Leaves the smoke of fire-cured leaf reminiscent of mesquite wood together with stone-fruit sweetness.

hearth-home-olde-tyme-swirl.z: Olde Tyme Swirl is an aromatic in the Hearth & Home Signature series. A base of Burley, Virginia, and black Cavendish leaf is rounded out with soft vanilla and chocolate notes; the topping is kept light enough not to mask the leaf's own taste. This makeup suits smokers who want both sweet-smelling aromatics and genuine tobacco taste together. A light-to-medium bodied, ribbon-cut recipe; the name's "swirl" refers to the intertwined combination of vanilla and cocoa.
hearth-home-olde-tyme-swirl.o: Leaves a vanilla-cream and cocoa aroma.

cornell-diehl-warped-saint-espresso-2022.z: Saint Espresso is an aromatic blend released in limited quantity in spring 2022 as a collaboration between Warped and Cornell & Diehl. It's built by combining three separate Cavendish types: a special Cavendish made from Eastern North Carolina red Virginia, black Cavendish from unsweetened One Sucker Kentucky Burley, and — taking the lead role in the blend — lightly flavored Dominican cigar-leaf Cavendish. The leaves are steamed and toasted; the mixture is mostly ribbon cut with some larger pieces mixed in. As its name suggests, it's built around an espresso association; its profile is described with cocoa, black coffee, and cream notes alongside fermented dark fruit, wood, and a hint of leather. The casing is more restrained than classic syrup-heavy Cavendish aromatics, letting the tobacco character come forward. Aimed at smokers who want an aromatic but avoid overly sweet blends; being a limited run, it isn't consistently available on the market.
cornell-diehl-warped-saint-espresso-2022.o: Leaves a light creamy sweetness alongside a scent of brewed dark coffee and cocoa.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-1997.z: Christmas Cheer 1997 is a tin in McClelland's annual Virginia series. Per its label, it's prepared with orange and red North Carolina flue-cured tobaccos selected from the 1991 harvest. The unflavored leaf is pressed and presented as broken flake. Using orange and red leaves together gives a darker, breadier profile leaning toward dried fruit compared to years dominated by lemon-orange leaf alone. No flavoring, and nicotine is medium. Since the series is explicitly made for cellaring, it's expected to mature with age; suited to smokers seeking unflavored Virginia flake.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-1997.o: Leaves a sweet hay, bread-crust, and faintly tangy dried-fruit aroma.

uhles-rise.z: No current source documenting the composition of the Uhle's Rise blend has been found.
uhles-rise.o: No reliable source describing the room note has been found.

robert-mcconnell-original-oriental.z: Original Oriental is a coarse-cut blend in which Oriental-Turkish tobaccos come forward, joined by Virginia, black Cavendish, and a small amount of Perique. Latakia is not mentioned in the product description, but the smoky layer in the smoke points to this leaf's presence. No casing is applied, and an intense raw-tobacco scent comes when the tin is opened. In the first quarter it gives the impression of a classic English blend; then the Oriental leaf's spicy, exotic taste comes forward. As the smoke progresses, the black-pepper sharpness from the Perique becomes noticeable in the throat and the blend hardens slightly. Even so, the overall character is sweet and mild, and the ash stays clean. Since it burns easily, it needs a tight pack. Aimed at those seeking Oriental-tobacco-forward blends.
robert-mcconnell-original-oriental.o: Leaves a scent of spicy Oriental leaf and light smoke.

nording-eriks-reserve.z: Erik's Reserve sits on the unflavored wing of the tobacco line bearing the name of Danish pipemaster Erik Nørding. Rested Virginia and burley leaves have a small amount of black cavendish added to bind the blend together; no flavoring is applied beyond that. It's offered in a 50-gram tin as a light-colored flake close to Danish tradition. Virginia's doughy, herbal sweetness is balanced by burley's earthy, nutty body; cavendish leaves a light sweetness in the background. With a nicotine strength running from light to medium, it gives a cool, non-biting smoke; since it can come a bit moist out of the tin, a short drying period before lighting is needed. It suits smokers newly moving into unflavored Virginia-burley character, or those wanting a flake that doesn't tire them out through the day.
nording-eriks-reserve.o: Leaves a calm scent at the sweetness of dry grass and baked dough, with a thin nutty aroma sensed behind it.

danske-club-peach-brandy.z: Peach Brandy is one of the fruited members of the Danske Club series, run under the Scandinavian Tobacco Group in Denmark.
