In keeping with the series' general construction, it's built on Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish leaf, ribbon cut. As the name suggests, the casing centers on a peach-and-brandy pairing. It's a blend with sweetness up front, nicotine sitting between mild and medium. Suited to smokers who like fruity, liquor-style casings and enjoy working with a long-burning fine cut. The series has had a place in the pipe tobacco market since the 1970s.
danske-club-peach-brandy.o: Leaves a scent of ripe peach and brandy.

dream-castle-tobacco-company-amaretto.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of Amaretto, a blend from Dream Castle Tobacco Company.

pauls-pipe-shop-st-patricks-day-tobacco.z: St. Patrick's Day is a member of the series of blends Paul's Pipe Shop prepares for particular days. Per the maker's recipe, a mixture of burley, Virginia, and some cavendish leaf is given a plum and whiskey essence. Burley gives the blend a dry base, Virginia a light sweetness, and cavendish mellowness. The topping sits on a fruity, boozy axis; the plum sweetness leaves a darker impression alongside the liquor note. Nicotine load is medium-low and the smoke texture is mild. It suits smokers who enjoy fruit- and liquor-flavored blends but want to steer clear of fully cavendish-based, syrupy mixtures.
pauls-pipe-shop-st-patricks-day-tobacco.o: Leaves a scent of plum, red wine, and whisky.

century-jamestown-1607-plug.z: Jamestown 1607 is one of the Century line's pressed-plug records. Per the seller's description, ten-year-aged orange and red virginia leaves are combined with latakia and pressed into a dense plug. The name refers to Jamestown, the first permanent English settlement in North America and the birthplace of the tobacco economy there. The plug tobacco needs to be sliced and rubbed out before smoking; a thick slice burns slowly, a finely rubbed leaf faster. The dark, fruity sweetness of aged virginia sits alongside latakia's smoky, resinous base; no top flavoring is applied. Suitable for smokers who enjoy working with pressed forms and are accustomed to smoky English blends.
century-jamestown-1607-plug.o: Leaves a burnt wood and smoke aroma, with a sweet dried-fruit note underneath.

van-erkoms-grand-national.z: One of the blends in South African maker Van Erkoms' pipe tobacco catalog; no source has been found indicating its composition, cut, or whether it remains in production.

uhles-blend-300.z: No current source documenting the composition of the Burley-based blend called Blend 300, attributed to the Uhle's tobacconist, has been found.

savinelli-doblone-doro.z: Doblone d'Oro takes its name from the Spanish gold coins whose origin dates to the sixteenth century; the tin lid's golden-yellow color also references this. The blend is built with selected virginia, burley, and fire-cured dark leaf, with perique added; the mixture is rolled into a rope, aged, then sliced into coin form and sold in 100-gram vacuum tins. The first draw brings virginia's fruity, lightly sour sweetness; then the fire-cured leaf's and burley's malt, nut, and cured-meat-like taste comes forward. Perique adds a peppery, sharp layer on top of these. The coins can be packed crumbled or whole; since the tin opens moist, some airing may be needed. Suited to experienced smokers seeking a medium-to-above-medium strength, layered Virginia-perique structure.
savinelli-doblone-doro.o: A sharp peppery trace accompanies a scent of wood-fire-cooked meat and molasses.

anthony-cranswick-green-castle.z: Green Castle is the aromatic member of Anthony Cranswick's Castle line, distinguished by color names. Burley and Virginia leaf form the blend's backbone; a small amount of black Cavendish and a vanilla flavoring are added over it. This structure places the blend somewhere between American-style Burley-heavy aromatics and Danish-style lightly sweetened aromatics. Since Burley's nutty, dry base balances the vanilla's sweetness, no wall of sugar forms; Virginia adds a measured bready sweetness. Nicotine load is light-to-medium, and the ribbon cut makes for an even burn. It's considered a suitable middle path for smokers new to aromatic blends or for those who don't want the tobacco taste erased in a vanilla tobacco.
anthony-cranswick-green-castle.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and light caramel room note.

dannemann-moods-filter.z: Moods Filter is not a pipe tobacco but a small filtered cigar made with Brazilian tobaccos. Records place Dannemann's production history back to 1872, and the brand is widely available across Europe. The product comes in short- and long-filter versions: the short-filter version is about the length of an ordinary cigarette filter, while the long-filter version is roughly half filter, half tobacco. The smoking character is mild and light; nicotine load is low and flavor intensity limited. A light fruit aroma is present but not dominant. It's a product aimed at those looking for a short, low-effort smoke rather than the intensity of pipe blends.
dannemann-moods-filter.o: Leaves a tobacco-forward scent typical of cigar leaf, carrying light fruity tones.

tinder-box-skilling.z: Skilling is one of the house blends the Tinder Box catalog describes as full-bodied. A Burley-forward body is joined by Virginia and Cavendish leaves; records indicate it is ribbon cut and burns slowly. The taste carries a light spicy tail and a nutty dryness, and any casing present stays in the background. Nicotine load is above medium. Suited to experienced smokers after a fuller smoke and a lingering taste.
tinder-box-skilling.o: Leaves a dry aroma reminiscent of roasted nuts with a light spice.

mccranies-porters-pride.z: Porter's Pride is one of McCranie's Cavendish-based bulk blends; no sufficient sources could be found on its flavoring or composition.

cornell-diehl-white-burley.z: White Burley is one of Cornell & Diehl's single-leaf bulk products. It's obtained by cutting top-grade light-colored Burley leaf from Kentucky fields into ribbon form. Since Burley has a low sugar content, it naturally burns slowly and offers a dry, nutty base rather than sweetness. It can be smoked on its own or used as a base leaf by those building their own blends; it takes well to combining with Virginia, Perique, or aromatic casings. On the maker's scale, strength, flavor, and room note are given as medium. Aimed at smokers wanting to get to know Burley character in its plain form.
cornell-diehl-white-burley.o: Leaves a low-sweetness scent reminiscent of dry nuts and bread crust.

rattray-summer-edition-2016.z: Summer Edition 2016 is an installment of the summer series released annually under the Rattray name. The series is prepared by German maker Kohlhase & Kopp in a Danish-style aromatic approach; while the Rattray brand is Scottish in origin, the tobacco is manufactured in Germany. The 2016 edition was presented with a Rio de Janeiro theme, foregrounding passionfruit, cachaça, and caramel flavoring. The blend is cut as a loose mixture and stays in the light-to-medium nicotine band. Since the flavoring is pronounced, it appeals more to smokers interested in fruity, sweet top notes and a sweet room aroma than to those looking for natural tobacco taste. Being a limited annual edition, it is not currently available on the market.
rattray-summer-edition-2016.o: Leaves a caramel aroma mixed with tropical fruit candy and sugarcane spirit.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-sweet-dub.z: This blend, also known as Sweet Dublin, is the yellow-packaged, Irish-whiskey-flavored variety of the Special Dublin family. The body is built from Virginia leaf of US, African, and Brazilian origin; after being lightly pressed and cut, the leaves are combined with sweet black cavendish and presented in a loose cut. The flavor profile is built on fruity sweetness, full yet mild; the whiskey casing adds a spicy depth. It stays below medium on nicotine, suiting long smoking sessions. Because of the loose cut's packing and lighting behavior, the producer describes this tobacco as aimed more at experienced smokers. Distributed in 50-gram pouch and 100-gram tin formats.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-sweet-dub.o: Leaves a scent evoking fruity sweetness and a whiskey-barrel echo.

abenaki-tobacco-co-creme-brulee.z: Creme Brulée is an Abenaki aromatic that follows the dessert it's named after. Per the maker's recipe, vanilla, caramel, and honey are applied over Burley, Virginia, and flavored black Cavendish; the aim is an intense, creamy taste texture. Using three leaf types together balances the blend's body: Burley adds dryness, Virginia natural sugar, and Cavendish darkness. It stays on the medium-light side for nicotine, aimed at smokers who like sweet aromatics. Abenaki Tobacco was a maker based in Conway, New Hampshire; since its own sales site isn't live today, the blend's current status is unclear.
abenaki-tobacco-co-creme-brulee.o: Leaves a burnt-sugar, vanilla, and honey room note.

e-hoffman-company-spilman-mixture.z: Spilman Mixture is E. Hoffman Company's classic English mixture. Virginia, latakia, Turkish orientals and cube-cut burley are used together; the coarse cut nods to pipe tobacco habits of the early last century. Since latakia, Virginia and burley are kept in balanced proportions, the blend gives a taste ranging between roasted hazelnut and open-air burning wood. It suits smokers seeking an unadulterated, direct taste who enjoy the smokiness-sweetness balance of English mixtures. Per the brand's history, E. Hoffman & Co. was founded in Chicago in 1857 by Edward Hoffman; after the founder's death the products were off the market for decades, and Spilman Mixture was brought back into production with its original tin design revived.
e-hoffman-company-spilman-mixture.o: Leaves a smoky scent evoking roasted hazelnut and wood fire.

park-lane-tobacconist-park-lane-no-10.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Park-Lane No. 10, one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-20.z: Match 20 is one of the bulk blends from the Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

faders-44.z: Fader's is a line of house blends offered under its own name by a long-established Baltimore tobacconist; no verifiable source could be found regarding this blend's composition and character.

pipesandcigars-com-match-hickory.z: Match Hickory is one of the house blends sold under its own name by the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com; no sufficient independent sources documenting its content and character could be found.

vauen-tab-150-jubilaum-jubilee.z: TAB 150 is the jubilee blend Vauen released in 1998 for the 150th anniversary of the company founded in 1848, and it has remained in production as one of the brand's founding tobaccos. The composition balances Virginia, Kentucky and Louisiana-origin leaf with black Cavendish, with some Perique added; curly-cut and flake pieces are used together. The varied cuts keep the burn cool and even. The flavoring leans toward tropical fruit and a light citrus note, kept at a level that doesn't overpower; thanks to the Perique and Kentucky, the body rises above that of pure aromatics. Suited to smokers seeking a middle ground between aromatic and unflavored tobacco.
vauen-tab-150-jubilaum-jubilee.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of ripe tropical fruit and citrus peel.

sutliff-tobacco-company-basin-street-blu.z: Basin Street Blues, part of Sutliff's Private Stock line, takes its name from New Orleans' Basin Street and the jazz standard of the same name. It's coarse ribbon cut, made predominantly of brown Virginia and Virginia-derived cavendish leaves, with roughly one-fifth of the mix being black cavendish. It may come out of the package slightly moist. The dominant flavor is caramel, accompanied by a measured black-cavendish touch in a vanilla direction. The Virginia-cavendish leaf gives the blend's sweetest, honey-like portion, leaving an herbal tone in the background. Nicotine is low, and it's structured for all-day smoking. Aimed at those seeking a sweet, non-heavy aromatic. It was discontinued along with the rest of the Private Stock line.
sutliff-tobacco-company-basin-street-blu.o: Leaves a scent of sweet caramel and honey.

blatter-blatter-sherlock.z: No reliable source documenting the composition of Sherlock, one of Blatter & Blatter's house blends, could be found.

watch-city-cigar-flake-556.z: This is one of the house blends of the Watch City Cigar shop; it does not appear in the current catalog, and no source could be found documenting its composition.

my-smoking-shop-peaches-and-cream.z: A peach-and-cream themed aromatic house blend sold under its own name by the tobacconist My Smoking Shop; no independent source explaining its composition and character could be found.
my-smoking-shop-peaches-and-cream.o: As the name suggests, it is understood to leave a sweet aroma in the direction of peach and cream.

elephant-castle-cromwell.z: No sufficient independent sourcing could be reached to document the composition and character of Cromwell, a pipe tobacco from Elephant & Castle.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-bear-blend.z: Bear Blend is an aromatic blend created at the Boswell shop with customer input, cased with cherry and caramel. The manufacturer describes the blend as full-bodied; its base is built from the premium cavendish-forward leaf the shop uses itself. The casing level is high; cherry and caramel are felt together throughout the smoke, yet the blend does not carry a sharp or burning character, and no tongue bite is reported. Suitable for smokers seeking an intensely flavored yet not harsh blend.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-bear-blend.o: Leaves a sweet aroma mixing cherry and burnt-sugar smells.

d-r-tobacco-blenders-bench-bulgarian-ori.z: Bulgarian Oriental is the Bulgarian-origin Oriental tobacco Daughters & Ryan sells as a single variety in the Blenders Bench line. Oriental tobaccos are small-leaved, sun-cured types carrying heavy aromatic oils. It carries a flavor line similar to the brand's Ramback Balkan blend, but since no flue-cured leaf is added, the Oriental character comes through more nakedly. Alongside woody, rooty, and earthy notes there's a subtle sweetness and faint floral tones. Nicotine is low, flavor intensity high; aimed at blenders building English and Balkan-style mixtures.
d-r-tobacco-blenders-bench-bulgarian-ori.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay, spice, and light incense.

richs-multnomah-falls.z: Multnomah Falls is a multi-component blend from Rich's Cigar Store, named after the Oregon waterfall of the same name. Its base is Virginia and Turkish-Oriental leaf, with Burley, Cavendish, and Perique added to build body and a spice layer. Oriental's tart-spicy taste and Perique's plum-like sharpness sit over the Virginia sweetness, while Burley grounds the blend. It suits smokers looking for an unflavored but complex smoke, and those who enjoy balanced blends with no single leaf dominating. It is sold in bulk at the Portland stores.
richs-multnomah-falls.o: Leaves an earthy trace where dry hay, spice, and light plum notes mix.

hu-tobacco-louisiana-broken.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the Louisiana Broken blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

levin-pipes-international-nutcracker-fla.z: Nutcracker Flake is an extra-matured, unflavored Virginia flake McClelland prepared for Levin Pipes International's 1993-1994 holiday season. Per the tin information, the leaf was rested three years before pressing, targeting a deep, fermented Virginia taste. Aimed at smokers who love pressed, long-cellared Virginias. Being a single-season limited release, it's found only in old tins.
levin-pipes-international-nutcracker-fla.o: Leaves a sweet room note reminiscent of baked dough and dried apricot.

sentimiento-nacional-choctaw.z: According to records, one of Sentimiento Nacional's unflavored blends containing Virginia, Burley, and perique; no sufficient source detailing its character could be found.

vauen-black-pepper.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Vauen blend called Black Pepper has been found.
vauen-black-pepper.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

cornell-diehl-belmont-station.z: Belmont Station is a ribbon-cut aromatic Cornell & Diehl centers on black cavendish and light-colored Virginias, deepened with dark burley and fire-cured Kentucky. Vanilla and dark rum are used as flavoring. Cavendish and Virginia form a sweet base while Kentucky adds a dry, smoky weight to the blend; this sets it apart from purely sweet aromatics. With its strength kept low, it suits daytime smoking and those looking for a middle ground between an aromatic and an American mixture.
cornell-diehl-belmont-station.o: A light smokiness accompanies the vanilla and dark-rum aroma.

pipe-and-pint-bear-creek.z: No sources describing the content of Bear Creek, recorded as a house blend of the American tobacconist Pipe and Pint, could be found.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-cherry-smash.z: Cherry Smash is one of J. M. Boswell's earliest blends and has long stood in the catalog as the brand's cherry-flavored product. Per the manufacturer's description, an intense cherry mixture is applied over a cavendish-based blend; its class is full aromatic. The body is between medium and full, yet the smoke runs soft and burns without issue to the bottom of the bowl. The cherry aroma, dominant at the start, recedes as the smoke progresses, giving way to a lighter tobacco taste. Suitable for aromatic smokers wanting a pronounced cherry note.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-cherry-smash.o: Leaves an intense ripe cherry aroma.

gallaher-limited-war-horse-bar.z: War Horse is a Gallaher brand widely smoked in Ireland that in time also found buyers in Britain. The version called Bar is the blend's pressed, plug-cut form. The original mix is built on earthy Burley, ripe red Virginia, a notable proportion of smoky fire-cured Kentucky, and a small amount of Perique; a single anise-forward flavouring is applied over it. It is a heavy tobacco in body and nicotine; the plug form gives a slow, cool burn. The Gallaher version has been out of production for a long time. Records indicate the Standard Tobacco Company of Pennsylvania produces a reinterpretation under the same name; this version is described as having a tin aroma reminiscent of tonka bean, dark cherry, liquorice root, and vanilla. It suits experienced smokers accustomed to dark leaf and high nicotine.
gallaher-limited-war-horse-bar.o: Leaves a sweet aroma leaning toward anise and liquorice root, along with dark earth and hay.

tabacos-cisne-branco-finamore-ltda-irlan.z: Irlandez Cavendish, a pipe tobacco from Tabacos Cisne Branco Finamore Ltda.; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

john-middleton-inc-london-dock.z: One of the blends from John Middleton, a company founded in Philadelphia in 1856 that has made pipe tobacco since the 1950s; the entry is left incomplete because not enough sources could be found to document the blend's contents and character.
john-middleton-inc-london-dock.o: No source could be found on the room note.

bufflehead-snow-goose.z: Bufflehead was a brand producing small batches in the United States in the early 2000s, naming its blends after waterfowl; since no independent source describing this blend's content and character could be found, the entry has been left incomplete.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-indian-ou.z: Indian Outlaw, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an aromatic mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

hu-tobacco-aus-dem-krater-nr-2.z: Aus dem Krater Nr. 2 is HU Tobacco's Virginia flake in the same series. Per the maker's description, a lightly spiced sauce has been applied to the leaf; this sauce brings out the Virginia sweetness while being kept measured enough not to mask the tobacco's own character. It's classified as a medium-to-light-strength, sweet-character flake, suited to daytime smoking. It's aimed at those wanting to experience Virginia tobacco close to its plain form; the series is no longer in production today.
hu-tobacco-aus-dem-krater-nr-2.o: Leaves a tobacco aroma carrying honey-and-hay sweetness, arriving with a light cedar-wood note.

samuel-gawith-cabbies-mixture.z: Cabbie's Mixture is an unflavored blend of Virginia and perique leaves. The tobacco is first twisted into rope, then sold cut into thin coins; so ready-sliced coins come out of the tin. Virginia's natural sweetness is balanced by perique's spicy, plum-echoing side. Suited to those seeking a medium-bodied, all-day-smokable Virginia-perique and to those who enjoy working with the coin presentation.
samuel-gawith-cabbies-mixture.o: A plum-and-pepper echo from perique mixes into a bready Virginia scent.

w-o-larsen-limited-edition-2017.z: This is one of W.Ø. Larsen's annual limited editions; no reliable source could be found regarding its composition and character.
w-o-larsen-limited-edition-2017.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-peanut-butter.z: This is a peanut-butter-flavored blend in Wilke Pipe Tobacco's bulk aromatic line; as the maker's product page provides no composition or character description, the details remain unclear.

my-smoking-shop-goldleaf-virginia.z: One of the Virginia blends My Smoking Shop sells in bulk; sufficient sources describing its cut and character could not be found.

seattle-pipe-club-puget-sound.z: Puget Sound is one of the Seattle Pipe Club series' traditional English mixtures. A sweet Virginia base is joined by spicy Orientals and fragrant Latakia; a pinch of Perique is added for a peppery bite. It is ribbon cut. The sweetness of the Virginia, the dry spice of the Orientals, and the smokiness of the Latakia are kept in proportions where none overpowers the others; the Perique adds a plum-and-pepper depth. Nicotine is medium, and the flavor intensity is close to that of the Latakia classics. Suited to smokers accustomed to English mixtures who want a spicier variation.
seattle-pipe-club-puget-sound.o: Smoky wood and dry spice mingle with the peppery sharpness of Perique.

watch-city-cigar-java-java.z: This is one of the house blends of the Watch City Cigar shop; it does not appear in the current catalog, and no source could be found documenting its composition.

ferndown-red-black.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for the Ferndown brand's Red & Black pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

cornell-diehl-conan-doyle.z: One of Cornell & Diehl's older burley-based blends; it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog, and not enough sourcing could be found to document its character.

pfeifendepot-mischung-no-95.z: No sources documenting the content and character of Mischung No. 95, listed among Pfeifendepot's numbered house blends, could be found.

drucquer-sons-blairgowrie.z: Blairgowrie is Drucquer & Sons' Scottish-style blend. Aged Virginia leaves, select orientals, Cyprus latakia and perique are brought together; after the mixture is pressed and rested, it's sliced and tinned rubbed out. The name comes from the town of Blairgowrie near Perth in Scotland. The resulting tobacco is full-bodied and richly sweet; latakia's smoky core is balanced by perique's fruity tartness and Virginia's sweetness. Thanks to the pressing, the flavors have melded, making it suitable for a long, slowly smoked bowl. Drucquer & Sons is a London tobacconist dating to 1841; it moved to Berkeley, California in 1928, and after the shop closed its blends were reorganized from the original recipes by Gregory Pease and began being produced at Cornell & Diehl.
drucquer-sons-blairgowrie.o: Leaves a heavy scent combining dark, smoky wood and dried fruit.

vegassmokes-nevada-64.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the VegasSmokes pipe tobacco called Nevada '64 to record the blend's composition and character.

ole-shenandoah-barrel-no-76.z: Barrel No. 76 is the aromatic blend of the Ole Shenandoah line, made in the US by Scandinavian Tobacco Group Lane Limited. It's built from burley and cavendish leaves; the topping carries warm butter with a touch of vanilla and honey, backed by sweet nutty notes. The smoke is cool and mellow; tendency to bite the tongue stays low throughout the bowl, the smoke comes thick and dense, and the room note is pronounced. The nicotine sensation is measured, so it's described as an aromatic smokable all day. It suits those who love sweet, creamy aromatics and newcomers to the pipe.
ole-shenandoah-barrel-no-76.o: Leaves a scent of melted butter, honey, and vanilla.

hearth-home-chestnut.z: Chestnut is a blend in the Hearth & Home series that combines American Burley tradition with English mixture sensibility. Its composition brings together light-colored Burley leaf, sweet Virginia, full-bodied Kentucky, Oriental leaf, and Latakia. Despite the high number of components, the flavor line is kept measured; no single leaf stands out on its own. The toasted-hazelnut taste from Burley sets the main line, while Latakia and Oriental provide smoke and spice in the background. There is no top note. Suited to smokers wanting a layered but understated blend — a mild American-English bridge for all-day smoking.
hearth-home-chestnut.o: Leaves a roasted-hazelnut and fine wood-smoke aroma.

peter-stokkebye-dark-fired-no-314.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Dark Fired (No. 314) could be found.

castello-gentile.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Gentile under the Castello brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-thin-mint.z: Thin Mint is a heavily cased aromatic taking its name from the mint-chocolate cookie of the same name. Chocolate and mint are pronounced in the pouch aroma. On lighting, cooling menthol mint comes first, with sweet chocolate behind it. The mint and chocolate notes fade toward the middle of the bowl; from that point a sweet, plain smoke continues. Being ribbon cut it packs easily, and nicotine is low. A blend designed for smokers after heavily flavored, sweet, cooling casings; it does not fall within the interest of those seeking unflavored tobacco.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-thin-mint.o: Leaves a scent of cool mint and sweet chocolate.

former-jubilee-pipe-tobacco.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Jubilee, part of the tobacco line released under the name of Danish pipe maker Former, could be found.

my-smoking-shop-irish-cream.z: An aromatic flavored with an Irish cream liqueur sauce, sold in bulk under the Century name in the UK and known as Irish CM following the 2017 naming change; sufficient sources describing its leaf composition could not be found.

peter-stokkebye-cherry-bonbon-no-305.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Cherry Bonbon (No. 305) could be found.

mcclelland-yenidje-highlander.z: Yenidje Highlander is the blend in which McClelland's Grand Orientals series pairs the Yenidje variety with Latakia. Yenidje leaf, grown in Western Thrace north of Xanthi, is joined by both Cyprian and Syrian Latakia, matured red Virginia, and a bit of Maryland to help regulate the burn. Records indicate the blend was built as a nod to the old Balkan Sobranie style; both the company and this source of Yenidje leaf have since disappeared. Yenidje's bright, faintly smoky, only slightly sweet character merges with Latakia's sooty base; the result is a Balkan structure with no harsh edges but high flavor intensity. Suited to those wanting a measured, layered smoke in which the Oriental stands out within a Latakia blend.
mcclelland-yenidje-highlander.o: Leaves a floral layer reminiscent of incense sticks over smoky wood smoke.

de-la-concha-mark-twain.z: Named after the writer Mark Twain, this is referred to as a Virginia-Perique-type blend prepared at the De La Concha shop; no independent source giving its profile could be found.
de-la-concha-mark-twain.o: No reliable record could be found for the room note.

sutliff-tobacco-company-caribbean-nights.z: Caribbean Nights is an aromatic in Sutliff's "B"-coded black series. Golden Virginia leaves are combined with Virginia-based black cavendish; tropical fruit and citrus essences are applied on top. The dominant note is coconut and spiced rum. The cut is ribbon, and due to the topping the leaf comes fairly moist; a short airing before lighting eases the burn. Nicotine is low, and flavor is sweet and full. A blend for those seeking a pronouncedly flavored, sweet smoke.
sutliff-tobacco-company-caribbean-nights.o: Leaves a scent of coconut, spiced rum, and tropical fruit.

d-r-tobacco-blenders-bench-blonde-virgin.z: Blonde Virginia is the light-colored, flue-cured Virginia leaf sold on its own in Daughters & Ryan's Blenders Bench line. Leaves of this type carry a high natural sugar content and are used in blends as the source of sweetness. Its flavor brings forward hay, grass, citrus acidity, and a sugary base; nicotine sits medium-low. A component leaf for smokers building their own mixture, looking for a sweet foundation to set against dominant leaves like Latakia or Perique.
d-r-tobacco-blenders-bench-blonde-virgin.o: Leaves a scent of hay and boiled sugar.

clan-shaw-galway-bay.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of Clan Shaw's Galway Bay blend could be found.

g-l-pease-odyssey.z: Odyssey is one of the fullest Balkan blends in the G. L. Pease line. A generous measure of Cyprus latakia is balanced with rare Oriental leaves; the base contains matured red Virginias and stoved jet-black Virginias, which give the blend natural sweetness. It is ribbon cut. The smoke is bold and intense but not coarse; latakia's spice works reciprocally with Virginia's sweetness, and the Oriental leaves carry the complexity in the background. Because the latakia proportion is high, it burns slowly and needs to be loaded loosely. It is a record aimed at smokers experienced with classic blends who want a dark, full smoke.
g-l-pease-odyssey.o: Fills the room with a heavy smoke and burnt-wood aroma.

davidoff-sweet-mixture-no-2.z: This is the second blend in Davidoff's Sweet Mixture line; no verifiable description of its composition and character could be found.

samuel-gawith-st-james-flake-bulk.z: St James Flake is a tobacco Samuel Gawith prepares in Kendal by pressing Virginia leaves together with Perique. The name comes from the St. James Parish region of Louisiana where Perique is grown; this leaf is fermented under its own pressure in a barrel, adding a plum-like, peppery sharpness to the blend. Virginia's bready, fruity sweetness and Perique's spice meet in the middle in this record; nicotine is a bit above medium. A blend for smokers who seek slow burning and concentrated flavor in pressed tobaccos and want to get to know the Virginia-Perique family. This record belongs to the loose, tinless version sold in bulk.
samuel-gawith-st-james-flake-bulk.o: Leaves a scent evoking dried fruit and grain, with a light peppery point at the end.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-longbotto.z: Longbottom Leaf is one of The Country Squire's blends referencing the Tolkien universe, named after the Shire region famed for its pipe-weed. It is a mild, sweet aromatic with a light cinnamon flavor. On the smoke, cinnamon is noticeable but not heavy; the blend is gentle on the tongue and throat, with no sharp bite. Nicotine is low. It was made for lovers of spiced aromatics wanting a light smoke. The blend was discontinued after supply of one of its components was cut off and no suitable replacement leaf could be found.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-longbotto.o: Leaves a scent of cinnamon pastry.

jacks-tobacco-campfire-dog.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of Campfire Dog, part of Jack's Tobacco's "Dog" line, could be found.
jacks-tobacco-campfire-dog.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-plug-rum.z: This is the rum-cased version of Dark Plug. The base blend is built from dark fire-cured Virginia and Indian-origin fire-cured leaf; records indicate this pair is used in equal proportions and the mixture is cold-pressed for more than a week. The plug is sold as it comes out of the press. The plug is packed sliced and rubbed out, or cube cut; since it's tightly pressed, it burns slowly and ages well in storage. The taste sits atop an earthy, smoky, salty base, with the rum casing adding a sweet edge. Nicotine is above medium; aimed at smokers experienced in handling plug tobacco.
gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-plug-rum.o: A sweet, syrupy rum aroma mixes with the dark wood smoke.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-lamb-with.z: Lamb with Jam is one of The Country Squire tobacconist's house blends; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

criss-cross-original-blend.z: Criss Cross Original Blend is a Virginia-Burley blend produced in the United States and sold in large bags. Its composition consists of Virginia and Burley leaf; it's ribbon cut, and its fluffy, light structure is noted for giving even burning. Unlike boutique tinned products, it sits in the bulk, economy product class. Its profile is described as medium and balanced; Virginia's light sweetness sits alongside Burley's dry texture. The casing isn't at a level to create a pronounced aromatic character. Aimed at smokers wanting a plain, straightforward American blend and using tobacco in large volume.
criss-cross-original-blend.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay and lightly sweet tobacco.

hu-tobacco-green-gold.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Green Gold, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

esoterica-tobacciana-peacehaven.z: Peacehaven is one of the Esoterica blends produced for Butera Pipe Co. by J. F. Germain & Son in Jersey. It is presented as pressed, sliced flake; retailer classifications list it in the virginia family, and the leaf color is close to honey-brown. Pressing concentrates the virginia leaf's sugars, producing a dark, distinctive flavor profile. It suits smokers who enjoy rubbing out the flake to adjust moisture and smoking slowly, familiar with the pressed virginia type. Due to limited production it appears in the market only periodically.
esoterica-tobacciana-peacehaven.o: Leaves a sweetish scent evoking honey and toasted bread crust.

watch-city-cigar-old-dominion-flake.z: Watch City Cigar's blend called Old Dominion Flake is, according to records, one of the house blends of the Waltham, Massachusetts tobacconist shop; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

lane-limited-ll-7.z: LL-7 is a ribbon-cut blend from Lane Limited's bulk aromatic line. Toasted cavendish leaf is supported by burley and Virginia; the applied casing is built around caramel and vanilla. In the smoke it gives a sweet profile toward chocolate and toasted candy; nicotine is low and the smoke is cool. Rather than complex development, it offers a stable sweetness throughout the bowl; aimed at those who love classic American bulk aromatics.
lane-limited-ll-7.o: Leaves a caramel, cocoa and toasted-candy room note.

paul-olsen-no-43.z: One of the Virginia-forward blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

the-smoker-202.z: 202 is recorded as one of the hand-prepared house blends from The Smoker, a tobacconist that operated in Albany from the 1930s until 2011; no independent source describing the blend's composition could be found.

mcclelland-pipesandcigars-lazy-day.z: One of the private-label aromatics McClelland produced for a retailer; no sufficient source describing its contents could be found.

mission-pipe-shop-english-tweed.z: English Tweed is one of the English-style house blends from Mission Pipe Shop in San Jose. According to the shop's description it is a light-bodied English mixture, with some aromatic black cavendish added to shape its taste and aroma. This construction produces a sweeter, softer smoke than classic smoke-forward English mixtures. Suitable for those newly moving into latakia blends and for those wanting English character alongside aromatic sweetness. Since the shop sells more than sixty blends loose by weight, this mixture too is distributed through the tobacconist's own channel.
mission-pipe-shop-english-tweed.o: Leaves a trace where light wood smoke mixes with a sweet cavendish aroma.

blenders-gold-toasted-cavendish.z: Blender's Gold is an affordable pipe tobacco line distributed through chain stores in the US; Toasted Cavendish is this line's Cavendish-heavy aromatic option. No reliable manufacturer statement on the blend's composition and production could be found, so a detailed profile cannot be given.
blenders-gold-toasted-cavendish.o: According to records it leaves a lightly sweet Cavendish room note.

cobblestone-vanilla-custard.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Cobblestone pipe tobacco named Vanilla Custard, so the blend's content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

milan-tobacconists-hillman.z: Hillman is Milan Tobacconists' burley-based, non-aromatic house blend. Traditional burley leaves are combined with ribbon- and flake-cut virginia, toasted black cavendish, and perique. According to the maker's description it carries undertones of roasted almond, hickory wood, and a soft spice. Though the cavendish share gives the mixture a light sweetness, the construction stays on the unflavored side; perique adds a sharpness in the direction of plum and pepper. Suitable for smokers looking for American-style burley mixtures, particularly a woody and nutty construction.
milan-tobacconists-hillman.o: Leaves a dry, lightly sweet aroma in the direction of roasted almond and hickory wood.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-vanilla.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Vanilla blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

james-fox-the-bankers-mixture.z: The Banker's Mixture is James J. Fox's ribbon-cut blend that pairs Virginia, Oriental, and Latakia with cigar leaf. The cigar leaf lends the blend a deep, earthy note; the Latakia here isn't dominant, but is kept at a level that enriches this cigar-like thread. It carries no added flavoring. It packs and lights without trouble, and produces a rich smoke. The flavor stays balanced through the first half of the bowl, with the second half turning somewhat harsher. Nicotine sits at a moderate level. This is a profile built for smokers who want cigar character in a pipe and who are familiar with Latakia blends; because the room note is pronounced, care is needed in enclosed spaces.
james-fox-the-bankers-mixture.o: Leaves a sharp smoke redolent of cigar ash and smokiness that lingers in the room.

mcclelland-tastemaster.z: Tastemaster is a chocolate-flavored aromatic in McClelland's Premium Aromatics line. The maker's description positions it as a mild, creamy smoke that doesn't weigh on the palate. The base rests largely on black Cavendish; the cut is ribbon. Body is light, and nicotine load is low. The flavoring stands out clearly, and the room note leaves more a sweet cocoa trace than a tobacco one. Suited to those new to aromatic blends or wanting a smoke dominated by sweet flavoring; it falls outside the interest of those seeking a straight tobacco character. McClelland stopped production in 2018.
mcclelland-tastemaster.o: Leaves a sweet chocolate aroma reminiscent of cocoa and cream.

cornell-diehl-pegasus.z: Pegasus is a classic American Burley mixture from blender Bob Runowski. Per Cornell & Diehl's listing, three separate Burleys, two Virginias, and a small amount of unflavored black Cavendish are brought together. Here the Cavendish isn't a flavor carrier but a component that rounds out the mixture and adds richness to the body. Burley's nutty, earthy line comes forward, while Virginia adds a measured sweetness. It burns cool and sits in the medium nicotine band. Suited to smokers curious about the character of the era when Burley dominated American pipe tobacco, wanting an unflavored, straightforward smoke.
cornell-diehl-pegasus.o: Leaves a dry, earthy tobacco scent reminiscent of nuts and cocoa.

sutliff-tobacco-company-st-georges-blend.z: St. George's Blend is a blend within Sutliff Tobacco Company's aromatic line; no reliable source on its content and character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-st-georges-blend.o: No reliable record of a room note could be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-velvet.z: Velvet is a burley-forward brand from the same American shelf-tobacco tradition as Sir Walter Raleigh; no sufficient primary source describing the blend's composition and character could be found.

manchester-tobacco-mahogany.z: No verifiable product information from maker or retailer sources could be found for the Mahogany blend attributed to Manchester Tobacco.
manchester-tobacco-mahogany.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

karl-erik-private-blend-no-19.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Karl Erik's Private Blend No.19.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-bayou-blend.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Bayou Blend.

ash-ember-the-snallygaster.z: No adequate independent source could be found for The Snallygaster, a house blend from the Ash & Ember shop.
ash-ember-the-snallygaster.o: No reliable information on the room note could be found.

gladora-tobacco-ydf-50.z: YDF 50 is a high-Latakia-ratio broken flake blend that Gladora Tobacco offers in the Turkish market under the name YD-50. Records indicate it was designed as an updated interpretation of the Yayladağ mixture known to Turkish pipe smokers from the 1950s through the early 2000s; the same product is also known in export markets as Latakia 40 Broken Flake. The combination of a Virginia body, Turkish Orientals, and dominant Latakia pulls the blend toward the Balkan style. On the smoke, incense and wood dominate, the Orientals add a spicy, lightly tart layer, and Virginia supplies sweetness in the background. There is no topping. The broken-flake structure eases packing, and with proper moisture it burns slowly and cool. Suited to smokers accustomed to Latakia-heavy blends and to those tracing a classic Turkish-made mixture.
gladora-tobacco-ydf-50.o: Fills the room with a heavy aroma of smoked wood and campfire.

gawith-hoggarth-co-scotch-flake-aromatic.z: Scotch Flake Aromatic is a flake prepared by pressing and slicing Virginia-forward leaf, flavored with the Kendal tradition's floral sauce. The soapy floral note that shows up in the dry leaf and on the smoke is this style's defining mark. The tobacco base is bready and lightly nutty; the floral topping stands out pronounced over this foundation. Rubbing out the slices and airing them briefly eases the burn. Suited to smokers wanting to get to know Lakeland aromatics.
gawith-hoggarth-co-scotch-flake-aromatic.o: Leaves a pronounced floral aroma reminiscent of soap and lavender.

intertabak-burley-po-47.z: No verifiable source could be found for this Burley tobacco registered under the INTERTABAK name.

brebbia-sonata.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named Sonata under the Brebbia brand could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-blending-latakia.z: Blending Latakia is the pure latakia leaf that the Kendal-based house of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. sells not as a finished blend but as a component for building blends. Latakia is produced by long smoke-curing oriental leaf over resinous wood and brush in closed cells; this process turns the leaf nearly black, lowers its nicotine, and leaves a heavy, smoky, tarry, leather-like flavour. Records indicate the firm offers this leaf only in bulk. It is not intended to be smoked on its own; it is added in small proportions alongside Virginia and oriental leaf to build the backbone of English and Balkan-style blends. It is aimed at smokers who build their own blends and want to decide the ratio themselves. When burned pure, the flavour is very intense while the nicotine stays low, so weight of flavour rather than strength is what stands out.
gawith-hoggarth-co-blending-latakia.o: Leaves an aroma of campfire smoke, tar, and soot.

leonard-dingler-ltd-nineteen-o-four-coff.z: Nineteen O'Four is a pipe tobacco line from South Africa's long-established tobacco manufacturer Leonard Dingler, its name taken from the year 1904. The company dates to the early twentieth century, remained a family business for a long time, and later passed to Swedish Match. The series' base rests on Burley and Kentucky leaf; this structure gives the smoke a nutty, bready and earthy body. The product is sold in 50-gram folding pouches and is largely aimed at the South African market. Nineteen O' Four Coffee is recorded as the line's arm distinguished by its coffee flavoring. The casing is applied at a level that doesn't mask the Burley base; the smoke stays cool and body stays at medium. Of interest to those seeking an aromatic profile but avoiding syrupy weight, and to those curious about counter tobaccos specific to the South African market. Hard to find outside the country.
leonard-dingler-ltd-nineteen-o-four-coff.o: Leaves a dark room note reminiscent of roasted coffee beans.

davis-and-son-tobacconists-black-cherry.z: Black Cherry is among the house blends of Davis & Son Tobacconists, a shop located in Wilmington, North Carolina. The shop keeps a wide list of bulk shop blends and offers them both by weight and in larger packages. The blend is built on a cavendish-forward base with its sharpness toned down through toasted leaf, given a cherry flavoring. The smoke is soft and cool, and nicotine is low. It suits smokers seeking a pronounced cherry taste and a strong room scent, without harshening the tongue.
davis-and-son-tobacconists-black-cherry.o: Leaves a scent of sweet ripe cherry and sugared preserve.

john-b-hayes-tobacconist-admirals-blend.z: One of the American tobacconist John B. Hayes' own counter blends; records indicate it's Virginia-and-Perique-based, but no detailed information could be found.
john-b-hayes-tobacconist-admirals-blend.o: No verifiable information on its room note could be found.

mcclelland-orient-996.z: Orient 996 is one of McClelland's Oriental-forward blends. Records indicate the blend was first produced in a limited run for the Pipe Club of America in 2007, with a second batch released in 2009 under the "Collectors Series" heading as Orient 996 Vintage 2007. It contains bright and red Virginias along with Yenidje, Katerini, and Samsun Orientals; the Latakia is Syrian and used very sparingly. The profile is built on the Oriental leaf's herbal, wine-like, and smoky tones; Virginia sweetness carries those tones, while the diluted Latakia leaves a fine smoke layer in the background. Complex but not overpowering. Aimed at smokers who want the Oriental character front and center, with Latakia serving only as a frame. Discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-orient-996.o: Leaves a fine smoky aroma with incense, dry-hay, and spice tones.

mac-baren-saint-claude.z: Saint-Claude is a pipe tobacco with origins tracing back to France. In the 1920s, when the market's Caporal series began being used for roll-your-own cigarettes, the era's French tobacco monopoly had a blend prepared specifically for the pipe; the name comes from the town of Saint-Claude, considered the world's pipe-making center. On the market since 1934, the blend is produced today by Mac Baren following the brand's takeover from Imperial Tobacco. Its composition holds Kentucky, Paraguayan, and Virginia leaves; the cut is a fine ribbon the French call scaferlati, and the tobacco arrives in the pack in block form, quite dry. In the aroma, Paraguay's characteristic tone stands out, with the honey and vanilla topping pulled back. In the smoke, Kentucky's full, faintly bitter, and strong taste is decisive; the smoke isn't flowing, and it doesn't bite the tongue. Suited to smokers familiar with dark, full-bodied French-style tobaccos who don't shy away from high nicotine.
mac-baren-saint-claude.o: A lightly burnt, floral sweetness mixes into a strong tobacco aroma.

peter-heinrichs-no-153.z: Peter Heinrichs No. 153 is a balanced blend built predominantly from black Cavendish and Kentucky leaf, rounded out with some Virginia. Per the maker's description, part of the tobacco is processed into curly cut, which contributes to an even burn. Black Cavendish gives a dark, sweet base while Kentucky adds a smoky, full body, and Virginia places a light freshness in between. It is presented as a naturally characterful structure; nicotine sits in the medium band while flavor intensity is pronounced. It is a suitable record for smokers who lean toward dark tobaccos but don't want a heavy flavoring.
peter-heinrichs-no-153.o: Leaves an aroma recalling dark sugar and a light smokiness.

watch-city-cigar-off-the-rails.z: This is a house blend from Watch City Cigar for which no sufficient source could be found.
watch-city-cigar-off-the-rails.o: No record could be found regarding the room note.

hearth-home-harvest-moon.z: Harvest Moon is the first cherry-flavored blend in the Hearth & Home Signature series. Cavendish-cut Burley and Virginia leaf are joined by some black Cavendish, topped with a soft, sweet cherry note. The cherry here shows more in the aroma than in the taste; its effect on the palate is more restrained, with Burley's nutty and Virginia's sweet base showing underneath. A light-bodied recipe suited to those new to aromatic mixtures and to anyone who enjoys the cherry scent while avoiding heavy syrupy flavors.
hearth-home-harvest-moon.o: Leaves a sweet cherry aroma with a light caramelized-sugar note.

paul-olsen-no-25.z: One of the Virginia-forward blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

house-of-windsor-revelation.z: Revelation was an American-style mixture in which Perique and a small amount of Latakia were added to a Burley-and-Virginia base. Its cut wasn't uniform: cube-cut pieces, ribbon leaves, and slice fragments were all present together. The top flavoring applied to it was light, and since its recipe was never disclosed, its description remains unclear in sources. The result was a layered profile carrying both Burley's nutty body and the smoke and spice from Latakia and Perique. The blend owes much of its fame to being remembered as the tobacco Albert Einstein smoked. After House of Windsor stopped production, the product left the market; different makers prepared match blends. It's a record of interest to smokers following classic American mixtures and historic blends.
house-of-windsor-revelation.o: A sweetish top note mixes into the light smoke and spice aroma.

brigham-enterprises-inc-canadian-winter.z: Canadian Winter is an aromatic blend in Canadian brand Brigham's Mr. B's line; no sufficient information based on the manufacturer or retailer could be found regarding its composition and casings.
brigham-enterprises-inc-canadian-winter.o: Leaves a sweet, soft aromatic aroma.

4noggins-painter-hills.z: Painter Hills is a bulk blend 4noggins built to evoke the old classic Revelation. It contains Virginia, Burley, Latakia, and Perique, over which a very light topping is applied. Records indicate it therefore sits somewhere between a pure English blend and a light aromatic. The topping is kept far enough in the background not to mask the tobaccos' own flavor; strength and flavor are described as moderate. With the Latakia ratio kept low, it's a middle-ground option for smokers who find heavy English blends too much, yet find completely unflavored blends too plain.
4noggins-painter-hills.o: Leaves a lightly sweet topping scent over woody Latakia smoke.

campbells-smoke-shop-30th-anniversary.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named 30th Anniversary under the Campbell's Smoke Shop brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

borkum-riff-pipepacks-orange-whiskey.z: A blend labeled as orange- and whiskey-flavored within Borkum Riff's PipePacks presentation; no adequate source on its content and character could be found.

robert-mcconnell-highgate.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of Robert McConnell Highgate.

bentley-the-classic-one.z: The Classic One is the unflavored blend in the Bentley line. Its composition is based on Virginia and Oriental leaf; the leaves are matured under press to let the flavors settle together. It's presented in 50- and 100-gram tins. In the smoke, Virginia's natural sugary sweetness stands out, while the Oriental leaves a light seasoning in the background. It's a cool, slow-burning blend with low strength. It suits smokers who don't want any flavoring added, looking for a classic, Virginia-weighted European blend.
bentley-the-classic-one.o: Leaves a dry-hay, faintly tangy leaf room note.

joseph-martin-langue-de-chien.z: A blend from the Joseph Martin house, known for Belgian Semois tobacco; not enough independent sources could be found on its contents and character.

lane-limited-captain-black-cherry.z: Captain Black Cherry is the brand's cherry-cased member. Per the manufacturer's description, it's built from matured wide-cut burley, bright Virginia and toasted black cavendish leaves; a pronounced cherry casing is applied on top. The cut is ribbon, and it's offered in both pouch and tin packaging. Nicotine is low, the smoke is cool and flat; the cherry casing is pronounced enough to override the tobacco character. A blend for newcomers to pipes or those seeking a familiar, single-note sweet aromatic. The Captain Black line has been in production since 1956 and became a product of the Scandinavian Tobacco Group when Lane Limited joined that group in 2011.
lane-limited-captain-black-cherry.o: Leaves a pronounced ripe-cherry and lightly sugary fruit room note.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-luxury.z: A blend listed in the Orlik catalog as Virginia-and-burley-based; not enough independent source material describing its composition and character could be found.

zechbauer-munchen-black-mixture.z: Black Mixture is the English-style blend sold under its own name by Zechbauer, Munich's long-established tobacconist. Known to longtime customers as "English Medium," the product took this name once it moved into a black-labeled tin. The composition is dominated by broadly cut Virginia leaves, with a measured amount of Latakia added. Because the cut includes large pieces, it may need to be rubbed out before packing. The smoke runs cool, and the flavor stays lightly smoky and on the dry side without letting Latakia take over. It suits those who like English blends but avoid a high Latakia ratio, and those seeking a mixture that can be smoked all day.
zechbauer-munchen-black-mixture.o: Leaves a woody, faintly tarry scent of smoke along with a trace of dry hay.

the-smoker-st-james.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the The Smoker pipe tobacco called St. James to record the blend's composition and character.

pipo-boya-degisimi-cilalama-ve-agizlik-y.z: This entry is not a pipe tobacco blend but the title of an article about pipe maintenance (finish restoration, polishing, renewing the mouthpiece); there is no blend information here to fill out a specification.

drucquer-sons-rule-britannia.z: Rule Britannia is an English mixture where light and red Virginia leaves are joined by an emphasis on Turkish-origin oriental tobaccos, with latakia adding a smoky depth. The tobacco is pressed into a block and presented as a crumbly plug; this preparation lets the smoker break off the leaf to whatever fineness desired. On the taste line, the orientals' spicy, sharp notes, Virginia's citrusy sweetness and latakia's earthy smoke sit together. The blend's name refers to the eponymous patriotic song of 1740. As with the rest of the line, this mixture too was reorganized based on old Drucquer recipes and, per records, is produced at Cornell & Diehl through Gregory Pease's work. It suits smokers who love oriental-forward, medium-full English mixtures and are willing to prepare their own plug tobacco.
drucquer-sons-rule-britannia.o: Leaves a pronounced layer of wood smoke alongside a spicy, resinous oriental scent.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-apple-strudel.z: Apple Strudel is an aromatic blend prepared by J. M. Boswell in 2006 at the Boswell workshop in Chambersburg, Pennsylvania. Per the manufacturer's description, a small amount of vanilla is added over a light apple aroma; the product was developed for customers wanting a soft apple blend. The casing, sitting on a soft, cavendish-forward base, leads throughout the smoke; nicotine level is low, the smoke cool. Suitable for smokers accustomed to aromatic blends wanting a pronounced but not sharp apple note. The casing's intensity is at a level some smoking notes find overly sweet.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-apple-strudel.o: Leaves a baked apple and vanilla-dough aroma.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-shepherds.z: No reliable source has been found for The Country Squire Tobacconist pipe blend called Shepherd's Pie.

king-smoking-pipes-and-cigars-king-frog-.z: Not enough independent sources could be reached to fill out the record for King Smoking Pipes and Cigars' blend called King Frog Morton.

4noggins-northstar.z: Northstar is one of 4noggins' Oriental-forward blends. Per the manufacturer's recipe, Turkish and Greek Oriental leaves are combined with high-quality Virginias, the mixture is aged for months, and then generously topped with Cyprus Latakia. No additives are reported. The Oriental leaf's spicy, dry character and Latakia's smoke form the blend's two defining axes, with Virginia underneath supplying sweetness and body. The maker notes the flavor profile stays consistent through the bowl. Nicotine is moderate and flavor medium-to-full. It's aimed at smokers seeking the Balkan style, where Oriental leaf stands out as much as Latakia.
4noggins-northstar.o: Leaves a smoky wood-fire and spicy dry-leaf aroma.

golden-blend-tobacco-co-black-cherry-no-.z: No. 2 in the Golden Blend's series, this is an aromatic previously sold under the name Black Cherry. It is manufactured at the Pöschl facility in Bavaria. Its composition includes hand-selected Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish; black Cavendish gives the blend its dark color and sugary base, Virginia adds a fruity sweetness, and Burley adds a nutty balance. The cut is ribbon. It carries the most pronounced fruit topping in the series: an intense, sweet aroma reminiscent of black cherry is noticeable both from the pouch and on the smoke. Nicotine is low and the smoke is mild; smoked at a measured pace, tongue bite stays limited. A product aimed at smokers seeking a distinctly sweet, fruit-flavored smoke, and at those new to the pipe.
golden-blend-tobacco-co-black-cherry-no-.o: Leaves an aroma of ripe cherry and sugary fruit jam.

theodorus-niemeyer-vier-heeren-baai.z: Vier Heeren Baai is one of Theodorus Niemeyer's pouch tobaccos carrying on the Dutch "baai" tradition. The "baai" in the name is a historical term describing leaf brought to the Netherlands via Chesapeake Bay since the 17th century. The cut is ribbon rather than shag, and the blend carries a natural, nutty taste close to Virginia character. On the palate it gives a woody, lightly nutty structure; the body is medium and can turn sharp when smoked fast, so it calls for a measured draw. Suited to smokers who enjoy unflavored or very lightly cased, plain European-style blends. Records indicate its distribution stayed largely confined to the Netherlands.
theodorus-niemeyer-vier-heeren-baai.o: Leaves a woody, lightly nutty, dry leaf aroma in the room.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-limited-edition-.z: Limited Edition XV2 is a limited-run Virginia-Latakia blend from Hermit Tobacco Works Co.; there is not enough sourcing to describe its composition and character.

garfinkels-marlowe.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of Garfinkel's Marlowe pipe tobacco could be found.

tinder-box-philosopher-blend.z: No reliable source has been found for the Tinder Box pipe blend called Philosopher Blend.

newminster-no-303-creamy-peaches.z: No. 303 Creamy Peaches is an aromatic built on Newminster's classic Danish formula: bright, hot-air-cured virginia leaves combined with soft burley and steam-processed black cavendish. A pronounced peach flavoring is added to this base; the result is a fruity, creamy flavor profile layered over the tobacco's sweetness. The nicotine load is low, the smoke is cool; suitable for those new to aromatic tobaccos and for those looking for a light, fruity smoke during the day. It is produced at Mac Baren's facilities in Denmark and sold in bulk.
newminster-no-303-creamy-peaches.o: Leaves an aroma of ripe peach and cream in the room.

billow-billow-bourbon-signature.z: One of the signature blends of the Billow cigar and pipe lounge in Indiana; no adequate source on its content could be found.
billow-billow-bourbon-signature.o: No verified information on the room note could be found.

d-r-tobacco-two-timer.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of D & R Tobacco's Two Timer blend were found.

cao-black.z: CAO Black is a black-cavendish-forward blend in the brand's aromatic pipe tobacco line. Its base is formed by steam-processed black cavendish and flue-cured virginia; a raspberry-based flavoring is applied on top, leaving vanilla and cocoa notes behind. The cut is ribbon and the tobacco comes moist; a brief airing before lighting eases things for most smokers. The smoke runs low in nicotine and does not turn harsh on the tongue; the dominant flavor comes from the fruity casing, with the leaf's own character staying in the background. Suitable for those new to aromatic blends and smokers seeking a light, sweet smoke during the day. Per records the line is manufactured in the US by Lane Limited under the CAO name.
cao-black.o: Leaves a pastry-like room note where sweet raspberry syrup meets cocoa and vanilla.

sutliff-tobacco-company-nut-n-honey.z: A blend listed in Sutliff's catalog as an aromatic themed around honey and nuts; no independent source describing its content and character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-nut-n-honey.o: Its name suggests it leaves a sweet scent leaning toward honey and roasted nuts.

grand-croupier-jack-pot.z: Jack Pot is the aromatic leg of the Grand Croupier series. The idea behind the series is a small-scale blender gathering leftover tobacco from different aromatic batches; because of this, the blend comes across not as a single topping but as several toppings heard at once. It is predominantly ribbon cut, arriving with vanilla, caramel, and chocolate traces intermingled. Its sweetness is measured; it doesn't reach the intensity of heavy syrupy aromatics. Since nicotine stays light to medium, it suits long sessions and everyday smoking. Not for those wanting a fixed recipe — it's a blend meant for smokers who love aromatic character and are open to details that vary from batch to batch.
grand-croupier-jack-pot.o: Leaves a sweet aroma where vanilla, caramel, and cocoa intertwine.

david-cigarpipe-love-substrate.z: No adequate sources were found documenting the composition or character of the David CigarPipe Love Substrate blend.

esoterica-tobacciana-scarborough.z: Scarborough is an untopped blend in which golden and dark Virginia leaves are lightly pressed and cut, then loosened by rubbing out. Because the pressing is kept gentle, the texture is neither a full flake nor a plain ribbon; an in-between form results. The brand is run in the US under Arango Cigar Co, produced in England by J. F. Germain & Son, and the blend is rested before going on sale. The dark leaves build a bread-like, earthy base, while the golden leaves leave a light sweetness on top. Its body is measured, so it suits any time of day; it is aimed at those who love untopped Virginia blends and are looking for softness rather than sharpness.
esoterica-tobacciana-scarborough.o: Leaves a plain tobacco aroma reminiscent of dry grass and stale bread crust.

castro-brothers-portrait.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Portrait under the Castro Brothers brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

sutliff-tobacco-company-almondine-j3.z: Sutliff's J3-coded bulk aromatic blend; no reliable source describing its composition and character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-almondine-j3.o: Records indicate it leaves an almond-direction scent.

nice-ash-cigars-nougat.z: An aromatic record among Nice Ash Cigars' house blends, flavored with nougat; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.
nice-ash-cigars-nougat.o: No description could be found in the records.

cornell-diehl-pirate-kake.z: Pirate Kake is a plug mixture in which Cornell & Diehl pushes the Latakia proportion to an extraordinary high. Per the maker's listing, Cyprus Latakia makes up seventy-five percent of the blend; the remainder is shared between Turkish Katerini leaf and Burley. Latakia's smoky, leathery, incense-like character sits at the center of the mixture, while Katerini opens the structure with a light floral, grassy layer. Being pressed into plug form, it's sliced and rubbed out for packing; this structure slows the burn and preserves flavor intensity. Nicotine sits in the upper band, flavor intensity at the top level; the room note is pronounced and lingers in an indoor space for a long time. Prepared for experienced smokers wanting Latakia as the main component; it may be heavy for those new to Latakia.
cornell-diehl-pirate-kake.o: A scent of campfire, leather, and incense fills the room, leaving a dark-chocolate-like sweetness behind.

sutliff-tobacco-company-tobacco-galleria.z: Blue Note is one of the members of the aromatic line Sutliff groups under the Tobacco Galleria name. It is a ribbon-cut blend made of black cavendish, burley, and Virginia; nicotine is low and taste intensity is moderate. Its flavoring leans distinctly toward caramel and cocoa.
sutliff-tobacco-company-tobacco-galleria.o: Leaves a sugary, caramel- and cocoa-forward flavoring scent.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-extra-mild-mix.z: A blend registered under the name of Danish Orlik Tobacco Company A/S, noted in records as mild in character; its details remain unclear since no independent source describing its composition and character could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-pork-chops-apple-sauc.z: Part of Ken Byron Ventures' Virginia-Perique line's 2020 batch; records indicate it's prepared by pressing matured Virginia leaf into a cylinder and fermenting it, with a light fruit casing applied on top. No detailed independent source could be found about the batch.

peretti-pride-of-loch-lomond.z: One of the house blends from L. J. Peretti's shop in Boston; it appears under the English blends heading in the maker's listing. No published description of the blend's composition and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.

wesleys-no-25-black-cherry.z: Black Cherry is one of the house blends Johannesburg-based Wesley's tobacconist prepares at its own counter. According to the maker's recipe, the blend's defining element is a maraschino-cherry-like flavoring, supported by the leaf's natural sweetness. It's presented in cube-cut form, which keeps the leaf loose and easy to light.
wesleys-no-25-black-cherry.o: Leaves a sweet scent of maraschino cherry and candied fruit.

watch-city-cigar-rouxgaroux.z: Watch City Cigar's blend called Rouxgaroux is, according to records, one of the house blends of the Waltham, Massachusetts tobacconist shop; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

hearth-home-el-nino.z: El Niño, part of the Marquee series, brings together Virginia, Perique, fire-cured Kentucky, and unflavored toasted black Cavendish leaf. Despite containing no Latakia, Kentucky's smoky character gives the blend a dark frame. The taste opens with a dry-hay sweetness and deepens into dark fruit and spice notes. Being full in both nicotine and body, it is aimed at smokers accustomed to carrying the weight of dark leaf; smoking it on an empty stomach can be demanding.
hearth-home-el-nino.o: Leaves a dark tobacco aroma blending dried fruit, smoke, and spice.

tavern-tobacco-co-boars-head.z: Boar's Head, a pipe tobacco from Tavern Tobacco Co.; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

samuel-gawith-jubilee-2012.z: A Virginia-forward Samuel Gawith blend released in limited quantity in 2012; no sufficient source detailing its composition could be found.

alsbo-vanilla-sungold.z: Alsbo's vanilla blend has over time also been sold under the names Sungold and Morning. It's made by combining bright, mellow Virginia leaf with very light black Cavendish and flavoring it with vanilla. The vanilla note is pronounced; even so, the tobacco's own taste comes through more clearly past the middle of the bowl, and the smoke moves toward a warm sweetness reminiscent of fire-toasted marshmallow. Strength is low. It suits those looking for a classic vanilla aromatic as well as pipe beginners.
alsbo-vanilla-sungold.o: Leaves a sweet room note reminiscent of vanilla ice cream and baked custard tart.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-erinmore-.z: Erinmore Flake is a pressed blend built on virginia and burley whose origin traces to production by Murray & Sons in Northern Ireland. Its recipe is not disclosed by the producer; it is presented in flake form in 50-gram tins. According to records, the brand moved to the Scandinavian Tobacco Group umbrella around 2005 and the production site changed. The blend's distinguishing trait is the fruit-based top layer applied over its virginia-burley base; it is said that in the old Murray production this was recognized as a clear pineapple note, while later production shifted to a more mixed and diffuse fruit character. Nicotine load is medium. Suited to smokers seeking a pressed tobacco that is aromatic without being syrupy; because there is a notable difference between old and new production, attention should be paid to the tin date.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-erinmore-.o: Leaves a sweet, sharp scent leaning toward tropical fruit, especially pineapple.

cornell-diehl-vanilla-cavendish.z: Vanilla Cavendish is one of the basic aromatics Cornell & Diehl sells in bulk. It's based on the maker's own black Cavendish; Burley and Virginia leaf are added, and the mixture is then flavored with a vanilla-based sauce. It's ribbon cut, making it an easy-to-pack, easy-to-light everyday entry. Nicotine load stays on the light side; what stands out is the soft, creamy flavor side where the Cavendish's own dark sweetness meets vanilla. An uncomplicated blend of the kind those new to aromatics, or smokers looking for a plain vanilla profile, tend to reach for. Cornell & Diehl is an American maker founded in 1992, with production continuing in Longs, North Carolina.
cornell-diehl-vanilla-cavendish.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough scent.

cornell-diehl-midnight-drive.z: Midnight Drive is one of Cornell & Diehl's blends presented pressed and coarsely broken into flake. Its composition holds bright Virginia leaf, Perique, a small amount of Cyprus Latakia, and a thin Oriental layer; in the tin it shows a dark brown, coarse-piece appearance. The flavor structure is built by citrusy, grassy, lightly honeyed bright Virginia. Perique gives spicy, grape-like, plummy support, while Latakia leaves a smoky, woody, leathery background, though it isn't used at a level that turns the blend into a Latakia bomb. Suited to smokers looking for a balance between sweetness and smoke, drawn to Virginia-based but smoky blends.
cornell-diehl-midnight-drive.o: Leaves a dark but sweetish, lightly smoky tobacco scent.

davidoff-royalty.z: Royalty is Davidoff's ribbon-cut English mixture. Sweet Virginia leaves and oriental tobaccos build the main body, with latakia added in a measured proportion; the blend carries a very light butter topping. The orientals' spice and Virginia's sweetness form a harmonious base, while latakia adds depth without making the soot dominant. The strength is light to medium and the smoke is easy. It suits those looking for a first approach to English mixtures, though it may feel light for those seeking a high-latakia blend.
davidoff-royalty.o: Leaves a sharp soot and burnt-wood scent that lingers long in the room.

lane-limited-cohiba.z: An aromatic pipe tobacco Lane Limited released under a cigar brand's name; not enough sources could be found for the blend's composition and character.

georges-smoke-shop-closed-breach.z: Referred to as one of the shop-only house blends from George's Smoke Shop in Holland, Michigan; no verifiable sourcing on its composition and character could be found.
georges-smoke-shop-closed-breach.o: No record of the room aroma could be found.

peter-heinrichs-no-39.z: This is one of the pipe tobaccos of the Cologne-based house Peter Heinrichs; the profile is left incomplete, as no reliable sources describing the blend's content and character could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-santas-chocolate-cove.z: Santa's Chocolate Covered Cherry Creme is a casing-forward record Wilke prepares for the holiday season. Earthy, woody, and distinctly nutty Burleys govern the base; red and bright Virginias add tart dark-fruit, bread, and light citrus notes. Sugary black cavendish sits just ahead of these two groups, carrying the casing. In the flavoring layout, deep cherry leads ahead of chocolate and a vanilla-cream garnish. Light in nicotine but intense in flavoring, this blend is intended for smokers who enjoy sweet, dessert-style profiles and want a seasonal bowl.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-santas-chocolate-cove.o: A scent of cherry, chocolate, and vanilla cream stands out clearly in the room.

tabac-benden-bloemfontein-navy-cut.z: Bloemfontein Navy Cut is a classic Virginia flake from the German tobacco house Tabac Benden. Virginias of varying color from the Commonwealth, Europe, and America are pressed under high pressure with no other tobacco type added and matured for an extended period; the result is thin but tightly packed slices that can be folded or rubbed out for packing. The blend's starting point is cited as the old 1947 Capstan Navy Flake tins; an exact copy of that period's recipe was not possible because of coumarin, whose use is no longer permitted. Production takes place at the Mac Baren facilities. The taste leans bright and light-colored Virginia: natural sweetness, notes of bread and yeasty dough, with a dried-fruit-leaning background. The casing is kept very light. It suits smokers looking for a near-unflavored Virginia flake carrying the sweetness that comes from pressing, who are willing to work with the slices.
tabac-benden-bloemfontein-navy-cut.o: A fine vanilla note accompanies a scent of freshly baked bread and dried fruit.

peretti-thanksgiving-day-2022.z: Thanksgiving Day is a seasonal tradition L.J. Peretti has carried on since 1939; it is prepared in limited quantities every year in early November, with the tins numbered. The 2022 edition is one year of this series. Per the maker's description, the blend is built from seven distinct leaves, flavored with dark rum and fruit juices, and pressed into hand-breakable roughly four-ounce blocks. Pressing lets the flavoring work into the leaf and soften over time; the block is broken apart and rubbed out for packing. The taste ranges between rum's dark sweetness and fruit, with a Burley-Virginia mixture carrying the body underneath. It suits smokers wanting to age a seasonal, blocked, flavored blend.
peretti-thanksgiving-day-2022.o: Leaves a dark rum and stewed fruit aroma.

holger-danske-royal-navy-flake.z: Royal Navy Flake is produced by maturing flue-cured Virginia leaves and forming them into flakes through hot pressing. A very light aromatic touch from fruit peel is added to the blend; this flavoring accompanies the Virginia's natural sugar rather than masking it. The slices are rubbed out before filling, the burn is cool, and the taste is described with notes of dry hay, lemongrass, and light plum. The Holger Danske line is produced by Mac Baren following Denmark's pipe tobacco tradition. It suits smokers who enjoy the plain sweetness of straight Virginia blends but are looking for a slightly milder profile than a fully unflavored flake. Because of its flake structure, it requires some familiarity with filling and lighting technique.
holger-danske-royal-navy-flake.o: A light plum tone mixes into the aroma of dry hay and lemongrass.

sobranie-of-london-reserve-blend-scottis.z: The number-three blend called Scottish in Sobranie of London's blue-tinned Reserve Blend line; it has long been out of production, and no source describing its composition could be found.

pipesandcigars-com-old-lodge.z: No independent sources sufficient to complete a full profile of pipesandcigars.com's blend Old Lodge could be found.

lane-limited-125th-anniversary.z: 125th Anniversary is the tobacco Lane Limited prepared for the 125th year of its founding, cited as the firm's first Virginia-perique blend. It's one of the select products through which this brand, known for aromatics, opens into the unflavored line. The blend uses equal weights of red and light-colored Virginia leaves, with Virginia flake mixed in; Louisiana perique is added in a measured amount on top. Perique adds a spicy sharpness to Virginia's taste, which leans toward dried fruit and sweet hay. The cut varies between ribbon and coarse slice; the jar note brings forward sugar, raisins and fresh hay. Fullness runs from light to medium; suited to smokers who love Virginia blends without top casing and don't want a heavy perique dose.
lane-limited-125th-anniversary.o: Leaves a lightly spicy tobacco note reminiscent of dry hay and bread crust.

mcclelland-2016-holiday-spirit.z: 2016 Holiday Spirit is among the later releases in the limited-edition aromatic series McClelland put out each year for the holidays starting in 2008. The recipe was kept consistent through the series: a base of nutty Burley, tangy Virginia, and black Cavendish sweetened with dark rum, walnut, and cocoa; the tobacco is presented as loose ribbon cut. Chocolate and praline stand out in the tin note, the rum's sweetness carries through the smoke, and nicotine stays low.
