Prepared for smokers seeking seasonal blends with a pronounced flavoring and light body. Among the series' final releases; the brand stopped production in 2018.
mcclelland-2016-holiday-spirit.o: Leaves a sweet aroma mixing cocoa, walnut, and rum.

nice-ash-cigars-english-toffee.z: An aromatic record among Nice Ash Cigars' house blends, flavored with something recalling English-style toffee; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.
nice-ash-cigars-english-toffee.o: No description could be found in the records.

hearth-home-lj-heart-burley.z: LJ Heart Burley is a straightforward blend built on unflavored Burley. The tin shows a color range from pale khaki to dark brown; the cut is a mix of coarse cut and cube cut, ready to smoke straight from the tin's moisture level. The flavor axis is nutty and salty; records also note an occasional tangy, heavy note reminiscent of dry cheese. It burns evenly with a heavy smoke volume and a low tendency to bite the tongue. With nicotine staying at a moderate level, it works as an all-day option, though smokers who don't care for Burley's own taste may find it too plain and one-note. It's a style particularly favored for after-meal smoking.
hearth-home-lj-heart-burley.o: Leaves a light cigar-like trace over dry hay and roasted-hazelnut aroma.

john-aylesbury-caminetto-panettone.z: No reliable source documenting the content and character of John Aylesbury's Caminetto Panettone blend could be found.

missouri-meerschaum-missouri-malta.z: No manufacturer- or retailer-level description could be found for Missouri Meerschaum's blend called Missouri Malta.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-sweet-m.z: Mr Christian's Sweet Muffin 2 Attack Of The Scone is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

torben-dansk-no-3-red-virginia-superb.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Torben Dansk blend No.3 Red Virginia Superb has been found.

peterson-luxury-blend.z: Luxury Blend is a ribbon-cut aromatic built from Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish leaf. Virginia brings natural sugar, Burley a nutty side, and black Cavendish a velvety softness. Its flavoring uses vanilla, honey, and citrus notes. The smoke is creamy and cool; nicotine strength stays between light and medium, and flavor intensity is moderate. The ribbon cut makes packing easy and gives an even burn. It suits newcomers to aromatic blends and those wanting a lightly sweet, everyday tobacco.
peterson-luxury-blend.o: Leaves a sweet trace recalling vanilla, honey, and light citrus.

cherokee-original-blend.z: The entry has been left incomplete as no reliable source could be found for Cherokee's Original Blend blend.

mcclelland-gkcpc-english-woods.z: English Woods is a Balkan-style blend in the selection McClelland prepared on behalf of the Greater Kansas City Pipe Club. Its composition holds bright-grade Virginia leaves, small-leaved Basma-type Oriental tobacco, and Cyprian Latakia. The Latakia builds the smoky frame, the Basma adds a dry, spicy sharpness, and the Virginia provides the sweet base. The blend is kept one notch below fully loaded Balkan mixtures in terms of Latakia proportion, making it a smokable range even for those new to smoky tobaccos. Its unflavored structure and ribbon cut make it a consistent-burning mixture suited to any hour of the day. Like the other blends in the GKCPC selection, it circulated in limited numbers to benefit the club, and production ended when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-gkcpc-english-woods.o: Leaves a sharp soot aroma reminiscent of burnt wood and smoked pine branches.

sutliff-tobacco-company-black-cordial-z5.z: Sutliff Z50 Black Cordial is a cherry-centered bulk aromatic combining black and light cavendish leaf in a ribbon cut. Per the maker's description, a touch of vanilla accompanies the cherry sweetness, and this profile shows up in both the taste and the room note. The blend's notable technical trait is its burning behavior: it's described as lighting easily and prone to tongue bite. Nicotine fullness is low. Suited to those who enjoy cherry aromatics, care about the room note, and want a technically forgiving tobacco.
sutliff-tobacco-company-black-cordial-z5.o: A thin vanilla undertone accompanies a sweet cherry-liqueur scent.

samuel-gawith-brown-virginia.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Brown Virginia, according to records a pure Virginia blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

kirsten-pipe-company-pergola-punch.z: One of the aromatic blends offered under its own label by Kirsten Pipe Company; no accessible source could be found about its contents and cut.
kirsten-pipe-company-pergola-punch.o: No verifiable information could be found regarding its scent.

pipesandcigars-com-russ-tastykake.z: No independent source material could be found sufficient to fill out a specification for pipesandcigars.com's blend called Russ' Tastykake.

1776-tobacco-co-klompen-kloggen.z: Klompen Kloggen appears in the aromatic section of the 1776 Tobacco Company catalog, prepared under Sterling Tobacco Co. in Illinois. Per the maker's recipe, the blend is hand-mixed and contains shag-cut Burley, Virginia bright, long-cut Virginia, No. 10 Virginia, Carolina leaf, Connecticut shade-grown leaf, and Turkish Yenidje. Its name is a reference to Dutch tradition; the blend is also kept light in that style, calibrated so as not to bite the tongue. The Connecticut shade leaf and Yenidje in the mix add both mellowness and a light spiciness to the Burley-Virginia body. Since it stays measured in nicotine and taste, it falls into the all-day-smokable class; it suits smokers avoiding heavy Latakia blends who want a light aromatic. The brand takes its name from the takeover of a now-closed Pennsylvania tobacco shop called 1776; per records the blends were sold by mail, in bulk quantities.
1776-tobacco-co-klompen-kloggen.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, tobacco-forward, faintly floral room note.

ashton-artisans-blend.z: Ashton Artisan's Blend is a ribbon-cut English mixture. Latakia forms the blend's backbone; Virginia, Oriental, black Cavendish, Perique, and a small amount of fire-cured Kentucky are added alongside it. On opening the tin, a classic English blend scent is noticed; Latakia isn't dominant on its own, and the Perique announces itself as a distinct layer. The smoke starts mild and smooth; toward the middle of the bowl, a light bitterness and tangy taste brought by the Perique come forward, and the ash stays medium gray. Nicotine sits between light and medium, while flavor intensity is high. It suits smokers wanting to try Latakia and Perique together, accustomed to unflavored English blends. The blend is produced for Ashton by Kohlhase & Kopp; records indicate it was produced by McClelland for the American market in earlier years.
ashton-artisans-blend.o: Leaves the room with Latakia's soot- and tar-dominated, faintly spicy smoke.

robert-mcconnell-glen-piper.z: Glen Piper is a flavored, broken-flake blend built on a black-Cavendish-heavy base with Virginia and a small amount of Perique added. The casing rests on cocoa-chocolate along with fruit and citrus notes, staying at a light-to-medium intensity. The high Cavendish proportion determines the blend's sweetness; nicotine is very low and the flavor stays in a mild band throughout the smoke. While the leaf quality used is evident, the blend is aimed more at smokers who want a sweet, mellow smoke than those seeking the tobacco's own raw flavor. It suits those looking for a light aromatic they can smoke all day.
robert-mcconnell-glen-piper.o: Leaves an aroma carrying cocoa and citrus-fruit sweetness.

borkum-riff-pipepacks-liquorice.z: The PipePacks small-pack presentation of Borkum Riff's licorice-flavored blend; no adequate source on content specific to this presentation could be found.

bbb-english-mixture.z: BBB is a tobacco brand named after the English pipe maker Blumfeld's Best Briars. English Mixture represents the brand's classic English style: Turkish tobacco and Latakia are added over a base of Virginia, Maryland, and Burley leaf. No flavoring is used; the taste comes entirely from the leaf selection and Latakia's smoky character. A smoky, salty, woody profile emerges; underneath, the Virginia base lays down a measured sweetness. Nicotine load is medium, but flavor intensity is high, which can be tiring for smokers unaccustomed to heavy English mixtures. It's generally the kind of blend preferred later in the day for a slow smoke.
bbb-english-mixture.o: Leaves a sharp, smoky room note reminiscent of pine smoke and leather.

schurch-cornola-320.z: Cornola 320, signed by Schürch, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

just-for-him-mystic-nerds.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for Just For Him's Mystic Nerds, so the profile is left incomplete; per catalog records, the blend is classified as "Virginia/Perique."

cornell-diehl-santas-mistake-2004.z: A seasonal Cornell & Diehl release from the year 2004; no adequate source documenting its composition and character was found.
cornell-diehl-santas-mistake-2004.o: No adequate information for a description could be found in records.

mccranies-murdocks-pipe.z: Murdock's is the third blend in Charlotte's McCranie's Pipe Shop's tinned lineup, coming after Red Ribbon and Red Flake. Its body is built on the shop's red Virginia leaf, joined by a small amount of Latakia and Oriental. At this ratio, the blend sits between a straight Virginia and a conventional English mixture. The smoke keeps Virginia's bready sweetness up front; rather than building a dominant sooty layer, the Latakia leaves a fine woody line in the background. Nicotine load runs light to medium. A middle step suited to smokers who don't smoke heavy Latakia but find straight Virginia too flat.
mccranies-murdocks-pipe.o: A fine wood-smoke line mixes into a sweet hay aroma.

tinder-box-mango-tango.z: Mango Tango is a blend in which Tinder Box combines a spicy black aromatic base with golden Virginia. Peach and mango are used as the casing, so the flavor direction sits on the tropical-fruit side. The Virginia leaf lends the blend a dry sweetness and an even burn, while the black Cavendish base carries the casing. Nicotine load is low and the smoke is mellow. Suited to smokers after a pronounced fruit aroma.
tinder-box-mango-tango.o: Leaves a sweet, sharp fruit aroma reminiscent of ripe mango and peach.

dan-tobacco-bulldog-medium-strength.z: Referred to as a medium-strength aromatic belonging to Dan Tobacco's Bulldog series; no adequate independent source documenting its composition was found.

tavern-tobacco-co-marrakesh-cafe.z: A blend under the Tavern Tobacco Co. name listed as Virginia-based; no accessible source describing its content could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-tavern-.z: A Virginia blend in Ken Byron Ventures' Mr. Christian's line, reportedly offered in plug form and based on the brand's Jupiter Slices blend; no detailed, independent source could be found.

peter-stokkebye-cube-cut-ps41.z: Cube Cut is produced by layering Tennessee-sourced air-cured, roasted Burley with rested red Virginia leaf and putting them through a Cavendish press for about 36 hours. The pressed block is cross-cut into small cubes; this cut makes packing a pipe easy and gives a slow burn. Where most cube-cut products rely on a single leaf type, this blend's distinguishing feature is its use of two leaves together. It is an unflavored American blend; the scent from the pouch carries tea and pepper associations, and on the palate Burley's nutty taste runs alongside Virginia's natural sweetness. It suits those who embrace the deliberate pace cube cut demands and are seeking an unflavored, satisfying but not heavy everyday tobacco.
peter-stokkebye-cube-cut-ps41.o: Leaves a dry hay, tea, and light pepper aroma.

ohm-bold.z: OHM Bold is an unflavored blend within the economical bagged line sold in the American market. According to the manufacturer's description, it combines full-bodied burley selected from the upper leaves of the plant with cured virginia; the cut is coarse, aiming for a steady, slow burn. No flavor casing is applied, so the taste comes entirely from the leaf itself. As its name suggests, the blend sits at the full end of the line: the burley content raises the nicotine, while virginia leaves a limited sweetness in the background. It is aimed at smokers looking for an everyday, filling, inexpensive smoke rather than a nuanced tobacco; its coarse cut suits pipes with wide chambers. It may be too strong for newcomers coming from aromatics.
ohm-bold.o: Leaves a distinctly dry, smoky, earthy aroma of unflavored burning leaf in the room.

e-a-carey-peaches-creme.z: Peaches & Creme is the peach-themed blend in E. A. Carey's aromatic line. Per the maker's description, warm-air-cured leaf from Zimbabwe and Malawi fields is combined with black cavendish and soft burley; it is presented in a medium-to-coarse, loose cut. The flavoring is pronounced peach, rounded off with a cream tone. The nicotine load is low and the flavor body is moderate; the coarse cut keeps the burn rate low, suiting long smokes. It's a record aimed at those wanting to smoke fruity aromatics all day, and it remains on the brand's current blend list.
e-a-carey-peaches-creme.o: Leaves a scent of ripe peach and sweet cream.

f-k-merde-de-cheval.z: Merde de Cheval is one of the unusually named blends known from the St. Louis-based F & K brand; not enough sourcing describing its composition and character could be found.
f-k-merde-de-cheval.o: Records do not contain enough information for a description.

john-patton-cathys-clown.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Patton's Cathy's Clown pipe tobacco.

faders-st-johns.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for the Fader's brand's St. Johns pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

john-patton-desert-pirate.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Patton's Desert Pirate pipe tobacco.

mcclelland-eastern-carolina-ribbon.z: A Virginia-forward ribbon-cut blend McClelland offered in bulk, per records; no sufficient source documenting its contents and character could be found.

hearth-home-admiralty.z: Admiralty is a Latakia-forward English mixture within American blender Russ Ouellette's Hearth & Home series. It is a relative of Armada in the same series; it differs from Armada by containing no Perique and by keeping a higher Latakia share. Red Virginia leaf forms a distinct sweetness and body at the base; Oriental tobaccos leave a spicy line beneath the smoke. It gives a heavy volume of smoke and finishes without leaving weight on the palate. It is unflavored, and while the flavor intensity is high, nicotine stays in the moderate range. True to its name's naval reference, it follows a classic English mixture line; suited to smokers wanting a blend that centers Latakia without reducing it to a single note.
hearth-home-admiralty.o: A toasted-bread sweetness can be detected beneath a heavy wood-smoke aroma.

vincenzo-black.z: Vincenzo Black is the black-Cavendish-forward aromatic blend from the Italian Vincenzo brand. A broad-cut black Cavendish is combined with bright Virginia leaf, cased toward coffee and vanilla, which gives the smoke a distinctly sweet, mellow character. Because it stays light on nicotine and burns easily, it suits morning smokes or anyone after a long, relaxed session. It works as an entry point for those new to aromatics, and comes in 50-gram tins.
vincenzo-black.o: Leaves a fresh-brewed coffee and vanilla-cream aroma.

mcclelland-biteless-burley.z: A Burley-forward blend in McClelland's bulk line; records indicate it was offered as a counterpart to the product called Lane BLWB, but no sufficient source detailing its composition could be found.

sillems-black.z: Sillem's Black is an unusual aromatic blend built by adding Latakia to a black-cavendish-forward body. The cavendish density gives a dark sweetness and a heavy smoke, while Latakia opens a smoky, salty layer rarely seen in aromatics. The flavor line reads as a cocoa-toned richness combined with a naturally fruity cherry-like trace; this combination is most often described as resembling Black Forest cake. The blend stands out for burning very slowly and coolly; the cavendish share's moist structure lowers the burn rate, leading to long bowls. It stays within the medium range for strength and body. Suited to smokers who want the sweetness of aromatic blends alongside a genuine tobacco body and a smoky layer; it is not built for those expecting an unflavored English blend.
sillems-black.o: Leaves a scent of dark chocolate, cherry, and a fine wood smoke.

missouri-meerschaum-independence-day-202.z: No verifiable manufacturer description could be found for Missouri Meerschaum's 2022 limited release called Independence Day.

tavern-tobacco-co-coventry-arms.z: A blend under the Tavern Tobacco Co. name listed as an aromatic; no accessible source describing its content could be found.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-50th-anni.z: 50th Anniversary is a limited, boxed Virginia-perique blend prepared by The Country Squire tobacconist in Jackson, Mississippi to mark its fiftieth year. Well-aged, high-quality Virginia leaves are combined with peppery St. James perique, and the mixture is pressed and sliced into cake form. On the smoke, tangy citrus, dried dark fruit, bread, and hay notes from the mature Virginia lead the way; the perique adds a tingling spice along with plum and raisin sweetness. Body and nicotine sit at a full level, so it suits smokers already used to hearty Virginia blends. As an anniversary release, it is not in continuous production.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-50th-anni.o: Leaves a scent of tangy citrus, dried fruit, and bread crust.

the-pipe-shop-white-sands.z: White Sands is listed among the aromatic blends The Pipe Shop in Edinburgh sells by weight from the jar; no source documenting its contents, cut, or casing could be found, so no further detail is given.
the-pipe-shop-white-sands.o: No room note has been described in available records.

american-tobacco-co-bourbon-blend.z: No source documenting the content and character of the Bourbon Blend, registered under the American Tobacco Company name, could be found.

peterson-summertime-2017.z: This is the 2017 edition of Peterson's annual limited-production Summertime series; no sufficient primary sources documenting this year's blend composition could be found.

cornell-diehl-caps-blend.z: Cap's Blend is a ribbon-cut composition of black cavendish and a separately flavored light cavendish; the blend also contains burley and Virginia leaf. The maker describes the blend with a flavor structure resembling one of the world's widely known aromatic pipe tobaccos. Because of its cavendish-heavy composition, nicotine sits on the light side; the taste, on the other hand, comes across full thanks to the flavoring. It suits smokers looking for a heavily flavored, soft, familiar cavendish blend, as well as those new to the pipe. As with high-moisture cavendish blends generally, airing it out for a while before packing eases the burn.
cornell-diehl-caps-blend.o: Leaves a sweet, syrupy cavendish aroma.

century-golden-honey.z: A blend in the Century line known for a honey aroma; no sufficient independent source could be found.

tabacos-cisne-branco-finamore-ltda-choco.z: Chocolate Alpino, a pipe tobacco from Tabacos Cisne Branco Finamore Ltda.; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

straus-tobacco-private-stock-aromatic.z: Private Stock Aromatic is one of the counter blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; records indicate the shop was founded in 1880 and that most of its house blends were named after Cincinnati neighborhoods and landmark buildings. Since no independent source on the blend's composition and character could be found, this record is kept at listing level only.

cornell-diehl-atlas-balkan.z: Cornell & Diehl Atlas Balkan, referred to as one of the brand's oldest recipes, is an unflavored, Latakia-heavy English mixture. Alongside a generous amount of Latakia, burley is used to thicken the body and perique to provide sweetness and spice. The cut is ribbon. Smokiness is dominant throughout; burley leaves a full, dry texture in the mouth, while perique breaks up that line with plum and pepper notes. Sitting on the hearty end for nicotine and flavor, it suits experienced smokers accustomed to Latakia blends who want a hearty, unflavored smoke.
cornell-diehl-atlas-balkan.o: Leaves a heavy campfire and smoky-wood aroma in the room, with a peppery trace on top.

e-a-carey-highland-fling.z: An aromatic blend referred to under the E. A. Carey name; no source could be found documenting its composition and character.

ken-byron-ventures-mind-the-gap-2021.z: Mind The Gap 2021 is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

edwards-black-watch.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Black Watch, a pipe tobacco from Edward's. Edward's is a tobacconist business based in Tampa, Florida.

mcclelland-frog-mortons-cellar.z: Frog Morton's Cellar is a blend matured by adding oak cubes cut from whiskey-barrel staves to the series' Latakia-and-Virginia body; placing these cubes inside the tin is the product's distinguishing feature. It's ribbon cut, and the whiskey note stands out as soon as it's lit, sitting noticeably atop the smoky core. Per the description in Turkish-language sources, this alcohol note also carries a faintly bitter edge at the start of the smoke. A boundary-pushing middle form aimed at smokers seeking both Latakia and a pronounced alcohol note; for those expecting an unflavored English blend, the flavor line is markedly different. Production ended when McClelland closed in 2018, and the blend now survives only in old tins.
mcclelland-frog-mortons-cellar.o: A sharp, alcoholic whiskey-barrel aroma sits atop the sooty wood.

sutliff-tobacco-company-2050-oriental-ma.z: 2050 Oriental Match is one of the bulk blends Sutliff built to correspond to another maker's oriental-forward classic. In the ribbon-cut mixture, oriental leaves and black cavendish accompany a Virginia body; no top flavoring is applied. Nicotine strength is light, flavor intensity is medium. Suited to smokers seeking a spicy, dry oriental character while avoiding a heavy latakia load.
sutliff-tobacco-company-2050-oriental-ma.o: A light woody trace accompanies dry spice and a tangy oriental leaf scent.

cornell-diehl-perique.z: This is the single-leaf Perique entry Cornell & Diehl offers; since the brand's current catalogue carries a product not under this name but under the name Long-Cut Perique, no adequate source on this entry's cut and presentation was found.
cornell-diehl-perique.o: No adequate information for a description could be found in records.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-english-origin.z: English Original is a blend produced under the Orlik label, classified in records as straight Virginia and known by its blue pack; no independent source describing its composition could be found.

motzek-twist-sea.z: Twist & Sea belongs to the limited-production rested twist line of the Motzek workshop. It is made entirely from Virginia leaf: the leaf is first matured for three to five years, then held for about six months in a plant-and-spice liquid based on an old recipe, hand-twisted into small batches, and rested for another six months. Rose petals, which can be loaded along with the tobacco, are placed inside the pack. In the taste, rounded notes reminiscent of straw and dry hay stand out along with a full sweetness and a light lemony quality; after airing for a few weeks, the fine floral layer typical of rested tobaccos emerges. Strength sits in the light-to-medium band, and it burns cool and clean. Suitable for smokers accustomed to cutting twists who are looking for a matured version of unflavored virginia; production is limited to small batches with each release.
motzek-twist-sea.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of dry hay and lemon peel, with a fine floral trace lingering behind it.

sutliff-tobacco-company-apple-208.z: Apple #208 is an aromatic blend in Sutliff's numbered bulk line, known for the apple flavor its name carries. Its composition is built on rested, soft burley leaves and roasted black cavendish; it's presented in ribbon cut. The caramel and brown-sugar tone from roasting the cavendish pulls the apple topping toward baked apple rather than fresh apple. The burn is gentle and nicotine is low; burley's earthy-nutty base is felt beneath the flavoring. Since Sutliff's bulk line has long been sold by weight at tobacconists, the blend is commonly found among smokers newly exploring aromatics or seeking a light sweet blend for all-day smoking.
sutliff-tobacco-company-apple-208.o: Leaves a scent of baked apple and brown sugar.

hilands-cigars-black-gold.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for this blend, described as aromatic, from the Hiland's Cigars brand.

tabakfabrik-roth-dreimaster.z: Dreimaster is one of the blends Tabakfabrik Roth prepares from entirely Swiss-grown Burley and Virginia leaf. The maker presents the mixture, likened to sea air, as spicy, fresh, and clear; it is flavored with aged brandy and finished with a fine caramel note. A honey and molasses casing gives the blend an open, soft body. The name refers to a three-masted sailing ship. It suits smokers looking for a light-bodied mixture with restrained flavoring that can be smoked throughout the day; it is filled in three cut options — fine, medium, and coarse.
tabakfabrik-roth-dreimaster.o: Leaves a sweet, warm scent leaning toward caramel and brandy.

peter-stokkebye-black-honey.z: No sufficient sources confirming the composition and character of the Peter Stokkebye blend Black Honey could be found.

peter-heinrichs-golden-sliced.z: This is one of the pipe tobaccos of the Cologne-based house Peter Heinrichs; the profile is left incomplete, as no reliable sources describing the blend's content and character could be found.

kanes-of-new-zealand-lamb-cake-slices.z: Lamb Cake Slices is one of the sliced-presentation blends from New Zealand's Kane's brand; not enough sources could be found to describe its contents and character.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-mistura-ext.z: One of the blends under the Wilder brand from Tabacos Wilder Finamore, which has been producing in Juiz de Fora, Brazil since 1949; according to the maker, the entire product family consists of handmade blends built on Virginia and Burley leaf, prepared through natural curing and fermentation. Since no independent source detailing the blend's own composition and character could be found, only brand-level facts are given here.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-mistura-ext.o: Records suggest it leaves a tobacco-like, lightly sweetish scent.

r-j-reynolds-madeira-gold.z: Madeira Gold was the pouch-format member of R.J. Reynolds' Madeira line of flavored pipe tobaccos; production ended when the company divested its pipe and roll-your-own tobacco products in 1985. No source could be found documenting the blend's composition and flavoring.
r-j-reynolds-madeira-gold.o: No information describing the room note could be found in available records.

hearth-home-sunjammer.z: Sunjammer is a traditional Scottish-style mixture in which bright and red Virginia leaves are brought together with Macedonian and other Oriental varieties, smoky Latakia, and a small amount of unflavored toasted black Cavendish. The cut is coarse; the Latakia proportion is kept at a level that won't overwhelm the blend, letting Virginia sweetness stay in front. It's built for smokers looking for medium-bodied, lightly sweet Latakia blends, and is referenced as an alternative to the classics of this class. It's an unflavored mixture; the sweetness comes from Virginia and Cavendish, not from added flavoring.
hearth-home-sunjammer.o: Leaves a measured trace of smoke and wood over the sweet Virginia aroma.

iwan-ries-british-medium.z: British Medium is one of the English-style house blends prepared for Chicago's long-established tobacconist Iwan Ries & Co. In this ribbon-cut tobacco, Cyprus Latakia builds the smoky roof; earthy, nutty Burley fills out the body, herbal, lemony Virginia gives sharpness, and black Cavendish balances the sweetness. In the maker's classification it counts as light-to-medium strength — meaning Latakia is pronounced while the nicotine load stays low. It's a suitable middle ground for smokers new to English blends, or those wanting to smoke Latakia all day without fatigue. Its cool, even burn keeps the sweet-salty campfire taste steady throughout the bowl. The blend is produced in Denmark.
iwan-ries-british-medium.o: A sweet, nutty undertone accompanies the fire-toasted wood smoke.

samuel-gawith-spring-time-flake.z: According to records a Virginia-and-Perique-based Samuel Gawith flake; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

samuel-gawith-virginia-latakia-flake.z: A Samuel Gawith product combining virginia and latakia leaf in pressed flake form, sold in bulk; no sufficient independent source confirming its proportions and character could be found.
samuel-gawith-virginia-latakia-flake.o: Leaves a scent of wood smoke and dry hay.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-burrus-ja.z: Burrus Jaune is the second member of the Swiss-origin Burrus pipe-tobacco trio. Like Bleu, it rests entirely on burley leaf and carries no flavor casing. The brand is now under Scandinavian Tobacco Group; the product is made in Denmark for the Swiss market and generally comes in pouch packaging. Its profile is very close to Bleu's: dry, toasted-nut and hay tones, an unflavored sweetness, and medium fullness. According to records the difference between the two products is quite subtle, with Jaune described as slightly rounder. Suited to those accustomed to unflavored burley smoking and to those wanting to compare the Burrus series.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-burrus-ja.o: Leaves a scent of toasted hazelnut and dry hay.

missouri-meerschaum-lord-morgan.z: No reliable source describing the composition of the Lord Morgan blend released under the Missouri Meerschaum name could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-bright-cr-flake-cocon.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Bright CR Flake-Coconut blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

peter-weinig-nr-33.z: This is one of the numbered house blends of the German tobacconist house Peter Weinig; records describe it as a mixture in the English style. The profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient sources describing its composition and character could be found.
peter-weinig-nr-33.o: Leaves a smoky aroma typical of English-style blends.

brigham-modern-english.z: Modern English is a hybrid blend in Brigham's Mr. B's line. It is built by adding a notable proportion of Syrian Latakia to two of the brand's aromatic recipes; the result is a profile sitting between aromatic and English mixture. Latakia forms a woody, smoky layer, while dark chocolate and malt-vanilla notes from the casings lay a sweet cover over this smoke. The body is medium. A blend conceived for those wanting to move from aromatics to English mixtures, or seeking a composition outside the familiar Latakia lane. It is offered in 50- and 400-gram packages.
brigham-modern-english.o: Leaves an aroma where bitter chocolate and vanilla sweetness mix with wood smoke.

outman-cigars-spiced-rum.z: Its name indicates an aromatic blend with a spiced rum topping; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found.
outman-cigars-spiced-rum.o: No description could be found in the records.

dunhill-ready-rubbed-re-release.z: Ready Rubbed is a lightly aromatic mixture in the Dunhill line and one of the blends reintroduced in 2015. Its base contains aged warm-air-cured leaves from the US, Brazil and Africa, joined by sun-cured and fire-cured tobaccos and orientals from Indonesia and India. The leaf is sweetened with a light fruit essence, then heated and pressed by the classic cavendish method and sliced into a rubbed-out cut. The result is a moderately sweet, mild blend; its nicotine load is light and its topping level low. It suits smokers wanting a middle ground between aromatic and unadulterated that can be smoked at length through the day. Production under the Dunhill name has ended.
dunhill-ready-rubbed-re-release.o: Leaves a lightly fruity, sweetish and soft scent.

up-down-edgars-spicy-black-cavendish.z: Recorded as a black-Cavendish-based aromatic house blend from the Up Down Tobacco shop in Chicago; no independent source describing the leaves used and the flavoring has been found.

newminster-no-9-creamy-vanilla.z: Newminster No. 9 Creamy Vanilla is an entirely Cavendish-based aromatic, prepared by converting African-origin flue-cured leaves into Cavendish. The blend is given a vanilla-bean flavoring and is sold in bulk as a loose cut. It is light in body and sweet, creamy in taste; nicotine is low. Suitable for smokers looking for a soft, vanilla-focused aromatic, and for those choosing their first pipe tobaccos.
newminster-no-9-creamy-vanilla.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and sugared-cream aroma in the room.

motzek-curly-strang.z: Strang is the rope-wound tobacco from the Motzek workshop in Kiel; production continues today under Thomas Darasz using the name TAK (Tabak aus Kiel). Virginia, burley, and perique leaves are wound into a thick rod resembling a cigar; the smoker slices this rod with a sharp knife into thin rings (curly) before loading. Records indicate the product was off the market for a period due to the unavailability of one of the tobaccos used, and was later brought back into production. Dark virginias give sweetness in the direction of honey, brown sugar, and molasses; burley builds a dry, nutty base, while perique adds sharpness at the finish. Strength and flavor sit a bit above medium. Aimed at smokers accustomed to cutting rope tobacco and smoking at the pace the slice dictates.
motzek-curly-strang.o: Leaves a warm tobacco aroma evoking honey, brown sugar, and nuts.

bc-royal.z: No manufacturer or retailer source could be found for this aromatic blend known under the BC name.

newminster-no-9r-rich-vanilla.z: Newminster No. 9R Rich Vanilla is prepared by converting high-quality Brazilian flue-cured leaves into a loose, soft Cavendish. It is a deeper-flavored version of the line's No. 9 vanilla blend; black Cavendish gives the blend an intense sweetness, while Virginia-derived Cavendish provides balance in the direction of honey and hay. The smoke is light-bodied and distinctly sweet, with the vanilla note sitting at the blend's center. Nicotine is low. Suitable for those who enjoy intensely flavored tobaccos; it is a blend far removed from what unflavored-tobacco seekers want.
newminster-no-9r-rich-vanilla.o: Leaves an intense, sweet vanilla aroma in the room.

players-whiskey-brown-flake.z: This is a flake blend carried under the Player's name, said to be flavored with a whisky casing; no independent source could be found to verify the details.

sutliff-tobacco-company-zurich-delight-2.z: SPS-2013 Zurich Delight is a chocolate-themed blend in Sutliff's bulk aromatic line. Its base is built from a Virginia and Burley mix, ribbon cut. A semisweet dark chocolate flavoring is applied as the top note; the name references Swiss chocolate, though the tobacco itself is produced in America. The chocolate note can be followed not just in the aroma but on the smoke as well; Burley's nutty base works in harmony with the cocoa, while the Virginia adds a light sugar note. Nicotine and taste intensity are moderate, so it serves as a stepping stone for those wanting to move from sweet aromatics toward more tobacco-forward blends. Being a cased tobacco, drying it before packing gives a cool, balanced smoke.
sutliff-tobacco-company-zurich-delight-2.o: Leaves a scent of semisweet dark chocolate and cocoa.

sutliff-tobacco-company-caramello-j2.z: Caramello J2 is a blend in Sutliff's bulk aromatic line prepared by resting burley and Virginia leaves in a caramel sauce. The cut is coarse and irregular; the leaf is medium brown and moist. The topping is noticeable, but unlike vanilla aromatics dominated by black cavendish, the tobacco base stands out. Burley's earthy, nutty character makes itself known beneath the caramel, while Virginia balances the sweetness. Tongue bite is low and nicotine strength is moderate. A record that could suit smokers who want an aromatic while still tasting the leaf beneath it.
sutliff-tobacco-company-caramello-j2.o: Leaves a scent of boiled sugar and buttery caramel.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-432.z: Referred to as a blend belonging to Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Virginia-forward Kendal series; no reliable sourcing on its composition and character could be found.

cornell-diehl-orions-arrow.z: Orion's Arrow is a Virginia-Perique mixture named after the Orion constellation used for navigation. Per Cornell & Diehl's listing, Oriental flake, Perique, red Virginia, and bright Virginia ribbon are combined in near-equal proportions. Pushing Perique to such a high proportion moves the mixture into sharper, spicier territory than classic VaPers. While the Oriental leaf adds a grassy layer, red and bright Virginias share the sweet base. Nicotine and flavor intensity sit in the upper band, while room note stays low. Designed for smokers wanting a heavy dose of Perique's plum-and-pepper character, accustomed to full VaPers.
cornell-diehl-orions-arrow.o: Leaves a spicy tobacco note mingling with a scent of plum and dry hay.

imperial-tobacco-group-plc-voortrekker-n.z: No sufficient independent source could be found about this tobacco, the unflavored version of the Voortrekker line released under a South-Africa-evoking name.

ken-byron-ventures-embrys-dream-eireann.z: A limited aromatic released under Ken Byron Ventures' Embry's line; no accessible maker's profile could be found to document its contents.

motzek-motzek-32.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called Motzek #32 could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-savage-fleet.z: A blend in Ken Byron Ventures' aromatic line, released in limited batches; not enough sources could be found to document its casing or composition.

davids-blend-executive-blend.z: This is a shop blend noted as aromatic; not enough sourcing could be reached to verify its composition and character.

ken-byron-ventures-byronic-fragments.z: Byronic Fragments is a product made from the broken pieces of Ken Byron Ventures' thick-cut Byronic Slices that break apart during shipping. Its content is stoved red Virginia leaf alone; the broken slices are packaged and sold under a separate name. Being an unflavored Virginia, the taste comes from the leaf's own sugar and tang.
ken-byron-ventures-byronic-fragments.o: Leaves a lightly tangy tobacco aroma reminiscent of dry bread crust and dark fruit.

park-lane-tobacconist-salmon-river.z: One of the aromatic blends Park-Lane Tobacconist of Clifton Park, New York prepares at its own counter; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

mac-baren-black-exotic.z: No content and character information could be found in the manufacturer's catalog or in two reliable independent sources for Mac Baren's blend called Black Exotic.

mccranies-owners-choice.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found on Owner's Choice, one of McCranie's Pipe Shop's house blends.
mccranies-owners-choice.o: No reliable description of the aroma could be found.

levin-pipes-international-red-woods.z: Red Woods is a now-discontinued blend McClelland prepared for Barry Levin, forward in matured red Virginia; no sufficient source could be found for its exact composition and cut.
levin-pipes-international-red-woods.o: Leaves a sweetish room note reminiscent of dry hay and cooked fruit.

briarworks-international-cherry-cobbler.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named Cherry Cobbler under the BriarWorks International brand could be found.

st-basils-tobacco-rasputin.z: A burley-based blend from a small-scale American brand, per records; no verifiable source describing its composition could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-scotch-mixture.z: Scotch Mixture is one of the Kendal-based Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. house's mixtures using Latakia in measured amounts. According to producer information, the blend's body is built from Brazilian, Zimbabwean, and Malawian Virginia leaf, joined by Malawi Burley, sun-cured leaf, cooling dark fire-cured black Cavendish, and roughly an eighth-part Latakia. The result is that Latakia doesn't emerge as a dominant top note but as a smoke-and-spice layer sitting in the background. A medium-bodied, cool-burning ribbon-cut blend holding Virginia sweetness and light spice together. Since it carries a faint trace of Kendal tradition, it departs slightly from a fully classic English mixture. Suited to smokers wanting Latakia not at a high dose but at a level smokeable any time of day; suited to those new to English mixtures or seeking a balanced smoky blend fit for all-day smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-scotch-mixture.o: Leaves an aroma of light smoke, dry wood, and sweetish hay.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-georges-d.z: George's Dragon, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as a Virginia-forward mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-172.z: Wilke No. 172 is a Virginia-Burley combination in the brand's unflavored blend listing. According to the records, lightly sweet, nutty, earthy Burley and lemony, grassy Virginia leaf sit at roughly equal weight in the blend; reviews note that Maryland leaf also contributes. Since no casing is used, the taste comes directly from the leaf itself. This structure gives the blend a balanced character suited to all-day smoking: Burley provides heft and body, while Virginia supplies sweetness and brightness. With no Latakia or Oriental present, it carries no smoky side. It suits smokers seeking American-style unflavored Burley blends who value a slow burn that doesn't harshen on the tongue.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-172.o: Leaves a scent of roasted nut and dry grass.

with-pipe-and-book-fishermans-pal.z: Fisherman's Pal is one of the house blends from the With Pipe and Book shop in Lake Placid; no verifiable source could be found regarding its composition and character.
with-pipe-and-book-fishermans-pal.o: No confirmed description of the room note could be found.

fincks-cigar-company-fincks-english.z: This is an English-style shop blend sold under its own name by Finck Cigar Company, active in San Antonio, Texas since 1893; no reliable source describing its composition and character could be found.

cascadia-pipe-co-trail-head.z: Trail Head is the member of Cascadia Pipe Co.'s nature-themed series built on a Virginia-Burley balance. It is offered in pressed-cake form; it is sliced and rubbed out for filling, and this structure lets the tobacco stay moist for a long time. Virginia's sweet-tart base intertwines with Burley's dry, nutty tone, evoking English VaBur flakes, particularly University Flake. The flavor casing is kept to a minimum. Nicotine is medium, burning cool and even. Aimed at smokers seeking the classic Virginia-Burley balance in cake form.
cascadia-pipe-co-trail-head.o: Leaves a dry hay and walnut-kernel aroma.

buchanans-tobacco-shop-stirlingshire.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Stirlingshire under the Buchanan's Tobacco Shop brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-gramercy-park.z: No sufficient source could be found documenting the composition and character of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Gramercy Park.

der-pfeifenladen-50.z: One of the numbered house blends of a German pipe shop, recorded as a Virginia-Perique type; no independent source stating its ratios could be found.
der-pfeifenladen-50.o: No reliable record could be found for the room note.

house-of-calabash-irishmans-5-oclock.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for House of Calabash's Irishman's 5 O'Clock blend, so its content and character could not be recorded.

anthony-cranswick-grey-castle.z: Anthony Cranswick Grey Castle is an old-style English blend with Oriental tobaccos in the foreground. It contains bright and fire-cured Virginias, Oriental leaf, and Syrian Latakia. It carries no added flavoring; records indicate it was sold in 100-gram tins and is no longer on the market today. The blend is known not for a high Latakia ratio, but for the leather- and soot-evoking character of Syrian Latakia specifically. Moisture is low and the smoke is dry; records note a tendency toward tongue bite if not smoked slowly. It suits smokers accustomed to Oriental-forward, unflavored, full-bodied English blends.
anthony-cranswick-grey-castle.o: Leaves a sharp, smoky room note reminiscent of leather and woodsmoke.

park-lane-tobacconist-loch-ness.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Loch Ness, one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

low-country-pipe-cigar-vanilla.z: Low Country Pipe & Cigar's Vanilla blend is formed by combining black cavendish and white burley leaf with a vanilla casing. The main color of this ribbon-cut tobacco is light brown burley; black cavendish scattered throughout provides both sweetness and a dark appearance. The brand prepares its blends by hand in South Carolina and offers this tobacco in bulk. It gives a drier smoke than most vanilla aromatics, and its sweetness is kept limited; the burley leaf's nutty, earthy character can be heard beneath the casing. It lights easily and burns calmly. An option for smokers seeking a fine vanilla note over natural tobacco taste rather than heavy, syrupy aromatics.
low-country-pipe-cigar-vanilla.o: Leaves a measured vanilla note beneath a dry, nutty tobacco.

g-l-pease-key-largo.z: Key Largo is a blend built by adding maduro cigar wrapper leaf over red Virginias, small-leaved Oriental tobaccos, and a small amount of Cyprus latakia. It is presented in broken-flake form; the cigar leaf gives both an earthy spice and a heavy, creamy smoke. Throughout the smoke, cocoa, dark roasted coffee, and leather notes open layer by layer, with a long finish. Given its ingredients, it leaves a milder room note than expected. It is a record aimed at smokers curious how cigar leaf behaves in a pipe, who want a full but not flavour-added blend.
g-l-pease-key-largo.o: Leaves an earthy cigar aroma reminiscent of cocoa and roasted coffee.

e-a-carey-black-cherry-supreme.z: This is one of E. A. Carey's cherry-line aromatics; in the maker's catalog it's listed under the name Black Cherry, among the brand's newer blends. Per the description, a small amount of cherry-flavored leaf is added over soft, light aromatic tobaccos, meaning the cherry note doesn't overwhelm the whole blend. This structure lightens the syrupy side of classic cherry tobaccos; the sweetness stays pronounced while the tobacco's own taste remains in the background. It's noted as light in nicotine. It suits smokers wanting cherry aroma but avoiding heavy flavoring.
e-a-carey-black-cherry-supreme.o: Leaves a scent of sweet cherry and dark cavendish.

smokers-paradise-clearwater-50-50.z: One of the counter blends from Smoker's Paradise, a tobacconist operating in Clearwater, Florida since 1976; no independent source documenting its composition could be found.

drucquer-sons-the-merry-monk.z: The Merry Monk is a mixture presenting the English blending approach in flake form. Red and light yellow Virginia leaves are pressed together with Cyprus latakia, St. James perique, white burley and black cavendish, then sliced. Because of its flake structure it burns slowly; how much the slices are rubbed out directly affects the smoking pace and intensity. Virginia's tart-sweet base, perique's plum- and fig-evoking spice, and latakia's soot meld together; burley and cavendish thicken the smoke. Nicotine is medium, and the flavor is above-medium intense. It's prepared for smokers accustomed to packing pressed tobacco who want a smoky and spicy structure together.
drucquer-sons-the-merry-monk.o: Leaves a dark, lightly spicy fruit note accompanying a smoky latakia scent.

niall-of-nine-blood-of-many-2026.z: One of the blends prepared in very small batches under the Niall of Nine signature; not enough independent source material documenting its composition and character could be found.

milan-tobacconists-diplomat.z: Diplomat is one of Milan Tobacconists' non-aromatic house blends. It is built by combining red virginia leaves with coarse-cut and cube-cut burley, with perique added on top. According to the maker's description it gives a medium-bodied, filling smoke with undertones of nuts and spice. Since it carries no casing, the tobacco's own taste comes forward; the perique share adds a sharpness in the direction of plum and pepper to the virginia sweetness. An entry geared toward smokers looking for American-type unflavored mixtures, particularly burley-based everyday smokes.
milan-tobacconists-diplomat.o: Leaves a trace close to the tobacco's own scent, in the direction of nuts and dry spice.

masterpiece-masterpiece-pipe-tobacco.z: A pipe tobacco record known under the name Masterpiece; since no source documenting its maker, origin, and composition could be found, the profile is left incomplete.
masterpiece-masterpiece-pipe-tobacco.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

mac-baren-three-nuns-yellow.z: Three Nuns Yellow is the branch of the Three Nuns name built solely from Virginia leaves. Virginias selected from different regions of the world are spun into rope using the curly-cut method and sliced; hand-selected Virginia leaves are again used for the outer wrap. This preserves the series' classic spiral-patterned coin look. Being an unflavored blend, the taste rests entirely on Virginia's own sugar: it follows a sweet, faintly herbal, citrusy line. Nicotine is on the light side, making it suitable for those newly moving to unflavored Virginia blends and for those seeking a mild, all-day tobacco.
mac-baren-three-nuns-yellow.o: Leaves a sweetish tobacco aroma with a toasted-bread and dry-hay association.

mcclelland-cpcc-new-century.z: New Century is a medium-bodied, Balkan-line mixture McClelland prepared for the Chicagoland Pipe Collectors Club. The blend's backbone is built from air-cured, small-leaved Oriental tobaccos, Basma included among them. These are joined by Virginia's tangy sharpness and a measured proportion of Cyprian Latakia. As a result, the blend offers a Balkan profile in which the Oriental tobaccos lead, rather than a classic English mixture where Latakia dominates: within a spicy, dry, faintly resinous taste frame, the smoke plays a secondary role. Nicotine dose is medium. Aimed at smokers interested in Oriental-forward mixtures who want the smoke as a frame rather than a dominant element; being a club blend, its distribution stayed limited.
mcclelland-cpcc-new-century.o: Leaves a dry spice and tangy herbal trace alongside an aroma of smoke and soot.

torben-dansk-virginia-mysore-ready-rubbe.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Torben Dansk blend Virginia Mysore Ready Rubbed Flake has been found.

torben-dansk-no-4-english-mixture.z: Torben Dansk No.4 English Mixture is a classic Virginia-Oriental-Latakia mixture. Per the maker's description, the Oriental proportion is kept high and rounded out with Latakia; it is unflavored. The mixed cut of leaves in varying widths gives a slow, cool burn. Despite being full and spicy, it is noted as staying mellow to smoke, with Virginia's understated natural sweetness sitting in the background. Suited to smokers who love English blends and want smoke and spice without going overboard.
torben-dansk-no-4-english-mixture.o: Leaves a smoky wood and dry spice aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-crumble-kake-lim.z: The third limited edition in the Crumble Kake series is a barrel-aged navy-style mixture. Matured Virginia leaves take the lead role, carrying citrus acidity, dark fruit, herb, bread, and sugar notes. Mild burley provides strong support with earth, wood, nut, and light molasses. Bourbon resting adds a tangy, lightly spicy layer without smothering the tobaccos. Body is medium, flavor a notch more intense, and nicotine sits just below body level. The crumbly cake breaks apart easily and needs no drying; it burns cool, clean, and slow. A non-continuous edition for those seeking pressed Virginia character in a non-aromatic frame.
sutliff-tobacco-company-crumble-kake-lim.o: Leaves a scent of tangy fruit and barrel wood.

mac-baren-vanilla-choice.z: Vanilla Choice is a vanilla-flavored blend in Mac Baren's Choice series. Its composition holds Burley, Cavendish, and Virginia leaves; the cut is loose ribbon. On opening the pack, the most pronounced element is an intense vanilla aroma; the taste proceeds along the same line and lingers in the mouth for a while after smoking. The tobacco arrives quite moist from the pack, so airing it before packing is necessary; smoked quickly, it can cause tongue bite and moisture buildup in the chamber, so a slow pace is needed. Nicotine stays light. Suited to those starting the pipe with aromatic blends and smokers seeking a pronounced sweet flavoring.
mac-baren-vanilla-choice.o: Leaves a pronounced vanilla and sweet-pastry aroma evoking a bakery.

wolfway-xvii.z: XVII is among Wolfway's unflavored blends, built on a structure of Greek Oriental leaf and Virginia. Its smoke is smooth, giving a natural tobacco taste reminiscent of cocoa; while mild to medium in nicotine, it leaves a full texture in the mouth. It is intended for smokers who want a full-bodied smoke without added flavoring.
wolfway-xvii.o: Leaves a fairly heavy scent evoking dark cocoa and dry leaf.

mostex-stanislaw-pragues-mixture.z: No independent, verifiable source describing the composition of this blend, released under the Stanislaw brand of the Brno-based maker Mostex, could be found.

up-down-chinese-laundry.z: One of the house blends from the Up Down Tobacco shop in Chicago's Old Town neighborhood; since no independent source describing the blend's composition and character has been found, the record is left incomplete.

ken-byron-ventures-van-gogh-2021.z: Van Gogh is an all-Virginia blend from Ken Byron Ventures, a small-scale producer based in Pennsylvania. Per the maker's description, domestic and imported Virginias are brought together and, after pressing, presented as broken flake with a mottled, dark-toned appearance. The leaf goes through a light casing; no dominant flavoring or heavy sweetening is added, so the taste comes largely from Virginia's own breadlike, dried-fruit character. KBV re-blends its offerings every year and releases them in limited numbers under a year stamp, so leaf sourcing and aging can differ between years of the same name. The broken-flake structure calls for rubbing out between the fingers before packing and rewards a slow smoke. Suited to smokers who want to follow unflavored Virginia's natural sweetness and its development in the jar over time, and to those already used to flake form.
ken-byron-ventures-van-gogh-2021.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma of dry hay and cooked fruit.

cornell-diehl-maple-cavendish.z: No adequate source documenting the composition and character of Cornell & Diehl's Maple Cavendish blend could be found; the blend isn't in the maker's current catalogue.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-flake.z: Kendal Flake is one of the house's blends offering its Lakeland essence tradition in flake form. The essence line is rose-forward; on the smoke it's accompanied by almond and a lightly spiced fruit tone. The slices are pressed and moist; crumbled and aired, they burn evenly. Nicotine is moderate, more measured than the same house's Grasmere Flake. Serves as an entry point for those wanting to get to know floral-essence English flakes.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-flake.o: Leaves a floral-sweet aroma combining rose and almond.

w-o-larsen-150th-anniversary.z: 150th Anniversary is a limited release prepared for the 150th year of the W.Ø. Larsen name, founded in Copenhagen in 1864. The brand's shop is no longer open today, but its tobaccos have continued to be produced in a line carrying on the Danish pipe tobacco tradition. The blend is built from orange Virginia, mature dark Virginia, fire-cured Kentucky, and long-aged soft black cavendish leaves. While the bronze-to-brown Virginias leave a sweet, tart foundation, the dark-fired Kentucky adds a smoky, earthy body to the blend; black cavendish softens that body. Warm vanilla, ripe plum, and nougat notes added on top pull the blend toward the aromatic side, but don't entirely mask the leaf's own taste. It's medium in nicotine. This is a release aimed at smokers seeking fuller blends where aromatic sweetness and Kentucky smoke coexist.
w-o-larsen-150th-anniversary.o: A light wood-smoke trace mixes into a scent of sweet plum and vanilla marzipan.

d-r-tobacco-two-timer-gold.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of D & R Tobacco's Two Timer Gold blend were found.

rattray-sir-william.z: Sir William is one of Rattray's ready-rubbed, loose-cut blends. Select Virginia leaf forms the main body; dark-fired Kentucky and Burley of Indian and Thai origin are added, with a light whisky flavoring applied on top. Virginia's sweetness sets the blend's balance, while Kentucky adds a smoky, full ground and Burley a nutty mellowness. Flavoring is at a low level and doesn't overshadow the tobacco taste; it is full-bodied in nicotine. It suits smokers who stay close to unflavored blends but want a subtle aromatic touch. The Rattray name draws on the Scottish pipe-tobacco tradition; the brand's tobaccos are produced today in Germany.
rattray-sir-william.o: Leaves a light whisky and woody trace over a roasted-tobacco aroma.

jons-pipe-shop-cumberland-gap.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Jon's Pipe Shop's Cumberland Gap blend.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-irlandez-bl.z: Irlandez Black Cavendish is the dark member of the Irlandez line produced by Tabacos Cisne Branco Finamore in Juiz de Fora, Minas Gerais. Black Cavendish is a blend built from cavendish and Virginia leaf; it is sold in aluminum-lined, vacuum-sealed packs. Opening the pack releases a fermented-fruit-leaning scent reminiscent of jabuticaba liqueur. On the smoke, Virginia's taste comes through distinctly while the Black Cavendish keeps a liqueur-like sweetness in the background; the burn is even and nicotine is moderate. It suits smokers looking for a sweet, not-too-heavy everyday blend that can be enjoyed alongside coffee or a drink.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-irlandez-bl.o: Leaves a sweetish scent reminiscent of fermented grapes and fruit liqueur.

villiger-orient.z: This is a Villiger tobacco named for its Oriental-leaf emphasis; no independent source could be found giving blend details.

mccranies-red-flake-vintage-1983.z: Red Flake is an unflavored red Virginia blend from Charlotte's McCranie's tobacconist, produced from a single harvest. The 1983-stamped version is the flake batch made from that year's harvest; since it's tied to a single harvest, it was never remade once the batch sold out, though later years saw releases under the same name from other harvests. Today it's remembered only through tins remaining in private cellars. Being an unflavored Virginia, the flavor comes from the leaf's own sugars; long aging brings out a round, creamy, vanilla-like line along with dried-fruit sweetness. Pressed into flake form, it burns slow and cool. Of interest to experienced smokers wanting to see how an aged single-varietal Virginia develops.
mccranies-red-flake-vintage-1983.o: Leaves a sweet, faintly creamy aroma reminiscent of dried fruit and bread yeast.

comoys-of-london-cask-9-spiced-virginia.z: Blend No. 9 in Comoy's of London's Cask series is an aromatic mixture built by combining bright Virginia leaves from three continents with some burley. Nougat, vanilla, and chocolate notes are used in the flavoring, aiming for a moderate profile that supports Virginia's own natural sweetness. The flavoring level is more measured than heavy aromatics, so the leaf taste isn't entirely masked; the burley component adds dryness and body. It suits smokers looking for a middle ground between an aromatic and an unflavored Virginia, or wanting a lightly flavored everyday blend. According to available records, Comoy's Cask series has not been in production for some time.
comoys-of-london-cask-9-spiced-virginia.o: Leaves an aroma of vanilla chocolate and nutty nougat in the room.

cornell-diehl-plantation-evening.z: Plantation Evening is a middle-of-the-road English mixture Cornell & Diehl builds on aged Virginia. Per the maker's listing, Latakia, Perique, and Turkish leaf are added to matured Virginia. The Latakia dose is enough to give a smoky layer but doesn't mask Virginia's sweetness. Body stays in a band stretching from mild to medium; Perique adds measured spice, and the Oriental leaf a grassy edge. The ribbon cut packs easily and burns evenly. Suited to smokers who find full-bodied Latakia bombs too heavy and want a balanced English mixture.
cornell-diehl-plantation-evening.o: Leaves a spicy tobacco note mingling with a light smoke and dry-hay scent.

watch-city-cigar-the-churchwarden.z: Watch City Cigar's blend called The Churchwarden is, according to records, one of the house blends of the Waltham, Massachusetts tobacconist shop; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

seattle-pipe-club-deception-pass.z: Deception Pass is a Virginia-Perique blend built as Seattle Pipe Club's Pacific Northwest take. The body is carried by English-type Virginia leaf; Oriental leaf, Perique, and a small amount of black cavendish are added as accents. The plum-and-pepper spice Perique brings sharpens the bready sweetness of the Virginia, while the cavendish share softens the blend's edges. Since it is not Latakia-forward, the smoke stays brighter and sweeter than the brand's better-known English blends. The blend takes its name from Deception Pass strait in Washington State. Per the producer's description, it has a low tendency to bite the tongue during the burn, making it suited to long smoking sessions. Suited to smokers seeking the fruity sweetness of Virginia-based blends who also want a measured layer of spice alongside it; also considered a transitional entry for those newly approaching Perique.
seattle-pipe-club-deception-pass.o: Leaves a scent of dried fruit and light spice over a bready Virginia sweetness.

samuel-gawith-hansom-flake.z: A blend signed Samuel Gawith, referred to in records as a Virginia-and-Perique-based flake; no sufficient source confirming its content and character could be found.

carroll-p-j-co-ltd-velvan-plug.z: Velvan Plug is a pressed-cake tobacco manufactured by the Irish firm P. J. Carroll & Co. Sweet light Virginia and dark Virginia leaf are pressed together, with a light fruit essence applied on top. Being sold in plug form, it needs to be sliced with a knife and rubbed out before smoking; this structure lets the tobacco's moisture be preserved for a long time. In the smoke, the dense, sweet Virginia base brought on by pressing comes forward, while the fruit casing stays subdued. Nicotine is medium and it burns slowly. It is no longer in production today; it stands among the examples of traditional plug tobaccos used daily in Ireland for many years.
carroll-p-j-co-ltd-velvan-plug.o: Leaves a sweet dried fruit and pressed-tobacco aroma.

james-barber-maryland-mixture.z: James Barber's mixture, classified as an American type; no independent source could be found to document its contents.

hu-tobacco-pfeifenecke.z: Pfeifenecke is a flavored blend HU Tobacco prepared in its Hommage to my Friends line, dedicated to the German-language pipe forum of the same name. Its composition includes dark and red Virginia, black Cavendish, Kentucky, and Burley leaves. The flavoring is built on tonka bean and amaretto; cherry remains a barely detectable background note. The flavoring is kept measured enough not to overwhelm the tobacco, instead giving the blend a distinctive sweet line. It's aimed at those looking for a medium-strength flavored blend suited to everyday smoking. Records indicate it's presented in 50-gram tins.
hu-tobacco-pfeifenecke.o: Leaves an aroma of tonka bean's spicy sweetness along with almond and a light cherry note.

uhles-blend-255.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend Blend 255 has been found.

straus-tobacco-anderson-ferry-cherry.z: One of the aromatic house blends from Straus Tobacconist bearing Cincinnati neighborhood and landmark names; no verifiable source describing its composition could be found.

iwan-ries-three-star-cordial-buttered-ru.z: This is a blend from the Three Star line prepared over the counter by the Chicago-based tobacconist Iwan Ries & Co.; no independent source detailing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
iwan-ries-three-star-cordial-buttered-ru.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-welcome-to-the-c.z: Welcome to the Circus is one of Kohlhase & Kopp's limited-run aromatics. Its body is built from broken-leaf Virginia and black cavendish. The casing is built on a profile reminiscent of salted-caramel popcorn; as the smoke progresses, the caramel sweetness recedes and gives way to a creamy, honey-character taste. It was offered in a colorful 100-gram tin bearing a carousel image. The broken Virginia ensures a cool burn; a light citrusy tanginess shows through beneath the casing at times. Black cavendish carries the sweetness to the end. Nicotine is light. Prepared for smokers who love pronouncedly cased, sweet and creamy aromatics.
kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-welcome-to-the-c.o: Leaves a salted caramel popcorn and honey room note.

sutliff-tobacco-company-berkshire.z: Berkshire, part of Sutliff's Private Stock line, is an unflavored English blend. It takes its name from England's county of Berkshire and represents the line's English-style wing. Its composition includes latakia, oriental, Virginia, and perique; the addition of perique is a detail that departs from the classic latakia-oriental-Virginia trio. On the palate, Virginia's sweetness, latakia's smoky woody weight, and the orientals' spicy sharpness interlock in a balanced way; perique adds a plummy, peppery edge to this sweet-spicy axis. It's light-to-medium in strength and offers an unfussy, straightforward English character. Suited to those newly transitioning into latakia blends and to those wanting a non-heavy English blend for daily smoking. It is no longer in production.
sutliff-tobacco-company-berkshire.o: Leaves a light spice scent mixed into smoke and wood.

lane-limited-captain-black-supreme.z: Recorded as a member of the Captain Black series; not enough sources could be found about its contents.

borkum-riff-mixture-with-licorice-indigo.z: The blend is a coarse, evenly cut mixture whose weight comes mainly from fermented black Cavendish sourced from Africa and South America, joined by Brazilian Virginia. It's flavored with real licorice root and a sambuca-style aniseed liqueur aroma, so the licorice-anise pairing dominates both the taste and the smell. Following a change in EU tobacco regulation, the product is sold within the Union under the name "Borkum Riff Indigo." Production takes place at Scandinavian Tobacco Group's Orlik factory in Assens, Denmark. It suits smokers looking for a pronounced, single-direction, sweet flavor with an affinity for licorice.
borkum-riff-mixture-with-licorice-indigo.o: Leaves a sweet room note bordering on sharp, reminiscent of licorice root and aniseed.

faders-carrolls-blend.z: Fader's is a line of house blends offered under its own name by a long-established Baltimore tobacconist; no verifiable source could be found regarding this blend's composition and character.

gawith-hoggarth-co-westmorland-slices.z: Westmorland Slices is a broken flake tobacco from Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. carrying the old name of the maker's own region. Dark-toned Virginia leaf is pressed and matured with fire-cured leaf support; the block, which reaches an ebony darkness, is then cut into strips. It comes out of the tin as broken flakes, so it can be packed folded or rubbed out and thinned. A licorice-and-honey-molasses-reminiscent flavoring is applied along with the distinctive floral "Lakeland" essence of Kendal tradition. On the smoke, wood smoke, leather, a light cigar-leaf note, and a tart-spicy Virginia base stand out; the Lakeland essence stays subtle enough not to mask this base and is felt more in the aroma. The smoke is creamy and full, burns cool when well aired, and doesn't bite the tongue unless forced. Nicotine is above average, so it's heavy going for those new to the pipe. A blend for smokers wanting pressed Virginia slices together with the Kendal-style floral flavoring.
gawith-hoggarth-co-westmorland-slices.o: A floral essence reminiscent of soap and rosewater arrives together with a wood-smoke aroma.

hbi-three-castles.z: The Three Castles name traces back to a historic English brand launched by W.D. & H.O. Wills in 1878, which quickly also became widespread as a cigarette tobacco. The American re-creation of the original recipe was made for HBI by D&R; the same blend was also sold under the D&R label as Three Sails.
hbi-three-castles.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of dry hay and baked bread crust.

golden-leaf-tobacco-hb-3-sweet.z: Beyond being a sweet-flavored blend under the Golden Leaf Tobacco name, there is no sourcing documenting its composition and character.
golden-leaf-tobacco-hb-3-sweet.o: Said to leave a sweet aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-flake-liquorice.z: This is the licorice-root-sauced version of the Dark Flake family. Virginia leaf, pressed and darkened by hot-press baking, forms the blend's body; Burley is added to it. The casing is the traditional Kendal trio of licorice root, fig, and tonka extract. Because the leaf is processed darker than in Brown Flake, the base is heavier. The slices are tight; once rubbed out, they're packed as a coarse cut and burn slowly. On the taste, the dark Virginia's bready, lightly tart sweetness runs alongside licorice's bitter edge, with tonka adding a sweet weight to the aroma. Nicotine is above medium. Aimed at smokers with experience in Kendal-style sauced flake tobaccos.
gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-flake-liquorice.o: Licorice root and dried-fig aromas sit atop a dark smoke base.

the-tobacco-shop-llc-back-room.z: No independent source revealing the composition of the house blend Back Room from The Tobacco Shop LLC has been found.
the-tobacco-shop-llc-back-room.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

diehl-munich-old-english-mixture.z: This is one of the house blends prepared under its own name by the Pfeifen Diehl tobacconist in Munich; the shop is now operated under the Wolsdorff umbrella. Though the name points to a traditional latakia-containing English mixture style, no independent source documenting its composition could be found.

synjeco-wenti-blend.z: Wenti Blend is a mixture named among Synjeco's own blends, described as Balkan-style; no sufficient independent source describing its content and character could be found.
synjeco-wenti-blend.o: No reliable record of a room note could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-rumbh.z: Rumbh is a tobacco Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. sells loose, made by combining Virginia and Burley leaf and rounding it out with a measured rum topping. The name comes from an abbreviation of this composition. Virginia gives the base sweetness and a herbal lightness, while Burley adds a nutty, dry body; the rum topping brings out the sweetness without dominating. Suited to smokers who avoid heavy aromatics but want a lightly flavored everyday smoke rather than a fully unflavored blend.
gawith-hoggarth-co-rumbh.o: Leaves a nutty tobacco aroma with light rum sweetness.

chief-catoonah-tobacconist-virginia-flak.z: The entry has been left incomplete as no reliable source could be found for Chief Catoonah Tobacconist's Virginia Flake #3 blend.

pfeifen-huber-diablo-nero.z: Diablo Nero is one of the best-known aromatics among the Munich house Pfeifen Huber's house blends, sold in a 100 gram tin as well as a larger 400 gram package. The body of the loose-cut blend is built from Virginia, black Cavendish, and Burley leaf; on top is applied a pronounced flavoring built from a trio of chocolate, vanilla, and hazelnut. Its character is dark and sweet but light in nicotine: the topping comes forward while the tobacco's earthy Burley base plays a balancing role behind it. The smoke is dense and creamy, with low bite. It suits those seeking a straightforwardly sweet aromatic, particularly for evening smokes and the cold season; it falls outside the interest of those seeking an unflavored blend.
pfeifen-huber-diablo-nero.o: Leaves a sweet, bakery-like aroma blending cocoa, vanilla, and toasted hazelnut.

dan-tobacco-london-blend-no-700.z: An English mixture belonging to Dan Tobacco's numbered London Blend series; no adequate independent sources documenting this particular number's composition were found.

peter-stokkebye-luxury-curly-cut.z: This is a Virginia-based, medallion-sliced curly-cut blend from Peter Stokkebye; it has reportedly been discontinued, with Luxury Bullseye Flake taking its place in the line.

pete-brothers-esperanto-premium-mixture.z: No verifiable description from the manufacturer or retailer could be found for the Esperanto Premium Mixture bearing the Pete Brothers name; the blend's content, cut, and character remain undocumented.

sutliff-tobacco-company-erin-go-bragh-ir.z: Erin Go Bragh Irish Whiskey is one of the bulk blends from the Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

iwan-ries-three-star-vanilla-cordial.z: Three Star Vanilla Cordial is the vanilla-flavored member of the Three Star Cordial line prepared specially for Iwan Ries & Co. in Chicago. A vanilla sauce is applied to a ribbon-cut mix of Burley, Virginia, and black Cavendish leaves; the black Cavendish carries sweetness, the Burley provides body, and the Virginia gives a light sugar layer in the background. It's considered light in nicotine, suited to smoking at any time of day. The Three Star Cordial line also includes other flavors like cherry and buttered rum; all are built on the same base with different flavorings. It's a blend suited to smokers who enjoy flavored tobaccos and are looking for a sweet, mild smoke rather than sharp nicotine, and to those new to the pipe. Iwan Ries has operated as a tobacconist in Chicago since 1857 and sells this line under its own name.
iwan-ries-three-star-vanilla-cordial.o: Leaves an aroma of sweet vanilla and sugared cream.

middle-earth-tobacco-gondor.z: The Virginia-Perique-centered blend in the Middle Earth Tobacco line; since no verifiable source could be found, no detail can be given.

peter-stokkebye-optimum-no-31.z: Optimum is built by blending Zimbabwe- and Malawi-origin flue-cured leaf with flavored black Cavendish and soft Burley. It is a loose cut, topped with a flavoring carrying vanilla and fruit notes. According to brand records, it has been in the line for more than forty years. It is very light in nicotine and straightforward in taste; the sweetness stays balanced throughout the bowl and the tobacco smokes comfortably. It suits smokers seeking a not-too-heavy aromatic for all-day smoking.
peter-stokkebye-optimum-no-31.o: Leaves a vanilla, lightly fruity, sweet aroma.

pipesandcigars-com-scottys-university-gr.z: University Graduate is the fullest-bodied installment among the university-named blends in pipesandcigars.com's Scotty's bulk line. It contains aged Virginias, dark and smoky Latakia, sweet-spicy Perique, and a slice of tobacco added to mellow the blend. Ribbon pieces sitting together with flake crumbs balance the burn rate. It is an unflavored English mixture: sweetness comes from Virginia, spice from Perique, and smoke from Latakia. Flavor intensity is pronounced and nicotine medium. It suits smokers familiar with Latakia blends looking for a body one step more layered than straight Virginia.
pipesandcigars-com-scottys-university-gr.o: Leaves a wood-soot and dry-spice aroma in the room.

doctor-pipe-strong-mixture.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Strong Mixture, a pipe tobacco from Doctor Pipe.
doctor-pipe-strong-mixture.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

e-a-carey-careys-peach-brandy.z: Its name suggests an aromatic flavored with peach and brandy; this blend, no longer in E. A. Carey's current catalog, has no primary source describing its composition.

diamante-negro-cachimbo.z: No reliable source could be found documenting the composition and character of this record, referred to by the Portuguese word "cachimbo" (pipe).

paul-olsen-28.z: One of the numbered house blends from Danish tobacconist Poul Olsen; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.

mcclelland-oriental-mixture-no-14.z: Oriental Mixture No. 14 is among the last numbers in McClelland's green-label Oriental series. The mixture contains toasted Virginia leaves, Oriental tobaccos, and Latakia. The dry leaf's color makes the Latakia share look higher than it is; in the smoke, the Latakia stays in the background and doesn't cover the blend. The flavor axis rests on a sweet, bready, buttery Virginia character, joined by nutty, earthy, and occasionally floral notes. Body is medium, and the nicotine load isn't jarring. Suited to smokers who know Latakia but don't want its weight, and who seek an Oriental-Virginia balance. The blend was withdrawn from the market when McClelland stopped production in 2018.
mcclelland-oriental-mixture-no-14.o: A fine wood smokiness rises beneath the aroma of baked bread and butter.

mac-baren-harmony.z: Harmony is one of Mac Baren's ready-rubbed Virginia-burley blends. The weight is on burley; Virginia and the brand's own cavendish accompany it.
