The tobacco is pressed and then rubbed before packing, which makes filling easy and ensures an even burn. In character, burley's dry, nutty taste sits alongside Virginia's light sweetness, with no pronounced applied casing. Suited to those seeking a near-unflavored, medium-bodied everyday smoke.
mac-baren-harmony.o: Leaves a nutty, lightly sweet, dry tobacco room note.

svendborg-english-mixture.z: Svendborg English Mixture is a medium-strength English blend that brings together black Cavendish, naturally sweet Virginia leaves, and smoky Latakia. The latakia proportion is moderate compared to what's considered heavy within the style; the Cavendish softens the smoky side and gives the blend a rounded sweetness. The cut is ribbon and the burn is even. The blend belongs to a brand named after the Danish town of Svendborg and is blended in the Danish style, though production takes place in Germany. It serves as an entry point for smokers curious about Latakia blends who don't want to start straight in on a heavy Balkan mixture. Nicotine is medium, and the room note carries the smoky character typical of English blends.
svendborg-english-mixture.o: Leaves a smoky scent reminiscent of wood smoke and campfire.

peterson-special-reserve-2004.z: This is the 2004 edition of Peterson's annual limited Special Reserve series; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient sources giving that year's composition and topping information could be found.
peterson-special-reserve-2004.o: Leaves the sweet aroma typical of aromatic blends.

clan-shaw-aaa-white-burley.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend AAA White Burley.
clan-shaw-aaa-white-burley.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

sillems-green.z: Green is a mixture in the highly flavored wing of the Sillem's series, produced by Kohlhase & Kopp. It is a loose ribbon-cut blend built from various sugar-rich Virginia leaves with brown and black cavendish added. The flavoring is built on pineapple, coconut, and macadamia; the tin and room note are intense enough to evoke a piña colada along with nutty tones. Nicotine is light, the smoke is cool and sweet. Suited to those who enjoy pronounced tropical-flavored tobaccos and want a light smoke.
sillems-green.o: Leaves a nutty, pineapple-and-coconut-forward tropical-cocktail scent.

ash-ember-owls-beak.z: No adequate independent source could be found for Owl's Beak, a house blend from the Ash & Ember shop.
ash-ember-owls-beak.o: No reliable information on the room note could be found.

lane-limited-pot-of-gold.z: Not enough independent sources could be found documenting the contents and character of American blender Lane Limited's blend called Pot of Gold.

cornell-diehl-scots-heather.z: No composition description published by the maker or retailers could be found for this Cornell & Diehl blend named Scot's Heather.

pipesandcigars-com-scottys-bass-pond.z: This is a blend offered under the American retailer pipesandcigars.com's name; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

port-williams-brown.z: This is a blend within the Port Williams line; no source could be found describing its content and character.

wessex-english-mixture.z: English Mixture is the blend in the Wessex series that most directly corresponds to the classic English mixture definition. It's offered in ribbon cut and follows the traditional scheme of Latakia and Oriental leaf set atop a Virginia foundation; no flavoring casing is used. In the smoke, wood soot leads, behind which sits the Oriental's dry, spicy tone and a measured sweetness from the Virginia. The Latakia ratio stays more measured than in Balkan-style blends, placing this blend at a middle point suitable for all-day smoking. It suits those new to smoky mixtures and those seeking an unflavored English blend.
wessex-english-mixture.o: Leaves a smoky wood and dry-leaf scent.

sutliff-tobacco-company-200-red-wine.z: 200 Red Wine is a blend in Sutliff's bulk aromatic line, taking its flavoring from a wine extract selected from California vineyards. The wine extract is applied in measured amounts to give the leaf bouquet and soft sweetness; the body includes Virginia and burley along with black cavendish. It's a mixture that lights easily with its ribbon cut and has moderate nicotine strength. A bulk option suited to smokers who enjoy the aromatic side but want to stay away from heavily sugared toppings. Sutliff is one of the long-established American pipe tobacco makers, based in Richmond, Virginia.
sutliff-tobacco-company-200-red-wine.o: Leaves a lightly sweet trace along with a scent of red wine and dark grape.

gallaher-limited-condor-ready-rubbed-gre.z: Condor Ready Rubbed is the rubbed-cut member of the Condor family produced under Gallaher Limited, recognisable by its green pack. Built on a Virginia leaf base, the blend carries the brand's distinctive floral, alcoholic Lakeland essence. The ready-rubbed cut makes filling easy and gives a steady burn; the smoke proceeds full-bodied, lightly sweet, and spicy. Nicotine is above medium, and since the tobacco can arrive moist, it calls for slow smoking. It is considered one of the best-known pipe tobaccos in the United Kingdom.
gallaher-limited-condor-ready-rubbed-gre.o: Leaves a floral essence and a lightly alcoholic, sweetish aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-coco-creme-333.z: Coco Creme #333 is a Sutliff bulk aromatic prepared by combining mahogany-colored burley grades with soft black cavendish and flavoring them with cocoa and vanilla. The topping is heavy; the flavor is creamy and smooth. The leaf's moisture content is high, and due to the sauce applied it can feel tacky to the touch; airing it out for a while before lighting notably eases the burn. Nicotine strength is light, flavor level is medium. A record for those seeking a chocolatey-vanilla sweet profile.
sutliff-tobacco-company-coco-creme-333.o: Leaves a scent of cocoa and cream.

seattle-pipe-club-plum-pudding-special-r.z: Plum Pudding Special Reserve Flake is the premium version of the Plum Pudding recipe, signed by Seattle Pipe Club's founding blender Joe Lankford, presented in pressed-leaf form. The base is built on mature red Virginia leaf; Cyprus latakia, Turkish-Oriental leaves, perique, and some cavendish are added on top. It differs from the standard version by being reinforced with long-aged sun-cured leaves and by pressing the whole leaf into flake form; according to records, the blend is produced at Cornell & Diehl. On the smoke, Latakia's smoky, tar-like core sits alongside the Virginia's dark, fruity sweetness; perique adds a plum-and-pepper sharpness, while the Oriental leaves bring a layer of dry hay and spice. Because of the flake structure, the smoke is slow and cool, and the leaf needs to be rubbed and aired for a while. Suited to smokers accustomed to flake preparation who seek a Latakia-forward, unflavored, intensely sweet blend.
seattle-pipe-club-plum-pudding-special-r.o: Leaves a scent of burnt wood, pine soot, and spicy incense.

p-lorillard-burgundy.z: One of the pipe tobaccos once marketed by P. Lorillard, founded in 1760 and considered America's oldest tobacco manufacturer; no usable source describing its composition could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-reserve-navy-cake.z: This is a Virginia blend carried under the Wilke Pipe Tobacco name; as it does not appear in the maker's current catalog, no reliable information could be found regarding its composition and character.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-brown-sliced.z: Not enough first-hand source material documenting the composition and character of Brown Sliced, one of Orlik's sliced-cut blends, could be found; records indicate it has been discontinued.

peterson-st-patricks-day-2016.z: St. Patrick's Day 2016 is a limited edition blend released as part of Peterson's St. Patrick's Day series specific to that year; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient first-hand sources confirming its content and character could be found.

peter-stokkebye-pistachio-no-27.z: Pistachio is an aromatic built from finely ribbon-cut red Virginia and soft black Cavendish. The blend is given a flavoring of creamy vanilla with a pistachio-recalling note; since the flavoring is worked into the mixture before pressing, the taste stays consistent throughout the bowl. The body is light, the sweetness measured, and it doesn't mask the tobacco's own taste. It suits smokers who enjoy nutty-sweet profiles and want to avoid heavily sugared aromatics.
peter-stokkebye-pistachio-no-27.o: Leaves a roasted pistachio and creamy vanilla aroma.

mcclelland-townsman-cavendish-black.z: No sufficient source detailing the contents and character of this black-Cavendish-based aromatic from McClelland's Townsman Cavendish series could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-baklava.z: A Sutliff blend whose name points to a honey-and-nut-flavored aromatic; sufficient independent sources confirming its composition could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-baklava.o: Records indicate it leaves a scent of honey and roasted nuts.

milan-tobacconists-buttered-rum.z: Buttered Rum is a house blend among Milan Tobacconists' classic rum aromatics. Golden virginia is combined with white burley; according to the maker's description, New England and Jamaican rums are added to the mixture in a buttery construction, and this is the source of the blend's pronounced aroma. The leaf selection builds a light-bodied base, with the weight resting in the casing. An entry geared toward those looking for a sweet aromatic in the direction of rum and caramel whose scent lingers a long time in the room. It may come across as overpowering to those looking for an unflavored tobacco character.
milan-tobacconists-buttered-rum.o: Leaves a heavy, sweet aroma in the direction of buttered rum and brown sugar.

dunhill-virginia-ready-rubbed.z: Ready Rubbed is a Dunhill blend built by applying a light cavendish process over Virginia and oriental leaves. After the leaves take on a measured fruity cast, they're steam pressed; then rubbed out to produce a structure between ribbon and flake. The cavendish stage files down the harsh, hot edge of flame-cured Virginia while also darkening the leaf's color. The resulting tobacco is moderately sweet, smokable throughout the day, and matures further when rested in the tin. It suits smokers seeking a pure Virginia character but wary of tongue bite, and those who'd rather not deal with preparing flake tobacco. The blend was among the old Dunhill recipes reintroduced to the US market in 2015; after Dunhill exited tobacco production, the same recipe has continued under the Peterson name.
dunhill-virginia-ready-rubbed.o: Leaves a scent of sweet hay and light dried fruit, with a warm bread-crust tone lingering behind.

w-o-larsen-selected-blend-no-80-mahogany.z: This is one of W.O. Larsen's numbered selected blends; no reliable source could be found documenting its composition and character.

cascadia-pipe-co-campsite.z: Cascadia Pipe Co. is an American line taking its name from the Pacific Northwest region, made up of five blends named after time spent outdoors; Campsite, Trail Head, Downwind, Open Water and Vertical Limit make up this series. All are offered in pressed-cake (plug) form, a structure that slows the tobacco's drying. Campsite is prepared by slow-pressing select hot-air-cured Virginia leaves. In the smoke, sweet grass and hay tones appear, with a soft citrus trace behind them. It is sliced from the cake and rubbed out for filling, burning slow and cool. Nicotine is medium, and flavor casing is limited. Aimed at fans of straight Virginia and smokers experienced with working slice and cake tobaccos.
cascadia-pipe-co-campsite.o: Leaves a dry hay, straw and light citrus aroma.

a-c-petersen-caledonian-melange-no-466-g.z: Caledonian Melange No.466 Grand Reserve is an English-style blend belonging to the Caledonian line of Alfred & Christian Petersen, a firm founded in 1865 in Horsens, Denmark. It was sold in green tins as a thick-cut mixture built from Latakia, Virginia, and Oriental leaf. The blend hasn't been produced for a long time; sealed tins today change hands in collector circles. With the firm's takeover by Orlik in 2000, this member of the Caledonian line was dropped from the catalog. It's referred to as an unflavored entry representing the classic Latakia-forward English style.
a-c-petersen-caledonian-melange-no-466-g.o: Leaves a room note dominated by woodsmoke and incense, with a trace of dry spice.

holger-danske-daily-mixture-classic.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for this blend, said to contain Virginia and Burley, from the Danish brand Holger Danske.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-antique-pressed-.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for this blend, described as English type, from the Hermit Tobacco Works Co. brand.

g-l-pease-barbary-coast-original-mixture.z: Barbary Coast is a cube-cut blend in G. L. Pease's Original Mixtures line, with Perique added to a Virginia and Burley base. A measured brandy topping is applied to the leaf mixture; this topping is not intense enough to place the blend in the aromatic class, remaining a flavouring that frames the tobacco's own taste. The cube cut makes filling easy, but tends to burn quickly if loaded loosely. Tin moisture runs relatively high; records note that airing it for a while improves both the burn and the taste. With Burley's fullness, Perique's peppery sharpness, and the brandy topping combined, the flavour runs intense and full-bodied; it is not a profile for those seeking a sweet Virginia. It suits smokers familiar with cube cut and Burley-heavy blends, using a medium-strength tobacco.
g-l-pease-barbary-coast-original-mixture.o: An earthy aroma from the Burley and Perique is mixed with light brandy sweetness.

avrasya-pipo-tutunu-turco-aryan-slim.z: Turco Aryan Slim is an aromatic product prepared by Eurasia Pipe Tobacco by blending Virginia and Oriental leaf with a small amount of black Cavendish. Its cut is a mix of shag and ribbon; the fine cut makes packing easy. Chocolate and vanilla flavors are given together in a diluted way, so the flavoring stays light and doesn't override the tobacco's own taste. The smoke is cool and light; strength is light-to-medium, flavor is medium. It suits those looking for a domestically produced aromatic with measured flavoring.
avrasya-pipo-tutunu-turco-aryan-slim.o: Leaves a sweet room note leaning toward chocolate and vanilla.

pcca-millennium-2000.z: For PCCA's blend called Millennium 2000, no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

traditab-1637.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Traditab blend 1637 has been found.

edwards-dolphin.z: This is one of Edward's Pipe & Tobacco's in-house aromatic blends prepared in the shop; not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition and character.
edwards-dolphin.o: Could not be described due to insufficient records.

sutliff-tobacco-company-ts12-dark-fire-c.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Sutliff Tobacco Company's TS12 Dark Fire Cured pipe tobacco could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-cherry-cream-flake.z: This is recorded as a Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. cherry-topped flake tobacco; no reliable source could be found regarding its content and character.

peter-stokkebye-black-kathy.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Black Kathy could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-festivus-mixture-2021.z: Festivus Mixture is a Virginia-Perique blend Ken Byron Ventures prepares for the holiday season. The production method reportedly involves partially Cavendish-processing aged Virginia leaf, steaming it for an hour, then combining it with Perique and pressing it into thin slices. This process aims to give the blend a mature character right out of the tin. On the taste side, stone fruit, earthy spice, and molasses stand out; Perique's sharp, spicy punch sits atop Virginia's natural sweetness. Suited to smokers seeking a pressed VaPer texture and an intensity that reads as long-aged. Released as a limited batch.
ken-byron-ventures-festivus-mixture-2021.o: Leaves a molasses-like sweetness alongside a spicy, lightly tangy fruit aroma.

barclay-rex-barclay-slice.z: Among Barclay Rex's unflavored blends, this is a Virginia product presented in flake form, as the name suggests; no adequate source detailing its content could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-black-bogie.z: Kendal Black Bogie is an unflavored tobacco where fire-cured and air-cured dark leaves are hand-twisted into rope form. The name "Bogie" is given to Kendal's traditional rope tobaccos; the product is sold as a near-black dark roll, packed sliced and rubbed out. The smoke is dark, smoky, and molasses-like; nicotine is very high. It can be demanding when smoked on an empty stomach or at a fast pace, so it's aimed at experienced smokers. Kendal ropes have historically been used both in the pipe and as chewing tobacco, and Gawith Hoggarth is the producer continuing this production tradition.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-black-bogie.o: An aroma of smoke, molasses, and burnt wood settles in the room.

partagas-cifuentes-y-cia-partagas-picadu.z: No reliable source could be found for the Partagas Cifuentes y Cia pipe tobacco called Partagas Picadura Granulata, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

straus-tobacco-queen-city.z: Queen City is one of the counter blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; records indicate the shop was founded in 1880 and that most of its house blends were named after Cincinnati neighborhoods and landmark buildings. Since no independent source on the blend's composition and character could be found, this record is kept at listing level only.

ken-byron-ventures-fat-old-sun-2020.z: The 2020 release of Ken Byron Ventures' Fat Old Sun; no independent source could be found to document its contents.
ken-byron-ventures-fat-old-sun-2020.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

peretti-century.z: This is a shop mixture L.J. Peretti lists in its English blends group and continues to produce; although its name references the company's hundred-year history, no published information about its composition could be found.

with-pipe-and-book-old-guides-mix.z: This is one of the house blends of the With Pipe and Book shop in Lake Placid, named for Adirondack guides. Production ceased when the shop closed; no adequate source could be found regarding its composition and flavor profile.
with-pipe-and-book-old-guides-mix.o: No description of its room note could be found in the records.

warped-scarecrow.z: Scarecrow is the first aromatic blend in the Warped series, prepared as a limited-run, autumn-themed seasonal release. Its composition includes a special red Virginia cavendish made from 2017 and 2019 harvest red and orange-red flue-cured leaf, 2014 white Burley, and aged dark air-cured leaf; this composition gives malted-chocolate and spice tones.
warped-scarecrow.o: A toasted-leaf scent mixes into cocoa, vanilla, and burnt-sugar notes.

exclusiv-rum-royal.z: No verifiable source could be found regarding the producer, composition, and character of this pipe tobacco marketed under the Exclusiv name.

newminster-no-1-all-natural.z: One of the cavendish-forward numbered blends in the Newminster series; reportedly light in character and free of top flavoring, though sufficient independent sources detailing its composition could not be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-8th-street.z: 8th Street takes its name from the tobacco shop on 8th Street where the blend was originally prepared; it's carried on today among Wilke Pipe Tobacco's bulk aromatics. Structurally it's Burley-based; a small amount of Virginia and vanilla-flavored cavendish are added, topped with a light raspberry touch. Burley gives the blend a nutty, dry, full body while cavendish carries the sweet, creamy layer; the raspberry stays a subtle fruit hint that doesn't override the casing. Nicotine is measured, and the burn pace is steady. It's an everyday blend suited to smokers seeking a balance between casing and leaf character, who find full aromatics too sugary.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-8th-street.o: Leaves a sweet scent reminiscent of vanilla cream and red berries.

wesleys-no-41-fruit-flake.z: Fruit Flake is a ready-rubbed flake product among Wesley's house blends, made from pressed leaf rubbed out. According to the maker's description, it carries a strength a little above medium, with a barely perceptible fruit flavoring applied on top.
wesleys-no-41-fruit-flake.o: Leaves a lightly fruity scent dominated by dried leaf.

esoterica-tobacciana-blackpool.z: Blackpool sits in the flavored dark virginia wing of the Esoterica line, produced by J. F. Germain & Son in Jersey. It follows the British tradition of dark flake blends; per sources, the leaf is dark-colored, sugary on the surface, with a pronounced licorice echo. Retailer classifications list it in the aromatic family and as ribbon cut. The smoke is slow and cool, combining virginia's darkened sweetness with licorice's refreshing bitter tone. It suits those seeking a dark virginia that is flavored but not syrupy and not heavy on nicotine.
esoterica-tobacciana-blackpool.o: Leaves a sweetish scent reminiscent of licorice root and dark confection.

villiger-virginia-no-444.z: Virginia No. 444 is, according to records, a Villiger blend where a small amount of Oriental tobacco is added to Virginia and Burley leaves; no second independent source could be found confirming its composition.

pfeifen-huber-irish.z: Irish is an aromatic house blend Pfeifen Huber offers under its Selected Blend line. In the mixture, built from Virginia, black Cavendish, and Burley leaf, Cavendish makes up roughly a third of the blend; the flavoring is built around baked fruit, vanilla, and Irish whiskey. Its body is light, its taste fruity-sweet; the whiskey note leaves a spicy depth behind the topping, while vanilla stays fainter alongside the fruit. Because the cut packs easily, it burns evenly. It suits smokers who enjoy fruity, liquor-toned toppings and want a light-nicotine aromatic for all-day smoking.
pfeifen-huber-irish.o: Leaves a baked-fruit sweetness and a whiskey aroma.

tabac-turc-yayladag-latakia-flake.z: Yayladağ Latakia Flake was released as Tabac Turc's latakia-containing product. According to records, the blend is not a new recipe but a remake faithful to a formerly produced latakia mixture, with the original recipe's roughly 24 percent latakia content reduced in this product to a 10-15 percent range. Its content includes Yayladağı, Bitlis, and İzmir leaf along with latakia and cavendish, with honey, molasses, maple syrup, and rum casing. It comes as flake slices and is more vividly colored than other Yayladağ products, with yellow, red, dark brown, and black leaves distinguishable. Opening the pack, a smoky note and a distinct alcohol sharpness mix into the classic Yayladağ aroma. Being moist, it needs airing, tends to go out after the first light, and settles into an even burn after a few relights. Because the latakia content is kept low, the smoky taste doesn't dominate; Turkish tobacco's spicy, nose-tingling character is what defines it, with latakia running underneath and strengthening toward the bottom of the bowl. It is light in nicotine and medium-to-full in taste. It suits smokers who like latakia in moderation and are curious about the combination of domestic tobacco with smoky leaf.
tabac-turc-yayladag-latakia-flake.o: Leaves a heavy scent, combining a smoky note with sweet syrup, that lingers in the room for a long time.

mac-baren-hh-mature-virginia.z: HH Mature Virginia is, per the manufacturer, a Virginia-centered blend bringing together twenty-two separate leaves. Fifteen of these are Virginias matured through years of storage: light golden leaf, ripe red leaf, dark Virginia and black Virginia cavendish are blended together. A small amount of oriental is added to support flavor, and a small proportion of pressed burley rounds out the body. The product is presented as a ribbon cut. On the first light, Virginia sweetness leads, then the heavier, riper tone of the dark Virginias takes over. The ribbon cut burns slowly and evenly, leaving light-colored ash. Made for those seeking unflavored Virginia character and a blend suited to cellaring in the tin; its thick, sturdy packaging is well suited to long-term storage. Since the tobacco can arrive moist from the tin, airing it before packing eases the smoke.
mac-baren-hh-mature-virginia.o: Leaves a lightly tangy note reminiscent of dry hay and baked bread crust.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-chocolate.z: Referred to as a chocolate-flavored version within the Kendal Gold shag series; no reliable sourcing giving details specific to this version's composition and character could be found.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-chocolate.o: Leaves a cocoa and sweet tobacco aroma.

d-r-tobacco-english-hoopla.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the D & R Tobacco brand as English Hoopla; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

robert-mcconnell-red-virginia-mc.z: Red Virginia MC is counted among the brand's earliest blends, dating back to 1848. Red Virginia leaf forms the core; Perique is not a dominant component but a seasoning that adds sweet-tart fruit and spice. After pressing and cutting, the leaf is rubbed into broken flake, and a light cocoa flavoring supports Virginia's natural sugars. Flavor intensity is high and nicotine moderate. It suits smokers looking for a blend that puts Virginia character front and center while using Perique sparingly, as well as those who want a Virginia that ages well in the tin.
robert-mcconnell-red-virginia-mc.o: Leaves an aroma of dark bread, dried fruit, and a hint of cocoa.

gawith-hoggarth-co-american-blend-vanill.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s American Blend Vanilla blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

hu-tobacco-old-fredders-broken-flake.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the Old Fredder's Broken Flake blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

5ive-kings-5ive-kings.z: There is not enough available source material describing this blend's composition and character.

paul-olsen-vintage-flake.z: Vintage Flake is described as the sweetest, fullest-bodied blend in the Virginia flake line of the Danish Paul Olsen (My Own Blend) house. It consists of pressed and sliced Virginia leaves; it carries no flavoring, drawing its sweetness from the leaf's own sugar. Sources highlight its nutty sweetness and satisfying fullness, noting the taste intensifies in larger bowls. The blend suits smokers who want unflavored Virginia flavor and are accustomed to preparing flake; drying and rubbing out the slice, or folding it into the bowl, are the usual ways to pack it. The Paul Olsen house has kept up Copenhagen's tradition of personal blending since the 1930s, accumulating over ten thousand recipes in its archive; this flake line is among the small number of recipes taken into regular production. Its aging-friendly nature has led to dated tins being kept on record.
paul-olsen-vintage-flake.o: Leaves a lightly sweet trace leaning toward toasted bread and dry grass.

peterson-university-flake.z: University Flake is a flake blend of pressed and sliced Burley and Virginia that also contains dark Kentucky leaf. The slices come out of the tin at a smokable moisture level and can be packed either folded or rubbed out. Burley is distinctly forward in the blend, overshadowing Virginia's sweetness; the result is a tobacco that is strong in nicotine and intense in flavor. Given its flake structure, it suits slow, unhurried smoking rather than short smokes squeezed between tasks. It suits experienced smokers seeking a Burley-forward, full-bodied blend.
peterson-university-flake.o: Leaves a toasted bread and dark nut aroma.

james-fox-aromatic-loose.z: An aromatic blend sold loose by weight at the James J. Fox shop in Dublin; no source could be found to document its composition.

mac-baren-vanilla-cream-loose-cut.z: Vanilla Cream Loose Cut is the unpressed, loose-cut version of the same blend. The composition base doesn't change: matured Virginia and mild black Cavendish, with a silky vanilla topping over them. The difference is in the preparation form; instead of being sliced and rubbed out, the tobacco is packaged directly as loose cut. This structure eases packing into a pipe and lets the tobacco burn faster. How the flavoring shows itself also changes: the vanilla that unfolds slowly in the pressed version is pronounced here from the start of the smoke, while the leaf character stays a bit further back. Nicotine level is low. Suited to smokers seeking a hassle-free aromatic who want to prepare their pipe quickly, and to those new to the pipe.
mac-baren-vanilla-cream-loose-cut.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough aroma.

f-k-bat-with-a-hat.z: Bat With A Hat is one of the oddly named blends of the F & K brand, founded in St. Louis, Missouri in 1926; no detailed producer record describing its composition could be found.
f-k-bat-with-a-hat.o: Records do not contain enough information for a description.

ken-byron-ventures-burlier-morning-pipe.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Ken Byron Ventures' Burlier Morning Pipe blend.

the-seasons-harvesttime.z: No reliable source could be found on the Harvesttime blend from The Seasons series.

pipesandcigars-com-fiddlesticks.z: No sufficient sources were found documenting the content and character of pipesandcigars.com's blend Fiddlesticks.

golden-blend-tobacco-co-vanilla-no-1.z: No. 1 in the Golden Blend's series, this is an aromatic long sold as Vanilla and the series' best-known product. It is a Pöschl production from Bavaria. Its composition includes hand-selected Virginia and Burley leaf; the cut is an irregular-width "wild cut," which makes for airier bowl packing. It is offered in a 50-gram pouch as well as 100- and 200-gram tins. A pronounced vanilla topping sets the flavor line; beneath it sits Virginia's light sugar and Burley's dry, nutty base. It is the mildest member of the series: nicotine is low, the smoke is mild, and tongue bite stays limited. Because of this mildness, it suits both those new to the pipe and those seeking a low-intensity aromatic that can be smoked all day.
golden-blend-tobacco-co-vanilla-no-1.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough aroma.

briarworks-international-country-lawyer.z: Country Lawyer is BriarWorks's blend containing cigar leaf. It is built by adding some cigar leaf to Virginia, Oriental, fire-cured Kentucky and black cavendish leaves; no casing is applied to the blend. The flavor is full-bodied, spicy and earthy; cigar leaf adds a leather and toasted-walnut-leaning depth to the blend. Since the nicotine load is on the high side, it is not suited to smoking on an empty stomach or at a fast pace. Appeals to smokers who want to find cigar taste in a pipe and are accustomed to unflavored, heavy blends.
briarworks-international-country-lawyer.o: Leaves an earthy, spicy and leathery aroma reminiscent of a burning cigar.

jacks-tobacco-moose-scat.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of Jack's Tobacco's Moose Scat blend could be found.

planta-golden-vanilla.z: This is cited as a vanilla-flavored mixture bearing the Planta name; there is not enough independent source material on its content, cut, or production status.

clan-shaw-dr-thomas.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of Clan Shaw's Dr. Thomas blend could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-dark-obsession-b.z: Dark Obsession B38 is a Sutliff bulk aromatic built on black cavendish produced from American burley leaf. The blend is enriched with a combination of sweet spice and nut aromas; the dominant note is walnut, with a measured cinnamon sharpness behind it. The leaf is coarse-cut and jet black. The smoke is smooth and nicotine strength is light. A record for those seeking a nutty, spiced profile distinct from vanilla-heavy cavendish aromatics.
sutliff-tobacco-company-dark-obsession-b.o: Leaves a scent of roasted walnut and cinnamon.

sutliff-tobacco-company-strawberry-delig.z: SPS-2003 Strawberry Delight is a strong fruity aromatic in Sutliff's "Sutliff Private Stock" bulk line. The base is built from burley, Virginia, and black cavendish; the cut is ribbon. Strawberry takes the lead role in the casing, though cocoa, praline, and vanilla notes are also identified. The taste in the mouth and the scent it leaves in the room lean distinctly toward strawberry; the base leaves' own taste stays beneath this casing. Nicotine is on the low side. It suits smokers who enjoy heavily cased, sweet fruit aromatics; those used to unflavored blends may find its intensity heavy.
sutliff-tobacco-company-strawberry-delig.o: Leaves a pronounced scent of strawberry jam and sweet cocoa in the room.

cornell-diehl-sams-blend.z: Sam's Blend is a plainly built Latakia mixture composed of a trio of Cyprus Latakia, Louisiana Perique, and unsweetened black Cavendish. Its three-component recipe leaves out the Virginia-and-Oriental layers usual in Latakia blends. Black Cavendish gives the blend an unflavored softness and dark sweetness, Latakia builds the smoky backbone, and Perique adds a measured spice and fruit sharpness. The result is a medium-bodied, smooth-textured smoke; suited to those wanting to reach the smoky taste on a soft base, avoiding the sharpness of heavy English mixtures.
cornell-diehl-sams-blend.o: Leaves a wood-smoke scent over a soft, sweetish base.

samuel-gawith-black-cherry.z: Recorded, according to records, as a black-cavendish-based, cherry-flavored blend from Samuel Gawith; detailed content information could not be found in verifiable sources.
samuel-gawith-black-cherry.o: Leaves a sweet scent evoking cherry.

intertabak-black-cavendish-374.z: No verifiable source could be found for this bulk Cavendish registered under the INTERTABAK name.

rattray-summer-edition-2019.z: Summer Edition 2019 is the nautically themed installment of the summer series Kohlhase & Kopp prepares for Rattray; the tin design references Charles Rattray's interest in the sea. The blend's body is built from high-sugar golden Virginia and broken Virginia added for a cooler burn; black Cavendish carries the sweetness. Watermelon and honey are used as the top note, making the blend a refreshing summer aromatic. With low-to-medium nicotine, it suits long, daytime smoking sessions. It is designed more for smokers drawn to fruity aromatics than those looking for natural Virginia taste. Being a limited annual edition, it is not in current production.
rattray-summer-edition-2019.o: Leaves a cool, sweet aroma reminiscent of juicy watermelon and honey.

sutliff-tobacco-company-royal-champagne.z: Royal Champagne (also listed in catalogs simply as Champagne) is one of the light aromatics in Sutliff's bulk line. Quality Virginias are combined with sweet black cavendish; a fine, fruity bouquet giving the blend its name is applied over it. The cut is ribbon. The casing is not intense but a subtle layer, which is why the blend is classed as a "light aromatic." Nicotine is low and the taste is soft, aimed at aromatic smokers who avoid heavily sugared blends. Champagne is one of Sutliff's registered blend names.
sutliff-tobacco-company-royal-champagne.o: Leaves a light fruity, floral, and cool scent.

hu-tobacco-joschis-oriental-sunrise.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Joschi's Oriental Sunrise, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

cornell-diehl-epiphany.z: Epiphany is a reinterpretation referencing Philip Morris's now-discontinued Revelation blend. It was developed by burley specialist Bob Runowski together with Craig Tarler: a nutty burley base, sweet Virginia, smoky Latakia, and sharp perique are brought together, topped with a light dark-fruit-like flavoring. The character recalls old-style American mixtures; the flavoring is kept light enough not to overwhelm the natural leaf tastes. It suits smokers looking for a classic American blend with measured Latakia and a light touch of sweetening.
cornell-diehl-epiphany.o: Leaves a lightly smoky, nutty room aroma mixed with dried-fruit sweetness.

watch-city-cigar-bada-bing.z: Bada-Bing! is a broadly cut aromatic blend the Watch City Cigar shop of Waltham, Massachusetts prepares under its own name. Its base is built from black and golden cavendish leaves, topped with a tart black-cherry casing. According to the maker's description, roughly a fifth of the blend is St. James Perique, adding a peppery, plum-leaning body that sets it apart from typical cherry aromatics. According to records, the blend returned to the shop's bulk shelves after being out of production for years due to a component becoming unavailable. It's an option aimed at smokers who like cavendish sweetness but find plain aromatics too flat, wanting a bit of spice and body; it's not heavy in nicotine.
watch-city-cigar-bada-bing.o: Leaves a lightly spicy, plummy trace beneath a sweet black-cherry scent.

pfeifen-huber-virginia-finest-virginia.z: Finest Virginia is an unflavored blend in Pfeifen Huber's Virginia line. Presented as a long-fibered, loose-cut mixture, the tobacco is built from selected, soft, pale golden Virginia leaf; it contains no other tobacco type or added flavoring. Its character stays true to pure Virginia style: natural leaf sugars come to the fore, the body sits between light and medium, and the smoke carries a dry freshness. The long-fiber cut helps it burn evenly, though bite typical of Virginias can appear if it isn't smoked slowly. It suits smokers who want an unflavored Virginia, a light blend for morning or midday smoking, and those interested in watching how a Virginia ages.
pfeifen-huber-virginia-finest-virginia.o: Leaves a plain tobacco aroma leaning toward dry hay and honey sweetness.

paul-olsen-best-blend-4.z: A blend in the Poul Olsen shop's Best Blend series, recorded as straight Virginia-based; not enough source material documenting its details could be found.

tabac-turc-yayladag-vanilyali.z: Officially named Yayladağ No. 2, but commonly called Yayladağ Vanilyalı (Vanilla), this is one of Tabac Turc's flavored Oriental products. Its content is made up of Yayladağı, Bitlis, and İzmir leaf, cased with vanilla, molasses, honey, and alcohol. It is described as a coarse cut, though the cut lengths are uneven and the blend has a high stem content. Because a heavy humectant is used, the tobacco arrives stuck together in a mass in the pack; once separated, its color fades within a few hours and it dries out quickly. Opening the pack releases an amber, spicy, fruity scent; as it dries, a synthetic vanilla note overtakes the other elements. Once dried, the tobacco is hard to remoisten. It lights slowly on the first pack but burns evenly once lit; the bowl heats up quickly, though without causing tongue bite. The smoke fills the mouth heavily but lacks body. Nicotine is light, and the taste is low in intensity. It stands out for its flavoring and the scent it gives off in the room; it is a blend more likely to be encountered by those wanting to try heavily flavored domestic products than by those seeking an unflavored tobacco taste.
tabac-turc-yayladag-vanilyali.o: Leaves a sharp, sweet scent reminiscent of synthetic vanilla and ready-made pastry that fills the room.

ash-ember-absolute-midnight.z: No adequate independent source verifying the content of Absolute Midnight, hand-blended by the Ash & Ember shop in Siloam Springs, Arkansas, could be found.
ash-ember-absolute-midnight.o: No reliable information on the room note could be found.

paul-olsen-red-caledonian.z: Referred to as one of the aromatic house blends from the Paul Olsen house; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found.

kramers-pipe-and-tobacco-shop-extra-smoo.z: Not enough independent sources could be reached to fill out the record for Kramer's Pipe and Tobacco Shop's blend called Extra Smooth.

e-a-carey-careys-bruno-special.z: Not enough sourcing exists to describe the composition and character of this tobacco, counted among the special blends E. A. Carey offers in the US.
e-a-carey-careys-bruno-special.o: Could not be described due to insufficient records.

port-williams-blue.z: This is the member of the Port Williams line referred to as aromatic; no source could be found documenting its content.

century-black-spice.z: A blend in the Century line whose name suggests a spice aroma; no sufficient independent source could be found.

brebbia-calvados-mixture-no-11.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named Calvados (Mixture No. 11) under the Brebbia brand could be found.

thompson-cigar-co-no-777-amaretto.z: The amaretto-flavored variety in Thompson Cigar's No. 777 series, sold only through the company's own catalog and offered in half-pound bags. Since the leaf composition is not disclosed by the retailer, the record is left incomplete.
thompson-cigar-co-no-777-amaretto.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of almond liqueur.

bennington-tobacconist-no-45-richs-blend.z: No. 45, Rich's Blend is Bennington's chocolate version built on the same body as No. 31 Donegal. Black, twice-heat-fermented Burley from the Green River region is pressed long-cut and rested; golden Virginia ribbon and Virginia flake are added along with a generous amount of air-cured, fermented Kentucky Burley. The topping that gives the blend its name is imported Swiss chocolate, added at the final stage. This topping thickens the tobacco's natural nutty and sweet sides toward cocoa, but since the structure stays Burley-heavy, it doesn't turn into a syrupy aromatic. The maker states the blend is smokable all day and doesn't bite the tongue. It suits smokers looking for a lightly flavored aromatic with body.
bennington-tobacconist-no-45-richs-blend.o: Warm cocoa and toasted-sugar notes are joined by a dry hazelnut note.

peterson-founders-choice.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of Peterson's Founder's Choice blend could be found; it is reportedly an aromatic blend.

poschl-tabak-hansa-krull.z: Hansa Krüll is the first line the Bavaria-based house Pöschl Tabak released in pipe tobacco. The blend is made by combining Virginia leaf of American and Java origin with other imported tobaccos, with no flavoring applied afterward; its taste comes from the tobacco's own character. Its medium-fine cut makes it easy to pack and suitable for mixing with other blends. It is a product for smokers looking for an unflavored everyday tobacco, and one that home blenders can consider as a base tobacco for their own mixtures. Pöschl continues production today.
poschl-tabak-hansa-krull.o: Leaves an unflavored tobacco aroma reminiscent of dry hay and burning leaf.

motzek-burleys-best-friend.z: Since neither the manufacturer's own description nor two independent reliable sources could be found for the Motzek blend called Burley's Best (Friend), its composition, cut, and character could not be documented here.

mike-russ-the-mind-meld-full-latakia.z: The Latakia-forward member of the Mind Meld line, born from the collaboration of Mike McNiel and Russ Ouellette; sufficient sources regarding the blend's detailed composition could not be found.
mike-russ-the-mind-meld-full-latakia.o: Leaves an intense wood-smoke and soot aroma.

clan-shaw-mountain.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Mountain.

old-morris-papeete.z: Papeete is an aromatic blend sold under its own name by Old Morris Tobacconist of Victoria, Canada. Its base is pressed, broad-cut cavendish leaf, topped with a tropical-fruit-character essence. Per the maker's recipe, the smoke is meant to be light, aimed at a structure that avoids tongue bite. In character it's a tobacco with low nicotine load, moderate flavor intensity, and pronounced flavoring. It suits those seeking mellow, cavendish-forward aromatics, those wanting a light blend smokable all day, and newcomers to the pipe. Old Morris, a tobacconist's shop dating back to 1892, continues selling blends under its own name.
old-morris-papeete.o: Leaves a scent of sweet tropical fruit and sugared melon.

pipesandcigars-com-the-taxman-cometh.z: This is a blend offered under the American retailer pipesandcigars.com's name; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

smokers-haven-mild-mellow.z: Mild & Mellow is a plainly built American mixture Smokers' Haven sells in bulk. Per the maker's description, cube-cut Kentucky burley forms the body, with just a touch of Syrian latakia added on top. Latakia here is not a direction-setting element but a secondary component adding a light smoke layer to burley's dry, nutty taste.
smokers-haven-mild-mellow.o: A thin trace of wood smoke mixes into a dry, nutty burley scent.

pcca-boston-1996.z: Boston is one of the limited-run tins PCCA (the Pipe Collectors Club of America) had McClelland produce for club members. The first entry in the series appeared in 1993 as a 1776-tin edition, and the Boston name was reused in later years with the date changed. Records indicate the blend is a flake made of high-grade bright red and yellow Virginia leaf, with roughly three percent Turkish leaf added. As an unflavored Virginia it gives a bready, herbal taste that deepens into sweetness over time; the small share of oriental leaf adds a spicy edge. The flake form gives a slow, cool burn and rewards resting. Because PCCA tins came out in small runs of 300-400, it survives today only in collections; with McClelland's closure in 2018, the blend is no longer in production.
pcca-boston-1996.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay and baked bread.

john-patton-gold-nugget-mixture.z: One of the small-scale blends released under the John Patton name; not enough independent sources could be found to document its contents and character.
john-patton-gold-nugget-mixture.o: No source could be found on the room note.

bennington-tobacconist-no-50-sheriff.z: No. 50 Sheriff is one of Bennington Tobacconist's Cavendish-centered shop blends. Its base is golden Cavendish, with a small amount of fire-cured black Cavendish added. The maker states the blend is one of the shop's best-selling mixtures. Golden Cavendish sets a sweet, mellow base, while the fire-cured leaf lays a thin layer of smoke and wood under that sweetness. This pairing sets the blend apart from a flat sugar profile, without letting smoke dominate as it does in English mixtures. It suits smokers looking for a mellow tobacco with a pronounced sweet side, while avoiding blends that are entirely flavoring-driven.
bennington-tobacconist-no-50-sheriff.o: Burnt sugar and caramel notes are joined by a thin line of woodsmoke.

connoisseur-scottish-ribbon.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Connoisseur blend Scottish Ribbon.

samuel-gawith-special-flake-no-7.z: No sufficient source documenting the composition of this sliced tobacco in Samuel Gawith's numbered Special Flake series could be found.

kadewe-mischung-no-40.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for KaDeWe's Mischung No.40, so the profile is left incomplete.

hearth-home-american-heritage.z: American Heritage is a blend in Russ Ouellette's Hearth & Home series that combines American Burley tradition with English blending sensibility. Its composition includes aged Burley leaf, red Virginia, Turkish tobacco, and Latakia. Burley forms the blend's backbone; red Virginia adds sweetness, Turkish tobacco adds spice, and Latakia adds a measured layer of smoke. It smokes cool, spicy but light overall. Since the Latakia ratio is kept low, it stays approachable even for those unaccustomed to the smoke of heavier English mixtures. Being on the light side for nicotine, it suits all-day smoking; it serves as a stepping stone for smokers wanting to move from Burley-based blends toward Latakia.
hearth-home-american-heritage.o: A nutty, dry tobacco aroma accompanies a light wood-smoke scent.

peter-stokkebye-gold.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Gold in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

cornell-diehl-black-duck.z: Black Duck is a ribbon-cut English mixture where burley and black cavendish are set atop Latakia and Oriental leaf. Using burley rather than Virginia as the base sets the blend apart from most English mixtures: the sweetness comes from a nutty, earthy place rather than a fruity one. Black cavendish adds a round layer that softens Latakia's smoke. In strength it sits between medium and hearty, with flavor intensity above its strength. It shows a structure where the layers shift through the bowl, with Latakia not staying constantly in front. Because of its moist cut, it is sensitive to packing and lighting habits. It suits smokers who want smoke and spice but prefer a burley body over Virginia sweetness.
cornell-diehl-black-duck.o: A light sweet undertone accompanies an aroma of wood smoke and spiced Oriental.

paul-olsen-condor.z: One of the Poul Olsen house blends; it should not be confused with the identically named English Condor brand. Not enough source material describing its composition could be found.

dan-tobacco-perfect-blend.z: M.A. Perfect Blend is an aromatic blend in Dan Tobacco's Michael Apitz-signed series. Virginia leaf is combined with black Cavendish, topped with a vanilla-leaning casing. It's ribbon cut and distributed in 100-gram tins. Black Cavendish gives the blend dark color, softness, and natural sweetness, while Virginia carries the body and coolness. Nicotine sits between mild and medium. Suited to smokers looking for a classic vanilla aromatic who don't want the casing to fully mask the tobacco.
dan-tobacco-perfect-blend.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough scent.

jerris-tobacco-shop-denver-co-honey-nut.z: No reliable source documenting the content and character of Jerri's Tobacco Shop Denver, CO's Honey Nut blend could be found.

samuel-gawith-brown-rope-no-4-whiskey.z: Brown Rope No. 4 Whiskey is the whiskey-cased version of Samuel Gawith's thick rope series. Virginia-and-burley-based leaf is twisted into rope, and a whiskey-based casing is applied during aging. It is sold in wheel form; slice and crumble to use. The casing leaves a light grain-and-oak tone, with the tobacco's dark body leading; nicotine load is high. Suited to smokers accustomed to rope preparation and strong smoke.
samuel-gawith-brown-rope-no-4-whiskey.o: Leaves a scent of whiskey and oak over dark tobacco.

orlik-black-diamond.z: Black Diamond is one of the tinned aromatic blends from Danish Orlik. Virginia, cavendish, burley, and Turkish leaf are used together; the cut is ribbon. It's given a moderate liqueur-and-alcohol-direction topping. The blend offers a very light-nicotine, cool, sweet smoke; records indicate its cavendish content carries most of the taste. It has an even, clean burn. It's a blend aimed at those who love mild, sweet Danish-style aromatics rather than those seeking Latakia or a full-bodied Virginia.
orlik-black-diamond.o: Leaves a scent of sweet liqueur and sugared cavendish on a warm base.

warped-until-the-end.z: Until the End consists of shade-grown Ecuadorian cigar leaf, light Virginia, cavendish made from cigar leaf, and specially selected dark-fired Kentucky leaf. Offered as broken flake, the blend shows notes of nut, bitter chocolate, and coffee grounds with citrus traces; on the retrohale, a peppery spice emerges. Body runs medium to full, with a dry, rustic character.
warped-until-the-end.o: Leaves a dark scent reminiscent of wood smoke, roasted coffee, and cigar leaf.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-sail-yello.z: Match Sail Yellow is a blend modeled after the yellow-packaged plain version of the Dutch-origin Sail brand. Oriental and Brazilian leaf are added to a burley and Virginia base, producing a soft mixture carrying tones reminiscent of honey and bread. Its body is light, nicotine is low, and it burns cool. It suits smokers who don't want a heavy casing and are looking for a plain mixture they can smoke all day, and those used to light Dutch-style blends.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-sail-yello.o: Leaves a scent of honey and fresh bread.

samuel-gawith-special-flake-no-1.z: No sufficient source documenting the composition of this sliced tobacco in Samuel Gawith's numbered Special Flake series could be found.

stanwell-vanilla-sungold.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Stanwell brand's Vanilla (Sungold) blend could not be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-ts18-latakia.z: TS-18 is the pure latakia product Sutliff offers as a blending component. According to the maker's description, it is prepared from long-cut latakia leaves, with a dark casing applied that sweetens and darkens the tobacco. Since latakia is an Oriental leaf cured with fire and smoke, its character comes entirely from that curing process. The smoke carries a very intense taste leaning toward tar and leather; nicotine stays at a medium level. Rather than being smoked alone, it is used to add a smoky layer to English and Balkan-type mixtures. It is one of the essential components for smokers preparing their own blends.
sutliff-tobacco-company-ts18-latakia.o: Leaves a scent of campfire smoke, tar, and dried leather.

ravenwood-fine-provisions-dread-pirate-r.z: Dread Pirate Roberts is the Virginia-Perique entry in the Ravenwood Fine Provisions line. It is described as a "navy" ribbon built from red Virginia and Perique; the cut is thin strips. The blender's flavor description lists medium-full red Virginia leaf, warmed Perique spice, and a semi-sweet malty beer and barley note. Flavoring is nearly nonexistent; the sweetness comes from the leaf itself. It suits smokers who want the pepper-dark fruit character Perique brings together with Virginia's tart sweetness, and who steer clear of aromatics.
ravenwood-fine-provisions-dread-pirate-r.o: Leaves a mixed tobacco aroma with tart dark fruit and malty beer.

dobies-dobies-four-square-aromatic.z: The Four Square series was launched in 1922 by George Dobie & Son, based in Paisley; in later generations, blending moved first to Denmark and then to the United States. Aromatic represents the flavored branch of the series. Since no independent source detailing the leaves used and the aroma composition could be found, the record has been kept limited.

pipesandcigars-com-royal-blunder-kake.z: Royal Blunder Kake is one of the blends the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com sells under its own name; there is not enough independent source material documenting its content and character.

mcclelland-frog-morton-on-the-town.z: Frog Morton on the Town is an English blend derived by adding Basma-type Oriental leaf to the main blend's Virginia-Latakia body. Since Basma thickens the smoke and gives it a creamy texture, the blend is positioned as the series' rounder, less sharp member. The ribbon cut gives a cool, even burn. Despite containing Latakia, nicotine load runs below medium; suited to those seeking a structure where soot and sweetness are balanced. Like the other series members, discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-frog-morton-on-the-town.o: Leaves a mild soot aroma along with dry hay and nut notes.

john-aylesbury-dragon-blend.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to document the contents and character of John Aylesbury's Dragon Blend.

mcclelland-no-401-darkest-caramel.z: A caramel-flavored blend presented as the dark-leaf-forward counterpart to No. 400 in McClelland's numbered bulk aromatic series; no sufficient source documenting its composition could be found.

watch-city-cigar-the-4th-nun-returns.z: According to records, this is a later version of Watch City Cigar's seasonal blend The 4th Nun; no independent source could be found documenting its composition and character.
watch-city-cigar-the-4th-nun-returns.o: No description could be found as no source was available.

mullingar-kenmare.z: One of the now-discontinued Latakia-containing blends from the Irish Mullingar brand; no independent source confirming its composition could be found.

thepiperoom-com-irish-cream.z: An aromatic blend the online retailer ThePipeRoom.com offers under its own name, apparently Irish-cream-themed as its name suggests; no independent source on its composition or production status has been found.
thepiperoom-com-irish-cream.o: Records describe it as leaving an aroma reminiscent of sweet cream and liqueur.

cobblestone-camping.z: A Virginia-heavy, ribbon-cut blend belonging to Cobblestone's Outdoors series; not enough independent sourcing could be found for detailed composition information.

schurch-rubino-363.z: Rubino 363, signed by Schürch, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

briarworks-international-back-down-south.z: Back Down South is a Virginia-Perique leaf in the small-batch series Tennessee-based BriarWorks has Cornell & Diehl manufacture. The blend, pairing Virginias with perique, is pressed into flake form and offered in a two-ounce glass jar; this packaging suits long aging of the leaf. In the flavor profile, fig and dark-chocolate echoes come forward along with the light peppery spice perique gives. No casing is used; the sweetness comes entirely from the Virginia's own sugar. The body is medium, flavor medium-to-full. A blend aimed at those accustomed to opening and drying out flake, expecting an intense smoke from the unflavored Virginia-Perique lane.
briarworks-international-back-down-south.o: Leaves a warm, lightly spicy aroma carrying dried fig and cocoa sweetness.

reiner-light-aromatic-blend.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of Reiner Light Aromatic Blend.

robert-mcconnell-red-virginia.z: As its name suggests, Red Virginia is a ribbon-cut blend built on red Virginia leaf with a small amount of Perique added. Its suitable moisture level and fine cut let it light easily; it is light enough to smoke in any pipe size at any time of day. On the flavor side there is tart red fruit, particularly a note reminiscent of lightly cooked strawberry jam, with an occasional chocolatey sweetness. Perique adds a touch of pepper and tang. It does not offer much shift in taste or coolness through the bowl; strength and flavor stay in the mild range. The ash is light-colored and clean. It suits smokers looking for a mild, low-nicotine, fruity Virginia.
robert-mcconnell-red-virginia.o: Leaves a soft aroma of tart red fruit and light chocolate sweetness.

tewksbury-company-rum-raisin.z: According to records, this blend was part of the lineup of Tewksbury & Company, an American blender that ceased operations following the 2009 tobacco regulation; no source documenting its content and character could be found.

kirsten-pipe-company-mariner-mixture.z: One of the aromatic blends sold under its own name by Seattle-based aluminum pipe manufacturer Kirsten Pipe Company; no source could be found describing its composition.
kirsten-pipe-company-mariner-mixture.o: No verifiable information could be found regarding its scent.

cornell-diehl-yorktown.z: Yorktown is an unflavored Virginia blend. Per the maker's description, stoved red Virginia is combined with bright Virginia and put through the steaming process again; plain red Virginia is then added on top of this base for sweetness. The result is a dark-colored, heavily sugared ribbon cut. Thanks to the double-processed leaf, flavor deepens toward dark fruit, molasses, and bread crust, with tartness staying in the background. It contains no Latakia, Perique, or any casing. Aimed at smokers looking for single-varietal Virginia blends and the taste of dark, stoved leaf.
cornell-diehl-yorktown.o: Leaves a heavy, sweet tobacco scent reminiscent of dark dried fruit and cooked sugar.

peterson-sweet-killarney.z: Sweet Killarney is an aromatic built on a Virginia-forward body with black Cavendish added; the blend reportedly also contains Burley and Maryland leaf. It carries a topping of cream and caramel notes, giving the tobacco a pronounced sweetness. Its strength is low and the smoke is mild. It suits smokers who enjoy sweet, milky aromatics as well as newcomers to the pipe. The blend's name comes from the town of Killarney in Ireland and it is part of Peterson's aromatic line, which references the brand's Irish identity.
peterson-sweet-killarney.o: Leaves a creamy caramel and sugared milk aroma.

peter-heinrichs-no-211.z: No. 211 is an English-type blend that stands out for its high Latakia proportion within the Cologne-based house Peter Heinrichs' self-titled series. Per the maker's description, the mixture's backbone is built from smoky Latakia; Oriental leaf, which adds a spicy twist, Virginia, which provides sweetness and softness, and Java leaf, which adds earthy depth, join it. The ribbon cut gives a packing that lights easily and burns evenly. The flavor profile is built on a smoky, salty core, with Virginia's light sugar tone audible in the background. Since nicotine and fullness stay at medium levels, the blend suits smokers familiar with classic Latakia-forward English mixtures who are seeking an unflavored, dry smoke. For those coming from flavored blends, the room note forms a noticeable transition.
peter-heinrichs-no-211.o: Leaves a sharp room aroma recalling smoke, pine tar, and dry wood smoke.

sutliff-tobacco-company-mellow-and-mild-.z: This is one of Sutliff's numbered blends sold in bulk. Nutty burley, golden cavendish made from Virginia leaf, and dark black cavendish are brought together; a measured vanilla and hazelnut essence is drawn over them. The cut is ribbon and the leaf's moisture is medium. As its name suggests, it is an aromatic light in nicotine and soft in taste; the casing is noticeable but doesn't fully mask the tobacco taste. It falls within the interest of those new to aromatics and those looking for a low-strength blend they can smoke all day.
sutliff-tobacco-company-mellow-and-mild-.o: Leaves a scent of warm vanilla and roasted hazelnut.

ken-byron-ventures-retro-mancer.z: Recorded as an English-type mixture modeled on the heavy latakia blends of the 1960s-70s; no adequate independent source could be found to confirm its proportions and composition.

hearth-home-scots-delight.z: Scot's Delight is a whiskey-flavored aromatic in Hearth & Home's Signature line. Some black Cavendish is added to a base formed by Burley and Virginia; the whiskey essence applied on top sits as a thin layer over the leaf's aroma rather than creating a heavy flavor layer. The Cavendish-processed cut contributes to the blend's mild, balanced burn. Because nicotine intensity stays below moderate, even those unaccustomed to strong blends can smoke it comfortably. It's an option prepared for smokers who find the pronounced alcohol emphasis of whiskey blends too much and want the flavoring in the background. Records indicate the Hearth & Home brand that produced this blend is no longer in operation today.
hearth-home-scots-delight.o: Leaves a toasted-leaf aroma mixed with light whiskey and sweet oak.

mac-baren-mixture-aromatic.z: Mixture Aromatic is Mac Baren's classic blend, distributed under the name Danish Mixture in some markets. Per the manufacturer's description, ready-rubbed Virginia and Burley leaves are combined with loose-cut Virginia and a pinch of the brand's own Original Mac Baren Cavendish. This structure gives the blend both an easy-packing loose texture and a soft sweetness from the cavendish. In the smoke, Virginia's sweet and Burley's dry, nutty sides come forward; the added flavor stays in the background without masking the tobacco. An extension of the Mixture family Mac Baren launched in 1958, this blend suits smokers looking for a middle step between heavy aromatics and natural tobacco blends and wanting a measured tobacco to smoke all day.
mac-baren-mixture-aromatic.o: Leaves a moderate tobacco note along with a sweetish vanilla and light caramel scent.

faders-swiss-chocolate.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for the Fader's brand's Swiss Chocolate pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

sutliff-tobacco-company-china-black-whis.z: China Black Whiskey is the whiskey-flavored member of Sutliff's China Black line, built on fire-cured dark leaf; a second independent source detailing its composition and character in depth could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-china-black-whis.o: Records did not provide sufficient information for a description.

ashton-celebrated-sovereign.z: Celebrated Sovereign is Ashton's modern English-style mixture produced during the McClelland era. The blend is built on Virginia leaf, Syrian Latakia, Turkish-Oriental tobaccos, and black Cavendish; records note it as one of the few blends to use Syrian Latakia. Its draw is easy, and the smoke is plentiful and spicy; Latakia sets a woody, smoky base while the Orientals bring sharpness, and Virginias carry a balancing sweetness. It has a structure well suited to resting. It's of interest to smokers looking for classic English mixtures containing Syrian Latakia; production stopped after McClelland closed.
ashton-celebrated-sovereign.o: Leaves an intense, woody, smoky room note characteristic of Syrian Latakia.

blenders-gold-burley-and-black.z: Burley and Black is an aromatic blend from the Blender's Gold line that brings together Burley and black Cavendish. The line was produced in the United States by Sutliff and sold for a long time under its own brand on drugstore-chain shelves; the same tobaccos were also packaged under other store brands. Burley gives the blend its body and nutty, dry base, while the black Cavendish adds sweetness and moisture. It carries a light, vanilla-leaning topping, comes in an easy-packing ribbon cut, and smokes cool. It's built for smokers looking for an everyday, inexpensive, mild aromatic.
blenders-gold-burley-and-black.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-grain room note.

cobblestone-kahlua.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Cobblestone pipe tobacco named Kahlua, so the blend's content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-westminst.z: No independent source describing the content and cut of this blend, referred to as an English-style mixture, could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-westminst.o: Recorded as leaving a woody, smoky scent.

rona-obester-vanilla.z: A pipe tobacco recorded in Rona's Obester series, classified, as its name suggests, as vanilla-flavored; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

cornell-diehl-king-cake.z: King Cake is a pressed blend in Cornell & Diehl's aging-focused Cellar Series, first released in summer 2016. It takes its name from the king cake dessert of New Orleans' Mardi Gras tradition; per the maker, the celebration period begins with Epiphany on January 6th. Its composition includes Virginia, black Cavendish, Oriental tobaccos, and Perique. The maker places the blend in the aromatic family; most of the sweetness comes from the Cavendish, while Perique and Oriental tobacco build a spicy background. Nicotine load is kept low. Records indicate it reaches its best point in aging between ten and fifteen years, placing it among the light aromatics taken for cellaring.
cornell-diehl-king-cake.o: Leaves a scent of sweet Cavendish and lightly spiced Oriental tobacco.

e-a-carey-caribbean-flake.z: This is on record as a Virginia-based, flake-cut blend under the E. A. Carey name; no source could be found documenting its composition and character.

paul-olsen-no-47.z: One of the Virginia-and-burley-based blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

villiger-mid-day.z: Villiger's blend called Mid-Day is referred to in records as aromatic; no reliable source could be found documenting its composition and character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-ts1y-yellow-virg.z: TS1Y Yellow Virginia is a member of Sutliff's straight-leaf series. It contains only bright yellow, top-grade Virginia leaf; no flavoring whatsoever is applied. Because bright Virginia's natural sugar content is high, the tobacco gives an unsmoked sweetness, a light citrus tartness, and a hay-like dryness. The cut is ribbon, making it easy both to smoke alone and to blend in measured amounts. The blend is meaningful for two kinds of readers. First, smokers who want to explore straight Virginia's plain taste by smoking it slowly; second, those building their own blends who need a sweet base leaf. Nicotine is medium-light, but like all bright Virginias it tends toward tongue bite when smoked fast, so it should be kept dry and not puffed hard. Records show Sutliff was founded in 1849 and is today an American company producing in Richmond, Virginia.
sutliff-tobacco-company-ts1y-yellow-virg.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay and sweet straw with a light trace of bread crust.

house-of-calabash-lord-cravens-cigar-ble.z: This is a blend in House of Calabash's Lord Craven's Private Reserve line, described as cigar-leaf-forward; no verifiable source describing its content could be found.

rain-city-cigar-emerald-city-light.z: This is a house blend from Rain City Cigar, open since 1997 in Seattle's Georgetown neighborhood; there is not enough source material describing its composition and character.

cornell-diehl-after-hours-flake.z: Cornell & Diehl After Hours Flake is a pressed tobacco built on a pure Virginia base, staying close to the naval flake tradition. Naturally high-sweetness Virginia leaves are lightly enriched with dark rum, then pressed and sliced; the flavoring is kept at a level that doesn't mask the leaf's own caramel-like sweetness. The slices are smoked either rubbed out or folded into the bowl; they draw a slow-burning, bready, caramel-leaning taste, with the rum's spiced trace staying in the background. It suits smokers interested in Virginia flakes who want a lightly flavored blend that doesn't quite count as aromatic.
cornell-diehl-after-hours-flake.o: Leaves a caramel-bread aroma in the room, topped with a light dark-rum and spice scent.

garfinkels-ridgeway.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of Garfinkel's Ridgeway pipe tobacco could be found.

house-of-windsor-bourbon-street.z: Bourbon Street is a semi-aromatic blend made up of a combination of nutty Burley, sweet and tart Virginia, fire-cured Kentucky leaf, and black Cavendish. Kentucky adds a smoky, earthy depth while Cavendish establishes a sweet base; the top flavoring applied over these is measured and leans close to old-style aromatic sensibility. Records indicate the product was previously on the market under the name Bond Street. With House of Windsor's closure, production of the original blend ended; match products prepared by other makers exist today. It suits smokers looking for a lightly flavored mixture where tobacco taste stays in front, rather than heavily syrupy aromatics.
house-of-windsor-bourbon-street.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly smoky aroma with a dried-fruit tone lingering behind it.

chieftain-stormy-skye.z: The Chieftain blend Stormy Skye is referred to in available records as an aromatic; not enough sourcing could be found to document its content and character.
chieftain-stormy-skye.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-pilgrims-.z: There is not enough independent documentation on The Country Squire Tobacconist pipe tobacco called Pilgrim's Muse to record the blend's composition and character.

wolfway-red-summer-cherry.z: Red Summer is Wolfway's cherry-flavored blend. According to the maker's stated composition, Izmir-type Oriental from the Katerini region predominates, with Maryland-grown golden Virginia, Green River Burley from Kentucky, and a very small amount of Latakia added. Dark cherry dominates the tin note, while in the smoke the flavoring is kept restrained enough not to override the natural tobacco taste. It suits those seeking an Oriental-based, lightly flavored blend.
wolfway-red-summer-cherry.o: Leaves a scent of ripe dark-cherry sweetness with a faint trace of tobacco.

rattray-7-reserve.z: 7 Reserve is a light-bodied English blend from the brand in which Virginia leaf is worked with a generous amount of Oriental tobacco, with a small amount of Latakia added. Black tobacco particles are visible within the overall dark brown-red appearance; moisture runs high straight from the tin, so airing before packing helps regulate the burn. The ribbon cut lights easily, doesn't overheat even with heavy smoking, and doesn't wet the inside of the pipe. The dominant color in the taste is the Oriental leaf's spicy side; sweet Virginia builds a plain ground underneath, and Latakia remains as a cooling trace. It sits in a line close to the same maker's Red Rapparee, but noticeably lighter. It suits smokers looking for an all-day English blend that leaves a clean ash.
rattray-7-reserve.o: Leaves an intense wood-smoke and smoky-leather aroma.

cornell-diehl-mixture-monster.z: No adequate source documenting the composition and character of Cornell & Diehl's Mixture Monster blend could be found; the blend isn't in the maker's current catalogue.

ken-byron-ventures-verge-engine-overdriv.z: Recorded as the 2022 edition of Verge Engine Overdrive, Virginia-and-perique-axis; not enough independent sources could be found to document its contents.
ken-byron-ventures-verge-engine-overdriv.o: No reliable record could be found regarding the room note.

gawith-hoggarth-co-american-blend-coffee.z: Coffee Caramel is the coffee-and-caramel-flavoured record within Kendal's Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s American Blend line; in recent years it has been listed in some markets under the name "American C&C." It contains Virginia, burley, and black cavendish, is ribbon cut, and is noted to burn slowly. The flavouring is pronounced and the nicotine level is low; it is a blend aimed at those who enjoy sweet aromatics.
gawith-hoggarth-co-american-blend-coffee.o: Leaves an aroma of milky coffee and burnt sugar.

von-eicken-kapt-n-barsdorfs-dark-fired-p.z: The Dark Fired version of the Käpt'n Barsdorf's Bester line sits on Von Eicken's unflavored side. The composition rests on a measured pairing of dark-fired Kentucky with Virginia leaf. Unlike the series' flavored members, the taste here comes directly from the leaf itself. Dark-fired Kentucky lends the smoke soot, peppery spice and a thick body; the Virginia sets a bready sweetness beneath that weight to balance the blend. Nicotine is notably higher than the rest of the series. Suited to smokers used to unflavored, full-bodied tobaccos who are after Kentucky character.
von-eicken-kapt-n-barsdorfs-dark-fired-p.o: Leaves a sharp, smoky aroma reminiscent of wood-fire-cured leaf.

my-smoking-shop-gentlemans-choice.z: Gentleman's Choice is one of the bulk blends English tobacconist My Smoking Shop prepares under its own name. Virginia leaves of varying color and ripeness are combined with Burley; no heavy sauce is used. It is ribbon cut and, with its balanced moisture, packs easily. Virginia's bready sweetness meets Burley's dry, nutty body in the middle; the result is a medium-strength smoke suited to being smoked throughout the day. Suitable for smokers looking for a plain, unflavored, everyday blend in the English-American tradition.
my-smoking-shop-gentlemans-choice.o: Leaves a dry-hay and nutty tobacco aroma.

pipe-republic-ashford.z: No reliable sources on Pipe Republic's blend Ashford could be found, so its content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

g-l-pease-embarcadero.z: Embarcadero is a blend in G. L. Pease's Fog City Selection line. Ripe red Virginia leaves and Turkish Izmir leaf are pressed and sliced, then further broken into flake form and boxed. It contains no Latakia; the blend's character is defined by Virginia's dark sweetness and Izmir leaf's dry, tart spiciness. Pressing and slicing give a slow-burning, layered smoke. It is aimed at those wanting to get to know Oriental tobacco in flake form on a smoke-free base.
g-l-pease-embarcadero.o: Leaves a dry-grass and spicy, lightly tart leaf aroma.

rattray-malcolm-flake.z: Malcolm Flake is a flavored blend in Rattray's flake line. Dark-colored slices made of Virginia, Burley, and Kentucky leaf are packed moist; opening the tin gives a pineapple-forward tropical fruit scent. Even moist it lights without difficulty, though crumbling the slices and airing them for a while makes the burn more even. The smoke lasts long, and the flavor intensifies as the bowl progresses toward the bottom. Though the flavoring is pronounced, the flake structure preserves the tobacco body; strength is medium. It suits smokers curious about fruit-flavored blends who enjoy a long-lasting flake structure. The Rattray name draws on the Scottish pipe-tobacco tradition; the brand's tobaccos are produced today in Germany.
rattray-malcolm-flake.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of tropical fruit juice, pineapple foremost.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-bills-ble.z: Bill's Blend, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an aromatic mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

a-c-petersen-escudo-navy-deluxe.z: Escudo Navy Deluxe is one of the best-known examples of coin-cut (spun cut) Virginia-Perique blends. Virginia leaves are spun around a Perique core, pressed, and cut into thin coins. Originating in England, this blend was produced for a long time in Denmark by A&C Petersen; the brand's production site and ownership have changed hands several times over its history. Alongside full Virginia sweetness, Perique's black-pepper-leaning spice is pronounced; despite being unflavored, flavor intensity is high, and the burn is measured and cool. Rubbing the coins out by hand and airing them for a while is the customary use. It's among the go-to blends for those wanting to get to know the Virginia-Perique family and looking for a spicy, unflavored smoke.
a-c-petersen-escudo-navy-deluxe.o: A sharp, tangy, peppery tobacco room note lingers in the room for a long time.

astleys-no-2-virginia-mixture.z: Astley's No.2 Virginia Mixture is prepared by ribbon-blending red and golden Virginia leaf with Perique added on top.
