The red Virginias set a toasted, bready base, while the light-colored flue-cured leaves carry a tangy sweetness; the Perique is kept noticeable but not enough to take over the blend. Nicotine sits between light and medium, offering a mild smoke that isn't harsh on the tongue. It suits those new to the Virginia-Perique family, as well as smokers wanting Perique's plummy, spicy contribution in moderation. The blend carries the name of Astley's, the tobacconist on Jermyn Street in London, and is produced today by Kohlhase & Kopp.
astleys-no-2-virginia-mixture.o: Leaves a plain tobacco room note leaning toward dry hay and a faint plum sweetness.

low-country-pipe-cigar-cherry.z: Cherry is a member of Low Country Pipe & Cigar's bulk aromatic line, its content evident from the name. Over a ribbon-cut Virginia base, it carries a measured cherry casing followed by a light vanilla note; further into the bowl the casing recedes and Virginia becomes more pronounced. It arrives at a moisture level ready to light straight from the package, burns cool and doesn't bite the tongue. Aimed at newcomers seeking a light aromatic and at those wanting a sweet base for their own blends.
low-country-pipe-cigar-cherry.o: Leaves a sweet cherry and light vanilla room note.

4noggins-tewksbury-hobbits-weed-match.z: Tewksbury Hobbit's Weed Match, as its name suggests, is an aromatic 4noggins built to reproduce an old blend. Its body is Burley, softened by adding fire-cured Cavendish to tame Burley's harshness. As a topping, a light cherry and a touch of vanilla are used; this makes the blend drier and more tobacco-forward than sugary aromatics. It suits smokers looking for a slow-burning, semi-sweet aromatic who don't want the tobacco flavor lost beneath the topping.
4noggins-tewksbury-hobbits-weed-match.o: Ripe cherry and vanilla mingle with the woody scent of fire-cured leaf.

consolidated-310-modern-english.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Consolidated blend 310: Modern English.

caminetto-barolo.z: Recorded as a cherry-flavored aromatic blend from Caminetto's short-lived tobacco line; the entry has been left incomplete as no detailed, independent source could be found.

the-tobacco-barn-grandfather.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the The Tobacco Barn pipe tobacco called Grandfather to record the blend's composition and character.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-poniatows.z: The red version of the Poniatowski line sold in the Polish market; no independent source describing the blend composition could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-poniatows.o: No detailed description of the room note could be found in the records.

paul-olsen-st-croix.z: A Paul Olsen aromatic taking its name from St. Croix, Denmark's former West Indies colony; no independent source describing its composition could be found.

e-a-carey-europe-careys-black-twist.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Carey's Black Twist, a pipe tobacco from E. A. Carey (Europe).

cobblestone-kentucky-plug.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Cobblestone pipe tobacco named Kentucky Plug, so the blend's content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

blatter-blatter-blatter-1907.z: A Blatter & Blatter house blend named after 1907, the year the shop was founded in Montreal; no reliable source documenting its content could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-nougat-24.z: A blend in Sutliff's numbered bulk aromatic line, named after nougat candy; no reliable source on its content could be found.

borkum-riff-original.z: Borkum Riff Original is a loose-cut aromatic bringing together generous amounts of black Cavendish, Virginia, and Burley leaf, topped with a light vanilla coating. Notes of chocolate, plum, and dried fruit stand out in the smoke; the topping is more restrained than in the brand's other products, letting the tobacco's own taste come through. For roughly the half-century it's been on the market, the blend was largely sold as Ultra Light before later taking the name Original. The brand was introduced in Sweden in 1962 and is now produced in Denmark under Scandinavian Tobacco Group. It suits those looking for a mild, low-nicotine, familiar everyday aromatic.
borkum-riff-original.o: Leaves a warm room note of light vanilla with plum and dried fruit.

pauls-pipe-shop-morning-smoke.z: Morning Smoke was Paul's Pipe Shop's unflavored blend built on Virginia and latakia; records indicate it stopped being blended once the shop's stock of Syrian latakia ran out.
pauls-pipe-shop-morning-smoke.o: Leaves a scent of wood smoke and char.

ashton-type-1.z: Ashton Type 1 is referred to as an English blend in the brand's numbered series; no adequate independent source verifying its content and character could be found.
ashton-type-1.o: According to records, not enough information could be found to describe it.

savinelli-special-tobacco.z: Referred to as a blend recorded under the Savinelli name, though no reliable source describing its content and character could be found.

affordable-pipes-shiloh.z: One of the house blends from the American seller Affordable Pipes; no accessible source describing its content could be found.

mcclelland-red-and-black.z: One of McClelland's Virginia-forward blends; beyond what the name suggests — a mix of red and stoved dark Virginia — no reliable source could be found.

iwan-ries-china-black-vanilla-burley.z: China Black Vanilla Burley is the vanilla-flavored member of Iwan Ries's China Black line, built on fire-cured dark leaf. The coarse-cut blend, made up of Burley and Virginia leaves, is classified by the maker as light-bodied; the vanilla flavoring sits atop the Burley's nutty, earthy side without masking it. The coarse cut makes for a slow burn, and the light nicotine level makes the blend suitable for long smoking sessions throughout the day. Though it falls on the aromatic side, it suits smokers wanting a blend that isn't syrupy and lets the leaf's own flavor come through.
iwan-ries-china-black-vanilla-burley.o: Beneath the sweet vanilla aroma, the dry smell of toasted Burley leaf can be detected.

sutliff-tobacco-company-balkan-luxury-bl.z: Sutliff Balkan Luxury Blend 957 is a Balkan mixture that appeared in the Private Stock tinned series, using oriental leaf, perique, latakia, and black cavendish together. The maker's description likens the blend to the complexity of the Balkan region, emphasizing that each leaf contributes its own flavor to the whole. Latakia's smoke and perique's spicy sharpness form the blend's backbone; black cavendish leaves a sweet base, softening the dry line typical of classic Balkan mixtures. In this respect it's a fuller, sweeter-leaning profile compared to sharper-edged Balkan blends. The source page does not list the tobacco in stock, so its current production status could not be confirmed.
sutliff-tobacco-company-balkan-luxury-bl.o: A sweet undertone accompanies a smoky latakia scent reminiscent of a campfire.

gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-plug-xx-unscente.z: This is the unflavored version of Dark Plug. Dark fire-cured Virginia and Indian-origin fire-cured leaf are combined in equal proportions and pressed cold for more than a week. The rum or natural casings found in other versions aren't applied here, so the taste comes entirely from how the leaf was processed. The plug is hard and dense; it's sliced with a knife and rubbed out, or cube cut. The burn is slow, the smoke thick; nicotine is at the top end for pipe tobaccos. Smoke, earth, and a salty weight lead on the taste. Aimed at those with experience in unflavored, dark fire-cured leaf who want a slow, hearty smoke.
gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-plug-xx-unscente.o: Leaves an aroma of heavy wood smoke, smokiness, and earth.

seattle-pipe-club-gentlemans-rum-vanilla.z: Gentleman's Rum Vanilla, signed by Seattle Pipe Club, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

tewksbury-company-bar-harbor.z: Bar Harbor, a pipe tobacco from Tewksbury & Company; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

nording-beagle.z: A blend in the tobacco line released under the name of Danish pipe maker Erik Nording, noted as Virginia-and-perique-based; not enough independent source material confirming its composition could be found.

straus-tobacco-gaslight.z: Gaslight is one of the counter blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; records indicate the shop was founded in 1880 and that most of its house blends were named after Cincinnati neighborhoods and landmark buildings. Since no independent source on the blend's composition and character could be found, this record is kept at listing level only.

motzek-latakia-cake.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called Latakia Cake could be found.

d-r-tobacco-picayune.z: Picayune is a full-bodied blend from Daughters & Ryan combining air-cured Burley leaf with flue-cured golden Virginia, topped with Perique and Turkish leaf. It takes its name from a long-discontinued cigarette brand of the same name and, per records, was prepared as an adaptation of that blend for pipe smokers. It's known for its fine cut and high nicotine level. On the palate, Perique's pepper-and-plum spice and the tangy, resinous tone of Samsun-type Oriental sit on top of Burley's earthy base; this spice spreads across a dry-hay-like background. Aimed at smokers accustomed to unflavored, strong blends with a high nicotine tolerance.
d-r-tobacco-picayune.o: Leaves a sharp, earthy, spicy, strong tobacco scent reminiscent of burning dry hay.

cornell-diehl-rajahs-court.z: Rajah's Court is an English mixture in which Cornell & Diehl foregrounds Oriental leaf. Per the maker's listing, Latakia, Turkish leaf, red Virginia, and bright Virginia flake are brought together. The maker describes the mixture as a full, rich blend carrying the spiced flavors of the Near East. Latakia builds the smoky frame, the Oriental leaves add a spicy, lightly tart layer, and Virginia flake provides the sweet base. The character stays balanced throughout the smoke. Suited to smokers who like a spicy-smoky line and are accustomed to medium-full-bodied English mixtures.
cornell-diehl-rajahs-court.o: Leaves a smoky scent reminiscent of incense and spice, with a sweetish grassy note.

per-g-jensen-virginia.z: Per G. Jensen Virginia is the Blender's Collection's straight Virginia offering. Light-colored and red Virginia leaves are pressed into a plug, rested for a time, then loosened into a ready-rubbed cut. True to the series' principle, no top-note flavoring is applied; the light fermentation from pressing and resting brings the leaf's own sugar forward. The smoke carries tart citrus, herbal freshness, bready and lightly toasted notes, a woody background, and measured sweetness; nicotine load stays low while flavor intensity is pronounced. It suits those who love smoking straight Virginia, whether as an all-day tobacco on its own or as a base for their own blend.
per-g-jensen-virginia.o: Leaves a scent of sweet hay, fresh bread, and light lemon peel.

2-guys-smoke-shop-sweet-black-cherry.z: This cherry-flavored retailer house blend lacks sufficient available sources describing its composition.

the-briary-yorkshire.z: Yorkshire is billed as The Briary's best-selling blend, a mild and sweet aromatic. Its body is built on golden cavendish, and records indicate some fire-cured leaf is also added to the blend. According to the shop, the name was given to the classic vanilla cavendish blend already on its shelves after the business split off from the Tinder Box chain. On the smoke, vanilla-forward sweetness and a creamy note lead, with the leaf's own taste staying in the background. Nicotine is low and tongue bite is minimal, making it the kind of blend new pipe smokers often try first. It suits those looking for the pronounced, consistent sweetness typical of aromatics.
the-briary-yorkshire.o: Leaves a scent of sweet vanilla and caramelized sugar.

watch-city-cigar-the-4th-nun-2016-christ.z: The 4th Nun is a limited production Watch City Cigar & Pipe of Waltham, Massachusetts released as its 2016 Christmas blend. According to the shop's own description, the blend was prepared based on a pre-World War II Three Nuns recipe that pipe smokers dug out of the archives. Since no machine was available to produce a curly cut, the same leaf list and processing method were applied with a coarse ribbon cut instead. Its composition includes Burley, light-colored Virginia, Perique, and what the original recipe calls "manufactured perique" — Virginia cavendished using rum and anise oil. In character it sits close to Danish-style mixtures: Burley provides body and nutty dryness, light Virginia its natural sugar, and Perique a plummy, peppery sharpness. The rum and anise of the cavendished portion stay at a casing level and don't turn the blend into a full aromatic. This was a seasonal, one-off production intended for smokers seeking old-style Three Nuns flavor who are accustomed to lightly flavored Virginia-Burley mixtures.
watch-city-cigar-the-4th-nun-2016-christ.o: Leaves a scent of sweet hay with a light anise-and-rum note.

sutliff-tobacco-company-mardi-gras.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of Mardi Gras, listed as an aromatic in Sutliff catalogs, could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-mardi-gras.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-crowleys-best.z: Crowley's Best is an unflavored American mixture named after Walter Crowley, a player from Fordham's glory-year football teams. A nutty burley base is joined by a small proportion of Latakia and perique; the cut is ribbon. The body sits at medium: burley's dry, nutty base gets a thin layer of Latakia smoke and a tangy-spicy twist from perique. It suits smokers looking for an unflavored, burley-based blend for everyday smoking who want the smoke kept moderate.
cornell-diehl-crowleys-best.o: Leaves a lightly smoky aroma along with a dry, nutty tone.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore.z: Finamore is the pipe tobacco that forms the brand's core line, produced by Tabacos Cisne Branco Finamore in Juiz de Fora. According to the maker's description, it is prepared by blending Burley and Virginia leaf; it is described as a light-colored mixture with a low nicotine load. In Brazil it is available in 45-gram packs as well as a 200-gram tin. On the smoke, Virginia's light sweetness and Burley's dry, nutty side come through together; no pronounced flavoring stands out. It suits smokers looking for an unflavored or very lightly flavored, plain blend that can be smoked throughout the day.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore.o: Leaves a plain, lightly nutty tobacco scent.

park-lane-tobacconist-park-lane-no-13.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Park-Lane No. 13, one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-vanilla-royale-d.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Sutliff Tobacco Company's Vanilla Royale D61 pipe tobacco could be found.

dunhill-three-year-matured-virginia.z: Three Year Matured Virginia is Dunhill's Virginia blend named for its production method. Select Virginia leaves, led by red Virginia, are combined with a touch of Turkish tobacco, and the blend is aged for three years before being tinned. A very light fruit essence is applied on top; this addition adds a fine accent rather than covering the tobacco's own taste. The long aging lets the flavors meld, so the blend shows a settled Virginia character without sharp edges. Its body stays in the medium band. It suits those seeking a tobacco standing between unadulterated Virginia and aromatic, with measured sweetness. Production under the Dunhill name has ended.
dunhill-three-year-matured-virginia.o: Leaves a sweetish scent evoking aged fruit and dry hay.

barling-tradition.z: Tradition is the full-bodied English mixture in the London-origin Barling brand's 1812 tobacco line; it's produced in Germany by Planta. Per the tin description, the blend uses Cyprus and Syrian Latakia together, spiced with strong Kentucky, and rounded out with a broad-cut Virginia. With its high Latakia share, the smoke is heavy, evoking mahogany and exotic wood; some accounts note a tangy edge close to tar. The Kentucky leaf pulls both nicotine load and body upward. It's aimed at experienced smokers who find even full-bodied English blends like Dunhill Nightcap mild and are looking for smoky intensity; it's too heavy for those starting out with light blends.
barling-tradition.o: Heavy woodsmoke and a sharp, tar-like soot note fill the room.

villiger-maryland-sami.z: This is another Villiger pipe tobacco built on Maryland leaf; no independent source could be found documenting its composition and cut.

mcclelland-dulcet.z: No sufficient independent source describing the contents and character of this blend could be found.
mcclelland-dulcet.o: Records indicate it leaves a mildly sweet aroma typical of Virginia blends.

mr-bs-wild-anatolia.z: Wild Anatolia is an aromatic blend from Canadian Brigham's Mr. B's line. A black-cherry flavoring is worked into a mix of toasted black cavendish, cavendish, and virginia leaves. The blend was previously sold under the name Mr. B's Wild Cherry before taking its current name; it is presented in 50-gram pouches and 400-gram bags. Nicotine is light, with the weight resting on the fruit sweetness.
mr-bs-wild-anatolia.o: Leaves an aroma of ripe black cherry and sweet cavendish.

cornell-diehl-awakened-elder.z: Awakened Elder is a ribbon-cut mixture where Cornell & Diehl brings together Latakia with Kasturi cigar leaf of Indonesian origin. The blend also contains Virginia, burley, perique, and black cavendish; the maker's description describes the blend by its dense, exotic smoke. Latakia forms a smoky, woody core while cigar leaf adds an earthy weight, and perique contributes a spicy-fruit touch; burley softens these layers. It suits experienced smokers looking for an unflavored, layered, hearty English mixture.
cornell-diehl-awakened-elder.o: The cigar leaf's heavy, earthy aroma mixes into the Latakia smoke.

niall-of-nine-dead-gods.z: One of the blends prepared in very small batches under the Niall of Nine signature; not enough independent source material documenting its composition and character could be found.

low-country-pipe-cigar-waccamaw.z: Waccamaw is a Virginia-perique flake Cornell & Diehl produces for Low Country Pipe and Cigar. Light-colored leaf grown in the region forms the base of the blend; red Virginia provides sweetness and texture, while perique and a pinch of Izmir oriental add depth. It's pressed into flake form and rubbed before packing. It's medium in strength and medium-bodied. In the smoke, the bright sweetness of the light Virginia rides atop a bready, filling base; the earthy spice from perique and oriental adds complexity to the blend. It contains no flavor casing. Suited to those seeking a Virginia-based, unflavored flake to smoke all day.
low-country-pipe-cigar-waccamaw.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly spicy note toward warm bread crust and dried plum.

motzek-nordwind.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called Nordwind could be found.

pcca-quest.z: A blend produced by McClelland within the PCCA club series, noted in records as oriental-forward; not enough source material confirming its composition could be found.

dunhill-my-mixture-965.z: My Mixture 965 is among Dunhill's best-known English mixtures. Virginia leaves, Turkish orientals, latakia and cavendish are combined and presented ribbon cut together. The cavendish addition adds a dark, sweetish base to the smoky structure; the orientals give sour and grassy edges, while latakia defines the blend's identity. Its strength is high and its flavor intensity is very high; because of this it fits a pattern favored at particular hours rather than repeated smoking throughout the day. It rewards aging, and the transitions between components soften over time. It's a mixture built for smokers familiar with classic, latakia-heavy English mixtures. Production under the Dunhill name has ended, though the recipe continues under another brand.
dunhill-my-mixture-965.o: Leaves a scent of heavy wood soot and a spicy, sweetish tobacco.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-kentucky.z: Kendal Kentucky is an entirely fire-cured blend built from Kentucky-seed leaf grown in Malawi, Uganda, and Tanzania. The curing method gives the tobacco a pronounced smoky, woody character. It's a dark brown, fine shag cut. The taste is earthy and smoky, carrying no essence. Nicotine sits at the highest level, though it's noted to burn cool. Suited to smokers wanting to experience dark fire-cured leaf character in its plain form, who are accustomed to high nicotine, as well as to those seeking a component for their own blends.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-kentucky.o: Leaves the sharp smoky aroma of leaf cured over wood fire.

samuel-gawith-black-honey.z: No sufficient source could be found for Samuel Gawith's Black Honey blend, which evokes black cavendish and honey casing.

ash-ember-st-michaels-holiday.z: No adequate independent source could be found for St Michaels Holiday, a seasonal blend from the Ash & Ember shop.
ash-ember-st-michaels-holiday.o: No reliable information on the room note could be found.

esoterica-tobacciana-tilbury.z: Tilbury is a ribbon-cut blend prepared by combining golden and dark Virginia leaves with a small amount of burley and air-cured leaf. It is produced by J. F. Germain & Son in Jersey and appears in the Virginia family on retailer lists. In the smoke, Virginia's plum-leaning sweetness leads, while the air-cured leaf balances this sweetness with a soft, buttery body. It contains no Latakia or spice element. It suits those seeking a dark-Virginia-character blend for all-day smoking.
esoterica-tobacciana-tilbury.o: Leaves a trace reminiscent of plum sweetness and buttery dough.

nice-ash-cigars-trafalgar.z: One of Nice Ash Cigars' house blends; records indicate it carries a Virginia and burley base with a small amount of Cyprian latakia along with cavendish and rum flavoring. The record is left incomplete since no detailed, independent source could be found.
nice-ash-cigars-trafalgar.o: No description could be found in the records.

smoke-king-cherry-cream-mixture.z: Recorded as one of the flavored house blends Smoke-King prepares at its own counter; no independent source describing the blend's composition could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-verge-engine-overdriv.z: Not enough independent sources could be reached to fill out the record for Ken Byron Ventures' blend called Verge Engine Overdrive 2019.

jacks-tobacco-mongrel-dog.z: This is a blend under the Jack's Tobacco name; no accessible source describing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
jacks-tobacco-mongrel-dog.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-erinmore-.z: Erinmore Latakia is a modern-style English mixture in which latakia, Oriental leaf, and black cavendish are added to a Virginia base. The Erinmore brand is Irish in origin; production is carried out today by Scandinavian Tobacco Group. Latakia becomes noticeable midway through the smoke; black cavendish pulls the blend toward the sweet side, binding the components together. In this respect it departs from dry, soot-forward traditional English mixtures. Suited to smokers wanting to get to know Latakia-bearing blends while also wanting a sweet foundation.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-erinmore-.o: Leaves a sweetish tobacco scent underneath the wood-smoke and soot scent.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-wilder-choc.z: This is the cocoa-cased aromatic blend of the Wilder line, built on the common Virginia-Burley base of the Wilder tobaccos produced in Juiz de Fora, Brazil. Since no independent source describing the blend's ratios and smoking course could be found, the record is kept limited.

sutliff-tobacco-company-states-of-virgin.z: States of Virginia is a product listed among Sutliff's unflavored Virginia blends; no sufficient source on its leaf composition, cut, and character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-states-of-virgin.o: No reliable record of a room note could be found.

captain-black-white-regular-beyaz.z: Captain Black White is the commonly used Turkish name for the brand's base aromatic sold in a white package. Its content is mainly leaf converted to Cavendish along with unprocessed light-colored Virginia in between; the cut is ribbon. It is very light in nicotine and flat in flavor; the defining element is a vanilla-forward casing. The aroma is of medium intensity but the room note is strong and lingers in a space for a long time. Because moisture is high, it burns poorly if filled without airing. As one of the most widely distributed pipe tobaccos in the world, it is among the blends most smokers try first.
captain-black-white-regular-beyaz.o: Leaves a sweet, chemical aroma reminiscent of vanilla baking powder.

lane-limited-burley-and-black.z: As the name suggests, a lightly flavored bulk blend where burley meets black cavendish. Burley builds a dry, nutty, earthy base; black cavendish adds softness and measured sweetness to that base. The ribbon cut packs easily into a pipe and burns slowly and coolly. It's a tobacco standing between aromatic and unflavored, where sweetness doesn't dominate. Suited to those wanting to steer clear of heavily essenced blends but not fully plain burley either. Nicotine is at a medium level, so it can feel heavy on an empty stomach.
lane-limited-burley-and-black.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, nutty, woody room note.

uhles-christmas-blend-2015.z: Uhle's seasonal Christmas blend for the year 2015; no source documenting its composition has been found.
uhles-christmas-blend-2015.o: No reliable source describing the room note has been found.

cornell-diehl-red-stag.z: Red Stag is one of Cornell & Diehl's English-style ribbon-cut blends. It's made of Latakia, Oriental leaves, and Virginia; the maker's description highlights a sharp, peppery taste with light earthy undertones. Its name comes from the position attributed to the red deer in medieval hunting tradition. On the maker's scale, strength is medium and the room note pronounced; the intensity left on the palate is kept measured. Suited to smokers looking for an evening blend along the Latakia-and-Oriental axis with a not-heavy nicotine load.
cornell-diehl-red-stag.o: A sharp, peppery, earthy smoky scent stands out distinctly in the room.

watch-city-cigar-jolly-bastard.z: This is a house blend from Watch City Cigar described as Burley-based, for which no sufficient source could be found.
watch-city-cigar-jolly-bastard.o: Records note it leaves a nutty, earthy scent typical of Burley-forward blends.

seattle-pipe-club-mount-rainier.z: Mount Rainier is a traditional English mixture in the American series bearing the Seattle Pipe Club name, blended by Joe Lankford. Selected Virginia leaves are combined with spicy Orientals; a generous share of Cyprus Latakia is added on top, bringing the dark leaf's smoky aroma forward. It is ribbon cut, in a structure suited to packing the bowl. Latakia is pronounced on the first draws; as the bowl progresses, the lemony sweetness of the Virginia and the herbal spice of the Orientals separate out. Nicotine load is medium, flavor intensity balanced; it carries no additives. Suited to smokers familiar with Latakia blends or wanting to know the classic English mixture character without excessive heaviness.
seattle-pipe-club-mount-rainier.o: A spicy, faintly resinous Oriental layer accompanies a smoky wood scent evoking a campfire.

hearth-home-beverwyck.z: Beverwyck is among the Hearth & Home series' cube-cut based mixtures. It takes its name from Beverwyck, the Dutch-era name of what is now the city of Albany. Three separate cube-cut leaves are brought together in the blend, joined by smoky Latakia and spicy-sweet Perique. Virginia is present alongside Burley. The cube cut allows for loose packing and a cool, even burn. In the flavor profile, the toasted-hazelnut, bready base from the Burley stands out; Latakia and Perique add smoke and spice on top. It is an unflavored blend. Suited to smokers who love American-style Burley mixtures but want a measured layer of smoke and spice mixed in.
hearth-home-beverwyck.o: Leaves a roasted-hazelnut and light wood-smoke aroma.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-ser-jacopo-scott.z: Ser Jacopo Scottish Mixture is the Scottish-style member of the threefold series Kohlhase & Kopp prepared in Germany for Ser Jacopo. Orange and red Virginia leaves form the base; a small latakia share is added along with oriental tobaccos. A pinch of perique rounding out the series adds a peppery, dried-plum sharpness to the blend. The Scotch whisky casing applied on top is pronounced at the finish. The result is a medium-bodied mixture where latakia doesn't dominate, and the orientals' dry tanginess and perique's spice come forward. Sources note the blend is a close relative in character to the same series' English Mixture; the main difference is set by the perique and oriental proportion. Aimed at smokers who like Virginia-based, lightly smoky and spicy mixtures and don't mind the presence of casing.
kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-ser-jacopo-scott.o: A tangy sweetness reminiscent of dried fruit runs through the smoke-and-spice scent.

uptowns-smoke-shop-early-morning-pancake.z: One of the aromatic blends prepared at Uptown's Smoke Shop's counter in Nashville; the shop has closed and no source documenting the blend's composition has been found.

g-l-pease-metropolis.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Metropolis.

bentley-orange-oriental-type.z: Orange Oriental Type is a ribbon-cut blend sold under the Bentley name. Per the maker's description, the composition is weighted toward Oriental and Virginia leaf, with Latakia used in only a very small proportion. Its moisture and cut are pack-friendly, burning quickly and evenly. The dominant element in the smoke is the Oriental's spicy, sharp seasoning; the first puffs can deliver a spice tone intense enough to catch the throat. The orange in the name shows itself less as a distinct fruit flavor and more in the room note. Traces of Latakia only emerge with slow, controlled smoking, alongside Virginia sweetness. It's aimed at smokers who like a spicy Oriental character and are interested in lighter-nicotine blends.
bentley-orange-oriental-type.o: Fills the room with orange peel and spice.

up-down-champagne.z: No sufficient source documenting the composition of the Up Down house blend Champagne has been found.
up-down-champagne.o: No reliable source describing the room note has been found.

edwards-pride-of-kings.z: No sufficient independent sourcing could be reached to document the composition and character of Pride of Kings, a pipe tobacco from Edward's.

big-lous-back-room-voodoo-child.z: One of the house blends prepared under its own name for the Big Lou's tobacconist in Chicago; no reliable source on its content could be found.
big-lous-back-room-voodoo-child.o: No verified information on the room note could be found.

1776-tobacco-co-country-store-aromatic.z: One of 1776 Tobacco Co.'s aromatic blends; no adequate source documenting its content and flavoring could be reached.

timm-city-line-no-3-honey-blend.z: City Line No. 3 is one of the blends Dan Tobacco Manufacturing in Lauenburg prepares for Hamburg's Timm pipe shops. Loosened Virginia flake at roughly a third of the mix is added to broad-cut golden Virginia, along with dark black Cavendish; Yucatán honey and grape flavoring are cased on top. The taste is full and sweet, moderate in nicotine. As with moist aromatics, large, wide-bowled pipes are recommended for a slow, cool burn. Suited to those new to aromatic tobaccos and to smokers after honey-fruit sweetness in a tobacco for regular smoking.
timm-city-line-no-3-honey-blend.o: Leaves a warm aroma of honey and ripe-grape sweetness.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-country-s.z: This blend is a commemorative release made for the five-hundredth and final episode of the tobacconist's Country Squire Radio podcast. It contains red Virginia leaf alone; records indicate the leaf used was aged for more than fourteen years, and the blend is cut as flake. The long aging softens Virginia's sharp grassy edge and brings dark bread, dried fruit, and deep sugar notes to the front. No casing is used, so the taste depends entirely on the leaf's age. It is intended for smokers familiar with aged straight Virginia and accustomed to preparing flake. Being a commemorative, limited release, it is not in continuous production.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-country-s.o: Leaves a scent of dark bread, dried fruit, and hay.

erik-stokkebye-no-1.z: Not enough sourcing could be found for the No.1 blend registered under the Erik Stokkebye name; according to available listings it is a Burley-forward mixture.
erik-stokkebye-no-1.o: Could not be described due to lack of sourcing.

paul-olsen-christmas-blend-2003.z: A seasonal Christmas blend the Poul Olsen shop released for 2003; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.

pipesandcigars-com-candy-cane-cocoa.z: No independent source material could be found sufficient to fill out a specification for the pipesandcigars.com blend called Candy Cane Cocoa.

vauen-auenland-evening-mixture.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Vauen blend called Auenland Evening Mixture has been found.
vauen-auenland-evening-mixture.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-warrior-p.z: Warrior Plug is, as the name suggests, a blend presented in plug form; no sufficient primary source describing its composition and character could be found.

state-express-london-mixture.z: State Express London Mixture is a latakia blend developed in the mid-1960s by the London-based Ardath Tobacco Company, prepared mainly with the American market in mind. Records indicate it launched around 1967, first sold in 2-ounce tins and, after 1972-73, in 50-gram rectangular tins. The tin lid carried a stylized map of Anatolia and its surroundings along with the names of raw material sources such as Samsun, Izmir, Xanthi, Kavala, and Syrian latakia. Production ended between the late 1980s and early 1990s, and the American trademark registration lapsed in 1992. The composition is roughly one-third bright Virginia, one-quarter oriental (Samsun, Izmir, Xanthi, Kavala), and the remainder Syrian latakia; the cut is ribbon. The smoke opens with a dry, black-tea-reminiscent start, settling onto Virginia's dark-fruit sweetness and the orientals' spice. Rather than building a dominant wall of smoke, the Syrian latakia here stays a background layer of wood smoke; in this respect the blend differs from Cyprus-latakia-forward English mixtures. Nicotine is medium. A historical reference point for smokers seeking the classic Balkan structure and examining tins no longer in production.
state-express-london-mixture.o: Leaves a smoky scent, a mix of wood smoke and dry herb.

cornell-diehl-apricot-brandy.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Cornell & Diehl blend Apricot Brandy.

peretti-blend-w.z: Blend W is one of L.J. Peretti's shop blends in the Burley group. Per the maker's own description, it is built by adding only a very small amount of Latakia to an intense cube-cut Burley; this composition, extremely simple on paper, gains a distinct dimension as the Latakia brings out Burley's nutty side. The company's Burley tradition rests on the hybrid Burley mixtures Robert Peretti developed in the postwar period, and Blend W is one of the unflavored examples of that line. The cube cut gives a slow, cool-burning packing. It is a record aimed at smokers seeking a medium-bodied tobacco where the Burley base is audible and the smoky side is kept measured, rather than a Latakia-heavy English mixture.
peretti-blend-w.o: Leaves an aroma where a thin layer of woody smoke rides over a nutty, roasted-bread scent.

dan-tobacco-green-label.z: A pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source on the blend's composition or character was found, so no further detail is given.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-holt-dark-coconu.z: Holt Dark Coconut is listed as McGahey The Tobacconist's house blend, given a coconut flavoring over dark leaf; sufficient sources for detailed composition information could not be found.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-holt-dark-coconu.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of coconut.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-vanilla-flake.z: No sufficient sourcing on the producer or retailer could be found for this entry, referred to as a vanilla-topped flake in Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Kendal line.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-vanilla-flake.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet, vanilla-forward aroma.

watch-city-cigar-old-black-magic.z: Watch City Cigar's blend called Old Black Magic is, according to records, one of the house blends of the Waltham, Massachusetts tobacconist shop; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

briarworks-international-peach-cobbler.z: Peach Cobbler is a member of BriarWorks's aromatic line inspired by Southern cuisine. It consists of sweet Virginias and black cavendish flavored with a light peach casing; it also takes its name from the oven dessert of the same name. Black cavendish forms the moist, sugary base of the blend, while the Virginias add a brighter sweetness on top. The body is medium, flavor intensity medium-to-full. Suitable for smokers who want to clearly taste the fruity casing while staying in the aromatic lane, without falling into a completely flat vanilla profile. It is produced in small batches in two-ounce glass jars.
briarworks-international-peach-cobbler.o: Leaves a trace reminiscent of baked peach and sweet dough.

reiver-pipes-tobacco-blackmail.z: This is a blend from Reiver Pipes & Tobacco listed as English style; there is not enough source material on its content and character.
reiver-pipes-tobacco-blackmail.o: Reports indicate it leaves a smoky aroma from Latakia.

drucquer-sons-trafalgar.z: Trafalgar is Drucquer & Sons' classic English mixture. Soft, spicy Turkish tobaccos, light and red Virginia leaves, perique and just enough latakia for a light smokiness are balanced together. The ribbon cut makes the blend smokable throughout the day. Its character is measured, where latakia doesn't leap forward, keeping the orientals' spice and Virginia's sweetness in front; perique adds a fruity tartness. This structure, which opens its layers slowly through the bowl, suits those seeking a more finely worked English mixture rather than a high-dosed latakia blend. The blend is one of the old recipes dating to Drucquer & Sons' London period.
drucquer-sons-trafalgar.o: Leaves an exotic scent mixing spicy Eastern tobacco and light wood smoke.

jons-pipe-shop-burley-blend.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Jon's Pipe Shop's Burley Blend pipe tobacco.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kentucky-maple-spirit.z: No verifiable sourcing on the producer or retailer could be found for this entry, whose name suggests fire-cured Kentucky leaf topped with maple.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kentucky-maple-spirit.o: Records indicate it carries a maple-syrup aroma.

peter-stokkebye-danish-de-luxe-black-cav.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Danish de Luxe Black Cavendish in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

rattray-royal-albert.z: This is a flavored blend sold under the Rattray name; it is not part of the brand's current product list, and no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.
rattray-royal-albert.o: There is not enough source material to describe its aroma.

pipe-republic-canterbury.z: No reliable sources on Pipe Republic's blend Canterbury could be found, so its content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

cornell-diehl-engine-382.z: Engine #382 is an American-type blend named after the passenger locomotive engineer Casey Jones operated. Per the composition the manufacturer reports, bright Virginia, dark and white burley, perique, and unsweetened black cavendish are present; the blend also uses deertongue, a traditional flavoring leaf. The cut is ribbon. Deertongue leaf naturally carries a soft, vanilla-like note into the blend; burley provides the nutty, earthy body, while perique gives a plummy spice. Nicotine stays medium. It suits smokers looking for a sweetish American blend without resorting to added aromatic flavoring.
cornell-diehl-engine-382.o: Leaves a soft, vanilla-like trace mixed into a nutty tobacco aroma.

magne-falkum-no-201.z: Listed in the Falkum catalog as an aromatic blend referred to by number; since no source documenting its contents could be found, the record is left incomplete.
magne-falkum-no-201.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

villiger-tropical-export.z: No sufficient independent source could be found regarding Villiger's pipe tobacco called Tropical Export, so the blend's composition and character could not be recorded.

peretti-english-no-110.z: One of the house blends from L. J. Peretti's shop in Boston; it appears under the English blends heading in the maker's listing. No published description of the blend's composition and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.

gawith-hoggarth-co-balkan-flake.z: Balkan Flake is a jet-black flake blend Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. produces by pressing and cooking Virginia together with Cyprus latakia; no other oriental leaf is used. The cooking process calms Virginia's sharp, tongue-biting side, while some of the leaf's natural sweetness is retained. In the smoke, a smoky, earthy texture leads, with woody, spicy, and leather-like notes sensed beneath it. This is a record for those who love the latakia-heavy, untopped English-Balkan line and are accustomed to working with flake tobaccos.
gawith-hoggarth-co-balkan-flake.o: Leaves an aroma of heavy campfire smoke, leather, and wood.

e-a-carey-light-mild.z: Light & Mild is a blend that appeared in E. A. Carey's catalog in the very light aromatics section. Per the maker's description, burley leaves grown in Kentucky are combined with specially processed dark tobacco; the result is a mixture that burns evenly and doesn't harshen the tongue. The topping level is low, and the flavor structure runs soft and straightforward. It is built for newcomers to the pipe and smokers who steer clear of heavy flavoring. The blend was on Carey's list for many years but does not appear in the current catalog.
e-a-carey-light-mild.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, nutty, mild tobacco scent.

gawith-hoggarth-co-cherry-vanilla.z: Cherry & Vanilla is a topped blend that Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. also offers within its Kendal Gold series. It is prepared by mixing light-coloured Virginia and Burley into fermented black Cavendish, then applying a cherry- and vanilla-based top dressing; the cut is ribbon. The proportion of black Cavendish gives the blend a dark colour and a syrupy sweetness. In the smoke, the tobacco flavour stays in the background; what stands out is the combination of dark cherry and vanilla, with the cherry leaning dark and slightly tart rather than candy-sweet. The nicotine load is low and the smoke is cool, though airing is needed before lighting since moisture tends to run high. This is a good record for those wanting a topped, sweet blend, as well as newcomers to the pipe.
gawith-hoggarth-co-cherry-vanilla.o: A sweet, fruity aroma of dark cherry and vanilla spreads through the room.

james-fox-dorisco-mixture.z: Dorisco Mixture is the full-bodied English blend from James J. Fox, which has operated on Dublin's Grafton Street since 1881. The tin description presents the blend as a Perique-forward Virginia mixture, but it also contains a considerable share of Cyprian Latakia — the detail most discussed about it. The ribbon-cut leaf is built on matured Virginia's sweetness, Perique's plum-and-pepper spice, and Latakia's char. On the smoke, char and spice balance each other, and the smoke is dense and full. Nicotine stays moderate; the real weight is on the flavor side. A profile designed for smokers familiar with Latakia blends who also want Perique's spice. Being unflavored, it won't appeal to those expecting an aromatic tobacco.
james-fox-dorisco-mixture.o: Leaves a dark, plum-like sweetness mixed into a smoky wood aroma reminiscent of a campfire.

pipesandcigars-com-belmont.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of the pipesandcigars.com blend called Belmont.

paul-olsen-bourbon-bronze.z: One of the Poul Olsen house blends; although its name points to a whisky-direction flavoring, not enough source material describing its composition could be found.

mccranies-red-ribbon-vintage-2008.z: McCranie's Pipe Shop is a long-established tobacconist in Charlotte, North Carolina; the shop's tinned tobacco line began with red Virginia leaf from a single harvest set aside exclusively for it. This leaf is rested and pressed; the name ribbon cut refers to the presentation in which the pressed block is rubbed out into ribbons. Records indicate the year on the tin (2008) marks the leaf's harvest/packing year, and batches stamped with other years circulate under the same name. Being unflavored, single-varietal Virginia, the tobacco's taste comes from the leaf's own sugar: a bready, creamy base with a sweet depth that deepens with age. Nicotine load runs light to medium, making it suitable for all-day smoking. Aimed at smokers seeking an unflavored Virginia who want to smoke slowly and follow the leaf's own taste. The shop no longer continues this line; what's on the market are older batches.
mccranies-red-ribbon-vintage-2008.o: Leaves a sweetish hay aroma with a faint bready note.

cornell-diehl-virginia-ribbon.z: Virginia Ribbon is one of the single-leaf, ribbon-cut Virginia bulk tobaccos from North Carolina-based Cornell & Diehl. Records indicate the same product now appears in the maker's catalogue under the name Bright Virginia Ribbon: it's obtained by cutting golden Virginia leaf from the US Old Belt region — high in natural sugar, relatively low in oil — into thin strips. The maker's description notes sweetness accompanied by a faint citrus edge. The family's second member, Red Virginia Ribbon, is based on darker, heavier, slower-burning red leaf. Being an unflavored leaf, it's smoked on its own as well as used as a base or sweetening component by those building blends; it's noted as particularly suited to pairing with Burley. High-sugar Virginias take well to aging, so this is suited to long-term storage. A product for smokers wanting to get to know plain Virginia character in its simplest form, or looking to build their own mixture.
cornell-diehl-virginia-ribbon.o: Leaves a subtle scent of dry hay carrying a light lemony sweetness.

schneiderwind-1846.z: A fine, lightly flavored house blend from the Schneiderwind house in Aachen bearing the firm's founding year; no second independent source describing its content and cut could be found.
schneiderwind-1846.o: Recorded as leaving a sweet, finely cased scent.

mcclelland-no-m-58-apricot-brandy.z: A blend in McClelland's M-series bulk aromatics, discontinued when the firm closed in 2018; no sufficient source documenting its contents and character could be found.

pipesandcigars-com-knights-of-malta.z: No independent sources sufficient to complete a full profile of pipesandcigars.com's blend Knights of Malta could be found.

sillems-silver-cloud.z: A blend under the Hamburg-based Kohlhase & Kopp's Sillem's brand; although said to contain Virginia and Latakia, no independent source describing the blend could be found.
sillems-silver-cloud.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

4th-generation-autumn-mixture.z: Autumn Mixture is the autumn entry in Erik Stokkebye's four-seasons series under the 4th Generation banner. The Stokkebye family's tobacco tradition is traced back to Erik Peter Stokkebye, born in 1855, and the brand's name refers to this fourth generation. The blend combines matured Virginia leaves with fire-cured Kentucky and a small amount of Perique; it's presented as broken flake after pressing, so it doesn't need additional rubbing out before packing. Its character is defined by Virginia's bready, grassy sweetness and dark-fired Kentucky's smoky, nutty body; Perique adds a peppery edge and a hint of dark fruit. It carries no flavoring — no topping is used. Because it carries moderate nicotine, it suits smokers already acclimated to the Virginia and VaPer families seeking a smoky but unflavored everyday tobacco, rather than complete beginners.
4th-generation-autumn-mixture.o: Leaves an earthy aroma reminiscent of wood smoke, dry grass, and dark fruit.

sutliff-tobacco-company-burma-road.z: Burma Road is an aromatic-to-English transitional blend built from latakia, Virginia, and black cavendish leaves, topped with vanilla and rum flavoring. Latakia gives a smoky, sooty base while cavendish and the topping add a sweet direction; the ribbon cut lights easily and burns cool. It takes its name from the roughly 717-mile road that connected Burma to southwestern China during World War II. Suited to smokers wanting to try smoky tobaccos alongside a sweet topping, and looking for something lighter than a full-bodied English mixture.
sutliff-tobacco-company-burma-road.o: A sweet trace of vanilla and rum lies beneath a smoky wood scent.

ken-byron-ventures-moriarty-2021.z: Moriarty 2021 is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

reymer-brothers-brindleys-mixture.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of Reymer & Brothers Brindley's Mixture.

j-f-germain-son-hampton-flake.z: This is a blend under the J. F. Germain & Son name, produced on the island of Jersey; no accessible source verifying its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
j-f-germain-son-hampton-flake.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

international-blend-sahara-international.z: No usable independent source could be found for this blend, described as Oriental-forward.

hu-tobacco-livinghardt.z: Livinghardt is one of the Latakia-forward blends in the Clans of Scotland line. Its Virginia base, built with Cyprus Latakia and black Cavendish, carries a strong English character; the flavoring is built on tart Ben Lomond blackcurrant and vanilla. The flavoring is kept measured; while the fruity, sweet notes stay in the background, Latakia and the tobacco base determine the blend's body. It's a full-nicotine option sitting somewhere between a flavored blend and a classic English blend. Records indicate it's presented in 50-gram tins.
hu-tobacco-livinghardt.o: A tart red-fruit and vanilla sweetness mixes into the smoky wood aroma.

gq-tobaccos-blenders-special.z: One of the eponymous blends from English mail-order tobacconist GQ Tobaccos; there is no sourcing documenting its composition and character.
gq-tobaccos-blenders-special.o: No record of its aroma could be found.

cornell-diehl-kajun-kake.z: Kajun Kake takes its name from the Louisiana Perique it contains and the crumbly cake form it's presented in. Measured Perique is added to naturally sweet red Virginias, and the mixture is pressed in the old style so the flavors meld together. It sits in the tin as a rectangular block, breaks apart at the lightest touch, and packs the bowl easily. Perique reins in Virginia's sweetness, building a character evoking earth and peat; the resulting profile moves between sweet and spicy, with notes of ripe fruit and earth. It carries no casing. Since it arrives moist, airing it out for a while after breaking it apart evens out the burn. Suited to those looking for the classic Virginia-Perique smoke in pressed form.
cornell-diehl-kajun-kake.o: Leaves a tangy, ripe-fruit and earthy tobacco scent.

mcclelland-no-5105-stoved-virginia.z: No. 5105 Stoved Virginia is an unflavored tobacco in McClelland's bulk series, presented as a stoved black Virginia cake. Per the maker's description, it's prepared in the style of the black Virginia cake that gives classic English mixtures their characteristic taste and finesse; the matured cake is sold fully rubbed out. The stoving process caramelizes the leaf's sugar, deepening its color and taste. In the smoke, it gives a rich, sweet, and naturally spiced profile; fresh Virginia's sharp tang gives way to cooked-fruit and dark-sugar tones. It can be smoked on its own or used as a base for Latakia blends. Aimed at smokers seeking dark Virginia taste who build their own blends. Discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-no-5105-stoved-virginia.o: Leaves a dark cooked-fruit and sweet-spice aroma.

pipesandcigars-com-log-cabin.z: No independent sources sufficient to complete a full profile of pipesandcigars.com's blend Log Cabin could be found.

edwards-scottish-bucc.z: No sufficient independent sourcing could be reached to document the composition and character of Scottish-Bucc, a pipe tobacco from Edward's.

planta-california-dream-orange.z: California Dream is an aromatic mixture in which a strong orange casing is applied to a dry body made of black Cavendish and golden Virginia. The orange note comes forward not only in taste but in the room note as well. Since no heavy sugar or sticky casing is used, the tobacco packs and lights easily. It was released as a limited edition in 2013 and later added to Planta's ongoing catalogue. Reports indicate it has also been sold under different names in the United Kingdom. It suits smokers looking for a light-bodied, one-dimensional, pronouncedly fruit-flavored tobacco.
planta-california-dream-orange.o: Fills the room with a pronounced fresh orange-peel aroma.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-holt-peach.z: Holt Peach is listed as McGahey The Tobacconist's peach-flavored house blend; sufficient sources regarding its composition and character could not be found.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-holt-peach.o: Leaves a fruity aroma reminiscent of peach.

middle-earth-tobacco-old-toby.z: The straight Virginia blend in the Middle Earth Tobacco line; no verifiable source could be found for this entry, which should not be confused with same-named blends from other makers.

lane-limited-dark-red.z: Dark Red is an aromatic blend registered under Lane Limited; not enough sources could be found to describe its content and character.
lane-limited-dark-red.o: Reportedly leaves a sweet aromatic room note.

robert-mcconnell-pilot-top-brand.z: Pilot Top Brand, released under the Robert McConnell name, is an aromatic blend flavored with clove and cinnamon notes; there is not enough source material on its leaf composition or cut.
robert-mcconnell-pilot-top-brand.o: Leaves the spicy, sweetish scent of clove and cinnamon.

wessex-mellow-aroma-brown.z: No sufficient independent source could be found documenting the composition of the Wessex Mellow Aroma (Brown) blend.
wessex-mellow-aroma-brown.o: According to the records, no scent description has been documented.

g-l-pease-robusto.z: Robusto is a coarse-cut blend built by adding a measured amount of maduro cigar leaf over sweet Virginias, earthy Oriental leaves, and smoky Cyprus latakia. The cigar leaf is used not to take on the main character but to support the other leaves and give the smoke a creamy quality. The tin aroma carries tart fruit, light spice, and smoke. The smoke is full, spicy, and complex; it is noted, however, not to be heavy on the tongue. It burns slowly. It is a record aimed at those coming from cigar smoking who want a similarly earthy richness in a pipe; records note it recalls the old Sobranie Virginia No. 10 blend.
g-l-pease-robusto.o: Leaves an earthy, spicy, lightly smoky aroma reminiscent of cigars.

cornell-diehl-bayou-morning-flake.z: Cornell & Diehl Bayou Morning Flake is the pressed form of the ribbon-cut mixture of the same name. Perique is added at roughly a quarter proportion to red Virginia leaves of Old Belt origin; after the whole mixture is pressed it is sliced into flake. Pressing lets the components interact with each other for longer. The slices are smoked either rubbed out or folded into the bowl; the burn is slower than the ribbon form. In taste, Virginia's sweetness and perique's plum-and-pepper notes are pronounced, with the body sitting on the full end. It suits experienced smokers looking for a high-perique flake, accustomed to slow smoking.
cornell-diehl-bayou-morning-flake.o: Leaves a dark-fruit and pepper aroma in the room, with a baked-bread scent beneath.

g-l-pease-kensington.z: Kensington is a measured Balkan blend in G. L. Pease's Classic Collection. Oriental tobaccos and Cyprus latakia are added over bright and red Virginia leaves; the latakia proportion is more measured than that of Charing Cross in the same series, so the blend carries a slightly sweeter, less full character. It has a spicy line, and records note it occasionally gives a floral note reminiscent of orange blossom. In the smoke, the tartish sweetness of the Virginias leads, the Oriental leaf plays a supporting role, and the latakia smoke wraps around the whole. With its complex but not heavy structure, this is a good record for those seeking a lighter Balkan blend for the middle of the day and those wanting to ease into Latakia blends.
g-l-pease-kensington.o: Leaves a smoky, lightly spicy aroma reminiscent of incense.

john-aylesbury-40-years-edition.z: No reliable source documenting the content and character of John Aylesbury's 40 Years Edition blend could be found.

hearth-home-lj-heart-virginia.z: LJ Heart Virginia brings together yellow and honey-colored Virginia leaf in a coarse cut, supported by a very small amount of Perique. Perique here isn't a dominant component but a background balancer, so the blend carries a mild, sweet Virginia character rather than a sharp one. A slow, cool-burning mixture. Built with a simplicity that can serve as an entry point for smokers newly discovering the Virginia family who haven't yet moved on to Perique-heavy blends, and suited to all-day smoking.
hearth-home-lj-heart-virginia.o: Leaves a light, sweetish aroma leaning toward dry hay and honey.

cornell-diehl-long-cut-perique.z: No adequate source documenting the composition and character of Cornell & Diehl's Long Cut Perique product could be found; the product isn't in the maker's current catalogue.

mcclelland-yenidje-supreme.z: Yenidje Supreme is the blend in which McClelland's Grand Orientals series presents Yenidje leaf without Latakia. Yenidje, from Western Thrace and known in pipe circles as "the queen of tobaccos," is joined by matured Virginia. The Latakia version of the same leaf is named Yenidje Highlander; both blends were discontinued when the company closed in 2018. The smoke is mild and cool; the flavor runs along a floral-herbal line reminiscent of incense, with no sharp or medicinal edge, and the sweetness from the Virginia stays measured. Suited to smokers who want to hear the Oriental leaf's own character unmasked, and who lean toward light-to-medium-bodied blends.
mcclelland-yenidje-supreme.o: Leaves a floral, faintly herbal aroma reminiscent of incense sticks.

erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-1855.z: 4th Generation 1855 is a straight Virginia blend in the Erik Stokkebye line. High in natural sugar, it is made from well-aged golden flue-cured leaf and presented ready rubbed, so it can be packed straight from the tin. On the palate, meadow grass, bread, citrus peel and spice tones stand out, backed by a sweetness leaning toward dried fruit, caramel and cream. The nicotine load is higher than many Virginias in its class, so it suits experienced smokers. The blend's name refers to the birth year of Erik Peter Stokkebye, born in 1855, who started the Stokkebye tobacco tradition.
erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-1855.o: Leaves a sweetish scent blending dried fruit, caramel and hay.

g-l-pease-westminster.z: Westminster, introduced in January 2007, is a classically structured English blend in G. L. Pease's Heirloom line. Its composition includes Cyprus Latakia, selected Oriental leaves, and ripe Virginias; the producer describes the blend as "English at its core." Latakia is felt distinctly, but is kept in balance between the spiciness of the Oriental leaves and the sweetness of the Virginias. It is aimed at smokers seeking one of the benchmark examples of the English-blend family and a consistent Latakia blend for everyday use.
g-l-pease-westminster.o: Leaves an aroma of smoky wood, campfire, and leather.

james-fox-hibernia.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to document the contents and character of James Fox's Hibernia blend.

cornell-diehl-safe-harbor-flake.z: No composition and character information could be found in the maker's own catalogue or retailer pages for the blend referred to as Cornell & Diehl's Safe Harbor Flake.
cornell-diehl-safe-harbor-flake.o: No reliable information on scent characteristics could be found in records.

gawith-hoggarth-co-no-5-mixture.z: No. 5 Mixture is a traditional English blend of medium-to-strong body, built by adding dark fire-cured leaf to a Virginia base. Dark fired leaf is the blend's signature, carrying an earthy, peppery, smoky depth. It runs high on nicotine, and sweetness is kept low. Suited to experienced smokers wanting an unflavored, dry, and full-bodied blend. Records indicate it can be confused with the brand's product referred to as "Black and Brown"; however, that is a separate, vanilla-sauced blend.
gawith-hoggarth-co-no-5-mixture.o: Leaves a smoky, woody, and earthy aroma.

danske-club-black.z: Danske Club Black is an aromatic blend processed by traditional methods in Denmark. Black Cavendish prepared from ten separate Burley and Virginia leaves goes through double fermentation, which produces the blend's velvety black character. It's offered as a loose-cut mixture. The double-fermented Cavendish gives it a pronounced vanilla aroma; flavor intensity sits between mild and medium. The product was previously sold under the name Black Luxury and was renamed due to European Union regulations. It's aimed at smokers looking for an easy, sweet-smelling everyday aromatic.
danske-club-black.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and dark-sugar scent.

dan-tobacco-hollys-non-plus-ultra.z: A pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source on the blend's composition or character was found, so no further detail is given.

sutliff-tobacco-company-field-master.z: Field Master is one of Sutliff Tobacco Company's latakia-based mixtures; independent sources do not provide sufficient information on its composition and production status.
sutliff-tobacco-company-field-master.o: Leaves a scent dominated by wood smoke.

walgreens-burley-and-black.z: This is one of the bulk blends sold under the Walgreens pharmacy chain's own name; no reliable source could be found documenting its composition.

charatan-curzon-mixture.z: Curzon Mixture is a Balkan blend prepared in the Charatan line to fill the gap left by Dunhill's Durbar Mixture. It is made up of Latakia, Oriental and Virginia leaf, all cut in ribbon form. The generous Oriental component gives the blend a dry, spicy layer; the Latakia carries a smoky, leathery note, while the Virginia leaves a measured sweetness underneath. No casing is used. Nicotine sits in the medium range. Suitable for smokers seeking a balance between heavy Latakia-forward English blends and Oriental-dominant Balkan mixtures.
charatan-curzon-mixture.o: Leaves a smoky, leathery, dry-spice room note.

cornell-diehl-orange-sherbet.z: No composition description published by the maker or retailers could be found for this Cornell & Diehl blend named Orange Sherbet.

g-smith-sons-old-london-export-mixture.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. Smith & Sons' pipe tobacco Old London Export Mixture.

vogels-tabakstube-primeur.z: Primeur is one of Vogel's Tabakstube's house blends, presented as a ready-rubbed flake. Its composition includes Virginia, Oriental tobacco, Burley and Perique; the leaf color ranges from golden yellow through walnut brown to deep black. A honey-like sweetness comes forward first, followed by a tangy, grassy layer opened up by the Oriental leaf. The Perique adds a plummy, spicy depth, while the Burley contributes body. The tobacco is well packed and easy to prepare. Suited to experienced smokers after an unflavored, multi-component mixture with high flavor intensity.
vogels-tabakstube-primeur.o: Leaves a honeyed sweetness alongside a grassy, faintly tangy tobacco scent.

straus-tobacco-mount-auburn.z: Mount Auburn is one of the counter blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; records indicate the shop was founded in 1880 and that most of its house blends were named after Cincinnati neighborhoods and landmark buildings. Since no independent source on the blend's composition and character could be found, this record is kept at listing level only.

consolidated-201-sangria.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Consolidated blend 201: Sangria.

ashton-signature-collection.z: Only a single forum entry could be found regarding this blend known under the Ashton name, so its content could not be verified and the profile is left blank.

hu-tobacco-tuarekh.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the Tuarekh blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

appalachian-customs-red-clay-reserve.z: No adequate independent source documenting the content and character of Red Clay Reserve, from Appalachian Customs, could be found.
appalachian-customs-red-clay-reserve.o: No reliable information on the room note could be found.

clan-shaw-high-plains.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend High Plains.

cornell-diehl-night-train.z: Night Train is a Virginia-burley mixture that Cornell & Diehl presses into a crumble cake. According to the manufacturer's description, it brings together bright Virginia ribbon and bright Virginia flake, cavendish-cut leaf, Virginia-grown brown burley, and perique. Because the pressing process concentrates the sugars, Virginia's bready sweetness comes through clearly, while perique adds a layer of plum-and-pepper spice. The cake is crumbled by hand before packing; since its density can be adjusted, the burn rate is largely in the smoker's own hands. Nicotine strength sits above medium, and as an unflavored blend it lets the natural taste of the leaf take center stage. It suits smokers who enjoy the Virginia-perique lineage and don't mind burley's earthy, nutty notes.
cornell-diehl-night-train.o: Leaves a dark, faintly plummy tobacco aroma mixed with bready sweetness.

two-friends-celtic-mist.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of the aromatic blend Celtic Mist, part of the Two Friends line, has been found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-clan-malt.z: Clan is a brand launched in the 1950s by the Dutch Theodorus Niemeyer and produced since the 1990s under Scandinavian Tobacco Group. Malt Whisky is one of the Clan body's versions aimed at the European market; Virginia, burley, black cavendish, and Kentucky leaf are topped with a whiskey-and-floral note, and according to records the brand's body also blends in Oriental leaf and a small amount of perique.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-clan-malt.o: Leaves a warm scent carrying malt and grain sweetness, with a floral edge.

w-o-larsen-kentucky-flowers.z: No reliable source could be found regarding the composition and character of this Danish blend bearing the W.Ø. Larsen name.
w-o-larsen-kentucky-flowers.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

peterson-special-reserve-2011.z: Special Reserve 2011 is a limited edition blend released as part of Peterson's Special Reserve series specific to that year; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient first-hand sources confirming its content and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-house-roll-cut.z: Brown House Roll Cut is a roll tobacco the firm released in its Reunion series. Hot-air-cured Virginia leaves are twisted into rope form together with dark fire-cured leaf of Mozambican origin, then cut into thin coins. A measured, maple-like sweetness is applied as topping. Since the roll cut has Virginia on the outside and dark leaf at the core, the taste changes through the bowl: grassy and sweet at first, becoming smoky and earthy as it progresses. The coins are filled either folded as-is or rubbed out; because they are tightly wound, they burn slowly. Nicotine is above medium. It suits a smoker familiar with the roll-tobacco format who is looking for the weight of dark fire-cured leaf.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-house-roll-cut.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of woodsmoke and maple syrup.

erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-1957.z: 1957 is named for the birth year of Erik Stokkebye, the fourth generation whose name the series carries. It is a ribbon-cut blend of bright virginia, burley and a pinch of black cavendish, given a topping delivering vanilla notes. The cut mixes leaf colors ranging from light to dark brown. The natural sweetness of the virginia moves together with the creamy tone of the vanilla, while burley adds a nutty balance to the body. It suits smokers seeking a moderate, all-day aromatic in terms of nicotine, and those who avoid heavy syrupy blends.
erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-1957.o: Leaves a soft, creamy vanilla scent along with a lightly sweet tobacco aroma.

g-l-pease-cairo.z: Cairo is a Latakia-free Virginia-Oriental blend. Exotic Oriental leaf and a very small amount of perique accompany red, orange, and light Virginia leaves; this structure makes the blend a non-smoky, spicy-sweet mixture. The flavour profile carries a natural sweetness, a lightly nutty body, and fresh notes reminiscent of citrus; these fine notes balance the fuller tastes of darker Virginias. It is a medium-bodied blend with low flavouring; it suits those wanting to get to know the Oriental leaf's character without the shadow of latakia.
g-l-pease-cairo.o: Leaves an aroma of dry grass, a nutty sweetness, and fine spice.

cornell-diehl-fires-on-the-levee.z: This is a Cornell & Diehl blend noted as Virginia-based; its composition and cut could not be verified as it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog.

connoisseur-the-london-castle-mixture.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Connoisseur blend The London Castle Mixture.

hu-tobacco-rocinante.z: Rocinante belongs to a limited, aged series released by German blender Hans Wiedemann under the HU Tobacco brand. Taking its name from Don Quixote's horse, the blend is built by adding Burley, a small amount of Kentucky, and a touch of Perique atop four separate Virginia leaves. The distinguishing feature of the series is that not just the raw leaves but the finished blend has also been rested for roughly two years; this resting softens and rounds out the Virginia's tart sweetness.
hu-tobacco-rocinante.o: Leaves a tart, herbal sweetness along with a light earthy and woody aroma.

tewksbury-company-twain.z: According to records, this blend was part of the lineup of Tewksbury & Company, an American blender that ceased operations following the 2009 tobacco regulation; no source documenting its content and character could be found.

ashton-gold-rush.z: Gold Rush is a ribbon-cut blend built entirely from Virginia leaf. A light lemon-and-honey-based top note is applied over it; when the tin is freshly opened, this lemony sharpness stands ahead of the honey sweetness, and the two draw closer together as the smoke progresses. Strength and flavor intensity stay medium-light. Since the blend is tinned without long resting, it delivers the deep, mature sweetness sought in pure Virginias only to a limited degree; when moisture is high it tends to run hot, so it should be aired and smoked slowly. It's aimed at those looking for a lightly flavored Virginia, wanting to start the day with a low-nicotine blend.
ashton-gold-rush.o: Leaves a lightly sweet tobacco room note accompanied by lemon peel and honey.

sutliff-tobacco-company-honey-chocolate.z: Honey & Chocolate is a blend in Sutliff's aromatic line that uses the two toppings named in its title together. The base of Virginia, burley, and black cavendish leaves is prepared as ribbon cut, with honey and cocoa essences applied on top. Available in both 1.5-ounce pouches and in bulk. On opening, dark cocoa and honey sweetness are perceived together. On the palate, a note reminiscent of dark chocolate comes forward, sugary sweetness stays moderate, and the smoke flows cool with a low tendency to bite the tongue. Offered at a moisture level that requires no extra drying, it's a record for those seeking a sweet-roasted style aromatic.
sutliff-tobacco-company-honey-chocolate.o: Fills the room with dark cocoa and honey scent.

uhles-marquette-blend.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend called Marquette Blend has been found.
uhles-marquette-blend.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

j-f-germain-son-royal-jersey-cavendish-a.z: This is a blend under the J. F. Germain & Son name, produced on the island of Jersey; no accessible source verifying its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
j-f-germain-son-royal-jersey-cavendish-a.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

mcclelland-coopersark-starter-blend.z: No sufficient independent source describing the contents of this blend, apparently prepared specially for a tobacconist, could be found.
mcclelland-coopersark-starter-blend.o: Records indicate it leaves a mildly sweet aroma typical of Virginia blends.

samuel-gawith-brown-pigtail.z: Brown Pigtail is the lighter-colored member of Samuel Gawith's fine-twist rope series. Virginia-forward leaf is twisted together with burley; because it undergoes shorter processing than its black counterpart, its color stays brown. The slices are cut and smoked crumbled. In the flavor profile, Virginia's bready sweetness and burley's nutty dryness sit together; nicotine is a touch more measured than its black counterpart. Suited to those accustomed to rope preparation who seek an unflavored, direct tobacco taste.
samuel-gawith-brown-pigtail.o: Leaves a dry-hay and nutty tobacco scent.

low-country-pipe-cigar-atalaya.z: One of the house blends of South Carolina-based Low Country Pipe & Cigar; described as Virginia-and-perique-forward, but not enough sources could be found to describe its character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-sps-2004-kahlua-.z: SPS-2004 is a liqueur aromatic in Sutliff's bulk line known as "Sutliff Private Stock." The base is built from a combination of nutty burley and sweet, soft black cavendish; an amaretto- and coffee-liqueur-character casing is applied over it. The cut is ribbon. On the smoke, the taste is soft and measured; the casing doesn't sit heavy in the mouth, though the scent it leaves in the room is pronounced enough to recall marzipan. Nicotine is on the light side. It suits smokers looking for a sweet, nutty-almond-character aromatic that doesn't suppress the tobacco taste.
sutliff-tobacco-company-sps-2004-kahlua-.o: Leaves a sweet scent reminiscent of marzipan along with a light coffee trace.

dan-tobacco-kiboko.z: Kiboko is one of Dan Tobacco's heavily fruit-cased aromatics. Its body is built from black Cavendish made with African-origin leaf, joined by some Virginia. The casing centers on a sweet cherry and lychee pairing, clearly noticeable both in the tin note and while smoking. The name means "hippopotamus" in Swahili, spoken in East Africa. The Cavendish-heavy construction brings low nicotine, a cool burn, and a sweet mouthfeel. Suited to smokers looking for a heavily aromatic blend who don't mind pronounced fruit notes taking precedence over tobacco flavor. Its character may come across as too dominant for those accustomed to unflavored Virginia or Latakia mixtures.
dan-tobacco-kiboko.o: Leaves a pronounced, sweet fruit trace of ripe cherry and lychee.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-private-blend-no.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Private Blend No.47.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-mapleton.z: Match Mapleton is Sutliff's counterpart to a classic maple-cased aromatic. Black cavendish is added to a burley and Virginia base, with a maple-forward casing applied over it. The casing's character shows a kinship with maple-cased blends of the same family, such as the Amphora Red type. On the smoke, maple leads along with a light floral tone accompanying it; a small amount of vanilla from the black cavendish can be sensed. Burley emerges from within the casing especially in the second half of the bowl, while Virginia leaves only a light grassy edge. It burns cool and dry, with little need for relighting. It suits those wanting a sweet but not heavy aromatic.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-mapleton.o: Leaves a light floral scent at a maple-syrup sweetness.

buchanans-tobacco-shop-wellingborough.z: The house blend noted as English-style from the tobacconist Buchanan's Tobacco Shop; no source documenting its composition could be found.

faders-barrister.z: Fader's is a line of house blends offered under its own name by a long-established Baltimore tobacconist; no verifiable source could be found regarding this blend's composition and character.

sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-oriental-fue.z: Apparently a more full-bodied version of Sentimiento Nacional's Oriental series, as the name suggests; no independent source describing the blend's content could be found.
sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-oriental-fue.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-billiard-room.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Cornell & Diehl blend Billiard Room.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-vermont-maple-cavendi.z: No sufficient source could be found documenting the composition and character of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Vermont Maple Cavendish.

sutliff-tobacco-company-bourbon-2007.z: SPS-2007 Bourbon is an aromatic blend in Sutliff's Private Stock line. A Kentucky-whiskey-based top flavoring is applied to a ribbon-cut combination of black cavendish, burley, and Virginia leaves; the resulting taste runs toward caramel and sweet grain. It's a measured blend nicotine-wise, with low bite. Suited to smokers seeking a liquor note in flavored blends who don't want the topping to completely mask the tobacco taste.
