Sutliff has been an American tobacco house producing in Richmond, Virginia since the 19th century; this blend is a typical example of the brand's American aromatic tradition.
sutliff-tobacco-company-bourbon-2007.o: Leaves a light oak scent alongside sweet caramel and whiskey.

villiger-cocktail-hour.z: No sufficient independent source could be found regarding Villiger's pipe tobacco called Cocktail Hour, so the blend's composition and character could not be recorded.

cornell-diehl-cordial.z: Cordial is a mixture where Cornell & Diehl softens the classic English mold with black cavendish. Unsweetened black cavendish is added to a trio of Virginia, Turkish leaf, and Latakia; this addition heightens both the sweetness and the prominence of the room note. The body stays at a medium level; Latakia's smoky tone and the Oriental's spicy-tangy edge move over cavendish's roundness. It suits those new to Latakia blends and smokers looking for the classic English structure on a slightly sweeter foundation.
cornell-diehl-cordial.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly sugared trace in the room along with a smoky wood aroma.

g-l-pease-lombard.z: Lombard is a member of the Fog City Selection line. A base of red and bright Virginias, sweetened with a small amount of perique, has a very small measure of Cyprus latakia added on top. Here, latakia is used not enough to turn the blend into a smoky structure, but only enough to add depth and a light smokiness. As a result, the Virginia character is preserved while perique's spicy, fruity contribution and latakia's fine smoke stay in the background. This is a good, everyday-suitable record as a transition point for the Virginia smoker not yet accustomed to Latakia blends.
g-l-pease-lombard.o: Leaves a fine woodsmoke on the edge of a sweetish hay and dried-fruit aroma.

samuel-gawith-big-ben.z: No reliable source could be found for the Big Ben blend, recorded under the Samuel Gawith name and said to be Virginia-based.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore-fr.z: Finamore Frutal e Floral is an aromatic in which fruity and floral essences are worked together into the brand's soft, cavendish-forward body. Like other Finamore products, it is produced at the Juiz de Fora facility and supplied in packs on the Brazilian domestic market. The cavendish processing lowers the tobacco's sharpness, so the smoke is soft and sweet; nicotine stays low. It is meant for smokers looking for a pronounced perfumed aroma rather than a strong tobacco character.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore-fr.o: Leaves a sweet scent combining fruit and floral essences.

john-aylesbury-golden-supreme.z: Golden Supreme is a golden-yellow-Virginia-forward blend prepared for John Aylesbury by Kopp Tobaccos. Its composition includes American Burley, North Carolina Virginia, Cavendish, and dark Virginia leaf; the maker describes the blend as a classic Virginia mixture. It's sold in 50- and 100-gram packages. The taste axis rests on Virginia's natural sugar; the Burley and dark Virginia share add an earthy, nutty body to the smoke. Since no pronounced casing is applied, it's suited to those who enjoy unflavored or very lightly flavored blends and want a medium-bodied tobacco for all-day smoking.
john-aylesbury-golden-supreme.o: Leaves a sweetish aroma reminiscent of baked bread and dry straw.

paul-olsen-no-800.z: One of the blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-white-ros.z: There is not enough independent documentation on The Country Squire Tobacconist pipe tobacco called White Rose to record the blend's composition and character.

chief-catoonah-tobacconist-bbb-mixture.z: The entry has been left incomplete as no reliable source could be found for Chief Catoonah Tobacconist's BBB Mixture blend.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.z: This is a mint-flavored aromatic in Imigrantes Fumos's Cândido Giovanella line. It shares the same base as the other flavors: Brazilian Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish, ribbon cut. In the smoke, mint's cooling, sharp sweetness dominates and leaves a refreshing sensation in the mouth; the tobacco's own taste stays behind this flavoring. Nicotine load is low, the smoke cool. It suits those who enjoy menthol and refreshing smokes, and those looking for a light tobacco in hot weather.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.o: Leaves a cooling mint and menthol aroma.

lane-limited-edgeworth-sliced.z: Edgeworth Sliced is the pressed-and-sliced, burley-based version of the Edgeworth brand; not enough sources could be found detailing the blend.
lane-limited-edgeworth-sliced.o: Reportedly leaves a note toward nuts and cocoa.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-no-7-unscented.z: Kendal No.7 Unscented is a dark ribbon-cut tobacco where fire-cured and flue-cured Virginias are blended without any essence. The "unscented" in the name sets it apart from the house's floral-essence products. Earth, leather, and smoke stand out on the flavor palette; the body is full and nicotine runs near the high end. It is recorded as a blend that has been available in the United Kingdom for a long time. Suited to those seeking a dark, full-bodied, essence-free English Virginia.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-no-7-unscented.o: Leaves a dry tobacco aroma reminiscent of leather and wood fire.

gawith-hoggarth-co-rum-twist-unsliced-ro.z: Rum Twist is a traditional rope tobacco produced by hand-twisting stoved Virginia leaf. Rum is added as a topping during production; the base leaf is the same as the brand's Black and Brown Irish X ropes. This version is offered as an unsliced rope, letting the smoker cut their own coin thickness. Because of the dark leaf and tight winding, nicotine is high and the taste intense; the rum sweetness sits atop a molasses-like base. Rubbing out the cut slices and airing them for a while is common practice. Suited to smokers accustomed to rope tobaccos who want a full-bodied, sweet blend.
gawith-hoggarth-co-rum-twist-unsliced-ro.o: Leaves a dark, sweet aroma reminiscent of rum and molasses.

lane-limited-black-spice.z: As its name suggests, a black-cavendish-based, spice-flavored bulk blend; not enough sources could be found to document its composition.

owl-shop-white-heather.z: Referred to as a house blend tied to the blending tradition the Owl Shop tobacconist in New Haven has carried on since 1934; its profile is left incomplete since no reliable source about its composition and character could be found.

players-medium-navy-cut.z: Medium Navy Cut is the medium-bodied pipe interpretation of the Navy Cut line from the Nottingham house John Player & Sons. The brand joined Imperial Tobacco in 1901, and the Navy Cut name became widespread in Britain from the late 19th century onward. Reports indicate this medium-strength member of the line reached a particularly wide following in the south of England. The blend is built by adding Burley to a Virginia-heavy base, presented pressed and sliced as flake. It is plain in flavoring, with a bready, herbal character; nicotine is medium. When the pipe tobacco division split off from Imperial, the line fell outside its scope and production stopped at the end of 2015. It appeals to those interested in the unflavored English flake tradition.
players-medium-navy-cut.o: Leaves an unflavored tobacco aroma reminiscent of dry hay and baked bread.

pipesandcigars-com-sugar-plum.z: Sugar Plum is cited as a sweet aromatic in the monthly blend line Russ Ouellette prepares for pipesandcigars.com; no source could be found documenting its composition, so no detailed specification is given.

mcclelland-el-7.z: No sufficient independent source describing the contents of this blend from the numbered bulk aromatic series could be found.
mcclelland-el-7.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet aroma typical of aromatic blends.

peter-stokkebye-luxury-twist-flake.z: Luxury Twist Flake is Peter Stokkebye's straight Virginia blend presented in flake form. The slices, obtained by twisting and pressing the leaves, are packed either rubbed out or folded; it is recorded as lighting easily, burning cool, and giving a long smoke. Most of the sweetness comes from the Virginia leaf's own sugar, joined by a very light vanilla-like top note. Nicotine strength is low and the flavor texture is on the delicate side; smoked at a fast pace it is prone to gumming up and overheating, so it wants a slow smoke. It suits smokers wanting to get to know flake tobaccos or seeking a Virginia that doesn't feel heavy at any time of day.
peter-stokkebye-luxury-twist-flake.o: Leaves a mild, sweetish aroma recalling light dried fruit and a faint vanilla.

paul-olsen-king-george-vi.z: A blend from the My Own Blend line that originated at the Paul Olsen shop in Copenhagen; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-brown-f.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to fill in the profile of Ken Byron Ventures' Mr. Christian's Brown Flek.

niall-of-nine-albatross.z: One of the blends prepared in very small batches under the Niall of Nine signature; not enough independent source material documenting its composition and character could be found.

mccranies-danish-delight.z: Danish Delight is one of McCranie's aromatic bulk blends, its name a nod to the Danish style; no sufficient sources could be found on its composition.

two-friends-redwood.z: Redwood is a ribbon-cut blend in the Virginia-Perique wing of the Two Friends line. Toasted and untoasted red Virginia grades are layered together; pure St. James Parish Perique is added for spice, with a small amount of unsweetened black Cavendish to gather the body. The Virginia leaf's natural sugar sets the blend's base, and the Perique layers a sharp, plummy, peppery edge on top of that sweetness. As no casing is used, the taste comes entirely from the leaf itself; nicotine sits in the medium range while flavor intensity is high. A fitting structure for smokers wanting to get to know the Virginia-Perique family, or after unflavored, spicy sweetness.
two-friends-redwood.o: A dry trace reminiscent of conifer resin mixes with bread-dough and dark-fruit sweetness.

esoterica-tobacciana-stonehaven.z: Stonehaven is produced for Butera Pipe Co. by J. F. Germain & Son in Jersey. Air-cured leaves, burley, and select Virginias are matured and pressed into dark brown flake slices. It is counted among the representatives of the British tradition's flavoured dark flake style. Its body is fuller than the other blends in the line; burley's earthy, bread-like depth runs together with the dark sugar and dried-fruit tones intensified by pressing. Flakes arriving moist need airing, rubbing out, and slow smoking. Due to limited production it appears on the market only periodically.
esoterica-tobacciana-stonehaven.o: Leaves an aroma of dark sugar, dried fruit, and earth together.

samuel-gawith-black-maple.z: No sufficient source could be found for Samuel Gawith's Black Maple blend, which evokes black cavendish and maple-syrup casing.

bennington-tobacconist-union-jack.z: One of the shop blends registered under the Bennington Tobacconist name; no reliable source documenting its content and character could be found.
bennington-tobacconist-union-jack.o: No recorded recipe could be found.

james-fox-campanile.z: Campanile is one of the unflavored blends from Dublin tobacconist James J. Fox, combining Virginia and Turkish (Oriental) tobacco in a ribbon cut. It contains no Latakia, so rather than the smoky character of English blends, Virginia's dry sweetness and the Oriental's light spiciness come forward. Records indicate the tin recommends it for the day's first pipe, and its flavor profile doesn't change markedly over the course of the smoke. Strength and flavor intensity are kept low. Nicotine isn't described as filling, though it's noted the blend can run a bit hot. It offers a profile suited to pipe smokers moving from aromatics to unflavored blends who want a light, calm smoke. Its body stays thin for those seeking a full, intense flavor.
james-fox-campanile.o: Gives a medium-intensity smoke leaving a dry-hay and lightly sweet straw aroma.

torben-dansk-virginia-mysore.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Torben Dansk blend Virginia Mysore has been found.

hearth-home-ashcroft-estate.z: Ashcroft Estate is an American mixture signed by blender Russ Ouellette in Hearth & Home's Signature series. A measured amount of Latakia along with some fire-cured leaf is added atop Virginia and Burley, producing a structure that resembles English mixtures in its light smokiness while still preserving Virginia's sweetness. Since Latakia doesn't take on a dominant role, the blend can serve as a stepping stone between smokers who find dark English mixtures too heavy and those who have never tried a smoky taste at all. A medium-bodied ribbon cut designed for everyday smoking. The Hearth & Home brand is US-based; production has historically been handled by contract manufacturers.
hearth-home-ashcroft-estate.o: Leaves a fine sweetness behind a light wood-smoke and dry-leaf aroma.

john-patton-moes-confetti.z: One of the small-scale blends released under the John Patton name; not enough independent sources could be found to document its contents and character.
john-patton-moes-confetti.o: No source could be found on the room note.

sutliff-tobacco-company-summer-night-b36.z: B36 Summer Night is a single-leaf cavendish product among Sutliff's bulk aromatics. The black cavendish, prepared through slow roasting and steaming, is sweetened with a mature-raspberry-character casing. The cut is ribbon. The smoke is very soft; nicotine is low and taste intensity measured. The fruit note only becomes pronounced when smoked slowly and cool, fading when smoked fast. It suits smokers looking for a light, sweet aromatic with little tendency toward tongue bite, as well as blenders wanting to sweeten other mixtures.
sutliff-tobacco-company-summer-night-b36.o: Leaves a soft, sugary scent carrying a light raspberry sweetness.

king-street-coffee-tobacco-emporium-king.z: One of the blends prepared in-house at King Street Emporium; though the name points to English mixtures, no accessible source could be found describing its composition.
king-street-coffee-tobacco-emporium-king.o: No verifiable information could be found regarding its scent.

milan-tobacconists-french-vanilla.z: French Vanilla is listed among Milan Tobacconists' vanilla-cased aromatic house blends; no verifiable source about its leaf composition and cut could be found.

g-l-pease-horizons.z: Horizons is the third entry in G. L. Pease's Zeitgeist series, released in 2024. Turkish Latakia and Oriental leaf are added to matured red Virginia and light flue-cured Virginia; the blend is pressed and cut into flake form. It is a medium-bodied English blend with a contemporary edge: Latakia's smoky weight is balanced by Virginia's sweetness, while the Oriental leaf lays a spicy layer over it. The Latakia proportion does not push the blend into heavy Balkan-mixture territory. It suits smokers used to working with flake tobaccos, those new to English blends, or anyone seeking a moderate Latakia dose for everyday smoking.
g-l-pease-horizons.o: A light sweet undertone accompanies the smoky wood and incense aroma.

cornell-diehl-mixture-monster-ii.z: No adequate source documenting the composition and character of Cornell & Diehl's Mixture Monster II blend could be found; the blend isn't in the maker's current catalogue.

edwards-scottish-moor.z: This is one of Edward's Pipe & Tobacco's burley-based house blends, prepared according to the shop's own tradition; not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition and character in detail.
edwards-scottish-moor.o: Could not be described due to insufficient records.

straus-tobacco-sleepy-hollow.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for Straus Tobacco's Sleepy Hollow blend could not be found.

mayan-spirit-mayan-spirit.z: No sufficient independent source describing the contents and character of this product, stated to be cigar-leaf-based, could be found.
mayan-spirit-mayan-spirit.o: Records indicate it leaves an earthy aroma typical of cigar-leaf-based products.

consolidated-506-sweet-danish-slices.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Consolidated blend 506: Sweet Danish Slices.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-436.z: Wilke No. 436 is, according to the maker's records, a recipe prepared specifically for Abercrombie & Fitch stores, a reminder of the era when Wilke's New York shop blended tobacco under other companies' names. The mixture brings together Virginia and Turkish leaf with black cavendish and Latakia. The maker describes the blend as finely cut; Latakia and Oriental smoke are noticeable, though the cavendish component softens the overall structure. Moderate in body, this is a record for smokers curious about a historic shop's recipe.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-436.o: Light wood smoke and spice with a sweetish undertone.

7-20-4-little-gold-dust.z: Little Gold Dust is the Virginia-heavy blend in the 7-20-4 Briary Blends line. Bright and mahogany-colored Virginia leaves are combined with fire-cured Kentucky. Its name references the brand's history: R. G. Sullivan's ten-cent cigar was first named Little Gold Dust, later renamed 7-20-4. The line was introduced in 2023. In the taste description, lemony citrus, hay, and smoky cedar tones stand out along with a sweetness reminiscent of cooked fruit. It's an unflavored blend; the Kentucky balances Virginia's sweetness with a smoky, earthy body. It suits those who like unflavored Virginia character but want a smoke a bit fuller and smokier than a straight Virginia.
7-20-4-little-gold-dust.o: Leaves a room note of dry hay, lemon peel, and smoked cedar.

tabac-turc-yayladag.z: Yayladağ, alongside Tabac Turc's Türk Pipo Tütünü, is one of the domestic blends that for a long time formed the backbone of pipe smoking in Turkey. It was once considered special due to periods of scarcity. Its content includes Yayladağı, Bitlis, and İzmir leaf; latakia appears on the label, but at around 0.10 percent, so no smoky taste is discernible. It is packed as broken flake, quite moist; it needs a long airing period before smoking, otherwise it is hard to light. The smoke itself isn't difficult, but it wants to go slowly; the taste is medium-light and can occasionally turn flat. It generally leaves a sweet trace, though different from the sweetness found in Virginia blends; at times a soapy note reminiscent of Lakeland-style blends appears. It burns clean, giving fine white ash. It is a classic Oriental-character blend suited to daily smoking, aimed at those who want to know the taste of domestic Oriental tobacco in its plain form.
tabac-turc-yayladag.o: Leaves a heavy, intense scent of spicy Oriental tobacco mixed with a light soapy sweetness.

john-aylesbury-dragon-flake.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to document the contents and character of John Aylesbury's Dragon Flake.

cornell-diehl-christmas-blend-2016-corn-.z: Corn Cob Pipe and a Button Nose was released as Cornell & Diehl's 2016 holiday blend and was permanently added to the catalog following the interest it received. A cube-cut burley base is joined by bright golden and red Virginia along with cavendish; it is topped with a flavoring along the lines of cocoa and marshmallow. The tin note is described as cocoa powder, a light tangy dark fruit, and toasted marshmallow. The cube cut burns slow and cool; a sweet top layer is added to a body reminiscent of old-style American burley mixtures. It suits smokers who enjoy burley's nutty dryness and don't mind a measured sweetness layered on top.
cornell-diehl-christmas-blend-2016-corn-.o: Leaves a sweet room aroma reminiscent of cocoa powder and toasted marshmallow.

brebbia-classic-english-mixture-no-70.z: One of the English-style mixtures in Brebbia's numbered series; though known to be Latakia-forward, no sufficient source could be found to verify its content and character in detail.

ken-byron-ventures-trail-mixture.z: Ken Byron Ventures' Trail Mixture is reported to be Virginia- and Burley-forward; no independent source could be found to document its contents.
ken-byron-ventures-trail-mixture.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

jack-lee-blend-autumn-walk.z: This is one of the English-style products from the now-closed small American blender Jack Lee Blend; no reliable source describing its content could be found.

butera-pelican.z: Pelican is one of the Latakia-forward blends prepared under the Michael Butera name. Cyprus Latakia, sharp Turkish and other Oriental leaf and sun-grown sweet virginia are brought together as whole leaf; the mixture is rested in cakes and then cut into fine ribbon. According to the manufacturer, the blend was first prepared by Peter Stokkebye in Denmark, with production later moving to J. F. Germain & Son in England. In the flavor, virginia's sweetness sits alongside Latakia's smoke, while the Oriental leaf adds a spicy layer in between. The body is medium. Suitable for fans of Balkan blends who want to smoke Latakia over a sweet base.
butera-pelican.o: Leaves a trace combining sweet wood smoke, spice and dried fruit.

dan-tobacco-2001.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of Dan Tobacco's blend named 2001 were found.

dan-tobacco-lutte-deern.z: Lütte Deern belongs to Dan Tobacco's Hamburg-themed series, previously sold under the name "Seute Deern" before taking its current name. The mixture brings together sweet Virginia and Burley with a pinch of black Cavendish. Since the leaf is prepared in a broad cube cut, it burns slowly and cool. Its character is soft, sweet, and lightly tart, with notes reminiscent of fresh fruit coming forward. Nicotine is kept low. The maker notes the blend opens up better in wide-bowled pipes. Suited to smokers wanting a slow-burning, not-too-heavy everyday blend, and those wanting to try a cube cut.
dan-tobacco-lutte-deern.o: Leaves a lightly sweet trace where fresh fruit and dry hay mingle.

esoterica-tobacciana-hastings.z: Hastings is a loosely cut, fine shag blend where Virginia leaves meet sugared black cavendish. It stays close to the traditional English aromatic approach: the topping isn't heavy, and most of the sweetness comes from the cavendish process itself. The brand belongs to the US-based Arango Cigar Co; the blend is produced in England by J. F. Germain & Son and rested before sale. Because of the cavendish share, a soft crust is expected to form in the bowl, so drying and a slow smoke help. It suits smokers seeking a middle ground between aromatic and unadulterated blends.
esoterica-tobacciana-hastings.o: Leaves a lightly toasted scent carrying sugared cavendish sweetness.

nat-sherman-139-center-cut-blend.z: One of the numbered house blends sold at Nat Sherman's New York store; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found.

j-f-germain-son-royal-jersey-original-la.z: Royal Jersey Original Latakia Mixture is a ribbon-cut English blend from J. F. Germain & Son's Royal Jersey line, named after the maker's home island. It contains Latakia, Virginia, and Oriental leaves; per the maker's description, it smokes mild and gives a balanced flavor. The Latakia proportion is more measured than in the same house's darker products like Special Latakia Flake; the smokiness stays in the background, while Virginia sweetness and Oriental dry spice come forward. Being ready-cut, it requires no preparation. It's aimed at smokers new to English blends or looking for a light-bodied Latakia mixture that can be smoked throughout the day.
j-f-germain-son-royal-jersey-original-la.o: Leaves a trace combining light wood smoke with dry hay.

newminster-no-403-superior-round-slices.z: No. 403 Superior Round Slices is cut from a rope with dark-fired Kentucky leaf at its core, wrapped and packed around with whole virginia leaves. Slicing the rope produces round coin shapes, dark in the center and lighter at the edges. It is noted to carry a light casing; it is not classified as an aromatic. The taste is herbal and lightly bitter; pine and dry herb lead, with hints reminiscent of black pepper and juniper behind, while the fire-cured character from the Kentucky adds weight to the body. Strength ranges from medium to full. The coin cut is easy to prepare and burns evenly regardless of how it is packed. Suitable for smokers who like the woody character of fire-cured leaf and are accustomed to rope cuts.
newminster-no-403-superior-round-slices.o: Leaves a faint trace of wood smoke mixed with pine and dry-herb aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-cloves.z: Kendal Cloves is an aromatic blend where a clove topping is applied to the Kendal Mixed shag base. Virginia and Burley leaf are cut into fine strands; the base tobacco carries an earthy, sweet character with a dry-hay association. Clove adds an intense, spicy layer, leaving a pronounced sharpness on the palate. Nicotine is low and the smoke cool, but since the fine cut burns fast, it needs to be smoked slowly. Suited to those curious about spiced aromatics.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-cloves.o: Dry hay and sweet tobacco accompany a spicy clove aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-virginia.z: Kendal Virginia is an unflavored tobacco of clean-cut pure Virginia leaf, belonging to the same family as the house's shag-cut products like Kendal Gold and Kendal Dark. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. runs both topped and untopped versions of this line side by side; this entry is the unflavored wing, so the taste comes entirely from the leaf selection: bready sweetness, a light herbal quality, and a citrusy sharpness. The very fine shag cut lights the tobacco easily but tends to burn fast, so a slow, even draw is needed to prevent it from burning hot. Suited to smokers seeking unflavored Virginia taste directly, and who enjoy working with a fine cut.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-virginia.o: Leaves a dry-hay and sweetish straw aroma.

4-aces-regular.z: 4 Aces Regular is an inexpensive Virginia-Burley blend produced by Republic Tobacco and sold in large zip-lock bags. It is cut shag-style, very finely shredded, which packs tightly, lights easily, and burns slowly. Per the manufacturer's description it is not marketed as an aromatic, delivering a full-bodied, sweetly rounded smoke where Burley's earthy, nutty body is balanced by Virginia's light sweetness. Although sold in the pipe tobacco category, the blend really falls into the economical class of product designed mainly for roll-your-own use and bulk consumption. Its fine cut and the sturdy nicotine hit it delivers can feel harsh to smokers coming from mild aromatics; it suits those looking for a plain, unflavored, full-bodied everyday tobacco. It's prepared for immediate smoking rather than for jarring and aging.
4-aces-regular.o: Leaves a mildly sharp tobacco scent reminiscent of dry hay and toasted nuts.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-515.z: No verifiable source could be found documenting the composition and character of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Wilke No. 515.

tinder-box-honey-maple.z: Tinder Box is the name of an American tobacconist chain founded in 1928 that sells blends prepared for its own shops under its own name; Honey Maple is one of these house blends, though no sufficient independent source describing its composition and character has been found.

watch-city-cigar-transvaal-express.z: This is one of the house blends Watch City Cigar releases in small batches; no maker or retailer record could be found describing its composition.
watch-city-cigar-transvaal-express.o: No description could be found as no source was available.

harrods-ready-rubbed.z: A house blend sold under the Harrods name, offered pressed and then rubbed out; there is not enough sourcing on its composition and character.
harrods-ready-rubbed.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

brebbia-preludio-mixture-no-60.z: A light English-style mixture in Brebbia's numbered series; no sufficient source could be found to verify its content and character.

watch-city-cigar-christmas-past-2014-chr.z: This is a Burley-based seasonal Christmas blend Watch City Cigar released specifically for 2014; production was not continued, and no detailed record was published.
watch-city-cigar-christmas-past-2014-chr.o: Could not be determined from the records.

samuel-gawith-scotch-cut-mixture.z: No sufficient source describing the content and character of this blend referred to under the Samuel Gawith name could be found.

dan-tobacco-fred-the-frog.z: A pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source on the blend's composition or character was found, so no further detail is given.

hearth-home-mean-bean.z: Mean Bean is a lightly aromatic blend in the Hearth & Home Signature series. It is built from Cavendish-cut Virginia and black Cavendish leaf, topped with a soft, background vanilla note. Since the topping doesn't override the leaf, the blend suits smokers who enjoy aromatics but want to avoid heavy, syrupy flavors. A light-bodied, cool-burning recipe fit for all-day smoking.
hearth-home-mean-bean.o: Leaves a soft vanilla and sweet baked-dough aroma.

fribourg-treyer-blackjack.z: Fribourg & Treyer is a tobacco house founded in 1720 in London around Haymarket, long serving the English elite; the company closed in the 1980s, and the brand name has since been continued by the German house Kohlhase & Kopp. Blackjack is one of this line's untopped Virginia blends. It consists of flue-cured leaves in red and orange tones and is presented ready-rubbed after pressing. In the smoke, grassy and woody tones are accompanied by a fine citrus acidity, with the sweetness kept measured. It suits smokers seeking an untopped Virginia palate and easy filling.
fribourg-treyer-blackjack.o: Leaves an aroma of dry grass, wood, and light citrus.

drew-estate-7th-avenue-blonde.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of 7th Avenue Blonde, a blend from Drew Estate.

von-eicken-barsdorf-aromatic-mixture.z: An aromatic mixture in Von Eicken's Barsdorf's Bester line, reportedly built on a base of sun-cured Virginia and dark Cavendish. No independent source giving further detail on the blend itself has been found for this record.

samuel-gawith-kendal-cream-mixture.z: No sufficient source confirming the composition of this Virginia-and-Burley-based tobacco, recorded as the mixture-cut member of the family known as Kendal Cream, could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-bosun-plug.z: This is the whole-plug form of the Bosun family; the same blend takes the name Bosun Cut Plug once sliced and bagged. A measured, Kendal-tradition clove-like bowl note is applied over the Virginia and burley body, giving a sweet aroma reminiscent of raisins and a spicy taste. Because it is held under cold press, the leaf comes as a tightly compressed block. Once the plug is sliced, it is filled by rubbing out or cube-cutting; stored as a block, it lends itself to ageing. Within the spicy line of Kendal-style plug tobaccos, it sits in a more balanced spot than heavier versions like Rum Flake. It suits a smoker willing to work with a plug and looking for a classic English smoke with above-average nicotine.
gawith-hoggarth-co-bosun-plug.o: Clove and raisin aromas are accompanied by a woody smoke.

w-o-larsen-golden-dream.z: No independent source sufficient to complete a record could be found regarding W.O. Larsen's Golden Dream blend, so this entry remains incomplete.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-sweet-and-long.z: Sweet and Long is counted among the Virginia-forward house blends of the McGahey tobacconist; sufficient sources regarding its composition, cut, and character could not be found.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-sweet-and-long.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet, herbal-like aroma.

levin-pipes-international-british-woods.z: British Woods is a dark oriental mixture prepared by McClelland for Barry Levin's Vermont-based Levin Pipes International brand. Over generous latakia, spice from Macedonian-sourced oriental leaves and measured sweetness from matured Virginia are layered; the components are rested together in their own juices for months before being tinned. It's marketed as a slow-burning, cool-smoking, medium-to-full-bodied blend. Suited to smokers seeking the classic English/oriental style where latakia leads, with no added flavoring. After Levin's death the recipe was carried on by McClelland in its own catalog, and production ended entirely when the company closed in 2018.
levin-pipes-international-british-woods.o: Leaves latakia smoke reminiscent of charred wood and pine tar, with a spicy leather note.

hearth-home-old-companion.z: Old Companion is a blend for everyday smoking where nutty Burley and sweet Virginia meet in a balanced ratio. It has a toasted, nutty flavor axis and burns cool; it needs relighting rarely and leaves a light gray ash. Its top note is either absent or very faint; records describe a lightly flavored structure reminiscent of classic American blends from old foil packaging. The Virginia ratio is pronounced enough to give a sharp edge on the tongue if smoked too fast, so it calls for a slow pace. Aimed at smokers who want something familiar and plain rather than flashy — a blend they wouldn't mind smoking all day.
hearth-home-old-companion.o: Leaves a mild aroma leaning toward roasted hazelnut and dry hay.

cornell-diehl-warped-the-haunting-cake.z: The Haunting Cake is the pressed form of The Haunting, a blend Warped founder Kyle Gellis and Cornell & Diehl head blender Jeremy Reeves prepared together. On top of a Virginia base, AA-grade Dominican Criollo cigar leaf — also used in Warped's cigar lines — and Dominican-origin black Cavendish are added. The mixture is formed into crumble cake; the maker notes pressing lets the flavors meld together. On the smoke, the leather and spice tones the cigar leaf brings come forward, while Virginia leaves a lingering, hazy sweetness underneath. Nicotine load is medium; the texture calls for a slow smoke from those unaccustomed to cigar leaf. It's released as a seasonal, limited run, so it isn't in continuous production.
cornell-diehl-warped-the-haunting-cake.o: A light sweet tobacco trace mingles with the leather-and-spice scent of cigar leaf.

charatan-first-bowl.z: First Bowl is a light English blend prepared in the Charatan line to take the place of Dunhill's Early Morning Pipe. As its name suggests, it is built for the day's first bowl: light Virginias form the body, Oriental leaf adds a dry spice layer, and Latakia is used only sparingly, enough to lend a thin thread of smoke. No casing is used. Flavor intensity is measured and nicotine is low; the ribbon cut burns quickly. Suitable for smokers new to Latakia blends and for those seeking a light English blend for the morning.
charatan-first-bowl.o: Leaves a light smoky, dry-hay room note.

brigham-enterprises-inc-yacht-club.z: One of Brigham's blends noted as Virginia-forward; no sufficient source documenting its composition and character could be found.

lane-limited-medal-of-valor.z: Medal of Valor is an English-style blend registered under Lane Limited; not enough sources could be found to describe its content and character.
lane-limited-medal-of-valor.o: Reportedly leaves a smoke and incense room note.

mac-baren-uncle-louie-whisky.z: Uncle Louie Whisky is the counterpart to the Rum release in Mac Baren's drink-themed Bar Selection series. Its base again consists of sweet Virginia, full Burley, and the brand's own Cavendish; single malt whisky from the Scottish highlands is stated to be used as the flavoring. Distributed as loose ribbon cut in large-capacity tins. In the smoke, the Cavendish's mildness combines with the whisky's grainy, lightly oaky tone; the Burley gives the smoke body and a dry background. Nicotine stays measured. Aimed at smokers who prefer liquor-flavored, pronounced aromatics that leave a trace in the room.
mac-baren-uncle-louie-whisky.o: Leaves an aroma of grainy whisky, light oak, and sweet tobacco.

thompson-cigar-co-high-society-coconut.z: One of the bulk aromatics Tampa-based mail-order retailer Thompson Cigar sells under its own name; the High Society series consists of heavily flavored blends, and the standout casing in this variety is coconut. Since the retailer does not disclose the leaf composition of its bulk blends, the mixture's details remain unclear.

tewksbury-company-custards-last-stand.z: According to records, this blend was part of the lineup of Tewksbury & Company, an American blender that ceased operations following the 2009 tobacco regulation; no source documenting its content and character could be found.

mac-baren-original-choice.z: Original Choice is the first member of the Choice series Mac Baren began in 1998. Per the maker, Virginia and Burley leaves sourced from North and South America are blended with the brand's Virginia-derived black Cavendish. It's presented as ribbon cut and carries a sweet, fruit-leaning top note. On opening the pack, the fruity aroma characteristic of Mac Baren Cavendish stands out. In the smoke, Virginia's weight is felt, and since the Burley proportion is low, body and nicotine stay measured. Since the tobacco can arrive moist, airing it out overnight reduces volatile flavoring and lets the taste balance settle; once aired, it can be smoked start to finish without going out. Suited to those seeking a lightly flavored blend fit for everyday smoking.
mac-baren-original-choice.o: Leaves a mild trace reminiscent of ripe fruit and sweet Cavendish.

edwards-friars-1804.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Friars 1804, a pipe tobacco from Edward's. Edward's is a tobacconist business based in Tampa, Florida.

nat-sherman-127-wayfarer.z: 127 Wayfarer is a Virginia-Perique composition among the numbered house blends of New York tobacconist Nat Sherman. According to the recipe of its creator, Christopher McGrath, roughly a third of the composition is Perique; the remainder consists of red, bright, and stoved Virginia leaves. This unusually high Perique proportion defines the blend's character from start to finish. In the smoke, peppery spice takes the lead, while Perique's typical plum-and-fig sweetness sits behind it as a deeper undertone. Being a full-bodied, nicotine-rich tobacco, it is not recommended on an empty stomach or as the day's first bowl, but rather for those looking for a filling smoke. It suits smokers accustomed to Perique as well as cigar smokers looking for intense flavor. Production ceased when Nat Sherman ended its tobacco operations in 2020.
nat-sherman-127-wayfarer.o: Leaves an aroma of dark dried fruit and tangy tobacco beneath a peppery sharpness.

peretti-cambridge-flake.z: Cambridge Flake is an English-type leaf blend Peretti offers among its pressed and sliced tobaccos. Oriental leaf and a measured proportion of Latakia are added to a Virginia base; records indicate the Latakia proportion is kept lower than the house's darker English mixtures, letting the Oriental's spicy, resinous side come through without pushing the smoky character forward. Being a pressed slice, it has a slow burn rate and the leaf needs to be opened by hand before packing. The body sits a little above medium; it suits smokers who don't want to give up on Latakia entirely but find dark Balkan mixtures too heavy. The slice form allows the tobacco to be stored in a jar for a long time, with Virginia's sugar becoming more pronounced over time.
peretti-cambridge-flake.o: Leaves a dry-hay note underneath a light smoke and toasted-bread aroma.

ken-byron-ventures-moriarty-2020.z: Moriarty 2020 is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

vogels-tabakstube-massimo.z: Massimo is Vogel's Tabakstube's unflavored, Burley-forward house blend. The leaf runs in deep brown tones, with lighter-colored pieces mixed in. It comes from a limited run the German tobacconist has made at its own facilities. The Burley lays a dry, nutty, cocoa-leaning base into the blend, while the Virginia sets a measured sweetness beneath it. As no casing is used, the flavor comes entirely from the leaf itself, giving a dry, direct smoke. Nicotine sits in the medium range. Intended for smokers who steer away from aromatics and want the plain taste of tobacco itself.
vogels-tabakstube-massimo.o: Leaves a dry tobacco aroma reminiscent of nuts and cocoa.

dunhill-my-mixture-1167.z: A discontinued mixture belonging to Dunhill's My Mixture line, for which no verifiable source on its composition could be found.

w-curtis-draper-executive.z: Executive is among the shop-specific blends from W. Curtis Draper, founded in 1887 and considered one of Washington's oldest tobacconists. Its structure is simple: an unflavored English mixture built by adding a generous amount of Latakia over Virginia leaves. Keeping the Latakia ratio high pulls the blend toward a smoky, woody, salty side; Virginia underneath leaves a measured sweetness and sugar foundation. Since it contains no flavoring, the taste comes entirely from the leaf itself. Sitting at a medium nicotine level, the blend is aimed at smokers familiar with smoky English mixtures and those seeking a single-layered, direct Latakia taste; as with this type of blend, the room note is pronounced and lingering.
w-curtis-draper-executive.o: Leaves a sharp smoke scent reminiscent of wood fire and smoky leather.

bayside-mixed-shag.z: Bayside Mixed is a shag pipe tobacco aimed at the English market. Owned by the Bull Brand, it's produced at Von Eicken's facilities in Germany — so the brand itself is British while production takes place in Germany. The blend is built from a combination of Virginia and Burley leaf, and its very fine cut makes it easy to light and slow to burn. It's a medium-bodied, understated, everyday tobacco. Its flavoring level is low; the taste that stands out is the leaf's own dry, hay-like, faintly nutty side. Because of the fine cut, the pipe needs to be packed loosely. It suits those looking for a plain, non-heavily-flavored everyday blend.
bayside-mixed-shag.o: Leaves a plain room note reminiscent of dry hay and nutty leaf.

dobies-dobies-four-square-cut-plug.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of Dobie's Four Square-Cut Plug, a blend from Dobie's.

ashton-old-dog.z: Old Dog is a full-bodied English mixture produced for Ashton, later continued by McClelland. At the blend's center is cool, smoky Cyprus Latakia; joined by Macedonian Xanthi Oriental, rested sweet Virginias, and smooth black Cavendish. Its color is dark and the smoke is heavy; the Oriental spiciness adds sharpness to Latakia's smoky base, while Virginia and Cavendish add a sweet counterweight. It's an entry for smokers accustomed to dark Latakia blends, looking for smoky intensity. Its production ended when McClelland closed and the recipes weren't transferred.
ashton-old-dog.o: Fills the room with Cyprus Latakia's heavy soot, tar, and woodsmoke scent.

peterson-early-morning-pipe.z: Early Morning Pipe is a lightly toasted, ribbon-cut English blend built by adding Oriental tobaccos and Cyprus Latakia to light and red Virginia leaf. As its name suggests, it is designed for the first pipe of the day; the Latakia proportion is kept low enough not to tire the palate. The blend comes from the Dunhill catalog and, after Dunhill ceased production, has been continued under the Peterson name with its original recipe. On the palate, Virginia's sugar and the Oriental's earthy, lightly spicy side stay in balance; the smoke merely provides a frame. Nicotine strength is between light and medium. It suits smokers wanting to get to know English blends and those seeking a smoky tobacco that stays light through the day.
peterson-early-morning-pipe.o: Leaves an unassertive trace recalling light smoke and dry spice.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-holt-coffee.z: Holt Coffee is listed as McGahey The Tobacconist's coffee-flavored house blend; sufficient sources regarding its composition and character could not be found.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-holt-coffee.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of roasted coffee beans.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-antique-pressed-.z: Antique Pressed Cigar Leaf is a pressed-cigar-leaf-based product from Hermit Tobacco Works Co., the American maker known for its Captain Earle's blends; no sufficient source describing its composition and character could be found.

samuel-gawith-black-pigtail.z: Black Pigtail is one of Samuel Gawith's finely twisted rope tobaccos. Virginia and burley leaf are twisted and matured, processed until they take on a dark color; the smoker cuts coin-sized slices and crumbles them. It is a continuation of the rope-production tradition that has run in Kendal for centuries. Its smoke is dark, earthy, and structured to bring forward the tobacco's own taste; nicotine load is high. It requires slow smoking and thorough drying. A record for smokers accustomed to rope and twist cuts who seek strong tobacco.
samuel-gawith-black-pigtail.o: Leaves a dark, tobacco-forward, lightly sweetish rope scent.

affordable-pipes-guys-favorite.z: Guy's Favorite is Affordable Pipes' unflavored Virginia-Burley blend. Only these two leaves are used; the sweetness and nutty tone come directly from the leaf itself, with no coating applied. Strength is low, taste is mild; it offers a plain smoke that can be repeated all day. It's a suitable starting point for those looking for a simple, inexpensive everyday tobacco instead of complex blends, and for smokers wanting to move from aromatics to unflavored blends.
affordable-pipes-guys-favorite.o: Leaves a dry-hay, nutty, lightly sweet tobacco room note.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-champlain.z: Champlain is among the light aromatics Wilke Pipe Tobacco prepares for everyday smoking. The blend's description is simple: a measured vanilla touch over roasted cavendish leaf. The brand devotes wide space in its bulk aromatic catalog to this type of single-note record without a heavy casing. Roasted cavendish builds a base reminiscent of brown sugar and a light toast edge; vanilla softens it without overpowering. Nicotine is low, and the burn is cool. Since the casing intensity is kept low, the tobacco's own sweetness is still felt. It suits smokers seeking an undemanding, all-day-smokable aromatic, and newcomers to the pipe.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-champlain.o: Leaves a scent of vanilla and toasted sugar.

john-b-hayes-tobacconist-fair-oaks.z: One of American tobacconist John B. Hayes' counter blends; no verifiable information on its contents could be found.
john-b-hayes-tobacconist-fair-oaks.o: No verifiable information on its room note could be found.

john-patton-oriental-dusk.z: One of the small-scale blends released under the John Patton name; not enough independent sources could be found to document its contents and character.
john-patton-oriental-dusk.o: No source could be found on the room note.

watch-city-cigar-quints-own.z: Watch City Cigar's blend called Quint's Own is, according to records, one of the house blends of the Waltham, Massachusetts tobacconist shop; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

ken-byron-ventures-spaghetti-western-2-t.z: The second, Latakia-containing installment of the Spaghetti Western series; not enough sources could be found to describe its composition.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-raven-e.z: Raven Eye Flake is a flake tobacco built from heat-matured Virginia, stoved Virginia, and Perique leaf with no added flavoring; it's offered as 2 oz. bulk. It's part of Ken Byron Ventures' budget-priced Mr. Christian's line and remains among the brand's current listings. Heat treatment and stoving darken Virginia's sugar and settle its tang; the Perique adds dark plum-and-fig fruit and a peppery spice. The flake structure gives a slow, cool burn and needs to be rubbed out and aired before smoking. Aimed at smokers seeking an unflavored Virginia/Perique blend who are used to high-intensity blends.
ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-raven-e.o: Leaves an unflavored tobacco aroma reminiscent of dark fruit and bread crust.

nording-fox-hound.z: Fox Hound is a member of the tobacco line carrying the name of the Hunting pipe series Danish pipemaker Erik Nørding has continued since 1995. The blend's name comes from hunting dog breeds. It's built from cube-cut burley, matured red and bright Virginia, cavendish, and St. James perique, with a small amount of Turkish latakia added. The line's first editions were produced by McClelland; after 2018 the line was reorganized under Cornell & Diehl. Here latakia isn't a standalone component but is used like a spice that thickens the body and cools the smoke. Cube-cut burley burns slowly and evenly, while perique leaves a fruity spice trace in the background. It suits smokers seeking an American-style blend where latakia stays measured.
nording-fox-hound.o: Leaves a thin layer of incense beneath a scent of nuts and dry grass.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-captain-earles-m.z: Mystic Blend is one of the English-character members of the Captain Earle's line, prepared by Cornell & Diehl for Hermit Tobacco Works. Records indicate it brings together nine separate tobacco types: Latakia, various Virginias, Oriental leaves, Perique, and black Cavendish are pressed into a crumble cake. Thanks to this structure, the tobacco is rubbed out by hand before filling, and the cut takes on an appearance between broken flake and ribbon. Latakia is pronounced, but the red Virginia's sugary tone is felt steadily beneath the smoke; Perique traces a spicy edge. The line's name comes from James A. M. Earle, captain of the 1841 whaling ship Charles W. Morgan; the blend's name also references Mystic, Connecticut, where the captain was born. Offering moderate nicotine and an intense taste, it suits smokers familiar with Latakia blends and those looking for depth in English mixtures. It carries no flavoring; the taste comes entirely from the leaf composition.
hermit-tobacco-works-co-captain-earles-m.o: Leaves a light sweet-bread trace beneath the aroma of wood smoke and smoked leather.

cornell-diehl-cavendish.z: One of Cornell & Diehl's cavendish-based single-leaf offerings; it does not appear under this name in the manufacturer's current catalog, and not enough sourcing could be found to document its details.

peter-stokkebye-tivoli-mild-cavendish.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Tivoli Mild Cavendish in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

e-a-carey-europe-dark-flake-no-7.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Dark Flake No 7, a pipe tobacco from E. A. Carey (Europe).

mcclelland-no-820-amaretto-amore.z: A blend in McClelland's bulk aromatic series, discontinued when the firm closed in 2018; no sufficient source documenting its contents and character could be found.

milan-tobacconists-101-burley.z: A blend in Milan Tobacconists' non-aromatic line, resting on a single leaf type. It is built from coarse-cut white burley and rested before being offered for sale; no other leaf or casing is added. It is a slow-burning mixture with a thick body where the tobacco taste comes forward directly. Suitable for experienced smokers looking for an unsweetened, plain burley character and wanting a long, cool smoke in their pipe. Its nicotine is markedly higher than that of aromatics.
milan-tobacconists-101-burley.o: Leaves a dry walnut-shell and earthy burnt-leaf aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-1m.z: Sutliff 1M is a ribbon-cut bulk aromatic built by adding Green River-style black cavendish to Virginia and burley leaves. The maker doesn't disclose the flavoring recipe; the description states only that a proprietary aroma blend is used to create an intense scent while keeping the smoke soft. The blend sits in the classic golden-cavendish mold of American shop aromatics: nicotine fullness is low, the flavor line is sweet and straightforward, and burning behavior is predictable. Suited to those seeking a soft, all-day aromatic with a lasting room note; since it comes moist, it may need airing before packing.
sutliff-tobacco-company-1m.o: Leaves a sweet, sugary, lightly creamy scent.

gawith-hoggarth-co-danish-blend.z: Danish Blend, also listed in the brand's catalog under the name "Exclusiv DB," is one of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Danish-style aromatics. Virginia and black Cavendish are processed with a casing based on ripe peach and honey. It's ribbon cut; the golden-yellow leaves and black Cavendish appear intertwined, packing easily and giving off plenty of smoke. On the smoke, Virginia's herbal-sweet base and Cavendish's fermented mellowness stand out, topped with a layer reminiscent of buttery candy and a peach note. Nicotine stays light. A structure suited to those wanting a classic Continental European aromatic away from Lakeland-style floral essences, and to smokers in their early years with the pipe.
gawith-hoggarth-co-danish-blend.o: The aroma of ripe peach and honey spreads through the room, with dry-hay and raisin notes behind it.

arrowhead-arrowhead-blue-pipe-tobacco.z: No adequate independent source describing the content and character of the blend called Arrowhead Blue could be found.
arrowhead-arrowhead-blue-pipe-tobacco.o: No reliable information on the room note could be found.

edwards-woodsman.z: No sufficient independent sourcing could be reached to document the composition and character of Woodsman, a pipe tobacco from Edward's.

sutliff-tobacco-company-creme-brulee-701.z: Sutliff Creme Brulee is a ribbon-cut bulk blend where a base of black cavendish, burley, and Virginia is given a heavy dose of creamy vanilla, honey, and caramel flavoring. Fittingly for the dessert it's named after, it aims for a custard-and-cream-oriented profile. The topping level is high; both the taste and the room note are pronouncedly sweet, with the tobacco's own leaf character staying in the background. Nicotine fullness is low. Suited to those seeking heavily sweet aromatics; since it comes out moist, letting it sit before packing changes its burning behavior.
sutliff-tobacco-company-creme-brulee-701.o: Creamy vanilla, honey, and burnt-sugar scent fills the room.

stanwell-classic.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Stanwell blend Classic could not be found.

e-a-carey-english-blend-no-2.z: English Blend No. 2 is E. A. Carey's unadulterated blend following the classic English mixture approach. Per the maker's description, soft Georgia Virginias, black cavendish, Mexican burley and Cyprus latakia are brought together loose cut. Latakia smoke forms the backbone of the taste; Virginia sweetness stays in the background while burley carries the body. The maker describes its strength as ranging from mild to medium. It suits smokers new to smoky, unadulterated blends and those wanting to smoke the classic English profile as an everyday choice. Per records, it has been sold in 50-gram tins and in bulk.
e-a-carey-english-blend-no-2.o: Leaves a smoky trace evoking soot, pine smoke and dry wood.

cup-o-joes-adirondack-balkan-pipe-tobacc.z: A Balkan-style mixture from the Cup O' Joes tobacco shop's Adirondack house-blend series; no source documenting its composition and ratios was found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-troost-sl.z: Troost Slices is a slice-cut blend that stands apart in the Dutch brand Troost's almost entirely sweet-aromatic range. Since the slices are cut thicker than flakes, they are packed by rubbing or folding and give a slow burn. The blend rests on a burley-forward body; virginia leaf carries a mild sweetness in the background and no pronounced casing is perceptible. Suited to those seeking an unflavored, full-bodied, plain Continental European press.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-troost-sl.o: Leaves a dry, bready, and lightly sweet, plain tobacco scent.

gallaher-limited-condor-blended-yellow.z: This is the yellow-packaged version of Gallaher's Condor series; no independent source could be found regarding the blend's composition and cut.
gallaher-limited-condor-blended-yellow.o: Leaves the floral Lakeland essence aroma characteristic of the Condor series.

nat-sherman-414-nat-sherman-85th-anniver.z: A blend Nat Sherman prepared for its 85th anniversary, reported to be an English-style mixture containing Latakia; no detailed independent source on its proportions and character could be found.
nat-sherman-414-nat-sherman-85th-anniver.o: Leaves a woody, smoky aroma from the Latakia.

sutliff-tobacco-company-brg-mixture.z: BRG Mixture is a blend made from a coarse-cut combination of burley and Virginia leaves, topped with a thin plum, vanilla, and liqueur-direction flavoring. Because the topping level is kept low, its character is built between burley's nutty fullness and Virginia's tangy sweetness. The name references Clare Briggs, a cartoonist known for comic strips published in American newspapers in the 1920s; records indicate the blend was developed as an equivalent to Briggs Mixture, which sold for many years. Suited to smokers seeking an old-fashioned, medium-bodied, lightly flavored everyday mixture.
sutliff-tobacco-company-brg-mixture.o: Leaves a dry, tobacco-forward scent carrying a light plum sweetness.

cornell-diehl-red-carpet.z: Red Carpet is a mixture in which Cornell & Diehl presents red Virginias and Perique pressed and sliced into flake. Per the maker's listing, the composition consists purely of Virginia and Perique; there's no Latakia, Oriental leaf, or casing. Pressing concentrates the red leaf's breadlike, fruity sweetness. Perique balances Virginia's sweetness by adding a measured spice layer evoking plum and pepper. When the flake is rubbed out or folded for packing, it burns cool and slow. Suited to smokers wanting to get to know the classic VaPer line and looking for a flake well suited to aging.
cornell-diehl-red-carpet.o: Leaves a lightly plummy tobacco note mingling with a scent of dry hay and citrus.

hu-tobacco-masai.z: Masai is a Latakia-containing blend that appeared in HU Tobacco's line, first called Foundation by Musicó and later African Line. Its base is built from ready-rubbed honeydew Virginia leaf; strong Malawi Burley, dark-fired Kentucky, and, records indicate, roughly seventeen percent Cyprus Latakia are added. Syrian Latakia was used in the blend's early versions; once that stock ran out, it switched to Cyprus Latakia. The result is a medium-to-full-strength mixture where spice and sweetness are balanced; smoky and cocoa-evoking notes come forward. Per the maker's statement, production of the blend has been discontinued.
hu-tobacco-masai.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma evoking smoky wood and cocoa.

hu-tobacco-soraya.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the Soraya blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

house-of-windsor-mapleton.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for House of Windsor's Mapleton blend, so its content and character could not be recorded.

julius-vesz-c-8.z: A blend bearing the name of Toronto pipe maker Julius Vesz; not enough independent sources could be found on its contents and character.

lane-limited-crown-achievement.z: Crown Achievement is Lane Limited's latakia-forward blend, built with latakia, Virginia, Macedonian-sourced oriental leaves and perique, in a ribbon cut. Perique was reportedly removed from the formula around 2004 and restored when the blend was reissued in 2012 using the original recipe kept in old records. At one point it was cited as the most expensive pipe tobacco on the market. The flavor profile is earthy and leathery, carrying a dry hay and spice side; it's neither distinctly sweet nor bitter. Latakia leads but isn't dominant on its own; Virginia and oriental leaves add a subdued sweetness and sharpness. Suited to smokers seeking a medium-bodied, unflavored English-Balkan-style blend.
lane-limited-crown-achievement.o: Leaves a smoke, incense and dry-hay room note with a sharp spice edge.

dan-tobacco-africa-black-and-bright.z: Africa Black and Bright is an aromatic blend in German maker Dan Tobacco's series referencing ocean-liner ships. Its composition is light and red Virginia leaf in varying cuts with a small amount of very soft black Cavendish, topped with a tropical-fruit-leaning flavoring. The Virginia base gives the blend a dry sweetness and hay character, while the black Cavendish rounds out the body and softens the smoke. Nicotine load is low, flavor intensity medium. Built for smokers who like fruited aromatics but want to avoid a heavy syrupy texture. The blend is no longer in production today.
dan-tobacco-africa-black-and-bright.o: Leaves a sweet tropical-fruit and caramelized-sugar scent.

hearth-home-old-kinderhook.z: Old Kinderhook is a cherry-flavored blend belonging to one of Hearth & Home's place-name-inspired series. It is built from a combination of Burley, Virginia, and toasted black Cavendish leaf; the cherry note comes through in both taste and aroma. The sharp bite on the tongue common to cherry-flavored mixtures is said not to be pronounced in this recipe; the black Cavendish ratio softens the blend. It was a light-to-medium bodied option for smokers seeking a cherry aromatic; the blend is no longer in production.
hearth-home-old-kinderhook.o: Leaves an aroma of ripe cherry with a light hint of burnt sugar.

fincks-cigar-company-early-english.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for Finck's Cigar Company's Early English pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

dunhill-ye-olde-signe-re-release.z: Ye Olde Signe is one of Dunhill's oldest mixtures; per records, it was first produced in 1915 and presented in period catalogs as a soft, finely sweet pure Virginia leaf with high natural sweetness. It's made from a composition of Virginia leaves in different colors, cut fine ribbon and put through a fermentation process; this gives the tin a natural, tea-like scent. On the smoke it shows a medium-strength, balanced structure; Virginia sweetness is pronounced and smoke volume is high. It suits smokers seeking unadulterated Virginia blends who want to keep the tobacco's own taste front and center. The blend was reissued after a long gap and left the list when pipe tobacco production under the Dunhill name ended.
dunhill-ye-olde-signe-re-release.o: Leaves a fine, sweet scent evoking brewed tea and dry hay.

g-l-pease-union-square-fog-city-selectio.z: Union Square is an untopped blend made entirely from Virginia leaves, part of G. L. Pease's Fog City Selection line. After pressing, it is presented in broken-flake form. Virginia's natural sugar and the leaf's characteristic light bitterness sit together throughout the smoke; the nicotine dose is medium. It comes moist from the tin and dries quickly; records note that airing it to remove moisture settles both the burn and the aroma. It suits smokers wanting to smoke pure Virginia blends at any time of day, and those intending to age it.
g-l-pease-union-square-fog-city-selectio.o: Leaves an aroma of dry grass and a honey-like sweet tobacco note.

dobies-dobies-four-square-red-aromatic.z: This is a blend in the aromatic branch of the Four Square series, distinguished by its red label. The series began in 1922 with George Dobie & Son in Paisley; over time, blending shifted from Scotland to Denmark and then to the United States. No independent source documenting this blend's leaf composition and aroma could be found.

tambolaka-natural-tobaccos-tambolaka-pip.z: No reliable source could be found on Tambolaka Natural Tobaccos' Tambolaka Pipe Tobacco blend.

joseph-martin-old-bohan.z: A blend from the Joseph Martin house, known for Belgian Semois tobacco; not enough independent sources could be found on its contents and character.

cornell-diehl-sansepolcro-2024.z: Sansepolcro is a blend in Cornell & Diehl's limited Small Batch series. It takes its name from Italy's Sansepolcro region, where tobacco growing dates back to the 17th century; the blend's core is KY171 Italian dark fire-cured Kentucky leaf, grown on a small farm there, cured and fermented twice. This leaf is joined by select red and light Virginia grades and unsweetened Dominican black Cavendish. In the 2024 release, the mixture was rested under press for seven days, then sliced as flake instead of ready-rub. On the flavor side, soft citrus notes come forward alongside a spicy undertone reminiscent of earth and clove. Thanks to the body the fire-cured leaf brings, it offers a filling smoke; suited to smokers who like dark Virginia-and-Kentucky compositions, accustomed to smoking flake.
cornell-diehl-sansepolcro-2024.o: Leaves a spicy tobacco scent mingling with woody smoke and dried fruit.

pauls-pipe-shop-58th-anniversary-tobacco.z: 58th Anniversary is one of the celebratory blends Paul's Pipe Shop of Flint, Michigan prepared for the shop's anniversary. Per the maker's recipe, it combines seven distinct cavendish varieties, topped with rum and raisin essence. Since the leaf selection is entirely processed cavendish, nicotine load is low and the smoke texture mild. The blend sits in the classic American shop-aromatic line, where the topping stands out more than the tobacco's own taste. The rum-and-raisin pairing leaves a sweet, fruity impression, at an intensity easy to smoke at any hour. It suits newcomers to aromatic blends and those looking for flavored cavendish rather than unflavored leaf. It's blended at the shop's own counter and sold only in person or by phone.
pauls-pipe-shop-58th-anniversary-tobacco.o: Leaves a scent of sugary rum and raisin.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-twist-coffee-ca.z: Brown Twist is a strong, earthy rope produced by twisting fire-cured Virginia and Indian leaves; the "brown" name shows that the rope is left as it comes off the machine without press-cooking. This version gives the rope a coffee- and caramel-based flavouring, so the smoky base of fire curing joins a roasted, sugary top note. Preparation follows the usual path for rope tobaccos: a thin slice, thorough rubbing, and airing before filling. In terms of nicotine and flavour it sits near the upper end and needs slow smoking. It is aimed at experienced smokers seeking a strong English rope with a sweet flavouring.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-twist-coffee-ca.o: A roasted coffee and burnt-sugar aroma spreads through the room together with the smoke of the fire-cured tobacco.

park-lane-tobacconist-turkish-mystery.z: Turkish Mystery is one of the English-style mixtures prepared at the counter of Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York. Per the shop's description, various oriental leaves form the blend's backbone, joined by a substantial amount of Cyprian latakia and a sugary Virginia that pulls the mixture toward sweetness at the finish. Although latakia holds a considerable share, the descriptions emphasize the oriental leaf's tart, spicy, dried-herb-like character; in this respect the blend sits in the line of an unflavored, full-bodied Balkan mixture. Offered as a ribbon cut, the tobacco tips the latakia-oriental balance toward the oriental side, setting it apart from classic English mixtures where latakia dominates. It suits smokers interested in unflavored mixtures who are used to smoky, spicy tastes; it isn't an entry blend for those coming from aromatic tobacco. Being a small retailer's house blend, its distribution is limited and its production status is unclear from records.
park-lane-tobacconist-turkish-mystery.o: Leaves a lightly sweet tobacco scent alongside wood smoke and spiced resin.

paul-olsen-no-75-full.z: One of the Virginia-forward blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-anisette.z: Referred to as an anise-flavored version within Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Virginia-bodied Kendal Gold shag series; no reliable sourcing giving details specific to this version's composition and character could be found.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-anisette.o: Leaves an anise and sweet tobacco aroma.

lane-limited-very-cherry.z: Referred to as one of Lane Limited's bulk cherry-flavored blends; since some retailers reportedly use the same name for other Lane blends, its content and character information could not be confirmed.
lane-limited-very-cherry.o: Leaves a sweet, cherry-forward room note.

cornell-diehl-gentleman-caller.z: Gentleman Caller is a Virginia-and-burley-based ribbon-cut American blend. Deer tongue, which gives the mixture a vanilla-like sweetness, is joined by a small amount of perique for spice; the sweetness comes not from an added flavoring but from this plant's natural scent. The intensity of its aroma is the source of the blend's name: Cornell & Diehl describes the product as reminiscent of a mixture grandmothers kept in a bowl as a room scent while entertaining guests. On the smoke, burley's nutty dryness, Virginia's light sweetness, and perique's occasional spice touch move along together. It suits those looking for an all-day blend sitting somewhere between unflavored and lightly aromatic.
cornell-diehl-gentleman-caller.o: Leaves a sweet, vanilla-like herbal aroma along with a nutty tobacco scent.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-47th-street.z: 47th Street originated as the blend of the shop called Tobacco Center, and was taken over by Wilke Pipe Tobacco in the mid-1900s and added to the brand's catalog. Named after one of New York's streets associated with tobacconist shops, this record is part of Wilke's tradition of keeping old city blends alive. The blend is Virginia-based; a notable amount of Latakia and Perique is worked over it. Virginia gives tart fruit and bready sweetness, while Latakia adds a layer of soot and burnt wood, and Perique contributes spice reminiscent of dried plum and black pepper. There's no casing, so the flavor is entirely leaf-derived. Since the body stays above medium, it suits smokers familiar with English mixtures who want a spicy edge.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-47th-street.o: Leaves a smoky scent reminiscent of wood fire and dry spice.

two-friends-valle-crucis.z: Valle Crucis is the member of the Two Friends line classed as an aromatic English. Turkish Latakia is blended with ripe red Virginia leaves; Oriental leaf and a pinch of light flue-cured leaf are added on top, and Perique and black Cavendish also appear in the composition. It is presented ribbon cut. While Latakia smoke sets the blend's frame, Virginia sweetness and the Oriental leaf's dry spice settle within that frame; a lingering sweetness and a soft spicy edge remain on the palate. Nicotine and flavor intensity stay in the medium range, and the room note is more reserved than typical English blends. A profile for smokers who don't find Latakia blends too heavy but want the smoke kept measured.
two-friends-valle-crucis.o: Spice and dried-fruit sweetness drift through a smoky wood aroma.

king-street-coffee-tobacco-emporium-blac.z: Black Cordial is a dark-colored blend King Street Emporium lists as black-cherry flavored. Per the description, black leaf fire-cured to four different degrees is combined with sweet Virginia accents; both its appearance and taste stand apart from usual aromatics. Records indicate the blend is credited as a Sutliff product and sold on the shop shelf under this name. It's a mixture with low nicotine and pronounced casing load. Suited to those seeking dark, fruity, sweet-leaning aromatics and to smokers who don't mind Virginia's own sugar staying in the background.
king-street-coffee-tobacco-emporium-blac.o: Leaves a dark, fruity, sweet room note reminiscent of black cherry liqueur.

davidoff-green-mixture.z: Green Mixture is one of the members of Davidoff's color-named aromatic trio. It consists of Virginia and black cavendish leaves, ready-rubbed cut, and carries vanilla and caramel flavoring. Its fullness is light and the smoke is soft. Turkish-language sources state it's built on a shared structure with Red and Blue Mixture in the same series. It suits smokers seeking an easy-smoking, flavored cavendish blend.
davidoff-green-mixture.o: Leaves a sweet scent where vanilla and caramel stand out.

cest-la-vie-creme-caramel.z: No independent, reliable source could be found for the blend named Creme Caramel under the C'est La Vie brand, so the entry details could not be verified.

d-r-tobacco-don-giovanni-sigaretta.z: Don Giovanni Sigaretta is the lighter member of the cigar-leaf-based line Mark Ryan created within Daughters & Ryan. Cigar leaf from Nicaragua, Ecuador, Indonesia, Brazil, and the Dominican Republic is added on top of Virginia leaf; the cut is a fine shag. Its flavor structure combines the earthy, creamy, spicy tones the cigar leaf brings with the sweetness Virginia adds. Compared to Sigaro, the other member of the line, it follows a lighter, sweeter line. When smoked dry it tends to burn fast, so it needs careful moisture management; aimed at smokers looking for cigar flavor within a pipe.
d-r-tobacco-don-giovanni-sigaretta.o: Leaves an earthy, sharp scent reminiscent of cigar smoke.

sir-william-english-latakia.z: A Latakia-forward blend recorded under the Sir William name; no source confirming its content and producer could be found.
sir-william-english-latakia.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

w-o-larsen-lotus.z: W.Ø. Larsen Lotus is a blend on the brand's distinctly aromatic wing. According to records, it's built from a combination of black cavendish, brown cavendish, and Virginia leaves; the heavy cavendish share darkens the blend's color and brings its natural sugar forward. A casing giving coconut and vanilla notes is applied on top, and this pairing is the main element that defines the tobacco's identity. The high cavendish ratio makes the blend soft and easy on the tongue; nicotine stays below medium. On the flavor side, the sweet, creamy line carried by the casing is heard more than the tobacco's own character, while Virginia leaves a light acidic balance in the background. It suits those who enjoy distinctly flavored, sweet blends and don't mind a scent that spreads through the room.
w-o-larsen-lotus.o: Leaves a sweet, creamy scent in which coconut and vanilla come forward.

peter-stokkebye-virginia-special.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Virginia Special in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

japan-tobacco-momoyama-3.z: No reliable source documenting the content and character of Japan Tobacco's Momoyama 3 blend could be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-sail-regu.z: The Sail brand's base version; no sufficient primary source describing the blend's composition and character could be found.

wesleys-no-22-virginian-cavendish.z: This blend, registered under the Wesley's name, does not appear in the maker's current house-blend listing; no source could be found documenting its composition and character.
wesleys-no-22-virginian-cavendish.o: No description could be found as no source was available.

pipesandcigars-com-acadian-vaper.z: No independent source material could be found sufficient to fill out a specification for the pipesandcigars.com blend called Acadian VaPer.

b-b-tobacconists-llc-becks-ol-limey-bast.z: Beck's Ol' Limey Bastard is an English mixture hand-blended and sold in bulk by B&B Tobacconists. In the maker's presentation, the blend is placed at the center of classic English mixtures and is noted as being approved by members of the London Pipe Club. The Latakia share is high enough to make the blend smoky and full, but it isn't built purely on Latakia intensity; a light sweetness from the Virginias sits beneath the smoky base. It has an easy-packing, easy-lighting, balanced structure. It suits smokers looking for a Latakia-forward but not overdone everyday English mixture.
b-b-tobacconists-llc-becks-ol-limey-bast.o: Leaves a smoky room note leaning toward wet moss and woodsmoke.

murray-sons-co-ltd-murrays-1862-whitehal.z: One of the discontinued blends from the Belfast-based Murray Sons & Co factory; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

doctor-pipe-good-morning.z: This is a blend where sweet Oriental leaf is combined with red Virginia and a small amount of Latakia, pressed and lightly toasted. It's noted as designed for the day's first bowls; despite its light body it carries a pronounced flavor.
doctor-pipe-good-morning.o: Leaves a light soot scent along with tart, herbal Oriental notes.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-nottingham-blend.z: Nottingham Blend is Gauntleys' shop blend carrying the store's own name. Selected Virginia leaves are joined with kentucky, latakia, spiced black cavendish, and cigar leaf; this combination gives the blend a smoky, spicy, tobacco-forward character. It is a record for those seeking traditional English mixtures over flavoured aromatics.
gauntleys-of-nottingham-nottingham-blend.o: Leaves a heavy aroma where woody latakia smoke meets spicy cigar leaf.

sutliff-tobacco-company-queen-annes-reve.z: Queen Anne's Revenge, coded D64, takes its name from the flagship of the pirate Edward Teach (Blackbeard). A measured rum flavoring is applied to a ribbon-cut base of sweet Virginia, soft burley, and black cavendish leaf. The rum note is kept light enough not to overshadow the base tobacco; nicotine and taste intensity are also low. It falls within the interest of those looking for an aromatic with a noticeable but not overpowering casing.
sutliff-tobacco-company-queen-annes-reve.o: Leaves a lightly rum-scented, sweet, soft aroma.

ken-byron-ventures-handsome-stranger.z: Handsome Stranger is one of Ken Byron Ventures' Burley-forward blends. Burley's dry, nutty, cocoa-leaning body is balanced by Virginia; the cut is ribbon. The brand states it uses its own dark-fired leaf in processing the Burley. Nicotine runs above medium and flavor intensity is pronounced, placing it among the blends often paired with coffee. Suited to experienced smokers seeking an earthy, full-bodied Burley character away from sugary aromatics. Produced in limited batches.
ken-byron-ventures-handsome-stranger.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of roasted nuts, cocoa, and bread crust.

john-dengler-pirates-chest.z: One of the aromatic blends from Dengler tobacconist in Hermann, Missouri; no verifiable information on its contents could be found.
john-dengler-pirates-chest.o: No verifiable information on its room note could be found.

davidoff-malawi-dark-cavendish.z: Malawi Dark Cavendish is a blend in Davidoff's Discovery series, black-Cavendish-forward with Burley and golden Virginia. Its cut consists of fairly thick ribbons, and in the pack you find a tobacco that has become block-like and is quite dry.
