On opening the pack, a Danish-style Cavendish scent carrying sour and sugary echoes rises; after airing and resting, a floral vanilla scent accompanied by coffee and chocolate echoes comes forward. It catches and sustains its burn easily; it doesn't bite the tongue, though it carries a risk of heating up fast if the pace picks up. The smoke is light, leaving a taste that's now sweet, now lightly bitter in the mouth. Despite a light nicotine load, its deep, full aromatic profile gives a heavy smoke; toward the end, Burley becomes pronounced, turning toward a bitterish tone. It's a record on the edge of Danish-type aromatics, worth considering for those wanting to move from mediocre aromatics to more substantial blends and those interested in Lakeland blends.
davidoff-malawi-dark-cavendish.o: Leaves a mild scent evoking a bakery, vanilla and baked dough.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-four-seaso.z: Four Seasons Match is a blend in Sutliff's Match line based on McClelland's Four Seasons. It follows the Dutch-style aromatic line: a not-heavy, grassy-spicy sweetness casing is applied over a Virginia, burley, and black cavendish base. A light herbal-spice note that holds steady throughout the smoke stands out. Smoked slowly and in moderation it gives a consistent taste; records note that a brief drying period before lighting helps. It is noted to differ from the original blend in its cut. It is aimed at smokers avoiding heavy aromatics and looking for a moderate sweetness.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-four-seaso.o: Leaves a scent combining an herbal-spicy sweetness with toasted leaf.

mcclelland-2017-holiday-spirit.z: Holiday Spirit is the name of McClelland's aromatic series released each year for the holiday season; the 2017 release is among the last batches right before the brand's closure. It's a ribbon-cut blend prepared by giving dark-rum, pecan, and cocoa notes over nutty Burley, sweet Virginia, and black Cavendish. With its medium-light nicotine level and pronounced sweetness, it's a structure suited both to smokers used to aromatic blends and those new to the pipe. The tin note and room note lean sweet; it contains no sharp components like Latakia or Perique. McClelland was founded in Kansas City in 1977 and stopped production in 2018, so the blend is found only in old stock.
mcclelland-2017-holiday-spirit.o: Leaves an aroma of dark rum, cocoa, and toasted walnut in the room.

ferndown-black-tan.z: Black & Tan is a member of a small tobacco line prepared for the British pipe maker Ferndown, sold in 50-gram packs. According to retailer records, the blend consists of toasted Virginia leaves and mild Oriental leaves; it carries no flavouring. The toasting process darkens Virginia's sugar, while the Oriental leaf adds a dry-grass and light-spice line to it. Since it contains no latakia, the smoke doesn't carry the smoky taste of English blends; the nicotine load is on the light side. It suits smokers seeking a plain, untopped Virginia-Oriental blend. The line's distribution has stayed limited and its current production status is unclear.
ferndown-black-tan.o: Leaves a measured aroma leaning toward toasted bread sweetness, with a dry-grass note behind it.

mcclelland-p-m-pipe.z: No sufficient source describing the contents and character of McClelland's blend named P.M. Pipe could be found.

straus-tobacco-harris-tweed.z: Harris Tweed is one of the counter blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; records indicate the shop was founded in 1880 and that most of its house blends were named after Cincinnati neighborhoods and landmark buildings. Since no independent source on the blend's composition and character could be found, this record is kept at listing level only.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-rosebud.z: Rosebud is, records indicate, one of the one-off blends released by Hermit Tobacco Works Co.; no sufficient source describing the blend's composition could be found.
hermit-tobacco-works-co-rosebud.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-family-res.z: Family Reserve is, according to available listings, a mixture drawn from Erik Stokkebye's grandfather's personal blending notebook; not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition.
erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-family-res.o: Could not be described due to insufficient sourcing.

hearth-home-concerto.z: An American-style Hearth & Home blend built on dark leaf; there is not enough independent sourcing to detail its composition.
hearth-home-concerto.o: Leaves a roasted-nut and earthy tobacco aroma.

roman-peter-sobranie.z: A mixture classified as English-style from Swiss blender Roman Peter; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

cornell-diehl-granby-station.z: Granby Station is a Cornell & Diehl aromatic named after the Granby station gateway to the Rocky Mountains. Black cavendish and red Virginia leaf are topped with perique; the blend is coated with a vanilla and applejack (apple liqueur) flavor. The cavendish-heavy composition keeps the smoke mild and sweet, while perique leaves a light spicy edge in the background. Carrying a pronounced flavoring, it suits those looking for a sweet, fruity aromatic and wanting a light bowl during the day.
cornell-diehl-granby-station.o: Leaves an aroma of vanilla and baked apple.

robert-mcconnell-special-london-mild.z: There is not enough independent source material on this straight Virginia blend from Robert McConnell's Special London line.

sutliff-tobacco-company-navigator-blend.z: Records present this as a Sutliff blend billed as a sweet aromatic built from dark leaf; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

craftsman-flake-supreme.z: Recorded as a blend sold under the Craftsman name, understood from its name to be flake cut; no source documenting its composition was found.

w-o-larsen-spring-meadow.z: This is an aromatic blend known under the W.O. Larsen name; no reliable source could be found documenting its composition and character.

mcclelland-anniversary-1977-2010.z: McClelland prepared a limited anniversary tobacco for its twenty-fifth founding anniversary in 2002 and repeated the same special production in 2005 and 2010. The 2010 edition is presented in a tin wrapped in heavy paper and sealed on top with brown wax; records indicate a rest of several years is recommended for this tobacco. Its contents consist of aged Virginia with a measured Latakia share, with no flavoring. The Latakia aroma that spreads on opening the tin leans sweet rather than bitter. The smoke starts mild and grows firmer as the bowl progresses; the final portion of the bowl gains noticeable fullness. It therefore falls within the territory of those used to Latakia blends who aren't bothered by a strong smoke. A tobacco that could be considered for winter, after-coffee, or after-dinner smokes.
mcclelland-anniversary-1977-2010.o: Leaves an intense Latakia-soot aroma that's sweet rather than bitter.

cornell-diehl-buffalo-soldier.z: Buffalo Soldier is a blend Cornell & Diehl dedicated to the U.S. Army's 9th, 10th, 24th, and 25th Regiments. These all-Black units, formed after the Civil War and serving through World War II, were known as the "Buffalo Soldiers." The blend is built by adding a measured proportion of Latakia and perique to a base of naturally sweet Virginia leaf; the cut is ribbon. Latakia is not dominant; Virginia's sweetness and perique's spicy accent balance the smoke. The maker places the blend in the English family and describes it as a mixture fit for all-day smoking. It suits those looking for a balanced, medium-strength English blend rather than heavy Latakia.
cornell-diehl-buffalo-soldier.o: Virginia's sweet, bready aroma accompanies a woody smoke scent.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-garibaldi.z: A pipe-tobacco brand within Scandinavian Tobacco Group's portfolio; no independent source on the blend's content and character could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-garibaldi.o: No detailed description of the room note could be found in the records.

pcca-new-world-flake.z: A flake blend within the USA series PCCA had McClelland produce; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

wesleys-no-42-mellow-cavendish.z: Mellow Cavendish belongs to the Scandinavian-American style house blend group from Wesley's tobacconist. According to the maker's recipe, some pressed leaf (flake) is added to a cavendish body; this addition keeps the blend's taste on a soft, sweet line.
wesleys-no-42-mellow-cavendish.o: Leaves a sweet, soft cavendish scent.

consolidated-136-cherokee.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Consolidated blend 136: Cherokee.

cornell-diehl-blue-ridge.z: Blue Ridge is a ribbon-cut blend Cornell & Diehl places in its Virginia family. Its base is stoved red Virginia leaf; a considerable proportion of black cavendish, Turkish leaf, and Louisiana perique are added. Red Virginia's dark, bready sweetness is balanced by perique's dried-plum-and-spice accent and the Oriental leaf's dry, grassy tang; black cavendish adds a softening sweetness to the blend. The blend's name references the Shenandoah section of the Appalachian range. It suits smokers looking for a medium-bodied Virginia blend with sugar sweetening low enough to be considered essentially unflavored, who enjoy the complexity of perique and Oriental leaf without wanting heavy Latakia. Being a ribbon cut makes it easy to pack and light.
cornell-diehl-blue-ridge.o: Leaves a lightly spiced, earthy tobacco aroma carrying a dried-fruit sweetness.

dunhill-alan-ladds-mixture.z: A discontinued blend from Dunhill's line of custom-order mixtures, for which no verifiable source on its composition could be found.

leonard-dingler-ltd-boxer.z: Not enough sources could be found to confirm the contents of South African manufacturer Leonard Dingler's Virginia-forward Boxer blend.

bentley-the-oriental-amber.z: Bentley is a pipe tobacco line put on the market by the German tobacco house August Schuster. Sitting at the spicier end of the line, The Oriental Amber is based on a combination of Virginia and Oriental leaf; small amounts of Perique and Latakia are added to deepen the blend. Virginia's measured sweetness is balanced by the Oriental leaf's dry, spicy, tangy tones; the Perique brings a plum-and-pepper sharpness, while the Latakia adds a light smoky layer that stays in the background. Because the flavoring load is low, the blend reads as close to natural taste rather than aromatic. It suits smokers who want Latakia as a complementary rather than dominant element and have an interest in Oriental-forward mixtures.
bentley-the-oriental-amber.o: Leaves a dry-spice room note with a faint woody smokiness.

hu-tobacco-night-owl.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the Night Owl blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

mac-baren-golden-blend.z: Golden Blend is a burley-forward blend Mac Baren launched in 1952. Specially selected brown burley tobaccos are mixed with a small amount of golden Virginia, then pressed and rested. The pressed cake is cut into wide slices and partly rubbed to give the brand's known burn. The character rests on burley's dry, nutty taste; Virginia adds a fine sweetness. A long-standing recipe for those seeking classic, non-aromatic burley flavor.
mac-baren-golden-blend.o: Leaves a dry tobacco note reminiscent of nuts and bread crust.

richs-mild-burley.z: Mild Burley is, as its name suggests, a mild Burley-based bulk blend from Rich's Cigar Store; no verifiable source could be found giving its detailed composition.
richs-mild-burley.o: No reliable information could be found on the room note.

king-smoking-pipes-and-cigars-king-of-sp.z: A blend sold at King Smoking Pipes and Cigars' own shop, listed as an English mixture; content details could not be confirmed since the product page could not be reached.
king-smoking-pipes-and-cigars-king-of-sp.o: Reportedly close to the smoky, canvas-like scent left by Latakia-containing English blends.

bjarne-viking-erik-the-red.z: The cherry- and vanilla-flavored aromatic in the Viking line named after Danish pipe maker Bjarne Nielsen; no adequate independent source on its content could be found.

dutch-blend-dutch-blend.z: No reliable source could be found identifying the maker, composition, or production status of this record, whose name is merely a generic label.
dutch-blend-dutch-blend.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-drake.z: Drake is an aromatic blend in Kohlhase & Kopp's Caribbean Blue line. Like the rest of the series, it's produced in Germany and named after a pirate captain. It contains both brown and black cavendish alongside naturally sweet Virginia leaves; the cavendish share raises the blend's sugar load. The top casing consists of pineapple, banana and Madagascar vanilla; this trio gives a taste between tropical fruit and a baked dessert. Nicotine level stays low, making it suited to long sessions and to those new to aromatic tobacco. Due to the high cavendish proportion, it's a moist tobacco; airing it before packing and smoking slowly reduces pooling in the bowl.
kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-drake.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla room note alongside pineapple and banana.

w-o-larsen-navy-flake.z: This is a flake blend bearing the W.O. Larsen name; no reliable source could be found documenting its composition and character.

balkan-sasieni-balkan-sasieni.z: Balkan Sasieni is a Balkan mixture with origins in London and a history of nearly a century. Macedonian and Black Sea Orientals are brought together with a generous amount of Cyprus Latakia over a base of golden and red Virginia; production today takes place in Denmark, with tins going mostly to the North American market. It carries no added flavoring. On opening, an intense Latakia scent is noticed; once moisture is adjusted, it offers a balanced, easy-lighting smoke. Latakia's soot and wood character dominates, but it doesn't mask the Virginia sweetness underneath or the spicy bitterness of the Orientals; strength builds gradually through the smoke, and the ash stays light gray. It suits smokers familiar with Latakia-forward English and Balkan mixtures, looking for a medium-bodied but flavor-intense tobacco.
balkan-sasieni-balkan-sasieni.o: A heavy Latakia scent, reminiscent of woodfire and soot, seeps into the room.

sutliff-tobacco-company-sunset-rum-2000.z: Sunset Rum 2000 is a blend listed among Sutliff's rum-cased aromatics; no reliable source on its leaf composition and cut could be found.

watch-city-cigar-mr-skips.z: This is a house blend from Watch City Cigar described as Burley-based, for which no sufficient source could be found.
watch-city-cigar-mr-skips.o: Records note it leaves a nutty scent typical of Burley-forward blends.

nice-ash-cigars-highlander.z: One of the house blends Nice Ash Cigars built in Scottish style; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.
nice-ash-cigars-highlander.o: No description could be found in the records.

drucquer-sons-princes-blend.z: Prince's Blend is a mixture standing in the more measured wing of English mixtures. High-sugar red Virginia leaves build the body; only a hint of latakia, a small amount of burley and just enough perique to round out the smoke are added on top. The ribbon cut packs easily and burns evenly. Here latakia is not the dominant component but plays an accent role; the blend therefore moves on Virginia sweetness and perique's fruity spice rather than smoke. Since nicotine and flavor intensity stay below medium, it suits long smokes and daytime use. It's a structure built for smokers new to latakia blends or who find heavily smoky mixtures too much. Drucquer & Sons recipes were reorganized by Gregory Pease, drawing on the brand's history founded in London in 1841 and moved to Berkeley in 1928.
drucquer-sons-princes-blend.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity tobacco scent over a lightly smoky background.

von-eicken-rosebud-country-cut.z: Rosebud - Country Cut is a blend that stands apart among Von Eicken's floral aromatics. Black Cavendish tobaccos treated with various flavors are combined with several Virginias; what distinguishes the blend is the addition of actual rose petals and crushed whole rosebuds to the mixture. In the tin it forms a dense, mostly dark-colored mass with yellow veins visible throughout. On the smoke, a floral, fruity sweetness comes forward; the rose note reads more as dried rose petal than an artificial perfume impression. Nicotine is moderate, giving the blend appeal to smokers after a flavor-focused, out-of-the-ordinary profile. Records note it can arrive relatively dry in the tin, and since Von Eicken blends are sensitive to moisture, minding the moisture balance before smoking directly affects the experience.
von-eicken-rosebud-country-cut.o: Leaves a floral aroma reminiscent of dried rose petal.

gq-tobaccos-ukptc-1.z: A Latakia-carrying GQ Tobaccos blend said to have been prepared for an English pipe tobacco club; there is no independent sourcing to confirm its composition.

ashton-golden-flake.z: No verifiable record could be found in current manufacturer or retailer catalogs for the blend known as Golden Flake, sold under the Ashton name.
ashton-golden-flake.o: No reliable information on the room note could be found.

torben-dansk-black-cavendish-english-typ.z: Torben Dansk is the first brand German tobacco house Dan Pipe released under its own name; the name carries on the legacy of the venture that brought Danish pipes to Germany in the 1970s. Black Cavendish English Type represents the unflavored black-Cavendish wing of this line, called the "English type." In the blend, pressed and aged, high-sugar Virginia leaves are combined with black Cavendish; the sweetness comes not from an external casing but from the leaf's own sugar. The cut is broad, long ribbon, giving the smoker freedom to pack tight or loose. The smoke is creamy, medium-bodied, and carries light floral and spicy notes; suited to those after an unflavored but sweet Cavendish and to smokers moving from aromatics toward natural tobacco. Distributed in 50-gram tins and 250-gram economy packs.
torben-dansk-black-cavendish-english-typ.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of fruit tea and lightly toasted bread, carrying the tobacco's own sweetness.

motzek-pipe-walker.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called Pipe Walker could be found.

peterson-holiday-season-2011.z: Holiday Season is Peterson's limited-edition, Christmas-themed aromatic tin series released each year; the 2011 edition was presented in a 100 gram tin. Gold and orange Virginia are combined with Burley and black Cavendish, given a cinnamon and candied fruit flavoring. Peterson is an Irish brand, but the blending and production of these special tins is outsourced; records indicate they were made by the Scandinavian Tobacco Group to a recipe specified by Peterson. The cut is described as ribbon. Because the recipe changes each year, every edition of the series counts as a distinct blend; the 2011 tin was likewise prepared for its release year and never reprinted. It is a notable record for smokers seeking flavored, sweet-profile tins and for those who collect the annual limited editions.
peterson-holiday-season-2011.o: Leaves a cinnamon and candied fruit aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-exclusive-plum-and-ru.z: Exclusive Plum and Rum is a ribbon-cut aromatic blend; Virginia leaf is combined with black Cavendish, topped with ripe plum and aged rum. Virginia builds a lightly citrusy, mild base, while Cavendish adds a creamy texture. The smoke is cool, nicotine is low; the aroma is intense but not syrupy. Suited to smokers who love fruit- and spirit-themed aromatics and want a mild blend for all-day smoking. In recent years the product has been packaged under the abbreviation "Exclusiv PR."
gawith-hoggarth-co-exclusive-plum-and-ru.o: Leaves a ripe plum and sugary rum aroma.

mike-russ-the-mind-meld-virginia-perique.z: The Virginia-Perique blend of the Mind Meld line; sufficient sources regarding its proportions and cut could not be found.
mike-russ-the-mind-meld-virginia-perique.o: Leaves a tangy fruit and light-pepper aroma.

mac-baren-norwood.z: Norwood is one of Mac Baren's blends pairing Burley with Virginia, carrying no top flavoring. It's presented ready-rubbed; this structure both eases packing and ensures an even burn. In the composition, Burley handles the body, while Virginia takes on a measured sweetness. The smoke is easy and cool, burning without trouble. Nicotine level is light-to-medium, so it may not meet the expectations of those seeking heavy Burley body and high nicotine, but it suits all-day smoking. Falls to those seeking an unflavored but mild Virginia-Burley blend and to those getting to know Burley character for the first time.
mac-baren-norwood.o: Leaves a faint, tobacco-like trace reminiscent of dry walnut and hay.

w-curtis-draper-wingate.z: Wingate is among the shop-specific blends from Washington's long-established tobacconist W. Curtis Draper. It's built from five components: Virginias, Burley, Perique, unflavored black cavendish, and a small amount of Latakia. This structure places the blend in the classic American mixture class. Despite the component variety, its character is kept light. Virginia sweetness and Burley's dry, nutty taste form the main axis; Perique adds a spicy, plum-evoking depth, the unflavored cavendish softens the body, and the limited Latakia leaves a smoky background without turning the blend into an English mixture. Since there's no flavoring, the taste comes from the leaf itself. Nicotine level runs from low toward medium; this is a suitable profile for those seeking a layered but not harsh smoke, and for those wanting to transition toward English mixtures.
w-curtis-draper-wingate.o: Leaves a scent of dry bread and nuts with a light smoky background.

j-f-germain-son-hampton-rich-dark-flake.z: Rich Dark Flake is a dark-colored flake in which Germain presses together several Virginia varieties with Burley. The pressing time is kept long; this extended fermentation brings the leaf's own sugar to the surface, creating a molasses-like dark sweetness and a heavy body. Nicotine is above average, and it isn't suited to smoking on an empty stomach. Records indicate this blend was released for the British market as the counterpart to Stonehaven, which goes to the US market under the Esoterica label; the name Hampton appears as one of the labels for the same product. Flake slices are rubbed out or folded before filling. It's suited to experienced smokers who enjoy dark, unflavored, full-bodied Virginia-Burley presses.
j-f-germain-son-hampton-rich-dark-flake.o: Leaves an aroma of molasses, toasted bread, and dark dried fruit.

paul-olsen-madagascar.z: A blend from the My Own Blend line that originated at the Paul Olsen shop in Copenhagen; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

peretti-midnight.z: One of the house blends from L. J. Peretti's shop in Boston; it appears under the English blends heading in the maker's listing. No published description of the blend's composition and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.

hearth-home-manor-heights.z: Manor Heights is counted among Hearth & Home's mild-bodied aromatics; there is not enough sourcing to document its composition and flavor profile.

vauen-trullerie.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Vauen pipe tobacco called Trüllerie to record the blend's composition and character.

newminster-no-701-straight-virginia.z: Newminster No. 701 Straight Virginia is an unflavored Virginia tobacco formed by blending eleven separate premium flue-cured Virginia grades. It is one of the examples on the unflavored side within the line's largely aromatic-heavy catalog; no flavoring is applied to it. The taste is confined to Virginia leaf's own natural sweetness and tangy fruit tones. Nicotine sits at medium, and tongue bite is limited when smoked carefully. Suitable for smokers who want to smoke unflavored Virginia and want to start out with bulk tobacco.
newminster-no-701-straight-virginia.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of dry hay and bread crust in the room.

borkum-riff-scandinavian-mixture.z: Scandinavian Mixture is a ribbon-cut Borkum Riff blend built on Virginia and Burley. Records suggest it carries a nutty flavor line close to cocoa; its flavoring is much more restrained than the brand's fruited versions, letting the leaf's taste come through. Borkum Riff launched in Sweden in 1962, taking its name from a lighthouse in the North Sea; the blends, originally produced for Swedish Match, are now prepared in Denmark under Scandinavian Tobacco Group. This version appeared in the brand's 2000s listings and was later withdrawn from wide distribution. It suits smokers looking for a faintly flavored, balanced, medium-light everyday blend.
borkum-riff-scandinavian-mixture.o: Leaves a nutty room note with a hint of cocoa.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-black-cavendish-.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Black Cavendish (English) blend.

sutliff-tobacco-company-cringle-flake-20.z: The 2020 edition of the Cringle Flake series consists of ten-year-rested, darkened Virginia leaves and seventeen-year-old Louisiana perique. The leaves are pressed and sliced into flake, and the run was produced in limited quantity. The aged Virginias' natural sweetness meets perique's peppery, fruity spice; no flavoring is used. A seasonal product prepared for smokers interested in Virginia-perique blends made with aged leaf.
sutliff-tobacco-company-cringle-flake-20.o: Leaves a scent where dark fruit sweetness is joined by peppery spice.

dan-tobacco-ascanian-no-2-sweet-gentle.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of Dan Tobacco's Ascanian No. 2 Sweet & Gentle were found.

planta-anno-mmxvi-cosmopolitan-mixture.z: Anno MMXVI is Planta's 2016 limited edition, inspired by the Cosmopolitan cocktail it's named after. A body of black Cavendish, traditionally prepared Virginia leaf, and nutty Burley is given an intense casing carrying ripe cranberry, a touch of lemon, and a sweet-herbal Cointreau note. For an aromatic mixture, nicotine stays medium, while the casing is quite pronounced. It suits smokers looking for fruity-liqueur, full-bodied aromatics and collectors of annual editions. It came in 100-gram decorative tins and, being a limited edition, didn't enter the ongoing catalogue.
planta-anno-mmxvi-cosmopolitan-mixture.o: A sweet, herbal orange-liqueur aroma mixes into tart cranberry and lemon peel.

ken-byron-ventures-fairway-driver.z: One of Ken Byron Ventures' limited, golf-themed Virginia releases; no accessible maker's profile could be found to document its contents.

reiner-blend-71-long-golden-flake.z: Reiner Blend 71 is a flake blend prepared from golden Virginia leaf with white Burley and a small amount of Perique added, then pressed, sliced into long strips, and coiled into the tin. Reports indicate a light orange-and-honey casing is applied before pressing. The Reiner brand was established within the German maker Kohlhase & Kopp in the late 1990s. In the smoke, Virginia's wheat-grass-like sweetness and citrus tang come forward; Perique adds a pronounced but measured spice and dark fruit layer on top, while Burley increases body and fullness. Thanks to its long-flake structure it can be packed rubbed out or folded, and burns slowly. It suits smokers used to the Virginia-Perique tradition looking for a medium-strength blend that ages well.
reiner-blend-71-long-golden-flake.o: Leaves a sweet hay and light orange-peel aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-apricots-creme.z: A Sutliff bulk blend that from its name appears to be an apricot-and-cream-flavored aromatic; sufficient independent sources confirming its composition could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-apricots-creme.o: Records indicate it leaves a scent of apricot and cream.

mcclelland-drama-reserve-grand-orientals.z: Drama Reserve is a member of McClelland's Grand Orientals series, which spotlights single-region Orientals, taking its name from the tobacco of Greece's Drama region. In the blend, Oriental tobaccos are joined by Virginia, with no Latakia or flavoring. It was sold in small 50-gram tins. In the smoke, a spicy, cigarette-like flavor typical of Oriental tobaccos leads; the sweet-tart tone characteristic of McClelland's leaves rides atop it. Leaving an oily texture on the palate reminiscent of olive oil is a commonly noted trait. It burns even and easy, giving a cool smoke that doesn't bite the tongue, with a light-colored ash; nicotine dose is medium. A record aimed at smokers wanting to get to know Latakia-free Oriental character and seeking a light-bodied tobacco.
mcclelland-drama-reserve-grand-orientals.o: Leaves a sweet-tart, faintly vinegary trace alongside a spicy Oriental-tobacco aroma.

ken-byron-ventures-the-jigsaw-plateau.z: Ken Byron Ventures' Jigsaw Plateau is classified as an English blend; no reliable source could be found to describe its contents and character.
ken-byron-ventures-the-jigsaw-plateau.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

g-l-pease-bohemian-scandal.z: Bohemian Scandal is a G. L. Pease blend distinguished by being built on Syrian latakia instead of Cyprus latakia. Small-leaved Oriental tobaccos and ripe Virginias form a base surrounding Syrian latakia's softer, sweeter smoke. The blend's character shows a wine-like, sweet-tart facet and a fine spice. Since the supply of Syrian latakia is seasonal, records indicate this blend's production is not continuous. It draws the interest of smokers familiar with classic English mixtures who want to follow the difference between the two latakia types.
g-l-pease-bohemian-scandal.o: Leaves a wine-like tart aroma alongside smoked wood and spice.

torben-dansk-no-1-original-scottish-blen.z: Torben Dansk No.1 Original Scottish Blend is a Scottish-style mixture, the first blend in the brand's numbered series; no independent source giving detail on its composition has been found.
torben-dansk-no-1-original-scottish-blen.o: Records describe it as leaving a lightly smoky, dry tobacco aroma.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-skandinav.z: The heavily cased cavendish version of the Skandinavik series; no sufficient primary source describing the blend's composition could be found.

cornell-diehl-rocking-chair.z: A blend, no longer in Cornell & Diehl's current catalogue, referred to as American style; no adequate source documenting its composition was found.
cornell-diehl-rocking-chair.o: No adequate information for a description could be found in records.

gawith-hoggarth-co-beacon-light-twist.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Beacon Light Twist blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

peretti-blend-d-7485.z: D-7485 is a blend Boston's L.J. Peretti reportedly created in 1933, founded by Joseph Peretti for then-British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald. The letter and number in the name indicate the blend's place in the firm's ledgers; this record is in ledger D. Peretti's own Burley forms the backbone, with Virginia, Oriental leaves, and a pinch of Latakia added on top. The cut is coarse, so it packs easily and burns without trouble; it comes out of the package at a smokable moisture. Burley leads, Virginia adds a fine sweetness, and Latakia adds body and depth. Given its cool, measured smoke, it suits smokers seeking a light, English-character American blend for all-day smoking.
peretti-blend-d-7485.o: Leaves a thin incense layer underneath a nutty, dry-hay aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-april-dawn.z: April Dawn is a cherry-flavored blend that appeared in Sutliff's Private Stock line. Cherry scent is noticeable when the tin is opened; on the palate, the topping recedes and the tobacco's own taste comes forward. Records note it's ribbon cut with a relatively dry preparation. It's stated to give a medium-intensity flavor, burn evenly, and stay light in nicotine. Suited to smokers who enjoy cherry aromatics but don't want a heavy syrupy topping on the palate. It went out of production with the scaling back of Sutliff's Private Stock line.

wellauer-co-balkan-mixture.z: Wellauer & Co's Balkan Mixture is, according to records, one of the blends carrying the Swiss tobacconist house's name; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

shpc-great-hiatus.z: Great Hiatus is one of the club blends prepared for the Sherlock Holmes Pipe Club (SHPC). It takes its name from the three-year interval during which Holmes was believed to have died at the Reichenbach Falls, ending with The Adventure of the Empty House. It is a classic English mixture built from Virginia, Oriental leaf, and a high proportion of Latakia; it stays close to old-school English recipes. On the smoke, Latakia's campfire-like smoke and a peaty undertone lead; the toasted, measured sweetness of the Virginia and Oriental leaves balances this, and the character changes little across the bowl. Nicotine and flavor intensity stay in the medium range. Suited to people accustomed to smoking unflavored, smoky English mixtures throughout the day. As a club blend, its distribution is limited.
shpc-great-hiatus.o: Leaves a smoky, peaty, faintly sweet scent reminiscent of a campfire.

tewksbury-company-mountain-honey.z: According to records, this blend was part of the lineup of Tewksbury & Company, an American blender that ceased operations following the 2009 tobacco regulation; no source documenting its content and character could be found.

smokers-haven-sids-mix.z: An aromatic blend produced under contract for Smokers' Haven, whose first edition, per records, released with an orange label; no reliable information about its composition could be found.

sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-oriental-azu.z: A blend belonging to the Oriental series of Sentimiento Nacional, one of Argentina's few handmade pipe-tobacco producers; no independent source could be found to confirm its composition.
sentimiento-nacional-mezcla-oriental-azu.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

consolidated-64-k-embassy.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Consolidated blend 64-K: Embassy.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-flake-scented.z: This is the Kendal-style scented version of Brown Flake. The body is built from hot-pressed dark Virginia and burley; a classic, tonka-heavy, floral Lakeland topping is applied over it. It shares the same leaf base as the family's untopped and liquorice-topped versions. The scent is dominant from the moment the tin is opened and lingers long in the room during smoking; it becomes especially noticeable when smoked indoors. In the smoke, the floral topping runs alongside without overtaking Virginia's sweetness. It suits a smoker wanting to get to know Lakeland scent or one already accustomed to the style; those unfamiliar with this family of scents would be wise to try a small amount first.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-flake-scented.o: A floral, soapy, sweet aroma lingers in the room for a long time.

iwan-ries-three-star-gray.z: This is a blend from the Three Star line prepared over the counter by the Chicago-based tobacconist Iwan Ries & Co.; no independent source detailing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
iwan-ries-three-star-gray.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

sailors-pride-sailors-pride-blond-virgin.z: No sufficient source confirming the content of the Sailor's Pride blend, understood from its name to be light-Virginia-based, could be found.

peretti-blend-no-432.z: This is a numbered blend L.J. Peretti lists in its Cavendish group, appearing in the shop's select Cavendish sample set; the details of its flavoring and taste have not been published.

peter-stokkebye-nougat-no-24.z: Nougat is one of the best-known records from the production Peter Stokkebye founded in the 1970s. Loose-cut golden African Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish leaf are given a flavoring made of vanilla bean and chocolate extract; the name comes from this nougat association. The body is light and the aroma intense; the sweet scent from the pouch turns into a more measured taste on the palate, staying consistent from the first draw to the last. It is one of the notable examples of Danish-style aromatics and suits those seeking a sweet, chocolatey profile.
peter-stokkebye-nougat-no-24.o: Fills the room with a vanilla and chocolate white-nougat aroma.

villiger-orientale.z: This is a Villiger blend described as Oriental-tobacco-forward; no independent source could be found confirming its composition.

d-r-tobacco-rowland-silver-blend.z: Rowland Silver Blend is the lightest-bodied member of Daughters & Ryan's Rowland family. It's made of Virginia, Burley, and Oriental leaf and, like the rest of the series, carries a light flavoring; ribbon cut. Alongside the original Rowland and Rowland Gold, it's positioned as a softened reading of the same character. Body is mild, flavor plain and smooth; nicotine is low. A reasonable choice for morning pipes, long smokes, and those new to the pipe. It won't meet the expectations of those wanting heavy Latakia or intense aromatics; what stands out here is a plain American mixture with casing kept to the edges.
d-r-tobacco-rowland-silver-blend.o: Leaves a faint, sweetish leaf scent that doesn't linger long in the room.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-bowsers-c.z: Bowser's Castle is one of The Country Squire tobacconist's house blends, listed as English-style; no reliable source on its content and character could be found.

tabac-turc-turk-pipo-tutunu-turkish-pipe.z: Türk Pipo Tütünü (Turkish Pipe Tobacco) is a domestic blend that brings together Oriental leaf from various regions of Turkey, notably tobacco from Yayladağı, Bitlis, İzmir, and Adıyaman. It is pressed into dark-colored flake slices; preparation takes place at the factory in Menemen, İzmir. According to the packaging, small proportions of cavendish along with plum, rum, licorice root, carob, fig extract, and honey casing are used, though the dominant taste on the smoke is the plain tobacco itself. It is a blend for smokers who want to experience Turkish tobacco's oily, sweet, spicy character directly. It burns slowly, gives a long, cool smoke, and leaves light-colored ash in the bowl. Because it arrives moist and sticky, it needs airing before packing; this resting period affects both the burn and the balance of the casing. The room note is strong and lingering, so smoking indoors should be planned with that in mind.
tabac-turc-turk-pipo-tutunu-turkish-pipe.o: Leaves the sharp scent of oily, spicy Oriental tobacco, and the smell lingers in the room for a long time.

golden-leaf-tobacco-shipwreck.z: Shipwreck is an English-style pipe blend sold under the Golden Leaf Tobacco name; there is no sourcing to confirm its manufacturer, composition, and character.

savinelli-aroma.z: A ribbon-cut blend in Savinelli's aromatic family; no sufficient source describing its casing and leaf composition could be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-john-bull.z: John Bull True English is the classic English blend of the England-rooted brand of the same name; it is produced at Scandinavian Tobacco Group's Lane arm in the US. It contains only mature Virginia, Oriental leaf, and Cyprus latakia — no casing aroma. Latakia sits at the blend's axis, building a smoky, woody body; Oriental leaf adds a spicy, dry edge, while Virginia holds the balance with a measured sweetness beneath. Its nicotine is medium. Aimed at smokers seeking unflavored, smoke-forward traditional mixtures.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-john-bull.o: Leaves a scent of heavy wood smoke and dry spice.

seattle-pipe-club-down-yonder.z: Down Yonder is an unflavored straight Virginia blend built from a single leaf type: Virginia leaf grown in Brazil is stoved for a long time at low heat and pressed into a crumble cake. The slow stoving caramelizes the leaf's own sugar, producing a smoky sweetness; the blend delivers an unflavored tobacco taste in the same line from start to finish. The name evokes, in rural American speech, a distant place beyond the horizon and a longing for simpler times. The stoving method was one frequently used by Joe Lankford, the creator of the Seattle Pipe Club blends. Suited to smokers who don't want added flavoring and seek a one-dimensional but deep Virginia, and who are accustomed to preparing cake tobacco.
seattle-pipe-club-down-yonder.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly smoky tobacco scent evoking caramelized sugar.

rivertown-tobacco-works-oak-ember.z: Oak & Ember is a ribbon-cut Burley blend with dark Burley in the driver's seat, accompanied by red Virginia. Burley's earthy, nutty character forms the blend's backbone, while Virginia brings natural sugar and a light spice that sweetens an otherwise plain smoke. Casing use is very light, so the leaf taste stays up front. Nicotine leans toward medium, and the flavor is measured and understated. It suits smokers looking for an everyday blend close to the leaf's natural taste, without heavy casing, as well as tobacconists building their own mixtures on a Burley base.
rivertown-tobacco-works-oak-ember.o: A light bready sweetness accompanies the dry walnut-shell and wood aroma.

peter-stokkebye-bright-virginia.z: No sufficient sources confirming the cut and detailed character of this record known as Peter Stokkebye Bright Virginia could be found; as its name suggests, it is based on light-colored Virginia leaf.

peterson-connoisseurs-choice.z: Connoisseur's Choice is a ribbon-cut aromatic blend built from black Cavendish and Virginia leaf. Its flavoring combines liquor, rum, whiskey, vanilla, coffee, and citrus notes together, so its flavor layer is crowded and doesn't run along a single axis. The smoke is light, its flavor intensity medium, and it has a sweet base. Reportedly the tobacco can show some resistance on the first light; once moisture is adjusted it smokes evenly. It suits smokers wanting to get to know liquor- and liqueur-flavored tobaccos who aren't bothered by a heavy topping.
peterson-connoisseurs-choice.o: Leaves a trace recalling sweet liqueur, vanilla, and a hint of coffee.

butera-golden-cake.z: Golden Cake is the light-colored virginia cake in Butera's Royal Vintage line. Long-leaf bright golden virginia, rested for years and hot-air cured, is pressed into cake form without further darkening. Since it is not darkened, a flavor turning between sweet and tart appears instead of Dark Stoved's dark spice; virginia's warm, hay-like natural taste is pronounced. Coming in cake form, it needs to be crumbled before smoking. Suitable for smokers seeking the simplicity of light virginias and a structure that matures with time.
butera-golden-cake.o: Leaves a dry hay, honey and lemon peel aroma.

davidoff-english-mixture.z: English Mixture is Davidoff's latakia-containing blend. Alongside Virginia and burley leaves, latakia stands out; a small amount of perique is added to broaden the bouquet. It's ribbon cut. The blend follows the classic English structure while also carrying a very light aromatic touch; because of this, the latakia soot arrives softened rather than sharp, and the taste lasts to the bottom of the bowl. Its fullness is medium. It suits those wanting to try a soft English mixture before moving to heavy latakia blends.
davidoff-english-mixture.o: Leaves a lightly smoky, woody scent.

hearth-home-allsorts.z: A topped entry within the Hearth & Home series that collects Russ Ouellette's blends, taking its name from the English licorice candy allsorts; there is not enough sourcing to confirm its composition.
hearth-home-allsorts.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of licorice candy.

straus-tobacco-firehouse.z: Firehouse is one of the counter blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; records indicate the shop was founded in 1880 and that most of its house blends were named after Cincinnati neighborhoods and landmark buildings. Since no independent source on the blend's composition and character could be found, this record is kept at listing level only.

mcclelland-no-700-baklava.z: A blend in McClelland's numbered bulk aromatic series, named after baklava and flavored toward honey and walnut; no sufficient source documenting its composition could be found.

wellauer-co-wellauers-latakia.z: Wellauer & Co's Wellauer's Latakia is, according to records, one of the blends carrying the Swiss tobacconist house's name; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

rain-city-cigar-b-b.z: This is a house blend from Rain City Cigar, open since 1997 in Seattle's Georgetown neighborhood; there is not enough source material describing its composition and character.

faders-luau.z: Not enough independent sourcing documenting the composition and character of Luau, one of the house blends of the Baltimore-based Fader's tobacconist, could be found.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-cupcake.z: Cupcake is an aromatic blend Dan and J. M. Boswell prepared in the fall of 2013. Per the manufacturer's description, it is built from black and golden cavendish with a buttery structure, resting on echoes of freshly baked cake and sugared cream. The casing level is high; vanilla leads in the smoke, with traces of cake and cream and cavendish's own sweetness behind it. Nicotine is low and no tongue bite is reported. Suitable for aromatic smokers seeking a pronounced sweet casing.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-cupcake.o: Leaves a vanilla cake and buttery cream aroma.

vauen-auenland-midnight-mixture.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Vauen blend called Auenland Midnight Mixture has been found.
vauen-auenland-midnight-mixture.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

mcclelland-virginia-woods-craftsbury-ser.z: Virginia Woods is a Virginia-based, lightly flavored ribbon-cut blend McClelland released under its Craftsbury Series. The topping level stays light enough not to mask the tobacco; the brand's natural tangy-sweet character and the mature taste of dark, cured Virginias remain in front, leaving a fruity sweetness on the tongue. Burns dry and even; once relit after the first light, it needs no further attention through to the bottom of the bowl. Its cool, slow burn suits long smokes, though nicotine stays light and a tin empties quickly. Suited to those wanting a lightly aromatic blend that stays close to the natural taste, smokable all day. Discontinued with McClelland's closure.
mcclelland-virginia-woods-craftsbury-ser.o: Leaves an aroma of tangy sweetness mixed with a fruity note.

4noggins-down-by-the-river.z: Down by The River is one of 4noggins' Burley-based blends. The manufacturer's description notes a predominantly nutty, lightly sweet smoke, without the wet-burn and ashy sharpness that often show up toward the bottom of the bowl in Burley blends. Strength is low and topping is minimal. It suits smokers seeking an easygoing, slow, cool-burning Burley, and those new to the Latakia-free American style.
4noggins-down-by-the-river.o: Leaves a trace close to toasted nuts and lightly sweet bread.

the-storytellers-pipe-shop-irish-meadows.z: Irish Meadows is the unflavored Virginia blend from The Story Teller's Pipe tobacconist. Per the maker's description, bright, red, stoved and fermented Virginia leaves are brought together; the side-by-side use of different processing methods gives the blend a broader flavor range than a single Virginia type would. Sweet, ripe, cooked-fruit notes and spice traces come forward in the taste, turning toward salty bread and a light floral base as the bowl progresses. Strength and flavor are moderate; it is noted as burning cool and clean, with the taste staying consistent throughout. Suited to smokers wanting to smoke unflavored Virginia but after a layered profile rather than one-dimensional sweetness. A version of the same blend with Louisiana Perique added, called IMP, also appears on the shop's list.
the-storytellers-pipe-shop-irish-meadows.o: Leaves a light aroma where cooked-fruit sweetness meets baked bread.

tres-cajones-tobacco-fairy-farts.z: No sufficient source has been found for Tres Cajones Tobacco's blend Fairy Farts.
tres-cajones-tobacco-fairy-farts.o: No reliable source describing the room note has been found.

cornell-diehl-bridge-mixture.z: Bridge Mixture is a ribbon-cut blend where a bright-and-red Virginia base is spiced with Turkish leaf, Latakia, perique, cavendish, and a small amount of fire-cured Kentucky. As its name suggests, it is built as a bridge blend: it carries enough smoke to draw a Virginia smoker closer to Latakia mixtures. The Latakia level is kept from taking over the body; the smoky layer sits like a thin veil over Virginia's sweetness and perique's spice. Black cavendish softens it, while Kentucky adds an earthy depth. Nicotine strength is medium, flavor intensity a notch above that. It suits smokers not yet accustomed to heavy English mixtures but looking for an unflavored, smoky taste.
cornell-diehl-bridge-mixture.o: A sweetish, spiced base sits beneath a light wood-smoke aroma.

cornell-diehl-skyward-gate.z: Skyward Gate is the pure Virginia blend rounding out Cornell & Diehl's Summit series. Its composition is entirely whole-leaf-processed red and orange flue-cured grades, with red grades predominant. The blend is offered in plug form — a pressed block — and, like other members of the series, is inspired by American national parks; this blend's source is Arches National Park in Utah. On the flavor side, layers of dark citrus, roasted grain, and baking spice appear over Virginia's natural sweetness. Since the plug form retains moisture, it can be smoked straight from the tin; the smoker adjusts their own cut by slicing and rubbing it out. Suited to smokers who like unflavored Virginia blends and pressed forms well suited to aging.
cornell-diehl-skyward-gate.o: Leaves a sweetish scent reminiscent of roasted grain and dry citrus peel.

sutliff-tobacco-company-tobacco-galleria.z: One of the aromatic blends in Sutliff's Tobacco Galleria line; no accessible source documenting its content could be found.

seattle-pipe-club-wild-man.z: Wild Man is Seattle Pipe Club's medium-bodied English blend. It is built from Cyprus Latakia, Oriental leaf, and sweet Virginias; it is easy to prepare since it comes pressed and hand-crumbled into a cake. The blend was named by Joe Lankford as a nod to the Bigfoot legend of the Pacific Northwest. On the smoke, Latakia's smoke is noticeable but not dominant; the spicy-sour tone of the Oriental leaves and the sweetness of the Virginia soften the blend. Its aroma resembles incense while the taste stays smooth, with nicotine in the light-to-medium range. Suited to those new to English blends and to those seeking a moderately smoky tobacco they can smoke throughout the day.
seattle-pipe-club-wild-man.o: Leaves a smoky, resinous scent reminiscent of an incense stick.

mac-baren-latakia-blend.z: Latakia Blend is one of Mac Baren's roll-wrapped tobaccos. The manufacturer states that whole Virginia leaves are chosen as the wrapper, with the brand's signature cavendish and latakia placed inside as filling; the resulting roll is later cut. This structure gives a more compact, slower burn than loose-cut blends. In the smoke, latakia's smoky, woody note is decisive; the Virginia wrapper leaf builds a sweetish, grassy base, and the cavendish adds roundness and a light sweetness. It carries a more measured smokiness than heavy latakia-laden English mixtures, making it suitable also for those wanting to get acquainted with latakia. Due to the roll structure, the slices need to be crumbled before packing.
mac-baren-latakia-blend.o: A smoky scent reminiscent of pine soot is accompanied by a lightly sweet tobacco tone.

mcclelland-cpcc-epitome.z: A limited club blend McClelland released for the Chicagoland Pipe Collectors Club, reportedly in 2010; no sufficient source describing its contents and character could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-celtic.z: Celtic is an aromatic blend listed in the Sutliff catalog; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-celtic.o: Records did not provide sufficient information for a description.

ken-byron-ventures-crumb-fu.z: One of Ken Byron Ventures' limited releases, its name a nod to the crumb cut; no accessible maker's profile could be found to document its contents.

ilsted-own-mixture-golden-flake.z: Golden Flake, a house blend sold under the Copenhagen-based Ilsted name, is reportedly a straight-Virginia-character flake; no independent source detailing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
ilsted-own-mixture-golden-flake.o: No room note described in the records could be found.

with-pipe-and-book-noah-johns-blend.z: This is one of the house blends of With Pipe and Book, a bookshop and tobacconist operating in Lake Placid, New York; the name refers to Noah John Rondeau, the well-known Adirondack hermit. Since the shop closed in the mid-2000s, the blend was also withdrawn from the market. As no independent source on its composition and character could be found, this record remains incomplete.
with-pipe-and-book-noah-johns-blend.o: No description of its room note could be found in the records.

charatan-no-27.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the British pipe maker Charatan.

sutliff-tobacco-company-coconut-almond-1.z: 19 Coconut Almond is a coconut-and-almond-flavored aromatic in Sutliff's bulk line; sufficient independent sources documenting its leaf composition and character could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-coconut-almond-1.o: Records did not provide sufficient information for a description.

tobacco-lane-hambletonian.z: One of the house blends from the tobacconist Tobacco Lane; no verifiable source on its composition and character has been found.
tobacco-lane-hambletonian.o: No source describing its aroma has been found.

amphora-full-aroma.z: Amphora Full Aroma is an aromatic pipe tobacco with a long history beginning in the Netherlands. Having gone through changes in maker, blender, and recipe over the years, its versions from different periods diverge from one another; today's production continues under Mac Baren. It contains Burley as the dominant component, along with Virginia, Oriental, and Kentucky. Its cut sits between ready rubbed and ribbon, and the tobacco tends to clump inside the pack. Among the matte dark brown leaves, lighter-colored pieces that could be Oriental tobacco are visible. The pack scent is settled but low in intensity; chocolate is the first thing that comes to mind. Strength is light, flavor intensity is low; the flavoring, however, is pronounced. It suits smokers looking for an everyday tobacco with low nicotine and high flavoring.
amphora-full-aroma.o: Leaves a sweet room note where chocolate leads, with brandy- and cognac-like fruit-spirit notes underneath.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-red-lace.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Red Lace blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

ascorti-piemonte.z: No adequate independent source documenting the content of the Piemonte blend, carrying the Ascorti name, could be found.
ascorti-piemonte.o: No reliable information on the room note could be found.

cobblestone-plum-rum.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Cobblestone pipe tobacco named Plum Rum, so the blend's content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

4noggins-mojo.z: MOJO is 4noggins' blend built around deertongue leaf. This herb is known for its coumarin scent reminiscent of dried grass and vanilla and has traditionally been used as a tobacco flavoring. Per the manufacturer's recipe, deertongue is kept measured, with Virginia, Burley, and Perique underneath it. The name is a playful nod to the folklore attached to the plant. Virginia brings sweetness, Burley a nutty base, and Perique a spicy, plummy twist; deertongue adds a grassy-vanilla layer on top. Nicotine is moderate and flavor medium-to-full. It's aimed at smokers familiar with the classic American blend structure who want to try an out-of-the-ordinary flavoring.
4noggins-mojo.o: Leaves a coumarin scent reminiscent of cut dry grass and vanilla.

motzek-16-8-perique-summer.z: Since neither the manufacturer's own description nor two independent reliable sources could be found for the Motzek blend called 16/8 Perique Summer, its composition, cut, and character could not be documented here.

cult-conspiracy.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the Cult brand as Conspiracy; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

hu-tobacco-janneman-flake.z: Janneman Flake is an unflavored flake HU Tobacco dedicated to the Dutch pipe forum PRF. Its base is fire-cured, spicy Virginia leaf; a measured amount of Perique is added, and the mixture is fermented and pressed under high pressure. The taste emerges from the combination of Virginia sweetness in the direction of wildflower honey, fruit, and citrus, with woody-earthy notes; Perique brings a fig-and-raisin-evoking tartness and spice. Cut as a whole flake, it gives a medium-strength, full smoke. It's aimed at those wanting to experience the Virginia-Perique tradition without added flavoring.
hu-tobacco-janneman-flake.o: A woody, lightly smoky aroma accompanies dark honey and dried-fig sweetness.

wessex-burley-slice.z: This is, according to records, a flake-cut blend belonging to the Burley family of the Wessex series; no sufficient source could be found to detail its character.

the-briary-blue-ribbon.z: One of the house blends from The Briary, a pipe shop that has operated in Birmingham, Alabama since 1974; no independent source describing the blend's composition and character could be found.

grants-tobacconist-black-n-brown.z: One of Grant's Tobacconist's bulk house blends; there is no independent sourcing describing its composition.

cornell-diehl-shandygaff.z: Shandygaff is one of the old Atlas Blending recipes whose rights Cornell & Diehl took over. It's a ribbon-cut mixture made of Burley, Turkish leaf, and Perique; the maker's description mentions flavors reminiscent of ginger and salty sea air. On the smoke, Burley is clearly up front; Oriental and Perique remain supporting components adding extra texture to the body. It's unflavored, low in sweetness, with an overall dry-earthy direction. Suited to those looking for a not-quite-plain, Burley-heavy everyday blend without Latakia.
cornell-diehl-shandygaff.o: A lightly spicy sharpness accompanies a scent of dry nuts and earth.

de-la-concha-tropical-mist.z: This is referred to as a tropical-fruit-themed aromatic shop blend from De La Concha; no independent source stating its topping could be found.
de-la-concha-tropical-mist.o: No reliable record could be found for the room note.

vcpo-selection-nr-3-english-mixture.z: The third blend in the VCPÖ Selection series, whose name points to an English-style mixture; since it was not distributed outside Austria, no independent source describing its composition and character has been found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-maple-shadows.z: Maple Shadows is an autumn-themed aromatic Sutliff released as a limited edition only in eight-ounce tins. The leading component of the blend is fire-cured Kentucky leaf, accompanied by nutty, bready burley and a lightly tart-citrus Virginia. The maple syrup sauce applied on top doesn't smother the leaves but adds a measured sweetness. In body it sits above typical light aromatics: notes of earth, wood, herb, and spice stand out clearly alongside the sweetness. The topping's effect fades somewhat in the second half of the bowl, letting leaf character come forward. Aimed at smokers who like the smoky weight of fire-cured tobacco but don't want a fully unflavored blend.
sutliff-tobacco-company-maple-shadows.o: Leaves a sweet-spicy scent where woody smoke, roasted nuts, and maple syrup mix together.

peter-stokkebye-sambuca.z: This is one of Peter Stokkebye's flavored blends; no sufficient first-hand sources documenting its content and character could be found.
peter-stokkebye-sambuca.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

cornell-diehl-honey-cavendish.z: A honey-flavored cavendish blend that previously appeared in Cornell & Diehl's bulk catalog; not enough sourcing could be found regarding its composition and character.

752-red.z: Not enough information based on a manufacturer or reliable retailer record could be found on 752 Red.

bentley-the-oriental-spice.z: The Oriental Spice is the spicy blend in the Bentley line, also offered in some markets under the name Oriental Amber. Its composition is weighted toward Virginia and Oriental, rounded out with small amounts of Latakia and Perique. The Oriental's dry spice seasoning sits at the center of the blend; the Latakia keeps its smoky tone measured, while the Perique adds a light fruit-and-pepper note. There's no added flavoring. It's medium on nicotine and intense in flavor. It's aimed at smokers looking for Oriental-forward English-style blends with a light Latakia touch.
bentley-the-oriental-spice.o: Leaves a spicy room note with a faint smoky edge.

smoker-friendly-cherry.z: A cherry-flavored product from the Boulder-based Smoker Friendly retail chain's private-label pipe tobacco line; the line is produced for the chain by Sutliff Tobacco, but no independent source describing this blend's composition could be found.

cornell-diehl-from-beyond-2023.z: Not enough information could be found, either in the manufacturer's current catalog or in primary sources, about From Beyond, one of Cornell & Diehl's 2023 limited releases.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-primrose.z: A blend listed in the Orlik catalog as Virginia-burley based; no independent source confirming its details could be found.

pfeifen-huber-louisiana-flake.z: Louisiana Flake is an unflavored Virginia-Perique blend produced under the Pfeifen Huber name, presented as pressed and leaf-cut flake; it is reportedly produced by Kohlhase und Kopp. The blend joins a Virginia base with Perique and dark-fired Kentucky. Perique is a heavy, spicy condiment tobacco grown only in a small area of the St. James district of Louisiana, which is also where the blend's name comes from. On the palate Virginia's sweetness leads, Perique layers a fine peppery spice on top, and dark-fired Kentucky leaves a woody depth in the background. The body sits between light and medium and nicotine strength is low, making it suitable for all-day smoking. It suits smokers wanting to get to know the unflavored Virginia-Perique structure in a mild dose as well as those seeking a spicy flake.
pfeifen-huber-louisiana-flake.o: Leaves a dried-fig sweetness together with black pepper and a woody smoke scent.

austria-tabak-gmbh-landtabak-spezial.z: Landtabak Spezial is a traditional rod-cut blend sold under the name of Austria Tabak, Austria's longstanding tobacco monopoly maker; the brand is today under the Japan Tobacco umbrella. The blend is built from Virginia, Burley, Kentucky, and Oriental leaf; Kentucky and Burley fill out the body, while the Oriental leaf leaves a spicy edge. Since it carries a light flavoring, it's counted in the aromatic class, but the topping stays measured enough not to override the tobacco; on opening the tin, a thin scent reminiscent of herbs and mint is noticed. Its character is medium-bodied, dry, and earthy; it suits smokers not looking for the sweetness of sugary aromatics but who also find plain Burley blends too flat. Records indicate two separate versions once existed — a plain Landtabak and a Spezial — and today it's mostly the Spezial version that remains with specialist tobacconists. It can be considered a surviving example of Central Europe's "village tobacco" tradition.
austria-tabak-gmbh-landtabak-spezial.o: Leaves a herbal tobacco room note reminiscent of dry hay and light mint.

sutliff-tobacco-company-breckinridge.z: Breckinridge, part of Sutliff's Private Stock line, is an unflavored burley blend. It consists of plug-cut Kentucky burley leaves; since no topping is applied, the flavor rests on the leaf's own nutty, bread-crust, and light cocoa tones. It's described as a slow, cool-burning mixture whose flavor stays balanced from the first third of the bowl to the last. It takes its name from John Breckinridge, who served as U.S. Attorney General under Thomas Jefferson and was also involved in tobacco farming. Suited to smokers who steer clear of flavored blends and want a straightforward tobacco taste, one they can smoke at any hour of the day.
sutliff-tobacco-company-breckinridge.o: Leaves an earthy tobacco scent reminiscent of nuts and cocoa.

richs-sasha.z: Sasha is a medium-bodied blend from Rich's Cigar Store combining natural Cavendish, Latakia, and Perique with a touch of Red Carolina Virginia. Unflavored Cavendish builds a soft, sweet base, Latakia's smoke sits on top, and Perique enlivens the blend with its plummy, peppery sharpness. This structure places the blend somewhere between classic English mixtures and the Virginia-Perique world. It suits smokers who enjoy smoky flavor but want a smooth body; it is sold in bulk at Rich's stores and belongs to the store's Perique-forward blend family.
richs-sasha.o: Leaves an aroma where smoke and dark plum mix into a sweetish wood trace.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-kendals-mixed-no.z: Kendal's Mixed No.6 is a blend produced by Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. in the town of Kendal, Cumbria, and sold in bulk by McGahey The Tobacconist. Its composition includes light-colored Brazilian and Indian leaves along with dark Indonesian and Indian leaves; fire-cured dark leaf forms the blend's backbone. The body is medium; the leaf's own sweetness sits alongside a woody, lightly smoky base. No pronounced casing stands out. Suitable for those curious about the unflavored English bulk tobacco tradition and looking for a balanced blend to smoke throughout the day.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-kendals-mixed-no.o: Leaves a dry-hay and lightly smoky wood aroma.

imperial-tobacco-group-plc-route-66.z: No independent source verifying the composition of Route 66, reportedly a Virginia-and-Burley-based blend, could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
imperial-tobacco-group-plc-route-66.o: No room note described in the records could be found.

j-b-vinche-black-amber.z: Black Amber is a classically structured aromatic blend made up of Burley, Virginia, and black Cavendish leaves. A light hand-applied flavoring of red fruit, some vanilla, and a touch of mirabelle plum is layered over the leaf; on opening the tin, the aroma doesn't come through strongly, and this restraint continues into the first part of the smoke. The black Cavendish carries sweetness, the Burley provides body, and the Virginia gives a dry sweetness in the background. Unlike heavily syrupy aromatics, it follows a line where the flavoring doesn't override the tobacco; both flavor and nicotine intensity stay below moderate. It suits smokers who want a fruity-vanilla flavor while still wanting to taste tobacco character. The Vinche name goes back to the pipe shop Jean-Baptiste Vinche opened in Brussels in 1864; the brand first became known for meerschaum and later briar pipes, and has continued its tobacco line under this long-established name.
j-b-vinche-black-amber.o: Leaves an aroma of sweet red fruit, plum, and light vanilla.

robert-mcconnell-mature.z: Mature is a blend in which matured dark Virginia leaves are combined with Greek- and Turkish-origin Oriental tobaccos, pressed and crumbled into broken flake form. Per the producer's description, the leaf selection is shared with the Special London Mature line; a very fine casing in the direction of cocoa and anise is applied on top. On opening the tin, a dark-brown, nearly black appearance and a lightly fruity, grassy scent greet you; the cut often gives a ready-rubbed impression. The casing does not come to the fore on the smoke; the blend largely reads as an unflavored Virginia. The flavor settles after the first quarter; the smoke is intense, satisfying, and above-medium in nicotine. It is on record that the flavor deepens when rested in a jar. Suited to smokers seeking the Virginia-and-Oriental duo in unflavored form and accustomed to smoking the pipe slowly.
robert-mcconnell-mature.o: Leaves a lightly fruity, grassy tobacco scent in the room, with a faint anise trace behind it.

cornell-diehl-competition-blend.z: This is a Cornell & Diehl blend noted as Virginia-and-burley-based; not enough sourcing could be found to verify its content and character, as it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog.

rattray-blossom-temptation.z: Blossom Temptation is an aromatic blend in Rattray's Artist Collection line. Its base holds golden Virginia leaf, broken flake, and black Cavendish; a cherry-and-blackcurrant flavoring is applied on top. It is presented in a 100-gram tin decorated with a Japanese cherry-tree motif. The Rattray brand is Scottish in origin, though its tobaccos are produced today in Germany by Kohlhase & Kopp. The cherry note is measured, reminiscent of bitten ripe fruit, and doesn't overwhelm the base tobaccos' taste; the blackcurrant undertone rounds out the fruitiness. Nicotine is low and the smoke is sweet. It suits smokers looking for cherry-flavored blends who want to steer clear of intense, sharp flavoring, as well as newcomers to aromatics.
rattray-blossom-temptation.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity aroma dominated by ripe cherry and blackcurrant.

cornell-diehl-watchmans-reach.z: Watchman's Reach is a plain Virginia blend in Cornell & Diehl's Summit series, inspired by US national parks. The maker states the blend is made entirely of whole-leaf Bright and Lemon grade flue-cured Virginias, pressed into a dense plug. The plug form lets the smoker choose their own slicing thickness and allows the leaf to mature over time. On the flavor side, Virginia's natural sugars are central; a lively citrus tartness, dry hay, and warm baked-goods tones are described. Nicotine load sits in the low-to-medium band, making it suited to long sessions during the day. Aimed at lovers of unflavored Virginia who don't mind working with pressed leaf.
cornell-diehl-watchmans-reach.o: Leaves a lightly lemony scent reminiscent of dry hay and bread fresh from the oven.

mostex-stanislaw-air-mixture.z: No independent, verifiable source describing the composition of this blend, released under the Stanislaw brand of the Brno-based maker Mostex, could be found.

uptowns-smoke-shop-sir-winston.z: One of the English-style house blends from Uptown's Smoke Shop; no independent source conveying the blend's leaf composition has been found.

mike-russ-the-mind-meld-caramel-nut.z: A blend from a very small-scale series that, judging by its name, appears to be a caramel-and-nut-leaning aromatic; no reliable source describing its composition could be found.

quintessence-no-4-curly-cut.z: The term "curly cut" in the name refers to a cut obtained by slicing tobacco that has been twisted into a rope into thin slices; beyond that, no source could be found documenting the blend's content or maker.
quintessence-no-4-curly-cut.o: No information describing the room note could be found in available records.

john-patton-dark-and-stormy.z: One of the small-scale blends released under the John Patton name; not enough independent sources could be found to document its contents and character.
john-patton-dark-and-stormy.o: No source could be found on the room note.

hearth-home-marble-kake.z: Marble Kake is an unflavored Virginia blend where bright, red Virginia leaf is pressed tightly into a cake. The cake is prepared either by hand-breaking or by slicing and crumbling; the preparation method also carries through to the taste — finely rubbed out it smokes faster and flatter, while smoked as a thick slice it gives a slower, more intense smoke. The flavor axis runs toward mild sweetness and light citrus, balanced by the bready depth coming from the red Virginia. Nicotine is light, and it keeps its coolness even when smoked at a faster pace. Suited to smokers willing to prepare cake tobacco who want a straightforward Virginia character.
hearth-home-marble-kake.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of baked bread and candied citrus peel.

peter-heinrichs-curly-special.z: Curly Special is a blend the Cologne-based house Peter Heinrichs prepares by twisting Virginia and Perique leaf like a rope. The twisted tobacco is cut into slices about the size of a small coin; because each slice carries a complete cross-section of all the blend's components, it forms a whole mixture on its own. This structure noticeably slows the burn. In the flavor profile, Virginia's classic bready sweetness leads; since the Perique proportion is kept measured, raisin, plum, and light spice notes are noticeable but not dominant. It suits people willing to work with rolled-cut tobaccos who are seeking a long, cool smoke. Rubbing the slices open before packing improves the burn.
peter-heinrichs-curly-special.o: Leaves a trace of raisin and plum alongside a light peppery note.

paul-olsen-75th-anniversary-blend.z: A commemorative blend Poul Olsen prepared for the 75th anniversary of his "My Own Blend" tobacco shop, begun in 1939; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.

e-a-carey-old-belt-virginia.z: A blend registered under the E. A. Carey name; it does not appear on the maker's current list, and not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition.

samuel-gawith-full-virginia-ready-rubbed.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Full Virginia Ready Rubbed, according to records a pure Virginia blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

nat-sherman-370-spring-street-cherry.z: A cherry-flavored numbered house blend from Nat Sherman; no independent source detailing its composition could be found.

villiger-virginia.z: This is a Villiger tobacco named as plain Virginia; no independent source could be found giving cut and leaf details.

petersen-sorensen-34th-mixture.z: 34th Mixture is an English-style mixture in which Syrian Latakia is combined with various Virginia leaves and matured under pressure. The Virginia tips accompanying the Latakia carry the blend's sweet side; some sales records also list a small amount of black Cavendish in the composition. The fine ribbon cut gives a slow burn and a cool smoke.
petersen-sorensen-34th-mixture.o: Leaves a smoke, dry wood, and burnt-leaf aroma.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-622.z: No. 622, one of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's numbered bulk blends, is recorded as an unflavored English-style mixture; detailed composition information could not be confirmed by a verifiable source.

james-and-sons-tobacconists-broadway-spe.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of Broadway Special, reportedly the house counter blend of an American tobacco shop, could be found.
james-and-sons-tobacconists-broadway-spe.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

gq-tobaccos-chocolate-vanilla.z: Chocolate & Vanilla is an unusual GQ Tobaccos experiment combining aromatic and smoky-blend traditions. Most of the ribbon-cut leaf is dark in color, threaded with golden veins, and comes at a smoke-ready moisture level. The pouch aroma is earthy and smoky; a plummy sweetness becomes especially noticeable on the exhale. The two toppings in the name don't sit separately in the blend but come together in Latakia's binding effect: cocoa's bitter edge and vanilla's creamy sweetness meet in the same smoke. The blend falls into the aromatic category but doesn't hide the leaf's taste. Just as Latakia's smoke doesn't override the sweet toppings, the toppings don't suppress the smoke either — so it suits not plain-aromatic seekers but those familiar with English blends who are curious about a sweet top note. It stays at a moderate level for nicotine and fullness, with an intensity suited to an evening bowl.
gq-tobaccos-chocolate-vanilla.o: A cocoa-and-vanilla aroma intertwined with smoke leaves a plummy sweetness behind it.

clan-shaw-white-burley-cube-cut.z: No reliable, independent sourcing could be found regarding Clan Shaw White Burley Cube Cut, so a detailed profile could not be compiled.

alt-smokers-pipes-a-s-p-thornhill-mixtur.z: No reliable source describing the content and character of A.S.P. Thornhill Mixture could be found.

clan-shaw-st-james-parish-perique.z: No reliable, independent sourcing could be found regarding Clan Shaw St. James Parish Perique, so a detailed profile could not be compiled.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-manaton-caramel.z: Manaton Caramel is an aromatic built on black cavendish, flavored in two layers based on caramel and coffee. It is sold in bulk in a ready-rubbed consistency and is described as medium-bodied. While cavendish's sugary, dark base works in the same direction as the caramel, the coffee note adds a roasted, lightly bitter counterpoint to the blend. Suitable for smokers who like sweet aromatics but don't want to stay solely on the vanilla axis, and for those looking for an after-breakfast smoke.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-manaton-caramel.o: Leaves a dark, sweet aroma reminiscent of burnt sugar and freshly brewed coffee.

the-storytellers-pipe-m-m-log-cabin.z: M/M Log Cabin is a house blend Mike and Meaghan Hulsey, who run The Story Teller's Pipe tobacconist, prepared to recreate the old Log Cabin blend. Per the maker's description, quality Burley leaves are joined by flue-cured, red, golden and stoved Virginias, with a pinch of black Cavendish added to round out the balance; it is cased with maple syrup flavor. It is a Burley-forward aromatic: the natural sweetness of maple syrup is felt on lighting, and after a quarter of the bowl the taste settles into an earthy, walnut-like base, with a light spice trace running through to the end. Suited to smokers after an aromatic that carries the tobacco's own taste rather than a syrupy casing, and to those who enjoy Burley's dry nuttiness. It is ribbon cut and sold loose.
the-storytellers-pipe-m-m-log-cabin.o: Leaves a scent of oats and molasses cookie on lighting, moving toward freshly baked sweet walnut bread as it progresses.

e-a-carey-europe-no-7-ready-rubbed.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of No. 7 Ready Rubbed, a pipe tobacco from E. A. Carey (Europe).

milan-tobacconists-our-prince-albert.z: Milan Tobacconists' own mixture following in the footsteps of an American code blend known for over a hundred years. Burley leaves are brought together with cavendish; the blend's sweetness comes not from a heavy sauce but from the leaf's own sugar and the cavendish processing. It is a clean, slow-burning tobacco with a measured nicotine level.
