It has a character suited to smokers looking for a nutty, straightforward body who keep their pipe going all day, as well as those new to the pipe.
milan-tobacconists-our-prince-albert.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, subtly nutty pipe-tobacco aroma.

friedman-pease-inverness.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Friedman & Pease's Inverness blend; records place it in the Scottish-style class.

cornell-diehl-unique.z: No listing documenting the composition of Unique, a Cornell & Diehl blend, could be found in the maker's current catalogue or reliable retailer pages.

mccranies-somerled.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found on Somerled, one of McCranie's Pipe Shop's house blends.
mccranies-somerled.o: No reliable description of the aroma could be found.

davidoff-mild-mixture.z: Mild Mixture is Davidoff's ribbon-cut aromatic blend of black Cavendish, Cavendish and Virginia leaves. It's caramel and vanilla flavored; the aroma is perceived at medium intensity, while the tobacco's own flavor load stays very light. Its nicotine is extremely light. The blend's defining trait is that sweetness comes to the fore: the sugary profile dominates enough to lead over the tobacco taste. It's therefore a low-bodied record for those drawn to heavily sweet aromatics.
davidoff-mild-mixture.o: Leaves a distinctly sugary scent evoking caramel and vanilla.

sutliff-tobacco-company-planters-punch-d.z: Planters Punch, coded D62, takes its name from the rum cocktail of the same name that became popular in the early 20th century. Rum, orange, pineapple, coconut, cherry, and raspberry notes are drawn into a ribbon-cut base of burley, Virginia, and black cavendish leaf. The casing is intense and multi-layered; fruit sweetness leads on the palate, with rum noticeable in the background. Nicotine stays light. It falls within the interest of those looking for an aromatic with a pronounced fruity flavoring.
sutliff-tobacco-company-planters-punch-d.o: Leaves a sweet scent reminiscent of a rum-based tropical fruit punch.

peter-stokkebye-evening-rose.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Evening Rose could be found.

smokinjoescigars-com-joes-black-cordial-.z: A blend in the numbered aromatic series signed by the retailer; no source describing its composition could be found.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-kendals-dark.z: Kendals Dark is a dark blend produced by Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. in Kendal and sold in bulk at McGahey The Tobacconist. Fire-cured dark Kentucky leaf carries most of its weight, giving an earthy, nutty, smoky, and lightly spiced taste. Virginia, staying in the background, adds a tangy, lightly fermented fruit quality to the blend. The nicotine load is high; smoking it in a small-chambered pipe on a full stomach is a customary approach for this type of blend. Geared toward experienced smokers accustomed to unflavored, dark, strong English tobaccos; it will be too heavy for a smoker coming from aromatic blends.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-kendals-dark.o: Leaves the smoky, sooty, woody aroma of fire-cured leaf.

e-a-carey-castle-blend.z: This is referred to in the E. A. Carey catalog as an English-style mixture, no longer appearing in current production; no primary source could be found about its composition.

mcclelland-gkcpc-nocturne.z: A blend among McClelland's club selections, reportedly containing Latakia; no sufficient source documenting its composition could be found.

milan-tobacconists-neapolitan.z: Neapolitan is one of the house blends Milan Tobacconists, in business in Roanoke, Virginia since 1912, prepares at its own counter. According to the maker's description, the blend is built by bringing together three separate cavendish leaves; the aim is to meet the chocolate, vanilla, and cherry trio of Neapolitan-style tri-color ice cream in tobacco form. Though the casing intensity is pronounced, the leaf side is kept light, so the nicotine load stays low. Suitable for those looking for a sweet aromatic that can be lit at any hour and doesn't tire the tongue, and for smokers new to the pipe wanting to get to know cavendish-based blends. The aroma it leaves in the room is sweet and bakery-like. Milan blends are mostly sold loose, by the ounce and pound, at the shop and through the maker's own website.
milan-tobacconists-neapolitan.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of cocoa, vanilla, and cherry candy.

park-lane-tobacconist-pipe-club-mixture.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Pipe Club Mixture, one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

sentimiento-nacional-macedonia-i.z: According to records, one of Sentimiento Nacional's dark blends combining Burley and Syrian Latakia in roughly equal proportions; detailed character information could not be substantiated with a verifiable source.

richs-rainy-days-and-mondays.z: Rainy Days and Mondays is a balanced English blend from Rich's Cigar Store, named in reference to Portland's rainy weather. Latakia's aroma is pronounced when the jar is opened; in the smoking, medium-bodied Virginia leaf softens Latakia's spicy smoke. This structure makes the blend more measured than heavy Balkan-style mixtures. It suits smokers who want the Latakia taste but prefer a balance they can smoke all day; it is unflavored and sold in bulk at the Portland stores.
richs-rainy-days-and-mondays.o: Leaves a damp wood-fire and soot aroma with a light sweet grain trace underneath.

hearth-home-frenchys-sunza-bitches.z: Frenchy's Sunza Bitches, part of Hearth & Home's Signature series, combines sweet Virginia leaf with dark Burley and a generous amount of Perique. Unflavored black Cavendish is added for body, along with a small amount of bourbon to adjust the aroma and depth. The blend is ribbon cut and the tobacco character dominates; Perique lends a plum-and-pepper edge, while Burley brings earthy, nutty weight. Since both nicotine and flavor intensity run above average, it suits evening or after-meal smoking more than a daytime tobacco. For smokers familiar with the Virginia-Perique family who don't mind Burley's weight and a light spirit-like seasoning, this is a thicker option than a typical VaPer. Records indicate the brand has kept the blend on its own shop list for a long time.
hearth-home-frenchys-sunza-bitches.o: Carries sweet Virginia aroma topped with a pepper-like edge and a light whiskey seasoning.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-john-cottons-h.z: According to a 1972 company document, Honeydew was among the tobaccos produced in Denmark under the John Cotton name; not enough independent source material describing the blend's composition could be found.

hilands-cigars-black-gold-plus.z: This is listed as a variant of Black Gold, a blend Arizona's Hiland's Cigars has sold for many years; no sufficient source explaining how this variant differs from Black Gold could be found.
hilands-cigars-black-gold-plus.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

with-pipe-and-book-common-sense.z: Common Sense is one of the house blends from the With Pipe and Book shop in Lake Placid; no verifiable source could be found regarding its composition and character.
with-pipe-and-book-common-sense.o: No confirmed description of the room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-sea-dog.z: Sea Dog is a ribbon-cut blend in Cornell & Diehl's English family. It's made of a combination of dark Burley, light Virginia flake, black Cavendish, Turkish leaf, and Cyprus Latakia; its name and marketing are built around nautical imagery. Burley's breadlike base gives the blend body, while Latakia and Oriental take on the smoky, spicy layer; black Cavendish softens the transitions. On the maker's scale, strength, flavor, and room note are medium. Suited to those looking for a full but not excessive English mixture.
cornell-diehl-sea-dog.o: Leaves a scent dominated by woody smoke from Cyprus Latakia, with a light sweetness underneath.

niall-of-nine-dead-men.z: One of the blends prepared in very small batches under the Niall of Nine signature; not enough independent source material documenting its composition and character could be found.

clan-shaw-mozambique.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Mozambique.

peter-stokkebye-swiss-delight.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Swiss Delight in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-van-gogh-2023.z: Van Gogh is an all-Virginia blend from Ken Byron Ventures, a small-scale producer based in Pennsylvania. Per the maker's description, domestic and imported Virginias are brought together and, after pressing, presented as broken flake with a mottled, dark-toned appearance. The leaf goes through a light casing; no dominant flavoring or heavy sweetening is added, so the taste comes largely from Virginia's own breadlike, dried-fruit character. KBV re-blends its offerings every year and releases them in limited numbers under a year stamp, so leaf sourcing and aging can differ between years of the same name. The broken-flake structure calls for rubbing out between the fingers before packing and rewards a slow smoke. Suited to smokers who want to follow unflavored Virginia's natural sweetness and its development in the jar over time, and to those already used to flake form.
ken-byron-ventures-van-gogh-2023.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma of dry hay and cooked fruit.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-5.z: No. 5, one of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's numbered bulk blends, is listed as an aromatic according to the records; no verifiable source could be found regarding the blend's composition and character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-expedition-25.z: Sufficient sources to confirm the composition and character of Expedition #25, mentioned among Sutliff's bulk aromatics, could not be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-cringle-flake-20.z: Cringle Flake is the first entry in the holiday-season series Sutliff launched in 2019, produced in limited quantity. It consists solely of red Virginia leaves, pressed and cut into flake. The tin includes space for a gift tag. On the palate, tart dark fruit, light citrus, bread, and sugared cooked-fruit tones stand out, rounded out by a woody, earthy base. Body and flavor are medium. Designed for smokers who enjoy unflavored Virginia flakes and want a holiday tin suited to aging. Being a limited edition, it is not in current production.
sutliff-tobacco-company-cringle-flake-20.o: Leaves a scent of tart dark fruit and baked bread.

charles-fairmorn-candlelight-blend.z: No sufficient independent sources could be found regarding this blend released under the Charles Fairmorn name.

mccranies-canterbury.z: Canterbury is one of the bulk blends McCranie's tobacco shop in Charlotte, North Carolina, has made under its own name. Matured Virginia leaf forms its core, joined per the shop's recipe by Xanthi-type Turkish Oriental leaf. The Oriental share is enough to break up the Virginia's sugary flatness and give the blend a dry, faintly tangy edge; there's no Latakia. Described as an all-day "cake tobacco" that can be smoked in the same pipe repeatedly, with moderate satiety. Since it carries no flavoring, it's a middle-ground option for smokers used to unflavored Virginia blends who nonetheless find straight Virginia a bit flat on its own. McCranie's was founded in 1979 by Tom McCranie and has since been run by his sons; the shop's bulk-blend list runs to dozens of entries and distribution is largely limited to its own stores.
mccranies-canterbury.o: Leaves a lightly spiced trace with a tangy sourdough and dry-hay aroma.

connoisseur-aaa-burley.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Connoisseur pipe tobacco named AAA Burley, so the blend's content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

g-l-pease-ravens-wing.z: Raven's Wing is a dark mixture using both Cyprus and Syrian latakia in high proportion. Latakia is pronounced but does not entirely mask the Oriental leaves and stoved dark Virginias; these two components add complexity and balance to the blend. Due to the high latakia proportion, it burns slowly, and loading the pipe more loosely than usual is recommended. Following the destruction of the aged Syrian latakia stock used in the blend in the November 2004 warehouse fire, production was halted. It is a record now found only in old tins, sought by those wanting a dark, smoky, full smoke.
g-l-pease-ravens-wing.o: Fills the room with a heavy smoke and tar-like woodsmoke aroma.

james-barber-best-virginia-shag.z: Best Virginia Shag, one of the house blends of the James Barber tobacconist house, is, as the name suggests, a straight Virginia tobacco in a fine shag cut; no independent source detailing its character could be found.
james-barber-best-virginia-shag.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

dan-tobacco-gold-label.z: No adequate independent sources were found documenting the composition of this blend, listed as Virginia-based in the Dan Tobacco catalogue.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-rum.z: Kendal Gold is one of the shag-cut main bodies produced at Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Kendal workshop in Cumbria. Its base is a fine golden-hued cut of flame-cured bright Virginia leaf; the producer states it uses no other tobacco type in this series, only cleanly cut Virginia. The Kendal Gold body is offered with numerous different flavorings, and Kendal Gold Rum is this family's rum-flavored member. The rum flavoring deepens the Virginia's own sugar without masking it; a sweet layer leaning toward raisin and molasses is felt on the smoke. Since the cut is shag, packing is loose and the bowl is drawn slowly. Suited to smokers seeking a middle ground between aromatic and unflavored Virginia.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-rum.o: Leaves a sweet molasses and rum aroma.

hearth-home-classic-burley-kake.z: Classic Burley Kake is a Hearth & Home blend that harks back to old-style Burley flakes and cakes. The mixture uses Burley leaf from Tennessee and Kentucky, ranging from pale cream to dark mahogany, joined by a measure of aged red Virginia. The blend is pressed into a cake and offered pre-sliced. It carries a top-dressing oriented toward cocoa, rum, and a touch of anise, which rounds out the tobacco's nutty, bready base without masking it. The smoke is full-bodied and the taste mildly sweet. The pressed structure supports a cool burn. Well suited to smokers who enjoy traditional American Burley flakes and want a sweetish everyday blend without going heavy into aromatics.
hearth-home-classic-burley-kake.o: Leaves a sweet room note of cocoa and rum with a light hint of anise.

nat-sherman-702-dragoon.z: Reportedly a Nat Sherman house blend containing Latakia and Perique, prepared to order rather than on a regular production run; no independent source documenting its composition in detail could be found.
nat-sherman-702-dragoon.o: A spicy sharpness from the Perique layers over the smoky Latakia aroma.

peterson-special-reserve-2010.z: Special Reserve 2010 is a limited edition blend released as part of Peterson's Special Reserve series specific to that year; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient first-hand sources confirming its content and character could be found.

john-middleton-inc-crosby-square.z: John Middleton's Virginia-Burley-based blend; no verifiable information on its profile could be found.
john-middleton-inc-crosby-square.o: No verifiable information on its room note could be found.

synjeco-bad-nun.z: Bad Nun is a Virginia blend produced for the Synjeco shop in Zurich by the Gawith firm in Kendal. The Virginia leaves used in the base carry a citrusy tartness, dark cooked-fruit sweetness, light grassiness, and a deep earthy note. Over this, a Lakeland flavoring — the signature of the English Lake District tradition — is applied, giving a floral, soapy, and distinctive character. The blend's Lakeland layer is strong and can overshadow the tobacco's own taste. Nicotine is also high, so it's best smoked slowly and in small amounts. Records note that the companion version, Bad Nun II, uses Perique, and that in this version raisin and plum sweetness stand out more than spice. It is a product intended for smokers familiar with the Lakeland style and used to strong Virginias.
synjeco-bad-nun.o: Leaves a dark fruit scent alongside a soapy, lavender-like floral Lakeland aroma.

peterson-st-patricks-day-2018.z: St. Patrick's Day 2018 is a limited edition blend released as part of Peterson's St. Patrick's Day series specific to that year; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient first-hand sources confirming its content and character could be found.

smokers-haven-20th-anniversary-mixture.z: 20th Anniversary Mixture is a discontinued mixture the Smokers' Haven tobacconist in Columbus, Ohio had prepared for its anniversary; sufficient sources on its composition could not be found.
smokers-haven-20th-anniversary-mixture.o: Records did not describe the room note.

robert-mcconnell-the-peddlers-pipe.z: This is a blend carried under the Robert McConnell name, said to belong to the straight Virginia class; there is not enough source material describing its content and character.
robert-mcconnell-the-peddlers-pipe.o: Could not be determined from available sources.

cornell-diehl-dark-chocolate.z: Dark Chocolate is a simple aromatic built on a single leaf group: dark chocolate flavoring is worked into a black cavendish base. The manufacturer lists the cut as ribbon and places the blend in the aromatic family. Nicotine is very low, flavor intensity is pronounced; cavendish's own sweetness supports the chocolate note. Its aroma spreads moderately through the room. It suits smokers looking for a sweet, pronounced flavor over strength, and newcomers to aromatics.
cornell-diehl-dark-chocolate.o: Leaves an aroma of bittersweet chocolate and cocoa.

van-erkoms-perique-navy-cut.z: A navy cut product from South African maker Van Erkoms whose name points to a Virginia-Perique structure; no sufficient independent source describing the blend's composition and smoking character has been found, so the record is left incomplete.

comoys-of-london-cornish-mixture.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Comoy's of London blend Cornish Mixture.

gawith-hoggarth-co-four-squires-flake.z: Four Squires is an unflavored plain Virginia flake prepared from Brazilian- and Malawi-origin Virginia leaf. Part of the leaves goes through flue-curing, part through sun-curing; this dual process gives the blend a bready body and a dark sweetness. The medium-thick slices are packed rubbed out or folded, giving a slow, cool burn. Suited to smokers seeking unflavored Virginia taste along the lines of toasted bread and honey rather than fruity tartness. Its structure is well suited to jar aging.
gawith-hoggarth-co-four-squires-flake.o: Leaves a dry-hay and baked-bread aroma.

f-j-smith-glasgow-smoking-mixture.z: F.& J. Smith is an old Scottish tobacco producer founded in Glasgow; no verifiable source could be found regarding the composition and character of the Glasgow Smoking Mixture blend.

brebbia-quartetto-mixture-no-22.z: Quartetto is one of the aromatic mixtures in Brebbia's numbered blend series. Light-colored, sweet Virginia leaves are brought together with soft black cavendish, topped with a flavoring made of fruit, herb and spice extracts. The cut is ribbon and it is offered in a 50-gram tin. Nicotine load is low, flavor body medium; the aroma it leaves in the room stays measured for an aromatic blend. Suitable for those not drawn to heavy Latakia mixtures and seeking an everyday sweet, but not syrupy, smoke.
brebbia-quartetto-mixture-no-22.o: Leaves a fruity, lightly spiced, measured sweet aroma.

cornell-diehl-mountain-camp.z: Mountain Camp, by Cornell & Diehl's own account, came about at a customer's request: it was created by swapping the Latakia and perique ratios of the Bayou Night recipe. The result is a full-bodied English mixture in which Latakia takes the lead while perique recedes into the background as a spicy, tangy edge. Virginia and burley build the body, while Oriental leaves add a tangy, herbal layer. The ribbon cut packs and burns easily, burning evenly throughout. With high nicotine and flavor intensity, it is intended as a hearty evening blend or for long outdoor sessions; the maker describes it as a fitting companion for a day of fishing. It appeals to the experienced smoker looking for a generous dose of Latakia and already familiar with perique's spice.
cornell-diehl-mountain-camp.o: A campfire-like smoke and resinous wood aroma, leaving a sweetish spice trail behind it.

the-smoker-woodsman.z: A house blend called Woodsman from the American tobacconist The Smoker; it is noted as an American-style mixture, but no verifiable source describing its composition has been found.

hu-tobacco-moroccan-bazaar.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the Moroccan Bazaar blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

w-o-larsen-scarlet-passion.z: No reliable source could be found regarding this blend bearing the W.O. Larsen name, so its details could not be recorded.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-special.z: A blend released as part of Ken Byron Ventures' small-batch production; no independent, verifiable source could be found on it.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-edition-iii-euro.z: Edition III – Europe is the 2019 installment of Kohlhase & Kopp's geography-themed limited series run under the name "Discovery World Tour." Each year the series covers a continent; this tin is devoted to Europe and its major cities. The leaf structure is built from black cavendish, golden Virginia, Burley and Virginia flake; because of the flake proportion, different cuts sit side by side in the tin. The casing brings together English mint, Spanish orange and Alpine cream, meaning a citrus and milk sweetness sits beneath a cool top tone. It suits smokers seeking a minty aromatic. Being a limited series, production has ended.
kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-edition-iii-euro.o: Cool mint and orange peel are topped with a fine milk-cream scent.

peter-stokkebye-chairmans-flake.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Chairman's Flake in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

1776-tobacco-co-british-grenadier.z: One of 1776 Tobacco Co.'s English-style blends; no adequate source describing its content could be reached.

mac-baren-virginia-blend.z: No detailed content or character information could be found for Virginia Blend attributed to Mac Baren, either on the maker's own product pages or in reliable retailer records.
mac-baren-virginia-blend.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

super-value-english-mixture.z: The English Mixture blend in the Super Value line; since it does not appear in current retailer listings and sufficient sources describing its composition could not be found, this record is kept limited.
super-value-english-mixture.o: Leaves a smoky scent typical of English-style mixtures.

lane-limited-wild-hare.z: No reliable source could be found for this blend, listed as aromatic in the Lane Limited catalog.

samuel-gawith-balkan-plug.z: Balkan Plug is a Latakia-forward blend the Samuel Gawith factory in Kendal offers in plug form. A high proportion of latakia and Oriental leaf is pressed onto a Virginia base into a tight block, leaving the slicing and crumbling to the smoker. The firm is known for continuing old pressing methods at its Kendal facilities, running since 1792. The flavor profile is built on soot, cedar, and dry spice; Virginia's sweetness plays a balancing role in the background. Nicotine is measured, flavor intensity high. Because of the plug cut and the thickness of the smoke, it suits smokers familiar with Latakia blends who don't shy from preparation work. Its pressed structure preserves moisture balance for a long time, making it suitable for cellaring.
samuel-gawith-balkan-plug.o: Leaves an intense campfire and soot scent.

sutliff-tobacco-company-alexander-bridge.z: Alexander Bridge, part of Sutliff's Private Stock line, is a classic American-style semi-aromatic combining golden sweet Virginia leaves with cool-burning white burley. Named after the Pont Alexandre III in Paris, the blend has a vanilla-and-rum mix applied with a light hand. Because the flavoring doesn't overpower the leaf, the tobacco taste stays noticeable; the smoke is soft and balanced. Suited to smokers who steer clear of heavy aromatics and enjoy lightly flavored Virginia-burley mixtures.
sutliff-tobacco-company-alexander-bridge.o: Leaves a sweet tobacco scent alongside light vanilla and rum.

sutliff-tobacco-company-honey-206.z: Honey #206 is a honey-flavored aromatic from Sutliff's numbered bulk line. Its base contains sweet Virginia and nutty burley, with some soft black cavendish added for coolness and a slower burn. Several honey essences are used in the topping, and the cut is ribbon. The honey topping dominates the first part of the bowl; further in, cavendish's and Virginia's own sweetness along with herbal notes come through. Body and nicotine are low, and the room note stays moderate. A record distributed by weight for those seeking a more balanced sweetness rather than heavily topped aromatics.
sutliff-tobacco-company-honey-206.o: Lightly fills the room with a scent of warm honey and dry grass.

pipesandcigars-com-pine-grove.z: No independent sources sufficient to complete a full profile of pipesandcigars.com's blend Pine Grove could be found.

middle-earth-tobacco-barrow-downs.z: Barrow Downs is one of the Tolkien-inspired series names from small-scale American blender Middle Earth Tobacco; no source documenting its composition and character could be found.
middle-earth-tobacco-barrow-downs.o: Records indicate it leaves a smoky, woody aroma.

consolidated-j-3-almondine.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Consolidated blend J-3: Almondine.

mcclelland-no-5125-coyote-classic-full.z: No. 5125 Coyote Classic Full is among McClelland's bulk full-bodied Latakia mixtures. Per the catalog description, generous Latakia and Turkish (Oriental) leaf combine with matured Virginia. It's related to No. 5110 in the same series; records indicate No. 5125 sits on a sweeter line owing to a more pronounced Virginia presence. Over the smoky Latakia axis sit the Oriental's spice and matured Virginia's sugar; flavor intensity is high and nicotine dose is above medium. Aimed at smokers who want a heavy English mixture but prefer a sweeter base over an entirely dry, sharp profile. Unavailable since the brand closed in 2018.
mcclelland-no-5125-coyote-classic-full.o: Leaves a sweet tobacco tone beneath an intense smoke and spice aroma.

cornell-diehl-aleppo.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Cornell & Diehl blend Aleppo.

mission-pipe-shop-105.z: #105 is one of more than sixty house blends prepared in-shop at Mission Pipe Shop in San Jose, California; no accessible source documenting its composition and character could be found.

cornell-diehl-latakia.z: This product isn't a blend but a single-varietal component tobacco: pure Cyprus Latakia offered ribbon cut by Cornell & Diehl. Latakia is obtained by smoking Oriental tobacco leaves over resinous wood and plant smoke; the result is a dark, nearly black leaf. It isn't designed to be smoked on its own; though nicotine is medium, the smoke and tar taste is very intense. It's used by smokers building their own English or Balkan blend, or wanting to raise the Latakia proportion of an existing mixture.
cornell-diehl-latakia.o: An intense scent of smoke, tar, and pine smoke fills the room.

svendborg-kirsberry.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Svendborg's Kirsberry pipe tobacco could be found.

kaptn-barsdorfs-bester-yellow-formerly-v.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Kapt'n Barsdorf's Bester's Yellow (formerly Vanilla) blend.

straus-tobacco-union-terminal.z: Union Terminal is one of the counter blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; records indicate the shop was founded in 1880 and that most of its house blends were named after Cincinnati neighborhoods and landmark buildings. Since no independent source on the blend's composition and character could be found, this record is kept at listing level only.

cult-blood-red-moon.z: Blood Red Moon is a dark-colored aromatic blend built from fire-cured Cavendish, bright Virginia, and Burley leaf. The maker's description states it's flavored with cherry and bitter chocolate; vanilla sits in the background as a rounding layer. It's ribbon cut, offered in a 50-gram tin. While the casing is pronounced, sources describe it as not fully detaching from the leaf, with cherry and chocolate together building a taste reminiscent of liqueur-filled cherry candy. Nicotine level is low, and it's described as a cool-smoking blend. Suited to smokers looking for a pronounced fruit aromatic who don't want heavy nicotine.
cult-blood-red-moon.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity, cocoa-laced scent reminiscent of a box of cherry chocolates.

motzek-vikings-hair.z: Vikings Hair is a straight virginia blend produced by the Kiel-based TAK (Tabak aus Kiel) workshop. According to the maker's recipe, strong virginia leaves in red and orange tones are aged and then pressed with a bit of Barbados rum; the resulting block is presented as broken flake. Here the casing doesn't build a dominant flavor layer but stays a subtle touch framing the leaf's own sweetness. The workshop states it uses nothing but sugar, salt, water, honey, vinegar, heat, and cold in processing its tobaccos.
motzek-vikings-hair.o: Leaves a warm aroma reminiscent of freshly baked bread and a light grainy sweetness.

ogden-st-bruno.z: St. Bruno is a classic English blend that Liverpool-based Ogden's has produced since the late nineteenth century. Its body is made of bright Virginia and dark-fired Kentucky leaf; the mixture is steam-pressed into flake form. In the 1920s a ready-rubbed version was added alongside the flake, with an appearance somewhere between broken flake and ribbon cut. Records indicate production moved to Denmark's Mac Baren starting in 2006, with the brand fully transferred to that firm in 2015; even so, the blend's origin is English. In the smoke, Kentucky's smoky, woody body balances Virginia's sweetness. The casing leaves a floral, fruity top note reminiscent of the English Lakeland tradition, with a noticeable citrus edge. Nicotine and body are medium, and it burns cool. Suitable for those looking for pressed English flakes, a smoky-sweet balance, and classic blends with a light casing.
ogden-st-bruno.o: Leaves a floral, citrus-tinged sweetness mixed with the woody aroma of dark-fired leaf.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-christmas-2012.z: No manufacturer or retailer source could be found for the contents of Kohlhase & Kopp's 2012 seasonal Christmas blend.

pipesandcigars-com-scottys-honey-chocola.z: Scotty's Honey & Chocolate is one of the bulk aromatics US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com sells under the name Scotty's Bulk Blends. A body built from Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish finishes with a warm chocolate taste, topped with a touch of honey flavoring. The smoke is mellow and round; nicotine stays light, while the taste follows a line where the casing is distinctly pronounced. The blend was prepared to replace a discontinued Mac Baren product of the same name. It is a ribbon rather than flake cut, so it packs and lights easily. It is a suitable everyday choice for smokers used to sweet aromatics and newcomers to the pipe; it is designed for those not looking for spicy components like Latakia or Perique.
pipesandcigars-com-scottys-honey-chocola.o: Fills the room with a warmed cocoa and honey aroma.

richs-bills-blend.z: Bill's Blend is described as the best-selling mixture among Rich's Cigar Store's house blends. It is made from a combination of various Cavendishes and Virginia leaf, designed to be light-bodied and smokable all day. Cavendish's mellowness works alongside Virginia's dry sweetness, and the room note stays measured. It suits smokers who steer clear of heavy aromatics and Latakia, looking for a plain, low-intensity everyday tobacco. It is available in bulk at the two Portland stores.
richs-bills-blend.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of baked pastry.

van-erkoms-jacaranda.z: One of Van Erkoms' blends sold in bulk in South Africa, taking its name from the jacaranda tree common around Pretoria and its surroundings. Records indicate it rests on a Virginia and Burley base; no independent source confirming its detailed composition and flavoring has been found, so the record is left incomplete.

mcclelland-oriental-mixture-no-1.z: Oriental Mixture No. 1 is the first number in McClelland's green-label Oriental series. Per the maker's description, the blend's backbone is small-leaved, sun-cured Oriental tobaccos; Virginia and Carolina leaves raise the sweetness, while a measured amount of Latakia is added for body and depth. The ribbon cut packs easily and burns evenly and cool. In the smoke, the Oriental tobaccos' tangy, pickle-like sharpness stands out; in the background there's an herbal note reminiscent of tea leaf and a fine smokiness from the Latakia. Nicotine load is moderate. Suited to smokers seeking blends built around Oriental tobacco where Latakia is used like a spice rather than a main ingredient. McClelland stopped production in 2018; the blend is no longer on the market.
mcclelland-oriental-mixture-no-1.o: A light wood smokiness mixes into dry hay and spicy incense aroma.

tabak-heinrich-privat-no-66.z: No accessible source describing the composition of this numbered blend from Tabak Heinrich's Nuremberg-based Privat series, filled under the shop's own name, could be found.

paul-olsen-901.z: One of the numbered aromatic house blends from Danish tobacconist Poul Olsen; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.

bosphorus-best-chocolate-flake.z: Bosphorus's chocolate-flavored flake blend; per records about 80% yellow and red sweet Virginia is joined by 10% Burley and 10% Latakia. The flavoring is built on cocoa, chocolate and vanilla; the note that comes forward in the smoke is milk chocolate together with Latakia's smoky taste, with vanilla and cocoa not distinguishable individually. The flake slices' moisture is at a level ready for direct filling. The blend was previously sold under the name Kenan's Chocolate Flake and later took the name Best Chocolate Flake. The bitter spice taste burley brings persists through every stage of the smoke and keeps the strength at a medium level. A blend suited to smokers in flavored tobaccos who don't want the tobacco taste entirely covered, wanting to experience the chocolate note together with Latakia.
bosphorus-best-chocolate-flake.o: Leaves milk chocolate sweetness together with Latakia's smoky aroma.

missouri-meerschaum-country-gentleman.z: Country Gentleman is the blend representing the more contemporary virginia-perique construction in Missouri Meerschaum's Russ Ouellette-signed line. Its composition includes light-colored and red virginias, joined by perique and a small amount of dark-fired Kentucky leaf for body. The blend takes its name from the company's corn cob pipe model of the same name. The virginia base gives a natural, tangy sweetness, while perique adds its peppery, dried-fruit-leaning layer; kentucky leaves a subtle smokiness and weight in the background. Suitable for those looking for an unflavored, medium-bodied virginia-perique blend and wanting to try this style in bagged tobacco form.
missouri-meerschaum-country-gentleman.o: Leaves a peppery, lightly smoky tobacco aroma with dried-fruit sweetness.

w-o-larsen-selected-blend-no-50-maple-mi.z: No reliable source could be found regarding this blend from W.O. Larsen's numbered selection series, so its details could not be recorded.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-applejack-twist.z: Applejack Twist is an apple-based twist product from McGahey The Tobacconist in Devon, listed in the shop's catalogue as a chewing tobacco; sufficient sources describing its composition could not be found.

samuel-gawith-sams-flake.z: Sam's Flake is Samuel Gawith's pressed slice tobacco combining Virginia with Oriental (Turkish) leaf. It carries no casing. Like the brand's other flakes, it is moist when tinned; slices can be packed intact or lightly broken, and burning noticeably eases when used closer to dry. It is on record that flavors settle a few days after the tin is opened. At the start of the smoke, Virginia's sweet, cool line leads; further into the bowl, the Oriental leaf's spiciness takes over, though Virginia sweetness remains the main axis. A slight freshness is felt during the smoke, the ash stays clean and mild; tongue bite is limited when smoked with control. Aimed at smokers who want to know the Virginia-Oriental combination without Latakia.
samuel-gawith-sams-flake.o: Leaves a lightly spicy, cumin-like trace beside the sweet Virginia scent.

leonard-dingler-ltd-nineteen-ofour-rum-r.z: Nineteen O'Four is a pipe tobacco line from South Africa's long-established tobacco manufacturer Leonard Dingler, its name taken from the year 1904. The company dates to the early twentieth century, remained a family business for a long time, and later passed to Swedish Match. The series' base rests on Burley and Kentucky leaf; this structure gives the smoke a nutty, bready and earthy body. The product is sold in 50-gram folding pouches and is largely aimed at the South African market. Nineteen O'Four Rum & Raisin is recorded as the line's arm distinguished by its rum-and-raisin flavoring. The casing is applied at a level that doesn't mask the Burley base; the smoke stays cool and body stays at medium. Of interest to those seeking an aromatic profile but avoiding syrupy weight, and to those curious about counter tobaccos specific to the South African market. Hard to find outside the country.
leonard-dingler-ltd-nineteen-ofour-rum-r.o: Leaves a dark, sweet room note reminiscent of rum and raisins.

owl-shop-pearl-pleasant-street.z: No reliable source describing the composition of this mixture, named among the Owl Shop's house blends, could be found.
owl-shop-pearl-pleasant-street.o: No description could be found in the records.

john-aylesbury-carolina-rose.z: No reliable source could be found to document the contents and character of John Aylesbury's Carolina Rose blend.

planta-fishermans-love-black.z: The black-tinned member of the Fisherman's Love line, produced at Planta's Berlin facility, stands apart by placing a small proportion of Latakia inside an aromatic blend. Its base rests on sweet Virginia and black Cavendish leaf; here Latakia isn't used to build the blend's backbone but as a component laying a light smoke-and-wood layer under the sweetness. Reports indicate a small amount of vanilla scent is also applied on top. The cut is ribbon, and packing and burning cause no trouble. Strength is light and flavor medium; it is a blend suited more to smokers who enjoy aromatic tobacco but want to add a bit of smoke and incense character than to those seeking nicotine. For those used to the heavy English character of Latakia-containing blends, it stays too sweet. It serves as a stepping stone for those considering a move from aromatics to English blends.
planta-fishermans-love-black.o: Leaves an aroma carrying soot and wood scent beneath a sweet Cavendish sweetness.

paul-olsen-dannebrog.z: One of the Virginia-based blends from the Poul Olsen shop, taking its name from the Danish flag; not enough source material documenting its details could be found.

newminster-no-3-very-cherry.z: The cherry-flavored numbered blend in the Newminster line; sufficient independent sources describing its composition and character could not be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-best-brown-2.z: Best Brown Flake #2 is a medium-bodied flake Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. prepares by pressing and slicing Virginia and burley leaves. Because the leaves are pressed, the flakes come out dense and mottled brown; they need to be rubbed out or cube cut before smoking. The blend does not carry a heavy top dressing, but does contain a measured amount of the essences typical of the Kendal tradition, making it a milder take on classic Lakeland flakes. Toasted, grassy, woody Virginia flavours lead early in the smoke, with the natural tobacco taste becoming more pronounced as it progresses. It is aimed at smokers wanting to get to know pressed English Virginia flakes.
gawith-hoggarth-co-best-brown-2.o: Leaves an aroma of dry grass, raisins, and a light tartness.

cornell-diehl-burley-flake-5.z: Burley Flake #5 is the series' cased member. Light and dark burley leaves are joined by red and bright Virginia and a measured amount of fire-cured Kentucky; a traditional casing of anise, rum, and molasses is applied on top. This casing doesn't make it fully aromatic, but it gives it the roundest profile in the series. Thanks to the casing, burley's dry, sharp side is softened; the taste becomes fuller rather than spicy and assertive. Kentucky provides a smoky base, while Virginia supplies sweetness. Nicotine strength again runs high. It suits smokers newly approaching unflavored burley blends and looking for a traditional cased-flake taste.
cornell-diehl-burley-flake-5.o: A sweet spice aroma reminiscent of anise spreads together with molasses sweetness.

samuel-gawith-bracken-flake.z: Bracken Flake is a pressed flake prepared from a balanced selection of fire-cured Kentucky and dark leaves. The producer states that a long-used essence has been applied to the blend; this casing gives the tobacco a distinctive scent. It has a medium-to-strong body; the fire-cured leaf's smoky, woody, and earthy character dominates. Suited to smokers seeking a high-nicotine, dark-leaf-forward flake.
samuel-gawith-bracken-flake.o: Leaves a smoky, woody, and spicy tobacco scent.

ark-royal-full-aroma.z: No adequate independent source documenting the content of Full Aroma, a blend from the Ark Royal brand, could be found.
ark-royal-full-aroma.o: No reliable information on the room note could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-dark-and-silky.z: Dark and Silky, part of Sutliff's Private Stock line, is an aromatic composed entirely of black cavendish leaf. A chocolate essence is applied on top, and this is the blend's single defining note. The ribbon cut makes packing and lighting easy. With its black cavendish base, nicotine strength is light and the smoke is soft; flavor follows a sweet line dictated by the topping. A record for those seeking a single-note, straightforward chocolate aromatic.

edwards-kentucky-bourbon.z: No sufficient independent sourcing could be reached to document the composition and character of Kentucky Bourbon, a pipe tobacco from Edward's.

straus-tobacco-mrs-bischops.z: Mrs. Bischop's is one of the counter blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; records indicate the shop was founded in 1880 and that most of its house blends were named after Cincinnati neighborhoods and landmark buildings. Since no independent source on the blend's composition and character could be found, this record is kept at listing level only.

mclintock-black-magic.z: Black Magic is one of the aromatic blends German maker Kohlhase & Kopp released under the McLintock brand. The mixture, built from Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish leaves, is a mixed-cut tobacco; its flavoring is built in an herbal, sweetish direction rather than a fruity one. Nicotine load is light. While the cavendish share softens the smoke and slows the burn, burley keeps the blend's body upright. An in-between construction appealing to smokers who avoid heavily sugared aromatics but don't want to move toward unflavored blends either. Product records indicate the blend has been discontinued, and its distribution in Germany was handled through Mac Baren Deutschland.
mclintock-black-magic.o: Leaves a sweetish, herbal, and spicy aroma.

golden-blend-tobacco-co-vanilla-supermil.z: Vanilla Supermild belongs to Golden Blend's vanilla-flavored line and, as the name suggests, is a low-intensity aromatic; there is not enough sourcing describing its composition and character.

de-la-concha-bulls-eye.z: This is a mixture noted as Virginia-Perique type among De La Concha's shop blends; no independent source describing its ratios and character could be found.
de-la-concha-bulls-eye.o: No reliable record could be found for the room note.

koltoma-april-water.z: One of the oriental-forward blends from Russian manufacturer Koltoma; no verifiable content information from the manufacturer or a retailer could be found.

mac-baren-chiefston-original.z: Chiefston Original, produced under the Mac Baren name, is remembered as a thinly sliced, apricot-flavored tobacco; no maker source or independent second record describing the blend's contents could be found.

pauls-pipe-shop-fisherman-special.z: Fisherman Special is an aromatic blend Paul's Pipe Shop built on ribbon-cut Virginia leaf and cavendish. Per the maker's recipe, a touch of Irish cream flavoring is given to a bright Virginia and cavendish base, then combined with the shop's Peaches and Cream mixture. The creamy peach note becomes the blend's defining line as a result. Virginia leaf adds a light sugar-and-acid balance to the smoke while cavendish supplies moisture and mellowness; nicotine load is measured. It suits those wanting a long, cool-burning smoke sweet along a fruit-and-cream axis. It's prepared in bulk at the shop's counter in Flint.
pauls-pipe-shop-fisherman-special.o: Leaves a scent of peach and creamy liqueur.

ashton-original-oldchurch.z: Ashton Original Oldchurch is, per records, a blend produced within Ashton's collaboration with McClelland in the 1990s and not currently on the market; no adequate source documenting its content and character could be found.
ashton-original-oldchurch.o: According to records, not enough information could be found to describe it.

e-a-carey-ready-rubbed-no-7.z: A blend registered under the E. A. Carey name; it does not appear on the maker's current list, and not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition.

levin-pipes-international-gorgorath-curl.z: Gorgorath Curly Cut is an unflavored Virginia blend McClelland prepared in very small batches from a limited Virginia harvest selected by Barry Levin. Its name, like many other Levin blends, is taken from J. R. R. Tolkien's geography. The leaf, in a short, curled shag appearance, burns evenly and relatively fast. Aimed at those seeking the tangy-sweet, grassy character of unflavored, matured Virginia. Production ended in the 1990s, and it's reportedly one of the hardest-to-find tins under the brand.
levin-pipes-international-gorgorath-curl.o: Leaves a sweetish room note reminiscent of dry hay and baked bread crust.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-191.z: No sufficient source could be found documenting the composition and character of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Wilke No. 191.

bosphorus-kenans-chocolate-flake.z: Kenan's Chocolate Flake is a chocolate-flavored flake built from about 80% yellow and red sweet Virginia, 10% burley and 10% Latakia. Cocoa, chocolate and vanilla are reported as flavor casings; the note distinguishable in the smoke is milk chocolate together with Latakia's smoky taste, with vanilla and cocoa not standing out individually. The bitter spice taste from burley spreads throughout the blend and keeps the strength at a medium level. The slices' moisture level is ready for direct filling. The product was later sold under the name Best Chocolate Flake. Aimed at smokers experiencing chocolate aroma together with Latakia, who don't want the flavoring to entirely cover the tobacco taste.
bosphorus-kenans-chocolate-flake.o: Leaves a milk chocolate aroma mixed with Latakia's smoky aroma.

american-tobacco-co-skallorna.z: No source documenting the content and character of the blend called Skallorna could be found.

james-fox-honeydew-aromatic.z: A Fox aromatic whose name draws on the old English "honeydew" tradition of honey-syrup flavoring; no source could be found to document its composition.

dan-tobacco-the-malthouse.z: This is a blend from the German maker Dan Tobacco, noted as aromatic; not enough sourcing could be reached to verify its composition and character.

cornell-diehl-haunted-bookshop.z: Haunted Bookshop is one of the blends by the late Cornell & Diehl blender Bob Runowski, named after Christopher Morley's novel of the same name. A burley base is joined by red Virginia and a measured amount of perique; it is offered as a crumble cake that breaks apart easily by hand. Burley defines the blend's character, giving an earthy, nutty, full-bodied smoke. Red Virginia adds natural sweetness and depth, while perique contributes a fine spice and complexity. Nicotine runs above medium; it is aimed at those seeking an unflavored, burley-driven classic American smoke.
cornell-diehl-haunted-bookshop.o: A fine peppery edge accompanies the nutty, earthy tobacco aroma.

bosphorus-2018-virginia-perique-flake.z: 2018 Virginia & Perique Flake is a flake-cut blend Bosphorus released in 2018, made of golden virginia and perique. Per the manufacturer's description, a very small chocolate touch has been applied to the blend; this casing is faint enough to be distinguishable only when one knows it is there. The product comes moist and its slices are thicker than usual. The chocolate touch, pronounced on first light, recedes as the smoke progresses, giving way to perique's spicy, grassy, lightly tart flavor; the sweet virginia base stays at the same level throughout. When filled as flake it can be finished with a single light without overheating or running wet; when brought to ribbon form it needs more frequent relighting. Suitable for those seeking a very lightly flavored Virginia/Perique.
bosphorus-2018-virginia-perique-flake.o: Leaves a light cocoa and woody tobacco aroma.

motzek-old-curly-mixture.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called Old Curly Mixture could be found.

samuel-gawith-westmorland-mixture.z: Westmorland Mixture is a mixture named after Westmorland, the historic name of the region where Samuel Gawith was founded. Its composition holds light Virginia, black Cavendish, and a small amount of Latakia; the blend is finished with a lightly sweet citrus-and-tonquin top note. Although product descriptions refer to it as a Latakia blend, the Latakia ratio is low and does not play a decisive role in the blend. On the smoke, the Cavendish's mild sweetness and the Virginia's light, bright line come forward; Latakia only leaves a fine smokiness in the background, and the top note gives the blend an aromatic tone close to the Lakeland style. Nicotine is light, flavor intensity medium. Fits smokers seeking a mild, lightly flavored, measured-smoke mixture.
samuel-gawith-westmorland-mixture.o: Leaves a light soot scent over sweet citrus peel and a sweet floral essence.

pipesandcigars-com-ice-cream-sundae.z: Ice Cream Sundae is one of the house blends sold under its own name by the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com; no sufficient independent sources documenting its content and character could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-pork-chops-apple-sauc.z: Part of Ken Byron Ventures' Virginia-Perique line's 2022 batch; records indicate it's prepared by pressing matured Virginia leaf into a cylinder and fermenting it, with a light fruit casing applied on top. No detailed independent source could be found about the batch.

samuel-gawith-demerara-flake.z: Demerara Flake is a flake blend Samuel Gawith makes by processing Virginia leaf with demerara sugar and a rum-based casing, then pressing it. Its name comes from the dark raw cane sugar; pressing and slicing are done using traditional methods at the Kendal facility. The casing is noticeable but not smothering; molasses and rum tones sit atop Virginia's bready sweetness. Nicotine is medium. Suited to smokers seeking a middle ground between unflavored Virginia flake and aromatic blends.
samuel-gawith-demerara-flake.o: Leaves a scent of brown sugar and rum.

just-for-him-figaro.z: One of the house blends the Just For Him tobacconist prepares at its own counter; no independent source could be found on its contents or character.

mcclelland-cpcc-caramel-rush.z: Caramel Rush is an aromatic McClelland released for the Chicagoland Pipe Collectors Club (CPCC) in May 2010, later folded into the brand's Club Blends series. It's described as a caramel-flavored, light-bodied blend built on a Cavendish-forward base. In the smoke, a sweet caramel note dominates, with the tobacco's own taste staying in the background. Nicotine dose is low and flavor intensity is measured; this structure suits long smokes that don't demand much attention. A record aimed at smokers who like aromatics and want a light, sweet profile.
mcclelland-cpcc-caramel-rush.o: Leaves an aroma of burnt sugar and buttery caramel.

gurkha-urban-legend.z: Urban Legend is an entry in Gurkha's pipe tobacco line that combines the English blending approach with American structure. Virginia and Burley leaf form the body; a small amount of Latakia and Perique serve as spice. A light coffee-like topping reminiscent of mocha is applied, and the tobacco is pressed and then coarsely rubbed out for packing. The pressed, coarsely broken structure gives a slow, cool burn. On the palate, Burley's nutty, earthy line and Virginia's sweetness stand out; Perique leaves dark fruit and Latakia a faint smokiness. Since the topping is applied in moderation, it isn't fully aromatic; it's a middle-ground entry for smokers who move between flavored and unflavored blends.
gurkha-urban-legend.o: Leaves a nutty aroma blending roasted coffee and a light smokiness.

milan-tobacconists-black-gold.z: Black Gold is among Milan Tobacconists' bulk aromatics. According to the shop's description, black and matured Maduro Cavendish, mahogany-colored Burley, and Virginia flake are used together; a vanilla-forward, caramel-supported flavoring is added on top. In the glass, impressions of bitter chocolate and coffee stand out. The burley share gives the blend a dry body and a nutty base, while cavendish sweetness softens the smoke. With its cool, slow-burning structure it suits long smoking sessions; it's a blend designed to be smoked alongside coffee.
milan-tobacconists-black-gold.o: Leaves an aroma of vanilla, bitter chocolate, and fresh coffee.

criss-cross-mint-blend.z: Criss Cross is a budget-class tobacco brand sold in large bags in the US. Although the product line is sold under the name pipe tobacco, its fine shag cut and structure lean closer to roll-your-own cigarette use; per the brand's own marketing, the blend is built from air-cured Burley combined with Virginia leaf, aiming for a clean cut with fewer stems than competitors. Mint Blend is the version with a mint-and-menthol-style cooling casing added to this base. The smoke is cool with a sharp mint accent, and the tobacco's own taste stays behind that casing. Aimed at those looking for a heavily flavored, fast-burning, cheap tobacco, accustomed to mentholated smokes. It doesn't offer a structure suited to those expecting a slow, complex pipe smoke.
criss-cross-mint-blend.o: Leaves a scent of cool mint and roasted tobacco.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-black-friar.z: Black Friar is a blend referred to under the Orlik Tobacco Company A/S label and classified in records as straight Virginia; no detailed source about its composition could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-pipe-force-episo.z: Pipe Force is a limited Signature Series the Danish blender Per Georg Jensen prepared for Sutliff; each episode was released in sequence as a separate blend. The first episode is a Latakia-forward English mixture: fire-cured leaf, stoved Rustica, naturally sweet top-grade Virginias, and Katerini — the line's only Oriental — are brought together. The use of Rustica noticeably raises the blend's nicotine load and its earthy, floral spice. It is aimed at experienced smokers used to unflavored, smoke- and spice-forward strong English mixtures; being a limited production, it left the catalog some time after release.
sutliff-tobacco-company-pipe-force-episo.o: The scent of smoke, burnt wood, and dry hay lingers in the room for a long time.

villiger-new-world-export.z: No sufficient independent source could be found regarding Villiger's pipe tobacco called New World Export, so the blend's composition and character could not be recorded.

vauen-tab-160.z: TAB 160 is the Virginia-forward jubilee blend Vauen prepared for its 160th founding anniversary. Fine curly-cut rings, Virginia varieties in different cut widths, and spiced flake pieces are used together; this variety of cuts gives a cool, even burn. The blend carries a subtle cinnamon flavoring. Though the scent is pronounced in an unopened tin, it stays in the background while smoking; the taste that comes forward is the bready sweetness from Virginia's natural sugar. Suited to those after a Virginia-based blend with restrained flavoring.
vauen-tab-160.o: Leaves a scent of sweet baked dough and a subtle trace of cinnamon.

century-peaches-cream.z: A blend in the Century line known for a peaches-and-cream aroma; no sufficient source could be found to document its content.

mccranies-coyote.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found on Coyote, one of McCranie's Pipe Shop's house blends.
mccranies-coyote.o: No reliable description of the aroma could be found.

d-r-tobacco-rowland-gold-blend.z: A blend in Daughters & Ryan's Rowland series; while the series is known to use sweet Virginia, nutty-tasting Burley, and Oriental tobaccos in varying proportions, no adequate source describing this particular blend's own character was found.

cornell-diehl-apples-cream.z: Apples & Cream is a ribbon-cut aromatic Cornell & Diehl builds on unsweetened black cavendish. The maker states that the blend is flavored to evoke apple pie, with a generous apple essence, the brand's own Green River vanilla, and a cream flavoring typical of the brand. The tobacco mixture appears dark in color. Nicotine is very light in the blend, with taste coming primarily from the flavorings; the cavendish base provides a soft, sweet body. It suits newcomers to aromatic smoking and those looking for a sweet, low-strength tobacco.
cornell-diehl-apples-cream.o: Leaves an aroma of baked apple and sweet cream.

newminster-no-80-norway-pipe-cut.z: No. 80 Norway Pipe Cut combines North and South American-origin virginia leaves with Mexican burley and oriental tobaccos from Turkey. The cut is a fine ribbon at near-dry moisture; this makes lighting easier and keeps the taste profile mild. It carries no pronounced top-flavoring, only a slight sweetening. It is a take on the plain, everyday-smoking mixtures found in the Scandinavian market. The nicotine load is low and the smoke is cool; suitable for smokers who avoid strong flavoring and are looking for the tobacco's own taste. It is produced at Mac Baren's facilities in Denmark and sold in bulk.
newminster-no-80-norway-pipe-cut.o: Leaves a dry hay and lightly nutty tobacco aroma in the room.

meine-mischung-gelb.z: Meine Mischung Gelb is a light aromatic pipe tobacco produced in Denmark that has become widespread in the German market. Golden-brown burley and sweet Virginia are used together; a measured vanilla and fruity cherry note is worked in on top. Since it is prepared with a loose-cut method, it comes apart easily between the fingers and packs into the pipe easily. Its smoke is light, yet it offers a body that isn't empty; nicotine strength is low. Suitable for those looking for a sweet, easy starting point before moving to unflavored blends, and for those wanting a soft tobacco to smoke throughout the day.
meine-mischung-gelb.o: Leaves a subtle vanilla aroma over a fruity sweetness.

tinder-box-sunset.z: Tinder Box is the name of an American tobacconist chain founded in 1928 that sells blends prepared for its own shops under its own name; Sunset is one of these house blends, though no sufficient independent source describing its composition and character has been found.

castello-fiammata.z: Fiammata is the Virginia-Perique wing of the tobacco line carrying the Castello name. Its name means "flame" in Italian and shares its name with the same surface finish on the brand's pipes. Virginia forms the body of the blend while a limited proportion of Perique adds a plum and spice note; a light burley tone sits in the background. Because the Perique ratio is kept measured, the spice settles alongside the Virginia sweetness without overpowering it. It has a cool, balanced burn and does not bite the tongue. Suitable for smokers who find heavy VaPer blends too much and want spice in moderation.
castello-fiammata.o: Leaves a dried fruit and light spice room note.

mcclelland-wilderness.z: Wilderness is an English-Balkan-style blend McClelland developed together with Fred Hanna. The aim was to reconstruct blends from the 1960s and '70s using leaf available today; records indicate the blend carries nearly a dozen components and went through close to twenty trial versions before reaching its final form. Syrian Latakia forms the base, joined by a small amount of Cyprian Latakia; four separate Oriental varieties — Drama, Yenidje, Mahalla, and Basma — are then added. It's an unflavored blend with high flavor intensity; over the smoky Latakia base, the Orientals' spicy, herbal, and faintly tangy layers can be picked out individually, and the tin note carries a smoky, wine-like earthiness. Aimed at experienced smokers accustomed to Latakia blends who want a complex Balkan structure.
mcclelland-wilderness.o: Leaves a spicy, earthy trace beneath a wood-smoke aroma reminiscent of incense and a campfire.

drucquer-sons-loch-ness.z: Loch Ness is a blend built by Gregory Pease in the Scottish tradition after the Drucquer & Sons name was revived. Light lemon-yellow and aged red Virginia leaves are joined by small-leaf oriental tobaccos, Cyprus latakia and Louisiana perique; the mixture is pressed, rested as cake, and cut as plug. The smoker packs it by rubbing out or slicing the plug; this structure slows the burn and lets the flavors open in layers. Its character rests on tension between Virginia's tart sweetness and perique's peppery spice; latakia's soot sits in the middle, while the orientals give sour, herbal notes from the edges. Because it's medium in nicotine, it also suits daytime smoking. It's prepared for smokers seeking the structure of traditional Scottish and English mixtures who aren't put off by working with pressed tobaccos.
drucquer-sons-loch-ness.o: Leaves smoky latakia soot together with a scent of cooked dark fruit.

barclay-rex-el-moreno.z: One of Barclay Rex's aromatic shop blends; no adequate source describing its composition and flavor profile could be found.

jacks-tobacco-lucky-dog.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of Lucky Dog, part of Jack's Tobacco's "Dog" line, could be found.
jacks-tobacco-lucky-dog.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

dan-tobacco-kriswill-golden-navy-cut.z: A pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source on the blend's composition or character was found, so no further detail is given.

faders-centennial.z: Fader's is a line of house blends offered under its own name by a long-established Baltimore tobacconist; no verifiable source could be found regarding this blend's composition and character.

ashton-brindle-flake.z: Brindle Flake is a pressed Virginia blend produced by McClelland for Ashton in the 1990s. Premium flame-cured Virginia leaf is tightly pressed, deepening the leaf's natural sweetness; the sliced flakes are tinned partly rubbed out, and the blend also contains a small amount of black Cavendish. Its flavoring is measured: a top note leaning toward apricot and peach turns, midway through the bowl, into buttery-candy and toasted-Turkish-delight tones, then into a sweetness close to brown sugar. It's an easy-packing, low-strength blend, appealing to those who like pure Virginia flakes and are inclined toward resting and slow smoking. Its production ended with McClelland's closure in 2018.
ashton-brindle-flake.o: Leaves a sweet, light tobacco room note dominated by apricot and caramelized sugar.

pauls-pipe-shop-likrish-stick.z: Likrish Stick is the aromatic blend Paul's Pipe Shop built around licorice. Per the maker's recipe, licorice liqueur is given as a top dressing to a combination of two distinct toasted black cavendish leaves. Toasted cavendish forms a base high in sugar and low in nicotine. Licorice root is one of pipe tobacco's most distinctive additives; it leaves a sweet-anise, faintly salty trace in the mouth and defines the blend's character on its own. The smoke is light and cool, with the leaf taste staying behind the topping. It suits those seeking a pronouncedly sweet, single-note aromatic, as well as smokers fond of licorice flavor.

mcclelland-corps-quantum.z: No sufficient independent source describing the contents of this blend, apparently prepared in a limited run for a pipe club, could be found.
mcclelland-corps-quantum.o: Records indicate it leaves a mildly sweet aroma typical of Virginia blends.

clan-shaw-old-timer.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Old Timer.

paul-olsen-5610.z: One of the numbered house blends from Danish tobacconist Poul Olsen; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.

thepiperoom-com-enchanted-forest.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the ThePipeRoom.com pipe tobacco called Enchanted Forest has been found.

peterson-elizabethan-mixture.z: Elizabethan Mixture is a ribbon-cut blend prepared by adding Perique to pressed, darkened Virginia leaf. Records indicate the blend originated in the Murray, Sons and Co. catalog, was later re-established under the Dunhill name, and after Dunhill ceased production has been continued by Peterson with the original recipe and tin artwork. On the palate, Virginia's tart-sweet fruitiness runs alongside Perique's peppery sharpness; the body sits between light and medium. A slow smoking pace lets the flavor open up. It suits smokers wanting to get to know the Virginia-Perique line and those who prefer the ease of ribbon cut over preparing slices.
peterson-elizabethan-mixture.o: Leaves a measured trace recalling dried fruit and light pepper.

jons-pipe-shop-windy-city.z: One of the house blends Jon's Pipe Shop sells under its own name; no independent source could be found on its contents or character.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-black-twist.z: Sliced Black Twist is a tobacco made by hand-twisting dark fire-cured leaf into rope form at the Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. facility in Kendal; a small amount of dark air-cured Indian leaf is also added to the blend. The twisted rope is pressed and steamed, a process that darkens the leaf thoroughly while also reducing some of its nicotine and sharp spicy edges. As a result, the black twist gives a milder smoke than the brown twist. The "sliced" in the product's name refers to the rope being factory-sliced to coin thinness, so the smoker doesn't need to cut it themselves. On the taste side, smoky, spicy, woody, earthy, and leathery layers stand out; despite this heavy fire-cured frame, the smoke stays cool and smooth. Nicotine is still pronounced, so sources note a full bowl can be too much for someone trying rope tobaccos for the first time; the slices need to be well rubbed out and thinned, and smoked slowly. A product made for smokers seeking the raw, unflavored taste of fire-cured leaf, staying close to English rope tradition.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-black-twist.o: Leaves a heavy smoke aroma reminiscent of burnt wood, smoke, and leather.

the-danish-pipe-shop-g-flake.z: G Flake is one of the house blends from The Danish Pipe Shop in Copenhagen, released for the shop's 50th anniversary in 2019. Aged Virginia leaf is made into flake and sprayed with real, aged Italian grappa. The idea is traced back to the same house's VV92 blend introduced in 2016 and to the company director Nikolaj Nielsen's interest in grappa. Grappa's woody, boozy character combines with the Virginia leaf's natural sugar to build a consistent sweet-woody line, a taste that lingers for a while after smoking. It burns clean and relatively slow. Suited to smokers used to working with flake cut and after a very lightly cased Virginia.
the-danish-pipe-shop-g-flake.o: Leaves a woody, lightly boozy, sweet grape aroma.

planta-osb-67.z: OSB 67 is an unflavored Virginia mixture based on an old pipe tobacco recipe. Opening the tin reveals brown Virginia leaf carrying no casing or flavoring. The flavor line leans sweet and honeyed rather than herbal. Because its cut is a very fine shag, cigarette-tobacco thin, it calls for small or even very small pipe chambers; it is thus suited to short smoking sessions not exceeding fifteen minutes. It is a versatile product that can also be used by cigarette smokers. It suits fans of unflavored Virginia and those looking for a quick-break smoke.
planta-osb-67.o: Leaves a light tobacco aroma evoking honey and dry hay.

davidoff-cool-mixture.z: Cool Mixture is Davidoff's ribbon-cut aromatic blend of Cavendish and Virginia leaves. As its name suggests, it's a very cool-burning tobacco; its nicotine load is extremely light, and its aroma and flavor intensity are quite low. The blend's defining feature is the scarcity of smoke and flavor production: it may require frequent checking during the smoke to see whether the pipe is still lit. It's not for smokers seeking intensity or a pronounced aroma profile; it's a record only worth considering for those wanting a very light, low-tempo smoke.
davidoff-cool-mixture.o: Leaves a faint, indistinct, lightly sweetish tobacco scent.

tinder-box-lamplighter.z: Lamplighter is one of the Cavendish-and-Burley-based aromatic blends in the Tinder Box catalog. Cavendish sets a sweet, moist base while Burley adds a nutty dryness that regulates the burn. The casing centers on vanilla and toasted caramel, with a faint trace of spice in the background. The smoke is mellow and nicotine load is low. Suited to those after the classic American shop-aromatic taste and a light blend that can be smoked all day.
tinder-box-lamplighter.o: A light spice trace accompanies the vanilla and toasted-caramel aroma.

hu-tobacco-fayyum.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Fayyum, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

mcclelland-honeydew.z: Honeydew is a flavored blend in McClelland's 22b series, with honeydew melon worked over a matured Virginia base. Rather than covering the Virginia leaf's tangy-sweet line, the flavoring adds a fruity layer to it; the tin note also carries the sharp, vinegary edge associated with the brand's Virginias. A structure for those wanting a flavored blend without losing the tobacco taste. It's ribbon cut and, with its light nicotine load, suits long smokes. Discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-honeydew.o: Leaves a sweet melon and ripe-fruit aroma.

yaqui-tobacco-cigars-azteca-14-aniversar.z: This is a limited blend prepared by Mexican producer Yaqui Tobacco & cigars for the Azteca Pipa Club's fourteenth anniversary; no verifiable source could be found regarding its composition.
yaqui-tobacco-cigars-azteca-14-aniversar.o: No description of its room note could be found in the records.

lane-limited-leo.z: LEO is a latakia-containing blend registered under Lane Limited; not enough sources could be found to describe its content and character.
lane-limited-leo.o: Reportedly leaves a smoke and wood room note.

chief-catoonah-tobacconist-litchfield-mi.z: The entry has been left incomplete as no reliable source could be found for Chief Catoonah Tobacconist's Litchfield Mixture blend.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-casino-royal.z: Casino Royal is the blend Kohlhase & Kopp devoted to 2021 within its annual limited-series tradition. The mixture brings together black cavendish, Virginia flake, coarsely broken dark Virginia, plain Virginia and Burley; the tin contents are therefore not uniform but a combination of different cuts side by side. The casing structure is built around maraschino cherry, accompanied by cocoa, a small amount of pistachio and pink pepper. This spicy top note sets it apart from the usual fruity aromatics. Due to the Burley and dark Virginia share, body is medium; a purely sweet smoke shouldn't be expected. Being a limited series, its production has concluded.
kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-casino-royal.o: Leaves a room note of cocoa and light spice over a sugary maraschino cherry.

danske-club-white-roses.z: White Roses is the most layered blend in the Danske Club series in terms of casing. On top of the Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish base, vanilla, various tropical fruits, caramel, and brandy casings are added, joined by the white rose petals that give the blend its name. The ribbon cut lights easily. Nicotine sits between mild and medium, while flavor intensity is high and the room note is distinctly floral. Built for smokers seeking a heavily aromatic blend; it sits far from the profile of those wanting restrained casing. Offered in 50-gram pouches and 100-gram tins.
danske-club-white-roses.o: Leaves a floral rose scent alongside vanilla and caramel.

g-l-pease-spark-plug.z: Spark Plug is an English blend produced by pressing Latakia, Izmir, and Basma-type Oriental leaves together with Virginias into a plug. Cyprus Latakia's smokiness and leather character layer with the Oriental leaves' peppery, near-incense spice; the Virginias provide depth and measured sweetness. Records indicate the name and design were inspired by classic English automobiles.
g-l-pease-spark-plug.o: Leaves a sharp aroma dominant in smoke, tar, and leather, reminiscent of incense.

borkum-riff-ultra-light.z: Ultra Light is a very mild aromatic built from golden Virginia and Burley leaf, processed to reduce nicotine content. Its vanilla coating is measured; the tobacco taste in the smoke stays mild and flat, with a low tendency toward sharpness or tongue bite. The blend was the brand's flagship product sold under this name for many years; later, the same-line tobacco was offered as Original. It suits pipe beginners and those looking for a bowl with nicotine kept to a minimum. Borkum Riff is produced in Denmark under Scandinavian Tobacco Group.
borkum-riff-ultra-light.o: Leaves a faint, lightly vanilla, sweetish room note.

edwards-bishop-burley.z: This is a burley-based tobacco listed among Edward's Pipe & Tobacco's bulk house blends; not enough sourcing exists to detail its composition and character.
edwards-bishop-burley.o: Could not be described due to insufficient records.

murray-sons-co-ltd-erinmore-cube-cut.z: Erinmore is a series Belfast-based Murray, Sons & Co launched in the mid-twentieth century, known for a casing recipe kept secret. Cube Cut is the cube-cut version of that same family: the pressed cake is chopped into small cubes instead of thin strips. The leaf base is built from mature Virginia, soft Burley, and sweet dark air-cured tobaccos; the series' familiar fruity sauce is applied on top. The cube cut burns slowly and concentrates the tobacco's sweetness; records note Cube Cut carries a more pronounced perfume and a stronger sense of nicotine than the other products in the series. It went out of production well before the Murray factory closed in 2005, and today it is found only in old tins. A blend suited to smokers looking for fruity, strongly scented aromatics who don't mind a lasting taste trace in the pipe.
murray-sons-co-ltd-erinmore-cube-cut.o: Leaves an aroma of ripe fruit mixed with a heavy floral perfume that lingers in the room for a long time.

planta-anno-mmxii-ripe-marula-fruit.z: Anno MMXII is the 2012 installment of the annual "year tobacco" limited series from the Berlin house Planta. Its body is built from sun-ripened Virginia leaf, light-colored Burley, and double-fermented black Cavendish; a sweet-fruity casing from African marula fruit and a light clove-and-pepper spice note are applied on top. Reports indicate the casing is pronounced enough to stand ahead of the tobacco's own taste, while nicotine stays measured. It is a product for smokers who enjoy intensely flavored, sweet fruity mixtures and collect annual limited editions; being a limited edition, it is not continuously available on the market.
planta-anno-mmxii-ripe-marula-fruit.o: Leaves an aroma where a light clove-like spice accompanies ripe tropical fruit sweetness.

larus-brother-company-inc-jack-o-diamond.z: Cited among the blends Larus & Brother Company discontinued in the mid-1980s; no reliable source could be found for its contents.

solani-639-tropical-mango-flake.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Solani blend 639: Tropical Mango Flake could not be found.

mccranies-red-ribbon-vintage-2000.z: The 2000-stamped release of Red Ribbon is the ribbon-cut batch of McCranie's tobacconist's unflavored red Virginia blend, made from that year's harvest. Since the blend is produced on a single-harvest basis, each stamp carries its own year's leaf; records mention the 1983, 1996, and 2000 releases. In the younger release, Virginia's herbal, tea-like line and natural sugar sweetness are more pronounced; the creamy depth that stands out in older harvests builds over time. Suited to those accustomed to smoking unflavored single-varietal Virginia and to those wanting to compare different years of the same blend.
mccranies-red-ribbon-vintage-2000.o: Leaves a sweet tobacco aroma reminiscent of fresh herbs and dried fruit.

gallaher-limited-condor-bar.z: Condor is one of the classic pipe tobaccos produced by the company Thomas Gallaher founded, sold off British market shelves. The form called Bar is the pressed, plug-form version of the blend; the smoker fills by cutting a slice from the plug or rubbing it out. The line's body rests on dark fire-cured Virginia leaf, joined by Burley and a small amount of flavoured black Cavendish. What defines the blend is the Lakeland-style essence applied over it; described as floral and soapy, this topping is accompanied by a sweet, liqueur-like note. The plug form gives a cooler, slower burn. Since the essence tends to settle into the pipe, it is recommended to try it in a dedicated pipe or a corn-cob pipe. Condor Bar is no longer in production today; the line's long-cut and ready-rubbed versions remain on the market.
gallaher-limited-condor-bar.o: Leaves an aroma of floral Lakeland essence, liquorice root, and dark dried fruit.
