mcclelland-no-x-60-burley-broadcut.z: A broadcut product from McClelland's X-series bulk Burley entries, discontinued when the firm closed in 2018; no sufficient source documenting its contents and character could be found.

torben-dansk-orient.z: Torben Dansk Orient is a single-varietal Oriental tobacco in the brand's blending-component line. It consists of sun-cured, small-leaved Oriental tobaccos; it is unflavored and presented ribbon cut. Nicotine load is low and flavor intensity is high; it carries astringent, grassy and smoky notes. Smoked alone it gives a light smoke, while in blends it is used to balance Virginia's sweetness and add spice to English mixtures. Suited to home blenders.
torben-dansk-orient.o: Leaves a dry grass, smoke and faintly tangy spice aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-shag-vani.z: Kendal Gold is one of the shag-cut main bodies produced at Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Kendal workshop in Cumbria. Its base is a fine golden-hued cut of flame-cured bright Virginia leaf; the producer states it uses no other tobacco type in this series, only cleanly cut Virginia. The Kendal Gold body is offered with numerous different flavorings, and Kendal Gold Shag Vanilla is this family's vanilla-flavored member. Vanilla is one of the most widely produced flavorings in the Kendal Gold series; it coats the bright Virginia's straw-like sweetness with a creamy layer. Since the shag cut toasts quickly, it calls for a slow draw and loose packing. Suited to those seeking a starter aromatic blend.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-shag-vani.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough aroma.

nice-ash-cigars-transit-valley-cordial.z: One of Nice Ash Cigars' liqueur-flavored aromatic house blends, taking its name from the Transit Road area where the shop is located; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.
nice-ash-cigars-transit-valley-cordial.o: No description could be found in the records.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-boswell-english-bi.z: English Biscuit is a medium-bodied English blend where Latakia is combined with toasted Virginias and some cavendish. The Latakia smoke is pronounced, but softened by the Virginias' sugar and the cavendish; it takes its name from J. M. Boswell, who prepared the blend, finding a lightly sweet biscuit echo, like something fresh from the oven, in the smoke. Per records, arriving at the blend's final form took about a year. Boswell is a family business that prepares its blends in its own shop in Chambersburg, Pennsylvania. This blend suits those who love Latakia but don't want the intensity of full-bodied Balkan blends, seeking a balanced smoke between sweetness and smoke.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-boswell-english-bi.o: The sweetness of freshly baked dough mixes into a smoky wood aroma.

roman-peter-fox-cake.z: Fox Cake is a Virginia-Perique mixture from Roman Peter, a Swiss pipe maker and blender working in Affoltern am Albis in the canton of Zurich. Reports indicate the leaf used is sourced from India and Malawi. The cut is curly cut, meaning it is rolled, pressed, and sliced; most of the slices arrive already crumbled, with the rest broken up by hand before packing. On the flavor side, Virginia's floral sweetness runs alongside Perique's peppery, earthy layer; body is medium, with flavor intensity a step above that. The tobacco arrives moist and needs airing before smoking. Because of its long, wide fibers it burns more comfortably in medium and large-chambered pipes. It suits smokers familiar with Virginia-Perique blends who follow a spicy, evolving flavor.
roman-peter-fox-cake.o: Leaves an earthy, peppery, faintly sweet tobacco aroma.

bennington-tobacconist-king-william.z: King William is a Virginia-Perique-character blend prepared at Bennington Tobacconist's own counter. It's named after William E. Bennington, who founded the shop in Florida in 1965. It's built on an unflavored structure; the taste comes from the meeting of Virginia's natural sugar and Perique's tangy, spicy contribution from fermentation. In blends of this family, Virginia typically leads while Perique creates a fruity, peppery tension in the background. It's aimed at smokers who steer clear of aromatic tobaccos, looking for a plain, mature taste. Since the product is shop-specific, tin and packaging details can vary from period to period; whether it remains in the current catalog could not be verified.
bennington-tobacconist-king-william.o: Dry hay and bread-crust notes are joined by a faintly peppery, plum-like edge.

hearth-home-larrys-morning-blend.z: Larry's Morning Blend is an English mixture built on Cyprian Latakia, Oriental leaf, and bright Virginia. The Latakia ratio is noticeable, but the bright side of the Virginia and the buttery sweetness of the Oriental open the blend up enough to suit the start of the day. As its name suggests, it is designed for smoking first thing in the morning — smoky but not overwhelming. Aimed at smokers who love Latakia blends but find the darkest examples too heavy for the morning.
hearth-home-larrys-morning-blend.o: Leaves a buttery, bready aroma over wood smoke.

mazatec-garden-nicotiana-rustica-bundles.z: This product is less a blended pipe tobacco than the raw form of a single leaf type. Instead of Nicotiana tabacum, it uses Nicotiana rustica, a species used ceremonially across the Americas for centuries; the leaves are hand-picked, dried, and then tied into bundles with string. The bundles arrive quite dry; resting them in a jar before use is common practice. Records indicate the leaf is grown in South America.
mazatec-garden-nicotiana-rustica-bundles.o: Leaves an intense, earthy, sharp green-leaf aroma.

samuel-gawith-black-rum.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Black Rum, according to records a flavored blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

dan-tobacco-limerick.z: Limerick is a Virginia-Perique flake in Dan Tobacco's "Treasures of Ireland" series. With Perique kept to about five percent, the spice is noticeable but not dominant; the blend's body is carried largely by dark Virginia leaf. The tin note carries breadlike, yeasty Virginia tones alongside traces of raisin, stone fruit, and bitter chocolate. On the smoke, a dark, soft sweetness leaning toward plum and fig comes forward, without any sharp tartness. Nicotine level is low, making it suitable for smokers looking for a VaPer they can smoke throughout the day.
dan-tobacco-limerick.o: Leaves a dark, sweetish scent reminiscent of dried plum and bread yeast.

motzek-sweet-curly-mixture.z: A sweet blend from the Motzek workshop built on curly-cut rings sliced from a twist; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition could not be found.

peterson-irish-oak.z: Irish Oak is a ribbon-cut Peterson blend built on a Virginia-Burley base with Perique and Cavendish added, carrying a sherry-wine flavoring. Peterson is an Irish brand; tobacco production is contracted out to manufacturing partners in Europe. As described in Turkish-language sources, it is a tobacco heavy in nicotine and intense in flavor; further into the bowl, a spicy, tart character from the Perique becomes pronounced. The sherry flavoring isn't intense enough to put the tobacco in the aromatic category. It is a record aimed at experienced smokers who can handle the Perique's assertiveness and high nicotine.
peterson-irish-oak.o: Leaves a sharp, spicy, tart tobacco aroma.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-figgy-pud.z: Figgy Pudding, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an aromatic mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

mccormick-selection-cherries-in-whiskey.z: As the name suggests, this is a cherry-and-whiskey-flavored aromatic; no sufficient sources could be found to confirm its maker or contents.

clan-shaw-buried-treasure.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Buried Treasure.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-clan-arom.z: Clan is an aromatic pipe tobacco produced under Scandinavian Tobacco Group; no reliable detail on the blend's composition could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-clan-arom.o: Recorded as leaving a sweet, casing-forward scent.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-virginia-pu.z: As its name indicates, this is an unflavored Wilder blend made of Virginia leaf alone. The maker, Tabacos Wilder Finamore, has worked in Juiz de Fora since 1949 using a handmade process based on natural curing and fermentation. Since no independent source detailing the blend could be found, the record is kept limited.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-virginia-pu.o: Records suggest it leaves a scent of dry hay and lightly sweet straw.

motzek-type-1-2-latakia-blend.z: Reportedly a Latakia-containing English-style blend from the production of the Kiel-based TAK (Tabak aus Kiel) workshop, marketed under the Motzek name; no further detail is given since no independent source confirming its composition and character could be found.

argento-latakia.z: Argento Latakia is the classic English blend in the Argento line, produced in Argentina. It contains golden Virginias, a small amount of Burley, and a generous amount of Latakia. It carries no added flavoring; it's sold in 50-gram pouches and is referred to as number six in the line. Keeping the Latakia ratio high pulls the blend's character toward a smoky, woody direction; the Virginias provide background sweetness, while the Burley supplies body. It suits smokers accustomed to unflavored, Latakia-forward blends.
argento-latakia.o: Leaves a heavy room note of woodsmoke and soot.

james-fox-honeydew-virginia.z: No reliable source could be found to document the contents and character of James Fox's Honeydew Virginia blend.

sutliff-tobacco-company-north-pole-peppe.z: This is one of the limited blends Sutliff prepares for the holiday season; it was first released in 2021 and has been repeated as a seasonal item in subsequent years. Cocoa, vanilla, and a small amount of mint essence are drawn into a ribbon-cut base of black cavendish, dark burley, and Virginia leaf. Nicotine is light; the taste that stands out recalls minty hot chocolate. The mint note lingers, so it can leave a lasting trace in the same pipe over time, which is why smoking it in a dedicated pipe is common practice. It falls within the interest of those looking for a seasonal aromatic.
sutliff-tobacco-company-north-pole-peppe.o: Leaves a scent of warm cocoa, vanilla, and cool mint.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-111.z: Wilke No. 111 is a light mixture among the maker's numbered bulk blends that puts Oriental leaf forward. According to the recipe, the Oriental base is joined by a small amount of Latakia along with Virginia and Burley. Keeping the Latakia ratio low prevents the smoke from masking the Oriental's spicy, dry-grassy character; the blend is generally light-bodied overall. It suits smokers wanting to get to know the Oriental leaf up close while avoiding heavy-smoke blends.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-111.o: A light smoky trace mixes into the dry-grass and spice scent.

dunhill-ye-olde-signe.z: Ye Olde Signe is among Dunhill's earliest mixtures; production began in 1915, and period catalogs presented it as a soft, naturally high-sweetness pure Virginia leaf. It's an unadulterated, fine ribbon-cut straight Virginia blend. The aging process applied to the leaves leaves a tea-like scent in the tin and creates a non-artificial sweetness on the smoke. It's a medium-strength, medium-burning tobacco producing plenty of smoke; despite its mild taste, its body is full, so it's mostly considered suited to after-meal smoking. It appeals to smokers seeking Virginia's own sugar front and center, without latakia or flavoring additives. After a long spell off the market it was reissued, then discontinued again.
dunhill-ye-olde-signe.o: Leaves a lightly sweet scent evoking brewed black tea and dry grass.

affordable-pipes-the-ceds-blend.z: One of the house blends from the American seller Affordable Pipes; no accessible source describing its content could be found.

drew-estate-central-park-stroll.z: Central Park Stroll is a dark-colored aromatic in Drew Estate's New York-themed pipe tobacco line. Virginia joins a cavendish-forward, near-black-looking structure; it's ribbon cut. It carries a pronounced chocolate, vanilla and caramel-direction topping. Its body is light and its smoke is soft and sweet. Since Drew Estate ended pipe tobacco production, the blend is no longer produced. It was a product aimed at those seeking a heavily topped, easy-smoking aromatic.
drew-estate-central-park-stroll.o: Leaves a sweet scent blending cocoa, vanilla and caramel.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-bright-.z: Recorded as the 2021 batch of Mr. Christian's Bright Side; no accessible source could be found detailing this batch's specific contents and character.

bentley-night-club-mixture.z: A mixture from the German Bentley brand with no trace found in current catalogs; no reliable source describing its content could be found.
bentley-night-club-mixture.o: No recorded recipe could be found.

mcclelland-town-topic.z: Town Topic is a maple-flavored aromatic in McClelland's Premium Aromatics line. The maker's description calls it a smoke with a pronounced room note that stays mild on the palate. The base is Cavendish-forward, and the cut is ribbon; packing and lighting are easy. Body is light, and nicotine load is low. The flavoring stands out, with the tobacco's own character staying in the background. Sources note it's a flavor profile favored in cooler seasons. Suited to smokers wanting a sweet, syrupy aromatic. McClelland ended production in 2018.
mcclelland-town-topic.o: Leaves a sweet, warm aroma reminiscent of maple syrup.

tewksbury-company-celtic-blend.z: According to records, this blend was part of the lineup of Tewksbury & Company, an American blender that ceased operations following the 2009 tobacco regulation; no source documenting its content and character could be found.

samuel-gawith-kbe-mixture.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of KBE Mixture, according to records a Virginia-Latakia blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

cigar-connoisseur-oriental.z: Oriental is one of the house blends the Cigar Connoisseur tobacco shop in England sells in bulk. Its backbone is built from Oriental leaves such as Basma and Katerini; a small amount of Latakia and again a measured Virginia share are added on top. It is coarse-cut and kept at a suitable moisture level in the pack. On opening, a pronounced but not sharp Oriental tobacco scent is noticeable, with very little Latakia detectable. It lights easily and gives a long, even smoke. Nicotine strength is felt from the first puffs; despite this, it doesn't turn harsh through the smoke. The Oriental leaf's lightly spiced taste is defining, while Virginia's sweetness provides continuity in the background. Its ash is unusually white and soft. It is a blend suited to smokers looking for Oriental-heavy, unflavored mixtures, accustomed to high nicotine; since the flavor line doesn't change much through the bowl, it may equally not suit those bothered by monotony.
cigar-connoisseur-oriental.o: Leaves a light smoky aroma mixed into the spiced Oriental tobacco scent in the room.

sutliff-tobacco-company-pipe-force-episo.z: The third episode of the Pipe Force series is a Virginia-forward mixture built on fire-cured leaf rather than Latakia. Red Virginia and dark fire-cured Kentucky are combined with stoved leaves; the Katerini leaf used throughout the series appears here as well. Stoving caramelizes the Virginia's sugar, carrying the blend toward a dark, bready sweetness; the Kentucky adds a woody saltiness and nicotine. It is aimed at smokers who enjoy dark, Latakia-free Virginia blends with a full-bodied smoke. It is a limited production.
sutliff-tobacco-company-pipe-force-episo.o: Leaves a woody, lightly smoky scent alongside bread-crust sweetness.

cornell-diehl-hearthside.z: Not enough primary sourcing could be found regarding the composition and character of the Cornell & Diehl blend Hearthside.

gawith-hoggarth-co-no-7-shag-unscented.z: No. 7 Shag is an unflavored shag-cut tobacco Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. has kept in production for decades, built from fire-cured and flue-cured Virginia leaf. Its character sits on an axis of earth, leather, and smoke; underneath, a light sweetness from the Virginia and a herbal-citrusy edge round it out. This blend's base is also used in several of the house's Lakeland-style topped products; No. 7 Shag is the unflavored form of that same base. The very fine cut lights the tobacco easily, but packed tightly and drawn fast, the burn speeds up and heats up. Suited to smokers seeking the unflavored, smoky-earthy English shag style.
gawith-hoggarth-co-no-7-shag-unscented.o: Leaves an aroma of smoke, leather, and dry earth.

drew-estate-toasted-black-cavendish.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of Toasted Black Cavendish, a blend from Drew Estate.

hu-tobacco-herbal-fruit.z: Herbal Fruit is a fire-cured-Kentucky-forward broken flake in HU Tobacco's The Blender's Pride line. The dark leaf, prepared by pressing and breaking, is lightly flavored with a fruity aroma; the described flavoring leans toward mango and candy. The flavoring is kept measured enough not to mask the tobacco taste, so the earthy, smoky Kentucky character remains pronounced. It's a full-nicotine blend, aimed at those looking for a thin fruit layer over dark, natural leaf.
hu-tobacco-herbal-fruit.o: Leaves a ripe tropical-fruit sweetness sitting atop a smoky, earthy aroma.

kramers-pipe-and-tobacco-shop-house-arom.z: An aromatic bulk blend sold by a tobacconist under its own name; no independent source could be found about its contents and character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-country-estate.z: Country Estate is a blend in Sutliff's bulk aromatic line. Fire-cured dark leaves are joined with sweet Virginia and black cavendish; a measured topping dominated by plum, dried fruit, and vanilla is applied on top. The ribbon cut lights quickly, burns cool and even, and leaves little moisture in the bowl. On the palate, Virginia's herbal and lightly citrus tones stay under the topping while cavendish's sugary, vanilla sweetness comes forward. Sitting between light and medium in nicotine, it suits smokers wanting a soft, all-day aromatic, particularly those new to the category.
sutliff-tobacco-company-country-estate.o: Leaves a scent of sweet plum and vanilla with light dried fruit.

planta-empire-latakia.z: Empire Latakia Flake is one of three flakes Planta introduced in 2015. It is built from a generous amount of Syrian Latakia, select Virginia leaf, and some Oriental tobacco, then pressed and rested. While most flakes on the German market are of Danish manufacture, this line was prepared at the Berlin production facility on the brand's own flake press. It is a spicy, smoky, full-bodied tobacco with no added casing. It suits experienced smokers used to Latakia-heavy Balkan-style mixtures. The slices are presented neatly stacked in a 50-gram tin.
planta-empire-latakia.o: Leaves an intense, lasting soot, leather, and pine-tar aroma in the room.

mac-baren-mixture-modern.z: Mixture Modern sits at the aromatic end of Mac Baren's Mixture family. Its content rests on Virginia and the brand's cavendish, presented as a coarse cut. The blend is given a pronounced fruit-and-vanilla top flavor, so both the tin note and the taste throughout the smoke largely come from the casing. Nicotine level is very low and the flavor load is light; the natural tobacco character stays well behind the casing. Since it can burn hot, a slow draw and loose packing help. A product for those who like sweet, distinctly flavored blends or newcomers to pipes looking for a soft entry point; it won't meet the expectations of those seeking unflavored leaf taste.
mac-baren-mixture-modern.o: Leaves a sweet, sugary room note reminiscent of vanilla and ripe fruit.

carroll-p-j-co-ltd-travellers-joy-mixtur.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Traveller's Joy Mixture under the Carroll P. J. & Co. Ltd. brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

super-value-chocolate.z: Super Value Chocolate is a budget aromatic where chocolate flavoring is applied to a black-cavendish-forward base. As across the line, burley, cavendish, and Virginia leaves are coarse cut and blended, with production in the US. It gives a sweet, soft, low-nicotine smoke. Appeals to smokers who enjoy sweet, doughy flavors and want bulky packaging for everyday use.
super-value-chocolate.o: Leaves a scent of cocoa and sweet chocolate.

gq-tobaccos-christmas-blend-2014.z: GQ Tobaccos's limited holiday blend released specially for the year 2014; there is no sourcing documenting its composition.
gq-tobaccos-christmas-blend-2014.o: No record of its aroma could be found.

torben-dansk-no-5-mixture.z: Torben Dansk No.5 Mixture is a blend in the brand's numbered series; no sufficient independent source describing its composition and character has been found.
torben-dansk-no-5-mixture.o: Records describe it as leaving a dry tobacco aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-crumble-kake-lim.z: The second limited edition in the Crumble Kake series brings together bright Virginias from two continents and dark fire-cured Kentucky leaf. The blend is heat-pressed, rolled, and rested for roughly thirty days in an aged oak cognac barrel, then cut into an easy-to-prepare crumbly cake form. Dark fire-cured Kentucky is the main component, giving earth, wood, spice, and a light smokiness; bright Virginia adds citrus acidity, herb, and bready sweetness. The cognac resting leaves a sugary, lightly spiced fruit layer. Body and nicotine are above average. Records indicate it was released as a run of four thousand tins and is not an ongoing product.
sutliff-tobacco-company-crumble-kake-lim.o: Leaves a scent of smoky wood and sugared fruit.

middle-earth-tobacco-fangorn-forest.z: The English-style blend in the Middle Earth Tobacco line; since no independent source from the maker could be found, no detail on composition and character can be given.

reiver-pipes-tobacco-invictus-maneo.z: Invictus Maneo is a layered Scottish-style mixture built on red Virginias with Latakia, dark-fired Kentucky, Izmir Oriental, and Perique added. Kentucky and Latakia together form a dark, smoky, earthy base, while Virginia sweetness balances that weight; Perique adds peppery sharpness and the Oriental leaf brings dry spice. It is a full-bodied blend in terms of both body and nicotine, suited to experienced smokers who enjoy unflavored, dark, intense smokes. It is counted among Reiver Pipes & Tobacco's first releases. The brand is run by Dan Armstrong, who prepares his blends in small batches.
reiver-pipes-tobacco-invictus-maneo.o: Leaves an intense aroma of wood soot and spice.

former-50th-anniversary.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Former's 50th Anniversary blend; records place it in the English-mixture class.

tobacco-lane-inidan-summer.z: One of the house blends from the tobacconist Tobacco Lane; no verifiable source on its composition and character has been found.
tobacco-lane-inidan-summer.o: No source describing its aroma has been found.

hearth-home-sycaway.z: Sycaway is a Burley-forward mixture in Hearth & Home's Landmark line, inspired by place names. It takes its name from the Sycaway neighborhood of Troy, New York. The blend's backbone is Burley's distinctive nutty, bready taste; this taste is supported by a very light flavoring, kept measured enough to accentuate rather than mask the leaf's natural character. The ribbon cut makes filling easy, and Burley's dry structure gives a slow, cool burn. It's at a medium level in nicotine. It's a record aimed at smokers wanting to avoid heavy aromatics but finding fully unflavored blends flat, particularly those looking for an everyday Burley. The brand isn't in operation today.
hearth-home-sycaway.o: Leaves an aroma of toasted nut and dry bread crust.

cornell-diehl-red-virginia-ribbon.z: Red Virginia Ribbon is a single-varietal product in which Cornell & Diehl presents high-grade Old Belt red Virginia leaf in an easy-lighting ribbon cut. It carries no casing; the leaf's natural sweetness is the blend's sole character source. The maker states the product can be smoked straight from the pack and is also well suited to aging; red Virginia's sugar load gives a flavor that deepens over time. On the maker's scale, strength, flavor, and room note are medium. Suited as a base leaf for those wanting to smoke pure Virginia and for smokers building their own blends.
cornell-diehl-red-virginia-ribbon.o: Leaves a sweetish tobacco scent dominated by dry hay and honey tones.

holts-cigar-company-trafalgar.z: This is an English mixture prepared for the Philadelphia-based Holt's Cigar Company, reportedly containing Virginia, Turkish tobacco, fire-cured Cavendish, and Latakia; no sufficient independent source verifying the blend's details could be found.

bufflehead-old-squaw.z: Bufflehead was a brand producing small batches in the United States in the early 2000s, naming its blends after waterfowl; since no independent source describing this blend's content and character could be found, the entry has been left incomplete.

mcclelland-yenice-agonya.z: Yenice Agonya belongs to McClelland's Grand Orientals series, which spotlights individual Oriental varieties. It takes its name from the Agonya variety grown in the Marmara region, considered a continuation of the Xanthi seed stock; in this blend, the Turkish tobacco is joined by matured Virginia, with no Latakia. The whole series was discontinued when the company closed in 2018. The Oriental and Virginia play off each other in a sweet-tart balance; the body is lightly spiced, with floral and herbal notes standing out. The smoke is mild, though the nicotine load isn't negligible. Suited to those wanting to get to know Latakia-free Oriental character in its plain form.
mcclelland-yenice-agonya.o: Leaves a spicy aroma reminiscent of dry hay and incense, with floral edges.

park-lane-tobacconist-english-cherry.z: One of Park-Lane Tobacconist's cherry-flavored house blends; no usable source describing its composition and character could be found.

panama-jack-daiquiri.z: Daiquiri is one of the aromatic blends in the tropically themed pipe tobacco line from Panama Jack, a brand identified with beach culture. The structure common to the line is a light body built from mild burley and bright Virginia with black cavendish added; it is ribbon cut and sold in fifty-gram tins. Taking its cue from the cocktail it's named for, it's given a rum-and-lime-direction flavoring. Nicotine load is low and the smoke cool and sweet; the leaf taste stays in the background, with the fruity flavoring as the leading element up front. It's a blend built for those just getting acquainted with aromatic tobacco, or those wanting to start the day with a light, sugary smoke.
panama-jack-daiquiri.o: Leaves a sugary coolness with sweet rum and crushed lime aromas.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-safari.z: Safari is one of the historic blends Wilke produced for Abercrombie & Fitch, and it continues today in bulk under the same recipe. According to the maker's description, Tennessee Burley cube cut is joined by Virginia and Maryland Burley, topped with a generous layer of Latakia. The cube cut brings out Burley's nutty, earthy side with a slow burn. It's an unflavored record; flavor intensity comes from the Latakia, and body from the Burley. It suits smokers who want an American-style Burley base paired with Latakia smoke. Wilke offers this blend in its non-aromatic bulk listing, and its stock status varies.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-safari.o: A roasted-nut tone mixes into a dense wood-smoke scent.

g-l-pease-gaslight.z: Gaslight is a dark, full-bodied blend in G. L. Pease's Old London Series line. Red Virginia leaves build a base of natural sweetness; Oriental leaves add measured spice, and Cyprus latakia sits along the blend's smoky axis. It is a slow-burning mixture whose flavour deepens as it progresses. It is prepared for smokers accustomed to classic English mixtures with a high Latakia proportion, who are looking for a full-bodied, smoky smoke.
g-l-pease-gaslight.o: Leaves a sweetish leaf aroma beneath heavy woodsmoke and smokiness.

davidoff-oriental-mixture.z: This is a Davidoff blend noted as oriental-leaf-forward; not enough sourcing could be reached to verify its composition and character.

emerson-southern-forged-shandwick.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing was found for the Emerson Southern Forged brand's Shandwick blend, so the entry has been left open; records place it in the Straight Virginia family.

levin-pipes-international-sophisticate.z: Sophisticate is a Virginia-forward blend McClelland produced for Levin Pipes International; production has stopped, and records indicate the recipe was later carried on in McClelland's own CORPS series, but not enough sources could be found for its composition.
levin-pipes-international-sophisticate.o: Leaves a light room note reminiscent of dry hay and honey.

the-storytellers-pipe-shop-sweet-galenas.z: Sweet Galenas is a house blend from The Story Teller's Pipe Shop referencing Tolkien's Middle-earth. Its name comes from galenas, the word hobbits use for "pipeweed." According to the maker, the blend was developed to recreate the taste of the discontinued Tewksbury Hobbit's Weed, but in a more balanced form with reduced risk of tongue bite. Its composition includes sweet black Cavendish, Burley and Virginia; it is cased with a flavoring carrying vanilla, cherry, cocoa and liqueur notes and sold ribbon cut. Strength and flavor are light to medium, making it suited to long sittings and daytime smoking. The casing is distinctly upfront; it is aimed at smokers after a profile driven by the flavoring rather than the tobacco itself, those new to the pipe, or anyone wanting to leave a sweet scent for people nearby. Sold loose by the ounce.
the-storytellers-pipe-shop-sweet-galenas.o: Gives an intense, sugary aroma where vanilla, cherry and cocoa sweetness leaves a liqueur-like trace.

astleys-no-109-medium-flake.z: Astley's No.109 Medium Flake is a fully matured flake tobacco obtained by pressing and slicing quality flame-cured Virginia leaf. The tin's contents arrive quite moist; records note it needs thorough airing before smoking, or it will need frequent relighting. The flakes are easy to prepare and burn evenly. Flavoring is nearly imperceptibly light, serving mostly to soften the room note. In the smoke, dry hay, citrus, and bready sweetness stand out; deeper in, a tone close to nutty chocolate and light fruity notes appear. Since nicotine and body stay low, it suits morning smokes and those looking for a mature, light Virginia.
astleys-no-109-medium-flake.o: Leaves a sweetish room note leaning toward warm dry hay and baked dough.

thepiperoom-com-paisley.z: No source describing the composition or character of Paisley, one of ThePipeRoom.com's house blends, has been found.
thepiperoom-com-paisley.o: Records describe it as leaving a neutral, tobacco-like aroma.

missouri-meerschaum-150th-anniversary.z: 150th Anniversary is a limited-production blend Missouri Meerschaum, known for its corn cob pipes, had prepared for the company's 150th founding anniversary. Select virginia and burley tobaccos from various regions of the world are joined by a soft, virginia-based black cavendish, with a small amount of vanilla applied before pressing. The blend is presented in rubbable crumble-cake form; it is rubbed apart by hand before smoking. Because the casing level is kept low, the tobacco's own sweetness leads, placing it closer to lightly flavored American mixtures than to intense aromatics.
missouri-meerschaum-150th-anniversary.o: Leaves a lightly vanilla-scented, sweetish, bready aroma.

hu-tobacco-nebari.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for the Nebari blend under the HU Tobacco name, so its content and character could not be recorded.

e-a-carey-grandmas-apple-pie.z: Grandma's Apple Pie is E. A. Carey's aromatic flavored to evoke apple pie. Per the maker's description, Green River district leaf forms the blend's backbone, and its body is somewhat fuller than the brand's Classic Black Aromatic. The topping is pronounced; a baked-apple and sweet-dough direction stands out both in taste and in the room's scent. It stays below medium in nicotine. It is built for smokers who enjoy pronounced fruity aromatics. The blend was in the Carey catalog for a long time but does not appear in current listings.
e-a-carey-grandmas-apple-pie.o: Leaves a scent of fresh-from-the-oven apple pie dough and baked apple.

craftsman-mixture-supreme.z: Recorded as a mixture sold under the Craftsman name; no source describing its composition and character was found.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-kings-hig.z: King's Highway, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as a Virginia-forward mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

charles-fairmorn-sundowner-mixture.z: Sundowner Mixture is an unflavored classic English mixture. According to records its composition is five parts light Virginia, three parts Latakia, one part black Cavendish and two parts specially matured leaf. The tart, cooked-fruit-like taste of mature Virginia meets the smoke of Cyprus Latakia; black Cavendish inserts a brief sweetness in between. The body sits between medium and full, with different flavors taking turns coming forward through the smoke. The blend is offered under the German firm Charles Fairmorn, whose origins trace to the Lübeck tobacco trade. A record aimed at those seeking English mixtures that use Latakia as a balancing rather than dominating component, and who want a structure suited to tin aging.
charles-fairmorn-sundowner-mixture.o: Beneath the smoke and wood aroma, a cooked-fruit sweetness from mature Virginia can be sensed.

vegassmokes-browns-extra.z: An aromatic mixture from the small-scale blender VegasSmokes; no independent source documenting its composition and character has been found.

royal-navy-pipe-tobacco.z: No sufficient source could be found for this pipe tobacco sold under the Royal Navy name, according to records straight-Virginia in character.

gawith-hoggarth-co-jubilee-blend.z: Jubilee Blend is a hand-blended Virginia-Burley mixture prepared for the 70th anniversary of Queen Elizabeth II's accession to the throne. Light yellow and darker Virginia leaves are combined with some Burley; the cut is an even, light-brown ribbon. On the smoke, Virginia sweetness evoking honey and dry hay stands out along with a light citrus sharpness; Burley lays a dry, chocolate-and-peanut-butter-leaning body underneath. Being unflavored, it's suited to smokers seeking tobacco taste who want a medium-bodied mixture for all-day smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-jubilee-blend.o: Leaves a lightly nutty trace with a dry-hay and baked-bread aroma.

cornell-diehl-after-eight.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Cornell & Diehl blend After Eight.

mcclelland-no-5115-old-world-classic-cak.z: No. 5115 Old World Classic Cake is a Virginia blend in McClelland's bulk series prepared in a matured-cake style. Per the maker's description, it's made from select lemon and orange-red Virginias, enriched with natural fruit essences. In this respect it isn't a fully unflavored Virginia but rather a lightly touched middle ground. Its taste is lightly sweet, full, and mild; the fruit essence forms a lively edge without overshadowing the tobacco. Nicotine dose is moderate. A middle option for smokers who keep their distance from heavily flavored tobaccos but also find unflavored Virginia too plain. Production ended when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-no-5115-old-world-classic-cak.o: Leaves a light aroma combining sweet fruit and matured Virginia tobacco.

bufflehead-surf-scooter.z: Bufflehead was a brand producing small batches in the United States in the early 2000s, naming its blends after waterfowl; since no independent source describing this blend's content and character could be found, the entry has been left incomplete.

cornell-diehl-purple-cow.z: Purple Cow is a mixture Cornell & Diehl blender Bob Runowski prepared for the Chicagoland pipe show. Per the maker's listing, Latakia and maduro cigar leaf are used alongside Burleys and bright Virginia ribbon. The cigar leaf adds a dark, earthy, peppery layer not often found in pipe tobaccos. Latakia builds a smoky background while Burley provides a cool body, and Virginia brings a measured sweetness. Nicotine sits in the medium band. Suited to smokers curious about pipe blends containing cigar leaf who aren't unfamiliar with Latakia mixtures.
cornell-diehl-purple-cow.o: Leaves a dark, earthy scent from cigar leaf mingled with a light smoky note.

mac-baren-amphora-special-reserve-no-2.z: Amphora Special Reserve No.2 belongs to the Special Reserve line, positioned as the higher-tier segment within Amphora. Per the manufacturer's description, Virginia, burley and cavendish leaves from three continents are blended and presented as a loose cut, which eases both packing and burn. Amphora is a Dutch-rooted brand, produced at Mac Baren's facilities in Denmark. The inclusion of cavendish pulls the blend toward the sweet side; Virginia builds a sugary base while burley adds body and dryness. Casing is measured, kept at a level that doesn't mask the tobacco taste. It sits in the light-to-medium band for nicotine. Suited to those avoiding heavily flavored products but still wanting a sweet smoke, and to smokers in their early years with the pipe.
mac-baren-amphora-special-reserve-no-2.o: Leaves a sweet room note toward light caramel and cooked fruit.

hearth-home-red-eye.z: Red Eye is Hearth & Home's first spun-cut blend. On opening the tin, coin-shaped slices are seen with fire-cured dark leaf at the center; matured Virginia and a considerable proportion of Perique wrap around this core. It takes its name from this eye-like cross-section as well. The smoky leaf at the roll's center and the sweet-spicy structure of the outer ring burn together with every draw; the taste swings between dried fruit and pepper. The slices are rubbed out by hand before filling. It suits those accustomed to Perique-heavy blends and looking for a full-bodied smoke.
hearth-home-red-eye.o: Leaves a tobacco aroma evoking smoke, dried plum, and pepper.

hearth-home-prince-andrew.z: Prince Andrew is a Burley-forward, lightly topped blend in the brand's Mid-Town series. Its flavor axis carries cocoa and nutty notes; the smoke is cool and doesn't bite the tongue. It is ribbon cut and built to be light enough for all-day smoking. The blend is positioned as an affordable counterpart to classic American Burley tin tobaccos; creamy softness, a lightly toasted edge, and a background hint of chocolate are the hallmarks of this style. Aimed at smokers looking for an unpretentious everyday tobacco that sits somewhere between unflavored Burley and an aromatic.
hearth-home-prince-andrew.o: Leaves a roasted-hazelnut and light-cocoa aroma.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-fraser.z: A blend appearing in the Orlik Tobacco Company A/S catalog, noted as burley-forward; no independent source confirming its composition could be found.

deans-full-flavor.z: Dean's is an economical pipe tobacco brand produced under the Ohserase Manufacturing umbrella in the US and sold in large-gram bags. Full Flavor is the brand's variant prepared ribbon cut from Virginia and burley leaves, adjusted for a fuller taste. It's a product made for everyday smoking, not aimed at a complex blend structure; due to its large-volume packaging it appeals to heavy smokers mindful of cost. The cut and moisture level are kept in the usual moist-to-medium range for bagged tobaccos.
deans-full-flavor.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay and nutty tobacco.

ravenwood-fine-provisions-gates-of-argon.z: Gates of Argonath is the Balkan-style entry in the Ravenwood Fine Provisions line. The blender describes it as a full-bodied English-Balkan mixture; the Oriental leaf share is kept high, building a dark profile together with Latakia. The flavor description lists woody Orientals, dark bread, and damp earth notes; in some bowls a natural sweetness reminiscent of gingerbread can also be noticed. No flavoring is applied. The room note is strong and Latakia's smoke permeates the space. It suits smokers used to dark, full, spicy blends who steer clear of aromatics.
ravenwood-fine-provisions-gates-of-argon.o: Leaves an intense Latakia smoke aroma with dark bread and damp earth.

g-l-pease-geometrie.z: Géométrie is the second entry in G. L. Pease's Zeitgeist series, reinterpreting the traditional Virginia-Oriental mould. Aged red Virginia leaves are layered with old-stock Basma and Izmir leaves; the blend is pressed and presented in plug form, and the smoker cuts or rubs out their own slice. Because the plug form lets the leaves fuse together, the flavour feels settled even straight from the tin: malt sweetness, fine spice, and a light floral sharpness sit together. The same form also lends itself to long-term ageing; sources note the sweetness becomes more pronounced over the years. It suits smokers familiar with untopped Virginia-Oriental blends and preparing plug tobacco.
g-l-pease-geometrie.o: Leaves an aroma of freshly baked bread and light floral spice.

amphora-mellow-blend.z: Amphora Mellow Blend is the mint-flavored ribbon-cut blend in the Amphora line. Its flavoring is used very sparingly; it doesn't give the coolness of menthol cigarettes and doesn't override the tobacco's own taste. It contains Burley, Kentucky, Oriental/Turkish tobacco, and Virginia. In the smoke, the Turkish tobacco and its accompanying Kentucky flavor can be followed to the end; Burley comes forward at the finish. Strength and flavor intensity are medium. It suits smokers looking for an aromatic they can smoke all day, with flavoring that stays barely perceptible.
amphora-mellow-blend.o: Leaves a predominantly tobacco room note carrying a cooling hint of mint.

lane-limited-captain-black-copper.z: Captain Black Copper is an aromatic blend tied to Lane Limited's Captain Black series; not enough sources could be found to describe its content and character in detail.
lane-limited-captain-black-copper.o: Reportedly leaves a sweet cavendish room note.

pipe-republic-viking-bay.z: No reliable sources on Pipe Republic's blend Viking Bay could be found, so its content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

mostex-stanislaw-atlantic-cruise-mixture.z: No independent, verifiable source describing the composition of this blend, released under the Stanislaw brand of the Brno-based maker Mostex, could be found.

peretti-devonshire.z: Devonshire is a blend that has long been part of L.J. Peretti's English-style line. Per the maker's account, only a pinch of Latakia is added on top of aged Virginia leaf; rather than driving the blend, Latakia gives it a light smoky edge. This construction produces an unflavored, measured English blend that keeps Virginia's bready sweetness at the center. It suits smokers who want to avoid heavy Latakia loads and are seeking a mild entry point into English-style tobacco. Being ribbon cut, it requires no preparation.
peretti-devonshire.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, hay-like aroma mixed into a light smoky wood scent.

motzek-dark-matter.z: Since neither the manufacturer's own description nor two independent reliable sources could be found for the Motzek blend called Dark Matter, its composition, cut, and character could not be documented here.

butera-kingfisher.z: Kingfisher is a blend prepared under the Michael Butera name and, per records, manufactured by J. F. Germain & Son in the 2010s. Lemon-yellow virginia, burley and perique are layered as whole leaf and pressed in cake form; after maturing they are cut and brought to ribbon form, then pressed a second time — a method the manufacturer calls double cut. A nutty base from the burley comes forward in the flavor; virginia's sweetness and perique's peppery touch sit on this base. The body is medium. Suitable for smokers seeking a Virginia-Burley-axis blend carrying perique at a non-dominant level.
butera-kingfisher.o: Leaves a toasted walnut, dried fruit and light pepper aroma.

dan-tobacco-michael-apitz-den-danske-dro.z: A blend in Dan Tobacco's Michael Apitz-signed series, said to be Cavendish-heavy; no adequate source on its composition or character was found.
dan-tobacco-michael-apitz-den-danske-dro.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

mac-baren-sweet-cherry.z: Remembered as a cherry-flavored Mac Baren blend; since no independent source documenting this specific name, distinct from the brand's other cherry-flavored blends, could be found, the record is left incomplete.
mac-baren-sweet-cherry.o: Said to leave a ripe-cherry aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-rich-dark-honeydew.z: Rich Dark Honeydew is a lively aromatic where an essence on the maple-and-honeydew-melon line is added to the natural sweetness of mature Virginia and Burley leaf. It also carries a fine floral trace from the house's Lakeland tradition. It's ribbon cut and arrives moist; airing before smoking is common. The taste runs sweet and syrupy, with the leaf's own body staying in the background. Nicotine is moderate. Suited to those wanting a pronounced sweet essence in an aromatic that isn't all-sugar.
gawith-hoggarth-co-rich-dark-honeydew.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of honey and maple syrup, carrying a light floral trace behind it.

cornell-diehl-three-friars.z: Three Friars is an unflavored mixture made of a trio of ribbon-cut Virginia, brown Burley, and Perique. Records indicate the recipe was built following in the footsteps of the classic Three Nuns blend, sitting somewhere between that blend's old and new compositions. Virginia carries natural sweetness, Perique adds a plummy, peppery sharpness, and dark Burley builds an earthy, spicy body. It carries no casing, following a balanced line between sweetness and spice. Suited to those looking for an unflavored, medium-bodied everyday blend.
cornell-diehl-three-friars.o: Leaves a spicy tobacco scent carrying sweet-hay and dried-fruit tones.

watch-city-cigar-deep-elem.z: This is one of the house blends of the Watch City Cigar shop; it does not appear in the current catalog, and no source could be found documenting its composition.

sutliff-tobacco-company-peaches-and-crem.z: Peaches and Crème, coded D52, is one of the fruity members of Sutliff's bulk aromatic line. Peach and cream essences are drawn into a ribbon-cut base of burley, Virginia, and flavored black cavendish leaf. The peach note is clear enough to make itself known, yet measured enough not to tire the palate; the creamy layer rounds out the sweetness. Nicotine is light, at an intensity that can be smoked throughout the day. It falls within the interest of those looking for a soft, fruit-forward aromatic.
sutliff-tobacco-company-peaches-and-crem.o: Leaves a scent of ripe peach and dairy cream.

sutliff-tobacco-company-burley-201-6.z: A record coded among Sutliff's bulk burley base tobaccos; sufficient independent sources giving its processing and composition details could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-burley-201-6.o: Records indicate it leaves a plain scent reminiscent of dry cocoa and walnut shell.

kaptn-brammers-klabautermann.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Kapt'n Brammers' Klabautermann blend.

samuel-gawith-amaretto.z: No sufficient source could be found for this bulk aromatic from Samuel Gawith, understood from its name to contain amaretto casing.

w-o-larsen-selected-blend-no-20-broad-cu.z: W.Ø. Larsen Selected Blend No. 20 is the broad-cut member of the brand's numbered Selected Blend series. Fully matured Virginia leaves build the blend's body; roasted black cavendish and a small amount of Latakia are added. The cut is kept broad, similar to No. 50, but this version has a higher share of dark leaves. The series generally uses leaves of Malawian, Brazilian, and Mexican origin. The Latakia amount isn't enough to make the blend an English mixture; it only leaves a lightly smoky, spicy line over the Virginia sweetness. Nicotine stays below medium, and the flavor is rounded out by the cavendish. It suits those seeking an unflavored or very lightly cased, Virginia-forward tobacco that isn't entirely plain; because of the broad cut, the leaves need to be rubbed out a bit before packing.
w-o-larsen-selected-blend-no-20-broad-cu.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay and bread crust carrying a lightly smoky trace.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-magnum-blend.z: Magnum Blend is a blend Boswell prepared for a friend who wanted a light-bodied English blend. The Latakia proportion is kept low; the smoke stays in the background between the Virginias' sweetness and the Oriental leaf's dry spice. This structure makes the blend an English option that can be smoked all day. Boswell is a family business that prepares its blends in its own shop in Chambersburg, Pennsylvania. This blend suits those newly discovering Latakia or seeking a measured smoke instead of the intensity of heavy English blends.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-magnum-blend.o: Leaves a lightly smoky wood and dry-leaf aroma.

hearth-home-anniversary-flake.z: Anniversary Flake is the Hearth & Home series' pressed Virginia-Perique blend. Its composition includes Virginia leaves of varying color and maturity along with top-grade Perique. A small amount of rum is added before the tobacco is pressed; during pressing, the leaves meld together and the flavors mature. The resulting slab is suited to being rubbed out by hand or packed folded. On the smoke, the Virginias' bready, fruity sweetness leads; Perique adds a depth of dried plum, fig, and pepper to that sweetness. The rum addition isn't dominant enough to place the blend in the aromatic category — it functions more as a top note tying the leaf flavors together. Suited to smokers who love the pressed VaPer style and want a slow, even smoke.
hearth-home-anniversary-flake.o: Dried-fruit and rum sweetness mingles with a baked-bread aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-black-cavendis.z: Kendal Black Cavendish is a ribbon-cut tobacco made of double-fermented Cavendish leaf, darkened through steaming and pressing. During the process, the leaf's own sugar caramelizes, giving it a sweet character even without added flavoring. The smoke is cool and mild, nicotine is low. It can be smoked on its own, or used by smokers building their own blends as a base tobacco to soften and sweeten Virginia- or Latakia-forward mixtures. A low-strength option for beginners.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-black-cavendis.o: Leaves a lightly toasted sugar and dried-fruit aroma.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-john-cottons-m.z: John Cotton's is a historic English-Scottish brand tracing back to Edinburgh; its No. 1 blend was reinterpreted and brought back to market after the brand had been discontinued. It contains matured bright Virginia, small-leaf select oriental, and Cyprian latakia; no flavoring is applied. The blend is built as a light, cool English mixture: Virginia and oriental sit at nearly equal weight, while latakia serves a constantly felt but non-dominant woody, smoky, spicy role. Nicotine and taste are moderate. It's aimed at those seeking a measured entry into latakia blends, and those wanting an all-day option instead of a heavy English mixture.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-john-cottons-m.o: Leaves a woody, lightly smoky scent together with a dry-grass aroma.

uptowns-smoke-shop-monticello.z: A house blend from Nashville's Uptown's Smoke Shop noted for its Virginia-Perique structure; since the shop has closed it is off the market, and no source confirming its proportions has been found.

peterson-summertime-2018.z: Summertime 2018 is that year's entry in the limited-production series the Irish brand Peterson releases each summer with a distinct composition. Peterson's pipe tobaccos have since the 2010s been produced in Germany by a blender working on the brand's behalf; the country of origin on the label nonetheless remains Ireland, the brand's home country. The core of the 2018 edition is Brazilian-sourced, light-colored, loose-cut Virginia leaf, joined by black Cavendish, rounded out with a light vanilla-and-caramel-leaning flavoring. Its character is a light-bodied, sweet-leaning aromatic; nicotine strength is low and the smoke texture is creamy. The Virginia's natural sugar isn't masked by the topping, while the Cavendish adds depth and softness to the body. It suits smokers wanting a light aromatic for long summer sessions and those looking to transition from aromatics toward natural tobaccos. Being a limited production, it was distributed only for that season and then pulled from shelves.
peterson-summertime-2018.o: Leaves a sweet, soft aroma dominated by vanilla and sugared caramel.

tinder-box-burley-light-without-a-bite.z: Tinder Box is the name of an American tobacconist chain founded in 1928 that sells blends prepared for its own shops under its own name; Burley Light Without A Bite is one of these house blends, though no sufficient independent source describing its composition and character has been found.

mac-baren-hh-acadian-perique.z: HH Acadian Perique belongs to Mac Baren's HH line, which carries no applied top casing. The blend contains Virginia, burley, the brand's signature cavendish, dark fire-cured Kentucky and oriental leaves; the Acadian perique that gives it its name is used in a notable proportion. The perique adds a plum and spice dimension, while the Kentucky lends a smoky depth. The ribbon cut makes packing easy. It sits above medium in nicotine and flavor; aimed at experienced smokers seeking an unflavored, spicy Virginia-perique profile.
mac-baren-hh-acadian-perique.o: Leaves a spicy note of light smoke and dried fig.

wessex-sovereign-curly-cut.z: The Brigade line's Sovereign Curly Cut is made by rolling Virginia and Perique leaves into a cylinder and slicing them into thin coin-shaped discs, a construction close to the classic Three Nuns style. Since the discs are loose, part of the tin's contents may come apart, and the moisture level is suited to filling straight from the tin. A light cider-based casing is applied to the blend; as a result, the first third of the smoke is described as having a sharp, biting alcohol-driven phase, after which Virginia's dough-like sweetness and Perique's steady spice note come forward. It's aimed at smokers open to a cased Virginia/Perique and coin preparation.
wessex-sovereign-curly-cut.o: A sweet, dough-like tobacco scent accompanies a light apple-fruit note.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore-ar.z: Finamore Aromatic is the flavored version of the Finamore line, produced at Tabacos Cisne Branco Finamore's Juiz de Fora facility. Like the brand's other products, the body is built on Burley and Virginia leaf, prepared with flavoring and casing agents added on top. Nicotine is low and the smoke is mild; the sweet flavoring leads while the tobacco's own taste stays in the background. It is an option for smokers who find the plain Finamore Tradicional too austere and want the same body in a flavored form.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore-ar.o: Leaves a sweet scent reminiscent of light candy.

pipesandcigars-com-pirates-cove.z: Pirate's Cove is one of the blends the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com sells under its own name; there is not enough independent source material documenting its content and character.

cornell-diehl-orthodoxy.z: A blend, no longer in Cornell & Diehl's current catalogue, referred to as English style; no adequate source documenting its ratios and character was found.
cornell-diehl-orthodoxy.o: No adequate information for a description could be found in records.

a-c-petersen-dukes-mixture.z: No adequate source describing the content and character of A & C Petersen's blend called Duke's Mixture could be found.

stone-pine-tobacco-company-seven-veils.z: One of the blends from Stone Pine Tobacco Company; no verifiable source describing its composition and character could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-nut-brown-burley.z: No sufficient source could be found documenting the composition and character of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Nut Brown Burley.

king-street-coffee-tobacco-emporium-vani.z: A house blend King Street Emporium sells as vanilla flavored; no accessible source could be found regarding its base leaves and cut.
king-street-coffee-tobacco-emporium-vani.o: As the name suggests, it leaves a vanilla scent; the detail could not be confirmed.

john-aylesbury-general-1776-flake.z: John Aylesbury General 1776 Flake is recorded as a pressed flake built on Virginia and Perique; since it doesn't appear in the maker's current listing, no verifiable source could be found on its composition and character.

dunhill-my-mixture-620.z: A blend tied to Dunhill's My Mixture line, not currently in production; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found, so a detailed record couldn't be compiled.
dunhill-my-mixture-620.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

james-barber-jamess-blend.z: An aromatic house blend from James Barber's tobacconist named after the founder; not enough sources could be found on its composition.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-royal-scot.z: Royal Scot is a mixture Wilke Pipe Tobacco produces to its own recipe and uses as a flavoring leaf in many of its blends. According to the maker's account, it's composed of pressed Virginia, North Carolina leaf, and Burley, carrying a distinctive sweetness set apart from the usual aromatics. The blend can be smoked on its own, or used as an additive leaf to enrich a smoker's own mixture. Because of this dual function, it's a record aimed at smokers experimenting with blending as well as those seeking a lightly sweet, measured aromatic base. It also appears as a component in Wilke's classic recipes such as No. 13 and No. 24.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-royal-scot.o: Leaves a mild scent, lightly sweet and reminiscent of dried fruit.

ken-byron-ventures-deep-house.z: Deep House is an aromatic built on scented golden and black Cavendish and earthy dark Virginia leaf. A small amount of Burley and bright Virginia round out the mixture as supporting players, over which a classic-style casing carrying vanilla and chocolate notes is applied. The maker describes it as a more polished take on the dark, scented house blends tobacconists have long sold.
ken-byron-ventures-deep-house.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and cocoa aroma.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-colts-bri.z: Colts is Scandinavian Tobacco Group's pouch-tobacco line for the Canadian market. Bright Virginia is a fine ribbon-cut blend forward with light golden Virginia leaf, joined by mild burley and a small amount of Oriental. No further flavoring is added on top; the sweetness comes from the leaf itself and leaves a fine sugar tone evoking honey and vanilla. Nicotine and flavor intensity are measured; suited to pipe newcomers seeking an unflavored but not harsh daily blend.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-colts-bri.o: Leaves a fine tobacco scent of dry hay with light honey sweetness.

tabac-turc-yayladag-visneli.z: Yayladağ Vişneli (Cherry) is one of Tabac Turc's fruit-flavored domestic blends. According to records, its composition is roughly 40 percent Yayladağı, 24 percent Bitlis, 12 percent İzmir, and 24 percent imported smoky tobacco; the casing and flavoring elements include cherry, honey, molasses, maple, rum, and trace amounts of latakia and cavendish. It is packed as broken flake, moist. On first opening the pack, a sharp fruity scent reminiscent of fermentation is noticeable; airing is needed to let this dissipate. Despite its moist state, it lights easily and leaves fine white ash. The blend has a high proportion of woody stem and needs picking over before packing. On the smoke, a bitterish spice taste stands out; the earthy aftertaste typical of Türk Pipo Tütünü and other Yayladağ products is also present here. It is light in nicotine and medium in taste. It is a blend for those wanting to try flavored domestic tobaccos and the combination of Oriental leaf with fruit casing.
tabac-turc-yayladag-visneli.o: Leaves a sharp, sweet-tart cherry scent reminiscent of fermented fruit juice alongside the tobacco scent.

samuel-gawith-sevilla-2012.z: According to records, a limited-run Samuel Gawith product prepared for a slow-smoking event held in Seville; no sufficient independent source describing its content could be found.
samuel-gawith-sevilla-2012.o: No reliable description of its scent could be found.

brigadier-black-antietam.z: Antietam is a later addition to the Brigadier Black line, an aromatic based entirely on black cavendish. A measured black-cherry casing is applied over the dark-colored but soft-textured cavendish leaf. Since cavendish's own sugary sweetness works in the same direction as the cherry casing, a fruity, sweet line is maintained throughout the smoke; nicotine is low and tongue bite is minimal. Being a high-moisture leaf, it calls for a slow smoke at low heat. A record aimed at those seeking an intense profile within the fruity aromatic lane and wanting a low-nicotine everyday blend.
brigadier-black-antietam.o: Leaves a dark, fruity aroma reminiscent of ripe black cherry syrup.

j-f-germain-son-plum-cake-mixture.z: Plum Cake Mixture is a ribbon-cut blend from J. F. Germain & Son's lightly aromatic line. Per the maker's description, six separate Virginia grades are combined with black Cavendish, and the mixture is flavored with a wine-and-spice recipe said to be eighty years old. It takes its name from the spiced fruit cake of English cuisine. The flavoring is noticeable, but not heavy enough to mask the Virginia's sweetness; the Cavendish establishes a soft, full base. Nicotine is on the light side. It's aimed at smokers who avoid heavily syrupy aromatics and want a measured, spiced-fruity flavoring.
j-f-germain-son-plum-cake-mixture.o: Leaves a sweet trace reminiscent of spiced fruit cake and wine.

motzek-black-gold-crumble.z: Since neither the manufacturer's own description nor two independent reliable sources could be found for the Motzek blend called Black Gold Crumble, its composition, cut, and character could not be documented here.

upshall-upshall-english-latakia.z: A Latakia-forward English mixture sold under the Upshall name; since no source confirming the blend's leaf composition and maker has been found, the record is left incomplete.

david-cigarpipe-summer-cottage.z: No adequate sources were found documenting the composition or character of the David CigarPipe Summer Cottage blend.

pcca-hairy-larry.z: A blend produced by McClelland within the PCCA club series, found today only in collectors' tins; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-uno.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Sutliff Tobacco Company's Uno pipe tobacco could be found.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-treasure-.z: Treasure Island is an aromatic carrying a spiced rum casing over a Virginia and Cavendish base. The Virginia leaf sets a lightly grassy base, and the Cavendish adds a brown-sugar sweetness; the rum casing joins that sweetness. The casing isn't heavy enough to overpower the leaf's taste, and the spice side stays mild. Nicotine is low, with no harsh or sharp notes reported. A blend suited to a wide range of smokers, including newcomers to the pipe, who want a rum-flavored, light and mellow aromatic.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-treasure-.o: Leaves a scent of spiced rum and brown sugar.

motzek-plug-no-2.z: Plug No. 2 is a product from the pressed-tobacco line of the Motzek workshop, founded in Kiel. It is a plug in which Virginia leaves are combined with black cavendish, honey is added, and the mixture is blocked under pressure, then sliced and cut into cubes before smoking. It is presented as a firmly pressed brick; it needs to be sliced with a sharp knife and, if necessary, allowed to lose some moisture. In character it is a blend that carries no artificial flavoring and stays on the natural-tobacco side: Virginia's bready sweetness leads, cavendish adds softness and darkness, and the honey rounds out the sweetness. Strength sits in the light-to-medium band, it burns clean and leaves little residue. A fitting starting point for smokers wanting to get to know the plug format, or considering moving from flavored tobaccos to natural virginia blends. The Motzek workshop passed to Tom Darasz after Herbert Motzek's retirement, and its products have since come to be known under the name TAK (Tabak aus Kiel).
motzek-plug-no-2.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, plain-burning tobacco aroma.

clan-shaw-windjammer.z: No reliable, independent sourcing could be found regarding Clan Shaw Windjammer, so a detailed profile could not be compiled.

gq-tobaccos-breakfast-blend.z: Breakfast Blend is one of the house blends from Nottingham-based English house GQ Tobaccos. Izmir-origin Turkish tobacco forms the backbone; a woody, smoky, sourish tang is the blend's most pronounced line. Alongside it comes nutty, naturally sweet Burley and gold- and mahogany-colored Virginia leaf. The Virginia side carries a bready, lightly herbal, earthy sweetness, topped with a sharpness reminiscent of citrus and vinegar. The maple topping applied over it is subtle — it doesn't mask the leaves' own taste and doesn't leave a pronounced sweet-pancake effect on the palate. In character, the first third starts out calm, and as the bowl progresses the layers open up and the peppery spice note common in GQ blends comes forward. Suited to those seeking blends with a topping present but not tipping into aromatic territory, where leaf taste dominates; it is not a starting blend for smokers unaccustomed to the sour-smoky side of Oriental tobacco. Since nicotine sits at a moderate level, it's a blend meant more for a particular bowl than for all-day smoking.
gq-tobaccos-breakfast-blend.o: A bready sweetness and a faint maple trace mingle with the woody, lightly smoky aroma of Turkish tobacco.

watch-city-cigar-old-dominion.z: No sufficient source could be found regarding this house blend from Watch City Cigar, so its details could not be recorded.

de-la-concha-classic-burley.z: This is referred to as the De La Concha tobacconist's burley-forward shop blend; no independent source giving a detailed profile could be found.
de-la-concha-classic-burley.o: No reliable record could be found for the room note.

kontor-tabak-no-6.z: Kontor-Tabak No. 6 is Tabak-Kontor's Oriental-tobacco-forward blend. Per the manufacturer's recipe, a floral Turkish oriental forms the blend's backbone; matured, sweetish broken Virginia, citrus-noted golden Virginia and a nutty Burley accompany it. Since it contains no latakia, its character is not smoky but dry, grassy and spicy. Its medium-strength smoke suits those seeking Oriental tobacco taste without the smoke load of English blends. Being a natural, unflavored record, flavor intensity comes from the tobacco's own spice; a balanced option for everyday smoking.
kontor-tabak-no-6.o: A light citrus peel and nutty tone mixes into the dry-hay and spice scent.

gawith-hoggarth-co-mellow-mahogany-flake.z: Mellow Mahogany Flake is a blend offered as broken flake, obtained by slicing dark mahogany-toned Virginia leaf under pressure. Records indicate it rests on the same leaf base as the brand's No. 7 Broken Flake product. Dried fruit, bread, and a measured woody depth stand out on the flavor palette; the smoky harshness of fire-cured leaf is restrained here. Suited to smokers seeking dark Virginia taste without heavy Lakeland toppings.
gawith-hoggarth-co-mellow-mahogany-flake.o: Leaves a measured tobacco aroma leaning toward dried fruit and wood.

samuel-gawith-best-brown-plug.z: Samuel Gawith is a longstanding tobacco house that has produced in the English town of Kendal since 1792. Best Brown Plug is the pressed plug-format member of the house's Best Brown family: it consists solely of Virginia leaf, with no sweetener or flavoring added, its sweetness coming from the leaf's own sugar. In this respect it is counted among the most unflavored Virginias produced in the United Kingdom. On the smoke, a light peppery sharpness comes forward along with dried fig, brown sugar, and a nutty core taste in the background. Nicotine stays between light and medium; flavor intensity, however, is high. Since it comes in plug form, it is packed by slicing and rubbing, or by folding after drying somewhat; since moisture is high, a slow smoking pace is needed to avoid tongue bite. Suited to smokers seeking unflavored Virginia character and the intensity pressing brings.
samuel-gawith-best-brown-plug.o: Leaves a lightly sourish tobacco scent leaning toward dried fruit and brown sugar.

dunhill-duke-street.z: A discontinued mixture, referring to Dunhill's Duke Street address in London, for which no verifiable source on its composition could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-bright-cr-flake.z: Bright CR Flake is an untopped Virginia blend produced by pressing Virginia leaves of Brazilian, Zimbabwean, and Malawian origin, letting them mature, and then slicing them into flakes. Using dark and light-coloured leaves together creates variety of colour and taste across the flakes. Even without an added topping, it carries a very light Lakeland trace from the production line. In the smoke, Virginia's typical sweet, grassy taste leads, accompanied by fruity and woody tones. It burns slow and cool, though it can bite the tongue if drawn quickly. The nicotine load is medium and suits all-day smoking. This is a record for those wanting the pure Virginia taste delivered in a full, straightforward way rather than a complex, multi-layered tobacco.
gawith-hoggarth-co-bright-cr-flake.o: Leaves an aroma of dry grass and baked bread with a very fine floral trace mixed in.

john-middleton-inc-apple-pipe-tobacco.z: John Middleton's apple-flavored pipe tobacco; no reliable source could be found on the blend's contents and cut.
john-middleton-inc-apple-pipe-tobacco.o: Leaves a sweet smoke reminiscent of baked apple and unspiced apple candy.

milan-tobacconists-bob-berglunds-bba-mix.z: BBA Mixture is a variation built on Milan Tobacconists' house blend called Buddy's Blend. Records indicate an additional component requested by Bob Berglund, who gives the blend its name, was added to Buddy's Blend, producing a light aromatic based on select virginia and black cavendish. Its body is thin and the smoke soft; the base blend's light sweetness in the direction of chocolate and coffee and its nutty finish are found here as well. An entry geared toward those who don't want a heavy casing and are looking for a low-nicotine mixture smokable over a long time. Since it falls into the category of special blends Milan prepares for named customers, its distribution is limited.
milan-tobacconists-bob-berglunds-bba-mix.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, soft aroma leaning toward cocoa and roasted beans.

tabac-benden-three-monks.z: Three Monks Rope Cut is a curly-cut tobacco Tabac Benden prepared together with Kopp Tobaccos, looking back to the old Three Nuns tradition. The blend contains various Virginia types, Burley, and a very small amount of Kentucky; roughly ten percent Perique is added on top. The discs appear in medium and dark brown tones, with light gold and reddish Virginia veins visible between them. The taste leans savory-spicy: rye bread tones are supported by the pepper and tart yeast notes Perique brings. Nicotine is pronounced, rated six out of eight on the retailer's scale. A brief airing before packing helps ensure an even burn. It suits smokers looking for a strong, spicy, unflavored smoke rather than sweet, mild blends.
tabac-benden-three-monks.o: A peppery note accompanies a scent of rye bread and tart yeast.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-1998.z: Christmas Cheer 1998 is a member of McClelland's annual unflavored Virginia series. Per its label, it's prepared with mature, mottled leaves gathered in Virginia state's Old Belt region in 1995. The leaf is pressed and presented as broken flake. Old Belt harvests are known for more intense sweetness and dried-fruit tones; since no flavoring is present in the blend, the taste comes entirely from the leaf's own sugars. Nicotine is medium. Like the whole series, it's produced to be stored for many years and suits smokers used to unflavored Virginia smoking.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-1998.o: A light tangy background accompanies a sweet hay and dried-fruit aroma.

tor-tor-turkish-budget-shag.z: A fine shag-cut tobacco offered as a budget option for the British market; despite the "Turkish" in its name, records indicate it is prepared from Virginia leaf. No other independent source has been found.
tor-tor-turkish-budget-shag.o: No detailed description of its aroma has been found in records.

solani-779-english-mixture.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Solani blend 779: English Mixture could not be found.

danske-club-ocean-blue.z: Ocean Blue is one of the more heavily cased blends in the Danish Danske Club series, previously listed in catalogues under the name Blue Sambuca. Like the rest of the series, it's built on Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish leaf. The casing comes from sambuca liqueur and real licorice root, giving the blend an easily identifiable, sweet, anise-forward direction. Nicotine sits between mild and medium. It's built for smokers looking for a strongly spiced, anise-leaning, clearly aromatic blend; it sits far from the profile of an unflavored Virginia or a Latakia mixture. The fine cut lights easily, though as is typical of heavily flavored blends, it calls for a slow, cool pace.
danske-club-ocean-blue.o: Leaves a sweet liqueur scent dominated by anise and licorice root.

sutliff-tobacco-company-zbc-245.z: 245 ZBC is Sutliff's classic American black Cavendish. Green River Burley is first roasted, then steamed for roughly twenty-four hours; fire-cured Kentucky leaf goes through the same process, yielding a dark, soft, moist Cavendish. A caramel-, cream-, and vanilla-forward flavoring is applied over it; records also note a trace of dark fruit and light spice. The blend serves two purposes: as a soft aromatic smoked on its own, and as a component that adds sweetness, moisture, and dark color to other blends. Nicotine is light. Because of the moisture the Cavendish carries, airing it before packing noticeably changes both the burn and the taste balance.
sutliff-tobacco-company-zbc-245.o: Leaves a scent of caramel, cream, and dark fruit.

esoterica-tobacciana-dunbar.z: Dunbar is one of the Esoterica line's virginia-perique blends, presented ribbon cut. Like the rest of the Esoterica blends, it is produced by J. F. Germain & Son in Jersey. After the first third of the bowl, apricot and cooked-fruit echoes become more pronounced, accompanied by sweet hay tones. The perique proportion is measured relative to the line's other VaPer blends, making it a mild enough entry point for smokers new to the virginia-perique type.
esoterica-tobacciana-dunbar.o: Leaves a scent of cooked apricot and sweet dry grass.

samuel-gawith-apricot-and-cream.z: No sufficient source could be found for this aromatic from Samuel Gawith, understood from its name to contain apricot and cream casing.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-ser-jacopo-engli.z: Ser Jacopo English Mixture is one of the blends produced in Germany by Kohlhase & Kopp for the Italian pipe maker Ser Jacopo. At the request of founder Giancarlo Guidi, a threefold series was prepared — one English, one aromatic, one Scottish-style; records indicate these tobaccos reached the US in 2001 via Iwan Ries. Its contents include golden and red Virginias plus a small amount of doubly fermented black cavendish, with Cyprus latakia added on top. What sets the blend apart from classic English mixtures is a pronounced Scotch whisky casing accompanying the latakia smoke. Latakia is more a character definer than a proportional dominator: smoke and wood notes frame Virginia's bready sweetness, while the whisky leaves a light harshness and grain sweetness at the finish. Suited to smokers accustomed to latakia-containing blends who don't mind a measured casing alongside them.
kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-ser-jacopo-engli.o: A light whisky sweetness mixes into latakia's campfire-like smoky scent.

pipes-pleasures-euphoria.z: Pipes & Pleasures is a tobacconist shop opened in Columbus, Ohio, in 1977; Euphoria is one of the blends the shop offers under its own name, though no sufficient sources describing the blend's content and character could be found.

levin-pipes-international-nocturne.z: Nocturne is a now-discontinued latakia-containing mixture McClelland prepared for Barry Levin's Levin Pipes International brand; no reliable detail could be found about its composition.
levin-pipes-international-nocturne.o: Leaves a smoky wood room note derived from latakia.

sutliff-tobacco-company-presbyterian-ord.z: A record listed in Sutliff's catalogs as a straight Virginia blend; no sufficient source on its content and character could be found.

peter-stokkebye-royal-guard-black-cavend.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Royal Guard Black Cavendish in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

park-lane-tobacconist-park-lane-no-11.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Park-Lane No. 11, one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

samuel-gawith-lakeland-dark-flake.z: Lakeland Dark Flake is a flake tobacco obtained at Samuel Gawith's production in Kendal, England, by pressing and slicing dark-colored Virginia leaves. "Lakeland" in the name references both the firm's location in the Lake District and the region's tradition of adding a floral essence — a tradition considered a distinct branch within English tobacco production. The slices are dark, oily, and dense in structure; since moisture is high, airing before lighting is needed. Its taste carries Virginia's bready sweetness together with the essence's soapy floral note, and nicotine is above medium. A record for those wanting to get to know the classic Lakeland style and accustomed to smoking dark flake.
samuel-gawith-lakeland-dark-flake.o: Leaves a dark, sourish tobacco scent together with a floral essence evoking soap and lavender.

smokers-haven-select-mixture.z: Select Mixture is a discontinued mixture prepared for Smokers' Haven; sufficient sources on its composition and character could not be found.
smokers-haven-select-mixture.o: Records did not describe the room note.

brigham-enterprises-inc-morning-pleasure.z: Morning Pleasure is one of the aromatic blends Brigham offers in the Canadian market.
