Burley grown in Kentucky forms the body; about fifteen percent black cavendish is added to it. This composition gives a medium-to-slow burn rate, a low nicotine feel, and a sweet aroma. Because cavendish's sugary softness sits over burley's dry, nutty base, the blend stays far from harshness and has low tongue bite. As its name suggests, suitable for the day's first pipes or for beginners seeking a light aromatic.
brigham-enterprises-inc-morning-pleasure.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly caramel-like and nutty aroma.

cornell-diehl-dark-cherry-cavendish.z: Dark Cherry Cavendish is an aromatic blend obtained by working a specially prepared dark cherry flavoring into an American-style cavendish base. The composition reported by the manufacturer includes black cavendish, burley, and Virginia; the cut is ribbon. While nicotine stays very light, the cherry note stands out; burley and Virginia hold a thin tobacco body beneath the flavoring. It suits those looking for a blend with high flavor intensity and low strength, as well as smokers coming from the aromatic tradition.
cornell-diehl-dark-cherry-cavendish.o: Leaves an aroma of dark, sweet cherry with a light caramel note.

imperial-tobacco-group-plc-caporal-expor.z: Records classify Caporal Export as a cigar-leaf-forward blend; no independent source describing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
imperial-tobacco-group-plc-caporal-expor.o: No room note described in the records could be found.

dobies-four-square-london-green.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of Four Square London (Green), a blend from Dobie's.

e-a-carey-black-raspberry.z: Black Raspberry, one of E. A. Carey's best-selling aromatics, is built by combining black cavendish with lightly pressed burley leaf. A raspberry-and-vanilla-direction topping is applied on top; the maker describes the blend as a Danish-style aromatic, presented loose cut. Because burley holds the body, the blend doesn't stay entirely flat despite its sweetness; the cavendish slows the burn and carries the sweet side. Nicotine is kept light. It suits smokers who love fruity aromatics and want a tobacco that doesn't weigh on them through the day.
e-a-carey-black-raspberry.o: Leaves a sweet raspberry and vanilla scent.

pipesandcigars-com-best-of-the-rest-pipe.z: No independent source material could be found sufficient to fill out a specification for the pipesandcigars.com blend called Best of the Rest Pipe Tobacco.

mcclelland-contest-blend.z: One of McClelland's limited-distribution blends; no reliable source documenting its contents and character could be found.

samuel-gawith-pure-louisiana-perique.z: Pure Louisiana Perique is a 100% perique product containing no casing or other leaf. According to records, leaf grown in the St. James region of Louisiana is fermented under pressure in oak barrels for years; this process gives the tobacco its characteristic vinegary tartness, dried-fruit tones, and sharp peppery character. It is packaged ribbon cut. It is not designed to be smoked alone; its nicotine and flavor intensity are heavy enough to make packing a bowl alone difficult. It is used as a blending component: added at five-to-ten percent to a Virginia-forward mixture, it builds the familiar pepper-plum balance of the va-per type. A component for experienced smokers who prepare their own blends.
samuel-gawith-pure-louisiana-perique.o: Leaves a scent of vinegary tartness, ripe fig, and sharp black pepper.

clan-shaw-brigadoon.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Brigadoon.

peretti-blend-d-9507.z: Blend D-9507 is one of the old formulas drawn from L.J. Peretti's alphabetically ordered blend ledgers, from ledger 'D,' and is still produced to the same recipe today. Per the maker's own description, the body is formed by fire-cured Cavendish; a small amount of Perique and a soft Turkish tobacco obtained from top leaves called Dubeck are added. This composition keeps the smoke mild while giving a measured sweetness and a pronounced sharpness. Although it is listed among English mixtures in the shop's catalog, no information is given about it containing Latakia; its character sits in a separate line formed by smoky-scented leaf and Perique rather than classic Latakia blends. Given its unflavored structure and medium body, it is a record aimed at smokers seeking a spicy taste without Latakia that isn't flat. The maker describes it as a mixture unlike any other it has encountered.
peretti-blend-d-9507.o: Leaves an aroma where the smoke and wood scent of fire-cured leaf mixes with a light tart fruit and spice trace from the Perique.

samuel-gawith-christmas-mixture-2006.z: A limited-run edition Samuel Gawith released for the 2006 holiday season; no independent source documenting that year's specific blend content could be found.

esoterica-tobacciana-woodbridge.z: Woodbridge is a blend built entirely on Virginia leaf within the Esoterica Tobacciana line. Records indicate twelve different Virginias are used: six light-coloured Virginias, four Virginias pressed until reddish-brown then rubbed out, and golden and dark Virginia leaves hot-pressed until jet black. Having these differently processed leaves together keeps the blend's cut from being uniform and gives the bowl a mixed-texture leaf. A light liquorice root and natural fruit essence is applied on top; this flavouring is kept at a level that accompanies rather than overtakes Virginia's own sugar. The smoke proceeds bread-like and sweet at a medium intensity, with a nicotine load that isn't heavy. Since it contains no Latakia, it suits smokers who don't want the smoky taste of English blends but want something a bit sweeter than plain Virginia.
esoterica-tobacciana-woodbridge.o: Leaves an aroma of liquorice root and light fruit over bread-like Virginia sweetness.

john-patton-delhi-township.z: One of the small-scale blends released under the John Patton name; not enough independent sources could be found to document its contents and character.
john-patton-delhi-township.o: No source could be found on the room note.

seattle-pipe-club-virginia-jazz.z: Virginia Jazz is Seattle Pipe Club's entry on the Virginia-perique wing. Red Virginia leaf aged for roughly a decade is joined by a notable share of Acadian perique and stoved Virginia; the mixture is pressed and presented as a crumble cake. The cake is broken into dark mahogany discs about the size of a tea biscuit and prepared by crumbling by hand. The tin note carries a vinegary tartness along with raisin, paper, and sweet wood traces. On the smoke, the mature Virginia's bready, dark-sugar base is constant; the perique opens up toward the middle of the bowl, adding a counterpoint of raisin, date, and pepper. Suited to smokers who enjoy unflavored, sweet-and-sour Virginia blends and cake-format tobaccos.
seattle-pipe-club-virginia-jazz.o: Leaves a slightly sour scent reminiscent of raisins and baked bread crust.

tabacosbr-frog-morton-opera.z: No reliable source describing the composition or character of this blend, recorded under the TabacosBR name, could be found.

paul-olsen-kong-frederik-full-english-mi.z: For Paul Olsen's blend called Kong Frederik Full (English Mixture), no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

mcclelland-lucky-day.z: No sufficient independent source describing the contents and character of this blend could be found.
mcclelland-lucky-day.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet aroma typical of aromatic blends.

dunhill-standard-mixture-full.z: The Standard Mixture family is among the classic English mixtures Dunhill introduced in 1921, offered in three grades by latakia proportion. Full is the heaviest of the three: an oriental leaf of Turkish origin and Cyprus latakia are layered over a flame-cured Virginia body, and the mixture is prepared fine ribbon cut. No flavoring is used; the sweetness comes from the Virginia itself and the sharpness from the latakia. The smoke runs cool and straight, and can scorch the tongue if smoked fast. It's a blend designed for smokers seeking latakia intensity, accustomed to unadulterated English mixtures; it is not an entry point for those coming from aromatic tobacco. After Dunhill exited pipe tobacco production around 2018, the recipe has been continued under the Peterson name, so Dunhill-labeled tins are now out of production.
dunhill-standard-mixture-full.o: Leaves a sharp scent dominated by soot and wood smoke, carrying dry leaf and a hint of spice.

planta-sans-souci-sans-souci-majestic-mi.z: Sans Souci is a blend from the Berlin house Planta named after the palace of the same name in Potsdam; no verifiable source could be found on its composition and casing.

erik-stokkebye-small-batch-peaty-kentuck.z: Small Batch Peaty Kentucky is a blend where aged Virginia leaves are joined by fire-cured Kentucky hand-rolled into rope. After resting for a few weeks, the rope is cut into thin coin-shaped slices, which need to be rubbed out before smoking. The fire-curing method gives the tobacco a pronounced woody smoke layer, while the Virginia leaves build a sweet base underneath. Because the nicotine load is high, it suits smokers accustomed to full-bodied, smoky blends, particularly for evening smokes after a full meal.
erik-stokkebye-small-batch-peaty-kentuck.o: Leaves a sharp scent reminiscent of wood smoke and hearth soot.

larus-brother-company-inc-edgeworth-cave.z: The green-labeled arm of the Edgeworth line was marketed as a light aromatic built on Cavendish-processed leaf. Per period ads, the blend's scent was defined by a casing known as tonka bean, giving a sweet note close to vanilla. The base softened by Cavendish is balanced with Burley and Virginia leaves. Nicotine load is low, smoke texture is soft; aimed at those seeking a sweet aromatic away from sharpness. After Larus & Brother Company's Richmond production ended in 1974, the Edgeworth name changed hands and this variant was eventually withdrawn from the market. Today it's a record found only in old stock and collector tins.
larus-brother-company-inc-edgeworth-cave.o: Leaves a sweet, vanilla-like tonka bean room note.

peterson-special-reserve-2018.z: Special Reserve 2018 is a limited edition blend released as part of Peterson's Special Reserve series specific to that year; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient first-hand sources confirming its content and character could be found.

park-lane-tobacconist-an-aperitif.z: One of the more than a hundred house blends Park-Lane Tobacconist of Clifton Park, New York prepares behind its counter; no usable source describing its composition could be found.

mac-baren-amphora-prestige-regular-mixtu.z: Prestige Regular Mixture is a product tied to the tradition of classic Dutch-style pipe mixtures. Per the manufacturer's description, Virginia, oriental and burley leaves are brought together in balancing proportions; the blend is said to carry over a century of blending heritage behind it. The cut is a loose, easy-packing ribbon. It's produced today under Mac Baren in Denmark. Its character stays away from heavy casing: Virginia's measured sweetness, oriental's dry spice line and burley's nutty body together give a plain, balanced smoke. Nicotine dosage runs from light to medium, suited to long sessions. It can be considered a starting point for those wanting to get acquainted with plain Continental European mixtures, especially the Dutch style.
mac-baren-amphora-prestige-regular-mixtu.o: Leaves a plain tobacco room note reminiscent of dry hay and bread crust.

up-down-red-raspberry.z: Recorded as a raspberry-flavored aromatic house blend from Up Down Tobacco; no independent source on its base leaves and cut has been found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-blueberry.z: Kendal Gold is one of the shag-cut main bodies produced at Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Kendal workshop in Cumbria. Its base is a fine golden-hued cut of flame-cured bright Virginia leaf; the producer states it uses no other tobacco type in this series, only cleanly cut Virginia. The Kendal Gold body is offered with numerous different flavorings, and Kendal Gold-Blueberry is this family's blueberry-flavored member. The blueberry flavoring is added to Kendal Gold's fine Virginia cut; the jar aroma is pronounced, and on the smoke the fruit sweetness combines with the Virginia's own sugar. The shag cut lights fast and needs slow smoking. Suited to those seeking a low-nicotine fruity aromatic.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-blueberry.o: Leaves a sweet blueberry and jam aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-toffee.z: Kendal Toffee is a fine shag-cut aromatic in the Kendal series from the Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. factory in the Cumbrian town of Kendal. Its base carries a darker, more mature Virginia leaf than the one used in the house's lighter Kendal Gold line; this dark leaf's own sweetness combines with an English-style toffee flavor applied on top. The topping is pronounced, but the dark character of the base leaf remains felt underneath. The fine shag cut makes the tobacco easy to pack and light; on the other hand, since it tends to burn fast, it calls for a slow draw. An entry suited to smokers wanting a sugar-caramel-axis Virginia with a clearly audible topping, and to anyone curious about the classic aromatic approach of English Lakeland houses.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-toffee.o: Leaves an aroma of boiled sugar and buttery caramel.

cornell-diehl-chopped-cigar-leaf.z: Chopped Cigar Leaf is an unflavored component tobacco obtained by chopping Pennsylvania-origin cigar wrapper leaf into ribbon form. Per the manufacturer's description, it is an earthy, semi-sweet leaf carrying hints of coffee, hay, and brown sugar. It can be smoked on its own, but its main use is in home blending: added in small amounts, it lends an existing blend the taste and aroma characteristic of cigar leaf. Because nicotine content runs high, it is difficult to smoke on an empty stomach or at a fast pace. It suits smokers seeking a cigar taste in a pipe and those building their own blends.
cornell-diehl-chopped-cigar-leaf.o: Leaves an intense, earthy, leather-like cigar aroma.

h-simmons-burlington-blend.z: An H. Simmons house blend named after the Burlington Arcade in London, where the shop is located; there is not enough sourcing on its composition and character.
h-simmons-burlington-blend.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

mclintock-pipe-smokers.z: Pipe Smoker's is an aromatic mixed cut positioned in the McLintock line's classic Danish style. A measured casing is applied to a body built on Virginia, burley, and black cavendish; the result is a tobacco smokable at any hour of the day with the nicotine strength kept low. The brand belonged to Berlin-based Planta; after being transferred to Mac Baren in 2019, production moved to Denmark, and the line was gradually withdrawn from the market.
mclintock-pipe-smokers.o: Leaves a soft aroma reminiscent of sweet cavendish and a light barrel scent.

paul-olsen-no-61.z: One of the Virginia-and-burley-based blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-burley-and-bri.z: Burley and Bright is a blend combining light Burley with bright Virginia in a ribbon cut, topped with a measured chocolate-and-vanilla flavoring. The topping level is low, keeping the leaf taste in front. The smoke is cool and mild with little tongue bite; nicotine is moderate. Burley's dry, nutty body and Virginia's light sweetness stay balanced. A product suited to smokers wanting a plain blend for all-day smoking, as well as used as a base tobacco by smokers preparing their own mixtures.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-burley-and-bri.o: A dry, nutty trace accompanies a light cocoa and vanilla aroma.

hearth-home-mt-marcy.z: Named after New York State's highest peak, Mt. Marcy is an Oriental-forward Balkan blend. Dry, woody, sour-sweet Oriental spice forms the blend's backbone; Cyprian Latakia adds smoky, woody sweetness, while Virginia leaves a citrusy, herbal brightness. Suited to those seeking the Balkan style's Oriental-forward line. The taste is layered and intense, while nicotine stays at a moderate level, allowing for long smoking sessions.
hearth-home-mt-marcy.o: Leaves an aroma of wood smoke, dry spice, and a sour, herbal edge.

park-lane-tobacconist-bengal.z: No reliable source could be found for the Park brand pipe tobacco called Lane Tobacconist-Bengal, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

sturks-tobacconists-black-velvet.z: Black Velvet is one of the hand-blended counter mixtures from Sturk's Tobacconists in Cape Town; records indicate the shop was founded on August 1, 1793, and is South Africa's oldest tobacconist. Since sufficient independent sources on the blend's composition and smoking character could not be found, this record is kept at listing level.

black-cat-cigar-company-black-cordial.z: Recorded as a blend of fire-cured dark leaf grades and sweet Virginias finished with a liqueur topping; the manufacturer's recipe could not be verified with an independent source.
black-cat-cigar-company-black-cordial.o: Leaves a sweet liqueur and smoky-leaf room note.

kaptn-barsdorfs-bester-red-formerly-cher.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for Kapt'n Barsdorf's Bester's Red (formerly Cherry), so the profile is left incomplete; per catalog records, the blend is classified as "Aromatic."

john-middleton-inc-philadelphia-mixture.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Middleton, Inc's Philadelphia Mixture pipe tobacco.

dan-tobacco-the-mellow-mallard.z: The Mellow Mallard is a pure Virginia blend of carefully fermented, aged sweet Virginia leaves; per records, some of the leaves are Zambian in origin. In European Union countries the product is sold only under the name The Mallard. The taste is full yet soft; it carries no harshness or sharpness, with Virginia's natural sweetness coming to the fore. Fullness is light. It suits smokers newly moving to unadulterated Virginia taste or seeking a low-nicotine blend smokable all day.
dan-tobacco-the-mellow-mallard.o: Leaves a scent evoking dry hay and a light caramel sweetness.

lane-limited-burley.z: Not enough independent sources could be found documenting the contents and character of American blender Lane Limited's blend called Burley.

peter-stokkebye-dansk-black-no-47.z: No sufficient sources documenting the content and character of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye's blend Dansk Black (No.47) could be found.

g-l-pease-night-wraith.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Night Wraith.

b-b-tobacconists-llc-doc-piedmont.z: A tobacconist blend noted as Virginia-Perique-centered; composition details could not be found in sources, leaving the profile blank.

pipesandcigars-com-scottys-levines-blend.z: Levine's Blend is a blend pipesandcigars.com prepared for Art Levine, a longtime customer, later added to the Scotty's line. Bright Virginia, smooth black Cavendish, and enough Latakia to be felt on the palate come over a mellow, nutty Burley. This structure places the blend somewhere between English mixtures and American Burley blends. Its smoke burns cool; the balance between sweetness and smoke is the blend's main feature. With the Latakia proportion kept low, the smoke doesn't overwhelm Virginia's dry sweetness. It suits smokers looking for Latakia at a spice level rather than dominant, in a medium-bodied, all-day ribbon cut.
pipesandcigars-com-scottys-levines-blend.o: A dry-hay sweetness mixes into a light woody smoke aroma.

peterson-special-reserve-2016.z: Special Reserve 2016 is a limited edition blend released as part of Peterson's Special Reserve series specific to that year; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient first-hand sources confirming its content and character could be found.

peterson-special-reserve-2015.z: Special Reserve 2015 is a limited edition blend released as part of Peterson's Special Reserve series specific to that year; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient first-hand sources confirming its content and character could be found.

watch-city-cigar-undead-scottsman.z: This is a very limited micro-batch Scottish-style blend produced by Watch City Cigar; since some of the leaves used could not be sourced again, it was never reproduced, and no source could be found documenting its composition.
watch-city-cigar-undead-scottsman.o: No description could be found as no source was available.

motzek-herbst-84.z: Herbst 84 is an entry reflecting the Motzek workshop's classic English blend approach. Bright and red Virginia leaves build the base, select Oriental tobaccos add a spicy, dry top layer, and Latakia draws the smoky frame. The Latakia proportion is not kept high enough to overwhelm the blend; the spice is present but not overpowering. The blend is reported to have been created during Herbert Motzek's time, and the date in its name refers to that period. The ribbon cut gives a slow, cool burn; nicotine sits from light toward medium. A fitting entry for smokers looking for the smoky side of Latakia-containing blends without wanting to venture into heavy Balkan-type compositions. No flavor casing is used; the taste comes entirely from the leaf composition.
motzek-herbst-84.o: Leaves an aroma of wood smoke and dry spice, with a lightly sweet tobacco scent lingering behind.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-comfy-m.z: An aromatic mixture released under Ken Byron Ventures' Mr. Christian's line; no accessible source could be found to document its contents.

lane-limited-partagas.z: One of the blends Lane Limited released under a cigar brand's name; not enough sources could be found for its contents.

dunhill-white-spot.z: "White Spot" is the name of the white-dot mark Dunhill has used on pipe mouthpieces since 1915, and of its current pipe brand; no sufficient sourcing could be found for an independent pipe tobacco blend described under this name.
dunhill-white-spot.o: Could not be described due to insufficient records.

imp-turkish-pride.z: This is one of the four blends IMP USA introduced in 2013; records indicate it's the lighter-colored, milder member of the line, with Oriental tobaccos, as the name suggests, coming forward. Production ended when the company changed hands in 2015, and no sufficient independent source detailing the blend's character could be found.

danske-club-ruby.z: Ruby is the cherry-cased blend in the Danske Club series, previously sold directly under the name Cherry. It's built on Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish; the ribbon cut lights easily and burns evenly. Cherry flavoring is the blend's defining trait, combined with the sweetness the Cavendish provides. Strength sits between mild and medium. This is a blend built for smokers looking for a classic fruity aromatic, particularly those who favor a cherry profile. It's distributed in 50-gram pouches and 100-gram tins.
danske-club-ruby.o: Leaves a sweet cherry, jammy fruit scent.

hearth-home-sweet-savory.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for this blend, described as Virginia-forward, from the Hearth & Home brand.

doctor-pipe-great-times.z: This is an unadulterated mixture where Latakia and Oriental leaves are balanced with Perique added. Perique lays a spicy, lightly fruity layer over the smoky core; it's built for smokers accustomed to Latakia-heavy mixtures.
doctor-pipe-great-times.o: A smoky wood scent is mixed with a spicy, fig-like note.

gatlin-burlier-newfound-blend.z: No reliable source could be found on the Gatlin brand's Burlier-Newfound Blend.

richs-house-of-craven.z: House of Craven is one of Rich's Cigar Store's house blends, said to be Virginia and Burley based; no verifiable source could be found describing its content.
richs-house-of-craven.o: No reliable information could be found on the room note.

sutliff-tobacco-company-black-vanilla.z: Black Vanilla, listed under the Sutliff Tobacco Company name, appears from its name to be a vanilla-flavored blend built on a black cavendish base; no reliable source on its composition, cut, and production status could be found.

dan-tobacco-virginia-flake.z: Part of the Dan Tobacco line, this is, as the name suggests, a straight Virginia flake, pressed and sliced; no adequate sources were found regarding the leaf used or its character.
dan-tobacco-virginia-flake.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

mac-baren-vanilla-chocolate.z: Remembered as a vanilla-and-chocolate-flavored Mac Baren blend; since no independent source documenting a product with this name could be found, the record is left incomplete.
mac-baren-vanilla-chocolate.o: Said to leave a vanilla and cocoa aroma.

brookline-news-and-gifts-boston-harbor.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Boston Harbor under the Brookline News and Gifts brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

mcclelland-bombay-extra.z: Bombay Extra is the enriched version McClelland built starting from its Bombay Court blend. The maker darkened the Virginias in the original recipe, added a pinch of Perique, and raised the Latakia proportion. Its contents hold Turkish Oriental tobaccos, Latakia, Perique, and extra dark, naturally sweet Virginia. It's ribbon cut. While the Oriental tobaccos' spicy-floral side is preserved, the Latakia soot and Perique's dark-fruit depth carry the blend to a fuller base; taste and satiety sit above Bombay Court's. It falls within the territory of those wanting Latakia together with Oriental tobacco and a measured Perique share.
mcclelland-bombay-extra.o: Leaves an aroma mixing dark soot, spice, and sweet dried fruit.

motzek-ralfs-burley-cup.z: A virginia-burley-based special-order blend from the Motzek workshop; sufficient independent sources for detailed composition and character information could not be found.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore-bu.z: Finamore's chocolate-flavored version is prepared by adding a cocoa-leaning flavoring to the brand's standard Burley- and Virginia-based body. The product is made in Juiz de Fora, Minas Gerais, and distributed in packs on the Brazilian domestic market. The chocolate note stands out both in the tin note and on the smoke; Burley's dry, nutty side provides a balancing base beneath this sweetness. Nicotine is low, making it suitable for long sessions. It suits smokers who like sweet, toasted-sweet aromatics.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-finamore-bu.o: Leaves a sweet scent reminiscent of cocoa and milk chocolate.

cornell-diehl-evening-rise.z: Evening Rise is an English mixture built on a burley base with Latakia, Turkish Orientals, and Virginia added. The maker's description positions the blend as tobacco for evening hours, for conversations by mosquito-ridden waterside spots. It is a ribbon cut. The burley base gives the blend an earthy, nutty body with low sugar, while Latakia adds smoky weight and the Orientals bring a tangy spice; Virginia leaves a thin trace of sweetness in between. Nicotine is medium, flavor intensity is high, and the smoke spreads noticeably through the room. It suits smokers wanting a classic English profile built on a burley body.
cornell-diehl-evening-rise.o: A heavy aroma of smoke and burnt wood spreads noticeably through the room.

samuel-gawith-fire-dance-plug.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Fire Dance Plug, according to records a Virginia-forward blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

cornell-diehl-visions-of-celephais.z: Visions of Celephaïs is a ribbon-cut aromatic blend in Cornell & Diehl's series inspired by H. P. Lovecraft's fictional world. Its base holds red and light-colored Virginia leaf, joined by dark fire-cured Kentucky, black Cavendish, and cigar leaf. Per the maker's description, what defines the blend are spice notes and a casing that leans on fermented wine — setting it apart from classic vanilla aromatics. On the maker's own scale, strength is medium and flavor intensity high. Despite being aromatic, the tobacco character isn't pushed to the background; the smoky weight of the fire-cured leaf sits alongside Virginia sweetness. Built for smokers who like cased blends but want to move away from a fruit or sweet-syrup axis.
cornell-diehl-visions-of-celephais.o: Leaves a scent where fermented-wine sweetness mingles with spice, with a woody smokiness underneath.

tinder-box-norse-gold.z: Tinder Box is the name of an American tobacconist chain founded in 1928 that sells blends prepared for its own shops under its own name; Norse Gold is one of these house blends, though no sufficient independent source describing its composition and character has been found.

w-o-larsen-the-masters-blend-17.z: No reliable source could be found regarding the composition and character of this entry in W.Ø. Larsen's Master's Blend series; the series as a whole generally consists of light, fruit-cased blends.
w-o-larsen-the-masters-blend-17.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

pfeifen-huber-virginia-old-belt.z: Virginia Old Belt is a single-varietal Virginia blend released under its own name by Pfeifen Huber, a house operating in Munich since 1863. Per the maker's description, selected, pale golden, soft Virginia leaves are presented in a long-fibered, loose cut; strands of varying width pack easily into a pipe. Flavoring is kept very low, so the tobacco's own sweetness comes through. The smoke carries a light sweetness reminiscent of wheat dough, honey, and citrus, with woody and grassy notes in the background. Its low nicotine makes it a candidate for all-day smoking; the maker recommends smoking slowly, since rushing it risks the bite typical of pure Virginias. It suits smokers seeking an unflavored, straightforward Virginia character who enjoy working with a ribbon cut.
pfeifen-huber-virginia-old-belt.o: Leaves a Virginia aroma with a sweetness recalling wheat dough, a hint of honey, and a touch of citrus.

mcclelland-m-94-light-cherry-cordial.z: No sufficient independent source describing the contents of this blend from the numbered bulk aromatic series could be found.
mcclelland-m-94-light-cherry-cordial.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of cherry liqueur.

hearth-home-grandmas-kitchen.z: Grandma's Kitchen is an aromatic where nutty-sweet Burley leaf meets the light spice of red Virginia. The mixture includes two separate naturally toasted black Cavendishes plus a vanilla-based, steam-processed black Cavendish. Contrary to what the name might suggest, it isn't dark black in appearance; because the Burley-to-Virginia ratio is high, the color is mixed, and the cut is a ribbon slightly thicker than average. The topping sits over the tobacco without fully masking its taste; there is a noticeable nicotine weight coming from the Burley. It can give a peppery bite on the tongue if smoked quickly, so it calls for a slow pace. A blend for aromatic smokers who want sweet top notes but also want the taste of unflavored tobacco to show through.
hearth-home-grandmas-kitchen.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and roasted-hazelnut aroma.

planta-cellini-classico.z: Cellini Classico is the base blend of Planta's Italian-inspired aromatic line. Light golden Virginia leaf is combined with dark black Cavendish, accompanied by Burley; leaf sourced from Tuscany and Umbria is reportedly used. A casing giving orange and floral notes is applied on top. It is a loose cut, low in strength, with pronounced flavoring. It suits smokers looking for sweet, citrusy aromatics, including newcomers to the pipe. Planta was founded in 1956 in Berlin-Spandau, ended its Berlin production in 2019, and production of the brands continues with the original recipes under Mac Baren.
planta-cellini-classico.o: Leaves an orange-blossom and tropical fruit aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-brown-rum.z: Sliced Brown Rum is the rum-topped, factory-sliced member of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s brown Burma family. The rope is prepared by hand-twisting dark fire-cured leaf; cutting it yields dark reddish-brown coin-shaped slices. The rum meets a lighter, less smoky base than in the black version; earth, bready sweetness, and spice notes stand out. Since it doesn't go through a pressure-cooking stage, it's intense in nicotine, suited to being thinly sliced and smoked slowly. An entry aimed at those wanting a topped Burma that doesn't tip into a sugary aromatic. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. is one of the English producers that continues traditional twist (rope) production at its Kendal factory, hand-twisting fire-cured leaves into rope form. Because twist tobaccos don't go through a pressure-cooking stage, they stay intense in nicotine; records indicate these ropes are sold for both chewing and pipe smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-brown-rum.o: Leaves an aroma combining sweet rum and woody tobacco scents.

sutliff-tobacco-company-english-oriental.z: English Oriental #400341 is an English mixture in Sutliff's numbered bulk line that puts Turkish/oriental leaf forward. Its tightly packed ribbon cut gives a mixed appearance of biscuit tones, golden yellow, russet copper, and veined browns with scattered black flecks. Records indicate the blend also contains Louisiana-origin perique. The aroma rising from the pouch carries campfire smokiness woven with a bright tartness and a musty spice impression. On the palate it's light-to-medium bodied, tracing a piney, peaty, cigar-like flavor line. A record for those seeking a bulk-sold latakia mixture intended for everyday smoking.
sutliff-tobacco-company-english-oriental.o: Leaves a combined scent of campfire smoke and musty spice.

james-barber-sherry-cherry.z: A James Barber aromatic whose name signals sherry and cherry casing; no independent source could be found to document its base tobaccos.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2015.z: Christmas Cheer is the straight Virginia series that Kansas City-based McClelland released once a year, in limited numbers, from the 1980s until the company's closure in early 2018. The series' idea is to present a single Virginia batch selected from that year's harvest on its own; each year is thus considered a separate record, and the year on the tin defines the blend's identity. The 2015 release was prepared the same way, with selected matured Virginia leaf pressed into cake and tinned as broken flake. Records indicate it was prepared from a batch selected from the 2015 harvest. Unflavored Virginia character dominates the smoke: natural leaf sweetness over a bready, herbal base, with a faint tang and a lemony sharpness in the background. Nicotine dose is measured, while flavor intensity is pronounced; it burns cool when smoked slowly, but tends to bite the tongue when rushed. Since the flake's moisture can run high straight from the tin, airing it before packing is common practice. A record aimed at smokers seeking unflavored Virginia who are considering cellaring the tin; not suitable for those expecting an aromatic.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2015.o: A tangy, sharp trace characteristic of McClelland tins mixes into an aroma of dry hay and toasted bread.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-vintage-c.z: Kendal Gold Vintage Cut offers Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s bright Virginia body in the thicker, wide-ribbon cut the company calls "vintage cut." It contains only flame-cured light Virginia leaf; no sweetening or flavoring is added. The same cut is also used for other bodies such as Kendal Dark and Kendal Kentucky. The thick cut burns slower than the shag form and keeps the bowl cool, so the Virginia leaf's lemon, straw, and honey flavor layers open up over a longer time. Nicotine is moderate to light. Suited to smokers wanting to smoke unflavored Virginia and enjoying watching the flavor develop as it rests in the jar.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-vintage-c.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of dry hay and bread crust.

cornell-diehl-old-joe-krantz-white-label.z: Old Joe Krantz White Label is the Burley-heavy member of Cornell & Diehl's Old Joe Krantz family. Its base is built from light and dark Burley leaf, joined by Virginia flake's sweetness, black Cavendish's softness, and Perique's spice. It's ribbon cut, with strength, flavor, and room note given as medium on the maker's scale. The blend carries an unflavored, natural tobacco character; Burley's breadlike, nutty base is balanced by Perique's dried-fruit-and-pepper tones. Suited to smokers wanting a not-heavy, non-aromatic everyday blend, accustomed to Burley-based American-style mixtures. It sits in the production catalogue alongside the same family's Blue Label and Red Label versions.
cornell-diehl-old-joe-krantz-white-label.o: Leaves a nutty, lightly earthy tobacco scent with a subtle sweetness behind it.

mcclelland-no-25.z: No. 25 is one of the unflavored Virginia blends in McClelland's "Matured Virginias" series. Turkish-language sources indicate it comes in the tin as a very fine cut with high moisture, carrying the brand's distinctive aroma. The fine cut dries quickly when aired, packs easily, and lights right away. Records position No. 25 within the series as a milder, slightly sweeter take on No. 27. In the first puffs it gives a surface-level taste owing to the fine cut; the blend's own character emerges past the first third of the bowl, bringing forward the sweet tobacco taste typical of matured Virginia. Body is light to medium and nicotine dose is low. Suited to those wanting a mild Virginia smokable during the day; not for those expecting high nicotine.
mcclelland-no-25.o: Leaves a sweet, faintly tangy dry-hay and baked-fruit aroma.

gambler-mint.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of the Gambler brand's Mint pipe tobacco could be found.

hearth-home-mazatec.z: Mazatec is referred to as a Hearth & Home blend that carries a cocoa note and runs aromatic and English character side by side; there is not enough sourcing to document its full composition.

schurch-onyx-128.z: No accessible source documenting the content and character of the Schürch-signed Onyx 128 blend could be found.

pipesworld-mcgees-exotic-fruit.z: McGee's Exotic Fruit appears among the fruity aromatic blends of the seller known as PipesWorld; no verifiable source could be found on the maker or composition.

e-a-carey-europe-careys-balkan-special.z: Recorded as a Balkan-type blend sold in Europe under the E. A. Carey name; not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition and character.

w-o-larsen-old-fashioned.z: Old Fashioned is a ribbon-cut blend from the W.O. Larsen house, built on Virginia and Burley leaf in the Danish aromatic tradition. A mixed-fruit-forward casing is worked over the leaf base; this casing is the element that defines the blend's identity. It smokes on the light side: nicotine load is low, flavor intensity is measured, making it suitable for smoking one bowl after another over a long stretch. Those seeking the leaf's own natural taste won't find it here; on the other hand, it's a defining example for smokers who prefer cased Danish-style aromatics and want a sweet scent left in the room. The ribbon cut makes packing easy and ensures an even burn.
w-o-larsen-old-fashioned.o: Leaves a sweet scent, richly fruity, reminiscent of a candy shop.

murray-sons-co-ltd-murrays-1810-belfast.z: 1810 Belfast is a current blend referencing Murray, Sons & Co's founding year of 1810. A Virginia-and-Burley-forward body, sweetened with black cavendish, has a very small amount of latakia added; a light sauce is applied on top. The result is a low-nicotine, easy-burning American-type mixture that sits at the edge of both aromatic and English blends. The original factory in Belfast closed in 2005; today the brand is under the Scandinavian Tobacco Group, and according to the tin information, it is produced in Denmark and packaged in the United States. Suited to smokers looking to get their first taste of Latakia, or wanting a very faint smoky note over a sweet body.
murray-sons-co-ltd-murrays-1810-belfast.o: Leaves a faint trace of wood smoke mixed with a sweetish tobacco aroma.

mcclelland-2014-holiday-spirit.z: 2014 Holiday Spirit is an entry in the limited-edition aromatic series McClelland prepared for the holiday season. The blend rests on a base of Burley, Virginia, and black Cavendish; it's sweetened with dark rum, walnut, and cocoa flavoring and presented as loose ribbon cut. In the smoke, a sweet chocolate-and-rum association dominates, with the tobacco's own taste staying in the background. Being light on nicotine, it suits long smokes. Produced for smokers interested in seasonal aromatic blends; no longer produced since McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-2014-holiday-spirit.o: Leaves a sugary sweet aroma where cocoa and rum lead.

motzek-toms-dark-twist.z: One of the twist tobaccos carrying Tom Darasz's signature at the Motzek workshop; sufficient independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character in detail could not be found.

hu-tobacco-dark-sea.z: Dark Sea is a nautically themed, Virginia-based blend prepared ready-rubbed by HU Tobacco. Alongside the Virginia leaves, it contains woody Burley, smoky dark-fired Kentucky, Perique, and a small amount of Latakia; the flavoring is built on rum and anise. It isn't a light blend in terms of nicotine; the spicy, salty-smoky tobacco base is balanced by anise's cooling sweetness. This structure, where Latakia and anise stand together, is described as a contemporary interpretation of classic nautical blends. Records indicate it's produced in 50-gram tins at Kopp Tobaccos's facilities in Germany.
hu-tobacco-dark-sea.o: Leaves a heavy trace where anise-and-rum sweetness mixes into a smoky, woody tobacco aroma.

bosphorus-black-angel-flake.z: Black Angel Flake is an unflavored English-type flake prepared by adding about 10% Burley and 45% Syrian Latakia to yellow and red Virginia. Despite the high Latakia proportion, Virginia's sweetness balances the strength; the result is a medium-strength smoke with intense flavor. Burley adds a bitter, spicy layer to the blend, and nicotine is at a satisfying level. When filling with flake it should be loaded loosely enough not to block airflow, and the smoking pace kept low; otherwise wetness can appear. Aimed at smokers accustomed to Latakia-forward blends, seeking an unflavored, full smoke.
bosphorus-black-angel-flake.o: The heavy Latakia's smoke, tar and pine-smoke aroma settles into the room and lingers for a long time.

iwan-ries-three-star-cordial-cherry.z: This is a blend from the Three Star line prepared over the counter by the Chicago-based tobacconist Iwan Ries & Co.; no independent source detailing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
iwan-ries-three-star-cordial-cherry.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

flandria-vieux-bruges-oud-brugge.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Flandria's Vieux Bruges/Oud Brugge blend; records place it in the aromatic class.

hearth-home-first-snow.z: First Snow belongs to Hearth & Home's Slow-Aged series. Full-bodied Burley, sharply sweet Virginia, and some fire-cured Kentucky are pressed and rested for about a month before being offered as broken flake; this resting period lets the flavors meld together. The profile runs along a nutty, earthy axis, with Kentucky leaving a smoky background. Suited to those wanting an unflavored, dark, and hearty everyday blend. Since it comes as broken flake, rubbing it out a bit by hand before packing eases the burn.
hearth-home-first-snow.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of roasted walnut and wood smoke.

milan-tobacconists-our-kentucky-club-mil.z: A burley-forward blend from Milan Tobacconists' "Our" line, whose name references an old American classic. It follows in the footsteps of old-style burley mixtures, with a construction that is either unflavored or has its casing kept well in the background; the maker describes the blend with a nutty, lightly sweet tobacco taste. It is an easy-lighting tobacco that doesn't bite the tongue and suits being smoked throughout the day. Suitable for those looking to move from aromatics to a plain tobacco taste and for smokers seeking classic American burley character.
milan-tobacconists-our-kentucky-club-mil.o: Leaves an aroma of toasted walnut meat and dry leaf.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-sweet-peach.z: Sweet Peach is a fruity aromatic prepared by dressing Virginia, Cavendish, and Burley leaf with a peach essence. Cavendish provides sweetness and softness, while Burley supplies the base and a cool burn. It's on the light side for nicotine, with the fruit note staying ahead of the tobacco taste. Suited to those new to the pipe or anyone wanting a pronounced fruity top note; because of the topping's intensity, its scent noticeably lingers in the pipe.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-sweet-peach.o: Leaves a sweet fruit aroma reminiscent of canned peach.

emerson-southern-forged-red-castle.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing was found for the Emerson Southern Forged brand's Red Castle blend, so the entry has been left open; records place it in the Straight Virginia family.

gawith-hoggarth-co-black-cherry-brown-pi.z: Not enough independent sourcing was found for this study on Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Black Cherry Brown Pigtail blend, so its content, cut, and character information have been left blank.

sutliff-tobacco-company-fruit-tart-2010.z: Fruit Tart 2010, referred to as a fruity Sutliff aromatic, lacks sufficient sources to confirm its composition and character.

james-fox-foxs-aromatic.z: One of the aromatic house blends sold under the James J. Fox name; no independent source could be found to document its contents.

players-gold-leaf.z: Player's Gold Leaf is a pipe tobacco blend for which there is not enough independent source material.
players-gold-leaf.o: Not enough records could be found on the room note.

dan-tobacco-monkeys-mixture.z: Monkey's Mixture is an aromatic blend in the Dan Tobacco catalogue defined, as its name suggests, by fruit and nut casings. Its body is built on Virginia and black Cavendish, ribbon cut. The casing level is kept pronounced, so the applied flavor stands out more than the tobacco's own character. Nicotine stays mild. Suited to those looking for the strongly cased end of aromatic blends and who enjoy a sweet, fruity smoke; it won't meet the expectations of those wanting English or straight Virginia mixtures.
dan-tobacco-monkeys-mixture.o: Leaves a sweet scent leaning toward fruit and roasted nuts.

david-cigarpipe-1001-nights.z: No adequate sources were found documenting the composition or character of the David CigarPipe 1001 Nights blend.

thepiperoom-com-sherlocks-reserve.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the ThePipeRoom.com pipe tobacco called Sherlock's Reserve has been found.

robert-mcconnell-pure-latakia.z: Pure Latakia is sold on its own as one hundred percent Latakia leaf, presented as a ribbon cut. Latakia is an Oriental tobacco cured over smoke and used in blends to add depth and a layer of smokiness. McConnell offers this product as a blending tobacco for smokers who build their own mixtures. Smoked alone it gives an intensely smoky, incense-like, earthy taste with a spicy sharpness; sugar content is low, so sweetness is almost entirely absent. Its strength depends on how it is used: even a small proportion blended with other leaf noticeably weights the body of a mixture. It suits blenders and anyone who wants to experience the character of Latakia in its pure form.
robert-mcconnell-pure-latakia.o: Fills the room strongly with the scent of incense and burnt pine wood.

d-r-tobacco-penhooker-silver.z: A Canadian-style blend in Daughters & Ryan's Penhooker line, recorded as aiming for a regional character through leaf selection, with a cool, light body; no adequate source detailing its composition was found.
d-r-tobacco-penhooker-silver.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay and light sweet tobacco.

peretti-2-14.z: 2-14 is a pressed blend L.J. Peretti offers in coin form. Per the maker's recipe, Virginia leaf seasoned with perique is wrapped around a core of medium-mellow black cavendish, then sliced into rolled discs. It carries a light flavoring, which places it in an intermediate territory rounded off by the cavendish rather than reading as an unflavored Virginia/perique blend. Perique adds a plum-and-spice depth to Virginia's lemony sweetness, while the cavendish core cools the burn. Because of the coin form, the slices need to be rubbed out or lightly dried before packing. It suits smokers who love the Virginia/perique line but want a tamer taste than a full-strength VaPer. Records indicate it's among the blends prepared in limited numbers.
peretti-2-14.o: Leaves a lightly peppery trace mingling with lightly sweet dry grass and honey aromas.

brobergs-tobakshandel-ab-cambridge-mixtu.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Cambridge Mixture under the Brobergs Tobakshandel AB brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

cup-o-joes-2-maricoxi.z: One of the Cup O' Joes tobacco shop's numbered house blends; records indicate a sweet character leaning toward honey, cocoa, and caramel, though no independent source documenting its composition was found.

tabac-benden-silk-road.z: Silk Road is a five-component mixture from Tabac Benden bearing the signature of Koppe-based blender Thomas Nitsche: Virginia, Burley, Kentucky, Oriental, and Perique are used together. The product is offered as a crumbly cake the smoker can slice for themselves; color variations across the reddish-brown surface hint at the blend's components. On the smoke, Oriental spice comes first, followed by Burley's nutty base and Kentucky's grassy-smoky tone; Virginia provides measured sweetness, while Perique lends a peppery, fruity background. The body is fuller than straight Virginia blends but more restrained than heavy Latakia mixtures. It suits experienced smokers looking for a complex, unflavored blend in cake form.
tabac-benden-silk-road.o: Leaves a measured tobacco scent leaning toward dry spice and nuts.

seattle-pipe-club-snoqualmie-falls.z: Snoqualmie Falls is a mild English mixture in the Seattle Pipe Club series. A base of selected Virginia leaf, black cavendish, and nutty Burley is joined by a small share of Latakia, so the dark leaf's smoke settles into the blend without becoming dominant. It is ribbon cut. Nicotine is low and flavor intensity is medium; the cavendish gives a sweet softness while the Burley supplies body. A suitable stepping stone for smokers trying Latakia for the first time and for those moving from aromatics toward English mixtures.
seattle-pipe-club-snoqualmie-falls.o: A light smoky wood scent is joined by a sweet, nutty background.

tavern-tobacco-co-blackbeards-queen-anne.z: Blackbeard's Queen Anne's Revenge, a pipe tobacco from Tavern Tobacco Co.; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

pipesandcigars-com-st-james-perique.z: St. James Perique is one of the single-varietal tobaccos pipesandcigars.com sells for home blenders. Perique is a tobacco grown in Louisiana's St. James Parish region and fermented under its own pressure inside a barrel; production continues on a small number of farms using methods passed down through generations. This process gives the leaf a sharp character evoking fermented fruit, vinegar, and pepper. It is a slow-burning tobacco high in nicotine, and smoked alone it sits heavy on the palate; its main use is adding spice to sweet leaves like Virginia. Being high in moisture, it should be stored cool. It suits smokers building their own blends who want to control the Perique proportion themselves; it is not a tobacco meant to be smoked alone by newcomers.
pipesandcigars-com-st-james-perique.o: Leaves a sharp, vinegary fermented-fruit and pepper aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-serendipity.z: Serendipity is a blend within Sutliff Tobacco Company's aromatic line; no reliable source on its content and character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-serendipity.o: No reliable record of a room note could be found.

4noggins-evening-cordial.z: Evening Cordial is an aromatic built entirely on black Cavendish. According to the manufacturer, the leaf is flavored twice: first with chocolate essence, then with a light touch of cherry. This double process produces the liqueur-like sweet profile suggested by the blend's name. Because only Cavendish is used, nicotine is very low and the smoke is gentle; flavor runs mild-to-moderate. It's ribbon cut. Since the flavoring outweighs the tobacco character, it suits smokers starting out on aromatics or looking for a low-nicotine sweet blend for the evening hours.
4noggins-evening-cordial.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of chocolate-covered cherry candy.

ken-byron-ventures-festivus-pudding.z: Festivus Pudding forms the "navy" branch of Ken Byron Ventures' Festivus trio. A body built from Virginia and Perique leaf is dressed with a dark, spiced modern rum and presented as a ribbon cut. Its name nods to the spiced pudding of an English holiday table. The rum casing doesn't quite push the blend fully into the aromatic class; it gives a measured sweetness intertwined with Perique's spice and Virginia's sugar. Sitting somewhere between an unflavored VaPer and an aromatic, it's suited to seasonal smoking. Produced in limited numbers.
ken-byron-ventures-festivus-pudding.o: Leaves a sweet tobacco aroma mixed with spiced rum and dark fruit.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-churchill.z: No verifiable composition and character information could be compiled for Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Churchill, which records indicate contains cigar leaf.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-churchill.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

uhles-blend-71.z: Blend 71 is an English-style blend Milwaukee's Uhle Tobacco Company prepares to its own recipe, presented by the company as its flagship product in that category. Its composition includes Latakia, Perique, Turkish leaf and Burley; sold in 1.5, 7 and 14-ounce bulk measures. The maker's description considers it medium-bodied, likening its taste to a medium-cooked piece of meat; Latakia's smoky side, Perique's spice and Burley's dry body sit together. As no flavoring is added, the taste comes entirely from the leaf; flavor intensity is high and nicotine is medium. A record aimed at smokers after an unflavored, smoky American counter blend.
uhles-blend-71.o: Leaves a dark, smoky trace reminiscent of wood smoke and seared meat.

the-tobacco-barn-ebony.z: No sufficient source describing the leaf composition and flavor profile of Ebony, listed in the dark toasted Cavendish group of Tobacco Barn's house blend list, has been found.

yaqui-tobacco-cigars-vicam.z: Named after the Yaqui settlements in Sonora, this blend is described as a combination of Mexican-grown Virginia and a Perique-like leaf produced in Veracruz; no adequate source could be found for its detailed composition and character.
yaqui-tobacco-cigars-vicam.o: No description of its room note could be found in the records.

james-barber-english-cherry.z: A cherry-flavored aromatic house blend from the James Barber tobacconist house; no independent source could be found to document its composition and character.
james-barber-english-cherry.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

bufflehead-redhead-duck.z: Bufflehead was a brand producing small batches in the United States in the early 2000s, naming its blends after waterfowl; since no independent source describing this blend's content and character could be found, the entry has been left incomplete.

john-middleton-inc-kentucky-club-mixture.z: The aromatic mixture in the Kentucky Club line; not enough sources could be found on its contents, cut, and flavoring.
john-middleton-inc-kentucky-club-mixture.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly vanilla-like aroma.

thomson-porteous-limited-drifter-navy-cu.z: Thomson & Porteous is a Scottish tobacco company founded in Edinburgh, known in the early twentieth century for tobaccos such as Luntin and Scots Cake. The Drifter name is known from the firm's roll tobaccos; since no source documenting this navy cut variety's composition has been found, the record is left incomplete.
thomson-porteous-limited-drifter-navy-cu.o: Records describe it as leaving a dry, tobacco-like aroma.

brebbia-adagio-mixture-no-50.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named Adagio (Mixture No. 50) under the Brebbia brand could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-coniston-cut-plug-aro.z: Coniston Cut Plug carries the name of Coniston in the Kendal lake district. Dark fire-cured leaf is combined with Malawi burley and Virginia, fermented under pressure, and presented sliced in plug form. In the aromatic version, the Kendal tradition's measured, clove-like bowl note is applied. The flakes are opened by rubbing out; because pressing fuses the leaves together, the cut stays coarse after rubbing and the burn slows. In the taste, the smoky base of the dark fire-cured leaf, burley's nutty body, and Virginia's sweetness sit stacked together; the topping leaves a fine spicy line over these. Nicotine is above medium, aimed at a smoker used to plug tobaccos.
gawith-hoggarth-co-coniston-cut-plug-aro.o: Clove and spice aromas are accompanied by dry woodsmoke.

pipesandcigars-com-cherry-cordial.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of the pipesandcigars.com blend called Cherry Cordial.

ken-byron-ventures-smooth-criminal.z: A limited-run blend containing Latakia; not enough sources could be found to confirm its contents.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2003.z: Christmas Cheer is the straight Virginia series that Kansas City-based McClelland released once a year, in limited numbers, from the 1980s until the company's closure in early 2018. The series' idea is to present a single Virginia batch selected from that year's harvest on its own; each year is thus considered a separate record, and the year on the tin defines the blend's identity. The 2003 release was prepared the same way, with selected matured Virginia leaf pressed into cake and tinned as broken flake. Records indicate it's among the early-2000s harvest releases. Unflavored Virginia character dominates the smoke: natural leaf sweetness over a bready, herbal base, with a faint tang and a lemony sharpness in the background. Nicotine dose is measured, while flavor intensity is pronounced; it burns cool when smoked slowly, but tends to bite the tongue when rushed. Since the flake's moisture can run high straight from the tin, airing it before packing is common practice. A record aimed at smokers seeking unflavored Virginia who are considering cellaring the tin; not suitable for those expecting an aromatic.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2003.o: A tangy, sharp trace characteristic of McClelland tins mixes into an aroma of dry hay and toasted bread.

smokinjoescigars-com-joes-buttered-rum-3.z: A retailer blend that from its name appears to carry a buttery, rum-direction topping; no source confirming its composition could be found.

tinder-box-royal-estate-espresso.z: Royal Estate Espresso is an aromatic blend from Tinder Box in which a dark espresso and cocoa casing is worked into rested leaves. The Cavendish base carries the sweet side of the casing, while Virginia and Burley leaves give the body a dry depth. The flavor concentrates on the coffee side; roasted-bean and bittersweet chocolate associations come forward rather than sugar. Nicotine load is medium. Suited to those after a dark, sweet aromatic for morning and afternoon smokes.
tinder-box-royal-estate-espresso.o: Leaves a scent of freshly ground espresso and bittersweet cocoa.

petersen-sorensen-vooroogst.z: Vooroogst is a cigar-leaf-based mixture whose name comes from the term used in the Netherlands for the early harvest in cigar-leaf cultivation. The blend contains Burley and Java leaf, with no flavoring added. It is a ribbon cut, presented in a 50 gram tin.
petersen-sorensen-vooroogst.o: Leaves an earthy, sharp leaf aroma recalling cigar ash.

jerris-tobacco-shop-denver-co-autumn-bai.z: No reliable source documenting the content and character of Jerri's Tobacco Shop Denver, CO's Autumn Bairn blend could be found.

telfords-pipes-cigars-north-point.z: One of roughly forty house blends prepared by Telford's Pipe & Cigar shop in Mill Valley, California; no accessible source describing the blend's composition and character could be found.

samuel-gawith-black-forest.z: Black Forest is a ribbon-cut aromatic produced in Kendal by flavoring Virginia and black cavendish leaves with a honey-based casing. Its fluffy structure makes it easy to pack. Honey-derived sweetness leads for most of the bowl; toward the end the tobacco's own plain character becomes more distinct, with the Virginia leaf supporting the burn and leaving light natural flavors beneath the sweetness. Suited to those seeking a measured-sweetness, light-bodied aromatic. According to records, the product is found irregularly on the market.
samuel-gawith-black-forest.o: Leaves a creamy scent evoking honey and sweet dough.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-sungold.z: Sungold is an aromatic Danish blend in Scandinavian Tobacco Group's Skandinavik series. It is formed by combining two separate bright Virginia types with black cavendish; most of the sweetness comes from the cavendish's sugared structure and a vanilla-direction casing. The blend moved from its former name, "Vanilla," to its current name after European Union regulations restricting the use of flavor names on tobacco packaging. The smoke is light and mild, nicotine load is low; with a low risk of biting the tongue, it is a structure pipe newcomers can use comfortably. The dried ribbon cut lights quickly, and since tin moisture is generally high, a short airing burn before packing is usual.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-sungold.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough scent.

paul-olsen-bs-759.z: No reliable source could be found for the Paul Olsen pipe tobacco called BS 759, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

mcclelland-3-oaks-original.z: Three Oaks Original is a Latakia mixture first created by Tad Gage in 1989 and, roughly two decades later, again under his direction, reproduced by McClelland. The blend was withdrawn from the market when the maker ceased operations in 2018. Its structure holds a generous amount of Cyprian Latakia, balanced by quality Oriental leaves and matured Virginia; no flavoring is used. The taste is built on Latakia's smoky, leathery body; the Orientals add a dry, spicy, faintly tangy top layer, while the Virginia supplies sweetness underneath. None of the components is set to overwhelm the others. Nicotine load is medium. A reference record from the McClelland era for smokers who follow classic English and Balkan mixtures and are used to smoky blends.
mcclelland-3-oaks-original.o: Leaves a spiced trace with an intense aroma of wood smoke and leather.

alfie-turmeaus-alfies-blend.z: Alfie's Blend is one of the eponymous blends from Turmeaus, the English tobacconist tracing its origins to 1817, distributed in 50-gram tins through the company's Liverpool-based store chain and C.Gars Ltd. Its weight rests on toasted, oily, mouth-filling Oriental leaf; a small touch of Perique and only trace-level Latakia are added over it. This dosage keeps the blend away from the smoky end of classic English mixtures, with Latakia remaining a light smoky frame in the background rather than a dominant layer. In character it's a medium-strength, unflavored, dry smoke; since it carries no sweetening sauce, the tobacco's own tangy-salty Oriental taste comes forward. Though the tin indicates a higher strength on the maker's scale, the smoke as described sits in the medium band. It suits smokers who like Latakia in moderation, looking for a balanced English mixture to smoke all day, and beginners wanting to get to know Oriental leaf's taste.
alfie-turmeaus-alfies-blend.o: Leaves a dusty trace in the room leaning toward smoked wood and dry hay.

hu-tobacco-geniet-moment.z: Geniet Moment is a flavored blend HU Tobacco prepared as part of its community projects. It's a loose-cut mixture made up of black Cavendish, golden Virginia, and Burley leaves; coffee and vanilla are used in the flavoring. It stays light in nicotine, while the coffee note is pronounced, with vanilla's sweetness sitting beneath it. It's a structure suited to those new to flavored blends and looking for a low-strength, sweet blend that can be smoked all day. Records indicate it's presented in 100-gram tins.
hu-tobacco-geniet-moment.o: Leaves an aroma of freshly brewed coffee and vanilla cream.

kaptn-brammers-rolling-home.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Kapt'n Brammers' Rolling Home blend.

dan-tobacco-kriswill-medium-navy-cut.z: A pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source on the blend's composition or character was found, so no further detail is given.

sutliff-tobacco-company-creamy-buttersco.z: Z89 Creamy Butterscotch is part of Sutliff's bulk-sold aromatic line. Burley, Virginia, and black cavendish leaves are combined in a ribbon cut; the sauce is built around butterscotch and cream. The ribbon cut ensures easy lighting, the body stays light, and the flavor is soft. Suited to those seeking a low-nicotine, all-day aromatic dominated by sweet, milky tones.
sutliff-tobacco-company-creamy-buttersco.o: Leaves a scent of butterscotch and cream.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-field-stre.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the content and character of Match Field & Stream, one of the bulk blends from Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company, could be found.

w-o-larsen-old-tradition.z: This is an aromatic blend known under the W.O. Larsen name; no reliable source could be found documenting its composition and character.

james-fox-harrods-knightsbridge-blend.z: Recorded as a Fox blend prepared for the Harrods shop in Knightsbridge, reported to be Virginia-forward; no detailed maker's description could be found.

cornell-diehl-engine-99.z: Engine #99 is one of Cornell & Diehl's high-Latakia, full-bodied English mixtures, its name referencing a locomotive. It contains Latakia, perique, Virginia, burley, Oriental, and toasted black cavendish. According to available sources, the blend was born from combining the unpressed components of Pirate Kake with Red Odessa. On the palate, Latakia's smoky, tarry character sits against the vinegary, tangy sharpness of the Orientals; perique adds spice and sweetness, while the burley-Virginia pairing carries the body. It is heavy in both nicotine and flavor intensity, suiting smokers accustomed to dark English mixtures.
cornell-diehl-engine-99.o: Leaves a strong room aroma of heavy smoke, tar, and burnt wood.

rain-city-cigar-black-tan.z: This is a house blend from Rain City Cigar, open since 1997 in Seattle's Georgetown neighborhood; there is not enough source material describing its composition and character.

motzek-old-louisiana-mixture.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called Old Louisiana Mixture could be found.

pipe-republic-westgate-on-sea.z: No reliable sources on Pipe Republic's blend Westgate-on-Sea could be found, so its content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-toffee.z: Kendal Gold is one of the shag-cut main bodies produced at Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s Kendal workshop in Cumbria. Its base is a fine golden-hued cut of flame-cured bright Virginia leaf; the producer states it uses no other tobacco type in this series, only cleanly cut Virginia. The Kendal Gold body is offered with numerous different flavorings, and Kendal Gold-Toffee is this family's toffee-flavored member. The toffee flavoring adds a sweet, buttery layer; the bright Virginia base's tart sweetness continues underneath that layer. The fine cut burns fast, calling for loose packing and a measured draw. Aimed at smokers who enjoy sweet aromatics.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-gold-toffee.o: Leaves a burnt-sugar and buttery-caramel aroma.

petersen-sorensen-skipper-special-navy-c.z: No sufficient information from the manufacturer or a reliable product page could be found for the Petersen & Sorensen-branded Skipper Special Navy Cut Mellow Mixture; it is reportedly an aromatic-character blend.

sutliff-tobacco-company-bacchanalia.z: Bacchanalia, taking its name from the festivals held in honor of Rome's god of wine, is a Virginia-burley blend from Sutliff's Private Stock line. A medium-brown, measuredly sweet Virginia leaf forms the base; an earthy, nutty burley is added on top. What sets the blend apart is the red-wine-direction flavoring applied. The topping is of medium intensity, leaving a tangy, sharp edge alongside the sweetness. The dry, bready base of the Virginia-burley structure is still felt beneath the topping; nicotine is medium. A middle-ground option for smokers who keep their distance from heavily sugared aromatics but also find unflavored blends too plain. It went out of production along with the Private Stock line.
sutliff-tobacco-company-bacchanalia.o: A dry tobacco scent mixes into a sweetish grape-and-wine scent.

w-o-larsen-limited-edition-2014.z: No independent source sufficient to complete a record could be found regarding W.O. Larsen's Limited Edition 2014 blend, so this entry remains incomplete.

blatter-blatter-burley.z: Blatter & Blatter's Burley-based house blend; no reliable source documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-captain-earles-h.z: Captain Earle's Honor Blend is an unflavored blend in which red Virginia, Oriental, mild Cavendish, and Perique leaves are stoved and pressed into an old-style crumble cake. It contains no Latakia; its center of gravity is Virginia. The stoving process gives a bready, dark sweetness, while Oriental and Perique build a spice layer in the background. The blend is named in memory of Captain Earle's New Zealand-born wife, Honor Matthews. Captain Earle's tobaccos were created within Hermit Tobacco Works by Jay and Louise Jones; after Jay Jones's death in 2011, production continued through a collaboration with Cornell & Diehl. It's aimed at smokers looking for a full-bodied Virginia blend without Latakia.
hermit-tobacco-works-co-captain-earles-h.o: Leaves an aroma where a light spice trace mixes into the bready sweetness of stoved tobacco.

rauch-lounge-rosalie.z: Rosalie is a flake listed as No. 6 in the house blend series of Rauch Lounge, a tobacco business in Heinsberg, Germany. It is prepared from one hundred percent Virginia leaf, so its sweetness comes largely from the leaf's own sugars. A light flavoring giving coriander and rose oil notes is applied to the blend; the casing is kept light enough not to mask the Virginia base. The maker describes it as medium strength. Being a flake cut, it offers a cool, slow smoke; it suits smokers looking for an exotic, floral top note alongside a classic Virginia structure. It is presented in a 50-gram package.
rauch-lounge-rosalie.o: Leaves a floral, lightly spicy aroma reminiscent of rose oil and coriander seed.

john-cotton-john-cottons-smyrna.z: John Cotton's Smyrna is the Balkan-character member of the brand's classic line, grouped alongside No. 1 and Nos. 1 & 2. It takes its name from Smyrna, the old name for İzmir, and is described as "a blend of Smyrna and other choice tobaccos." In the version that became widespread in the 1970s, Latakia, Virginia, and Turkish leaf appear together; the Oriental share is kept high enough that the blend doesn't collapse into a one-dimensional Latakia bomb. On the smoke, cedar, spice, a dark cocoa-leaning sweetness, and leather notes are reported; nicotine runs a bit above medium without tongue bite. Original production has ended; in 2015 The Standard Tobacco Company of Pennsylvania reissued some blends under the John Cotton name. A profile for those seeking Balkan blends and Oriental-forward smokes.
john-cotton-john-cottons-smyrna.o: Leaves a heavy smoke where dense soot, cedar, and leather aromas carry a spiced sweetness on top.

teds-pipe-shoppe-private-stock.z: One of the house blends prepared at Ted's Pipe Shoppe in Tulsa, Oklahoma; though records show it among the more than forty house blends of the business founded in 1961, no independent source describing the blend's content and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-curly-cut-de-luxe-sli.z: Curly Cut De Luxe is one of the firm's hand-rolled rope tobaccos. Leaves are hand-rolled as in twist-making, pressed, and sliced to give coin-shaped cuts. In the blend, air-cured dark leaf takes up more room than the flavored light-colored leaf. When lit, the dark leaf's nutty, earthy side leads; the light leaf adds a herbal, bright sweetness, and the two trade places through the bowl. Since the slices are tight, they can be packed folded without rubbing out, and burn slowly. Aimed at those familiar with rope-cut texture wanting a natural, unsauced Virginia smoke.
gawith-hoggarth-co-curly-cut-de-luxe-sli.o: Leaves a dry-hay, nutty, and lightly wood-smoke aroma.

paul-olsen-black-cavendish.z: A black cavendish tobacco the Poul Olsen shop sells under its own label, used either on its own or as a topping in blending. Not enough source material documenting its details could be found.

dunhill-marcs-mixture.z: A discontinued blend from Dunhill's line of custom-order mixtures, for which no verifiable source on its composition could be found.

nice-ash-cigars-mild-burley.z: One of Nice Ash Cigars' light, burley-based house blends; not enough source material describing its composition and processing could be found.
nice-ash-cigars-mild-burley.o: No description could be found in the records.

dan-tobacco-cock-robin.z: Cock Robin is one of Dan Tobacco's English-style blends. Virginia leaf makes up the bulk of the mixture, topped with just a pinch of Latakia. That ratio lets the smoky leaf stay in the background without masking the Virginia sweetness; the blend is defined by its unflavored construction and cool smoke. It takes its name from an old English folk song. It's an introductory option for smokers curious about Latakia blends but not ready for heavily smoky mixtures, and also suits those looking for a low-nicotine English mixture they can smoke all day.
dan-tobacco-cock-robin.o: Leaves a lightly sweet trace where wood smoke mingles with dry hay.

hearth-home-house-of-lords.z: House of Lords is one of Hearth & Home's high-Latakia English blends. Its color is dark; its taste carries a heavy smokiness often compared to smoked dried meat or pemmican. Oriental and Virginia leaf play a balancing role beneath that weight. It is noted for burning slowly and producing a heavy volume of smoke; it is recorded as smoking well in a variety of pipe shapes. Aimed at smokers accustomed to Latakia-heavy blends who want an intense flavor.
hearth-home-house-of-lords.o: Leaves a dark aroma reminiscent of smoked meat and wood smoke.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2013.z: Christmas Cheer 2013 is the 2013 release of McClelland's unflavored Virginia series, in which a separate harvest is tinned each year. The leaf is dried by the flue-cure method, matured pressed into cake, sliced, and packaged as broken flake. No flavoring is present in the smoke; sweetness and a bready texture come directly from the leaf, with nicotine dose at medium. The series' well-known sharp tin note is present in this release too. Since releases are made from a single crop, differences appear between years; tins continue to change in character as they're cellared. A record aimed at smokers interested in unflavored Virginia. The brand closed in early 2018.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2013.o: Leaves a tangy, vinegary sweetness along with a toasted-bread aroma.

nat-sherman-205-virginia-perique.z: A Virginia-Perique blend in the numbered pipe tobacco line of New York-based Nat Sherman; sufficient independent sources documenting its composition and character could not be found.

fincks-cigar-company-value-blend-mild-ca.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for Finck's Cigar Company's Value Blend Mild Cavendish pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

kramers-pipe-and-tobacco-shop-english-bl.z: Not enough independent sources could be reached to fill out the record for Kramer's Pipe and Tobacco Shop's blend called English Blend.

villiger-after-dinner.z: No sufficient independent source could be found regarding Villiger's pipe tobacco called After Dinner, so the blend's composition and character could not be recorded.

edwards-blue-ridge.z: This is one of Edward's Pipe & Tobacco's in-house blends prepared in the shop; not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition and character.
edwards-blue-ridge.o: Could not be described due to insufficient records.

peretti-irish-mist.z: One of the house blends from L. J. Peretti's shop in Boston; it appears under the burley blends heading in the maker's listing. No published description of the blend's composition and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.

sutliff-tobacco-company-tobacco-galleria.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Sutliff Tobacco Company's Tobacco Galleria - Classic Vanilla pipe tobacco could be found.

mcclelland-no-5120-fragrant-virginia-ble.z: No. 5120 Fragrant Virginia Blend is a fully rubbed, ribbon-cut blend prepared from red and stoved Virginias in McClelland's bulk catalog. The maker's description uses the term "fragrant"; the blend sits within the brand's lightly essence-touched Virginia line. The flavoring is kept light enough not to mask the tobacco's own taste. In the smoke, stoved Virginia's dark sweetness is joined by a faint fruity top note. Body and nicotine are moderate, and the ribbon cut makes packing and lighting easy. Suited to smokers seeking a lightly sweet Virginia without going toward heavy aromatics. Discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-no-5120-fragrant-virginia-ble.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity aroma with dark tobacco tones.

synjeco-holker-twist.z: Holker Twist, a pipe tobacco from Synjeco; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

fincks-cigar-company-value-blend-virgini.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for Finck's Cigar Company's Value Blend Virginia & Burley pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

samuel-gawith-2013.z: A limited-run Samuel Gawith record from 2013; no independent source documenting its content and character could be found.

mission-pipe-shop-hazelnut.z: Hazelnut is a hazelnut-flavored, cavendish-based house blend that Mission Pipe Shop weighs out in-store; no accessible source documenting its detailed composition and cut could be found.
