r-c-owen-co-gallatin-tenn-red-ox.z: Red Ox is one of the products from R.C. Owen Tobacco Company, which has hand-twisted tobacco in Gallatin, Tennessee since 1931. Like about ten other twist brands from the firm, it is prepared by hand by twisting the leaves into a rope shape and sold in two sizes, small and giant. The leaf used is reportedly a dark-colored variety known as "One Sucker," over a century old; it is thought to be the same as the Ox Tongue tobacco referenced in old texts.
r-c-owen-co-gallatin-tenn-red-ox.o: Leaves a heavy, sharp aroma reminiscent of earth, dry hay, and soot.

rattray-bagpipers-dream.z: Bagpiper's Dream is a blend combining four separate Virginia leaves, flavored with a light brandy casing. The cut isn't uniform: ribbon cut, spun-cut slices, and crumbled flake pieces all sit together in the same tin; this mixed structure requires a little hand-sorting during packing but keeps the burn balanced. The casing stays light enough not to cover Virginia's own sweetness; the pronounced brandy scent from opening the tin translates to something more measured in the smoke. It suits smokers who aren't looking for a heavily flavored product but want a subtle sweetening added to a straight Virginia.
rattray-bagpipers-dream.o: Leaves a sweet, fragrant aroma of grape spirit and dried fruit.

uhles-house-of-uhle.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Uhle's blend called House of Uhle has been found.
uhles-house-of-uhle.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

w-o-larsen-the-masters-blend-dark-flake.z: No reliable source could be found regarding the composition and character of this entry in W.Ø. Larsen's Master's Blend series; the series as a whole generally consists of light, fruit-cased blends.
w-o-larsen-the-masters-blend-dark-flake.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

w-curtis-draper-507.z: 507 is one of the shop-specific numbered blends from Washington-based tobacconist W. Curtis Draper; no sufficient source could be found regarding its composition and character.
w-curtis-draper-507.o: No reliable information could be found regarding the room note.

cornell-diehl-hoodoo-ridge.z: Hoodoo Ridge is one of four traditional plug tobaccos in Cornell & Diehl's Summit series, a line inspired by U.S. national parks. Its composition includes whole-leaf bright and red Virginias, genuine St. James perique, and Izmir-type Oriental, giving it a Virginia-Oriental-Perique structure. Because the leaves are pressed into a dense plug, the flavors meld together over time, producing a smooth smoke. The profile leads with dark stone fruit and vivid citrus, alongside light floral tones and measured spice. It is aimed at smokers accustomed to slicing plug and looking for unflavored, layered Virginia-Perique blends.
cornell-diehl-hoodoo-ridge.o: A light grassy tone accompanies the dark fruit and spice aroma.

mcclelland-smyrna-no-1.z: Smyrna No. 1 is a blend in McClelland's Grand Orientals series, named after the tobaccos of the İzmir (Smyrna) region. It contains İzmir-origin Oriental tobaccos supported by Virginia leaf; the cut is ribbon. On opening the tin, a whole leaf laid over the blend stands out, and the aroma carries the brand's familiar tanginess. In the smoke, Virginia's sweetness comes first, followed by the distinctive flavor of Turkish tobacco. The leaf lights easily; smoked quickly it can run hot and turn bitter, so it calls for a slow smoke. Turkish-language sources note that airing the tin for a few days after opening settles the moisture and flavor. Suited to smokers who want to hear Oriental tobacco as the main ingredient. McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-smyrna-no-1.o: Leaves a dry-hay and sweetish Turkish-tobacco aroma.

mccranies-mellow-mix.z: Mellow Mix is one of McCranie's light aromatic bulk blends; no sufficient sources could be found on its composition.

mac-baren-coconut.z: No sufficient information could be found in the maker's current catalog or in verifiable independent sources for this Mac Baren blend, whose name suggests a coconut flavoring.

edwards-vintage-cube.z: No sufficient independent sourcing could be reached to document the composition and character of Vintage Cube, a pipe tobacco from Edward's.

mac-baren-amphora-english-blend.z: Amphora is a brand with roots in the Netherlands, produced today under Danish Mac Baren. English Blend is the English-type blend in the brand's unflavored line: over a Virginia body come latakia and oriental leaves, plus burley, presented as a ribbon cut. In the smoke, the smoky, woody taste from latakia is decisive; Virginia sweetness and oriental's spicy tone balance this smoky core. It carries no applied flavor. Nicotine stays at a medium level and it's suited to smoking all day. Aimed at those new to smoky English blends and those seeking an unflavored everyday mixture.
mac-baren-amphora-english-blend.o: Leaves a smoky, woody room note reminiscent of a campfire.

torben-dansk-no-15-sailors-flake.z: Torben Dansk No.15 Sailor's Flake is a classic sailor's flake prepared from American and Indian Virginia leaf. Its taste is shaped by traditional pressing followed by aging under low pressure; it is unflavored. It contains darker leaf than No.14 in the same series, giving a noticeably spicier, fuller impression. Suited to smokers who enjoy unflavored Virginia flake and are after tangy, bready notes.
torben-dansk-no-15-sailors-flake.o: Leaves a lightly tangy aroma reminiscent of stale bread and dry hay.

peterson-old-dublin.z: Old Dublin is a Latakia blend built around Cyprus Latakia, described as a mixture close to the Scottish style. It contains golden Virginia, unflavored black Cavendish, and Greek Basma-type Oriental leaf. The unflavored Cavendish gives the blend softness and natural sweetness. It has a medium body, a cool burn, and a smoky-sweet character. For smokers trying Latakia for the first time, it offers a more measured entry point than heavier blends like Nightcap; for those seeking the full intensity of an English blend, it remains an option for everyday smoking. The blend has been in the Peterson catalog for many years.
peterson-old-dublin.o: Leaves a smoky wood and incense aroma with a sweetish trace of dried fruit underneath.

ole-shenandoah-drunken-cherry.z: Drunken Cherry is one of the cherry-essenced aromatic blends in the Ole Shenandoah line; no published description of its composition could be found, and the blend has been discontinued.
ole-shenandoah-drunken-cherry.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweet, cherry-forward scent.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-bourbon-st.z: Bourbon Street Match is a member of Sutliff's Match line, in which the company reinterpreted discontinued blends, and it is based on House of Windsor's Bourbon Street. Sweet Virginia, nutty burley, black cavendish, and strong Kentucky leaf are used together; the casing side carries a measured bourbon-leaning sweetness. The blend gives a rich but soft smoke: a medium-bodied balance is struck between Kentucky's woody weight and cavendish's sweetness. Because the casing is kept at a level that doesn't mask the leaf character, it occupies a middle position that appeals to both aromatic and unflavored blend smokers. Like the entire Match line, this blend went out of production when Sutliff closed in 2025.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-bourbon-st.o: Leaves a sweetish scent recalling bourbon and vanilla alongside woody smoke.

cobblestone-virginia-plug.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Cobblestone pipe tobacco named Virginia Plug, so the blend's content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

gq-tobaccos-cypriot-sunset.z: Cypriot Sunset is one of the eponymous blends from England-based mail-order tobacconist GQ Tobaccos. Red Virginia steeped in a fruity sauce forms the body; joined by sliced black Burma tobacco, Turkish Orientals, dark Virginias, and Cyprian Latakia. A light whiskey touch is applied on top. On the smoke, Latakia's sweet, smoky, woody character is felt without dominating; the Orientals add spice, the Virginias fruity sweetness, and the Burma tobacco adds weight to the body. The flavoring stays light, so the blend falls into the English mixture category rather than the aromatic one. Suited to smokers who want a fruity, lightly spirit-touched top note added to a Latakia blend.
gq-tobaccos-cypriot-sunset.o: A trace of ripe fruit and light whiskey sits within the smoky wood aroma.

cup-o-joes-adirondack-gold-pipe-tobacco.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the Cup O' Joes brand as Adirondack Gold Pipe Tobacco; since neither the maker's own marketing nor independent reliable sources could be reached, the blend's composition, cut, and character could not be confirmed for this entry.

faders-balkan-blend.z: Fader's is a line of house blends offered under its own name by a long-established Baltimore tobacconist; no verifiable source could be found regarding this blend's composition and character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-brandy-alexander.z: A blend listed among Sutliff's brandy-flavored bulk aromatics; sufficient independent sources describing its composition and character could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-brandy-alexander.o: Records indicate it leaves a scent of brandy and creamy sweetness.

sutliff-tobacco-company-english.z: Sutliff English is a bulk English blend combining American- and African-origin Virginia leaves with a good proportion of oriental and a measured amount of Cyprus latakia. Oriental leaf sets the blend's direction; floral, lightly tart notes stand out, with latakia grounding them on a smoky base. Virginia adds enough sweetness to keep the taste from running too dry. It's ribbon cut, unflavored, and offers a medium-bodied smoke. Suited to those seeking an entry-level English blend without a heavy latakia push.
sutliff-tobacco-company-english.o: Leaves a scent of floral spice and wood smoke.

vauen-no-7-crunchy-blend.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Vauen pipe tobacco called No. 7 Crunchy Blend to record the blend's composition and character.

ken-byron-ventures-anne-cap.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Ken Byron Ventures' Anne Cap blend.

peter-heinrichs-chateau-henri-no-44.z: Chateau Henri No. 44 is a dark-colored, spicy-structured Virginia-Kentucky flake described by the Peter Heinrichs house. Per the maker's account, the blend is prepared by pressing high-quality Virginia and Kentucky leaves into slices; Virginia carries natural sweetness and a light nutty bouquet while fire-cured Kentucky lays down a smoky, full base layer. Because of its unflavored structure, the taste comes from the tobacco's own processing: as the slices are rubbed out, Virginia sweetness comes forward first, followed by Kentucky's earth and smoke notes. It is described as sitting above medium in nicotine and as a slow, cool-burning flake. It is a record aimed at smokers interested in unflavored, full-bodied Virginia-Kentucky slices who are used to rubbing out flake.
peter-heinrichs-chateau-henri-no-44.o: A smoky aroma recalling wood fire leaves a dry-hay sweetness behind it.

wessex-original.z: This is described as a Virginia-based blend in the Wessex series; detailed composition and character information could not be found in verifiable sources.
wessex-original.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

clan-shaw-caribbean-sea.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Caribbean Sea.

gawith-hoggarth-co-gawith-red.z: Gawith Red is a blend built mostly from air-cured leaf, developed as an option to replace Amphora Red in the English market. Its composition includes Burley, Kentucky, Oriental, and Virginia; Kentucky provides body and earthy depth, while Oriental carries a spicy edge. Records indicate a very light floral essence is applied on top; because of this, the blend isn't quite unflavored, but stays fairly restrained compared to the heavy sauces of Lakeland style. Suited to smokers wanting an everyday nutty, bready blend where sweetness doesn't lead.
gawith-hoggarth-co-gawith-red.o: Leaves a light floral note over a nutty tobacco aroma.

my-smoking-shop-hazelnut-cream.z: A bulk aromatic flavored with a hazelnut-and-cream sauce; sufficient sources describing its leaf composition could not be found.

e-a-carey-old-scotch.z: A blend registered under the E. A. Carey name; it does not appear on the maker's current list, and not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition.

comptons-of-galashiels-york-medium-mixtu.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Compton's of Galashiels pipe tobacco named York Medium Mixture, so the blend's content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

cornell-diehl-43rd-anniversary-blend-bon.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Cornell & Diehl blend 43rd Anniversary Blend/Bonfiglioli.

cao-bella-vanilla.z: Bella Vanilla is a soft aromatic in CAO's pipe tobacco wing. Rubbed virginia slices are seasoned with Madagascar vanilla-bean extract, joined by rich black cavendish. Per records it is prepared in the Danish style and is neither cut wet nor in ribbon, but comes in a ready-rubbed slice form. A creamy sweetness and pronounced vanilla come forward in the smoke, with the virginia base forming a sweet foundation behind it. Its measured moisture makes it easy to light and keep lit. Suitable for smokers seeking a classic vanilla aromatic while wanting to avoid a syrupy texture.
cao-bella-vanilla.o: Leaves a pure vanilla-bean and sweet dough aroma.

comoys-of-london-cask-4-stand-fast-navy.z: Blend No. 4 in Comoy's of London's Cask series is an unflavored Virginia-perique mixture prepared in the traditional navy-flake style. Ripened Virginia leaves are pressed together with Louisiana perique and sliced; the flake can be smoked rubbed out or folded into the bowl. On the flavor channel, the Virginias' bready, dried-fruit-leaning sweetness leads; perique layers on top of that a dark-fruit, plum-like note with a peppery spice. It suits smokers looking for an unflavored, medium-bodied, slow-smoking flake. According to available records, Comoy's Cask series has not been in production for some time.
comoys-of-london-cask-4-stand-fast-navy.o: Leaves a bready tobacco aroma carrying a dried-fruit sweetness, with a light pepper trace.

samuel-gawith-curly-cut.z: Curly Cut is an unflavored blend Samuel Gawith obtains by slicing twisted virginia rope into coin form. It rests on the old rope and curly-cut production method continued at the Kendal factory; each slice shows the cross-section of the spirally wound leaf. Its character is built on the sweetness coming from virginia's own sugar, along with dry hay and cooked-fruit tones; nicotine stays medium. The slices need crumbling and drying. Suited to smokers seeking unflavored virginia and the intensity of twisted cuts.
samuel-gawith-curly-cut.o: Leaves a sweet dry-hay and cooked-fruit scent.

faders-istanbul.z: Not enough independent sourcing documenting the composition and character of Istanbul, one of the house blends of the Baltimore-based Fader's tobacconist, could be found.

james-barber-golden-dutch-shag.z: A fine shag-cut blend sold under his own name by James Barber, a longstanding English tobacconist based in Harrogate; no independent source could be found to document its contents and character, so no further detail is given.

sutliff-tobacco-company-dutch-masters-ch.z: Dutch Masters Cherry Cavendish is a cherry-flavored blend in Sutliff's Dutch Masters line. Black cavendish, burley, and cavendish leaves are combined in a coarse ribbon cut; the sauce is built on cherry liqueur. Per the maker's description, the leaves are sourced from Europe, Africa, and North and South America, and the blend is rested slowly to preserve its natural tobacco flavor. Tart cherry is prominent in the pouch aroma; on the palate the sauce is kept restrained enough not to overtake the tobacco, so leaf flavor is noticeable. Body is light. Suited to smokers seeking classic cherry aromatics.
sutliff-tobacco-company-dutch-masters-ch.o: A sugary sweetness accompanies a tart cherry-liqueur scent.

dunhill-my-mixture-36609.z: A discontinued mixture belonging to Dunhill's My Mixture line, for which no verifiable source on its composition could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-black-raspberry.z: Black Raspberry, listed under the Sutliff Tobacco Company name, is a raspberry-flavored aromatic blend as its name suggests; no reliable source on its composition and cut could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-festivus-cheer.z: A blend from Ken Byron Ventures' limited holiday-season Festivus series; no independent source could be found to document its contents.
ken-byron-ventures-festivus-cheer.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

mcclelland-penmans-choice.z: Presented as a very mild aromatic with no harsh edges within McClelland's Penman line; no sufficient source describing its contents could be found.
mcclelland-penmans-choice.o: Leaves a mild, lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of old-fashioned tobacco shops.

comptons-of-galashiels-balkan.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Compton's of Galashiels blend Balkan.

d-r-tobacco-avanti.z: A blend in the catalogue of North Carolina-based Daughters & Ryan (D & R); no adequate source describing its composition and character was found.

cornell-diehl-longevity-ii.z: No adequate source documenting the composition and character of Cornell & Diehl's Longevity II blend could be found; the blend isn't in the maker's current catalogue.

sutliff-tobacco-company-taste-of-spring.z: Taste of Spring is the spring member of Sutliff's season-named aromatic line; no reliable source on its content and character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-taste-of-spring.o: No reliable record of a room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-black-knight.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to describe the content of this blend, which does not currently appear in the Cornell & Diehl catalog.

rattray-macbeth.z: Macbeth is among Rattray's unflavored blends, said to be based on an old recipe. It is a ribbon-cut mixture prepared by combining select Virginia leaf with Burley, carrying no flavoring. The blend's taste is built between Virginia's natural sweetness and Burley's nutty, earthy body; strength is medium and its room note stays measured. It suits smokers looking for an unflavored everyday blend, especially those transitioning from flavored tobaccos to plain mixtures. The Rattray name draws on the Scottish pipe-tobacco tradition; the brand's tobaccos are produced today in Germany.
rattray-macbeth.o: Leaves a plain tobacco aroma reminiscent of dry hay and nutshell.

trebol-american-mixture.z: No sufficient source documenting the composition of the Trébol blend American Mixture has been found.
trebol-american-mixture.o: No reliable source describing the room note has been found.

schurch-almandino-319.z: One of the flavored mixtures in the series of tobaccos Hans Schürch has hand-blended since 1964, named after precious stones; no sufficient source documenting its content could be found.
schurch-almandino-319.o: Recorded as leaving a sweet, cased scent.

the-briary-ephemeris-tobacco-the-finest-.z: Ephemeris is a straight Virginia blend hand-prepared at the counter by The Briary, a tobacconist in Homewood, Alabama. The maker states that several Virginia leaves are combined, with no cavendish or any other casing in the blend. The goal is to build a balance no single leaf could achieve on its own, bringing softness, tang, and natural sugary sweetness together in the same bowl. Because it carries no casing, the taste comes entirely from the leaf's own notes of grass, hay, and light fruit. The nicotine load stays below medium, making it suitable for long smokes throughout the day. It is meant for smokers moving over from flavored blends toward natural Virginias, as well as for lovers of straight Virginia smokes. The blend is sold only at The Briary's own shop.
the-briary-ephemeris-tobacco-the-finest-.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay with a light, bready tobacco note.

sterling-tobacco-co-chairman-of-the-boar.z: Chairman of the Board is a light English mixture from Sterling Tobacco Company, which blends tobacco to order in the town of Sterling, Illinois. Per the maker's description, the blend contains costly oriental leaves such as Dubek, Yenidje, and Mahala, along with sun-cured Virginia, light-colored burley, and latakia. The weight of the oriental leaves sets this blend apart from classic English mixtures where latakia dominates. Black latakia sprinkled among leaves in tones of light mahogany, caramel, and camel-hair stands out visually. On opening the tin, a floral sweetness comes with a biscuity grain note; on the palate, latakia stays in the background as a smoke layer, while the orientals' dry spice comes forward. Nicotine is medium, and flavor intensity is above average. Being unflavored, it suits smokers not seeking aromatic sweetness who are interested in oriental-forward light English mixtures.
sterling-tobacco-co-chairman-of-the-boar.o: Carries dry bread and a floral sweetness over a light smokiness.

brigham-wild-cherry.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named Wild Cherry under the Brigham brand could be found.

mcclelland-3-oaks-syrian.z: 3 Oaks Syrian is a blend McClelland built around Syrian Latakia. The blend's original recipe was prepared by Tad Gage for a tobacconist near Kansas City, and McClelland produced it to this recipe starting in 2009. What sets it apart from Three Oaks Original, the same series' Latakia-free/Cyprian-Latakia version, is that it's rebuilt around Syrian Latakia, which gives a milder, less sharp smoke. Its contents hold Syrian Latakia, sweet Oriental tobaccos, and aged Virginia. The coarsely cut ribbon-form tobacco consists of a mix of brown, bronze, and black leaves, with moisture at a level smokable straight out of the tin. The woody-sooty side of the Latakia smoke is balanced by the Virginia's sweetness; a blend designed for smokers used to Latakia who seek the taste of classic Syrian-Latakia mixtures. Withdrawn from the market when McClelland stopped production in 2018.
mcclelland-3-oaks-syrian.o: Leaves a mild, sweetish soot aroma reminiscent of a wood fire.

emerson-southern-forged-connemara.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing was found for the Emerson Southern Forged brand's Connemara blend, so the entry has been left open; records place it in the Virginia/Perique family.

hill-hill-tobacconists-virginia-puro.z: This is a house blend of Hill & Hill Tobacconists based, as the name suggests, on unflavored Virginia leaf; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found.
hill-hill-tobacconists-virginia-puro.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

wessex-red-virginia-flake.z: Red Virginia Flake is a medium-thickness Navy Cut flake made from red Virginia leaf. It's unflavored Virginia, pressed and then sliced into flakes and tinned. The flavor description notes tart dry grass, raisin, and bread notes with a wine-like finish. It's said to be smooth enough not to bite the tongue even when drawn quickly; nicotine sits in the mild-to-medium band. It suits smokers seeking an unflavored red Virginia character in flake form.
wessex-red-virginia-flake.o: Leaves a scent of dry grass, raisin, and bread crust.

nat-sherman-363-riverside-whisky.z: An aromatic among Nat Sherman's numbered house blends, flavored with a whiskey aroma; no independent source documenting its detailed composition could be found.
nat-sherman-363-riverside-whisky.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly oaky and caramel-leaning aroma reminiscent of whiskey.

sutliff-tobacco-company-mountain-pass.z: Mountain Pass, part of Sutliff's Private Stock line, is an aromatic built on black and golden cavendish. By design, the leaf's own flavor is kept in the background; what stands out is a buttery, creamy vanilla custard taste. A light honey sweetness from the golden cavendish rounds out the picture. It is a light-to-medium blend in nicotine that doesn't bite the tongue. The cut is ribbon, and it presents a drier leaf compared to the same maker's heavier, moister aromatics. Aimed at those seeking a smoke where the sweet topping, rather than the tobacco flavor, is the defining trait.
sutliff-tobacco-company-mountain-pass.o: Leaves a scent of creamy vanilla custard and butter.

robert-mcconnell-flake.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of Robert McConnell Flake.

jerris-tobacco-shop-denver-co-prime-mini.z: No reliable source documenting the content and character of Jerri's Tobacco Shop Denver, CO's Prime Minister blend could be found.

peter-stokkebye-late-night.z: This is a pipe tobacco listed under the name Late Night in the catalogs of the Danish brand Peter Stokkebye; the profile is left incomplete, as no independent sources documenting the blend's composition and character could be found.

paul-olsen-no-111.z: No. 111 is the flake in Danish Paul Olsen's My Own Blend line. North Carolina-sourced Virginia leaves form the base, joined by perique and fire-cured Kentucky. Straight out of the tin, the moisture level is ready for smoking; the slices catch easily and burn evenly with little intervention. The taste is full and the strength moderate; amid Virginia's natural, measured sweetness, a note recalling bergamot and perique's spice appear in turn, with a light sharpness felt on the retrohale. It suits smokers looking for a balanced Virginia flake where perique doesn't dominate.
paul-olsen-no-111.o: Leaves a lightly spiced trace mingling with dry grass and bread-crust aromas.

virginia-gold-cherry-cavendish.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Virginia Gold pipe tobacco called Cherry Cavendish to record the blend's composition and character.

hearth-home-darbyshire.z: Darbyshire is described as a lightly topped Virginia-Burley blend that Hearth & Home released as a one-time offering for World Pipe Smoking Day; there is not enough independent sourcing available for it.

low-country-pipe-cigar-natural-virginia-.z: One of the house blends of South Carolina-based Low Country Pipe & Cigar; described as a Virginia-burley mixture, but not enough sources could be found to describe its character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-ts11-cigar-leaf.z: TS-11 Cigar Leaf is the cigar leaf in Sutliff's blending-component line. According to the maker's description, it is prepared from the tip sections of Pennsylvania-origin maduro cigar leaves, loosely cut, with a casing applied that sweetens and darkens the leaf. It is offered in large, resealable packs. The taste is dark, earthy, and woody; nicotine and taste intensity are on the high side. It is positioned primarily as a filler leaf that blenders preparing their own mixtures use to add a cigar character to pipe blends. It suits smokers wanting a cigar taste in their pipe when used in small proportions.
sutliff-tobacco-company-ts11-cigar-leaf.o: Leaves a dark, earthy, sweet-woody scent reminiscent of cigar tobacco.

jons-pipe-shop-majestic.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Jon's Pipe Shop's Majestic pipe tobacco.

cornell-diehl-tartus.z: No listing for Cornell & Diehl's Tartus blend could be found in the maker's current catalogue or in major retailer listings; its composition and character could not be confirmed.

pfeifen-huber-epikur.z: Epikur is the Munich house Pfeifen Huber's unflavored Virginia blend, sold as a plug, meaning a pressed block. Only Virginia leaf is used in the blend, with no flavoring added. Plug tobaccos are made by pressing leaf under high pressure; this method helps the tobacco retain moisture over long periods and is recorded as having historically been developed to keep tobacco from drying out on long sea voyages. Before smoking, the block needs to be cut into cubes or thin flakes and then aired. Turkish-language records report that the tobacco is exceptionally moist straight out of the box, that it stays damp inside even after months left open, and that this creates real difficulty in lighting and keeping it lit. It offers a medium strength and medium-intensity flavor; it suits smokers willing to do patient preparation who are seeking an unflavored Virginia and pressed-tobacco experience.
pfeifen-huber-epikur.o: Leaves a plain tobacco aroma leaning toward dry straw and baked bread.

gawith-hoggarth-co-no-25-mixture.z: No. 25 Mixture is a light English blend where the Latakia ratio is kept measured. Light and dark Virginias make up the bulk of the body; Latakia sits as a spicy, herbal frame over this sweet base. A cool-burning, ribbon-cut blend, light to medium in nicotine. This makes it suitable for all-day smoking. Suited to smokers who prefer Latakia in balance rather than intensity, or to those new to English mixtures.
gawith-hoggarth-co-no-25-mixture.o: Leaves a smoke aroma mixing light smoke with dry hay.

paul-olsen-mester-blanding.z: Mester Blanding is the aromatic mixture in the My Own Blend line carrying the master blender's signature. Its base is built from Virginia and cavendish leaves, topped with vanilla, passion fruit (maracuja), and tonka bean essence. This trio pulls Virginia's natural sweetness toward a tropical, creamy direction. Nicotine load is measured and the smoke stays mellow in the mouth. It suits newcomers to aromatic tobaccos and smokers looking for a pronounced topping aroma. The blend belongs to the series that today carries on the personal-blending tradition Paul Olsen began in Copenhagen in 1939; it has also been released in annual editions.
paul-olsen-mester-blanding.o: Leaves an intense bakery scent mingling vanilla, tropical fruit, and sweet almond-tonka aromas.

smokers-haven-krumble-kake.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Smokers' Haven blend Krumble Kake could not be found.

thepiperoom-com-black-forest.z: No independent source documenting the composition of the ThePipeRoom.com house blend Black Forest has been found; the brand's own site is no longer online.
thepiperoom-com-black-forest.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-ripples-brown-.z: Referred to as a blend within the Ripples series registered under the Danish Orlik Tobacco Company A/S name; no reliable source describing its composition and character could be found.
orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-ripples-brown-.o: No description could be found in the records.

lane-limited-hg-2000.z: One of Lane Limited's bulk ribbon-cut aromatic blends; still listed by retailers as a member of the code-named Lane series. Since no independent source detailing the blend's leaf composition and casing could be found, these fields have been left blank.

cornell-diehl-bright-flake.z: As its name suggests, this product appears to be a flake pressed from bright Virginia leaf; its content and character could not be verified, as it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog.

pipesandcigars-com-match-blue-boar.z: No independent sources sufficient to complete a full profile of pipesandcigars.com's blend Match Blue Boar could be found.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-cherry-vanilla.z: Cherry Vanilla is built from golden-cut cavendish along with black and fire-cured cavendish leaves; cherry and vanilla aromas are added in balanced proportion on top. It gives a slow-burning, soft smoke that does not turn sharp. The blend was introduced in 2021. Suitable for aromatic smokers seeking the classic fruit-and-sweet pairing where neither casing overpowers the other.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-cherry-vanilla.o: Leaves a sweet, pastry-like aroma from cherry and vanilla together.

seattle-pipe-club-hogshead-bourbon-barre.z: Hogshead Bourbon Barrel Aged, signed by Seattle Pipe Club, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

dunhill-ultra-mild.z: Ultra Mild is a Virginia-burley-based blend in Dunhill's low-intensity wing. Virginia's sweetness is balanced against burley's nutty body, with a light plum topping applied; per records, the mixture also contains a small amount of menthol leaving a cooling effect. It's ribbon cut and among the mildest nicotine-wise in the line. It's a tobacco for those seeking a long, untiring smoke at any hour of the day, or newcomers to the pipe avoiding strong mixtures. Due to regulations restricting the use of terms like "mild" and "light" on tobacco packaging, the blend was withdrawn from the UK market and sold mainly in Japan. Following Dunhill's 2017 decision to end pipe tobacco production, the blend was discontinued.
dunhill-ultra-mild.o: Leaves a light plum sweetness and roasted hazelnut scent, with a cooling hint of mint sensed behind it.

clubmaster-superior-mini-brown-chocolate.z: Clubmaster Superior Mini Brown Chocolate is not a pipe tobacco but a mini-sized cigarillo made from cigar leaf. It is produced in Germany using mild tobaccos of Brazilian origin; the leaf is flavored to give a chocolate taste. The body is extremely light, the smoking time short, and the pack contains twenty pieces. It was included in this pipe-tobacco guide because it is encountered on the same shelves and referenced as a light, chocolate-flavored alternative. It is a product aimed at those wanting a short, light smoke with a pronounced flavoring.
clubmaster-superior-mini-brown-chocolate.o: Leaves a pronounced aroma of cocoa and chocolate.

smokers-pride-menthol-taste.z: Smoker's Pride Menthol Taste is a blend where a pronounced menthol flavoring is applied over a medium-bodied American base of burley and Virginia leaves. The leaf mix stays in line with the rest of the series; what sets the product apart is the menthol topping, which cools the smoke and leaves a minty effect on the palate. It's prepared in ribbon cut and sold in 340-gram bags. Because menthol overrides the tobacco's natural flavors, the blend suits those seeking a cooling smoke rather than the classic burley-Virginia character. Nicotine strength is medium-light. As is common with mentholated tobaccos, since the scent can cling to the pipe and smoker for a long time, smoking it in a dedicated pipe is standard practice.
smokers-pride-menthol-taste.o: A sharp mint and menthol scent fills the room with a light tobacco tone beneath it.

the-ridge-pipe-tobacco-helms-deep.z: No reliable source could be found on The Ridge Pipe Tobacco's Helm's Deep blend.

john-cotton-john-cottons-latakia-re-rele.z: A pipe tobacco blend released under the John Cotton name; not enough independent sources could be found to document its contents and character.
john-cotton-john-cottons-latakia-re-rele.o: No source could be found on the room note.

blatter-blatter-arome-de-la-nuit.z: One of the house blends prepared at the counter of the Blatter & Blatter shop in Montreal; no reliable source documenting its content could be found.

iwan-ries-three-star-red.z: This is a blend from the Three Star line prepared over the counter by the Chicago-based tobacconist Iwan Ries & Co.; no independent source detailing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
iwan-ries-three-star-red.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

tavern-tobacco-co-grey-man-flake.z: A Tavern Tobacco Co. blend that, as its name suggests, is flake-cut; no accessible source documenting its composition could be found.

pearl-tobacco-company-colliers-ready-rub.z: A blend registered under the Pearl Tobacco Company name, apparently a ready-rubbed cut judging by its name; no reliable source about the maker or composition could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-cherry-12.z: Also known as Cherry Cavendish, #12 is one of Sutliff's longest-running bulk aromatics. Cavendish leaves are combined with soft burley and bright Virginia; a cherry liqueur flavoring is applied on top. The topping is noticeable but not heavy. The smoke is soft and full-bodied, though nicotine strength is light and tongue bite is low. The ribbon cut makes packing easy. A type of blend that those new to fruity aromatics frequently gravitate toward.
sutliff-tobacco-company-cherry-12.o: Leaves a scent of sweet cherry liqueur and sugared fruit.

murray-sons-co-ltd-punchbowle.z: Punchbowle was part of a trio of blends produced by Murray, Sons & Co of Belfast, Northern Ireland, on behalf of John Sinclair Ltd. Compared with Parson's Pleasure and Barney's in the same series, this blend has the highest Latakia proportion; virginia leaves build the body, latakia is added as the spice, and records indicate no sweetener or top-flavoring is applied to the blend at all. In the smoke, latakia's smoky, leather-like layer sits over virginia's dry, lightly sweet base; being unflavored, the taste comes directly from the leaf. This production ended when the Murray factory closed in January 2005; later productions carrying the name were made by other companies. It can be recommended for smokers seeking a classic English blend who enjoy latakia at a moderate level.
murray-sons-co-ltd-punchbowle.o: Leaves a trace of dry hay beneath the aroma of wood smoke and soot.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-merryval-likrish.z: Merryval Likrish is a McGahey house blend, reportedly launched in 1988, in which licorice-root flavoring dominates both the aroma and the taste. Sufficient sources regarding its leaf composition and cut could not be found.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-merryval-likrish.o: Leaves a dark, anise-toned aroma reminiscent of licorice candy.

bufflehead-stellars-eider.z: Bufflehead was a brand producing small batches in the United States in the early 2000s, naming its blends after waterfowl; since no independent source describing this blend's content and character could be found, the entry has been left incomplete.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-chieftains-islay.z: Not enough independent sources could be reached to fill out the record for Kohlhase, Kopp und Co. KG's blend called Chieftain's Islay Mixture.

bufflehead-red-throated-loon.z: Bufflehead was a brand producing small batches in the United States in the early 2000s, naming its blends after waterfowl; since no independent source describing this blend's content and character could be found, the entry has been left incomplete.

tabacos-catarinenses-ltda-havana-laranja.z: Havana Laranja is an orange-flavored pipe tobacco in Tabacos Catarinenses' Havana line. According to the maker's description, it is prepared by homogeneously blending selected tobaccos with aromatic casing; like the other members of the line, it is built on a Virginia- and Burley-forward body. In Brazil it is generally distributed in 40-45 gram packs, sold in multi-packs. The citrus aroma stands out both in the tin note and on the smoke; the tobacco's own character stays in the background, and nicotine is kept low. It is a blend meant for smokers new to aromatic tobaccos or looking for a fruity, light smoke.
tabacos-catarinenses-ltda-havana-laranja.o: Leaves a citrus scent reminiscent of orange peel.

dan-tobacco-shannon-flake.z: Shannon Flake belongs to Dan Tobacco's Treasures of Ireland line, dedicated to Ireland. Virginia, burley and black cavendish are brought together, flavored with a fruity coating, then pressed and sliced into flake. While burley gives the blend an earthy body and nicotine, Virginia provides cool sweetness and black cavendish softness. Because of its flake structure it burns slowly; the slice needs to be rubbed out and aired a bit before smoking. It suits smokers on the aromatic side who still want a full-bodied smoke and don't mind flake preparation.
dan-tobacco-shannon-flake.o: Leaves a fruity, lightly caramel-sweet scent.

mac-baren-hh-pure-virginia.z: HH Pure Virginia, as its name suggests, is a flake made solely from Virginia leaves. Top grades of red and light-colored Virginias sourced from North America and Brazil are matured through hot pressing; this process fuses the leaves' flavors and gives the blend a light fermented sweetness. Like the rest of the HH series, casing is minimal and it carries no top flavor. In the smoke, the red Virginia's tangy sweetness, reminiscent of dried dark fruit, moves alongside the light leaf's grass, hay and citrus tones, while the brown Virginia adds an earthy sweetness. The slices crumble easily, and moisture is at a level suited to smoking. Nicotine load is moderate. Suited to those wanting to know unflavored Virginia character in its plain form and those seeking a mild flake to smoke throughout the day; its tin also suits cellaring.
mac-baren-hh-pure-virginia.o: Leaves a fine, sweetish scent reminiscent of dry hay and citrus peel.

petersen-sorensen-bankers.z: Banker's is a smoky mixture in which Latakia is combined with Virginia and Oriental leaf. What sets the blend apart is the Havana cigar leaf included in its composition; it is counted among the small number of pipe tobaccos that include a notable proportion of cigar leaf. With its medium-full body, it is aimed at smokers familiar with classic English mixtures who are seeking an earthy, spicy taste. The brand is Danish in origin; the products are reportedly produced in Germany by Planta.
petersen-sorensen-bankers.o: An intense smoky aroma is mixed with the earthy scent of cigar leaf.

solani-779-english-luxury-mixture.z: Solani 779 is the brand's gold-labeled English blend. It presents a classic composition of latakia, oriental (Turkish) leaf, and Virginia in ribbon cut; it carries no flavoring. Moisture may run high when the tin is opened, and letting it rest for a while brings out the blend's character more clearly. Strength and flavor sit at a medium level; rather than a structure full of surprises, it draws a measured, familiar English mixture profile. Suited to those wanting latakia at a ratio that doesn't crush the body and seeking a balanced smoke-and-oriental composition for everyday smoking.
solani-779-english-luxury-mixture.o: Latakia's woody smoke scent settles into the room, leaving a dry oriental sharpness behind it.

hu-tobacco-great-dixter.z: Great Dixter is a flavored blend in HU Tobacco's United Passion line, taking its name from the famous English garden. Light-colored loose-cut Virginia and a small amount of white Burley are added to a base obtained by rubbing out medium-brown Virginia flake. The flavoring is built on geranium; because of this the blend carries a directly floral, rather than fruity, character. It offers a medium-strength, light, and mild smoke. It forms a separate category for those wanting to try a flavoring outside the usual vanilla-fruit axis. Records indicate it's presented in 50-gram tins.
hu-tobacco-great-dixter.o: Leaves a sharp floral aroma reminiscent of geranium leaf along with a light herbal trace.

bulwark-cut-plug.z: Bulwark Cut Plug is, per records, a British-origin plug tobacco released by Bristol-based W. D. & H. O. Wills; today its name survives only in old advertisements and collector records. The entry has been left incomplete as no sufficient independent source describing the blend's content and smoking character could be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-mayflower.z: Mayflower No.1 is among the classic Danish-style blends prepared by putting Virginia and burley leaves through the cavendish process. A measured, not-pronounced sweet aroma is applied on top. It is produced in Denmark by Scandinavian Tobacco Group. The smoke is mild, nicotine stays light, and it has a low tendency to bite the tongue. A suitable middle ground for smokers who don't want the intensity of strong aromatics but also find unflavored blends too dry.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-mayflower.o: Leaves a light, sweet, measured scent evoking candied fruit.

cornell-diehl-from-beyond.z: This is a Cornell & Diehl blend recorded as an English type; its composition and character could not be verified as it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog.

gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-flake.z: Dark Flake is an unflavored blend produced by combining Malawi-origin fire-cured leaf and Indian-origin air-cured dark leaf in equal proportions, then pressing and slicing them. No flavoring or topping is applied; the taste comes entirely from the leaves' curing method. The slices are dark, heavy, and oily. On the smoke, the fire-cured leaf's smoky taste combines with the sweeter, cigar-like body of the air-cured dark leaf. Nicotine sits at the highest end of the catalog, though thanks to the pressed structure, the burn is slow and cool. Well suited to a small-chambered pipe, on a full stomach, and for short sessions. An entry for experienced smokers seeking dark, very strong tobaccos; not suited to those new to the pipe.
gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-flake.o: A heavy aroma of intense smoke, burnt wood, and cigar-like leaf fills the room.

cornell-diehl-bayou-night.z: Cornell & Diehl Bayou Night is an unflavored blend falling into the Scottish-style mixture class, built from Latakia, perique, Virginia, Oriental leaves, and burley. Compared to classic examples of the type, the perique proportion is kept noticeably high; this choice defines the blend's character throughout. A peppery sharpness is noticeable from the first puffs; Latakia builds the smoky frame, Virginia and burley balance the body, and Oriental leaves leave a dry spice layer in the background. It sits on the hearty end for nicotine and flavor. It suits experienced smokers wanting to see Latakia and perique together, both at a high dose.
cornell-diehl-bayou-night.o: Leaves a smoky wood aroma in the room, topped with sharp pepper and dark fruit.

tabac-benden-shamkat.z: Shamkat is Tabac Benden's blend revisiting the Oriental-forward Krüll tradition common in German-speaking countries before the Second World War. Its name comes from Shamhat in the Epic of Gilgamesh. Selected Lebanese Oriental, chosen for its body and leaf structure, is combined with mature medium-brown Virginias; production takes place at the Dan Tobacco Manufactory in Lauenburg. The cut is loose: the leaves are neither too fine nor too coarse, sitting as large pieces that are easy to pack by ordinary methods. The taste leans savory-spicy rather than sweet; grassy and floral notes stand out alongside nutty and dry-spice tones, with Virginia providing measured sweetness from behind. The body is light to medium and carries no bitterness. It suits smokers looking for a Latakia-free Oriental blend with low nicotine and a spicy smoke.
tabac-benden-shamkat.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay, spice, and a fine mineral note.

cornell-diehl-green-river-vanilla.z: Green River Vanilla is one of Cornell & Diehl's best-known aromatics. Its base is burley leaf grown in the Green River valley, often used in black cavendish production for how well it holds flavoring; after the leaf is sweetened and toasted, it receives a heavy vanilla flavoring and is offered as a ribbon cut. On the smoke, tobacco body stays in the background while soft, sweet vanilla leads; nicotine is low and the texture is soft. It suits newcomers to aromatics and anyone wanting a simple, pronounced sweet room-note blend.
cornell-diehl-green-river-vanilla.o: A heavy, sweet vanilla and sugared-tobacco aroma spreads through the room.

straus-tobacco-fountain-square.z: Fountain Square is one of the counter blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; records indicate the shop was founded in 1880 and that most of its house blends were named after Cincinnati neighborhoods and landmark buildings. Since no independent source on the blend's composition and character could be found, this record is kept at listing level only.

peter-stokkebye-champagne-no-35.z: PS35 Champagne is a bulk aromatic the Peter Stokkebye house prepared for its 110th anniversary. The base is built from selected Virginias and Mexican Burley; sweet black Cavendish in two distinct cuts is added on top. A light essence recalling French forest fruits is used as flavoring, and the blend is cut into a medium-loose ribbon. The profile is a measured sweetness; the flavoring comes forward but is kept at a level that doesn't overwhelm the leaf's own taste. Nicotine is low and the smoke is mild. It suits smokers who enjoy aromatic blends but want to avoid heavily sugared flavorings, and who are seeking a light tobacco for all-day smoking.
peter-stokkebye-champagne-no-35.o: Leaves a lightly fruity, sweetish, floral aroma.

nat-sherman-518-soho-high-noon.z: One of Nat Sherman's numbered aromatic house blends; no independent source documenting its composition and character could be found.

mcclelland-mcraspberry.z: No sufficient independent source describing the contents of this raspberry-flavored blend from the bulk aromatic series could be found; records indicate production stopped before McClelland's closure.
mcclelland-mcraspberry.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity aroma reminiscent of raspberry.

vincenzo-white.z: Vincenzo White is a mixture bringing together North American tobaccos and Oriental leaf. Gold and brown Virginia leaves are joined by Macedonian-origin Oriental tobacco with a small amount of Latakia. It is unflavored. The Virginia base lays a bready, lightly sweet foundation; the Oriental leaf adds a spicy, dry top note, while the small dash of Latakia adds a thin thread of smoke to the mix. Nicotine and flavor sit at a medium level. Suited to smokers after a balanced English-American blend with low Latakia intensity.
vincenzo-white.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay and lightly smoky tobacco.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-captain-earles-r.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for this blend, part of the Captain Earle's line, described as American type.

smoker-friendly-whiskey.z: The whiskey-flavored product in the Smoker Friendly private-label line; no independent source describing the blend's leaf composition could be found.

gatlin-burlier-chimney-smoke.z: Chimney Smoke is one of the house blends of the Gatlinburlier tobacconist in Gatlinburg. Roasted black Cavendish leaf is flavoured with vanilla and a small amount of maple syrup. The cut is kept relatively large so it burns cool, and the moisture is set low enough that it won't go out. The tobacco's own taste is light; what stands out is the topping, which, while noticeable, is kept measured enough not to leave weight on the palate. It is a shop blend prepared to reduce the excessive moisture and gurgling issue often seen in aromatic blends; it suits smokers seeking a classic vanilla cavendish.
gatlin-burlier-chimney-smoke.o: Leaves a sweet aroma leaning toward vanilla and maple syrup.

bufflehead-root-head-decoy.z: Bufflehead was a brand producing small batches in the United States in the early 2000s, naming its blends after waterfowl; since no independent source describing this blend's content and character could be found, the entry has been left incomplete.

sutliff-tobacco-company-stone-cottage.z: Stone Cottage is recorded as a burley-based blend from Sutliff; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-stone-cottage.o: No reliable record of a room note could be found.

missouri-meerschaum-party-line.z: No reliable source describing the composition of the Party Line blend released under the Missouri Meerschaum name could be found.

tabacos-dalberto-jaguari.z: Jaguari, a pipe tobacco from Tabacos Dalberto; no sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of this blend could be found in the records.

ken-byron-ventures-mycroft.z: A blend released as part of Ken Byron Ventures' small-batch production; no independent, verifiable source could be found on it.

schurch-pirite-242.z: Pirite 242, signed by Schürch, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-gentry-royal-blend-2.z: No verifiable composition and character information could be compiled for Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend Gentry Royal Blend #2.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-gentry-royal-blend-2.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

castello-old-antiquari.z: Old Antiquari is the English blend in the Castello tobacco line, taking its name from the brand's sandblasted finish name. Cyprus Latakia stands at the front of the blend, with Virginia's sweetness felt underneath; the Oriental share is kept limited. The smoke-and-wood-forward flavor stays steady through the bowl; since no casing is used, the tobacco's own character remains exposed. Nicotine sits in the medium range. Suitable for smokers accustomed to classic Latakia-forward English blends and those seeking an evening smoke.
castello-old-antiquari.o: Leaves a woody, smoky, campfire room note.

st-basils-tobacco-golden-brown.z: A Virginia-burley blend from a small American brand distributed, per records, only in a narrow region; sufficient sources confirming its composition and character could not be found.

with-pipe-and-book-adirondac-mixture.z: This is a house blend produced for With Pipe and Book; no verifiable source could be found describing its composition and character.

butera-latakia-no-2.z: Latakia No.2 is the full-bodied English mixture in Butera's Royal Vintage line. Cyprus Latakia, Turkish and other Oriental leaf are brought together with matured red and orange virginias; a small amount of toasted Carolina leaf is added to give the flavor a nutty softness. The blend is cut in ribbon form. Compared to the line's first blend, the Latakia share here is more pronounced, so the smoke comes to the fore; the virginias form a sweet base in the background. The body is full. Suitable for those who want classic English mixtures in their smoky, satisfying form.
butera-latakia-no-2.o: Leaves a heavy wood smoke, toasted walnut and dried fruit aroma.

cornell-diehl-carolina-red-flake-with-pe.z: This limited-production flake, the 2023 edition of the Carolina Red Flake series with perique added, could not have its content and character verified, as it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog.

w-o-larsen-edition-2024.z: Edition 2024 is the annual release marking the W.Ø. Larsen name's 160th year; produced in a limited run with individually numbered tins, offered in a 100-gram package. The blend is built from Virginia and cavendish leaves of African and South American origin and Burley from Malawi and Mexico; the combined use of loose cut and cross cut defines its texture. In the smoke, notes reminiscent of cinnamon, clove, and spiced cookies come forward; a sweet but not overwhelming profile emerges, preserving the tobacco body behind it. Its impact on the tongue during the burn is light, and nicotine level stays measured. This is a blend prepared for smokers following spiced aromatics and those collecting Larsen's annual releases.
w-o-larsen-edition-2024.o: Leaves a scent of cinnamon-spiced cookies and clove.

pipes-pleasures-pipe-maker.z: No sufficient sources were found documenting the content and character of Pipes & Pleasures' blend Pipe Maker.

d-r-tobacco-winter-gold.z: A blend in Daughters & Ryan's aromatic line, recorded as carrying a cooling wintergreen-leaning flavoring; no adequate source documenting its composition and cut was found.
d-r-tobacco-winter-gold.o: Records indicate it leaves a cooling, mint-leaning scent.

alfie-turmeaus-after-dinner-mint.z: One of the blends sold under its own name by Turmeaus Tobacconist; although its name suggests a mint-flavored aromatic, no accessible source documenting its content and character could be found.

pipesandcigars-com-match-presbyterian.z: No independent sources sufficient to complete a full profile of pipesandcigars.com's blend Match Presbyterian could be found.

mcclelland-no-2005-university.z: One of McClelland's numbered bulk blends; no sufficient source confirming its contents and character could be found.

gq-tobaccos-peach-apple-no-2.z: GQ Tobaccos's peach-and-apple flavored blend; there is no sourcing documenting the tobacco composition.
gq-tobaccos-peach-apple-no-2.o: The name implies it leaves a peach-and-apple aroma.

lane-limited-rlp-6.z: RLP-6 is one of Lane Limited's classic bulk-sold American aromatics. A body built by adding golden Virginia and burley over toasted cavendish leaves is presented as a ribbon cut. On opening the pack, a sweet scent of vanilla, honey and chocolate comes forward; in the smoke these notes are joined by a dark sweetness resembling cream and molasses. It's a blend that stays light in nicotine, suited to smoking all day. Because of the high moisture common in flavored tobaccos, airing it before packing reduces the tongue bite that can occur when smoked quickly. Suited to smokers seeking a balance on the aromatic side that doesn't fully mask tobacco taste, and to newcomers to pipes.
lane-limited-rlp-6.o: Leaves a sweet, bakery-like room note dominated by vanilla, cocoa and honey.

motzek-old-school.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called Old School could be found.

clan-shaw-ithica.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Ithica.

torben-dansk-no-10-nice-n-easy.z: Torben Dansk No.10 Nice 'n Easy appears in sales listings as a light, loose-cut blend; no sufficient independent source describing its composition has been found.
torben-dansk-no-10-nice-n-easy.o: Records describe it as leaving a sweetish, mellow aromatic aroma.

gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-black-rum-twis.z: Sliced Black Rum Twist is the factory-sliced form of black Burma, made entirely by tightly twisting fire-cured leaf into rope. The coin-shaped slices arrive ready enough to pack straight into the bowl, and a short airing is usually enough. Its character rests on a dark core reminiscent of earth, leather, and cigar leaf; the rum topping on top adds a sweet, fragrant layer to that dark base. Because of the smoky intensity from fire-curing and the high nicotine, it calls for slow smoking; an entry designed for smokers familiar with dark, strong Burma tradition. Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. is one of the English producers that continues traditional twist (rope) production at its Kendal factory, hand-twisting fire-cured leaves into rope form. Because twist tobaccos don't go through a pressure-cooking stage, they stay intense in nicotine; records indicate these ropes are sold for both chewing and pipe smoking.
gawith-hoggarth-co-sliced-black-rum-twis.o: Leaves a heavy aroma combining smoke, leather, and sweet rum.

sturks-tobacconists-3-bells.z: 3 Bells is one of the hand-blended counter mixtures from Sturk's Tobacconists in Cape Town; records indicate the shop was founded on August 1, 1793, and is South Africa's oldest tobacconist. Since sufficient independent sources on the blend's composition and smoking character could not be found, this record is kept at listing level.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-no-bite-delite.z: No Bite DeLite is an aromatic blend J. M. Boswell built from light and dark cavendish, taking its name from its non-tongue-biting structure. Per the manufacturer's description it carries a dark-chocolate-forward casing; in the pouch aroma, caramel traces sit alongside the chocolate. The body is full, the smoke soft. Among cased blends, it is a product that lights easily and does not need frequent relighting. Suitable for smokers wanting an intense sweet casing while avoiding tongue bite.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-no-bite-delite.o: Leaves a bitter chocolate and caramel aroma.

bufflehead-black-bellied-tree-duck.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Black Bellied Tree Duck under the Bufflehead brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

synjeco-ambleside-curly.z: Ambleside Curly is a Kendal-style Virginia-Perique blend produced for the Synjeco pipe shop in Zurich, Switzerland. In the Kendal tradition, tobacco is first formed into a rope; the product called curly cut is that same rope sliced into thin, coin-like discs. Sources note that the rope and curly versions are the same blend, differing only in cut. The profile is dark and intense: dried-fruit and tart sweetness from the Virginia meet the peppery spice of the Perique. Because of the rope structure, nicotine is high; the discs need rubbing out and thorough drying, and are best smoked slowly in small pipes. It is a product for experienced smokers used to strong Virginia-Perique blends.
synjeco-ambleside-curly.o: Leaves a scent of dark dried fruit, pepper, and smoked leaf.

sutliff-tobacco-company-duke-albert-prin.z: Duke Albert is a matching product Sutliff prepared to approximate the classic Prince Albert blend. A burley-forward base is combined with Virginia and cavendish leaves in a ribbon cut; the sauce is kept light. Burley's nutty, dry, lightly earthy character leads; sweetness stays in the background and the room note is not pronounced. Suited to smokers seeking a medium-bodied, straightforward traditional shop blend for all-day smoking.
sutliff-tobacco-company-duke-albert-prin.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, dry, smoky tobacco scent.

blenders-gold-peach-melba.z: A peach-flavored blend from Sutliff's Blender's Gold line; no reliable source on its composition or smoking character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-black-irish-xxx.z: Black Irish XXX is the black-leaf branch of the traditional rope tobacco Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. has long produced in Kendal. Like all the firm's twist tobaccos, it is spun from dark-fired wrapper leaf; the black ropes are built primarily from dark-fired leaf with a smaller amount of air-cured dark Indian leaf added. The partial cooking of the leaf gives it a milder smoke than the family's brown-leaf ropes. Even so, the blend is quite full-bodied overall and heavy in nicotine; since it is sold in rope form, the smoker must cut coin-thin slices and rub them out. This is a record for experienced smokers accustomed to dark, smoky tobaccos.
gawith-hoggarth-co-black-irish-xxx.o: Leaves a heavy woodsmoke and earthy aroma from the dark-fired leaf.

rona-jacht-club.z: A pipe tobacco recorded under the Rona brand, classified as aromatic; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

abenaki-tobacco-co-tropical-splendor.z: A blend listed in Abenaki Tobacco Co.'s catalog as a Cavendish-based aromatic; no adequate source describing its content and character could be found.

smokers-haven-syrian-limited.z: Syrian Limited is an English-style mixture tinned in limited quantity for Smokers' Haven and distributed at the Chicago pipe show. Records indicate the tins were numbered, production was limited to roughly six hundred seventy tins, and tinning was done in McClelland's familiar round containers. Virginia leaves form the blend's body; Syrian latakia is used at a ratio not exceeding one-tenth of the total, so the smoky taste remains an accompanying element rather than the defining one. It's noted to contain no oriental leaf. A structure aimed at smokers who don't seek the heavy end of latakia mixtures but want a measuredly smoky Virginia character.
smokers-haven-syrian-limited.o: A measured campfire smokiness is perceptible behind a sweet hay scent.

wessex-gold-virginia-flake.z: Gold Virginia Flake is a flake obtained by double-pressing light-colored Virginia leaf. It's produced without any casing; it comes in tight slices in the tin and is rubbed out before packing. The flavor description notes baked bread and oat notes with a subtle citrus tartness in the background, leaving a creamy, soft texture in the mouth. Since it sits in the light band for both nicotine and intensity, it's a blend even newcomers to Virginia flakes can prepare.
wessex-gold-virginia-flake.o: A light citrus-peel note mixes into a scent of fresh bread and oats.

robert-mcconnell-old-london-pebble-cut.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Robert McConnell's Old London Pebble Cut blend could be found.

wesleys-no-47-vanilla-gold.z: Vanilla Gold is a house blend combining lightly matured Virginia leaf with soft Oriental leaf, topped with a measured vanilla flavoring. According to the maker's description, the vanilla isn't dominant, kept at an intensity that complements the leaf's natural sweetness.
wesleys-no-47-vanilla-gold.o: Leaves a warm vanilla and sweet hay scent.

cascadia-pipe-co-vertical-limit.z: Vertical Limit is the fullest member of the Cascadia Pipe Co. series. Sweet Virginia, hearty Burley and dark fire-cured Kentucky leaf are brought together in equal parts; the blend is then matured and pressed into cake form. Dark-fired Kentucky gives the blend a pronounced smoke and wood-fire character; Virginia's sweetness and Burley's dry body balance this smoky base. No flavor casing is used. Nicotine is at the highest level in the series, so it should be smoked on a full stomach and slowly. It is sliced from the cake and rubbed out for filling. Aimed at experienced smokers seeking a blend without Latakia but with heavy smoke and strength.
cascadia-pipe-co-vertical-limit.o: Leaves a wood-fire smoke and smoky-tobacco aroma.

gq-tobaccos-latakia-layer-kake.z: Latakia Layer Kake is a cake blend GQ Tobaccos presses in layers. The middle, making up roughly forty percent of the blend, is smoky, sweet-woody Cyprian Latakia, flanked on either side by citrus-and-fruit-sweet dark and light Virginias along with woody, spicy Turkish Oriental. The pressed cake springs back and crumbles easily by hand. The high Latakia ratio pulls the blend toward the Balkan style: the smoke is smoke-forward, with the Virginias providing sweetness and light tartness and the Orientals supplying spice. There is no topping. Because of the cake structure, it needs to be crumbled and aired out before smoking. Suited to smokers wanting an unflavored, slow-burning blend where Latakia is pronounced.
gq-tobaccos-latakia-layer-kake.o: A citrusy, floral top note accompanies the heavy aroma of smoked wood.

motzek-burley-s-crumble.z: Since neither the manufacturer's own description nor two independent reliable sources could be found for the Motzek blend called Burley's Crumble, its composition, cut, and character could not be documented here.

peter-stokkebye-balkan-supreme.z: Balkan Supreme is a Balkan-style mixture offered under the Peter Stokkebye name, high in Latakia content. Alongside Latakia it contains selected Oriental leaf, ripe Virginias, and some black Cavendish; no flavoring is applied to the blend, so the taste comes entirely from the leaf composition. The cut is loose ribbon. Records place the blend among mixtures that follow the classic Balkan Sobranie line. The profile is smoky and spicy; Latakia's leather and wood notes lead while Oriental leaf brings sharpness, and Virginia and Cavendish stay in the background adding sweetness. Flavor intensity and room note are strong. It suits smokers accustomed to Latakia-forward mixtures who are seeking a full-bodied tobacco for evening hours.
peter-stokkebye-balkan-supreme.o: Leaves an intense aroma of smoke and leather recalling a campfire.

sutliff-tobacco-company-cringle-flake-20.z: Cringle Flake 2023 is the fifth entry in the series. Ten-year-rested red Virginia leaves, 2003-harvest perique, and steamed Katerini oriental are combined, pressed, and sliced into flake. Virginia's natural sweetness, perique's peppery spice, and Katerini's dry, herbal, lightly tart character sit together; no flavoring is used. For smokers seeking oriental-supported Virginia-perique blends made with aged leaf. Being a limited seasonal edition, it is not in current production.
sutliff-tobacco-company-cringle-flake-20.o: A spicy, lightly dry-herbal oriental scent mixes into sweet dark fruit.

g-l-pease-renaissance.z: Renaissance is a classically structured, medium-bodied English mixture rich in Oriental tobaccos. Both Cyprus and Syrian latakia are used; golden, red, and matured Virginias are added enough to give the smoke body. It is among the first blends offered under the G. L. Pease name, alongside Samarra, Cairo, and Mephisto. In the smoke, the Oriental leaf's nutty taste sits on the main axis; latakia adds a spicy layer leaning toward leather, while Virginia's fine sweetness binds these two components. After supply problems with Syrian leaf, it could not be continued in its original form and was reintroduced under the name Renaissance Reserve, said to stay true to the same formula.
g-l-pease-renaissance.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of smoky leather and nuts.

svendborg-extra.z: A product listed among the Svendborg brand's Danish-style blends; no independent source describing the blend's content and character could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-ennerdale-flake.z: Ennerdale Flake is one of the best-known examples of the floral-soapy essence tobaccos known as "Lakeland" in Kendal tradition. A dough of Virginia and Burley leaf is pressed and sliced, topped with an almond-and-fruit-citrus-forward essence. This essence is pronounced, but records indicate it doesn't fully mask the Virginia's own sweetness, so the blend sits on a line that's both aromatic and tobacco-forward. The smoke is cool, nutty, and fruity; nicotine sits at a light-to-medium level, making it suitable for all-day smoking. Since it holds strongly to jar and pipe, it's usually smoked in a dedicated pipe. Can serve as a starting point for those wanting to get to know Lakeland style and for anyone seeking an essence-topped but not sugary flake.
gawith-hoggarth-co-ennerdale-flake.o: Leaves a sharp sweetness described as soapy, along with a mix of almond and floral fruit.

john-aylesbury-sun-of-kentucky.z: Sun of Kentucky is an aromatic blend produced for John Aylesbury by Kopp Tobaccos. Its composition includes Virginia, Burley, Kentucky, and Maryland leaf, with black Cavendish added as a complement. Its casing is amaretto-based, and the maker rates its intensity at two out of five. It's offered in a 100-gram package. Despite "Kentucky" in its name, the blend doesn't rely on fire-cured leaf's heavy smoky character but on a combination of measured body and almond sweetness. Nicotine is kept low. Suited to smokers who enjoy nutty, liqueur-like casings and want a light-bodied aromatic.
john-aylesbury-sun-of-kentucky.o: Leaves an almond and sweet-liqueur aroma reminiscent of amaretto.

emerson-southern-forged-abercastle.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing was found for the Emerson Southern Forged brand's Abercastle blend, so the entry has been left open; records place it in the Burley Based family.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-palmer.z: Palmer is a Wilke blend built around Maryland Burley. According to the maker's recipe, the Burley is joined by Virginia, Perique, and the house's own Royal Scot cavendish. Burley contributes nut, earth, wood, toasted bread, light sugar, and molasses, while Virginia adds citrus, grass, and a light floral tone; Perique provides spice and dried-fruit sharpness. The Royal Scot cavendish keeps a creamy vanilla sweetness in the background. Strength stays mild to medium, and the burn is cool and smooth. It suits smokers seeking a nutty, lightly sweet, balanced profile, and those who favor Burley blends where the casing stays barely perceptible, making it good for long bowls. It's part of Wilke's non-aromatic bulk listing and can occasionally go out of stock.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-palmer.o: Leaves a soft scent carrying nutty, faintly molasses sweetness.

comoys-of-london-cask-7-single-coin-slic.z: Blend No. 7 in Comoy's of London's Cask series is a pressed tobacco cut into coin shape. The outer ring of the wide slice is made up of a Virginia and pure perique mixture; at the center sits a dark core made of soft black cavendish. A very light flavoring is applied to the blend. The coins can be smoked rubbed out or placed whole into the bowl. On the flavor channel, Virginia's sweetness and perique's plum and pepper notes stand out; the cavendish core at the center softens this line, giving a rounder body. It suits smokers wanting to get to know the coin cut and interested in lightly flavored Virginia-perique blends.
comoys-of-london-cask-7-single-coin-slic.o: Leaves a sweet, bready tobacco aroma in the room, topped with a lightly spiced, sweetish trace.

milan-tobacconists-doctors-orders.z: A shop blend referred to within Milan Tobacconists' bulk aromatic line; no source describing its composition and flavoring could be found.

w-f-monroe-cigar-co-conways-private-blen.z: Conway's Private Blend Pipe Mixture is a shop-specific mixture prepared for the American firm W.F. Monroe Cigar Co.; no sufficient source could be found regarding its composition and character.
w-f-monroe-cigar-co-conways-private-blen.o: No reliable information could be found regarding the room note.

alois-dallmayr-scottish.z: One of the pipe tobaccos sold under its own name by the Munich-based Alois Dallmayr house, a mixture noted as Scottish-style; no accessible source documenting its content and character could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-oriental-hot.z: Referred to as an oriental-forward aromatic small-batch blend in Ken Byron Ventures' Yoshimi's line; not enough sources could be found to document its composition.
ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-oriental-hot.o: Could not be described due to lack of accessible records.

mac-baren-7-seas-gold-blend.z: 7 Seas Gold Blend is the light-colored member of Mac Baren's American-style aromatic series. Per the manufacturer's recipe, the blend's base is selected Virginia leaves; burley and modern cavendish provide balance. It's loose-cut, packing easily into the pipe. The light Virginia's natural sugar carries the blend's sweetness; the applied flavor pulls this sweetness toward a creamy, lightly fruity direction. Nicotine level is low, body is light. Suited to those seeking a lighter, less intense aromatic than dark-cavendish-forward blends, and to newcomers to pipe smoking.
mac-baren-7-seas-gold-blend.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly fruity, creamy room note.

hearth-home-very-nice.z: Very Nice is a mixture among Hearth & Home's fruit-flavored aromatics. A raspberry flavoring is applied to a base formed by combining black Cavendish and Virginia leaf; it's one of the members of the brand's fruity blend family bearing the "Nice" name. The Cavendish's sugar load carries the flavoring, while Virginia adds a light sweetness and body to the base. Nicotine load stays low, and since the cut is ribbon, it fills easily and burns evenly. It's aimed at smokers looking for pronouncedly fruit-flavored, light blends, and those new to the pipe. Records indicate Hearth & Home's production has ended, so the blend is no longer on the market today.
hearth-home-very-nice.o: Leaves an aroma of fresh raspberry and sugary jam.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-royal-cherry.z: Royal Cherry is among the single-note cherry records in Wilke's bulk aromatic line. According to the maker's description, the blend consists of a heavy cherry casing over a cavendish base; the point is not leaf complexity but the clarity of the flavoring. The sugary cavendish provides a soft, creamy foundation to carry that casing. It's a smoke that stays light in nicotine and mild in flavor. It suits newcomers to aromatic blends or those seeking a fruit-forward, low-strength bowl. Wilke offers this record in 2, 4, 8, and 16-ounce bulk packages.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-royal-cherry.o: A pronounced ripe-cherry scent is joined by sweet cavendish sugar.

mcclelland-no-403-darkest-chocolate.z: No. 403 Darkest Chocolate is one of McClelland's dark-toned aromatics sold in bulk. Its base is lightly sweetened black Cavendish leaf; the main flavoring applied over it is dark chocolate. Thanks to the high-sugar Cavendish, it burns slow with a cool smoke; nicotine load stays low. McClelland's 400-series is a line presenting the same Cavendish base with different flavorings; No. 401 Darkest Caramel belongs to the same series. Suited to smokers new to aromatics or those seeking the topping flavor over the tobacco character. McClelland Tobacco Company closed in 2018, so the blend is no longer produced.
mcclelland-no-403-darkest-chocolate.o: Spreads a dark cocoa and sweetened-dough aroma through the room.

wessex-summertime.z: No sufficient verifiable information could be found from maker or retailer sources regarding the Wessex Summertime blend.
wessex-summertime.o: According to the records, no scent description has been documented.

peter-stokkebye-french-vanilla-no-9-f.z: French Vanilla is built on Stokkebye's traditional Cavendish base: Virginia and Burley leaves are pressed and sliced, then opened into a loose cut. Zimbabwe-origin flue-cured leaves are also part of the blend. Brand records indicate the vanilla flavoring used in this blend is twice as intense as its stablemate Vanilla Creme. The vanilla scent from the pouch and in the room is strong; by contrast, the taste in the mouth stays more measured than the scent promises, and the tobacco's own sweetness is noticeable. The body is light. It suits smokers seeking a pronounced vanilla aromatic as well as newcomers to the pipe.
peter-stokkebye-french-vanilla-no-9-f.o: Fills the room with an intense vanilla and creamy sweet aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-old-san-francisc.z: Old San Francisco, part of Sutliff's Private Stock line, is prepared as an unflavored medium English mixture. Latakia and a small amount of perique are added to a Virginia and burley base; fire-cured burley gives the blend a nutty body, while the perique leaves a light pepper note in the background. The latakia carries the smoky side but doesn't overpower the mixture; in that sense it counts as a more measured take on heavier latakia blends. The leaf comes dry out of the tin and keeps its burn going through the bowl. It falls within the interest of those looking for an unflavored, medium-strength English mixture.
sutliff-tobacco-company-old-san-francisc.o: Leaves a scent combining smoky latakia with dry, nutty leaf.

gatlin-burlier-franks-blend.z: Not enough sourcing setting out the content and flavour character could be found for Frank's Blend, mentioned among the house blends of the Gatlinburlier tobacconist in Gatlinburg.
gatlin-burlier-franks-blend.o: Records do not document a room note.

fincks-cigar-company-danish-mild-cavendi.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for Finck's Cigar Company's Danish Mild Cavendish pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

big-star-cigar-delta-mojo.z: Recorded as a Latakia-forward house blend; its content and production status could not be verified with independent sources.
big-star-cigar-delta-mojo.o: No verified information on the room note could be found.

warped-the-red-hunt.z: The Red Hunt is a Virginia-Perique blend where red, mahogany, and light-yellow Virginia leaves meet Perique. Aged Basma and Izmir-origin Oriental leaves add a floral, lightly smoky layer to the composition. It's pressed and offered as broken flake; in the smoke, sweetness reminiscent of citrus, vanilla, and baked goods comes forward, while body stays medium.
warped-the-red-hunt.o: A light spice and smoky trace accompanies a scent of lemon cake and caramelized sugar.

consolidated-501-light-english.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Consolidated blend 501: Light English.

kontor-tabak-no-8-ready-rubbed-rr.z: Kontor-Tabak No. 8 Ready Rubbed is the same-numbered blend pressed and then rubbed out by hand. It's a natural mixture built on the pairing of Oriental tobacco and Virginia; it also contains Kentucky, Perique and a limited amount of Latakia.
