Per the manufacturer, the ready-rubbed cut gives the tobacco a notable juiciness; since the leaf is pressed, the flavors meld more, and the burn is slower than a ribbon cut. The smoke is soft, medium-strength and spicy, with the body gathering somewhat by the end of the bowl. A presentation designed for smokers seeking a packing ease between flake and ribbon.
kontor-tabak-no-8-ready-rubbed-rr.o: A fine smoky tone accompanies the dry hay and honey sweetness.

bennington-tobacconist-no-29-roanoke.z: No. 29 Roanoke is Bennington Tobacconist's one-hundred-percent Virginia shop blend. Its distinguishing trait is that it isn't tied to a single region: heat-cured leaves from the United States as well as Tanzania, Mozambique, Italy, Brazil, and Canada are brought together. Combining Virginias from different climates produces a broader flavor range than single-source blends; hay, bread, and citrus notes stand side by side. The maker states the blend is designed to smoke cool and clean. It's aimed at smokers wanting to get to know unflavored Virginia character, avoiding heavy Latakia or aromatics. Since Virginia blends are prone to tongue bite, slow smoking is recommended.
bennington-tobacconist-no-29-roanoke.o: Leaves a room note of dry hay, warm bread, and a faint lemony sweetness.

middle-earth-tobacco-rivendell.z: The aromatic blend in the Middle Earth Tobacco line; since no verifiable source could be found, no detail on composition and casing can be given.

ken-byron-ventures-your-welcome-2022.z: A year-stamped limited edition in Ken Byron Ventures' pure Virginia line; not enough sources could be found to document its composition and character.
ken-byron-ventures-your-welcome-2022.o: Could not be described due to lack of accessible records.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-walnut.z: A blend recorded within Sutliff's "Match" line, which mimics other makers' blends, known for its walnut note; no reliable source on its content and character could be found.

bufflehead-blue-winged-teal.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Blue Winged Teal under the Bufflehead brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

john-patton-latakia-junction.z: One of the small-scale blends released under the John Patton name; not enough independent sources could be found to document its contents and character.
john-patton-latakia-junction.o: No source could be found on the room note.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-winter-time-2021.z: Winter Time 2021 is an installment of Kohlhase & Kopp's winter-season limited aromatic series. Its body is built from Virginia leaves, cube-cut Virginia, black cavendish and some burley. On the casing side, a sweet profile of waffle, vanilla and caramel character dominates, accompanied by fruity notes. The blend burns cool and clean; burley's nutty earthy taste and Virginia's tangy sweetness show through beneath the casing. Nicotine is light, suited to long smokes. Being produced in limited numbers, it is not in continued production. Aimed at smokers seeking a wintry, sweet, creamy aromatic.
kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-winter-time-2021.o: Leaves a sweet room note toward waffle, vanilla and caramel.

mccranies-burley-light.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found on Burley Light, one of McCranie's Pipe Shop's house blends.
mccranies-burley-light.o: No reliable description of the aroma could be found.

brebbia-serenata-mixture-no-28.z: Serenata is a medium-intensity English mixture numbered 28 in Italian pipe manufacturer Brebbia's numbered blend series. Its composition includes small-leaf Syrian Latakia, bright Virginias and a mahogany-colored, spicy dark burley. Per records the blend was previously released under the name English Mixture No. 80 and later took the name Serenata. Syrian Latakia sets the taste at the blend's center; but since the proportion is not kept heavy, the smoke gives a balanced woody spice rather than dry smoke. Burley adds a nutty, earthy body while the Virginias round out the mixture with a light sugar sweetness. With nicotine and flavor staying at a medium level, it is a suitable option for smokers newly moving into Latakia blends or wanting to get to know Syrian Latakia in a soft frame.
brebbia-serenata-mixture-no-28.o: A nutty background accompanies the Latakia aroma reminiscent of wood smoke and pine tar.

hearth-home-whiteknight-10th-anniversary.z: WhiteKnight is the best-known blend in Hearth & Home's Marquee line, built to keep alive the memory of the 1970s Balkan Sobranie Original Smoking Mixture. Its composition includes light Virginia leaves, Orientals — among them Yenice, referred to as the "queen of tobaccos" — and Cyprus Latakia. The 10th Anniversary edition is a special release prepared for the tenth anniversary of the blend's launch. As expected of Balkan style, Latakia smokiness and the Oriental's dry spice lead; Virginia lays a sweet base beneath this structure. Body runs between medium and medium-full, while flavor intensity is high. The aroma left in the room is pronounced and lingers for a long time. It's aimed at those looking for Balkan and English-style, unflavored, smoke-forward blends.
hearth-home-whiteknight-10th-anniversary.o: Heavy woody smoke, pine smoke, and spicy leather aroma spread through the room.

missouri-meerschaum-missouri-pride.z: Missouri Pride represents the classic American burley blend in the Missouri Meerschaum line. Its composition is mostly burley, with some virginia added, and top-level flavoring is kept to a minimum. The leaf is prepared with a mixed cut combining broken flake and ribbon-cut burley; this structure aims for an even burn in the bowl. In the taste, burley's nutty, bready, dry character leads; virginia leaves only a thin measure of sweetness. Suitable for those looking for the traditional American style of smoking associated with the corn cob pipe, in a form close to unflavored.
missouri-meerschaum-missouri-pride.o: Leaves a plain tobacco aroma reminiscent of nuts and dry bread crust.

kendal-rum-and-maple.z: Rum and Maple is a dark-colored broken flake produced at Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s factory in Kendal, England. Naturally sweet sun-cured leaves and Virginias are slowly cooked under pressure into a cake alongside maple sugar and some rum; the cake is then sliced and coarsely rubbed. In recent years, due to naming restrictions, the product has been offered in some markets under the abbreviation "R & M." The casing is applied at a noticeable but not leaf-overwhelming level; it therefore sits closer to the English tradition of bowl-forward pressed flakes than to syrupy American aromatics. In the smoke, maple's dark sugar sweetness and rum's dry, alcoholic spice sit over Virginia's bready, fruity base; body is medium and, due to pressing, it burns cool. The broken-flake texture is also convenient for packing without rubbing. Suited to smokers seeking a cased but not syrup-thick, pressed blend.
kendal-rum-and-maple.o: A burnt-sugar and maple-syrup sweetness mixes with rum's alcoholic, lightly spicy scent.

sturks-tobacconists-golden-blend.z: Golden Blend is one of the hand-blended counter mixtures from Sturk's Tobacconists in Cape Town; records indicate the shop was founded on August 1, 1793, and is South Africa's oldest tobacconist. Since sufficient independent sources on the blend's composition and smoking character could not be found, this record is kept at listing level.

milan-tobacconists-rovada.z: Rovada is a medium-strength, ribbon-cut blend built from five separate virginia tobaccos, with a small amount of latakia, perique, and toasted cavendish added on top. Here latakia isn't dominant; it functions as a casing that frames the virginia sweetness. The blend's character is described as toasted and soft, more measured than heavily smoky English mixtures. Suitable for those expecting a light smoky layer from a virginia-based blend but wanting a low latakia load.
milan-tobacconists-rovada.o: Leaves a lightly smoky, toasted-bread and dry-hay aroma.

pipes-pleasures-sailors-delight.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of the Pipes & Pleasures blend called Sailor's Delight.

newminster-no-47-danish-black.z: No. 47 Danish Black is a traditional European-style black cavendish obtained by putting sweet bright virginia leaves through a special fermentation and steaming process. The resulting dark leaf is flavored with soft caramel and a light fruit note. The nicotine load is low, and the smoke is cool and sweet. It can be smoked on its own or used to add sweetness and body to other blends. Suitable for aromatic-tobacco lovers as well as those who blend their own mixtures; it is produced at Mac Baren's facilities in Denmark and sold in bulk.
newminster-no-47-danish-black.o: Leaves an aroma of burnt sugar and caramel in the room.

van-erkoms-jock.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of Van Erkoms' blend called Jock has been found.
van-erkoms-jock.o: No recorded recipe has been found.

savinelli-armonia.z: Armonia is an aromatic blend in the tobacco line the Italian pipe manufacturer Savinelli offers under its own name. Its structure holds virginia, golden-colored Oriental leaves, some burley, and fire-cured kentucky; a notable proportion of black cavendish is also added to the base. The leaf is packaged in a mixed presentation combining ribbon cut with broken flake pieces, sold in 50-gram tins. A natural citrus-based flavoring is applied as the top layer; once lit, darker notes in the direction of cocoa and rum emerge beneath it. Burley's nutty taste and kentucky's toasted tone balance the cavendish's sweetness. It is medium strength. Suited to smokers seeking a cased but non-syrupy blend who are accustomed to a slow smoke; it is noted that a quick draw may cause tongue sensitivity.
savinelli-armonia.o: Leaves a sweet citrus scent alongside cocoa and rum.

mullins-westley-ltd-highlanders-choice.z: Reportedly a malt whisky-flavored blend from the Mullins & Westley tobacconist in London's Covent Garden; no independent source confirming its composition could be found.

backwoods-forest.z: An entry referred to within the Backwoods pouch series; no manufacturer or retailer description for this name could be found, leaving the profile blank.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-berry-cobbler.z: Berry Cobbler is among Boswell's fruit-cased aromatics. Per the manufacturer's description, spice traces are found in its aroma alongside an intense fruit aroma; it is described as a blend that stays soft throughout the smoke and burns cool. The cavendish-forward base is built to carry the casing; smoking notes bring forward a creamy texture along with caramel and indistinct fruit tastes. Nicotine level is low. Suitable for fans of fruit aromatics seeking a light blend to smoke all day.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-berry-cobbler.o: Leaves a sweet, spice-tinged aroma reminiscent of a fruit dessert fresh out of the oven.

grants-tobacconist-macon-supreme.z: One of Grant's Tobacconist's aromatic house blends; there is no independent sourcing to confirm its topping and leaf composition.

1776-tobacco-co-tavern.z: 1776 Tavern is a blend the maker classifies as "heavy English," carrying no flavoring at all. Per the catalog description, its composition includes numerous Oriental leaves such as Turkish Mahalla, broad-cut Yenidje, Samsun, Cavalla, and Dubek, alongside red Virginia, Burley, and Latakia. Such a large share of Oriental leaves pulls the blend from the classic English recipe toward the Balkan side; indeed, the product is also referred to as an Oriental-forward Balkan style. Latakia's soot and the Orientals' dry, spicy taste come forward; red Virginia and Burley provide sweetness and body underneath. Because of its unflavored structure and high Oriental ratio, it's a full smoke in both nicotine and taste, so it falls into the class of blends reserved for a particular session rather than all-day smoking. It's aimed at smokers accustomed to Latakia and Oriental taste.
1776-tobacco-co-tavern.o: Leaves a smoky woodfire and spicy dry-hay room note.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-1996.z: Christmas Cheer is the seasonal series McClelland began in 1992, prepared each year with flue-cured Virginia leaf from a single harvest year. What sets the series apart is stating both the leaf's composition and the harvest year clearly on the tin; per the tin information, the 1996 release is prepared with orange South Carolina flue-cured leaf selected from the 1993 harvest.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-1996.o: Leaves a trace leaning toward sweet dried fruit and warm bread.

connoisseur-turkish-black.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Connoisseur blend Turkish Black.

owl-shop-lockwoods.z: No reliable source describing the composition of this mixture, named among the Owl Shop's house blends, could be found.
owl-shop-lockwoods.o: No description could be found in the records.

the-ridge-pipe-tobacco-hobbiton-fable.z: No reliable source could be found on The Ridge Pipe Tobacco's Hobbiton Fable blend.

hearth-home-mohawk-river.z: Mohawk River belongs to Hearth & Home's Mid-Town series, which carries names from the Albany area; there is not enough sourcing to document its composition and character.

watch-city-cigar-boston-blackie.z: According to records, Boston Blackie is not Watch City Cigar's own blend but the Lane Limited BCA mixture sold under the name used at the old C.B. Perkins shops; the shop kept this name due to customer habit.
watch-city-cigar-boston-blackie.o: Could not be determined from the records.

just-for-him-morning-coffee.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for Just For Him's Morning Coffee, so the profile is left incomplete; per catalog records, the blend is classified as "Aromatic."

sir-william-special-blend.z: A special blend listed under the name Sir William; no source describing its composition, cut, and character could be found.
sir-william-special-blend.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

georgetown-tobacco-councilman.z: Councilman is one of the English-style house blends sold at Georgetown Tobacco's shop in Washington; there is not enough sourcing describing its composition and character.

w-o-larsen-limited-edition-2018.z: This is one of W.Ø. Larsen's annual limited editions; no reliable source could be found regarding its composition and character.
w-o-larsen-limited-edition-2018.o: No detailed description of the room note has been recorded.

kontor-tabak-no-8.z: Kontor-Tabak No. 8 belongs to Leipzig-based Tabak-Kontor's natural, unflavored blend line. Its weight rests on the pairing of Oriental tobacco and Virginia; the blend also contains Kentucky, Perique and a small amount of Latakia. The smoke is soft and sweet, burning slowly with a structure that doesn't leave tongue bite. Since latakia proportion is kept low, smoky tones aren't dominant; the blend's character is defined by oriental notes. Strength increases somewhat toward the end of the bowl. An entry-level record for smokers who keep their distance from latakia-laden blends but are curious about unflavored mixture tobacco.
kontor-tabak-no-8.o: A light smoky undertone is accompanied by dry hay and honey sweetness.

pearl-tobacco-company-perle-blended.z: A blend registered under the Pearl Tobacco Company name; no reliable source about the maker, composition, or character could be found.

tobacco-trader-savannah.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Tobacco Trader blend called Savannah has been found.

g-smith-sons-old-london-mixture.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of G. Smith & Sons' pipe tobacco Old London Mixture could be found.

dan-tobacco-independence.z: Independence belongs to Dan Tobacco's "American History" series, a ribbon-cut blend with a small amount of Latakia added to a Virginia and black Cavendish base. Because it's flavored with a fruit casing, it's classed as aromatic, though the Latakia it contains sets it apart from classic aromatics. The Virginia's natural sugar meets the fruit casing on the palate, while the Latakia builds a smoky, resinous edge in the background. Body sits between mild and medium, burning evenly. A fitting choice for smokers wanting to try aromatic sweetness alongside the smoky side of English mixtures.
dan-tobacco-independence.o: A light smoky tobacco trace can be sensed beneath a sweet fruit scent.

orlik-bulls-eye.z: Bull's Eye is an Orlik blend offered in curly-cut disc form with a dark core at its center. It contains black cavendish, Virginia, and perique; no flavoring is applied. The discs are rubbed out or folded by hand for packing, and are described as trouble-free in packing and burning. Virginia's natural sweetness forms the backbone of the taste; perique layers a measured spice and plum direction over it, without dominating. Strength is medium. It suits those wanting to get to know the Virginia-perique family, and those who love unflavored, disc-cut blends with a pronounced tobacco taste.
orlik-bulls-eye.o: Leaves unflavored tobacco's bready, lightly spiced scent.

golden-blend-tobacco-co-mild-chocolate.z: Beyond being a chocolate-flavored pipe tobacco under the Golden Blend Tobacco Co. name, there is no independent sourcing documenting the blend's composition and character.
golden-blend-tobacco-co-mild-chocolate.o: Said to leave a sweet, cocoa-forward aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-majestic-english.z: Coded SPS-14, Majestic English is an English blend in Sutliff's Private Stock line where the latakia ratio is kept above average. Alongside latakia sit burley, Virginia, Turkish leaf, and perique; burley thickens the body, while perique adds a spicy, fruity twist. Body and flavor are intense, and nicotine is pronounced. Aimed at experienced smokers seeking near-upper-limit intensity in smoky blends and wanting an unflavored, full-bodied mixture; it may prove heavy for those new to English blends.
sutliff-tobacco-company-majestic-english.o: Leaves a strong wood-smoke scent reminiscent of a campfire that lingers in the room for a long time.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-mixed-shag-men.z: Kendal Mixed is the second of Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s shag-cut main bodies. Unlike Kendal Gold's pure-Virginia structure, this body is built by adding Malawi-origin dark leaf and some fire-cured Kentucky to golden Virginia; because of this, its color is more mottled and its taste more earthy. This is the version with menthol added to the Kendal Mixed body. Menthol pushes the dark leaf's earthy taste into the background and leaves a pronounced coolness in the mouth. The fine shag cut lights quickly. Aimed at those accustomed to smoking menthol-topped tobacco and wanting a palate-cleansing blend.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-mixed-shag-men.o: Leaves a sharp menthol and cool mint aroma.

tewksbury-company-xo.z: According to records, this blend was part of the lineup of Tewksbury & Company, an American blender that ceased operations following the 2009 tobacco regulation; no source documenting its content and character could be found.

samuel-gawith-navy-plug.z: No sufficient source documenting the content and character of Navy Plug, according to records a Virginia-Latakia blend produced at Samuel Gawith's factory in Kendal, could be found.

brigham-enterprises-inc-ripley-avenue.z: Ripley Avenue is a distinctly flavored blend in Brigham's Legend line. Bright Virginia is scattered into a select brown and black cavendish base; vanilla and rum flavoring is applied on top. Because of the cavendish-forward structure, nicotine feel is low, and the smoke is dense and sweet; the Virginia share leaves a fine tobacco sweetness underneath the aroma. Suitable for fans of aromatic blends and for those new to the pipe. The name refers to Brigham's historic address in Toronto.
brigham-enterprises-inc-ripley-avenue.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of sweet vanilla and rum confection.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-twist-sweet-van.z: This is a product from Gawith, Hoggarth & Co.'s twisted-rope family, sweetened with invert sugar and vanilla. The body is fire-cured Virginia and Indian leaf; the rope is left as it comes off the twisting machine, without additional pressing or cooking. The vanilla topping wraps a sweet layer around the smoky, earthy base of the leaf but doesn't lighten the body. It is prepared by slicing thin, rubbing out, and airing. It is strong in nicotine and requires slow smoking. It is aimed at those accustomed to the rope format who want a flavoured but full-bodied tobacco.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-twist-sweet-van.o: A sweet vanilla and sugared-dough aroma sits over the smoky tobacco aroma.

watch-city-cigar-christmas-present.z: This is a Virginia-based seasonal blend in Watch City Cigar's Christmas series; no record exists in the maker's current catalog.
watch-city-cigar-christmas-present.o: Could not be determined from the records.

srensen-srensen-irish-whiskey.z: SØRENSEN Irish Whiskey is one of the flavored house blends from Sørensen Tobakk in Bergen. Naturally sweet Virginia is combined with Burley, with an Irish whisky flavoring applied in measured amounts; the product is sold as a loose cut in a 50-gram tin. On the retailer's scale, aroma intensity is rated two out of five and strength three out of five — that is, a medium-bodied aromatic where the casing doesn't overpower the tobacco. Burley's nutty base and Virginia's sweetness run beneath the whisky note. It suits smokers who find heavily sugared aromatics excessive but aren't ready to go fully unflavored either.
srensen-srensen-irish-whiskey.o: Leaves a scent reminiscent of sweet malt and barrel-aged whisky.

dan-tobacco-bulldog-mans-best-friend.z: Records indicate this blend belongs to Dan Tobacco's Bulldog series; no adequate independent source describing its composition was found.

fribourg-treyer-wingate-mixture.z: Wingate Mixture is one of the English-style blends in the line carrying the name of Fribourg & Treyer, founded in London in 1720 and whose shop closed in the 1980s. A small amount of perique is added to the classic structure built on Virginia and latakia, and the blend is presented ribbon cut. Perique adds a plummy, peppery sharpness to latakia's woody smoke, setting the blend apart from a plain English mixture. It suits smokers who know the English style and are looking for a spicy layer added to it.
fribourg-treyer-wingate-mixture.o: Leaves a sharp aroma of smoky wood and black pepper.

310-pipe-tobacco-battleground.z: This is one of the house blends from the 310 Pipe & Tobacco shop in Murfreesboro, Tennessee; records indicate the shop's recipes were later passed on to another tobacconist in the same county, but there is not enough available source material describing the blend's composition.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-revelation.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the content and character of Match Revelation, one of the bulk blends from Richmond-based Sutliff Tobacco Company, could be found.

mcclelland-ringlow-syrian-reserve.z: Ringlow Syrian Reserve is an English blend built from Virginia, Oriental tobacco, and Latakia, offered as ribbon cut in a 50-gram tin. The "Syrian Reserve" in the name indicates the blend's Latakia is Syrian rather than Cyprian in origin. Syrian Latakia gives a milder, more incense-like, sweeter smokiness than Cyprian Latakia, which lets the Virginia sweetness underneath and the Oriental leaf's spice stand without being pushed down. McClelland set aside its Syrian Latakia stock before the 2004 fire that destroyed most of the world's supply, and used this leaf in a limited number of blends over the years. As the firm's Syrian Latakia stock ran out, Ringlow Syrian Reserve was withdrawn from the market and discontinued entirely with the 2018 closure. A record for those seeking a medium-bodied, smoky but not overwhelming English blend, and for those curious about the taste of Syrian Latakia.
mcclelland-ringlow-syrian-reserve.o: Leaves a smoky aroma reminiscent of wood smoke and incense.

cornell-diehl-winchester.z: Winchester is a ribbon-cut blend combining red Virginia with unsweetened black Cavendish. Per the maker's description, the smoke is light and the room note recalls old-school pipe tobaccos. Since the Cavendish carries no flavor casing, the blend doesn't fall into the aromatic class; the dark leaf only adds a toasted softness. It's a plain entry with no complex components, sauce, or casing. Red Virginia's dark, sugary taste combines with the Cavendish's breadlike tone. Suited to smokers wanting to move from aromatics to unflavored blends, or looking for a low-nicotine Virginia to smoke all day.
cornell-diehl-winchester.o: Leaves a toasted, lightly sweet tobacco scent reminiscent of old-fashioned pipe tobacco.

blenders-gold-royal-cherry-cavendish.z: Royal Cherry Cavendish is the cherry-flavored Cavendish blend in the Blender's Gold line. Produced by Sutliff, the line was sold for a long time under its own brand on drugstore-chain shelves, in tins of roughly three and a half ounces. The blend's base is Cavendish flavored with cherry essence, backed by Burley for a mellow foundation. The flavoring is pronounced and stands out both in the tin note and in the room note. Nicotine is low and the smoke is mild; it's aimed at smokers looking for classic fruit-flavored American aromatics.
blenders-gold-royal-cherry-cavendish.o: Fills the room with a sweet cherry-candy note.

racine-laramie-cherry-mystique.z: Cherry Mystique is a flavored mixture among the house blends of Racine & Laramie in San Diego. Its base is Danish-style Cavendish; nicotine is kept quite light, with an intense cherry flavoring applied on top. With its light body and pronounced fruit sweetness, it is the type newcomers to the pipe and those looking for a sweet taste all day tend toward. For fans of unflavored blends, its flavoring level stays high.
racine-laramie-cherry-mystique.o: Leaves a pronounced ripe cherry and candied-fruit aroma.

milan-tobacconists-sunset-rum.z: Sunset Rum is Milan Tobacconists' rum-flavored house blend. Its base is formed by virginia and burley; a measured amount of black cavendish is added, and the blend is flavored by resting in rum. Since there's also a separate bulk blend of the same name made by Sutliff, it's easy to confuse the two. The smoke is soft and cool, with nicotine staying low; virginia's natural sweetness meets rum's sugary, lightly burnt edge, and the cavendish share is kept low enough not to weigh the blend down. Suitable for smokers looking for a sweet aromatic that isn't harsh but doesn't entirely mask the tobacco's character.
milan-tobacconists-sunset-rum.o: Leaves a sweet, warm aroma reminiscent of rum sugar and molasses.

bufflehead-hooded-merganser.z: No independent, reliable sources could be found for the blend named Hooded Merganser under the Bufflehead brand, so a detailed entry could not be prepared.

lane-limited-virginia.z: Lane Limited's bulk Virginia is, as the name states, a plain Virginia blend. It's formed by bringing together light-colored bright leaf and darker-toned flue-cured leaf in a ribbon cut; it contains no casing. The flavor axis rests on Virginia's own natural sugar: grass, dry bread and a light fruity sweetness come forward, with low sharpness. It's a record meant both to be smoked on its own and to be used as a base leaf by those building their own blends. Nicotine load is moderate, suiting all-day smoking; it provides a plain base for those wanting to build blends by adding dominant leaves like Latakia or Perique in their own proportion.
lane-limited-virginia.o: Leaves a fine, lightly sweet note reminiscent of dry hay and baked bread.

brigham-enterprises-inc-solitude.z: Solitude is a black-cavendish-forward aromatic in the Mr. B's series. Select Virginia and burley leaves undergo a heat treatment and are cured in bulk for a week; this process lowers the leaf's natural sharpness, giving a very soft, low-nicotine smoke. A sweet vanilla flavoring is applied on top. Because of low nicotine and a soft smoke, it is suited to long, calm smoking sessions and to those new to the pipe. The ribbon cut makes filling easy; since the cavendish proportion is high, care must be taken that the tobacco does not stay too moist.
brigham-enterprises-inc-solitude.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough aroma.

peretti-blend-b-94.z: A mixture drawn from Peretti's old blend ledgers, named by letter and number, listed in the burley group and still in production; its detailed composition has not been published.

davidoff-scottish-mixture.z: Scottish Mixture is a whisky-flavored blend from Davidoff built on burley, Kentucky, oriental and Virginia leaves. It's ready-rubbed cut; on opening the tin you find an almost dry, very finely cut, veinless tobacco. The tin scent carries a light grape echo. The weight is in Virginia and oriental tobaccos; a spicy taste familiar to smokers acquainted with Turkish tobaccos runs from the start to the end of the bowl. The burley proportion is low and only makes itself known toward the end of the smoke. Because the topping is kept low, the whisky tone doesn't overwhelm the tobacco. No tongue bite or watering has been reported. It suits those seeking a very mild blend smokable all day.
davidoff-scottish-mixture.o: A lightly grapey, whisky-evoking scent mixes with spicy oriental tobacco scent.

ole-shenandoah-pressed-burley-black-cave.z: An Ole Shenandoah blend built on pressed burley and black cavendish, as its name indicates; no detailed maker's description could be found.

cornell-diehl-new-market.z: Not enough sourcing could be located to document the composition and character of Cornell & Diehl's New Market blend; it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog.

clan-shaw-saratoga.z: No reliable, independent sourcing could be found regarding Clan Shaw Saratoga, so a detailed profile could not be compiled.

cornell-diehl-derringer.z: Derringer is a blend built from unflavored Virginia leaves, offered as a broken flake (pre-rubbed). This cut lets the smoker skip the step of crumbling the flake by hand while still preserving flake texture's slow burn. The flavor runs between Virginia's bready sweetness and tea-like, grassy notes; with no flavoring present, the leaf's own character leads. Nicotine is medium. It suits smokers who love a straight Virginia profile and want to use flake while avoiding the preparation hassle.
cornell-diehl-derringer.o: Leaves a light trace reminiscent of dry grass and baked bread.

timm-no-name-orange.z: The orange variety in the Timm No Name series is a light-colored mixture aimed at fans of unflavored Virginia. It is built from six separate Virginia types; sweet leaves of Argentine and Mysore origin dominate, with a small amount of Oriental added to give the blend a spicy edge. As there is no flavoring, the taste comes directly from the leaf's own sugar; nicotine is moderate and the smoke is cool. Suited to those wanting to smoke plain Virginia mixtures daily in a large package.
timm-no-name-orange.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of dry hay and bread crust.

kontor-tabak-no-20.z: Kontor-Tabak No. 20 is a vanilla blend representing Tabak-Kontor's Danish-style aromatic wing. Per the manufacturer's recipe, Virginia and black cavendish leaves are combined with some Burley; creamy vanilla and honey notes come forward on the palate and in the room. Although the casing level is pronounced, since the tobacco base is cavendish-forward and sweet, the smoke is soft and low in nicotine. An everyday aromatic designed for newcomers to pipes and for those who love sweet blends whose scent lingers in the room. As with any moist aromatic, it should be smoked slowly and packed at a measured level to avoid wetting the pipe.
kontor-tabak-no-20.o: Leaves a creamy vanilla and honey room note.

cornell-diehl-oak-alley.z: Oak Alley is a pressed mixture named after the historic Oak Alley Plantation in Louisiana. Per Cornell & Diehl's description, sweet red Virginias along with white and brown burleys form the body, topped with a measured amount of perique and Katerini Oriental leaf. Because it is pressed into a cake, Virginia's sugars concentrate, while burley cools the smoke and adds a nutty depth. As perique and Katerini are used in small proportions, they stand as a complementary layer of spice and herbal tang rather than a dominant note. The maker positions the blend as well suited to cellar aging. It suits smokers accustomed to tobaccos with above-medium nicotine who want a Latakia-free blend with more layering than a straight Virginia.
cornell-diehl-oak-alley.o: Leaves a lightly spiced tobacco aroma mingled with baked bread and nuts.

cornell-diehl-professor.z: Professor is a ribbon-cut blend in Cornell & Diehl's English family. A measured amount of Latakia, Perique, and black Cavendish is added to a Virginia base; the maker named the blend around the idea of quiet hours spent with a book. Keeping the Latakia proportion balancing rather than dominant sets the blend apart from heavy Balkan mixtures: Virginia's sweetness and Perique's spice stay up front while the smoky leaf builds a frame in the background. On the maker's scale, strength, flavor, and room note are medium. Suited to those new to English mixtures or looking for a measured Latakia blend to smoke all day.
cornell-diehl-professor.o: Leaves a light sweet layer over a scent of woody smoke and dry leaf.

peterson-3ps-peterson-perfect-plug.z: 3P's Peterson Perfect Plug is a molded tobacco combining African and Brazilian-origin Virginia leaf with Malawi Burley. The blend is pressed under heat and rested for about two weeks before being cut into blocks; the smoker slices off a portion of the desired thickness from the block and rubs it out. The leaf carries a light fruit topping. Burley's earthy, nutty body balances Virginia's sugar; dark fruit and bready notes come forward through the smoke. Nicotine strength is medium. It suits smokers who enjoy working with pressed tobacco, preparing their own slices, and aging it in the tin. Letting a prepared slice sit in the air for a while afterward makes the burn easier to manage.
peterson-3ps-peterson-perfect-plug.o: Leaves a warm, unassertive aroma recalling dried fruit and bread crust.

radfords-classic-port.z: No source could be found documenting the content and flavoring of Radfords Classic Port.
radfords-classic-port.o: No information describing the room note could be found in available records.

peterson-special-reserve-2003.z: No sufficient sources giving composition information for the 2003 edition of Peterson's annual Special Reserve series could be found.

mac-baren-solent-mixture.z: The Solent Mixture is one of Mac Baren's oldest products, dating back to 1950. The blend's founding idea was to build a mixture that let Latakia be felt enough without leaving a heavy odor in the room. So matured Virginia leaves were used as the base, with full-bodied Burley, the maker's own Cavendish, and Cyprian Latakia added on top. Once the mixture was complete, it's finished with dark Jamaican rum and a pinch of vanilla. The result is a structure sitting between a full English mixture and an aromatic. Latakia's leather and soot stay in the background, while the Cavendish's and rum's sweetness soften the edges of the taste. Nicotine and flavor intensity are medium. Suited to those wanting to warm up to Latakia blends and to smokers seeking a smoky character softened with flavoring support.
mac-baren-solent-mixture.o: A sweet rum and vanilla aroma rides atop a light soot aroma.

eric-christie-pipe-tobacco-american-heri.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing could be found for American Heritage, a blend from Eric Christie Pipe Tobacco, so the record has been left open; according to available listings it is classified in the Aromatic family.

w-o-larsen-limited-edition-2010.z: No independent source sufficient to complete a record could be found regarding W.O. Larsen's Limited Edition 2010 blend, so this entry remains incomplete.

holger-danske-red-kirsberry-wine.z: This is Holger Danske's aromatic blend carrying, as the name suggests, a cherry-wine-themed flavoring; no independent source detailing its composition could be found.
holger-danske-red-kirsberry-wine.o: No detailed record of its aroma could be found.

nat-sherman-510-blend-spuyten-duyvil.z: One of Nat Sherman's Cavendish-forward numbered house blends; no independent source giving detailed composition could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-178.z: Wilke No. 178, per the maker's recipe, is a Burley-centered blend built by adding a small amount of black cavendish to Tennessee Burley. The weight rests entirely on the Burley side; here the cavendish functions less as a sweetening addition and more as a helper component that softens the blend's dry, earthy structure. Burley leaf is naturally low in sugar and relatively high in nicotine, so the blend offers a full-bodied smoke that's rich in the mouth and burns cool. It suits smokers who want to steer clear of the tartness of Virginia-forward blends or the sugar load of aromatics, staying close to the American Burley tradition. Flavoring is not pronounced.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-178.o: Leaves a scent of dry nutshell and dark cocoa.

tabac-manil-la-brumeuse.z: One of Tabac Manil's burley-based blends; no accessible source could be found to fill out the profile.

edwards-english-supreme.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of English Supreme, a pipe tobacco from Edward's. Edward's is a tobacconist business based in Tampa, Florida.

kadewe-mischung-no80.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for KaDeWe's Mischung No80, so the profile is left incomplete.

sutliff-tobacco-company-mulled-wine-j15.z: Mulled Wine J15 is a Sutliff aromatic inspired by the spiced hot wine drunk in Europe during the winter months. Over a base of burley, Virginia, and black cavendish, spice notes reminiscent of wine along with cinnamon, clove, and citrus peel are applied. Cavendish supplies the blend's sweetness while burley provides its body; Virginia leaves a light grainy tone in the background. The topping is noticeable but not one-dimensional; fruit sweetness and spice run together. Nicotine strength is below average. Suited to smokers who enjoy seasonal, spiced aromatics and sweet-spicy combinations.
sutliff-tobacco-company-mulled-wine-j15.o: Leaves a scent of mulled wine, cinnamon, and orange peel.

dream-castle-tobacco-company-top-value-c.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Top Value Cherry, a pipe tobacco from Dream Castle Tobacco Company.
dream-castle-tobacco-company-top-value-c.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

bosphorus-golden-blend.z: One of Bosphorus's ribbon-cut blends; per records its recipe has been changed, and no sufficient source could be found regarding its content and character.

cornell-diehl-ghost-of-christmas-past.z: Ghost of Christmas Past is the burley-forward member of Cornell & Diehl's 2022 Wintertime Reserve trilogy. Dark, white, and cube-cut burley varieties are combined with bright flue-cured leaf and a measured amount of Latakia, then pressed into a cake; it is a hand-prepared seasonal series made in small batches. The flavor profile combines burley's nutty, cocoa-like dryness, Latakia's woody smoke, and Virginia's measured sweetness. It carries a medium-to-full-bodied, dry, earthy character; it is unflavored. It is intended for smokers accustomed to burley-based, smoky, hearty blends, and for cold-weather smoking. Being a limited release, it is not part of current production.
cornell-diehl-ghost-of-christmas-past.o: Leaves an aroma of toasted nuts and wood smoke.

srensen-srensen-mixture.z: SØRENSEN Mixture is the aromatic member of the two house blends from the historic Sørensen Tobakk in Bergen. Light-colored Virginias, black Cavendish, and spicy Burley are brought together; the blend is given a honey- and vanilla-leaning casing. The retailer's scale records its strength as two out of five. The smoke is velvety and low in nicotine; a sweet, creamy-caramel taste sits atop a mild tobacco base. Because of the vanilla casing, the tin note is sweeter than what comes through on the smoke. It suits smokers looking for a light, sweet, Danish-style aromatic that can be smoked all day, as well as those new to pipes.
srensen-srensen-mixture.o: Leaves a sweet scent reminiscent of honeyed, vanilla pastry.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-van-dyck-.z: Van Dyck Mixture is a cavendish blend produced by Scandinavian Tobacco Group and built following classic Dutch blending tradition. Its body is formed by Virginia and burley leaves; these leaves are sweetened and softened through the cavendish process. As is typical of Dutch-style blends, the casing is not heavy — most of the sweetness comes from the leaves' own sugars and the process. The smoke is medium-bodied; due to the burley share, nicotine and fullness sit above the light Danish-style aromatics. Suited to smokers who stay away from intensely flavored tobaccos yet still want a sweet foundation, and to those curious about traditional Dutch-style blends. According to records, the blend has limited distribution in the European market.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-van-dyck-.o: Leaves a lightly sweet scent evoking dry bread crust.

cornell-diehl-afternoon-delight.z: Afternoon Delight is a ribbon-cut mixture Cornell & Diehl builds by adding fire-cured Kentucky and Oriental leaf to a Virginia-heavy body. Per the maker's description, maple and smoky campfire notes stand out in the blend; a small amount of Latakia and black cavendish round out this frame. Kentucky and Latakia add a dry smoke to the blend while black cavendish carries a measured sweetness; since the flavoring level is kept low, the blend sits closer to a smoky American mixture than an aromatic. It suits those approaching Latakia blends for the first time or looking for a lightly flavored, smoky smoke.
cornell-diehl-afternoon-delight.o: Leaves a light campfire aroma blended with maple sweetness.

st-basils-tobacco-ivan-the-terrible.z: A Virginia-and-perique-forward blend from the small-scale American house St. Basil's Tobacco; sufficient independent sources describing its composition and character could not be found.
st-basils-tobacco-ivan-the-terrible.o: No description is available in records.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-boswell-military-f.z: Military Force is Boswell's English-style blend: Latakia, toasted Virginia, aged cube-cut burley and Oriental leaf are brought together. Latakia takes the carrying role for the smoke while burley gives body and the Oriental adds spicy top notes; the result is a layered but not harsh smoke. The blend is presented by the manufacturer as having been prepared with smokers in the US military in mind. Suitable for smokers newly moving to Latakia-containing mixtures or seeking a smoky taste without excess.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-boswell-military-f.o: Leaves a wood smoke and soot aroma, with a dry spice trace behind it.

g-l-pease-sixpence.z: Sixpence is a Virginia-Perique blend in G. L. Pease's Old London Series line. Its base is ripe red Virginia leaf; a generous measure of perique is added, along with a small amount of dark fire-cured Kentucky for body and depth. After a light preparation process, the leaves are pressed into plug form and rested, then sliced for boxing; the result is a tobacco with a broken-flake appearance. It takes its name from the English sixpence coin and is the first Virginia-Perique record in the series.
g-l-pease-sixpence.o: Leaves an aroma of dry grass, stone fruit, and light earth.

pcca-panache.z: A blend produced by McClelland within the PCCA club series; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.

telfords-pipes-cigars-golden-gate.z: One of roughly forty house blends prepared by Telford's Pipe & Cigar shop in Mill Valley, California; no accessible source describing the blend's composition and character could be found.

g-l-pease-balrog.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Balrog.

hu-tobacco-bahia-orange.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Bahia Orange, one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-everton.z: Not enough source material documenting the composition and character of the Everton blend, named among the brands under the Scandinavian Tobacco Group umbrella, could be found.

4noggins-harvest-moon.z: Harvest Moon is built by combining cube-cut Burley, a measured amount of Latakia, and steamed (stoved) red Virginia for sweetness. Cube-cut Burley gives the blend a slow, even burn; the manufacturer notes it lights easily and leaves clean white ash. The smoky layer of Latakia sits between Burley's dry, nutty base and stoved Virginia's dark sweetness; no additives are reported. Nicotine is moderate and flavor medium-to-full. It's aimed at smokers wanting Latakia kept measured and who enjoy the long, calm smoke of cube-cut Burley; the maker positions it among all-day blends.
4noggins-harvest-moon.o: Leaves a nutty, dried-fruit aroma over smoky wood fire.

cornell-diehl-bow-legged-bear.z: Bow-Legged Bear is a hearty English mixture bringing together Virginia, Latakia, perique, burley, and Oriental leaf. The leaves are baked, pressed, and sliced into an old-style crumble cake; this preparation lets the components meld together and brings the smoke closer to a single unified taste. Thanks to its five separate leaf types it carries a wide flavor range: Latakia's smoke, the Oriental's dry spice, perique's plummy sharpness, burley's nutty body, and Virginia's sweetness. Because of the cake structure, its smoke is dense and the room note stays pronounced; nicotine strength is above medium. Being pressed, it needs to be crumbled and aired before smoking. It suits those looking for a layered, unflavored, hearty English mixture.
cornell-diehl-bow-legged-bear.o: A spicy, earthy layer sits within a dense wood-smoke aroma.

mcclelland-latakia-flake.z: Latakia Flake, released within the Blakeney's Best series, is a full-bodied English blend in which generous Cyprian Latakia is combined with Yaka Oriental from Greece's Xanthi region, toasted, then matured pressed into cakes. The flake sliced from the cake gives a slow, cool burn; soot and spice notes stay upfront through the smoke. Aimed at experienced smokers seeking heavy-Latakia, unflavored, full-bodied blends; being flake, it needs to be rubbed out or folded before packing. The blend was produced from 2005 and withdrawn from the market when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-latakia-flake.o: Leaves a heavy soot, burnt-wood, and spice aroma.

park-lane-tobacconist-park-lane-pl-11010.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Park-Lane PL-11010, one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

brigham-enterprises-inc-english-mixture.z: English Mixture, offered by Brigham under its Mr. B's umbrella, is a traditional English-style mixture made up of a combination of red Virginia, Turkish (Oriental) leaf, burley, Latakia and perique. Per the manufacturer's description, the blend stays in the medium-strength band on the English-mixture scale; Latakia is not dominant, used instead as a component that frames Virginia's sweetness and the Oriental's dry spice. The small addition of perique adds a light fruity-peppery edge to the flavor. Since the cut is ribbon, filling and lighting the pipe is easy; this makes it suitable both for those new to Latakia blends and for those seeking a balanced English blend for everyday smoking. Brigham is a Canadian-origin firm that began with Roy Brigham's pipe-repair workshop in Toronto in 1906; per records, a portion of the brand's tobaccos are manufactured at factories outside Canada.
brigham-enterprises-inc-english-mixture.o: Leaves a woody smoke and dry-leaf aroma from the Latakia.

w-o-larsen-classic-elegant.z: No independent source sufficient to complete a record could be found regarding W.O. Larsen's Classic Elegant blend, so this entry remains incomplete.

tinder-box-sweet-english.z: Sweet English is a name that appears among Tinder Box house blends; no verifiable source describing its composition and character has been found.
tinder-box-sweet-english.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

dan-tobacco-liberty.z: A pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source on the blend's composition or character was found, so no further detail is given.

ken-byron-ventures-kings-ransom.z: King's Ransom is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-old-school-j-m-b.z: Old School J.M.B is a blend built by adding some Virginia to ribbon-cut burley. J.M. Boswell aimed to bring back old-style burley blends without tongue bite; the mixture was shaped through trials in the shop. It carries a nutty, bready flavor line with a faint molasses hint; its body is pronounced enough to give backbone compared to other blends. Suitable for smokers seeking the classic American burley style in its plain form.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-old-school-j-m-b.o: Leaves a bready, nutty aroma with a light molasses trace.

richs-woz.z: There is not enough source material documenting the content and character of Rich's WOZ.

gladora-tobacco-latakia-flake-20.z: Pesse Canoe Latakia Flake 20 is Gladora's unflavored, English-style flake. A twenty-percent share of Turkish Latakia is added to a base built from Turkish-grown Virginia and Oriental leaf; unlike Cyprian Latakia, the curing is done entirely in Turkey, leaving a depth close to dried fruit alongside the smoke. Keeping the Latakia ratio measured makes the Oriental's floral spice and the Virginia's citrus-leaning tartness audible; plum, wood, and a light sweetness are the standout flavor lines. Since it's pressed as flake, it burns slowly and cool. Suited to smokers new to English mixtures as well as those wanting a daytime smoke without a heavy smoke load.
gladora-tobacco-latakia-flake-20.o: Leaves a measured wood-smoke, earth, and dried-plum aroma.

tabakfabrik-roth-jagertabak.z: Jägertabak is a Tabakfabrik Roth blend named for hunting. The maker builds the mixture on the unflavored spice of mature Virginia and Burley leaf, joined by a measured caramel flavoring along with a honey and molasses casing. The result is a light-colored, soft-bodied classic where the flavoring stays in the background. The tobacco is prepared entirely from Swiss-grown leaf and, like the factory's other products, hand-filled to order. It suits smokers looking for a long-burning, unobtrusive everyday blend who enjoy smoking outdoors.
tabakfabrik-roth-jagertabak.o: Leaves a sweet, bready scent leaning toward honey and caramel.

nat-sherman-314-city-island-dawn.z: 314 City Island Dawn was one of the house blends New York-based Nat Sherman produced under its own name. Bright golden cavendish leaf forms the base, topped with a measured vanilla casing. It is noted as the lightest and best-known aromatic in the Nat Sherman catalog; records indicate it was long sold only in bulk. The casing is applied more sparingly than in heavily sauced aromatics; in the smoke, vanilla, milk chocolate, and occasional hints of orange stand out, with a low sense of nicotine. Suitable for smokers who like a vanilla cavendish profile and want a light, easy-burning aromatic. Production stopped when Nat Sherman ended its tobacco operations in 2020.
nat-sherman-314-city-island-dawn.o: Leaves a vanilla and milk chocolate aroma with a light trace of citrus at the edges.

comptons-of-galashiels-viceroy.z: No independent, reliable sourcing could be found regarding the Compton's of Galashiels pipe tobacco named Viceroy, so the blend's content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

cornell-diehl-back-porch.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to describe the content of this blend, which does not currently appear in the Cornell & Diehl catalog.

imperial-tobacco-group-plc-saint-claude.z: Saint Claude is a blend that has been on the market for decades, belonging to the fine-cut "scaferlati" branch of French pipe tobacco tradition. It takes its name from Saint-Claude, the town in France associated with briar pipe making; the brand and recipe were long owned by the state monopoly SEITA, later passing to Imperial Tobacco, and records indicate the SEITA pipe tobacco catalog was taken over by Mac Baren in 2015. The backbone of the blend is fire-cured (dark fired) Kentucky; light-colored natural Virginia and air-cured leaves giving it its French character are added. The result is a woody, smoky, earthy taste with pronounced nicotine strength; the flavoring share is very low. It appeals to smokers curious about traditional French "brown tobacco" character who don't shy away from strong, near-unflavored smokes.
imperial-tobacco-group-plc-saint-claude.o: Leaves the woody, smoky, sharp aroma of fire-cured leaf.

samuel-gawith-best-brown-flake.z: Best Brown Flake is an unflavored flake made solely from hand-selected, hot-air-cured Virginia leaves. The leaves are first pressed into a block, then put through a steam press; the combination of heat and pressure turns the leaf a dark brown and matures the flavor. The result is a deep, nutty, naturally sweet smoke carrying grass, bread, and earth echoes. Since no moisture-retaining agent is used at the Kendal factory and moisture level varies with climate conditions, the flakes coming out of the tin may need airing. One of the go-to blends for those seeking unflavored Virginia character.
samuel-gawith-best-brown-flake.o: Leaves a sweetish tobacco scent evoking dry hay and freshly baked bread.

levin-pipes-international-white-downs.z: White Downs is one of the Virginia-based blends McClelland produced for Barry Levin; 1991-dated tins are known, but not enough sources could be found for its composition and character.
levin-pipes-international-white-downs.o: Leaves a room note of dry hay and lightly sweet straw.

mccranies-red-flake-vintage-2000.z: McCranie's Pipe Shop is a long-established tobacconist in Charlotte, North Carolina; the shop's tinned tobacco line began with red Virginia leaf from a single harvest set aside exclusively for it. This leaf is rested and pressed; the name flake refers to the presentation in which the pressed block is left in slices rather than broken up. Records indicate the year on the tin (2000) marks the leaf's harvest/packing year, and batches stamped with other years circulate under the same name. Being unflavored, single-varietal Virginia, the tobacco's taste comes from the leaf's own sugar: a bready, creamy base with a sweet depth that deepens with age. Nicotine load runs light to medium, making it suitable for all-day smoking. Aimed at smokers seeking an unflavored Virginia who want to smoke slowly and follow the leaf's own taste. The shop no longer continues this line; what's on the market are older batches.
mccranies-red-flake-vintage-2000.o: Leaves a sweetish hay aroma with a faint bready note.

niall-of-nine-riddle-of-steel.z: A small-scale blend noted as Balkan type; not enough independent source material documenting its composition and maker could be found.

mcclelland-black-sea-sokhoum.z: Black Sea Sokhoum belongs to McClelland's Grand Orientals series, which spotlights individual Oriental tobaccos. The blend's core is Samsun-origin leaf grown on Georgia's Black Sea coast, joined by Virginia carrying McClelland's characteristic tangy-sweet aroma. It's ribbon cut. The tin aroma carries a pronounced cigarette-tobacco smell alongside the sweet-tart ferment; this character is reflected in the taste too. Virginia's sweetness balances the Oriental tobacco's exotic, spicy side, and flavor intensity reaches its peak toward the middle of the bowl. Since strength stays medium, it suits long smokes. Falls within the territory of those wanting to get to know Oriental tobacco directly rather than in Latakia's shadow.
mcclelland-black-sea-sokhoum.o: Leaves a sharp, spicy, and tangy aroma reminiscent of cigarette tobacco.

mullingar-irish-mead.z: A blend reportedly manufactured in the Netherlands for the Irish company Mullingar Tobaccos, not seen on the market after the 1980s; no independent source confirming its composition could be found.

mcclelland-no-2035-dark-navy-flake.z: No. 2035 Dark Navy Flake is an unflavored Virginia flake in McClelland's bulk series. Per the maker's description, very light lemon Virginias and Eastern Belt leaves are pressed, rested, and lightly stoved into a dark, sharply aromatic cake, which is then sliced as flake. The "navy" in the name nods to traditional sailors' tobaccos, but the blend carries no rum or similar flavoring. Since stoving deepens Virginia's natural sugar, the taste shifts away from fresh lemon Virginia's tang toward cooked fruit and dark bread. Airing the flakes and rubbing them out, or folding and packing them, suits smokers who favor a slow pace. Nicotine dose is medium. Discontinued when McClelland closed in 2018.
mcclelland-no-2035-dark-navy-flake.o: Leaves an intense tobacco aroma with dark bread-crust and dried-fruit tones.

rize-pazar-tutunu-wisconsin.z: Pazar tobacco is a domestic tobacco grown around the Pazar district of Rize in the Eastern Black Sea region. It traces back to a Wisconsin cigar-leaf seed variety, but the region's ecological conditions along with the curing, fermentation, and processing methods applied have shaped the leaf into a distinctive form. The leaves are large and elliptical, with a broad base; some reach 40-60 centimeters. Colors range from light brown to dark brown. The leaf texture is thin, flexible, and durable; the midrib is thick while the side veins are fine and sparse, meeting the midrib at close to a 90-degree angle. These physical traits make the leaf suitable for both cigar filler and wrapper use. Its physiological effect when smoked is firm, and it carries an aroma characteristic of cigar tobaccos. Burn quality is medium, and the ash is light gray. Its chemical composition shows nicotine content of about 1-2 percent, protein nitrogen 1.5-3 percent, and total reducing substances around 3.5 percent. It is a reference point for anyone interested in cigar rolling and looking for a domestic leaf.
rize-pazar-tutunu-wisconsin.o: Leaves a spicy, heavy leaf aroma reminiscent of cigar tobaccos.

mcclelland-no-615-calypso.z: One of McClelland's numbered bulk aromatics; no sufficient source describing its contents and character could be found.

faders-maharajah.z: Maharajah is recorded as an English blend among the house blends of Baltimore's Fader's tobacconist, which opened in 1891 and closed in 2018; no detailed record documenting its composition could be found.
faders-maharajah.o: Records do not contain enough information for a description.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-honey-roast.z: Honey Roast is a combination of golden-cut cavendish and black, fire-cured cavendish leaves; honey-flavored black cavendish is added to the mixture as a flavor booster. The honey note sits on a flatter, more sugary line than the fruit casings usual in aromatics. The manufacturer describes the blend as an option suited to all-day smoking. Suitable for smokers seeking a sweet but single-layered aromatic with a smoke that does not weigh on the tongue.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-honey-roast.o: Leaves a warmed honey and lightly toasted tobacco aroma.

pipesandcigars-com-old-glory.z: Old Glory is one of the house blends sold under its own name by the US-based retailer pipesandcigars.com; no sufficient independent sources documenting its content and character could be found.

d-r-tobacco-blenders-bench-bright-virgin.z: Bright Virginia Leaf is the bright Virginia leaf sold in Daughters & Ryan's Blenders Bench line. Taken from the upper leaves of the plant and flue-cured, this tobacco is light yellow-gold in color and carries a high sugar content. On the flavor side there's citrus tartness, grass and hay, tones recalling honey and bread, and a pronounced sweetness. It can be smoked on its own, but its main use is building the sweet, acidic backbone of blends; aimed at smokers wanting to build their own mixture.
d-r-tobacco-blenders-bench-bright-virgin.o: Leaves a sweet hay scent with a light citrus note.

teds-pipe-shoppe-1-11.z: One of the counter house blends from Ted's Pipe Shoppe in Tulsa; no independent source documenting its content could be found.

hearth-home-armada.z: Armada is one of the Latakia-containing mixtures in the Hearth & Home series, and records indicate it was discontinued as the brand's lineup was narrowed. In character, Latakia gives a creamy, smoky opening at first, followed by dark-fruit sweetness from the Virginia. The Latakia presence is more measured than in the brand's heavier English mixtures, while the fruity layer persists throughout the bowl. No top note is used. Body is medium. Suited to smokers who want Latakia as a balancing rather than dominant component; this blend is said to be found today only in old tins.
hearth-home-armada.o: Leaves a fine wood-smoke aroma along with dark dried-fruit scent.

synjeco-greenodd-rope.z: No sufficient primary source documenting the content and character of Synjeco's Greenodd Rope pipe tobacco could be found.

lane-limited-la-gloria-cubana.z: One of the blends Lane Limited released under a cigar brand's name; not enough sources could be found to describe its composition and character.

tabakfabrik-roth-seetaler.z: Seetaler is the medium-cut house blend from Tabakfabrik Roth in Beinwil am See, Switzerland. According to the maker, all the leaf comes from Swiss agriculture; the Burley and Virginia base is flavored with a light, Danish-style casing carrying subtle vanilla and caramel notes. The casing is kept light enough not to mask the leaf's own grassy, bready character. Thanks to its medium cut, the blend lights easily and burns cool; the nicotine load stays moderate. It suits smokers who want their aromatic in modest doses, avoid heavily cased blends, and are curious about tobacco grown and made locally. Tabakfabrik Roth is recorded as Switzerland's only operating tobacco factory, and offers Seetaler in packaging ranging from 100 grams up to a kilogram.
tabakfabrik-roth-seetaler.o: Leaves a lightly grassy background beneath sweet vanilla and burnt-sugar scent.

emerson-southern-forged-aberdeen.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing was found for the Emerson Southern Forged brand's Aberdeen blend, so the entry has been left open; records place it in the English family.

paul-olsen-square-flake.z: A blend from the Paul Olsen house's Virginia flake line; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found.

black-man-tobacco-company-royal-scot.z: No reliable source documenting the content and character of Royal Scot, from Black Man Tobacco Company, could be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-special-d.z: Special Dublin Loose Mixture is the series' loose-cut main variety. Virginia leaves of US, African, and Brazilian origin are lightly pressed, then cut and blended with dark black cavendish; a casing evoking Irish whiskey is applied on top. The result is a fruity-sweet, full yet mild aromatic. Moisture is average, lighting is easy and the burn is slow. It is not considered heavy on nicotine; it appeals to newcomers to aromatic tobaccos as well as those seeking a light daytime indulgence. Because the loose cut requires a habit of packing and lighting, the producer describes this tobacco as aimed at experienced smokers. It is distributed in a 50-gram pouch and 100- and 200-gram tins; European distribution goes through Scandinavian Tobacco Group.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-special-d.o: Leaves a lightly alcoholic scent evoking fruity sweetness and whiskey.

ken-byron-ventures-keep-calm.z: One of Ken Byron Ventures' limited-release blends; no independent source could be found to document its contents.
ken-byron-ventures-keep-calm.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-river-of-deceit-2020.z: A Virginia-forward blend released in 2020; not enough sources could be found to document its composition.

piatro-lee-tobacco-company-one-shilling.z: No sources documenting the content and character of the One Shilling blend, recorded under the Piatro & Lee Tobacco Company name, could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-wilke-no-78.z: No. 78, one of Wilke Pipe Tobacco's numbered bulk blends, is recorded as an unflavored English-style mixture; no verifiable source could be found regarding the blend's composition.

cornell-diehl-morning-drive.z: Morning Drive is Cornell & Diehl's ribbon-cut English mixture. Red and bright Virginia leaves form the base; burley adds a nutty body, Turkish leaf and perique bring spice, and Latakia layers in a measured touch of smoke. As an unflavored blend, the taste comes entirely from the balance of leaf, and the Latakia level has been deliberately kept low. Being on the milder end of strength, it works well as a morning smoke or for long sessions, and also serves as a good entry point for smokers new to Latakia blends. According to reports, the Latakia and perique notes become more pronounced with age. It is offered in a 2-ounce tin and an 8-ounce size.
cornell-diehl-morning-drive.o: Carries a fine trace of smoke and spice within a nutty tobacco aroma.

clan-shaw-lucerne.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Lucerne.

tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-wilder-frut.z: This is the aromatic blend of the Wilder line flavored with fruit and floral essences; the maker's stated Virginia-Burley base and handmade process built on natural fermentation apply to this blend as well. Since no independent source describing the composition ratios and smoking character could be found, the record is kept limited.
tabacos-wilder-finamore-ltda-wilder-frut.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity and floral scent.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-mandle-vanilla.z: Mandle Vanilla is an American-type aromatic bringing together burley, golden cavendish, and Virginia leaves. It is noted to be flavored with McGahey's own vanilla extract and is sold in bulk. Burley gives the blend a dry, nutty base and a medium nicotine level, while Virginia and cavendish balance the sugar. Vanilla is pronounced but doesn't entirely cover the leaf's taste. Suitable for smokers accustomed to American-type aromatics and those looking for a sweet blend for regular daily smoking.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-mandle-vanilla.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of vanilla and baked dough.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-butters.z: An aromatic blend released under Ken Byron Ventures' Mr. Christian's line; no accessible source could be found to document its contents.

d-r-tobacco-blenders-bench-red-virginia.z: Red Virginia is the dark-colored Virginia leaf sold in Daughters & Ryan's Blenders Bench line. Coming from the plant's lower leaves or darkened through heat treatment, this tobacco gives a less sharp, deeper flavor than bright Virginias. Its flavor brings forward dark fruit, bread, light earth, and a heavier sweetness; nicotine sits medium. In blending it's used as a source of body and mature sweetness, to balance out the acidity of bright Virginias.
d-r-tobacco-blenders-bench-red-virginia.o: Leaves a scent of baked bread and dark fruit.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-cowboy-co.z: Cowboy Coffee, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as a Virginia-forward mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

john-aylesbury-luxury-flake-classic-flak.z: John Aylesbury Classic Flake is an unflavored Virginia flake known under two names, since one side of its tin reads "Classic" and the other "Luxury." The leaf is pressed in the navy-cut style, processed to bring out Virginia's natural sweetness; the blend is produced in Denmark. The John Aylesbury name doesn't belong to a single person but to a group of German tobacconists united under a joint brand. On the smoke it gives a citrusy, herbal sweetness that deepens into a breadier line further into the bowl. Strength is below medium and the smoke is cool and even. A good option for smokers used to preparing flake, seeking unflavored Virginia, and wanting a tobacco suited to cellaring.
john-aylesbury-luxury-flake-classic-flak.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma reminiscent of dry straw and citrus peel.

dream-castle-tobacco-company-top-value-n.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Top Value Natural, a pipe tobacco from Dream Castle Tobacco Company.
dream-castle-tobacco-company-top-value-n.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

sentimiento-nacional-arandu.z: According to records, one of Sentimiento Nacional's unflavored blends built on Virginia and Burley; detailed content and character information could not be substantiated with a verifiable source.

middle-earth-tobacco-erebor.z: Erebor is one of Middle Earth Tobacco's Tolkien-inspired blend names; no source could be found regarding its composition, cut, and character.
middle-earth-tobacco-erebor.o: No source describing its aroma could be found.

poschl-tabak-tilbury-sweet-vanilla.z: Tilbury Sweet Vanilla is the member of Pöschl Tabak's Tilbury line flavored with a vanilla casing. Black Cavendish is added to a Virginia and Burley base, presented in ribbon cut. The vanilla note is clearly upfront both in the tin note and the smoke. Nicotine is low and the tobacco taste mellow; the burn is even. It suits fans of classic vanilla aromatics as well as those looking for a light-bodied everyday smoke. The product is continued in 40-gram packs.
poschl-tabak-tilbury-sweet-vanilla.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of vanilla and sweet baked pastry.

organic-smoke-inc-kentucky-select-organi.z: Kentucky Select is Organic Smoke Inc.'s line of unflavored tobacco produced in Kentucky. Sweet Virginia and mild burley leaf form the core of the blends; one line member uses oriental leaf and two use menthol. The maker states it adds no essence or chemical additives to the leaf and applies an organic processing method. Finely cut and coming relatively dry, this tobacco is mainly sold in resealable bags ranging from 170 grams to 2.3 kilograms. It suits smokers seeking an unflavored, straightforward tobacco taste who want to stock up long-term with bulk packaging; nicotine load is medium, and it carries no aromatic sweetness.
organic-smoke-inc-kentucky-select-organi.o: Leaves a straightforward tobacco scent recalling dry hay and toasted bread crust.

mcclelland-no-400-creme-caramel.z: A caramel-flavored blend in McClelland's numbered bulk aromatic series; no sufficient source documenting its composition could be found.

samuel-gawith-r-c-turkish.z: A Samuel Gawith product built on Oriental leaf and offered as a blending component; no sufficient independent source on its content and production status could be found.
samuel-gawith-r-c-turkish.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay and light spice.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-nutty-mixture.z: Nutty Mixture is one of the blends carrying the own name of the McGahey tobacconist, in business in Devon since 1880. Bright and dark fire-cured Virginia leaves are combined with burley, with latakia scattered in between giving the mixture a smoky edge. The leaf is presented as ready-rubbed ribbon, which makes packing the pipe and getting an even burn easier.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-nutty-mixture.o: Leaves an aroma of toasted walnut and light woody smoke.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-five-brot.z: Five Brothers is an old, single-blend American brand named after the Finzer brothers who first released the product. Its content is solely air-cured burley; no casing or flavoring is applied, and the leaf is cut fine enough to resemble cigarette tobacco, in a shag cut. It is sold in small tins. The blend's defining trait is its nicotine load; according to records, this plain burley, once the everyday tobacco of American smokers a few generations back, is considered very strong by today's standards. Because of the fine cut it burns fast, so moistening it and half-filling small pipes is a common approach. Suited to experienced smokers seeking unflavored, straight, high-nicotine burley; not for those accustomed to mild blends.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-five-brot.o: Leaves a sharp, dry, earthy burley scent carrying no sweet trace.

just-for-him-black-cordial.z: One of the house blends the Just For Him tobacconist prepares at its own counter; no independent source could be found on its contents or character.

sutliff-tobacco-company-peach-cobbler-20.z: Sutliff's SPS-2011-coded Peach Cobbler blend takes its name from the fruit-filled baked dessert of the same name. Fresh peach, vanilla, and a small brown-sugar note are drawn into a ribbon-cut base of burley, Virginia, and black cavendish leaf. Nicotine is light and tongue bite is minimal, making it a blend that even those new to pipes could smoke. Since the leaf can arrive moist, airing it for a while before packing makes for an easier burn. It suits those looking for a fruity smoke that fits the summer months.
sutliff-tobacco-company-peach-cobbler-20.o: Leaves a scent of baked peach, vanilla, and brown sugar.

sutliff-tobacco-company-days-end.z: Sufficient sources to confirm the composition and character of Days End, referred to as a Sutliff-branded aromatic, could not be found.

gatlin-burlier-cumberland.z: Not enough sourcing explaining its content could be found for Cumberland, referenced as one of the house blends of the Gatlinburlier tobacconist in Gatlinburg, Tennessee.
gatlin-burlier-cumberland.o: Records do not document a room note.

lane-limited-black-cherry.z: A black-cavendish-forward bulk aromatic whose body is sweetened with dark cherry essence. It's a ribbon cut with high moisture; the burn is cool and nicotine is low. The cherry note stays within a smoky, sweet frame and defines the smoke's main character. It's among the best-known members of Lane Limited's bulk aromatic line, representing the classic fruity blend concept sold by the pound at American tobacconists. Suited to smokers seeking a sweet, easy-smoking everyday tobacco rather than heavy latakia or intense Virginia character, and to newcomers to pipes.
lane-limited-black-cherry.o: Leaves a ripe cherry and sweet syrup room note.

reiner-long-golden-flake.z: Long Golden Flake is a Virginia, Burley, and Perique blend released under the Reiner name. Its cut is long flake; reports note strips roughly 40 centimeters long and 4 centimeters wide, coiled and placed in an airtight tin. The moisture level straight from the tin is ready for smoking; if needed, sections can be cut from the coil with scissors for packing. At the start of the smoke, Virginia's sweetness and Perique's peppery tone come forward; further in, Burley takes over to build a tangy body, and Perique recedes into the background. Nicotine is medium and flavor intensity between medium and high. The ash stays light gray; smoked quickly it doesn't gum up but is prone to heating the pipe. It suits smokers looking for natural Virginia sweetness without added flavoring who are used to flake tobacco.
reiner-long-golden-flake.o: Leaves a warm, lightly sweet tobacco and baked-bread aroma.

butera-blended-flake.z: Blended Flake is the flake tobacco in the Royal Vintage line bearing the name of pipe maker Michael Butera; the blend was prepared at the McClelland workshop. Its composition includes matured red virginia, hand-selected Oriental leaf, hot-air-cured leaf from North Carolina, and long-cut St. James perique. The slices range between medium and dark brown; the aroma is spicy and earthy. It is one of the few Latakia-free Oriental blends; the flavor moves back and forth between virginia's tart sweetness, Oriental's dry spice, and perique's peppery hit. Suitable for smokers seeking a complex flake without Latakia.
butera-blended-flake.o: Leaves a tart dried fruit, pepper and lightly musty bread aroma.

clan-shaw-grandpas-blend.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of Clan Shaw's Grandpa's Blend blend could be found.

watch-city-cigar-viral-vanilla.z: Watch City Cigar's blend called Viral Vanilla is, according to records, one of the house blends of the Waltham, Massachusetts tobacconist shop; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

robert-mcconnell-paddington.z: Paddington is one of the replacement blends that appeared after Dunhill-branded tobaccos ceased production, offered as a stand-in for Royal Yacht, which Dunhill began producing in 1912. It is made under the Robert McConnell name by the German firm Kohlhase & Kopp. The tin holds neatly cut, reddish-brown ribbon strands with a heavy casing aroma; tin moisture runs high and it benefits from airing out before packing. The flavoring leans toward plum and mixed fruit with a tart edge; an acidic sharpness from the underripe Virginia base shows through in the first bowls. The abundance of burn additives is noted to make it burn fast and leaves it prone to tongue bite; toward the end of the bowl the flavoring recedes and a firm, lightly sweet Virginia taste comes forward. It is aimed at smokers who want a fruit-forward aromatic and are careful to smoke slowly.
robert-mcconnell-paddington.o: Leaves a sweet, bakery-like room note carrying fruity overtones.

pauls-pipe-shop-darwin-asa.z: For Paul's Pipe Shop's blend called Darwin Asa, no independent sources such as the maker's own materials or a reliable product record could be found, so no definitive information can be given about the blend's composition and character.

consolidated-z-50-black-cordial.z: No verifiable sourcing could be found for this blend sold under the Consolidated name, so its content and character cannot be described.

sutliff-tobacco-company-bahamian-rhapsod.z: A blend from Sutliff's Z-coded bulk aromatic line; sufficient independent sources describing its composition and character could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-bahamian-rhapsod.o: Records indicate it leaves a tropical fruit scent.

hu-tobacco-directors-cut.z: Director's Cut is a Virginia-Perique blend in HU Tobacco's Original Warehouse line. Its structure brings together curly-cut discs containing Virginia and Perique, selected Burley grades, sugary loose-cut Virginia, and a small amount of fire-cured leaf. The traditional method, based on maturing rolled tobaccos, lets resinous sweet notes evoking dried plum, anise, and port wine come forward on opening the pouch; in the smoke, the Perique's spice becomes pronounced. HU Tobacco is a brand producing in small batches in Germany. This blend suits smokers looking for the spicy, full end of the Virginia-Perique family, accustomed to complex structures where different cuts are combined. It carries no flavoring.
hu-tobacco-directors-cut.o: Leaves a sweet-spicy aroma in the direction of dried plum and anise.
