nat-sherman-chinatown.z: One of Nat Sherman's aromatic house blends named after New York neighborhoods; no independent source describing its composition could be found.

kadewe-flake-no-100.z: No reliable sources — neither the maker's own description nor an independent review — could be found for KaDeWe's Flake No.100, so the profile is left incomplete.

black-cat-cigar-company-buttered-rum.z: A rum-and-butter-themed bulk aromatic from Black Cat Cigar Company; no manufacturer recipe for its content could be found.
black-cat-cigar-company-buttered-rum.o: Leaves a rum and buttered-sugar room note.

hearth-home-strikeforce.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for this blend, said to contain cigar leaf, from the Hearth & Home brand.

milan-tobacconists-centennial.z: Centennial is a house aromatic prepared under a name tied to Milan Tobacconists' hundredth anniversary. Golden virginia leaves are combined with black cavendish; according to the maker's description it carries a subtle vanilla note, a light fruit touch, and a measured sweetness. Its body is light and the nicotine load stays low. Since the casing is set so as not to mask the tobacco taste, it forms an in-between option for smokers who avoid heavy aromatics but don't want a fully unflavored virginia either.
milan-tobacconists-centennial.o: Leaves an aroma of vanilla and light fruit, with the sweetness of honey-colored tobacco underneath.

wolfway-pyramid.z: Pyramid is a Wolfway blend that references the Egyptian pyramids. According to the maker's stated composition, Egyptian Latakia, Maryland-grown golden Virginia, and Izmir-type Oriental leaf from Greece's Katerini region are combined. It is a light blend with a pronounced Oriental character that only touches on the English style; with its nicotine kept low, it suits those seeking an Oriental blend that can be smoked all day.
wolfway-pyramid.o: Leaves a scent of dry grass and spice alongside a faint trace of incense.

drew-estate-grand-central.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of Grand Central, a blend from Drew Estate.

borkum-riff-limited-edition-22-mixture-f.z: One of Borkum Riff's limited-run numbered blend series; as the name suggests, it carries fruit and vanilla flavoring. No source documenting its leaf composition could be found, leaving the profile incomplete.
borkum-riff-limited-edition-22-mixture-f.o: Leaves a room note of vanilla and fruit sweetness.

chonowitsch-t-15.z: T 15 is a Latakia-containing English mixture belonging to the series prepared in small batches under Jess Chonowitsch's name; no reliable manufacturer or retailer description detailing its composition and character could be found.
chonowitsch-t-15.o: Leaves a smoky aroma derived from Latakia.

mcclelland-mellow-mack.z: Mellow Mack is a light flavored blend in McClelland's Premium Aromatics line. Records indicate pecan and honey notes are used at the casing stage; the flavor line runs mild and plain, and nicotine load stays low. Suited to those seeking a sweet but non-syrupy flavored blend that doesn't weigh you down during the day, and to those new to the pipe. Discontinued when the brand closed in 2018.
mcclelland-mellow-mack.o: Leaves a honeyed and nutty, sweet aroma.

holts-cigar-company-sansom-street.z: This is a house blend of Holt's Cigar Company named after a street in Philadelphia; it's mentioned among the company's unflavored house blends, but no independent source describing its composition could be found.
holts-cigar-company-sansom-street.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

mac-baren-mellow-choice.z: Mellow Choice is a member of Mac Baren's aromatic Choice line. In this loose-cut blend, golden Virginia provides its natural sugar, the brand's own modern cavendish gives a sweetish, lightly sour character, and air-cured burley balances the body. The top casing works in two directions: sweet vanilla and dark chocolate notes are used together. Nicotine is low, the smoke is soft, and the loose cut lights easily. A moderately flavored blend that both newcomers and habitual aromatic smokers can smoke all day.
mac-baren-mellow-choice.o: Leaves a vanilla and bitter chocolate room note.

seattle-pipe-club-plum-pudding.z: Plum Pudding is Seattle Pipe Club's best-known entry and the centerpiece of the brand's Balkan line. The blend combines Cyprus Latakia, Turkish Orientals, Virginia leaf, Perique, and black cavendish. The Latakia density makes the blend distinctly smoky, while the Orientals open a bitter, spicy layer; the cavendish and Perique feed the dried-fruit and plum direction the name evokes. The ingredient list carries no additives; the sweet and fruity traces in the blend come from the leaves' own composition. The smoke is intense and full-bodied, so it falls within the territory of smokers accustomed to Latakia. One of the go-to records for those wanting to get to know the Balkan class; due to its nicotine and flavor intensity, it is usually reserved for later in the day.
seattle-pipe-club-plum-pudding.o: Leaves a scent of heavy pine smoke, dried fruit, and leather.

schrauf-nr-218-whisky.z: Nr. 218 Whisky is one of the house blends prepared on-site by the Tabak Schrauf house in Nuremberg. Selected Virginia leaves matured in wooden barrels are conditioned with bourbon whiskey; a spice casing completes the blend's dark, near-black appearance. The smoke is mild, calibrated not to leave harshness on the tongue; nicotine load stays between low and medium. Suited to smokers who enjoy alcohol-cased aromatics and want a spicy depth alongside the sweetness. The blend is offered in a 100-gram tin within the producer's house-blend line.
schrauf-nr-218-whisky.o: A light spice accompanies the oak-barrel and sweet bourbon scent.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-north-star.z: North Star is prepared by combining light Brazilian- and Indian-origin leaf with dark Indonesian- and Indian-origin leaf, sauced with licorice root. The light leaves carry the sweetness, while the dark leaves carry the body and earthy depth. The licorice topping is the blend's most pronounced marker; its sweetness is rooty and lightly bitter rather than sugary. Suited to smokers wanting a pronounced top note that steers away from Kendal tradition's floral, soapy notes.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-north-star.o: Leaves a dark, sweet aroma reminiscent of licorice root and anise.

black-man-tobacco-company-flake-royal.z: No reliable source documenting the content and character of Flake Royal, from Black Man Tobacco Company, could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-mixed.z: Kendal Mixed is formed by blending together the house's Kendal series' flue-cured and fire-cured Virginias. Its fine-cut structure lights easily and burns evenly. On the flavor palette, the light Virginia's sweetness is balanced by the dark leaf's smoky tone; nicotine is moderate. Suited to smokers wanting a middle ground between Kendal Gold and Kendal Dark, looking for an unflavored everyday blend.
gawith-hoggarth-co-kendal-mixed.o: Leaves a lightly smoky tobacco aroma reminiscent of dry bread.

admirals-choice-vanilla-cavendish.z: Admiral's Choice Vanilla Cavendish is a blend in the classic American aromatic mold. Nutty Burley, mellow black Cavendish, and a small amount of sweet Virginia are brought together; a vanilla top layer is applied over them. The vanilla note is creamy and kept at a level that doesn't fully mask the tobacco; strength is low. Per records, Admiral's Choice was born as a major American drugstore chain's own tobacco brand, and after the chain stopped selling tobacco, its distribution moved to mail-order and online sellers. It suits those looking for a mellow, sweet aromatic they can smoke all day.
admirals-choice-vanilla-cavendish.o: Leaves a trace close to vanilla pastry cream and sweet bakery scent.

gq-tobaccos-burper-kake.z: GQ Tobaccos's Burley-and-Perique blend, pressed into cake form; records indicate it is one of the producer's highest Perique-ratio blends. There is not enough independent sourcing to describe the blend's composition and character in detail.

cornell-diehl-the-beast-2023.z: The Beast is one of Cornell & Diehl's year-to-year repeating limited releases, taking its name from the extraordinarily high proportion of Perique that forms the blend's backbone. The maker states roughly half the mixture is Perique from its own Louisiana farm, joined by Virginia, dark fire-cured Kentucky, and black Cavendish leaf. Before blending, the leaf is rested in rum for close to a week; this step functions less as a flavoring and more to let the tobaccos fuse together. Cut is ribbon. On the flavor side, stone-fruit tones like fig and plum, earth, mesquite wood, and a pronounced black-pepper sharpness stand out; the umami note Perique brings is considered the blend's signature. Nicotine load and flavor intensity are shown at the top of the maker's own scale, making this a blend cut out for experienced smokers accustomed to strong blends. The 2023 release is that year's batch of the same recipe; C&D releases this series in limited quantity every year.
cornell-diehl-the-beast-2023.o: Leaves a dark trace reminiscent of mesquite wood smoke, with a heavy, spicy, tangy tobacco scent.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrug-no-176.z: Surbrug No. 176 is one of the historic Surbrug recipes Wilke absorbed into its lineup. According to the maker's description, the base consists of Virginia and Latakia, topped with Turkish leaf and black cavendish. This structure adds a soft sweetness from the cavendish to a classic English framework. It's described as a medium-intensity smoke. It suits smokers who want Latakia in moderation, along with the Oriental leaf's spice and the rounding effect of the cavendish. It's part of Wilke's non-aromatic bulk listing.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrug-no-176.o: A lightly sweet tone accompanies the woody smoke scent.

cornell-diehl-pipe-smokers-forum-kickin-.z: A limited Virginia-Perique blend prepared for a pipe forum; no adequate source documenting its ratios and character was found.
cornell-diehl-pipe-smokers-forum-kickin-.o: No adequate information for a description could be found in records.

my-smoking-shop-black-kathy-vanilla-blac.z: Black Kathy is one of the American-style bulk blends under the Century name, sold by weight from the jar at English tobacconists. Virginia leaves, soft Burley, and black cavendish are brought together; the mixture is sauced with vanilla. Thanks to its ribbon cut and high moisture, it burns cool and slow. Nicotine is low, and the taste is sweet and single-noted: vanilla leads from start to finish, while the tobacco's own taste stays in the background. A blend fitting the classic vanilla cavendish description, one that even a beginning pipe smoker could comfortably smoke.
my-smoking-shop-black-kathy-vanilla-blac.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough aroma.

deadwood-tobacco-house-blends-sweet-jane.z: This is an aromatic pipe blend sharing its name with Deadwood Tobacco's cigar series of the same name; per records it has a sweet profile evoking cocoa and coffee. Since the maker hasn't published a detailed ingredient list for the pipe version, its leaf composition is unclear.
deadwood-tobacco-house-blends-sweet-jane.o: Leaves a dark, sweet scent evoking cocoa and coffee.

mac-baren-scaferlati-caporal-bleu.z: Scaferlati Caporal is one of the names in French pipe tradition dating back centuries. Produced for many years under the Seita umbrella, the series has since been continued by Scandinavian Tobacco Group and Mac Baren. Bleu is the series' dark-leaning member: dark-fire-cured Kentucky is balanced with bright Virginia leaf, and air-cured, fermented tobacco is added to the blend. Its loose cut packs easily into a pipe, with no topping or flavoring applied. The smoke gives an earthy, spicy, dry tobacco taste; no sugar or vanilla-like sweetness is sought. Records indicate it's the fullest-bodied member of the series, with a pronounced nicotine load. Suited to smokers used to unflavored, strong-edged French-style tobaccos who want a full pipe later in the day; heavy for first-time pipe smokers.
mac-baren-scaferlati-caporal-bleu.o: Leaves an aroma of dry earth, soot, and light grain.

solani-113-sweet-mystery.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Solani blend 113: Sweet Mystery could not be found.

emerson-southern-forged-mountaineers-res.z: Not enough first-hand sourcing was found for the Emerson Southern Forged brand's Mountaineer's Resolve blend, so the entry has been left open; records place it in the Cigar Leaf Based family.

d-r-tobacco-vengeur-silver-blend.z: Vengeur Silver Blend is the light-bodied member of Daughters & Ryan's Vengeur line. As across the line, Virginia, Burley, and Oriental leaf are used, and records indicate no chemical flavoring is added; the distinction is built on body and leaf ratio. It's ribbon cut, offered in large packagings. In the Silver version, nicotine and flavor load sit below Regular and Platinum; Virginia's dry sweetness and Burley's nutty base come forward while Oriental stays in the background. A fitting choice for those wanting the unflavored American mixture line with a softer body, or looking for long, low-intensity smokes.
d-r-tobacco-vengeur-silver-blend.o: Leaves a light woody and dry-hay scent.

japan-tobacco-condor-plug.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of Japan Tobacco's Condor Plug blend could be found.

cornell-diehl-seersucker.z: Seersucker is a blend in Cornell & Diehl's Cellar series, presented in plug (pressed) form. It takes its name from the South's summer fabric and was first released in July 2016. Its composition includes cigar leaf, fire-cured Kentucky, Burley, Oriental, Virginia, and black Cavendish. The combination of cigar leaf and dark fire-cured Kentucky gives the blend a dark character along the axis of leather, earth, and spice; the plug form is well suited to letting the leaves fuse together over time. The maker states the product is designed to mature over seven to ten years of aging, and gives strength, flavor, and room note values as high. Suited to experienced smokers accustomed to cigar tobacco character and presentations sliced from a block.
cornell-diehl-seersucker.o: A dark scent dominated by leather and earth, coming from cigar leaf, spreads through the room.

wessex-rotary.z: Wessex Rotary is a blend not found in current maker and retailer listings; no sufficient source could be found documenting its composition.
wessex-rotary.o: According to the records, no scent description has been documented.

seattle-pipe-club-hood-canal.z: Referred to as one of Seattle Pipe Club's Balkan-style blends, an earthy and full-bodied mixture; no sufficient source detailing its composition could be found.

rattray-red-lion.z: Red Lion is one of Rattray's traditional English blends. Golden Virginia leaf is joined by Latakia's smoky character, black Cavendish's sweetness, and the spicy sweetness of Greek Basma-type Oriental leaf; it is a ribbon cut. The blend's body is full and filling in nicotine. Latakia smoke and Oriental spice trade off through the smoke, while Cavendish builds a sweet ground in the background. It carries no flavoring. It suits smokers looking for a classic Latakia-heavy English mixture, wanting a full-bodied tobacco suited to evening smoking. The Rattray name draws on the Scottish pipe-tobacco tradition; the brand's tobaccos are produced today in Germany.
rattray-red-lion.o: Leaves a heavy aroma reminiscent of wood smoke and incense, carrying a spicy trace.

hu-tobacco-red-sparkle.z: This is a limited mixture appearing on retailer listings in the "United Passion" special blends line of Hans Wiedemann's HU Tobacco workshop in Germany; no reliable source describing its content and character could be found.

clan-shaw-royal-court.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Royal Court.

stanislaw-helfstyn.z: A Virginia-based blend from the Czech firm Mostex's Stanislaw brand, taking its name from Helfštýn Castle in Moravia; sufficient independent sources describing its composition could not be found.
stanislaw-helfstyn.o: No description is available in records.

savinelli-cavendish.z: An aromatic, ribbon-cut Savinelli blend built on cavendish-processed leaf; no sufficient source documenting its casing and proportions could be found.

davidoff-red-mixture.z: Red Mixture is part of Davidoff's aromatic line known as Red-Green-Blue. It's prepared from Virginia and black cavendish leaves, ready-rubbed cut, and flavored with vanilla and caramel. With its light fullness and soft smoke, it has an aromatic structure suited to daily use. Turkish-language sources report it's built on a similar setup to the other members of the series. It suits those seeking a pronounced, non-strong flavored blend.
davidoff-red-mixture.o: Leaves a vanilla and caramel scent.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-mediterranean-nights.z: Mediterranean Nights is among the bulk blends of Wilke Pipe Tobacco, founded in New York in 1872 and today carried on in Massachusetts. According to the maker's recipe, the blend's backbone is flue-cured bright Virginia; citrus tartness, grass, bread, sugar, floral tones, and a light spice with a hint of lemon sourness sit clearly above the flavoring level. The maker states that body is strong, depth and nicotine are high, and the flavor is full; in this respect the blend appeals to smokers seeking Oriental-forward, unflavored smokes accustomed to fullness. Given its unflavored construction, it's not suitable for newcomers seeking an aromatic. According to records, though the blend occasionally goes out of stock, it continues to appear in the maker's bulk catalog.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-mediterranean-nights.o: Leaves a lightly spicy, bready trace alongside a scent of tart lemon and dry grass.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-bovey-orange.z: Bovey Orange is an American-style aromatic from McGahey The Tobacconist's series of blends named after Devon place names. Its composition includes black cavendish and bright Virginia leaves, joined by a small amount of fermented burley. It is flavored with a bit of honey and orange aroma. Since the burley share is kept low, the nicotine strength stays limited; cavendish and Virginia together build a soft, sugary body. Rather than covering the blend, the orange note is balanced by the honey's sweetness. An entry geared toward those looking for an aromatic that can be smoked over long periods without tiring the tongue. The brand traces back as a tobacconist to 1880 in Devon and distributes its blends through its own channel.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-bovey-orange.o: Leaves a sweet trace where orange peel mixes with a honey aroma.

cornell-diehl-five-oclock-shadow-working.z: Five O'Clock Shadow is a member of Cornell & Diehl's Working Man series, dedicated to the working person. Red Virginia, fire-cured Kentucky, and perique are pressed into a cake, presented as an easily crumbled, dark-flecked block; once crumbled it yields a fine cut close to shag, making it practical to pack. On opening the tin, dry grass and floral Virginia sweetness are layered with Kentucky's smoky aroma and perique's tangy-spiced fruit note. On the smoke, perique's spice turns raisin-like, joined by Virginia's sweetness and an earthy note from the Kentucky, with pronounced nicotine. Its heavy body and long burn suit smaller-chambered pipes; it is aimed at those seeking an unflavored, high-nicotine blend.
cornell-diehl-five-oclock-shadow-working.o: The fire-cured leaf's woody, smoky aroma lingers in the room together with sweet dry grass and fermented fruit spice.

cornell-diehl-easy-times.z: Easy Times is an unflavored mixture Cornell & Diehl builds in the classic American-English mold. Red Virginia is joined by fire-cured Kentucky, burley, and a small amount of Latakia; the cut is ribbon. On the smoke, Virginia's sweetness leads first, followed by an earthy, lightly coffee-like tone brought by the burley and fire-cured leaf. It doesn't treat the tongue harshly, holding its balance when smoked slowly. It suits those looking for an everyday blend with measured Latakia and a hearty body.
cornell-diehl-easy-times.o: Leaves an earthy, smoky aroma in the room reminiscent of wood fire and coffee.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrugs-crystal-pala.z: Surbrug's Crystal Palace, according to the maker's records, is based on a recipe going back to 1859 and is carried on today by Wilke Pipe Tobacco. A small amount of Perique, black cavendish, and Burley is added to a Virginia and Latakia base. The maker describes the blend as light, soft, and naturally aromatic; no flavoring is added, and the sweetness comes from the leaf's own processing. Since the Latakia ratio is moderate, it's an entry-level record for those new to English blends and for smokers who don't want heavy smoke.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-surbrugs-crystal-pala.o: Leaves a measured scent, lightly smoky and sweetish, reminiscent of dry leaf.

robert-mcconnell-oriental-turkish-blend.z: Oriental Turkish Blend is considered one of Robert McConnell's oldest recipes; according to records it was first prepared in the early 1800s. The blend's weight is made up of light-colored Oriental leaves of Turkish, Syrian, and Cyprus origin. Small leaves from Macedonia and the Levant hills are rested together with Carolina bright leaf and Virginia's Red Old Belt leaves for a week so the flavors merge, then Carolina black cavendish is added and the mixture is stored loosely. The result is a spicy, dry-hay, lightly sour taste; the cavendish builds a small but sweet foundation. Nicotine is medium, flavor intensity high. A suitable example for those wanting to get to know Oriental-leaf-centered blends that don't contain Latakia.
robert-mcconnell-oriental-turkish-blend.o: Leaves a dry hay, spice, and lightly sour incense scent.

cobblestone-cafe-black-coffee.z: Cobblestone's Cafe Black Coffee blend is, per available records, a ribbon-cut, flavored mixture, though not enough independent sourcing could be found to detail its composition.

chacom-saint-claude.z: Saint Claude takes its name from the town in France's Jura region that is Chacom's home base and considered the cradle of French pipe-making. Light and red Virginias form the body of the blend, with a small proportion of black cavendish added alongside them. A lightly applied chocolate-and-vanilla casing sits on top. The casing is kept restrained enough not to overtake the leaf; chocolate is somewhat more pronounced, giving a marshmallow-like tone at times. The smoke is cool and clean, flavor intensity leans light, and nicotine is low. Suitable for those seeking a soft aromatic with a measured casing that can be smoked all day.
chacom-saint-claude.o: Leaves a cocoa and vanilla-confection room note.

doctor-pipe-pure-dark-fired.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Pure Dark Fired, a pipe tobacco from Doctor Pipe.
doctor-pipe-pure-dark-fired.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

stanwell-jubilee.z: Poul Stanwell Jubilee is a blend prepared for the brand's founding anniversary that became a permanent line member. It's built from Virginia, burley, Kentucky, and oriental leaves; after resting in wooden barrels, it's tinned in a ready-rubbed cut. The topping level is measured: fruit and vanilla notes stay light enough not to mask the leaf's own flavor, while Kentucky adds a smoky depth and body to the blend. This structure places it somewhere between a full aromatic and an unflavored blend; it functions as a stepping stone for smokers wanting to move from aromatics toward natural tobacco.
stanwell-jubilee.o: A dry trace of smoky Kentucky leaf sits beneath a light fruity vanilla scent.

peter-heinrichs-no-108.z: Peter Heinrichs No. 108 is a blend described as a traditional English mixture, built from Latakia and Old Belt-region Virginias. The maker states that although the blend stays very low in nicotine, it offers a satisfying smoke. The Virginia base provides sweetness and a cool burn while Latakia adds a smoky layer; since no flavoring is used, the taste comes entirely from the processing of the leaves. It is a record suitable for smokers who want to get to know Latakia mixtures but don't want high nicotine, one that can be spread across any time of day.
peter-heinrichs-no-108.o: Leaves a smoked wood and campfire aroma.

cornell-diehl-tawny-port.z: No listing for Cornell & Diehl's Tawny Port blend could be found in the maker's current catalogue or in major retailer listings; its composition could not be confirmed.

hearth-home-black-house-10th-anniversary.z: BlackHouse is one of Hearth & Home's Latakia-forward classics: it contains plentiful Cyprian Latakia, bright and fragrant Orientals, sweet Virginias, and a pinch of fire-cured Kentucky. To imitate the effect of long aging, the blend also includes a small amount of Perique and unflavored black Cavendish. The 10th Anniversary edition is a limited release prepared for the blend's tenth year. Records indicate that when a small quantity of well-aged Oriental leaf remained on hand, the Orientals in the original recipe were replaced with this old stock; since the leaf quantity was limited, production stayed limited as well. Here Latakia doesn't stand out on its own but mainly frames the Orientals' complex flavor with camphor and peat-like tones. Designed for smokers who enjoy the Balkan style and are accustomed to smoky, spicy mixtures.
hearth-home-black-house-10th-anniversary.o: Leaves an aroma of campfire smoke, camphor, and resinous incense.

pipesandcigars-com-summer-splash.z: Summer Splash is the August installment of the monthly blend line Russ Ouellette designs for pipesandcigars.com. A bright blackberry-strawberry-evoking fruit flavoring, with a pastry note sitting in the background, is added to a body of Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish. It is a ribbon cut; against light nicotine, the casing side is pronounced. It is a blend designed for summer months and outdoor smoking, aimed at fans of fruity aromatics. Being part of the monthly line, it is not kept in continuous production.
pipesandcigars-com-summer-splash.o: Leaves a fresh forest-fruit and baked-pastry aroma in the room.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-clan-high.z: A blend referred to as a variety under the Clan brand; no sufficient source describing its content and character could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-byzantium-525.z: Byzantium #525 is a mixture in Sutliff's bulk line, associated with records tying it to a same-named blend reportedly produced for Georgetown Tobacco; sufficient sources reliably documenting its composition and character could not be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-byzantium-525.o: Records did not provide sufficient information for a description.

faders-fort-mchenry.z: Not enough independent sourcing documenting the composition and character of Fort McHenry, one of the house blends of the Baltimore-based Fader's tobacconist, could be found.

cornell-diehl-black-tan-cavendish.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Cornell & Diehl blend Black & Tan Cavendish.

consolidated-my-vineyard.z: Not enough independent sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Consolidated blend My Vineyard.

tobacco-land-mocca.z: Mocca, associated with the Tobacco Land name, is recorded as a coffee-themed flavored pipe blend; no verifiable source describing its composition, cut, or maker has been found.
tobacco-land-mocca.o: Noted as a coffee-flavored blend; no detailed description of its aroma has been found in records.

gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-flake-liquorice.z: This is the liquorice-topped version of the Brown Flake family. Burley is added to Virginia leaves that have been pressed hot and darkened by stoving; liquorice root, fig, and tonka extract are then applied on top. This trio makes up the traditional topping line long used by Kendal houses. Because the flakes are pressed tightly, rubbing them out gives a thick cut and a slow burn. The taste is built between Virginia's bread-like sweetness and liquorice's bittersweet edge; the tonka extract adds a heavy sweetness to the aroma. It suits a smoker used to Kendal-style topping, or one wanting to get to know this tradition, who is willing to work with a medium-bodied, flaked tobacco.
gawith-hoggarth-co-brown-flake-liquorice.o: Liquorice root and dried fig aromas are accompanied by a sweet, slightly soapy floral note.

carroll-p-j-co-ltd-ye-olde-virginia-hone.z: No reliable source could be found for the pipe tobacco named Ye Olde Virginia Honeydew under the Carroll P. J. & Co. Ltd. brand, so its character, content and production status could not be recorded.

erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-1897.z: 4th Generation 1897 is an aromatic blend within the series Erik Stokkebye dedicated to the birth years of his family's generations. Light golden Virginia leaves are joined by bronze-toned Burley and a pinch of black cavendish; a topping delivering vanilla and sweet honey notes is applied over them. It is presented ribbon cut and, like the rest of the series, produced in Denmark. The blend suits a smoker looking for measured sweetness that doesn't entirely cover the tobacco's own taste. Because the nicotine load stays low, it is well suited to long smokes throughout the day; it can serve as an entry point for someone new to aromatics or seeking a mild Virginia-based mixture.
erik-stokkebye-4th-generation-1897.o: Leaves a scent carrying vanilla and honey sweetness, close to a light bakery aroma.

brebbia-allegro-mixture-no-24.z: An aromatic mixture in Italian pipe manufacturer Brebbia's numbered blend series; no reliable source regarding its content and character could be found.

dunhill-my-mixture-prince-of-wales.z: A record left over from Dunhill's custom blending program, not currently in production; no independent source describing its composition could be found, so a detailed record couldn't be compiled.
dunhill-my-mixture-prince-of-wales.o: No reliable description could be found for the room note.

milan-tobacconists-our-mixture-965.z: Referred to as an English mixture from Milan Tobacconists' "Our" line, in which the shop rebuilds discontinued classics; since it doesn't appear in the maker's current catalogue and no source describing its composition could be found, no further detail can be given.

rain-city-cigar-black-cherry-reserve.z: This is a house blend from Rain City Cigar, open since 1997 in Seattle's Georgetown neighborhood; there is not enough source material describing its composition and character.

gawith-hoggarth-co-curly-cut-deluxe.z: Curly Cut Deluxe is produced by hot-pressing dark and light Virginia leaf, hand-twisting it into thick ropes, and then slicing those ropes into coin shapes. It comes from the same family as Curly Cut; the difference is that a twisting line producing thicker rope is used, giving noticeably larger slices. Since it's factory-sliced, the step of cutting from the rope is eliminated. The blend contains no Perique or other topping; the taste rests entirely on Virginia. On the smoke, a malty sweetness reminiscent of dry hay and bread dough stands out, with a very fine Lakeland trace in the background. Because of the tight structure, the slices need to be rubbed out or packed folded; the burn is slow and cool. An entry suited to smokers seeking pressed Virginia taste in long sessions.
gawith-hoggarth-co-curly-cut-deluxe.o: Leaves a malty bread-dough and dry-hay aroma, with a fine floral trace behind it.

wolfway-1920.z: 1920 is the full aromatic blend from Wolfway Tobacco, based in the Xanthi region of northern Greece. It takes its name from the year Prohibition began in the US; chocolate, vanilla, and whiskey notes are worked over a Virginia and Burley base, with a small amount of Latakia also added. The maker states that it hand-processes its tobaccos and personally oversees fermentation and aging.
wolfway-1920.o: Leaves a scent of cocoa and vanilla sweetness underlaid with a hint of light smoke and whiskey-barrel character.

gawith-hoggarth-co-nessmuk-navy-plugbrow.z: There is not enough independent sourcing available for this product, referred to as a rum-topped brown plug tobacco.

cornell-diehl-trade-winds.z: No listing for Cornell & Diehl's Trade Winds blend could be found in the maker's current catalogue or in major retailer listings; its composition could not be confirmed.

philip-morris-barking-dog.z: This is one of the pipe tobaccos Philip Morris sold in the mid-twentieth century that is no longer produced; no reliable sources describing its content and character could be found.

peretti-london-flake.z: London Flake is a Virginia/perique leaf blend among Peretti's pressed tobaccos. Per the maker's description, orange and lemon Virginias form the sweet side of the blend, while perique adds a spicy, sharp counterpoint to that sweetness. Because it is pressed and sliced, it burns slowly; the slices need to be rubbed out or folded before packing. It follows the typical arc of the Va-Per family: Virginia sugar at the start of the smoke, giving way to plum and pepper notes from the perique as it progresses. It's aimed at smokers who want an unflavored blend and enjoy a fruity-spicy line. Its pressed form makes it well suited to long jar aging.
peretti-london-flake.o: Leaves a lightly peppery trace alongside a scent of dried fruit and baked bread.

wesleys-no-46-full-gold-blend.z: Full Gold is the aromatic Burley-centered member of Wesley's house blends. According to the maker's recipe, Burley is joined by matured Virginia and Oriental leaf; a small amount of Perique is also added to the mixture. Since the Perique ratio is kept low, the spice stays behind the main sweet line, and the blend offers average strength.
wesleys-no-46-full-gold-blend.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly spicy, nutty tobacco scent.

grand-croupier-double-down.z: Double Down is the Grand Croupier series' near-unflavored Virginia-Burley blend. It contains both light and dark Burley leaf together, joined by a wide range of Virginias. Any casing applied to the leaves is very light and doesn't mask the tobacco's own taste. Since the series rests on the idea of combining leftover quality leaf from a producer's various batches, the composition can show small differences from batch to batch. On the smoke, Burley's nutty, earthy dryness bordering on a mustiness leads; the Virginia side adds a measured sweetness to that dryness. Some batches have also reported a Perique-like spice trace. Nicotine is not light, suiting Burley smokers who want heft; the flavor profile, however, is plain and everyday rather than showy.
grand-croupier-double-down.o: A lightly musty earth note mingles with the dry-hay and roasted-hazelnut aroma.

ken-byron-ventures-artifact-blend.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Ken Byron Ventures' Artifact Blend.

peter-heinrichs-no-154.z: Peter Heinrichs No. 154 is a Virginia-Burley blend built by combining leaves cut to different widths. Per the maker's account, one-millimeter, long-fibered Burley and Kentucky are combined with three-millimeter golden Virginia; this cut difference produces an evenly, slowly burning tobacco. Burley and Kentucky give the blend a dry, earthy, smoky body while Virginia serves a balancing function with its sweetness. It is an unflavored structure; nicotine sits above medium while flavor intensity is pronounced. It is a record aimed at smokers seeking slow-burning, unflavored, full-bodied everyday blends.
peter-heinrichs-no-154.o: Leaves a dry nutshell and lightly smoky leaf aroma.

dan-tobacco-bpk-first-experience.z: A limited-distribution Dan Tobacco blend prepared for a pipe club; no adequate source documenting its composition and character was found.

nording-no-1.z: One of the numbered blends tied to the Nording name; no reliable source describing its composition and character could be found.

seattle-pipe-club-hogshead.z: Hogshead is a pure Virginia entry that departs from Seattle Pipe Club's better-known Latakia-forward line. The blend is prepared by heavily pressing orange and red Virginia leaves aged around ten years, then slicing them into a thick plug. No additives are used; the flavor comes entirely from the leaf's own sugar and the maturation that occurs during pressing. The pressed structure concentrates the smoke and brings out a bready, honeyed, faintly sour Virginia character. The plug format asks preparation of the smoker: how the slice is crumbled and aired is decisive for the burn. A blend designed for smokers who want to follow the flue-cured leaf's own taste in its plain form and who make time for a slow smoke.
seattle-pipe-club-hogshead.o: Leaves a scent of dry straw, honey, and baked bread crust.

dunhill-gold-label.z: A discontinued mixture referred to under the Dunhill name, for which no verifiable source on its composition could be found.

4noggins-jesses-own.z: Jesse's Own is a mild English blend built by adding a portion of Maryland leaf on top of sweet Virginias. Per the manufacturer's recipe, a small amount of Oriental leaf is added for a soft, tangy flavor, followed by light touches of Cyprus Latakia and Perique. No additives are reported. Because the Latakia ratio is kept low, the smoke stays in the background without covering the Virginia sweetness; Perique adds a spicy twist. Nicotine is mild and flavor mild-to-moderate. With this structure, the blend offers a middle path smokable all day by both fans of unflavored Virginias and smokers not yet accustomed to heavy English blends.
4noggins-jesses-own.o: Leaves a sweetish, grassy aroma with a thin trace of smoke.

hu-tobacco-aus-dem-krater-nr-4.z: Aus dem Krater Nr. 4 is a flake obtained by rolling and pressing various Virginia leaves of US and African origin and then cutting them. A measured flavoring in caramel, ginger, and vanilla notes has been applied to the leaf. Representing the aromatic wing of the series, this blend counts as medium strength, and since the flavoring level is kept light, the Virginia leaf's own sweetness doesn't stay in the background. It's aimed at those avoiding heavy aromatics and looking for a lightly flavored flake.
hu-tobacco-aus-dem-krater-nr-4.o: Leaves an aroma where ginger's spicy edge accompanies caramel and vanilla sweetness.

clan-shaw-moonshine.z: No reliable sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Clan Shaw blend Moonshine.

whitehall-products-inc-greenbrier-smokin.z: Greenbrier Smoking Mixture is a menthol American blend bearing the name of Whitehall Products Inc., based in Helmetta, New Jersey. The company was one of the tobacco firms under Culbro Corp. alongside Bloch Bros. Tobacco Co. and Helme Products; the blend has long been out of production and today mostly turns up in old tin collections. The composition combines predominantly Burley, mild Virginia, Carolina bright leaf, and Turkish tobacco, topped with natural imported menthol. The cut is a ready-rubbed type, made up of a mix of reddish-brown, tan, dark brown, and black leaves. The tin note gives a sweet, resinous impression reminiscent of spearmint gum. The burn pace is below medium, and it may need several relights. Menthol provides measured coolness that stays in the background throughout; nicotine is mild to medium. This is a record of interest to smokers seeking menthol tobacco or studying period American blends.
whitehall-products-inc-greenbrier-smokin.o: Leaves a cool, sharply herbal scent reminiscent of spearmint gum.

hu-tobacco-edward-g.z: No sufficient independent source verifying the content and character of Edward G., one of the small-batch blends prepared by the German maker HU Tobacco, could be found.

a-c-petersen-caledonian-melange-no-421-s.z: Caledonian Melange No.421 Superior Mixture is one of A & C Petersen's mellow, sweet blends representing the Danish style. Records indicate it's prepared by resting four separate base blends — Virginia, Cavendish, fire-cured leaf, and Oriental — separately before combining them by hand. In appearance, thickly cut red Virginia ribbons dominate, with brown tones and a small amount of black Cavendish among them. Strength is low, taste is medium; the fire-cured leaf adds a smoky depth, and the Oriental a lightly tangy-spicy edge. It's for smokers who want a smoky undertone without going into heavy English blends, who like mellow Danish-style mixtures. The brand is discontinued today.
a-c-petersen-caledonian-melange-no-421-s.o: A faintly smoky undertone mixes with a sweetish dry-hay room note.

gladora-tobacco-latakia-40-broken-flake.z: Pesse Canoe Latakia Flake 40 is Gladora's unflavored flake with the Latakia ratio raised to forty percent. All the blend's components are grown in Turkey; the brand's Latakia is also cured entirely in Turkey rather than sourced from Cyprus or historic Syrian production, making it a rare production method today. Its smoke-forward structure stands out: alongside smoke and wood tones, a plum-like dark-fruit sweetness from the Latakia is added, with the Turkish Virginia adding a measured sugar and tartness to that base. Nicotine and flavor intensity run moderate to high; suited to those accustomed to Latakia-heavy English and Balkan mixtures who want an evening smoke.
gladora-tobacco-latakia-40-broken-flake.o: Leaves a heavy wood-smoke and incense aroma with dried plum behind it.

leonard-dingler-ltd-nineteen-ofour-1904-.z: Nineteen O'Four is a pipe tobacco line from South Africa's long-established tobacco manufacturer Leonard Dingler, its name taken from the year 1904. The company dates to the early twentieth century, remained a family business for a long time, and later passed to Swedish Match. The series' base rests on Burley and Kentucky leaf; this structure gives the smoke a nutty, bready and earthy body. The product is sold in 50-gram folding pouches and is largely aimed at the South African market. Nineteen O'Four (1904) Vanilla Blend is recorded as the line's arm distinguished by its vanilla flavoring. The casing is applied at a level that doesn't mask the Burley base; the smoke stays cool and body stays at medium. Of interest to those seeking an aromatic profile but avoiding syrupy weight, and to those curious about counter tobaccos specific to the South African market. Hard to find outside the country.
leonard-dingler-ltd-nineteen-ofour-1904-.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough room note.

petersen-sorensen-blue-sapphire.z: This is one of the blends released under the Petersen & Sorensen name; no sufficient first-hand sources documenting its content and character could be found.
petersen-sorensen-blue-sapphire.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

olaf-poulsson-flake-cut.z: A blend tied to Dan Tobacco's Olaf Poulsson line; no separate record under this name in current product listings, and no reliable source describing its composition, could be found.

mac-baren-gold-of-denmark.z: Not enough first-hand sources could be found to confirm the contents and character of the Mac Baren-branded Gold of Denmark blend.
mac-baren-gold-of-denmark.o: The room note description for this record could not be confirmed.

h-simmons-down-the-road-mixture.z: One of the mixtures from H. Simmons, a tobacconist operating in London's Burlington Arcade that was acquired by Dunhill in the late 1980s; there is not enough independent sourcing describing the blend's composition and character.

samuel-gawith-100-unsweetened-black-cave.z: A single-leaf product Samuel Gawith, which has produced in Kendal since 1792, offers in bulk, consisting, as its name states, of unsweetened black cavendish. No detailed independent source on the blend itself could be found, so no definite information on its character is given.

newminster-no-52-ultimate-english.z: One of the Latakia-containing English mixtures in the Newminster line; sufficient independent sources detailing its composition could not be found.

hermes-11.z: Hermes /11 is a pipe tobacco classified as English style; no reliable source about the brand, maker, and the blend's composition could be found.

rattray-winter-edition-2020.z: Winter Edition 2020 is an edition of Rattray's winter series pulled toward the darker side. Its body is built from ebony-colored black Cavendish, broken dark Virginia, and nutty Burley; the high proportion of dark leaf gives the blend a fuller body. On the flavor side, gingerbread and plum notes are pronounced, with vanilla staying in the background throughout the smoke. Nicotine sits in the medium range. It suits smokers looking for a spicy, fruity, comparatively full-bodied winter aromatic; being a limited annual edition, it is not in current production.
rattray-winter-edition-2020.o: Vanilla accompanies the gingerbread and cooked-plum aroma.

per-g-jensen-burley.z: Per G. Jensen Burley is the burley-based member of the Blender's Collection series bearing the blender's name. Per the series' shared principle, no top-note flavoring is applied and casing is kept to a minimum, letting the leaf's own taste come forward. Burley forms the blend's body, with a small share of Virginia added alongside it to provide balance and a touch of sweetness, and the tobacco is presented as a ready-rubbed cut. On the smoke, burley's characteristic dry, nutty-shell, bread-and-cocoa-adjacent earthiness stands out; sweetness is low and dryness high. It suits those looking for a slow-burning tobacco whose temperature is easy to manage, as well as blenders who want to add burley body to their own mixture.
per-g-jensen-burley.o: Leaves a scent of dry hazelnut, bread crust, and light earth.

watch-city-cigar-elf-dandruff.z: Elf Dandruff is a limited house blend Watch City Cigar prepared for its 2021 holiday season. According to the shop's description, it's an American mixture notable for flavoring reminiscent of the English Kendal tradition's essences, taking its name from a holiday-themed joke by blender Ernie Q. As it falls in the flavored product class, it is not sold within Massachusetts.
watch-city-cigar-elf-dandruff.o: The sweet, sharp, spicy scent of Kendal-style essences lingers in the room for a long time.

barclay-rex-maravilla.z: Maravilla is one of Barclay Rex's shop blends in the aromatic class. It carries the weight of long-cut red Virginia, with toasted Cavendish and a small amount of Burley added. Red Virginia gives the blend a natural sweetness, while the Cavendish mellows and deepens that sweetness. It offers a slow-burning, light-bodied smoke with low flavor intensity, without carrying the sugar load of heavy aromatics. It suits smokers looking for an everyday blend that stays comfortable in hand for long periods without weighing on the tongue. It's one of the examples of Barclay Rex's tradition of blending in-house and selling in bulk.
barclay-rex-maravilla.o: Leaves a sweetish, bready room note from the toasted Cavendish.

leonard-dingler-ltd-nineteen-ofour-whisk.z: Nineteen O'Four is a pipe tobacco line from South Africa's long-established tobacco manufacturer Leonard Dingler, its name taken from the year 1904. The company dates to the early twentieth century, remained a family business for a long time, and later passed to Swedish Match. The series' base rests on Burley and Kentucky leaf; this structure gives the smoke a nutty, bready and earthy body. The product is sold in 50-gram folding pouches and is largely aimed at the South African market. Nineteen O'Four Whisky is recorded as the line's arm distinguished by its whisky flavoring. The casing is applied at a level that doesn't mask the Burley base; the smoke stays cool and body stays at medium. Of interest to those seeking an aromatic profile but avoiding syrupy weight, and to those curious about counter tobaccos specific to the South African market. Hard to find outside the country.
leonard-dingler-ltd-nineteen-ofour-whisk.o: Leaves a woody, lightly sweet room note reminiscent of spirit rested in an oak cask.

karl-erik-private-blend-no-18.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Karl Erik's Private Blend No.18.

bjarne-viking-william-the-conqueror.z: William The Conqueror is the Latakia-forward English mixture in the Viking line named after Danish pipe maker Bjarne Nielsen. Tangy, spicy Oriental leaves, moderately sweet Virginias, and a high proportion of Cyprus Latakia come together. Latakia stands out in the blend both in taste and smoke; Virginia leaves a light sweetness in the background, while the Oriental leaf carries a dry spice line. It contains no added flavoring. Nicotine stays medium, and thanks to its Latakia intensity it suits long, unhurried smokes. It's aimed at smokers looking for classic Latakia-dominant English mixtures.
bjarne-viking-william-the-conqueror.o: Leaves a heavy room note of soot, tar, and dried leaf.

comoys-of-london-scottish-mixture.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Comoy's of London blend Scottish Mixture.

r-r-tobacco-indonesian-blend.z: R&R is one of the few pipe tobacco blenders in Indonesia, and Indonesian Blend is cited as an unflavored blend built from leaf grown on local fields such as Java, Sumatra, and Borneo; there is not enough source material giving details of its content.
r-r-tobacco-indonesian-blend.o: No information describing the room note could be found in available records.

cornell-diehl-burley-light.z: One of Cornell & Diehl's older burley-based blends; it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog, and not enough sourcing could be found to describe its character.

ken-byron-ventures-pork-chops-apple-sauc.z: Part of Ken Byron Ventures' Virginia-Perique line's 2019 batch; records indicate it's prepared by pressing matured Virginia leaf into a cylinder and fermenting it, with a light fruit casing applied on top. No detailed independent source could be found about the batch.

seattle-pipe-club-harbor-lights.z: Harbor Lights, signed by Seattle Pipe Club, is left as an undetailed record since no independent source sufficient to fill in its profile could be found.

e-a-carey-dark-flake-no-7.z: Not enough sourcing exists to describe the composition and character of this dark flake tobacco, listed in the E. A. Carey catalog.
e-a-carey-dark-flake-no-7.o: Could not be described due to insufficient records.

mcclelland-syrian-full-balkan.z: Syrian Full Balkan is from McClelland's line using Syrian Latakia. Per the maker's description, the blend's character is built by Syrian Latakia, known for its distinctive, non-harsh aroma; it's joined by Oriental tobaccos and Virginia leaf. It's noted to give a drier, more incense-like, less tarry smokiness than Cyprian Latakia. The smoke is cool and flowing, with medium body. Though Latakia dominates, it doesn't overpower the blend; the Orientals' spicy notes and Virginia's sweetness can be read in the background. Suited to smokers wanting to get to know the Balkan style through Syrian Latakia. The blend was withdrawn from the market when Syrian Latakia supply was cut off and the brand closed in 2018.
mcclelland-syrian-full-balkan.o: Leaves an aroma of incense and cedar wood, with a faintly spiced trace behind it.

watch-city-cigar-americano.z: This is described as one of Watch City Cigar's American-type house blends; since no detailed record exists in the maker's current catalog, its composition could not be confirmed.
watch-city-cigar-americano.o: Could not be determined from the records.

faders-chesapeake.z: Not enough independent sourcing documenting the composition and character of Chesapeake, one of the house blends of the Baltimore-based Fader's tobacconist, could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-rc-272.z: RC-272 is a blend in Sutliff's bulk line sitting between an aromatic and an English mixture. Its base contains burley, Virginia, hot-air-cured leaf, Smyrna (İzmir) Oriental, and Latakia; this English-style skeleton is completed with a triple casing of vanilla, rum, and cinnamon. The smoky, spicy background of the Latakia and Oriental forms an unusual layer together with the sweet topping. It is aimed at smokers curious about the "English aromatic" style who are tired of one-dimensional sweet blends.
sutliff-tobacco-company-rc-272.o: A fine smoky scent seeps through the cinnamon and rum sweetness.

watch-city-cigar-masala.z: This is a house blend from Watch City Cigar described as Virginia-based, for which no sufficient source could be found.
watch-city-cigar-masala.o: Records note it leaves a spicy, sweetish scent.

lane-limited-black-knight.z: Lane Limited's record called Black Knight is referred to as an English-type, Latakia-containing mixture; since no independent source could confirm its composition and the product has long been off the market, the record is left incomplete.

mclintock-marillen-mixture.z: McLintock Marillen Mixture is an aromatic mixed cut taking its name from the German word "Marille," meaning apricot. The blend's leaf composition has not been published; the brand's general construction rests on Virginia, burley, and black cavendish. It is out of production.
mclintock-marillen-mixture.o: Leaves a fruity, sweet aroma in the direction of apricot.

dunhill-a-20000-toasted-cavendish.z: A-20000 Toasted Cavendish is among Dunhill's numbered blends sold in bulk. It's built from Virginia, burley and Maryland leaves ranging from black to brown to golden; toasted golden cavendish is the component giving the blend its name. Per records, no pronounced artificial flavoring is added to the tobacco; the sweetness mostly comes from the cavendish process. Its nicotine load is very light and its flavor intensity is also low; it therefore carries an undemanding character suited to smoking one after another through the day. It suits those who don't like the heavily sauced wing of aromatics but still want a sweet, soft smoke. Since pipe tobacco production under the Dunhill name has ended, the blend is not currently found on the market under its own name.
dunhill-a-20000-toasted-cavendish.o: Leaves a lightly toasted, sweetish, dry tobacco scent.

sutliff-tobacco-company-danish-cavendish.z: R18 Danish Cavendish is part of Sutliff's bulk aromatic line. Burley and unsauced black cavendish are added to red and light Virginia leaves; a cocoa-and-marshmallow-heavy sauce is applied on top. The ribbon cut is easy to pack and burns evenly. Flavor is soft and sweet, and nicotine stays low. Suited to those seeking a Danish-style sweet cavendish character in an all-day aromatic.
sutliff-tobacco-company-danish-cavendish.o: Leaves a sweet scent reminiscent of cocoa and confectionery.

smittys-cigar-and-tobacco-505.z: A numbered house blend, classified as English style, sold by a tobacconist under its own name; no source describing its composition could be found.
smittys-cigar-and-tobacco-505.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

solani-656-aged-burley-flake.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Solani blend 656: Aged Burley Flake could not be found.

redbreast-redbreast-flake.z: Redbreast Flake was a long-cut pressed Virginia-Burley flake once carried in the portfolio of the Liverpool house Ogden's. It belongs to the family of lightly scented pressed tobaccos within the English tradition; compared to the more familiar example of that school, St. Bruno, the casing stays further in the background and the leaf taste comes forward. The Virginia component supplies sweetness and sharpness, while Burley provides body and a cool burn; Burley also serves as the base to which the flavoring adheres. Listed in Ogden's early-twentieth-century catalogue alongside names like St. Bruno, Walnut Flake, and St. Julian, the blend reportedly went out of production long ago, with the recipe passing to Imperial Tobacco. Today it can only be found through old tins or English tobacconists selling it in bulk. It appeals to smokers looking for a classic English pressed-tobacco tradition, a middle ground sweeter than a straight Virginia but not fully aromatic.
redbreast-redbreast-flake.o: Leaves a dry hay and tobacco aroma accompanied by a lightly soapy floral casing.

mr-bs-rise-and-shine.z: Rise and Shine is a light Oriental-Virginia blend in Brigham's Mr. B's line, designed for the first bowls of the day. Select Oriental leaves stand out in the composition; balanced with bright and red Virginias, this gives a smoke that is light but not empty. Due to Canada's bilingual labeling rules, the tin also carries the French name "Aube." Nicotine is low, and the flavor profile is dry and spicy; Virginia's sweetness softens the base. Since it isn't Latakia-heavy, it doesn't weigh down the palate and can be smoked throughout the day. A recipe geared toward smokers looking for a light Oriental profile for morning pipes. It was distributed in fifty-gram tins and pouches.
mr-bs-rise-and-shine.o: Leaves a dry-bread and incense-like spice aroma.

blatter-blatter-plaisir-oriental-orienta.z: A Blatter & Blatter house blend whose name points to Oriental leaf; no reliable source documenting its composition could be found.

samuel-gawith-st-james-flake-burnt-ends.z: Burnt Ends is a product resulting from collecting the leftover edge pieces from Samuel Gawith's St. James Flake production. It carries the main blend's leaf structure: bright virginias are combined with perique from Louisiana's St. James region, a bit of sugar is added to the mixture, and it is pressed and sliced. Since the edge portions of the pressed block don't yield neat slices, they are collected separately; so the product consists of irregular, partly rubbed pieces rather than a regular flake. The flavor profile sits on the same ground as St. James Flake: virginia's hay and bready sweetness is topped by perique's peppery, lightly plummy spice. Because the edge pieces come from the block's outer surface, color and moisture distribution are more variable. Suited to smokers seeking ease of packing without giving up virginia-perique character.
samuel-gawith-st-james-flake-burnt-ends.o: Leaves a scent of dry hay, stale bread, and light black pepper.

mac-baren-hh-rustica.z: HH Rustica is a hot-pressed flake that puts Nicotiana rustica — a historic tobacco variety native to the Americas — at the center of the blend. Alongside the rustica leaf are naturally sweet dark Virginias and cool-burning burley, both Nicotiana tabacum varieties. In line with the HH series' method, it is heat-pressed and thinly sliced; casing is minimized and there's no top flavor. The nicotine content of rustica leaf is markedly above that of usual pipe tobaccos; the manufacturer describes this product as the strongest in its catalog. Even so, the flavor isn't just about strength: over an earthy, woody base there is a spicy, peppery sharpness with nutty, lightly molasses-like burley tones behind it, finishing with a tangy grapefruit impression. Being tightly pressed, it can be hard to light; filling it well-rubbed and aired eases the burn. A product designed for pipe smokers accustomed to high nicotine.
mac-baren-hh-rustica.o: Leaves a sharp, dry note reminiscent of burnt wood, walnut shell and black pepper.

milan-tobacconists-irresistible-chocolat.z: Irresistible Chocolate is referred to as Milan Tobacconists' chocolate-cased, dark-colored ribbon-cut aromatic house blend; no verifiable source about its leaf composition could be found.

cornell-diehl-walter-franklin.z: A blend, no longer in Cornell & Diehl's current catalogue, recorded as Burley-heavy; no independent source confirming its composition and character was found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-dorset-blend-520.z: Sufficient sources to confirm the composition and character of Dorset Blend #520, referred to as one of Sutliff's English types, could not be found.

pipesandcigars-com-candy-corn.z: No independent source material could be found sufficient to fill out a specification for the pipesandcigars.com blend called Candy Corn.

garfinkels-old-scottish-cut-cake-6.z: No reliable source documenting the composition and character of Garfinkel's Old Scottish Cut Cake #6 pipe tobacco could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-opulence-31.z: Opulence is an aromatic listed under the code SPS-31 in Sutliff's SPS (Sutliff Private Stock) bulk series. Its base contains flavored blackened leaf along with lemon-yellow Virginia; a casing carrying creamy vanilla-malt notes with a light rum note in the background is applied over it. The cut is ribbon. The blend suits smokers looking for a sweet, dessert-like aftertaste and enjoying a low-nicotine aromatic. Sutliff is an American maker founded in 1849; production was run for many years in Richmond, Virginia, and the brand later passed to Mac Baren before coming under the Scandinavian Tobacco Group.
sutliff-tobacco-company-opulence-31.o: A scent of vanilla malt and light rum sugar spreads through the room.

ken-byron-ventures-901q.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Ken Byron Ventures' 901Q blend.

vauen-no-08-sparkling-blend.z: No. 08 Sparkling Blend is the current name for the aromatic blend Vauen previously sold as Strawberry & Champagne. Brown, golden and reddish Virginia leaves are used in varying cut widths; toasted black Cavendish supports a cool burn, and a pinch of Burley rounds out the structure. On the flavor side, ripe strawberry sweetness is built alongside the lively, lightly acidic edge of sparkling wine. Nicotine is low and the taste is fruity and sweet. Suited to smokers interested in fruity aromatics who don't mind a pronounced room note.
vauen-no-08-sparkling-blend.o: Leaves the tangy-sweet aroma of ripe strawberry and sparkling wine.

e-a-carey-wild-cherry.z: As the name suggests, this is a cherry-flavored E. A. Carey blend; it does not appear on the maker's current list, and not enough sourcing exists to describe its composition.

century-black-cordial.z: Black Cordial is one of the Century line's pre-rubbed aromatics. Per the seller's description, four separate classes of fire-cured black leaf are used together, sweet virginia leaf is added, and the blend is flavored with a top aroma reminiscent of fruit liqueur. The cut is ready to load directly and needs no further rubbing. The dark, faintly smoky base from the fire-cured black leaves combines with virginia's sugary sweetness; the top flavoring is described as applied at an intensity that does not fully mask the tobacco's own taste. It is not heavy in nicotine and burns cool. Suitable for smokers who love sweet aromatics but still want to taste the leaf itself.
century-black-cordial.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of sweet fruit syrup and a light liqueur.

hilands-cigars-dutch-honey.z: Dutch Honey is one of the house blends prepared at its own facility by Hiland's Cigars, which has operated in Arizona since 1963. Honey flavoring is applied to a mix of Burley and Virginia leaves; Burley provides body and a nutty base taste, while Virginia's natural sugar accompanies the honey. The flavoring is kept measured enough not to mask the leaf's own taste, resulting in a medium-level aromatic profile. It's a structure suited to those not looking for a heavy-nicotine aromatic that can be smoked all day, and to those wanting to move from aromatic toward natural tobacco taste. It's recorded as having been one of the components of the same maker's now-discontinued Mixture D blend.
hilands-cigars-dutch-honey.o: Leaves an aroma of warmed sugar and dry hay carrying honey sweetness.

mcclelland-virginia-no-24-matured-virgin.z: Virginia No. 24 is part of McClelland's Matured Virginias series, a flake blend of matured Virginias topped with Drama-district Oriental leaf. It's unflavored — the sweetness comes from the leaf itself. The small flakes deliver their fullest flavor when packed by air-fluffing rather than rubbing out, though this packing method can make burn control tricky for less experienced smokers. Smoked at a slow pace, a pure, sweet Virginia character comes through clearly. Nicotine is moderate and doesn't build toward the bottom of the bowl. Suited to smokers who want an unadulterated Virginia taste and are comfortable with flake tobaccos. McClelland closed in early 2018, so the blend is no longer produced.
mcclelland-virginia-no-24-matured-virgin.o: Leaves a tangy-sweet, mature tobacco aroma.

american-spirit-black-perique.z: American Spirit is the brand of the Santa Fe Natural Tobacco Company known for its claim of unadditized tobacco; the black-pack Perique version is prepared, in keeping with the "unadditized leaf" concept built around the brand name, without any sweetener or humectant. American Burley leaf forms the blend's backbone; Perique, fermented in its own juice in oak barrels in Louisiana's St. James region, is added over it. Perique is obtained by fermenting a red-Burley-derived leaf under pressure, giving the blend a sharp spice that ranges between plum, fig, and pepper. In character it offers a full, dry smoke; the absence of sweetening leaves a pronounced earthy and nutty taste on the tongue, while the Perique adds tangy fruit touches in between. Nicotine load is above medium, so it isn't suited to smoking on an empty stomach or quickly. It can serve as an entry point for smokers looking for unadditized Burley taste and wanting to get to know Perique's spice; for someone coming from flavored blends, the absence of sweetness requires a noticeable adjustment.
american-spirit-black-perique.o: Leaves a dark-plum room note carrying an earthy, faintly vinegary tang.

cornell-diehl-u-s-s-mason.z: U.S.S. Mason is a ribbon-cut blend adding a small amount of Latakia and Perique to a Virginia-and-Burley body, topped with a light brandy touch. Cornell & Diehl prepared this mixture in memory of the crew of the U.S.S. Mason, the first ship in the American navy during World War II crewed entirely by Black sailors. Keeping the Latakia proportion low sets the blend apart from heavy English mixtures; Perique adds a spicy sharpness, Burley a dry, nutty base. The brandy casing is kept to a level that doesn't overshadow the tobacco. While staying light on nicotine, it offers a layered flavor structure, suiting those looking for a measured Latakia blend they can smoke all day.
cornell-diehl-u-s-s-mason.o: Leaves a scent where a subtle brandy sweetness sits over light wood smoke.

the-seasons-spring.z: No reliable source could be found on the Spring blend from The Seasons series.

j-f-germain-son-balkan-sobranie.z: Balkan Sobranie Original Smoking Mixture traces its origin to the 1920s, to the Sobranie house founded in London by the Redstone family in 1879. In its classic form, the blend was made up of Syrian Latakia, Oriental leaf known as Yenidje, and Virginia, and it disappeared when Gallaher withdrew its products from the US market in 1998. The recipe was later taken up by J. F. Germain & Son on the island of Jersey, and production has continued at that factory since. Its current form is a fine ribbon cut; the weight is carried by Latakia, accompanied by Oriental, Virginia, and Cavendish leaves. The flavor is earthy, smoky, and spicy, with a subtle sweetness from the Virginia rounding out the Latakia. It's aimed at smokers who want to experience the unflavored, heavily Latakia-forward Balkan style and who aren't put off by a strong room note; it's also one of the key blends in pipe tobacco history.
j-f-germain-son-balkan-sobranie.o: A heavy smoke reminiscent of a campfire, along with cedar and spice, fills the room.

mcclelland-blending-latakia.z: Blending Latakia is a single-component product McClelland sold in bulk for those building their own blends; it isn't a finished blend but a building block. It consists of ribbon-cut Cyprian Latakia, and records indicate Smyrna leaf was used as the base leaf. Smoked on its own, its taste and aroma lean heavily toward soot; since Latakia is processed by smoking, it carries a woody, tarry, dry character, while staying low on nicotine. It's a component that those building their own blends add in measured proportions to a Virginia or Oriental base. Withdrawn from the market when McClelland closed.
mcclelland-blending-latakia.o: Leaves an intense wood-soot and campfire aroma that lingers in the room for a long time.

nice-ash-cigars-tremendous-chocolate-tru.z: An aromatic record among Nice Ash Cigars' house blends, flavored with chocolate truffle; not enough source material describing its composition could be found.
nice-ash-cigars-tremendous-chocolate-tru.o: No description could be found in the records.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-route-22.z: Route 22 was prepared for the opening of Boswell's second shop in Alexandria, Pennsylvania, and takes its name from the highway where that shop is located. It is built mainly on toasted cavendish; burley's nutty base is joined by buttery-caramel and vanilla notes over this core. Nicotine load is measured, flavor body medium. The flavor casing is perceptible but not dominant, making it suitable for smokers seeking an aromatic that does not entirely cover the tobacco taste. The manufacturer positions the blend as one that can be smoked all day.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-route-22.o: Leaves a buttery caramel and vanilla aroma.

robert-mcconnell-pure-caribe.z: Pure Caribe is a single-component, ribbon-cut product made entirely of Caribbean-origin cigar leaf. It belongs to Robert McConnell's line of pure components meant for blending; like Pure Virginia, Pure Perique, and Pure Latakia, it is designed either to reinforce existing blends or for home blenders building their own mixtures. No flavoring is applied, letting the leaf's own taste come through. Smoked on its own, it is reported to give a mild cigar taste, a subtle sweetness, and tones reminiscent of baker's chocolate. It suits smokers experimenting with blending who want to add body and earthy depth to their mix using cigar leaf.
robert-mcconnell-pure-caribe.o: Leaves the earthy, faintly cocoa-like aroma of cigar leaf.

niall-of-nine-marleys-deep-reserve.z: Marley's Deep Reserve is the blend Niall of Nine released as its 2024 New Year edition, taking its name from Marley in Dickens's A Christmas Carol. Records indicate 2016-dated burley and cavendish leaves are combined with 2018 latakia, topped with a light maraschino cherry, cocoa, and vanilla dressing. The result is a hybrid character sitting between an aromatic and a latakia mixture: beneath the baked sweetness and cherry note run burley's nutty body and latakia's smoky line. Since the topping is kept light, it doesn't carry the syrupy weight of aromatic tobaccos. It's a record for smokers wanting to try a sweet top note alongside smoky tobacco, seeking a medium-strength winter blend. It was produced in limited numbers in vacuum-sealed jars.
niall-of-nine-marleys-deep-reserve.o: A thin trace of wood smoke is sensed beneath the sweetness of cocoa and cherry liqueur.

rattray-exotic-orange-a-k-a-exotic-passi.z: Exotic Orange, also known in some markets as Exotic Passion, is an aromatic blend with a citrus-forward flavoring applied over a Virginia and black Cavendish base. The tin note distinguishes honey, maple syrup, sweet orange, and orange blossom; the casing structure resembles the same maker's brandy blend. It burns slow, cool, and clean; the flavor line stays consistent, in a creamy texture, throughout the smoke. Being light in nicotine, it suits long sessions. It is a fitting choice for smokers looking for pronounced fruity-honeyed aromatics.
rattray-exotic-orange-a-k-a-exotic-passi.o: Leaves a honeyed orange and orange-blossom aroma.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-no-5-english-sty.z: No manufacturer or retailer record could be found giving the contents of this English-style blend in Kohlhase & Kopp's numbered series.

tom-eltang-mixture.z: No sufficient independent source documenting the composition and character of the Tom Eltang blend called Mixture has been found.

park-lane-tobacconist-park-lane-no-5.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Park-Lane No. 5, one of the counter blends from Park-Lane Tobacconist in Clifton Park, New York, could be found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-birds-eye.z: Dark Bird's Eye is produced by rolling and slicing whole fire-cured Virginia leaf together with finely cut Kentucky leaf. Since whole leaf is used instead of strands, the midrib section stands out in cross-section; this ring-like pattern in the slices gives the blend its "bird's eye" name. The leaves are lightly sauced before curing and pressing, then heated and rested for about two weeks before slicing. A sweet, fruity side leads in the first half of the smoke; as it progresses, the smoky, earthy, salty body of the Kentucky and fire-cured leaf takes over. Nicotine is high. The slices are packed after being rubbed out and aired, and stay cool when smoked slowly. An entry for experienced smokers accustomed to dark, strong, lightly flavored English tobaccos.
gawith-hoggarth-co-dark-birds-eye.o: Leaves a smoky, earthy aroma with a fruity sweetness sensed behind it.

ken-byron-ventures-carry-on.z: One of Ken Byron Ventures' small-batch releases; since the maker's page no longer carries a profile, no verifiable information on its contents and character could be found.

ken-byron-ventures-plague-bringer-2019.z: A blend Ken Byron Ventures released as part of its small-batch production; no independent and verifiable source could be found about it.

mac-baren-black-ambrosia.z: Black Ambrosia is a wide-cut Mac Baren aromatic where cavendish forms the weight, with a small amount of Virginia added. Its moisture level is right and it can usually be packed without airing. The casing runs toward various fruit extracts and citrus; the casing level is kept lower than the rest of the series' aromatics, which lets the tobacco taste be followed to some degree. Nicotine is light and flavor sits a little above light. Suited to those seeking a low-casing aromatic to smoke all day; blending it with an unflavored Virginia is recorded to increase its body.
mac-baren-black-ambrosia.o: Leaves a sweet room note toward dark fruit and citrus peel.

sutliff-tobacco-company-lord-nelson-528.z: Coded 528, Sutliff's Lord Nelson is a ribbon-cut mixture built from latakia, lemon-yellow Virginia, oriental, and burley leaf, taking its name from the English naval commander Horatio Nelson. The inclusion of burley moves the blend out of the classic English mold toward the fuller-bodied style known as American-English. The balance struck between smoky latakia and Virginia's sweetness delivers a cool burn over a nutty burley base. Suited to smokers seeking a medium-strength, unflavored evening blend and who enjoy full-bodied English mixtures.
sutliff-tobacco-company-lord-nelson-528.o: Leaves a scent of woody smoke and toasted nuts.

douwe-egberts-egberts-44.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Egberts 44, a pipe tobacco from Douwe Egberts.
douwe-egberts-egberts-44.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

john-middleton-inc-regimental-mixture.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Middleton, Inc's Regimental Mixture pipe tobacco.

cornell-diehl-carolina-red-flake-2024.z: Carolina Red Flake is an unflavored Virginia blend Cornell & Diehl releases in limited quantity each year as part of its Small Batch series; the 2024 edition is a member of that yearly cycle. According to available records, the blend is presented as flake, obtained by pressing and slicing ripe red Virginia leaves, and offered in two-ounce tins. No flavoring is added; the sweetness comes from the leaf's own sugar and the ripening that occurs during pressing. The flavor profile runs along a bready, dark-fruit Virginia character, sitting at medium nicotine. Being a flake, it needs to be rubbed out or folded before packing, marking it as a blend aimed more at the experienced Virginia smoker than the beginner. Being limited production, it was only on the market the year it was released, later becoming a record kept in aged stashes.
cornell-diehl-carolina-red-flake-2024.o: Leaves a bready sweetness together with an aroma of dried fruit and hay.

nice-ash-cigars-burley-delight.z: One of Nice Ash Cigars' burley-forward house blends; not enough source material describing its proportions and flavoring could be found.
nice-ash-cigars-burley-delight.o: No description could be found in the records.

tabacos-catarinenses-ltda-havana-horse-b.z: Havana Horse Black is the dark-looking member of the Havana line produced by Tabacos Catarinenses in the Brazilian state of Santa Catarina. According to the maker's description, it is prepared from selected Virginia and Burley leaves processed with aromatic casing; the Virginia side carries the sweetness while the Burley side carries the body and burn balance. The leaf is ribbon cut and sold in 45-gram packs. Nicotine is moderate and the smoke's fullness is medium, positioning it as an everyday blend that can be smoked throughout the day. It suits smokers curious about one of the accessible aromatics on the Brazilian market, looking for a soft, sweet smoke rather than heavy Latakia or intense English blends.
tabacos-catarinenses-ltda-havana-horse-b.o: Leaves a sweetish, lightly caramel-like tobacco scent.

peretti-150th-anniversary-blend.z: A blend said to be issued to mark the 150th anniversary of L.J. Peretti Company of Boston; it has no counterpart in the maker's current tobacco listing, so there is no verified information about its composition and character.

intertabak-virginia-po-34.z: No verifiable source could be found for this Virginia registered under the INTERTABAK name.

uhles-blend-00.z: Blend 00 is a single-component tobacco prepared at the counter of Uhle Tobacco Company, operating in Milwaukee since the 1940s. It contains only pure ribbon-cut Burley leaf, with no flavoring added. This single-leaf setup reduces the taste to Burley's own dry, nutty character; it carries no sweetness and nicotine sits in the medium range. The maker presents this tobacco both for straight smoking and as a base leaf for home blenders. A useful record for those wanting to get to know unflavored Burley character or add body to their own blend.
uhles-blend-00.o: Leaves a plain tobacco aroma reminiscent of dry nuts and toasted bread crust.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-balkan.z: Because the maker's own page for Wilke Pipe Tobacco's blend called Balkan was not accessible during this research, verifiable composition information could not be compiled.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-balkan.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

uptowns-smoke-shop-blue-ridge.z: A house blend from Nashville's Uptown's Smoke Shop noted as plain Virginia; since the shop has closed, the blend is also off the market and no source describing its composition has been found.

holger-danske-premium-blend-and-flake-el.z: This is a blend called Elegant in Holger Danske's Premium Blend and Flake line; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found.
holger-danske-premium-blend-and-flake-el.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-beeker-street.z: No verifiable composition and character information could be compiled for Wilke Pipe Tobacco's aromatic blend Beeker Street.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-beeker-street.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.
