peretti-bostons-best-cavendish.z: This is a shop blend L.J. Peretti lists in its Cavendish group and continues to produce in three package sizes; the flavoring used and the taste profile have not been published.

john-patton-spyglass.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of John Patton's Spyglass blend.

ken-byron-ventures-mozgus.z: Mozgus is a blend Ken Byron Ventures releases in small batches; without access to the maker's own description or two independent sources, its contents and character details aren't specified here.

hu-tobacco-white-horses.z: White Horses is a medium-strength blend in HU Tobacco's Original Warehouse Blend line. Its weight lies in various sweet Virginia leaves; Kentucky, some Havana leaf, and Perique are added to these. Kentucky gives the blend spice and bite, keeping the Virginia sweetness from becoming one-dimensional; Perique leaves a dark, fruity depth. It's aimed at smokers looking for an unflavored leaf taste, wanting the Virginia a bit fuller and spicier.
hu-tobacco-white-horses.o: Beneath the dry hay sweetness, the smoky aroma of fire-cured leaf can be detected.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-chocolate.z: No verifiable composition and character information could be compiled for Wilke Pipe Tobacco's aromatic blend Chocolate.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-chocolate.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

the-storytellers-pipe-shop-m-m-log-cabin.z: M/M Log Cabin is a house blend Mike and Meaghan Hulsey, who run The Story Teller's Pipe Shop, prepared to recreate the old Log Cabin blend. Per the maker's description, quality Burley leaves are joined by flue-cured, red, golden and stoved Virginias, the mixture rounded out with a pinch of black Cavendish and cased with maple syrup flavor. It is a Burley-forward aromatic; maple sweetness is pronounced on lighting, and after the first quarter of the bowl an earthy, walnut-like taste with a light spice runs through to the end. Suited to smokers who steer away from heavy syrupy aromatics and want a measured flavoring that preserves the tobacco taste. Presented ribbon cut and sold loose.
the-storytellers-pipe-shop-m-m-log-cabin.o: Leaves a scent of oats and molasses cookie on lighting, moving toward freshly baked sweet walnut bread as it progresses.

sillems-commodore-flake.z: Commodore Flake is a flake blend made by pressing full-bodied, smoky Latakia with Kentucky leaf and a pinch of black cavendish. Latakia sets the blend's main color; the fire-cured Kentucky adds an earthy depth to the body and a notable nicotine share. The cavendish ratio is low and serves only to soften the edge. The pressed structure concentrates the flavor and the burn character varies with how the slices are crumbled. The smoke stays dry, smoky, and faintly salty throughout the bowl; no additives are used. Suited to smokers accustomed to Latakia-forward flake blends who want high nicotine and intense flavor.
sillems-commodore-flake.o: Leaves a dry scent evoking heavy wood smoke, soot, and old paper.

tobacco-land-pipe-cherry-no-13.z: Tobacco Land Pipe Cherry No. 13 is listed as a cherry-flavored pipe blend, as its name suggests; no sufficient source on its leaf composition and production details has been found.
tobacco-land-pipe-cherry-no-13.o: Recorded as leaving a fruity aroma carrying cherry essence.

thomas-radford-sundays-fantasy.z: Sunday's Fantasy, bearing the Thomas Radford name, is a flavored blend built on black Cavendish and Virginia leaf. It is presented ribbon cut and arrives quite moist in the tin; if not aired out before packing, it burns with difficulty. The casing leans toward fruit and citrus. On the smoke it gives a very sweet, fruity profile; nicotine is extremely light and flavor intensity is mild. Because the bowl heats up easily, it calls for slow, careful smoking, otherwise the taste turns harsh. A product for pipe smokers who enjoy flavored blends and want a low-nicotine, sweet smoke.
thomas-radford-sundays-fantasy.o: Leaves a light aroma reminiscent of sweet fruit and citrus peel.

motzek-logic-blend.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of the Motzek blend called Logic Blend could be found.

dunhill-night-cap.z: Night Cap is among Dunhill's heaviest English mixtures. A blend of Virginia, perique, latakia and oriental leaves, presented coarse cut. Latakia soot forms the blend's backbone, perique sharpens the spice, while the Virginia side holds a sweet base underneath. It's very strong in nicotine; as its name suggests, it suits being smoked slowly and at length as the day's last pipe. Its effect notably intensifies when smoked on an empty stomach. It's built for experienced smokers accustomed to strong tobaccos who aren't put off by latakia's weight; it is not a first choice for newcomers to pipe tobacco. Production under this name ended with the brand's exit from pipe tobacco.
dunhill-night-cap.o: Heavy wood soot and spice scent settles into the room and lingers long.

edwards-good-companion.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of Good Companion, a pipe tobacco from Edward's. Edward's is a tobacconist business based in Tampa, Florida.

paul-olsen-perique.z: One of the blends from the Copenhagen-based Paul Olsen name; no independent sources documenting its composition and character could be found.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-mick-mcqu.z: Mick McQuaid is an Irish brand that Dundalk's P. J. Carroll firm released in 1889, inspired by the pipe-smoking hero of William Francis Lynam's folk tales; no sufficient primary source describing this plug-format version's blend composition could be found. According to records the brand passed through Carreras/Rothmans and British American Tobacco before moving to Orlik in 2007, then to Scandinavian Tobacco Group, and was discontinued in 2016.

tabac-manil-fleur-de-semois.z: Fleur de Semois is made from Semois leaf, grown in the Semois valley in Belgium's Ardennes region. Grown on Vincent Manil's farm and processed by traditional methods, this tobacco is a Burley variety that has adapted over centuries to the region's damp, misty soil and has been known in Europe for over a hundred years. Fleur de Semois is the fine-cut (coupe fine) version of this leaf and carries no casing or flavoring whatsoever. The taste doesn't resemble familiar pipe blends: it gives an earthy, floral, cool smoke, with a tin note and smoke reminiscent of cigar tobacco. The leaf can seem coarse when young, but records indicate it mellows with a few years of aging. Because it is finely cut, it needs a loose fill. It suits anyone curious about an unflavored, single-leaf tobacco with a taste close to cigar leaf.
tabac-manil-fleur-de-semois.o: Leaves a dry, earthy, floral leaf scent reminiscent of cigar tobacco.

teds-pipe-shoppe-virginia-blend.z: One of the house blends prepared at Ted's Pipe Shoppe in Tulsa, Oklahoma; though records show it among the more than forty house blends of the business founded in 1961, no independent source describing the blend's content and character could be found.

mac-baren-stockton.z: Stockton is one of the first rope-cut products introduced in 1953 and produced under the Mac Baren name. Whole Virginia leaves are used as the outer wrap; inside the wrap is a spicy Cavendish core prepared from dark-fire-cured Kentucky. The spun ropes are rested for weeks before being cut into thin coins. Per sources, roughly four-sixths of the mixture is North American Virginia, with the rest dark-fire-cured Kentucky. The product was originally marketed as "navy cut." The taste arises from the combination of the flame-cured leaf's natural sugar with Kentucky-sourced tangy, woody, and sharp tones; underneath there's a steady smoky layer. As with Mac Baren's rope products, only a thin maple-sugar coating is used. Among the company's spun products, it carries the highest Cavendish proportion and is thus considered the most full-bodied. Nicotine load is high; aimed at smokers used to coin cut and a strong Virginia-Kentucky structure.
mac-baren-stockton.o: Leaves a wood-smoke and sweetish dry-leaf aroma.

sutliff-tobacco-company-black-golden-cav.z: Black & Golden Cavendish B27 is a bulk blend from Sutliff's "B"-coded black-cavendish line. Its name comes from the two colors of leaf used together: golden Virginia leaves and cavendish blackened through steaming. Burley is added to give body, and the blend is rounded out with a creamy vanilla topping. Black cavendish holds moisture and slows the burn; golden Virginia brings a sweet, lightly tart top note. The topping is noticeable but leaves a soft sweetness that doesn't sit heavy on the tongue, and nicotine is low. Since Sutliff's bulk line is sold by weight at tobacconists, this blend is commonly found among those starting to explore aromatics and those wanting a moderately sweet everyday tobacco. It is ribbon cut.
sutliff-tobacco-company-black-golden-cav.o: Leaves a scent of creamy vanilla and sweet dough.

straus-tobacco-seven-hills.z: Seven Hills is one of the counter blends from Straus Tobacconist in Cincinnati; records indicate the shop was founded in 1880 and that most of its house blends were named after Cincinnati neighborhoods and landmark buildings. Since no independent source on the blend's composition and character could be found, this record is kept at listing level only.

brigham-enterprises-inc-buttered-rum.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named Buttered Rum under the Brigham Enterprises Inc. brand could be found.

jons-pipe-shop-stonehenge.z: One of the house blends Jon's Pipe Shop sells under its own name; no independent source could be found on its contents or character.

iwan-ries-canadian-plug.z: This is a pressed blend that appeared in Iwan Ries's past catalogs; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
iwan-ries-canadian-plug.o: No room note described in the records could be found.

wessex-gold-brick.z: Gold Brick is Wessex's uncut plug product made from unflavored Virginia; it's sold as a 100-gram cake, and the smoker slices and rubs out as much as needed. It follows an old-fashioned, unflavored Virginia recipe. In the flavor profile, malty, bready tones and caramel-candy sweetness come forward; nicotine and intensity sit in the light band, making it suitable for long sessions. It suits smokers willing to take the time to prepare a plug and wanting to taste unflavored Virginia in its plain form.
wessex-gold-brick.o: Leaves a scent of freshly baked bread and light caramel.

jacks-tobacco-ok-bayou.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of Jack's Tobacco's OK Bayou blend could be found.

fincks-cigar-company-mild-english.z: No independent, reliable source could be found to fill out an entry for Finck's Cigar Company's Mild English pipe tobacco; the blend's composition, cut, and character were not recorded.

ken-byron-ventures-b-frogs-peaty-hunt.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Ken Byron Ventures' B. Frog's Peaty Hunt blend.

rattray-black-mallory-british-collection.z: Black Mallory is a classic English blend in Rattray's British Collection line. Latakia, Oriental leaf, and black Cavendish are added to a Virginia base; it is a ribbon cut. The Latakia proportion is pronounced enough to define the blend's character, and its smoky, incense-like taste is felt from the first bowl to the last. It is medium in strength but high in flavor intensity. It lights easily, requires no extra effort to keep lit, and leaves a taste that lingers long on the palate after smoking. It carries no flavoring. It suits smokers familiar with Latakia-heavy English blends, as well as those curious about the style who don't want too harsh a starting point. The Rattray name draws on the Scottish pipe-tobacco tradition; the brand's tobaccos are produced today in Germany.
rattray-black-mallory-british-collection.o: Leaves a smoky, incense-like, heavy aroma reminiscent of wood fire.

dan-tobacco-shannon.z: This is a pipe tobacco under the German maker Dan Tobacco Manufaktur; no reliable source about the blend's composition and character could be found, so no detail is given.

milan-tobacconists-our-london-dock.z: "Our" London Dock is one of the house blends from Milan Tobacconists in Roanoke, Virginia. It takes its name from, and is built in memory of, Middleton's London Dock blend, sold for many years before being discontinued. Its composition includes perique, Turkish tobacco, and burleys; a small amount of buttered-rum note is applied on top. The burley base gives the blend a nutty, dry body, while perique adds a peppery spark and the oriental leaf a spicy edge; the rum casing isn't intense enough to count the blend as aromatic, and the maker has also placed it in the non-aromatic line. Suitable for those looking for a classic American-style, measuredly flavored blend.
milan-tobacconists-our-london-dock.o: Leaves a thin layer of buttered-rum sweetness over the nutty tobacco aroma.

paul-olsen-hot-nuts-d3846.z: A blend from the My Own Blend line that originated at the Paul Olsen shop in Copenhagen; not enough source material describing its composition and character could be found.

robert-lewis-st-james-mixture.z: St. James Mixture is a blend carrying the name of Robert Lewis, the well-established tobacconist on St. James's Street in London; no source could be found documenting its content and character.

charatan-black-flake.z: Charatan is a pipe brand founded in London in 1863; after Dunhill withdrew from the tobacco business in 2017, a tobacco line under the Charatan name was released by Tor Imports, with the blends manufactured by Kohlhase & Kopp in Germany. Black Flake is the dark Virginia flake built in this line to take the place of Dunhill's Dark Flake. Dark, matured Virginia leaves are pressed and sliced; no casing is used. The flavor is bready and dark-fruited, and its high sugar content calls for a slow smoke. Nicotine sits at the high end of the line. Suitable for smokers accustomed to dark, full-bodied Virginia flakes.
charatan-black-flake.o: Leaves a dark bread and dried fruit room note.

iwan-ries-three-star-banner-lite.z: This is a blend from the Three Star line prepared over the counter by the Chicago-based tobacconist Iwan Ries & Co.; no independent source detailing its content and character could be found, so the profile is left incomplete.
iwan-ries-three-star-banner-lite.o: No reliable information about the room note could be found.

tinder-box-honey-cavendish.z: Honey Cavendish is one of Tinder Box's Cavendish-based aromatic house blends. Honey casing is worked into steam-processed, sweetened Cavendish leaf; it gives a slow-burning, mellow smoke. The flavor stays sweet from start to finish, and the tobacco's own sharpness stays in the background. Nicotine load is low, so it doesn't weigh on long smokes. Suited to those loading an aromatic into their pipe for the first time and to fans of honey-and-sugar-forward casings.
tinder-box-honey-cavendish.o: Leaves a scent of warm honey and baked dough.

sutliff-tobacco-company-507c-virginia-sl.z: Sutliff 507C Virginia Slices is a flake-cut bulk blend pressed and sliced from flue-cured Virginia leaf. Per the maker's description, a soft aromatic coating is placed over the leaf; this topping doesn't push the blend into the aromatic category but adds a thin scent-and-flavor layer alongside the Virginia character. The blend stays within the pure Virginia category while following a more accessible line than fully unflavored flakes. The slices need to be rubbed out or folded before packing; suited to those wanting to sample Virginia's tangy-sweet structure at bulk pricing and to those wanting to get accustomed to flake use.
sutliff-tobacco-company-507c-virginia-sl.o: A light flavoring scent mixes into herbal, tangy Virginia sweetness.

bufflehead-king-eider.z: One of the discontinued blends from the Bufflehead shop; no source documenting its composition could be found.

kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-winter-edition-2.z: Winter Edition 2013 is an installment of Kohlhase & Kopp's seasonal limited series released each winter. The series' shared design is adding plenty of black cavendish onto selected Virginia leaves and applying a casing evocative of the holiday season. In the 2013 edition, the main flavor rests on cherry; almond sits second, with licorice in the background. The tin is decorated with snowflake and deer motifs. Bright Virginia gives a grassy, citrus-leaning tanginess, while dark Virginia adds ripe dark fruit and woody depth; black cavendish builds the sugary body. Nicotine level is low, giving a long, cool smoke. Since it was produced only for that season, it wasn't renewed in later years.
kohlhase-kopp-und-co-kg-winter-edition-2.o: A light licorice scent can be heard behind the cherry and almond sweetness.

chacom-1.z: Chacom is the long-established pipe manufacturer based in Saint-Claude, France; the tobacco line bearing its name is produced at Kohlhase & Kopp's facilities in Germany. #1 is the Latakia blend in the line: broken Virginia forms the body, black cavendish adds sweetness, and Oriental leaf together with Cyprus Latakia supply the smoke-and-spice layer. The flavor is smoky and woody, with a fine perfumed tone from the Oriental; Virginia's sweetness is felt underneath this layer. Nicotine is in the medium range. The broken cut makes it easy to fill. Suitable for smokers seeking a balanced English blend without a heavy Latakia share.
chacom-1.o: Leaves a smoky, woody, lightly spiced room note.

sutliff-tobacco-company-metropolitain.z: An aromatic blend listed in Sutliff catalogs; no reliable source documenting its composition and character could be found.

consolidated-503-heavy-english.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Consolidated blend 503: Heavy English.

cornell-diehl-snow-day.z: Snow Day is a blend in Cornell & Diehl's Wintertime Reserve series, prepared for the year-end season. The series is hand-produced in small batches using recipes developed by head blender Jeremy Reeves; new blends come out every year, and previous years' blends aren't repeated. The blend's core is sweet, tangy red Virginia leaf; a light honey touch is added on top. This preserves Virginia's natural sugar while adding a measured layer of casing. Suited to smokers looking for lightly cased, Virginia-focused winter blends. Wintertime Reserve blends are distributed as part of the Peterson pipe campaign, so they haven't been sold as standalone products.
cornell-diehl-snow-day.o: Leaves a sweet scent leaning toward honey and baked bread.

mcgahey-the-tobacconist-broad-and-burley.z: Broad and Burley is listed as one of the burley-forward house blends from McGahey The Tobacconist; no reliable source about its composition and character could be found.
mcgahey-the-tobacconist-broad-and-burley.o: No reliable record regarding its room note could be found.

low-country-pipe-cigar-carolina-christma.z: Carolina Christmas is the limited holiday edition, re-blended each year, prepared for Low Country Pipe & Cigar in Little River. The 2024 edition consists of red Virginia cavendish, heirloom burley varieties, matured red and light Virginia, St. James Parish perique from Louisiana's 31 Farms, and oriental leaf from Katerini; the wide, irregular ribbon cut is at a moisture level ready to smoke straight from the tin. The warm spice, sweet-wine impression, dark fruit and cocoa notes in the taste come not from casing but from the leaves' own character. Body and strength sit above medium; for smokers seeking an unflavored yet sweet and complex holiday blend.
low-country-pipe-cigar-carolina-christma.o: Leaves a sweetish room note reminiscent of dried fruit, warm spice and cocoa.

dan-tobacco-no-name-no-3.z: A blend in Dan Tobacco's No Name series under the Timm line, recorded as Virginia-heavy; no adequate source was found for detailed composition and character information.
dan-tobacco-no-name-no-3.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

cornell-diehl-innsmouth.z: Innsmouth is a Virginia-forward blend belonging to Cornell & Diehl's series inspired by the H. P. Lovecraft universe. Virginia leaf is joined by Oriental tobaccos, perique, and black cavendish; the cut is ribbon. Over Virginia's tangy-sweet body, Oriental tobacco's dry spice and perique's plum tone layer in, while cavendish softens the smoke. Carrying no added flavoring, at a medium body, this composition makes an all-day option for smokers who love unflavored Virginia blends and want a bit of spice.
cornell-diehl-innsmouth.o: Spicy Oriental tobacco aroma mixes with Virginia's tangy sweetness.

orlik-three-nuns-original.z: Three Nuns is a historic brand rooted in English tobacco tradition; the version discussed here is the curly-cut blend produced by Orlik carrying the original name. It contains Virginia, burley, and fire-cured Kentucky leaf; no flavoring is applied. The blend sits at the full end of the unflavored wing: nicotine is high, taste very intense, and it has a dry character leaving a pronounced dryness in the mouth. A balance between strength and taste is noted as being maintained. It's aimed at experienced smokers accustomed to high-nicotine unflavored blends; it isn't a suitable start for those coming from mild or sweet blends. The brand name has been carried on over the years by different manufacturers with changing compositions.
orlik-three-nuns-original.o: Leaves a dark, smoky, dry-leaf scent on a lightly tart base.

paul-olsen-no-7000.z: No. 7000 is the latakia-forward English blend in Paul Olsen's My Own Blend line. Cyprian latakia comes forward, joined by Samsun oriental and black cavendish. It's at a smoking-ready moisture straight out of the pack. The taste sits between medium and full and stays consistent through the bowl; a buttery sweetness, strong wood smoke, a floral top note, and a tangy background line up with traces of musty grass, dry earth, and leather, with a peppery sharpness coming on the retrohale. It burns quickly and leaves a dry ash, which also makes it useful for a new pipe's first bowls. It suits smokers who love classic English blends with pronounced latakia.
paul-olsen-no-7000.o: Leaves a scent of heavy wood smoke, leather, and dry earth.

low-country-pipe-cigar-rum.z: One of the house blends of South Carolina-based Low Country Pipe & Cigar; described as a rum-flavored aromatic, but not enough sources could be found to describe its character.

ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-honey-butter.z: An aromatic small-batch blend in Ken Byron Ventures' Yoshimi's line; not enough sources could be found to document its composition and character.
ken-byron-ventures-yoshimis-honey-butter.o: Could not be described due to lack of accessible records.

cornell-diehl-espresso.z: Espresso is one of Cornell & Diehl's all-black-looking aromatic mixtures. Unsweetened black cavendish is joined by a portion of Green River vanilla-flavored leaf, topped with the brand's own cream flavoring and a pronounced coffee aroma. The name references the image of macchiato served at Italian street cafes. The body is light, offering a smoke driven more by the flavoring than the leaf itself; coffee, vanilla, and cream tones sit together. It suits users looking for a starter aromatic blend or a sweet-coffee flavor profile.
cornell-diehl-espresso.o: Leaves a sweet room aroma reminiscent of freshly ground coffee and cream.

g-l-pease-arrakis-spice.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Arrakis Spice.

mab-stary-presporok.z: Starý Prešporok is a latakia-forward blend from Slovak manufacturer MAB; its name references Pressburg, the old German-Hungarian name for Bratislava. Cyprus latakia forms the backbone of the blend, accompanied by golden Virginia, sweetish oriental leaf from Greece's Basma region, and black cavendish. It's presented as a ribbon cut in 50-gram packages. The smoke is dense and full-bodied, with strength in the medium-to-high range. Latakia's smoky, woody character dominates; cavendish balances this dryness with a little sweetness, and the oriental leaf adds a tangy spice. It's reportedly positioned among Slovak retailers as the local counterpart to Peterson Old Dublin. Suited to smokers accustomed to latakia who want an unflavored, full-bodied English blend.
mab-stary-presporok.o: Leaves a room note of smoke, pine smoke and dry wood.

dobies-four-square-medium-navy-light-blu.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the character of Four Square Medium Navy (Light Blue), a blend from Dobie's.

frederick-tranter-brindle-mixture.z: Not enough independent sourcing to fill out an entry could be found for Frederick Tranter's Brindle Mixture blend; records place it in the Virginia-heavy class.

sutliff-tobacco-company-maryland-burley.z: No independent source detailing the leaf composition and smoking character of Maryland Burley, listed among Sutliff's unflavored blending tobaccos, could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-maryland-burley.o: No reliable description of the room note could be found.

cobblestone-walnut-maple-pie.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the content and character of the Cobblestone blend Walnut Maple Pie.

old-virginia-tobacco-co-commonwealth.z: Commonwealth is one of the labeled blends from Old Virginia Tobacco Co. described as Virginia-forward; no independent source describing its composition and character could be found.

dan-tobacco-fleetenkieker.z: Fleetenkieker is an aromatic blend from Dan Tobacco's Hamburg-themed "Hamburger Pfeifentabak" series. It contains sun-ripened golden Virginia leaf in varying cut widths, a generous amount of black Cavendish, and a very small pinch of Louisiana Perique, topped with a modest fruit casing. The name refers to people who, when Hamburg's canals (known as "Fleete") ran low, would wade in to collect whatever had settled at the bottom. The weight of black Cavendish makes the blend sweet and soft; the small amount of Perique leaves a light spice and tartness in the background. Its low nicotine makes it suitable for all-day smoking. The maker notes the blend opens up more evenly in medium-sized bowls. Suited to smokers who like sweet aromatics but want to avoid heavily syrupy mixtures.
dan-tobacco-fleetenkieker.o: Leaves a sweet, lightly fruity, warm sugar scent.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-picayune-.z: Picayune Pancake, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi; catalog records note it as an aromatic mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its composition and character has been found, the record's details are left blank.

mac-baren-dark-twist-loose-cut.z: Dark Twist is one of Mac Baren's products that continues the brand's old-fashioned handcraft. Selected Virginia leaves and the brand's signature cavendish are wrapped as a filling inside whole Virginia leaves; the resulting twist is cut into rounds and packed by hand. The loose cut presentation is this same twisted tobacco prepared as a loose cut rather than rounds, which makes packing easier. The density from the rope structure carries through to the taste: the dark, tangy sweetness of the Virginia and the depth of the cavendish stand out, with reportedly a light liqueur-like accent on top. Nicotine sits in the medium range and it burns slowly. Suited to smokers curious about the character of twist tobaccos but who don't want to bother slicing rounds.
mac-baren-dark-twist-loose-cut.o: Leaves a dark, sweetish room note with a light liqueur-like edge.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-sail-clas.z: Sail is a brand that began production under a century-old Dutch recipe by the storied Dutch tobacco house Koninklijke Theodorus Niemeyer, and is now continued under Scandinavian Tobacco Group. Classic Basic Mixture is the version following the line's traditional Dutch cavendish direction. The blend's base is built from burley and Virginia; Oriental and Brazilian leaf are added, and a small amount of latakia gives depth. There is almost no casing aroma; the flavor comes from the leaf's processing and forms a creamy, lightly spicy character. Aimed at those seeking a measured blend standing between aromatic and English mixtures that they can smoke all day.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-sail-clas.o: Leaves a creamy, lightly spicy scent carrying a fine trace of smoke behind it.

peretti-blend-500.z: A numbered house mixture L.J. Peretti lists in its English blends group and continues to produce; no source describing its leaf proportions and flavor profile could be found.

peter-heinrichs-no-14.z: Peter Heinrichs No. 14 is a house blend in which vanilla flavoring is pronounced. Per the maker's description, the blend's backbone is built from Old Belt Virginia known for its natural sweetness; American Burley adds an earthy, nutty body, while black Cavendish leaves a sweet, soft layer at the finish. While the flavoring is pronounced, it doesn't fully mask the tobacco base; the Virginia and Burley texture shows through under the vanilla. Nicotine sits in the light band and the burn is cool and even. It is a suitable record for smokers who love classic vanilla aromatics or are new to the aromatic group.
peter-heinrichs-no-14.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and baked-dough aroma.

boswell-pipes-tobacco-chocolate-cream.z: Chocolate Cream is Boswell's chocolate-cased aromatic blend. Per the manufacturer's description, the chocolate taste is followed by a vanilla finish; the blend is built to smoke soft and stay light on the palate. The base is black-cavendish-forward; nicotine is low, lighting is easy, and no tongue bite is reported. Suitable for smokers seeking a familiar, sweet-level chocolate note in a light aromatic.
boswell-pipes-tobacco-chocolate-cream.o: Leaves a cocoa and creamy vanilla aroma.

peter-heinrichs-no-29.z: No. 29 is a Peter Heinrichs blend built from very soft Burley leaf. Per the maker's account, the leaves are processed with a sweet flavoring, then roasted, rested under pressure for a long time, and cut into small cubes. This cubic cut gives a slow, cool burn, suitable for setting the pipe aside and picking it back up later. On the palate, Burley's nutty, bready base comes forward; the flavoring leaves a light sweetness recalling caramel, honey, and pastry. Nicotine strength is measured and bite is kept low. It suits smokers who want to steer clear of heavily flavored blends and are seeking a lightly flavored Burley for all-day smoking, as well as those wanting to try cube cut.
peter-heinrichs-no-29.o: Leaves a lightly roasted, nutty tone alongside caramel, honey, and baked-dough aromas.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-peanut-butter-and-cho.z: Peanut Butter and Chocolate is a dual-flavored blend among Wilke Pipe Tobacco's bulk aromatics. According to the maker's recipe, peanut-butter and chocolate flavoring is worked over a nutty-character Maryland Burley and Virginia leaf base. The maker describes the blend as an easy, all-day mixture; the sweet side comes forward while the nicotine stays moderate. This is a record for those seeking dessert-style sweet aromatics and for those wanting a high-flavor option within the aromatic line.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-peanut-butter-and-cho.o: Leaves a sweet scent reminiscent of roasted peanuts and cocoa.

lane-limited-black-cavendish.z: Lane Limited's bulk-sold, single-component black cavendish tobacco. Cavendish is a processing method obtained by sweetening and darkening tobacco under pressure and heat; the resulting leaf is dark-colored, moist and soft. Nicotine is low, the smoke is cool. Georgia-based Lane Limited is among the leading houses producing bulk aromatic tobacco for many years, and this cavendish also forms the base of many of the brand's aromatic blends. It can be smoked alone or used as a casing to sweeten and soften Virginia- or burley-forward blends. Suited to those seeking a light, sweet tobacco that doesn't bite the tongue and to those who blend their own.
lane-limited-black-cavendish.o: Leaves a sweet vanilla and cooked-sugar room note.

tabacos-catarinenses-ltda-havana-pessego.z: Havana Pêssego is the peach-flavored member of the Havana line Tabacos Catarinenses produces in Santa Catarina. As across the line, it is prepared by homogeneously blending selected Virginia and Burley leaves with aromatic casing, and it is packed ribbon cut. The peach note leads the smoke, with the tobacco's own taste remaining a soft base; nicotine is low. It suits smokers drawn to fruity aromatics who want a light-bodied, easy smoke.
tabacos-catarinenses-ltda-havana-pessego.o: Leaves a sweet fruity scent reminiscent of ripe peach.

cornell-diehl-riverboat-gambler.z: Riverboat Gambler is a ribbon-cut American mixture bringing together tobaccos of the American South: Virginia, Louisiana Perique, and Turkish leaf are added on top of a Burley base. It takes its name from the gamblers of Mississippi riverboats; records note the blend grew out of a joint effort between Craig Tarler and Bob Runowski. On the smoke, Burley comes forward, Perique follows with a plum-and-pepper sharpness, and Oriental leaf leaves a spicy texture in the background. It follows an unflavored, straightforward flavor line reminiscent of a cigar smoke; nicotine level is fairly high, and each leaf in the blend can be tasted separately. Suited to smokers accustomed to Burley who want body rather than sweetness.
cornell-diehl-riverboat-gambler.o: Leaves a heavy, earthy, sharp scent reminiscent of cigar smoke.

borkum-riff-champagne.z: One of Borkum Riff's aromatic offerings from the 2000s listings, named for its topping; according to records it's counted among blends where the flavoring stays faint. No manufacturer statement on its leaf composition could be found, leaving the profile incomplete.
borkum-riff-champagne.o: According to records it leaves a faint, lightly sweet room note.

mcclelland-dark-star-personal-reserve.z: Dark Star is a flake in McClelland's Personal Reserve series, made from Virginia leaf processed until dark. It carries no flavoring; the dark color and deep taste come from the leaf's own processing. Production ended when the brand closed in early 2018. Moisture is high straight out of the tin, and the flakes don't rub out easily; airing them thoroughly before packing, then breaking them up coarsely, corrects the burn. Prepared this way, it burns cool and long. Its flavor frame rests on mild sweetness with spiced touches, and nicotine dose reaches a satisfying level in a medium-sized pipe. Suited to smokers accustomed to preparing flake; not an easy record for pipe beginners given the packing and lighting difficulty.
mcclelland-dark-star-personal-reserve.o: Leaves a dark, tangy, sweet-spiced tobacco aroma.

john-aylesbury-own-mixture.z: Not enough independent sources could be found to document the contents and character of John Aylesbury's Own Mixture.

hermit-tobacco-works-co-party-blend-2007.z: This is a limited 2007 release from Hermit Tobacco Works Co.; no details are given, as there is no independent sourcing describing its content and character.
hermit-tobacco-works-co-party-blend-2007.o: No reliable record of its aroma could be found.

watch-city-cigar-497.z: This is described as one of Watch City Cigar's cavendish-based house blends; since no record was published in the maker's current catalog, its composition could not be confirmed.
watch-city-cigar-497.o: Could not be determined from the records.

abenaki-tobacco-co-new-castle-english.z: New Castle English is one of Abenaki Tobacco's two English mixtures. Per the maker's recipe, African- and Turkish-origin leaf is brought together with Virginia; Latakia is added only enough not to overpower the blend. The brand describes this mixture as the mildest among its Latakia products. The low Latakia ratio makes it an entry point for smokers trying the smoky line of English mixtures who aren't ready for a heavy Balkan structure. The Oriental leaf adds a dry, grassy, faintly tangy edge to the blend, while the Virginia sets the sweet base. Abenaki Tobacco was based in Conway, New Hampshire; the brand's own sales site isn't live today.
abenaki-tobacco-co-new-castle-english.o: Leaves a lightly woody smoke and dry-hay room note.

peterson-summertime-2014.z: Summertime 2014 is a limited edition blend released as part of Peterson's Summertime series specific to that year; the profile is left incomplete, as no sufficient first-hand sources confirming its content and character could be found.

tabakfabrik-roth-alplertabak.z: Älplertabak is Tabakfabrik Roth's house blend prepared entirely from Swiss-grown leaf. According to the maker's stated ratio, two-thirds of the mixture is Burley and one-third Virginia; the blend is enriched with mint and coltsfoot leaf tea. The resulting taste is built on Burley's nutty fullness, with a fine sweetness, traces of dry hay and spice, and a cooling touch of mint. Because of the Burley weight, the nicotine sensation sits a notch above Seetaler's, and the taste is earthy rather than flat. As its alpine name suggests, it suits smokers looking for a plain, grassy, herbal character who want to steer clear of heavily fruit-cased aromatics. The blend is produced in 100-gram, 500-gram, and one-kilogram packages.
tabakfabrik-roth-alplertabak.o: A light honeyed sweetness mixes into the scent of cool mint and dry hay.

robert-mcconnell-folded-flake.z: Folded Flake is an unflavored blend, cut into thin slices, made by pressing two separate Virginia leaves together with dark-fired Kentucky and Perique. Adding Kentucky to the classic Virginia-Perique framework pushes the blend toward a darker, woodier place than the style's usual examples. The tin note carries ripe plum and a vinegary sharpness. In the smoke, Virginia's sweetness is softened by Kentucky's earthy smokiness, and Perique's spicy-tangy layer comes forward on the finish. Strength is medium. It suits smokers used to flake packing who want an unflavored, spicy Virginia blend.
robert-mcconnell-folded-flake.o: Leaves the woody smokiness of dark-fired leaf together with a ripe plum aroma.

clan-shaw-cool-mint.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of Clan Shaw's Cool Mint blend could be found.

low-country-pipe-cigar-carolina-christma.z: Carolina Christmas 2009 is the 2009 member of the limited-edition holiday blend series South Carolina-based Low Country Pipe & Cigar releases; since the composition changes each year, not enough sources could be found for the 2009 version's contents.
low-country-pipe-cigar-carolina-christma.o: Leaves a spicy, sweetish room note.

sutliff-tobacco-company-ts20-perique-gra.z: TS20 is the pure Louisiana Perique sold in Sutliff's straight-leaf series; the 208-R code indicates the product's granulated cut. Perique is grown only in Louisiana's St. James region; after harvest it is pressed under its own weight in barrels and fermented, turning it into an extremely dark, moist, intense leaf. Its taste carries a peppery, spicy depth reminiscent of plum and fig, with a fruity character and a light earthy note as well. This product is generally taken as a blending ingredient rather than smoked on its own. Even adding a few percent to a Virginia-forward base adds a distinct layer of spice and fermented fruit to the taste. If smoked pure, it should be tried in very small amounts and drawn slowly; both nicotine load and taste intensity are high.
sutliff-tobacco-company-ts20-perique-gra.o: Leaves a sharp scent of pepper, vinegared dried fruit, and earth.

cornell-diehl-tuskegee-airman.z: Tuskegee Airman is a blend built from Virginia, Perique, Turkish leaf, and Latakia, pressed so the flavors meld together and sliced for easy packing. It takes its name from the Tuskegee Airmen, the first Black military pilots of the United States; records note the bomber crews they escorted called them "Red Tail Angels" for the red-painted tails of their P-51 aircraft. On the smoke, spice, sweetness, and smoke move together: Virginia sets the base, Perique adds sharpness, Oriental leaf adds dry spice, and Latakia carries the smoky layer. Thanks to its sliced structure it can be packed rubbed out or folded; its body sits at a medium level.
cornell-diehl-tuskegee-airman.o: Leaves a smoky scent accompanied by spicy and sweet tones.

sutliff-tobacco-company-cd-blend.z: CD Blend is an American mixture bringing together burley, Virginia, latakia, flake leaf, and perique, coarse cut with moisture kept low. Latakia gives a light smokiness, and perique adds a peppery, dried-fruit-leaning sharpness; burley forms the base body. Top flavoring is nearly nonexistent. In Sutliff's Private Stock line, it's referred to as an equivalent to the long-selling Country Doctor blend. Suited to smokers seeking an old-fashioned, full-bodied, lightly flavored mixture.
sutliff-tobacco-company-cd-blend.o: Leaves an old-fashioned tobacco scent carrying smoky tobacco and dried-fruit directions.

lane-limited-captain-black-grape.z: Captain Black is Lane Limited's aromatic pipe tobacco line sold in pouches, and one of the most widespread brands to reach even supermarket shelves in the US. Grape is the series' member flavored with grape essence; a pronounced grape note sits atop a soft, cavendish-forward base. Moisture is regulated, the cut is ribbon, and nicotine is low. It's a tobacco that lights easily and burns cool. The fruit aroma also carries into the smoke's taste, though the tobacco's own character stays in the background. Suited to those seeking a sweet, direct aromatic and to those filling a pipe for the first time.
lane-limited-captain-black-grape.o: Leaves a sweet black-grape and sugary-juice room note.

samuel-gawith-cob-flake.z: Cob Flake is a flake blend Samuel Gawith makes by pressing and slicing virginia and burley leaf together. Its name rests on the idea of a structure suited to daily smoking, compatible with corncob pipes. It is produced using the traditional pressing method applied at the Kendal facility. In the flavor profile, virginia's light sweetness sits alongside burley's dry, nutty body; nicotine is medium. Crumbling the slices and airing them briefly regulates the burn. Suited to those seeking a plain, balanced daily blend without a pronounced casing.
samuel-gawith-cob-flake.o: Leaves a scent of baked bread and toasted hazelnut.

orlik-tobacco-company-a-s-old-company.z: A blend listed in the Orlik catalog as Virginia-based; not enough independent source material describing its composition could be found.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-summer-br.z: Summer Breeze is one of The Country Squire's aromatic house blends intended for the warm season. Its base contains grassy, citrus-leaning Virginia Cavendish; nutty, earthy Burley supports the body, while unsweetened black Cavendish adds a light brown-sugar sweetness. The peach and honey casing on top is pronounced, with peach coming forward. Nicotine is low and the taste is mellow; no tongue bite or harshness is reported. Being a moist blend it can leave dampness at the bottom of the bowl and may need relighting partway through. Suited to smokers after a sweet, fruity, light aromatic and a low-nicotine mixture that can be smoked all day.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-summer-br.o: Leaves a sweet, fruity air with a syrupy peach and honey scent.

pipesandcigars-com-up-all-night.z: Up All Night is cited as an aromatic bulk blend appearing in pipesandcigars.com's catalogue; no independent source could be found describing its composition, so no detailed specification is given.

alfie-turmeaus-mr-sadorians-blend.z: One of Turmeaus's house-recipe mixtures, per records prepared by combining Kentucky, Latakia, and a ready-made English mixture; no detailed, independent source for its profile could be found.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-red-oriental.z: Red Oriental is among Wilke's Oriental-forward records. According to the maker's description, Turkish leaf governs the profile with earth, wood, floral notes, sourness, grass, spice, and a light buttery sweetness. It's joined by maduro cigar leaf, which brings toasted tones, cocoa, light coffee, dark fruit, and a touch of molasses to the smoke. Red Virginia carries the tart dark-fruit, bread, and sugar side, while the house's Royal Scot cavendish leaves a subtle vanilla in the background. Above medium in both nicotine and strength, this is a blend with a pronounced sweet-sour and smoky character. The salty-spicy framework built jointly by the cigar leaf and the Oriental leaf suits smokers open to full-bodied, unusual profiles more than those seeking light bowls.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-red-oriental.o: Leaves a woody, herbal, lightly smoky scent along with a trace of dried fruit.

peter-stokkebye-skilling.z: This is a Peter Stokkebye blend reported to be Cavendish-based; no sufficient first-hand sources documenting its content and character could be found.
peter-stokkebye-skilling.o: No sufficient information for a room note could be found in the records.

cornell-diehl-syrian-trawler.z: No listing documenting the composition of Syrian Trawler, a Cornell & Diehl blend, could be found in the maker's current catalogue or reliable retailer pages.

watch-city-cigar-terrapin-station.z: Watch City Cigar's blend called Terrapin Station is, according to records, one of the house blends of the Waltham, Massachusetts tobacconist shop; as no sufficient independent source could be found documenting its composition and character, this entry remains incomplete.

peretti-blend-d-9575.z: This is an old mixture that survives from Peretti's 'D' blend ledger, and per the company's statement is produced staying true to its original formula; the record is incomplete since the details of its content have not been published.

tsuge-premium-pipe-tobacco-summer-daydre.z: No independent source reliably documenting the composition and character of the Tsuge Premium Pipe Tobacco blend Summer Daydream has been found.

gawith-hoggarth-co-perique-flake-27.z: Perique Flake is a flake tobacco belonging to the same product family also known under the name Louisiana Flake, made by adding Perique to a Virginia base and pressing it. It's counted among the few Perique-containing blends in the brand's catalog. Since the Perique share is kept measured, the dark fruit sweetness leaning toward plum and fig stands out, with the peppery sharpness staying in the background. Suited to smokers wanting an unflavored Virginia-Perique structure without a harsh peppery hit; the slices are packed rubbed out or folded and burn slowly.
gawith-hoggarth-co-perique-flake-27.o: Leaves a tobacco aroma of dried fig with a light peppery edge.

cornell-diehl-black-cavendish.z: Cornell & Diehl's Black Cavendish is a single-component tobacco; the company describes it both as the base for its aromatic blends and as a leaf used to thicken the body of other mixtures. It is a ribbon cut and arrives with high moisture; drying it out from its as-tinned state can be difficult. On the smoke, it leaves a toasted-tobacco, creamy taste throughout, with a light caramel note beneath. Though described as unflavored, its sweet side is pronounced. It is a fast-burning tobacco; smoked quickly it carries a risk of hot smoke and tongue bite, so it calls for slow smoking. Being mild, it can be used any time of day; it suits those wanting to get to know plain cavendish taste and those building their own blends.
cornell-diehl-black-cavendish.o: Leaves an aroma of toasted tobacco and light caramel.

wilke-pipe-tobacco-lizzie-blood-red-virg.z: Lizzie Blood Red Virginia: Final Verdict is the heaviest link in the Lizzie Blood series from the New York-based Wilke house. According to the maker's recipe, roughly half of the blend is Perique; the rest consists of golden Virginia. Perique brings spice, lightly sweet plum, fig, raisin, and earth notes, while Virginia carries the citrus, bread, and sugar side. Blood-orange essence is applied on top, though the Perique intensity leaves this casing largely in the background. This is a dry, cool-burning, medium-strength but flavor-full record. It suits smokers seeking Perique's spice, accustomed to low-casing Virginia/Perique blends; the first bowl may feel heavy for those without Perique experience. Wilke offers this blend in bulk packages ranging from 2 to 16 ounces.
wilke-pipe-tobacco-lizzie-blood-red-virg.o: Leaves a sharp pepper and dried-plum scent with a light citrus trace.

sutliff-tobacco-company-tobacco-galleria.z: One of the aromatic blends in Sutliff's Tobacco Galleria line; no accessible source documenting its content could be found.

barclay-rex-jungle-leaf.z: Jungle Leaf is one of the blends prepared at Barclay Rex's own counter. Per the maker's description, it brings together African-origin leaf, Turkish tobacco, and Virginia; with no added flavoring, it gives an aromatic impression through the leaf's own sweetness and scent. It appeals to smokers looking for an unflavored yet sweet character, who like the spicy side of Oriental leaf. Nicotine and flavor intensity are medium; it's built for long smoking sessions during the day.
barclay-rex-jungle-leaf.o: Leaves a lightly sweet room note reminiscent of dry hay and spice.

the-tobacco-barn-my-pleasure.z: No sufficient source describing the leaf composition and flavor profile of this aromatic, listed as "My Pleasure Vanilla Fudge" in the toasted Cavendish group of Tobacco Barn's house blend list, has been found.

cornell-diehl-coconut.z: As its name suggests, this is a coconut-flavored aromatic blend from Cornell & Diehl; it does not appear in the manufacturer's current catalog, and not enough sourcing could be found to describe its composition.

ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-scary-s.z: Scary Spice is a spiced, chai-scented aromatic prepared for autumn. Burley, Virginia, and black Cavendish leaves are dressed with cream, cinnamon, allspice, nutmeg, and clove aromas. The maker notes the flavoring isn't heavy and the blend is meant as a light daytime mixture; it's sold as 2 oz. bulk. Thanks to its Burley-forward structure, the taste develops on a flat, nutty base, with the spice notes sitting on top of it. Suited to smokers who want an aromatic but wish to avoid a heavy sugar load and thick casing, and who are after a light bowl for early in the day.
ken-byron-ventures-mr-christians-scary-s.o: Leaves a spiced-tea aroma where cinnamon, clove, and nutmeg meet cream.

pipe-republic-cliftonville.z: No reliable sources on Pipe Republic's blend Cliftonville could be found, so its content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

smokers-haven-our-best-blend.z: Sufficient independent sources to fill out the record for the Smokers' Haven blend Our Best Blend could not be found.

erik-stokkebye-morning-blend.z: Morning Blend is a ribbon-cut, bulk blend built on Virginia and Burley leaves with a small amount of black cavendish added. The topping is kept very light; the additive is dosed to leave a small background sweetness rather than covering the tobacco's own taste. Although classified as aromatic in this respect, its character sits close to Virginia-Burley mixtures. It stays moderate in body and nicotine. It suits smokers looking for a light option for the day's first bowls, who find heavily topped aromatics too much but aren't ready for a fully unadulterated blend either.
erik-stokkebye-morning-blend.o: Leaves a lightly sweet, nutty and bready tobacco scent.

mclintock-rednut.z: Rednut is a McLintock variety combining sun-matured Virginia leaves with American burley, given a subtle hazelnut-cocoa flavoring on top. The flavoring is kept restrained enough not to cover the tobacco's own taste; its role is to round out the character and add sweetness. The nicotine strength is low, and the mixed cut gives a structure smokable throughout the day.
mclintock-rednut.o: Leaves an aroma of toasted hazelnut and cocoa.

gawith-hoggarth-co-balkan-mixture.z: Balkan Mixture is an untopped Balkan blend Kendal's Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. builds from Virginia, Oriental leaf, and Latakia. It is coarse cut and often arrives from the pack with high moisture; it needs airing before smoking. Latakia's resinous, burnt-wood-like aroma stands out in the blend. A review from Turkey reports that the cut and mix are not uniform, with individual leaves sometimes standing out separately, but also notes that it lights easily and its ash stays a clean grey. It is aimed at smokers seeking a latakia-heavy, untopped blend at an accessible price.
gawith-hoggarth-co-balkan-mixture.o: Leaves a heavy, sharp burnt-wood and resinous smoke aroma that lingers long in the room.

dunhill-my-mixture-73.z: My Mixture 73 is an English blend within Dunhill's "My Mixture" line, distinguished by its latakia weight. Syrian latakia was used in the original recipe; this leaf gives a drier smoke evoking leather and spice compared to Cyprus latakia. High-quality Virginia leaves and orientals form the base, while perique remains as a fruity spice accent. The blend became unavailable in the US market from the mid-1980s, discontinued during major changes to Dunhill's recipes. The replacement of Syrian latakia with Cyprus latakia, changes in blending methods, and shortened aging periods are the defining developments of that period. It draws the interest of those seeking latakia-heavy English mixtures; today it's a record found only in old tins.
dunhill-my-mixture-73.o: Heavy wood soot and leather scent fill the room.

richs-smoking-wicked.z: Smoking Wicked is, according to available reports, a rubbed flake from Rich's Cigar Store combining pressed Virginia leaf with Latakia and a noticeable dose of Perique; no second independent source could be found to confirm its detailed composition.
richs-smoking-wicked.o: No reliable information could be found on the room note.

hu-tobacco-sancho-panza.z: Sancho Panza is the second entry in HU Tobacco's aged, limited series bearing Don Quixote-related names. Its base is Virginia and Burley; a notable proportion of Latakia is added on top, which makes the blend a German-made English mixture. The finished blend was jarred after two years of resting; this rest calms Latakia's sharp smokiness and fuses it with the Virginia's sweetness.
hu-tobacco-sancho-panza.o: The wood smoke and smokiness from the Latakia hang in the room for a long time.

jons-pipe-shop-smoking-mixture.z: No independent source could be found to document the contents and character of Jon's Pipe Shop's Smoking Mixture blend.

nording-labrador-hunting-2025.z: Labrador is the Virginia/Perique wing of the Hunting (Hunter Blends) series inspired by Erik Nørding's hunting dogs. This new interpretation of the line was blended by American manufacturer Cornell & Diehl; the brand itself is Danish in origin. It contains flame-cured red and light-yellow Virginia leaves alongside genuine St. James Parish perique and a small amount of black cavendish. Per the maker, the perique proportion is around eight percent, placing the blend in the middle of classic VaPer measures. On the smoke, Virginia's natural sugar and tart sharpness lead; perique layers a dark fig-and-plum fruitiness and a light spice over it. Being ribbon cut, it packs easily and burns evenly. In nicotine terms it sits in the medium range. It suits smokers already familiar with unflavored Virginia blends who are newly moving into the VaPer type, and those wanting a tobacco that doesn't weigh them down through the day yet isn't plain.
nording-labrador-hunting-2025.o: Leaves a lightly spiced tobacco scent recalling dried fruit and toasted bread.

affordable-pipes-guys-navy-blend.z: Guy's Navy Blend is a mainly Virginia-based blend from Affordable Pipes' bulk line. Some Burley and a small amount of Perique are added to it. Per records, its profile is nutty, toasted, and lightly spicy, with a measured sweetness behind it. It offers a mild-on-the-palate smoke with low strength. Like many blends carrying the name "Navy," it's built on a balance of spice and sweetness. It suits users wanting to get to know Perique's contribution without seeking a heavy Virginia-Perique load.
affordable-pipes-guys-navy-blend.o: Leaves a sweetish room note of toasted nuts and light spice.

gawith-hoggarth-co-balkan-plug.z: Balkan Plug is the unsliced, plug-form presentation of the jet-black cake Gawith, Hoggarth & Co. produces by pressing and cooking Virginia and Cyprus latakia; records indicate it comes from the same dough as the firm's Balkan Flake. Since it rests as a plug, it retains its moisture for a long time, and the smoker chooses their own cut. Cooking softens Virginia's harsh side while bringing out the blend's earthy, smoky character; woody, spicy, and leather-like notes round this out. It is a record designed for smokers willing to spend time working with plug tobacco, slicing with a knife, and drying.
gawith-hoggarth-co-balkan-plug.o: Leaves an aroma of heavy woodsmoke and leather.

scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-special-d.z: No independent source describing the content and cut of Double Mixture, said to be a variant in the Special Dublin series according to records, could be found.
scandinavian-tobacco-group-stg-special-d.o: Recorded as leaving a sweet, lightly alcoholic casing scent.

peter-heinrichs-crue-pierre-henri-no-2.z: Crue Pierre Henri No. 2 is a blend in the Peter Heinrichs house's Crue Pierre Henri series, based on a composition of Virginia, Oriental, and Louisiana Perique. Per the maker's account, the blend uses oil- and aroma-rich, red-spotted Virginia leaves, small-leaved Macedonian-origin Orientals, and light-colored, broad-leaved Virginias with a nutty bouquet. The leaves are pressed sailor-style into a cake, then cut and roasted; this process gives the blend its characteristic taste and intense aroma. Virginia's sweetness and Perique's plum and spice note are balanced by the Oriental's dry tartness. Nicotine sits in the medium band, while flavor intensity is high due to the pressing and roasting. It is a suitable record for smokers wanting to get to know pressed Virginia-Perique structures and their Oriental-inclusive variations.
peter-heinrichs-crue-pierre-henri-no-2.o: Leaves a warm aroma recalling roasted bread and dried fig.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-tres-lech.z: Tres Leches is noted among The Country Squire's aromatic house blends inspired by the milk dessert of the same name; since no source documenting its composition and smoking character has been found, no further detail is given.
the-country-squire-tobacconist-tres-lech.o: No described room note has been found in records.

brigham-enterprises-inc-cambridge-blend.z: No sufficient independent sources documenting the content and character of the blend named Cambridge Blend under the Brigham Enterprises Inc. brand could be found.

jacks-tobacco-mangy-dog.z: No independent source documenting the composition and character of Mangy Dog, part of Jack's Tobacco's "Dog" line, could be found.
jacks-tobacco-mangy-dog.o: No reliable record of the room note could be found.

mac-baren-light-blend.z: No content and character information could be found in the manufacturer's catalog or in two independent sources for Mac Baren's blend known as Light Blend.

astleys-no-66-cavendish-club.z: Astley's No. 66 Cavendish Club is a light aromatic blend combining golden and black Virginias with flavored black Cavendish. Vanilla and the other toppings used alongside it are applied in a measured way; the tobacco's own sweetness stays up front. It's ribbon cut, with leaf colors ranging from yellowish tan to brown and black. The tin note carries spice notes reminiscent of clove and allspice, along with traces of fruit and earth. Nicotine load is light, and flavoring is light-to-medium. It suits those looking for an aromatic that doesn't let its topping dominate and keeps the Virginia character, as well as those wanting a light blend for all-day smoking.
astleys-no-66-cavendish-club.o: Leaves a sweet, spicy room note reminiscent of vanilla and allspice.

rotary-rotary-navy-cut.z: According to records, a Virginia-based navy cut blend from Rotary; no independent source confirming its producer and content could be found.

deans-natural-blend.z: Dean's Natural is a pipe tobacco produced in the US and sold in bags. Per the maker's description, it's prepared by combining select Virginia and burley leaves ribbon cut, without artificial flavoring or preservatives added; the aim is to bring out the leaves' own taste. The blend carries a light-to-medium fullness and, with its unadulterated body, appeals to those wanting to stay away from aromatics. Its large-gram packaging targets users consuming it regularly for everyday smoking.
deans-natural-blend.o: Leaves a plain, bready and lightly grassy tobacco scent.

tobacco-lane-irvin-cobb.z: A Tobacco Lane house blend that appears to take its name from Kentucky writer Irvin S. Cobb; no verifiable source on its composition has been found.
tobacco-lane-irvin-cobb.o: No source describing its aroma has been found.

peter-heinrichs-reserve-crue-no-6.z: Reserve Crue No. 6 is a pressed Peter Heinrichs blend whose base is built from red-spotted Virginia and Carolina leaf, with a small amount of Oriental-origin Havana leaf and medium-strength Kentucky added on top. Per the maker's account, the mixture is cold-pressed for weeks into blocks of about five kilograms; during this process the leaves fuse together, producing a very slow-burning flake. On the palate, Virginia's dark, dried-fruit-leaning sweetness leads; Kentucky adds a woody, lightly smoky base while Oriental leaf adds dry spice. There is no flavoring, and the body is medium. It suits those who love natural Virginia blends and long, patient smokes.
peter-heinrichs-reserve-crue-no-6.o: Leaves a dried fruit, bread crust, and light woody-smoke aroma.

the-country-squire-tobacconist-delta-hon.z: Delta Honeydew, one of the house blends from The Country Squire Tobacconist in Mississippi, is listed in catalog records as an aromatic mixture, but since no accessible independent source describing its content and character could be found, the full profile is left blank.

g-l-pease-isengard.z: No reliable source could be found establishing the composition and character of G. L. Pease's pipe tobacco Isengard.

argento-negro.z: Argento Negro is the Cavendish-based blend in the Argento line, produced in Argentina, referred to as number four in the line. Alongside Virginia and Latakia, it contains a touch of Oriental and mellow black Cavendish. The black Cavendish adds sweetness and body to the blend, while the Latakia gives a limited smokiness; the result is a milder profile than a full English blend, sitting between aromatic and unflavored. It's sold in 50-gram pouches. It suits those wanting to try Latakia in a measured dose over a sweet base.
argento-negro.o: Leaves a faintly smoky room note beneath a sweetish black Cavendish scent.

danske-club-sepia.z: A blend from the Danish brand Danske Club said to be aromatic; there isn't enough reliable source material to confirm its composition and character.

hearth-home-virginia-memory.z: No sufficient independent source could be found for this blend, described as straight Virginia, from the Hearth & Home brand.

g-l-pease-lagonda.z: Lagonda is a blend built by bringing together a generous amount of Cyprus latakia, ripe red Virginia, and Oriental leaf, with some bright Virginia added for sweetness. The mixture is pressed into plug form and aged; during this stage the flavours integrate and the leaves partially ferment. The plugs are later sliced and rubbed into ribbon form before boxing. In the smoke, latakia and Oriental leaf lead, with the Virginia base providing support. Beneath a smoky, woody, earthy body sit spicy, lightly tart, and floral notes; when exhaled through the nose, a peppery sharpness comes through. It is a record aimed at smokers accustomed to classic blends with a high latakia proportion who are seeking a full smoke.
g-l-pease-lagonda.o: Leaves a heavy woodsmoke and smokiness aroma that lingers long in the room.

stanwell-cherry.z: Stanwell is a Denmark-based pipe brand; its tobacco line is today produced at Scandinavian facilities in Denmark and Germany. Cherry represents the brand's cherry-flavored aromatic wing and, along with Ruby in the same line, counts among Stanwell's fruit-flavored everyday blends. The body is built from Virginia, burley, and black cavendish; the loose mixture cut makes packing easy. Nicotine stays light, and flavor level is kept low so the cherry topping leads. A product designed for those new to aromatic blends and the pipe, and for those seeking a sweet fruit profile.
stanwell-cherry.o: Fills the room with ripe cherry and sugared fruit scent.

john-aylesbury-spring-edition-2022.z: The 2022 entry in John Aylesbury's seasonal Spring Edition series; since the maker's current catalog only lists later years' spring editions, no verifiable source could be found on this release's composition.

hu-tobacco-the-swan.z: The Swan is an English-style mixture HU Tobacco prepared for CO Pipes. Cyprus Latakia, English black Cavendish, and a trace of Perique are added atop Virginia leaves of African and North and South American origin. Latakia stands at the forefront of the blend, while Perique adds a peppery sharpness. The thin coating on top rounds off the blend's edges but doesn't push the tobacco into the aromatic category. It's a blend aimed at those looking for Latakia-forward, smoky smokes.
hu-tobacco-the-swan.o: Leaves a smoky, incense-like aroma reminiscent of pine smoke.

p-lorillard-india-house-mixture.z: A historic aromatic mixture seen under the name "India House Aromatic Mixture" on old P. Lorillard tins, traceable today only through collectors' tins; no usable source describing the blend's composition could be found.

alfie-turmeaus-vanilla-bourbon.z: An aromatic house mixture from Turmeaus tobacconist noted as flavored toward vanilla and bourbon; no accessible source documenting its profile could be found.

mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2012.z: Christmas Cheer 2012 is the 2012 release of McClelland's single-crop annual Virginia series. Select flue-cured Virginia leaves are pressed into cake, matured, sliced, and partly broken up before being tinned as broken flake; this form eases packing and lighting. The blend is unflavored, and its taste rests on the leaf's own sugar: a sweet-tart Virginia line over a bready base. The sharpness in the tin note is a well-known trait of the brand. Suited to smokers wanting to follow the aging process who stay within the unflavored Virginia line. Production ended in 2018.
mcclelland-christmas-cheer-2012.o: Leaves a tangy, vinegary sweetness along with a toasted-bread aroma.

tinder-box-balkan.z: There is not enough independent documentation on the Tinder Box pipe tobacco called Balkan to record the blend's composition and character.

douwe-egberts-house-blend-regular.z: Not enough sourcing could be found to document the composition and character of House Blend Regular, a pipe tobacco from Douwe Egberts.
douwe-egberts-house-blend-regular.o: Not enough records exist for the scent it leaves in the room.

sutliff-tobacco-company-rl-bd.z: RL-BD is a mixture in Sutliff's bulk line sharing the same components as the blend called Man's Best Friend. Roasted cube-cut burley, selected Latakia, and lemon-yellow Virginia flake are brought together; a light rum casing is applied over the mix. The cube-cut burley gives a slow, cool burn, Latakia gives smoke, and Virginia gives sweetness; the touch of rum carries the blend to a light aromatic edge without making it fully unflavored. It suits smokers looking for a place between soft English mixtures and light aromatics.
sutliff-tobacco-company-rl-bd.o: Leaves a light rum and nutty scent mixed with wood smoke.

thepiperoom-com-balmoral.z: No independent source documenting the composition of the ThePipeRoom.com house blend Balmoral has been found; the brand's own site is no longer online.
thepiperoom-com-balmoral.o: No reliable record of the room note has been found.

cao-moontrance.z: CAO Moontrance is an aromatic prepared by adding exotic fruit essences and Madagascar bourbon vanilla to virginia leaf and silky black cavendish. The casing is built on a tropical fruit composition rather than a single fruit; vanilla rounds out this fruity core, leaving a light coconut trace behind. The smoke is cool and light in nicotine; it follows a sweet, flat line on the palate, with the leaf character in the background. Suitable for those seeking a light, sweet, distinctly aromatic blend to smoke all day, and for those new to aromatics. It is manufactured in the US as part of the CAO aromatic line.
cao-moontrance.o: Leaves a sweet tropical fruit aroma with vanilla and a light coconut note.

d-r-tobacco-ramback-gold.z: No reliable sources sufficient to establish the composition and character of D & R Tobacco's Ramback Gold blend were found.

pipe-republic-st-peters-flake.z: No reliable sources on Pipe Republic's blend St. Peter's Flake could be found, so its content, cut, and character could not be recorded.

carroll-p-j-co-ltd-maltan-ready-rubbed.z: P. J. Carroll & Co. was a company founded in Dundalk that was, for a long time, one of the leading manufacturers in the Irish tobacco market. Maltan Ready Rubbed is the company's product offering its dark Virginia slice ready-rubbed for use; its packaging also carries the wording "Maltan Rich Dark Flake." Because the pressed and matured mahogany-colored Virginia leaf is brought to a fine ribbon, it needs no further rubbing before filling. In the smoke, dark bread, molasses and lightly smoky tones come forward; no casing is used. Nicotine is medium. It is no longer in production today and stands as a historical record for those seeking Ireland's old household blends.
carroll-p-j-co-ltd-maltan-ready-rubbed.o: Leaves a dark bread and lightly smoky tobacco aroma.

fincks-cigar-company-sir-winston.z: No reliable source describing the composition and character of Sir Winston, one of Finck Cigar Company's shop blends, could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-black-cavendish-.z: Black Cavendish B20 is the cornerstone of Sutliff's bulk "B" line and consists entirely of black cavendish leaf. The leaves are darkened in the manner specific to the cavendish process, held under steam for an extended time under pressure; the maker describes this stage as a full day of steaming. The resulting leaf is soft, pliable, and moist. A soft, vanilla-heavy flavoring is applied on top. The smoke carries no pronounced nicotine weight or sharpness; flavor stays flat, sweet, and creamy. This makes the blend useful in two ways: as a very light aromatic on its own, or as a component added to soften the sharpness of other blends and correct their moisture balance. This second use is common among smokers who blend their own tobacco. It's ribbon cut and sold in bulk.
sutliff-tobacco-company-black-cavendish-.o: Leaves a scent of soft vanilla and sweet baked sugar.

bosphorus-chocolate-flake.z: Chocolate Flake is a chocolate-flavored flake, yellow-Virginia-forward, containing a small amount of burley and cavendish. Its color is nearly black; in the smoke the chocolate note stays faint, with Virginia's lightly bitter, tart taste coming forward. Strength and flavor intensity are low. The slices are at a moisture level ready to be filled and smoked without needing to be aired. Suitable for smokers seeking a light-smoking flake whose aroma does not overpower, or those newly moving to the flake format.
bosphorus-chocolate-flake.o: A faint cocoa trace accompanies a lightly sweetish, tart tobacco aroma.

4noggins-bald-headed-teacher.z: Bald Headed Teacher is one of the house blends from American bulk tobacco seller 4noggins. Unlike most Latakia-forward blends, its backbone is not Virginia but Burley, with Virginia and a small amount of Latakia layered on top. According to the records, no sweetener or topping is applied to the blend, and it contains no Perique. On the smoke, Burley's nutty, dry character leads; as the Virginia warms up it brings a mild tangy sweetness, while the Latakia sits in the background more like a spice note than a stand-alone component. It suits smokers looking for an unflavored, medium-strength American-style blend that can be smoked all day, with a light touch of Latakia.
4noggins-bald-headed-teacher.o: Leaves a thin layer of wood smoke over a scent of nuts and dried grass.

dan-tobacco-broder-petersens-special-pfe.z: A Virginia-and-Perique-focused Dan Tobacco blend whose tin bears an image of an old captain with a curved pipe; no adequate source documenting its ratios and cut was found.
dan-tobacco-broder-petersens-special-pfe.o: Records indicate it leaves a sweetish scent leaning toward dried fruit.

watch-city-cigar-american-cut-plug.z: This is one of the house blends of the Watch City Cigar shop; it does not appear in the current catalog, and no source could be found documenting its composition.

samuel-gawith-special-flake-no-2.z: No sufficient source documenting the composition of this sliced tobacco in Samuel Gawith's numbered Special Flake series could be found.

sutliff-tobacco-company-match-union-lead.z: A Virginia-burley-forward blend in Sutliff's Match line, prepared to correspond to the American drugstore classic Union Leader; no independent source detailing its content could be found.
sutliff-tobacco-company-match-union-lead.o: Records suggest it leaves a dry, grainy tobacco scent.

watch-city-cigar-mister-bs.z: This is a house blend from Watch City Cigar described as English-style, for which no sufficient source could be found.
watch-city-cigar-mister-bs.o: Records note it leaves a smoky scent typical of Latakia-containing English blends.

g-l-pease-ashbury.z: Ashbury is one of G. L. Pease's Latakia-heavy blends in the Balkan style. Cyprus latakia and a notable proportion of Oriental leaf are placed over a Virginia body; according to the producer's own comparison, the Orientals in this blend are sharper and more upfront than in Abingdon. This structure makes the blend less a smoky-layer mixture than a Balkan mixture led by a spicy, tart Oriental layer. It is aimed at smokers seeking the sharpness of Oriental leaf, accustomed to full-bodied mixtures; records note its availability on the market varies.
g-l-pease-ashbury.o: Leaves a heavy aroma dominated by sharp spice and burnt wood.

tinder-box-waffle-house.z: Waffle House is one of the specialty blends weighed at Tinder Box stores. A Cavendish-forward base is worked with a syrup-like casing; the blend is moistened to burn cool. Its smoke is light, the taste distinctly sweet, giving a smoke that doesn't bite the tongue. Nicotine load is low. Suited to fans of sweet, breakfast-evoking aromatics who want a light tobacco during the day.
tinder-box-waffle-house.o: Leaves a sweet aroma reminiscent of warm waffle batter and maple syrup.

lane-limited-captain-black-red-sky.z: Recorded as an aromatic blend tied to the Captain Black series; not enough sources could be found to document its composition.

intertabak-virginia-po-1004.z: No verifiable source could be found for this Virginia registered under the INTERTABAK name.

imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.z: This is the flavored version of the Cândido Giovanella line inspired by panettone, the bread commonly eaten in Brazil around New Year's. The base, as with the brand's other flavors, is built on Virginia, Burley, and black Cavendish; the cut is ribbon. In the smoke, notes of dried fruit, citrus peel, and vanilla evoking a bakery sweet come forward; the Virginia's bready sweetness overlaps with this flavoring. Nicotine is moderate, the smoke cool. It suits those who enjoy seasonal, sweet aromatics.
imigrantes-ind-e-com-de-fumos-ltda-candi.o: Leaves an aroma of sweet dried-fruit bread and vanilla.

peter-heinrichs-no-100.z: Peter Heinrichs No. 100 is an unflavored Virginia record among the firm's numbered house blends. Per the maker's description, selected Virginia leaves from different growing regions are brought together through a special flake process to form a balanced whole. Since it carries no flavoring, the taste comes entirely from the leaf's own sugar and the ripening that develops during pressing: grass, hay, and a light fruity sweetness lead. Nicotine stays in the medium band, while flavor intensity is pronounced due to the pressed structure. It is a suitable record for smokers interested in pure Virginia slices who are used to smoking slowly.
peter-heinrichs-no-100.o: Leaves a lightly sweet aroma recalling dry hay and baked bread.

dunhill-durbar.z: Durbar is one of Dunhill's classic oriental-forward mixtures. Per records, it was formed in the early 1910s with "eastern tobaccos" and its recipe has been updated several times over the years. In the blend the orientals take the lead role; latakia provides a smoky, woody base, while Virginia supplies a measured, meadow-like sweetness. The body runs medium to full, and the smoke is dark and balanced, carrying floral and tannic tones. It's designed for experienced smokers accustomed to Balkan-style mixtures with a pronounced oriental character. Since pipe tobacco production under the Dunhill name has ended, the blend is not found on the market under its original name.
dunhill-durbar.o: Leaves a heavy scent combining spicy Eastern tobacco, incense and wood smoke.

planta-anno-mmxiii-california-dream.z: This is a blend in Planta's limited-production Anno series, named after a year; no verifiable source could be found on its content and character.

james-fox-harrods-london-mixture.z: Recorded as one of the English-type Fox blends prepared for the Harrods shop; no independent source could be found to document its contents.

park-lane-tobacconist-red-paramour.z: No reliable source could be found for the Park brand pipe tobacco called Lane Tobacconist-Red Paramour, so a detailed profile could not be produced.

brobergs-tobakshandel-ab-brobergs-burley.z: Brobergs Burley is one of the house blends from Brobergs Tobakshandel, one of Sweden's long-established tobacconists. It is a classic mixture built on pure burley without a pronounced casing; it carries a light-to-medium strength, a full body, and a lightly spicy character that at times leans sweet. Thanks to burley's low sugar content it burns dry and cool, with a low tendency to bite the tongue. Suitable for smokers who want to avoid sugared aromatics and seek a plain, earthy tobacco. Brobergs traces back to the shop Johan August Broberg opened in Gothenburg in 1881; today it has stores in Gothenburg, Stockholm and Malmö.
brobergs-tobakshandel-ab-brobergs-burley.o: Leaves an aroma reminiscent of dry nut shell and cocoa powder.

gauntleys-of-nottingham-private-blend-no.z: No reliable source could be found on Gauntleys Of Nottingham's Private Blend No12.

sutliff-tobacco-company-highlander-2012.z: Highlander is a ribbon-cut blend Sutliff classifies as a Scottish mixture. Its composition of Virginia, burley, and cavendish leaves relies on a measured processing approach that lets the leaves' own sweetness come through rather than a heavy sauce; records indicate it's a well-balanced, easy-packing tobacco moisture-wise. The "2012" designation was used to distinguish that year's production run. In character it offers a medium-light fullness, balanced by burley's nutty, earthy side, Virginia's tangy sweetness, and cavendish's smoothing effect.
